english: Is there any danger in using the same knife to prune all the mango trees on my land?
ga: Ani oshara yɛ he akɛ mikɛ tsɔne kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ baafolɔ mango tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Using the same uncleaned knife across your whole farm can spread infection everywhere. If even one tree is infected, the knife will carry that sickness to every other tree you cut.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tsɔnei ni he tseee lɛ nɔŋŋ tsu nii yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ egbɛ hela lɛ eshwa he fɛɛ he. Kɛji tso kome he hela lɛ Kpãa lɛ baawo nakai hela lɛ kɛya tso fɛɛ tso ni obaafo lɛ nɔ.

english: How do tree diseases travel from one farm to another in my community?
ga: Te tsei ahe helai yaa ŋmɔ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔ mli yɛ mi akutso lɛ mli ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Diseases often travel when farm workers share cutlasses and tools or move contaminated equipment from an infected farm to a clean one without washing the tools first.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛ́ ŋmɔ mli nitsulɔi lɛ ja tsɔji kɛ nitsumɔ dadei. aloo nibii ni mli ewo muji ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ ni hela emɔ mli lɛ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔ ni mli tse mli ni ahooo nibii lɛ ahe klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Why do insects always gather around the spots where I pruned my crop branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii sumɔɔ ni amɛbua amɛhe naa lɛ? Nɛgbɛ mifoɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Insects are attracted to the sap and fresh wood exposed by pruning wounds. These open cuts act like an easy entrance for pests to feed and nest.
ga: Tso mli nu kɛ tsei ni afo ehee lɛ gbalaa kooloi. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii ni agbele naa nɛɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni ŋmeii baanyɛ abote mli koni amɛna niyenii kɛ amɛshĩa.

english: How do pests manage to get deep inside the trunk of my mango tree?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ boteɔ mango tso lɛ mli shɔŋŋ?

english: Pests look for weak entry points like cracks, holes, or cuts left by farm tools. Once a tree has an open wound, insects use it as an easy doorway to go inside.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baatao hei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛboteɔ mli tamɔ ŋmeii, bu loo ŋmeii ni ŋmɔ mli nibii eshi. Kɛ tso lɛ yɛ pilamɔ ko ni agbele naa lɛ Kplukai kɛbaatsu nii akɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni atsɔɔ nɔ aboteɔ mli.

english: Why do my mango trees suddenly get sick after I cut off some of their branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ hela mɔ mango tso lɛ trukaa beni mifo niji komɛi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cutting branches leaves open wounds on the tree. Disease germs floating in the air or sitting on your tool enter through these cuts and make the tree sick.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ haa pilamɔi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi. Muawai ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli loo ni kpɛtɛɔ odɛŋdadei lɛ ahe lɛ boteɔ pilamɔi nɛɛ amli ni amɛhaa tso lɛ hela mɔɔ lɛ.

english: Does wounding or cutting a tree make it easier for diseases to attack it?
ga: Tsei ni ayeɔ amɛ awui loo amɛfoɔ amɛhe lɛ kɛ helai srɔtoi baa. Ani tutuamɔ waaa?

english: Yes, a tree's bark acts like protective skin. Any cut or hole breaks this protection, making it much easier for diseases in the environment to invade the plant.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmei lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ hewolo ni buɔ mɔ he. Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni afolɔ loo bu ni afolɔ mli lɛ baafite hebuu nɛɛ Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa akɛ shihilɛ mli helai baatutua tsei.

english: What actually causes new tree diseases to start spreading on farms in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni miiha tso hela hee ko miije shishi egbɛ eshwa ŋmɔji amli yɛ Ghana?

english: Many crop diseases start when germs enter trees through open wounds made by tools during routine farm work like weeding, pruning, or harvesting.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe helai babaoo jeɔ shishi kɛ́ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ boteɔ tsei amli kɛtsɔɔ pilamɔi ni agbele ni nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔi ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ amli, tamɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. ŋmɔshi nibii loo kpamɔ

english: What should I do to protect my crop trees from getting sick when I prune them?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee koni mabu mitsei lɛ ahe koni hela akamɔ amɛ kɛ́ miikpa tsei lɛ?

english: Always sanitize your tools before cutting, make clean cuts that heal quickly, and avoid leaving rough cuts or unnecessary wounds on the tree trunk.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, tsumɔ odɛŋdadei lɛ ahe dani ofolɔ. Bɔɔ pilamɔi ni he tse ni tsaa oya. Ni tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo pilamɔi ni he ehiaaa ni oooshi yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ he.

english: Why are my plantain trees taking so long to produce fruit and giving small bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii ni ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Plantains need plenty of water and rich, nutrient-dense soil to form large bunches. If there is a drought or the soil lacks nutrients, the tree slows down its growth and produces smaller, lighter fruits.
ga: Nu babaoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ he miihia plantains koni enyɛ efee jwɛi wuji. Kɛji hɔmɔ ba loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii bɛ lɛ Tso lɛ baaha edalɛ aya hiɛ fioo ni ebaawo yibii bibii.

english: How long does it take from the day I plant a plantain sucker until I can harvest the plantains?
ga: Be enyiɛ ebaahe kɛjɛ gbi ni adu ŋmeii diji lɛ nɔ kɛyashi abaakpa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: It generally takes between 11 and 15 months for a plantain tree to grow, flower, and mature a bunch of fruit ready for harvest, depending on water availability and soil fertility.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ nyɔji 11 kɛyashi 15 dani dumɔwui lɛ daa, amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛshwereɔ ni amɛfeɔ aduawai akui ni asaa he kɛha kpamɔ. Edamɔ nu ni yɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I need to cut away extra young shoots growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Extra shoots compete directly with the main tree for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Pruning them down so only one or two strong suckers remain allows the main tree to put all its energy into a large, healthy bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli. Kɛtsɔ tsei niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi koni eshi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso titri lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ afee ŋmeii agbo ni mli wa.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my plantain trees turning yellow and drying up early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi oya lɛ?

english: Early leaf yellowing often means the plant lacks crucial nutrients like potassium, is suffering from water stress, or is affected by leaf spot diseases. Adding organic manure and clearing sick leaves helps keep the canopy healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ mra lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium, ni nu he haomɔ miipiŋ lɛ. loo leaf spot hela lɛ emɔ lɛ Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛfataa he ni ajieɔ baai ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my yams come out small and twisted when I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ feɔ bibioo ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ akpa lɛ?

english: Yams require loose, soft soil in high mounds or ridges so the tuber can expand downward easily. Hard, clay-heavy, or rocky soil stops the tuber from expanding, resulting in small or misshapen yams.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei amli bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mlɛo. Shikpɔŋ ni wa, shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ, loo tɛi baatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce energy for the tuber underground. Training the vines onto tall stakes spreads the leaves out to catch solar light, which helps build bigger, heavier yams.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ́ otsɔse wain tso lɛ yɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ, ebaagbɛ ebaa lɛ eshwa koni ekɛhere hulu la lɛ atuu. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni afeɔ sweet potatoes ni dara ni tsii.

english: How can I store my harvested yams so they do not rot quickly before my family can use them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ ato koni ekafite oya dani miweku lɛ kɛtsu nii?

english: Store your yams off the ground in a shaded, well-ventilated structure like a yam barn. Avoid storing bruised or cut tubers, as damaged skin lets in bacteria and fungi that cause rot.
ga: Kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ato shikpɔŋ nɔ yɛ he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ, tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ shĩa. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni etse loo afo lɛ ni oootoo lɛ he. Enɛ ji akɛ, hewolo ni efite lɛ baanyɛ ajie helatsɛmɛi kɛ ŋmeii ni kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ.

english: Why do my yams start sprouting green shoots on their own when kept in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ kɛ́ akɛto he ko ni akɛtoɔ nii lɛ?

english: After harvest, yams enter a natural resting phase called dormancy. Once this period ends, the tuber uses its stored energy to sprout shoots, sensing that it is time for a new planting season.
ga: yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Sweet potatoes boteɔ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy mli. Kɛ be nɛɛ ba naagbee lɛ Bulbs lɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni ato lɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛkwɛ̃. Henumɔ akɛ be eshɛ kɛha shweremɔ be hee.

english: Can I grow plantains and yams together on the same farm plot?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu plantain kɛ sweet potato yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting yams and plantains together is a great strategy. The plantains grow tall and provide shelter, while yams grow in soil mounds, allowing you to harvest food at different times of the year from the same land.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ ji gbɛ kpakpa. Plantains lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛha wɔɔhe. Be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ muji lɛ mli Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa niyenii yɛ bei srɔtoi amli. afi lɛ mli kɛjɛ shikpɔŋkuku nɛɛ nɔŋŋ mli

english: What short-term crops can I plant to feed my family while waiting for long-season crops like plantains to yield?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni heɔ be kukuoo manyɛ makwɛ koni makwɛ miweku lɛ yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni heɔ be kakadaŋŋ tamɔ plantains lɛ koni amɛwo yibii?

english: Fast-maturing crops like vegetables, maize, or legumes can be harvested within three to four months. Planting these between long-season crops ensures your family has food while waiting for main harvests.
ga: Abaanyɛ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ aduawai, ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. Nibii nɛɛ ni ooodu yɛ be mli nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni oweku lɛ náa niyenii yɛ be mli ni amɛmɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔ titri lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of maize plants usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or well-decomposed manure will help the crop regain its green color and produce larger cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛsu ni ji eŋɔli lɛ mli ekoŋŋ ni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Crops cannot absorb dry fertilizer directly through their roots; the nutrients must first dissolve in water. Applying fertilizer to dry soil can burn plant roots or waste fertilizer, so it is best applied when the soil is moist after rain.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi kɛtsɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Esa akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ awo nu mli klɛŋklɛŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso shishifãi lɛ ashã loo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afite. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ.

english: Excessive water in the soil deprives cassava roots of air and encourages fungal rot. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away, keeping the roots healthy.
ga: Nu ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaha ŋmei shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ewo ŋmei ni fiteɔ lɛ he hewalɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. ni oha shishifãi lɛ awa

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is usually caused by a virus spread by tiny whitefly insects, or by severe heat stress. Managing whiteflies with spraying and keeping the soil moist helps prevent the leaves from curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli Nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my cowpea plants produce healthy leaves but very few seeds inside the pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ shi dumɔwui fioo pɛ yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Small insects like pod borers often attack cowpea flowers and young pods, feeding on developing seeds inside. Controlling these pests with timely, safe spraying during flowering ensures pods fill up with healthy seeds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ pod borers lɛ tutuaa cowpea fɔfɔi kɛ pod bibii lɛ. Amɛyeɔ dumɔwui ni miiya hiɛ yɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛtsɔ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe yɛ be ni sa mli yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ eyiɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli obɔ.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they face environmental stress, such as long dry spells, poor soil nutrients, or insect damage. Providing shade trees, watering during droughts, and controlling pests help flowers develop into full cocoa pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe shihilɛ mli haomɔi, tamɔ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ mli. Niyenii ni esaaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli loo kooloi amli lɛ fiteɔ, ni ehaa hulutsoo, nu yɛ hulutsoo be mli Ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe nitsumɔ haa fɔfɔi lɛ daraa kwraa ni amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii.

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems that struggle to support heavy fruit bunches, especially during storms. Supporting the main stem with strong wooden props or bamboo stakes prevents them from uprooting.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛye amɛbua aduawai ni tsii lɛ. Titri lɛ yɛ ahum beaŋ Kɛ́ okɛ tsei ni wa loo ŋmei tsei fi tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi enaa koni ekaje shishi.

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same land exhausts specific soil nutrients and lets maize-specific pests and diseases accumulate in the soil. Rotating maize with leguminous crops like groundnuts or cowpeas restores nitrogen and breaks disease cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi baafite. ni eha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ ŋmãa helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa ekoŋŋ ni ekpaa hela lɛ sɛɛkuu.

english: Why do yam vines need to climb up wooden stakes to give bigger yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛná sweet potatoi wuji lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce energy that feeds the tuber growing underground. Staking holds the leaves up to catch sunlight and keeps them off damp soil, preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ ni akɛhaa ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ aba. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ hiɔ hulu la mli ni ehaaa sũ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Koni akɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa

english: Why do my young vegetable seedlings die suddenly right after I move them to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables dumɔwui bibii lɛ gboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ amɛ wo ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seedlings experience transplant shock when moved into hot, direct sunlight without enough soil moisture. Shading young plants with palm fronds for a few days and watering them regularly helps them recover and grow strong.
ga: Dumɔwui naa piŋmɔ kɛji ajie amɛ kɛtee he ko ni edɔ, hulu la tɛ̃ɛ ni sũ mli nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei baai wo tsei bibii amli gbii fioo komɛi ni okɛ nu wo amɛmli daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛhe awa amɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I just plant the leftover beans I bought from the market, or do I need special seeds?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmeii ni eshwɛ ni mihe yɛ jara nɔ lɛ? Aloo dumɔwui krɛdɛɛi he miihia mi?

english: Market beans are intended for cooking and eating; they may grow poorly, yield less, or carry diseases. Certified planting seeds are specially treated and selected to sprout reliably, resist diseases, and give you a much higher harvest.
ga: Ayɛ jarayeli mli ŋmeii ni akɛhooɔ nii ni ayeɔ. Ekolɛ amɛdaŋ jogbaŋŋ. Ehaa yibii fioo loo eyɛ hela Akwɛɔ tsei dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ahalaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ, amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: How should I keep my saved seeds safe so they will grow well during the next rainy season?
ga: Te esa akɛ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ ahi shweshweeshwe bɔni afee ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Seeds must be dried thoroughly and stored in airtight containers kept off the bare floor in a cool, dry place. Dampness and warmth attract insects and mold, which destroy the seed's ability to sprout.
ga: Esa akɛ agbi dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni akɛto tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ yɛ he ko ni mli ejɔ ni egbi. Fɛ̃i kɛ latsaa gbalaa kooloi kɛ ŋmeii. ni fiteɔ nyɛmɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ yɔɔ ni amɛkɛbaa lɛ.

english: How does growing beans on my land make the soil better for other crops later?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: Beans and other legumes have natural helpers in their roots that pull nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil, acts like a free natural fertilizer that feeds the crops you plant afterwards.
ga: Beans kɛ legumes krokomɛi Adebɔɔ mli yelikɛbuamɔi yɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very thin and tall with small cobs when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ shwilafoi bibii lɛ? Be ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he?

english: When crops are planted too close, they struggle against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving them proper spacing allows each plant to get enough food and light to build thick stalks and large cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli tsei ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the plant lacks nitrogen fertilizer. When nitrogen is short, the plant takes what little it has from its older lower leaves and sends it up to keep the young top leaves growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛ nitrogen faaa Tso lɛ heɔ nɔ fioo ni eyɔɔ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli ni etsuɔ ​​kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ aya nɔ ada.

english: Peppers drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as very dry soil, extreme heat, or a lack of plant nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist and well-nourished keeps the flowers attached so fruit can form.
ga: Peppers baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔi tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa, dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa, loo tso mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ he. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni eye niyenii jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ he ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why does my cassava grow huge leafy branches above ground but tiny tubers under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ niji agboi ni yɔɔ baai yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: If cassava receives too much nitrogen fertilizer or grows in heavy shade, it puts all its energy into making lush leaves instead of sending food down into the ground to build thick tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmei babaoo nɔ loo eda yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛhaa ebaa lɛ feɔ eŋɔli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsu niyenii kɛba shi koni ekɛma ŋmeii ni mli tse yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why does my harvest get smaller every time I grow the exact same crop on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ faaa be fɛɛ be ni madu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop year after year drains the same specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and soil diseases that love that specific crop to build up in huge numbers.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni akwɛɔ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni sumɔɔ nakai tso lɛ buaa amɛhe naa babaoo.

english: Why is it better to start tomato seeds in a seedbed before moving them to the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaaje tomato dumɔwui ashishi yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli dani ajie amɛ kɛya ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato seeds are tiny and delicate. Starting them in a small nursery lets you protect them easily from heavy rain, hot sun, and insects, so you can pick only the strongest seedlings to transplant into the big field.
ga: Tomato dumɔwui lɛ daraaa ni amɛhe waaa. Kɛ́ obɔi tsei yɛ tsei akwɛmɔhe bibioo ko lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ obuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he oya. Hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kooloi bibii yeɔ amɛ, no hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ ohala dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ pɛ ni okɛdu yɛ ŋmɔji wuji amli.

english: Does it matter if I wait until my crops grow big before I clear the weeds around them?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mamɛ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adara dani mikɛ jwɛi awo amɛhe?

english: Yes, it matters a lot. Weeds steal water and fertilizer when young crops need them most, permanently stunting your crop's growth even if you remove the weeds later in the season.
ga: Hɛɛ, ehe miihia waa. Jwɛi juɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be mli ni tsei bibii he hiaa amɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ. Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akafee nɔ ko kwraa. Kɛji ojie jwɛi lɛ yɛ be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli po lɛ,.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize start turning yellow from the bottom leaves going upward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛmiijɛ baa lɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the bottom usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, a key nutrient in the soil. The plant moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the younger top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Tsei lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli koni ekɛya ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop many of their flowers without producing any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop extra flowers if they don't have enough water, shade, or soil nutrients, or if pests like mirids are attacking the small flower stems.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ baajie fɔfɔii kɛjɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji amɛbɛ nu, hulutsoo loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi tamɔ pollen miitutua fɔfɔi bibii lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow very big green leaves but produce very few peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yɛ baai wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi ewoɔ pepper fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: When crops get too much nitrogen fertilizer, they focus all their energy on making tall stems and lush green leaves instead of developing flowers and fruits.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná nitrogen fertilizer babaoo lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa tsei lɛ ashishifãi kakadaji kɛ tsei ahe tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ afeemɔ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai

english: Why does covering the soil around my young crops with dry grass help them grow better in hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo mi dumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass (mulching) acts like an umbrella for the soil, blocking direct sunlight so water doesn't evaporate quickly and keeping the plant roots cool.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ. Tsi hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa No hewɔ lɛ, nu lɛ shwieee oya ni ehaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: Why should I apply my fertilizer after it rains instead of when the soil is dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ moŋ fe be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi lɛ?

english: Fertilizer must dissolve in water for roots to drink it; applying chemical fertilizer on hot, dry soil can burn plant roots and cause the fertilizer to waste away in the air.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo nu mli koni shishifãi lɛ anu nu. Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi nɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: Groundnuts and beans have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which helps keep the soil rich and feeds nearby crops like maize.
ga: Akpɔlɔi kɛ ŋmeii yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ni ehaa niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ abele.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground before I can harvest them during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani abaanyɛ akpa amɛ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when wet soil stays flooded for too long because roots need air to breathe, which allows underground water mold and fungi to attack and decay the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ nu ho shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees snap and fall over easily when a light wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ fãa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ fioo ko tswa lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and can be eaten from the inside by microscopic worms (nematodes) or root borers, leaving the heavy tree without a strong grip in the soil.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni ŋmeii bibii baanyɛ aye amɛ kɛjɛ mli. (nematodes) loo shishifãi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ Enɛ haa tsei ni tsii lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɔmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling upwards and turning small and pale?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛji bibii ni amɛhe tseee lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by a virus spread by tiny whiteflies feeding on the plant, which prevents the tomato leaves from growing to full size.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni ŋmeii yɛŋ bibii ni yeɔ tsei lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni no haaa tomato baai lɛ ada kɛyashɛ amɛdalɛ naa.

english: Yams are living roots that wake up and sprout when exposed to heat and light, signaling to the tuber that it is time to grow a new vine.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji shishifãi ni hiɛ ka ni teɔ shi ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛji akɛ amɛwo la kɛ la mli. Enɛ haa bulb lɛ leɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ adu wain tsei heei.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize is starving for nitrogen, an important nutrient it needs to grow. It can also happen when heavy rains wash away nutrients from the soil or flood the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa lɛ koni eda Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ho niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe loo ekɛ nu ewo shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before they can turn into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani amɛbatsɔmɔɔ cacao ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they suffer from stress, such as a lack of shade, prolonged dry weather, or insect attacks. Providing shade trees and protecting the farm from dry winds helps the flowers stay on the tree and develop into pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ haomɔi tamɔ hulutsoo ni bɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ hewɔ. loo kooloi ni tutuaa ŋmɔ lɛ he hulutsoo ni abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking the sap from the leaves, or by a virus spread by these insects. Controlling these pests early keeps the leaves healthy and flat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ Kudɔmɔ kooloi nɛɛ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baa lɛ mli waa ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: This is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium from the soil, often because the soil moisture keeps changing from too dry to too wet. Consistent watering helps prevent it.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni haa ebaa lɛ nakai ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni mli edɔ lɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ nɔ ni egbi tsɔ kɛyaa nɔ ni mli edɔ tsɔ nɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests every year when I plant maize in the exact same spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii fioo daa afi beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop in the same soil every season removes the same nutrients over and over while allowing crop pests to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores nutrients back into the soil naturally.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii mli nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ shii abɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai buaa amɛhe naa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Cassava roots rot when water stays trapped in the soil around the roots for too long, creating conditions for rot diseases. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps extra water drain away easily.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Ebaanyɛ ekɛ hela ni fiteɔ nii aba. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya.

english: Why do my yams grow small, thin, and twisted instead of big and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potatoes lɛ ji bibii, ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni ebɔle ehe yɛ agbo ni etse lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yams need soft, loose, and deep soil to expand downward easily. If the soil is hard or full of rocks, the tuber cannot grow straight, so building high mounds with loose topsoil gives them room to swell.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse, ni mli kwɔ koni egbɛ eshwa kɛya shi mlɛo. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa loo tɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ Yitso lɛ nyɛŋ ada tɛ̃ɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ama gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ ni sũ ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ etse lɛ, ebaaha hei komɛi afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Where can I get reliable, high-quality seeds that yield good crops, and how do I know if they are official?
ga: Nɛgbɛ maná dumɔwui ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ, ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni woɔ yibii kpakpai yɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nakai dumɔwui lɛ ji nɔ ni maŋ lɛ ŋmɛ gbɛ?

english: Good seeds can be bought from registered agro-dealers, local Ministry of Food and Agriculture (MOFA) offices, or approved seed cooperatives. Look for official certification tags on the bag to ensure the seeds will germinate well and resist common diseases.
ga: Abaanyɛ ahe dumɔwui kpakpai kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔi ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo wolo nɔ lɛ adɛŋ. Niyenii kɛ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ (MOFA) loo dumɔwui akuu ni akpɛlɛ nɔ. Taomɔ wolo ni tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni helai ni afɔɔ namɔ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and weak with small leaves when I plant seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ daa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni amɛyɛ baai bibii beni mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing plants compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Spacing seeds according to recommendations ensures every plant gets enough light and nutrients to grow strong.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ taakɛ atsɔɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my plantain stems bending and snapping at the base before the fruits mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkuɔ yɛ shishigbɛ dani aduawai lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: This usually happens when banana weevils or root worms attack the stem and roots underground, weakening the plant. Using clean, healthy planting suckers and keeping the base of the plant free of weeds prevents this damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ banana ŋmeii loo shishifãi amli ŋmeii tutua shikpɔŋ shishi tsei kɛ shishifãi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ Kɛ akɛ tsei ni he tse ni yɔɔ hewalɛ tsu nii ni akɛ jwɛi akafee shishi lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do small caterpillars keep eating the inner leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ yeɔ mi ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli baai lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that targets the tender central leaves of maize. They feed inside the leaf whorl to hide from heat and predators while destroying the plant's growing point.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni tswaa ŋmãa bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ. Amɛyeɔ nii yɛ baai lɛ amli koni amɛkɛ amɛhe ahi dɔlɛ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni amɛfiteɔ hei ni tsei lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers usually drop off when temperatures get too high or when plants experience water stress. Excessive heat makes the pollen sterile, so the flower cannot produce fruit and dies off.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ. Dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ haa pollen lɛ feɔ nɔ ni bɛ fɔmɔ nii. Fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɛɛ awo yibii ni egbo.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crop turning yellow starting from the bottom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the bottom of maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil. The plant moves available nitrogen from older lower leaves to feed newer growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋmeii heei ni eda yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt in the afternoon sun even if I water them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ leebi moŋ?

english: During hot afternoons, pepper plants lose water through their leaves faster than roots can absorb it. Wilting is a natural reaction to reduce leaf surface area exposed to heat, and plants usually recover by evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Wilting ji adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni haa baai ni hulutsoo baa lɛ anɔ lɛ baa shi. Ni bei pii lɛ, tsei lɛ he waaa amɛ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why are my yam vines remaining short with pale leaves this season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ yɛ baai ni egboi kɛ baai ni mli tse lolo yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Short vines and pale leaves usually mean the soil nutrients have been depleted from previous farming, or the seed yams had hidden diseases or pest damage before planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, wain tsei kukuji kɛ baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ efo kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni adu tsutsu lɛ mli. aloo sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ yɛ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai efite amɛ dani adu.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are delicate and easily scorched by full sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide broad leaves that act as natural shade umbrellas to protect young cocoa plants during their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shãa amɛ oya. Dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: What happens to my cassava crop if I plant the stem cuttings too close together?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji midu ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When planted too close, cassava stems compete for light, water, and soil space. Instead of growing large tubers underground, the plants spend all their energy growing tall, thin stems with small yields.
ga: Kɛ adu Cassava tsei lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, amɛyeɔ la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ he akaŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaadu bulb agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ Tsei nɛɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ ni amɛhe tseee shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ.

english: Why should I strip off the lower leaves of my growing tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo mi-tomato tsei ni miida lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ?

english: Removing lower leaves improves airflow around the base of the plant to prevent fungal diseases caused by wet soil splash, allowing the plant to direct more energy toward growing larger fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie shishigbɛ baai lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ tso lɛ he lɛ aya hiɛ. Tso shishitoo koni akɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ shwiemɔ mli baa lɛ naa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ babaoo woɔ aduawai wuji ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ mli.

english: Weeds grow faster and have stronger root systems than most crops, allowing them to absorb fertilizer and water quickly before your main plants can reach those nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛshishifãi lɛ wa fe tsei babaoo. Enɛ haa amɛnáa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu oya dani tso titri lɛ nyɛɔ enáa nakai niyenii lɛ.

english: How do I know if my planted corn seeds are rotting underground from too much rain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ hewɔ?

english: If corn seeds fail to sprout after 7 to 10 days of heavy rain, digging up a few will show soft, discolored, or mushy seeds that failed to breathe due to waterlogged soil.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa gbii 7 kɛyashi 10 sɛɛ lɛ, kɛ́ atsa amɛ fã ko lɛ, ebaajie ŋmãa ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni ehiɛ su, loo ni etsɔ muji ni miihoso yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ hewɔ lɛ kpo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main plant nutrient responsible for leaf growth and green color. It can also happen when heavy rains wash nutrients deep into the ground where roots cannot reach them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji tso lɛ mli niyenii titri ni haa baa lɛ daa kɛ eŋɔli su. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sun. Plantain trees grow very fast and produce large leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving cocoa trees the shade and moist air they need during their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ shade. Enɛ haa kookoo tsei lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni he hiaa amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants and prevents pollen from fertilizing the flowers. When heat is too high, the plant drops its blossoms to save energy instead of growing fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa pollen lɛ nyɛɛɛ ekɛ fɔfɔi lɛ awo fɔfɔi lɛ amli. Kɛji latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baafɔ̃ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: What causes small holes to appear in my cabbage leaves overnight?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cabbage baai lɛ feɔ bu bibii? lɛ je kpo nyɔɔŋ kome mli

english: Small holes are usually caused by caterpillars or beetles that hide in the soil or under leaves during the day and feed on the foliage at night when it is cooler.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo shikpɔŋ loo baai ashishi yɛ gbi mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii baa. ni oye baai lɛ gbɛkɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ

english: Yams need loose, deep, and well-drained soil to expand downward easily. If the soil is hard clay, rocky, or compacted, the tubers struggle to push deep and end up bent or stunted.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni mli kwɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ koni egbɛ eshwa kɛya shi oya. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa, tɛi yɔɔ mli, loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛya shɔŋŋ ni amɛbaagbe naa akɛ amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants stay small and produce few peppers when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ ji bibii ni amɛwoɔ pepper fioo kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight over the same water and soil nutrients while their leaves block each other from getting sunlight, resulting in weak growth.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa amɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dalɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ

english: Why do my harvested cassava roots start turning black and spoiling after just two days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa lɛ bɔi ediŋŋ ni amɛgboi yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots start a natural chemical breakdown as soon as they are cut from the stem. Because they do not have a thick skin like yams, exposure to air causes rapid discoloration and spoilage.
ga: Cassava shishifãi jeɔ shishi amɛgbalaa tsofai yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji ajie amɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi pɛ. Ejaakɛ amɛbɛ hewolo ni mli tse tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ mɔ ko kɛ ehe wo kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ, ehaa ehe su tsakeɔ oya ni efiteɔ.

english: Why do some of my nursery seeds rot in the soil before they even sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ dumɔwui lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ po lɛ?

english: Seeds rot when the nursery bed stays too wet or flooded. Too much water cuts off oxygen to the seed, allowing soil fungi to destroy the seed before it can sprout.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ ŋmɔ mli saatso lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ. Nu babaoo ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa dumɔwui lɛ amli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ dumɔwui dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl upward in the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural survival trick plants use to shield themselves from strong sunlight and slow down the amount of water lost through their leaf pores during the hottest hours.
ga: Baai lɛ ni abɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ ŋaa ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni eha nu ni laajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ baai amli buji amli yɛ bei ni mli edɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do weeds grow back much faster than my crops right after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to local conditions, meaning their roots absorb water and nutrients faster than cultivated crops, allowing them to shoot up quickly after rain.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsɔ amɛhe amɛwo shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ gbalaa nu kɛ niyenii oya fe tsei ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ nɛ.

english: How do I know when my green plantains are ready to cut down?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ plantains eŋɔli lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa?

english: Plantains are ready to harvest when the individual fruits lose their sharp edges and become plump and round. You should harvest them while they are still firm and green if you need to transport them to the market before they ripen.
ga: Plantains lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛ́ aduawai lɛ eko fɛɛ eko sɛɛ efo ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Esa akɛ okpa amɛ be mli ni amɛyɛ shiŋŋ ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔji lolo lɛ. Kɛji oosumɔ ni okɛ amɛ aya jara nɔ dani amɛshwere lɛ,.

english: What is the safest way to cut down a heavy bunch of plantains without damaging the fruit?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ afoɔ plantain babaoo ni afiteee aduawai lɛ?

english: Make a shallow cut about halfway up the trunk of the plantain tree so it slowly bends down under its own weight. This allows you to catch or gently lower the heavy bunch to the ground before cutting it off, which stops the fruit from getting bruised.
ga: Feemɔ ŋmei ni mli ekwɔɔɔ aaafee dumɔwu lɛ shishi fã koni eha eda blɛoo. Bent under its own weight Gbɛ nɛɛ haa onyɛɔ omɔɔ loo okɛ ŋmeii ni tsii baa shi blɛoo kɛyaa shikpɔŋ dani ofoɔ amɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni tso yibii lɛ akafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that struggle to support heavy fruit bunches, especially in soft soil or strong winds. Supporting the main stem with a sturdy bamboo pole or wooden prop helps hold the weight until the plantains mature.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛfi aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ. Titri lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei tso loo tso ni wa fi tso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni efi muji lɛ sɛɛ kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are some of my plantain trees giving me small bunches while others give big ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantains komɛi woɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi woɔ ŋmeii wuji lɛ?

english: Plantain trees need plenty of nutrients and water to grow large bunches. If too many young shoots grow around the main trunk, they steal food from the plant, which results in smaller fruit bunches.
ga: Niyenii kɛ nu babaoo he miihia dumɔwui koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔmɔ jwɛi wuji. Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii bibii komɛi yɛ ni miida yɛ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ he tsɔ lɛ Ebaaju niyenii kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli. ni haa aduawai bibii baa

english: How many young shoots should I leave around a main plantain tree?
ga: Tso bibii enyiɛ esa akɛ mashi yɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ he?

english: It is best to leave only two or three shoots of different sizes around the main trunk—one medium-sized shoot for the next harvest and one tiny sucker for the future. Pruning away the rest gives the main plant full energy to produce big fruit.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshi ŋmeii ni dalɛi srɔtoi enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ abɔle tso wulu lɛ he - ŋmeii ni dalɛ ji teŋgbɛ kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii kome kɛha wɔsɛɛ be. Kɛ́ afo nɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ náa hewalɛ fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ewo yibii wuji.

english: Why do the leaves on my plantain tree dry up and turn yellow before the fruit is ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani aduawai lɛ shwere lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant lacks water or nutrients, or it has been affected by leaf diseases. Cutting off dead lower leaves and spreading animal manure or compost around the base will help the tree stay green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu loo niyenii bɛ tso lɛ mli. loo baa helai emɔ amɛ Kpãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni egboi lɛ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ashwie amɛhe. Kɔnii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɔ shi eŋɔli ni ehiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: How much distance should I leave between plantain shoots when planting a new farm?
ga: Gbɛ enyiɛ esa akɛ maŋmɛ plantains lɛ ateŋ kɛ́ midu ŋmɔ hee?

english: Plantains grow best when planted about 3 meters (roughly 10 feet) apart. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough sunlight, air, and room for its roots to gather food.
ga: Plantains lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mitai 3 (aaafee ninetalɔi 10). Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ abua niyenii naa.

english: Can I plant maize or vegetables together with my plantains on the same land?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa loo aduawai kɛ plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, you can plant quick-growing crops like maize or garden eggs between young plantain trees during their first few months. As the plantains grow large leaves and shade the ground, you can transition to focusing solely on the plantains.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ obɔɔ lɛ mli. yɛ dumɔwui bibii ateŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji 2-3 lɛ amli, beni dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ baai wuji ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo Obaanyɛ otsake kɛya plantains pɛ nɔ ni okɛ ojwɛŋmɔ ama nɔ.

english: How can I protect my plantain plants from drying out during the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-plantain lɛ naa koni ekagbi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Covering the ground around the base of your plantain plants with dead leaves, dry grass, or old chopped plantain stems keeps the soil cool and moist by reducing evaporation from the sun.
ga: Akɛ baai ni egboi, jwɛi ni egbi, loo plantain tsei momo ni afolɔ ashwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle Base plantains lɛ he lɛ nɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛtsɔ la ni jɛɔ hulu la mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my plantain farm produce less fruit after three or four years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain ŋmɔ lɛ wooo yibii fioo yɛ afii etɛ loo ejwɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: As plantain stands age, their root systems push closer to the surface where soil nutrients have been depleted. Adding organic compost, clearing excess suckers, and replanting new suckers every few years keeps harvest yields high.
ga: Beni plantains hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ Amɛshishifãi lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛbɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa lɛ. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ amli Kɛ ŋmeii heei ni aduɔ daa afii fioo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni anáa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen in the soil. The plant moves nitrogen from its older, lower leaves to feed the new growth at the top. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted manure fixes this issue.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ kɛ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi dalɛ hee lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why do people advise me to plant cowpeas or beans between my maize rows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ mi-ŋmei ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and beans take nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots. This naturally fertilizes the soil, helping your maize grow stronger while giving you an extra harvest from the same field.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ beans lɛ jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Gbɛ nɛɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii afata he yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ye obua o-corn lɛ ni ehiɛ wa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebua bo ni onáa yibii babaoo kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ kome mli.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with plenty of leaves, but the tubers underground remain tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii lolo?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or is packed too tightly, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing heavy leaves above ground instead of storing starch in roots below. Loosening the soil and avoiding excess nitrogen encourages root growth.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ tsɔ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ŋmei baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa ni tsii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ajie nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛjɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ adara.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain trees next to my young cocoa seedlings on a new farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ? Kookoo tsei bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ hee ko mli

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and produce large, wide leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa the cool shade and moist air it needs to survive its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya waa ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Enɛ haa kookoo bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up into tight cups and stopping new growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe kɛmiifee kɔɔpoi ni mli wa ni amɛmiikpa dalɛ hee lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves. They suck out the leaf sap, causing the leaf to dry out and curl up. Spraying with neem oil or recommended insecticide controls them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. Amɛmuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ gbiɔ ni amɛkpãa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni ajieɔ yi lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaakudɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of flowers, but the flowers keep falling off without forming tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee tomato?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme afternoon heat, irregular watering, or attacks by tiny pests like thrips. Keeping the soil evenly moist and mulching around the roots helps protect the flowers so they turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ thrips ni tutuaa mɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ baaye abua ni abu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛtsɔmɔ aduawai.

english: Why do some of my harvested yams have deep cracks and strange twisted shapes instead of being smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ ekomɛi yɛ ŋmeii ni mli kwɔ kɛ fãji ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Yam tubers crack or bend when the soil is hard, stony, or compacted, making it difficult for the tuber to expand smoothly underground. Heavy rains after a long dry period can also cause the tuber to swell too fast and split open.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baakumɔ loo amɛbaabɔle amɛhe kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa, tɛi yɔɔ mli, loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni no baaha ewa aha ŋmeii lɛ akɛ amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ shishi. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha bulbs lɛ agbɔjɔ oya tsɔ ni efo.

english: Why do small, young cocoa pods turn shriveled and black on the tree before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This is often caused by 'cherelle wilt,' which happens when the cocoa tree doesn't have enough nutrients or water to feed all its pods, or when minor pests bite them. The tree naturally sacrifices smaller pods to save the bigger ones.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ‘cherelle wilt’, ni baa beni cacao tso lɛ bɛ niyenii loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua pod muu lɛ fɛɛ. Aloo kɛ́ kooloi bibii ŋmɔ amɛ. Tsei kɛ ŋmeii bibii shaa afɔle yɛ adebɔɔ naa. koni akɛbu pods wuji lɛ ahe

english: Why do the leaves of my crops wilt and drop during heavy rainy seasons when there is plenty of water in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? He ni nu babaoo yɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When farmland gets waterlogged, water fills all the air spaces in the soil, suffocating the plant roots because they cannot breathe. Root rot sets in, preventing the roots from drinking water, which makes the leaves wilt even in wet soil.
ga: Beni nu eyi okwaayeli hei lɛ Nu baaha kɔɔyɔɔ hei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ayi obɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔlɔ hewɔ. Shishifãi ni efite lɛ baabote mli ni ebaatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkanu nu. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ po nɔ.

english: Why do the seeds I saved from my last maize harvest yield smaller cobs than the original certified seeds I bought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee ŋmãa kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ wo ŋmãa bibioo fe shishijee dumɔwu ni awo he odaseyeli ni mihe lɛ?

english: Certified hybrid seeds are specially bred for maximum strength in their first generation. When you replant seeds saved from that harvest, the offspring lose that hybrid vigor, resulting in mixed plant heights, smaller cobs, and lower yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee nɔ ko ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Beni oduɔ dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ nakai kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ. Seshibii lɛ baafite hewalɛ ni yɔɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náa ŋwɛi ŋta ni efutu. Cob lɛ ji bibioo fe no. ni nibii ni anáa lɛ ba shi

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build healthy leaves. Adding well-rotted chicken manure or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea near the roots will help the maize green up and grow fast.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛmaa baai ni wa Kɛ́ okɛ tsina ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmei ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea fata shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua oŋmei lɛ ni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda oya.

english: How can I keep tiny insects from eating and destroying my harvested dried maize in storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa? Te aaafee tɛŋŋ aye ŋmãa ni egbi ni akpa momo yɛ nitoohe lɛ ni akpata hiɛ?

english: Maize weevils multiply quickly when grain is stored wet or in open rooms. Make sure your maize is fully dried until the kernels snap cleanly between your teeth, and store them in clean, airtight storage bags or treated storage bins to suffocate pests.
ga: Abɛi mli ŋmeii lɛ faa oya kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmaa wo ŋmɔtɔ mli loo yɛ tsu ko ni agbele mli. Kwɛmɔ ni o-corn lɛ agbi kwraa kɛyashi ŋmeii lɛ baafo mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ onyanyɔji ateŋ. Ni okɛto kotoku ko ni mli tse ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo kotoku ko ni akɛ tsofa ewo mli lɛ mli koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akamɔ bo.

english: Why do the young cocoa pods on my trees turn black and shrivel up during the heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji bibii ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by a fungal disease called Black Pod, which spreads easily when the air on your farm is very humid and wet. Pruning excess branches and clearing weeds lets sunlight and fresh air flow through, drying out the pods and stopping the fungus.
ga: Fungi hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ blackpod kɛ enɛ baa. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli edɔ waa ni edɔ waa. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ojie jwɛi lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa atsɔ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ kpaa.

english: Why do experienced farmers tell me to keep large forest trees on my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ kɛɛ mi akɛ mikɛ koo mli tsei wuji ahi mikookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees get burned easily by intense sunlight and hot dry winds. Keeping selective shade trees shields the cocoa, traps moisture in the soil, and creates a cool atmosphere that helps cocoa live longer and produce pods for many years.
ga: Hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi lɛ shãa cacao tsei bibii lɛ oya. Kɛ́ tso lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu kookoo lɛ he. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa kookoo lɛ ni ehiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa afii babaoo.

english: How can I tell under the ground if my cassava roots are mature enough to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ edara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Most cassava varieties mature between 9 to 12 months after planting, when the bottom leaves turn yellow and drop off naturally. You can test harvest by digging up just one plant at the edge of your field to check if the roots are thick and woody before harvesting the rest.
ga: Cassava henɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo daa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ. Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛbaagbee shi. Obaanyɛ oka okpamɔ lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ tso kome ni oootsi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ nɔ koni okwɛ kɛji shishifãi lɛ mli edɔ ni eyɛ tsei dani okpa nɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ.

english: Why do I have to heap the soil into high mounds before planting my yam seed pieces?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ okɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ato dani odu sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow downwards and swell beneath the surface, so they need loose, soft earth to grow long and thick. Soil mounds also capture rain without drowning the seeds, making it easy for you to harvest intact tubers later.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishigbɛ ni amɛfuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ he miihia amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Gɔji lɛ hu hiɛɔ nugbɔ ni ehaaaa dumɔwui lɛ ashwie shi. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa bo akɛ obaakpa ŋmeii ni efiteee lɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: This problem is called blossom-end rot, caused when the plant cannot pull enough calcium from the soil due to irregular watering. Keeping your soil evenly moist and adding wood ash or lime helps the plant build firm, healthy fruits.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni akɛ tso sũ loo lime fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ewo yibii ni mli wa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper bushes curling up tightly and stopping the plant from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe waa ni ehaa tso lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap from leaves and spreading plant diseases. Spraying your pepper plants early with a mixture of crushed neem leaves and water will control these insects so new leaves grow flat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ tsei ahelai amɛshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Pepper tsei ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ oya Neem baai ni atswa kɛ nu ni akɛfutuɔ mli lɛ kudɔɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ. koni ekɛfee baai heei lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why do my plantain trees always fall over easily during strong winds when they carry big bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi mlɛo be fɛɛ be yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli kɛ́ amɛfee kui wuji lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that do not go deep into the earth, making them top-heavy once a large bunch forms. Propping up the stems using sturdy bamboo forks or wooden stakes supports the weight and keeps winds from blowing them down.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kɛji eje kpo yɛ kui wuji amli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei loo tsei ni wa fĩɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛfiɔ tsɔne lɛ mli tsiimɔ lɛ sɛɛ, ni ehaaa kɔɔyɔɔ atswa lɛ shi.

english: Why do my oil palm trees stop producing new fruit bunches during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tsei lɛ kpaɔ aduawai akui heei yɛ harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Oil palms need plenty of water to produce fruits, so when rainfall stops, the tree naturally rests to protect itself from drying out. Spreading dead leaves and organic mulch around the base keeps the root area cool and saves water during dry months.
ga: Oil palm biɔ nu babaoo dani enyɛ efee nibii ni ekɛtsuɔ nii lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa lɛ Tsei lɛ jɔɔ amɛhe yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi. Gbalamɔ baai ni egboi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ashwã he fɛɛ he. Shishitoo lɛ haa shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli.

english: How many acres am I actually getting if my land size is given to me in hectares?
ga: Acre enyiɛ minine shɛɔ nɔ diɛŋtsɛ kɛji akɛ akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ dalɛ ha yɛ hectares mli?

english: One hectare is equal to about 2.5 acres (specifically 2.47 acres). So, if you have a 10-hectare plot of land, you are working with roughly 25 acres.
ga: Hectare kome kɛ aaafee acre 2.5 yeɔ egbɔ (pɔtɛɛ akɛ acre 2.47), no hewɔ lɛ, kɛji oyɛ shikpɔŋ hectare 10 lɛ, no lɛ okɛ aaafee acre 25 miitsu nii.

english: How do I calculate how many maize seeds I need to buy for a 5-acre farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu ŋmãa ŋmeii enyiɛ ni esa akɛ mahe kɛha ŋmɔ ni dalɛ ji acre 5 lɛ he akɔntaa?

english: Seed requirement depends on spacing. For standard maize spacing (75cm by 40cm), you generally need about 8 to 10 kilograms of seed for every acre, meaning a 5-acre farm will require around 40 to 50 kilograms of seed in total.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ataoɔ lɛ damɔ gbɛ ni kã amɛteŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛha ŋmãa ni ato he gbɛjianɔ (75 cm x 40 cm) lɛ, bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui aaafee kiloi 8 kɛyashi 10 he baahia bo yɛ acre kome mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔ ni dalɛ ji acre 5 lɛ baabi aaafee dumɔwui kilogram 40 kɛyashi 50 fɛɛ.

english: Which crops are easiest to manage when starting a very large farm of over 100 acres?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo fe fɛɛ akɛ aaakwɛ nɔ kɛji akɛ aje ŋmɔ agbo ko ni fe acre 100 shishi?

english: Grain crops like maize, sorghum, and legumes like soybeans are typically easier to manage on massive plots because planting, weed control, and harvesting can be mechanized far more easily than with delicate root or vegetable crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa nibii tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, kɛ ŋmãa tamɔ soybeans lɛ akwɛmɔ waaa yɛ hei wuji. yɛ jwɛi ni aduɔ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ hewɔ Ni abaanyɛ akɛ tsɔne akpa ŋmaa lɛ mlɛo fe shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo loo aduawai.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow long and tall with tiny tubers when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni ekwɛɔ ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Cassava plants need enough space and sunlight to store energy in their roots. When planted too close together, they fight for light and nutrients, spending all their energy growing tall leaves instead of swelling their underground tubers.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ he miihia he ko kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ato amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo baai kakadaji. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: What happens if I plant cocoa seedlings in direct sunlight without any shade crops around?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu kookoo dumɔwui yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni tsei ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn under full, hot sunshine. Without shade crops like plantains to act as living umbrellas, young cocoa plants easily dry out and die before they can mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo ni yɔɔ ekãa ni baatsu nii akɛ hulutsoo lɛ bɛ lɛ, Cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛshɛɔ amɛdalɛ he.

english: Why do plantain stalks fall over so easily during heavy wind and rain on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that stay near the topsoil. When heavy rain softens the ground and strong winds blow, the heavy bunches on top pull the shallow-rooted plant out of the soil.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswaa. Niji ni tsii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ gbalaa tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ he eko lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my young corn turn yellow when rain does not fall for two weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛko otsii enyɔ nɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are a sign of water and nitrogen stress. Without moisture, roots cannot draw nutrients from the soil, forcing the corn plant to slow down its growth and drop its green chlorophyll to survive the dry spell.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji nu kɛ nitrogen he haomɔ he okadi. Kɛji hulutsoo be bɛ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ ajie niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ daraa fioo ni amɛshɛrɛɔ klorofil eŋɔli amɛshwieɔ koni amɛhi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping all their flowers before growing any pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ dani eduɔ pepper aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat or lack of water, as the plant sheds its flowers to conserve energy and survive rather than spending energy producing fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ mli lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛhi shi lɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo yibii

english: How does clearing all the big shade trees off my land affect how my groundnut crops grow?
ga: Te tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ saa mi-peanut tsei lɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Clearing all trees exposes the soil to direct sunshine, which dries out ground moisture rapidly and hardens the earth, making it difficult for groundnut pegs to penetrate the soil and form nuts.
ga: Tsei fɛɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ gbiɔ oya, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa ŋmei ŋmeii lɛ akɛ amɛaabote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛfee ŋmeii.

english: Why do crops planted at the bottom of a gentle slope grow greener and bigger than those at the top?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu fioo yɛ gɔŋ ko shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdaraa fe tsei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Rainwater washes topsoil, nutrients, and natural organic matter down from the top of the hill to the bottom, creating a richer, moister soil layer at the bottom that feeds the crops better.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ, niyenii mli nibii, kɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋwɛi kɛyaa shishi. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji ni mli edɔ yɛ shishigbɛ ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green leaves and grow big. Applying the right amount of NPK or urea fertilizer when the plant is young will restore its green color and health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛfee baai eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ akɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii loo urea ni sa wo tsei lɛ amli beni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cowpeas seem to make the soil better for the maize I plant in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that work with helpful bacteria in the soil to capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the crop is harvested and the roots rot, that nitrogen remains in the soil to feed your next crop.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ bacteria ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Beni akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni shishifãi lɛ egbo Nakai nitrogen lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to strong, direct sunlight and hot winds. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain alongside them creates a canopy that shields the young cocoa until it is mature enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ he waa. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ lateral plantains lɛ adumɔ Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ amɛtsui shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he.

english: Why is it bad to plant my rice seeds very close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: When rice seeds are planted too closely, the growing plants end up competing with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant room to spread out, grow strong stems, and produce large grain heads.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni adu lɛ kɛ amɛhe yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso tsu fɛɛ tsu mli gbeleɔ ehe. Eyɛ tso ni mli wa. ni ebɔ dumɔwui ayitsei wuji

english: Should I cut away the small suckers growing around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii bibii? ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛbɔleɔ he lɛ Ani ajie plantain shishifã titri lɛ?

english: Yes, you should leave only one or two strong suckers and remove the rest. If too many suckers grow together on one plant, they steal food and water from the main tree, resulting in small plantain bunches.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ oshi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ojie nɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ. Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo ni miidara yɛ tso kome nɔ lɛ fa babaoo lɛ, Ebaaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji plantains bibii bibii.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves droop in the middle of the afternoon heat even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tsei lɛ gboɔ yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ Nɛgbɛ esa akɛ awo amɛ nu leebi?

english: During the hottest part of the day, leaves lose water faster through evaporation than the roots can draw up from the ground. The plant temporarily wilts to protect itself from losing more water and usually recovers in the evening when temperatures drop.
ga: yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya ŋwɛi. Tso lɛ baagbo be kukuoo ko koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ nu ni elaaje lɛ he. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ beni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi lɛ.

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to lift their leaves up toward sunlight. Staking allows the leaves to catch maximum light to make food, which is then sent down underground to grow large yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ miikwɔ wain tso ko ni esa akɛ ewo ebaai lɛ anɔ koni hulu lɛ ajie ehe kpo lɛ nɔ. Staking haa baai lɛ naa la babaoo kɛha nihoomɔ. ni abaamaje shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛdu sweet potato ŋmeii wuji

english: How can I know that my cassava tubers underground are big enough to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cassava shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa?

english: Cassava lets you know it is mature when its lower leaves start turning yellow and falling off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack upward due to the expanding tubers underneath.
ga: Yucca haa oleɔ akɛ edara beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni bulb lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off before any tomatoes start forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani tomato lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping soil moisture consistent and avoiding excess fertilizer keeps the flowers healthy so fruit can set.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ hao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa waa mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: What is causing tiny holes in my maize leaves and fine powder inside the main stem?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ powda kpakpa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa titri lɛ mli lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by the stem borer insect, whose caterpillars hatch from eggs laid on the leaves and burrow into the stem to feed. Scouting your field early helps you spot these signs before the caterpillars destroy the central shoot.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmeii ni boteɔ tso lɛ mli. Lalabii lɛ fɔɔ kɛjɛɔ wɔji ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ amli ni amɛfoɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli koni amɛyatao niyenii. Oŋmɔ lɛ mli kwɛmɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua bo ni ona okadii nɛɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ akpata teŋgbɛ he lɛ hiɛ.

english: How does putting rotted leaves and food scraps back into the soil help my maize grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ baai ni egboi kɛ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ ni mikɛkuɔ sɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi-ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: When leaves and food scraps rot into compost, they break down into natural plant food. This feeds your maize with rich nutrients, keeps the soil moist longer, and helps the crops grow stronger roots and bigger yields.
ga: Kɛ́ baai kɛ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ fite lɛ, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. Amɛgbalaa amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei aniyenii amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ baaha o-corn lɛ aye niyenii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ niyenii. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni wa ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo

english: Will my cassava plants grow well if I feed them homemade compost instead of chemical fertilizer?
ga: Ani mi-cassava tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛji mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ najiaŋ lɛ ha amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee shia lɛ?

english: Yes, cassava grows very well with compost because organic manure releases nutrients slowly into the soil without burning the crop, while keeping the ground soft so the cassava roots can expand easily.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Ejaakɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fiofio. ni ekɛ tsei lɛ ashãaa Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo bɔni afee ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo.

english: Why does soil mixed with compost stay moist longer during short dry spells than plain soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii efutu mli lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ be kukuoo mli fe shikpɔŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ?

english: Compost acts like a sponge under the ground. It holds onto rainwater and releases it slowly to your crops' roots, preventing the plants from wilting quickly when the rains stop.
ga: Kompost tsuɔ nii tamɔ shikpɔŋ shishi sponji. Ebuaa nugbɔ nu lɛ naa ni ejieɔ lɛ fiofio. kɛya otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkagbo oya kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa.

english: Why shouldn't I throw fresh animal droppings and wet waste directly onto my young crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmeii heei kɛ ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ shwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?
