english: Fresh waste produces high heat and sour liquids as it decomposes, which can burn tender plant roots. Composting the waste first lets it break down safely into a cool, soft fertilizer that won't harm your crops.
ga: Shwɛmɔ hee jieɔ nu ni mli edɔ waa ni mli edɔ waa beni efiteɔ lɛ. ni baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ Klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, sũ lɛ haa sũ lɛ fiteɔ shweshweeshwe ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni mli ejɔ ni eyeee oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui.

english: How do crop roots absorb food from old plant leaves if plants don't have mouths?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tso shishifãi aŋɔ niyenii kɛjɛ tso baai momoi amli kɛji tso lɛ bɛ naabu?

english: Tiny organisms and insects in the ground break down old leaves into tiny, invisible nutrients. These nutrients dissolve in the soil's moisture, allowing crop roots to drink them up like water.
ga: Nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli kɛ kooloi bibii Yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ajara baai momoi amli awo niyenii bibii amli. invisible Niyenii mli nibii nɛɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ mli nu mli. Ehaa tso shishifãi feɔ nɔ ni anuɔ tamɔ nu.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow when wet, smelly waste pools near their stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni ŋshɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ yɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: When unmanaged waste turns into a sour, smelly liquid, it suffocates the plant roots and blocks them from taking in air and nutrients, causing the leaves to turn yellow and decay.
ga: Beni jwɛi ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ tsɔɔ nu ni mli edɔ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ehaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaaa amɛná kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: What can I do with the rotten harvest leftovers in my field so they don't spoil my next crop?
ga: Mɛni mikɛ nikpamɔ nibii ni eshwɛ ni fiteɔ yɛ miŋmɔji amli lɛ feɔ? Bɔni afee ni mikafite miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Instead of leaving wet waste to turn into harmful liquid, you can collect and compost it into clean fertilizer, or use insects like Black Soldier Fly larvae to rapidly break it down into rich soil food and animal feed.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni jwɛi ni efɔ lɛ baatsɔ nu ni yɔɔ oshara. Obaanyɛ obua naa ni okɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii ni he tse, loo okɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ black soldier fly larvae lɛ atsu nii ni okɛfite lɛ oya ni efee sũ ni jara wa kɛ kooloi aniyenii.

english: Are there helpful insects that can turn my farm waste into food for my soil?
ga: Ani kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni baanyɛ atsake miŋmɔ mli jwɛi lɛ afee niyenii aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ?

english: Yes, insects like the Black Soldier Fly lay eggs that hatch into hungry larvae. These larvae eat up rotting farm waste very fast before it turns into foul liquid, leaving behind clean, nutrient-rich compost for your soil.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kooloi tamɔ asraafonyo diŋ lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ yeɔ ŋmɔ mli jwɛi ni efite lɛ oya dani amɛtsɔɔ nu ni mli ewo muji. ni oshi ŋmɔshi nibii ni he tse ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ oha oshikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: How does turning my wet crop waste into dry compost prevent plant diseases from spreading?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni efɔ lɛ ni mikɛfeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa?

english: Leaving stagnant wet waste in the field breeds harmful fungi and bacteria that infect new seedlings. Composting heat kills off those bad germs and converts the waste into clean organic food for healthy plant growth.
ga: Shwɛi ni efɔ ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni gbɛɔ eshwaa dumɔwui heei amli lɛ baa. Dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ gbeɔ helai fɔji ni etsɔɔ jwɛi mli niyenii ni he tse, ni jɛɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii amli kɛhaa tsei adalɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my plant roots struggle to spread in hard soil, and how does compost fix this?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ lɛ? Ni te ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Hard, compacted soil lacks air pockets, making it difficult for roots to push through. Adding compost lightens the soil structure, making it loose and airy so roots can easily stretch deep to fetch water and nutrients.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa, ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bɛ mli. Ehaa ewaa kɛhaa shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaabote mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔne lɛ afee mlɛo. Ha efee mlɛo ni kɔɔyɔɔ hu ahi mli. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ashɛ amɛhe kɛya shɔŋŋ oya koni amɛgbala nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why should I buy modern certified corn seeds instead of just replanting seeds saved from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ? Mohu ɔ, mo du wuhi nɛ a he yi kɛ je ngmɔ kpami nɛ be ɔ mi ɔ ekohu.

english: Modern certified seeds are specifically bred to give higher yields, resist common pests, and tolerate unpredictable weather better than saved traditional seeds, which gradually lose their strength over time.
ga: Akwɛɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni afɔɔ namɔ Ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ fe blema dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ, ni fiofio lɛ amɛhewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ.

english: What is the main difference between traditional local corn varieties like 'Aberefu' and new foreign or improved varieties?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔi titrii ni yɔɔ blema maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa henɔi tamɔ ‘Aberefu’ kɛ maŋsɛɛ ŋmãa henɔi heei loo ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ateŋ?

english: Traditional varieties like 'Aberefu' often take longer to mature and produce smaller yields, whereas modern improved varieties mature faster, grow stronger stalks, and produce fuller cobs.
ga: Kusum mli tsofai srɔtoi tamɔ ‘Aberefu’ lɛ fɔɔ be babaoo heɔ dani ekwɛɔ ni ewoɔ yibii bibii. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii heei ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ shwereɔ oya lɛ. Eyɛ tso ni mli wa ni ehaa cob yibii ni eyi obɔ

english: How do I know which modern corn variety is right for the soil and rainfall in my area?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋmãa ni sa kɛha shikpɔŋ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Agricultural extension officers recommend specific certified seed varieties tested for your specific zone, such as early-maturing seeds for drier areas or high-yielding hybrids for places with heavy rainfall.
ga: Okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ kɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ hegbɛ ni aka amɛ akwɛ kɛha he pɔtɛɛ ni oyɔɔ lɛ, tamɔ dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ mra kɛha hei ni nu bɛ lɛ he ŋaawoo haa. loo dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni woɔ yibii babaoo kɛha hei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ lɛ.

english: If I plant a modern hybrid corn this season, can I save its seeds to plant again next year?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ hybrid ŋmãa yɛ be nɛɛ mli Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui lɛ ato koni madu ekoŋŋ afi ni baa lɛ?

english: It is best to buy fresh hybrid seeds every season. Planting saved seeds from hybrid corn results in a second generation that grows unevenly and produces much smaller yields.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui heei ni akɛfee hybrid daa be. Dumɔwui ni jara waaa ni aduɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa mli lɛ haa yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli dumɔwui ni daaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ baa ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo kwraa.

english: Why does my neighbor's modern corn produce bigger cobs than my local corn even though we planted on the same day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋmãa lɛ woɔ ŋmãa ni da fe mimaŋ ŋmãa lɛ beni wɔdu lɛ nakai gbi lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Modern corn varieties are bred to convert soil nutrients, water, and sunlight into grain growth far more efficiently than older traditional varieties.
ga: Akwɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋmãa koni ekɛtsake niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli lɛ ewo dumɔwui ni miida jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmãa henɔi ni etsɛ, ni ji blema ŋmãa lɛ.

english: Do modern corn varieties require different spacing in the field compared to traditional corn?
ga: Ani ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋmãa henɔi lɛ biɔ ŋmɔ mli ŋmãa srɔtoi kɛ akɛto blema ŋmãa he?

english: Yes, many modern corn varieties grow shorter and sturdier, which allows you to plant them closer together to fit more plants per acre without them choking each other out.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋmãa henɔi babaoo yɛ kuku ni amɛhe wa. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ oduɔ amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni tsei babaoo ahi acre kome mli ni amɛtsiii amɛhe gbɛ.

english: Why do pests like armyworms seem to cause less damage to some modern corn varieties?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ cutworms lɛ efiteee ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋmãa henɔi komɛi babaoo lɛ?

english: Certain modern crop varieties are developed with natural toughness or chemical defenses that discourage insects from eating the leaves and cobs.
ga: Afee ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi komɛi ni adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ loo tsofai ni buɔ he lɛ yɔɔ mli. Enɛ haaa kooloi aye baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Does modern corn need more fertilizer than traditional local corn to grow properly?
ga: Ani ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋmãa biɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fe blema ŋmãa ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Because modern corn grows faster and produces much larger cobs, it consumes nutrients quickly and requires timely fertilizer applications to reach its full yield potential.
ga: Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋmãa daa oya ni ewoɔ ŋmãa wuji babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii oya ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ be ni sa mli koni anyɛ aná yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo.

english: How do early-maturing modern corn varieties help me if the rains stop early in the season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ mra lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa mra yɛ be lɛ mli?

english: Early-maturing varieties complete their flowering and grain formation quickly, allowing you to harvest full cobs before dry spells damage the crop.
ga: Henɔi ni kwɛɔ mra lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi oya kɛ dumɔwui ni yeɔ emuu. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa ŋmei lɛ kwraa dani hulutsoo be fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Does modern corn store as well in traditional granaries as our old local corn?
ga: Ani akɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋmãa toɔ blema ŋmãatoohei tamɔ wɔ maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa momo lɛ?

english: Traditional corn often has tighter husks that keep insects out, so modern corn may require thorough drying and proper storage treatment to protect it from grain weevils.
ga: Kusum mli ŋmãa lɛ fɔɔ ŋmãa ni mli wa koni ekɛtsi kooloi akabote mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ekolɛ ehe baahia ni agbi ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋmãa lɛ kwraa ni akɛto jogbaŋŋ koni ŋmãa mli ŋmeii akabote mli.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my plants with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, keeps the soil moist under the hot sun, prevents weed growth, and cools the roots of your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa ni ehaa otsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why is it a bad idea for me to plant maize on the exact same plot of land every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ makwɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously on the same land drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests that feed on maize to multiply. Rotating with crops like beans or groundnuts puts nutrients back into the soil naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni yaa nɔ aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ koni amɛfɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni akɛtsakeɔ amɛhe lɛ baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen nutrients or are getting waterlogged. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele tsei lɛ bɛ nitrogen niyenii loo nu eyi mli obɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight on their leaves to produce food for the tubers underground. Staking holds the leaves off the damp ground, exposing them to light and protecting them from soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ jeɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Okɛ amɛ awo la mli ni obu amɛhe kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: When is the best time of day for me to spray fertilizer or pesticide on my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ?

english: Early morning or late evening is best because the heat from the afternoon sun can dry out the liquid too fast or burn the delicate leaves of your crops.
ga: Leebi loo gbɛkɛ ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ la ni jɛɔ shwane hulu lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha nu lɛ agbi oya tsɔ loo eshã tso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Why should I wait for the main rains to start before planting my corn seeds instead of planting in dry soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ aje shishi dani madu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ moŋ?

english: Seeds require steady water to sprout and establish roots properly. Planting in dry soil risks having the seeds eaten by insects or dying if only a small, brief rain falls.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ nu daa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfee shishifãi jogbaŋŋ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ kɛ oshara baa akɛ kooloi baaye dumɔwui lɛ loo amɛbaagbe amɛ kɛji nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛ.

english: How do I know when my cassava crop is ready to be dug up for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-cassava tsei lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakumɔ koni akpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 to 12 months after planting, when the lower leaves begin turning yellow and falling off, and the soil around the base of the stem cracks due to swollen tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli gbala yɛ tso lɛ ŋmei ni efuu lɛ hewɔ.

english: Curling, sticky leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the sap out of the plant. Washing the leaves with soapy water or using safe insecticides will clear them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe ni ekpɛtɛɔ he lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli edɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too high or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet repeatedly. Keeping the soil consistently moist and giving plants light shade during extreme heat prevents flower drop.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake shii abɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulutsoo ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akagbee shi.

english: Why should I plant my maize in neat rectangular rows instead of scattering the seeds around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ fɛo mli moŋ fe ni mafɔ dumɔwui lɛ abɔle he lɛ?

english: Planting in straight, rectangular rows ensures each plant gets equal space, sunlight, and nutrients. It also creates open pathways that allow air to flow freely through the field, making it easier for you to weed, apply fertilizer, and harvest without stepping on your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja, ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ. Ehaa gbɛ ni agbele nɔ hu haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli oya. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa bo akɛ obaajie jwɛi, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli, ni okpa ŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni okɛ onaji shwieee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ.

english: How does leaving space between my crop rows help protect my farm from diseases?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ gbɛ ni kã ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato lɛ ateŋ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ebu miŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ helai ahe?

english: When crops are spaced properly in clear rows, fresh air can circulate between the plants. Good airflow dries excess moisture off the leaves after rain, preventing humid conditions where fungal diseases and rot easily spread.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe jogbaŋŋ yɛ srɔtoi ni mli tse mli lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa baanyɛ abɔle tsei lɛ ateŋ. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ahe yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Tsi ŋmɔtɔ ni baa shi yɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya lɛ naa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during heavy winds, and what can I do about it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miitswa lɛ? Ni mɛni mikɛfeɔ?

english: Plantains have broad leaves that catch strong wind like a sail and shallow roots that pull out easily. You can prevent them from falling by planting windbreak trees around the edge of your farm, propping stems up with wooden poles, or spacing rows so wind passes through without pushing the plants down.
ga: Plantains yɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni nyɛɔ etsuɔ ​​kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tamɔ lɛlɛ he nii kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni ejiemɔ waaa. Obaanyɛ otsi tsei anaa koni amɛkagbee shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔŋ tsɔnei ni ooodu yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ ni akɛfiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ Aloo ni akɛto amɛhe yɛ sɛɛ mli koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli ni ekɛ tsei lɛ akashwie shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants turning pale and thin when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plants are overcrowded, their leaves block sunlight from reaching one another. Without enough direct sunlight, the plants cannot make food efficiently, causing them to grow tall and weak with pale leaves and fewer peppers.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe. Kɛji hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ faaa Tsei hu nyɛŋ afee niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ, ni amɛbaai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ amɛhe.

english: How can I figure out the true shape and size of my plot so I know how much fertilizer to buy?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male bɔ ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ diɛŋtsɛ kɛ bɔ ni elɛɛmɔ da ha? Koni ale ŋmɔshi nibii ni esa akɛ ahe

english: Measuring your field into clear rectangular sections using ropes or measuring sticks helps you calculate the exact area. Knowing the true size prevents you from wasting money by buying and applying too much or too little fertilizer.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ kpãa loo tso ni akɛsusuɔ nii ahe lɛ susu he ni oyɔɔ lɛ mli yɛ fãi ni mli tse ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni obu he pɔtɛɛ ni oyɔɔ lɛ he akɔntaa. Kɛ́ ole bɔ ni edara ha diɛŋtsɛ lɛ, ebaatsi bo gbɛ koni okafite shika kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo loo fioo ni ooohe lɛ nɔ.

english: Will I get a bigger harvest if I squeeze more cassava stems into my small piece of land?
ga: Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛji mikɛ ŋmeii tsei babaoo shwie mishikpɔŋ bibioo lɛ nɔ?

english: No, crowding your farm forces crops to fight over water, soil nutrients, and sunlight. Fewer plants given enough space to spread out will yield larger, heavier cassava tubers than many crammed plants with tiny roots.
ga: Dabi, mɛi ni fa babaoo yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nyɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ koni amɛwu amɛtao nu. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la. Tsei fioo komɛi ni aha amɛ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ baawo ŋmei bibii ni da ni tsii fe tsei ni eyi obɔ kɛ shishifãi bibii.

english: Why do my tomato fruits turn soft and rot on the bush before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato yibii lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ jwɛi lɛ nɔ dani amɛshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: Tomato bushes that grow too dense and close together trap heat and moisture around the fruit. Pruning lower leaves and spacing the plants apart allows breeze to blow through, keeping the fruit dry and healthy.
ga: Tomato tsei ni shwereɔ tsɔ ni amɛbɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe lɛ mɔ̃ɔ dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɔleɔ aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ. Kɛ́ afo baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli ni ashi gbɛ yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli. Ehaa aduawai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli.

english: Why is my maize growing tall and thin with very small cobs under the big shade trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ daa ni ekwɛɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ bibii lɛ? Yɛ tso agbo ko ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ shishi?

english: Maize needs full, direct sunlight to produce thick stems and large grains. Under tree shade, the crop stretches upward to search for light instead of putting energy into forming healthy, full cobs.
ga: Abɛi he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee tsei ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji. tsei ashishi Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ mli lɛɛɔ kɛtaoɔ la. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ he wami tsuɔ ní kɛ peeɔ cob nɛ e hyi nɛ e he wa.

english: Why does heavy rain wash away my seeds on flat ground, and how can I fix it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ midumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kplanaa lɛ nɔ lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa?

english: Flat ground allows rainwater to collect and flow freely across the surface, washing away topsoil and seeds. Planting on raised rectangular beds or ridges guides water off the field gently while keeping your seeds locked in place.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ buaa ehe naa ni etsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi kɛ dumɔwui lɛ tsuɔ nii. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛitsu loo ŋwɛitsu ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nu lɛ yaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli blɛoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ dumɔwui lɛ ŋmɛɔ amɛhe.

english: Which direction should I align my crop rows on a sloped land to stop my soil from washing away?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esa akɛ mafo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ koni sũ lɛ akaho?

english: You should lay out your rows across the slope (along the contour) rather than up and down the hill. These horizontal rows act like tiny dams that slow down rainwater, preventing soil erosion and helping the ground absorb water.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai lɛ ama ŋshɔ lɛ naa. (yɛ ŋshɔ lɛ naa) yɛ ŋwɛi kɛ shi najiaŋ Nɛkɛ ŋshɔi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ nɛɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋshɔkei bibii. ni yeɔ ebuaa ni nugbɔ nu lɛ baa shi Etsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwiemɔ naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekɛ nu shwieɔ shi.

english: Why are some of my crops still producing fruit late in the year around December when others have already dried up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi miiwo yibii lolo yɛ afi lɛ naagbee gbɛ yɛ December mli shi ekrokomɛi hu egbo momo lɛ?

english: Different crop varieties have different maturation cycles and water needs. Long-duration crops or late-planted varieties naturally continue fruiting into the dry season if they still have deep root systems that reach moisture deep in the soil.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi yɛ bɔ ni amɛdaraa amɛhaa kɛ nu he hiamɔ nii srɔtoi. Tsei ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ loo tsei ni shwereɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ baawo yibii lolo yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛji amɛyɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lolo ni haa nu shɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my maize so pests do not ruin it in the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa? Koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akafite ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize is ready to harvest when the outer leaves turn dry and brown, the silk becomes black and dry, and the grains become hard and glossy with a small dark mark at the tip.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Siliki lɛ baatsɔ ediŋŋ ni ebaagbi. ni dumɔwui lɛ wa ni amɛkpɛɔ ni amɛyɛ okadi bibii diji yɛ amɛnaa.

english: Can I leave my cassava or yams in the soil past harvest time until I am ready to sell them?
ga: Ani manyɛ mashi ŋmei loo ŋmei ni mli edɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ dani akpa kɛyashi be mli ni amɛbaafee klalo akɛ mahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Root crops can stay safely underground for a few extra months as natural storage, but leaving them too long makes them woody, rots them if heavy rains return, or leaves them exposed to burrowing pests.
ga: Shishifãi ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi shweshweeshwe nyɔji 2-3 kɛha adebɔɔ mli nibii ni akɛtoɔ. Shi kɛ́ oshi lɛ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha etsɔ tso. Ebaanyɛ egbo kɛji nugbɔ ni naa wa ku esɛɛ eba. loo okɛ tsei lɛ awo sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai amli.

english: Is it good to plant cassava inside my maize farm at the same time?
ga: Kasava ni miduɔ yɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be kome mli Ani ebaafee nɔ ni hi loo ehiii?

english: Yes, planting cassava with maize works well because maize grows quickly and is harvested early, leaving full sunlight and space for the slower-growing cassava to mature later without competing for sunlight.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya ni akpaa lɛ mra. Ha hulu lɛ fɛɛ kɛ he ko ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ aha yucca ni daa blɛoo lɛ ada sɛɛ mli ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ hulu la lɛ akaŋ.

english: Will planting cowpeas or beans alongside my maize help my crops perform better?
ga: Ani tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni mikɛduɔ yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ baaye abua mi ŋmãa lɛ ni etsu nii jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, legumes like beans and cowpeas trap nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil, acting as a natural food source that feeds heavy-feeding crops like maize.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa kooloi aniyenii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do some of my pepper plants keep producing food for months while others harvest all at once and die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi chili tsei lɛ ekomɛi woɔ niyenii nyɔji babaoo yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi kpaa amɛ fɛɛ shikome ni amɛgboiɔ lɛ?

english: Some crop varieties are continuous producers that grow, flower, and set fruit as long as they get nutrients, while other crop varieties are bred to ripen all their fruit at the same time and then end their life cycle.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ekomɛi yaa nɔ amɛwoɔ yibii, amɛdaraa, amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi, ni amɛwoɔ yibii, be fɛɛ be ni amɛnáa niyenii mli hewalɛ. yɛ be mli ni tsei krokomɛi Afɔ amɛ koni amɛwo amɛyibii lɛ fɛɛ yɛ be kome mli, ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgbe amɛwala shihilɛ naa.

english: Why do my crops wilt during hot afternoons even when the soil still feels damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ edɔ lolo moŋ?

english: During hot afternoons, plant leaves lose moisture into the air faster than the roots can drink water from the soil. The plant wilts temporarily to close its pores and save water, and it usually recovers in the cooler evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tso baai lɛ laajeɔ nu ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tso lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni ekɛŋa eshishifãi lɛ ni ekɛ nu akafite. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: What happens if I leave old crop stalks in my field after harvest instead of clearing them?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mishi tsei ahe tsei momo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni majie amɛ?

english: Leaving old stalks can trap harmful pests and plant diseases that will attack your new crops. However, if you clear and bury them in the soil early, they break down into rich natural manure.
ga: Shi kɛlɛ, kɛ́ oshi tsei akutsei momoi lɛ ni amɛhiɛɛɛ amɛhe lɛ, ebaanyɛ emɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ tsei ahe helai ni baatutua onibii heei lɛ, kɛji ojie amɛ ni ofu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli mra. Amɛfiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa.

english: Can I plant seeds saved from my previous harvest, or should I buy certified seeds from a dealer?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli? Aloo esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ kɛjɛ mɔ ko ni jaa lɛ dɛŋ?

english: Saving traditional seeds works, but saving seeds from high-yielding hybrid crops causes future harvests to grow unevenly and produce fewer crops. Fresh certified seeds give you stronger, uniform, and higher yields.
ga: Kusum nifeemɔi ni akɛtoɔ dumɔwui ahe. Shi dumɔwui ni jɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ amli lɛ ni akɛbaahere lɛ baaha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmaa lɛ aya hiɛ ni ekɛ yibiiwoo fioo aba. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ baaha oná yibiiwoo ni mli wa, ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ nɔ ni fa babaoo.

english: How can I estimate how many bags of produce I will harvest before I finish cutting down the crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu ŋmɔshi nibii abɔ ni maná dani magbe ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛmɔ naa lɛ he akɔntaa?

english: You can estimate your harvest by counting the cobs or fruits on a few sample plants across different areas of your farm, calculating the average yield per plant, and multiplying it by your total number of surviving plants.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu okpamɔ lɛ he akɔntaa kɛtsɔ ŋmeii loo aduawai ni yɔɔ tsei fioo komɛi ni yɔɔ hei srɔtoi lɛ anɔ lɛ akanemɔ nɔ. ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Buu yibii ni tso kome baa lɛ mlijaa mlijaa he akɔntaa. ni okɛ otsei ni hiɛ ka lɛ fɛɛ ayibɔ abɔ he.

english: How many days does my rice crop need from the day I plant it until it is ready for me to harvest?
ga: Gbii enyiɛ eheɔ ni akɛduɔ ŋmãa kɛjɛɔ be mli ni aduɔ lɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni eshɛɔ be ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Most common rice varieties in Ghana take between 100 to 120 days (about 3 to 4 months) to mature fully. You will know it is ready when about 80% of the rice grains turn from green to a bright golden yellow color.
ga: Omɔ henɔi ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ ateŋ babaoo heɔ aaafee gbii 100 kɛyashi 120 (aaafee nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4) dani eshɛɔ shweremɔ he. Obaale akɛ ŋmãa lɛ efee klalo beni ŋmãa lɛ mli aaafee 80% tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa shika tsuru ni mli tse mli.

english: How tall or big should my rice plants grow in the field before I start seeing grain heads form?
ga: Te esa akɛ mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ akwɛ loo amɛdara yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli aha tɛŋŋ dani amɛje shishi amɛjie ŋmaa yitsei akpo?

english: Healthy rice plants usually grow to about waist height (around 80 to 100 centimeters tall) before flowering, depending on whether you are growing upland or lowland rice and how well the soil is nourished.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ daa kɛyashɛɔ aaafee sɛntimita 80 kɛyashi 100) dani amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi, ni enɛ damɔ ŋmãa ni oduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ loo yɛ shikpɔŋ kplanaa nɔ lɛ nɔ. kɛ bɔ ni akwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ahaa lɛ

english: Why do birds attack my rice farm just when the grains start forming, and how can I stop them from destroying my harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okpoi tutuaa mi ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ beni dumɔwui lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi enaa koni ekafite miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Birds target rice when the young grains are soft and filled with sweet milky fluid. You can protect your field by hanging shiny plastic ribbons or cassette tapes, setting up scarecrows, or clearing nearby bush areas where birds nest.
ga: Okpoi baatutua ŋmãa beni dumɔwui lɛ efee blɛoo ni ŋmãa ni ŋɔɔ eyi mli obɔ lɛ. Obaanyɛ obu oyale lɛ he kɛtsɔ plastic tsɔji loo kasɛt ni okɛbaafɔ̃ shi lɛ nɔ. Too gbeyeishemɔ ko Aloo jiemɔ jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ he ni okpoi feɔ amɛshĩa lɛ.

english: Can wild weeds actually choke and kill my young crops if I leave them in the field?
ga: Ani koo mli jwɛi baanyɛ agbɔjɔ ni efite miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Yes, fast-growing weeds steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer nutrients from young crop roots. Clearing weeds during the first 3 to 4 weeks after planting is critical to keep your young plants from dying.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii baa kɛjɛɔ tsei bibii ashishifãi amli. Klɛŋklɛŋ otsii 3 kɛyashi 4 ni okɛ jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ lɛ he miihia koni otsei bibii lɛ akagboi.

english: Does the color of seed grains—like white, yellow, or dark seeds—change how well the plant grows on my farm?
ga: Ani dumɔwui lɛ ahe su, tamɔ yɛŋ, ŋmɔŋ loo ediŋŋ tsakeɔ tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ adalɛ?

english: Seed color indicates different crop varieties; for instance, yellow maize often contains higher nutrients like Vitamin A, while white maize is preferred for local cooking. Each color variety may require slightly different maturity times and water levels.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ahe su tsɔɔ tsei srɔtoi. Ákɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa tamɔ vitamin A lɛ fa yɛ ŋmãa ni ji yellow mli. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa yɛŋ ji nɔ ni mɛi babaoo kɛtsu nii yɛ maŋ lɛ mli niyenii homɔ mli. Ekolɛ sui srɔtoi lɛ eko fɛɛ eko baabi ni amɛkwɛ be kɛ nu ni falɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ srɔtoi fioo.

english: Why did some of the seeds I buried in the ground fail to come up out of the soil at all?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mifuɔ lɛ ekomɛi ejeee kpo kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if they were planted too deep in the dirt, if the soil dried out completely before sprouting, or if soil insects and birds ate the seeds beneath the surface.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi kwraa dani ekwɛ̃ loo kɛji kooloi bibii kɛ okpoi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ye dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Why are the green leaves on my growing crop turning yellow before the plant even produces food?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani tsei lɛ baanyɛ awo niyenii lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are a signal that the plant is starving for essential nutrients like nitrogen, or that the ground has too much standing water or too little rain. Adding manure or urea fertilizer helps restore the healthy green color.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ kɛha niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu ni damɔ shi babaoo loo nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo urea fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my heavy crop plants suddenly fall flat on the ground right before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ trukaa dani kpamɔɔ be shɛɔ lɛ?

english: Plants fall over (called lodging) when heavy winds hit plants with weak stems, often caused by planting seeds too shallow or over-using certain fertilizers. Earthing up soil around the plant stems helps support their weight.
ga: Tsei gbeeɔ shi (ni atsɛɔ amɛ shĩai) kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa tsei ni amɛshishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi ni akɛtsuɔ nii babaoo tsɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni bɔleɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛfiɔ etsitsinɔnii lɛ sɛɛ.

english: How do I know if the soil has enough moisture after the early rain for me to sow my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ sɛɛ koni manyɛ madu dumɔwui?

english: Squeeze a fistful of topsoil in your hand; if it forms a firm ball that stays together without leaking water, the soil holds the right moisture level for seeds to germinate safely.
ga: Mimɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli nine kome awo onine mli. Kɛji efee bɔɔlu ni mli wa ni ŋmɛɔ shi ni nu shwieee shi. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ ni sa lɛ ahi shi koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and produce very small yields when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa ni yibiiwoo fioo pɛ baa kɛji midu dumɔwui babaoo lɛ? Dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the young plants fight each other for root space, soil nutrients, and sunlight. Giving each plant proper spacing allows the stems to grow thick and produce larger crop heads.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei bibii lɛ baawu koni amɛná shishifãi ahe gbɛ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la. Gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ tsei ateŋ lɛ baaye abua ni eshishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee bulbs wuji.

english: Why is it important for me to clear weeds and dead plant leaves away from my crop beds regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛ tsei ahe baai ni egboi kɛjɛ midumɔ saatso lɛ nɔ daa lɛ?

english: Keeping your farm clean removes the hiding places of harmful pests and fungal spores. Just as keeping animal coops clean prevents disease, maintaining a weed-free field stops plant illnesses from multiplying and spreading to your healthy crops.
ga: Kɛ́ oha oŋmɔ lɛ mli tse lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie hei ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ. Nakai nɔŋŋ eji yɛ koolooi atsu lɛ mli ni aaakwɛ koni helai akamɔ amɛ lɛ he. Kɛ́ oha he ni jwɛi bɛ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei ahe helai shwereɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ eshwaa onibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why should I remove and burn a crop if its leaves start rotting instead of leaving it in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmɔshi nibii ni adu lɛ ni mashã lɛ kɛji ebaai lɛ bɔi fitemɔ moŋ fe ni mashi yɛ sũ lɛ mli?

english: A rotting plant carries contagious fungal or bacterial diseases that travel through wind and rain to nearby plants. Removing and destroying the sick plant acts as a quarantine, saving the rest of your farm from getting infected.
ga: Tsei ni fiteɔ lɛ hiɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ mli kɛyaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli. Tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛ amɛfitemɔ baatsu nii akɛ he ni akɛtoɔ he kroko. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehereɔ oŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ helai amli.

english: How does feeding my crops fertilizer at specific intervals help them produce bigger yields?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ bei pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua amɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo?

english: Crops need a steady supply of nutrients at key growth stages to build roots, stems, and fruit. Providing measured nutrients regularly ensures the plant doesn't starve or become weak, leading to heavier and healthier harvests.
ga: Tsei lɛ hia niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ amɛdalɛ bei titrii amli koni amɛfee shishifãi, amɛshishifãi kɛ aduawai. Niyenii ni akɛ mitai toɔ he daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni hɔmɔ yeee tsei loo amɛhe waaa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nibii ni anáa lɛ mli tsii ni eyɛ hewalɛ.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a cry for food, specifically nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Giving your maize the right fertilizer or well-rotted manure early in its life restores its green color and fuels proper growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ bolɔɔ amɛbiɔ niyenii. Titri lɛ, nitrogen ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni sa loo ŋmãa ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ha ŋmãa lɛ yɛ egbekɛbiiashi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha eŋɔli lɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ, ni ewo ŋmãa lɛ dalɛ kpakpa he hewalɛ.

english: Can I use dried animal manure to feed my crop soil, and how does it help?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmeii ni egbi aha mi tso lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ eyeɔ ebuaa?

english: Yes, dried manure acts as rich organic food for your crops. It gradually releases essential nutrients into the soil while improving the soil's ability to hold water, helping plants stay healthy even during dry spells.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa babaoo kɛhaa onibii, ni ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ kpo fiofio kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli po.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience extreme heat, drought, or nutrient stress. The plant aborts the flowers to conserve energy for its own survival until growing conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛ kpe dɔlɛ ni naa wa, hɔmɔ, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ he haomɔ. Tsei baakpa fɔfɔii ni amɛwoɔ lɛ koni amɛto hewalɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni amɛhi shi kɛyashi shihilɛi ni haa amɛdaraa lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots and carry heavy fruit bunches at the top, making them top-heavy. Propping them up with sturdy bamboo poles and planting them in blocks reduces wind damage.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akuu ni tsii yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. make it top heavy Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei tsei ni wa fi esɛɛ ni okɛdu yɛ blɔki mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni fiteɔ nii lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small and thin even when the plant top grows very tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ yiteŋ lɛ kɛlɛ waa moŋ lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or is packed too tightly, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing tall leaves instead of expanding its underground tubers. Loose, well-nourished soil allows tubers to swell.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai ni kɛlɛ fe nine ni ekɛbaagbɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amli. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kɛ bulbs ni efuu.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn under direct sunshine. Fast-growing plantains provide large leaves that act as living umbrellas, supplying the shade and cool moisture cocoa needs to establish itself.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ shade. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo koni ekɛ ehe awo mli lɛ haa.

english: Why does covering the soil around my vegetable roots with dry grass help them grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo mishishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass (mulching) acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool and prevents moisture from evaporating quickly under the hot sun, allowing crop roots to drink water for longer periods.
ga: Mulching (mulching) tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ ni ehaaa ŋmɔtɔ akaho oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Enɛ haa tso shishifãi lɛ nuɔ nu be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to heat and direct sunlight. Their young leaves scorch easily, and their small roots cannot suck up enough water, which is why temporary shade plants like plantain are needed to protect them during their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Amɛbaai bibii lɛ shãa oya, ni amɛshishifãi bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu bɔ ni sa. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni akwɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains koni abu amɛhe yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli lɛ.

english: How many years do I have to wait for a newly planted cocoa tree to start giving me pods?
ga: Afii enyiɛ esa akɛ kookoo tso ni adu ehee lɛ amɛ dani ebɔi ŋmeii feemɔ?

english: With modern hybrid cocoa seeds, trees usually start producing pods within 2 to 3 years after planting, whereas older traditional cocoa varieties can take 4 to 5 years to bear fruit.
ga: Kɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ hybrid cocoa beans Tsei jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ, yɛ be mli ni blema cocoa henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahé afii 4 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do many of the small flowers on my cocoa trees fall off without ever turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ babaoo shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii?

english: A cocoa tree produces thousands of flowers, but only a small fraction get pollinated by tiny insects called midges. Unpollinated flowers drop off naturally so the tree can save its strength to grow pods from the flowers that were successfully pollinated.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔii akpei abɔ. Shi fã bibioo ko pɛ yɔɔ mli. Kplukai bibii pɛ ji mɛi ni feɔ lɛ pollin. Atsɛɔ lɛ Midge. Fɔfɔi ni shwieee amɛhe lɛ baagbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ ahiɛ hewalɛ mli ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jɛ fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ amɛhe lɛ amli lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the tree lacks essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or that the ground is waterlogged and drowning the roots. It can also happen during severe dry spells when the tree tries to save water.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hia, tamɔ nitrogen, loo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni shishifãi lɛ miiho nu. Ebaanyɛ eba yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa be mli hu beni tsei miitao ni amɛbu nu he lɛ.

english: This is caused by a fungal infection called Black Pod disease, which thrives in cool, overly shaded, and wet conditions. Clearing heavy weeds and pruning branches allows air and sunlight to dry out the farm and prevent the fungus from spreading.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela kɛ enɛ baa. ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ lɛ Shade babaoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Jwɛi ni tsii kɛ tsei aniji ni ajieɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli gĩɔ ni ehaaa ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Pruning removes weak, dead, or overcrowded branches so that sunlight and air can reach all parts of the tree. This reduces fungal diseases and directs the tree's food and energy into growing bigger, healthier cocoa pods.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni egboi, loo ni eyi obɔ lɛ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ashɛ tso lɛ fã fɛɛ fã he. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi, ni ekwɛɔ tso lɛ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ nɔ koni ekwɛ̃ kookoo ŋmɔji ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees stop bringing out new pods during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ekwɛɛɛ ŋmeii heei yɛ harmattan be ni nu lɛ egbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees need steady rainfall to form pods. During the dry season, the trees slow down their growth and shed flowers to conserve water and protect themselves from heat stress.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ hia nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be koni amɛfee ŋmeii. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Tsei lɛ haa amɛdaramɔ kɛ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ baa shi koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he.

english: Can I grow crops like plantain or cassava together with my young cocoa trees on the same land?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantain loo cassava afata kookoo tsei bibii ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, plantains and maize are great companion crops because they provide shade and food while the cocoa grows. However, cassava should be planted far from young cocoa trees because its large root system aggressively steals water and nutrients from the soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, plantains kɛ ŋmãa ji nanemɛi tsei kpakpai ejaakɛ amɛhaa hulutsoo kɛ niyenii yɛ be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa lɛ. Shi kɛlɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni kɛ ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, eshishifãi wuji lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa.

english: Why is it harmful to burn all the bush on my land before I plant cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mashã jwɛi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu kookoo lɛ?

english: Burning destroys the rich organic matter and beneficial micro-organisms in the topsoil that feed cocoa roots. Leaving cleared bush to decay naturally creates mulch that keeps the soil moist and fertile.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa babaoo kɛ nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ ni haa kookoo shishifãi lɛ niyenii lɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ tsei bibii ni he tse lɛ gbɛ ni amɛgboi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ, ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why am I getting very few pods from my farm even though my cocoa trees are very big and thick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ pods fioo ko pɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ dara waa ni amɛhe wa moŋ?

english: As cocoa trees grow very old and oversized, they spend more energy maintaining their heavy wood structure than producing flowers. Old farms also accumulate pests and shade themselves out, requiring rehabilitation or replanting with fresh seedlings.
ga: Ejaakɛ kookoo tso lɛ etsɛ waa ni eda. No hewɔ lɛ amɛkɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛkwɛ tso ni tsii fe nine lɛ nɔ fe bɔ ni amɛkɛfeɔ fɔfɔii. Okwaafoi momo lɛ buaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa lolo ni amɛhaa hulu lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Esa akɛ asaa lɛ loo adu dumɔwui heei.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. They need partial shade from large trees or fast-growing food crops like plantains to protect their delicate leaves from burning and to keep moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo fioo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo niyenii tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni ebu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he, ni koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Why do some of my plantain shoots grow thin and take a very long time to produce bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ ekomɛi yɛ mlɛo ni amɛheɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Shoots with wide, broad leaves early on are called 'water suckers' and produce weak fruit. You should select 'sword suckers'—shoots with thin, spear-like leaves—because they stem from strong root connections and grow faster with bigger fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni mli kwɔ yɛ shishijee mli lɛ akɛ ‘tsei ni nuɔ nu’ ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo. Esa akɛ ohala ‘klante ŋmeii’, ni ji ŋmeii ni baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni tamɔ akpɔlɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛjɛɔ shishifãi ni mli wa waa lɛ amli, ni amɛdaraa oya kɛ aduawai wuji.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to grow green and healthy. It can also happen if heavy rains flood the soil and drown the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná hewalɛ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni eha shishifãi lɛ shwie nu.

english: Why are the center leaves of my young corn stalks full of holes with tiny caterpillar dropings inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-babi ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ eyi kɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni shwieɔ shi yɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. The moth lays eggs on the leaves, and the hatched caterpillars crawl into the central funnel of the plant to feed on tender growing leaves.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmei, ni ji ŋmei ni woɔ ewui yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ. Ni ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ shwereɔ kɛboteɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ nu lɛ mli koni amɛye baai ni miida blɛoo lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce big, bushy green leaves but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ jwɛi wuji ni baai eŋɔli yɔɔ mli shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen fertilizer or is planted in soil that is too rich, the plant sends all its energy upward to build big leaves instead of storing energy in the root tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ nitrogen ŋmei babaoo nɔ loo adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋmei tsɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, etsuɔ ​​ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛfee baai wuji.

english: Yam vines need to reach high into the sunlight so their leaves can create food energy. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing leaf diseases and encouraging larger tubers.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ afee niyenii hewalɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Etsiɔ baa helai anaa ni ehaa yitsei wuji yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the stem before turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi dani ebatsɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop off when the plant experiences heat stress, extreme dry periods followed by heavy watering, or attacks from tiny insects like thrips.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Be ni nu egbi ni nu ni mli wa nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. loo tutuamɔi ni jɛɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips mli.

english: Why is it beneficial to plant groundnuts or beans in the same farm with my corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which pulls nitrogen food naturally out of the air and puts it into the soil, helping feed the corn crop beside it.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli nibii ni ji nitrogen lɛ amli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. koni akɛ niyenii aha ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ

english: Why does my farmland produce less crop yield every harvest season even when weather is good?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo yɛ kpamɔ be fɛɛ kpamɔ be mli eyɛ mli akɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi lɛ hi moŋ lɛ?

english: Crops remove natural nutrients from the ground every time you harvest. If you do not replenish the soil with compost, manure, or rest periods, the soil becomes depleted of food.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be ni obaakpa amɛ. Kɛji okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo hejɔɔmɔ bei fataaa he lɛ, Niyenii baaho yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I place dry grass or cocoa pods around the base of my crop plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii awo he lɛ? mi tso lɛ shishitoo lɛ

english: Covering the soil with organic material, called mulching, protects the soil from hot sun, prevents water from evaporating quickly, and stops weeds from taking over your garden.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye obɔɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does some rice smell sweet like perfume, while regular rice has no scent at all?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa henɔi komɛi ŋɔɔ tamɔ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa ni afɔɔ feemɔ lɛ bɛ ŋmɔlɔ kwraa lɛ?

english: Certain rice varieties naturally produce aromatic chemical compounds inside the grain as they grow. This sweet scent is built into the seed's genetics, so some varieties naturally have it while others do not.
ga: Omɔ henɔi komɛi kɛ tsofai ni ŋɔɔ baa yɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Nɛkɛ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma ni ŋɔɔ nɛɛ ehi dumɔwui lɛ a-fɔmɔ nii amli. No hewɔ lɛ, srɔtoi komɛi yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekomɛi hu bɛ.

english: Is perfume rice a completely different type of plant, or can I grow it the same way as regular rice?
ga: Ani ŋmãa ni ŋɔɔ lɛ ji tso ni yɔɔ srɔto kwraa loo manyɛ makwɛ nɔ tamɔ ŋmãa ni afeɔ daa lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Perfume rice is the exact same type of plant as regular rice, just a different variety that naturally produces a scent. You can generally plant and care for it using the same basic rice farming methods.
ga: Omɔ ni ŋɔɔ lɛ ji tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛ omɔ ni afɔɔ feemɔ yɛ gbɛ fɛɛ gbɛ nɔ. Amɛji srɔtoi ni haa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔlɔ ko kɛkɛ. Bei pii lɛ obaanyɛ okɛ shishijee gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ ŋmãa lɛ nɔŋŋ atsu nii ni okɛdu ŋmãa ni okwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Are scent and artificial flavors added to perfume rice in the factory during processing?
ga: Ani akɛ nibii ni akɛfee nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ kɛ nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa ni ŋɔɔ mli yɛ nitsumɔhe lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni atsuɔ he nii lɛ?

english: No, factory processing does not add any artificial scents or perfume to rice. The scent is a natural part of the crop that develops in the field while the plant is growing.
ga: Dabi, nitsumɔhe nine lɛ kɛ nibii ni akɛfee ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ loo tsofai ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ fataaa ŋmãa lɛ he. Scents ji adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa yɛ ŋmɔji amli beni tsei lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: If I polish or mill my harvested rice too heavily, will it lose its natural perfume smell?
ga: Kɛji okɛ hewalɛ shwie ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ nɔ loo okɛ hewalɛ tsɔ mli lɛ, Ani tsofa-kɛ-ŋma lɛ mli adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa lɛ baaje mli?

english: Yes, heavy milling can remove the outer layers of the grain where many of the natural aromatic oils are located, which reduces the strength of its natural scent.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔtɔ ni tsii baanyɛ ajie dumɔwui lɛ asɛɛgbɛ fã ni adebɔɔ mli mu ni ŋɔɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ baaha adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔlɔ lɛ hewalɛ aba shi.

english: Why can I smell a strong sweet scent in my rice field when the crop is almost ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minuɔ ŋmãa ni naa wa ni ŋɔɔ waa yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ amli beni eshwɛ fioo ni abaakpa ŋmãa lɛ?

english: As aromatic rice matures on the stalk, the natural oils inside the plant reach their highest level. Warm sunlight causes the plant to release these natural scents into the air, signaling that the grains are ripe.
ga: Beni ŋmãa ni ŋɔɔ waa lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ Adebɔɔ mli fɔji ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ baashɛ amɛhe ni nɔ kwɔ fe fɛɛ. Hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ jieɔ nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai nɛɛ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ omɔ ŋmaa lɛ ekwɛ̃.

english: Will harvesting my perfume rice crop too early affect its natural smell?
ga: Ani ŋmãa ni ŋɔɔ ni akpaa mra tsɔ lɛ baaná adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa lɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, harvesting before the grains are fully mature prevents the plant from fully developing its natural aromatic oils, which results in a weaker scent.
ga: Hɛɛ, nikpamɔ dani dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ tsiɔ tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee amɛ adebɔɔ mli mu ni ŋɔɔ lɛ kwraa. Enɛ haa ŋmɔlɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ baa.

english: Can I make my regular rice crop smell sweet by spraying scents or using special liquid fertilizers?
ga: Ani manyɛ maha mi-ŋmã tsei ni miduɔ daa lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni mikɛshwieɔ nɔ loo ŋmɔlɔ krɛdɛɛ ko ni ji nu ni mikɛbaatsu nii lɛ nɔ?

english: No, fertilizers only provide food for plant growth and cannot create a perfume scent in non-aromatic crops. The aroma comes strictly from the natural traits of specific seed varieties.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii ji niyenii pɛ kɛha tsei adalɛ. ni enyɛŋ ejie ŋmɔlɔ kpo yɛ tsei ni bɛ ŋmɔlɔ amli. Nɔ ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ jɛɔ adebɔɔ mli sui ni yɔɔ dumɔwu pɔtɛɛ ko mli lɛ mli pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Does the type of soil I plant in affect how strong the natural scent of perfume rice will be?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ saa mi-ŋmãa ni ŋɔɔ lɛ he adebɔɔ mli muji lɛ he?

english: Yes, soil nutrients, water availability, and local climate influence how well an aromatic crop can produce its natural oils, though the plant must already have the aromatic trait in its seed.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni yɔɔ Kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ náa bɔ ni tsei ni ŋɔɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛfeɔ fɔ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ esa akɛ tso lɛ aná sui ni ŋɔɔ yɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli momo moŋ.

english: Does the strong natural smell of perfume rice attract more pests and birds to my farm?
ga: Ani adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa ni ŋɔɔ lɛ gbalaa kooloi kɛ okpoi babaoo kɛbaa miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, the natural scents released by aromatic crops in the field can sometimes attract pests like rice bugs or birds more than unscented varieties, requiring careful field monitoring.
ga: Hɛɛ, adebɔɔ mli tsofa-kɛ-ŋma ni tsei ni ŋɔɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ jieɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbala kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmeii loo okpoi babaoo fe tsei srɔtoi ni tsofa-kɛ-ŋma bɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ biɔ ni akwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does perfume rice start losing its sweet smell after being kept in storage for many months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni ŋɔɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ beni akɛto nyɔji babaoo lɛ?

english: The natural aroma comes from delicate natural oils inside the grain. Over time, exposure to heat, light, and air causes these natural oils to break down, making the scent slowly fade away.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli tsofa ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ jɛɔ adebɔɔ mli fɔji ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ amli. Beni be hoɔ lɛ Dɔlɛ, la, kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ haa nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli mu nɛɛ fiteɔ. Ha ŋmɔlɔ lɛ aya fiofio.

english: Why is it bad to rush my seed planting just because the rains have started?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ oooya oya du dumɔwui akɛni nugbɔ ebɔi nɛmɔ hewɔ lɛ?

english: Rushing to plant without properly preparing the soil or checking soil moisture can lead to poor seed germination, weak roots, and crops that are easily damaged by pests or sudden dry spells.
ga: Kɛ́ mɔ ko kɛ oyaiyeli miidu nii ni esaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ loo ekwɛɛɛ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ha lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ akakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ, shishifãi lɛ akagbɔjɔ, ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsɛŋemɔ helai loo hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ afite oya.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seeds very close together to get more crops from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni maná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This overcrowding leaves you with small, weak plants that produce lower yields.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ shweremɔ ni fe nine nɛɛ haa onáa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii fioo.

english: What causes my crops to get sick and wither even when I plant good seeds?
ga: Mɛni haa midumɔ nii lɛ yeɔ hela ni amɛgbiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui kpakpai moŋ?

english: Crop sickness is often caused by tiny pests, fungi, or bacteria in the soil or air. Poor soil nutrients, bad drainage, or planting infected seed stock can also cause plants to weaken and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii, ŋmei, loo muawai kɛ tsei helai baa. yɛ shikpɔŋ loo kɔɔyɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni ehiii nu ni hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ ni ehiii Loo dumɔwui ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ ni amɛgboi.

english: Why do the leaves on my crops turn yellow and dry up during the sunny period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the plant lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen or is struggling to get enough water. In severe heat, plants shed leaves to protect themselves from losing too much moisture.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, loo eebɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ená nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ he.

english: Why do my harvested vegetables spoil so fast before I can take them to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔi lɛ fiteɔ oya dani akɛwoɔ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Harvesting crops during the hot afternoon traps heat inside the produce, causing it to rot quickly. Harvesting in the cool morning or late evening keeps the produce fresh for much longer.
ga: Nibii ni akpaa yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa dɔlɛ baa nibii ni adu lɛ amli. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, tso lɛ baagbo oya. Nikpamɔ yɛ leebi ni hulutsoo loo hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nibii ni anáa lɛ hiɔ shi ehee be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How can I store my harvested maize so that insects do not destroy it before I sell?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ ato koni kooloi akafite lɛ dani mahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Insects thrive in damp maize. Drying your maize fully in the sun until it is hard, and storing it in airtight sacks or clean, elevated cribs stops insects and mold from ruining your harvest.
ga: Kplukai yeɔ omanye yɛ ŋmãa ni mli efɔ mli. Okɛ hulu la atsu nii ni okɛgbi ŋmãa kɛyashi ebaawa ni okɛto vacuum kotoku loo ŋmãa ni mli tse ni awo nɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii akafite nibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why are some of the seeds I planted refusing to come out of the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ ekomɛi kwɛɛɛ kɛjɛɛɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to sprout if they are buried too deep, if the soil is too dry or too flooded, or if insects and birds ate them under the soil before they could shoot up.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ tsɔ Aloo kɛji kooloi bibii kɛ okpoi ye dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why does my land produce fewer crops each year even though I work just as hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii faaa daa afi lɛ? Ni mitsuɔ nii waa nakai nɔŋŋ?

english: Planting the same crop on the same piece of land every season drains specific nutrients from the soil. Rotating your crops with beans or adding manure helps restore the soil's strength.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ nɔŋŋ daa be lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nibii ni akɛ ŋmeii tsakeɔ loo ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops produce smaller fruits and grains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii bibii kɛ ŋmaa lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than main crops and steal the water, sunlight, and soil food meant for your crops, leaving your plants starved and unable to develop big produce.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ mli. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ otsei lɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: How do I know if my crops need fertilizer or if the soil is just tired?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo shikpɔŋ ni mli tse?

english: If your crops grow very slowly, have thin stems, or show pale green and yellow leaves early in the season, the soil lacks essential nutrients and needs manure or fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji akɛ otso lɛ daa blɛoo waa, eyɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo, loo eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: Why do my harvested maize grains get full of small holes and powder after sitting in my store for just a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli eyi kɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni otsii fioo komɛi pɛ ehi shwapo lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ

english: Weevils eat into stored maize when the grains are not dried completely before storage or when they are stored without protection. Drying maize thoroughly until it crackles and storing it in airtight bags (like PICS bags) starves pests of air and prevents this damage.
ga: Moŋ lɛ baaye ŋmãa ni ato lɛ kɛ́ ŋmãa lɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛto loo kɛ́ akɛto ni abuuu he. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa kɛyashi ebaagbala ni akɛwo kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli (tamɔ PICS kotoku mli) lɛ, ebaaha hɔmɔ agbe kooloi ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ, ni ebaatsi nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes spoil and turn soft so quickly before I can carry them to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ ni efeɔ blɛoo oya dani akɛwoɔ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Harvesting tomatoes in the hot sun and stacking them too deep in woven baskets crushes the bottom fruit and builds up heat, which speeds up rotting. Harvesting early in the cool morning and using shallow crates protects the fruit from bruising and keeps them fresh longer.
ga: Tomato ni akɛtoɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli ni akɛtoɔ tsɛnsi ni akpɛ́ mli tsɔ lɛ shwieɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ anɔ ni ehaa hulutsoo baa. ni haa fitemɔ yaa oya Kɛ́ akpa yibii lɛ yɛ leebi ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli, ni akɛ adekai ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaabu aduawai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ ŋmɔlɔ he, ni ebaaha ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: What is causing the leaves of my young maize to look ragged with small green worms inside the central leaves?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-baby corn baa lɛ miifee tamɔ nɔ ni egbɛ eshwa ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli eyi mli obɔ lɛ? Yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a common pest in Ghana that feeds on young crop leaves. Catching them early by inspecting your farm every few days and applying recommended biopesticides or ash into the leaf funnel stops them before they ruin the whole crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmei, ni ji ŋmei ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni yeɔ baai bibii. Amɛmɔmɔ mra Afeɔ enɛ kɛtsɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ nɔ daa gbii fioo ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo sũ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ woɔ tsei lɛ ahe gbɛi lɛ amli. Tsi amɛ gbɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ.

english: Why are my green cocoa pods turning black and rotting right on the trees during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads fast in cool, damp, and shaded conditions. Pruning excess cocoa branches and clearing weeds allows sunlight and wind to dry the farm, which stops the disease from spreading to other pods.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, fɔ́, kɛ hulutsoo kɛbaa. Kookoo niji ni fa fe nine ni aaafolɔ ni ajieɔ jwɛi lɛ baaha hulu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ akagbi ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haaa hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã podi krokomɛi amli.

english: Cassava root rot occurs when heavy rains cause water to log in heavy soils around the roots, allowing fungal germs to breed. Planting your cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps water drain away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu tsɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli, ni ehaa ŋmei lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my corn plants turning yellow from the tips downward even though it is raining?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛnaa kɛyaa shi kɛji nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to make leaves green and grow big. Adding animal manure or well-timed nitrogen fertilizer gives the plant the quick food boost it needs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛbaai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ oya.

english: Why do my maize plants stay short and yellowish whenever these bright purple-flowered weeds grow near them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ kukuji ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ be fɛɛ be ni jwɛi ni fɔfɔii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ?

english: That weed is called Witchweed (Striga), and its roots attach to your maize underground to steal all the crop's food and water. You must pull up Striga plants before they produce seeds, and rotate your field with crops like groundnuts to weaken the weed.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi nɛɛ akɛ Witchweed (Striga) ni eshishifãi lɛ kpɛtɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmãa he koni eju ŋmãa lɛ niyenii kɛ nu fɛɛ. Esa akɛ otsi Striga tso lɛ shishi dani ewo dumɔwui. Ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii atsake oŋmɔji lɛ koni eha jwɛi lɛ afee blɛoo.

english: Why do agriculture officers recommend that I plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same field with my corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni aduɔ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that trap natural nitrogen from the air and leave it in the soil. This enriches the ground naturally, helping neighboring corn plants grow better without buying as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli nitrogen ni amɛshiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ shika babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛhe tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli.

english: Why do my pepper plant flowers keep falling off instead of turning into pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ pepper aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant is stressed by extreme afternoon heat, a lack of water during dry spells, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil moist with mulch around the base helps the plant retain its flowers so fruits can form.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ shwane latsaa ni naa wa lɛ mli. Nu ni bɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛfataa he Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my yam vines wilt and droop during the afternoon heat even when it rained a few days ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli be mli ni mifeee nakai lɛ? Ni nugbɔ nɛ gbii fioo komɛi ni eho nɛ?

english: When the soil lacks organic matter (like dried leaves or compost), it cannot hold onto rainwater for long, causing the ground to dry out rapidly under hot sunshine. Adding compost or manure to your yam mounds helps the soil trap moisture longer.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli (tamɔ baai ni egbi loo ŋmɔshi nibii) lɛ, enyɛŋ ehiɛ nugbɔ nu lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata o-sweet potato pile lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because direct sunlight burns their tender leaves and dries out the moisture in the soil. Leaving big trees or planting temporary crops like plantains gives young cocoa the shade and cool air it needs to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ agbi. Kɛ́ ashi tsei wuji loo adu be kukuoo mli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo plantain lɛ, ebaaha kookoo bibii lɛ aná hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the crop even forms cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ dani tsei lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops use to stay green and grow. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure gives the plants the food they need to stay green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛha amɛhiɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli.

english: How does planting groundnuts alongside my corn help the soil without using bought fertilizer?
ga: Te ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua shikpɔŋ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ ni akɛ ŋmãa ni aheɔ lɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to a special family of crops that trap natural food from the air and store it in their roots. When the roots stay in the dirt, they release this extra food into the soil, feeding nearby corn plants for free.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji tsei akuu krɛdɛɛ ko ni mɔ̃ɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi amli. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ebaajie niyenii ni fa nɛɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni oha ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ niyenii yaka

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot underground when there is heavy rainfall for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When heavy rain fills flat soil with water, air cannot reach the roots. The trapped water suffocates the cassava roots and creates conditions where soil germs multiply and cause the tubers to rot. Planting on raised mounds or ridges lets extra water drain away.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu yiɔ shikpɔŋ tɛtrɛɛ lɛ nɔ obɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Nu ni emɔ mli lɛ baaha ŋmei shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. ni ekɛ shihilɛi ni helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aya hiɛ ni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbo lɛ baa. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu babaoo hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather is too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet too quickly. Without steady, regular water and mild weather, the plant drops its flowers to protect itself from drying out.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ oya tsɔ. Kɛji nu ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni ehiii lɛ bɛ lɛ Tso lɛ baajie fɔfɔii koni ekɛbu ehe kɛjɛ ŋmɔlɔ he.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves out in the sunlight. When the leaves catch plenty of sun, they make food that travels down into the ground, which makes the yam tubers grow big and heavy.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛbaai lɛ aje kpo yɛ hulu la mli. Kɛji baai lɛ ná hulu la babaoo lɛ mahoo niyenii ni gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ tsiimɔ.

english: Why do weeds cause my maize crop to produce small, thin ears?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi ŋmãa toi lɛ feɔ bibii ni egbɔjɔɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients directly from your crop. When weeds grow close to maize, they eat the food intended for the corn, leaving the corn plants too weak to build large cobs.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ jwɛi kwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmãa he lɛ Amɛyeɔ niyenii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha ŋmãa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmãa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛfee ŋmãa wuji.

english: What causes tiny worms to eat holes in the middle leaves of my young corn during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmei feɔ bibioo nɛkɛ? Ye bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baa lɛ teŋgbɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ.

english: These worms are fall armyworms that hatch from eggs laid by moths. They crawl into the central leaves where it is soft and moist to feed on the growing point of the corn, especially when dry weather prevents rain from washing them away.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji ŋmeii ni afolɔ ni fɔ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni ŋmeii fɔɔ lɛ amli. Amɛkplekeɔ kɛboteɔ teŋgbɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli efɔ lɛ amli koni amɛye ŋmãa lɛ hei ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛ́ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ tsiɔ nugbɔ naa koni ekafɔ amɛ.

english: Why will putting three or four maize seeds in one small hole give me less food than putting just one or two?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ŋmãa etɛ loo ejwɛ ni akɛwoɔ bu bibioo kome mli lɛ haaa niyenii babaoo fe ŋmãa ŋmãa kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ?

english: When too many seeds grow out of one single spot, the plants crowd each other out and fight for the same soil food and water. This makes all of them thin and weak, resulting in small cobs or no cobs at all.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui babaoo kwɛ̃ kɛjɛ he kome lɛ Tsei lɛ baabua amɛhe naa ni amɛbaatswa niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Ha efee fɛɛ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii loo eko kwraa baaa.

english: Why do small dark beetles destroy my stored dried maize after a few months in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ kpata mi-abele ni egbi ni mikɛto lɛ hiɛ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi ni mikɛhi ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Storage insects like grain weevils often lay tiny hidden eggs inside the grain while it is still in the field or in damp storage bags. If the grain is not dried completely until it is hard, those eggs hatch inside the barn and the insects eat the inside of the seeds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni akɛtoɔ nii ahe tamɔ dumɔwui amli ŋmeii fɔɔ ŋmeii bibii. Akɛwoɔ dumɔwui amli be mli ni amɛyɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo loo awoɔ kotokui ni mli efɔ ni akɛtoɔ mli lɛ amli. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ egbiko kwraa ni amɛhe waaa. Nakai ŋmeii lɛ baafɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. ni kooloi baaye dumɔwui lɛ amli.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow before the crop even matures?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani tso lɛ eda lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to stay green and grow. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure early in the season keeps the foliage healthy and helps produce larger cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ yibii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni eye ebua ni eha ŋmeii wuji aba.
