english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate direct, strong sunlight because their leaves lose moisture faster than roots can draw water. Planting fast-growing nurse crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides crucial shade and keeps the soil cool during their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, baai lɛ amli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu. Nurse tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ cocoa masɛi lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to grow well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally climb to expose maximum leaf area to sunlight, which the plant uses to make food and swell the underground tuber. Staking keeps leaves off the wet ground where diseases spread and ensures the vine gets enough light to make big yams.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛha hulu la lɛ ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe babaoo. ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii ni ehaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ fũuɔ Staking baaha baai lɛ akaje hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hela lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã lɛ. Ni ehaa wain tso lɛ mli kpɛɔ bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them because saturated soil prevents roots from breathing. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges lets excess rainwater drain away naturally, keeping root tubers healthy and firm.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa yɛ amɛhe. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ ni eyi obɔ lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ waa ni amɛhiɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do agricultural officers tell me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts before planting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔdu tsina loo ŋmei dani wɔdu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts trap nitrogen from the air and store it in their root nodules. When the plant dies, that nitrogen stays in the soil, working like free natural fertilizer for the maize crop planted in the next season.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ sũ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa ŋmãa ni adu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Why do the new hybrid seeds I buy produce a good harvest, but seeds saved from that harvest produce poor crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui heei ni akɛfee hybrid ni miheɔ lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai lɛ? Shi dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ haaa yibii kpakpai.

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred from two distinct parent plants to give maximum strength and yield in the first generation. Seeds collected from that harvest lose those superior combined traits, leading to uneven growth and lower yields if replanted.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ fɔɔ kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔi tsei srɔtoi enyɔ amli koni amɛná hewalɛ babaoo kɛ yibiiwoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔ mli lɛ laajeɔ amɛ sui ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni ejaaa baa ni kɛji akɛ adu ekoŋŋ lɛ, yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from the undersides of leaves, or spreading leaf-curl viruses. Applying neem oil solution or recommended sprays controls these pests before they stunt plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo helai ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ dani tso lɛ akpa dalɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop all their flowers without setting fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiho amɛfɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off unpollinated when air temperatures get extremely high or when plants suffer sudden water stress. Regular watering at the root zone during flowering helps maintain plant humidity so flowers can develop into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni pollination bɛ mli kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ trukaa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifã lɛ he daa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ anyɛ atsɔ aduawai.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my crops very close together to get more yield from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting too closely forces crops to compete aggressively with each other for light, soil nutrients, and water, resulting in thin, weak plants with small fruits. Giving plants recommended spacing yields healthier crops and bigger harvests overall.
ga: Kɛ́ adu amɛ kɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi la akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ nu lɛ mli waa Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yibii bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ aha tsei lɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ akɛ amɛhi shi lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo babaoo.

english: Why are my crops failing even when I plant during the exact same month my elders traditionally planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ehiii eyɛ mli akɛ midu yɛ nyɔŋ ni mi onukpai lɛ duɔ yɛ kusum naa lɛ nɔŋŋ mli moŋ?

english: Weather patterns have shifted over time, causing rains to start later or end unpredictably compared to past decades. Checking seasonal rainfall advisories from local extension officers helps you adjust your planting dates to match current weather patterns.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi tsakeɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi sɛɛ loo egbeɔ naa yɛ gbɛ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ nɔ kɛ akɛto afii nyɔŋmai abɔ ni eho lɛ ahe. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be mli lɛ he ŋaawoi ni jɛ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua bo ni otsake odumɔ gbi lɛ koni ekɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni yɔɔ amrɔ nɛɛ akpã gbee.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning brown and dying during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight because their leaves lose moisture faster than their small roots can take in water. Planting shade crops like plantains near them shields the young cocoa from burning until their root systems grow stronger.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, baai lɛ amli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya fe shishifãi bibii lɛ. ni baanyɛ aná nu Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ shãa he kɛyashi amɛshishifãi lɛ baawa.

english: Extreme daytime heat or irregular watering causes severe stress to the tomato plant, making it drop its flowers to conserve energy and water. Keeping the soil consistently damp with mulch helps the flowers stay attached and produce tomatoes.
ga: Gbi mli dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa baa tomato tsei lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa ashɛrɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ashwieɔ koni akɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he. Kɛ́ akɛ muji wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ tomato.

english: Pale yellow leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants use to build green leaves and grow tall. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores their dark green color and health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tso lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii koni ekɛwo baai eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ehiɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni ená hewalɛ kpakpa ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows pests that feed on that crop to build up in the ground. Rotating maize with crops like cowpeas or groundnuts refills the soil with nitrogen and starves crop-specific pests.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni yeɔ tsei lɛ ni amɛbuaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmei tsakeɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nitrogen. ni ehaa niyenii ni baa tso lɛ mli kooloi pɔtɛɛ komɛi anɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why do my vegetable seeds fail to grow when I push them deep into the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ kɛji mikɛ amɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Small seeds only carry a tiny amount of stored energy. If planted too deep, the young shoot burns through all its energy trying to push through the heavy soil and dies before reaching sunlight, so small seeds only need a thin blanket of loose topsoil.
ga: Dumɔwu bibioo hiɛɔ ehewalɛ ni ato lɛ fioo ko pɛ. Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ mli tsɔ Tso bibioo lɛ baashã ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni etsɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ mli lɛ mli ni egbo dani eshɛ hulu la lɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui bibii No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ekɛ ehe afɔ̃ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni etse ehe lɛ nɔ pɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up tightly and stop the plant from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe waa ni ehaa tso lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or mites that hide under the leaves and feed on the plant's sap. Spraying early with neem water or soapy water removes these insects and allows new leaves to uncurl and grow.
ga: Kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. which hides under the leaves and feeds on the plant's sap Spraying with neem water or soapy water early This will help get rid of these insects and allow new leaves to unravel and grow.

english: Why do the middle leaves of my young maize plants look like holes were chewed into them overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni abu ko yɛ mli nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm, which hide inside the center whorl of the maize plant during the day and feed on the tender leaves at night. Checking the center leaves early and clearing the caterpillars protects the growing tip of the stalk.
ga: This damage is caused by pests such as Fall Armyworm, which hides in the middle of corn plants during the day and feeds on young leaves at night. Nibii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Ni ŋmeii lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tso lɛ yitsei ni miida lɛ ahe.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are mature enough to dig up without opening the soil?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be mli ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni obaanyɛ okɛfo ni ogbeleee shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava plants show maturity when their lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, leaving a bare main stem, and the soil around the base of the stem starts to crack as the tubers expand beneath the ground.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ shɛɔ dalɛ he beni amɛshishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ. Ashiɔ tsɔne lɛ mli tsɔne titri lɛ efolo. Ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni bulb lɛ mli lɛɛɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Plantain plants have broad, shallow roots that do not grow deep into the ground, making them top-heavy when carrying a full bunch of fruit. Supporting the main stem with a sturdy wooden fork prop prevents the weight and wind from pushing the tree down.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔlɔ ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni ekwɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa efeɔ nɔ ni tsii kɛ́ ootere aduawai ni eyi obɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tso ni akɛfee tsɔne ni mli wa fiɔ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, no tsiɔ muji kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekatsi tso lɛ shi.

english: Why do my harvested seed yams start growing sprouts inside the storage barn before the planting season begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Yam tubers naturally wake up from their resting period after a few months regardless of soil moisture because of their internal biological clock. Storing them in a cool, well-ventilated shade barn slows down sprouting, but growing shoots mean the seed yam is ready for the field.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ baate shi kɛjɛ wɔɔhe mli yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ. ekɔɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ mligbɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ ahewɔ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ amɛ wo ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha amɛkwɛ̃ fioo. Shi ŋmeii ni fata he lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii dumɔwui lɛ efee klalo kɛha dumɔ.

english: Why do I need to clear the weeds around my crops before doing anything else on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ? Miŋmɔshi nibii dani mafee nɔ kroko yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients from your crops. Clearing them first ensures that your crops get all the soil food and attention when you feed or trim them later.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni ebaaha amɛná miishɛɛ beni ohaa amɛ niyenii loo ofoɔ amɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: What happens to my cocoa trees if I leave weeds growing around them during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mishi jwɛi komɛi yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ? Cocoa tsei yɛ nugbɔ be mli?

english: Overgrown weeds trap excess moisture and block air flow around the stem. This creates a dark, damp environment that encourages fungal diseases like black pod disease to spread quickly.
ga: Jwɛi ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nu ni fa fe nine ni etsĩɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛbɔleɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ naa. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli ewo duŋ ni mli edɔ ni woɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pod hela lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã oya.

english: Trimming excess or dead branches—known as pruning—allows direct sunlight and fresh air to reach the inner tree. This prevents diseases and helps the tree direct its energy into growing larger cocoa pods.
ga: Ale niji ni fa fe nine loo ni egboi lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ hu akɛ niji ni afoɔ. Enɛ baaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ashɛ tsei ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ tsiɔ helai anaa ni ehaa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ kookoo ŋmɔji wuji.

english: How does trimming branches actually help my cocoa trees yield more fruit?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tso ni afoɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi-cacao tso lɛ ni ewo yibii babaoo?

english: When you prune weak or overcrowded branches, the plant stops wasting energy on unnecessary leaves and instead sends nutrients directly to the main trunk and branches where flowers and pods develop.
ga: Kɛji ofo tsei niji ni bɛ hewalɛ loo tsei niji ni egbɔjɔ tsɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baakpa hewalɛ ni efiteɔ yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ. ni yɛ no najiaŋ lɛ, ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ yaa tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ kɛ eniji ni fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why is it best to apply fertilizer only after I have finished weeding and trimming my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo mli beni migbe jwɛi lɛ ni mifolɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ naa pɛ?

english: If you apply fertilizer before weeding, the weeds will eat up the nutrients before your cocoa trees can reach them. Cleaning and pruning the farm first makes sure only the healthy crop absorbs the fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli dani okɛ jwɛi lɛ shwie shi lɛ, Jwɛi lɛ baaye niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ dani cacao tsei lɛ ashɛ amɛhe. Okwaafoi lɛ amli saamɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afolɔ mli klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ pɛ baaŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: If your crop leaves turn yellowish, growth slows down, or the trees produce few small pods, the soil is low on nutrients and requires fertilizer to boost pod production.
ga: Kɛji tso lɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdaraa blɛoo loo tso lɛ mli ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ lɛ, no lɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmeii awo mli koni ŋmeii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Is there a specific routine I should follow every year for farm tasks like weeding, pruning, and fertilizing?
ga: Gbɛjianɔtoo pɔtɛɛ ko yɛ ni esa akɛ makwɛ nɔ daa afi kɛha ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔi tamɔ jwɛi ŋmɔmɔ. ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli loo awooo mli

english: Yes, following a set seasonal sequence protects your crop. Clearing weeds first, pruning second, and fertilizing last prepares the tree in stages to produce a strong main harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, be mli gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ ni oooye nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu onibii ahe. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli klɛŋklɛŋ Nɔ ni ji enyɔ ni afoɔ Ni naagbee ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii ji ni asaa tso lɛ yɛ be kɛ bei amli kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii titri ni mli wa.

english: Why does the main cocoa harvest usually happen toward the end of the year around December?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ, akpaa kookoo titri lɛ yɛ afi lɛ naagbee gbɛ, aaafee December mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees flower during the mid-year rainy season, and the pods take about five to six months to mature fully, making them ready for harvesting right around December.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ teŋgbɛ. Ni ŋmeii lɛ heɔ aaafee nyɔji 5-6 dani amɛdaraa kwraa. Ha efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ lɛ yɛ December aaafee.

english: Ripe cocoa pods change color as they mature—usually changing from green to bright yellow, or from red to orange-yellow—and make a hollow sound when gently tapped.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, etsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. loo kɛjɛ etsuru nɔ kɛyashi ŋmɔŋ-ŋmei nɔ ni ebaafee gbee ni mli ewo muji kɛji akɛ ata he fioo.

english: How does the dry weather around December affect how I dry my harvested cocoa seeds?
ga: Te kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi yɛ December mli lɛ saa kookoo yibii ni akpa lɛ agbimɔ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: The sunny, dry weather in December provides ideal natural conditions for drying cocoa beans thoroughly on raised mats, preventing mold and keeping the crop quality high for sale.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ yɛ December mli lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha kookoo ŋmeii ni agbiɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ tsɔji ni awo nɔ lɛ anɔ. Tsi fungus naa ni okwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do imported crop seeds from other countries perform differently on my farm in Ghana compared to local seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni akɛjɛɔ maji krokomɛi anɔ aba lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ yɛ miŋmɔ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ mli kɛ akɛto maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui ahe lɛ?

english: Imported seeds are bred for the specific weather, soil, and sunlight conditions of their home countries. While they can produce high yields under controlled conditions, local seeds are naturally adapted to withstand Ghana's high heat, native pests, and rainfall patterns.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛbaajɛ maŋsɛɛ aba lɛ anɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ, shikpɔŋ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ naa. Eyɛ mli akɛ nɛkɛ dumɔwui nɛɛ baanyɛ awo yibii babaoo yɛ shihilɛi ni akudɔɔ mli moŋ, Shi maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui lɛ ji adebɔɔ naa tsakemɔi ni baanyɛ adamɔ hulutsoo ni naa wa naa. Shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ Ghana nugbɔshiimɔi

english: Tomatoes drop their blossoms when the weather gets too hot or when soil moisture fluctuates rapidly. High daytime temperatures destroy the pollen, causing the plant to shed the flowers instead of forming fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake oya. Gbi mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ pollen ŋmeii. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo yibii.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants roll up during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a plant's natural defense to survive intense heat. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the sun to conserve water and prevent drying out.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu koni ehi wala mli yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli. Tsei haa amɛhe ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ mli koni nu akafite ni amɛtsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient for growth. Rain can wash nitrogen deep into the soil where young roots cannot reach it, or the soil may simply need manure or fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Nugbɔ baanyɛ afɔ nitrogen lɛ he kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi bibii nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Aloo ekolɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he baahia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: Why do my vegetable plants produce small, weak fruits when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ woɔ yibii bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots and leaves compete against each other for water, soil nutrients, and sunlight. This leaves no single plant with enough energy to grow large, healthy fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ amɛteŋ Enɛ haaa tso ko kwraa aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do caterpillars attack my maize farm more aggressively during dry spells than during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tutuaa mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ waa yɛ fɛ̃i be mli fe nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Warm, dry weather shortens the hatching cycle of pest eggs, allowing caterpillar populations to explode quickly. Heavy rains, on the other hand, wash young insects off the leaves and reduce their numbers.
ga: Shihilɛ ni mli edɔ, ni egbi lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ fɔmɔ be lɛ feɔ kuku. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ayibɔ yaa hiɛ oya. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ahe ni ehaa amɛyibɔ ​​baa shi.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster and stronger than my crop seedlings in the same soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe mitso lɛ dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native wild plants that have evolved to survive harsh conditions and absorb water and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crop seedlings.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli ni amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe dumɔwui ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why are my seeds failing to sprout even after I water them every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni mikɛ nu wo amɛmli daa gbi po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if they are buried too deep, if the seeds are old and dead, or if the soil is so waterlogged that air cannot reach the seed to start its growth.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ tsɔ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ egbɔ ni amɛgboi Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu aahu akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ dumɔwui lɛ ahe koni ebɔi dalɛ.

english: How do I know the best time to plant cassava cuttings when the rains start?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ adu ŋmei kɛji nugbɔ nɛ?

english: The best time to plant cassava is after two or three steady rains have deeply soaked the ground, ensuring the soil stays continuously moist so the stem cuttings can sprout roots before any sudden dry spell.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu ŋmei ji beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ shii 2-3 ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ewo nu lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni tsei niji lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ shishifãi dani amɛgbi trukaa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings need shade trees above them while mature cocoa trees can stand in the open sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tso bibioo lɛ he hiaa ni aná tso ko ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni kookoo tsei ni eda jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ adamɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants have thin, delicate leaves that easily burn under direct sunshine. Temporary shade plants act as shields until the young cocoa develops deep roots and a thick leaf canopy to handle full sunlight.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be kukuoo mli lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ tsɔne ni buɔ mɔ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ baaná shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ baai ni mli tse ni baaye abua hulu la ni yeɔ emuu lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to them acts like a living umbrella, preserving soil moisture and shading the cocoa until it matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ ni ehaa kookoo lɛ shwereɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ekwɛɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds as close together as possible to get more crop yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe bɔ ni manyɛ koni maná yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for limited sunlight, groundwater, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space to build strong stems and produce large, full ears of corn.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la fioo, shikpɔŋ shishi nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa hegbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni wa baakwɛ̃ ni ekɛ ŋmãa toi wuji baa.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize turning yellow and drying up from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ kɛjɛɔ eshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves are usually a sign that your soil is low in nitrogen, an essential food for plant growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps the plant regain its healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛdara ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the field. Rotating with crops like groundnuts or beans restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. ni ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei Yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad to throw chemical fertilizer on my field during heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaashi tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes the fertilizer off the field before the plant roots have a chance to drink it in. Fertilizer should be applied when the soil is moist but not during torrential downpours.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ mli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ náa hegbɛ amɛnuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi jeee yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to cut long wooden sticks to support my yam vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei kakadaji lɛ? Koni akɛfi sweet potato wain tso lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yam is a climbing vine that needs to lift its leaves high off the ground to catch as much sunlight as possible. Good sunlight exposure through staking helps the plant send energy down to produce big, thick tubers.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni ehe hiaa ni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Hulu la ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛtsɔ staking nɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ kudɔɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa shi koni ekɛ bulbs agboi ni mli tse aba.

english: Why do my tomato blossoms keep falling off without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist and protecting plants from extreme heat helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Kɛ́ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni abu tsei ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava bushes twisting, shrinking, and getting white and yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, egbɔjɔ, ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This leaf damage is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whitefly insects. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties prevents this virus from spreading through your farm.
ga: Cassava mosaic hela, ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Cassava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni ooodu lɛ baaye abua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ eshwa oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that burrows into the funnels of young maize plants to feed on fresh foliage. Detecting them early allows you to use appropriate pest control before they destroy the growing tip.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ amli koni eye baai heei. Amɛ ni oooyɔse mra Ebaaye ebua bo ni okɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe gbɛjianɔtoo ni sa atsu nii dani amɛfite tsɛŋemɔ helai ni miida lɛ.

english: Why does covering the bare dirt around my crops with dry grass stop them from wilting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko nɔ ko nɔ ko shwieɔ shi lɛ Feed mi ŋmɔshinii lɛ kɛ jwɛi koni ekɛtsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkagboi?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves (mulching) acts like a blanket that shades the soil, stopping heat from evaporating groundwater and keeping plant roots cool.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi (mulch) ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ tsɔne ni tsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ naa. Etsiɔ dɔlɛ naa koni ekafee shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni hoɔ. ni ehaa tsei shishifãi lɛ mli jɔɔ

english: What actually makes the flowers on my cocoa trees turn into pods?
ga: Mɛni haa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny beneficial insects, like midges, to carry pollen from one flower to another. Without this pollen transfer, the flower cannot form a pod and will simply fall off the tree.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi biɔ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii, koni amɛjie pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛya ekroko mli. Kɛji akɛ pollen transfer bɛ lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛŋ afee pods ni amɛbaagbee shi kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ.

english: I hear extension officers talking about hand pollination; how does that help my cocoa farm?
ga: Minu ni extension nitsulɔi lɛ miiwie fɔfɔi ni akɛ niji feɔ pollen lɛ he. Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ eyeɔ ebuaa mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Hand pollination is when you manually move pollen to cocoa flowers using tiny tools or brushes. Because natural insects don't visit every flower, doing this yourself ensures more flowers get pollinated, which can significantly increase the number of pods on your trees.
ga: Nine nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ji be mli ni okɛ onine shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ dɛŋdade bibioo loo brɔsh nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, adebɔɔ mli kooloi bibii eyasaraaa fɔfɔi fɛɛ fɔfɔi. Kɛji bo diɛŋtsɛ ofee enɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eba akɛ fɔfɔi lɛ baaná ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ aya hiɛ waa.

english: Are all insects on my cocoa farm harmful to my crop?
ga: Ani kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: No, not all insects are bad. Tiny midges are essential because they pollinate your cocoa flowers so pods can grow. You only need to spray pests like mirids (capsids) that destroy your leaves and pods.
ga: Jeee kooloi bibii fɛɛ ehiii. Koolooi bibii ahe miihia ejaakɛ amɛwoɔ kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ koni ŋmɔtɔi lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃. Ehe miihia ni okɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ mirids (capsids) ni fiteɔ obaai kɛ o-pods lɛ pɛ afɔ nɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop so many flowers onto the ground without making pods during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efeee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When cocoa trees do not get enough water, they drop their flowers to save energy and protect the main tree from dying of stress. Giving the trees partial shade and water helps them hold onto flowers better.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ nine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ lɛ Ebaajie fɔfɔii koni ekɛbu hewalɛ he ni ebu kookoo tso lɛ he kɛjɛ haomɔ he. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo kɛ nu ha tso lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do cocoa pods grow directly on the main trunk and thick branches instead of the tips of the twigs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ kɛ niji ni mli tse lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ moŋ fe ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ niji lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees produce pods on the trunk and main stems so the heavy weight of the mature pods doesn't break thin outer branches. This unique growth habit is called cauliflory.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii yɛ amɛshishi kɛ amɛshishifã titri lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ haŋ niji bibii lɛ amli agbala. Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ dalɛ su krɛdɛɛ nɛɛ akɛ kɔliflower.

english: Why do some of the tiny cocoa pods on my tree turn black and shrivel up when they are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ etsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbo eyɛ mli akɛ Eji bibioo kwraa lolo lɛ?

english: This is often caused by 'cherelle wilt,' which happens when the tree has more small pods than it can feed, or by fungal diseases like black pod. Good pruning and feeding the soil help the tree support more healthy pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ‘cherelle wilt’ ni baa kɛji tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii tsɔ ni enyɛŋ eye ebua lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni etsɔ diŋ lɛ kɛbaa. Tso lɛ mlifomɔ kpakpa kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛfiɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa lɛ asɛɛ.

english: Why is it important to cut off the water sprouts and extra branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei niji kɛ tsei niji ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Extra branches and unwanted shoots (chupons) steal nutrients and water away from the pods. Cutting them off opens the tree to sunlight and air, which encourages more flowers to grow and reduces disease.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine kɛ ŋmeii ni ataooo (chupon) lɛ juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli. Tso ni afoɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ naa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛdaraa babaoo ni ehaa helai baa shi.

english: How does having shade trees on my farm affect how my cocoa trees produce?
ga: Te tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ saa kookoo tsei lɛ ayibiiwoo he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Shade trees shield young cocoa from strong sun and harsh winds, keeping the soil moist. However, too much shade creates damp conditions that bring diseases, so keeping moderate, balanced shade helps trees flower and yield well.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Shi kɛlɛ, hulutsoo be ni fe nine lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ helai baa lɛ baa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ohiɛ hulutsoo ni sa ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ewo fɔfɔi ni ewo yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my neighbor's cocoa trees yielding more pods than mine even though our farms receive the same rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ kookoo tsei lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe mipod lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ wɔŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ moŋ?

english: Higher yields are usually due to good farm practices such as timely pruning, weeding, controlling pests, and following expert advice on pollination and soil care rather than weather alone.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔ mli nifeemɔi kpakpai tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afoɔ lɛ hewɔ ni yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo baa lɛ. weeding Be ni sa mli nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ ŋaawoi ni he esa ni kɔɔ pollination kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ he lɛ ni ayeɔ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ ohe afɔ̃ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ lɛ pɛ nɔ lɛ

english: How can I tell if my cocoa trees are healthy enough to bear a good harvest this season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cacao tsei lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo ŋmaa kpakpa yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: A healthy cocoa tree has thick, dark green leaves, a clean trunk free of heavy moss, strong flower clusters, and green young pods that do not turn yellow or dry up prematurely.
ga: Kakao tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ yɛ baai ni mli tse, ni ji eŋɔli ni tsuɔ. Tso lɛ mli tse ni ŋmeii babaoo bɛ mli. fɔfɔii akuu ni mli wa kɛ fɔfɔi bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tsakeee ŋmɔŋ loo egbiee mra.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize are usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency or waterlogged soil starving the roots of air. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea when the soil is moist will help the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa loo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ yeɔ shishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ urea fata he beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Is it better to apply fertilizer to my crops right before a heavy rain or after the rain falls?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaawo ŋmɔshi nibii amli ŋmɔshi nibii dani nugbɔ nɛ waa loo no sɛɛ?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer shortly after a light rain when the soil is already moist. If you apply it right before a heavy downpour, the rain can wash the fertilizer away from your crops before their roots can soak it in.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooowo ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ, be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo. Kɛ okɛtsu nii dani nugbɔ nɛ waa Nugbɔ baanyɛ afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ.

english: Why does burning the bush on my land before planting cause my crops to perform poorly in the second year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei bibii ni ashãa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani aduɔ lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ afi ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: While burning bush creates ash that briefly boosts the soil, it kills beneficial soil organisms and destroys organic matter. Over time, this leaves the soil dry, hard, and lacking natural nutrients needed for future crops.
ga: Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsei bibii ni ashãa lɛ haa sũ lɛ feɔ sũ ni haa sũ lɛ mli eyiɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ be kukuoo mli. Egbeɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ni efiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ebɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do I need to use wooden stakes to lift up my yam vines as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe hia mi koni mikɛwo sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ kɛya ŋwɛi be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to catch as much direct sunlight as possible to produce large tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing disease and helping the plant make food more efficiently.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛwo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Etsiɔ helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain trees tend to fall over when the fruit bunches grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ fɔɔ gbee shi kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ dara lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that struggle to support heavy weight, especially during strong winds. Propping up the main stem with a sturdy bamboo or wooden pole supports the weight of the growing bunch and keeps the tree standing.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛfi tsɔne ni tsii ni tsii lɛ nɔ. Titri lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei loo tso ni mli wa to tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ kuu ni miida lɛ muji lɛ ni eha tso lɛ ahi shi.

english: If I plant my crops very close together, will I get a larger harvest from my small piece of land?
ga: Kɛ midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ. Mi nɔ loo daabi?

english: Planting too close actually reduces your total yield because crops must compete for sunlight, water, and soil food. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to produce larger, healthier food.
ga: Kɛ́ odu nii yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ bo tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha onibii fɛɛ ni obaaná lɛ aba shi. Enɛ ji akɛ esa akɛ dumɔwui ashi akaŋ kɛha hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ niyenii ni da ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the flowers on my cocoa trees dropping off without forming any cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni cacao ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa efeee lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers often drop off due to water stress from hot dry winds, lack of shade, or attacks by insects like mirids (capsids). Providing shade trees and protecting the farm from sucking insects helps the flowers set into pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nu ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi, hulutsoo ni bɛ, loo kooloi tamɔ mirids (capsids) ni tutuaa amɛ lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do my cassava roots start to rot underground when the rainy season gets very heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when excess water stays around them for too long, cutting off oxygen and allowing fungal decay to start. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ebɔle amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, ni no haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ baa shi. ni oha ŋmei lɛ aje shishi egbo. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: What is causing holes in my maize leaves with small caterpillars hidden inside the tops of the plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi lɛ amli ni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ baa? Akɛtee tso lɛ yiteŋgbɛ

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that feeds on young maize leaves. Spraying early with recommended organic mixtures like neem leaf extract or approved insecticides can control them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ neem baa mli nu loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ afɔse mra. Abaanyɛ akudɔ lɛ dani efite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: You should not plant immediately after the very first rain, as a dry spell often follows. Wait until the rains become steady and the soil stays moist for several inches down so your seeds can germinate without drying out.
ga: Esaaa akɛ oduɔ nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Ejaakɛ bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo inchii babaoo koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow when there is a long dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ eba lɛ?

english: When there is no rain, maize plants cannot absorb essential nutrients like nitrogen from the soil. The yellowing is the plant's way of showing it is stressed and conserving energy because it lacks the water needed to take up food.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ, Abɛi nyɛɛɛ ajie niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yellowing ji gbɛ kome ni tso lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ etsɔɔ akɛ eyɛ haomɔ mli ni ekɛ hewalɛ miikwɛ ejaakɛ ebɛ nu ni he hiaa lɛ ni ekɛye niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot under the ground when my field gets flooded with rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu eyi ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay alive. Excess water fills up all the tiny air spaces in the soil, suffocating the roots and allowing rot-causing organisms to attack and decay the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ amli, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni eha nibii ni kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ atutua ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛfite.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very thin and fall over easily when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the plants compete with each other for sunlight. They stretch upward very quickly to get light, resulting in tall, weak stems that cannot support themselves in strong winds.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Amɛkpã amɛhe oya koni amɛmɔ kane lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni kɛlɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni nyɛɛɛ adamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa naa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer pods when my farm has too many large shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmɔtɔ fioo yɛ be mli ni miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ tsei wuji ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ babaoo tsɔ lɛ?

english: Mature cocoa trees need a good amount of direct sunlight to make food and produce flowers. Excessive shade limits light and creates damp conditions that encourage diseases like black pod, reducing fruit production.
ga: Cocoa tsei ni eda lɛ he miihia hulu la ni hi jogbaŋŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛwo fɔfɔi. Shade ni fa fe nine lɛ haa la shɛɛɛ shi ni ehaa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni woɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji ahe hewalɛ baa, ni no haa aduawai ni anáa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my pepper flowers fall off without growing into peppers when the sun is very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the pollen inside pepper flowers, preventing proper pollination. When a flower is not pollinated, the plant drops it to save water and energy for future growth.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ pepper fɔfɔi amli lɛ. Enɛ haaa amɛnyɛŋ amɛfee pollination jogbaŋŋ. Beni fɔfɔii lɛ ehiɛɛɛ pollen Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛha wɔsɛɛ dalɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden poles to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso koni ekwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally climb to spread their leaves high up toward the sun to make food. Lifting the leaves off the damp ground also protects them from soil diseases, helping the plant store more food in the growing tuber underneath.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã ŋwɛi kɛya hulu lɛ he koni amɛhoo nii. Baai ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ anaa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii babaoo toɔ bulb ni miida yɛ eshishi lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves of my garden egg plants curling up and turning pale?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites feeding on the underside of the leaves. They suck out the plant's juice and nutrients, causing the leaves to twist and lose their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Amɛmuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tsei amli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛ su fɛfɛo ni ji eŋɔli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts or cowpeas makes the soil better for next season's crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni adu lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas belong to a family of plants that trap nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots. When the plant dies, that nitrogen stays in the soil, acting as natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Peas kɛ cowpeas fata tsei ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ sũ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi.

english: Why do my young tomato seedlings wilt and look dead right after I move them to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni egboi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ amɛ tee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Moving seedlings damages their tiny feeder roots, causing 'transplant shock.' The plant wilts because its damaged roots cannot draw water from the soil fast enough to replace what the sun bakes out of the leaves.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ fiteɔ niyenii bibii lɛ ashishifãi, ni ekɛ "dumɔwui ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ahe gbeyeishemɔ" baa. Tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ shishifãi ni efite lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya bɔ ni sa ni ekɛto nɔ ni hulu lɛ shãa kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why should I cut off the small side shoots growing out of my main tomato stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni jɛ mi tomato tso titri lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Those extra shoots, called suckers, steal energy and nutrients from the main stem. Removing them forces the plant to direct its energy into growing bigger, healthier tomatoes instead of extra leaves.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ, juɔ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ mli. Tomatoi lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛkwɛ tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ moŋ fe ni ekɛ baai ni fata he lɛ baatsu nii.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is essential for green growth, so when soil nutrients are low, the plant pulls nitrogen from its older leaves to feed the young growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tsei lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara lɛ amli koni ekɛha gbekɛbii ni daraa yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava plants have bushy leaves above the ground, but very small tubers when I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ beni mikpaa amɛ lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are planted too close together or receive too much nitrogen, they put all their energy into leafy top growth rather than underground roots. Spacing stem cuttings properly ensures roots have room and nutrients to expand.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo enine shɛɔ nitrogen babaoo nɔ Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛkwɛ̃ɔ baai lɛ anɔ moŋ fe shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Tso lɛ yibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni haa amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa.

english: Why do my cassava leaves have yellowish patches and twisted, curled shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Twisted leaves with yellow patches are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease. It is spread by tiny whitefly insects or by using stem cuttings taken from plants that were already sick.
ga: Baai ni etsilɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Akɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Aloo okɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ momo lɛ amli ŋmeii atsu nii.

english: Why are my tomato blossoms falling off the stem instead of turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop without fruiting when heat gets too extreme or when the soil goes from very dry to suddenly wet. Extreme heat damages the pollen inside the flower, preventing it from forming fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa lɛ nɔ kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ trukaa lɛ nɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. ha efee nɔ ni wooo yibii

english: What is making tiny holes in my young maize leaves and leaving brown waste inside the plant funnel?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi ŋmãa bibii lɛ amli ni eshiɔ ŋmãa ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tso lɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide deep inside the central funnel of the maize plant during the day to feed on young leaves, leaving behind holes and ragged edges as the leaf unrolls.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛye baai bibii. Amɛshiɔ bu kɛ ŋmeii ni etsilɛ be mli ni baa lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during rainstorms even when they are full of fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ? He ni aduawai lɛ eyi lolo lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that get damaged by pests like banana weevil borers or microscopic roundworms in the soil. Damaged roots lose their grip in wet soil, causing the heavy plant to top over under wind.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni kooloi bibii tamɔ banana borer lɛ fiteɔ. loo ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Shishifãi ni efite lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɔmɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. ni haa tsei ni tsii shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ shishi

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow rapidly with broad leaves that act as temporary shade trees, protecting tender young cocoa plants from heat while keeping the soil moist during their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ be kukuoo mli hulutsoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why does spread dry grass around my vegetable plants help them grow better in hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ Mi tsei lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Covering soil with dry grass (mulching) acts like a blanket that blocks direct sunlight. It keeps the soil cool, slows down water evaporation, and stops weeds from sprouting and stealing food from your crops.
ga: Mulching ni egbi (mulching) tsuɔ nii tamɔ blanket ni tsiɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni eju niyenii kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: Why shouldn't I apply dry fertilizer to my crops during a long dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi tsuɔ nii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ mli?

english: Chemical fertilizer needs soil moisture to dissolve so plant roots can safely drink it in. Applying dry fertilizer to dry soil leaves the concentrated chemicals on root tips, which can scorch the roots and waste expensive fertilizer.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anu amɛ shweshweeshwe. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi fata shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ he lɛ, eshiɔ tsofai ni mli eyi obɔ yɛ shishifãi lɛ ashishi. Enɛ baanyɛ ashã shishifãi lɛ ni efite ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa.

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts belong to the legume family, which pulls nitrogen out of the air and stores it in the ground. Planting them with maize naturally enriches the soil with free nutrients that maize needs to grow strong.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni amɛjieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abele ni akɛduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa niyenii ni he hiaa ni aheee nɔ ko koni abele lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why is it important for me to remove large stones and clear my land smoothly before planting cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie tɛi wuji ni majie he ni miyɔɔ lɛ dani madu ŋmei lɛ?

english: Removing stones and leveling the soil allows crop roots to spread easily and gives cassava tubers enough soft space to expand big and straight, while also making harvest much easier without breaking the roots.
ga: Tɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni afee lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa mlɛo. Ni enɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara ni amɛfee tɛ̃ɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa ni efiteee shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn pale yellow even when I water the farm regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil is lacking nitrogen or the ground is too hard for roots to absorb food. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant regain its deep green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná amɛsu ni mli kwɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ, ni amɛdara waa.

english: Tomato plants drop flowers when they get stressed by intense heat, dry soil, or excessive wind. Keeping the soil moist continuously and providing light shade during extreme sunshine helps flowers stay attached and form fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be ni eyɛ hulutsoo yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are the bottom ends of my ripening tomatoes turning dark and soft?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomatoi ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ashishigbɛi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛhe yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the developing fruit, usually when watering is irregular. Consistent watering helps the plant transport calcium from the soil into the fruit steadily.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji nu ni afɔɔɔ be fɛɛ be. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛyaa nɔ amɛjieɔ calcium kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa aduawai lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up while still hanging on the branch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbo be mli ni amɛkã tso lɛ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Black, shriveled pods are caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungus that thrives in cool, overly damp shade. Pruning dense branches lets sunlight and fresh air into the farm, which stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Pods diji ni egbo ni black pod hela kɛbaa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ tsɔ. Nibii ni afolɔ mli babaoo lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up and showing yellow patches on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Curled leaves with yellow spots are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties recommended by extension agents prevents this virus from spreading on your farm.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ akɛ mɛi ni kɛ hela lɛ baa lɛ Kɛ́ odu ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni o-extension agent lɛ wo he ŋaa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ hela nɛɛ akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Yam tubers twist and stay small when the soil mounds are too shallow or full of hard clay and rocks. Making high, soft mounds with loose topsoil allows the tuber to push downward smoothly and expand.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ bibii kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ kɛ tɛi ni wa eyi mli obɔ. Gɔŋ ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni sũ ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ mli etse lɛ ni afee lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shi mlɛo ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa.

english: Why does my maize crop fall over easily whenever a mild wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ gbeeɔ shi mlɛo be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ fioo ko baa lɛ?

english: Maize falls over easily if its root system is shallow or if stem borer insects have eaten the inside of the stalk. Heaping soil around the base of the plant (earthing up) supports the stalk and keeps it upright.
ga: Abɛi shwieɔ shi oya kɛji akɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ loo kɛji akɛ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ yeɔ tso lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni abɔleɔ tso lɛ shishi (shikpɔŋ) yeɔ ebuaa ni efiɔ tso lɛ shishi ni ehaa ehiɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why are my plantain suckers taking so much longer to bear fruit compared to my neighbor's farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii kɛ akɛto mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Plantains grow slowly when weeds compete with them for water and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds regularly around the base and feeding the soil with decomposed manure will speed up growth and give larger fruit bunches.
ga: Plantains lɛ daa fiofio kɛ́ jwɛi lɛ kɛ amɛhe miibɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Jwɛi ni ebɔle shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ ajiemɔ Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii ni egbo lɛ shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni okɛye nii daa lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ adara ni ewo yibii wuji.

english: Why do my cabbage leaves have so many small holes eaten through them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ye nii babaoo?

english: Small holes in cabbage leaves are caused by hungry caterpillars and beetles feeding on the crop. Applying an organic neem seed oil solution or suitable crop protection spray prevents pests from destroying the leaves.
ga: Buji bibii ni yɔɔ kaabeji baai lɛ amli lɛ jɛɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ neem dumɔwui amli fɔ ni sa loo tsofa ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ wo mli lɛ, ebaatsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa koni amɛkafite baai lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the essential plant food needed for green growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or NPK early in the plant's life restores the green color and helps the stalks grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea loo NPK wo tso lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii aku sɛɛ aba ekoŋŋ ni eha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ adara waa.

english: Planting maize continuously on the same soil drains the specific nutrients maize needs and allows pests to build up in the ground. Rotating your maize with crops like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil nitrogen naturally and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni yaa nɔ aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ haa abɛi lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ hoɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmei tsakeɔ Ehaa adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees get severe sunburn and dry out under direct sunlight. Leaving some tall shade trees or planting plantains beside young cocoa creates a protective living umbrella that keeps the soil cool and moist until the cocoa roots mature.
ga: Hulu shãa cacao tsei bibii lɛ waa ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. releasing tall trees Akɛ hulutsoo loo adu yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ, amɛfeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ daa.

english: Staking lifts the yam leaves up into the sunlight so they can make food to build large, heavy tubers. It also keeps leaves off damp soil, which prevents diseases from attacking the leaves.
ga: Staking haa sweet potato baai lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ hulu la mli koni akɛhoo nii koni ekɛfee bulbs agboi ni tsii. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni baai lɛ akahi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ helai ni tutuaa baai lɛ anaa.

english: Why should I cut off most of the young shoot suckers growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ midumɔwu titri lɛ he lɛ ateŋ babaoo?

english: Too many suckers compete with the main plantain tree for nutrients and water, resulting in small, light bunches. Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two strong stems, ensuring the plant produces large, healthy plantain fingers.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ plantain titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu. Enɛ haa tsei niji bibii ni waaa lɛ baa. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ aba ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ ana niji wuji ni he wa.

english: Why do I see small holes in my maize leaves with tiny sawdust-like dirt inside the central funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? yɛ ŋmãa baai ni yɔɔ muji tamɔ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the leaf funnel to feed safely. Applying recommended organic extracts like neem or targeted insecticides directly into the funnel stops them before they destroy the growing point.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai amli koni amɛye nii shweshweeshwe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Akɛ tsofai ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ bɔɔ nii amli tamɔ neem loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ awoɔ tsɔne lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Kpa nibii nɛɛ dani amɛfite he ni edaa yɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot from the tip during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ kɛjɛɔ amɛnaa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Black Pod disease is caused by a water-borne fungus that spreads easily in cool, wet, and shady conditions. Pruning dense branches and weeding under the trees lets sunlight in to dry out damp pods and slow down fungal growth.
ga: Nu mli tsɛŋemɔ hela ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ, kɛ shade yɔɔ lɛ kɛ black pod hela baa. Niji ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ashishi lɛ haa hulu la lɛ haa ŋmeii ni mli efɔ lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ baa shi.

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids that transmit a plant virus. Controlling these insects early with proper sprays prevents leaf curling and keeps the plant fruiting properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. ni ji mɛi ni hiɛɔ helai ni baa tsei amli lɛ Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛji akɛ afɔse tsofa lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot inside the soil if left harvested in heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains soak the ground for too long, water fills up the air spaces and causes fungal rot that turns firm cassava starch into soft slush.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Nu lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui lɛ amli ni ehaa ŋmei lɛ fiteɔ, ni ehaa ŋmei ŋmei lɛ mli wa ni etsɔɔ muji ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants shed their flowers without producing any fruit during hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat destroys the pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing fruit from forming. When a flower is not fertilized, the plant drops it to save energy for survival.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Ehaa aduawai lɛ efeee Kɛ́ afɔɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Why am I getting only one bag of cocoa from my whole acre of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛ kookoo kotoku kome pɛ nɔ kɛjɛ mihe fɛɛ he lɛ?

english: Getting low yields like one bag per acre usually means your soil is low on essential nutrients, your trees are overgrown, or pests and diseases are attacking the pods. Proper pruning, weed control, and applying the right fertilizer can significantly increase your harvest.
ga: Yibiiwoo ni baa shi, tamɔ kotoku kome yɛ acre kome mli lɛ, bei pii lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ faaa. Otso lɛ etsɔ agbo tsɔ. Aloo ani tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai miitutua ŋmeii lɛ? pruning weed control Ni kɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ waa.

english: How do I know if my farm soil needs fertilizer for crops to grow well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: If your crops grow very slowly, have pale yellow leaves instead of deep green ones, or produce very small fruits, the soil is likely lacking nutrients. Applying recommended fertilizers at the start of the rainy season feeds the soil so your plants can grow strong.
ga: Kɛji otsei lɛ daraa blɛoo waa Eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ najiaŋ. loo ewoɔ yibii bibii waa Etamɔ nɔ ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛwo mli lɛ wo mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ koni tsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I test a new variety of cocoa on a small plot before planting it across my whole farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maka kookoo henɔ hee ko makwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ? dani adu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ

english: Testing a new crop variety on a small patch of land allows you to observe how well it resists pests and handles your local soil and rain. This careful trial helps you learn how to manage the crop without risking your entire investment.
ga: Kaa tsei srɔtoi heei yɛ he bibioo ko Ehaa okwɛɔ bɔ ni tso srɔtoi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ jogbaŋŋ, ni etsuɔ ​​he ni eyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ nugbɔ lɛ he nii jogbaŋŋ. Nɛkɛ kaa ni akwɛɔ jogbaŋŋ nɛɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni okaseɔ bɔ ni ooofee okwɛ onibii anɔ ni okɛ oshika fɛɛ ni okɛwo mli lɛ wooo oshara mli.

english: Pruning removes dead or unnecessary branches that waste the tree's energy and block sunlight. Opening up the tree allows air to flow through, reduces fungal diseases, and directs nutrients straight into making bigger cocoa pods.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni he ehiaaa lɛ. Enɛ fiteɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni etsĩɔ hulu la lɛ naa. Tsei lɛ ni agbeleɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi, ni etsɔɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ gbɛ koni ekɛfee kookoo ŋmɔji wuji.

english: How do heavy weeds hurt the growth and yield of my crops?
ga: Te jwɛi ni tsii lɛ baaná miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo nɔ hewalɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm, stealing water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your main crops. Keeping your farm clean ensures your crops get all the food and light they need to produce high yields.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli, ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ oha oŋmɔ lɛ mli tse lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii kɛ la ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die during the intense hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli nyɔji ni mli wa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate roots and thin leaves that burn easily in full sunlight. They need shade from fast-growing nurse crops, such as plantains, to shield them from harsh weather during their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a water-loving fungus that spreads in damp, heavily shaded conditions. Removing infected pods quickly and clearing weeds allows sunlight to dry out the farm and protect healthy pods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni sumɔɔ nu ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ waa. Pods ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ oya kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la lɛ haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ebuɔ pods ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahe.

english: When is the best time of the year for me to plant new cocoa seedlings in Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ madu kookoo dumɔwui heei yɛ Ghana?

english: The best time to plant cocoa seedlings is at the start of the major rainy season, typically around May or June. This gives the young plants plenty of rainwater to grow deep roots before the dry harmattan season begins.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu kookoo dumɔwui ji nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee. Bei pii lɛ, aaafee May loo June. Enɛ haa nugbɔ babaoo nɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ koni amɛwo shishifãi ni mli kwɔ dani harmatta ni egbi lɛ jeɔ shishi.

english: Where can I get reliable advice on crop care if an extension officer is not near my village?
ga: Nɛgbɛ maná ŋaawoo ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ he yɛ? Kɛji akɛ extension nitsulɔ lɛ bɛŋkɛɛɛ mi akrowa lɛ

english: You can gain expert knowledge by watching educational television shows, such as agricultural broadcasts on UTV, or listening to farmer programs on local radio stations that explain modern farming methods step-by-step.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona nilee ni he esa kɛtsɔ tsɔsemɔ he tɛlivishiŋ nɔ nifeemɔi tamɔ okwaayeli he adafitswaa ni ajieɔ yɛ UTV nɔ lɛ kwɛmɔ nɔ loo okwaafoi anifeemɔi ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli redio nitsumɔhei ni tsɔɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ okwaayeli gbɛi lɛ amli fitsofitso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is cocoa considered such an essential crop for farmers in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ abuɔ kookoo akɛ eji ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa waa kɛha okwaafoi ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ?

english: Cocoa is essential because it provides reliable long-term income for families over decades and is Ghana's primary agricultural export, making it highly valuable and supported by government research and subsidies.
ga: Abuɔ kookoo akɛ ehe hiaa waa ejaakɛ ehaa wekui náa shika ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ, ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ yɛ afii nyɔŋmai abɔ ni eho lɛ amli. ni eji Ghana okwaayeli mli nibii titri. Enɛ haa kookoo jara wa waa, ni niiamlitaomɔ kɛ nɔyeli yelikɛbuamɔ fiɔ sɛɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves and shallow roots that dry out quickly under harsh sunlight. When water is scarce, the plant sheds its leaves to reduce water loss and protect itself from dying completely.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Beni nu faaa lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni amɛtsi gbele kwraa naa.

english: When maize seeds are planted too close, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. The plants stretch upward to catch light instead of building thick stems and food for big cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Tsei lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ koni amɛmɔ la lɛ, moŋ lɛ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni mli tse ni amɛhaa ŋmeii wuji lɛ niyenii.

english: How can I tell that my cassava tubers are mature and ready to harvest without digging up the plant?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be mli ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa ni okɛtsuuu nii?

english: You can tell cassava is ready when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, leaving a bare stalk, and the soil around the base of the stem starts to crack as the expanding tubers push upward.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona akɛ ŋmei efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Enɛ haa tso lɛ fã ko bɛ ni shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle shishi lɛ he lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni tso lɛ ni eda lɛ tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests every year even though I plant the same seeds and get good rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi lɛ? He ni miduɔ dumɔwui kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni minine shɛɔ nugbɔ kpakpa nɔ yɛ?

english: Crops pull food and nutrients out of the soil every time they grow. If you harvest continuously without adding manure, fertilizer, or resting the land, the soil becomes hungry and exhausted, leading to smaller yields.
ga: Tsei gbalaa niyenii kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni adu amɛ. Kɛji okpaa nii be fɛɛ be ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo okɛhaaa sũ lɛ he ajɔɔ lɛ, hɔmɔ baaye sũ lɛ ni egbɔjɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ fioo.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plant without forming any fruits during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ? Yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Extreme heat causes tomato flowers to dry up and fail to pollinate. When the temperature gets too hot, the plant sheds its flowers to save energy until conditions improve.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni ehaaa pollination aba. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do people say that planting groundnuts on my plot before planting maize makes the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ midu ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani midu ŋmei lɛ, ŋmei lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which has special roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil. When you plant maize afterward, it eats this stored nitrogen to grow strong and green.
ga: Peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni eyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji odu ŋmãa sɛɛ mli lɛ Ebaaye nɛkɛ nitrogen ni ato nɛɛ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni efee ŋmɔŋ.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my young maize leaves and white powder inside the center leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii amli ni powda yɛŋ ko yɛ baai lɛ ateŋ

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the deep central funnel of the maize plant during the day and feeds on the tender leaves.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii ni mli kwɔ lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Why should I remove some of the leafy shoots growing on the sides of my tomato stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ ahe lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Removing side shoots (suckers) helps the plant direct its water and nutrients into growing larger, healthier fruits rather than wasting energy on extra leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ ŋmeii (ŋmeii) lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekwɛɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɔ koni ekwɛ̃ aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ lɛ
