english: The black spots are caused by a fungus known as Black Pod disease. Rain splashes water droplets containing tiny fungal spores from the soil or infected pods onto healthy ones, spreading the sickness in humid weather.
ga: Fɛ̃i ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela lɛ kɛ heji ni tsuɔ ediŋŋ lɛ baa. Nugbɔ lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ŋmɔtɔi ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ anɔ. kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ loo ŋmeii ni hela emɔ mli kɛtee ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli Egbɛɔ hela eshwaa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ mli

english: Why do weeds make my crops look weak and sickly even when it rains heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni hela mɔ amɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster and have stronger roots than most crops. They drink up the water and steal the plant food from the soil before your crop's roots have a chance to reach them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛshishifãi lɛ wa fe tsei babaoo. Amɛnuɔ nu ni amɛjuɔ tsei aniyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ naa hegbɛ ni amɛshɛɔ he.

english: When maize plants are too close, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough food and light to produce large, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ yɛ amɛteŋ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yes, planting too deep prevents the sprout from reaching sunlight before its stored energy runs out, while planting too shallow leaves seeds exposed to heat and birds. A depth of about two to three fingers is ideal for fast sprouting.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ adu tsei bibii ni mli kwɔ tsɔ lɛ, ebaatsi tsei bibii anaa koni amɛkashɛ hulu la lɛ he dani amɛ hewalɛ ni amɛto lɛ baaho. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ aná dɔlɛ kɛ okpoi. He ni mli kwɔ aaafee inchi enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwereɔ oya.

english: Why must I build high mounds of earth before planting my yam setts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafee shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ dani madu sweet potatoes lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow downward deep into the earth. Soft, loose mounds give the roots space to expand easily without being squeezed by hard soil, resulting in bigger yams.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Gɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni etse ehe lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ amli gbɛ lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya ni shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ emɔɔɔ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, sweet potato lɛ baatsɔ agbo.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sun. Plantains grow fast and have wide leaves that act as umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo bibii koni amɛhi shi lɛ haa.

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the ground around the base of the main stem begins to crack as the underground tubers swell.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni he ni ebɔle tso titri lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni tso lɛ mli ŋmei lɛ mli fũuɔ lɛ.

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to quickly soak up surface water and nutrients. They steal these resources before your crop's roots can fully spread, which is why clearing them early is critical.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ oya. Amɛjuɔ nibii nɛɛ dani otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã kwraa. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie amɛ mra lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia.

english: Why do my tomato plants wither and drop their blossoms when the soil stays too wet for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Too much water suffocates crop roots by cutting off air in the soil. Damaged roots cannot absorb nutrients or support flower growth, causing the plant to droop.
ga: Nu babaoo haa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni efoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Shishifãi ni efite lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii loo amɛye amɛbua fɔfɔi lɛ adalɛ. haa tsei gboiɔ

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants turning pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is lacking key nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, or that waterlogged roots are unable to absorb food from the ground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii titri, tamɔ nitrogen, yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo shishifãi ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow stronger when I mix dry animal manure into the soil before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ mli wa waa kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmeii ni egbi futu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani midu lɛ?

english: Animal manure serves as long-lasting food for the soil, slowly releasing nitrogen and organic matter that help the ground retain moisture during dry weather.
ga: Koolooi ashishifã tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ kɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ, ni ejieɔ nitrogen kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fiofio. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why do my yields decrease when I plant maize on the exact same plot of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil. Rotating maize with beans or groundnuts helps restore nitrogen and keeps the soil fertile.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa lɛ, ehaa nitrogen lɛ baa ekoŋŋ ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Young cocoa trees get easily scorched by intense sunlight. Plantains grow fast and provide tall, broad leaves that shade the young cocoa plants while keeping the soil moist during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ. Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni kɛlɛ ni haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Cassava drops its leaves during hot, dry spells to save water and protect its roots. As soon as the rainy season returns, the plant will sprout fresh leaves and continue growing normally.
ga: Yucca shwieɔ ebaa lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebu eshishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛji akɛ ebote nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai heei ni ebaada bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do the leaves on my small maize plants turn purple or yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ purple loo yellow lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, while purple leaves show a lack of phosphorus. Adding manure or the right starter fertilizer provides the nutrients needed for dark green, healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. yɛ be mli ni baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs bɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo shishijee ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ lɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts alongside my maize help my maize grow bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. Nearby maize plants feed on this natural fertilizer, which helps them build stronger stems and larger cobs.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ yeɔ nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni eha tso lɛ mli awa ni ekɛ ŋmei agbo aba.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is commonly caused by a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies, or by extreme heat. Controlling whiteflies with insect netting or organic neem spray helps prevent this spread.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly loo kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli Whiteflies ni akɛ ŋmeii loo organic neem spray yeɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsĩ nɛkɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ nɛɛ naa.

english: Why does striga weed keep appearing on my maize farm even after I clear the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Striga jwɛi lɛ miijie ehe kpo lolo yɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mijie jɛmɛ moŋ?

english: Striga seeds live deep in the soil for years and attach to maize roots underground before emerging. Rotating your field with crops like cowpeas or soybeans starves the striga seeds and reduces their numbers.
ga: Striga dumɔwui hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ afii babaoo ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmãa shishifãi ahe dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ cowpea loo soybeans ni atsakeɔ lɛ baaha striga dumɔwui lɛ aye hɔmɔ ni ebaaha amɛyibɔ ​​aba shi.

english: Why do my pepper flowers fall off without producing any pepper pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni pepper ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa kwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when temperatures get too high or when the soil lacks moisture during flowering. Keeping the soil evenly watered and applying mulch helps preserve the flowers so peppers can form.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu bɛ mli yɛ fɔfɔi be mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ afee.

english: Plantain roots are shallow and can get weakened by microscopic root pests called nematodes. Propping up bearing trees with wooden poles and using clean planting suckers prevents them from uprooting under heavy weight.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni shishifãi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛgbɔjɔ. Tsei ni akɛ tsei ni akɛfee ŋmɔji tsuɔ nii kɛduɔ kɛ tsɔne ni mli tse ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekaje shishi yɛ jatsui ni tsii shishi.

english: Why do my harvested yams start rotting so fast in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛto lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly if they are bruised during harvest or stored in hot, poorly ventilated rooms. Storing intact tubers in an elevated, shaded yam barn allows cool air to flow around them, preventing decay.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ yɛ kpamɔ be mli loo akɛto tsu ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tubers ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko wo sweet potato ŋmɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ ni yɔɔ hulutsoo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ aya nɔ abɔle amɛhe. Etsiɔ fitemɔ naa

english: Why do my oil palm seeds take so many months to sprout compared to maize seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm dumɔwui lɛ heɔ nyɔji babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛ akɛto ŋmãa dumɔwui ahe lɛ?

english: Oil palm seeds have thick, hard outer shells that prevent water from reaching the embryo inside. Heating the seeds safely in a warm germinator breaks their hard shell dormancy so they can sprout much faster.
ga: Oil palm dumɔwui lɛ yɛ kponɔgbɛ fã ko ni mli wa ni tsiɔ nu naa koni ekashɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe. Kɛ akɛ tsɔne ni haa dumɔwui lɛ shwereɔ lɛ wo dumɔwui lɛ amli shweshweeshwe lɛ, efoɔ ŋmeii ni wa lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi lɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni enyɛ ekwɛ̃ oya kwraa.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive direct, harsh sunlight because their leaves burn easily. Retaining scattered shade trees creates a cool environment and preserves soil moisture so the young seedlings can grow safely.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya. Tsei ni akɛaawo hulutsoo be mli lɛ haa shihilɛ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi bɔni afee ni tsei bibii lɛ anyɛ ada shweshweeshwe.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil. This acts as a natural fertilizer that helps feed your maize and makes the soil richer for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛmɔɔ lɛ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa o-ŋma lɛ niyenii ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How can I tell that my cassava is ready for harvesting without digging up the whole tuber?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmãa lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni okɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋtayaa lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava is typically ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the main stem near the ground turns a dark brown, woody color, usually between 9 and 12 months after planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni tso titri ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ tamɔ tso. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ dumɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why are my tomato plants growing tall with thick green leaves, but not producing many flowers or fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi loo aduawai babaoo bɛ jɛmɛ?

english: Giving plants too much nitrogen fertilizer causes them to focus all their energy on growing tall leaves instead of flowers. Balancing nitrogen with phosphorus and potassium encourages healthy flowering and fruit production.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen babaoo ha tsei lɛ, ebaaha amɛjwɛŋmɔ ahi baai kakadaji ni yaa hiɛ lɛ anɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔii. Nitrogen kɛ phosphorus kɛ potassium ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ni mli wa baa.

english: Why are tiny white insects gathering under my pepper leaves and causing them to curl up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii yɛŋ Buaa amɛhe naa yɛ mi-pepper baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛhaa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: These insects are whiteflies that suck important juices from the leaves and spread viruses that cause leaf curling. Spraying a light mixture of neem oil or soapy water under the leaves helps clear them away.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ ji ŋmeii yɛŋ ni nuɔ nu ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ baai amli ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ amɛshwãa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ fioo loo nu ni akɛ samla efutu mli lɛ shwie baai lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni efɔ amɛhe.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants drop to the ground without turning into peppers during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ pepper yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: When crops do not get enough water during very hot periods, they drop their flowers to conserve energy and save themselves from drying out completely.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa lɛ, ashwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ koni akɛto hewalɛ he ni akagbi kwraa.

english: Why are the leaves of my plantain trees turning yellow and brown around the edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing and drying leaf edges are often caused by leaf spot diseases like Black Sigatoka or a lack of potassium in the soil. Cutting off heavily spotted leaves prevents the disease from spreading to healthy plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ahe helai tamɔ Black Sigatoka loo potassium ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ egbi lɛ baa. Kɛ́ afolɔ baai ni mli ewo muji waa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ eshwa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why do weeds lower the yield of my yam crop even if I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi sweet potato yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds aggressively steal water, light, and nutrients from the soil before the yam roots can reach them. They also trap heat and moisture around the stems, encouraging fungal rot.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ kɛ ekãa juɔ nu, la, kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani sweet potato shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe. Emɔɔ dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i hu bɔleɔ tso lɛ he, ni no haa ŋmeii fiteɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I save seeds from my harvested hybrid maize to plant for the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mi-hybrid corn harvest lɛ mli lɛ toɔ koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specifically bred to give a high yield for only one generation. Seeds saved from that harvest lose their strength, resulting in weak, uneven plants and lower yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ yinɔ kome pɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ baafite amɛhewalɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, ni amɛhe ejɔɔɔ amɛhe, ni yibiiwoo lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize crop roll up into tight tubes during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tsɔnei ni mli wa yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up during the hottest hours of the day as a natural defense to hide their surface area from the hot sun, preventing water from evaporating too quickly.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli bei ni mli edɔ waa lɛ amli koni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni buɔ he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ yɔɔ lɛ he. Tsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya tsɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which helps plants stay green and grow big, or it means the soil is too waterlogged and suffocating the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa. Aloo etsɔɔ akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ miigbɔjɔ.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they experience stress from prolonged dry weather during Harmattan, lack of soil moisture, or damage from sap-sucking insects like mirids.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe shihilɛi ni mli egbi ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ ahe haomɔ mli yɛ harmattan beaŋ. ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nɔ ni kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ pollen lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Staking lifts yam leaves up to catch direct sunlight, which helps the plant produce more food and ultimately build larger, healthier tubers underground.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ koni hulu la ashɛ enɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ niyenii babaoo. ni yɛ naagbee lɛ, ebɔɔ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: How do I know which direction is up when I am planting cassava stems in my farm?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole he ni obaadu o-cassava tso lɛ?

english: Look closely at the small buds or nodes on the stem where leaves grow out; these buds should always point upwards toward the sky when you plant the cutting in the ground.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii loo nodes lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ tso lɛ shishi he ni baai lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ Esa akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi be fɛɛ be kɛ́ odu ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots and carry heavy fruit at the top; if pests like stem borers or root nematodes weaken their base, wind easily uproots them.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai ni tsii yɛ amɛyiteŋ. Kɛji akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ stem borers loo root nematodes lɛ ha amɛshishitoo lɛ gbɔjɔ lɛ, Kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ ajie amɛ kɛjɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli oya.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up into small cups and shrinking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe kɛmiifee kɔɔpoi bibii ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking sap from under the leaves, or by viruses spread by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and die even when the soil around them is still wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitato tso lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni egboɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ miida moŋ? Ani efɔ lolo?

english: This quick wilting is often caused by bacterial wilt, a soil-borne disease that enters the stem and blocks water channels inside the plant, causing it to collapse.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa oya nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni shikpɔŋ ni boteɔ tso lɛ shishi ni etsĩɔ nu gbɛi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ naa lɛ kɛbaa. fite lɛ

english: Why are holes appearing in the leaves of my cabbage plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-cabbage tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Holes in cabbage leaves are typically made by caterpillars, such as the diamondback moth larvae, which hatch from eggs laid on the leaves and feed on the green tissue.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ diamondback ŋmei lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ kɛ bu ni yɔɔ kaabɛji baai amli lɛ baa. Amɛfoɔ kɛjɛɔ wɔji ni akɛwoɔ baai anɔ lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ fãji eŋɔli lɛ.

english: Watering early in the morning is best because plants absorb water before the sun gets strong, whereas afternoon watering leads to quick evaporation and can stress hot leaves.
ga: Nu ni ashwieɔ nɔ leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ tsei lɛ gbalaa nu lɛ dani hulu la lɛ mli wa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ afɔ nu yɛ shwane mli lɛ, ebaaha etsɔ la oya, ni ebaanyɛ eha tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ afee nɔ ni haoɔ.

english: Why do people tell me to plant groundnuts or beans on the same land where I grow my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ mi akɛ midu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmei yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Beans and groundnuts are legumes that capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, which enriches the soil and naturally feeds the neighboring maize crop.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo, ni ehaa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ náa adebɔɔ mli niyenii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen nutrients or that there is too much water pooled around the roots, which prevents the plant from taking up food properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen niyenii bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu babaoo ebua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni no haaa tso lɛ aye nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when the weather gets too hot, when the soil stays too dry, or if you apply too much chemical fertilizer which causes the plant to grow leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Aloo kɛji akɛ okɛ tsofai babaoo fata he, ni no haa tso lɛ woɔ baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: The first rain in the season is often followed by a long dry spell that can scorch young seedlings; it is best to wait until the rains become regular before planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni baanyɛ ashã tsei bibii lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ bɔ ni sa dani odu.

english: What happens to my crop if I plant my corn seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When plants are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, which results in thin stalks and very small corn cobs.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa baa.

english: What is eating small holes in my corn leaves and leaving dark dirt inside the plant leaves?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ muji ni tsuɔ yɛ tso lɛ baai lɛ amli?

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a common crop pest that eats young leaves from the inside out and requires early pest control.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm caterpillar, ni ji tso mli tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ baai bibii kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ ni biɔ ni akwɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela nɛɛ nɔ mra lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: How do weeds actually harm my crops if they are just growing in the soil nearby?
ga: Te jwɛi baaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crop by stealing the fertilizer, soil water, and sunlight that your main plants need to grow well and yield food.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ onibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, shikpɔŋ nu kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa onibii titrii lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná niyenii lɛ ni amɛjuɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my farm produce less harvest if I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔ lɛ naa ŋmaa bibioo kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the specific nutrients that crop relies on and causes crop pests and diseases to build up in the soil over time.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni tso lɛ kɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ hoɔ be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei ahe helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why are my cassava roots staying small and thin even after being in the ground for a whole year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe ejɔ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ mli ni amɛyɔɔ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots cannot expand if the soil is packed too hard, lacks organic matter, or if poor quality stem cuttings were planted.
ga: Kasava shishifãi nyɛŋ alɛɛ mli kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni bɛ loo kɛji niji lɛ bɛ sɛɛnamɔ

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to produce a high yield for only one season; planting saved seeds from a hybrid crop usually produces weak plants with low yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ be kome pɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and burn when there are no big trees growing around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiishã be mli ni tsei wuji komɛi bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves are tender and easily burn under intense sunlight, so they require fast-growing shade crops like plantains to protect them during their early years.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ akɛ shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains lɛ atsu nii kɛbu he yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, a key plant food. Giving the crop extra attention with nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea early enough helps the leaves stay green and make food for big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso lɛ niyenii titri lɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli. Esa akɛ agbala jwɛŋmɔ krɛdɛɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea lɛ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni eha niyenii aha ŋmeii wuji lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce very thin tubers when I plant them close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni mli tse waa kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are packed too tightly, their underground roots compete for limited space, water, and nutrients. Giving each plant proper spacing allows the roots enough room to expand and absorb nutrients to grow big, heavy tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ he ko ni faaa, nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛŋɔ niyenii ni haa tsei wuji ni tsii lɛ.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant suffers stress from intense heat, lack of water, or low soil nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist and feeding the soil helps the flowers stay attached and develop into healthy peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ mli edɔ waa, nu bɛ, loo sũ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ be fɛɛ be ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomatoes get black rotten patches at the bottom while still growing on the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomatoi lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This problem, called blossom-end rot, happens when tomato plants cannot get enough calcium from the soil, often caused by irregular watering. Maintaining steady soil moisture helps the plant move calcium smoothly to the growing fruit.
ga: Naagba nɛɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ blossom end rot lɛ baa kɛ́ tomato tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhaa calcium lɛ yaa aduawai lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it good for me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts alongside my maize on the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu cowpeas loo peanuts kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts naturally pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. Planting them with maize feeds the soil naturally, helping the maize grow stronger without relying entirely on bought fertilizers.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ diɛŋtsɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ daa waa ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ ehe afɔ̃ ŋmãa ni ahe lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds prevent my crops from growing well even during the heavy rain season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa miŋmɔshi nibii akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli po lɛ?

english: Weeds grow very fast and aggressively steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients away from your crops. Clearing weeds early gives your main plants full access to the nourishment they need to thrive.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa tsei ni oyɔɔ mli lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛshwere.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb instead of trailing on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso tso ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeetsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need maximum sunlight to manufacture food that feeds the underground tuber. Staking lifts the leaves into the light and keeps them clean and away from ground pests and diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la babaoo koni amɛná niyenii ni haa ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa la lɛ mli ni ehaa amɛhe tseɔ ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ahe.

english: Seeds need air and warmth near the soil surface to wake up and germinate. Planting them too deep suffocates the seed and wastes all its stored energy before the seedling can break through the ground into the sunlight.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ dɔlɛ ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ koni amɛte shi ni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ amli tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agbɔjɔ ni efite amɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ato lɛ dani dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛya hulu la lɛ mli.

english: Why should I cut off the extra shoots and water branches growing on my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine kɛ nu niji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-koko tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Unnecessary water shoots steal water and nutrients away from the main tree trunk where cocoa pods grow. Pruning these shoots directs energy back into pod production and lets air flow through the tree to stop fungal diseases.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni he ehiaaa lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso wulu lɛ shishi he ni kookoo ŋmeii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ. Nɛkɛ tsei nɛɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hewalɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa pod feemɔ mli. ni eha kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ tso lɛ mli koni ekɛkpa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I spread my fertilizer on the soil right before a heavy downpour?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes loose fertilizer off the topsoil into streams before plant roots have time to drink it. Applying fertilizer when the soil is lightly moist or burying it slightly ensures the plant actually swallows the food.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni etse ehe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa faai amli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ naa be ni amɛkɛnuɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ fioo loo efu fioo lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ ami niyenii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Why do some crop diseases spread suddenly all over my field overnight while others take weeks to show up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe helai komɛi gbɛɔ eshwaa miŋmɔji lɛ amli nyɔɔŋ kome mli yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi heɔ otsii babaoo dani amɛjeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Some diseases erupt immediately when weather conditions are right, while others infect plants silently, building up strength underground or inside the stems before bursting out on the leaves later.
ga: Helai komɛi baa kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hi pɛ. yɛ be mli ni helai krokomɛi Ekɛ tsei yeɔ dioo. Etswaa hewalɛ emaa shi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi loo yɛ tso lɛ mli dani baai lɛ jeɔ kpo sɛɛ mli.

english: How long do I need to keep treating my crop once a major disease outbreak erupts on my farm?
ga: Be enyiɛ ehe baahia ni makwɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ beni hela ko ni naa wa eba miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When a severe outbreak erupts, you usually need to maintain active chemical or organic treatment for about three to four months until the crop fully recovers and completes its main growing phase.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hela ko ni naa wa ko ba Bei pii lɛ, ehe bahiaa ni okwɛ tsofa loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni tsuɔ nii lɛ anɔ aaafee nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ kɛyashi tso lɛ baaná hewalɛ kwraa ni egbe edalɛ fã titri lɛ naa.

english: Why did my yam tubers rot inside the soil even though the green leaves looked fine for months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be mli ni baai eŋɔli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ nyɔji babaoo lɛ?

english: Soil diseases often build up strength underground quietly without showing outer symptoms, and by the time the rot bursts through or becomes visible, the damage inside is already advanced.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ helai toɔ amɛhewalɛ shishi dioo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. ni ejieee kponɔgbɛ okadi ko kpo Ni beni be lɛ shɛ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efo mli loo ebafee nɔ ni anaa. Nɔ ni efite yɛ mli lɛ mli wa waa momo.

english: If my crops start recovering after a pest outbreak, can I stop caring for them right away?
ga: Kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɔi tsakemɔ yɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ sɛɛ Ani manyɛ makpa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛmɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: No, even after an outbreak subsides, you must continue intensive field management for three to four months to help the plants rebuild their strength and prevent the pests from returning.
ga: Dabi, kɛji akɛ hela lɛ ba shi po. Ebaabi ni oya nɔ okwɛ ŋmɔ mli waa nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ koni eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ ni otsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa koni amɛkaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba.

english: Why does my cassava plant look like it is not growing on top even though it has been in the ground for weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni mi-cassava tso lɛ ekwɛɛɛ ekoŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ ehi shikpɔŋ otsii babaoo moŋ?

english: Cassava plants spend their early weeks establishing deep root systems to gain strength underground before they burst into rapid branch and leaf growth on the surface.
ga: Yucca tsei kɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii komɛi lɛ toɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛwoɔ niji kɛ baai oya yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants suddenly produce a big burst of flowers all at once instead of one by one?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ miifɔlɔ babaoo shikome moŋ fe ni amɛaawo fɔfɔi komekomei lɛ?

english: Pepper plants accumulate nutrients and energy until climatic triggers cause them to erupt into full flowering simultaneously, leading to a concentrated fruiting period.
ga: Pepper tsei kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ hewalɛ toɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi haa amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi kwraa yɛ be kome mli, ni no haa amɛwoɔ yibii waa.

english: Why is deep soil tilling necessary before planting crops like sweet potatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ dani adu ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Loose soil allows roots to gain strength quickly without resistance so the tubers can swell properly under the surface before the shoots burst above ground.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa hewalɛ oya ni nɔ ko nɔ ko tsiii amɛnaa. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwa jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi dani ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Once my maize field finishes flowering, how long will I wait before the cobs are ready for harvest?
ga: Beni mi-abele ŋmɔji lɛ fɛɛ ewo fɔfɔi lɛ Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee klalo kɛha kpamɔ?

english: After flowering erupts across your field, it generally takes about three to four months of regular care for the ears to fill out and dry properly for harvest.
ga: Beni fɔfɔi lɛ efo yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ Bei pii lɛ eheɔ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ dani toi lɛ eyiɔ jogbaŋŋ ni egbiɔ kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Why do weeds suddenly erupt all over my cleared field immediately after the first heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi shwie miŋmɔ ni mli tse lɛ nɔ trukaa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds sit dormant in dry soil during the hot season; once the rains arrive, they gain moisture strength together and burst through the surface all at once.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui yaa shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, nu lɛ mli nu lɛ yaa hiɛ ni eboteɔ nu lɛ hiɛ shikome.

english: How long will the fertilizer I apply today continue supporting my crop's growth?
ga: Be enyiɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛtsuɔ nii ŋmɛnɛ lɛ baaye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ?

english: Fertilizer helps crops build internal strength over time, and its active nutrient boost usually supports plant development through a critical period of three to four months.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtswaa amɛmli hewalɛ amɛmaa shi yɛ be ni sa mli. Ni bei pii lɛ, niyenii mli nibii ni tsuɔ nii ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛyaa hiɛ yɛ be ni he hiaa waa ni ji nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli.

english: Why is it important for me to cut off some of the healthy-looking branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mafolɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ aniji ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes excess or overcrowded branches so the tree can send its nutrients directly to the main healthy branches, improving airflow and sunlight to help the tree produce more high-quality pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ niji ni fa fe nine loo ni ebɔle amɛhe fe nine lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ majeɔ niji titrii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛ hulu la lɛ yaa hiɛ koni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ babaoo aba.

english: Will leaving weeds around the base of my cocoa trees help keep the soil cool during hot weather?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ kookoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: No, tall weeds steal valuable water and nutrients from your cocoa trees and trap unwanted dampness that breeds disease. Clearing around the base keeps the tree healthy, while using dried fallen leaves as mulch is a better way to keep the soil cool.
ga: Dabi, jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni jara wa kɛjɛɔ o-cacao tsei lɛ amli ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ataooo ni kɛ hela baa lɛ. clearing around Shishitoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ mli waa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, baai ni egbee shi ni egboi ni akɛtsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ahaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why would an agricultural officer advise me to completely cut down a cocoa tree that still has green leaves on it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ lɛ wo mi ŋaa akɛ mifolɔ kookoo tsei fɛɛ ni baai yɔɔ ŋmɔji lolo lɛ?

english: Certain dangerous diseases, like the swollen shoot virus, spread underground and through tiny insects from one tree to another. Removing an infected tree early stops the disease from spreading and destroying the rest of your farm.
ga: Helai komɛi ni yɔɔ oshara, tamɔ bud swollen virus lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ shishi kɛtsɔ kooloi bibii anɔ. Kɛjɛ tso kome nɔ kɛtee ekroko nɔ Tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã ni efite oŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot on the tree before they are ready to be harvested?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in damp, heavily shaded conditions. Trimming thick tree branches to let in sunlight and removing infected pods early stops the rot from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ. niji ni mli tse ni afoɔ Ha hulu la babaoo aba ni ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii akagbɛ ashwã.

english: How can I be sure that an extension officer visiting my farm has the right training to treat my cocoa properly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ extension nitsulɔi ni baasara miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ tsɔsemɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaatsu mi-kookoo lɛ he nii jogbaŋŋ?

english: Trained agricultural extension officers carry official identification and will always explain the science behind their instructions, showing you how specific practices like proper pruning or disease management will protect your farm in the long run.
ga: Nitsulɔi ni atsɔse amɛ ni tsuɔ okwaayeli he nii lɛ baaná woji ni tsɔɔ akɛ amɛji mɛi ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ. ni ebaatsɔɔ jeŋ nilee ni yɔɔ amɛ ŋaawoi lɛ asɛɛ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. Etsɔɔ bo bɔ ni abaanyɛ afee nifeemɔi pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ tsei ni afolɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Aloo bɔ ni helai ahe nitsumɔ baanyɛ aye abua ni abu oŋmɔ lɛ he yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: If I plant my cocoa trees very close together, will I harvest more cocoa from my land?
ga: Kɛji midu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe Ani makpa kookoo babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: No, planting too closely forces trees to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each tree proper spacing allows it to grow strong branches and yield more pods per tree.
ga: Dabi, dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ abɔ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko teŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niji lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ ni eha tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko afee ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Why do the flowers on my cocoa trees drop to the ground without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Flowers drop when the tree is stressed by dry weather, lacks soil nutrients, or when natural pollinators like small midges are not present on your farm.
ga: Fɔfɔi baagbee shi kɛji shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli Aloo be mli ni adebɔɔ mli nibii ni haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmeii bibii, bɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: When cocoa trees get too much direct sun, their leaves turn pale yellow, burn at the tips, or curl up. Planting shade crops like plantains nearby shields them from harsh heat so they can thrive.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ ná hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo lɛ, baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Naagbee ni ashã loo ni ebɔle ehe Shade tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he koni amɛshwere.

english: Why do my cocoa trees lose so many leaves when the dry Harmattan season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa tsei lɛ ahe baai babaoo miifite yɛ harmattan be ni egbi lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Losing leaves is the tree's natural way of saving water; shedding leaves prevents moisture from evaporating through the foliage so the tree can survive the dry season until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni laajeɔ lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ nu toɔ. Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ tsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekatsɔ baai lɛ amli bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil has lost its power and needs fertilizer to help my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli ewo muji ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni eye ebua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Signs of tired soil include slow tree growth, leaves turning yellowish, and smaller harvest sizes year after year. Applying the right fertilizer restores essential food back into the soil.
ga: Nɔ ni fata okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ efite lɛ he ji tsei ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo. baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ŋmaa lɛ dalɛ baa shi afi fɛɛ afi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in an open field with no shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kooko dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni hulutsoo bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains alongside young cocoa creates a living shield that provides the shade and moisture needed for survival during their first few years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe lɛ haa gbɛtsii nii ni hiɛ ka ni haa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa kɛha wala yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ baa.

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling up and drooping in the afternoon even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: Plants curl their leaves during the heat of the day to protect themselves and conserve water. Watering deeply in the early morning allows roots to drink before the heat sets in, preventing heat stress.
ga: Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe ni amɛbu nu he. Kɛ́ afɔ nu babaoo leebi lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ nuɔ nu dani latsaa lɛ baa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ latsaa he haomɔ naa.

english: Leaves yellowing from the bottom up is a clear sign that the soil is running low on nitrogen. Adding animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore healthy green growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ada jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my cassava produce huge leafy stems above ground but very small roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kɛ baai wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi shishifãi bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil encourages the plant to put all its energy into growing big leaves instead of expanding tubers. Using balanced soil nutrients and keeping soil loose lets the roots swell properly.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ama baai wuji ni amɛkwɛɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaagbɛ bulbs lɛ amɛshwã. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni sa ni akɛtsu nii ni akɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my groundnuts stay small and yellowish while my neighbor's crop right next door is healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanuts lɛ ji bibioo ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni mikutsoŋnyo ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ tso lɛ yɛ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Soil conditions can change significantly over short distances, and hard or acidic soil prevents groundnuts from taking up food. Adding compost or agricultural lime helps loosen the soil and unlock nutrients.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ shihilɛ baanyɛ atsake waa yɛ gbɛ kuku nɔ. Ni shikpɔŋ ni wa loo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ baatsi ŋmeii anaa koni amɛkaye nii. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo okwaayeli mli lime fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbele niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ anaa.

english: Why are my cassava leaves covered in sticky white spots and curling inward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ? Akɛ nɔ ko ha nɔ ni akɛwo mli?

english: Those white spots are small insects like mealybugs or whiteflies that suck energy from the plant leaves. Spraying a mixture of water and gentle soap or neem oil wipes them out before they destroy the crop.
ga: Nakai ŋmeii yɛŋ lɛ ji kooloi bibii tamɔ mealybugs loo whiteflies ni shwieɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli. Nu ni akɛ samla ni mli jɔ loo neem fɔ efutu mli lɛ baatsumɔ he dani efite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are black spots spreading across my yam leaves during the heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa sweet potato baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Persistent wet weather creates humid conditions that encourage fungal leaf diseases to spread. Leaving wider spaces between plants improves air movement and keeps foliage dry, stopping the fungus.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ baa ni woɔ ŋmeii ahe baa helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he hewalɛ. Kɛ́ ashi gbɛ babaoo yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛgbiɔ ni amɛkpaa ŋmeii

english: Why is it bad practice for me to grow tomatoes on the exact same spot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji nifeemɔ gbonyo akɛ madu tomato yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop in one spot continuously lets soil pests and diseases build up over time. Rotating tomatoes with crops like maize or beans starves tomato pests and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Kɛ́ oya nɔ adu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai abua shikpɔŋ lɛ naa yɛ be ni sa mli. Tomato ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsakeɔ Enɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants produce plenty of flowers, but the flowers drop off without making any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛjieee ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa?

english: Pepper flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture fluctuates sharply. Keeping soil moist with straw mulch helps regulate temperature so flowers turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baa shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake oya. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why does growing weeds near my young maize cause the crops to stay thin and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni aduɔ yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ masɛi ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with young crops for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds within the first few weeks gives young crops full access to the nourishment they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi lɛ to he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa tsei bibii lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why should I use a rope or thread to make straight lines when planting my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ kpãa loo tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli lɛ atsu nii yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ kɛ́ midu ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Using a planting line ensures proper spacing between crops, makes weeding and harvesting much easier, and allows each plant equal access to sunlight and soil nutrients without crowding.
ga: Dumɔwui ahe linei ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa gbɛ ni sa kã ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ. Enɛ haa jwɛi lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa. ni ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ekɛ amɛhe ebɔko amɛhe.

english: How does planting my crops in neat rows help them produce a better yield?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ mitsei lɛ ni miduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni yɔɔ fɛo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mitsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai?

english: Planting in straight rows gives each crop its own room to expand roots and leaves, ensures water spreads evenly across the farm, and prevents crops from blocking each other's sunlight.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eko fɛɛ eko naa hegbɛ ni ekɛ eshishifãi kɛ ebaai lɛ akwɛ̃ɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. ni amɛtsi tsei anaa koni amɛkatsi amɛhe hulu la lɛ naa.

english: Why is it important to leave regular walking paths between my crop rows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mashi gbɛi ni mitsɔɔ nɔ minyiɛɔ daa lɛ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Walking paths allow fresh air to flow through the farm to reduce diseases, and give you space to spray, weed, and harvest without trampling on your growing plants.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi ni akɛnyiɛɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni helai aba shi. ni ehaa bo gbɛ ni okɛshwie, jwɛi kɛ kpamɔ ni okɛ ohe wooo tsei ni miida lɛ amli.

english: Why do my young seedlings need to be protected and nurtured like newborn babies?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni abu midumɔwu bibioo lɛ he ni atsɔse lɛ tamɔ abifao ni afɔ lɛ ehee lɛ?

english: Young plants have weak roots and soft leaves, making them very vulnerable to hot sun, heavy rain, and pests; giving them shelter and early care allows them to build strong roots for high yields.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ baai ni bɛ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa hulu ni tsoɔ waa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛnɔ oya. He ni amɛhiɔ kɛ mra be mli kwɛmɔ Ye obua amɛ ni amɛma shishitoo ni ma shi shiŋŋ kɛha nitsumɔ ni nɔ kwɔ.

english: Why do my young crops dry up when exposed to intense heat right after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbɛ́ɔ kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ la ni naa wa waa he beni adu amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Very young crops do not have deep root systems yet to drink enough soil water, so strong sunlight dries out their leaves faster than the roots can supply water.
ga: Tsei ni darako waa lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lolo shi amɛbaanyɛ amɛnu nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, hulu la ni naa wa lɛ baaha baai lɛ agbi oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aha nu.

english: Why should I clear weeds around my crops while the plants are still very young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe be mli ni amɛji bibii waa lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and will steal the soil food, water, and sunlight meant for your crops if you do not remove them early.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii. Ni ebaaju niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Kɛ́ ojieee oya lɛ,.

english: Why is it necessary to clear and loosen the soil before putting my seeds into the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni mafolɔ mli dani madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Properly prepared soil allows delicate young roots to push easily through the ground to find water and nutrients, giving seeds the best start to grow strong.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni asaa he jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya koni amɛyatao nu kɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ jeɔ dalɛ shishi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What happens if I bury my seeds too deep in the soil during planting?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ midumɔwui lɛ futu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ yɛ dumɔ be mli?

english: If seeds are buried too deep, the young shoots exhaust all their stored food trying to push through the thick soil and die before reaching the sunlight.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afu dumɔwu lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ, ŋmeii bibii lɛ baaye niyenii ni ato ni amɛmiitao amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji lɛ mli ni amɛgboi dani hulu la lɛ aba amɛnɔ.

english: How can I tell if my sprouted seeds are growing healthily in the first few weeks?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji midumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli?

english: Healthy young crops show bright green leaves, firm stems standing upright, and uniform growth across your planted rows without yellowing or wilting.
ga: Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ yɛ baai ni mli tse, amɛshishifãi ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ, ni amɛdaraa po yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli fɛɛ ni amɛfeee ŋmɔŋ loo amɛgbooo.

english: What will happen if I plant my seeds too close to one another in the field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for water, light, and soil nutrients, resulting in tall, thin, weak plants with small fruits or grains.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, amɛshiɔ nu, la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ aduawai loo dumɔwui bibii lɛ baa.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate full direct sunlight because their leaves burn and lose water too quickly. Big shade trees or companion crops like plantains protect young cocoa by blocking harsh sunlight and keeping the air cool and moist around them.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa ni nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya tsɔ. Tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo tsei ni fata he tamɔ plantains yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛtsɔ hulu la ni naa wa ni amɛtsiɔ naa lɛ nɔ. ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ

english: Maize leaves turn yellow from the bottom up when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrients plants need to build food and stay green. It can also happen when heavy rain washes soil nutrients away or when weeds steal the food from the maize.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛkwɛ amɛ ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hole niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ loo kɛ́ jwɛi ju niyenii kɛjɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli.

english: Does it matter which way up I stick a cassava stem into the ground when planting?
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ, ani abaadu ŋmei tsei lɛ yɛ gbɛ ko nɔ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, planting cassava stems upside down causes the new buds to grow downward first before turning up, which wastes the plant's energy, weakens growth, and significantly reduces the weight of the cassava tubers you harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ okɛ o-yucca tso lɛ wo ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii heei akwɛ̃ shi dani amɛdara. ni haa tsei ahewalɛ baa shi lɛ haa amɛdalɛ baa shi ni ehaa ŋmei shishifãi ni okpaa lɛ tsiimɔ baa shi waa.

english: Why do I need to cut off extra shoots or suckers growing around my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Mi dumɔwui lɛ eje kpo.

english: Too many shoots around one plantain stem fight with each other for water, light, and soil nutrients. Leaving only one or two healthy shoots allows the mother plant to focus its energy on growing a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii babaoo ni bɔleɔ plantain tso kome he lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu, la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa plantains akui wuji ni tsii ni amɛkwɛɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Yam leaves need direct exposure to sunlight to produce energy for expanding the tubers underground. Staking keeps leaves off the wet ground where they could rot or catch diseases, allowing maximum sunlight reach.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking baabu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi loo hela aba amɛnɔ lɛ ahe. Ehaa hulu la lɛ kpɛɔ kɛtsɔɔ mli bɔ ni eeenyɛ.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when conditions are too hot, too dry, or when the plant experiences sudden water stress. When stressed, the plant drops flowers to save its water and energy to survive.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ, egbi tsɔ, loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ trukaa. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and making the stems look twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiiha shishifã lɛ miifee tamɔ nɔ ni efite lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking pests like whiteflies or aphids that feed on the leaf juices and spread plant viruses, or by severe dry heat causing heat stress.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo aphids ni yeɔ baai lɛ amli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli. aloo kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa ni kɛ latsaa he haomɔ baa lɛ mli.

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas belong to a plant family that traps nitrogen food from the air and stores it in the soil through small nodules on their roots, naturally fertilizing the soil for crops planted after them.
ga: Peas kɛ cowpeas fata tsei aweku ko ni mɔɔ nitrogen nibii ni haa mɔ he waa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ he ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ anɔ, ni ehaa tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Covering soil with dry plant material, known as mulching, stops sunlight from evaporating soil water, keeps plant roots cool during dry heat, prevents weeds from growing, and decomposes into natural organic fertilizer.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔ. Ehaa hulu la lɛ shwieɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛfiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii

english: Why shouldn't I spread dry fertilizer on my crops when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi shwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Plant roots can only absorb fertilizer when it is dissolved in water. Applying dry fertilizer on dry ground leaves it unusable and can concentrated chemicals that burn and damage crop roots.
ga: Tso shishifãi baanyɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji akɛ amɛwo nu mli pɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi tsu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaaha anyɛɛɛ akɛtsu nii, ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsofai ni mli wa ni shãa ni efiteɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ aba.

english: Bottom leaves turn yellow when the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. Giving your maize a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ urea wo ŋmãa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: High temperatures, lack of water, or poor pollination cause tomato plants to get stressed, leading them to drop flowers to save their remaining energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo pollination ni ehiii Enɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ ashɛrɛ fɔfɔi ashwie koni akɛbu hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: Why do my groundnut plants leave the soil fertile for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ miishi shikpɔŋ ni baa nii kɛha ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their root nodules. When the crop is harvested, this nitrogen remains in the soil as natural fertilizer for future plants.
ga: Peanuts jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifã bɔɔlu lɛ mli. Beni akpaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Nɛkɛ nitrogen nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha tsei ni baaba wɔsɛɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to harsh sunlight and high heat. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains nearby creates a safe, moist environment until the cocoa matures.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ he waa. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Ehaa shihilɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for the plant. Staking lifts the vines so the leaves catch maximum sunlight, leading to larger tuber growth.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni efee niyenii eha tso lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ baai lɛ aná hulu la babaoo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yitso ni da.

english: Why does putting dry grass around my vegetable beds keep the soil damp longer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mikɛwoɔ mi-vegetable saatso lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Dry grass acts as mulch, covering the dirt like a blanket to block direct heat from the sun and slow down water evaporation from the soil.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ mulch. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛbuɔ he kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni ehaa nu ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo

english: Why do small caterpillars hide inside the central funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-ŋmei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Fall armyworms hide inside the central leaves where it is cool and moist, keeping them safe from direct sunlight and predators while they feed on the young leaves.
ga: Fall worms lɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ baai lɛ ateŋ ni mli ejɔ ni edɔ lɛ mli. Buu ohe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ ahe be mli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that suck sap from the underside of the leaves and spread leaf curl viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Amɛmuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ hela lɛ amɛshwãa baai lɛ ashishi.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to survive. Waterlogged soil drowns the roots and creates the right environment for rot-causing fungi to multiply.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ baanyɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my farm crops after the first rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni adu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds have deep, hardy roots that adapt quickly to dry conditions and absorb nutrients faster than cultivated crop seeds when water becomes available.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa. ni baatsake ehe oya kɛya shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ amli ni eŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe dumɔwui ni aduɔ kɛji nu yɛ mli lɛ.

english: This yellowing is a sign that your maize plants lack nitrogen, which is essential for strong, green growth. Applying a nitrogen-based fertilizer like Urea or NPK at the right growth stage will restore their healthy green color.
ga: Nɛkɛ su ni ji ŋmɔŋ nɛɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ he miihia kɛha hewalɛnamɔ kɛ dalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛ akɛ nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli tamɔ urea loo NPK tsu nii yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do extension officers advise us to plant cowpeas or beans alongside our maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ wɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔdu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ wɔ ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and beans capture nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil through their roots. This naturally enriches the soil, helping your maize grow stronger without needing as much commercial fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ beans lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ye obua o-abele lɛ ni ehiɛ wa ni jarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo he ehiaaa.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa trees need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: How do I know which direction to stick cassava cuttings into the soil when planting?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole he ni esa akɛ okɛ o-cassava ŋmɔtɔi lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Look closely at the small leaf nodes or buds on the cassava stick; these buds must point upward toward the sky. Planting them upside down causes the stem to struggle to sprout, leading to poor tuber growth.
ga: Kwɛmɔ baai bibii loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Esa akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu ŋwɛi ŋwɛi lɛ, ebaaha ewa aha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛakwɛ̃. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yitso ni edaaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Does placing long wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb really make the tubers grow bigger?
ga: Tsoi kakadaji ni akɛwoɔ mli Ani kɛ́ aha sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔ kɛtee ŋwɛi lɛ, ehaa sweet potato tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ daa?

english: Yes, lifting yam vines on stakes exposes more leaves to sunlight, allowing the plant to produce more energy. This energy is sent down into the soil to feed and expand the yam tuber.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kɛ́ owó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ebaaha hulu la babaoo ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa hewalɛ babaoo. Akɛ hewalɛ nɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ niyenii ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Covering soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like a protective blanket. It stops soil moisture from evaporating in the heat, prevents weeds from growing, and keeps the roots cool.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ latsaa be mli. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating the central leaves inside the funnels of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that attacks young maize. Applying recommended biopesticides or neem extract into the center of the plant funnels early in the morning stops them before they destroy your harvest.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni tutuaa ŋmãa bibii. Akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu lɛ awo dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ leebi maŋkpa. Tsi amɛ gbɛ dani amɛfite onibii.

english: Why do my tomatoes get black, rotten patches on the bottom of the fruit before ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ hiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egboɔ yɛ shishi dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This black rot, called blossom end rot, happens when tomato plants cannot absorb enough calcium, often due to dry soil. Keeping the soil consistently watered helps the roots take up calcium for healthy fruit development.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ hela ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe nɛɛ akɛ blossom end rot. Ebaa kɛ́ tomato tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu daa lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ náa calcium koni amɛwo yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does a purple-flowered weed cause my cereal crops to stay short and dry even when it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni fɔɔ fɔfɔii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ haa miŋmaa tsei lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ?

english: That weed is called Striga, or witchweed. It attaches its roots directly to your crop's roots under the ground to steal water and nutrients, which stunting your plants.
ga: Atsɛɔ nakai jwɛi lɛ akɛ Striga loo abɛi jwɛi. Ekɛ eshishifãi lɛ kpɛtɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ koni eju nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ haa otsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my small vegetable seeds fail to sprout if I water them heavily right after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai bibii dumɔwui No hewɔ lɛ minɔ lɛ kwɛŋ kɛji mikɛ nu wo nɔ babaoo amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni midu lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Heavy watering washes tiny seeds too deep into the dirt or packs the top layer of soil too tight. Gentle misting or light watering keeps the topsoil soft so delicate shoots can push through.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ babaoo lɛ baaha dumɔwui bibii lɛ akwɛ̃. Afu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsɔ loo ehaa sũ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ Afua loo nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni sũ lɛ yiteŋ sũ lɛ feɔ blɛoo bɔni afee ni ŋmeii bibii lɛ anyɛ abote mli.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the grain is ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani dumɔwui lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, which is a key nutrient for green growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea at the right stage helps keep the leaves green so the ears can fill out properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ urea wo mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayi obɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off without setting any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. Keeping soil moisture consistent with light watering and mulching helps the flowers turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ waa mli lɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu fioo kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ tomatoi.

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up and turning yellow with blotches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by cassava mosaic disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies and infected stem cuttings. Planting disease-resistant stem varieties and uprooting infected plants early stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmei mosaic hela. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni amɛfoɔ Tsoi srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe lɛ adumɔ kɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni akpa helai gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking sap from the leaves. Spraying with recommended neem extracts or insecticides early protects the young leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Akɛ neem mli nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ afɔ nɔ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni ebu baai bibii ahe.

english: Young cocoa seedlings get scorched easily under strong direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide living shade to shield the young cocoa while also giving you food and income while you wait for the cocoa to mature.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui shãa oya kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Plantains ni shwereɔ oya lɛ haa hulutsoo ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ehaa onáa niyenii kɛ shika yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni kookoo lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch enough sunlight to produce food for the tubers underground. Staking also lifts the foliage off damp ground, reducing fungal diseases on the leaves.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛfee niyenii amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baa shi

english: When seeds are planted too close, plants compete with each other for sunlight, ground nutrients, and water. Correct spacing ensures each crop gets enough resources to grow strong and yield big fruits.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. niyenii mli hewalɛ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ naa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ekwɛ̃ waa ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo aba.

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same plot drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows maize-specific pests to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpea or groundnut restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, abaajie niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa mli tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to stunt even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miikpa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo po lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal the plant food, space, and sunlight intended for your crops. Removing weeds during the first few weeks of planting gives your crops the best chance to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii. ni oju tsei aniyenii, he ko, kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Kɛ́ otsi jwɛi kɛjɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni okɛduɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ waa.

english: Covering soil with dry grass, known as mulching, stops heat from drying out the earth too fast and blocks weeds from coming up. It keeps the root zone cool and moist between waterings.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baatsi la ni tsoɔ lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya tsɔ. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ yɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ teŋ.

english: Cassava is usually mature and ready for harvest between 9 to 12 months after planting, when the lower leaves start turning yellow and dropping off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ eda ni efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ.

english: Curled and yellow-spotted leaves are symptoms of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting certified disease-resistant stem cuttings is the best way to prevent this.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadii. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ enɛ naa ji tsei ni atswa ni ana he odaseyeli akɛ helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ adumɔ.

english: How long does a plantain sucker take from planting until it bears a full bunch?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani anyɛɔ akwɛɔ banana ŋmeii akuu ko nɔ?

english: A plantain sucker typically takes between 12 to 15 months to produce a mature bunch ready for harvest, depending on soil quality, rainfall, and proper weed control.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, plantain suckers lɛ heɔ nyɔji 12 kɛyashi 15 dani amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni eda ni esa akɛ akpa. Edamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young plantain plants turning yellow and drooping?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves turn yellow mostly due to poor soil nutrients like nitrogen, insufficient water during dry spells, or root damage caused by microscopic soil worms called nematodes.
