ga: Plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ titri lɛ yɛ sũ mli niyenii ni ehiii tamɔ nitrogen kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. loo shishifãi ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ kɛbaa lɛ.

english: Can I plant cassava and plantain together on the same piece of farm land?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafee ekome kɛdu ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Yes, intercropping plantain and cassava works well because plantains grow tall and provide shade while cassava roots grow deeper, but you must space them properly so they do not compete for nutrients.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ ŋmãa woɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ plantains lɛ daa ni amɛhaa hulutsoo. yɛ be mli ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ lɛ. Shi ehe miihia ni okɛ amɛ abɔ he jogbaŋŋ koni amɛkaye niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: How often can I cut leaves from my kontomire plants without weakening the crop?
ga: Shii enyiɛ manyɛ mafo conetomir tso lɛ baai ni mahãaa tso lɛ agbɔjɔ?

english: You can harvest two to three of the outer, older leaves per plant every few weeks, making sure to leave at least three healthy inner leaves so the plant can continue growing strong.
ga: Obaanyɛ okpa kponɔgbɛ baai ni etsɛ 2-3 yɛ tso kome mli daa otsii 2-3, ni kɛ hoo lɛ, oshi mligbɛ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ 3 koni tso lɛ aya nɔ ada kɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why are tiny holes appearing all over my kontomire leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ani ejie ehe kpo yɛ mi contomire baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ?

english: Small holes in kontomire leaves are caused by leaf-eating caterpillars and beetles. Spraying the leaves with organic neem leaf extract or mild soapy water helps protect them without making the leaves unsafe to eat.
ga: Buji bibii ni yɔɔ contomire baai lɛ amli lɛ jɛɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ amli. Akɛ neem baa mli nu loo samla ni mli ejɔ baafɔ baai lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baabu neem baai lɛ ahe ni ehaaa baai lɛ afee nɔ ni esaaa akɛ ayeɔ.

english: Why do my kontomire plants grow bigger leaves when planted under tall trees than in full sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-contomire tso lɛ baa lɛ woɔ baai wuji kɛ́ eda yɛ tsei kakadaji ashishi fe hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Kontomire naturally thrives in moist, shady conditions. Full sun causes the large leaves to lose water quickly and scorch, whereas partial shade keeps the leaves tender, deep green, and broad.
ga: Kontomire daa yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Hulu la ni naa wa lɛ haa baai wuji lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya ni amɛshãa. yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo fã ko baaha baai lɛ afee blɛoo. Eyɛ eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ.

english: Why does my freshly harvested cassava go dark and spoil after just two days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ni mikpa ehee lɛ mli edɔ ni egbo yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots lose moisture rapidly and react with oxygen once dug up, causing internal discoloration and rotting within 48 hours. Keeping roots shaded or buried in moist soil helps delay spoilage.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ amli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya ni amɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ji oxygen lɛ feɔ ekome kɛji atsa amɛ. Enɛ haa emli su lɛ tsakeɔ ni efiteɔ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 48 mli. Kɛ́ akɛ shishifãi lɛ wo hulutsoo mli loo afu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: What is the best way to stop my harvested plantain from ripening too fast before I take it to market?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ matsi mi-plantain ni mikpa lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ oya tsɔ dani mikɛya jara nɔ?

english: To delay ripening, store your plantain bunches hanging in a cool, well-ventilated shade, away from direct sunlight and away from already ripe fruits that release ripening gases.
ga: koni ekɛ sɛɛ atsɛ shweremɔ Ha plantain tsei lɛ ahi he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ. Ekɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ akabɔ he, ni ekɛ aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ ni jieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ he

english: Why should I plant different crops like maize, cassava, and plantains together instead of just one crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, kɛ ŋmãa afee ekome? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookwɛ tso kome pɛ

english: Growing multiple crops protects your family from hunger and financial loss if bad weather or pests destroy one crop. It also ensures you have food to harvest at different times throughout the year.
ga: Nibii babaoo ni ooodu lɛ buɔ oweku lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hɔmɔ kɛ shika ni fiteɔ lɛ he. Kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ gbonyo loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kpata ŋmɔshi nibii kome hiɛ Ekwɛɔ hu koni oná niyenii ni obaakpa yɛ bei srɔtoi amli yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Can I plant maize and cassava together on the same farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafee ekome kɛdu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Yes, maize and cassava grow very well together. Maize grows fast and is harvested in three to four months, which frees up space and sunlight for the cassava to mature slowly over the rest of the year.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ he kome. Abɛi lɛ daa oya ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji 3-4 mli, ni no haa gbɛ babaoo kɛ hulu la ni haa ŋmei lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Rice grows best in low-lying areas or clay soil that holds onto water for long periods, as rice roots need constant moisture to produce heavy grains.
ga: Omɔ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi loo shikpɔŋ ni shikpɔŋ yɔɔ nɔ ni nu hiɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmɔtɔ he miihia ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ daa koni amɛwo dumɔwui ni tsii.

english: What short-term crops can I plant near my young plantains while waiting for them to grow?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei ni yeɔ be kukuoo manyɛ madu yɛ dumɔwui bibii ahe be mli ni mimɛɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: You can plant quick crops like maize, pepper, or leafy vegetables between young plantains because plantains take nearly a year to bear fruit, leaving open ground and sunlight early on.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu nibii ni aduɔ oya tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, loo aduawai ni yɔɔ baai yɛ plantains bibii lɛ ateŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, plantains heɔ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ afi dani ewoɔ yibii. Shi he ni oyɔɔ lɛ ni hulu la lɛ ashɛ nɔ mra.

english: Why do plantain trees keep the soil around them damp even during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui haa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi po lɛ?

english: Plantain trunks store a lot of water, and their broad leaves block sunlight from reaching the ground, preventing soil water from evaporating quickly.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ hiɛɔ nu babaoo. ni amɛbai ni mli lɛɛ lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ shikpɔŋ. Ehaa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ oya.

english: Why does cassava stay good in the soil for months without rotting before I harvest it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ nyɔji babaoo ni egbooo dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots act as underground food stores that stay alive as long as the stem remains attached, allowing you to leave them in the ground until you are ready to eat or sell them.
ga: Cassava shishifãi tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni baahi shi be fɛɛ be ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baakpɛtɛ he lɛ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ oshiɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni obaanyɛ oye loo ohɔ̃ɔ amɛ.

english: How does a plantain plant produce new shoots if it doesn't grow from seeds?
ga: Te dumɔwu ko baafee tɛŋŋ ewo ŋmeii heei kɛji akɛ ekwɛɛɛ kɛjɛɛɛ dumɔwu mli?

english: Plantains grow from underground stems called corms, which naturally sprout small baby shoots called suckers around the main plant.
ga: Plantains lɛ daa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni atsɛɔ amɛ rhizomes lɛ amli. ni kwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii bibii Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii bibii ni bɔleɔ tso titri lɛ he.

english: Which way up should I plant cassava stem cuttings in the soil?
ga: Te esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Plant cassava stems slanted at an angle with the small raised buds pointing upward toward the sky, so the new shoots can easily grow toward the light.
ga: Yucca tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ koŋ ko nɔ ni fɔfɔi bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmeii heei baanyɛ adara kɛya la lɛ he oya.

english: Why are weeds able to choke my young rice plants so quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miifo mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ amli oya nɛkɛ?

english: Young rice grows slowly in its first few weeks and has narrow leaves that don't shade the soil, giving fast-growing weeds the opportunity to steal sunlight and nutrients.
ga: Omɔ bibii lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli, ni eyɛ baai bibii ni haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ naa hegbɛ ni amɛjuɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize crop turn yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, a vital soil nutrient that plants need to grow strong green leaves and healthy cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai eŋɔli ni mli wa kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow leaves and stay green. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure will help them turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛbaakwɛ̃ ni amɛhi shi eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Will planting groundnuts or cowpeas together with my main crops help my soil?
ga: Ani ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ baadu lɛ baaye abua shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yes, planting legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas helps your soil because their roots trap nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. This naturally enriches the land and acts as free fertilizer for nearby crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni ooodu lɛ baanyɛ aye abua oshikpɔŋ lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ.

english: Choose healthy stems from mature plants that are 8 to 12 months old and free from diseases or insect holes. Cut the middle parts of the stem with active buds, as they sprout faster and grow stronger roots than the soft top stems.
ga: Halamɔ tsei ni eda ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 ni hela loo kooloi ŋmeii bɛ mli lɛ ahe tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Kpɔ̃ɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ fã ni fɔfɔii ni tsuɔ nii lɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛdaraa oya ni amɛyɛ shishifãi ni wa fe tsei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ.

english: Sword suckers—the young shoots with narrow, sword-like leaves and a broad base—are best. They have a strong connection to the mother plant's corm, sprout faster, and produce heavier fruits than water suckers with broad leaves.
ga: Sword suckers—ni ji tsei bibii ni baa bibii ni tamɔ klante kɛ shishigbɛ ni mli kwɔ lɛ—ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ. Amɛkɛ fɔlɔ tso lɛ ŋmeii lɛ bɛŋkɛ kpaakpa, amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni tsii fe nu mli ŋmeii ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and delicate roots that burn easily under full sunlight and harsh winds. They need living shade from temporary crops like plantains to retain moisture and survive their first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa shishi. Ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni yeɔ be kukuoo, tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Staking lifts yam leaves high off the ground so they can catch maximum sunlight to build large tubers underground. It also prevents the leaves from rotting against wet, hot soil and protects the plant from diseases.
ga: Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi tsɔnei wuji. Ehaa baai lɛ hu shwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. ni ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ helai srɔtoi ahe

english: Why is clearing weeds so important during the first few weeks after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and steal the sunlight, water, and soil nutrients your seedlings desperately need to get established. Clearing weeds early gives your crops full access to resources during their most critical growth period.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii. ni ejuɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa odumɔwui lɛ waa koni amɛma shi lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa onibii lɛ naa nibii ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ yɛ amɛdalɛ be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why should I avoid spraying pesticides on my crops in the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ he?

english: Spraying in hot afternoon sun causes liquid chemicals to evaporate too quickly before working, and intense heat combined with chemicals can scorch leaves. It is best to spray early in the morning or late in the evening.
ga: Tsofai ni mli edɔ lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ ha tsofai ni ji nu lɛ shwieɔ shi oya tsɔ dani nitsumɔ jeɔ shishi. Ni dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni akɛ tsofai fata he lɛ baanyɛ aha baai lɛ ashã. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshwie nɔ lɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ.

english: Why are flowers dropping off my tomato plants without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ tomato tsei anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat, irregular watering, or too much nitrogen. Keeping the soil evenly moist and providing light shade during scorching afternoons helps flowers turn into tomatoes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa loo nitrogen babaoo yɛ mli Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ ni eha hulutsoo be mli hulutsoo be lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ tomatoi.

english: What causes the leaves of my pepper plants to curl up tightly?
ga: Mɛni haa pepper tsei lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking pests like aphids, thrips, or mites hiding under the leaves. Spraying with organic neem oil solution or an approved mild insecticide will clear the pests and allow normal leaves to grow back.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. Kɛ́ akɛ organic neem oil solution loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaagbe kooloi lɛ ni eye ebua tso lɛ yibii ni sa lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die during the bright sunny season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate intense direct sunlight because their root systems are shallow and leaves burn easily. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains around them provides shelter, keeps the air humid, and protects the young trees until they grow stronger.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ baaha aná wɔɔhe. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli feɔ fɛ̃i ni ebuɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ amɛhe waa

english: Leaving too many suckers causes them to fight with the main plant for nutrients and water, resulting in smaller bunches. Keeping only one main plant and one or two growing suckers ensures your plantain tree produces large, heavy fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, ebaaha amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu ni jɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei niji lɛ feɔ bibii. Tso titri kome kɛ dumɔwui kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni oookwɛ lɛ baaha o-plantain lɛ awo yibii wuji ni tsii.

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight on their leaves to make food for the tubers underground. Lifting the vines on wooden stakes prevents leaf diseases caused by damp ground and allows the plant to form bigger yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Wein tsei ni awóɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tsei ahe helai ni hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ anaa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa sweet potato ŋmeii wuji

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that your maize is lacking nitrogen, which is essential for green leaf growth. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure will help restore the green color and grow healthy ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha toi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is adding decomposed animal manure better for my farm's soil than using only chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mikɛ kooloi ashishifãi ni egbo baawo miŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hi fe tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ pɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer feeds the plant quickly, but animal manure improves the soil itself. Manure adds organic matter, helps the soil hold moisture during dry spells, and keeps nutrients available for crops over a longer period.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei niyenii oya. Shi kooloi ashishifãi haa shikpɔŋ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ feɔ fɛo. Manure haa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ baashɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli

english: Why is it helpful to spread dry grass around the base of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ makɛ jwɛi abɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishi lɛ he lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass (mulching) acts like a protective blanket. It retains water in the soil, stops weeds from growing, and keeps the plant roots cool during hot afternoon sun.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jwɛi ni egbi (mulching) ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why should I wait to plant my crop seeds instead of sowing right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mimɛɔ koni madu dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The very first rain is often followed by a dry spell before the real rainy season sets in. Sowing too quickly can cause your seeds to germinate and then dry up and die if the rain stops for a few weeks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be diɛŋtsɛ lɛ baashɛ. Kɛ́ adu mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃. Ni no sɛɛ lɛ, egbiɔ ni egboɔ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa otsii fioo komɛi.

english: How do I know that my cassava roots are mature enough to harvest without uprooting the whole plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa ni mijieee tso muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Cassava is typically ready when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, leaving a mostly bare main stem, usually between 9 to 12 months after planting depending on the variety.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. ni tso lɛ yitso lɛ fã titri ni eshwɛ lɛ Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ tso lɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Edamɔ srɔtoi lɛ anɔ

english: Pepper flowers fall off when the plant experiences extreme heat, irregular watering, or poor soil fertility. Giving the plants steady water and shade during peak heat helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ daa loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii Nu kɛ hulutsoo ni akɛhaa tsei yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomato fruits turn dark and rotten as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishi feɔ duŋ ni egboɔ beni edara lɛ?

english: This problem is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium reaching the fruit, often due to irregular watering. Keeping the soil moisture consistent allows the tomato plant to absorb and move calcium into the fruit properly.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. ni calcium ni faaa lɛ kɛbaa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tomato tsei lɛ ni amɛŋɔɔ calcium lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛkɛyaa aduawai lɛ amli.

english: When maize leaves turn yellow starting from the tip downward in a V-shape, it usually means the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow strong.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛnaagbɛ ni amɛfee V su lɛ, bei pii lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots rot in the ground when water sits in the soil for too long without draining well, or when underground pests bite into the tubers, allowing rot diseases to enter.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Aloo beni shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ŋmɔɔ yitso lɛ ni ehaa helai ni egboi boteɔ mli lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to lift their leaves up to catch direct sunlight to produce food for the tubers underground, and keeping leaves off wet ground stops fungal diseases from attacking the plant.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ. Ni kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, ehaaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ akatutua tso lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they get stressed by extreme heat, lack of regular water, or when too much fertilizer makes the plant focus only on growing leaves instead of fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. nu ni hoɔ daa Aloo kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ pɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: What makes my small cocoa pods turn black and dry up on the branches?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ bibioo nɛkɛ? Minɔ lɛ tsɔɔ ediŋŋ ni egbiɔ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast in cold, wet, or dark shade; clearing weeds and trimming tall trees lets sunlight in to keep the pods dry.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Fungal hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ, loo he ni duŋ yɔɔ. Tsei kakadaji lɛ ahe jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ amɛhe ni afoɔ koni hulu la lɛ aha ŋmeii lɛ agbi.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily during wind even when the stem looks strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ?

english: Plantains fall over because microscopic pests called nematodes destroy their underground roots, leaving the plant without a strong anchor to hold up heavy bunches.
ga: Plantains shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ fiteɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ bɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli wa ni ekɛbaamɔ ŋtayaai ni tsii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my young maize leaves look like pests chewed small holes all through them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baa lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ŋmeii emɔ bu bibii yɛ amɛhe fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by Fall Armyworms hiding inside the central leaf funnel and feeding on the tender leaves before they unfold.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms ni kɛ amɛhe teeɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋshɔ lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ baa bibii lɛ dani amɛgbeleɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bulɛ baa ŋmãa baa bibii amli.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass (mulching) keeps the ground cool, prevents moisture from evaporating under the hot sun, and stops weeds from getting sunlight to grow.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (mulching) lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. ni etsĩ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkaná hulu la koni amɛkwɛ̃

english: Why shouldn't I apply chemical fertilizer on my farm when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ woɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs moisture to dissolve into the soil so plant roots can drink it; putting fertilizer on dry ground can burn plant roots or evaporate without helping the crop.
ga: Fɛ̃i he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni ekɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anu. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ shishifãi ashã loo etsɔ la ni eyeee ebuaaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing plants fight each other for soil food, water, and sunlight, resulting in thin stems and small or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ dumɔwui bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: How can I tell if the seed maize I bought will actually sprout before I plant my whole farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmãa dumɔwui ni miheɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ diɛŋtsɛ dani madu ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Good quality seed looks clean, full, and has no insect holes or rot. You can test a small sample by wrapping 10 seeds in a damp cloth for a few days to see if at least 8 or 9 of them sprout before planting your entire field.
ga: Dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe tse ni amɛhe tseee, ni bu loo kooloi ni fiteɔ nii bɛ mli. Obaanyɛ oka nɔkwɛmɔnɔ bibioo ko okwɛ. Obaanyɛ ofee enɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui 10 ni oookɛwo mama ni mli efɔ mli gbii fioo komɛi koni ona kɛji kɛ hoo lɛ dumɔwui 8 loo 9 baakwɛ̃ dani odu ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Is it better to plant seeds saved from my last harvest or buy new certified seeds from the store?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli loo mahe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ shwapo ko mli?

english: While saved seeds are free, certified seeds are specially selected and treated to resist diseases, handle bad weather better, and give you a much higher yield at harvest time.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ he ehiaaa moŋ, shi ahalaa dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ ni atsuɔ he nii koni helai akamɔ amɛ. Enyɛɔ etsuɔ ​​kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni ehiii lɛ ahe nii jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa yibii babaoo yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen fertilizer or the ground is flooded with too much water, which prevents the roots from feeding the plant properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen fertilizer bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ aha tso lɛ niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they get too hot or stressed from dry weather and lack of shade. Plantains planted nearby provide shading and cool air to help flowers turn into pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ edɔ amɛ tsɔ loo amɛhao kɛjɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi kɛ hulutsoo ni bɛ lɛ mli. Plantains ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ haa hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and stop growing during the warm season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekpaa dalɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Curly leaves in hot weather are usually caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips sucking the juice from young leaves, combined with stress from hot, dry soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo thrips ni nuɔ baai bibii amli nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ nɔ haomɔ fataa he lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Black pods are caused by a fungal disease that spreads fast in wet, dark conditions. Trimming extra tree branches lets air and sunlight in to keep pods dry and healthy.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ duŋ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ black pods baa. Niji krokomɛi ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la boteɔ mli koni ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I clear weeds around my young cassava plants when they are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Kasava tso lɛ ji bibioo lolo?

english: Weeds grow faster than young cassava and steal water, sunlight, and nutrients from the soil, causing the young crops to stay weak and produce small tubers.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmei bibii ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii.

english: How does covering the soil with dried plant leaves around my crops help them grow?
ga: Mulching kɛ tsei ahe baai ni egbi ni ebɔle he Te mi ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa mi tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the dirt with dried leaves creates mulch, which keeps the soil cool under hot sun, stops water from evaporating quickly, and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii baa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye nɔ.

english: What causes my farm soil to stay soggy and wet for days after rain stops?
ga: Mɛni haa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa gbii babaoo beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Soggy soil happens when the earth is hard or full of heavy clay, which traps water and starves plant roots of air, leading to root rot.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa loo shikpɔŋ ni tsii eyi mli obɔ. ni hiɛɔ nu ni ehaa tsei shishifãi lɛ bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: What can I do to make my young plantain suckers establish faster after transplanting?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni mi-plantain tsei bibii lɛ ama shi oya beni mikɛwo he kroko lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Plantain suckers grow faster if you trim off old roots and dead leaves before planting, place them in deep holes mixed with decomposed manure, and keep them well-watered.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya kɛji ofo shishifãi momoi kɛ baai ni egboi lɛ dani odu. Okɛwo bu ko ni mli kwɔ ni akɛ ŋmeii ni egbo efutu mli lɛ mli. ni amɛná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa

english: Why do I need to leave proper space between my cassava stems when planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ashi gbɛ yɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ kɛ́ adu lɛ?

english: Proper spacing ensures each cassava plant gets enough sunlight, air, soil nutrients, and water without competing with neighboring plants, which helps the roots grow into larger tubers.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ ŋmei tso lɛ he lɛ haa ŋmei tso fɛɛ ŋmei naa hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ yeee akaŋ Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves in direct sunlight to produce energy for tuber growth. Staking also keeps leaves off the damp ground, preventing fungal diseases and leaf rot.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ajie amɛbaai lɛ awo hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha tuber lɛ dalɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ baai ni fiteɔ lɛ naa.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize lacks nitrogen in the soil or is receiving too much standing water. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-decomposed manure will restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo enine eshɛ nu ni damɔ shi babaoo nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha efee ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant groundnuts on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting groundnuts repeatedly in the same spot allows crop-specific pests and soil diseases to build up. Rotating groundnuts with cereal crops like maize helps break disease cycles and keeps soil fertile.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ shii abɔ yɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ nɔŋŋ baanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai pɔtɛɛi kɛ helai aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ni akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekpaa hela lɛ sɛɛkuu ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweremɔ yaa hiɛ.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, stops water from evaporating quickly under the hot sun, keeps the soil cool, and prevents weeds from growing around your crops.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaha nu lɛ akatsɔ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi akakwɛ̃ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: What is making small ragged holes in my corn leaves and how can I stop it?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa?

english: Ragged holes in corn leaves are typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. Checking your crop early in the morning and applying recommended natural or chemical treatments inside the leaf funnel early in the season will manage the damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okwɛ onibii amli leebi ni okɛ adebɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ awo baai lɛ amli yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids feeding on the sap, or viruses spread by these insects. Controlling sucking insects early prevents leaf curl disease.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni yeɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ hela naa.

english: Why are my tomato blossoms dropping off the plant without forming any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni efeee tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant suffers from high heat stress, irregular watering, or poor pollination. Consistent watering during dry spells helps the plant hold onto its flowers and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ naa dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa loo pollination ni ehiii Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why do experienced farmers recommend keeping shade trees on a cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ kookoo ŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees, especially young ones, burn easily under intense sunlight. Shade trees regulate field temperature, maintain soil moisture, and protect cocoa trees from dry winds.
ga: Cocoa tsei, titri lɛ gbekɛbii lɛ Shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ kudɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli latsaa lɛ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni obuɔ kookoo tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi he

english: Why is it better to buy new certified seed maize instead of planting seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ ooohe ŋmãa dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ? Mohu ɔ, i du duwuhi nɛ a yi wami kɛ je ye nyagbe kpami ɔ mi ɔ.

english: Seeds saved from hybrid harvests lose their strong traits and produce lower yields. Certified seeds are bred for uniform growth, disease resistance, and high harvests every season.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee nibii krokomɛi amli lɛ laajeɔ amɛsu ni wa lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni baa shi. Akwɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ koni amɛdara be fɛɛ be, amɛnyɛŋ amɛye helai anɔ, ni amɛwo yibii babaoo daa be mli.

english: Is it better for me to spray chemical medicine on my crops early in the morning or late in the evening?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ makɛ tsofai afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ?

english: It is best to spray early in the morning or late in the evening because the heat of the sun is low, which stops the medicine from evaporating too quickly. Additionally, many crop pests come out to feed during these cooler hours, making the treatment much more effective.
ga: Esa akɛ afɔse nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ ejaakɛ la ni jɛɔ hulu la mli lɛ faaa. Enɛ haa tsofa lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ. Kɛfata he lɛ, kooloi bibii babaoo jeɔ kpo koni amɛbatao niyenii yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli ejɔ. Ehaa tsofafeemɔ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do I see eaten leaves on my maize field, but I cannot find any insects on the plants during the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa akɛ miiye baai yɛ mi-ŋma ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Shi shwane mli lɛ, anaaa kooloi bibii komɛi?

english: Many crop pests, such as fall armyworms, hide deep inside the plant stalk or in the soil during the hot afternoon to escape the sun. They only crawl out to feed late in the evening and early in the morning when temperatures drop.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui srɔtoi babaoo tamɔ cutworms Hiɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei ashishifãi amli shɔŋŋ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni amɛjo hulu lɛ naa foi. Amɛfoɔ kɛyaa kɛbaa koni amɛyatao niyenii yɛ gbɛkɛ kɛ leebi maŋkpa pɛ beni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves droop during the hot afternoon but look fresh and active again in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, shi amɛnáa hewalɛ ekoŋŋ kɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ leebi lɛ?

english: Cassava leaves droop or fold during hot sunny hours as a defense mechanism to reduce water loss. Once the sun sets and the air cools, the plant restores its moisture levels overnight and looks fresh by morning.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ shi loo efoɔ ehe yɛ hulutsoo be mli akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ naa. Kɛ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baaku sɛɛ ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba nyɔɔŋ kome mli ni ebaafee tamɔ nɔ ni ehe ejɔ lɛ leebi.

english: Young cocoa trees are soft and burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa kookoo bibii lɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Fertilizers need moisture to dissolve so that plant roots can drink them in. When placed in dry soil, the concentrated fertilizer chemicals cannot move and can actually burn and damage the plant roots.
ga: Fɛ̃i he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anu. Kɛ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji lɛ mli lɛ tsiii ehe ni ebaanyɛ eshã ni efite tsei shishifãi.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. When nitrogen is low, the plant takes whatever nitrogen it has left from the older bottom leaves and sends it to keep the growing top leaves green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji nitrogen lɛ faaa lɛ Tsei lɛ jieɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli ni amɛkɛmajeɔ koni ŋwɛi baai ni miida lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the weather gets too hot or when the soil goes dry for too long. Severe heat or water stress stops pollination, causing the plant to drop its flowers to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu mli haomɔ haa pollination kpaɔ. Enɛ haa tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my pepper fruits develop dark, rotten spots at the bottom before they are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper aduawai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋŋ ni egboi yɛ amɛshishi dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: Rotten spots on the bottom of peppers, called blossom-end rot, happen when the plant lacks calcium or receives irregular watering while the fruit is growing rapidly.
ga: Atsɛɔ hei ni egbo yɛ ŋmeii ashishi lɛ akɛ blossom end rot. Ebaa kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ calcium loo afɔ lɛ nu be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida oya lɛ.

english: Why is it better for me to water my garden vegetables in the morning rather than during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ nu woɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli babaoo leebi fe shwane lɛ?

english: Watering in the morning gives the soil time to soak up moisture before the heat of the day. Watering in the afternoon heat causes most of the water to evaporate instantly into the air before the roots can take it up.
ga: Nu ni afɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa be ni ekɛŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani gbi lɛ mli latsaa lɛ baa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa nu lɛ fa ko shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my food crops right after the heavy rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe miniyenii ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, strong plants with roots that are naturally adapted to grab water and soil nutrients much faster than farm crops, allowing them to shoot up rapidly as soon as rain falls.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa. Amɛyɛ shishifãi ni nyɛɔ amɛjieɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Enɛ haa kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ pɛ kɛkɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade to protect them from direct sunlight and heat while their roots develop. Leaving some large shade trees or planting plantains around them keeps the soil cool and moist so the cocoa can survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ biɔ hulutsoo be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ. Tsei wuji ni ashiɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo loo plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ bɔni afee ni kookoo lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, steal water and nutrients from the main tree. Pruning them away leaves only the strongest shoot, ensuring your plantain tree produces large, healthy bunches of fruit.
ga: Tso lɛ mli ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ, tsei lɛ ahe tsei ni wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ baashi. Enɛ baaha o-plantains lɛ awo yibii wuji ni mli wa.

english: Why do my tomatoes rot so quickly when I transport them in wooden crates from Kumasi to Accra?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ fiteɔ oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ mikɛwo tso adekai amli kɛjɛ Kumasi kɛtee Accra lɛ?

english: Tomatoes produce a natural ripening gas that gets trapped inside tightly packed, unventilated wooden crates. Heat during long truck journeys speeds up this process, causing them to soften and rot quickly.
ga: Tomatoi jieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa mɔ shwereɔ ni shwieɔ tso adekai ni akɛwo mli shiŋŋ ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli lɛ kpo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Dɔlɛ ni yɔɔ lɔle gbɛfaa kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ haa nifeemɔ nɛɛ yaa oya. Enɛ haa tsɔne lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni efiteɔ oya.

english: Why do my harvested yams rot faster when I stack them directly on the bare ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ mikɛwo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Bare ground holds dampness and heat, which encourages fungi and bacteria to enter the skin of the yam. Storing yams on raised wooden racks allows air to circulate around them and keep them dry.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ dɔlɛ mli. Enɛ woɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helatsɛmɛi ahewalɛ koni amɛbote sweet potato lɛ hewolo mli. Kɛ́ akɛ sweet potato to tso ni awo nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ amɛhe. Atomɔ ni ŋɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape down the center?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni V su yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves in a V-shape are a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Maize plants need nitrogen to stay green and grow, so adding poultry manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help restore their green color.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tamɔ V lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ kooloi ashishifã loo nitrogen ŋtayaa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small and woody even after growing for over a year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛji tsei nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ adu amɛ nɔ ni fe afi moŋ?

english: Cassava roots remain thin and woody if the soil is too hard and compacted for the roots to expand, or if the soil lacks nutrients like potassium which help the plant store starch in the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ baakã he ahi shi mlɛo ni amɛfee tsei kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa ni ebɔle ehe tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã. Aloo kɛji akɛ niyenii tamɔ potassium, ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ starch toɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off before growing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani midu amɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they experience extreme heat or dry soil. The plant sheds its flowers to save energy and moisture until growing conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛyashɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Plants shed their flowers to conserve energy and moisture until growing conditions improve.

english: How do I know when my cassava crop is fully ready for harvesting under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-cassava tsei lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is usually ready to harvest when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the plant starts cracking as the tubers expand below.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. and the soil around the base of the plant begins to crack as the bulb expands below.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the inner leaves of my young corn plants overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ye mi ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli baai lɛ nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely fall armyworms. They hide inside the tight center whorl of the corn plant during the hot day and crawl out to feed on tender leaves at night or early morning.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛgbee asraafoi ŋmeii amli. Amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋtayaai amli yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. ni amɛfoɔ kɛyaa koni amɛyaye baai bibii gbɛkɛ loo leebi maŋkpa

english: Why do my maize seeds rot in the ground when I plant right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni midu amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The very first rain often heats up the dry soil without providing lasting moisture. If no rain follows immediately, seeds get trapped in warm, damp earth and rot before they can sprout.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli dɔɔ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni hiɔ shi daa haaa. Kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ efo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ nɔ. ni amɛgboi dani amɛdara.

english: Cocoa flowers must be pollinated—transferring tiny pollen grains from flower to flower—before a pod can form. In nature, tiny insects called midges do this, but if there aren't enough insects, most flowers drop off without growing into pods.
ga: Esa akɛ afee cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛtsɔ pollen ŋmeii bibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko mli lɛ nɔ Dani abaanyɛ afee pods yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ midges lɛ feɔ enɛ. Shi kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii babaoo bɛ lɛ Fɔfɔi babaoo shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: What is hand pollination, and how does it help my cocoa tree produce more pods?
ga: Mɛni ji nine nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ eyeɔ ebuaa cacao tso lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii babaoo?

english: Hand pollination is when you manually move pollen from one cocoa flower to another using small tools or brushes. Because natural insects don't visit every flower, doing this by hand ensures far more flowers get fertilized, resulting in many more pods on each tree.
ga: Nine nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ji be mli ni okɛ onine jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ kookoo fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ kɛtsɔ dɛŋdade bibioo loo brɔsh nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, adebɔɔ mli kooloi bibii eyasaraaa fɔfɔi fɛɛ fɔfɔi. Enɛ ni akɛ niji baafee lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ fɔfɔi babaoo baawo fɔmɔ nii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso fɛɛ tso yɛ ŋmeii babaoo.

english: How long does it take for a cocoa flower to grow into a fully mature pod ready for harvest?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni eda ni amɛfeɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ?

english: After a cocoa flower is successfully pollinated, it takes about five to six months for it to grow, swell, and change color into a fully mature pod ready to be harvested.
ga: Beni agbe kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ anaa jogbaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ, eheɔ aaafee nyɔji 5-6 dani kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ daa, amɛwoɔ, ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe su ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni eda ni asaa he kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Why is it important for me to prune or cut extra branches off my cocoa trees regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ loo majie niji krokomɛi ni fata mi-kookoo tso lɛ he lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Pruning lets sunlight and fresh air reach all parts of the tree, which lowers moisture levels that cause fungal diseases and encourages the tree to direct its energy into growing bigger, healthier pods.
ga: Tso lɛ mlifomɔ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shɛɔ tso lɛ hei fɛɛ. Enɛ haa hulutsoo ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa lɛ baa shi. ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ lɛ awo ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: How does clearing weeds around my cocoa trees help them yield more cocoa?
ga: Jwɛi ni ebɔle mi lɛ ajiemɔ Te mi-cacao tsei lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni mi-cacao lɛ aya hiɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your cocoa trees for water, sunlight, and nutrients in the soil. Clearing them gives your trees full access to food and moisture, helping them grow stronger and yield more pods.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ kookoo tsei yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ojie otsei lɛ, ebaaha otsei lɛ aná niyenii kɛ nu babaoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehaa ehe waa ni ewoɔ ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Why shouldn't I leave diseased pods or dead branches on the ground after clearing my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishiɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ loo tsei niji ni egboi yɛ shikpɔŋ beni mijie ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dead branches and infected pods carry fungi and pests. Leaving them on the soil allows diseases like black pod to survive and splash back onto healthy trees when it rains.
ga: Niji ni egboi kɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui. Kɛ́ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ hiɔ shi. ni ekɛ ehe shwieɔ tsei ni wa anɔ ekoŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ.

english: This is typically caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in dark, overly damp environments. Keeping your farm well-pruned to let in sunlight and removing infected pods helps stop the rot from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni edɔ tsɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ. Ehe miihia ni okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ koni hulu la ashɛ nɔ, ni ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Ebaaye ebua ni akpa hela ni fiteɔ nii lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Why do the flowers on my cocoa trees suddenly dry up and die during rainy weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Excessive rain and heavy shade can create high humidity, leading to fungal attack on delicate cocoa flowers. Ensuring proper airflow through pruning helps keep flowers dry and healthy.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo kɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa baanyɛ aha hulutsoo be babaoo aba. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kookoo fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛtsɔ tsei ni afoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: Why should I add fertilizer to my cocoa farm if my trees already look green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mi-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji akɛ mitsei lɛ efee ŋmɔji momo?

english: Green leaves mean the tree is alive, but producing heavy pods drains huge amounts of nutrients from the soil over time. Fertilizer replaces those lost nutrients so the tree has enough strength to produce heavy yields year after year.
ga: Baai eŋɔli tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo. Shi ŋmeii ni tsii ni yɔɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli yɛ be ni sa mli. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ niyenii ni elaaje lɛ najiaŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ he wa bɔ ni sa ni ewoɔ nikpamɔ babaoo daa afi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees lose their leaves and stop fruiting during severe dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa yibiiwoo yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves during hot, dry spells to reduce water loss and protect themselves from dying of thirst. Keeping shade trees on the farm helps keep the soil moist and protects cocoa trees from intense heat.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ. Koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni obu ohe kɛjɛ kumai he. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ akwɛmɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa he.

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves and shallow roots that burn quickly in harsh sunlight. They need partial shade from nurse crops like plantain or shade trees to retain soil moisture and stay cool while establishing their roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be ko kɛjɛ nurse tsei tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eha edɔ be mli ni amaa shishifãi lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips, mites, or aphids that feed on the leaf sap and sometimes transmit viruses, which makes the plant leaves twist and stop growing properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ thrips, mites loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Amɛyeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni bei komɛi lɛ amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ amɛshwãa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaaa eda jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, an essential food for plant growth. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen out of the soil, or the soil itself may just be exhausted from repeated planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo ekolɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ kɛjɛ dumɔ ni aduɔ shii abɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why is it wrong for me to spread dry fertilizer on my crops when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ejaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi baawo miŋmɔshi nibii amli be mli ni mikɛfeee nakai lɛ? Ani shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa?

english: Crops cannot drink dry fertilizer through their roots. Fertilizer needs water to dissolve into liquid food, and if it stays dry on hot soil, it concentrated chemicals that can burn and damage the roots.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nyɛŋ anu ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi kɛtsɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛtsɔ nu mli. Ni kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbi lolo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tsofai ni mli wa ni baanyɛ aŋɔ la ni efite shishifãi lɛ baafata he.

english: Why do my crops grow weaker and produce less harvest if I plant maize on the exact same plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly drains the same specific nutrients out of the soil every season without giving the land time to rebuild, while also allowing crop-specific pests and diseases to multiply in the field.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shii abɔ daa be mli ni ehaaa jɛmɛ be ni ekɛma ekoŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, aŋmɛɔ tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo gbɛ ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why am I finding small caterpillars eating holes inside the green central leaves of my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ bu yɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ baai eŋɔlii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, moths that lay eggs on maize leaves. Once hatched, the young caterpillars crawl inside the warm, moist center whorl of the plant to feed safely on the soft young leaves.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni woɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmãa baa nɔ. Beni ŋmei lɛ fɔɔ lɛ ŋmei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛboteɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmei ni mli edɔ ni edɔ lɛ mli koni amɛye baai bibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Cassava roots rot underground when the soil holds too much standing water or has poor drainage, causing root-rot fungi to thrive and starve the tubers of air.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu ni damɔ shi babaoo loo nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shishifãi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ daa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why should I prune away some of the small suckers growing around my plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ Plantain tsei lɛ ahe lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjeɔ kpo.

english: Plantain suckers compete directly with the main mother plant for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Removing excess suckers allows the main plant to focus all its energy into growing a bigger bunch of plantains.
ga: Dumɔwui kɛ fɔlɔ tso lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ dumɔwui wuji ni amɛkwɛɔ lɛ ahe nii.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant suffers from sudden heat stress, extremely high temperatures, or erratic watering, which prevents proper pollination from taking place.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na hulutsoo trukaa haomɔ. hulutsoo ni naa wa waa loo nu ni bɛ shiŋŋ Enɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa naa koni ekafee.

english: Why do weeds cause my maize crop to stay small even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi ŋmãa lɛ feɔ bibioo eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds act as silent thieves in your farm. They grow much faster than maize and steal the soil nutrients, sunlight, and root space that your crops need to mature.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi ni efee dioo yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛdaraa oya kwraa fe ŋmãa ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, hulu la, kɛ shishifãi ni he hiaa ni otsei lɛ adara lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa plants do not have deep root systems yet to reach underground water, and direct sunlight burns their leaves. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains protects young cocoa from heat stress until their roots fully establish.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni shɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lolo. Ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha baai lɛ ashã. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains lɛ, ebaabu kookoo bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baaje shishi.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my young maize crop turning yellow before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, a vital nutrient plants need to grow green and strong. Applying a nitrogen fertilizer like urea at the right growth stage helps restore leaf color and improves your yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Enɛɛmɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ baaye abua ni eha baai lɛ ahe afee fɛo ekoŋŋ ni eha yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do I see small holes in my maize leaves and tiny caterpillars hidden inside the stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni akɛtee tso lɛ mli lɛ amli

english: This damage is caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm, which feed on leaves and young shoots. Inspecting your farm early and applying recommended biological or safe chemical controls when larvae are small stops them from destroying your harvest.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni yeɔ tsei ahe baai kɛ tsei bibii. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra ni okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛbuɔ he lɛ atsu nii beni ŋmeii lɛ daraaa lɛ. Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite onibii ni oduɔ lɛ.

english: Why do elders recommend that I plant cowpea or groundnuts on the same plot where I harvested maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ onukpai lɛ wo ŋaa akɛ adu tsina loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni akpaa ŋmãa yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. Rotating them with maize naturally feeds the soil, reducing the amount of expensive fertilizer you need for the next season.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Abɛi ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa ni he hiaa bo kɛha be ni baa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting underground and smelling bad before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when rainwater collects around them in flat or compacted soil, causing fungal infections. Planting cassava on raised ridges or mounds allows excess water to drain away and keeps the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nugbɔ nu buaa amɛhe naa lɛ. amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse loo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. cause fungal infection Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli ni eye ebua ni ewaje shishifãi lɛ.

english: Yam plants produce larger tubers when their leaves receive direct sunlight to make plant food. Staking keeps the vines off the wet ground, maximizing sunlight exposure and preventing leaves from rotting or catching soil-borne diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji kɛji amɛbaai lɛ ná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛha tso lɛ niyenii. Staking baaha wain tsei lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Na hulu la babaoo ni otsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite loo helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ akamɔ amɛ

english: Tomato flowers drop off when plants suffer from extreme heat or lack of regular water, which prevents successful pollination. Keeping the soil consistently moist around the base of the plant helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa loo nu ni faaa yɛ emli daa lɛ hewɔ. ni tsiɔ pollination ni yeɔ omanye lɛ naa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha ebɔle ehe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ Shishitoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why is it harmful to burn all the weeds and cleared brush on my land before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mashã jwɛi lɛ fɛɛ ni majie tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ dani adu nii lɛ?

english: Burning destroys valuable organic matter, kills helpful earthworms, and leaves the topsoil vulnerable to washing away in heavy rains. Leaving cleared plant waste to rot turns it into rich natural compost that nourishes your crops.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni jara wa ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ. Gbemɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ woɔ oshara mli akɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaho. Ha tso mli jwɛi ni ajie lɛ lɛ agbo. Enɛ haa efeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli ni haa onibii lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why should I spray pesticide early in the morning or late in the evening instead of afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ anɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ moŋ fe shwane?

english: Hot afternoon heat causes liquid spray to dry up before plants absorb it, and intense sun mixed with chemicals can scorch plant leaves. Cooler morning or evening temperatures allow crops to safely absorb treatments effectively.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ mli latsaa lɛ haa nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ dani tso lɛ nyɛɔ eŋɔ. Ni hulu la ni naa wa ni akɛ tsofai efutu mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei ahe baai lɛ ashã. He ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ tsofa ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and preventing the plant from growing tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies or mites that carry plant viruses. Spraying plants early with neem oil or organic insecticidal soap controls these pests before they stunt growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo mites ni hiɛɔ helai ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Akɛ neem fɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ baashwie tsei anɔ mra. Eyeɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ dani amɛtsiɔ dalɛ naa.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil, or the ground has too much water which suffocates the roots. Adding compost or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK helps restore the green color and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ NPK fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants have very large stems and leaves but tiny roots under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai wuji waa shi shishifãi bibii yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or water, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing big leaves above ground instead of storing food in the underground tubers. Adding potassium to the soil encourages tuber growth.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo nu babaoo Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ niyenii baato shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ ŋmei lɛ mli lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ potassium wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ daa.

english: Maize uses up a lot of nutrients from the soil. Beans and cowpeas naturally trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots, which restores fertility for your next crop without needing extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Peas kɛ cowpeas lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ fɔmɔ aba onibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli ekoŋŋ ni tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Why is it important for me to plant my seeds at specific measured distances instead of spreading them randomly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu midumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko pɔtɛɛ ni abaanyɛ asusu he lɛ? Yɛ dumɔwui ni aduɔ trukaa lɛ najiaŋ?

english: Planting seeds too close together makes crops fight with each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, making them thin and weak. Proper spacing ensures each crop gets enough space and nutrients to produce big fruits or tubers.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo yibii loo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds around my crops when they are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe be mli ni amɛji bibii kwraa lolo lɛ?

english: Young crops have soft, weak roots that cannot compete with fast-growing weeds. Weeds steal the water, sunlight, and nutrients meant for your young plants, which can stunt their growth completely.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ bibii yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni nyɛŋ ekɛ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ ashi akaŋ. Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii kɛhaa otsei bibii lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ atsĩ dalɛ naa kwraa.

english: How can I tell if my soil has enough moisture before I plant my maize seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa dani madu ŋmãa dumɔwui?

english: Squeeze a handful of topsoil in your palm; if it forms a ball that stays together without dripping water, the moisture is just right for seeds to sprout. If it crumbles completely dry or drips water, it is either too dry or waterlogged.
ga: Mimɔ shikpɔŋ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ fioo ko mli yɛ onine mli. Kɛji efee bɔɔlu ni kpɛtɛɔ he ni nu shwieee shi. The humidity is just right for the seeds to germinate. If it is completely dry or dripping water Indicates that it is too dry or waterlogged.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures are too high, when water supply is irregular, or when there is a lack of calcium in the soil. Maintaining regular watering and mulching the soil helps keep flowers attached.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. When the water supply is uneven or when the soil lacks calcium Regular watering and mulching help keep the flowers stuck.

english: Black cocoa pods are caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungus that spreads quickly in cold, wet weather when there is too much shade. Pruning overhead tree branches lets sunlight in and keeps the pods dry to prevent the disease.
ga: Black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ cocoa ŋmɔtɔ diŋ lɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ fɛ̃i kɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛ́ hulutsoo be babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ. Niji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ni afolɔ koni hulu la abote mli ni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbi koni hela akamɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my yam leaves turn brown and dry up at the end of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ afi lɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally turn brown and dry up when the plant has finished storing energy into the underground tuber. It is a natural behavior showing that the yam is mature and ready for harvesting.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ baatsɔ blɔfo ni amɛbaagbi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji tso lɛ egbe hewalɛ ni ekɛtoɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ naa. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli subaŋ ko ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii edara ni esa akɛ akpa.

english: Why do insects attack my cowpea flowers as soon as they start blooming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi-cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛfɔ̃ pɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers produce sweet nectar and soft young pods that attract sap-sucking pests like thrips and pod borers. Protecting the crops right when flowering begins prevents insects from destroying your yield.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔii lɛ woɔ nu kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni gbalaa ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips kɛ pod borers lɛ. Kɛ́ obu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛji amɛbɔi fɔmɔ pɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kooloi akafite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: The main plantain stem acts like a parent feeding all the young shoots attached to its roots. If too many shoots are left to grow at once, they drain all the nutrients and water, leaving the main plant exhausted and producing small bunches or dying early.
ga: Plantain tso lɛ tso titri lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ fɔlɔ, ni eyeɔ ŋmeii bibii fɛɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpɛtɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ niyenii. Kɛji akɛ ashi ŋmeii babaoo yɛ be kome mli lɛ Niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu fɛɛ baaho. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso titri lɛ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe ni ŋmeii lɛ mli gbalaa kɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii loo amɛgboiɔ oya.

english: Why do some of the young green pods on my cocoa tree turn black and shrivel up on their own?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbo lɛ?

english: This is often 'cherelle wilt,' which happens when a tree produces more pods than it can feed. If the tree tries to nourish too many pods at once, it becomes overloaded and naturally drops the extra young pods so the main tree does not weaken and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ ‘cherelle wilt’, ni baa kɛji tso lɛ wo ŋmeii babaoo fe bɔ ni ebaanyɛ eye. Kɛji tso lɛ bɔ mɔdɛŋ ni eha ŋmeii babaoo niyenii shikome lɛ, Ebaafee nɔ ni tsii tsɔ ni ebaaha ŋmeii bibii ni eshwɛ lɛ agbo yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Enɛ baatsi tso titri lɛ naa koni ekagbɔjɔ ni egbo.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die if I clear away all the big trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji mijie tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are fragile and cannot survive harsh, direct heat from the sun. Tall shade trees act as a protective cover, keeping the ground cool and moist until the young cocoa roots are strong enough to handle full exposure.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui waaa ni amɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛ kpɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni jɛɔ hulu la mli lɛ naa. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ni buɔ mɔ he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo shishifãi bibii lɛ baaná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná la ni fa.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce very small fruits when I let all the extra side branches grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitato tso lɛ woɔ yibii bibii waa beni mihaa niji ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: When a tomato plant grows too many side shoots, it splits its food and water among all those stems. The plant becomes overburdened trying to support too much growth, resulting in tiny, poor-quality tomatoes.
ga: Kɛji tomato tso ko yɛ sɛɛ ŋmeii babaoo tsɔ Ebaagbala niyenii kɛ nu fɛɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi. Akɛ jatsu tsii fe nine ni miitao ni amɛye amɛbua dalɛ ni fe nine. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tomatoi lɛ daraaa, ni amɛhe ehiaaa.

english: Why does the Striga weed make my maize plants turn yellow and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Striga jwɛi lɛ miiha mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Striga is a parasitic weed that attaches itself directly to the roots of your maize. It cannot feed itself, so it steals all the water and fertilizer from the maize plant, effectively starving the crop until it dies.
ga: Striga ji jwɛi ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni kɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ ŋmãa shishifãi ahe tɛ̃ɛ. Enyɛŋ eye ehe niyenii. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛju nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ abele tsei lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Can I attach a branch from a sweet orange tree onto any wild tree trunk in the bush to get sweet oranges?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ tso ni ŋɔɔ ni ji ŋmei tso lɛ nine akpɛtɛ koo mli tso ko ni yɔɔ koo mli lɛ shishi koni maná ŋmei ni ŋɔɔ?

english: No, trees will only support branches from closely related varieties. A wild tree of a completely different family will reject the sweet orange branch and refuse to pass water and nutrients to it, causing the branch to dry up and die.
ga: Dabi, tso lɛ baafi niji ni jɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ kpaakpa lɛ amli pɛ sɛɛ. Koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ weku kroko kwraa mli lɛ baakpoo ŋmei ni ŋɔɔ ni amɛŋmɛŋ gbɛ ni nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ abote mli. Ehaa tsei niji lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I drop four or five maize seeds into the same planting hole to get more corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ejwɛ loo enumɔ woɔ ŋmãa bu kome mli koni maná ŋmãa babaoo?

english: Putting too many seeds in one hole forces the growing plants to compete aggressively for the same tiny spot of soil water and manure. Instead of getting more corn, all the plants remain thin, weak, and produce small or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui babaoo wo bu kome mli lɛ, ebaaha tsei ni miida lɛ abɔi shikpɔŋ nɔ nu kɛ ŋmeii bibii ahe akaŋ waa. yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni aaaná ŋmãa babaoo Tsei fɛɛ hiɔ shi ni amɛhe waaa, amɛhe waaa ni amɛwoɔ ŋmãa bibii. loo nɔ ko bɛ mli

english: Why does my land produce smaller cassava tubers every year if I plant it on the same plot without resting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmeii bibii daa afi kɛji midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni mikɛ amɛ ejɔɔɔ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Cassava pulls heavy amounts of food out of the soil to grow its tubers. Repeating this every year without giving the soil fertilizer or rest completely drains the earth, leaving no nutrients for the next generation of crops to grow well.
ga: Cassava gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃. Kɛ́ ofee enɛ daa afi ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli loo okɛ ohe ejɔɔɔ mli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ atsɔ nu kwraa. No hewɔ lɛ, niyenii kpakpa ko eshwɛɛɛ ni baaha tsei ni baa lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt and drop leaves right after I move them from the nursery bed to the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛbaai lɛ sɛɛ foɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli tsei lɛ amli kɛtee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Moving a young plant damages its tiny root hairs, making it temporarily unable to drink water. This 'transplant shock' puts severe stress on the plant until it grows new roots to handle the tougher conditions of the open field.
ga: Tso bibioo lɛ ni oootsi lɛ baaha yitsɔi bibii lɛ adara. Efite Enyɛŋ enu nu yɛ be kukuoo mli Nɛkɛ ‘tso ni atsakeɔ lɛ he gbeyeishemɔ’ nɛɛ kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa baa tso lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shishifãi heei daa koni amɛnyɛ amɛkpee shihilɛi ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ ni agbele naa lɛ mli lɛ naa.

english: If I harvest maize from high-yielding store-bought seeds, why do the seeds saved from that harvest perform poorly next season?
ga: Kɛji mikpa ŋmãa kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni ahe yɛ shwapo mli lɛ amli lɛ, Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ nakai ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Store-bought hybrid seeds are specially bred for a single planting. The seeds produced by those crops lose their original strength and uniformity, leading to weaker plants and much lower yields if planted again.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni akɛdu shikome pɛ. Dumɔwui ni tsei nɛɛ woɔ lɛ laajeɔ amɛshishijee hewalɛ kɛ bɔ ni amɛyɔɔ daa lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, ni kɛji akɛ adu ekoŋŋ lɛ, yibiiwoo ni baa lɛ baa shi kwraa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turning brown and dying in the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are like human infants—their leaves burn easily under direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains planted next to them to act as living umbrellas and retain soil moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ adesai abifabii. Amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ tsei bibii ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Koni etsu nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baaná hewalɛ.

english: Why should I clear away the extra small shoots growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Krɛdɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛbɔleɔ Mi dumɔwui lɛ ashishitoo lɛ etee.

english: When too many young shoots grow around one main plantain stem, they fight over the food and water in the soil. Removing extra shoots leaves only one or two strong ones, which helps the main tree produce larger fruit bunches.
