ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii bibii babaoo dara yɛ tso wulu kome he lɛ Ebaatswa niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ, niji kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ shwɛɔ, ni no yeɔ ebuaa tso titri lɛ ni ewoɔ aduawai wuji ni mli eyi obɔ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in a shape like an arrow tip?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ tamɔ akpɔlɔi ashishifãi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the tips are a clear sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, which maize needs to stay green and grow fast. Adding manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer restores their health.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. The corn must remain green and grow quickly. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help restore their health.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts on my plot help my maize grow better next season?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmãa lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts and beans have tiny living helpers on their roots that capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground. When you harvest them, that natural fertilizer stays in the soil to feed your next crop.
ga: Akpɔlɔi kɛ ŋmeii yɛ yelikɛbualɔi bibii ni hiɛ ka yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji okpa amɛ Nakai adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot under the ground when we get too much heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain leaves standing water around the roots for days, the roots choke, and soil rot fungi quickly attack and destroy the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu shwieɔ he fɛɛ he. shishifãi lɛ gbii babaoo Shishifãi lɛ baatsi ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baatutua ŋmeii lɛ oya ni amɛbaakpãtã amɛhiɛ.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make energy for expanding the tubers underground. Lifting the vines up on stakes helps leaves catch maximum light and keeps them off wet soil where diseases spread.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ ni haa ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ aba. Kɛ́ awó wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ náa la babaoo, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi, he ni helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã lɛ.

english: Why do the yellow flowers on my tomato plants fall off without forming any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛfeee tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop off when the plant suffers from extreme heat or sudden dryness. The plant discards its flowers to save water and protect its own survival during stressful conditions.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ mli edɔ waa loo egbi trukaa. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala he yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli.

english: Why are the fresh leaves of my pepper plants curling up tightly into little cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tso lɛ baai heei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛfeɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap from fresh leaves, or by a leaf virus spread by these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai heei amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli ni nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli lɛ mli.

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by weeks of dry heat before real rains begin. Seeds planted too early will sprout but quickly dry up and die before the regular rainy season starts.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ otsii babaoo ni mli edɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi. Dumɔwui ni adu mra tsɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ shi amɛbaagbi oya ni amɛbaagboi dani nugbɔ be ni baa daa lɛ aje shishi.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops even when I do not apply fertilizer to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ? Ni mikɛ fertilizer wooo mli?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted over thousands of years to survive in harsh conditions. They aggressively pull water and nutrients out of the soil faster than cultivated crops can.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ yɛ afii akpei abɔ ni eho lɛ amli koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Amɛgbalaa nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe bɔ ni tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee.

english: Why is it good for me to plant beans or groundnuts alongside my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa adu ŋmãa loo ŋmãa?

english: Beans and groundnuts naturally grab nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. Planting them with maize helps feed the soil naturally so your maize grows stronger without needing as much expensive fertilizer.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. Abele ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. O-corn lɛ baafee nɔ ni wa ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa awo mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is low on nitrogen, which plants need to stay green and healthy. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer early will help the leaves turn green and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehe hiaa ni tsei lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii afata he mra Ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ni eha amɛdaramɔ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my groundnut pods come out empty without nuts inside when I harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut pods lɛ jeɔ kpo efolo ni ŋmeii bɛ mli kɛ́ mikpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Empty groundnut pods, often called pops, happen when the soil lacks calcium while the seeds are forming inside the soil. Spreading wood ash or lime on the farm helps the pods fill out properly.
ga: Peanut pods ni bɛ nɔ ko, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ pops lɛ baa kɛji akɛ calcium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui miifee yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Tso sũ loo lime ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ ayi obɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad for me to plant cassava on the same plot of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the exact same crop on the same spot every year drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases to build up. Rotating crops gives the soil time to recover and breaks disease cycles.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa ŋmeii kɛ helai bua amɛhe naa. Nibii ni aduɔ ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa be ni ekɛbaatsa ehe ni efoɔ helai ni baa lɛ amli.

english: Black pods are caused by a fungal disease that spreads quickly in wet, dark conditions. Pruning extra shade branches to let air and sunlight in, and picking off infected pods early, stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ duŋ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ black pods baa. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofo tsei niji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo lɛ amli koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la aba mli. kɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Leaf curling is caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the plant's juices and spreading plant viruses. Clearing weeds around the plot and applying neem oil or appropriate insect sprays helps control them.
ga: Kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Emuɔ tsei amli nu ni egbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa tsei amli. Jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni sa ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ jwɛi lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground when the rains are heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water stays trapped in the soil around them for too long. Planting your cassava on raised earth mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my seeds after the long dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the main rainy season has truly set in and the ground has received two or three deep rains. Planting after the very first light rain can cause seeds to germinate and then dry up if rain stops.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ baashɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Ni shikpɔŋ lɛ baaná nugbɔ ni naa wa aaafee shii 2-3. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the air gets too hot or when the plants get uneven amounts of water. Keeping the soil constantly moist with mulch around the plant base helps prevent flowers from falling off.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ afɔɔɔ tsei lɛ nu jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ akagbee shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf yellowing can happen if your soil is low on essential nutrients like nitrogen, or if small pests are sucking the juice and energy out of the leaves.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ aba kɛji akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ nu kɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baa lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if my plant is suffering from poor soil or an attack by insects?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mitso lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii loo kooloi bibii miitutua lɛ?

english: Poor soil usually makes the whole plant grow slowly and look pale all over, whereas insect attacks often leave visible bugs, sticky residue, holes, or spots on individual leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ haa tsei lɛ daa blɛoo ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he. Beni kooloi bibii lɛ tutuaa lɛ, bei pii lɛ amɛshiɔ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi, bu ni anaa loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai aŋkroaŋkroi anɔ lɛ.

english: How often should I inspect my crop field to catch health problems early?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ makwɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mana helatsamɔ mli naagbai mra?

english: You should walk through your farm and inspect plants closely at least twice a week, checking under the leaves and around the stems where early signs of pests or disease hide.
ga: Esa akɛ otsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni okwɛ tsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ hoo lɛ shii enyɔ yɛ otsi mli. Kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ashishi kɛ ehewɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ nɔ. Tsoi ni yɔɔ mra be mli tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai ahe okadii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ

english: What are these tiny white insects hiding underneath my crop leaves?
ga: Mɛni ji nɛkɛ kooloi bibii yɛŋ nɛɛ ni kɛ amɛhe ewo mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ ashishi?

english: Those are usually sap-sucking pests like whiteflies or mealybugs that gather under leaves to feed on plant juices and hide from rain and direct sunlight.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛɛmɛi ji kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo mealybugs ni buaa amɛhe naa yɛ baai lɛ ashishi koni amɛye tso lɛ mli nu. ni akɛtee nugbɔ kɛ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he.

english: Why do small white bugs make my crop leaves dry up and turn yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii yɛŋ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: These insects drain the plant's food and water reserves through constant feeding, which starves the leaf until it turns yellow, dries out, and eventually falls off.
ga: Nɛkɛ koolooi nɛɛ shwieɔ tso lɛ niyenii kɛ nu kɛtsɔ niyenii ni amɛyeɔ daa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ baai lɛ aahu kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛgbiɔ, ni yɛ naagbee lɛ amɛgbeeɔ shi.

english: Can small insects on just a few crops spread to my whole farm?
ga: Ani kooloo bibioo ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo komɛi pɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: Yes, pests like whiteflies reproduce quickly and can fly or be carried by the wind to neighboring healthy crops if you do not control them early.
ga: Hɛɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ whiteflies lɛ fɔɔ oya ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛfo loo kɔɔyɔɔ aŋɔ amɛ kɛya ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ okudɔɔɔ amɛ mra lɛ,.

english: What simple step can I take to remove unknown bugs from my plants without buying expensive chemicals right away?
ga: Nɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo Te mafee tɛŋŋ majie kooloi bibii ni aleee kɛjɛ mitsei lɛ amli ni miheee tsofai ni jara wa amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: You can spray a mixture of mild soap and water or neem leaf extract directly onto the bugs to suffocate them without harming the crop or spending a lot of money.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ samla ni mli ejɔ afutu nɔ. kɛ nu loo neem baa mli nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ kooloo lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛmu ni efiteee ŋmɔshi nibii loo efiteee shika babaoo.

english: What causes my farm soil to lose its fertility over time?
ga: Mɛni haa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ?

english: Planting crops repeatedly on the same land without adding compost, manure, or fertilizers drains the soil of its natural food, leaving crops weak and vulnerable.
ga: dumɔ ni afɔɔ feemɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ nɔŋŋ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baaná niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa lɛ baa.

english: How does poor soil make my crops more likely to get damaged by pests?
ga: Te shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ baanyɛ aha tsɛŋemɔ helai afite miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Just like a person who does not eat well gets sick easily, crops growing in poor soil become too weak to defend themselves against pest attacks.
ga: Taakɛ mɛi ni yeee nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaná hela oya lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: How can I make my soil healthy again so my crops stay dark green?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ koni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli?

english: Adding well-rotted animal manure, compost, or balanced fertilizers returns vital nutrients to the earth, helping crops grow strong, green leaves that resist stress.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ hewalɛ, baai eŋɔli ni teɔ shi woɔ nɔnyɛɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen away from the roots, or the soil may simply be tired, so applying nitrogen fertilizer or compost helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Aloo ekolɛ sũ lɛ etɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it better to space my cassava stems far apart instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ajie ŋmei tsei kɛjɛ amɛhe lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need space underground to expand and store starch. When planted too close together, the stems compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin, small roots instead of large, heavy tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi he ko he miihia cassava shishifãi koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛkɛ starch ato. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ kɛ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Enɛ haa shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo baa yɛ bulb agbo ni tsii najiaŋ.

english: Why am I finding small worms eating the inside funnel of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ mi-ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ?

english: These worms are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that targets the soft, growing leaves inside the central funnel of young corn. Catching them early with recommended biopesticides or localized ash/soapy water applications prevents them from destroying the growing point.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni kwɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ anɔ ni edaa yɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋgbɛ faa lɛ mli. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni awieɔ he akɛ akɛbaatsu nii loo sũ/samla nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ he lɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Every crop pulls specific nutrients out of the ground. Planting the same crop on the same spot continuously drains those specific nutrients faster than the soil can rebuild them, leading to poorer soil and lower yields each season.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fɛɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome be fɛɛ be lɛ haa nakai niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ afee ehee ekoŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ ni yibiiwoo baa shi yɛ be fɛɛ mli.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into natural food for the soil. Once harvested, the leftover roots and leaves enrich the soil for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ehaa efeɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ. Kɛji akpa Shishifãi kɛ baai ni eshwɛ lɛ baaye abua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha dumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do hybrid seeds bought from agricultural shops yield better than seeds I save from my own harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni akɛ tsofai ebɔ he ni aheɔ yɛ okwaayeli shwapoi amli lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai fe dumɔwui ni mikɛtoɔ kɛjɛɔ mi diɛŋtsɛ mikpamɔ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially cross-bred to give high yields and disease resistance in their first generation. Seeds saved from that harvest lose those special traits in the next planting season, producing weaker and less predictable plants.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ nakai nibii krɛdɛɛi lɛ yɛ shweremɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni anyɛɛɛ atsɔɔ nɔ ni baaba lɛ baa.

english: Why do the blossoms on my tomato plants fall off without forming fruits during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat causes tomato flowers to dry out, which prevents successful pollination. Without pollination, the plant sheds the dry flowers to conserve its energy until milder temperatures return.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. ni nyɛŋ atsĩ pollination naa Kɛji pollination bɛ Tsei baashwie fɔfɔi ni egbi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛyashi hulutsoo be lɛ mli baajɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do experienced cocoa farmers plant plantain trees next to their young cocoa saplings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ duɔ plantains yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ? amɛ kookoo tsei lɛ

english: Young cocoa trees get scorched easily under intense sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce broad leaves that shade young cocoa plants, keeping the soil cool and moist while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and roll inward during the dry afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ shwane mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in dry weather is a natural defense mechanism. By rolling its leaves, the pepper plant reduces the surface area exposed to the hot sun, helping it retain precious moisture inside the leaf.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. kɛtsɔ baai ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ Pepper tsei lɛ baaye abua ni eha he ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ aba shi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nu ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ hiɔ shi

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants adapted to survive in local soils. They have deep seed banks and aggressive root systems ready to absorb moisture instantly, which is why early clearing gives your planted crops a head start.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛhi shi yɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔji anɔ. Amɛyɛ dumɔwui akuu ni mli kwɔ kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni efee klalo akɛ ebaaŋɔ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni kɛ́ otsi oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa kɛtsɔ hiɛ lɛ, ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa sɛɛnamɔ lɛ.

english: Why are tiny green worms eating small holes in the center of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ Koni amɛye bu bibioo ko Yɛ mi ŋmãa tso bibioo lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana. They crawl into the moist inner funnel of young maize leaves to hide from the heat while feeding on the leaves, which can reduce your harvest if not controlled early.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana. Amɛfoɔ amɛhe kɛboteɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ amli gbɛjegbɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ amli koni amɛtee amɛhe kɛjɛ latsaa lɛ he be mli ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha okpamɔ lɛ aba shi kɛji akɛ akudɔɔɔ mra.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up and turn yellow in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually a defensive reaction to heat stress or tiny sucking pests like whiteflies and thrips. The insects drink the plant's sap and spread viruses, causing the leaves to distort and yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies kɛ thrips he. Kplukai nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ amɛshwãa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains close to my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily in full sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide necessary shade and keep the surrounding air humid, helping cocoa seedlings survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa lɛ, ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do I have to make tall mounds of soil before planting my seed yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yam tubers expand straight down under the earth. Creating loose, high soil mounds gives the roots space to grow long and thick without struggling against hard, compacted ground.
ga: Atomɔ ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi. Gɔŋ ni kɛlɛ ni etse ehe lɛ ni afeɔ lɛ haa shishifã lɛ he lɛ daa ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ.

english: Groundnuts are legumes that work with good soil bacteria to pull nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into plant food, leaving richer soil behind for crops like maize or vegetables.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli helai kpakpai tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen gas kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsake lɛ amɛfee tsei aniyenii. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot when water stays on my farm for long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air inside the soil to stay alive. Excess standing water blocks oxygen from reaching the underground tubers, causing them to drown, suffocate, and rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Nu ni damɔ shi babaoo lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa lɛ ayashɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛshwieɔ nu mli, amɛmuɔ, ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers before producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani ewo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they suffer from sudden stress, such as very high midday temperatures, irregular watering, or a lack of key nutrients needed to support fruit development.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛna nɔnyɛɛ trukaa, tamɔ hulutsoo be ni mli wa waa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa kɛha aduawai lɛ adalɛ ni bɛ

english: Why does my plantain farm yield small bunches when many shoots grow around one stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui aŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso kome he lɛ.

english: When too many sucker shoots grow from the same base stem, they steal nutrients, water, and light from each other, leaving less energy for the main plant to build large plantain bunches.
ga: Be mli ni ŋmeii babaoo ni miida kɛmiijɛ tso kome mli lɛ fa babaoo. Amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ la kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Enɛ haaa tso titri lɛ hewalɛ fioo ni ekɛfee plantain jwɛi agbo.

english: Why does my farm produce less maize when I grow it on the exact same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo beni miduɔ yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Maize consumes large amounts of specific soil nutrients every season. Planting it continuously without resting the land or rotating crops drains those nutrients, causing yields to drop.
ga: Abɛi kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛi babaoo tsuɔ nii yɛ be fɛɛ mli. Kɛ́ aya nɔ adu nii ni aŋmɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hejɔɔmɔ loo atsakeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ebaaha nakai niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ ajɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ ni baa shi.

english: Why do weeds cause more harm to young rice plants than to older rice plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii awui fe ŋmãa tsei ni edara lɛ?

english: Young rice plants grow slowly and have short roots, making it hard for them to compete with fast-growing weeds for sunlight, water, and fertilizer. Older rice plants have taller leaves that block weed growth.
ga: Omɔ tsei bibii lɛ daa blɛoo ni amɛshishifãi lɛ yɔɔ kuku. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa amɛ akɛ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ baashi akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Omɔ tsei ni egbɔ lɛ yɛ baai kakadaji ni tsiɔ jwɛi adalɛ naa.

english: How many years does it usually take for newly planted cocoa trees to start producing pods?
ga: Afii enyiɛ eheɔ dani cacao tso ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ shishi ewoɔ ŋmeii?

english: Traditional cocoa varieties usually take between 3 to 5 years to start producing pods, but modern hybrid varieties can start yielding fruit in as little as 2 years if given proper water, shade, and soil care.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, blema kookoo henɔi lɛ heɔ afii 3 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛjeɔ ŋmɔtɔ shishi. Shi ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo ni akɛfee tsofai lɛ baanyɛ aje yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii enyɔ pɛ mli kɛji akɛ aha amɛ nu, hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔkwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my young cocoa trees are healthy enough to yield a good harvest in the future?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai wɔsɛɛ?

english: Healthy cocoa trees have thick green leaves without yellowing, strong stems, and free-branching canopies. After 2 to 3 years, you should also notice small flower cushions forming on the main stem and major branches.
ga: Cacao tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli ni ŋmɔŋ bɛ mli, amɛshishifãi lɛ wa, ni amɛhe tsei niji shwieɔ amɛhe. Yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 sɛɛ lɛ, esa akɛ ona fɔfɔi bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi. ni ama yɛ tso lɛ shishifãi wuji lɛ kɛ niji wuji lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: Can I plant new cocoa seedlings on land that already has older trees growing on it?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu kookoo dumɔwui heei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsei momo yɔɔ nɔ momo lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, you can plant new cocoa among older trees, provided the old trees do not block all sunlight or steal all soil nutrients. Thinning out diseased or unproductive old trees helps the young ones get enough light and space.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ tsei momo adu kookoo tsei heei. Kɛji akɛ tsei momoi tsiii hulu la naa loo amɛjuuu niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ. Tsei ni egbɔ, ni hela emɔ amɛ loo ni wooo yibii lɛ ni aaafolɔ ashwie shi lɛ baaye abua ni tsei bibii lɛ ana la kɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do experienced cocoa farmers plant food crops like plantain alongside new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ duɔ niyenii tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo dumɔwui heei ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily in direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains provides essential shade to protect the young cocoa while also giving the farmer food and income before the cocoa starts producing.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa koni akɛbu kookoo tsei bibii ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa okwaafoi lɛ niyenii kɛ shika dani amɛjeɔ kookoo feemɔ shishi.

english: What basic steps should I take before clearing land to start a new cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii titri esa akɛ mafee dani majie shikpɔŋ koni maje kookoo ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: Before clearing, you should evaluate the soil quality, ensure there is adequate water access, secure quality hybrid seedlings from a trusted nursery, and plan for temporary shade crops like plantains or cassava.
ga: dani obaajie Esa akɛ okwɛ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ha. Kwɛmɔ ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ahi jɛmɛ. Na dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛ dumɔwui akwɛmɔhei ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ amɛnɔ. Ni oto gbɛjianɔ oha tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo cassava.

english: Is it safe to clear an old, abandoned farm and immediately plant fresh cocoa on it?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ abaajie ŋmɔji momoi ni ashi amɛ lɛ amli ni adu kookoo hee amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: It is safe, but you must first clear out dead wood, weeds, and diseased plants from the old farm to prevent pests and fungal diseases from spreading to your new cocoa seedlings.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe, shi esa akɛ ojie tsei ni egboi, jwɛi, kɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ momo lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ. Enɛ baatsi tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa o-cocoa dumɔwui heei lɛ anɔ lɛ anaa.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest cocoa pods so I don't pick them too early?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ? Bɔni afee ni okaŋɔ oya tsɔ?

english: Cocoa pods are ready for harvest when their color changes completely, usually turning from green to bright yellow, or from dark red/purple to orange-yellow depending on the variety.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni amɛhe su etsake kwraa lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, etsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. aloo kɛjɛ tsuru/purple ni mli edɔ kɛyashi ŋmɔŋ-orange nɔ. Edamɔ srɔtoi lɛ anɔ

english: What causes some young cocoa pods to turn black and dry up before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani akpaa?

english: This is typically caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in excessive shade, high humidity, and poor farm ventilation. Trimming excess shade branches and removing infected pods helps control it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hulutsoo be babaoo mli, hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ehiii yɛ ŋmɔji amli. Niji ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ ni ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni akudɔɔ amɛ.

english: What should I do if my cocoa trees were planted two years ago but still look stunted and weak?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji akɛ adu mi-kookoo tso lɛ afii enyɔ ni eho nɛ, ni etamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ lolo?

english: Stunted growth after two years is usually caused by lack of shade, poor soil nutrients, or heavy competition from weeds. Clearing weeds around the base, adding fertilizer, and ensuring light shade can boost their growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni haa shweremɔ ni tsiɔ mɔ naa yɛ afii enyɔ sɛɛ lɛ jɛɔ hulutsoo ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo akaŋshii ni naa wa ni jɛɔ jwɛi amli Jwɛi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli kɛ nɔmimaa akɛ la babaoo yɛ lɛ baaye abua ni dalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why is it important to prune older cocoa trees on an existing farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afolɔ kookoo tsei ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ momo lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead, diseased, or overgrown branches. This allows sunlight and air to reach the lower branches, encourages flower development, and reduces the spread of fungal diseases.
ga: Niji ni egboi, ni hela emɔ amɛ, loo ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ, ni ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ahe. Ha fɔfɔi lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ ni oha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli baa lɛ aba shi

english: Why do my tomato plants need to be tied to wooden stakes while they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ mi tomato tsei lɛ akpɛtɛ tsei ahe be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Tomato plants have weak stems that bend under the weight of heavy fruit. Staking lifts the plant off the ground, which prevents soil-borne diseases, stops the fruit from rotting on wet dirt, and ensures leaves get enough sunlight to grow strong.
ga: Tomato tsei yɛ ŋmeii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni shwieɔ shi yɛ aduawai ni tsii ni tsii lɛ shishi. Staking woɔ tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni tsiɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli baa lɛ anaa Etsiɔ aduawai anaa koni amɛkafite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛnáa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara waa.

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to intense heat and burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow very fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving cocoa the shade and moisture it needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ he waa, ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient for green growth. This happens when the soil lacks organic matter or when heavy rains wash away nutrients from the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ Enɛ baa mli kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa niyenii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ laajeɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What is the difference between using dried cow manure and bagged chemical fertilizer on my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ tsina ŋmei ni egbi kɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ kotoku mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ teŋ?

english: Animal manure feeds both the plant and the soil by adding organic material that holds moisture long-term, though it acts slowly. Bagged fertilizer gives plants a fast, concentrated food boost but does not improve long-term soil health.
ga: Manure haa tsei kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ niyenii kɛtsɔ nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ ni ekɛfataa he lɛ nɔ, eyɛ mli akɛ etsuɔ ​​nii blɛoo moŋ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ kotoku mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ náa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa oya. Shi eyeee ebuaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or plants receive too much shade, the cassava puts all its energy into growing top leaves instead of storing energy in the roots. Balanced soil nutrients and clear sunlight direct energy downward into tuber formation.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo loo tso lɛ ná hulutsoo babaoo lɛ, Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ hewalɛ baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, ŋmei duɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ yɛ ebaa lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja kɛ hulu la ni mli tse haa hewalɛ kɛyaa tuber feemɔ mli.

english: What happens if I plant my yam seeds too close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu sweet potato dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Planting yams too close forces them to compete with each other for water, nutrients, and sunlight. This competition leaves less food for each plant, resulting in smaller tubers at harvest time.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ amɛkɛ amɛhe abɔ nu, niyenii, kɛ hulu la he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ niyenii fioo nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii baa yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli.

english: What causes small ragged holes in the middle leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi-abɛi tso bibioo lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ nɔ

english: Small holes in young corn leaves are typically caused by caterpillars like the fall armyworm feeding inside the plant's funnel. Spotting them early allows you to treat the crop before pests destroy the growing point.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ ŋmeii ni afolɔ, ni egbee shi ni amɛye tso lɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii baa bibii amli lɛ baa. Amɛtaomɔ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ obuɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ ahe dani kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fiteɔ he ni ŋmɔshi nii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ lɛ.

english: How do weeds hurt my main crops if they are just growing naturally in the same dirt?
ga: Te jwɛi baaye miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm; they steal soil nutrients, water, and sunlight that your main crops need to yield well. They also hide pests and crop diseases that can spread to your harvest.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni he hiaa otsei titrii lɛ koni amɛwo yibii kpakpai kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli. Ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei ahelai ni baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã okpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ hu teeɔ.

english: It is best to wait until rains fall consistently for two or three consecutive times and soak deep into the soil. Planting after just one light shower can cause seeds to germinate and then dry up when the heat returns.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ baajɛ mli aba, ni no sɛɛ lɛ ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ Shikome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ la ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves drop down and look lifeless in the afternoon even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni wala bɛ mli yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: In hot afternoon heat, plants lose water through leaves faster than roots can draw it up from the soil. The leaves limp temporarily to conserve moisture and usually recover by evening when temperatures drop.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ baagbɔjɔ be kukuoo ko koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ beni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi lɛ.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off instead of turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant gets stressed by too much heat, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients. Giving your plants steady water at the roots and shade during extreme heat helps the flowers stay attached and form tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ hao kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ aha shishifãi lɛ nu kɛ hulutsoo yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛfee tomatoi.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, and it happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil, often due to irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the plant absorb calcium properly.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ni ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa calcium lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do extension officers advise us to tie tomato plants to wooden sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ wɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔkɛ tomato tsei akpɛtɛ tsei ahe lɛ?

english: Tying tomato plants to wooden stakes keeps the leaves and fruits off the wet soil. This prevents fungal diseases from soil splashes and makes it much easier to harvest clean fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tomato tsei fĩ tsei ahe lɛ, ebaaha baai kɛ aduawai lɛ akahi shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akashwie shikpɔŋ nɔ. Ni ehaa aduawai ni he tse ni akpaa lɛ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up and turn yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking pests like aphids or mites that carry viruses. Spraying your peppers early with neem oil or appropriate pest controls helps stop these insects before they ruin the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni hiɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. Ni akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ baashwie ŋmɔtɔ nɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni akpa kooloi nɛɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Is it better to start my pepper seeds in a nursery bed before moving them to the main field?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaaje pepper dumɔwui lɛ shishi yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli dani ajie amɛ kɛya ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli?

english: Yes, pepper seeds are tiny and delicate. Starting them in a shaded nursery bed allows you to protect young seedlings from hot sun and heavy rains until they are strong enough to transplant.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, pepper dumɔwui lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. Kɛ́ obɔi dumɔwui lɛ akwɛmɔhe ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ obuɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu amɛ.

english: Why are my fresh pepper fruits getting soft, watery spots before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper yibii heei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni nu yɔɔ mli dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Soft rotting spots are usually fruit rot caused by fungi or insect punctures. Harvesting ripe peppers promptly and avoiding spraying water directly on the fruits helps keep them healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso yibii ni ŋmeii loo kooloi bibii kɛbaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ soft rot spots baa. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ oya ni ajie nu ni akɛshwieɔ aduawai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is tamarind a good tree to plant on my land, and how long will I wait to harvest from it?
ga: Tamarind ji tso kpakpa ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ni be enyiɛ manyɛ mamɛ ni makpa?

english: Tamarind is very good for dry regions because it tolerates heat and drought well, but it takes about 4 to 7 years to start bearing fruit. Once mature, it yields fruit every year for decades with minimal care.
ga: Tamarind he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa kɛha hei ni nu bɛ lɛ ejaakɛ eŋmɛɔ hulutsoo kɛ hɔmɔ naa jogbaŋŋ. Shi ebaahe aaafee afii 4 kɛyashi 7 dani ebɔi yibiiwoo. Kɛ́ amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ, amɛbaawo yibii daa afi afii nyɔŋmai abɔ ni akwɛɛɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I grow tomatoes or peppers on the same land where I have growing tamarind trees?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu tomato loo ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni aduɔ tamarind tsei yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, while tamarind trees are young and small, you can plant short-season crops like peppers or tomatoes between them. Once the tamarind trees grow large and create heavy shade, you will need to move vegetable crops to open sunlight.
ga: Hɛɛ, eyɛ mli akɛ tamarind tso lɛ ji gbekɛ lolo ni eji bibioo moŋ. Shi obaanyɛ odu ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kukuoo tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo tomato hu yɛ tamarind tsei lɛ ateŋ. Kɛ tamarind tso lɛ da ni ekɛ hulutsoo be ni tsii ha lɛ Ebaabi ni okɛ aduawai lɛ aya he ko ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ yɛ.

english: How do I know if my land is good enough for planting vegetables like peppers and tomatoes?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu aduawai tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ tomato?

english: Good land for vegetables needs loose soil that drains water easily and is rich in decomposed manure or compost. If water sits in pools on top of your field after rain, you should make raised ridges or beds so roots do not rot.
ga: Esa akɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni akɛduɔ aduawai lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli oya, ni ŋmeii ni egbo loo ŋmeii ni efite babaoo yɔɔ mli. Kɛji nu damɔ nubu lɛ mli yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ Esa akɛ ofee ŋmeii loo saatsoi ni awó nɔ. Koni shishifãi lɛ akafite

english: How can I store my harvested crop seeds safely in plastic or zip bags so insects do not destroy them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ awo plastic loo zipper kotokui amli shweshweeshwe koni kooloi akafite amɛ?

english: You must dry seeds completely before sealing them inside airtight containers or zipper bags in a cool, dark place. Keeping moisture out prevents mold growth and stops insects from multiplying inside the stored seeds.
ga: Esa akɛ ogbi dumɔwui lɛ kwraa dani okɛwo tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo zip kotoku mli yɛ he ko ni mli ejɔ ni duŋ ewo mli. Kɛ́ aha ehiɛ edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii babaoo bɛ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ amli.

english: Why do extension officers encourage us to plant trees alongside our food crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ wɔ hewalɛ ni wɔdu tsei yɛ wɔ niyenii ni wɔduɔ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Trees help protect your farm from soil erosion, provide shade to sensitive young crops, improve soil fertility through fallen leaves, and give you valuable wood or fruit in the long run.
ga: Tsei yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ he. Ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii jogbaŋŋ kɛtsɔɔ baai ni egbee shi lɛ nɔ. ni eha bo tsei loo aduawai ni jara wa yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up like straw to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, which helps the plant conserve water and survive extreme heat.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ jwɛi koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he ni amɛnyɛɔ amɛdamɔɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa naa.

english: What happens to my soil if I plant groundnuts together with my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni baaba mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmei du ŋmei?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil, providing free natural plant food that helps the maize grow stronger.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ha adebɔɔ mli tso niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni edara waa ni aheee nɔ ko.

english: This is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. It weakens the plant and stops the tubers underground from growing big.
ga: Enɛ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi, ni koolooi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Ehaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaaa ŋmeii lɛ adara.

english: Why do my pepper plant flowers keep dropping off before making any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani mifeɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences stress, usually from extreme heat, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer causing leaf growth instead of fruiting.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ kɛ haomɔ kpe. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Ehaa baai kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Why do cassava crops grown under big shade trees yield very small tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei ni adu yɛ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ shade shishi lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: Cassava needs direct, strong sunlight to make food through its leaves. Under dense shade, the plant uses all its energy trying to grow taller to reach light instead of feeding the tubers below.
ga: Cassava he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni enyɛ eye nii kɛtsɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ. Yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa lɛ shishi Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni eda ni eshɛ kane lɛ he moŋ fe ni eeeye bulb ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close together, will I get more harvest?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ Ani manyɛ makpa babaoo?

english: No, planting seeds too close together forces the crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, resulting in thin stalks and empty or small cobs.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko loo bibii baa.

english: How can I tell that my farmland soil is getting tired and needs a rest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni ehe miihia ni majɔɔ mihe?

english: Tired soil shows signs like stunted crop growth, leaves turning pale yellow early in the season, lower crop yields every year, and the sudden growth of stubborn weeds like Striga.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ jieɔ okadii tamɔ tsei ni edaaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ kpo. Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ miiba shi daa afi. Ni jwɛi ni yitsoŋ wa tamɔ Striga lɛ daa trukaa.

english: How do I know that my yams are fully mature and ready for harvest under the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Yams tell you they are mature when the green vines and leaves on top of the ground naturally dry up and turn yellow at the end of the rainy season.
ga: Sweet potatoes tsɔɔ bo akɛ amɛdara beni wain tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ gĩɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster and stronger than my food crops on the same farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe miniyenii ni miduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that naturally adapt to consume soil water and nutrients very quickly, making them stronger competitors than food crops which need extra protection and care.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe koni amɛkɛ sũ mli nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛi atsu nii oya. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ akaŋshilɔ ni wa kɛha niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni biɔ hebuu kɛ kwɛmɔ babaoo lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants rolling up and turning light green during hot dry days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up like tubes to protect themselves from losing too much water when the sun is too hot. Light green leaves show that the crop is stressed from heat and lacks enough water or nutrients in the soil.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa baai shwieɔ ŋmãa mli koni nu akafite fe nine kɛ́ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ enɔ. Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ etsɔ hulutsoo be mli ni nu loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop their bottom leaves when the heat becomes too intense?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ shwieɔ ebaa lɛ shishi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava naturally sheds its lower leaves during prolonged heat or dry periods to conserve moisture, keeping the main stem and underground roots alive until the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ eshishi baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hulutsoo loo hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ mli koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. Enɛ haa tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: Should I keep planting the traditional maize seed I saved from last year or switch to certified seeds from the agriculture store?
ga: Ani esa akɛ maya nɔ madu blema ŋmãa dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ loo matsake kɛya dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ ni jɛ okwaayeli shwapo ko mli lɛ nɔ?

english: Saved seeds gradually lose their strength over generations and yield less. Certified seeds are specially bred to resist local droughts and common pests in Ghana, giving you a bigger harvest even under tough conditions.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi fiofio yɛ yinɔi amli ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo. Akwɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni ekɛte shi ewo maŋ lɛ mli hɔmɔ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa nii babaoo yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli po.

english: How do I know if the ground has enough rain moisture for me to start sowing my crop seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa ni baaha mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ?

english: Dig down with your hands; if the soil is wet up to your wrist level, it has enough moisture to germinate your seeds safely without them drying up if rains pause for a few days.
ga: Kɛ oniji atsa Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ kɛyashɛ onineshi he lɛ Fɛ̃i ni fa bɔ ni sa baaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe ni dumɔwui lɛ egbiŋ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa gbii fioo komɛi.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and thin with tiny ears when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ toi bibii kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete for sunlight, water, and soil food. The plants stretch upward to fight for sunlight instead of spending energy to produce big grains.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛye hulu la lɛ he akaŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛwo dumɔwui wuji.

english: Why does planting groundnuts on my farmland first make my next season's maize grow much better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa mi-be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen food from the air and store it in the soil through their roots, acting as natural fertilizer for the maize planted after them.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the young leaves of my pepper plants curling upward into small cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ baai bibii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe kɛfee kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking juices from the underside of the leaves, which distorts their growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. ni kɛ dalɛ ni ejaaa baa

english: Why are small worms eating holes in my young maize leaves right inside the central funnel of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn baai ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ faa lɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: These are fall armyworms that love to hide in the tender center of maize plants where it is moist; treating them early prevents them from destroying the plant's growing point.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji fall armyworms ni sumɔɔ ni amɛhiɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ. Tsamɔ ni afeɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite hei ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why do my rice plants survive in flooded water while my maize plants turn yellow and rot in the same flooded field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ je nu afua lɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, mi-abele tsei lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboi yɛ ŋmɔ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ mli.

english: Rice plants have special internal air tubes in their stems that carry oxygen down to their roots underwater, whereas maize roots suffocate and rot when water covers them for too long.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko ni yɔɔ amɛmli yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shi kɛyaa amɛshishifãi lɛ amli yɛ nu shishi. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ kɛji akɛ nu ha amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: Why do my vegetable crops wither fast even when I give them water in the middle of the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ gboɔ oya eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Watering in the afternoon causes most water to evaporate quickly before roots can absorb it, and hot water droplets on leaves can scorch the plant under strong sunlight.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ shwane mli lɛ baaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ oya dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Ni nu ni mli edɔ ni shwieɔ baai anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ ashã yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green and healthy. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer will restore the green color and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ ni ebaaha edalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Cowpeas produce their own nitrogen in the soil. If you give them extra nitrogen fertilizer, the plant focuses on growing big green leaves instead of flowers and pods. Using phosphorus-rich fertilizer or wood ash instead helps the plant produce more pods.
ga: Cowpeas feɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ okɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ha lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ anɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛ́ okɛ phosphorus ni fa babaoo loo tso mli sũ tsu nii moŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua otso lɛ ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking juices from the leaves, or by a virus spread by whiteflies. Spraying neem seed oil or soapy water on the leaves early can clear the insects and protect new growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Neem dumɔwui amli fɔ loo nu ni akɛ samla shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni ajie kooloi bibii kɛjɛ jɛmɛ ni ebaatsi nibii heei ni yaa hiɛ lɛ anaa.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in wet, dark conditions. Pruning excess shade tree branches to let in sunlight and removing diseased pods right away stops the rot from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ fɛ̃i, duŋ shihilɛi amli kɛbaa. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ shade fe nine lɛ koni hulu la aba ni ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii akagbɛ ashwã ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay thin and small even after a full year in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ bibii yɛ be mli ni mikɛ afi muu fɛɛ ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ po lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need loose soil and full sunlight to swell up. If the soil is hard packed or heavily shaded by large trees, the plant puts its energy into growing stems and leaves instead of storing starch in large tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse kɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo he miihia cassava shishifãi koni amɛfu. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa loo tsei wuji komɛi yɛ ni tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa. Tsei kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛda amɛshishifãi kɛ baai. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ baato ŋmɔtɔi wuji amli lɛ

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high, when water supply is irregular, or when insects are not visiting to pollinate them. Keeping soil moist with mulch and watering regularly helps flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Be mli ni nu lɛ ejaaa Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii baaa koni amɛbafee pollination. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni okɛ nu shwieɔ nɔ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow twisted and cracked instead of smooth and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbɛ eshwa moŋ fe ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Yams bend and crack when they hit hard ground or rocks while growing underground, or when heavy rains follow a dry period. Making tall, loose soil mounds without stones lets the yam expand smoothly.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛji etswa shikpɔŋ loo tɛi ni wa beni ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. aloo be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha ehi shi ni efee mlɛo ni tɛi bɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cabbages stay soft if they do not get steady water or enough nutrients while growing. Consistent watering and adding good compost early on helps the leaves fold tightly together to form a solid, firm head.
ga: Cabbage baakã he ahi shi bɔdɔɔ kɛji akɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu nɔ daa loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa be mli ni edaa lɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai ni akɛwoɔ mli mra. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ amɛhe jogbaŋŋ koni yitso lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ ni ehi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why should I clear weeds around my young crops so early when the crops are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi yɛ mitsei bibii lɛ ahe mra be mli ni tsei lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: Young crops have small roots and struggle to compete with weeds for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Removing weeds during the first month gives crops a head start to grow strong enough to shade out weeds later.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi bibii ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkɛ jwɛi lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ ada waa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ jwɛi ni baaba sɛɛ mli lɛ aha.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when heavy winds and rain come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and can be weakened by tiny soil worms or soggy soil. Supporting fruiting trees with strong bamboo props and heaping rich soil around the base prevents them from blowing over.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii bibii baanyɛ aha amɛgbɔjɔ. loo shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ Yibii tsei ni akɛ ŋmeii ni wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni jara wa ni abua naa ni ebɔle amɛshishi lɛ fiɔ amɛsɛɛ lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ akatswa amɛ.

english: What fast-growing crops can I plant in my small backyard plot in Accra to get food quickly?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya manyɛ makwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ? Shia ni yɔɔ Accra lɛ sɛɛ koni aná niyenii oya

english: Vegetables like leafy spinach (kontomire), pepper, and garden eggs grow very quickly in small spaces and can be harvested repeatedly within a few months, making them ideal for small backyard plots.
ga: Aduawai tamɔ spinach ni yɔɔ baai (contomire), ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ abɔɔ mli ŋmɔtɔi kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ he bibioo ko. ni abaanyɛ akpa ekoŋŋ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli Enɛ haa efeɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha sɛɛ shikpɔji bibii.

english: Why are my maize plants growing tall and thin with pale yellow leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Maize needs full sunlight and proper soil nutrients like nitrogen; when planted in dense shade or poor soil, the plant stretches upward searching for light and lacks the energy to produce strong stems and green leaves.
ga: Hulu ni fa kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni sa, tamɔ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa, kɛji akɛ adu yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ. Tso lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛyaa la lɛ he ni ebɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa kɛ baai eŋɔli.

english: Tomato leaves curl up to protect themselves from losing too much water in intense heat, but it can also mean tiny insects like whiteflies are feeding on the plant and spreading leaf diseases.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe koni nu babaoo akafite yɛ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ mli. Shi ebaanyɛ etsɔɔ hu akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ miiye tsei ni amɛmiigbɛ helai amɛmiigbɛ amɛmiitsɔ baai lɛ anɔ.

english: How do I know if my cassava plants are getting too much water on my small plot?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cassava tsei lɛ miiná nu babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ bibioo lɛ nɔ?

english: Cassava needs well-drained soil; if the soil stays flooded or overwatered, the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the roots under the ground will start to rot instead of growing into large tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ he miihia cassava. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi lolo loo eyi obɔ lɛ Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi. Ni shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ baabɔi fitemɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: What happens if I plant my pepper seeds too close together in a small garden space?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu pepper dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ abɔɔ mli he bibioo ko?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots and leaves fight for the same limited water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, resulting in small, weak plants that yield very little fruit.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ falɛ kome. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ daraaa ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ.

english: Can I grow cassava and maize together on the same small piece of land?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mafee ekome kɛdu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ. Ani ebaanyɛ efee nakai nɔŋŋ?

english: Yes, intercropping maize and cassava works well because maize grows and matures quickly in three months, while cassava grows slowly at first and takes over the space after the maize is harvested.
ga: Yes, growing corn and cassava works well because the corn grows and ripens quickly in three months. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli ni eyeɔ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ nɔ beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when the weather is extremely hot and dry, or when the soil lacks adequate moisture and organic nutrients needed to support fruit development.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ. aloo be mli ni sũ lɛ bɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa koni aduawai akwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: How does adding poultry manure to my small plot help my vegetables grow better?
ga: Kooloi ashishifãi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔji bibii amli Te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua mi-aduawai lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Poultry manure acts as a rich food source for crops by slowly releasing essential nutrients like nitrogen into the soil and helping the soil hold water for longer periods.
ga: Kooloi afɔfɔi tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni jara wa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii kɛtsɔ fiofio Ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli ni eyeɔ ebuaa sũ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds prevent my yam plants from producing large tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miitsi mi sweet potato tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkawo ŋmeii wuji lɛ?

english: Weeds steal essential water, sunlight, and fertilizer directly from the soil before your crop can get them, leaving the yam plant undernourished and unable to build large underground tubers.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu ni he hiaa, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ aná. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ sweet potato tso lɛ mli, ni enyɛɛɛ efee ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are dark spots appearing on my garden egg leaves after heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni nugbɔ nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ jeɔ kpo yɛ eggplant baai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: High humidity and rainwater splashing onto leaves allow fungal spores to spread, creating dark spots that can damage the leaves if the plants do not get good air circulation.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ nugbɔ nu ni shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ baa ni baanyɛ afite baai lɛ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shɛɛɛ tso lɛ he.

english: Why does my cocoa farm only produce pods during specific months of the year instead of giving me yield all year round?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii yɛ afi lɛ mli nyɔji komɛi pɛ amli moŋ fe afi muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Crops like cocoa rely on natural weather triggers like rainy seasons to flower and dry periods to ripen fruit. During the rest of the year, the tree uses its energy to rest, grow leaves, and store food for the next harvest season.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ kookoo damɔ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi tamɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ nɔ koni amɛkwɛ fɔfɔi. kɛ be mli ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ koni eha aduawai lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ afi lɛ mli be ni eshwɛ lɛ mli Tsei kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii kɛjɔɔ amɛhe, amɛwoɔ baai, ni amɛkɛ niyenii toɔ kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops seem to stop growing completely during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ kwraa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When water is scarce, plants enter a temporary resting state to protect themselves. They slow down their food-making process to preserve moisture in their stems and roots until rain returns.
ga: Beni nu faaa lɛ Tso lɛ boteɔ shihilɛ ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli mli koni ebu ehe he. Amɛhaa niyenii homɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi tsei lɛ ashishi kɛ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: If I apply fertilizer bags to my farm today, how long does it take for my plants to start using it?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɛnɛ Be enyiɛ ebaahe dani mi tsei lɛ ajie amɛhe?

english: Fertilizer does not work instantly. Rain or soil moisture must first dissolve the granules so the roots can drink up the nutrients, which usually takes a few days to a week depending on soil wetness.
ga: Fertilizer tsuuu nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Esa akɛ nugbɔ loo shikpɔŋ nɔ nu lɛ atsɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli klɛŋklɛŋ bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anu niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ gbii fioo kɛyashi otsi kome yɛ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ha lɛ naa.

english: What will happen to my crops if I put too many bags of fertilizer on my land at once?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be kome mli?

english: Applying too much fertilizer can 'burn' the plant roots due to high salt levels, causing leaves to dry up and potentially killing the crop instead of making it grow faster.
ga: Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ ‘ashã’ tsei shishifãi yɛ ŋmei ni fa babaoo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ gbiɔ ni ebaanyɛ efite ŋmɔshi nii lɛ moŋ fe ni eeeha eda oya.

english: Why does my land give me fewer bags of harvest each year even though I plant the exact same crop every time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmaa kotokui fioo pɛ daa afi lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ be fɛɛ be moŋ.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the specific nutrients that crop loves from the soil. Over time, the soil becomes exhausted unless you rest the land, add compost/fertilizer, or rotate with different crops like beans.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni oookwɛ shii abɔ Ebaaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni tsei taoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafo ja okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ jɔɔ ohe. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii/ŋmɔshi nibii afata he. loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi tamɔ ŋmeii atsu nii ni okɛtsake.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops turning yellow even when it is raining well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ miinɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your plants are missing essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or the soil has become waterlogged, which smothers the roots and prevents them from taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli, loo akɛ nu eyi sũ lɛ mli obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo, ni ehaaa amɛye nii.

english: Why are the flowers dropping off my crops before turning into actual fruits or pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ dani amɛfeɔ anɔkwa aduawai loo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Plants drop their flowers when they feel stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, insect attacks, or lack of soil nutrients, as they cannot support the weight of growing fruit.
ga: Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, kooloi ni baatutua amɛ, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hao amɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛnyɛŋ amɛfi tso yibii ni miida lɛ muji lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my maize crops yield smaller cobs when I plant them very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he kpaakpa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for limited sunlight, groundwater, and soil food, leaving no single plant with enough energy to make big cobs.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la ni faaa, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tso ko bɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaafee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why should I cut off some branches and leaves from my trees when they look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tso ko niji kɛ baai komɛi beni etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes unnecessary branches so the plant stops wasting energy on useless leaves and directs all its food into producing bigger, healthier fruits and pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ. Bɔni afee ni tsei akpa hewalɛ ni amɛfiteɔ yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ. ni ekwɛ niyenii muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ koni ekɛ aduawai kɛ ŋmeii ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba.

english: The very first rain is often followed by a hot dry spell. If you plant immediately, the young seeds will sprout but then dry out and die before the real rainy season starts.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ, ni mli egbi nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ adu amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, dumɔwui bibii lɛ baakwɛ̃ shi amɛbaagbi ni amɛgboi dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ diɛŋtsɛ aba.

english: How can I tell if my land is good enough to grow maize and vegetables?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ aduawai?

english: Good soil for crops usually has a dark rich color, holds moisture without staying waterlogged, and contains decaying organic matter like leaves, which provides essential nutrients for young plants to grow strong.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni nu ehiɛɛɛ mli Ni nibii ni fiteɔ, tamɔ baai, ni haa tsei bibii lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa koni amɛdara waa lɛ yɛ jɛmɛ.

english: Why do my crop yields keep reducing every year even though I plant on the same plot of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ miiba shi daa afi lɛ? Ni midu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Planting the same crop on the same land repeatedly drains the soil of specific nutrients. Rotating your main crop with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts helps restore nitrogen and keeps the soil healthy naturally.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ nɔŋŋ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni akɛtsuɔ nii shii abɔ. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii atsake oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa ekoŋŋ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves during dry spells as a natural defense to conserve water and protect their underground tubers. Mulching around the base keeps moisture in the soil and prevents excessive leaf loss.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ nu he ni abuɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ahe. Mulching ni akɛwoɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaa baa lɛ shwieɔ shi fe nine.

english: How do I know if I am giving my pepper plants too much or too little water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mikɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiha lɛ babaoo loo fioo tsɔ?

english: If pepper plants get too little water, their leaves wilt and curl downward; if they get too much water, the leaves turn yellow and drop off because waterlogged soil prevents roots from breathing.
ga: Kɛji akɛ nu fioo pɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ tso lɛ ná lɛ Baai lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaakpã shi. Kɛji onine shɛ nu babaoo nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in an open field without tall trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei kakadaji bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn under direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a cooler microclimate and protects young plants until their roots are deep enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains ni yɔɔ Emasɛi lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli ejɔ aba. ni obu tso bibioo lɛ he kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ amli baawo wu bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are my tomato plants growing long stems and plenty of leaves, but producing very few fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ shishifãi kakadaji kɛ baai babaoo shi ewoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: Excessive leafy growth often happens when plants receive too much nitrogen fertilizer or are planted too close together, causing them to fight for sunlight instead of focusing energy on flowering and fruiting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yaa hiɛ fe nine lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ ná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo loo adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la he akaŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ baama fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo nɔ.

english: How do I know the right time to sow my seeds after the first rains begin?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adũ dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the soil stays consistently moist after two or three steady rains, ensuring seeds do not germinate during a false start of the rainy season and dry out.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi fioo komɛi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ koni dumɔwui akakwɛ̃ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee ni ejaaa mli ni amɛgbi.

english: What causes tiny holes in my cabbage leaves and how can I stop it without buying expensive chemicals?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ cabbage baai anɔ Ni te aaafee tɛŋŋ akpa ni aheee tsofai ni jara wa?

english: Holes in cabbage leaves are usually caused by caterpillars that hatch from eggs laid by moths. Spraying a mixture of water and crushed neem seeds or soap acts as a safe, natural deterrent.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni amɛwoɔ lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ kaabɛji baai amli lɛ baa. Nu ni akɛ neem dumɔwui loo samla ni atswa lɛ efutu mli lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baatsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni tsiɔ mɔ naa ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: How can I keep my harvested plantains from ripening and spoiling too quickly before getting them to market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-plantain ni mikpa lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni efite oya tsɔ dani mikɛwo jara nɔ?
