english: Harvesting plantains while still fully green and storing them in cool, shaded crates away from direct sunlight slows down the natural release of ripening gases, extending their shelf life.
ga: Plantains ni akpaa be mli ni amɛji eŋɔli lolo ni akɛtoɔ adeka ko ni mli ejɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli mli. Ekɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ Enɛ baaye abua ni eha kɔɔyɔɔ ni kɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii homɔ baa lɛ aba shi. ni eha shihilɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ aya hiɛ

english: How can I grow crops with less heavy manual weeding so younger family members will be interested in farming?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ madu ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ niji tsuuu nii babaoo koni weku lɛ mli bii ni darako lɛ aná okwaayeli he miishɛɛ?

english: Using modern techniques like cover cropping, organic mulching, or drip irrigation reduces heavy manual weeding labor significantly while increasing crop yields and farm profitability.
ga: Kɛ akɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋaai tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ adumɔ tsu nii Organic Mulching Loo, nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ baanyɛ aha nine nitsumɔ ni he hiaa koni akɛjie jwɛi babaoo lɛ aba shi waa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa kɛ ŋmɔ mli sɛɛnamɔi yaa hiɛ.

english: What kind of crops can I plant in Northern Ghana that will withstand dry periods and still bring good income for my family?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ ni baanyɛ adamɔ hɔmɔ naa ni eha miweku lɛ aná shika kpakpa lolo?

english: Crops like groundnuts, cowpeas, sorghum, and millet grow very well in Northern conditions because they require less water and mature quickly, making them reliable choices to support household income.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii, tsina ŋmeii, ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ waa yɛ kooyigbɛ shihilɛi amli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu fioo pɛ he hiaa amɛ, ni amɛdaraa oya. Enɛ haa efeɔ nɔ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ kɛha shika ni anáa kɛhaa shiabii.

english: How do I know if 6 acres of land is too big for me to farm successfully on my own?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni dalɛ ji acre 6 lɛ da tsɔ ni mi diɛŋtsɛ manyɛ matsu okwaayeli he nii yɛ omanyeyeli mli?

english: A 6-acre farm requires significant labor for land preparation, weeding, and harvesting. If you plan to farm that size, choosing low-maintenance crops like leguminous grains or hiring seasonal labor ensures you can manage it without losing yields.
ga: Okwaafoi ni dalɛ ji acre 6 lɛ biɔ nitsumɔ babaoo koni akɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ, jwɛi lɛ kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ. Kɛji oto gbɛjianɔ akɛ obaatsu okwaayeli ni dalɛ tamɔ nakai lɛ Halamɔ tsei ni esaaa akɛ akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, tamɔ ŋmeii. loo nitsulɔi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ be mli lɛ ni oooŋɔ Ebaaha onyɛ okwɛ nɔ ni nibii ni otsuɔ lɛ akafite.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly like drinking straws on hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ jwɛi ni anuɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up during the hottest part of the day as a natural self-defense mechanism to reduce water loss through their surfaces, helping the plant conserve moisture until cooler weather arrives.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni haa nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my young crop plants turn yellow instead of staying bright green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves are usually a sign that the plant is short on nitrogen or that the roots are underwatered or waterlogged, which prevents the crop from absorbing essential nutrients from the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli loo akɛ shishifãi lɛ yɛ nu shishi loo nu eyi mli obɔ. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or beans in my field make the soil better for future crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans gather nitrogen from the air and store it in small nodules on their roots. When the plant harvested, that stored nitrogen remains in the soil to naturally feed the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Buaa nitrogen naa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ ŋmeii bibii amli yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛji akpa tso lɛ. Nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: What happens to my crops if I sow seeds too close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni baaba midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the growing plants compete heavily with one another for sunlight, ground water, and soil nutrients, resulting in tall but weak plants with low grain yields.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii he akaŋ waa. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ shi amɛhe waaa, ni dumɔwui hu baa shi.

english: It is best to wait until the soil receives two or three steady, deep rains rather than planting after the very first light rain, ensuring the soil stays moist enough for seeds to germinate and survive.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa shii enyɔ loo etɛ daa, moŋ fe ni ooodu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ fioo lɛ sɛɛ, koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why are my vegetable plants growing leaves very fast but not producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ miida oya shi amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Adding too much nitrogen fertilizer causes plants to focus all their energy on growing tall stems and leafy foliage rather than producing flowers and fruits.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ tsei ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ahe nii moŋ fe ni amɛaawo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai.

english: Flowers drop off prematurely when the plant suffers stress from extreme heat, dry soil, or lack of pollination by beneficial insects like bees.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni haaa amɛhe afee shoo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my crop harvests get smaller every season if I plant maize in the exact same field year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa lɛ faaa yɛ be fɛɛ mli kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes the specific soil nutrients that crop needs and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ baaha shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tsei lɛ aba shi be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when there are no big shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboiɔ lɛ? Beni tsei wuji komɛi bɛ ni baaha hulutsoo,

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because direct, intense sunlight scorches their soft leaves and dries out the soil moisture. Planting tall companion crops like plantains provides shade and protects the young cocoa until it grows strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai bibii lɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ agbi. Hefatalɔi tsei ni kɛlɛ tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa kookoo bibii lɛ náa hulutsoo kɛ hebuu kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni enáa hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and soft during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Rainy and humid weather creates ideal conditions for a fungal disease called Black Pod to spread across cocoa pods. Pruning extra shade branches lets sunlight and air flow through the farm, drying out the moisture that the fungus needs to grow.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ hulutsoo shihilɛi haa shihilɛ ni sa baa koni tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ amli fɛɛ. Niji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo lɛ ahe ni afolɔ babaoo lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa nu ni he hiaa ŋmeii lɛ koni amɛdara lɛ gbɛ́ɔ.

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil stays waterlogged for too long because the roots cannot breathe. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away from the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ehi nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ amli.

english: Dropping leaves is a natural survival trick for cassava to save water during dry periods. As long as the stems stay green inside, the plant is alive and will grow fresh leaves once the rains start again.
ga: Baai ni ashwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ gbɛ kɛha ŋmei koni ekɛbu nu he yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Shii abɔ ni tso lɛ shishi lɛ baafee eŋɔli yɛ mli lɛ Tso lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo ni ebaana baai heei ni baaje kpo kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Yam vines naturally climb up high to spread their leaves toward sunlight. Staking the vines helps the leaves catch maximum sunlight, which provides the energy needed to grow large underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã koni amɛkɛ hulu lɛ akpee. Wein tso lɛ ni akɛwoɔ tso mli lɛ haa tso lɛ yibii lɛ naa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Enɛ ji hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow and dying early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egboɔ oya lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the soil has run out of nitrogen, which maize needs in high amounts to stay healthy. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure early in the plant's growth fixes this problem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi he miihia lɛ babaoo koni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsu nii mra yɛ tso lɛ dalɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni asaa naagba nɛɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves have long yellow stripes running down them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kakadaŋŋ agboi ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Yellow stripes along maize leaves are a symptom of Maize Streak Virus, which is carried and spread by tiny insects called leafhoppers. Planting virus-resistant maize seeds is the best way to prevent this disease.
ga: Abele ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa nɔ lɛ ji Maize Streak Virus, ni kooloi bibii kɛbaa lɛ he okadi. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ leafhoppers lɛ ji mɛi ni hiɛɔ nibii ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa. Abele dumɔwui ni tsɛŋemɔ helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ hela nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during heavy winds when they start carrying fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli beni ejeɔ yibiiwoo shishi lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that struggle to support the heavy weight of a full bunch of plantains during strong winds. Supporting the fruiting tree with strong wooden Y-sticks keeps it upright until harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛye amɛbua ŋmeii muu lɛ fɛɛ ni tsii lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Fi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ asɛɛ kɛ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni tamɔ Y, ni oha amɛhi shi jaŋŋ kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat stress or lacks enough water in the soil. Consistent watering during the flowering stage keeps the blossoms healthy so they can turn into fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ afɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ nu daa yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ mli waa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is usually caused by tiny whitefly insects that spread a virus while feeding on the leaves. Spraying neem oil or using insect netting prevents whiteflies from damaging the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. ni gbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa be mli ni eyeɔ baai lɛ Neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo kɛ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ baatsi ŋmeii yɛŋ lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow and falling off before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi dani kpamɔɔ be baashɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava leaves often turn yellow during dry spells as a natural way to save water, or when the soil lacks nitrogen. However, if you notice web-like structures under the leaves, it could be a sign of damage caused by green mites.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ naa gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ nu toɔ. aloo be mli ni nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi, kɛji ona nibii ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ No baanyɛ afee okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ efite nii.

english: Why are my maize plants producing tassels at the top but failing to grow full corn cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ miiwo ŋmeii yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ shi ehiɛɛɛ ŋmeii ni ekwɛɛɛ kwraa lɛ?

english: Maize needs a steady supply of water and nitrogen when flowering. If the plants suffer from heat stress or poor soil nutrients during tasseling, the silk dries out and pollen cannot fertilize the cobs properly, resulting in small or empty ears.
ga: Nu kɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmã be fɛɛ be kɛ́ eewo fɔfɔi. Kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo sũ mli niyenii ni ehiii yɛ be mli ni amɛshwieɔ amɛhe lɛ, Silk lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni pollen lɛ nyɛŋ aha cob lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa toi lɛ feɔ bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli.

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop many flowers they cannot support, but heavy flower drop usually happens when there is too much direct sunlight, drought, or a lack of tiny pollinating insects like midges in the farm.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, cacao tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi babaoo ni anyɛɛɛ akɛto. Shi bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔi babaoo ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ faaa, hɔmɔ loo fɔfɔi bibii ni haa fɔfɔii tamɔ ŋmɔ mli adafitswaa woji lɛ faaa.

english: Can I plant cassava and maize together on the same plot without reducing my harvest?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni ŋmãa lɛ baa shi?

english: Yes, intercropping cassava and maize works well because maize grows quickly and is harvested within three to four months, leaving the slower-growing cassava to take over the land and mature over the rest of the year.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa teŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. Ha ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ aŋɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eda yɛ afi lɛ mli be ni eshwɛ lɛ mli.

english: What causes my yam tubers to grow short and misshapen instead of long and deep?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-sweet potato tubers lɛ feɔ kuku ni ehiii yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni mli kwɔ?

english: Yams need soft, deep, and loose soil to push downward. If the soil is hard, rocky, or planted on shallow mounds, the growing tuber hits resistance and expands sideways or becomes twisted.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli kwɔ, ni mli tse koni ekɛtsi kɛbote mli. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa, tɛi yɔɔ nɔ, loo adu yɛ gɔŋ ko ni mli ekwɔɔɔ nɔ lɛ, Bulbs ni adu lɛ kɛ shitee-kɛ-woo kpeɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa kɛyaa sɛɛgbɛ loo amɛfeɔ srɔtoi.

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist right after a mild rain, placing it near the root zone and covering it lightly with soil so heavy rain runoff does not carry it off the field.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Okɛma he ni shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ lɛ masɛi ni okɛ sũ bibioo ko aha nɔ. Koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa akaho yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ kponɔ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like thrips, mites, or whiteflies, or by a plant virus transmitted by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, mites, loo whiteflies lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛbaa lɛ amli

english: Why do wild weeds seem to grow much faster than my crops at the start of the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Weed seeds in the soil are adapted to sprout rapidly and absorb the first rains quickly, allowing them to overpower young crops that are still developing their initial root systems.
ga: Atsakeɔ jwɛi dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya ni amɛmu klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛyeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni miiya hiɛ lolo lɛ anɔ kunim.

english: Why do my harvested cassava roots start turning dark and spoiling after only two or three days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ duŋ ni egboɔ yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Unlike yams, cassava roots lack a thick protective skin. Once harvested, exposure to air causes rapid chemical breakdown and rotting within 48 to 72 hours unless processed or stored under moist soil.
ga: Nɔ ni tamɔɔɔ sweet potato lɛ, cassava shishifãi bɛ hewolo ni mli tse. Kɛji akpa lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa tsofa lɛ fiteɔ oya ni egboɔ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 48 kɛyashi 72 mli ja atsu he nii loo akɛto shikpɔŋ shishi ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli.

english: Why do seeds saved from my last hybrid maize harvest yield less corn than new store-bought seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ mi naagbee ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo fe dumɔwui heei ni ahe yɛ shwapo mli lɛ?

english: Store-bought hybrid seeds are produced through special cross-breeding for maximum yield in the first generation. Saving and replanting those seeds causes the next generation to lose that hybrid strength, resulting in lower yields.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛtsɔɔ crossbreeding krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni anyɛ ana yibiiwoo babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ abu he ni adu ekoŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha yinɔi ni baaba lɛ afite tsofa ni akɛfee tsofa lɛ hewalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ ni baa shi.

english: Can I plant other food crops like cassava or legumes together with my coconut trees, or must coconut grow alone?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmei tso lɛ atsu niyenii krokomɛi tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei? Aloo esa akɛ odu ŋmei pɛ?

english: You can plant other crops between coconut trees, especially when the coconuts are young. Intercropping coconut with crops like cassava, legumes, or plantain makes efficient use of land, provides early income, and helps suppress weeds while the trees mature.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu tsei krokomɛi. ŋmei tsei ateŋ Titri lɛ, kɛ́ ŋmei lɛ ji gbekɛ lolo. Akɛ ŋmei kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii fata he. loo dumɔwui ni akɛbaatsu shikpɔŋ lɛ he nii jogbaŋŋ Ha shika oya ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ jwɛi kɛjɛɔ shi yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Is it better for me to plant my entire farm with coconut trees at once, or should I add new seedlings in stages over time?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu miŋmɔ ni mikɛ ŋmeii tsei tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ shikome? Aloo esa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui heei afata he yɛ be kɛ bei amli? Beni be hoɔ lɛ

english: Planting all your trees at once gives you a uniform crop that flowers and fruits at the same time, making harvesting and selling easier. However, planting in stages allows you to spread out labor costs and seedling expenses if money is tight.
ga: Kɛ́ odu otsei lɛ fɛɛ yɛ be kome mli lɛ, ebaaha oná fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ be kome mli. Enɛ haa nikpamɔ kɛ nihɔɔmɔ feɔ mlɛo. Shi kɛlɛ, shweremɔ yɛ fãi srɔtoi amli lɛ haa onyɛɔ ogbɛɔ nitsumɔ kɛ dumɔwui akwɛmɔ he nyɔmɔwoo oshwaa kɛji shika faaa.

english: Can coconut flesh be turned into flour for baking bread and biscuits after extracting the milk?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ akɛ ŋmei loo afee blodo kɛ biskit ashikishaŋ beni ajie mliki lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yes, once you squeeze the milk out of mature coconut flesh, the leftover dry solid pulp can be dried and ground into coconut flour. This flour can be blended with wheat or cassava flour to bake bread, biscuits, and cakes.
ga: Hɛɛ, beni okɛ mliki lɛ shwieɔ ŋmei loo ni ahoo lɛ mli lɛ. Abaanyɛ agbi ŋmei loo ni egbi ni eshwɛ lɛ ni atsɔ ŋmei ashikiŋsha nɔ. Abaanyɛ akɛ ashikishaŋ nɛɛ afutu ŋmaa ashikishaŋ loo tapioca ashikishaŋ ni akɛshã blodo, biskit, kɛ keeki.

english: Why should I process my harvested crops into products like flour or powder instead of just selling them raw?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafee miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpa lɛ mafee nɔ ko, tamɔ ashikishaŋ loo powda, moŋ fe ni mahɔ̃ɔ amɛ ŋmɔŋ kɛkɛ?

english: Processing raw crops into flour or powder prevents post-harvest spoilage, extends their shelf life, and allows you to sell value-added products to bakers and shops for a much higher price than fresh raw produce.
ga: Nibii ni adu lɛ ŋmɔŋ ni afee lɛ ashikishaŋ loo powda yeɔ ebuaa ni etsĩɔ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ fitemɔ naa. Extend shelf life Ni ehaa onyɛɔ ohɔ̃ɔ onibii ni jara wa lɛ ohaa aboloofeelɔi kɛ shwapoi yɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ kwraa fe nibii ni afee ehee lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I process my cocoa beans at home to use as flavor in local drinks and foods?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafee cocoa ŋmeii yɛ shia koni mikɛtsu nii akɛ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ maŋ lɛ mli nibii ni anuɔ kɛ niyenii amli?

english: After drying your cocoa beans, you can roast them, remove the outer shells, and grind the inner nibs into a smooth cocoa paste or powder. This pure cocoa can be added to porridge, baked goods, or milk drinks for natural chocolate flavor.
ga: Beni ogbi cocoa ŋmeii lɛ Obaanyɛ oshã Jiemɔ kponɔgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ. Ni okɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse. Abaanyɛ akɛ nɛkɛ kookoo krɔŋŋ nɛɛ afata ŋmɔtɔ, nibii ni ashãa loo mliki nibii ni anuɔ lɛ ahe koni eha efee tsokolate ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli.

english: How do I know when a coconut is ready for drinking water versus when it is ready for oil and flour?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmei ko eshɛ he ni anuɔ? kɛ be mli ni fɔ kɛ ashikishaŋ lɛ eshɛ.

english: Young green coconuts (around 6 to 7 months old) contain maximum sweet water and soft flesh suitable for drinking. Mature brown coconuts (11 to 12 months old) have thick, hard meat containing high oil content, making them ideal for oil extraction and flour processing.
ga: Kokoobii bibii (ni eye aaafee nyɔji 6 kɛyashi 7) lɛ ji mɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ fe fɛɛ, ni amɛhe yɔɔ blɛoo kɛha nu ni anuɔ. Kokooi ni edara (ni eye nyɔji 11 kɛyashi 12) lɛ yɛ loo ni mli wa ni mli wa ni fɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa efeɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mu jiemɔ kɛ ŋmei nitsumɔ.

english: How long does a coconut seedling take from the day I plant it until it starts producing fruits?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani ŋmei dumɔwui jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ yibii?

english: Dwarf coconut varieties usually start fruiting within 3 to 4 years after planting, while traditional tall varieties take around 6 to 8 years to start producing fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii srɔtoi ni ji dwarf lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli beni adu amɛ sɛɛ, yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii srɔtoi ni yɔɔ blema lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 6 kɛyashi 8 dani amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi.

english: Will growing coconut trees drain all the nutrients from my soil and prevent other crops from growing nearby?
ga: Kokoo tsei ni miduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ni ehaaa ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi akwɛ̃. Growing nearby?

english: Coconut trees draw nutrients from the soil, but they do not ruin it if you feed the soil. Returning fallen coconut leaves and husks to the ground as organic mulch puts nutrients back into the soil for companion crops.
ga: Kokoo tsei jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ekpãŋ ehiɛ kɛji okɛ sũ ha lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei baa kɛ ŋmei ŋmɔji ni egbee shi lɛ ku sɛɛ kɛtee shikpɔŋ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ kɛha tsei ni fata he lɛ.

english: Can the solid waste left after processing coconuts and cocoa be eaten or fed to livestock?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ aye jwɛi ni eshwɛ yɛ ŋmei kɛ kookoo nitsumɔ sɛɛ loo akɛha kooloi?

english: Yes, leftover coconut pulp and cocoa pod husks are rich in fiber and nutrients. Dried coconut pulp can be eaten by humans as food flour or mixed into animal feed for pigs and poultry.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmei loo kɛ kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ mli fiber kɛ niyenii kpakpai babaoo yɛ mli. Adesai baanyɛ aye ŋmei loo ni egbi akɛ niyenii ashikishaŋ loo amɛkɛfutu kooloi aniyenii kɛha tsinai kɛ kooloi.

english: What causes some cocoa trees on my farm to produce pods with very rich flavor while others taste weak?
ga: Mɛni haa cacao tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli wa waa, yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu woɔ ŋmɔtɔ fioo?

english: Flavors in cocoa pods vary based on the cocoa variety planted, soil fertility, shade levels, and how well the beans are fermented and dried after harvest. Proper fermentation develops the deep, rich chocolate flavor.
ga: Nɔ ni yɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔji amli lɛ srɔtoi yɛ kookoo henɔ ni aduɔ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, bɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ, kɛ bɔ ni kookoo yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ kpamɔ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ afee lɛ ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsokolate lɛ mli ŋɔɔ ni mli kwɔ baa.

english: Maize leaves roll up during extreme heat as a natural defense mechanism to reduce their surface area, which helps the plant trap moisture inside and prevent drying out.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he lɛ aba shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ emli ni ehaaa egbi.

english: Sudden wilting in wet soil is usually caused by bacterial wilt or root rot. The disease clogs the plant's internal water transport tubes, preventing water from reaching the upper stems and leaves even though the roots are soaked.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa. Hela nɛɛ tsiɔ tso lɛ mli nu paipii lɛ anaa. Ehaaa nu shɛɔ tso lɛ shishi kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ahe, kɛji akɛ shishifãi lɛ ewo nu po.

english: Why are my pepper flowers falling off the plant before turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani ebatsɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant experiences extreme temperature changes, severe drought, or a shortage of essential soil nutrients like phosphorus and potassium needed to support fruit development.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ tso lɛ kɛ ehe wo hulutsoo tsakemɔi ni naa wa mli. hɔmɔ ni naa wa loo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni he hiaa kɛha aduawai adalɛ

english: Why do my young cocoa saplings die when I clear all the big trees off my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate intense direct sunlight because their root systems are not yet strong enough to handle extreme heat. They require protective shade trees or temporary nurse crops like plantains to cool the microclimate.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa lolo ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsu hulutsoo ni naa wa lɛ he nii. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo loo tsei ni kwɛɔ amɛhe nɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛha kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ bibioo lɛ mli ajɔ.

english: Cowpeas are legumes that fix nitrogen gas from the air and store it in small nodules on their roots. As the plant roots interact, this natural nitrogen acts as extra fertilizer for the neighboring maize crop.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni saa nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ ŋmeii bibii amli yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen nɛɛ baatsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fata he kɛha ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ.

english: Why do the stems of my vegetable plants turn black and burn when I place fertilizer right next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛshãa kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo amɛhe lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer contains concentrated mineral salts that draw moisture out of tender plant tissue if touched directly. Fertilizer should always be buried in a small ring or sideband a few inches away from the stem.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yɛ mineral salts ni mli eyi obɔ ni gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ amli kɛji akɛ amɛkpe tɛ̃ɛ. Esa akɛ afu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ ŋmeii bibii amli. Aloo sɛɛgbɛ ŋta lɛ kɛ ŋta lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko pɛ.

english: Why does my cassava crop grow tall and leafy, but produce very small roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai shi eyɛ shishifãi bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to potassium, the cassava plant spends all its energy producing leaves and stems instead of transferring starches down to grow large storage tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa fe nine kɛ akɛtoɔ potassium he lɛ. Kasava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ baai kɛ tsei ashishifãi. Mohu ɔ, mo ngɔ ngmlɛfia ɔ kɛ ya si konɛ e hyɛ ngmlɛfia agbohi nɛ a piɛɛ he ɔ.

english: Why should I buy fresh hybrid seeds instead of saving seeds from last season's harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui heei ni akɛfee hybrid lɛ moŋ fe ni makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ nyɛsɛɛ be ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ ato?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for uniform growth, pest resistance, and high yields. Saving seeds from a harvested hybrid crop causes those special traits to break down, resulting in weaker plants and lower yields in the next season.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛdara yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ. Nɔ ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni ehaa yibii babaoo baa Dumɔwui ni jɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome ni akpa lɛ amli lɛ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ baafite nakai sui lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why is it smart to plant a small demonstration plot of a new crop variety before planting my whole field with it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nilee yɔɔ mli akɛ madu tso hee ko he nɔkwɛmɔnɔ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko dani madu miŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: A small demonstration plot lets you test how a new crop behaves under your specific local soil, pest, and rainfall conditions without risking your entire farm's harvest if the variety struggles.
ga: Nɔkwɛmɔnɔ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko haa onyɛɔ okaa bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii heei tsuɔ nii yɛ omaŋ shikpɔŋ, tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ shihilɛi shishi lɛ okwɛ. ni okɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii ni afeɔ lɛ awo oshara mli kɛji tso henɔ lɛ kɛ naagbai kpe.

english: How can I tell if my orange-fleshed sweet potatoes are fully mature and ready to harvest underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-sweet potatoes ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Sweet potatoes are usually ready to harvest when the outer leaves begin to turn yellow and dry back, typically three to four months after planting, or when cut sample tubers dry rapidly without turning dark.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potatoes lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ je shishi amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi. Bei pii lɛ, aaafee nyɔji 3-4 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ. Aloo kɛ́ oofo nɔkwɛmɔnɔ yitso lɛ, ha egbi oya ni etsɔ duŋ.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to cut down a whole cocoa tree when only one branch looks sick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔfo cocoa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ be mli ni tso lɛ nine kome pɛ hela mɔ lɛ?

english: Diseases like Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus spread inside the entire tree before you can see symptoms on every branch. Cutting down the infected tree completely is necessary to stop the disease from spreading through root contact or insects to surrounding healthy cocoa trees.
ga: Helai tamɔ Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa tso lɛ mli fɛɛ dani onaa okadii yɛ tso lɛ nine fɛɛ nine nɔ. Ehe miihia ni afo tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ amli kwraa koni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã kɛtsɔ shishifãi loo kooloi ni akɛbaashɛ kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa trees turning yellow and swollen swellings appearing on the branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cocoa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ŋmeii ni efuu miije kpo yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: This is a key sign of Cocoa Swollen Shoot Disease, a viral infection spread by tiny insects called mealybugs. The virus weakens the tree's ability to transport water and nutrients, leading to yellowing leaves, swollen stems, and eventual tree death.
ga: Enɛ ji Cocoa Swollen Shoot Hela, ni ji hela ko ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he okadi titri. Atsɛɔ no akɛ ŋmeii. Virus lɛ haaa tso lɛ nyɛmɔ ni ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ aya lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ, tsei lɛ efuuɔ, ni naagbee lɛ tso lɛ gboɔ.

english: Why do small insects like mealybugs cause so much damage to a cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ mealybugs fiteɔ kookoo ŋmɔji babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Mealybugs feed on the sap of cocoa trees, but the main danger is that they carry and spread deadly plant viruses like swollen shoot disease from infected trees to healthy ones as they crawl around.
ga: Mealybugs yeɔ kookoo tsei amli nu lɛ. Shi oshara titri ni yɔɔ mli ji akɛ, amɛhiɛɔ tsei amli helai ni yɔɔ oshara tamɔ bud swollen disease kɛjɛɔ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ lɛ amli ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa beni amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa he fɛɛ he lɛ.

english: Can I immediately plant new cocoa seedlings in the exact spot where sick cocoa trees were cut down?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu kookoo dumɔwui heei yɛ he ni afo kookoo tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: It is risky to plant immediately because disease-carrying insects or infected root fragments can remain in the soil. You should clear the ground, wait a short period, and plant protective shade crops first to ensure the area is safe for new cocoa seedlings.
ga: Oshara ji dumɔ ni aduɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ejaakɛ kooloi bibii ni hiɛ helai loo shishifãi ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Esa akɛ ojie he ni oyɔɔ lɛ. Mɛɛ be kukuoo ko. ni odu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ klɛŋklɛŋ koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ he lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha kookoo dumɔwui heei.

english: When cocoa trees pass 25 to 30 years old, their yield naturally drops significantly, and they become more vulnerable to pests and diseases. If fertilizing and pruning no longer improve pod production, the farm needs to be cut down and replanted.
ga: Kɛ́ kookoo tso ko ye afii 25 kɛyashi 30 lɛ, eyibii lɛ baa shi kwraa yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ aba amɛnɔ waa kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afoɔ lɛ haaa tsɛŋemɔ helai afeemɔ aya hiɛ dɔŋŋ. Ehe miihia ni afo ŋmɔji amli ni adu ekoŋŋ.

english: What food crops can I safely plant on cleared land while waiting for new cocoa trees to grow?
ga: Mɛɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu yɛ he ko ni gbɛ yɔɔ shweshweeshwe be mli ni mimɛɔ ni cacao tsei heei akwɛ̃?

english: Plantain, cassava, and maize are ideal crops. Plantains provide vital shade to protect delicate young cocoa seedlings from the sun, while cassava and maize give you quick harvests for food and income during the early years.
ga: Plantains, cassava kɛ ŋmãa ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Plantains haa hulutsoo be ni he hiaa ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa haa onyɛɔ okpaa amɛ oya kɛha niyenii kɛ shika yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees yield fewer pods when all the big shade trees around them are cut down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ wooo yibii babaoo yɛ be mli ni tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ dara lɛ? Ani afo lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally thrive under moderate shade. Without shade trees, direct heat and hot winds stress the cocoa, cause soil moisture to dry out quickly, and attract harmful pests like capsids that ruin harvests.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ daa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛji tsei bɛ ni baaha hulutsoo tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ baaha kookoo lɛ aná haomɔ. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. ni egbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ capsids ni fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why does cutting off extra branches help my cocoa trees produce more cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso ni afolɔ ashwie shi krokomɛi lɛ baaye abua mi cacao tso lɛ ni ewo cocoa ŋmeii babaoo lɛ?

english: Pruning removes non-producing branches so the tree can direct its nutrients straight into growing pods. It also opens up the canopy to sunlight and airflow, reducing humidity that breeds fungal diseases.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni afolɔ mli lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni wooo yibii lɛ koni tso lɛ anyɛ atsɔɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛya tsei ni miida lɛ anɔ. Gbelemɔ hulutsoo be lɛ lolo koni onine ashɛ hulu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela baa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why is my cocoa tree producing plenty of flowers, but the small young pods dry up and drop off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo shi ŋmeii bibii lɛ miigbo ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: This is known as cherelle wilt. It happens when the tree lacks sufficient nutrients or soil moisture to feed all its young pods, forcing it to drop extra pods to keep the main tree alive.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ cherel ni shwieɔ shi. Ebaa beni tso lɛ bɛ niyenii loo shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha tso lɛ mli ŋmeii bibii lɛ fɛɛ aye abua lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii krokomɛi koni tso titri lɛ ahi shi.

english: What causes cocoa pods to turn black and rot during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in cool, damp, and overly humid weather. Water droplets from rain bounce the fungal spores from the soil or infected pods onto healthy pods.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni shwereɔ yɛ fɛ̃i, fɛ̃i, kɛ fɛ̃i shihilɛi ni mli edɔ fe nine lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Nu ni jɛɔ nugbɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ fungal spores kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: How many years does it take for a newly planted cocoa tree to start giving me pods?
ga: Afii enyiɛ eheɔ dani cacao tso ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ shishi ewoɔ ŋmeii?

english: Traditional cocoa varieties usually take 3 to 5 years to start bearing fruit, while improved hybrid varieties can start producing pods in as little as 2 to 3 years when given proper care and nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, blema kookoo henɔi lɛ heɔ afii 3 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kookoo henɔi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aje ŋmɔtɔ shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 pɛ mli kɛji akɛ akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni aha amɛ niyenii kpakpa.

english: Planting trees too close together causes them to fight for sunlight, water, and soil food, making them thin and weak. Overcrowded farms also trap damp air, which allows diseases to spread quickly between trees.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ akaŋshii baa kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ. Okwaafoi ni eyi obɔ lɛ hu mɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli efɔ. Enɛ haa hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei ateŋ oya.

english: Why do my cocoa trees need shade trees planted around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ abɔle mi-kokoo tso lɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees get scorched easily in full sunlight. Shade trees act like umbrellas, keeping the ground cool and moist while protecting young cocoa leaves from burning during hot weather.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ. Shade tsei tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ kookoo baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa tree leaves wither and fall off during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ gboɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During the Harmattan, dry winds pull water out of the tree faster than roots can drink it from the dry ground. Shedding leaves is the tree's natural way of saving water so it can survive until the rains return.
ga: Yɛ Harmattan beaŋ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tsei amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ nu toɔ. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ ahi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in wet and humid conditions. Water sitting on the pods lets the fungal spores grow, which rots the pod and ruins the beans inside.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. ni ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ mli Nu ni kpɛtɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe lɛ haa ŋmei mli ŋmeii lɛ daa. Enɛ haa pod lɛ fiteɔ ni efiteɔ kɔfe yibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: What causes yellow spots and dead, dry patches on my young cocoa shoots?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi ni egbi ni egboi ni yɔɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ baa?

english: This is usually caused by small pests called capsids or Akate. They bite into the soft stems and pods to suck out juices, releasing a liquid that burns and kills that part of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ capsids loo akates lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Amɛyeɔ tsei bibii kɛ tsei ashishifãi koni amɛnu nu lɛ. Ejieɔ nu ko ni shãa ni egbeɔ nakai tso lɛ fã lɛ.

english: Why do so many flowers fall off my cocoa tree without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo miiho kɛmiijɛ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: A cocoa tree produces thousands of flowers, but only a few turn into pods. Flowers drop naturally if tiny insects do not pollinate them, or if the tree is stressed by dry weather and poor soil food.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔii akpei abɔ. Shi fɔfɔi fioo komɛi pɛ tsakeɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii. Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe wooo mli, loo kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ.

english: Will cutting off unnecessary branches hurt my cocoa tree or reduce my yield?
ga: Ani tsei niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ baafite mi-kookoo tso lɛ loo ebaaha mi-cocoa tso lɛ yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi?

english: Pruning unnecessary or dead branches actually helps the tree. It directs energy into growing big pods and lets sunlight and air flow through the branches, which prevents diseases from taking hold.
ga: Niji ni he ehiaaa loo ni egboi ni aaafo lɛ baanyɛ aye abua tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Ebaaha hewalɛ aba koni ekɛha ŋmeii wuji ni miida lɛ niyenii. ni oha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ amli Enɛ baaye abua ni helai akaye nɔ.

english: How can I tell if my soil lacks the nutrients my cocoa trees need to grow well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa cacao tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When soil lacks nutrients, cocoa leaves often turn yellow, growth becomes slow, and the pods remain small or misshapen. Healthy soil produces deep green leaves and strong pod growth.
ga: Kɛ́ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, Cocoa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ. Dalɛ baafee blɛoo. ni ŋmeii lɛ dara lolo loo amɛyɛ su ni ejaaa Shikpɔŋ kpakpa haa baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ ni mli wa yaa hiɛ.

english: Why must I cover my wet cocoa beans with plantain leaves for a few days before drying them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ plantain baai haa kookoo ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ anɔ gbii fioo komɛi dani migbiɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the beans creates warmth for fermentation. This process kills the seed inside so it won't sprout, removes the harsh bitter taste, and creates the rich chocolate flavor and brown color buyers look for.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛha kɔfi yibii lɛ anɔ lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo baa kɛha ŋmɔlɔ. Nɛkɛ gbɛ nɛɛ gbeɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ koni amɛkakwɛ̃. Ejieɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni naa wa lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli ni ehaa tsokolate ŋmɔlɔ ni mli wa kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ lɛ baa.

english: Yellow leaves starting at the bottom of maize plants usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen. Maize needs nitrogen to stay green and grow well, so adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant maize on the same piece of land every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously drains the exact same nutrients out of the soil year after year. Rotating maize with beans, cowpeas, or groundnuts helps put nitrogen back into the soil naturally and stops crop diseases from building up.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa afi. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii, tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni ekpa tsei ahe helai ni buaa amɛhe naa lɛ

english: Weed seeds naturally sit in the soil ready to sprout at the first drop of rain. They grow fast to steal light and food, so clearing them early gives your young crops the water and nutrients they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ taraa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ kɛji klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ nɛ. Amɛdaraa oya koni amɛju la kɛ niyenii. No hewɔ lɛ, jiemɔ amɛ mra. Ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ aná nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara waa.

english: Cassava roots rot underground when water sits around them for too long or when a soil fungus attacks. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps extra water drain away so the tubers stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu hi shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ loo kɛ́ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tutua amɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu kroko ni fa lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni amɛná hewalɛ

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when the sun gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. Giving the plants consistent water at their roots keeps the flowers healthy so they can turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji hulu lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ waa mli lɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa ni amɛfeɔ tomato.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that suck juices from the leaves. Controlling these small pests early stops the leaves from twisting and keeps the plant producing peppers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Nibii bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ Enɛɛmɛi kɛjɛ shishijee Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba.

english: Why do insects attack my dried maize in storage even when the grains looked clean when I put them away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miitutua mi ŋmãa ni egbi yɛ nitoohe lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmãa lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ehe tse beni mikɛtoɔ lɛ moŋ?

english: Tiny insect eggs often hide inside the grain or in old storage sacks before you store them. Drying your maize properly in the sun until it is hard, and using clean, airtight bags or approved storage dust, stops insects from hatching and destroying your grain.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, akɛ kooloi bibii akui woɔ dumɔwui amli loo kotokui momoi amli. dani okɛto Abɛi ni agbiɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛtsɔ hulu la nɔ kɛyashi ebaawa ni okɛ vacuum ni he tse loo vacuum kotokui ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ akɛtoɔ lɛ atsu nii. Enɛ baatsi kooloi bibii anaa ni amɛkafite odumɔwui lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct, hot sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have big leaves that act like living umbrellas, giving the young cocoa plants the shade and cool air they need to survive their first few years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Enɛ haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do I have to train my yam vines to climb tall wooden sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsɔse mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ koni enyɛ ekwɔ tsei niji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the sunlight to make energy that feeds the tuber underground. Lifting the vines off the wet ground with tall sticks also prevents diseases from getting onto the leaves.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã hulutsoo be lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni ekɛ hewalɛ ni haa shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ hewalɛ lɛ aba. Wein tsei ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni efɔ kɛ niji ni kɛlɛ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni helai akabote baai lɛ amli.

english: When too many small shoots grow around one main plantain stem, they steal food and water from the main tree, making the plantain bunch small. Leaving only two or three strong shoots ensures you get big, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Beni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ lɛ Dalɛ babaoo ni bɔleɔ tso wulu kome he. Ebaaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, plantain tsei lɛ akui lɛ daraaa. Kɛ́ oshi tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha plantain tso agbo ni tsii aba.

english: Why do some of my pawpaw trees produce plenty of flowers for months but never bear any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi papaya tso lɛ ewo fɔfɔi nyɔji babaoo shi ewooo yibii ko pɛŋ lɛ?

english: Some pawpaw trees are male trees. They only produce flowers to pollinate other trees, but they will never produce fruit themselves. Having too many male trees together wastes space and nutrients in your field.
ga: Pawpaw tsei komɛi ji hii tsei. Amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛwo tsei krokomɛi amli pɛ. Shi amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwoŋ yibii. Kɛ́ oyɛ tsei hii babaoo lɛ, efiteɔ he ko kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ oyale mli.

english: Why is my plantain crop producing small fruit bunches when there are many shoots around the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ woɔ yibii bibii bibii lɛ? Beni ŋmeii babaoo ebɔle tso lɛ he lɛ

english: When a main plantain tree has too many young shoots growing around its base, they all fight for the same food and water in the soil. Cutting away extra shoots leaves the plant with enough energy to produce large fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui titrii lɛ yɛ ŋmeii babaoo ni miida yɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ, amɛwuɔ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛwoɔ yibii wuji.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which maize needs to build healthy green leaves. Applying manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help the maize leaves turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekɛ baai ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ aba. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with plenty of leaves, but the tubers underground stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii?

english: When crops are given too much nitrogen or planted too close together, they put all their energy into growing tall leaves instead of storing food in their underground roots.
ga: Kɛ tsei nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ loo adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatsu amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ he nii amɛkwɛ tsei ni yɔɔ baai kakadaji lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ

english: You should wait until the soil receives steady, deep rainfall over several days. Planting after just one light shower can cause seeds to dry up and die when the sun returns.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ baaná nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa gbii babaoo. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Saramɔ kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi kɛji hulu lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Planting crops too close together forces them to compete for limited sunlight, soil water, and nutrients, which results in thin stems and small yields.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la ni faaa, shikpɔŋ nɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off the stem without forming any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of pollinating insects can stress tomato plants, causing them to drop their flowers before the fruit can develop.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo ŋmeii ni haa ŋmeii baa lɛ ni bɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha tomato tsei lɛ aná nɔnyɛɛ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ daa.

english: Why are holes appearing on my cabbage leaves after a few weeks in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-cabbage baai lɛ anɔ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi ni mikɛhi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Caterpillars and pests feed on tender green leaves as the plant grows. Inspecting leaves early and using safe controls will stop insects from ruining the crop.
ga: Kplukai kɛ kooloi krokomɛi yeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ be mli ni tso lɛ miida lɛ. Baai lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Ni akɛ nibii ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haaa kooloi bibii akafite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungus that spreads in cold, damp, and overly shaded conditions. Trimming extra branch shade and removing infected pods keeps the crop dry and healthy.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni mli ejɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ fe nine. Pruning additional shade branches and removing infected pods. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbi ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I rely only on cocoa and instead grow other crops on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ mihe fɔ̃ɔ kookoo pɛ nɔ ni miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi yɛ nakai he lɛ nɔŋŋ moŋ?

english: Relying on a single crop like cocoa makes you vulnerable if pests, bad weather, or low prices hit. Growing food crops alongside cocoa spreads your income risk, gives you food to eat, and keeps money coming in while waiting for the cocoa harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kome tamɔ kookoo tsu nii lɛ, ekɛ ohe woɔ oshara mli kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai. kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni ehiii loo jara ni baa shi Niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ haa oshika ni onáa lɛ feɔ srɔtoi. feemɔ niyenii ni ayeɔ ni eye ebua ni shika aya nɔ aba be mli ni amɛmɛɔ kookoo ŋmaa lɛ.

english: Is it true that I can plant plantains or cassava together with my young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ manyɛ mikɛ kookoo tsei bibii akwɛ plantains loo cassava?

english: Yes, intercropping young cocoa with crops like plantain is very effective. The plantains provide necessary shade to shield young cocoa from harsh sunlight while giving you food and extra income from the same piece of land.
ga: Hɛɛ, kookoo bibii ni akɛ plantain tsei duɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa. Tsei bibii lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa koni akɛbu kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, amɛhaa niyenii kɛ shika kroko kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: Will planting two different crops together cause them to fight each other and ruin my harvest?
ga: Ani tsei enyɔ ni mikɛbaadu yɛ he kome lɛ baaha amɛkɛ amɛhe awuu ni amɛfite miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Not if you space them correctly. Different crops use nutrients from different soil depths and can actually help each other—for example, tall crops provide shade while ground crops keep the soil moist and reduce weeds.
ga: Dabi kɛji akɛ okɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ to he jogbaŋŋ. Tsei srɔtoi lɛ heɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli hei srɔtoi ni mli kwɔ lɛ amli ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye amɛbua amɛhe diɛŋtsɛ. Ákɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, tsei kakadaji haa hulutsoo. yɛ be mli ni tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehaa jwɛi lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die during the hot, dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender roots and leaves that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Without taller shade trees or plantains around them to trap moisture and block direct heat, the sun dries them out completely.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi kɛ baai bibii ni hulu la nyɛɛɛ ashɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo loo plantains bɛ he lɛ Koni emɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ekɛtsi dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Hulu lɛ baaha tsei lɛ agbi kwraa.

english: How do shade trees on my farm actually help my crops survive long periods without rain?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni haa miŋmɔ lɛ mli hulutsoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ?

english: Shade trees lower the temperature on your farm, prevent the sun from drying out the soil, and drop leaves that rot and turn into natural sponges that hold rainwater in the ground longer.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Tsi hulu la lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Ni enɛ haa baai lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli sponji ni yeɔ ebuaa ni nugbɔ nu lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot before they are ready for me to pick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ mafo lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungus that thrives in dark, overly wet, and crowded farms. Pruning extra branches and weeding allows air and sunlight to dry the pods and stop the fungus.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. ni ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ewo duŋ ni efɔ tsɔ Ni eyi obɔ kɛ gbɔmɛi. Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ ahe kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la haa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛkpaa ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why are the flowers on my crops falling off before they turn into actual fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛbatsɔmɔɔ anɔkwa yibii lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the plant is stressed by severe heat, lack of water, insect damage, or poor soil food. Giving the crop proper shade, water, and nutrients helps it hold onto its flowers to make fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, kooloi ni fiteɔ nii, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni esaaa lɛ hao tsei lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo, nu, kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ha tsei lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ fɔfɔi ahe koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoa trees turn yellow and fall off early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi oya lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that the tree is stressed, usually from a lack of nutrients in the soil, insect damage, or extreme drought. The tree drops leaves to save water and protect its main trunk.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miihao. Bei pii lɛ nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, koolooi ni fiteɔ nii, loo hɔmɔ ni naa wa. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ he.

english: Why does my farmland produce less yield every year even though I work just as hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiba shi daa afi lɛ? Ni mitsuɔ nii waa nakai nɔŋŋ?

english: Crops remove food from the soil every time you harvest them. Over time, the soil becomes tired and empty unless you return nutrients to it using manure, compost, or fertilizer.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni obaakpa amɛ. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee shoo ni ehiɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ja okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than the main crops I planted on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii titrii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are natural wild plants that are very strong and efficient at stealing water, sunlight, and soil nutrients before your crops can get them. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food they need to grow well.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni wa ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ aná. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellowing leaves starting at the tip usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps them green up again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: If I plant my cassava stem cuttings slanting instead of standing straight up, how does it affect the crop?
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei niji lɛ slanted moŋ fe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, Te ebaaná dumɔ nɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Planting cassava stems at a slight angle encourages the roots to spread out horizontally near the topsoil where nutrients are rich, making it easier for tubers to grow thick and be harvested cleanly.
ga: O-cassava tsei lɛ ni ooodu yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ fioo lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋwɛigbɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ he. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efeɔ mlɛo akɛ abaakpa yɛ gbɛ ni he tse nɔ.

english: Why do I have to tie my yam vines to tall wooden poles instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ sweet potato wain tsei fĩɔ tsei kakadaji ahe lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbee shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally climb to catch maximum sunlight, which their leaves use to feed the growing tuber below. Keeping the vines off the damp ground also protects them from rotting and leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Akɛ ebaai lɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ niyenii. Wein tsei ni akɛaatsi amɛhe kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ tsei ahe helai ahe.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the afternoon heat gets too extreme or when the plant doesn't get enough water. Extreme heat stresses the crop, causing it to drop blossoms to save energy until conditions improve.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ shwane mli latsaa lɛ fa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ haa tsei haoɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards like little cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are a common sign that tiny insects like thrips or mites are hiding under the leaves and sucking out the sap, causing the leaf tissue to twist and cup.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni afɔɔ namɔ akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛmiinu nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ tsɔɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ kɔɔpoo.

english: Groundnut plants form their pods underground. After the flower is pollinated above ground, the plant grows a peg that burrows into loose soil so the actual groundnuts can expand safely under the earth.
ga: Peanut tsei feɔ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Beni afee fɔfɔi lɛ pollen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmei ko ni atsa awo shikpɔŋ ni etse ehe lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji koni ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi shweshweeshwe.

english: What happens to my cowpea crop if heavy rains fall while the plants are flowering?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cowpea tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa be mli ni tsei lɛ miikwɛ?

english: Heavy rain during flowering can wash away pollen or knock blossoms off the stems before insects can pollinate them, leading to fewer bean pods forming on the plant.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ baanyɛ afɔ fɔfɔi loo fɔfɔii lɛ ahe dani kooloi bibii atsɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji bean pods fioo ko pɛ.

english: Why does my cassava crop stay green through dry spells while my maize wilts and dies?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ? Beni mi ŋmãa lɛ gboɔ ni egboɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava has deep root systems and can drop older leaves to conserve moisture, relying on stored food in its thick tubers to survive long dry periods until rains return.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni abaanyɛ ajie baai momoi lɛ ashwie shi koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli. Amɛkɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ niyenii ni ato yɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse lɛ amli lɛ nɔ koni amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Too many young shoots, called suckers, compete with the main plantain stem for food and water. Leaving only one or two strong suckers ensures the main stem grows a large, heavy cluster of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei bibii babaoo ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ kɛ plantain tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ adara ni etsɔ plantains akuu agbo ko ni tsii.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to build strong leaves. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers become very hard and woody if I leave them in the ground too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa waa ni efeɔ tso kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: As cassava plants mature past their ideal harvest time, the soft starch in the tubers converts into tough wood fibers to support the plant. Harvesting at the right age keeps the tubers soft and easy to cook.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ dara fe ŋmaakpamɔ be ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ Starch ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ tsɔɔ tso mli ŋmeii ni wa ni yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ. Kɛ́ akpa amɛ yɛ afii ni sa mli lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ hoomɔ waaa.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants before any tomatoes start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ dani tomato lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: High heat, dry soil, or too much nitrogen food can stress tomato plants, causing them to drop their blossoms to save energy rather than forming fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha tomato tsei lɛ aná haomɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tomato tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: This is typically caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in damp, shady conditions. Pruning excess branches to let in light and air helps protect the pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Kɛ́ afo tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ amli koni la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ebu tsei lɛ ahe.

english: Why does poultry manure make my crops grow faster than using plain soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ashishifãi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya fe shikpɔŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ?

english: Poultry manure acts as concentrated plant food rich in essential nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus. As it breaks down in the soil, it steadily feeds the crop roots so they can grow quickly.
ga: Kooloi ashishifã tsuɔ nii akɛ tso niyenii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus. Kɛ́ egbee shikpɔŋ lɛ Ebaaya nɔ eha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ niyenii koni amɛdara oya.

english: Why does the soil on my farm turn hard like a rock just three days after the rain stops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa tamɔ tɛ yɛ gbii etɛ sɛɛ beni nugbɔ lɛ kpa lɛ?

english: Soil low in organic matter loses water rapidly and bakes hard under the sun. Adding compost or leaving crop residues as mulch traps moisture and keeps the soil soft and spongy.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli faaa yɛ nɔ lɛ nu fiteɔ oya ni ewaa yɛ hulu la shishi. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he loo oshi tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ebaaha sũ lɛ ahi shi ni eha sũ lɛ afee bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmeii.

english: Why do I need to pile soil in mounds around my yam and cassava plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ muji toɔ mi yucca kɛ cassava tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Mounding creates soft, loose soil that makes it easy for tubers to expand, improves drainage so roots do not rot in standing water, and keeps the soil aerated.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ebaaha efee bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ, ni no baaha efee mlɛo aha bulb lɛ akɛ ebaagbɛ eshwa. improve drainage Enɛ ji koni shishifãi lɛ akafite kɛji amɛyɛ nu ni damɔ shi mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Plantain leaves have large surfaces that lose water quickly in hot weather. The plant intentionally lets older leaves dry out to conserve water in its main stem for survival.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ he ko ni da ni nu fiteɔ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Tsei tsɔɔ amɛyiŋ amɛhaa baai ni egbɔ lɛ agbiɔ koni nu ahi tso lɛ yitso lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why does my pepper plant stop producing new peppers even though it is still green and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ kpaɔ pepper heei feemɔ be mli ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔji lolo lɛ?

english: When pepper plants receive too much nitrogen food, they put all their energy into growing lush leaf branches instead of developing flowers and fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ aha pepper tsei niyenii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ tsei niji ni kwɛ̃ɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai

english: Why do my harvested yams start rotting so fast when stored inside my room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛto mitsu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams are living roots that breathe after harvest. High room temperatures and low airflow make them sweat and respire faster, creating a warm environment where rot fungi grow easily.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji shishifãi ni hiɛ ka ni muɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Tsu mli latsaa ni yaa hiɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ oya lɛ haa latsaa kɛ mumɔ baa oya. Feemɔ shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni ŋmei ni egbo lɛ baanyɛ ada yɛ mli mlɛo.

english: How do I know if the land I just cleared is suitable for planting yams?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji shikpɔŋ hee ni ajie lɛ lɛ sa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ?

english: Yams require deep, loose, well-drained soil so the tubers can expand easily. If your cleared land has heavy clay or too many rocks, the yam tubers will be small, misshapen, or rot easily in waterlogged soil.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. koni yitso lɛ anyɛ alɛɛ mli mlɛo Kɛji he ni ojie lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo tɛi babaoo tsɔ Sweet potato tubers lɛ ji bibii. ebɛ gbɛjianɔtoo mli loo egboɔ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ

english: Should I burn the bushes and debris after clearing my new farmland?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashã brɔshi kɛ sũ ni efite beni mijie tsei heei ni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: While burning clears the land quickly, it destroys rich organic matter and kills beneficial soil microbes. Clearing without burning and allowing weeds to rot naturally creates compost that feeds your soil for future crops.
ga: Shi kɛlɛ, la ni ashãa lɛ haa jɛmɛ tseɔ oya. Shi efiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni woɔ yibii lɛ, ni efiteɔ sũ mli nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ otsi jwɛi lɛ anaa ni oshãaa ni oha jwɛi lɛ fite yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa oshikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do crops on freshly cleared bush land sometimes look weak during their first month?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni agbele ehee lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Freshly cleared soil can still be hard or compacted beneath the surface, making it difficult for root systems to breathe and absorb nutrients until the ground is properly tilled and broken up.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ajie ehee lɛ mli wa lolo loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shishigbɛ. Enɛ haa ewaa ahaa shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaamu ni amɛŋɔ niyenii mli nibii kɛyashiɔ be mli ni akwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni akuɔ mli.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to produce energy for tuber growth under the ground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp soil to get maximum sun while protecting the plant from ground-borne leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tuber dalɛ. Staking woɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ koni ená hulu la babaoo yɛ be mli ni ebuɔ tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ baai helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my yam vines start turning yellow and dry up towards the end of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ yɛ be lɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: When yam vines naturally turn yellow and wither near the end of the season, it usually means the plant has finished growing and the underground tubers are fully mature and ready for harvest.
ga: Enɛ ji be mli ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgboɔ beni be lɛ naagbee lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ eshɛ shweremɔ he. Ni ŋmeii lɛ edara kwraa ni amɛfee klalo kɛha kpamɔ.

english: What causes my seed yams to start sprouting in storage before the planting season begins?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nitoohe lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃mɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi?

english: Seed yams sprout when stored in hot or humid conditions because the warmth signals to the seed that it is time to grow. Keeping them in a dry, cool, and shade-covered barn keeps them dormant longer.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dɔlɛ haa dumɔwu lɛ leɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ ekwɛ̃. Kɛ́ akɛ amɛ wo ŋmɔ ko ni mli egbi, ni mli ejɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛwɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why is it important to write down how much money I spend on clearing and seeds before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni maŋma shika ni mifiteɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔji kɛ dumɔwui adumɔ he lɛ ashwie shi dani midu lɛ?

english: Tracking your clearing, seed, and labor costs helps you understand your total investment so you can price your crops correctly at market time and ensure your farm makes a profit.
ga: Nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli, dumɔwui, kɛ nitsumɔ he nyɔmɔwoo sɛɛdii baaye abua bo ni onu shika ni okɛwo mli lɛ fɛɛ shishi. Bɔni afee ni onyɛ okɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo jara nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ jarayeli be mli. ni okɛ nɔmimaa aha akɛ oŋmɔ lɛ baaná sɛɛnamɔ.

english: Why do my young crops wilt quickly when the rain stops for just three or four days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ oya nɛkɛ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ kpaɔ gbii etɛ loo ejwɛ pɛ lɛ?

english: Young plants have shallow root systems that cannot reach deep underground water. Covering the soil around your crops with dried grass or leaves (mulching) keeps the moisture in the ground during short dry spells.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ he. Mulching around Okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi aha oŋmɔshi nibii ahe (mulching) yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli ni nu bɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow very tall and thin when planted under tall shade trees, but give very small harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo waa kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulutsoo lɛ ashishi lɛ? Shi ewoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ?

english: Crops stretch upward to search for missing sunlight instead of using their energy to develop strong stems, fruits, or underground tubers.
ga: Nibii ni adu lɛ shwie shi koni amɛtao hulu la ni elaaje lɛ. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ he wami tsuɔ ní kɛ peeɔ tsohi, yiblii, aloo tsohi nɛ a he wa.

english: How do I prevent insects in the soil from destroying root crops on newly cleared land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi sũ mli kooloi ni fiteɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ he ni mijie lɛ ehee lɛ naa?

english: New land often has active soil pests like grubs and termites. Turning the soil over to expose it to direct sunlight before planting helps kill off hidden pests naturally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hei heei lɛ yɛ sũ mli kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii. Kɛ́ otsake shikpɔŋ lɛ koni hulu la ashɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ dani odu lɛ, ebaajie tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How long does a young cashew tree take before it starts producing nuts?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani cashew tso bibioo ko jeɔ ŋmeii feemɔ shishi?

english: A cashew tree planted from seed usually starts bearing fruit 3 to 5 years after planting, but grafted trees can produce within 2 to 3 years. The tree reaches its full yield potential around its 8th to 10th year.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cashew tsei ni akɛ dumɔwui duɔ lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 5 sɛɛ, shi tsei ni akɛwo mli lɛ baanyɛ awo yibii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli. Tsei lɛ shɛɔ amɛ yibiiwoo he yɛ afii 8 kɛ 10 teŋ.

english: Can I plant maize or groundnuts between my young cashew trees, or will it damage them?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii ateŋ? Aloo ebaaha tso lɛ afite?

english: Yes, you can plant crops like maize, groundnuts, or beans between young cashew trees during the first 2 to 3 years. This helps you get food and income while the trees are small, as long as you leave enough space around the base of each cashew plant.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu nibii tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ cashew tsei bibii ateŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha oná niyenii kɛ shika yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ darako lɛ. Shii abɔ ni obaashi gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ cashew tso fɛɛ tso shishi lɛ,

english: Will cashew trees grow well on sandy soil, or do they only like rich forest soil?
ga: Ani cashew tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋã shikpɔŋ nɔ loo amɛbaasumɔ koo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ eyi obɔ kɛ nii babaoo pɛ?

english: Cashew trees are very resilient and can grow well in sandy or poor soils where many other crops fail. However, they need well-drained soil and will not survive in swampy or waterlogged land.
ga: Cashew tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛhiɔ shi waa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋã loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ nɔ. Shi kɛlɛ, tsei srɔtoi babaoo nyɛɛɛ atsu nii, amɛbiɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. ni enyɛŋ ehi shi yɛ ŋmeii loo hei ni nu damɔ shi yɛ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to cut off some of the lower branches of my growing cashew trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ cashew tso ni miida lɛ niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Cutting lower branches, known as pruning, helps the tree build a single strong trunk and allows light and air to pass underneath. This reduces diseases and makes it easier to walk through the farm during harvest.
ga: Ale tsei niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ hu akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afoɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni efeɔ tso kome ni mli wa. ni ehaa la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ shishi. Enɛ haa helai baa shi, ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ aaatsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ kpamɔ be mli.
