english: Why is it bad to plant my cashew trees very close together so I can fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu cashew tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni aná gbɛ babaoo lɛ?

english: When cashew trees are planted too close, their branches grow into each other and block sunlight. Without enough sun on the lower and inner branches, the trees produce far fewer flowers and nuts.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu cashew tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Niji lɛ feɔ ekome ni amɛtsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa. Kɛji hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shishigbɛ kɛ mligbɛ niji lɛ anɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baawo fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii fioo kwraa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cashew saplings turning yellow and drying up during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cashew tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cashew trees have shallow root systems and lose water quickly in severe heat. Placing dried grass or leaves around the base of the stem as mulch helps keep moisture in the soil until the roots grow deep.
ga: Cashew tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni kɛ́ hulutsoo be ni naa wa ba lɛ, nu lɛ fiteɔ oya. Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he Mulch ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ shishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ.

english: Why are my cashew trees dropping their flowers without producing any nuts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cashew tso lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni ekɛ ŋmeii ko baaa lɛ?

english: Flower drop is often caused by insect pests like thrips or dieback disease attacking the blossom stems. Prolonged dry spells or a lack of soil nutrients during the flowering stage can also cause flowers to dry up and fall.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ thrips loo blight ni tutuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ahe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi lɛ agbi ni amɛgbee shi.

english: What causes dark spots and sticky liquid on my fresh cashew shoots and young leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ kɛ nu ni shwieɔ shi yɛ mi-cashew ŋmeii heei kɛ baai bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ baa?

english: This is caused by sap-sucking pests, such as the tea mosquito bug. They puncture young leaves and shoots to feed, leaving wounds that turn black and dry out the new growth.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ helai ni nuɔ nu tamɔ tii ŋmeii. Amɛfoɔ baai bibii kɛ ŋmeii amli koni amɛye nii. Enɛ haa pilamɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni ehaa nɔ hee ni eda lɛ gbɛ́ɔ.

english: Should I pluck cashew fruits directly from the tree or wait for them to fall to the ground?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ cashews kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo mamɛ ni amɛgbee shikpɔŋ?

english: It is best to let cashew fruits fall naturally to the ground. When the fruit drops on its own, it means the nut inside is fully mature, dried, and of the highest quality for sale.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha cashew ŋmeii lɛ agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Kɛ aduawai lɛ diɛŋtsɛ gbee shi Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa, egbi ni ehi jogbaŋŋ fe fɛɛ ni abaanyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ.

english: Why does bushfire destroy cashew farms so easily, and how can I protect my trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli la fiteɔ cashew ŋmɔji lɛ mlɛo nɛkɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mitsei lɛ ahe?

english: Cashew leaves and nuts contain natural oils that ignite very quickly when hot. Creating wide firebelts by clearing all weeds and dry bushes around the perimeter of your farm before the harmattan season helps block fires.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli fɔji ni shãa oya waa kɛji edɔ lɛ yɛ cashew baai kɛ ŋmeii amli. Bɔɔ la gbɛ ni da kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle ohe kɛ brɔshi ni egbi lɛ fɛɛ ni oootsi lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ oŋmɔ lɛ wo husu naa dani harmattan be lɛ aba lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni la lɛ akatswa.

english: How do I know if my land is suitable for growing cocoa before I start planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha kookoo ŋmɔ dani mibɔi ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ?

english: Cocoa trees need deep, well-drained soil that holds moisture without staying soggy. If your soil is too sandy, rocky, or waterlogged, the roots cannot spread properly, causing the cocoa trees to struggle and die.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni baanyɛ ahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni ŋmɔtɔ akafee amɛ. Kɛji akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋã, tɛi, loo nu eyi mli obɔ tsɔ. Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa kookoo tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do crops grow very well on my neighbor's farm but refuse to grow on my land nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ mli shi amɛkpooɔ akɛ abaadu yɛ mishikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Soil conditions like depth, underground rock layers, water drainage, and nutrient levels can change drastically even over short distances. Your neighbor's soil might hold water and nutrients better than yours.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shihilɛ tamɔ emlibotemɔ, tɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi, nu ni hoɔ, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Ebaanyɛ etsake kwraa yɛ gbɛ kuku po nɔ. Ekolɛ okutsoŋnyo lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ ahi nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ mli jogbaŋŋ fe onɔ̃ lɛ.

english: What are the signs that my cocoa trees are not doing well in my soil?
ga: Mɛni ji okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ mi cacao tsei lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ?

english: If your cocoa trees remain stunted, turn yellow, drop their leaves prematurely, or fail to produce pods after a few years, it is a strong sign that the soil or environment is unsuitable for cocoa.
ga: Kɛji akɛ o-cocoa tso lɛ egbɔjɔ lɛ, ebaatsɔ ŋmɔŋ Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi oya loo enyɛŋ ewo ŋmɔŋ yɛ afii fioo komɛi asɛɛ. Eji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ shikpɔŋ loo shihilɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ esaaa kɛha kookoo.

english: What causes young crop seedlings to stop growing after I plant them in the field?
ga: Mɛni haa dumɔwui bibii lɛ kpaɔ amɛdalɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Seedlings usually stop growing if their roots cannot penetrate hard soil, if the soil lacks key nutrients, or if poor drainage causes water to gather around the roots and starve them of oxygen.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ kpaɔ dalɛ kɛji amɛshishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ abote shikpɔŋ ni wa mli. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa Aloo nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa nu buaa ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ faaa.

english: If my land cannot grow cocoa successfully, what other crops can I try instead?
ga: Kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ kookoo jogbaŋŋ lɛ Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka tso kroko akwɛ yɛ esɛɛ?

english: If cocoa fails, hardy fruit crops like citrus (oranges or lemons), oil palm, or cashew are great alternatives because they tolerate a wider range of soil conditions and temporary dry spells better than cocoa.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii lɛ Hardy yibii ni aduɔ tamɔ citrus (orange loo lemon), oil palm loo cashew nuts hu ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ amɛŋmɛɔ shikpɔŋ shihilɛi srɔtoi babaoo kɛ be kukuoo mli hɔmɔ shihilɛi ahe gbɛ fe kookoo.

english: Is citrus farming a profitable choice for a farmer in Ghana?
ga: Ani citrus okwaayeli ji gbɛ ni sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he kɛha okwaafoi ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ?

english: Yes, citrus farming is very beneficial because there is constant local demand for fresh fruit and juice. Once established, citrus trees can produce reliable yields and income for decades.
ga: Hɛɛ, citrus okwaayeli he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa ejaakɛ abiɔ maŋ lɛ mli aduawai kɛ nu heei be fɛɛ be. Kɛ adu Citrus tsei lɛ baanyɛ aha nibii ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ kɛ shika ni anáa afii nyɔŋmai abɔ.

english: How many years does a citrus tree take to start giving fruit after planting?
ga: Afii enyiɛ eheɔ dani ŋmei tso ko jeɔ yibii womɔ shishi beni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Grafted citrus seedlings usually start bearing fruit within 2 to 3 years, whereas seedlings grown directly from seed take much longer, usually around 5 to 7 years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, citrus dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli, yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui ni jɛ dumɔwui amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ heɔ be babaoo. Bei pii lɛ, aaafee afii 5 kɛyashi 7.

english: What kind of conditions do citrus crops need to thrive?
ga: Mɛɛ shihilɛi he hiaa citrus tsei koni amɛshwere?

english: Citrus trees need plenty of direct sunlight, warm weather, and soil with good drainage so water flows away easily after heavy rain.
ga: Orange tsei lɛ hia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ, kɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Nu hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ.

english: How can an agricultural extension officer help me choose the right crops for my field?
ga: Te okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko baanyɛ aye abua mi tɛŋŋ ni mahala ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Extension officers inspect your farm land, check the soil type and water conditions, and recommend specific crops that are proven to grow well in your exact location.
ga: Extension nitsulɔi lɛ baakwɛ he ni oduɔ nii yɛ lɛ. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ henɔ kɛ nu lɛ shihilɛ. ni otsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ ni ana akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ he pɔtɛɛ ni oyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Can I replace cocoa trees that are failing with a different fruit crop like citrus?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ aduawai tso kroko, tamɔ ŋmei ato cacao tso ni efite lɛ najiaŋ?

english: Yes, removing struggling cocoa trees and switching to citrus is a practical farm strategy. Different crops draw nutrients differently, which allows you to make productive use of land that failed with cocoa.
ga: Hɛɛ, cacao tsei ni miiwuu lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛyaa ni akɛ citrus baaye amɛ najiaŋ lɛ ji okwaayeli gbɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ shikpɔŋ ni hɔmɔ yeɔ kookoo lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and dry up when I cut down all the large trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ mifolɔ tsei wuji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to intense heat and wind. Large trees provide shade and keep the air humid, acting like a protective blanket until the young cocoa plants grow strong enough to withstand direct sunlight.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ latsaa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he waa. Tsei wuji haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni cacao tso bibioo lɛ daa ni ewaa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ edamɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Why do my pepper plant flowers drop to the ground without producing any peppers during hot spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni ekɛ pepper ko baaa yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When heat or drought becomes too severe, pepper plants shed their flowers to conserve water and survive. Keeping the soil consistently moist during hot weeks encourages the plant to retain its blooms and produce fruit.
ga: Kɛji latsaa loo hɔmɔ lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ otsii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ efɔfɔi kɛ eyibii lɛ amli.

english: Why do the leaves on my yam vines turn yellow and fall off after heavy rain leaves standing water on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ? Baa ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Crop roots need oxygen in the soil to breathe. When water sits flooded on the field without draining, the roots drown, preventing the plant from pulling up nutrients and causing the foliage to turn yellow.
ga: Tse shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nu eyi ŋmɔ ko mli ni nu bɛ mli lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni no haaa tso lɛ aná niyenii kpakpai. ni eha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ.

english: Will leaving weeds around my cassava for a few weeks really reduce the size of the roots I harvest?
ga: releasing weeds around Ani mi-cassava lɛ ni mikɛtoɔ otsii fioo komɛi lɛ baaha shishifãi ni mikpaa lɛ aba shi diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes. Weeds compete directly with cassava for soil nutrients, sunlight, and water. If you neglect weeding during the early growing months, the cassava plant spends its energy fighting off competitors instead of swelling its tubers underground.
ga: Hɛɛ. Jwɛi kɛ ŋmei yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, hulu la kɛ nu. Kɛji oku ohiɛ oshwie amɛ nɔ yɛ jwɛi ni aduɔ lɛ shishijee nyɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwuɔ eshiɔ akaŋshilɔi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha eshishifãi lɛ afuu yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Soil harbors fungal spores and dampness that easily infect tomato fruit when they touch the wet ground. Staking lifting the vines keeps the crop dry, exposed to fresh air, and safe from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni haa tomatoi lɛ náa helai oya kɛji amɛyashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei wo wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gĩɔ. Na kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe

english: Why is it helpful to cover the bare soil around my crops with dry grass or dead leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi No hewɔ lɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ni jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni egboi yɔɔ mli lɛ baa mli.

english: Covering soil with dry vegetation acts like an insulator that blocks hot sunlight from evaporating water out of the dirt. It keeps root zones cool, conserves moisture, and eventually decomposes into natural plant food.
ga: Tsei ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni tsiɔ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ naa, ni ehaaa nu akajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ. Kwɛmɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ ahi shi ni yɛ naagbee lɛ, efite ni etsɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii

english: Pale yellow lower leaves indicate that your soil is running low on nitrogen, a vital nutrient plants need for healthy vegetative growth. The plant starves its older leaves to feed newer growth, signaling it needs fertilizer or organic manure.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei taoɔ koni tsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ Tso lɛ baagbe baai ni egbɔ lɛ hɔmɔ koni ekɛha tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii. Kɛtsɔ okadi ni etsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli he miihia lɛ nɔ.

english: What happens to my corn yield if I plant four or five seeds in the exact same hole?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ejwɛ loo enumɔ yɛ bu kome mli?

english: Planting seeds too closely causes the crowded plants to fight one another for water, light, and soil minerals. The result is tall, weak stalks that produce very small cobs or no corn at all.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei ni gbɔmɛi babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ abɔi nu, la kɛ shika tsuru ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tso kakadaŋŋ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ ŋmãa bibii kwraa loo nɔ ko kwraa bɛ mli.

english: Why does my maize crop grow much better on land where I planted groundnuts the previous season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ kwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni midu mi-peanuts lɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that extract nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil through their root system. When maize follows groundnuts, it feeds on the nutrient enrichment left behind in the soil.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Beni Abɛi Nyiɛɔ Abɛi Sɛɛ Ebaaye niyenii ni eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my garden eggs grow small and bitter when the soil gets hard and packed down around their roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ waa yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Compacted soil makes it difficult for roots to spread out and absorb water and nutrients efficiently. Loosening the earth around the base allows air and moisture to penetrate so the crop can grow sweet, plump fruits.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa ewaa ahaa shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaajara nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii jogbaŋŋ ni amɛŋɔ amɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishitoo lɛ he lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ boteɔ mli. Koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ yibii ni ŋɔɔ ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my maize crops get sick easily even when I spray them with chemical medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ hela mɔɔ lɛ oya lɛ? Namɛi hu wo tsofai amli?

english: Just like humans, crops get sick when they are weak. If you feed your soil with good manure or compost early on, the plants build up their own natural strength to fight off diseases, meaning you won't need to waste money on medicine later.
ga: tamɔ adesai nɔŋŋ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ hela kɛji egbɔjɔ. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai ha shikpɔŋ lɛ mra lɛ, Tsei feɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛi ni amɛkɛwuɔ ashiɔ helai. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe ehiaaa ni ofite shika yɛ tsofafeemɔ he yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Is it true that feeding my crops well from the start can prevent disease?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ tsei ni ayeɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛ shishijee lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ helai anaa diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, crops that get good soil nutrients from the day they are planted grow strong defense systems. When a plant is well-nourished, it naturally resists pests and sickness on its own.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni náa sũ mli niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛɔ gbi ni adu amɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo ko ni mli wa. Kɛji akɛ aha tsei niyenii jogbaŋŋ lɛ Ebaate shi ewo tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai yɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehe.

english: Why do my cassava plants look weak and yellow even though I cleared all the weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikwɛɔ lɛ moŋ? Akɛ ajie jwɛi lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ jɛmɛ?

english: Weed control is good, but crops also need proper food in the soil. Without rich organic matter or fertilizer, plants become malnourished and susceptible to crop diseases.
ga: Jwɛi nɔkwɛmɔ hi. Shi niyenii ni sa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo bɛ Tsei lɛ amli lɛ, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli ni tsei ahe helai baanyɛ aba amɛnɔ oya.

english: Is it better for me to invest in plant medicine or good soil preparation before planting?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oookɛ shika awo tsei ahe tsofa mli loo ooosaa shikpɔŋ kpakpa dani odu?

english: It is much better to invest in good soil care and proper feeding early. Plants that are taken care of from the start grow strong enough that you rarely need to buy expensive chemical treatments.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ shika awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ kpakpa kɛ niyenii ni sa mli mra. Tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shishijee lɛ baakwɛ̃ waa bɔ ni sa ni ehe ebahiaŋ ni ohe tsofai ni jara wa.

english: Does the quality of water I use to water my tomatoes really affect their health?
ga: Ani bɔ ni nu ni mikɛwoɔ mi-tomato lɛ mli lɛ hi ha lɛ saa amɛ hewalɛnamɔ he?

english: Yes, plants need clean water just like farm animals do. Using dirty or contaminated water can stress your crops and introduce diseases directly into their roots.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsei he hiaa nu ni mli tse tamɔ ŋmɔ mli kooloi pɛpɛɛpɛ. Nu ni mli ewo muji loo nu ni mli ewo muji ni okɛaatsu nii lɛ baanyɛ aha onibii lɛ afee nɔ ni haoɔ ni ekɛ hela aba shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt and catch diseases when the dry season hits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni helai yeɔ amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Water allows plants to carry food from the soil into their stems and leaves. When crops lack clean water, they get weak and stressed, making it very easy for diseases to attack them.
ga: Nu yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛyaa amɛshishifãi kɛ baai amli. Kɛ tsei bɛ nu ni mli tse Tso lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni ebaahao. Ekɛ helai baa mlɛo waa.

english: How often should I water my vegetable crops to keep them from getting sick?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mawo mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ nu koni hela akamɔ amɛ?

english: Crops need a steady supply of clean water to maintain their strength. Keeping the soil consistently moist—without drowning the roots—helps plants build thick stems and healthy leaves that resist diseases.
ga: Nu ni mli tse ni anáa daa lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛná hewalɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni shishifãi lɛ shwieee shi Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ baai ni wa ni helai nyɛŋ amɛye amɛnɔ.

english: Why do crops grown in poor soil suffer more pest attacks than crops in fertile soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo tutuaa tsei ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ lɛ fe tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Plants growing in poor soil lack the energy to protect themselves. When a crop is properly fed and cared for, its tissues become tougher, making it harder for pests to damage it.
ga: Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaabu amɛhe. Kɛji akɛ ayeɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ ni akwɛɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Ehe fãji lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa. Ehaa ewaa kɛhaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akɛ amɛbaafite

english: Why do young seedlings need extra attention compared to older plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei bibii biɔ kwɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ ko kɛ akɛto tsei bibii ahe lɛ?

english: Young plants are like growing children; if you protect them, water them well, and feed them early, they build a strong body that keeps them healthy and productive all the way to harvest.
ga: Tso bibioo tamɔ gbekɛ ni miida. Kɛji obu amɛhe Nu lɛ Nu amɛ jogbaŋŋ. ni oha amɛ niyenii mra. Amɛfeɔ gbɔmɔtsei ni he wa ni haa amɛnáa hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ be lɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: Why are my neighbor's crops healthy without spraying, while mine keep dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ tsei lɛ yɔɔ hewalɛ ni akɛ tsofa shwieee nɔ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni mitsei lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboiɔ lɛ?

english: Your neighbor is likely focusing on proper plant care early on by building up rich soil and giving enough clean water. Good basic care builds strong plants that do not depend on chemical medicines to survive.
ga: Esa akɛ okutsoŋnyo lɛ afee lɛ oti akɛ ebaakwɛ otsei lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ mra. Kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ni ebɔɔ kɛ nu ni mli tse ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛhaa lɛ nɔ. Shishijee kwɛmɔ kpakpa baaha tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni tsofai ni akɛ tsofai tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ he ehiaaa koni amɛhi shi.

english: Is the seed rice I get from the extension office different from the rice I buy at the market to cook and eat?
ga: Ani ŋmãa ni anáa kɛjɛɔ Extension Office lɛ yɛ srɔto yɛ ŋmãa ni aheɔ kɛjɛɔ jara nɔ koni ahoo lɛ he?

english: Yes. Market rice is meant only for eating and may not grow well or could carry diseases. The seed rice provided by officers (foundation seed) is specially selected, treated, and tested to produce healthy plants with high yields when you plant it.
ga: Hɛɛ. Jarayeli ŋmãa ji niyeli pɛ ni ekolɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ jogbaŋŋ loo ekɛ hela baa. Ahala ŋmãa ni onukpai (shishijee dumɔwui) saa lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ, atsu he nii ni aka amɛ akwɛ koni amɛwo tsei ni he wa, ni woɔ yibii babaoo kɛ́ adu.

english: Why do my crops produce a smaller harvest when I plant seeds saved from last year's hybrid harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa ŋmaa bibioo beni miduɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee ekome lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred from two different parent plants to give maximum strength and yield in their first generation. When you save and replant seeds from that harvest, the plants lose those special qualities, resulting in mixed growth and lower yields.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ fɔɔ kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔi tsei srɔtoi enyɔ amli koni amɛná hewalɛ babaoo kɛ yibiiwoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Kɛji okɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ nakai kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ to ni okɛdu ekoŋŋ Tso lɛ baafite nakai nibii krɛdɛɛi lɛ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni futuɔ kɛ yibiiwoo baa shi.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean your maize plant is hungry for nitrogen. When the soil lacks nutrients, the plant starves its older bottom leaves to feed the younger growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn tso lɛ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii bɛ lɛ Tso lɛ baagbe shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ hɔmɔ koni ekɛha baai bibii ni miida yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without producing any fruits during hot periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers need mild temperatures and humidity to pollinate. When the heat gets too intense, the pollen dries out and dies, causing the plant to shed the flowers to save its energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi biɔ hulutsoo kɛ latsaa ni sa kɛha pollination. Kɛ́ latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, pollen lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni egboɔ. Enɛ haa tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Weeds are wild native plants that have adapted over centuries to survive harsh soil conditions. They immediately capture water and nutrients faster than domesticated crops, which need extra care to establish root systems.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni etsake amɛhe yɛ afii ohai abɔ ni eho lɛ amli koni amɛhi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa nɔ. Amɛmɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe shia tsei, ni biɔ hiɛdɔɔ babaoo koni amɛto shishifãi ahe gbɛjianɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I plant my crops in straight rows instead of scattering the seeds across the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Planting in straight rows ensures each crop has equal access to sunlight, water, and soil nutrients without crowding. It also makes weeding, applying fertilizer, and harvesting much easier for you.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ekɛ ehe wooo mli. Ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ hu feɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa bo.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer pods when my farm has too many shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmɔtɔ fioo ko pɛ yɛ be mli ni miŋmɔ lɛ mli tsei babaoo ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ?

english: While cocoa needs some shade when young, too much shade creates high moisture and dark conditions where fungal diseases like black pod thrive. It also prevents the trees from getting enough sunlight to bloom properly.
ga: Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, hulutsoo he miihia Cocoa kɛ́ eji gbekɛ. Shi hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa kɛ shihilɛi ni mli ewo duŋ baa. he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai diji baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ lɛ Etsiɔ tso lɛ hu naa koni ekaná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo fɔfɔi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Planting cassava continuously on the same plot drains the specific nutrients that cassava needs from the soil. Rotating crops helps the soil recover its fertility and prevents root diseases from building up in the earth.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni aduɔ ŋmei be fɛɛ be lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni ŋmei he hiaa lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni enáa ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ, ni ehaaa shishifãi ahe helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot underground when there is heavy rainfall for a long period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When excess rain fills all the space in the soil, the roots drown, rot, and become food for destructive soil fungi.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ babaoo ni eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛgboiɔ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips, aphids, or whiteflies feeding on the sap underneath the leaves, or by a virus carried by these insects that distorts plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips, aphids, loo whiteflies ni yeɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ hiɛɔ ni fiteɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Can I grow cotton on my farm here in Ghana, and what kind of weather does the plant like?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu odonti yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ Ghana biɛ? Ni mɛɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ nɛkɛ tso nɛɛ sumɔɔ?

english: Yes, cotton grows very well in Ghana, especially in drier regions like Northern Ghana. The plant thrives in hot weather with plenty of sunshine and needs a dry period when the pods open so the fluffy cotton does not get damaged by rain.
ga: Hɛɛ, kotoku kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ waa yɛ Ghana. Titri lɛ, yɛ hei ni nu bɛ tamɔ Ghana kooyigbɛ lɛ, tso lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ hulu la babaoo mli. Ni ehe miihia ni ená be ni ekɛgbi beni ŋmeii lɛ gbeleɔ amɛhe lɛ. Bɔni afee ni nugbɔ lɛ akafite ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse lɛ.

english: How does the cotton plant turn from a simple flower into that soft white material we harvest?
ga: Odonti tso lɛ tsake kɛjɛ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo mli Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ebafeɔ nibii yɛŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni wɔkpaa lɛ?

english: After the cotton flower blooms and drops off, it leaves behind a small green pod called a boll. Inside this pod, seeds grow wrapped in fine fibers; as the pod matures and dries out, it splits open naturally to reveal the fluffy white cotton.
ga: Beni ŋmɔtɔ fɔfɔi lɛ etse ni amɛgbee shi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ baashwɛ. Atsɛɔ lɛ bɔɔlu, yɛ nɛkɛ pod nɛɛ mli lɛ, dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ ni akɛ tsɔji bibii ebɔ he. Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii lɛ dara ni amɛgbi lɛ Ebaajara mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ejie ŋmeii yɛŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ kpo.

english: Why do my cotton pods spoil or go moldy if rain falls on them right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cotton ŋmɔji lɛ fiteɔ loo amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ dani akpa kpamɔ lɛ?

english: When mature cotton pods open, the dry fibers and seeds inside absorb rainwater like a sponge. This excess moisture creates a damp environment where mold rapidly grows, which ruins the lint quality and spoils the seeds.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii momo lɛ gbeleɔ ŋmɔji ni egbi kɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ nugbɔ nu tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine nɛɛ haa shihilɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Fuji lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya. Enɛ baafite fɔmɔ kotoku lɛ mli ni ebaafite dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Does the cotton plant store its oil in its leaves and stem, or only in the seed?
ga: Ani ŋmɔtɔ tso lɛ toɔ fɔ yɛ ebaai kɛ eshishifãi amli loo ekɛtoɔ edumɔwui pɛ amli?

english: The plant produces and concentrates its oil almost entirely inside the seeds. The leaves and stems use sunlight to make energy, but the plant sends that energy to the seeds, storing it as oil to nourish the next generation of plants.
ga: Tsei feɔ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ mu fɛɛ ni yɔɔ amɛdumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ ni amɛbuaa naa. Baai kɛ tsei lɛ kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ hewalɛ. Shi tso lɛ kɛ nakai hewalɛ lɛ yaa dumɔwu lɛ nɔ. ni akɛtoɔ akɛ fɔ koni akɛha tsei ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ayinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii

english: People tell me we can get oil from cotton seeds, but isn't cotton just grown for making cloth?
ga: Mɔ ko kɛɛ mi akɛ wɔbaanyɛ wɔná fɔ kɛjɛ kotoku dumɔwui amli. Shi ani jeee akɛ aduɔ kotoku koni akɛfee mama kɛkɛ?

english: Cotton is actually a dual-purpose crop. While the soft white fibers are spun into thread to make fabric, the seeds left behind contain a lot of natural oil that can be squeezed out to make cooking oil and soap.
ga: Odonti ji tso ko ni tsuɔ yiŋtoi enyɔ ahe nii diɛŋtsɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ atsɔ tsɔji yɛŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ anɔ afee mama moŋ, shi adebɔɔ mli fɔji babaoo yɛ dumɔwui ni eshwɛ lɛ amli. ni abaanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ mli ni akɛfee fɔ kɛ samla

english: Why do crop seeds like cotton or groundnuts contain so much oil inside them in the first place?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ fɔ babaoo yɛ amɛmli yɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Plants pack oil into their seeds as a dense store of food and energy. When the seed drops into the soil and germinates, it uses this stored oil as fuel to sprout roots and push its first leaves up into the sunlight.
ga: Tsei kɛ fɔ toɔ amɛdumɔwui lɛ amli koni ekɛ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ ni fa babaoo aba. Beni adu dumɔwui lɛ awo shikpɔŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ. Ekɛ mu ni ato nɛɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ tsofa ni ekɛwoɔ shishifãi amli ni ekɛtsiɔ klɛŋklɛŋ baai lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛyaa hulu la lɛ mli.

english: What can I do with crop seeds after harvest besides keeping them to plant next season?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee kɛ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ? Kɛfata he lɛ, akɛtoɔ koni adu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Many crop seeds can be processed into valuable household products. For instance, seeds from cotton, groundnuts, sunflower, or oil palm can be crushed to produce edible oil, while the leftover seed cake makes nutritious feed for livestock.
ga: Abaanyɛ afee dumɔwui srɔtoi babaoo ni afee shia nibii ni jara wa. Akɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmei, hulutsoo loo mu tso dumɔwui anɔ atsɔ mli koni aná mu ni ayeɔ. yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ haa kooloi lɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: Is it possible for a local farmer like me to extract oil from my seeds, or do I need a big city factory?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ maŋ lɛ mli okwaafonyo ko tamɔ mi baanyɛ ajie fɔ kɛjɛ midumɔwui lɛ amli? Aloo nitsumɔhe ko he miihia mi yɛ maŋtiase wulu ko mli?

english: You do not need a large factory to start. Local farming groups can use simple mechanical screw presses or small motorized expellers to crush seeds and extract oil right in the community.
ga: Nitsumɔhe wulu ko he ehiaaa bo koni onyɛ oje shishi. Akutsoŋ okwaafoi akui baanyɛ amɛkɛ skru tsɔnei ni yɔɔ mlɛo loo tsɔnei bibii ni akɛ tsɔne tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛshwieɔ dumɔwui amli lɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛjie fɔ kɛjɛ akutso lɛ mli.

english: How does using a simple machine for seed crushing help me more than trying to press oil by hand?
ga: Kɛtsɔ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ dumɔwui anɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo nɔ lɛ, Te eyeɔ ebuaa mi tɛŋŋ fe mu ni akɛ niji shwieɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seed coats are tough, and oil is tightly trapped inside the seed cell walls. Processing machines apply intense, steady mechanical pressure that squeezes out far more oil than human hands ever could, saving you time and preventing wasted yield.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ahe nɔ lɛ wa. ni fɔ lɛ ŋmɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli wala yibii lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ. Mshinii ni yɔɔ nifeemɔ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli lɛ kɛ tsɔne mli hewalɛ ni naa wa ni yaa nɔ daa tsuɔ nii. ni shwieɔ mu babaoo fe bɔ ni adesa nine baanyɛ ashɛ he lɛ Ehaa okɛ obei tsuɔ nii ni ehaa nibii ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ lɛ ni elaajeɔ lɛ naa.

english: Are there crops I can plant that give me more than one product to sell at market?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi yɛ ni manyɛ madu ni woɔ nibii ni fe ekome ni mikɛhɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ?

english: Yes, crops like cotton give you fiber for textile mills and seeds for oil pressers. Similarly, oil palm gives you palm oil from the flesh and palm kernel oil from the nut, allowing you to earn money from multiple parts of the same harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ odonti haa fiber kɛha atadei afeemɔ he kɛ ŋmaa kɛha mu tsɔnei. Nakai nɔŋŋ Oil palm lɛ feɔ palm fɔ kɛjɛɔ loo lɛ mli kɛ palm kernel fɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli. Enɛ haa onáa shika kɛtsɔ ŋmaa kome mli fãi babaoo ni oookpa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and wither when I clear all the shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ beni mijie hulutsoo tsei fɛɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to survive because direct, harsh sunlight burns their soft leaves and dries out their roots. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains nearby creates a cool canopy that protects the cocoa seedlings until they are mature.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ koni amɛhi shi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã ebaa bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Ehaa hulutsoo ni buɔ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ amɛdaraa.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential plant food. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer around the base helps the plant regain its green color and grow strong stems.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tso shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa. Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fataa he Konii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni enáa eŋɔli su kɛ eshishifãi ni wa ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I tell that my cassava crop is fully ready to be dug up from the farm?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakumɔ amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava is usually ready for harvest around 9 to 12 months after planting, when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the main stem begins to crack open as the tubers expand below.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Beni baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso titri lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni bulb lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off without producing fruit due to extreme heat stress, lack of water, or poor pollination. Gently shaking the flowering stems early in the morning helps spread pollen within the flower so tomatoes can form.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ, nu ni bɛ, loo fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. Fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifã lɛ ni aaakpokpo blɛoo Leebi lɛ, enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni egbɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ eshwaa bɔni afee ni tomatoi lɛ anyɛ afee.

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in small nodules on their roots. As the groundnut roots grow, they release this natural plant food into the soil, feeding the nearby maize plants.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmãa ko ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ ŋmeii bibii amli yɛ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Beni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ, Amɛjieɔ nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli tso niyenii nɛɛ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. koni amɛkwɛ ŋmãa tsei yɛ akutso lɛ mli

english: What is causing tiny holes in my maize leaves and small dirt pellets inside the growing shoots?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ sũ bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ amli lɛ amli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which burrows into the center whorl of young maize plants to feed on tender leaves before they unfold. Early application of approved organic or chemical sprays directed into the funnel helps control them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii amli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ dani amɛfee ŋmeii. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ko ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ momo lɛ wo ŋmei lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it harmful to pour water on my vegetable plants during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mawo mi-vegetable tsei lɛ nu yɛ shwane ŋmɛlɛtswai ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Watering under intense afternoon heat causes the water to evaporate rapidly before roots can drink it, and hot water drops on leaves can scorch them while creating humid conditions that attract fungal diseases. It is best to water early in the morning or late evening.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ shwane mli latsaa be mli lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya dani shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnuɔ. Ni nu ni mli edɔ ni shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha baai lɛ ashã. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa, ni no gbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai. Esa akɛ afɔ lɛ nu leebi loo gbɛkɛ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves toward sunlight so they can make food for underground tuber growth. Staking also lifts leaves off wet soil, preventing damp foliage from rotting or catching diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã koni amɛkɛ hulu la lɛ akpee. Koni akɛtsu nii akɛ niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ baai ni efɔ lɛ naa koni ekafite loo hela akamɔ amɛ.

english: Why do the seeds I save from my hybrid maize harvest produce smaller cobs compared to new certified seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akpaa lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmãa bibii kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ he lɛ?

english: Certified hybrid seeds are specially bred for high performance in their first generation only. When you save and replant seeds from that harvest, the resulting crops lose that special strength and produce smaller ears with uneven yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee nɔ ko ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ krɛdɛɛ kɛha nitsumɔ ni nɔ kwɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli pɛ. Beni okɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ nakai kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ toɔ ni oduɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ Tso ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ laajeɔ nakai hewalɛ kroko lɛ ni ewoɔ toi bibii kɛ yibiiwoo ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my crops with dry palm leaves or dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo he ni ebɔle ehe lɛ he sũ? Nibii ni akɛ ŋmei baai ni egbi loo jwɛi ni egbi?

english: Covering bare soil with dry plant material, known as mulching, traps moisture in the ground so you water less, lowers soil temperature during dry spells, stops weeds from popping up, and enriches the soil as it rots over time.
ga: Ale shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni akɛ tsei ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni okɛ nu akawo mli fioo. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ latsaa baa shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii beni efiteɔ yɛ be ni ehoɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why should I pluck off some small mangoes from my tree when they are still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mango bibii kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Removing some small young fruits (a practice called thinning) allows the tree to direct all its food and water into the remaining ones, making them grow much bigger, healthier, and higher in quality.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ tso yibii bibii ni darako lɛ (nifeemɔ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ ŋmɔlɔ) lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ kɛ eniyenii kɛ nu fɛɛ woɔ tso yibii ni eshwɛ lɛ amli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, amɛdara, amɛyɛ hewalɛ, ni amɛhi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my mango tree produce so many tiny fruits that never grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tso lɛ woɔ yibii bibii lɛ? Ani amɛfa babaoo aahu akɛ ebaada kɔkɔɔkɔ?

english: A tree has a limited amount of food and water it can feed its fruits. When it carries too many fruits at once, none of them get enough strength to become large.
ga: Tsei yɛ niyenii kɛ nu fioo ko ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkɛwo yibii. Beni ewoɔ yibii babaoo yɛ be kome mli lɛ Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba lɛ eko kwraa bɛ ni mli wa bɔ ni sa ni etsɔ agbo.

english: Is it good to let every single flower on my fruit tree turn into a fruit?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ maha fɔfɔi fɛɛ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tso lɛ nɔ lɛ atsɔ tso yibii?

english: No, because if every flower turns into a fruit, the tree gets overcrowded and overloaded, resulting in small, poor-quality fruits and heavy stress on the tree.
ga: Dabi, ejaakɛ kɛji fɔfɔi fɛɛ fɔfɔi batsɔ aduawai lɛ Tso lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni etsii tsɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ yibii bibii ni ehiii, ni tso lɛ nɔ haomɔ ni naa wa baa.

english: Why do my fruit trees drop a lot of small fruits on the ground by themselves before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ yibii bibii babaoo shwieɔ shikpɔŋ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Trees naturally drop excess fruits when they realize they are carrying more than their roots and leaves can support, which helps protect the tree from exhausting itself.
ga: Tsei shwieɔ aduawai ni fa fe nine yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji amɛle akɛ amɛmiiwo muji babaoo fe bɔ ni shishifãi kɛ baai baanyɛ akwɛ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ tɔlɛ he.

english: How does removing extra fruits from a tree help me make more money at the market?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tso yibii ni fa fe nine ni mijieɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ni mináa shika babaoo yɛ jara nɔ?

english: Market buyers pay much better prices for large, attractive fruits than for many small ones; removing extra early fruits gives you big fruits that sell faster and for higher prices.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ woɔ aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ fɛo lɛ ahe nyɔmɔ babaoo fe aduawai bibii babaoo. Kɛ́ ojie aduawai ni fa lɛ, ebaaha oná aduawai wuji ni ahɔ̃ɔ oya ni amɛjara hu wa.

english: When is the best time for me to remove extra small fruits from my crop?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ majie aduawai bibii krokomɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: It is best to remove them very early in the season when they are still tiny, so the plant doesn't waste energy growing fruits that you will end up throwing away later.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooojie amɛ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli beni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ. Enɛ ji koni tso lɛ akafite hewalɛ ni ekɛduɔ aduawai ni esa akɛ oshɛrɛ ashwie sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: What happens to a fruit tree if I allow it to carry too many fruits every season?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ anɔ kɛji miha amɛwo yibii babaoo tsɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli?

english: Overloading the tree weakens it over time, which can break its branches and cause it to produce very little or no fruit in the following year.
ga: Kɛ́ tso ko jatsu fe nine lɛ, ebaagbɔjɔ yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ baanyɛ akumɔ tsei niji ni eha yibii fioo pɛ awo loo ewooo kwraa yɛ afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Will adding extra fertilizer make my tree grow huge fruits even if I leave all the small ones on it?
ga: Kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fata he lɛ, ebaaha mitsei lɛ awo yibii wuji kɛji mishi bibii lɛ po. Okɛwo jɛmɛ loo okɛwooo?

english: Fertilizer helps, but a tree still has a maximum capacity; even with rich soil, too many fruits on one tree will compete with each other and remain small.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa, shi tso lɛ yɛ he ni ekɛwoɔ nii babaoo lɛ lolo. Eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tse moŋ Shi aduawai babaoo ni yɔɔ tso kome nɔ lɛ baanyɛ amɛkɛ amɛhe abɔ akaŋ ni amɛhi shi bibii.

english: Why do some of the fruits growing tightly together on my tree rot before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai komɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mitsei lɛ anɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe dani kpamɔ baa lɛ fiteɔ lɛ?

english: When fruits are packed too closely together, air cannot flow and sunlight cannot reach them, creating damp spots where pests and diseases easily destroy the fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ aduawai lɛ ebɔ he tsɔ lɛ, Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abɔle he ni hulu la hu nyɛŋ ashɛ he. Enɛ haa hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni kooloi bibii kɛ helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. Efiteɔ aduawai oya

english: Is it better for a farmer to harvest fewer big fruits or many small fruits?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ okwaafoi lɛ baakpa aduawai wuji fioo loo aduawai bibii babaoo?

english: Harvesting fewer big fruits is usually better because larger fruits fetch higher prices in Ghanaian markets, are easier to harvest, and attract serious buyers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ abaakpa aduawai wuji fioo komɛi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, aduawai wuji lɛ fãa jara ni nɔ kwɔ yɛ Ghana jarayelihe lɛ. Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ abaakpa ni egbala mɛi ni kɛ hiɛdɔɔ heɔ nii lɛ

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle strong direct sunlight because their roots are shallow and their leaves burn easily. Planting tall shade crops like plantains alongside them protects them with living shade until they grow stronger.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo ni nɔ kwɔ, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi Ekɛ hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka buɔ tso lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ naa hewalɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and tall without producing big cobs when I plant seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ bibii ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji beni mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant enough space allows its stem to grow thick and produce larger cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaha eshishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaawo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and healthy. Adding manure or appropriate nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo tso lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ shi.

english: Why does my land become hard and give smaller harvests if I keep burning the farm before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni mikpamɔ lɛ hu faaa kɛji mitee nɔ mishã miŋmɔ lɛ dani midu nii lɛ?

english: Burning clears weeds quickly, but it destroys rich organic matter and useful insects in the topsoil. Over time, this makes the soil hard, poor, and unable to hold water for your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ni ashãa lɛ gbeɔ amɛ oya. Shi efiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa babaoo kɛ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋgbɛ lɛ. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa, ni ehiii, ni enyɛɛɛ ehiɛ nu kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they suffer stress, such as sudden hot dry spells, irregular watering, or too much nitrogen fertilizer which forces the plant to grow leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛmiihao, tamɔ hulutsoo trukaa. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa Aloo akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo afata he, ni no haa tso lɛ baa shwereɔ yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: How do I know if pests are damaging my cassava crops under the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ miifite mi-cassava tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: If cassava leaves begin curling, yellowing, or wilting for no obvious reason above ground, pests or root rot may be attacking below. Checking a few plant roots early helps catch soil pests before the whole farm is affected.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei baai lɛ bɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yiŋtoo ko bɛ he yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baanyɛ atutua shishigbɛ. Tso shishifãi lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni amɔmɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi dani ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ aba.

english: Why are my tomatoes getting dark, rotten spots at the bottom before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ hiɛ ŋmɔtɔ diji ni egboɔ yɛ shishi dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: Dark rotten spots on tomato bottoms are caused by blossom-end rot, which happens when the soil lacks calcium or when the plant gets irregular amounts of water while the fruit is forming.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato lɛ nɔ lɛ baa ji ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ calcium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ nine shɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miikwɛ fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: Yes, planting maize and cassava together works well because maize grows quickly and is harvested in about three months, while cassava grows slowly over a year without competing early on for space.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa lɛ daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ aaafee nyɔji etɛ mli. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei daa blɛoo yɛ afi kome mli ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ he akaŋ mra.

english: The very first rain is often followed by a short dry spell that can dry out and kill newly sprouted seeds. It is safer to wait until the rains become regular so the soil stays moist enough for young plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku ni baanyɛ agbi ni egbe dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ daa koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa kɛha tsei bibii.

english: If I spend extra money to buy certified seeds instead of using seeds saved from my last harvest, will I get more crop yield?
ga: Eji mikɛ shika ni fa lɛ tsu nii koni mikɛhe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ moŋ fe dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli kulɛ. Ani maná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo?

english: Certified high-yield seeds are specially bred to fight off local diseases and produce more grains or fruits than saved seeds, making the extra investment profitable when you harvest.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni ekɛ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ awuu ni ewo ŋmaa loo aduawai babaoo fe dumɔwui ni ato lɛ. Ha nibii krokomɛi ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ afee nɔ ni sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he beni okpaa nii lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt and die when the sun gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are like tiny children who cannot withstand harsh direct sun; they need temporary shade crops like plantains or cassava planted nearby to protect them while their roots grow deep.
ga: Kokoo tsei tamɔ gbekɛbii. ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ plantains loo yucca, ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ koni ebu tsei lɛ ahe beni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli woɔ wu lɛ.

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that aggressively steal water, sunlight, and soil food from your crops, which is why clearing them early gives your main crops room to feed.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa ni kɛ ekãa juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli lɛ. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie lɛ mra lɛ. Enɛ baaha otsei titrii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛye nii.

english: Why are the flower buds falling off my pepper plants before turning into pepper pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛtsɔɔ pepper ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they suffer from water stress or high heat, saving their internal energy to survive rather than producing fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji nu he haomɔ loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa kpe amɛ. Enɛ haa mligbɛ hewalɛ baa shi kɛha wala moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii.

english: Yellowing lower leaves mean your maize plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is the essential plant food needed to make leaves dark green and healthy.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn tso lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Enɛ ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa koni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni ehiɛ hewalɛ.

english: Will putting animal manure into the soil actually help my cassava roots grow bigger?
ga: Ani kooloo ŋmei ni akɛbaafata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ baaye abua mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ni amɛdara?

english: Yes, animal manure acts like rich food for the soil, slowly releasing nutrients that allow cassava roots to expand and store more starch.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii ni jara wa kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ, ni ejieɔ niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli hewalɛ fiofio koni eha ŋmei shishifãi lɛ alɛɛ mli ni ehiɛ ŋmei babaoo.

english: Why does planting beans together with my maize make the soil better for next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: Beans and other legumes have a natural ability to pull plant food out of the air and fix it into the soil, which feeds the surrounding crops.
ga: Beans kɛ legumes krokomɛi Eyɛ adebɔɔ mli nyɛmɔ ni ekɛgbalaa tsei aniyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, he ni eyeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ebɔle ehe lɛ niyenii yɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I plant my crops in straight rows instead of scattering seeds everywhere?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja moŋ fe ni magbɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashwã he fɛɛ he lɛ?

english: Planting in rows leaves open paths that make it easier for you to walk through to weed, while making sure every crop gets equal light, water, and soil space.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ haa gbɛ ni agbele naa lɛ baa koni efee mlɛo aha bo akɛ oootsɔ jwɛi lɛ ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, kwɛmɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do I need to break up hard soil into soft mounds before planting my yam seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mijaraa shikpɔŋ ni wa mli mifeɔ gɔji ni yɔɔ blɛoo dani miduɔ sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need loose, deep soil so they can easily expand downward into long, thick tubers without pushing against hard ground.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli tse bɔni afee ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã oya ni amɛfee ŋmeii kakadaji ni mli tse ni amɛmiimiii shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ.

english: Why are the stems of my tomato plants turning black and rotting during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess water sitting around the roots creates damp conditions where diseases attack the stem, so roots need well-drained soil to stay healthy.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni bɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni helai baa mɔ mli lɛ baa. baatutua tso lɛ No hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ he miihia shishifãi lɛ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow lots of green leaves but very few pods under big shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ hiɛ baai ŋmɔji babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii fioo komɛi yɛ tso agbo ko ni yɔɔ hulutsoo shishi?

english: Cowpeas need direct sunlight to flower and make pods; in deep shade, the plant uses all its energy just making leaves to search for light.
ga: Cowpeas he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ekwɛ fɔfɔi ni efee pods. Yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, tso lɛ baafite ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛbaafee baai kɛkɛ ni ekɛtao la.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow very quickly and provide broad leaves that shade the young cocoa plants and keep the surrounding soil moist during their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni eha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants dropping off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava naturally sheds its leaves during long dry spells to conserve water inside its stem and roots. Once the rains return, the plant will quickly sprout fresh green leaves and continue growing.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli koni nu ahi tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ oya ni ebaaya nɔ eda.

english: Why do my yam plants grow better when I lift the vines onto wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tso lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ miwo wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛtee tso ko nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants need direct sunlight on their leaves to make energy, which is then sent underground to swell the tuber. Lifting the vines off the ground prevents diseases from wet soil and helps the leaves catch maximum sunlight.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ taoɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ. Akɛ enɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni eha ŋmeii lɛ amli alɛɛ. Kɛ́ owó wein tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ aba, ni ebaaha tso lɛ yibii lɛ aná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ.

english: Why do the bottom tips of my tomatoes turn black and rotten before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomatoi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ dani amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil, usually caused by irregular watering or long dry periods between rainfalls.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni ashwieɔ shi be fɛɛ be loo nugbɔshiimɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ateŋ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up into small tight balls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni efee bɔɔlu bibii ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves, or by a virus spread by whiteflies. They drink the plant's sap and distort the leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why are my maize stalks falling over in the farm even when there is no wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ eyɛ mli akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ moŋ?

english: Insects called stem borers lay eggs on the leaves, and their larvae chew holes into the center of the stalk. This hollows out the stem from the inside, making it too weak to support the weight of the plant.
ga: Kplukai ni atsɛɔ amɛ stem borers lɛ fɔɔ amɛwuji yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Ni amɛ ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ bu ko ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ shishi ajɛ mli. Enɛ haa egbɔjɔɔ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ tso lɛ muji lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my cocoa trees dropping their flowers before any pods can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miigbee shi dani ŋmeii lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees produce thousands of flowers but naturally shed many of them if the tree is stressed by a lack of water, missing soil nutrients, or insect damage from pests like mirids.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ. Shi amɛbaashwie baai babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji akɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ ha tso lɛ miihao. Niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kooloi bibii lɛ fiteɔ kɛtsɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ pollen nɔ.

english: How do I know if the soil on my farm is moist enough to plant my maize seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli edɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui?

english: Scoop up a handful of soil and squeeze it gently into a ball. If it holds its shape without dripping excess water, but easily crumbles apart when you tap it, the soil has the right moisture for seeds to sprout without rotting.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ ni okɛ onine shɛɔ nɔ lɛ ni okɛmimɔ mli blɛoo. feemɔ lɛ bɔɔlu Kɛji ehiɛ egbɛhe lɛ mli ni ekɛ nu shwieee shi fe nine. Shi kɛ́ ota he lɛ, efoɔ oya. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baaná nu ni sa ni baaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛfiteee.

english: Why do my stored cowpea seeds develop small round holes a few weeks after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea dumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ yɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ? Otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ

english: Weevil insects often lay invisible eggs on the bean pods while they are still growing in the field. After harvest, these eggs hatch inside the stored seeds, and the adult beetles chew their way out.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ ŋmeii ni anaaa lɛ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa lolo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ. kpamɔ sɛɛ Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ fɔɔ kɛfeɔ dumɔwui ni ato. Ni ŋmeii lɛ baatsɔ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛjeɔ kpo lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my harvested sweet potatoes rot so quickly when I store them indoors?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji mikɛto shĩa mli lɛ?

english: Sweet potatoes have delicate skin that easily gets tiny cuts during digging. If they are not left in a warm, shaded area for a few days to heal their skin before storage, rot fungi enter through these wounds.
ga: Sweet potatoes yɛ hewolo ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni baanyɛ afee mlɛo akɛ aaafo mli fioo yɛ be mli ni atsaa lɛ. Kɛ jeee nakai lɛ, shi amɛ yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo yɔɔ gbii fioo komɛi koni etsa hewolo lɛ dani okɛto. Rot fungus boteɔ pilamɔi nɛɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is short on nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops use to build green leaves. Adding manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps bring back the healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting maize in the same spot repeatedly drains all the nitrogen from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the dirt. Switching to leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts returns natural plant food to the soil.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha nitrogen fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ajie shii abɔ. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmãa tamɔ tsina loo ŋmãa nɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei aniyenii ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Fertilizer works best when the soil is damp and the crop is actively growing, usually a few weeks after sprouting. Applying it during dry droughts wastes it, and applying it right before a heavy rain washes it away.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni tsei miida jogbaŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ otsii fioo komɛi beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ akɛtsu nii yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ, ebaaha afite nii. Ni okɛwo nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ aho lɛ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the center leaves of my young corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that targets the tender growth centers of maize plants. You can manage them by checking your farm early and applying recommended treatments or neem extracts directly into the plant center.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni kwɛɔ hei ni ŋmãa tsei lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ. Obaanyɛ okwɛ amɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni oookwɛ mra lɛ nɔ. ni okɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii loo neem mli nu lɛ awo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when too much water gets trapped in the soil around them, suffocating the roots and causing mold to grow. Planting your cassava on raised earth mounds helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu babaoo eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii shwereɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full, hot sunshine. Plantain trees grow fast and have large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli akpɔlɔi. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo bibii koni amɛhi shi lɛ haa.

english: Why is planting my seeds too close together bad for my final harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ ehiii kɛha naagbee kpamɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing crops fight each other for limited sunlight, groundwater, and soil food, resulting in thin, weak plants that produce smaller crops.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la ni faaa, shikpɔŋ shishi nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ baa.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to produce energy and grow big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves high in the air and prevents them from rotting on wet soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking haa baai lɛ hiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ehaaa amɛfite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop when temperatures get too high or when water supply is irregular. Keeping the soil consistently moist around the roots helps the flowers stay on the vine long enough to set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ejaaa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha ebɔle he lɛ mli afee fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ Shishifãi lɛ baaye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi wain tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why does covering the soil around my plants with dry grass keep them alive during hot dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi tsei lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Covering the dirt with dry grass or leaves—called mulching—acts like a blanket that blocks direct heat from the sun, trapping moisture in the soil so roots stay cool and hydrated.
ga: Mulching kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi Enɛ (ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching) tsuɔ nii tamɔ blanket, ni tsiɔ la ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni emɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Koni shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: This is a sign of nitrogen deficiency. When maize lacks nitrogen in the soil, it moves the remaining nitrogen from older lower leaves to feed the young upper leaves, causing the bottom ones to turn yellow and dry up.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Kɛji ŋmãa bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ejieɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baa bibii lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why does my cassava crop produce very bushy green leaves but small tubers when I harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii kɛ́ mikpa lɛ?

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil causes cassava to spend all its energy growing branches and leaves above ground rather than storing food and swelling the tubers underground.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛtsɔ niji kɛ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ niye ní kɛ toɔ, nɛ a haa nɛ tubers ɔmɛ fuɔ.

english: Why do young cocoa leaves turn brown and burn when planted in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshãa kɛ́ akwɛ amɛ yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot withstand harsh, direct sunlight. They require temporary shade, such as plantain trees, to protect their tender leaves from heat stress until they mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be kukuoo mli, tamɔ dumɔwui, koni ebu baai bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: Why do my cowpea leaves fold together during the hottest hours of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpea plants fold their leaves to reduce the leaf surface area exposed to the sun. This natural defense mechanism helps the plant save water and stay cool during peak heat.
ga: Cowpea tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ baa lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why do I need to tie my yam vines onto tall wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ sweet potato wain tsei fĩɔ tsei kakadaji ahe lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to spread out in full sunlight to produce food for the underground tuber. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground, maximizing light absorption and reducing contact with soil-borne diseases.
ga: Esa akɛ agbɛ sweet potato baai lɛ ashwã hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni ekɛ niyenii aha ŋmeii lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ awó amɛhe nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ha la ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ babaoo ni oha helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ aba shi

english: Why should I cut off some of the extra suckers growing at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-plantains lɛ ashishi lɛ ekomɛi?

english: Multiple suckers compete with the main plantain stem for water, light, and nutrients. Pruning excess suckers and leaving only two or three allows the main plant to produce a larger, healthier fruit bunch.
ga: Suckers babaoo kɛ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, la, kɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashi tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ woɔ aduawai akui wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: High temperatures make tomato pollen dry and sticky, preventing proper pollination. Unpollinated flowers cannot form fruit and eventually drop off the plant.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato mli ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛkpɛɔ. Etsiɔ pollination ni sa naa. Fɔfɔi ni awoko amɛmli lɛ nyɛɛɛ awo yibii ni yɛ naagbee lɛ amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in humid, wet conditions. Excess moisture and dense foliage allow the fungus to spread quickly from pod to pod.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine kɛ tsei ahe tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmei lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ pod mli kɛyaa pod mli.

english: Why are small caterpillars hiding inside the leaf funnels of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-abɛi bibii lɛ ahe tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms. The adult moths lay eggs on young maize leaves, and once hatched, the caterpillars crawl inside the central leaf funnel to feed on the tender growing point.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Asraafoi. Kplukai ni eda lɛ fɔɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmãa baa bibii anɔ. Ni kɛ́ efɔ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ nu lɛ mli koni amɛye hei ni ŋmeii lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is typically caused by sap-sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies, or by viruses transmitted by these pests, which disrupt normal leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. ni tsiɔ baai lɛ adalɛ ni sa lɛ naa.

english: Why do the leaves of my young corn plants turn yellow before they produce cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Corn leaves usually turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen nutrients or when there is too much water sitting around the roots, preventing the plant from breathing and feeding properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛ́ nu babaoo ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛye nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do small worms always eat the leaves inside the center of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: These are pests known as fall armyworms that hide deep inside the tender central shoot of the maize plant where it is moist and safe while they feed on the growing leaves.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni atsɛɔ amɛ fall armyworms ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛyɔɔ shweshweeshwe beni amɛyeɔ baai ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft or watery if I leave them in the ground during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo loo amɛfeɔ nu kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots absorb excess water from waterlogged soil during rainy periods, which reduces their starch content and makes them rot or turn soft quickly.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu ni fa fe nine kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli. Enɛ haa ŋmei lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa egboɔ oya loo efeɔ blɛoo.

english: Why do cassava leaves drop off during the dry harmattan season and grow back when the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli ni amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves in dry weather to save water and survive drought; once the rains return, the plant uses energy stored in its underground roots to sprout fresh leaves.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ mli. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ Tsei kɛ hewalɛ ni ato yɛ amɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo baai heei.

english: Why do I need to build high soil mounds to plant my yams instead of planting directly in flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matswa gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ koni madu ŋmeii yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kplanaa lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need deep, loose soil to grow large and smooth without obstruction, and high mounds help excess rainwater drain away so the tuber does not rot.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli tse he miihia sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ koni ŋmeii lɛ adara ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nɔ ko akatsi amɛ gbɛ. ni gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. No hewɔ lɛ, egbooo.

english: Yam vines climb to catch as much sunlight as possible so the leaves can produce food for the underground tuber, while also keeping leaves off the ground away from heat and fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ bɔni afee ni baai lɛ anyɛ afee niyenii aha ŋmeii lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akaje shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni okɛ amɛ akabɔ dɔlɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: Why do some of my harvested yams come out small and twisted instead of big and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ ekomɛi ji bibii ni egbɛ eshwa moŋ fe ni amɛaafee agboi ni ja lɛ?

english: Yams become small or twisted when planted in hard, stony soil that stops the tuber from expanding freely, or when small underground pests like nematodes attack the root tips.
ga: Sweet potatoes baafee bibii loo amɛbaafite kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haaa tuber lɛ mli alɛɛ ehe. aloo beni shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi bibii tamɔ nematodes tutuaa shishifãi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ.

english: How do I know if my land is better suited for planting cassava or maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Maize requires rich soil with plenty of nutrients and steady rain, whereas cassava is very hardy and can survive in poorer soils and drier conditions where maize would fail.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ he miihia ŋmãa. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa wa waa ni ebaanyɛ ehi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ kɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi ni ŋmãa baafee nɔ ni bɛ lɛ.

english: Can I plant corn and cassava together on the same field at the same time?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ be kome mli yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting them together works well because maize grows quickly and is harvested in a few months, leaving space and light for the slower-growing cassava to mature later.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya, ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Shi he ko kɛ la koni ŋmei ni miida blɛoo lɛ atsɔ sɛɛ mli.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests every year when I plant maize on the same field continuously?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop year after year drains the specific nutrients that crop needs without giving the soil time to rest, while allowing pests and diseases tailored to that crop to build up in the soil.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tsei lɛ lɛ hoɔ ni ehaaa sũ lɛ be ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni etsake amɛhe amɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I plant plantain shoots right next to my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ kookoo dumɔwui bibii ashishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are extremely sensitive to heat and will scorch in strong sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and produce broad leaves that act as natural sunshades, keeping the soil moist and protecting the cocoa plants while they establish themselves.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ he waa, ni amɛbaashã yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli. Plantains daa oya waa ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe be mli ni amɛtswaa shi lɛ.
