english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants adapted to steal light, space, and fertilizer away from your crops. Clearing them early prevents them from overpowering your crop seedlings during their critical growth stage.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛju la, ŋwɛi, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ onibii amli. Amɛjiemɔ mra Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaye otso lɛ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ kunim yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa waa lɛ.

english: Flowers drop when the plant experiences extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of pollinating insects like bees. Maintaining steady moisture and encouraging pollinators helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmeii lɛ faaa Fɛ̃i ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa kɛ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ ni awoɔ he hewalɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Yes, you can plant them together, but you must space them properly. Both crops need a lot of food and water from the soil, so if they are planted too close, they will fight for nutrients and neither will grow well.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ amɛ afee ekome. Shi esa akɛ okɛ ohe akabɔ he bɔ ni sa. Tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ biɔ niyenii kɛ nu babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji akɛ adu amɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Amɛbaatswa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ edaŋ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it safe for me to plant corn and cassava in the same field at the same time?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaadu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ be kome mli?

english: Yes, maize and cassava work well together. Maize grows fast and is harvested in about three to four months, which clears space for the slower-growing cassava to take over the field and produce roots.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Abɛi daa oya ni akpaa yɛ aaafee nyɔji 3-4 mli, ni no haa gbɛ haa ŋmeii ni daa blɛoo lɛ koni amɛye nɔ ni amɛwo shishifãi.

english: Can I plant corn, plantain, and cassava all together on my farm in one season?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa, ŋmãa, kɛ ŋmãa yɛ be kome mli yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be kome mli?

english: Yes, this is called mixed cropping. You can harvest the corn first after a few months, followed by cassava later in the year, and finally plantains, giving you food and income at different times.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ intercropping. Obaanyɛ okpa ŋmãa klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ. Nɔ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ ji ŋmei yɛ afi lɛ naagbee. ni naagbee lɛ adu plantains Enɛ haa onine shɛɔ niyenii kɛ shika nɔ yɛ bei srɔtoi amli.

english: Why do some agricultural officers advise me not to plant cassava close to young tree crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi komɛi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ mikadu ŋmei yɛ tsei bibii ahe lɛ?

english: Cassava grows very big underground roots and dense leaves above ground. It can steal water and nutrients from young trees and block the sunlight they need to survive.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi wuji waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ baai ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ. Ebaanyɛ eju nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ tsei bibii amli ni etsĩ hulu la ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi lɛ naa.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall stems with small roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ shishifã kakadaŋŋ waa kɛ shishifãi bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava is shaded by taller crops or planted too close together, it wastes its energy growing tall stems to reach the sunlight instead of putting energy into growing big tubers.
ga: Beni tsei kakadaji ewo cassava he shade loo adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Ebaafee hewalɛ ni afiteɔ akɛ aaakwɛ tsei kakadaji koni hulu la ashɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni akɛkwɛ bulb agboi lɛ

english: When I harvest cassava, should I throw away the tall stalks or can I use them again?
ga: Be ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei Ani esa akɛ ashɛrɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ ashwie loo abaanyɛ akɛtsu nii ekoŋŋ?

english: You do not need to throw them all away. You can cut healthy, thick cassava stalks into smaller pieces (cuttings) and plant them to grow your next batch of cassava.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa ni oshɛrɛ fɛɛ oshwie. Obaanyɛ ofolɔ ŋmei tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ bibii bibii (cutions) ni okɛdu koni okɛ ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ atsu nii.

english: How do I know which cassava stems are good to save for planting and which ones to discard?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmei tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ makwɛ nɔ? Ni mɛɛ tsei esa akɛ ashɛrɛ ashwie?

english: Save strong, mature stems from the middle part of healthy plants. Throw away stems that are dry, thin, diseased, or damaged by pests, as they will produce weak plants.
ga: Kwɛmɔ tsei ni wa, ni eda kɛjɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔ. Shĩ tsei ni egbi, ni egbɔjɔ, ni hela emɔ amɛ, loo ni tsɛŋemɔ helai efite lɛ fɛɛ oshwie. Ejaakɛ ebaaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why does my farm become difficult to weed after cassava grows big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewaa kɛhaa miŋmɔ lɛ akɛ ebaajie jwɛi beni ŋmei lɛ ebɔi shweremɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: As cassava grows, its branches expand and block the walkways between crop rows. Proper spacing at planting time leaves enough room for you to walk through and weed comfortably.
ga: Beni ŋmei kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ Eniji lɛ dara ni amɛtsi gbɛ ni kã ŋmei ŋtayaai lɛ ateŋ lɛ naa. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he yɛ dumɔ be mli lɛ baaha gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa aha bo ni obaanyɛ otsɔ mli kɛ hejɔɔmɔ ni okɛ jwɛi atsu nii.

english: If I plant corn, cassava, and plantains together, how do I know when each crop is ready to harvest?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa, ŋmãa kɛ plantain fee ekome Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni tso fɛɛ tso eshɛ he ni ebaakpa?

english: Each crop matures at a different speed. Corn matures quickly in about 3 to 4 months, cassava takes 8 to 12 months, and plantains take around 12 to 15 months to yield.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi lɛ shwereɔ yɛ oyaiyeli srɔtoi amli. Abele daa oya yɛ aaafee nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, ŋmei heɔ nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12, ni plantains heɔ aaafee nyɔji 12 kɛyashi 15 dani ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why does cassava leave my soil feeling tired after I harvest it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ etɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Cassava takes up a lot of nutrients and water from the soil to grow its heavy tubers. Adding manure, compost, or fertilizer after harvesting helps restore the soil for the next crop.
ga: Cassava heɔ niyenii kɛ nu babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha eshishifãi ni tsii lɛ akwɛ̃. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to cut down my old cocoa trees completely instead of just trimming the top branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo cacao tso momo lɛ fɛɛ mli moŋ fe niji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ lɛ?

english: When cocoa trees become old or infected with diseases like swollen shoot, trimming is not enough. Cutting them down completely (stumping) clears out the disease and allows strong new shoots to sprout, or creates space to plant improved seeds that produce much more yield.
ga: Kɛ́ kookoo tsei lɛ egbɔ loo helai tamɔ ŋmeii ni efu lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ, ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ pɛ kɛkɛ faaa. Kɛ́ afo amɛ kwraa (stumping) lɛ, ejieɔ helai kɛjɛɔ mli ni ehaa ŋmeii heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ shwereɔ. Aloo afee he ko ni abaadu dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ.

english: Why should I cut off the top shoots of my tomato plants when they grow too tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo mi-tomato tso lɛ yiteŋ beni eshɛɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cutting the main top shoot stops the plant from using up its strength just to grow taller. It forces the plant to direct its food and energy into developing bigger, healthier fruits instead of extra leaves.
ga: Kɛtsɔ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ ni ooofo lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehe ebahiaŋ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛkwɛ̃. Enyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛkɛ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ atsu nii koni amɛwo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ baai krokomɛi baatsu nii.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my cassava stems too close to my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight over the water and nutrients in the soil while their leaves block sun from each other. Spacing them properly ensures each plant gets enough light and food to grow big tubers and healthy grains.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. yɛ be mli ni baai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe Gbɛ ni sa lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ bulb agboi kɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: Why do my young plantain suckers die when I plant them during the main hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni midu amɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young suckers do not have strong roots yet to pull water from deep underground. The hot dry heat dries them out faster than they can drink water, so it is best to plant them at the start of the rainy season when the soil stays constantly moist.
ga: Gbekɛbii lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni mli wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbala nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ lolo. Dɔlɛ ni mli egbi lɛ baaha amɛgbi oya fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛnu nu. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ adu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo be fɛɛ be lɛ.

english: Why should I leave dried maize leaves on the soil around my plants instead of burning them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi ŋmãa baai ni egbi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ lɛ? Tsei moŋ fe ni abaashã amɛ?

english: Leaving dead leaves on top of the soil forms a natural blanket (mulch). This keeps the soil cool under the hot sun, traps rainwater so the soil stays moist longer, and slowly decays into free fertilizer for your crops.
ga: Shi baai ni egboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni efee adebɔɔ mli tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. (Mulch) yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Emɔɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ ni efiteɔ fiofio akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa onibii.

english: Why does my soil turn hard like stone after a heavy rain, and how does it hurt my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wa tamɔ tɛsaa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ? Ni te eyeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Heavy rains wash away topsoil and pack clay soil tightly together, driving out air. Hard soil makes it very difficult for crop roots to stretch out and breathe, which slows down the crop's growth.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ekome. expel air Shikpɔŋ ni wa haa ewaa waa kɛhaa tsei shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaagbala ni amɛmu. Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up tightly and turn small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe waa ni eyɛ bibioo lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves and sucking out the plant's juices. Using a simple neem water mixture or recommended spray kills these insects so fresh, flat leaves can grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ nu lɛ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ neem nu ni akɛfutu loo spray ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni agbe nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ. Enɛ haa baai heei ni yɔɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why are the flowers on my bean plants falling off before turning into actual pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-bean tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani ebatsɔ anɔkwa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the plant suffers from sudden heat stress or lack of water. It can also happen if there are no bees around to pollinate the flowers so they can form seeds and pods.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na piŋmɔ trukaa yɛ latsaa loo nu ni bɛ hewɔ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji akɛ ŋmeii ni baawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ bɛ koni amɛfee dumɔwui kɛ ŋmeii.

english: Why shouldn't I place fertilizer right against the stem of my maize plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ he ko ni bɛŋkɛɔ mi-abele tso lɛ shishifã lɛ?

english: Fertilizer contains concentrated salts that can burn the soft stem and surface roots of the plant if touched directly. It is safer to place fertilizer in a small hole a few centimeters away so the roots can reach out to drink it safely.
ga: Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni baanyɛ ashã tsei lɛ ashishifãi bibii kɛ amɛshishifãi kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo bu bibii amli. ni kɛ jɛmɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji sɛntimita fioo ko pɛ Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ashɛ he shweshweeshwe ni amɛnu nu.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my maize turn yellow in a V-shape while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: When lower leaves turn yellow from the tip downward, it is a sign that the plant is starving for nitrogen. The plant is moving whatever food it has left to the top leaves to survive, showing you that the soil needs more manure or fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛnaa kɛba shi lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Tso lɛ miitsi niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛmiiya ebaa lɛ nɔ koni ehi shi. Etsɔɔ bo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize farm turning yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen. When the soil runs low on food, the plant moves the remaining nutrients from its older bottom leaves up to feed the new, growing leaves at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ nitrogen. Kɛ niyenii fioo pɛ eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei lɛ tsiɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momoi lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛkɛha baai heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: If I put commercial fertilizer on my farm, why do my crops still need good soil to grow well?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ jarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii fata miŋmɔ lɛ he Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ kpakpa he miihia miŋmɔshi nii lɛ lolo koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer is like medicine or extra food for plants, but soil is their home. Healthy soil holds water like a sponge and gives roots a firm grip so the plants can actually drink up the fertilizer you apply.
ga: Fertilizer tamɔ tsofa loo niyenii ni akɛfataa tsei ahe. Shi shikpɔŋ lɛ ji eshia. Shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ hiɛɔ nu mli tamɔ sponji ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ. Tsei lɛ baanyɛ anu ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛfataa he lɛ diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Rolling leaves is the plant's clever way of saving water. When the sun is too hot, the plant rolls its leaves so that less surface is exposed to the heat, preventing water from drying out inside the plant.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji ŋaa gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ nu he. Kɛ hulu lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baafolɔ ebaa lɛ bɔni afee ni he ko ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ akafee nɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Koni nu ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ akagbi.

english: Flowers fall off when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, too much water, or not enough plant food. When the crop feels stressed, it drops its flowers to save energy to survive rather than trying to feed fresh peppers.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu babaoo, loo tsei niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa mli. Kɛ tsei nu he akɛ amɛmiifee nɔ ko lɛ Ebaashwie fɔfɔi koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato kɛha wala. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni oha amɛ chili ŋmɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wither and dry up when I cut down all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ mifo tsei ni eda ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are like human babies—they burn easily under full sun. They need shade from bigger trees or plantains to shield them from high heat and keep the surrounding air moist until their roots grow strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ adesai abifabii. ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo plantains amli koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa he. ni eha kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baawa.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with very tiny fruits when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe ejɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, soil food, and water. They waste all their energy stretching upward to catch sunlight instead of using that energy to make big, heavy fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ niyenii, kɛ nu he akaŋ. Amɛfiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛmɔ hulu la lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ nakai hewalɛ lɛ baatsu nii kɛma aduawai wuji ni tsii.

english: Why does my plantain tree give smaller bunches if I leave all the young shoots growing around its base?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ daa bibii kɛji mishi ŋmeii bibii yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ?

english: The young shoots around the main plantain tree drink from the same water and food in the soil. If you leave too many shoots, they steal food from the main mother plant, leaving it with less energy to make a large bunch.
ga: ŋmeii bibii ni ebɔle Dumɔwui titrii lɛ baanu nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛji oshi ŋmeii babaoo Ejuɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ nyɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Enɛ haaa hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ ahi shi ni akɛfee kuu agbo.

english: Why do the leaves on my tomato plants curl upward and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiikpa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Curling and twisted leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or mites hiding under the leaves, sucking the plant's juice and passing diseases that weaken the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi, ni amɛmuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe lɛ baa.

english: Why do my cassava roots become hard like wood if I delay harvesting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ wa tamɔ tso kɛji mikɛ be ni mikɛkpaa lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ?

english: As cassava plants get very old, they stop storing soft food in their roots and start turning those roots into tough, woody fibers to support the heavy weight of the bush above ground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tso lɛ egbɔ waa lɛ Amɛkpaa niyenii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni amɛtoɔ yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ. Ni nakai shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ tsei ahe tsɔi ni wa koni amɛkɛfi jwɛi ni tsii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my garden eggs turn yellow and bitter if I leave them on the plant for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When garden eggs stay on the plant too long, the crop thinks it is time to reproduce. It turns yellow and forms hard seeds inside, making the skin tough and the flesh bitter so animals won't eat its seeds.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ abɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ hi tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baasusu akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ amɛfɔ. Etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni efeɔ dumɔwui ni wa yɛ emli. Enɛ haa hewolo lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni loo lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. No hewɔ lɛ kooloi yeee emli dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is a main plant food. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer like Urea helps the leaves turn green so the crop can produce bigger cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen, ni ji tso lɛ mli niyenii titri lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii amli, loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ nitrogen tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli koni tso lɛ afee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars hiding inside the leaves of my young corn and chewing holes through them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli ni amɛmiitsɔ mli amɛmiiye bu lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that attacks young corn. Spraying recommended pest control solutions directly into the plant funnel early in the morning or late evening when the worms feed helps get rid of them.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni tutuaa ŋmãa bibii. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe ŋaa ni akɛgbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni adu lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ eye amɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie amɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plant without forming any fruit when the weather becomes very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat causes tomato plants to get stressed, which makes their flowers fall off before they can produce fruit. Watering your plants at the roots early in the morning and providing light shade during very hot days helps prevent this.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei anɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nu yɛ eshishigbɛ lɛ leebi, ni aha lɛ hulutsoo yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting in the soil when heavy rains fall for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni nugbɔ enɛ waa gbii babaoo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When extra rainwater sits in heavy soil, it starves the cassava roots of air, causing them to rot. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges lets excess water drain away quickly, keeping the roots safe.
ga: Beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ nɔ lɛ Enɛ baaha ŋmei shishifãi lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ. ha egbo Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya. ni oha shishifãi lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe

english: Why do I need to spend time putting tall wooden sticks next to my yam plants for the vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maŋɔ be ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama sweet potato tso ko masɛi koni wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can trap direct sunlight to produce energy for growing big tubers underground. Keeping leaves off the wet ground also protects them from soil diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ashɛ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why do agricultural officers advise us to plant groundnuts or beans on our land before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he onukpai woɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔdu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ wɔshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani wɔdu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Beans and groundnuts are special crops that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When you harvest them, they leave this free natural fertilizer behind, making the soil richer for the next crop.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts ji tsei pɔtɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji okpa amɛ Amɛbaashi adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nii babaoo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants produce small fruits when I plant many seeds close together in the same row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ woɔ yibii bibii kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: When crop seeds are planted too close together, the growing plants struggle against each other for soil food, water, and sunlight. Proper spacing gives each plant its own room to feed well and grow big fruits.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa lɛ diɛŋtsɛ etsu ni ekɛ niyenii kpakpa baaha ni ewo yibii wuji.

english: Why do young cocoa trees need shade plants like plantains placed near them when starting a farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he hiaa ni akɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains awo amɛhe lɛ? Be ni esa akɛ aje okwaayeli shishi

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn under full, direct sunlight. Fast-growing plants like plantains act as natural umbrellas, providing shade and cool moisture until the young cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni mli ejɔ. kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso bibioo lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa

english: Why should I spread dry grass on top of the soil around my vegetables?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbɛ jwɛi ashwã shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Spreading dry grass, or mulching, blocks the hot sun from drying out water in the dirt, keeping the soil moist for a longer time. It also stops weeds from growing fast and eventually turns into natural manure.
ga: Okɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni ekɛtsi hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ naa ni eha nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ akagbi. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Ehaa jwɛi hu shwereɔ oya, ni yɛ naagbee lɛ ebafeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper bushes curling up and getting wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper bush lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies or aphids that pass viruses to the plant. Controlling these insects early using organic sprays like neem seed extract stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo aphids ni kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛyaa tsei amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nibii anɔ tamɔ neem dumɔwui amli nu lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii. Ebaaha helai akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why is it important for me to measure the exact distance between my plants instead of just guessing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni masusu he pɔtɛɛ ni mitsei lɛ yɔɔ lɛ he moŋ fe ni masusu he kɛkɛ?

english: Measuring proper distance ensures every crop gets enough sunlight, air, water, and soil nutrients to grow strong. If crops are spaced properly, they do not have to fight each other for food or space.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei fɛɛ naa hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ adu tsei kɛ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa Ehe ehiaaa ni amɛye niyenii loo he ko he akaŋ yɛ amɛteŋ.

english: What will happen to my crops if I plant them too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ amɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli?

english: When crops are too close, their leaves and roots compete for sunlight, water, and nutrients. This competition makes the plants grow tall and thin with weak stems, resulting in a poor yield.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Baai kɛ shishifãi kɛ amɛhe miitswa hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nitsumɔ ni ehiii

english: If I put three seeds or plants in one spot instead of two, won't I get a bigger harvest?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui loo tsei etɛ wo he kome yɛ enyɔ najiaŋ hu? Ani minine shɛɛɛ yibii babaoo nɔ?

english: Putting too many seeds in one spot creates overcrowding right at the roots. Instead of getting more produce, the plants fight each other for food, leading to smaller, weaker crops and a lower harvest overall.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni akɛwoɔ he kome lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ ayi obɔ fe nine. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaana nibii babaoo ni amɛbaafee lɛ, Tsei lɛ baawu amɛhe kɛha niyenii. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii, ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa lɛ hu faaa kwraa.

english: How can I use my walking steps to measure spacing when I don't have a measuring tape on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ nyiɛmɔ gbɛjianɔtoi asusu he ni jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ lɛ he? Akɛni mibɛ tsɔne ni akɛsusuɔ nii ahe yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli hewɔ lɛ.

english: You can use your footsteps to measure space because a normal adult step is usually around 50 centimeters long. Taking regular, equal steps helps you keep consistent distance between your planting holes across the field.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ onaji asusu ŋwɛi. Akɛni mɔ ko ni eda lɛ gbɛfaa ni sa lɛ kɛlɛ ji aaafee sɛntimitai 50 hewɔ lɛ, gbɛfaa ni yaa nɔ daa, ni po nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni okwɛɔ dumɔ bui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What does it mean when an officer tells me to plant my crop in a 'two by two' pattern?
ga: Beni onukpa lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ madu nii yɛ gbɛjianɔtoo ni ji ‘enyɔ-enyɔ’ mli lɛ, mɛni ji nɔ ni amɛtsɔɔ?

english: A 'two by two' planting pattern means placing your crops in straight lines where the distance from one plant to the next is two units (like two feet or two steps), and the distance between rows is also two units. This gives equal space on all sides of the plant.
ga: Enyɔ kɛ enyɔ’ dumɔ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo gbɛ ni ja nɔ he ni jɛkɛmɔ ni yɔɔ tso kɛ tso teŋ lɛ ji yibɔi enyɔ (ni ji naji enyɔ loo naji enyɔ) ni sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai ateŋ lɛ hu ji yibɔi enyɔ. Ha gbɛ ni tamɔ amɛhe afee ekome yɛ tso lɛ fãi fɛɛ.

english: Why do my crops need open space in the middle between the rows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ he hiaa gbɛ yɛ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Open space between rows lets air move freely through the field and allows sunlight to reach the stems and lower leaves. Good air circulation keeps leaves dry and prevents dampness that causes plant diseases.
ga: He ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ teŋ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli oya. ni ehaa hulu la shɛɔ tso lɛ shishi kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ahe Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni baa lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ tso helai baaa.

english: Why are the crops in the middle of my crowded farm growing tall but not producing fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ ni eyi obɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida shi amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: When crops are packed too tightly, the plants in the center get shaded by their neighbors. They waste all their energy stretching upward to find sun light instead of using energy to grow thick stems and produce fruit.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii eyi obɔ lɛ Tso ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ baaná hulutsoo kɛjɛ ekutsoŋnyo lɛ dɛŋ. Amɛfiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛtao hulu la lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛkɛbaatsu nii ni amɛkɛkwɛ tsei ni mli tse ni amɛwo yibii.

english: How does proper spacing between rows help me when it is time to work on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ teŋ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi yɛ ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ mli?

english: Proper spacing leaves clear paths so you can walk through the farm easily to remove weeds, apply fertilizer, or harvest without stepping on plants or damaging their stems.
ga: He ni jɛkɛ ni sa lɛ haa gbɛ ni yɔɔ faŋŋ baa. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ otsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli oyajie jwɛi, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli loo okpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛ onaji efɔɔɔ tsei anɔ loo ofiteee tsei akui.

english: Why should I pull out extra seedlings if too many sprout in one planting hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie dumɔwui krokomɛi kɛji akɛ dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ babaoo yɛ dumɔ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Removing extra seedlings—a process called thinning—gives the best remaining plant all the room and nutrients it needs. It is better to have one or two strong plants that produce well than three weak plants that produce nothing.
ga: Dumɔwui ni fa fe nine lɛ ajiemɔ Enɛ ji gbɛ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ thinning. Enɛ baaha tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ aná hegbɛ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ. Ha tso kome loo enyɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni miiwo yibii kpakpai. Ehi fe ni ooona dumɔwui etɛ ni wooo yibii kwraa.

english: How do crop roots behave under the ground when plants are spaced far enough apart?
ga: Te tsei shishifãi feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa tɛŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ bɔ ni sa lɛ?

english: Underground, roots spread outwards in all directions to search for moisture and plant food. Proper spacing prevents roots from neighboring plants from tangling together and stealing nutrients from one another.
ga: Yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ, shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ amɛshwãa he fɛɛ he koni amɛyatao tsei lɛ amli nu kɛ niyenii. He ni akɛtoɔ he ni sa lɛ baatsi shishifãi ni jɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ekome ni amɛkaye niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ.

english: Yellowing and rolling leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen in the soil, or they are suffering from heat stress and water shortage. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or ensuring the soil stays moist can help the crop turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn tsei lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo hulutsoo kɛ nu ni faaa lɛ miipiŋ amɛ? Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea fata he loo okɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: What causes white, powdery dust to cover the leaves of my garden eggs?
ga: Mɛni haa sũ yɛŋ haa eggplant baai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ?

english: This powdery white coating is a fungal disease called powdery mildew, which thrives in hot and humid weather. Removing the heavily infected leaves and improving airflow around the plants helps prevent the disease from spreading to the rest of your farm.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ nɛɛ ji ŋmɔtɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ ŋmɔtɔ. ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli Ajieɔ baai ni hela emɔ amɛ waa lɛ ni ajieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ jogbaŋŋ Tsei lɛ baaye abua ni hela akagbɛ ashwã hei krokomɛi. ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ

english: Cassava cuttings should be planted about 1 meter apart from each other in all directions. Giving them this space allows the roots room to expand into large tubers without competing with neighboring plants for light, water, and soil nutrients.
ga: Esa akɛ adu tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ aaafee mita 1 kɛjɛ amɛhe yɛ he fɛɛ he. Kɛ́ aha amɛ gbɛ nɛɛ, ehaa shishifã tsu lɛ mli lɛɛɔ ni etsɔɔ ŋmeii wuji ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛkɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ abɔ akaŋ kɛha la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii.

english: What makes my tomato plants drop their flowers before any fruit forms?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛwoɔ yibii?

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when the weather gets extremely hot, when there is irregular watering, or when there is too much nitrogen in the soil. Consistent watering and using fertilizers balanced with phosphorus and potassium will help the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomatoi baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa loo be mli ni nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni phosphorus kɛ potassium yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ahi shi.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under strong direct sunlight. Fast-growing crops like plantains provide broad leaf shade that shields young cocoa trees from the heat while keeping moisture in the soil.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he, yɛ be mli ni amɛbuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he.

english: Is it safe for me to plant my maize seed right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ afi lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Planting after just one rain is risky because early rains often stop for weeks, causing young seeds to dry up in the hot dirt. It is safer to wait until the rain falls regularly two or three times so the ground has enough stored moisture to support germination.
ga: Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ sɛɛ ji oshara. Akɛni nugbɔ nɛɔ mra hewɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ekpaa otsii babaoo. Enɛ haa dumɔwui bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa nɔ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ nɛɔ daa shii enyɔ loo etɛ bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua ni ekwɛ̃.

english: Why are my pepper plants growing tall with thick green leaves but no peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ daa kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi chili bɛ?

english: When crops receive too much nitrogen fertilizer, they put all their energy into growing tall stems and bushy green leaves instead of making flowers and peppers. Switching to fertilizers higher in phosphorus helps trigger flower and pepper growth.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ tsei ashishifãi kakadaji ni miida kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofee fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ Kɛ́ otsake kɛya fɔsfɔs ni fa babaoo mli lɛ, ebaaha fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ adara.

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to give strong yields only in their first planting generation. If you harvest and replant seeds from that crop, the next harvest will grow unevenly, produce smaller cobs, and yield much less grain.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔwui lɛ pɛ mli. Kɛji okpa ni odu dumɔwui kɛjɛ nakai tso lɛ mli lɛ Nikpamɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni ekɛ ehe kpaaa gbee. Ehaa cob yibii bibii ni ehaa dumɔwui fioo kwraa.

english: How can I tell when my yams are completely ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-sweet potato lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Yams are ready for harvest when the leaves and climbing vines begin to turn yellow and naturally dry up. This signals that the plant has finished feeding the tubers under the ground and that the yams have reached full size.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe ŋmeii lɛ niyenii naa ni ŋmeii lɛ eshɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do weeds grow back so quickly after I clear my farm with a hoe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mikɛ ŋmei shwieɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hoeing cuts off weeds at the surface but leaves live roots and hidden seeds under the soil, which quickly sprout again when exposed to sunlight and rain. Covering cleared soil with dry grass or palm fronds blocks sunlight and prevents new weed seeds from growing.
ga: Tilling shwieɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Shi eshiɔ shishifãi ni hiɛ ka kɛ dumɔwui ni akɛtee shikpɔŋ shishi. Ni baakwɛ̃ oya ekoŋŋ kɛji akɛ hulu la kɛ nugbɔ nɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo tsei ahe tsei ha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ faŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi hulu lɛ naa ni ebaatsi jwɛi dumɔwui heei akwɛ̃mɔ naa.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing lets each plant grow strong and produce large ears of corn instead of many tiny, weak ones.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso daa waa ni ewoɔ ŋmãa toi wuji. Yɛ tso bibioo najiaŋ lɛ, mɛi babaoo ni bɛ hewalɛ

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen. Nitrogen keeps leaves green and strong, so adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help the plants recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn tso lɛ. Nitrogen haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts trap nitrogen from the air and feed it into the ground. Rotating them with maize naturally restores soil fertility so your next crop grows better without needing as much expensive fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa babaoo he ehiaaa bo.

english: Why should I cover the dry soil around my crops with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, called mulching, keeps the hot sun from drying out the soil. It holds water in the dirt so your crops stay hydrated longer, stops weeds from growing, and feeds the soil as it rots.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Ehaa nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ. Tsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii be mli ni efiteɔ lɛ.

english: Does it matter which direction the buds face when I stick cassava cuttings into the soil?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmei shishifã yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ Ani ekɔɔɔ he eko he ni ŋmei lɛ tsɔɔ he ni ŋmei lɛ tsɔɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, the small raised buds on the cassava stem must point upwards toward the sky. If you plant them upside down, the new shoots struggle to grow up, wasting plant energy and lowering your final harvest.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji odu ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ, ebaawa akɛ aakwɛ̃ tsei heei. Ehaa tso lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ. ni eha naagbee nibii ni anáa lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do I have to make high soil mounds before planting my yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni owó shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii adu lɛ?

english: Yams need deep, soft, and loose dirt to expand underground. Building mounds creates a loose pile of topsoil that makes it easy for the yam roots to swell into big, long tubers.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia muji ni mli kwɔ, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse koni egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ shishi. Gɔŋ nɔ ni ama lɛ haa sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa sweet potato shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ oya ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii kakadaŋŋ agboi.

english: Why do my crops grow much better if I plant immediately after the first major rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa kɛji akɛ midu amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Early planting allows crops to catch the full rainy season and benefit from the 'nitrogen flush'—a sudden natural release of rich nutrients from the dry soil when the first rains hit.
ga: Dumɔ kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Enɛ haa anyɛɔ akpaa ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli fɛɛ. ni amɛná ‘nitrogen leaching’ he sɛɛ, ni ji adebɔɔ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ trukaa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Tomato leaves usually curl up because of extreme heat, irregular watering, or tiny insects like whiteflies spreading plant diseases. Keeping the soil evenly moist and controlling tiny bugs helps keep leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ fɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa hewɔ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ tsei ahe helai amɛshwãa Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ kooloi bibii ni akudɔɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when the weather is too hot, when they lack water, or when the soil lacks essential nutrients like phosphorus. Watering regularly and keeping the root area cool helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ, nu faaa yɛ mli, loo kɛ́ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ fɔsfɔs bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nu ni oooha amɛ daa ni amɛha shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i lɛ baaye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my crop plants grow weak and small when I plant them close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi ni amɛfeɔ bibii kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close to each other, they compete for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to spread its roots and leaves, resulting in stronger plants and a bigger harvest.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ nu. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaagbɛ eshishifãi kɛ ebaa lɛ eshwa. Enɛ haa tsei ni wa waa kɛ ŋmaa babaoo baa.

english: How can I tell if my farmland soil is healthy enough to grow good crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Healthy soil is usually dark in color, smells fresh, stays moist without becoming muddy, and has earthworms crawling in it. Soil that is very pale, hard like clay, or sandy often lacks the food and nutrients crops need to grow well.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ hee. Ehiɔ shi yɛ nu mli ni ehiɛɛɛ muji. Ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii yɛ ni shwereɔ yɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa, ni wa tamɔ sũ, loo ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ bɛ niyenii kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei lɛ baanyɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant lacks essential plant food, especially nitrogen, or when there is too much water trapped around the roots. Adding compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps restore the healthy green color.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji tso lɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa. titri lɛ nitrogen Aloo kɛ́ nu babaoo ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato leaves curl up during hot afternoons to slow down water loss and protect themselves from harsh sunlight. If the leaves uncurl when the sun goes down, it is normal heat stress; if they stay curled all day, it could be a sign of a plant disease.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli koni nu lɛ akafite fioo ni ebu he kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ shwie shi beni hulu lɛ nyɔ shi lɛ Enɛ ji nɔ ni yaa nɔ kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ mli haomɔ mli. Kɛji amɛfo amɛhe gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ Ebaanyɛ efee tso hela he okadi.

english: Why do weeds always grow faster than my main crops after the rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ be fɛɛ be beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants naturally adapted to the local soil, so they absorb rain and soil nutrients faster than farmed crops. Clearing weeds early prevents them from stealing food and water from your planted crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji koo mli tso ko ni wa ni ekɛ ehe ewo maŋ lɛ mli shikpɔji lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛmɔɔ nugbɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Jwɛi ni ooojie mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ tsei ni oduɔ lɛ amli.

english: What is causing small holes in my young corn leaves and chewed-up centers inside the plant?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? Yɛ mi-baby corn baai kɛ fãi ni ashɛre yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ anɔ.

english: Small holes and powdery droppings inside young corn stalks are typically caused by caterpillars such as Fall Armyworms. These insects hide inside the central shoot and eat the soft leaves before the corn can form ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworms ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni afee lɛ powda ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ dani ŋmei lɛ shwieɔ toi.

english: Cassava roots rot in the ground when heavy soil holds too much rainwater or when fungal diseases infect the roots. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows extra water to drain away easily, keeping the tubers dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ hiɛ nugbɔ nu babaoo loo kɛ́ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ba shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya. Ehaa yitso lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when planted under direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily in harsh sunlight because their roots cannot absorb water fast enough. Planting shade crops like plantain trees next to young cocoa provides living shade and moisture until the cocoa grows big.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu oya bɔ ni sa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ dumɔwui, yɛ kookoo tso lɛ masɛi lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when exposed to extreme heat, irregular watering, or poor soil nutrients. Watering your plants consistently and placing dry grass around the roots to keep the soil cool helps the flowers stay on and produce fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi fɔ̃ɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my crops wilt during the dry season even if I water them in the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gboɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ yɛ gbi mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Watering crops under the hot sun causes water to evaporate into the air rapidly before reaching the roots, and hot water droplets on leaves can cause stress. Watering early in the morning or late in the evening allows moisture to soak deep into the soil.
ga: Kɛ́ afɔ dumɔwui anɔ nu yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ, ehaa nu lɛ hoɔ oya kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani eshɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ni nu ni mli edɔ ni shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha mɔ aná haomɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo mli leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaha nu ni mli edɔ lɛ abote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some cash crops like cocoa bring in high prices at the market while food crops like maize sell for much less?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shika helɛtemɔ mli nibii komɛi, tamɔ kookoo, jara wa waa lɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, niyenii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ jara waaa kwraa.

english: Cash crops like cocoa are exported globally to make high-value goods like chocolate, creating high international demand, whereas staple food crops like maize are grown abundantly locally, keeping local market prices lower.
ga: Akɛ shika nibii tamɔ kookoo yaa je lɛŋ hei srɔtoi koni akɛfee nibii ni jara wa tamɔ tsokolate, ni no haa majimaji ateŋ nibii taoɔ. Yɛ be mli ni aduɔ niyenii ni he hiaa waa tamɔ ŋmãa babaoo yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa jara baa shi yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ.

english: If a crop has a very high selling price, does that mean it will cost me more money and labor to farm it?
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ yɛ jarayeli jara ni nɔ kwɔ waa Ani no tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ mafite shika kɛ nitsumɔ babaoo yɛ okwaayeli mli?

english: Yes, high-value crops usually require more investment in quality seeds, fertilizers, chemical sprays, and intensive daily care compared to basic food crops to yield high-quality produce that buyers expect.
ga: Hɛɛ, bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa waa lɛ biɔ ni akɛ shika awo dumɔwui ni hi, ŋmɔshi nibii, tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ kɛ daa gbi kwɛmɔ ni mli wa mli. kɛ akɛto niyenii shishijee nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ahe koni ekɛ nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kpaa gbɛ lɛ aba.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize crops turning yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that your crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil, which is the main food plant leaves need to stay healthy and make energy from sunshine.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei ahe koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee hewalɛ kɛjɛ hulu la mli.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers onto the ground before any tomatoes grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ dani tomato lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when the weather gets too hot or when soil water changes drastically from dry to wet, which stresses the plant and prevents fruit formation.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo be mli ni nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsakeɔ waa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ ni ehaaa ewo yibii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear away all the large trees on my farm site?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mijie tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that scorch in direct, hot sunlight; they require shade from taller trees or plantain plants to keep them cool and moist during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei kakadaji loo plantains amli koni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do wild weeds grow much faster and stronger than the vegetable seeds I carefully plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe aduawai dumɔwui ni miduɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild local plants adapted to survive tough conditions, so they steal soil nutrients, light, and water faster than cultivated crops can.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛjuɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, la, kɛ nu oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ.

english: What will happen to my pepper plants if I plant them very close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni ekɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ?

english: Planting crops too close causes them to fight for nutrients, water, and sunlight, resulting in tall, thin plants that produce very small and few peppers.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la, ni no haa tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ baa.

english: When is the right time to apply fertilizer to my crops so it doesn't just waste away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni amɛkafite?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist after a light rain so the roots can absorb it immediately, avoiding heavy rains that wash fertilizer away from the farm.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni baajie ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he.

english: Why do my harvested cassava roots rot underground if I leave them in the soil too long during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess water in heavy soil cuts off oxygen to the cassava tubers underground, causing fungi to multiply and rot the roots before you can dig them up.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii mli lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ babaoo ni efiteɔ shishifãi lɛ dani obaanyɛ okɛ amɛ atsu nii.

english: Why do buyers weigh my fresh cocoa beans as lighter after I sun-dry them for a week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ susuɔ mi-kokoo yibii heei lɛ ahe mlɛo fe beni mikɛ otsi kome egbi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Fresh cocoa beans carry a lot of water weight inside them; sun-drying removes this water so the beans don't rot, leaving behind only the dry weight that buyers pay for.
ga: Nu babaoo yɛ kookoo yibii ni afee ehee lɛ amli. Hulu ni akɛgbiɔ lɛ jieɔ nu nɛɛ koni kɔfi yibii lɛ akafite. Nibii ni egbi ni hɔlɔ lɛ woɔ lɛ pɛ eshwɛɔ.

english: What is a hybrid seed, and how is it different from the traditional seeds I usually save?
ga: Mɛni ji dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esoro lɛ yɛ dumɔwui ni mikɛtoɔ daa lɛ ahe?

english: A hybrid seed is created by deliberately crossing two different strong plant varieties to combine their best traits. Unlike traditional seeds that stay the same when saved, hybrids give a massive boost in yield and disease resistance in their first generation.
ga: Akɛ tsei sɔrɔtoi enyɔ ni wa ni akɛ amɛsui ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ feɔ ekome lɛ feɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee hybrid lɛ. Enɛ tamɔɔɔ blema dumɔwui ni baahi shi kɛji akɛ akɛto lɛ. Dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ eha yibiiwoo kɛ helai ahe hewalɛ etee hiɛ waa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why shouldn't I save seeds from my hybrid harvest to plant again next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ hybrid ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ toɔ koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from a hybrid harvest lose their special strength in the second generation. If you replant them, you will get unpredictable growth, smaller crops, and significantly lower yields compared to buying fresh hybrid seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ amɛhewalɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Kɛji odu ekoŋŋ Obaana dalɛ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ faaa. Ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi waa kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni akɛ tsofai ebɔ he lɛ ahemɔ he.

english: Why are hybrid seeds more expensive to buy than local seeds at the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfutuɔ nii amli lɛ jara wa fe maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui ni aheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds require careful, specialized breeding by seed experts every single season. While they cost more upfront, the increased yield and better crop quality usually bring in far more income at harvest time.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ biɔ ni dumɔwui ahe nilelɔi akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ daa be mli. Eyɛ mli akɛ shika ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ji hiɛyaa moŋ. Shi bei pii lɛ, yibiiwoo ni yaa hiɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa anáa shika babaoo yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli.

english: Why do my neighbor's crops grow to the exact same height while mine are all different sizes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo tsei lɛ daa kɛyashɛɔ he kome yɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ dalɛi srɔtoi lɛ?

english: Your neighbor is likely using commercial hybrid seeds. Hybrid seeds are genetically uniform, meaning every plant grows at the same speed, flowers at the same time, and produces equal-sized produce.
ga: Ekolɛ okutsoŋnyo lɛ kɛ dumɔwui ni akɛwoɔ jarayeli mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Hybrid dumɔwui lɛ yɛ ekome yɛ amɛfɔmɔ su mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei fɛɛ daa oya yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ. fɔfɔi yɛ be kome mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni dalɛ tamɔ amɛhe

english: If I plant hybrid seeds, will my crops survive dry weather better than local seeds?
ga: Kɛji midu dumɔwui ni akɛ tsofai ebɔ he lɛ Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli jogbaŋŋ fe maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Many modern hybrid crop varieties are specifically bred to be drought-tolerant and mature faster, helping them produce a good harvest even when rainfall is irregular.
ga: Akwɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ babaoo yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛnyɛ amɛŋmɛ amɛtsui shi yɛ hɔmɔ mli ni amɛshwere oya. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni onáa ŋmaa kpakpa kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ po.

english: Why do I get a smaller yield when I replant seeds from my biggest and healthiest maize cob?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɛɛ yibiiwoo nɔ babaoo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni da fe fɛɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Even if the cob looks perfect, seeds from a hybrid plant split back into the weaker traits of their grandparent plants when replanted. High yield only comes from planting fresh first-generation hybrid seeds.
ga: Shi kɛlɛ, cob lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eye emuu. Shi dumɔwui ni jɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ baaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛtsɛkwɛ̃ tsei lɛ asui ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ amli kɛji akɛ adu amɛ ekoŋŋ. Yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo jɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ ni ji hybrid dumɔwui ni afee ehee fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ ni aduɔ lɛ mli.

english: Do hybrid crop varieties mature faster than our traditional local crops?
ga: Ani tsei sɔrɔtoi ni akɛfee ekome lɛ daa oya fe wɔ maŋ tsei lɛ?

english: Yes, many hybrid varieties are developed to mature early. This allows farmers to harvest sooner, avoid late-season drought, and sometimes plant twice in one rain season.
ga: Hɛɛ, afee tsofai srɔtoi babaoo ni akɛfee tsofai krokomɛi koni amɛdara oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa okwaafoi ni amɛkpaa nii oya. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ hɔmɔ ni baa yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ lɛ he. ni bei komɛi lɛ, aduɔ shii enyɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kome mli.

english: Is it fine to give my unused commercial seeds to my family members to plant on their farms?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ maha miweku lɛ mli bii lɛ jarayeli dumɔwui ni akɛtsuuu nii koni amɛdu yɛ amɛŋmɔji amli?

english: Yes, sharing fresh, unused seeds from sealed original packets with family is fine, as long as the seeds have been stored properly and have not passed their expiration date.
ga: Hɛɛ, ehi akɛ oooja dumɔwui heei ni akɛtsuuu nii kɛjɛ wolo kotoku ni atsĩ naa lɛ mli kɛ owekumɛi. Shii abɔ ni akɛ dumɔwui lɛ eto jogbaŋŋ ni be ni akɛbaatsu nii lɛ hoko lɛ,.

english: How can I know if a specific crop variety will grow well in my area in Ghana?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tso pɔtɛɛ ko baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ni miyɔɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Always look for certified seeds approved by agricultural authorities. These varieties have been tested specifically against the soil types, local rainfall patterns, and common diseases in your region.
ga: Taomɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni okwaayeli nitsumɔhei ewo he odase lɛ be fɛɛ be. Akwɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii srɔtoi nɛɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛha shikpɔŋ henɔi. nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ kɛ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ

english: How should I store my leftover seed packets so they remain good for the next planting season?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ dumɔwui ni eshwɛ lɛ ato koni amɛhi kɛha midumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Keep sealed seed packages in a cool, dry, and dark place off the floor. Moisture, heat, and direct sunlight will ruin the seeds and stop them from germinating properly.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui ni atsĩ naa lɛ ato he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni egbi, ni yɔɔ duŋ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ. Fɛ̃i, dɔlɛ, kɛ hulu la baafite dumɔwui lɛ ni ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crops are hungry for nitrogen or the soil is waterlogged. Adding recommended fertilizer or improving farm drainage helps the leaves turn green and produce good yields.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ fata he loo oha nu ni hoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Avoid planting after the very first rain because the soil underneath remains hot and dry. Wait until you get two or three steady rains so the ground stays moist enough for seeds to germinate safely.
ga: Tsi ohe kɛjɛ dumɔwui ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli edɔ lolo ni egbi. Mɛɛ kɛyashi obaaná nugbɔshiimɔi fioo komɛi ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: Cassava roots rot when rainwater collects around them without draining. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges keeps the roots above standing water and prevents rotting.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu bua amɛhe naa. nu ni hoɔ ni bɛ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ hiɔ nu ni damɔ shi lɛ nɔ ni ehaaa egbo.

english: Cocoa flowers drop when the tree suffers from drought, poor soil nutrients, or attacks by insects like capsids. Providing shade trees and spraying recommended treatments protects the flowers so pods can grow.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na hɔmɔ. shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo kooloi tamɔ capsids ni tutuaa amɛ, hulutsoo ni ajieɔ yi kɛ shwiemɔ baaye abua ni abu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ adara.

english: Why do weeds make my young crops stay small and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔwui lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and plant food in the soil. Clearing weeds early leaves all the water and nutrients for your crops to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaashi nu kɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni baaha onibii lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are tiny worms eating holes in the funnel of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn leaf cones lɛ mli lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a pest that feeds on young maize leaves. You can control them by spraying approved pest treatments or putting a little clean sand or ash directly into the center funnel of the leaves.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ. Obaanyɛ okudɔ amɛ kɛtsɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni oookɛshwie nɔ lɛ nɔ. Aloo okɛ ŋã loo sũ ni he tse fioo awo ŋã ni yɔɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: This is blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium when watering is irregular. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps the tomato plant draw calcium from the ground into the fruit.
ga: Enɛ ji fɔfɔii lɛ anaagbee fitemɔ, ni calcium ni bɛ lɛ kɛbaa kɛji akɛ afɔɔɔ nu lɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, ebaaye ebua o-tomato tsei lɛ ni amɛgbala calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya aduawai lɛ amli.

english: Why do I get smaller harvests when I plant maize on the exact same plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɛɛ yibiiwoo nɔ babaoo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas restores nutrients naturally and reduces soil diseases.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ baa ekoŋŋ ni ehaa helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi.

english: Will cutting off some side branches from my tomato plants help them yield better?
ga: Ani niji ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ ahe lɛ ni mifoɔ lɛ baaha mi yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Yes, trimming extra side shoots stops the plant from wasting energy on excess leaves, directing its food toward growing larger, healthier fruits.
ga: Hɛɛ, sɛɛ tsei krokomɛi ni afoɔ lɛ haaa tso lɛ afite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, eniyenii lɛ kɔɔ aduawai ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni akwɛ̃ɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why does my harvested maize grow mold and spoil while inside my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egboɔ be mli ni miyɔɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Maize spoils if it is stored before drying completely. Sun-drying your grains until they are hard before storing them in a cool, well-ventilated space prevents mold growth.
ga: Abɛi baafite kɛji akɛ akɛto dani egbi kwraa. Kɛ́ agbi dumɔwui lɛ aahu kɛyashi amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani akɛto he ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii akakwɛ̃.

english: Why do I have to support my yam vines with sticks instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tsei fiɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ sɛɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni maha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves toward the sunlight and keeps them off the hot, damp ground. This helps the leaves make more food from sunlight while preventing ground fungal diseases from damaging the plant.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu lɛ he ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ adɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ hulu la mli ni ehaaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akafite tsei lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants showing small holes and getting eaten from the inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni aye kɛjɛ mli?

english: Holes in young maize leaves are usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm hiding in the central leaves. Checking the leaf funnels early and applying recommended treatments protects the plant before the growing point is destroyed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworm ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baa. Nibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Ni akɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu tso lɛ he dani afite he ni edaa yɛ lɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil stays soaked with excess water for too long, suffocating the roots and causing fungal infections. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps rain water drain away so the tubers remain healthy.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ akɛ nu ni fa fe nine wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni yitso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: How do I know if my farmland needs fertilizer before I start planting my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii dani mabɔi tsei akwɛmɔ?

english: If your previous crop leaves turned yellow early or produced small harvests, your soil is running low on nutrients. Inspecting leaf color during growth or having an extension officer run a simple soil test tells you what nutrients your field lacks.
ga: Kɛji tso ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ oya loo amɛwooo yibii fioo Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kwɛmɔ baa lɛ su yɛ be mli ni edara lɛ loo ha extension nitsulɔi lɛ afee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kaa ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Ebaatsɔɔ bo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni onitsumɔhe nine lɛ bɛ.

english: Why do people say planting cowpeas or beans makes the soil better for my main crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and convert it into natural food inside the soil. When planted together with or right before main crops, they fertilize the ground naturally without extra chemical cost.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ adu kɛfata tso titri lɛ he loo dani eshɛ lɛ Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni tsofai krokomɛi ahe ehiaaa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures become too hot or when soil water levels bounce between too dry and too wet. Keeping soil moisture consistent with regular morning watering helps flowers stay on the plant and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo beni shikpɔŋ nɔ nu lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni egbi tsɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ teŋ lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my pepper leaves droop and wilt in the hot afternoon even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli ni edɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: On hot afternoons, pepper plants lose water from their leaves faster than roots can drink it up. As long as the plant recovers by evening when temperatures drop, this daytime drooping is just the plant's normal way of protecting itself from heat.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛjɛɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Shii abɔ ni tso lɛ baaná hewalɛ yɛ gbɛkɛ mli beni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi lɛ. Nɛkɛ hulutsoo be mli tsei ni shwieɔ shi nɛɛ ji gbɛ ni tso lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he lɛ pɛ.

english: It is safer to wait until the rains become steady. The very first rain is often followed by a long dry spell, which can heat up the soil and dry out newly sprouted seeds before they establish deep roots.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ aba shi. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔi ni nɛɔ mra lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli adɔ ni eha dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ agbi dani amɛwo shishifãi ni mli kwɔ.

english: Why does clearing weeds during the first month help my crops grow so much bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa lɛ?

english: Young crops struggle to share food, water, and sunlight. Clearing weeds in the first three to four weeks removes aggressive competitors, allowing young crop roots to establish quickly without stress.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ bibii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛja niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la, no hewɔ lɛ, jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni ajie akaŋshilɔi ni yɔɔ basabasa lɛ kɛya. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi oya ni haomɔ ko bɛ he.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green and strong. Adding fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure will restore their color and help them produce large, healthy cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha amɛhe su lɛ aba ekoŋŋ, ni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii wuji ni mli wa.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving the young cocoa trees the shade and moist soil they need to survive their first two years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops wilt in the hot afternoon even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mibɛ eko moŋ? Nɛgbɛ mikɛ nu woɔ mli leebi?

english: During the hottest part of the day, crops lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull it from the soil. The leaves curl to protect themselves from drying out, but they will bounce back once the heat drops in the evening.
ga: yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi. Shi efoɔ ehe ekoŋŋ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi gbɛkɛ.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my cassava stems too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When cassava is planted too close together, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving them proper space allows each plant to spread its roots and grow big tubers underground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛhaa lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso shwereɔ eshishifãi lɛ amli ni ekwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why should I avoid planting pepper on the exact same plot of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ dumɔ he yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop in the same spot causes soil pests and diseases to build up, while draining the soil of specific nutrients. Changing the crop every season keeps the soil rich and prevents diseases from attacking your harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nine shɛɔ niyenii komɛi anɔ. Kɛ́ otsake ŋmɔshi nibii daa be lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii, ni ehaaa helai atutua oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do weeds cause my tomato plants to produce such tiny fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiwo yibii bibii tamɔ nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm, stealing water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your tomatoes. Clearing weeds early ensures your tomatoes get all the food they need to produce big fruits.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli, ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ o-tomato lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha tomatoi lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo yibii wuji.

english: Why are small insects leaving holes in my cabbage leaves, and how does it affect the crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii shĩɔ bu yɛ kaaba baa nɔ lɛ? Ni te enáa tsei anɔ hewalɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Insects like caterpillars and aphids eat the leaves to feed themselves, which weakens the plant and stops it from forming a tight, healthy cabbage head. Using neem leaf extract or approved sprays protects the leaves so the crop can mature.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii yeɔ baai lɛ koni amɛye niyenii. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaaa kaabe yitsei lɛ adara ni amɛhe awa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu loo tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ akɛshwie nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu tso lɛ he koni tso lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Extra shoots suck food and water away from the main stem. Leaving only one or two strong shoots ensures the main plant gets enough energy to produce a big, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine lɛ shwieɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ he. Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo tso wuji babaoo ni tsii.

english: Why do I need to trim off the bottom leaves of my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo mi-tomato tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ?

english: Trimming the lower leaves allows fresh air to blow around the stem and stops dirt from splashing onto the plant during heavy rains, which prevents fungal diseases from spreading.
ga: Kɛ́ afo shishigbɛ baai lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa tsɔɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli. Ni ehaaa muji akashwie tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: How do I know if my soil is soft and healthy enough to grow good yam tubers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ akwɛ sweet potato ŋmeii kpakpai?

english: Good soil for yams is loose, rich in organic material, and drains water well without getting sticky. If the land is hard or stony, clearing it well and mounding loose topsoil makes it easy for yams to expand.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ mli tse. Eyɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo ni ekɛ nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ ehe wooo mli Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa loo tɛi yɔɔ nɔ Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tse jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ ŋwɛi sũ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ to he lɛ, ebaaha efee mlɛo aha sweet potatoes lɛ akɛ amɛbaagbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow and fail to grow when planted in very sandy soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekwɛɛɛ kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Sandy soil cannot hold water or crop nutrients well, so rain washes them away before plant roots can drink them. Adding compost or animal manure mixes into sandy soil helps hold moisture and nutrients for your crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ ahiɛ nu loo tsei amli niyenii jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ nugbɔ lɛ shwieɔ amɛ dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nuɔ amɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii wo sũ ni ŋã yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni haa onibii lɛ ahi mli.

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetable crops during the hot afternoon or early in the morning?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo aduawai anɔ nu yɛ shwane mli loo leebi?
