english: Watering early in the morning allows roots to absorb moisture before the heat sets in. Watering in the hot afternoon causes most water to evaporate into the air before reaching the roots, and can burn or stress the plant.
ga: Kɛ́ afɔ nu lɛ leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛjieɔ nu ni mli edɔ lɛ dani hulutsoo be lɛ baa, ni kɛ́ afɔ amɛ nu yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani eshɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ni ebaanyɛ eshã loo eha tso lɛ aná nɔnyɛɛ.

english: How can I easily tell if my farm soil is healthy enough for the upcoming planting season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be ni baa lɛ?

english: Healthy soil is dark, crumbly, smells fresh, and holds moisture well after rain. If your soil dries out into hard rock or washes away easily like loose sand, it needs organic matter like decomposed leaves or manure added to it.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni ehiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ, ebatsɔ tɛ ni wa loo efoɔ oya tamɔ ŋã ni etse. Esa akɛ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo afata he.

english: How do I know if a new seed variety I heard about will actually grow well on my specific farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwu hee ko ni minu he lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ pɔtɛɛ lɛ mli?

english: Seed varieties perform differently depending on local rainfall and soil types. It is best to test a small amount of the new seed on a small plot first to observe how it performs on your land before planting your entire farm with it.
ga: Dumɔwui srɔtoi lɛ yɛ bɔ ni amɛtsuɔ nii amɛhaa lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ nɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooka dumɔwui heei fioo ko okwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ. klɛŋklɛŋ ni okwɛ bɔ ni etsuɔ ​​nii ehaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani okɛ nakai dumɔwui lɛ adu oŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight for sunlight, water, and soil food, resulting in thin, weak stalks and tiny cobs. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space and food to grow large, heavy cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛbaatswa hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why did many of the seeds I planted last week fail to sprout out of the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni midu yɛ otsi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ ateŋ babaoo ekwɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if they were stored in heat, buried too deeply, or if the soil dried out completely right after planting. Using quality certified seeds and keeping the soil damp helps them sprout evenly.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ akɛ amɛ wo la mli, afu amɛ tsɔ, loo kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi kwraa beni adu lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ. Dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni aŋmala he odaseyeli akɛtsu nii ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under intense direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to them acts like a living umbrella, giving the cocoa the shade and moisture it needs to survive.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka Enɛ haa kookoo lɛ naa shade kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi.

english: Why are my cassava plants producing huge leafy tops but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ dara shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer causes cassava plants to spend all their energy growing leaves above ground instead of roots below. Cassava needs balanced soil nutrients, especially potassium, to grow thick, healthy tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ haa yucca tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ baai ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii moŋ fe ni eeejɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli. Nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni sa yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia Cassava. titri lɛ potassium Koni eha yitso lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why does my land yield fewer crops every year even though I plant the exact same crop every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo daa afi lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi moŋ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year and lets specific pests multiply. Rotating with crops like beans or groundnuts restores nutrients back into the soil naturally.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. kɛ gbɛ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi shwereɔ Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei tsakeɔ Ebaaye ebua ni niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do insects seem to damage my crops more during a hot dry spell than during rainy weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni kooloi bibii fiteɔ miŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ hulutsoo be mli fe nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Heat speeds up insect reproduction while drought stresses crops, making the plants weaker and less able to fight off damage. Rain helps keep crops strong and washes away many small pests from the leaves.
ga: Dɔlɛ haa kooloi afɔɔ oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, hɔmɔ haa tsei haoɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ekɛ nɔ ni efite lɛ awuu. Nugbɔ haa ŋmɔshi nibii hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni efoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii kɛyaa. baai babaoo

english: Why do cassava processing factories prefer buying the white cassava variety instead of the red ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nitsumɔhei ni feɔ ŋmei lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛhe ŋmei henɔi yɛŋ fe ŋmei tsuru lɛ?

english: Processing factories prefer white cassava because it produces bright white starch and flour, which local consumers and industrial buyers prefer. White varieties also often have a higher starch content compared to red varieties, giving the factory more product per kilogram.
ga: Nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ sumɔɔ ŋmei yɛŋ ejaakɛ ejieɔ ŋmei yɛŋ ni kpɛɔ kɛ ŋmei. ni maŋbii ni heɔ nii kɛ nitsumɔhei ni heɔ nii tamɔ White henɔi lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛná starch ni fa fe red henɔi lɛ. Ehaa nitsumɔhe lɛ feɔ nibii babaoo yɛ kilogram kome mli.

english: Why do oil palm processors pay a higher price for the dark red fruits compared to the lighter ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni feɔ oil palm lɛ woɔ aduawai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ahe nyɔmɔ babaoo fe aduawai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: The dark red oil palm fruits (often from the improved Tenera variety) contain a higher oil content and have much thinner shells. Processors get significantly more palm oil from them than from lighter, wild varieties with thick shells.
ga: Mu tso yibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ (ni bei pii lɛ ejɛ Tenera henɔi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli) lɛ mli mu fa babaoo, ni ehiɛ hu yɛ mlɛo kwraa. Mɛi ni feɔ nibii nɛɛ naa ŋmei fɔ babaoo kɛjɛɔ amɛmli fe ŋmei fɔ ni yɔɔ koo mli, ni eyɛ mlɛo ni eyɛ ŋmei ni mli tse lɛ.

english: Is red maize better for feeding my livestock or for selling to food buyers than white maize?
ga: Ani ŋmãa tsuru hi kɛha mi kooloi lɛ niyenii loo jarayeli kɛha mɛi ni heɔ lɛ niyenii fe ŋmãa yɛŋ?

english: White maize is preferred by food buyers because it makes popular local dishes like banku and kenkey look bright and clean. However, yellow or red maize contains higher vitamin A content, making it excellent for poultry and livestock feed.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ niyenii lɛ sumɔɔ ŋmãa yɛŋ ejaakɛ ehaa maŋ lɛ mli niyenii ni ehe gbɛi tamɔ banku kɛ kenky feɔ nɔ ni kpɛɔ ni ehe tseɔ. Shi kɛlɛ, ŋmãa ni ji ŋmɔŋ loo tsuru lɛ yɛ vitamin A babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ ehi kɛha kooloi kɛ kooloi aniyenii.

english: Why do buyers reject my cocoa beans when they are purple inside instead of brown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kpooɔ mi-cocoa ŋmeii lɛ beni amɛfeɔ purple yɛ brown najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Purple cocoa beans mean the beans were not fermented long enough after harvesting. Buyers reject unfermented beans because they create a bitter, harsh chocolate taste rather than the rich, smooth flavor required by chocolate factories.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii ni ji purple lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ efɔɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kpooɔ ŋmeii ni afeee lɛ ŋmɔtɔ ejaakɛ ehaa tsokolate lɛ mli ŋɔɔ ni mli wa. Yɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tsɔklate nitsumɔhe lɛ taoɔ lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do food processing factories reject my crop harvest even when the fruits look big and healthy to me?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niyenii afeemɔ he ko ekpoo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ aduawai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛyɛ hewalɛ moŋ.

english: Factories test for unseen issues like high moisture levels, internal rot, or insect damage inside the crop. High moisture causes crops to mold quickly during processing, which can ruin an entire batch of factory products.
ga: Tso lɛ kaa naagbai ni anaaa tamɔ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo, mligbɛ fitemɔ loo kooloi ni fiteɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ ekwɛɔ. Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo haa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya be mli ni atsuɔ he nii. ni baanyɛ afite nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ nitsumɔhe lɛ

english: How do factories determine if my harvested crops have defects or low quality before they agree to buy them?
ga: Te nitsumɔhe lɛ baafee tɛŋŋ ale kɛji mikpamɔ lɛ efite loo ehiii kwraa dani makpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ mahe?

english: Factories take random samples from your bags to test moisture content, check for pest holes, weigh the seeds, and inspect the color. They use these tests to determine if your harvest meets their processing standards.
ga: Nitsumɔhe lɛ jieɔ nɔ ko kɛjɛɔ obaagi lɛ mli koni ekɛka ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ekwɛ. Kwɛmɔ kɛji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ mli lɛ Susumɔ ŋmaa lɛ he ni okwɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ su ha. Akɛ kaai nɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛna kɛji okpamɔ lɛ kɛ nitsumɔ he mlai lɛ kpãa gbee.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants turning reddish-purple, and will it reduce my yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ red-purple lɛ? Ni ani ebaaha nitsumɔ ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ aba shi?

english: Reddish-purple leaves usually show that your crop lacks phosphorus, an important soil nutrient for root and fruit development. Without enough phosphorus, your plants grow slowly and produce smaller fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs faaa yɛ otso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛha shishifãi kɛ aduawai lɛ akwɛmɔ Kɛji fɔsfɔs ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ Otso lɛ baakwɛ̃ fiofio ni ebaawo aduawai bibii.

english: Why do my stored cowpeas turn dark red or brown after a few months in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpeas ni mikɛto lɛ feɔ etsuru loo ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi ni mikɛto lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas darken when exposed to heat, moisture, and air over time, or when damaged by weevils. Keeping them in cool, dry conditions or using airtight storage bags protects their original color and market value.
ga: Cowpeas lɛ su feɔ ediŋŋ beni hulutsoo, fɛ̃i, kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ. aloo kɛ́ ŋmeii efite amɛ Kɛ́ okɛto he ko ni mli ejɔ ni egbi loo okɛ kotoku ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛshishijee su kɛ jara ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ he.

english: What makes an improved crop variety better than the traditional local seeds I usually plant?
ga: Mɛni haa tsei srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ lɛ hi fe blema maŋbii dumɔwui ni miduɔ daa lɛ?

english: Improved crop varieties are specifically bred to yield more, resist common diseases, mature faster, and produce the exact color, size, and texture that commercial factories and buyers want.
ga: Akwɛɔ tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Eteɔ shi ewoɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ, ekwɛ̃ɔ oya, ni ehaa su, dalɛ, kɛ bɔ ni tso ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ jarayeli mli kɛ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: How can I find out what crop specifications a processing factory wants before I plant my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmɔshi nibii ahe saji ni he hiaa nitsumɔhe ko dani adu ŋmɔ?

english: You can speak with your local agricultural extension officer or directly contact the buying agents of processing factories. They can provide crop guidelines, specify preferred varieties, and sometimes offer contracts before planting season.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ okwaayeli he nitsumɔ he nitsulɔ ni kwɛɔ okwaayeli nɔ lɛ awie loo okɛ nitsumɔhe nine lɛ nihɔɔmɔ he nitsulɔ lɛ agba sane tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛha bo gbɛtsɔɔmɔi yɛ tsei akwɛmɔ he. Tsɔɔmɔ srɔtoi ni ataoɔ lɛ Ni bei komɛi lɛ, akɛ kpaŋmɔi haa dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛmɔ be lɛ baashɛ.

english: How can I tell if my crops are just dry from the sun or actually getting sick?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbi kɛjɛ hulu lɛ mli kɛkɛ loo hela mɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Thirsty crops usually droop during the hottest part of the day and recover in the evening, whereas sick crops stay wilted, turn yellow, or develop spots regardless of how much water they get.
ga: Tsei ni kumai yeɔ amɛ lɛ fɔɔ shwiemɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, ni amɛhe baajɔ amɛ gbɛkɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ baagboi. tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ Loo ŋmeii jeɔ kpo bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni nu ni anáa lɛ fa ha.

english: If I see just one sick plant on my farm, should I destroy it or try to save it?
ga: Kɛji mina tso kome pɛ ni hela mɔ lɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli Ani esa akɛ makpãtã hiɛ loo mabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni mabu he?

english: Removing and safely disposing of a single infected plant immediately is usually best, as it prevents contagious diseases from spreading and destroying your entire crop yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso kome ni hela lɛ emɔ lɛ ni ajieɔ oya ni shweshweeshwe lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ he nii. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ebaatsi helai ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ lɛ anaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa ni efite onibii fɛɛ.

english: Why are my cocoa pods still rotting even after I sprayed them with medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ fiteɔ lolo beni mikɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ po lɛ?

english: Chemical sprays mostly prevent new infections rather than cure pods that are already infected inside, or heavy rains may have washed the spray off before it could work.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mɔ nɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ helai heei ahe. Mohu ɔ, mo tsa pods nɛ hela ɔ ngɛ mi ɔ. Kɛ jeee nakai lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ atsɔ mli dani akɛtsu nii.

english: What happens if I wait a few weeks before treating the pests I see on my cassava plants?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mimɛ otsii fioo komɛi dani mitsa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni minaa yɛ mi yucca tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Insects multiply rapidly within days, so delaying treatment allows a small pest problem to turn into a full farm invasion that is much harder and more costly to fix.
ga: Kplukai lɛ faa oya yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli. No hewɔ lɛ, helatsamɔ ni akɛbaatsu nii be ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ahe naagba bibioo ko nɔ etsɔ ŋmɔ mli tutuamɔ ni fa babaoo. Enɛ saamɔ wa fe tsutsu lɛ, ni ejara hu wa fe tsutsu lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants slowly turning yellow starting from the bottom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ fiofio kɛjɛ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing that starts at the lower leaves usually means the soil lacks nitrogen, so the plant is shifting its remaining nutrients upward to support new leaf growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ tsiɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni eye ebua baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ adalɛ.

english: Plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme heat, irregular watering, or having too much nitrogen fertilizer in the soil.
ga: Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ he. aloo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: Why are the tips of my yam leaves turning brown and drying up gradually?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato baai lɛ ayiteŋ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbiɔ fiofio lɛ?

english: Leaf tip burning is often caused by scorching winds, dry soil conditions, or too much chemical fertilizer building up salts around the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsoɔ waa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli babaoo ni haa ŋmei baa shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ yitsei shãa.

english: Why is it important for me to keep extra seedlings in a nursery instead of planting everything at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui krokomɛi ahi ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni madu nɔ fɛɛ nɔ shikome lɛ?

english: Keeping spare seedlings in a nursery allows you to quickly replace any plants that die or fail to grow in the main field, keeping your farm space fully productive.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ dumɔwui ni eshwɛ lɛ to tsei akwɛmɔhe lɛ, ebaaha onyɛ okɛ tsei ni gboi loo amɛkwɛɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ lɛ ato najiaŋ oya. Ha oŋmɔ lɛ mli kpokpaa lɛ awo yibii kwraa

english: How do crop diseases move from one healthy plant to another in my field?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni tsei ahe helai jɛɔ tso kome ni yɔɔ hewalɛ mli kɛyaa ekroko mli yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Diseases spread through tiny fungal spores or germs carried by splashing rain, wind blowing across the field, or on dirty farm tools and clothing.
ga: Hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ fungal spores loo helatsɛmɛi bibii anɔ. ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ woɔ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa kɛtsɔɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli loo yɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii kɛ atadei ni he tseee lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato plants weak and small even though I added fertilizer to the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛji bibii lɛ? Nɛgbɛ esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Fertilizer cannot work properly if the soil is too dry, overly acidic, or if underground pests like root worms are damaging the roots and stopping nutrient uptake.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Eyɛ acid tsɔ. Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ shishifãi amli ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ ni amɛkpaa niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ.

english: Most grain crops like rice or maize reach full maturity around 90 to 120 days after planting. You will know they are ready when the stalks and leaves turn yellow and dry, and the seeds become hard and firm to the touch.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmaa mli lɛ ateŋ babaoo, tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa, shɛɔ shweremɔ he aaafee gbii 90 kɛyashi 120 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaale akɛ amɛfee klalo beni amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi lɛ. ni dumɔwui lɛ wa ni amɛhe wa kɛji akɛ ata he.

english: Can I leave my mature crop standing in the field until I am ready to harvest and sell it?
ga: Ani manyɛ mashi ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛyashi be mli ni mafee klalo akɛ makpa ni mahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Leaving ripe crops in the field past their maturity date exposes them to rain, birds, and field pests, which causes the grains to rot or fall off. It is best to harvest on time and keep the crop in a dry place.
ga: Nibii ni ekwɛ̃ ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli ni eho be ni sa lɛ he Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ aná nugbɔ, okpoi kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ loo amɛshwieɔ shi. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookpa yɛ be naa ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ ato he ko ni egbi.

english: Why do some grain crops take 120 days to mature while others take shorter?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi heɔ gbii 120 dani ekwɛ̃ɔ ni ekrokomɛi hu heɔ be kuku dani ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Different crop varieties have different genetic lifecycles. Medium-duration varieties take about 120 days because they spend more time building strong roots and larger grains, which often leads to higher yields.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi yɛ wala yibii sɔrɔtoi. Henɔi ni yeɔ be fioo lɛ heɔ aaafee gbii 120, ejaakɛ amɛheɔ be dani amɛnáa shishifãi ni wa kɛ dumɔwui wuji. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ haa yibii babaoo baa.

english: Do I have to mill my harvested grain immediately, or can I keep it raw for some time?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mafolɔ dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ loo manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni akpɛ lɛ ato be fioo?

english: You do not have to mill it immediately. As long as you dry the grain properly right after harvest, you can safely store un-milled paddy or corn for many months until you are ready to process or sell it.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa ni okɛshwie shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Shii abɔ ni obaagbi dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni atswako lɛ ato shweshweeshwe nyɔji babaoo kɛyashi obaafee klalo akɛ obaatsu he nii loo ohɔ̃ɔ.

english: Can I hold onto my harvested crops for a few months to sell when market prices go up?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ mikpamɔ lɛ ato nyɔji fioo komɛi koni mikɛhɔ̃ɔ kɛ́ jara lɛ tee hiɛ?

english: Yes, holding your harvest until the dry season or off-peak periods usually yields better prices. However, you must dry the crop well and store it in clean, sealed bags off the ground to prevent pest damage.
ga: Hɛɛ, bei pii lɛ, ŋmaakpamɔ kɛyashiɔ hulutsoo be loo hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ kɛ jara ni hi fe fɛɛ baa. Shi kɛlɛ, esa akɛ ogbi ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛto kotokui ni mli tse ni atsĩ naa mli koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akafite.

english: How can I safely store my harvested grain at home so it does not spoil while I look for buyers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ ato shia shweshweeshwe? Bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ akafee yaka be mli ni ataoɔ mɛi ni baahe lɛ.

english: Dry the grain until it crackles cleanly when bitten, then store it in airtight sacs or hermetic bags inside a well-ventilated room, kept away from walls and lifted off the bare floor on wooden planks.
ga: Gbimɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ aahu kɛyashi amɛbaakumɔ kɛji amɛye amɛhe. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛto kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo kotoku ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli yɛ tsu ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ mli jogbaŋŋ mli. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ gbogboi ahe. ni ewo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ tso ni akɛfee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Why is sun-drying my harvested crops so important before taking them for processing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ mikpamɔ lɛ agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani atsu he nii lɛ?

english: Sun-drying removes internal moisture from the seeds. Dry grains easily separate from their outer husks during processing and will not mold or rot when packed.
ga: Hulu ni haa egbiɔ lɛ jieɔ mligbɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli. Dumɔwui ni egbi lɛ mli gbalaa kɛjɛɔ kponɔgbɛ ŋmei lɛ mli oya yɛ be mli ni atsuɔ he nii lɛ. ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ baawo mli loo ebaafite kɛji akɛ awo mli.

english: What happens if I send my grain to the milling machine right after harvesting without drying it?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ tee ŋmɔ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni akpa amɛ ni migbiko amɛ?

english: Freshly harvested grain contains too much water. If you mill it wet, the soft seeds will crush into a sticky paste or break into tiny pieces, ruining the crop quality.
ga: Nu babaoo yɛ dumɔwui ni akpa ehee lɛ amli. Kɛji okɛ ŋmɔtɔ Dumɔwui bibii lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ebaagbala ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. loo akumɔ mli bibii bibii Enɛ baafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahilɛ-kɛhamɔ.

english: Will the quality of my milled grain drop if I wait a long time before taking it to the mill?
ga: Ani mi-ŋmãa ni mikɛmiikpa lɛ baafite kɛji mimɛ be kakadaŋŋ dani mikɛtee ŋmãa lɛ?

english: No, as long as the raw, un-milled crop is kept completely dry and free from insects, storing it before milling will not reduce the quality of the final grain.
ga: Dabi, be fɛɛ be ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akwɛɛɛ mli lɛ baakã he ahi shi ni egbi kwraa ni kooloi bɛ mli lɛ. Nibii ni akɛtoɔ dani ashɛɔ ŋmãa lɛ haŋ naagbee ŋmãa lɛ nɔ aba shi.

english: Is it better to mill my crop right in the village or carry it raw to the main market town?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mafolɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli yɛ akrowa lɛ mli loo mikɛ mu ni afee lɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ aya jarayeli maŋ wulu lɛ mli?

english: Milling in the village saves transport costs and gives you fast food or quick cash, but larger market towns often have better machines that produce cleaner, higher-value grain for commercial buyers.
ga: Omɔ ni ajieɔ yɛ akrowa lɛ mli lɛ haaa okɛ gbɛfaa he nyɔmɔwoo aba shi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa bo ni onáa niyenii ni ayeɔ oya loo shika oya. Shi bei pii lɛ, jarayeli maji wuji lɛ yɛ tsɔnei ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni feɔ ŋmaa ni he tse ni jara wa waa kɛhaa mɛi ni heɔ jarayeli lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and delicate root systems that burn easily under full sunlight. They need partial shade from nurse crops like plantains to retain leaf moisture and cool down until they are strong enough to handle bright sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo fã ko kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛɔ helatsɛmɛi anɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛbaai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe ajɔɔ kɛyashi amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhe hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ.

english: Why do my chili pepper plants wilt during the middle of the day but stand firm again by morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi chili tso lɛ gboɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ? Shi shidaamɔ ekoŋŋ leebi?

english: During hot afternoons, pepper plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can take it up from the soil, causing temporary wilting. As temperatures cool down in the evening and night, the plant recovers its water balance and bounces back.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be kukuoo mli Kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ kɛ gbɛkɛ lɛ Tso lɛ baaná nu ni eyɔɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ ni ebaaku esɛɛ eba.

english: Why is it better to water my vegetable crops early in the morning rather than during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mawo mitsei lɛ nu leebi fe shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ?

english: Watering in the early morning allows the soil to absorb moisture and feed the crop roots before the sun gets strong. If you water during hot afternoons, much of the water evaporates instantly into the air, wasting effort and leaves can burn under scorching water droplets.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni eŋɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ niyenii dani hulu lɛ mli waa tsɔ. Kɛji okɛ nu wo mli yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ Nu lɛ babaoo shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Mɔdɛŋbɔɔ ni afiteɔ Ni baai baanyɛ ashã yɛ nu ni shãa lɛ shishi.

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants and causes their pollen to dry out and become sterile. Because the flowers cannot be fertilized properly under high heat, the plant drops them to conserve its energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ. ni ehaa pollen lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ehaa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, anyɛɛɛ afee fɔfɔi jogbaŋŋ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa shishi. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ akafite hewalɛ lɛ, amɛshiɔ fɔfɔii lɛ amɛgbeleɔ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly into narrow tubes when the dry spell sets in?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ mi-abele baai lɛ ebɔle tsɔne bibioo ko mli shiŋŋ lɛ? Beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baa?

english: Rolling up leaves is a self-defense mechanism maize uses to survive heat. By curling its leaves inward, the plant reduces the leaf surface area exposed to the sun and wind, slowing down moisture loss.
ga: Baai ni atsiɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ ehe ni ŋmãa kɛtsuɔ nii koni enyɛ ehi wala mli yɛ dɔlɛ mli. Kɛ́ atsɔ baai lɛ anɔ awo mli lɛ, ebaa baa lɛ hiɛ ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Ha ŋmɔtɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ aya hiɛ

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my cassava plants yellow and drop off during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants shed their lower leaves during dry spells to cut down on water consumption. By dropping older leaves, the plant protects its main stem and stores vital energy in the underground tubers until rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛshishi baai lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli koni akɛba nu ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ shi. Tso lɛ buɔ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ he ni ekɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tso lɛ mli kɛtsɔ baai ni egbɔ ni ejieɔ lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my seeds take much longer to sprout when the soil is cold and heavily soaked with rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Seeds require air and warm soil temperatures to activate germination. Excess rainwater fills all soil air pockets and lowers soil temperature, which slows down seedling emergence and can cause seeds to rot underground.
ga: Dumɔwui he hiaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ mli dɔlɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃. Nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ latsaa lɛ aba shi Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ aya hiɛ fioo. ni ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why should I plant beans or groundnuts together with my maize on the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and groundnuts take nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots. This naturally enriches the soil with free fertilizer, which feeds the maize and improves crop yields.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni haa ŋmãa hewalɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ yaa hiɛ

english: Why do my yam vines dry up and turn brown on top of the soil when the yams are mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ mli egbi ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: When yam tubers reach full maturity, the plant naturally stops sending water and food to the above-ground leaves and branches. It transfers all remaining nutrients down into the tuber, causing the foliage to wither naturally.
ga: Kɛji akɛ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ dara kwraa lɛ Tsei lɛ kpaɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni amɛtsuɔ amɛbaai kɛ amɛniji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ebaajie niyenii mli nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ kɛba shi kɛya tuber lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do my harvested maize grains rot or get moldy quickly if I bag them right after harvesting in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ fiteɔ loo ehiɛɔ oya kɛji akɛ awo kotoku mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni akpa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested grain contains high internal moisture, especially during rainy periods. If bagged immediately without proper sun-drying, the trapped moisture creates an ideal breeding ground for mold and grain-boring insects.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akpa ehee lɛ yɛ mligbɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa babaoo. Titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli Kɛji akɛ awo kotoku lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni hulu lɛ mli egbiko lɛ Fɛ̃i ni emɔ mli lɛ feɔ he ko ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ŋmeii kɛ dumɔwui ni shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ yɛ.

english: Sir, why do rubber trees produce that white milky liquid when we cut the bark?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni hewɔ rɔbɔt tso lɛ jieɔ nu yɛŋ ni tamɔ atatu kɛji wɔfo tso lɛ yibii lɛ?

english: That white liquid is called latex. The tree produces it naturally to heal its bark when injured, sealing cuts to protect itself from pests and diseases.
ga: Atsɛɔ nakai nu yɛŋ lɛ akɛ latex. Tsei feɔ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛkɛbu amɛhewolo lɛ he kɛji amɛpila. Tsɔɔmɔ pilamɔi lɛ koni obu ohe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai ahe.

english: Why is it better to cut or tap my rubber trees early in the morning instead of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaafo loo atswa rɔbɔt tsei leebi moŋ fe shwane lɛ?

english: In the cool early morning, water pressure inside the tree trunk is at its highest, which makes the liquid latex flow out much faster and longer than in the hot afternoon heat.
ga: Yɛ leebi ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ mli lɛ Nu ni tsiimɔ yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ fe fɛɛ. Enɛ haa nu ni ji latex lɛ hoɔ oya ni etsɛɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Sir, why do my rubber trees stop dripping latex when the dry season comes?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni hewɔ mi rɔba tso lɛ kpaɔ latɛs feemɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During the dry season, the tree loses water and conserves its energy to survive, which causes the water pressure inside the trunk to drop and temporarily slows down or stops the sap flow.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ Tsei lɛ fiteɔ nu ni amɛbuɔ hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi. Enɛ haa nu ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ baa shi ni ehaa nu lɛ hoɔ blɛoo loo be kukuoo ko.

english: Why does heavy rain ruin the milky liquid if it falls while the tree is dripping into the cup?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fiteɔ nu ni tamɔ mliki lɛ kɛji egbee shi yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ hoɔ kɛboteɔ kɔɔpoo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rainwater mixes directly with the fresh sap in the cup, diluting it and causing it to wash away or spoil before it can curdle and be collected.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ futuɔ mliki hee ni yɔɔ kɔɔpoo lɛ mli lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Ehaa nu shwieɔ shi ni efoɔ loo efiteɔ dani ebɔleɔ ehe ni ebua ehe naa.

english: How many years does a young rubber tree need to grow before I can start harvesting latex from it?
ga: Afii enyiɛ esa akɛ rɔbɔt tso bibioo ko adara dani enyɛ ekpa latɛs?

english: Rubber trees usually need about five to seven years of steady growth until their trunks grow thick enough—about the width of a human thigh—to safely endure regular harvesting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ehe bahiaa ni rɔba tsei lɛ ada be fɛɛ be afii enumɔ kɛyashi kpawo kɛyashi amɛshishifã lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa. (aaafee gbɔmɔ tsitsi lɛ mlilɛɛmɔ) koni ekɛdamɔ ŋmaakpamɔ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ naa shweshweeshwe

english: Why do all the leaves on my rubber trees turn yellow and drop off at the same time of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-gum tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ afi lɛ mli be kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: This is a natural process called leaf shedding or wintering. The tree drops its leaves during the dry period to conserve water and protect itself from drying out.
ga: Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ shedding loo winter. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Sir, why do some of my rubber trees give plenty of sap while others of the exact same age give very little?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni hewɔ mi rɔba tsei lɛ ekomɛi jieɔ latɛs babaoo lɛ? yɛ be mli ni rɔbɔt tsei krokomɛi Yɛ afii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ haa latɛs fioo ko pɛ?

english: Yield depends on the individual tree's health, soil quality in that specific spot, amount of sunlight it receives, and natural genetic variations among seedlings.
ga: Yibiiwoo damɔ tso fɛɛ tso hewalɛnamɔ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ mlihilɛ yɛ nakai beaŋ Hulu la ni anáa kɛ dumɔwui amli tsakemɔi

english: Can I plant food crops like maize or cassava between my young rubber trees while waiting for them to mature?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Ani manyɛ madu mi-gum tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni amɛdara lɛ?

english: Yes, during the first two to three years when the trees are small, intercropping with food crops works well, though you should keep heavy root crops like cassava slightly away from the young tree stems.
ga: Hɛɛ, yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ lɛ mli beni tsei lɛ daraaa lɛ. Nibii ni akɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ ekome kɛduɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Eyɛ mli akɛ esa akɛ okɛ tsei ni shishifãi ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmei lɛ ato amɛhe fioo kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ahe moŋ.

english: What will happen to my rubber tree if I cut too deep into the wood when harvesting sap?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi rɔba tso lɛ nɔ kɛji mifo mli tsɔ beni mikpaa rɔba lɛ?

english: Cutting into the wood damages the living layer underneath the bark, creating permanent scars that stop fresh bark from regrowing smoothly and can cause the trunk to rot.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli lɛ, efiteɔ wala yibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni hiɔ shi daa ni haaa tso lɛ yibii heei afee ehee jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa. ni ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ tso lɛ agbo.

english: Why do weeds and grass grow so much faster around young rubber trees than around old ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kɛ jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ rɔbɔt tsei bibii amli fe tsei ni edara lɛ?

english: Young rubber trees have small branches that let sunlight reach the damp soil directly, feeding weed growth, whereas fully grown trees block out the sun with a thick leafy roof.
ga: Rɔba tso bibioo ko yɛ niji bibii. ni haa hulu la lɛ shɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ Ha jwɛi lɛ niyenii yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda lɛ kɛ baai ni mli edɔ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, a key nutrient plants need to grow green and strong. It can also happen when heavy rains wash away soil nutrients or when excess water stays around the roots for too long.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛɛmɛi ji niyenii titrii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ loo kɛ́ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ tara shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: Why do my crops perform so poorly when I plant maize on the exact same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyaaa nɔ jogbaŋŋ beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly drains the same specific nutrients from the soil every season and lets maize-loving pests build up in the dirt. Rotating your field with leguminous crops like groundnuts or cowpeas restores soil nitrogen and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be ni ehaa ŋmeii ni sumɔɔ abɛi lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii atsake he ni oyɔɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under strong direct sunlight and high heat. They need temporary shade from larger forest trees or plantain plants to protect them and keep the soil moist while their root systems develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa shishi. Ehe miihia ni amɛná be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛjɛ koo mli tsei wuji loo dumɔwui amli koni ebu amɛhe ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why do I get small bunches of plantain when I leave all the young shoots growing around the main mother plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miyɛ plantain tsei bibii lɛ? Mɛɛ be oshiɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ tso titri lɛ nyɛ lɛ he?

english: All those extra young shoots, called suckers, steal water and food from the main plant. Pruning away extra suckers so only two or three remain allows the mother plant to direct its energy into growing large, heavy bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei bibii ni fata he lɛ fɛɛ, ni atsɛɔ amɛ tsei lɛ, juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afo tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ amli koni tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ahi shi lɛ, ehaa tso nyɛ lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ lɛ ewoɔ kui agboi ni tsii amli.

english: Yam leaves need to capture as much direct sunlight as possible to produce the energy required to grow large underground tubers. Staking lifts leaves off the damp ground, improving sunlight exposure and preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato baai lɛ aná hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni ekɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji lɛ aba. Staking baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la lɛ yaa hiɛ ni ekɛtsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and twisting into tight shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle ehe ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites, or viruses spread by whiteflies. These pests feed on leaf sap, causing the young leaves to deform and stunt the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo virus ni whiteflies gbɛɔ eshwaa Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ yeɔ baa mli nu. Ehaa baai bibii lɛ fiteɔ ni etsĩɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ naa.

english: Why do insect pests attack my vegetables much more when my farm is full of weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo tutuaa mi aduawai lɛ be mli ni jwɛi eyi miŋmɔ lɛ mli obɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds act as safe hiding places, food sources, and breeding grounds for insects and plant diseases. Clearing weeds starves pests, improves airflow around crops, and ensures crops get full access to soil nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii akɛ he ni kooloi bibii kɛ tsei ahe helai fɔɔ yɛ, niyenii ni amɛyeɔ, kɛ he ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni amɛfɔɔ yɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ yaa hiɛ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa niyenii kpakpai babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: What causes my cassava tubers to rot in the soil before I am ready to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa?

english: Cassava tuber rot is mainly caused by excess water trapped in heavy soil or fungal diseases during periods of high rainfall. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away from the roots.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni etsi shikpɔŋ ni mli wa mli loo ŋmeii helai ni baa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa be mli lɛ ji nɔ titri ni kɛ ŋmeii shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without producing any actual fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences stress from very high afternoon temperatures, extreme drought, or a lack of soil nutrients like calcium and boron during flowering.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa waa lɛ hao tsei lɛ. hɔmɔ ni naa wa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tamɔ calcium kɛ boron ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli.

english: Why do the leaves of my crop droop during hot afternoons even when I watered the soil in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli be mli ni mi lɛ shwieee shi lɛ? Nɛgbɛ mikɛ nu woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ leebi?

english: Leaves droop temporarily in intense heat because the plant loses water into the air faster than its roots can pull water from the soil. If the leaves recover by evening, it is just the plant's natural way of protecting itself from drying out.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli ejaakɛ tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ he wa yɛ gbɛkɛ mli lɛ No ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ naa gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔlɔ he kɛkɛ.

english: Why do I need to cut down my whole cocoa tree if only a few leaves are showing signs of sickness?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mifoɔ cacao tso muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛji akɛ baai fioo komɛi pɛ hela mɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Diseases like the Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus travel through the entire sap system of the tree. Even if only a few leaves look sick, the virus is already inside the whole tree and will quickly spread to neighboring healthy cocoa trees if the infected tree is not cut down completely.
ga: Helai tamɔ Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus lɛ tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ mli fɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ baai fioo komɛi pɛ tamɔ nɔ ni hela mɔ amɛ po lɛ, Shi no mli lɛ, hela lɛ miitswa kookoo tso muu lɛ fɛɛ momo. ni ebaagbɛ eshwa oya kɛya kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ. Kɛji akɛ afolɔko tso ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ lɛ kwraa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees stop bearing plenty of pods when their branches become very bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ kpaɔ ŋmeii babaoo ni amɛwoɔ lɛ beni amɛniji lɛ feɔ ŋmeii waa lɛ?

english: When cocoa branches grow too thick and overcrowded, sun rays cannot reach the inner stems and lower trunk where pods grow. Pruning excess branches allows light and air to move freely through the tree, which encourages more flowering and pod growth.
ga: Beni kookoo niji lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbɔjɔ tsɔ. Hulu la nyɛŋ ashɛ tsei lɛ amli kɛ shishigbɛ he ni ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli oya. Enɛ baaha fɔfɔi babaoo kɛ pod lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Can using the same pruning slasher on all my cocoa trees cause sickness to spread?
ga: Ani tsɔne kome ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ cacao tso fɛɛ tso nɔ lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ hela aba?

english: Yes, cutting an infected cocoa tree leaves diseased plant sap on the slasher blade. When you use that same tool on a healthy tree, the fresh cut allows the disease to pass directly into the healthy tree's system.
ga: Hɛɛ, cacao tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa tso ni hela emɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ shwieɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ okɛ nakai dɛŋdadei lɛ nɔŋŋ tsu nii yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ lɛ, Fresh cuttings haa hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How does clearing my land with a slashing machine help my new cocoa farm better than burning the bush?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni mikɛ slasher tsuɔ he nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-kokoo ŋmɔ hee lɛ jogbaŋŋ fe jwɛi lɛ ni mikɛshãa lɛ?

english: Slashing leaves plant material on top of the ground to form a natural blanket. This blanket decomposes into organic fertilizer, keeps the soil moist, and protects young cocoa roots from harsh sunshine, whereas burning destroys nutrients and dries out the land.
ga: Shearing shwieɔ tsei ahe nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ koni ekɛfee adebɔɔ mli blanket. Nɛkɛ blanket nɛɛ baafite ni etsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo shishifãi bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he yɛ be mli ni shãa fiteɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbiɔ.

english: How long must I wait before planting new cocoa seedlings in a spot where I removed a sick tree?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani madu kookoo dumɔwui heei yɛ he ni ajie tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: It is best to wait a few months after clearing the sick tree and removing its main roots. This rest period gives time for any remaining disease pathogens in the soil and root debris to die off before young seedlings go into the ground.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi beni ajie tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajie amɛshishifãi titrii lɛ sɛɛ. Hejɔɔmɔ be nɛɛ haa be ni helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni eshwɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli kɛ shishifãi ni etse ehe lɛ gboiɔ dani dumɔwui lɛ shɛɔ sũ lɛ he.

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves during severe dry weather as a natural way to conserve water. Without enough ground moisture or shade trees overhead, the heat stresses the plant, forcing it to drop leaves so it does not dry out entirely.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi waa lɛ. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ nu he. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ adɛŋ lɛ, Dɔlɛ lɛ baaha tso lɛ aná nɔnyɛɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ akagbi kwraa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees grow very tall and thin with very few pods when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe tsei fioo pɛ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When trees are planted too closely, they compete with each other for sunlight and shoot straight upward instead of spreading out branches. This leaves the trunks thin and reduces the side branches where cocoa pods usually form.
ga: Kɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ ni amɛshwieɔ ŋwɛi tɛ̃ɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaagbɛ amɛniji lɛ amɛshwã. Tsɔɔmɔ tso lɛ shishi ni otsi niji ni yɔɔ esɛɛ he ni bei pii lɛ kookoo ŋmeii fɔɔ baa lɛ shi.

english: Why do some of the small, young cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii komɛi feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Tiny pods often shrivel up due to a natural process where the tree sheds pods it cannot feed, or because of fungal infections like Black Pod disease caused by excessive dampness and poor airflow around the tree.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni yaa nɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ nɔ ni ayeee. aloo yɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni tamɔ black pod hela ni jɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ehiii ni bɔleɔ tso lɛ he lɛ hewɔ.

english: What will happen to my cocoa tree if I slash and prune it during the peak of the dry season?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-kokoo tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mifo amɛ ni mifo amɛ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Pruning in the middle of a dry spell exposes the main branches directly to intense sunlight without the cover of leaves, causing bark sunburn and heavy stress that can stunt or kill the tree.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ haa hulu la shɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛbaa lɛ haaa amɛhe ajɔ amɛ. Enɛ haa hulu lɛ shãa tso lɛ yibii lɛ, ni ehaa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli waa ni baanyɛ aha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ loo egbe lɛ.

english: How do I know if the swelling on my cocoa tree branches is caused by disease or just normal growth?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hela loo bɔ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ ni mi-kookoo niji lɛ efuu lɛ?

english: Normal tree growth leaves the bark smooth and uniform, while swollen shoot disease creates unnatural, lumpy swellings on young shoots and roots, often accompanied by yellow patterns on the leaves.
ga: Tso lɛ dalɛ ni sa lɛ haa tso lɛ yibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ po baa. yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii ni fũuɔ lɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii kɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ fũu ni jeee adebɔɔ naa nɔ, ni ji ŋmeii baa. Bei pii lɛ, amɛyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay green and healthy. Applying a nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or NPK can help restore the green color and boost plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo NPK ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii aku sɛɛ aba ni eha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why does adding animal manure make my sandy farm soil hold water longer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mi ŋã ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Manure acts like a natural sponge in the soil. It mixes with the sand to hold onto water and nutrients that would normally wash away quickly, keeping the moisture available for your crops' roots.
ga: Manure tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli sponji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Akɛ ŋã futuɔ mli koni nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni kulɛ ebaaho oya lɛ ahi mli. Koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ

english: How do I know which way to push cassava stem cuttings into the soil when planting?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni esa akɛ otsi ŋmei niji awo shikpɔŋ mli kɛ́ oodu?

english: Look closely at the small bumps or 'eyes' on the stem where old leaves grew; make sure these buds are pointing upward toward the sky before planting so the cassava sprouts correctly.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii loo ‘ŋmeii’ ni yɔɔ baai ni edara lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kwɛmɔ akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ miitsɔɔ ŋwɛi dani odu koni ŋmei lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it dangerous to plant my maize seeds immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a hot dry spell before the continuous rains start. Seeds that sprout after that first rain can easily dry up and die in the hot soil if no rain falls for the next few weeks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔ lɛ yaa nɔ nɛɔ. Dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ agbi oya ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ yɛ otsii fioo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli.

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. Leaving some large trees or planting fast-growing plantains provides the shade and cool air young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya kɛji akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Tsei wuji ni aaashi loo adu plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ baaha kookoo bibii lɛ aná hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and thin with very small cobs when I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa beni midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. They spend all their energy growing tall to reach light instead of building big, heavy cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛdara koni amɛshɛ la lɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetswa cob agbo ni tsii

english: What is eating small ragged holes in the middle leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni ji buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ mi-bibii ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ yeli?

english: Ragged holes in the center leaves of young corn are usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. It hides inside the central funnel of the plant during the day and chews on the tender leaves before they open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ baa. Ekɛ ehe teeɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ yɛ gbi mli. ni okɛ baai bibii lɛ atsu nii dani ogbele amɛ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny pests like thrips, aphids, or whiteflies sucking the sap from young leaves, or by a virus transmitted by these insects as they feed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ thrips, aphids, loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛbaa beni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences heat stress or uneven watering. If the weather is extremely hot or the soil dries out completely while flowering, the plant drops its blossoms to save water.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli. Tsei baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to produce poor yields if I delay clearing them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa yibiiwoo kpakpa aba miŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛji mikɛ jwɛi lɛ shwiemɔ sɛɛ tsɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal soil food, water, and sunlight directly from your crop plants. Removing weeds early during the first month gives your crops total access to the nutrients they need to produce a good harvest.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ, nu kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ onibii amli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkpa nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is drip irrigation, and how does it help my crops grow better than using a watering can?
ga: Mɛni ji nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi? Ni te eyeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ jogbaŋŋ fe bɔ ni mikɛ nu woɔ mli lɛ?

english: Drip irrigation uses thin tubes to drop water slowly directly onto the soil at the base of your plants. This ensures water goes straight to the roots where the plant needs it most, reducing water waste and keeping leaves dry to prevent fungal diseases.
ga: Drip nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ kɛ paipi bibioo ko tsuɔ nii. koni ekɛ nu ashwie shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ fiofio Enɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ yɛ he ni tso lɛ he hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ. Tsɔɔmɔ nu ni afiteɔ kɛ baai ni egbi lɛ nɔ koni akafee tsɛŋemɔ helai.

english: Will watering my crops directly at their roots make them stronger than spraying water over all the leaves?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha amɛhe awa fe nu ni mikɛshwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, targeted root watering allows plants to absorb moisture efficiently without wasting energy. Wetting leaves unnecessarily under the hot sun can scorch them or encourage diseases, whereas root watering keeps the soil around the roots consistently moist.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni akɛhaa shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛheɔ nu jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfiteee hewalɛ. Kɛ́ afɔ baai lɛ anɔ nu ni he ehiaaa yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã baai lɛ loo ewo helai ahe hewalɛ, yɛ be mli ni kɛ́ afɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ nu fe nine lɛ, ebaafite shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ. Shishifãi lɛ mli fũuɔ be fɛɛ be.

english: What is a micro-sprinkler, and when should I use it on my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji tsɔne bibioo ni akɛshwieɔ nu nɔ? Ni mɛɛ be esa akɛ mikɛtsu nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: A micro-sprinkler is a small nozzle that sprays a fine mist of water over a tiny area. It is best used for young seedlings or delicate crops that need gentle moisture without heavy water drops washing away the soil.
ga: Micro sprinkler ji tsɔne bibioo ko ni akɛshwieɔ nu ni mli tse jogbaŋŋ nɔ yɛ he bibioo ko nɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛha dumɔwui bibii loo tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni biɔ nu ni mli edɔ fioo ni nu ni tsii ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ mli lɛ.

english: During intense sun, crops lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it from the soil, causing temporary wilting to protect themselves. If the soil is moist, the leaves will usually bounce back once the sun cools down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gboɔ be kukuoo ko koni ekɛbu ehe. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ baaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba kɛji hulu lɛ jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: How do I tell if my crops are getting too much water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiná nu babaoo tsɔ?

english: When crops get too much water, their leaves often turn yellow, feel soft or mushy, and the soil stays muddy. Excess water drowns the roots by blocking air, which stops the plant from taking up nutrients properly.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei lɛ ná nu babaoo lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ebaai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ. Ani enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ blɛoo loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ? Ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ efee muji lolo. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsiɔ amɛnaa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ nyɛŋ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it better for me to water my farm early in the morning instead of during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli nu leebi moŋ fe shwane?

english: Watering early in the morning gives plants time to drink before the sun gets hot, and less water is lost to evaporation. Watering in peak afternoon heat wastes water to steam and can stress the hot crop tissue.
ga: Nu ni afɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ haa tso lɛ náa be ni ekɛnuɔ nu dani hulu lɛ tsoɔ. kɛ nu ni laajeɔ kɛjɛɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Nu ni awoɔ yɛ shwane mli la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ baaha nu lɛ atsɔ la ni hoɔ. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ haomɔ aba tso lɛ mli fãji ni mli edɔ lɛ anɔ

english: Why do wet crop leaves develop spots and rot during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai ni efɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Many crop diseases are caused by tiny fungi that thrive in warm, damp conditions. When water sits on crop leaves for hours, it creates the perfect home for leaf spots and rot to spread quickly across your farm.
ga: Fungi bibii kɛ tsei ahelai babaoo baa. ni shwereɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli Beni nu ta tsei ahe baai anɔ ŋmɛlɛtswai babaoo. Nu lɛ feɔ shia ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha baai amli ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why are some farmers growing pepper and tomatoes inside rice sacks instead of directly in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmãa kotokui amli moŋ fe ni amɛduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Planting in sacks lets farmers control the soil quality, save water, and protect crops from soil-borne diseases present in the ground. It also allows you to grow vegetables easily in small spaces or areas with rocky soil.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ kotokui amli lɛ haa okwaafoi nyɛɔ amɛkwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, amɛbuɔ nu he jogbaŋŋ ni amɛbuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baa lɛ ahe. Ehaa onyɛɔ oduɔ aduawai yɛ hei bibii loo hei ni tɛi yɔɔ lɛ hu mlɛo.

english: Do crops planted inside bags need more frequent watering than crops in the main field?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni awo tsei ni adu yɛ kotokui amli lɛ nu shii abɔ fe tsei ni yɔɔ saatsoi wuji amli lɛ?

english: Yes, soil in bags and containers dries out faster than open land because the heat touches all sides of the bag and drainage is quick. They need smaller, more frequent amounts of water to stay healthy.
ga: Hɛɛ, sũ ni yɔɔ kotokui kɛ tsɛnsii amli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya fe hei ni yɔɔ faŋŋ lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, la ni tsoɔ lɛ taa kotoku lɛ fãi fɛɛ ahe ni nu lɛ hoɔ oya. Nu fioo pɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛnuɔ shii abɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Can I set up automated drip water pipes to feed crops that are planted in separate sacks?
ga: Ani manyɛ mato hose ni hoɔ nu ni haa nu hoɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni ekɛ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awo kotokui sɔrɔtoi amli?

english: Yes, you can run a main hose along a line of planting sacks and attach tiny drip tubes into each bag. This delivers a set amount of water directly into every sack automatically, saving you time and heavy lifting.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ hose wulu lɛ atsɔ grow sack lɛ nɔ ni okɛ paipi bibioo ko ni hoɔ nu lɛ afata he. abaanyɛ akɛwo kotoku fɛɛ kotoku mli. Ekɛ nu abɔ ni atsɔɔ lɛ woɔ kotoku fɛɛ kotoku mli lɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Ehaa onáa be kɛ nibii ni tsii ni owoɔ lɛ.

english: How does water from the soil manage to travel all the way up to the top leaves of my tall plantain trees?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni nu ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ayashɛ mi-plantain kakadaŋŋ lɛ baai lɛ ashishi?

english: Plants have small inner tubes that act like drinking straws. As sunlight causes water to evaporate from the leaves, it creates a gentle pull that sucks fresh water and dissolved nutrients from the roots all the way up to the leaves.
ga: Tso lɛ yɛ mligbɛ tsɔne bibioo ko ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ jwɛi ni anuɔ nii. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu la haa nu shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli. Ehaa hewalɛ ko ni gbalaa mɔ blɛoo ni ekɛgbalaa nu kpakpa kɛ niyenii ni mli ewo la kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛyaa baai lɛ amli.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa plants wilt and dry up when there is too much hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves have very delicate skins that lose water faster than their small roots can drink it up. In direct heat, the plant wilts to protect itself from losing more water, which is why providing shade trees helps keep them cool and healthy.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa ni nu fiteɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Tsei lɛ baagbi koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe koni nu babaoo akafite amɛ. Enɛ hewɔ ni otsei lɛ ni ooofee shade lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛhaa amɛhe jɔɔ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flower buds fall off the plant before turning into actual fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato ŋmɔji lɛ miigbee shi kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani ebatsɔ anɔkwa yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from severe heat, sudden dry spells, or lack of food in the soil. Maintaining steady moisture and rich soil helps the flowers stay attached and turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔshiimɔ trukaa loo niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo be fɛɛ be kɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ yɔɔ fɛo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that the maize plant is missing key food nutrients from the soil, particularly nitrogen. When the plant does not get enough food through its roots, it cannot produce the green color needed to make its energy.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ bɛ niyenii titrii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen Kɛ́ tso lɛ nine shɛɛɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ kɛjɛɛɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ Enyɛŋ ejie ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa koni ekɛfee hewalɛ lɛ kɛkɛ.

english: When seeds are planted too closely, their roots fight underground for the same food and water, while their leaves fight for sunlight. Giving plants enough space allows each root to get full nourishment and grow big harvest yields.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Eshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ baawu koni amɛná hulu la. Kɛ́ aha tsei lɛ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ eko fɛɛ eko nine shɛɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ nɔ, ni ehaa yibiiwoo lɛ yaa hiɛ waa.

english: Yam vines climb so their leaves can spread out and catch as much sunlight as possible. Sunlight helps the leaves manufacture food, which travels down to make the yam tuber under the ground grow big and thick.
ga: Akwɔɔ sweet potato wain tsei anɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni aaanyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛwoɔ niyenii. ni fãa gbɛ kɛyaa shi ni ehaa sweet potato tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground when heavy rain floods my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa ni eha miŋmɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ?

english: Roots need air in the soil just like they need water. When water stays trapped around cassava roots for too long without draining, the roots cannot breathe and begin to rot, which is why planting on soil mounds or ridges helps drain water away.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli taakɛ nu he hiaa amɛ lɛ. Beni nu ebɔle he lɛ Kasava shishifãi lɛ yaa shɔŋŋ tsɔ ni amɛjieee nu lɛ. Shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ. Yɛ yiŋtoo nɛɛ hewɔ lɛ, dumɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Why should I plant beans or groundnuts on my land after harvesting maize, instead of planting maize again?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mikpa ŋmeii lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaadu ŋmãa ekoŋŋ lɛ

english: Maize consumes a lot of nutrients from the soil. Planting beans or groundnuts afterwards helps feed the soil naturally by putting vital nutrients back in, preparing the ground for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekɛ ehe awo mli ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni ekɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ. Koni akɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha dumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow poorly even when I give my crops plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ nu babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds are fast-growing plants that steal water, sunlight, and soil food directly away from your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures that all the nourishment goes straight to your main crop.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni daa oya ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ yaa oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Pests like the Fall Armyworm prefer to eat the softest, newest leaves inside the center funnel of the plant where it is moist and safe. Catching and treating them early stops them from destroying the growing point of your crop.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛye tso lɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ehee fe fɛɛ lɛ, he ni amɛhe yɔɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛyɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ. Amɛmɔmɔ ni otsa amɛ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni amɛkafite hei ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily in direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside your young cocoa provides shade and preserves soil moisture until the trees are strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ odu hulutsoo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ o-cocoa bibioo lɛ masɛi lɛ, ebaaha oná hulutsoo ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi tsei lɛ baaná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ hulutsoo be muu lɛ fɛɛ gbɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which crops need to grow green and healthy. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer can restore their color and growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Biɛ ji he ni ehe hiaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha ehiɛ afee fɛo ni ekwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava stems very close to each other to get more yield from my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing allows each plant to get enough food and light to develop larger, heavier tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛ bulbs wuji ni tsii.

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm, a common pest that hides inside the central funnel of young corn. Checking leaves early and applying approved pest treatments directly into the plant funnels protects the growing points.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ naa yɛ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni oookwɛ baai lɛ amli mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ awo tso lɛ ŋmei lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaye abua ni abu he ni edaa yɛ lɛ he.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot inside the ground after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them in saturated soil because roots need air to stay healthy. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away naturally.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni eyi obɔ kɛ nu lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why is my land yielding less crop when I plant maize in the exact same field every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop every year drains the same specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the ground. Rotating corn with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores natural soil fertility.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni akwɛɔ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I keep my harvested tomatoes from rotting while I wait for farmgate transport to the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi tomato ni mikpa lɛ naa koni ekafite be mli ni amɛmiimɛ ni akɛ amɛ aya jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Harvesting produce early in the cool morning, using well-ventilated plastic crates instead of heavy sacks, and storing the harvested crop under tree shade prevents heat buildup and delays spoilage during transport delays.
ga: Akɛ plastic adekai ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkpaa nii leebi maŋkpa yɛ kotokui ni tsii najiaŋ. Ni nibii ni akpa lɛ ni akɛtoɔ tsei ashishi lɛ tsiɔ dɔlɛ ni baa lɛ naa ni ehaa efiteɔ sɛɛ tsɛɔ yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa he kroko yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: What can I put on my farm soil to keep my vegetables from drying up during hot, dry spells?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mikɛwo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ koni aduawai akagbi yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Covering the soil around your plant stems with dry grass, leaves, or palm leaves—a practice called mulching—traps soil moisture, blocks direct heat, and prevents water from evaporating quickly.
ga: Mulching ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi, baai, loo tsei ahe tsei ahe shwieɔ tsei lɛ ahe. Ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya.

english: Why do weeds growing near my crop plants make my crop yield small and thin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa lɛ?

english: Weeds grow rapidly and steal essential groundwater, sunlight, and plant nutrients directly from your crops. Clearing weeds early in the growth cycle ensures your main crops get all the food required to yield well.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni he hiaa, hulu la, kɛ tsei amli niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli mra yɛ be mli ni edara lɛ haa tso titri lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why do seeds saved from my previous maize harvest give smaller crops than fresh certified seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpa tsutsu lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii bibii fe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from harvested grain lose their strong genetic qualities over seasons and can carry diseases from the old crop, whereas fresh certified seeds are specially bred for maximum yield and disease resistance.
ga: Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ amɛfɔmɔ su ni mli wa lɛ kɛ bei lɛ hoɔ. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ helai ni jɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni etsɛ mli lɛ aba Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, akwɛɔ dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo ni helai akamɔ amɛ.

english: My cocoa yield has been dropping every year even though I work hard; could there be something wrong with my soil?
ga: Mi-cocoa ni mifeɔ lɛ miiba shi daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mitsuɔ nii waa moŋ. Ani ekolɛ nɔ ko yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ he?

english: Yes, over time, crops take up essential nutrients from the soil. If those nutrients are not replaced with fertilizer or organic matter like compost, the soil becomes exhausted, leading to smaller harvests.
ga: Hɛɛ, yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, Tsei lɛ shwieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ jeee nakai lɛ, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ato nakai niyenii lɛ najiaŋ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji kpamɔ fioo.

english: How can I tell if my farm's soil still has enough food left in it for my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni eshwɛ lolo kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Healthy soil is usually dark, retains moisture without staying muddy, and supports earthworms. If your plants grow slowly or have yellowish leaves despite getting enough water, the soil is likely low on nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa mli tseɔ. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni ekɛ muji baaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii Kɛji otso lɛ miida blɛoo loo eyɛ baai ŋmɔŋ. ni nine shɛɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ lolo lɛ Tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: If I cut down old trees and plant new crops in the same ground, will the new crops grow well right away?
ga: Kɛji mifo tso momo ko ni midu tso hee yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ. Ani tso hee lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Not always. Old trees may have used up specific soil nutrients over many years. It is best to enrich the soil with manure or fertilizer before planting new crops in the same spot.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be. Ekolɛ tsei ni egbɔ lɛ efite niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ afii babaoo. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii baatsake shikpɔŋ lɛ dani adu tsei heei yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ.

english: What is the difference between the older cocoa tree varieties and the newer ones available today?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ kookoo tsei momo lɛ kɛ henɔi heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɛnɛ lɛ ateŋ?

english: Older cocoa varieties take longer (5 to 7 years) to produce pods and grow very tall, whereas modern varieties start bearing fruit much faster (2 to 3 years), stay shorter, and tend to yield more pods.
ga: Kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii (afii 5 kɛyashi 7) ni amɛdaraa waa. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo henɔi lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi mra kwraa (afii 2 kɛyashi 3) lɛ, amɛyɛ be kukuoo. ni esumɔɔ ni ewo yibii babaoo

english: Can I still get a good harvest from my older cocoa trees, or do I have to replace them?
ga: Ani manyɛ maná ŋmaa kpakpa kɛjɛ kookoo tsei ni egbɔ lɛ amli lolo? Aloo ehe miihia ni makɛ tso hee ato cacao tso lɛ najiaŋ?

english: You can still get a good harvest from older trees if you prune them properly, protect them from diseases, and feed the soil with nutrients, though their output may eventually decline with extreme age.
ga: Obaanyɛ oná yibii kpakpai kɛjɛ tsei ni egbɔ lɛ amli lolo kɛji ofolɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ, otsĩ helai anaa, ni okɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ yɛ naagbee lɛ amɛyibiiwoo lɛ baa shi beni amɛdaraa lɛ moŋ.

english: Do cocoa trees naturally stop producing pods as they get older?
ga: Ani cacao tsei lɛ kpaɔ ŋmeii ni amɛfeɔ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: After about 25 to 30 years, a cocoa tree's productivity naturally slows down. While good management can prolong their output, very old trees eventually need to be replaced to maintain high yields.
ga: Yɛ aaafee afii 25 kɛyashi 30 sɛɛ lɛ, kookoo tso lɛ yibii lɛ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyɛ mli akɛ nɔkwɛmɔ kpakpa baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ moŋ, Shi yɛ naagbee lɛ, esa akɛ atsake tsei ni egbɔ waa lɛ koni ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo aya nɔ.

english: What does farm rehabilitation mean, and how does it help my farm?
ga: Mɛni ŋmɔ mli saamɔ tsɔɔ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Farm rehabilitation means restoring an unproductive farm by clearing weeds, pruning overgrown or diseased branches, reviving the soil, and replacing dead or weak trees with healthy young seedlings.
ga: Okwaafoi asaamɔ tsɔɔ akɛ abaatswa ŋmɔji ni wooo yibii lɛ ama shi ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ, ha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ, ni okɛ dumɔwui bibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ awo tsei ni egboi loo ni egbɔjɔ lɛ anajiaŋ.

english: Will pruning my old cocoa trees reduce the amount of harvest I get this year?
ga: Ani kookoo tsei momo ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ baaha afi nɛɛ kpamɔ lɛ aba shi?

english: Pruning may temporarily reduce the tree's foliage, but it helps long-term. Cutting away dead or weak branches allows sunlight in and directs the tree's energy into producing healthier, stronger pods.
ga: Tso lɛ he tsei ni afolɔ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ baai lɛ aba shi yɛ be kukuoo mli shi ebaaye ebua yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli. Niji ni egboi loo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la boteɔ mli ni ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni mli wa.

english: Why are my neighbor's cocoa trees producing so many pods while mine in the same area are struggling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ be mli ni ekutsoŋnyo lɛ cacao tso lɛ naa amanehulu lɛ?

english: Differences in harvest usually come down to soil fertility, the age and variety of the trees, and field care such as regular pruning, weeding, and protecting plants from pests.
