ga: Bei pii lɛ, srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmaakpamɔ mli lɛ damɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ. Afii kɛ tsei srɔtoi kɛ ŋmɔ mli kwɛmɔ tamɔ jwɛi ni afolɔ kɛ tsei ahebuu kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ahe

english: Why do some of my cocoa pods turn black and spoil before they are ready to pick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛfee klalo akɛ abaajie amɛ lɛ?

english: This is typically caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads in cool, overly shaded, or moist environments. Pruning excess leaves to let in sunlight helps prevent it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ lɛ Shade loo ŋmɔtɔ babaoo. Kɛ́ ofolɔ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la ashɛ amɛnɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ebu amɛhe.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are usually a sign that your crop is hungry for nitrogen. When there is not enough food in the soil, the plant pulls nitrogen from its old bottom leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa Tsei lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with thick leaves, but the tubers underground are tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni mli tse lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer and not enough potassium, the plant spends all its energy building big stems and leaves above ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers below.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ ni potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ bɛ lɛ, Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni tso lɛ kɛ starch baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ shishifãi wuji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving the young cocoa trees the shade and moisture they need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the sunlight to produce food for the root. Lifting the vines off the ground prevents leaf diseases and helps the plant produce larger tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã hulutsoo be lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha amɛshishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ owó wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ foliar helai anaa, ni ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ewo bulbs wuji.

english: Can I use vegetable or plant oil sprays from the Agric office to stop insects from eating my crop leaves?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ tsofa mli loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ tsofa mli ni jɛ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ atsu nii koni kooloi akaye mi tsei lɛ ahe baai?

english: Yes, botanical oil sprays coat insect bodies so they cannot breathe, and they leave a taste on leaves that deters pests from chewing without putting harsh synthetic chemicals on your food.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei amli fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ ahe bɔni afee ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu. Ni amɛshiɔ ŋmɔlɔ ko yɛ baai lɛ anɔ ni tsiɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye ni amɛkɛ tsofai ni akɛfee nibii ni mli wa fataaa oniyenii lɛ he.

english: Why are insect pests attacking my vegetables more during the dry season than in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo tutuaa mi aduawai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli fe nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Insects reproduce faster in warm weather, and rain normally washes small insects off leaves. Without rain to knock them off, pest populations grow quickly and feed heavily on dry crops.
ga: Kplukai fɔɔ oya yɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ lɛ. Ni bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ lɛ shwieɔ kooloi bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ anɔ, kɛji nugbɔ ko bɛ ni miigba amɛnaa. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ayibɔ baaya hiɛ oya ni amɛbaaye ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi babaoo.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off before producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures become too high or when water is unpredictable. Extreme heat damages pollen, causing the plant to drop its flowers to conserve energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nu lɛ mli. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ fiteɔ pollen. Enɛ haa tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Leaf curling in the afternoon heat is a defense mechanism. The leaf rolls inward to hide from direct sunlight, reducing water loss so the plant does not dry out.
ga: Baai lɛ ni shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ he. Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli koni amɛtee amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu ni laajeɔ lɛ baa shi No hewɔ lɛ tsei lɛ akagbi.

english: Why do my crops grow weak and thin when I plant too many seeds in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa beni miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, their roots fight over sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, causing every plant in that hole to stay thin and produce smaller yields.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ bu lɛ mli lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do the roots of my crops rot when rainwater sits on top of the soil for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water covers the ground for too long, it cuts off air supply, drowning the roots and causing rot.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nu ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Nu lɛ gbáa kɔɔyɔɔ ni baa lɛ mli, ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli, ni ehaa ŋmeii baa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are missing nitrogen, which acts like essential protein for plants. Adding well-rotted manure or the right fertilizer gives them the boost they need to stay green and grow healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ protein ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: If I plant cowpeas on the same land with my maize, will the cowpeas steal food from the maize?
ga: Kɛji midu tsina ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi ŋmãa yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ Ani tsina ŋmãa baaju niyenii kɛjɛ ŋmãa mli?

english: No, cowpeas actually help feed the maize. Legumes like cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil, acting like natural food that helps neighboring crops grow better.
ga: Dabi, tsina ŋmeii yeɔ ebuaa diɛŋtsɛ kɛhaa ŋmãa niyenii. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crop yields get smaller if I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yibiiwoo lɛ faaa kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Maize draws the same specific food nutrients out of the soil every season. Planting it continuously drains those nutrients completely and allows specific pests to build up in the soil.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Tsei ni yaa nɔ amɛdaraa lɛ jieɔ nakai niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi buaa amɛhe naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava leaves fold up and droop during the hottest hours of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava leaves fold or droop in intense heat to protect themselves from losing too much water. It is a natural self-defense behavior to save moisture until the weather cools down in the evening.
ga: Cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ fe nine lɛ he. Eji adebɔɔ mli su ni buɔ mɔ he akɛ aaahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashi gbɛkɛ lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow much slower during the harmattan season even when I manually water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji mi diɛŋtsɛ mikɛ nu wo mli po.

english: Dry harmattan winds and cool night air cause plants to conserve their energy and water. The crop slows its growth down to protect itself from drying out in the low-humidity air.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi kɛ gbɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ hewalɛ kɛ nu he. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ haa amɛdalɛ baa shi koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ fioo lɛ mli ni amɛgbi lɛ he.

english: What happens to my tomato plants if I plant the seeds too close to each other in the bed?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ saatso lɛ nɔ?

english: When tomato plants grow too close together, they fight for sunlight, air, water, and soil food. This competition makes them grow tall and thin, resulting in small and fewer fruits.
ga: Kɛji tomato tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa amɛfeɔ kakadaŋŋ ni amɛhe waaa, ni no haa amɛfeɔ bibii ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, shields the ground from the direct sun. It keeps the soil cool and locks in moisture so the yam roots stay fed and hydrated.
ga: Mulching ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli bɔni afee ni sweet potato shishifãi lɛ aná niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Will trimming off the bottom leaves of my tomato plants hurt the crop?
ga: Ani tomato tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ ni afolɔ lɛ baaye ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: No, removing the lowest leaves actually helps the plant. It stops soil diseases from jumping onto the leaves during rain and directs more energy into growing larger fruits.
ga: Dabi, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ ni ooofo lɛ baaye abua tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ akaho yɛ baai anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli, ni ekɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ aduawai wuji.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps the plant hold its flowers and form fruits.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa ha tso lɛ hao. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ fɔfɔii amli ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do weeds make my young crops look weak and stunted so quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi dumɔwui lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ oya lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster and are aggressive feeders. They quickly drink up the water and swallow the nutrients in the soil before your crop's roots have a chance to reach them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛyeɔ nii waa. Amɛnuɔ nu oya ni amɛyeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ dani otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ náa hegbɛ ni amɛshɛɔ amɛhe.

english: Young cocoa plants have shallow roots and tender leaves that cannot handle direct heat. Without shade plants like plantains nearby to block the harsh sun, the dry heat burns the leaves and dries out the soil before the roots can find water.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ gbɛ. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa tamɔ plantains bɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ ni baatsi hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa lɛ, Dɔlɛ ni mli egbi lɛ shãa baai lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ dani shishifãi lɛ naa nu.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the key food plants need to stay green. When food runs low in the soil, the plant moves its remaining nutrients to the new leaves at the top, leaving the bottom leaves to starve and turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe nɔ. Kɛ niyenii fioo pɛ eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tso lɛ tsiɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ anɔ. Ha baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ aye hɔmɔ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Planting maize in the same spot continuously drains the exact nutrients maize needs from the soil. It also allows pests and soil diseases that target maize to hide in the ground and grow stronger season after season.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ lɛ jeɔ abele lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ŋmãa lɛ sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni ekɛ ehiɛ fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ teeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni edaraa waa afi fɛɛ afi.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the liquid out from under the leaves, or by a virus spread by those insects. Curling prevents the leaf from catching sunlight properly to make food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ Curling tsiɔ baa lɛ naa koni ekashɛ hulu la lɛ he jogbaŋŋ koni akɛhoo nii.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off the stems before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi dani amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot, when the soil dries out too much, or when the plant lacks nutrients. When the plant gets stressed, it drops its flowers to save energy to keep itself alive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ Beni tsei lɛ miihao Ebaashwie fɔfɔi koni ekɛto hewalɛ ni ekɛha ehe ahi wala mli lɛ he.

english: How can I tell underground that my cassava roots are big enough to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the leaves at the bottom of the stem turn yellow and drop off, and when you see the soil around the base of the stem cracking open as the tubers swell underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ baai ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Ni kɛ́ ona shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli lɛ, egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni tuber lɛ mli fũuɔ yɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Yam is a climbing vine that needs to lift its leaves off the ground into the sunlight. Staking allows the leaves to spread out and catch light, which gives the plant the energy it needs to grow big tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni esa akɛ amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ koni hulu la ashɛ amɛnɔ. Staking haa baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni amɛheɔ la lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo bulb agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why should I remove some of the small shoots growing around my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni miida kɛbɔle Mi dumɔwui lɛ eje kpo.

english: When too many shoots grow from the same plantain base, they compete with the main tree for water and soil nutrients. Removing extra shoots leaves only the strongest ones, ensuring the main plant gets enough food to produce big bunches.
ga: Beni ŋmeii babaoo ni miida kɛjɛɔ plantain shishitoo kome mli lɛ Nakai ŋmeii lɛ kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ ashiɔ. Enɛ baaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do weeds stop my crops from growing big even when it rains well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi tsiɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anaa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than crops and steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight before the crop roots can take them in. Even with rain, the weeds eat the crop's food first, leaving the crop weak.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la dani tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ, jwɛi lɛ yeɔ tsei klɛŋklɛŋ. shi tso lɛ ni egbɔjɔ

english: The very first rain is often followed by a long dry period before the real rainy season settles in. If you plant too early, your seeds will sprout but then wither and die when the soil dries up completely.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be diɛŋtsɛ lɛ baashɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ shi amɛbaagboi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa.

english: Why is my cocoa farm suddenly producing fewer bags of cocoa this season compared to previous years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ miifee kookoo kotokui fioo yɛ afi nɛɛ mli kɛ akɛto afi ni eho lɛ he lɛ?

english: A sudden drop in harvest is usually a sign of an untreated disease or pest infestation spreading through your farm, or depleted soil nutrients preventing trees from producing full pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmaa ni abaakpa trukaa lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hela ko ni asaaa loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Aloo niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa ni no haa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ awo ŋmeii kwraa.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa trees are getting sick before I lose my entire harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cacao tsei lɛ hela mɔ amɛ dani amɛŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ afite?

english: Look for early warning signs such as yellowing or swollen leaves, strange lumps on stems, dark spots on green pods, or pods drying up and turning brown early.
ga: Taomɔ kɔkɔbɔɔ okadii mra tamɔ baa ŋmɔŋ loo efuu, kuji ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ yɛ tsei lɛ ashishi, kɛ hei ni tsuɔ yɛ tsei eŋɔli nɔ. Aloo ŋmeii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii oya.

english: This is typically caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in dark, overly damp conditions and attacks the pods, destroying the cocoa beans inside.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ewo duŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ fe nine lɛ, ni etutuaa ŋmei lɛ, ni efiteɔ kookoo ŋmei ni yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: If a disease affects just one cocoa tree in my farm, will it spread to my other healthy trees?
ga: Kɛji hela lɛ ba yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kookoo tso kome pɛ nɔ Ani ebaagbɛ eshwa mikookoo tsei krokomɛi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ?

english: Yes, cocoa diseases easily spread from tree to tree through wind, rain splashes, insects like mealybugs, or dirty farm tools used during pruning and harvesting.
ga: Hɛɛ, kookoo hela gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ oya kɛtsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii, loo ŋmɔ mli nibii ni he tseee ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ tso lɛ ŋmɔmɔ kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Can a disease actually completely ruin my cocoa farm and leave me with no bags at all at harvest time?
ga: Ani hela ko baanyɛ akpata mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ hiɛ kwraa ni eha mibɛ kotoku ko yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli?

english: Yes, severe diseases like Swollen Shoot Virus or untreated Black Pod can slowly kill your trees or destroy all your pods, reducing a harvest of many bags down to nothing.
ga: Hɛɛ, helai ni mli wa tamɔ Swollen Shoot Virus loo Black Pod ni ashi ni atsaaa lɛ baanyɛ agbe otsei lɛ fiofio. loo okpãtã o-pods lɛ fɛɛ ahiɛ Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, baagi babaoo ni akpaa lɛ eba shi kɛyashɛ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ nɔ ko kwraa.

english: Why does my cocoa yield keep dropping lower and lower every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ni mifeɔ lɛ yaa nɔ ebaa shi daa afi lɛ?

english: Yields decline continuously when a disease remains on the farm without treatment, gradually weakening more trees each season and stopping them from bearing pods.
ga: Nibii ni anáa lɛ yaa nɔ ebaa shi yɛ be mli ni hela lɛ yaa nɔ ehiɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni atsaaa lɛ, ni ehaa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ fiofio yɛ be fɛɛ mli ni ehaa amɛkpaa ŋmeii ni amɛwoɔ lɛ.

english: What should I do immediately if I notice a cocoa tree on my farm showing signs of disease?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji mina akɛ kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miitsɔɔ hela he okadi?

english: You should remove infected pods or cut away sick branches immediately, avoid moving tools from sick trees to healthy ones, and consult an extension officer to identify the exact illness.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ loo ofolɔ tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ dɛŋdadei ni oootsi kɛjɛ tso ni hela mɔ lɛ nɔ kɛya tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ lɛ he. ni obi mɔ ni kwɛɔ helatsamɔhe lɛ nɔ lɛ koni ona hela pɔtɛɛ ni eyɔɔ lɛ.

english: If my farm's yield has dropped from many bags down to almost zero, can the sick trees ever recover?
ga: Kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ mli yibiiwoo lɛ ba shi kɛjɛ kotokui babaoo mli kɛtee nɔ ni miihe ashɛ zero. Ani tso ni hela mɔ lɛ baanyɛ aná hewalɛ?

english: Trees infected with fungal diseases can often recover with proper spraying and care, but trees infected with viral diseases like Swollen Shoot cannot be cured and must be cut down to save the rest of the farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni tsɛŋemɔ helai emɔ amɛ lɛ baanyɛ aya hiɛ kɛji akɛ afɔse amɛ tsofa ni sa ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ. Shi tsei ni helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli, tamɔ amɛyitsei ni efuu lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ, anyɛɛɛ atsa amɛ kwraa. ni ehe bahia ni afo koni akɛhere ŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ yiwala.

english: Does leaving thick weeds and heavy shade around my cocoa trees make them more likely to get sick?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ hulutsoo ni tsii ni mashi yɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ ahe lɛ baaha amɛhe ajɔ amɛ waa?

english: Yes, high weeds and dense shade trap moisture and block sunlight, creating a damp environment where diseases and pests thrive and multiply quickly.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, jwɛi kakadaji kɛ shade ni mli ewo muji lɛ mɔ̃ɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛtsiɔ hulu la naa. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ baa ni helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ daa ni amɛfɔɔ oya.

english: How often should I walk through my farm to inspect my cocoa trees for sickness?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ matsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni makwɛ kɛji kookoo hela yɛ?

english: You should inspect your farm at least once a week during the growing season so you can catch early signs of sickness before it spreads to the rest of your trees.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, esa akɛ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli shikome yɛ otsi mli yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ. Enɛ ji koni onyɛ ona hela he okadii mra dani egbɛ eshwa otsei krokomɛi lɛ anɔ.

english: Yellowing on lower leaves is usually a sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential food for plant growth, or that waterlogging is stopping the roots from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Aloo nu ni hoɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground, reducing your yield over time.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, nitsumɔ ni otsuɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why shouldn't I spread fertilizer right before a heavy rain fall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ ashwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes fertilizer away from the plant's roots before it can absorb it, wasting your money and carrying the nutrients off into nearby streams.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ tsei shishifãi amli dani enyɛɔ eshɛɔ. Enɛ fiteɔ shika ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ yaa faai ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the soil without proper drainage, creating soggy conditions where root-rot fungi quickly spread and destroy the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. ni kɛ shihilɛi ni mli ewo fɔ baa Shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baagbɛ ashwã ni ekpata ŋmeii lɛ ahiɛ oya.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking the sap from young leaves, or by a virus transmitted by those insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ kɛbaa lɛ nɔ

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the developing fruit, usually triggered by irregular watering patterns.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛhaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ kɛ enɛ baa.

english: What happens if I plant my seed crops too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for light, soil nutrients, and water, resulting in thin, weak stems and lower crop yields.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ la mli akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa, ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi.

english: How do weeds actually reduce the amount of food my crop produces?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi lɛ haa niyenii ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ lɛ baa shi?

english: Weeds grow faster than main crops and steal essential sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, while also acting as breeding grounds for insect pests.
ga: Jwɛi daa oya fe tsei ni amɛ juɔ hulu la ni he hia, nu kɛ sũ mli niyenii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii hu akɛ he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai fɔɔ yɛ.

english: Cocoa trees shed their flowers when they suffer from water stress, sudden heat, lack of soil nutrients, or when beneficial insects fail to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Cocoa tsei baawo fɔfɔi kɛji nu he haomɔ miipiŋ amɛ. latsaa ni baa trukaa Niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo be mli ni kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee fɔfɔii lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ.

english: How does a short drought hurt my crops even if the plants do not die?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ hɔmɔ ni yeɔ be kukuoo lɛ yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui kɛji amɛgbooo po?

english: During dry spells, plants close their leaf pores to save water, which stops them from taking in air to make food, resulting in stunted growth and smaller harvests.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Tsei lɛ ŋaa amɛbaai lɛ amli koni amɛbu nu he. Enɛ haaa amɛmu kɔɔyɔɔ ni amɛkɛfee niyenii. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraaa oya, ni ŋmaa lɛ hu baaa shi.

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana. Spraying recommended insecticides or applying neem extracts directly into the center of the young plant early in the morning or late evening helps eliminate them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni awieɔ he akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ shwie shi loo okɛ neem mli nu lɛ wo tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie amɛ kɛjɛ mli dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning black and soft before they get mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani edaa lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, often due to irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the roots absorb calcium properly and prevents the fruit from rotting.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛnáa calcium lɛ jogbaŋŋ, ni ehaa aduawai lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why is it important for me to clear weeds from my field during the first month after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ ni mikɛdu nii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and will steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer from the soil. Clearing them in the first few weeks ensures your crops get all the nutrients they need to establish strong roots.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei bibii ni amɛbaaju nu, hulu la kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa otsei lɛ náa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen or that water is sitting around the roots for too long. Applying nitrogen-based fertilizer like Urea or NPK early in the plant's life helps restore the green color and supports healthy cob development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu eta shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Nitrogen ni akɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo NPK ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli mra lɛ baaye abua ni eha tso lɛ su lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ ni eye ebua ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Can I use dried poultry manure on my vegetable farm instead of buying chemical fertilizers?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ kooloi aŋmɔŋ ni egbi atsu nii yɛ mi-vegetables ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mahe tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Yes, dried and well-rotted poultry manure improves soil structure, holds water longer, and supplies slow-release nutrients to your crops without burning their roots like fresh manure or excessive chemical fertilizer can.
ga: Hɛɛ, kooloi ashishifã ni egbi ni egbo jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii yaa hiɛ. Ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni jeɔ kpo blɛoo lɛ baa onibii amli ni eshãaa shishifãi lɛ tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ.

english: Why do people advise me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the same land where I grow my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. Planting them alongside or in rotation with maize naturally enriches the soil with free nutrients for the maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Abele ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ loo yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa niyenii ni he ehiaaa ni abele lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain trees around my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo dumɔwui heei ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow quickly and produce large leaves that provide temporary shade and keep the air moist, protecting young cocoa plants until they grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli fũuɔ. Buu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: How far apart should I space my cassava cuttings when planting them on ridges?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ lɛ, gbɛ enyiɛ esa akɛ ahi ŋshɔŋ niji ateŋ?

english: Cassava stem cuttings should usually be planted about 1 meter apart from each other. Proper spacing gives the underground roots enough room to expand into large tubers without competing for moisture.
ga: Taakɛ eji lɛ, esa akɛ adu ŋmeii ni afo lɛ aaafee mita kome kɛjɛ amɛhe. He ni jɛkɛmɔ ni sa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ bulbs agboi ni amɛyeee akaŋ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ he.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines with wooden poles after they sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei awo mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ he beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need sunlight to make food for growing big tubers. Staking lifts the leaves off the hot ground toward the sun, preventing leaf diseases and increasing the underground yam yield.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa hulu la koni amɛná niyenii kɛha bulb agbo ni miida. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ he ni edɔ lɛ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ mli. Tsi foliar helai anaa ni oha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How can I tell if the ground is wet enough to start planting my seeds at the beginning of the rainy season?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni obaanyɛ oje dumɔwui adumɔ shishi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: It is best to wait until the rains become steady for two to three consecutive weeks so the soil is thoroughly wet deep down. Planting after just one light rain can cause seeds to sprout and then die if a dry spell follows.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be otsii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i jogbaŋŋ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ Mɔdɛŋbɔɔ kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwu lɛ akwɛ̃ ni egbo kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be nyiɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why are the flowers on my plants drying up and dropping off during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excessive afternoon heat stresses crops, causing delicate flowers to burn and fall off before they can produce fruit. Without flowers, the crop cannot yield, leading to a total loss of the money you invested.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ shãa ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii. Kɛji fɔfɔii bɛ lɛ Dumɔwui nyɛŋ awo ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, ekolɛ shika ni okɛwo mli lɛ fɛɛ baafite.

english: How does extreme heat cause me to lose money on my crops during the flowering stage?
ga: Te hulutsoo ni naa wa waa baanyɛ aha mifite shika yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ?

english: When flowers scorch and fall off due to high heat, the plant cannot form fruits or pods. You end up losing your harvest yield, which means you cannot recover the money spent on seeds, land preparation, and care.
ga: Kɛji fɔfɔii lɛ shã ni amɛgbee shi yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ hewɔ lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ afee aduawai loo ŋmeii. Obaafite okpamɔ lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ onyɛŋ okɛ shika ni ofite yɛ dumɔwui, shikpɔŋ he saamɔ, kɛ amɛkwɛmɔ he lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: What can I do to keep my flowering plants from burning in strong sunlight?
ga: Mɛni mafee koni mi tsei ni woɔ fɔfɔi lɛ akashã yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: You can protect flowering plants by planting shade crops, applying mulch around the roots to keep soil cool, and ensuring adequate watering early in the morning so the plants can survive peak heat hours.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu fɔfɔi tsei ahe kɛtsɔ shade tsei ni ooodu lɛ nɔ. Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii abɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe koni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ni kwɛmɔ ni okɛ nu awo mli bɔ ni sa leebi maŋkpa koni tsei lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli edɔ lɛ amli.

english: Is it unsafe to spray liquid chemicals or fertilizer on my crops when the sun is very hot?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mafɔ tsofai ni ji nu loo ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulu lɛ miitso waa?

english: Yes, applying chemicals under intense heat can burn leaves and delicate flowers. The hot sun causes chemicals to concentrate rapidly on plant surfaces, scorching the crop and ruining your investment.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa shishi lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai kɛ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ haa tsofai lɛ feɔ ekome oya yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ. Eshãa ŋmɔshi nibii ni efiteɔ oshika ni okɛwo mli lɛ.

english: Why is it bad to water or irrigate my crops during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mawo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nu loo mawo amɛ nu yɛ shwane mli ŋmɛlɛtswai ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Watering during peak heat can trap hot steam around foliage and root zones, overheating the plant tissue and burning soft flowers. It is best to water early in the morning while temperatures are cool.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli yɛ be mli ni latsaa waa lɛ baanyɛ amɔmɔ nu ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lasu ni ebɔle ehe. Baai kɛ shishifãi ahe hei haa tso lɛ mli fãji lɛ mli woɔ la tsɔ Ni fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ baanyɛ ashã. Esa akɛ afee nu lɛ leebi be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ lolo lɛ.

english: What happens if liquid fertilizer sits on plant leaves under intense sunlight for hours?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ta tsei ahe baai anɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi ŋmɛlɛtswai babaoo?

english: Strong sunshine evaporates the water in the liquid fertilizer, leaving concentrated chemical salts that burn small leaves and flowers, causing lasting damage to the crop.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baaha nu ni yɔɔ nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Shĩ tsofai ni mli edɔ ni shãa baai kɛ fɔfɔi bibii lɛ. Ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fiteɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why does fresh animal manure get hot, and will it damage my crops if applied directly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ mli edɔ lɛ? Ni ani ebaafite miŋmɔshi nibii kɛ akɛtsu nii tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Fresh manure ferments naturally and generates high heat. If placed near living plants without cooling or composting first, this heat will burn delicate plant roots and flowers.
ga: Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii heei feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ la mli. Kɛ akɛwo tsei ni hiɛ ka lɛ ahe ni ajieee amɛhe fɛ̃i loo afeee amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, Nɛkɛ dɔlɛ nɛɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: How does mulching the soil prevent my crop flowers from burning up in the sun?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni mulching lɛ atsĩ mi tso lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni hulu lɛ akashã lɛ?

english: Mulch acts as a protective blanket over the soil, keeping ground temperatures cool and retaining moisture so plants can continue feeding their flowers safely through hot hours.
ga: Mulch tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dɔlɛ ahi shi ni eha hulutsoo ahi shi. Enɛ ji koni tsei lɛ anyɛ aye amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shweshweeshwe yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why is morning time better than afternoon time for treating and feeding my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ leebi hi fe shwane kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ahe tsamɔ kɛ niyenii hamɔ lɛ?

english: Morning conditions are cool, allowing plants to absorb nutrients and moisture steadily before the harsh sun rises, preventing heat shock and leaf burn.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli tseɔ leebi. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ yaa nɔ amɛmuɔ niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ dani hulu lɛ teɔ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ latsaa kɛ baa shãa naa.

english: What signs should I look for to know if my crops are overheating and about to lose their blooms?
ga: Mɛɛ okadii esa akɛ matao koni male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miidɔ fe nine ni eesumɔ ni amɛgbee shi?

english: Look for drooping leaves, scorched brown leaf edges, and dry, discolored flowers during midday heat. Noticing these signs early allows you to provide shade or water before you lose your yield.
ga: Taomɔ baai ni egbee shi lɛ. Baai lɛ ashishigbɛi lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. kɛ fɔfɔi ni gbiɔ ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane mli Okadii nɛɛ ni onaa mra Enɛ baaha oná hulutsoo loo nu dani onibii lɛ afite.

english: I see a lot of ants crawling on my big mango tree, will they kill the tree?
ga: Mina ŋmeii babaoo ni miiho yɛ mi mango tso agbo lɛ nɔ. Ani ŋmeii baagbe tsei?

english: No, a mature mango tree is too strong and well-established to be destroyed by common ants, so small insects like that will not affect its overall health.
ga: Dabi, mango tso ni eda lɛ he wa tsɔ ni ŋmeii ni afɔɔ namɔ nyɛŋ afite lɛ, no hewɔ lɛ ŋmeii bibii ni tamɔ nɛkɛ enaaa ehewalɛ fɛɛ nɔ hewalɛ.

english: Do small insects like ants affect big fruit trees the same way they harm small vegetable crops?
ga: Ani kooloi bibii, tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ náa aduawai tsei wuji anɔ hewalɛ tamɔ bɔ ni amɛtutuaa aduawai tsei bibii lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: No, larger fruit trees have deep roots and high water storage that give them strength, making them far less vulnerable to minor pests like ants compared to small crops.
ga: Dabi, tsei wuji ni woɔ yibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ, ni amɛnyɛɔ amɛhiɛɔ nu babaoo, ni no haa amɛnáa hewalɛ. Enɛ haaa amɛhe afee shoo kwraa kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ akɛto tsei bibii ahe.

english: Should I spend money buying chemical sprays to remove ants from my mature fruit trees?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafite shika yɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmeii anɔ kɛjɛɔ aduawai tsei ni eda lɛ anɔ?

english: Usually you do not need to spray mature fruit trees for minor pests like ants, because a strong tree with enough water can naturally withstand them without losing its yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ tsofa afɔ aduawai tsei ni edara lɛ anɔ koni ogbe kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii, ejaakɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni nu yɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ ate shi amɛwo amɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni yibiiwoo lɛ fiteee.

english: Can insects on the trunk stop my mango tree from producing flowers?
ga: Ani kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ mango tso lɛ shishi lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ mango tso lɛ fɔfɔi anaa?

english: Insects like ants on the trunk generally cannot stop a strong, well-hydrated tree from flowering properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii, tamɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ lɛ nyɛŋ atsĩ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni nu yɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ anaa koni amɛkafɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my fruit trees seem to get weaker and easily damaged when there is no rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛfiteɔ oya kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Trees gain their full strength from the water stored inside them, so without enough water, they lose their natural defense and structural strength.
ga: Tso lɛ naa ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ nu ni ato yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Tso lɛ baafite ebɔɔ su hebuu kɛ eshishitoo hewalɛ.

english: Is water really still important for fully grown fruit trees that already look big and strong?
ga: Ani nu he miihia lolo diɛŋtsɛ kɛha aduawai tsei ni eda ni tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa momo lɛ?

english: Yes, even big trees require steady water to maintain their full internal strength, stay resilient against pests, and power the growth of flowers and fruit.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsei wuji po he miihia nu daa koni amɛmli hewalɛ ahi shi. Enyɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ ni ehaa fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai daa

english: What actually gives a fruit tree its strength to grow well and resist harsh conditions?
ga: Mɛni haa tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ náa hewalɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ shihilɛi gbohii?

english: A tree gains its full strength primarily through the water it holds inside, which allows it to build strong branches, produce flowers, and remain healthy.
ga: Tsei náa amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ kɛtsɔ nu ni ato yɛ amɛmli lɛ nɔ ni amɛkɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni etswaa niji ni wa, ewoɔ fɔfɔi, ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does ensuring my fruit trees have enough water help them produce flowers?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ miha mi aduawai tsei lɛ amli nu lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi?

english: Water gives the tree the internal strength and energy it needs to push out healthy flowers during the bloom season.
ga: Nu haa tsei hewalɛ kɛ mligbɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni he wa yɛ fɔfɔi be lɛ mli.

english: Why are the flowers on my fruit trees dropping off instead of staying on the branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaakpɛtɛ tsei lɛ aniji ahe lɛ?

english: Flowers often drop when the tree does not have enough water stored inside to reach the full strength needed to support flowering.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛto koni enyɛ eshɛ fɔfɔii lɛ fɛɛ he.

english: How can I tell if my tree has enough strength to produce a good yield this season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mitsei lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛwo yibii jogbaŋŋ yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: A healthy tree with enough water will show its strength by blooming abundantly with strong, firm flowers.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni nu yɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ baajie amɛhewalɛ kpo kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi ni mli wa ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛbaafɔ babaoo lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nutrients like nitrogen, or the soil is too wet. Giving them the right fertilizer early gives them the strength they need to grow tall and yield heavy cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn tsei lɛ kɛha niyenii tamɔ nitrogen. aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ Ni oooha amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa mra Enɛ baaha amɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛdara ni amɛwo ŋmeii ni tsii.

english: How often do I need to walk through my vegetable farm to check for sick plants?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ matsɔ aduawai aŋmɔ lɛ mli koni makwɛ kɛji tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ?

english: It is best to walk through your field every day or two. Checking your crop leaves and stems daily helps you catch pests and early signs of sickness early before they spread to the whole farm.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ obaanyiɛ oŋmɔji lɛ amli daa gbi loo gbii enyɔ. Kɛ́ okwɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli daa gbi lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni omɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ hela he okadii klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ mra. dani egbɛ eshwa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings struggle to survive when I plant them in full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛhi shi kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are like small children—they cannot stand harsh, direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing food crops like plantains nearby creates shade that protects the cocoa leaves from burning and drying out.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ gbekɛbii. ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ Niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Ehaa ŋmɔlɔ ni buɔ kookoo baai lɛ ahe koni amɛkashã ni amɛkagbi.

english: How does feeding my crops the right fertilizer prevent them from getting diseases?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni helai akamɔ mi?

english: Just like well-fed animals stay healthy, crops that get proper nutrients grow strong immune systems. Healthy plants can resist plant diseases much better than weak, malnourished crops.
ga: Taakɛ koolooi ni ayeɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hu yɛ hewalɛ lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ ni nine shɛɔ niyenii ni sa nɔ lɛ baaha amɛgbɔmɔtso lɛ mli nii ni gbeɔ helai lɛ aya hiɛ. Tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ tsei ahelai anɔ fe tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa lɛ.

english: Can using bad quality chemicals or fertilizer cause my crops to dry up and die?
ga: Ani tsofai loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehiii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbi?

english: Yes, using the wrong chemical mix or fake fertilizers can burn your crop roots and leaves, causing permanent damage or plant death. Always use recommended inputs from certified agro-dealers.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni akɛfutuɔ nii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ ashã. Enɛ haa tso lɛ fiteɔ loo egboɔ daa. Kɛ saji ni ajie yi kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ ko ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ atsu nii be fɛɛ be.

english: Flowers drop when plants feel stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients. Keeping the soil moist and well-fed keeps the plant calm so flowers turn into peppers.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni niyenii kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ feɔ dioo. Fɔfɔi lɛ batsɔ chili ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my cassava plants look weak and small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa ŋmeii tsei lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛji bibii lɛ?

english: Weeds steal the water, sunlight, and food intended for your cassava. Clearing weeds early ensures your cassava gets full nourishment to build strong roots.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ aha o-cassava lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha ŋmei lɛ aná niyenii ni yeɔ emuu ni ekɛma shishifãi ni wa.

english: How do I know if my newly planted crops are growing strong and healthy?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tso ni midu ehee lɛ miida waa ni eyɛ hewalɛ?

english: Healthy crops show firm, bright green leaves, sturdy stems, and steady weekly growth. If growth stops or stems feel soft, the plant is struggling with sickness or water issues.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli ni kpɛɔ, tsei ni wa, kɛ dalɛ ni yaa nɔ daa otsi. Kɛji akɛ tso lɛ dalɛ kpa loo tso lɛ shishifã lɛ nu he akɛ eyɛ blɛoo Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miina hela loo nu he naagbai.

english: Plantains curl their leaves to protect themselves from losing water in intense heat. It is a natural defense, but if leaves stay limp till evening, your crop desperately needs water.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ he. Eji adebɔɔ mli hebuu. Shi kɛji akɛ baai lɛ tee nɔ amɛgbɔjɔ kɛyashi gbɛkɛ lɛ Nu babaoo he miihia Onibii.

english: What causes holes to appear in my cabbage leaves overnight?
ga: Mɛni ha buji je kpo yɛ mi-cabbage baai lɛ anɔ nyɔɔŋ kome?

english: Holes are usually caused by pests like caterpillars or beetles feeding on tender leaves while you sleep. Inspecting under the leaves during early mornings helps you spot and stop them before they ruin your harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai bibii beni owɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji baa. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi leebi maŋkpa lɛ, ebaaha ona amɛ ni okpa amɛ dani amɛfite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay green and grow strong. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or well-rotted animal manure will fix this problem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sucking pests like thrips, mites, or aphids feeding on the leaf sap, or by a virus spread by whiteflies. Spraying neem oil or an appropriate insecticide can control these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, mites, loo aphids ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ lɛ baanyɛ akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: How can I tell if fall armyworms are attacking my corn field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ fall cutworms miitutua mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Fall armyworms leave ragged, chewed holes in the leaves and deposit dark waste inside the central funnel (whorl) of the maize plant. If you look closely inside the funnel, you may see small caterpillars feeding.
ga: Fall cutworms lɛ shiɔ bu ni ashɛre yɛ baai lɛ amli kɛ jwɛi ni tsuɔ yɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmãa (ring) lɛ mli. Kɛ okwɛ ŋshɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ Ekolɛ obaana ŋshɔŋlooi bibii ni miitao niyenii.

english: Young cocoa trees dry out easily under full sun. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide temporary shade and keep the soil moist, protecting the young cocoa until it grows stronger.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe waa.

english: Why do I have to put sticks next to my yam plants for them to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ niji awo sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe koni amɛkwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight. Sunlight allows the leaves to make food, which is sent down into the ground to build larger yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaa lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. ni akɛmajeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi koni ekɛfee sweet potato ŋmeii wuji

english: Spacing cassava about 1 meter apart gives the roots enough room in the soil to expand into big tubers and prevents the plants from fighting each other for sunlight and soil nutrients.
ga: Aaafee mita kome ni ka ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji. ni etsĩɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkawuu amɛhe koni amɛná hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts or beans helps improve the soil for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans are legumes that take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant dies and rots, this stored nitrogen stays in the soil as free food for the next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsei gboi ni amɛfite Nitrogen ni ato nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, keeps the soil cool, prevents sunlight from evaporating soil moisture, stops weeds from growing, and slowly rots into plant manure.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i Etsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekafee ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ tsei ahe ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot, when the plant doesn't get enough water, or when tiny insects attack the blossoms. Keeping the soil evenly watered during hot spells helps save the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Aloo kɛ́ kooloi bibii tutua fɔfɔi lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ nu wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akafite.

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a hot dry spell before the main rains start. If seeds sprout after the first rain, the young seedlings will dry up and die if rain does not fall regularly afterwards.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ be ni mli edɔ, ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔ titri lɛ jeɔ shishi. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ Tsei bibii lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ daa yɛ no sɛɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow from the middle to the tip?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ teŋgbɛ kɛyaa naagbee lɛ?

english: Yellowing that starts at the tip of the leaf and moves down the middle in an inverted 'V' shape usually means your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants need to grow strong, green leaves.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai lɛ anaa ni eyaa shi kɛyaa teŋgbɛ yɛ ‘V’ ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ mli lɛ fɔɔ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: If I plant groundnuts together with my corn, will the groundnuts steal all the soil food from the corn?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmãa du ŋmãa Ani ŋmãa baaju shikpɔŋ mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ?

english: No, groundnuts actually add food to the soil. They are legumes that capture nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil, which helps feed the corn growing next to them.
ga: Dabi, ŋmei kɛ niyenii kpakpai baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ diɛŋtsɛ. Eji ŋmãa ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ejieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my crops get smaller and weaker when I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibii ni egbɔjɔɔ kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the specific nutrients that crop needs and allows field pests to multiply. Changing crops each season—like switching to beans or cassava—gives the soil time to rebuild its nutrients.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tso lɛ lɛ hoɔ be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ babaoo. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsakemɔ daa be mli, tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei tsakemɔ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná be ni ekɛsaa ehe nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have huge leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving young cocoa plants the shade and cool moisture they need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Look closely at the small buds or nodes on the stem cutting; they must point upward toward the sky. Planting cassava stems upside down forces the leaves and roots to grow in the wrong direction, weakening the plant.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ jogbaŋŋ, esa akɛ amɛtsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kasava tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ kɛyaa shishi lɛ baaha baai kɛ shishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tso lɛ ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Yam vines produce tubers underground using light captured by their leaves. The wooden poles lift the leaves up to catch full sunlight, which helps the plant make larger, healthier yams.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii kɛtsɔ la ni amɛbaai lɛ mɔ̃ɔ lɛ nɔ. Tso ko woɔ baai lɛ anɔ koni ená hulu la ni fa babaoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ sweet potatoes ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies hiding under the leaves, or by viruses transmitted by these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: This black rot at the bottom of the fruit is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium, often caused by irregular watering where the soil gets too dry and then too wet.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ ni yɔɔ aduawai lɛ shishi lɛ akɛ blossom end rot. Ebaa kɛji tsei lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ ni edɔ tsɔ.

english: It is best to water early in the morning so the roots absorb the water before the heat of the day. Watering in the afternoon heat wastes water through quick evaporation and can stress hot plants.
ga: Esa akɛ afee nu leebi maŋkpa koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ dani kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli adɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ shwane latsaa mli lɛ baafite nu lɛ yɛ la ni hoɔ oya lɛ hewɔ. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ haomɔ aba tsei lɛ anɔ.

english: Covering soil with dry grass or mulch keeps the ground cool, stops rainwater from evaporating quickly so you water less, and prevents weeds from taking over your garden.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Etsiɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ oya. koni okɛ nu akashwie nɔ fioo ni otsi jwɛi anaa koni ekaye obɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my maize plants turn yellow and dry up early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ ŋmãa be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen in the soil or the roots are suffocating because the land is waterlogged.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo akɛ shishifãi lɛ miigbɔjɔ ejaakɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with many leaves but produce tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen or water, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing top leaves and stems instead of storing food in the tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo nu babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ eŋwɛi baai kɛ eshishifãi lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato tuber ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli lɛ

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or beans together on the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa afee ekome yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for your maize while keeping the soil shaded and moist.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa o-corn lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni edɔ.

english: How do I know if fall armyworms have attacked my maize field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ fall armyworm etutua mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: You will see ragged, eaten holes on the leaves and small brownish droppings inside the central funnel where the new leaves emerge.
ga: Obaana buji ni ekpɔtɔ ni aye yɛ baai lɛ anɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Eyɛ gbɛjegbɛ lɛ teŋgbɛ he ni baai heei jeɔ kpo yɛ lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my harvested maize grains are dry enough to store safely in bags?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mikɛto kotokui amli shweshweeshwe?

english: Try biting a grain—if it cracks sharply without leaving a dent, or if the grains do not stick together when pressed inside a sealed glass jar, it is dry enough for storage.
ga: Bɔɔmɔdɛŋ ni okɛ ŋmãa ŋmãa ko atsu nii. Kɛji egbɛ eshwa babaoo ni eshiii ŋmeii ko kwraa loo kɛji akɛ dumɔwui lɛ ekpɛtɛɛɛ amɛhe kɛji akɛ ashɛre glase tsinsii ko ni atsĩ naa lɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akɛto.

english: Hybrid seeds lose their strength in the second generation, so planting saved hybrid seeds will yield weak plants, uneven growth, and a much smaller harvest.
ga: Hybrid dumɔwui lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui ni akɛfee hybrid ni ahere lɛ ni adu lɛ baaha tsei lɛ afee nɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ. shweremɔ ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee Ni kpamɔ lɛ faaa kwraa.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my crop seeds very close together to get more plants on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni maná tsei babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, leading to thin stems and low total yields.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛbaatswa amɛhe adafi koni amɛná hulu la. Niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni yibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up tightly during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe shi waa yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants curl their leaves during intense heat to reduce leaf surface area, which slows down water loss and protects the plant from drying out.
ga: Pepper tsei baafolɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa koni ebaaba lɛ nɔ he ni baa lɛ shi. Enɛ baaye abua ni nu ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ fioo ni ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekagbi.

english: Why does my soil become hard and stop producing good yields after farming it for a few years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ais ni ekpaa ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai ŋmɔmɔ yɛ afii fioo komɛi ni mikɛtsu nii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Continuous planting without adding compost or rotating crops depletes organic matter and nutrients, making the soil compact and unable to hold water.
ga: Dumɔ ni yaa nɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ bɛ mli lɛ baaha nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ afite. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ehiɛ nu.

english: How do I know when my groundnuts are ready to harvest before they start rotting in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmeii lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa dani amɛje shishi amɛgboi yɛ sũ lɛ mli?

english: Pull up a few test plants and open the pods; if the inner lining of the shell has turned dark brown with visible veins and the seeds fill the pod completely, they are ready.
ga: Gbalamɔ kaa tsei fioo komɛi ni ogbele ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ŋshɔŋloo lɛ mligbɛ fã lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni lá fãji ni anaa yɔɔ mli, ni dumɔwui eyi ŋshɔŋloo lɛ mli obɔ lɛ, no lɛ efee klalo.

english: Why does my land produce much smaller yields now than it did five years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii fioo kwraa fe bɔ ni eji afii enumɔ ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Farming the same piece of land year after year without giving it a break or adding organic matter drains the essential nutrients from the soil, leaving it too weak to nourish healthy crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kome nɔ nɔŋŋ ni atsuɔ okwaayeli he nii afi fɛɛ afi ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni bɛ mli loo akɛfataaa he lɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ eye ebua ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why should I leave dry leaves and crop waste on my land instead of burning everything before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi baai ni egbi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni mashã nɔ fɛɛ nɔ dani madu nii?

english: Burning destroys valuable natural nutrients and kills helpful living organisms in the ground, whereas leaving crop waste to decay acts as natural fertilizer and keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni jara wa ni egbeɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni ashiɔ koni egbo lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why does rainwater carry away my topsoil when I clear all the natural trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ shwieɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ mijie adebɔɔ mli tsei kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tree roots act like sponges and glue that hold the soil together; removing them leaves the rich topsoil loose and vulnerable to being washed away by heavy rains.
ga: Tso shishifãi tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji kɛ glu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ekome. Amɛjiemɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni eyɛ oshara akɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaho kɛya.

english: Why does using heavy tractors on my land make the ground hard and my cassava tubers small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ traktɔ agbo ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii lɛ?

english: Heavy machinery squeezes the air and water spaces out of the soil, making it too dense for root crops like cassava to expand and absorb nutrients easily.
ga: Tsɔnei ni tsii miimiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi tsɔ ni shishifãi tamɔ ŋmei nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛhe niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds immediately after the very first light rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo yɛ afi lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first light rain is often followed by a long dry period, which can scorch and kill young germinating seeds before the main rainy season fully established itself.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ ashã ni efite dumɔwui bibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ aba kwraa.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without producing any tomatoes during very hot weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ shwie fɔfɔi ni ewooo tomato ko yɛ otsi kome ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, tomato plants experience heat stress and drop their blossoms to save water and energy needed for basic survival.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Tomato tsei lɛ kɛ hulutsoo be mli haomɔ kpeɔ ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa kɛha shishijee wala lɛ he.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a cry for help showing that the crop lacks nitrogen nutrient in the soil or that water logging around the roots is suffocating the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji yelikɛbuamɔ he bolɔmɔ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo nu shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni ehaa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do farmers around here plant plantains next to young cocoa shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ biɛ lɛ duɔ dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight, so fast-growing plantain trees are planted alongside them to provide shade and cool air until the cocoa grows strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ adu dumɔwui ni daa oya yɛ amɛmasɛi. Koni ekɛ hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i aba kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ.

english: How does planting groundnuts on my field help my next crop of corn grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi-ŋmei srɔtoi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which takes nitrogen from the air and traps it in the soil, leaving behind natural food for the next crop of corn.
ga: Peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni ejieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ashiɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha ŋmãa dumɔ kroko.

english: Curled, yellow-patterned cassava leaves are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried from plant to plant by tiny insects called whiteflies.
ga: Kasava baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ woɔ kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa ekroko nɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning brown and dying when there is full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight because their leaves burn easily. Planting shade crops like plantains or cassava next to them provides living shade and keeps the soil moist while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo cassava yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the plants fight each other for water, sunlight, and nutrients in the soil. Proper spacing allows each maize plant enough food and light to grow thick stems and full, healthy ears.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa he lɛ haa ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ náa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ toi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my cassava tubers become watery and hard to cook if I leave them in the ground after heavy rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ nu ni ewa akɛ abaahoo kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When heavy rains return, mature cassava plants stop storing starch and start using energy from their roots to grow new leaves. Leaving tubers in wet soil causes them to lose starch, absorb excess water, and turn woody.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ku esɛɛ eba Cassava tsei ni eda lɛ kpaɔ starch ni amɛtoɔ lɛ ni amɛjeɔ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ shishi kɛ nitsumɔ koni amɛkɛbaa heei akwɛ̃. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛmli ŋmeii lɛ afite. shwieɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ebatsɔ tso

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when water supply is irregular. Heat stress causes the plant to drop its blossoms to conserve water and energy for survival.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ejaaa. Dɔlɛ haa tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch maximum sunlight with their leaves. Sunlight allows the leaves to make food, which travels down to build large, healthy yam tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛbaji lɛ ajie amɛhe kpo yɛ hulu la ni fe fɛɛ lɛ mli. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. Enɛ tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shi ni efeɔ sweet potato ŋmeii agboi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and stopping new leaves from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiitsi baai heei anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies or thrips. As they feed on leaf sap, they spread viruses that distort the leaf structure and stunt plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Beni amɛyeɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ Amɛgbɛɔ helai ni fiteɔ baai lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔtoo ni amɛtsiɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ naa lɛ amɛshwãa.

english: Why should I cut off extra shoot suckers from my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni yɔɔ mi-plantain tso titri lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The main plantain stem shares its soil nutrients and water with every sucker growing around it. Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two strong stems, ensuring the main plant gets enough food to produce big, heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Plantain tso lɛ tso titri lɛ kɛ ŋmeii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ jaa niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ, ni ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo yibii wuji ni tsii.

english: How do groundnut and cowpea plants help my soil stay rich for the next crop?
ga: Te ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei tsei baanyɛ aye abua ni amɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas have special nodules on their roots that capture nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Peas kɛ cowpeas yɛ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my young maize leaves and powdery dirt inside the central funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ ehiɛ bu kɛ sũ yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which crawls deep inside the central funnel of young maize plants to feed on soft new leaves before they unfold.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni shwereɔ kɛboteɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ koni amɛye baai bibii heei dani amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why does my lowland rice grow much better when the field is kept flooded with shallow water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa beni nu ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ eyi ŋmɔ lɛ mli obɔ lɛ?

english: Lowland rice plants are adapted to thrive in standing water, which prevents competing weeds from growing and helps the rice roots easily absorb soil nutrients needed to produce full grain heads.
ga: Atsakeɔ ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ nu ni mli ejɔ mli. Enɛ tsiɔ jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii ni he hiaa koni amɛwo dumɔwui ayitsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ mli oya.

english: Why do the leaves of my corn plants curl up during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When maize leaves curl into tight tubes during hot weather, the plant is protecting itself to save water. Reducing its exposed leaf surface stops moisture from evaporating too quickly in the heat.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Tsei lɛ baabu amɛhe koni amɛbu nu he. Kɛ́ ajie baa lɛ nɔ ni ajie lɛ kpo lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ yɛ latsaa be lɛ mli.

english: Why are the tops of my corn plants flowering before I see any cobs forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ayitsei lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi dani minaa ŋmeii ni miifee lɛ?

english: The flowers at the very top of the corn stalk are called tassels. They bloom first to produce pollen, which the wind carries down to fertilize the silks on the stalk where the ears of corn will form.
ga: Atsɛɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ abele tso lɛ yiteŋ lɛ akɛ tassels. Amɛfɔ̃ɔ klɛŋklɛŋ koni amɛjie pollen. Ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tswaa koni ekɛ siliki ŋmeii afɔ yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ, ni baabɔle ŋmãa toi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do some of my harvested corn cobs have missing kernels?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ ekomɛi bɛ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Incomplete or missing kernels usually happen when the corn plant suffers from dry weather or extreme heat during pollination, preventing all the silks from getting fertilized properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni eshɛɛɛ he loo ni elaaje lɛ baa kɛji ŋmeii tsei lɛ na shihilɛi ni mli egbi loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa yɛ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ amli. Enɛ haa siliki lɛ fɛɛ nyɛɛɛ afee nɔ ni sa.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize crop lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient the plant needs to build strong leaves, process sunlight, and produce healthy grain.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Amɛji niyenii ni he hia ni tsei taoɔ koni amɛkwɛ baai ni wa, amɛtsu hulu la he nii, ni amɛwo dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Corn is ready for harvest when the outer husks turn dry and brown, and a small dark layer forms at the bottom tip of each kernel where it attaches to the cob.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ egbi ni efee ŋmɔtɔ. Ni ŋwɛi ŋta bibioo ko yɛ jɛmɛ. Ebaa yɛ ŋmei fɛɛ ŋmei ni akɛkpɛtɛ ŋmei lɛ he lɛ shishigbɛ naagbee.

english: How can I store my harvested corn so pests do not destroy it before the next season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ ato koni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akafite lɛ dani be ni baa lɛ aba?

english: To prevent pest damage, dry the corn grains completely until they are hard, then store them off the ground in well-ventilated cribs or tightly sealed airtight bags that keep insects out.
ga: Bɔni afee ni tsɛŋemɔ helai akafite lɛ Ha ŋmãa lɛ agbi kwraa kɛyashi ebaawa. No sɛɛ lɛ, akɛ amɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ tsɔne ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli loo kɔɔyɔɔ kotoku ko ni atsĩ naa mli koni kooloi akabote mli.

english: Why does my stored corn spoil so quickly if I harvest it during the rainy weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji mikpa yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Corn harvested during damp conditions carries excess moisture. High moisture causes fungi and mold to grow rapidly, which destroys the quality of the stored grain.
ga: Abele ni akpa yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ mli lɛ baaná ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine. Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ shwereɔ oya. Enɛ fiteɔ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I feed the same corn I grow for my family to my egg-laying chickens?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ kooloi ni fɔɔ bii kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni miduɔ mihaa miweku lɛ mli?

english: Yes, maize is a versatile grain that provides high energy and carbohydrates for human foods like banku, while also serving as the main energy ingredient in chicken feed.
