ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ji ŋmaa ni yɔɔ srɔtoi ni haa hewalɛ kɛ carbohydrates yɛ adesai aniyenii tamɔ banku mli, yɛ be mli ni etsuɔ ​​nii hu akɛ nɔ titri ni haa hewalɛ yɛ tsina niyenii mli.

english: Why does feeding maize to my chickens help them lay better eggs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmãa ha mikooloi lɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii kpakpai lɛ?

english: Maize provides high levels of energy that chickens need to maintain good health and fuel the daily body processes required to lay eggs consistently.
ga: Abɛi haa hewalɛ babaoo ni he hiaa kooloi koni amɛná hewalɛ kpakpa, ni ehaa gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli nifeemɔi ni he hiaa daa gbi koni amɛwo amɛwui daa lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: What type of soil should I choose if I want my maize crop to produce high yields?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ esa akɛ mahala kɛji miitao ŋmãa babaoo?

english: Maize performs best in rich, well-draining loamy soil that holds moisture well without staying waterlogged after heavy rains.
ga: Abɛi tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ eyi obɔ kɛ nu, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni sũ yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ. ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehiɛɛɛ nu mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ

english: Why are agricultural extension officers encouraging us to plant orange sweet potatoes instead of the traditional white ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni ji orange sweet potatoes lɛ akwɛmɔ he hewalɛ moŋ fe blema ŋmeii yɛŋ lɛ?

english: Orange sweet potatoes are rich in Vitamin A, which improves night vision and boosts immunity in young children. While white varieties are standard for starch, orange ones offer higher health benefits and are increasingly demanded by health-conscious consumers.
ga: Vitamin A babaoo yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ji orange mli, ni ehaa gbekɛbii bibii naa nii jogbaŋŋ gbɛkɛ, ni ehaa gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli hewalɛ ni gbeɔ helai lɛ yaa hiɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmei yɛŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛhaa ashikishaŋ moŋ, shi ŋmei henɔi lɛ yɛ hewalɛnamɔ he sɛɛnamɔi babaoo. ni mɛi ni heɔ nii ni susuɔ amɛhe waa lɛ sumɔɔ.

english: I have seen purple sweet potatoes in the market; are they natural and can I grow them on my farm in Ghana?
ga: Mi na ŋmɔtɔ ni ji purple ŋmɔtɔ yɛ jara nɔ. Ani amɛji adebɔɔ mli nibii ni manyɛ makwɛ amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ mli?

english: Yes, purple sweet potatoes are completely natural and grow very well in Ghanaian soils. Their deep color comes from powerful natural antioxidants, making them popular with specialized buyers who pay good prices for healthy, unique produce.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔtɔ ni ji purple lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ kwraa ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ waa yɛ Ghana shikpɔŋ nɔ. Ehe su ni mli kwɔ lɛ jɛɔ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ amli. Enɛ haa ehe gbɛi waa yɛ mɛi ni heɔ nii krɛdɛɛi ni woɔ jara kpakpa yɛ nibii ni ekɛbaa lɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ ahe lɛ ateŋ.

english: Does growing different colors of sweet potatoes require different farming methods or fertilizers?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ sui srɔtoi lɛ akwɛmɔ biɔ okwaayeli gbɛi srɔtoi loo ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Most sweet potato varieties—whether white, orange, or purple—require the same basic soil preparation, sunlight, and weed management. However, some improved orange varieties mature a bit faster than traditional white varieties.
ga: Sweet potato henɔi babaoo, kɛji eyɛŋ, eyɛŋ loo eyɛŋ jio, biɔ shikpɔŋ he saamɔ, hulu la, kɛ jwɛi ahe nitsumɔ ni he hiaa waa lɛ nɔŋŋ. Shi kɛlɛ, ŋmeii komɛi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ shwereɔ oya fioo fe blema ŋmeii yɛŋ lɛ.

english: What will happen if I plant orange, purple, and white sweet potato vines together in the same plot?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ odu sweet potato wain tsei ni ji orange, purple, kɛ white lɛ ekome yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: The plants will grow normally without changing each other's colors or flavor, but mixing them in one plot makes harvesting confusing. It is better to plant each color in its own bed so you can package and sell them easily to buyers who want specific types.
ga: Tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ bɔ ni sa ni amɛtsakeee amɛhe su loo amɛmli ŋɔɔmɔ. Shi kɛ akɛ amɛ futu ekome yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, ekɛ basabasafeemɔ baa ŋmaakpamɔ mli. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu kɔla fɛɛ kɔla yɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ etsu mli bɔni afee ni okɛwo tsɔne mli ni okɛhɔ̃ɔ oha mɛi ni heɔ nii ni miitao henɔ pɔtɛɛ ko lɛ oya.

english: If I harvest sweet potatoes from my land today, can I immediately replant new vines in the exact same field?
ga: Kɛji ŋmɛnɛ mikpa ŋmeii kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ani manyɛ madu wain tsei heei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Replanting immediately in the same spot encourages soil pests like sweet potato weevils to build up and ruin your next harvest. It is best to rotate your field with corn, beans, or vegetables between crop cycles to keep the soil healthy.
ga: Kɛ́ odu ekoŋŋ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaawo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ mli, tamɔ sweet potato ŋmei lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛbua onibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ anaa ni amɛfite. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsake ŋmãa, ŋmãa, loo aduawai yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ateŋ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can root crops like sweet potatoes really be used to produce items like yogurt, or are they strictly for boiling and eating?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ akɛ shishifãi tamɔ sweet potatoes afee nibii tamɔ yogurt diɛŋtsɛ, aloo afee koni akɛhoo ni aye pɛ?

english: Certain sweet potato varieties, especially orange-fleshed ones, can be cooked and mashed into a smooth purée. Food processors blend this purée into dairy or plant-based yogurt to add natural sweetness, rich texture, and Vitamin A.
ga: Sweet potato henɔi komɛi Titri lɛ, ŋmei loo lɛ Abaanyɛ ahoo ni atsɔ mli ni efee ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse. Mɛi ni feɔ niyenii lɛ kɛ nɛkɛ purée nɛɛ futuɔ mliki loo yogurt ni akɛ tsei fee lɛ mli koni eha e-adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔlɔ lɛ aya hiɛ. Nɔ ni yɔɔ fɛo kɛ vitamin A

english: How do I choose the right sweet potato variety if my goal is to sell directly to food processing companies?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala sweet potato henɔ ni sa? Kɛji akɛ oti ni ma mihiɛ ji ni mahɔ̃ɔ niyenii mahã nitsumɔhei ni feɔ niyenii lɛ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: You should ask the processor what they need before planting. Factories making drinks or yogurt usually buy orange sweet potatoes for their smooth texture and nutrients, whereas starch and flour makers often prefer high-starch white varieties.
ga: Esa akɛ obi mɔ ni feɔ nibii lɛ nɔ ni he hiaa amɛ dani odu. Bei pii lɛ, nitsumɔhei ni feɔ dãai loo yogurt lɛ heɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ji orange yɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ hewɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, mɛi ni feɔ ashikishaŋ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ sumɔɔ ashikishaŋ henɔi ni ashikishaŋ yɛŋ babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why is it beneficial for a farmer like me to grow more than one variety of crop on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ okwaafonyo ko tamɔ mi baadu nibii ni fa fe ekome yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Growing multiple varieties helps you serve different market demands and reduces financial risk. Traditional buyers might buy white roots for everyday cooking, while schools, hospitals, and processors pay premium prices for nutritious orange or purple varieties.
ga: Nibii sɔrɔtoi babaoo ni oookwɛ lɛ haa onyɛɔ otsuɔ jarayeli hiamɔ nii srɔtoi ahe nii ni ehaa shika he oshara baa shi. Kusum mli jarayelɔi baanyɛ ahe shishifã yɛŋ lɛ kɛha daa gbi niyenii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, skul, helatsamɔhei kɛ mɛi ni feɔ niyenii lɛ woɔ jara ni nɔ kwɔ waa kɛha ŋmeii loo ŋmeii srɔtoi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do buyers in the local market offer different prices for orange, white, and purple sweet potatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayeli hei lɛ kɛ jara srɔtoi haa ŋmeii ni ji orange, white kɛ purple lɛ?

english: Prices differ based on market demand and supply. White potatoes are widely available for standard meals, while health-conscious consumers and commercial processors pay higher prices for orange and purple varieties due to their special nutritional and processing values.
ga: Jara lɛ srɔtoi yɛ jara nɔ nibii ni akɛhaa kɛ nibii ni ataoɔ lɛ naa. Ayɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ babaoo kɛha niyenii ni afɔɔ feemɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, mɛi ni yeɔ nii ni kwɛɔ amɛhe nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ jarayeli mli lɛ woɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei srɔtoi lɛ ahe nyɔmɔ babaoo yɛ niyenii ni mli wa kɛ bɔ ni afeɔ amɛ nii ahaa lɛ hewɔ.

english: How does feeding my family orange sweet potatoes help cut down on household expenses?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ mikɛ miweku lɛ niyenii ni ji orange sweet potatoes lɛ haa shia shika ni afiteɔ lɛ baa shi?

english: Orange sweet potatoes are rich in essential nutrients that prevent frequent illnesses and vitamin deficiencies in children. Eating them regularly keeps your household healthy, reducing medical bills and doctor visits.
ga: Nibii ni he hiaa ni tsiɔ helai ni baa shii abɔ kɛ vitamin ni faaa yɛ gbekɛbii amli lɛ naa lɛ fa babaoo yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Niyenii nɛɛ ni oooye daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni oshia lɛ náa hewalɛ. Tsɔɔmɔ tsofafeemɔ he nyɔmɔwoo kɛ datrɛfoi asaramɔi anɔ

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen helps plants stay green and grow strong, so when it runs low, the plant moves what is left to the newer leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ kɛ́ nɔ ko fioo pɛ eshwɛ Tso lɛ baajie nɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛya baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ.

english: What does adding animal manure to my farm do for my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ miŋmɔ mli kooloi ashishifã ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Animal manure acts as food for your soil. It releases nutrients slowly, improves the soil's ability to hold moisture, and helps roots grow deeper and stronger.
ga: Manure tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii kɛhaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ. Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii fiofio. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛmɔ ni ekɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛhe waa

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their leaves and wilt during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: On very hot days, leaves lose water faster than roots can draw it from the ground. The plant wilts to protect itself from losing too much moisture, and usually recovers when the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni mli edɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baagbo koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine ni efiteɔ lɛ he. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi kɛ́ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate direct, harsh sunlight. They need shade from larger trees to protect their leaves from burning and to keep the soil moist during their early years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji adɛŋ koni ebu amɛbaai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he, ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ amɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my crops very close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Spacing them correctly allows each plant to grow bigger and produce a heavier harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Tsei ni akɛto amɛhe jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha tso fɛɛ tso agbo ni ebaaha ŋmaa ni tsii aba.

english: Growing the same crop in the same spot every season drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases that target that crop to build up in the dirt.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 and 12 months after planting. You will notice the lower leaves turning yellow and falling off, and the ground around the stem will start to crack as the tubers grow big underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu. Obaana akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi. kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso lɛ baabɔi mligbalamɔ be mli ni tuber lɛ daa agbo yɛ eshishi lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops produce smaller fruits and smaller grains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii bibii kɛ dumɔwui bibii lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal the water, fertilizer, and sunlight that your crops need. When weeds take those resources away, your crops don't have enough energy to develop full fruit or grains.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei lɛ. Kɛ jwɛi kpata nakai nibii lɛ ahiɛ lɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛwo yibii loo ŋmaa kwraa.

english: Holes in the center leaves of young maize are usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm. They feed on the tender leaf funnel and require early action to keep them from destroying the plant's growing point.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ baa. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ahe niyenii ni esa akɛ atsa amɛ mra. Enɛ ji koni akafite he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves get black spots and rot after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ feɔ diji ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rain splashes dirt containing fungal spores onto the leaves, and the wet conditions help the fungus spread quickly across the leaves, causing spots and decay.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa muji ni tsɛŋemɔ helai yɔɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ. Ni shihilɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmei lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa baai lɛ amli oya. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize lacks nitrogen, an important nutrient it needs to stay green and grow strong. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer early in the season helps the leaves turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. Amɛji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni ŋmɔ lɛ ahi shi ni ehiɛ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my cassava lose all its leaves during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baai fɛɛ fiteɔ yɛ harmatha be lɛ mli kɛji egbi pɛ?

english: Cassava naturally drops its leaves in dry weather to conserve water and survive the heat. As soon as the rains return, the plant will sprout new green leaves and continue growing its underground roots.
ga: Yucca shwieɔ ebaai lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ koni ekɛhiɛ nu mli ni enyɛ edamɔ dɔlɛ naa. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba pɛ kɛkɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli ni ebaaya nɔ ekwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi.

english: Why do my groundnut flower stems bend down and dig into the dirt after blooming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants produce flowers above the ground, but the peanuts grow underground. After the flower is pollinated, the stem naturally grows downward into the soil where the peanut pods can safely mature.
ga: Peanut tsei fɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi ŋmeii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Beni afee fɔfɔi lɛ pollen sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe yɛ lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot or when the plant lacks enough water. When stressed by heat or drought, the plant drops its flowers to save energy for survival.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Kɛ hulutsoo loo hɔmɔ kpe lɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot while still attached to the tree trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ be mli ni amɛkpɛtɛ tso lɛ shishi lolo lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungus that spreads when the farm is too damp and shaded. Clearing weeds and pruning heavy branches lets sunlight and air in to keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛji ŋmɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni eyɛ hulutsoo. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi waa Enɛ baaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba mli.

english: Curling leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking juices from the leaves or spreading a plant virus. Catching the insects early and spraying recommended insecticides prevents the curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu loo helai ni baa tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ni ooomɔ kooloi mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni ajieɔ yi lɛ afɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni akafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do the center leaves of my young corn look like they have holes and sawdust inside them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ bu ni ŋmeii yɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the fall armyworm caterpillar eating the soft young leaves inside the center of the plant. Applying appropriate insect control directly into the plant whorl early in the morning helps eliminate the pest.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi ni yeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni sa ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi bibii ahe lɛ wo tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie kooloi bibii lɛ kɛya.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch maximum sunlight. The light helps the leaves create food, which flows down into the ground to grow large, heavy yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. La yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. ni hoɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii

english: Plantains have shallow roots and weak stems that struggle to hold heavy fruit bunches. Supporting the tree with a strong wooden prop pole takes the weight off the trunk and prevents wind from blowing it down.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛmɔmɔ aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ amli. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei ni mli wa fĩ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ shishi tsiimɔ aba shi, ni ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ akatswa lɛ shi.

english: Why do my cowpea flowers drop before the bean pods have a chance to form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani ŋmeii lɛ ená hegbɛ amɛfee lɛ?

english: Tiny insects like thrips feed on tender flower buds and cause them to drop off prematurely. Protecting the plants with mild insect spray as soon as flowers appear allows pods to form properly.
ga: Kplukai bibii tamɔ thrips yeɔ fɔfɔi bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ. ni eha egbee shi oya. Akɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ lɛ abuɔ he Kɛji fɔfɔi lɛ je kpo pɛ kɛkɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ feɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate strong, direct sunlight because their delicate leaves lose water rapidly; they need shade crops like plantains to protect them while they build deep, strong root systems.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo tamɔ plantains koni ebu amɛhe yɛ be mli ni amɛfeɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa lɛ.

english: When maize plants are crowded, their roots and leaves compete fiercely for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, which leads to thin, weak stalks and very small or empty corn cobs.
ga: Beni ŋmãa tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmãa bibii waa loo nɔ ko bɛ mli baa.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize plant is lacking nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient needed for leaf growth, or that dry soil is preventing the plant from taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni he hiaa koni baai lɛ akwɛ̃ Aloo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ tsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaye nii.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil, which acts as a natural fertilizer for maize grown alongside or after them.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi loo yɛ esɛɛ.

english: Why should I cover the ground around my crops with dry leaves or straw?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil, known as mulching, traps moisture in the ground under the hot sun, keeps the soil cool, and prevents weed seeds from getting enough light to sprout.
ga: Ale mulching hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ aná la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes into the inner leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ amli baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These pests are likely Fall Armyworms, which crawl into the growing whorl (funnel) of young maize plants because it provides a safe, moist environment with fresh green leaves to feed on.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni shwereɔ kɛboteɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii ni miida lɛ amli. Ejaakɛ eyɛ he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli. Eyɛ baai eŋɔli heei akɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn dark brown or black during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in humid, wet weather and spreads easily when rain droplets splash spores from the soil onto the pods.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli, kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli edɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔi shwie ŋmeii ni jɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ kɛshwie ŋmeii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the soil if I leave them in the ground when the rains are heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ sũ mli kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ sũ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli lɛ?

english: Excess rain fills the air spaces in the soil with water, which suffocates the cassava tubers and allows water-loving fungi to invade and decay the roots.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yiɔ kɛ nu. Enɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa hydrophilic fungi lɛ boteɔ mli ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal the moisture, fertilizer, and sunlight your crops need to produce high yields, while also hiding destructive insects.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ekɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii hu teeɔ.

english: Should I apply chemical fertilizer to my field as soon as I put the seeds in the ground?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa awo miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ pɛ?

english: It is better to wait until the seeds germinate and grow green leaves, because young plants need working roots to absorb fertilizer, otherwise heavy rains will wash the expensive nutrients away.
ga: Ehi akɛ ooomɛ ni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei bibii lɛ ahe miihia shishifãi ni tsuɔ nii koni amɛnyɛ amɛŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛ jeee nakai lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baajie niyenii mli nibii ni jara wa lɛ kɛya.

english: Why should I use pegs and ropes to plant my crops in straight lines instead of planting seeds randomly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi ni mikɛ ŋmeii kɛ kpãa akwɛ̃ tsei yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu dumɔwui trukaa lɛ?

english: Planting in straight lines using line pegging ensures each crop gets equal access to sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. It also makes weeding, applying fertilizer, and walking through your farm much easier without damaging your crops.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ kɛtsɔ pinning nɔ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Agbɛnɛ hu, ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli nyiɛmɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa ni efiteee oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: What will happen to my crops if I plant them too close to each other on the field?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ amɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli?

english: When plants are crowded together, they compete with each other for sun, water, and nutrients. This causes them to grow tall and thin, making them weak and leading to smaller harvests.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ shwiili kɛ shwiili. Enɛ haa amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa amɛkpaa nii fioo.

english: Why do extension officers advise planting across a sloping land rather than straight up and down the hill?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni aduɔ gɔji lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa shi lɛ?

english: Planting across a slope stops rainwater from rushing down the hill. This prevents your fertile topsoil and crop nutrients from being washed away during heavy rains.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ baatsi nugbɔ nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ gɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ naa. Enɛ baatsi osũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ kɛ tsei amli niyenii ni fa babaoo lɛ naa koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akaho.

english: Is it true that using fertilizer makes the soil good, or will it ruin my farmland after a few years?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ, kɛ akɛ ŋmei tsu nii lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo? Aloo ebaafite miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ afii 2-3 sɛɛ?

english: Fertilizer supplies missing nutrients to help your crops grow strong and yield more. When applied in the correct amounts alongside organic manure, fertilizer improves crop output without damaging the land.
ga: Fertilizer haa niyenii ni elaaje lɛ koni eye ebua otsei lɛ ni amɛdara ni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Kɛ akɛfata he yɛ bɔ ni sa mli kɛfata ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ yaa hiɛ ni efiteee shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Signs of weak soil include crops with yellowish or pale leaves, slow and stunted growth, and lower harvest yields compared to previous seasons.
ga: Nɔ ni fata shikpɔŋ ni bɛ hewalɛ he okadii ahe ji tsei ni baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ. Nɔ ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo ni ehiɛɛɛ shi kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ ba shi kɛ akɛto nyɛsɛɛ be lɛ he.

english: Should I apply fertilizer at the time of planting or wait until my crops start growing?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ dumɔ be mli loo mamɛ kɛyashi tso lɛ baabɔi edamɔ?

english: Some fertilizers work best when mixed into the soil during planting to build strong roots, while others should be added weeks later when the plant is actively growing and needs a boost to produce fruit.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ekomɛi tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛfutu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ dumɔ be mli koni shishifãi ni wa aba. Yɛ be mli ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi afata he yɛ otsi kome sɛɛ beni tso lɛ miida ni ehe miihia ni awo lɛ hewalɛ koni ewo yibii lɛ.

english: Can farmyard manure work as well as chemical fertilizer to feed my crops?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ atsu nii tamɔ bɔ ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni akɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Yes, manure provides essential nutrients while also improving the soil's ability to hold water and stay rich over time, though chemical fertilizer usually acts faster for immediate crop needs.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii haa niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɛɔ nu mli ni ehaa ehiɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ hu. Eyɛ mli akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii oya kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa amrɔ nɔŋŋ moŋ.

english: Why do some farmers leave a piece of farmland uncultivated for a year or two before planting on it again?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi shiɔ ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ ni amɛduuu nii yɛ nɔ afi kome loo afii enyɔ dani amɛduɔ nii ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leaving land to rest, known as fallowing, allows the soil time to naturally recover its nutrients, moisture, and organic health so it can produce better crops in future seasons.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ejɔɔ ehe, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ defoliation lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛ niyenii, ŋmɔtɔ kɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ahewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ. Koni enyɛ ewo ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ wɔsɛɛ bei amli.

english: Why is it important for me to clear weeds completely before putting seeds in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi lɛ fɛɛ dani madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and will steal sunlight, moisture, and soil nutrients, preventing your young seeds from getting off to a healthy start.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei bibii. ni ebaaju hulu la, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsi odumɔwui bibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkaje shishi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How often do I need to clear weeds once my crops start growing?
ga: Shii enyiɛ ehe baahia ni mafolɔ jwɛi kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɔi kwɛ̃mɔ pɛ?

english: You should weed your farm early and regularly, especially during the first few weeks of growth, to ensure your crops do not have to fight weeds for nutrients while forming their stems and fruits.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie jwɛi kɛjɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra ni ofee nakai daa, titri lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni ŋmɔ lɛ daa lɛ amli. Enɛ haa ehe ehiaaa ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ jwɛi lɛ awuu koni amɛná niyenii kpakpai yɛ be mli ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii kɛ aduawai lɛ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains on the same land as my new cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ kookoo tso hee lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce large leaves that act as living shade, protecting the young cocoa seedlings and keeping the soil moist until the cocoa becomes strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Buu kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahe ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi kookoo lɛ mli baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Will plantain trees steal water and food from my young cocoa plants if I grow them together?
ga: Ani dumɔwui lɛ baaju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ amli kɛji mikɛ amɛ fee ekome?

english: If properly spaced, plantains and cocoa share the soil without harming each other. Plantains absorb nutrients from different soil depths and eventually return good organic matter back to the dirt when their leaves fall, which actually feeds the cocoa.
ga: Kɛji akɛ he ni jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ lɛ sa Dumɔwui lɛ kɛ kookoo lɛ baajara shikpɔŋ lɛ ni amɛyeee amɛhe awui. Plantains baajie niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ hei srɔtoi ni mli kwɔ. Ni naagbee lɛ, ekɛ nibii kpakpai ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ kuɔ sɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ baai lɛ gbee shi, ni no ji nɔ ni haa kookoo lɛ niyenii diɛŋtsɛ.

english: What happens to my young cocoa seedlings if they get full direct sunlight without any shade?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ ni hulutsoo bɛ amɛhe?

english: Direct sunlight dries out the soil around young roots and scorches the soft tender leaves of young cocoa, causing the plants to stunt, turn yellow, or die from heat stress.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni bɔleɔ shishifãi bibii lɛ ahe lɛ gĩɔ ni eshãa kookoo baai bibii lɛ. tsei ni egbɔjɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo amɛgboiɔ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ

english: Can I raise snails on the same land where I grow my cocoa and plantain crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ kookoo kɛ plantains yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, snails thrive on cocoa and plantain farms because the thick leaves create a cool, shady, and humid environment that protects snails from drying out in the sun.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmeii yeɔ omanye yɛ kookoo kɛ plantain ŋmɔji amli ejaakɛ baai ni mli tse lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: What do farm-raised snails eat, and will they destroy my main crops?
ga: Mɛni ŋmeii ni akwɛɔ amɛ yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ yeɔ? Ni ani ebaafite miŋmɔshi nii titri lɛ?

english: Snails mainly eat fallen fruits, decaying leaves, and tender vegetable scraps. If properly contained in a pen or managed area, they feed on organic waste without damaging your main standing crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii yeɔ aduawai ni egbee shi, baai ni egboi, kɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni eshwɛ. Kɛji akɛ akɛwo pɛn loo he ko ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Amɛbaaye nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni amɛfiteee tsei titri ni damɔ shi lɛ.

english: How long does a plantain sucker take to grow large enough to shade my small crops?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani plantain sucker ko daa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛha miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ ahe?

english: Plantain suckers grow very rapidly and usually develop broad, shady leaves within 3 to 6 months after planting, providing quick relief for shaded crops.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni bei pii lɛ amɛfeɔ baai ni mli kwɔ, ni yɔɔ shade yɛ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 6 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ. Ehaa tsei ni yɔɔ shade lɛ he jɔɔ amɛ oya.

english: Why does a plantain tree wither and die after it produces a bunch of fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni amɛwo aduawai kui lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: A plantain stem is designed to fruit only once in its life. Once the bunch matures and is harvested, the main stem naturally dies so its nutrients can flow into the young suckers growing at its base.
ga: Afee plantain tsei lɛ koni amɛwo yibii shikome pɛ yɛ amɛshihilɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔ lɛ shwere ni akpa lɛ Tso titri lɛ baagbo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, niyenii mli hewalɛ baanyɛ atsɔ ŋmeii bibii ni miida yɛ amɛshishi lɛ amli.

english: Once my cocoa trees grow big and thick, do I still need to keep the plantain trees?
ga: Beni mi-cocoa tso lɛ da ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ Ani ehe miihia ni makwɛ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ lolo?

english: No, mature cocoa trees form their own thick canopy that blocks out the sun. Once the cocoa matures, you slowly remove the plantains so the adult cocoa trees get enough sunlight to produce maximum pods.
ga: Dabi, kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa. Beni kookoo lɛ miida lɛ, jiemɔ plantains lɛ blɛoo bɔni afee ni kookoo tso ni eda lɛ aná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ.

english: How far apart should I plant my plantain suckers when setting up shade for cocoa?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu plantain tsei lɛ kɛjɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ beni mikɛ mi-kokoo lɛ miiwo shade mli lɛ?

english: Plantains are usually planted about 3 meters by 3 meters apart, placing one plantain sucker between every few cocoa plants so light is filtered evenly without overcrowded roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, aduɔ plantains yɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mitai 3 kɛ mitai 3, ni akɛ plantain ŋmeii woɔ kookoo tsei fioo komɛi ateŋ koni la ni atsɔ mli po aba ni ekɛ shishifãi lɛ eyimɔ obɔbɔ.

english: How does government support or agricultural grants help a farmer manage a large cocoa land?
ga: Te nɔyeli yelikɛbuamɔ loo okwaayeli he yelikɛbuamɔ yeɔ ebuaa okwaafoi ni amɛkwɛɔ kookoo ŋmɔji wuji anɔ amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Government assistance often provides free or discounted inputs like fertilizers, seedlings, or cash support, which lowers your starting costs and allows you to clear more land and hire farm labor.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔyeli yelikɛbuamɔ haa nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, dumɔwui, loo shika ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yaka loo ajieɔ nyɔmɔwoo kɛjɛɔ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishijee shika ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ baa shi. Ni ehaa onyɛɔ ojieɔ shikpɔji babaoo ni okɛ ŋmɔ mli nitsulɔi tsuɔ nii.

english: How can I get a much bigger harvest from just my one acre of land without buying more farm land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ ni dalɛ ji acre kome pɛ nɔ ni ehe ehiaaa ni mahe ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ babaoo?

english: You can dramatically increase yield on one acre by using certified high-yielding seeds, maintaining proper plant spacing, applying fertilizer at the exact right time, and keeping weeds out during the first critical month of growth.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha yibiiwoo aya hiɛ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni dalɛ ji acre 1 nɔ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni yɔɔ he odaseyeli lɛ ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ nɔ. Ha tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa ahi shi. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ be ni sa mli. ni ojie jwɛi lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ ni shweremɔ wulu lɛ mli.

english: When crops are crowded, their roots fight for the same soil nutrients and water, while their leaves block sunshine from one another. Proper spacing gives each plant enough sunlight, water, and soil food to develop full, healthy ears.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ amɛhe lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ená toi ni eyi obɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How do I know if my soil is tired, and how can I bring it back to life?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ miifite? Ni te aaafee tɛŋŋ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ aba wala mli ekoŋŋ?

english: Tired soil shows when crop leaves turn pale yellow, growth stays stunted, and yields drop every year. You can restore soil life by adding animal manure, compost, or alternating food crops with nitrogen-fixing plants like groundnuts or cowpeas.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ tsɔɔ be mli ni tso baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Nɔyaa lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ ni nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi daa afi Obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ ŋmei, ŋmei, loo niyenii ni akɛ tsei ni haa nitrogen hiɔ shi tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it good to plant beans or groundnuts on the same land where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmeii yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Maize feeds heavily on soil nutrients, especially nitrogen. Beans and groundnuts are unique because they take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the earth, naturally restoring fertility for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen Beans kɛ peanuts yɛ srɔto ejaakɛ amɛgbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ baa oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli ekoŋŋ.

english: Can I grow cassava and maize together on the same plot, or will they spoil each other?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ loo amɛbaaye amɛhe awui?

english: They grow very well together because maize grows quickly and is harvested in about 3 to 4 months, while cassava grows slowly underneath. Once you harvest the maize, the cassava has plenty of space and time to mature.
ga: Amɛfeɔ ekome kɛkwɛɔ jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ aaafee nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo yɛ shishi. Kɛji okpa ŋmãa lɛ Cassava baaná he kɛ be ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃.

english: Why should I buy certified seeds from the agrodealer instead of saving seeds from my last maize harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ okwaayeli mli jarayelɔ dɛŋ lɛ? Mohu ɔ, a he dumɔwuhi nɛ a je nyagbe ngma kpami ɔ mi ɔ yi.

english: Certified seeds are bred to grow uniformly, withstand local diseases, and produce high yields. Saved seeds from previous harvests lose their vigor over time, leading to uneven growth, smaller crop heads, and lower overall yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ koni amɛdara daa. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ maŋ lɛ mli helai ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho mli lɛ baafite hewalɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dalɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee. Tso lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii. ni nibii fɛɛ ni afee lɛ ba shi

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up and stop growing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa yibiiwoo lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking juices from the plant and spreading viruses. Spraying neem oil extract or proper organic pesticides early keeps these pests away so the plant can flower and fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ baa. Neem mu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ wala mli lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ akashɛ he koni tso lɛ anyɛ afɔ fɔfɔi ni ewo yibii.

english: Does clearing weeds early in the first few weeks really make a big difference to my final crop?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ haa srɔtofeemɔ kpele baa minaagbee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, because weeds grow faster than young crops and steal the moisture, fertilizer, and sunlight your plants need to grow strong roots. Removing weeds within the first 3 to 4 weeks gives your crops a strong start.
ga: Hɛɛ, akɛni jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei bibii ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ni hi jogbaŋŋ hewɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi kɛjɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii 3 kɛyashi 4 lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aje shishi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I protect my crops from drying out when the rains stop suddenly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe koni amɛkagbi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa nɛmɔ trukaa?

english: You can cover the bare soil around your crop roots with dry grass, straw, or leaves (a practice called mulching). This traps soil moisture, reduces water loss from heat, and keeps crop roots cool.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ sũ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko awo ehe. Kɛ jwɛi, jwɛi loo baai aha tso shishifãi ahe (nifeemɔ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ mulching). Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ha nu ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ la mli lɛ aba shi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my cassava so the roots don't turn watery or rot?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei? Koni shishifãi lɛ akatsɔ nu loo amɛkafite?

english: Most improved cassava varieties are ready for harvest between 9 to 12 months after planting. Leaving cassava in the ground too long into another heavy rainy season makes the roots woody, watery, or prone to stem rot.
ga: Cassava henɔi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ateŋ babaoo efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ afee tsei, nu loo ŋmeii lɛ agboi oya.

english: Why do my cassava roots start going soft and turning dark just two days after I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ bafee bɔdɔɔ kɛ ediŋŋ yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ beni mikpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots are living parts of the plant that lose water very quickly once harvested. This triggers a natural chemical process inside the root called physiological deterioration, which causes it to spoil rapidly if not processed or consumed immediately.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ji tso lɛ fã ni hiɛ ka ni kɛ́ akpa lɛ, nu fiteɔ oya. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli tsofafeemɔ nifeemɔ ko jeɔ shishi yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli ni atsɛɔ lɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ fitemɔ. Enɛ haa efiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ atsuuu he nii loo ayeee amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my yams start growing green shoots on their own while stored in my barn during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ bɔi ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛkwɛ̃mɔ be mli ni akɛtoɔ mi-ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yam tubers naturally enter a resting stage after harvest, but when they feel warm temperatures, their internal clock tells them it is time to reproduce, causing them to sprout shoots in search of soil and water.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ boteɔ wɔɔhe be mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Shi kɛ́ amɛnu hulutsoo be lɛ he lɛ Emli ŋmɛlɛtswaa lɛ kɛɛ lɛ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ efɔ bii. Ha amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛtao shikpɔŋ kɛ nu.

english: Why do my cassava roots become hard and woody if I leave them in the ground past their normal harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ wa ni amɛfeɔ tsei kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛho ŋmaakpamɔ be ni sa lɛ he lɛ?

english: As cassava plants pass their mature stage, they shift their energy from storing food starch in the roots to forming tough plant fibers, which turns the soft, edible root woody and difficult to cook.
ga: Kɛji akɛ cassava tso lɛ ho dalɛ be lɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ Amɛtsakeɔ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ starch ni atoɔ yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ amɛfeɔ tso mli tsɔji ni wa. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ, ni ji shishifãi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni ayeɔ ni ehoomɔ wa lɛ tsɔɔ.

english: Why do all the plantains on a bunch turn yellow and soft at the same time after I cut it down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantains ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be kome mli beni mifo amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When a plantain bunch is cut from the tree, it produces a natural ripening gas called ethylene. This gas spreads throughout the whole bunch and triggers all the plantains to ripen and soften together.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afo plantains kuu ko kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ ko ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsɛɔ lɛ ethylene lɛ baa. Gas nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmeii lɛ amli fɛɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfee blɛoo yɛ ekomefeemɔ mli.

english: Why do my green peppers keep changing color to red or yellow after I harvest them from the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-chili eŋɔli lɛ tsakeɔ efeɔ etsuru loo ŋmɔŋ beni mikpa amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Peppers continue their natural living processes even after being picked. They use their remaining internal energy and natural pigments to finish the ripening process, turning from green to red or yellow.
ga: Chili ŋmeii yaa nɔ amɛtsuɔ amɛ adebɔɔ mli wala he nii yɛ be mli ni ajie amɛ po sɛɛ. Akɛ amɛmli hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔlɔi lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛgbe ŋmɔlɔ nitsumɔ lɛ naa. Etsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa etsuru loo ŋmɔŋ mli.

english: Why do my ripe cocoa pods turn black and rot if I leave them on the tree for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Overripe cocoa pods attract moisture and fungal spores from the air. In warm and humid weather, these fungi quickly grow on the sugars inside the pod, causing black pod disease and rotting the beans.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni egbɔ fe nine lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli nibii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Yɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ daa oya yɛ sugar ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. Ekɛ black pod hela baa ni ehaa ŋmeii shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do small insects and tiny holes appear inside my stored maize grains after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii kɛ buji jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ amli yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize grains often contain invisible insect eggs laid while still in the field, or they attract grain weevils in storage. If the maize retains moisture, these insects hatch, multiply, and feed on the inside of the grain.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni anaaa amɛ lɛ awui yɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui amli be mli ni amɛyɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo lɛ. Aloo amɛgbalaa dumɔwui amli ŋmeii ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ lolo Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ fɔɔ, amɛfɔɔ bii, ni amɛyeɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli.

english: Why do my tomatoes turn watery and rot so quickly when transported to the market in hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ mli woɔ nu ni egboɔ oya kɛ́ akɛtee jara nɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomatoes have high water content and thin skins. When exposed to heat and pressure during transport, their skin breaks easily and heat speeds up microbial growth, causing them to rot fast.
ga: Tomato mli nu babaoo yɛ mli, ni ehewolo hu yɛ mlɛo. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo kɛ nɔnyɛɛ ba amɛnɔ yɛ gbɛfaa mli lɛ Amɛhewolo lɛ fãa oya ni hulutsoo lɛ haa nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ daraa oya. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, amɛgboɔ oya.

english: Why do my harvested leafy vegetables turn soft, wet, and hot when packed tightly in large sacks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ baai ni akpa lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ, edɔɔɔ, ni edɔɔ kɛ́ akɛwo kotokui wuji amli jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Harvested vegetables continue to breathe and release heat and moisture. When packed tightly without air circulation, the trapped heat and steam cook the leaves, causing them to wilt and rot.
ga: Aduawai ni akpa lɛ yaa nɔ amɛmuɔ ni amɛjieɔ dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kpo. Kɛji akɛ abɔ he jogbaŋŋ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ Dɔlɛ kɛ lasu ni amɔmɔ lɛ baaha baai lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when planted in direct sunlight without plantains nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni plantains bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees naturally adapted to grow under big forest trees. Their young leaves lose water faster than their roots can absorb under direct sun, so they need shade crops like plantains to shelter them until they mature.
ga: light cocoa tree Etsake koni eda yɛ tsei wuji anɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Amɛbaai bibii lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo tamɔ plantains koni amɛha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: Leaf curling in cassava is usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whitefly insects. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties provided by agricultural officers is the best way to prevent this and protect your harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ, ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi etsɔɔ mli lɛ adumɔ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ onibii ahe ni abuɔ he.

english: Why do my harvested maize grains get full of small holes and white powder after a few weeks in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ mli eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? kɛ powda yɛŋ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi ni akɛto lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Small insects called maize weevils eat into stored corn when the grains are not dried completely before storage. Drying your maize until it is hard and storing it in airtight bags (like PICS bags) starves the insects of air and protects your grain.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ corn weevils lɛ yeɔ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ beni ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛtoɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ ogbi ŋmãa kɛyashi ewa ni okɛto kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli (tamɔ PICS kotoku mli) lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eshi kooloi ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ebu oŋmãa lɛ he.

english: Why do my young maize leaves turn pale yellow instead of dark green, even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ? Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key food plants need to build strong, green leaves. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure gives the soil the nourishment the maize needs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahiamɔ nii aba mli.

english: Why should I stop burning dried grass on my farm before I clear the land for planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makpa jwɛi ni ashãa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ dani majie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha dumɔ nii?

english: While burning clears the land quickly, the fire kills good soil bugs and burns away natural organic matter. Leaving cut grass to rot on top of the soil feeds your crops naturally and keeps moisture in the ground during dry spells.
ga: Shi kɛlɛ, la ni ashãa lɛ haa jɛmɛ tseɔ oya. Shi la gbeɔ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ nɔ lɛ, ni eshãa adebɔɔ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ oha jwɛi ni afo lɛ fite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli

english: Why does covering the dirt around my pepper plants with dry grass keep them from wilting in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ haaa amɛgboi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Covering the dirt with dry grass is called mulching. It acts like a shade umbrella for the soil, keeping the ground cool, stopping water from evaporating in the hot sun, and preventing weeds from growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii akɛ shade kɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ. shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛji akɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ shɛ enɔ. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantain plants grow quickly and have large leaves that act as natural shade umbrellas, keeping the young cocoa plants cool and moist while their roots grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli shade. Ehaa cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe jɔɔ yɛ be mli ni ehaa amɛshishifãi lɛ waa.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences heat stress or sudden changes in watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering and mulching helps the plant hold onto its flowers so fruit can form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ lɛ tsake trukaa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli koni ewo yibii.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when a strong wind blows through my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains fall over if their roots are weak, planted too close to the surface, or damaged by root pests. Planting suckers deep in good soil and using clean, healthy stems helps roots grip the earth tightly.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baagbee shi kɛji shishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ. Adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ tsɔ loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ efite lɛ Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii awo shikpɔŋ kpakpa mli shɔŋŋ ni akɛ ŋmeii ni he tse ni wa tsuɔ nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow poorly if I plant seeds immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛji midu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a long dry spell before the main rains actually start. Seeds planted too early will sprout and then dry up in the hot ground before the regular rains return.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔi wuji lɛ jeɔ shishi diɛŋtsɛ. Dumɔwui ni adu mra tsɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛbaagbi yɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why does removing small extra branches from my tomato plants make the fruit grow bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mijie niji fioo komɛi kɛjɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa aduawai lɛ daraa lɛ?

english: When a tomato plant has too many branches, it splits its energy among many small leaves instead of fruit. Trimming off extra side shoots allows the plant to send all its food and water straight into making bigger, healthier tomatoes.
ga: Kɛji tomato tso ko yɛ niji babaoo Ebaajara hewalɛ lɛ mli ewo baai bibii amli. babaoo yɛ aduawai najiaŋ Kɛ́ afolɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ ŋmeii lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ tsɔɔ eniyenii kɛ nu lɛ fɛɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Is it better for me to grow only cocoa on my whole farm, or should I mix it with food crops like plantain and yam?
ga: Ebaafee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ madu kookoo pɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Aloo esa akɛ akɛ niyenii ni aduɔ tamɔ plantains kɛ sweet potato afutu mli?

english: Relying only on cocoa leaves you without income for years while waiting for the trees to mature. Intercropping food crops like plantain provides crucial shade for young cocoa plants, feeds your family, and gives you regular cash flow throughout the year.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ohe fɔ̃ kookoo pɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha oná shika afii babaoo yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ tsei lɛ ni amɛdara lɛ. Niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ náa hulutsoo ni he hiaa waa. Ha oweku lɛ niyenii ni oha amɛ shika ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ

english: If I plant cassava on the same land where I grow my maize, will the cassava steal all the nutrients and ruin my maize?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ, Ani ŋmãa lɛ baaju niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni baafite mi ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Cassava and maize feed at different soil depths and mature at different times. If you space them correctly, planting them together allows you to harvest maize early while cassava continues growing, giving you two crops from the same land without harming either.
ga: Aduɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ srɔtoi anɔ ni amɛdaraa yɛ bei srɔtoi amli. Kɛji ojara he lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ Amɛ ni ooodu yɛ he kome lɛ baaha okpa o-corn lɛ oya. be mli ni ŋmei yaa nɔ edaa Enɛ haa onine shɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ he kome ni oyeee nɔ ko nɔ ko.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants keep drying up and dying whenever the heavy sunshine comes during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ be fɛɛ be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate roots and thin leaves that cannot handle full, direct sunlight. They require fast-growing shade crops like plantains planted alongside them to act as living umbrellas and keep the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo. ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fɛɛ Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Koni etsu nii akɛ hulutsoo ni hiɛ kã ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close together, will I get a bigger harvest because I have more plants?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ Ani maná ŋmaa babaoo ejaakɛ miyɛ tsei babaoo?

english: Planting too close forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin stalks and tiny corn cobs. Giving each plant proper spacing produces stronger plants and much larger cobs, giving you a bigger total yield.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ tso lɛ atswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei bibii kɛ ŋmãa bibii baa. Kɛ́ aha gbɛ ni sa yɛ tso fɛɛ tso teŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ mli awa ni ebaawo ŋmei ni da kwraa. Ehaa onine shɛɔ nibii babaoo ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences stress from severe heat, uneven watering, or a lack of essential soil nutrients like calcium. Keeping the soil consistently moist and applying the right fertilizer helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ calcium. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why should I trim off healthy branches from my cocoa trees when they are growing so big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛ mi-cacao tso lɛ mli beni edara nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Trimming (pruning) allows sunlight and fresh air to reach the middle of the tree, which stops moisture from trapping fungal diseases like black pod. It also forces the tree to direct its energy into growing cocoa pods instead of useless leaves.
ga: Trimming (pruning) haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shɛɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ. Enɛ haaa ŋmɔtɔ akamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji black pods lɛ. Enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ hu ni ekɛ ehewalɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa kookoo ŋmeii ni miida lɛ amli, ni ekɛyeɔ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do my plantain trees keep falling over easily whenever strong winds blow during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ baatswa yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots and carry heavy fruit bunches at the top, making them top-heavy. Supporting them with sturdy bamboo props and planting windbreak trees around your farm edges protects them from blowing over.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akuu ni tsii yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. make it top heavy Kɛ okɛ ŋmeii ni wa fiɔ amɛsɛɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔŋ tsɔnei ni ooodu yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ amɛhe koni kɔɔyɔɔ akatswa amɛ.

english: How do I know if my farm soil is tired, and what will happen to my pepper plants if I plant on it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli edɔ? Ni mɛni baaba mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ kɛji mikɛwo nɔ?

english: Tired soil causes crops to grow slowly, develop pale yellow leaves, and produce very small fruits. You can restore tired soil naturally by rotating your crops and planting leguminous plants like cowpeas, which put nitrogen back into the dirt.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii daa blɛoo, eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ewoɔ yibii bibii waa. Obaanyɛ okɛ shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni oootsake kɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii ni ooodu lɛ nɔ, ni no baaha nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and turn yellow during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies feeding on the plant's sap and spreading viruses like Cassava Mosaic Disease. Using disease-resistant cassava varieties prevents this yellowing and protects your harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni yeɔ tsei amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni egbɛɔ helai tamɔ cassava mosaic hela lɛ eshwaa. Kɛ́ okɛ cassava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔlɔ akafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ebaabu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Why do my crops grow better when I add animal manure into the soil before planting instead of using only chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ kooloi ashishifãi wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani midu yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ sũ mli lɛ pɛ baatsu nii lɛ?

english: Animal manure improves the actual structure of the soil so it can hold water longer during dry spells and feeds healthy soil microbes, whereas chemical fertilizers only provide short-term plant food without improving the soil itself.
ga: Koolooi ashishifãi haa bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ yaa hiɛ. Bɔni afee ni enyɛ ekɛ nu ato be kakadaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. ni ekɛ niyenii haa shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii bibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa tsei niyenii pɛ yɛ be kukuoo mli ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kwraa.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive under strong direct sunlight because their roots are shallow and their leaves dry out quickly. Leaving shade trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantain provides living shade and holds moisture in the soil until the cocoa matures.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ ahi shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, eshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni baai lɛ hu gbɛ́ɔ oya. Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha hulutsoo aba ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in cold, wet, and humid conditions. Pruning excess cocoa branches opens up the farm to air and sunlight, drying out the leaves and pods so the fungus cannot spread easily.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, fɛ̃i, kɛ fɛ̃i yɔɔ. Kookoo niji ni fa fe nine ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la baa ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Fungus nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my crop roots with dry leaves and grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai ni egbi kɛ jwɛi awo tsei shishifãi ahe lɛ?

english: This practice is called mulching. It acts like a protective blanket over the ground, keeping the soil cool, preventing water from evaporating quickly under the hot sun, and stopping weeds from taking over.
ga: Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. ni etsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: Heavy rainfall washes the fertilizer away off the surface or deep down into the ground past where the plant roots can reach, wasting your money and time without helping the crops grow.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni tsei shishifãi baanyɛ ashɛ he lɛ. Eheɔ bo shika kɛ be ni eyeee ebuaaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the lower parts of the plant usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which maize needs in large amounts to grow healthy and green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishigbɛ hei lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi he miihia lɛ babaoo koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni efee eŋɔli.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow smaller even if there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ bibioo kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa po lɛ?

english: Weeds act as silent thieves on the farm. They aggressively pull water, sunlight, and soil food away from your crops, leaving the main plants starved and weak.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi ni efee dioo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli: amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛmu nu, hulu la, kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ mɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: You must check the small growth buds along the stem and make sure they are pointing up toward the sky. Planting them upside down forces the shoots to grow downwards first, causing weak plants and low yield.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ hiŋmɛii bibii lɛ. yɛ tso lɛ shishi ni okwɛ koni amɛtsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ kɛya shikpɔŋ klɛŋklɛŋ. Ehaa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my main crop seeds immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui titrii lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a short dry spell. If seeds sprout during this dry gap, the tender roots will burn in the dry soil and die before the real rainy season settles in.
ga: Nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku sɛɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ amli lɛ, shishifãi bibii lɛ baashã yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ ni amɛbaagboi dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ diɛŋtsɛ aba.

english: Why is it a good idea to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on the farm after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that grab nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, naturally fertilizing the ground for your next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Koni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are there small caterpillars eating holes into the central leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ bu yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana. They hide in the central funnel of the plant to feed, but early detection allows you to apply neem oil extract or recommended chemicals directly into the whorl to control them.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli koni amɛye nii. Shi mra be mli ni ana Enɛ baaha okɛ neem fɔ mli nu loo tsofai ni ajieɔ yi lɛ awo ŋwɛi ŋtayaai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni okɛkudɔ amɛ.

english: Why should I cut my green plantains into small thin slices before sun-drying them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ plantain eŋɔli lɛ mli bibii bibii lɛ? Dani okɛbaawo hulu lɛ mli?

english: Small, thin slices dry much faster and more evenly under the sun. Removing the water quickly prevents mold and bacteria from causing the plantains to rot before they are fully dry.
ga: Nibii bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ baagbi oya kwraa ni amɛbaafee ekome yɛ hulu la shishi. Nu ni ajieɔ oya lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ akafite plantains lɛ dani amɛgbi kwraa.

english: What is the best way to dry my harvested plantains so they do not get black mold?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ agbiɔ plantains ni akpa koni ŋmɔtɔ diŋ akafee nɔ ko?

english: Spread sliced plantains in a single layer on raised wooden drying tables or clean mats off the ground where air can circulate. Covering them or bringing them inside at night prevents night dew from making them damp and moldy.
ga: Okɛ plantain fãi ni afo lɛ ashwã tso okpɔlɔ ni egbi loo tsɔne ni he tse nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ atsɔ mli lɛ nɔ yɛ fã kome mli. Kɛ́ oha amɛhe nɔ loo okɛ amɛ ba gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaatsi gbɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaha amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my plantains rot so quickly after I harvest them from the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains lɛ fiteɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mikpa amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains continue to breathe and produce natural heat and gas after harvest, which speeds up ripening and decay. Keeping harvested bunches in a cool, shaded place away from direct sunlight slows down this process.
ga: Dumɔwui yaa nɔ amɛmuɔ ni amɛjieɔ dɔlɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpo yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Enɛ baaha ekwɛ̃ ni efite oya. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ to he ko ni mli ejɔ ni hulu la shɛɛɛ he tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaha nifeemɔ nɛɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Why do my dried plantain chips turn soft and soggy after I store them for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains ni egbi lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ beni akɛto gbii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Dried plantains absorb moisture from the humid air around them. To keep them crisp and dry, store them in airtight containers or tightly sealed plastic bags as soon as they cool down after sun-drying.
ga: Plantains ni egbi lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbi Kɛ amɛ awo tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo plastic kotoku ko ni atsĩ naa mli kɛji amɛhe ejɔ pɛ beni amɛgbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ sɛɛ.

english: How can I keep flies and dust off my plantains while they are drying outside?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahã ŋmeii kɛ sũ akaje mi-plantains lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni migbiɔ amɛ yɛ kpo nɔ lɛ?

english: Build a simple solar drying frame or cover your drying plantain slices with a thin, clean mosquito net or mesh cloth. This lets the sunlight and wind in while keeping flies, insects, and dust out.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ hulutsoo tsɔne ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Aloo ha plantain lɛ nɔ fãi bibii. Kɛ ŋmeii loo mama ko ni he tse ni akɛ ŋmeii fee. Ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ mli, ni yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii, kooloi bibii, kɛ sũ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Can I turn my extra green plantains into flour so they store longer, and how do I do it?
ga: Ani manyɛ matsɔ plantains eŋɔli ni fa fe nine lɛ mafee ashikishaŋ koni mikɛto be kakadaŋŋ? Ni mɛni mifeɔ?

english: Yes, green plantain flour lasts for months. You peel green plantains, slice them thinly, dry them completely in the sun until hard, and then mill them into fine flour.
ga: Hɛɛ, plantain ashikishaŋ ni ji eŋɔli lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi nyɔji babaoo. Ofolɔɔ plantains eŋɔlii lɛ, ofoɔ amɛ bibii bibii, ni ogbiɔ amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, shwiemɔ ni efee ashikishaŋ kpakpa.

english: How can I easily peel sticky green plantains without the sap ruining my hands?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafolɔ plantains eŋɔli ni wa ni miniji eyeee awui?

english: Rubbing a small amount of cooking oil on your hands or soaking the unpeeled plantains in warm water for a few minutes loosens the sticky latex sap and makes peeling much easier.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ fɔ fioo ko ni akɛhooɔ nii shwie oniji anɔ loo okɛ plantains ni ajieee amɛhe tsɔi lɛ wo nu ni mli edɔ mli minitii fioo komɛi lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa lɛ ajie ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe tsɔi lɛ afee mlɛo kwraa.

english: Is it better to harvest my plantains when they are still green or when they turn yellow?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ abaakpa plantain lɛ be mli ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo loo be mli ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ?

english: Harvest while green and firm if you plan to dry them, make flour, or travel long distances with them. Harvest when they start turning yellow if you want to eat them fresh or sweet right away.
ga: Kpãa be mli ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo ni eyɛ hewalɛ kɛji oto gbɛjianɔ akɛ okɛbaagbi, ofee ashikishaŋ, loo okɛfã gbɛ kakadaŋŋ. Kpãa be mli ni ebɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji oosumɔ ni oye lɛ ehee loo ŋmɔlɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do plantain and banana trees fall over easily when heavy rain and wind come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ banana dumɔwui kɛ dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ ni kɔɔyɔɔ miitswa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems and heavy fruit bunches at the top. Supporting the main stem with a bamboo pole or strong wooden Y-prop helps hold up the weight against strong winds.
ga: Dumɔwu lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akuu ni tsii yɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei tsei loo tsei ni wa ni tamɔ Y fi ŋmei titri lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni enyɛ edamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa naa.

english: Why are some of my plantain bunches very small while others on the same farm grow large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ ekomɛi ji bibii nɛkɛ lɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, plantains komɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ dara.

english: Small bunches usually happen when the plant doesn't get enough water or manure, or when too many young suckers are growing around the mother stem and stealing nutrients from the main crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii baa kɛji tso lɛ náaa nu loo ŋmeii ni fa bɔ ni sa. aloo be mli ni ŋmeii bibii babaoo miida yɛ ehe lɛ. nyɛ stem lɛ ni ejuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli

english: Young cocoa plants need shade from direct sun because their young leaves dry out quickly. Planting shade trees or plantains nearby shields them from harsh sunlight and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he hulutsoo ejaakɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la ni naa wa lɛ tsiɔ naa, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why is my oil palm tree taking so many years before it starts producing fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani ebɔi yibiiwoo lɛ?

english: Oil palm trees focus their early energy on growing strong trunk and root systems. Most varieties take between 3 to 4 years of proper care, weeding, and feeding before they produce their first harvestable fruit bunches.
ga: Mu tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa amɛshishifãi ni mli wa kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Henɔi srɔtoi lɛ ateŋ babaoo heɔ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 ni akɛkwɛɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ, ajieɔ jwɛi, ni akɛhaa amɛ dani amɛwoɔ yibii akui ni abaanyɛ akpa klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa.

english: How can I tell if my rubber trees are old enough for me to start collecting latex?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-rɔba tso lɛ egbɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi nu ni hoɔ lɛ naa?

english: Rubber trees are ready for tapping when the trunk reaches about 50 centimeters in width at a height of one meter from the ground, which usually happens around 6 to 7 years after planting.
ga: Rɔba tsei lɛ efee klalo kɛha gbee kɛji amɛtso lɛ shishi lɛ mlilɛɛmɔ aaafee sɛntimitai 50 ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kwɔ aaafee mita 1, ni bei pii lɛ, ebaa yɛ afii 6 kɛyashi 7 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and green in one part of my farm but stay small and yellow in another?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miikwɛ̃ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔji yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fã ko nɔ lɛ? Shi ebatsɔ bibioo ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ he kroko.

english: Soil quality is not the same everywhere on a farm. Areas where crops turn yellow often lack key nutrients like nitrogen or hold too much water, which prevents roots from feeding properly.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su lɛ jeee ekome yɛ he fɛɛ he yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, hei ni tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa, tamɔ nitrogen, loo amɛhiɛɔ nu babaoo mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Will using chemical fertilizers spoil my land for future farming?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye mishikpɔŋ lɛ awui kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii wɔsɛɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizers will not spoil your soil if used in the correct quantities. Adding organic materials like compost or animal manure along with fertilizer keeps the soil soft, rich, and productive for years.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ eyeee shikpɔŋ lɛ awui kɛji akɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ bɔ ni sa mli. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee bɔdɔɔ, ebaawo yibii afii babaoo.

english: Is it safe for me to plant cassava and maize together on the same field?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting maize and cassava together works well because maize grows quickly and is harvested within three to four months, leaving plenty of room and sunlight for the slower-growing cassava to mature.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa lɛ daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. Enɛ haa gbɛ kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ŋmei ni daa blɛoo lɛ anyɛ eda.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and rotting right on the branch when it rains heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in dark, damp conditions. Trimming extra tree branches lets air and sunlight flow through the farm to dry out moisture and slow the disease.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ewo duŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Tsei krokomɛi ni afolɔ ashwie shi koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli Koni ŋmɔtɔ agbi ni eha hela shishijee aba sɛɛ.

english: Weeds naturally produce thousands of tough seeds that lie hidden in the soil. When you clear the land, sunlight and rain trigger these weed seeds to sprout instantly, growing faster than newly planted crop seeds.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ woɔ dumɔwui akpei abɔ ni wa ni akɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji ojie jɛmɛ lɛ Hulu kɛ nugbɔ baaha jwɛi dumɔwui nɛɛ akwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Edaa oya fe dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, dry soil, or lack of soil nutrients. Regular watering and placing dry grass around the base helps keep the soil cool and moist.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwieɔ shi kɛ́ amɛna nɔnyɛɛ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli kɛ jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Shishitoo ni afeɔ daa lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ.

english: Why should I grow my crop seeds in black plastic bags first instead of planting them directly in the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu miŋmɔshi nibii amli dumɔwui lɛ yɛ plastic kotokui diji amli klɛŋklɛŋ moŋ fe ni madu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?
