english: Starting seeds in plastic bags allows you to protect fragile young plants from pests, heavy rains, and hot sun, ensuring only strong and healthy seedlings are moved to the main field.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ooobɔi plastic kotokui amli lɛ haa onyɛɔ obuɔ dumɔwui ni waaa lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa dumɔwui ni he wa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ pɛ ji nɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa plants drop leaves during the Harmattan because intense sunlight and dry winds make them lose water faster than their roots can drink. Providing shade plants like plantains keeps the air cool and humid, protecting the young cocoa leaves from scorching.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai yɛ Harmattan beaŋ ejaakɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ haa nu lɛ fiteɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo ha tsei tamɔ plantains lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo baai bibii ahe koni amɛkashã.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay very small even though the stems and leaves above ground look bushy and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Kɛji shikpɔŋ nɔ tsei ashishifãi kɛ baai lɛ tamɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ po lɛ,

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or lacks potassium, the cassava plant spends all its energy producing tall branches and green leaves instead of transferring starch into the tubers beneath the soil.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo potassium bɛ mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ niji kakadaji kɛ baai eŋɔlii. Mohu ɔ, ngɔ starch ɔ kɛ ya tubers ɔmɛ a mi.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upward into tight bunches and stopping new growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiikpa dalɛ hee lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies, or a virus they spread, which feeds on the plant sap and distorts new leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa ni yeɔ tso mli nu ni efiteɔ baai heei lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why are there tiny ragged holes in my young maize leaves with small dirt pellets inside the central funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? ni etse ni eyɛ sũ bibii yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which crawls into the central whorl of the maize plant during the day to feed safely on the tender young leaves before they unfurl.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni shwereɔ kɛboteɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ ateŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ shweshweeshwe dani amɛjie amɛhe kpo lɛ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my growing tomatoes turn dark brown and soft before the fruit even ripens?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This issue is blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit during development, which commonly happens when soil moisture fluctuates unpredictably between wet and dry conditions.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ naagba nɛɛ baa ji fɔfɔi lɛ anaagbee fitemɔ, ni ji nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ yɛ gbɛ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ ateŋ.

english: Why does my lowland swamp rice grow well in flooded fields while my maize rots and dies in standing water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-swamp rice lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔji ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni mi-abele lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egboɔ yɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rice plants have internal air channels that transport oxygen down to their roots underwater, whereas maize roots suffocate and drown when deprived of oxygen in waterlogged soil.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ amɛmli ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ nu shishi lɛ amli. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I allow all the young suckers to grow around my main plantain stem at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mihaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ fɛɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Mi plantain titri lɛ shwereɔ yɛ be kome too mli

english: Allowing too many suckers forces them to compete with the parent tree for soil nutrients and light, resulting in small, thin bunches instead of large, heavy plantain fingers.
ga: Kɛ́ amɛshi ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, enyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛkɛ tso nyɛ lɛ abɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kpakpai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ la. Enɛ haa niji bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo baa yɛ niji wuji ni tsii najiaŋ.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall wooden stakes to climb on instead of growing along the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛkwɔɔ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeetsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eda lɛ?

english: Lifting yam leaves off the ground allows them to capture more sunlight to make food for larger tubers while keeping the leaves dry to prevent fungal diseases from spreading.
ga: Kɛ́ awo sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa amɛnáa hulu la babaoo ni amɛkɛhaa amɛ ŋmeii wuji lɛ niyenii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ agbi koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why does planting cowpeas in my field make my next crop of maize grow much stronger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa mi ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ daa waa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that work with helpful soil bacteria to absorb nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil, creating natural fertilizer for future nitrogen-hungry crops like maize.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tsuɔ nii koni amɛjie nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛmɔmɔ lɛ awo sũ lɛ mli. Bɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa nitrogen wɔsɛɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why does applying chemical fertilizer to dry soil burn my crops instead of feeding them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ shãa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ moŋ fe ni mahã amɛ niyenii lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer needs moisture to dissolve safely into the soil; on dry soil, the concentrated fertilizer salts suck water out of the crop roots, causing the plant to wilt and burn.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he miihia ŋmɔtɔ koni etsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shweshweeshwe. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tsei shishifãi amli, ni no haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshãa.

english: Rolling leaves is the maize plant's way of sweating less and saving water. By curling its leaves inward, it hides its leaf surface from the hot sun so water does not evaporate too quickly.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ kome ni ŋmãa tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛshwieɔ latsaa fioo ni amɛbuɔ nu he. Kɛ́ atsɔ baai lɛ anɔ awo mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ baa lɛ hiɛ teeɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Bɔni afee ni nu lɛ akafee ŋmɔtɔ oya tsɔ

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When excess rainwater floods the farm and stays trapped, it drowns the roots, allowing tiny fungi in the wet soil to infect and rot the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyi ŋmɔ lɛ mli obɔ ni ekɛ ehe wo mli lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli, ni amɛshiɔ ŋmeii bibii. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ emɔ hela ni egbo.

english: Leaf curling happens when tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips suck the liquid juice from the underside of young leaves and pass a virus into the plant, causing it to grow twisted and stunted.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips lɛ nu nu kɛjɛ baai bibii lɛ ashishi ni amɛkɛ hela lɛ bote tso lɛ mli. ni haa efeɔ nɔ ni efiteɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the plant without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsɔko aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant feels too much heat or doesn't get enough steady water. The extreme heat weakens the flower parts so pollination fails, causing the plant to dump the useless flower.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo enáaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ fãi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, pollin lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii. Ha tso lɛ ashɛrɛ fɔfɔi ni he ehiaaa lɛ ashwie.

english: Why are the bottom leaves on my maize stalks turning yellow in the shape of a V?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ?

english: When maize lacks nitrogen food from the soil, it steals nitrogen from its older bottom leaves and sends it up to feed the young growing leaves at the top, leaving the lower leaves yellowed.
ga: Kɛji ŋmãa bɛ nitrogen niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Ejuɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ, ni edara lɛ mli ni etsuɔ ​​kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni eyaha baa bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii. Ha baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why does my cowpea farm have plenty of big green leaves but very few seed pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea ŋmɔ lɛ mli baa agboi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli shi dumɔwui ŋmɔji fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas gather their own nitrogen from the air. If you give them too much nitrogen fertilizer, the plant thinks it only needs to grow leafy branches instead of spending energy to produce flowers and seed pods.
ga: Cowpeas buaa amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ nitrogen naa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Kɛji okɛ nitrogen babaoo wo mli Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni tsei kɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛfee fɔfɔi kɛ dumɔwui ashishifãi lɛ, tsei susuɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni amɛkwɛ̃ niji kɛ baai.

english: Why does my harvested maize spoil with mold and insects if I store it right after picking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii fiteɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ? Kɛji mibua naa amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mibua naa lɛ?

english: Freshly picked maize still holds water inside the grain. Moisture acts like an invitation for mold fungi to grow and attracts grain-eating insects, so drying the grain thoroughly in the sun stops them.
ga: Abɛi ni ajie ehee lɛ yɛ nu yɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli lolo. Fɛ̃i tsuɔ nii tamɔ ninefɔ̃ɔ kɛha ŋmɔtɔ ni eda ni egbalaa koolooi ni yeɔ ŋmaa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ agbi dumɔwui lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ehaa amɛkpaa nitsumɔ.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers start sprouting green shoots inside the barn even without rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tubers ni akpa lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔshi nibii ŋmɔji yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers are alive and have a natural biological clock. After resting dormant for a few months after harvest, internal chemical changes trigger the tuber to break its sleep and push out new shoots to plant itself.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ yɛ wala mli ni amɛyɛ adebɔɔ mli wala yibii ahe ŋmɛlɛtswaa. Yɛ hejɔɔmɔ kɛkɛ sɛɛ Nyɔji enyɔ loo etɛ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ Tsofai amli tsakemɔi haa ŋmeii lɛ wɔɔ ni amɛtsiɔ ŋmeii heei kɛjɛɔ mli koni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do my heavy plantain trees fall over so easily when strong winds blow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui ni tsii lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants do not grow deep taproots into the ground; they only have shallow surface roots. If nematodes damage these shallow roots or the soil is too wet, the heavy plant loses its grip and falls over.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ shishifãi kɛyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Amɛyɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ pɛ. Kɛji akɛ nematodes lɛ fite shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ nɛɛ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ lɛ, Tsei ni tsii lɛ nyɛŋ amɔmɔ amɛhe ni amɛbaagbee shi.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains near them creates a natural shelter that keeps the young plants cool and retains moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli shihilɛhe ni yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei bibii lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the maize is lacking nitrogen, which is the key food plants need to build green leaves. Applying balanced fertilizer or organic compost supplies the needed nitrogen to restore healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha nitrogen ni he hiaa koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba.

english: How do I know when my cassava stems are ready for harvest underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-cassava tsei lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is ready for harvesting when the lower leaves yellow and drop off, and the ground around the base of the plant begins to swell and crack open as the tubers expand.
ga: Cassava efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi lɛ. ni he ni ebɔle shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni bulb lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ.

english: When too many small shoots (suckers) grow around a plantain tree, they compete with the mother plant for food and water. Removing extra suckers leaves more energy for the main stem to produce a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmeii bibii (ŋmeii) babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ dumɔwu ko he lɛ, amɛkɛ fɔlɔ tso lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu. Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ yitso lɛ hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛfee kuu agbo ni tsii.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close to each other, will I get a larger harvest from my farm?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ Ani maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting seeds too close together makes the crops compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin stalks and small cobs. Giving each plant proper spacing allows it to grow strong and yield bigger cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii baa. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni sa yɛ tso fɛɛ tso teŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛdara waa ni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to expose all their leaves to sunlight. Sunlight helps the leaves manufacture food, which travels down to feed and expand the yam tubers beneath the soil.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ fɛɛ ashɛ hulu la lɛ he. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛwoɔ niyenii. ni fãa gbɛ kɛyaa shi koni eyaye ni ekwɛ̃ yam ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi

english: What is causing holes in my young corn leaves and leaving small dirt pellets inside the plant center?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli kɛ sũ bibii ni eshiɔ lɛ baa? yɛ tso lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides and feeds inside the growing tip of the corn plant. Applying recommended treatments early in the morning or late evening directly into the leaf funnel targets these pests effectively.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ ashishifãi amli ni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ wo tso lɛ baai lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaagbe nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ahe jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do extension officers advise leaving dry leaves and cut grass around the base of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ ashɛrɛ baai ni egboi lɛ ashwie ni akpɛtɛ mitsei lɛ ashishigbɛ he lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry plant material (mulching) acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool, slows down water evaporation during hot days, and stops weeds from popping up around your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni egbi (mulch) shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ha nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aya hiɛ fioo yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. ni otsi jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ naa.

english: Pepper flowers drop off mainly due to heat stress or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist and protecting plants from dry wind helps the flowers stay attached and form pepper pods.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baa shi yɛ dɔlɛ haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa kɛ tsei ahe ni abuɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa egbiɔ lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛfeɔ pepper pods.

english: Is it helpful to plant groundnuts together in the same field with my maize crop?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ baadu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Yes, groundnuts naturally pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, which enriches the earth and feeds nearby heavy feeders like maize, improving total yield.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni ehaa niyenii babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa, ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: If I only have a small amount of fertilizer for my farm, what is the best way to apply it so it actually works?
ga: Kɛji miyɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ko pɛ kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ. Te aaafee tɛŋŋ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni ana yibii diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Instead of scattering a small quantity over the whole field where rain and weeds will wash it away, place a small pinch right next to the base of each crop stem (ring placement or spot application). This concentrates the food directly where the plant's roots can drink it up.
ga: Mohu ɔ, mo ngmɛɛ lɛ bɔɔbɔɔbɔɔ kɛ pue ngmɔ ɔ mi he nɛ nugbɔ kɛ jwɛi ma tsɔ lɛ ɔ. Okɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibioo ko awo tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko shishi. (Ring placement loo topical application) Enɛ haa niyenii lɛ feɔ ekome tɛ̃ɛ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anu.

english: Why does my farmland produce smaller harvests every year even though I plant the same way?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiba shi daa afi lɛ? Ni midu yɛ nakai gbɛ nɔ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Crops feed on specific nutrients in the dirt. Planting the same crop in the same spot year after year drains those exact nutrients completely, leaving the soil empty. Rotating your crops or adding compost helps replenish the soil's strength.
ga: Tsei yeɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome afi fɛɛ afi lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni yeɔ emuu aba. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ Nibii ni atsakeɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ewajeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why are my young rice plants turning yellow when there is too much water on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni nu babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: While rice loves moisture, young plants still need oxygen in their roots. When submerged completely under deep water for too long without air, the roots suffocate and stop absorbing food, causing the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmãa sumɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ moŋ Shi tsei bibii lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lolo. Kɛji akɛ awo nu shishi kwraa ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa niyenii ni amɛyeɔ lɛ. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: How do I know if the rice variety I bought is meant for low swampy areas or dry land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmãa ni miheɔ lɛ ji hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ loo hei ni nu bɛ lɛ anɔ?

english: Upland rice varieties are bred to grow like maize in normal rain-fed soil, while lowland rice varieties need shallow standing water to control weeds and thrive. You should always check the seed label or ask an officer before planting, as planting lowland rice on dry hills will cause it to dry up and fail.
ga: Akwɛ ŋmãa henɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ tamɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ nɔ daa lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmãa henɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ biɔ nu ni mli ekwɔɔɔ koni enyɛ eye jwɛi lɛ anɔ ni ekwɛ̃. Kwɛmɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe wolo lɛ be fɛɛ be loo bi nitsulɔi lɛ dani odu. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɛ́ adu ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gɔji ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmãa lɛ agbi ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my crop leaves roll up tightly like sticks during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ tsei niji yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rolling leaves is a survival mechanism. When the sun is too hot, plants roll their leaves inward to cover their pores, reducing water loss through evaporation so they do not dry out completely.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa wala. Kɛ hulu lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ Tso lɛ shwieɔ ebaa lɛ mli kɛyaa mli koni ekɛ ŋmeii lɛ ato. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nu ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi. Koni baai lɛ akagbi kwraa

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with weak stems when I throw many seeds close together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛshishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ beni mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo shwieɔ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight. They waste all their energy stretching upwards to reach the sun, leaving them thin, weak, and easy for strong winds to blow over.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Amɛfiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛshɛɔ hulu lɛ he lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ mlɛo, amɛhe waaa ni ewaaa akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baatsɔ mli.

english: Why are my maize plants producing tiny cobs with missing kernels?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ miiwo ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Mɛɛ nɔ ni bɛ dumɔwui?

english: Small or incomplete maize cobs usually happen when the plant lacks nitrogen fertilizer or suffers from drought during flowering. Silks need plenty of water and nutrients to properly collect pollen and fill every seed on the cob.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa bibii loo ni eshɛɛɛ he lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ nitrogen ŋmãa loo hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ awui yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Nu kɛ niyenii babaoo he miihia siliki lɛ koni ekɛbua pollen lɛ naa jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛwo dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: Why do my vegetable plants suddenly collapse and die after a heavy rain following a long dry period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Dry, hot soil can shock thirsty root systems when flooded suddenly. Extreme moisture after drought also encourages quick-spreading soil fungi that rot the weakened roots instantly.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi ni kumai yeɔ amɛ lɛ atswa nu afua trukaa. Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo yɛ hɔmɔ sɛɛ lɛ hu woɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni haa shishifãi ni egbɔjɔ lɛ fiteɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya lɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil (or over-using certain fertilizers) encourages the plant to build big branches and leaves while 'forgetting' to store food in the roots. Balance fertilizer use so energy goes into the tubers.
ga: Nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nibii komɛi ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine (loo nibii komɛi ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine) woɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛwo tsei niji kɛ baai wuji yɛ be mli ni ‘amɛhiɛ kpaa nɔ’ akɛ amɛbaato niyenii yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Tsakemɔ bɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii ahaa lɛ mli koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha ŋmeii lɛ.

english: You can monitor the age of the crop (usually 9 to 12 months after planting) and observe the leaves. When lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, carefully dig out soil around just one side of the plant to inspect tuber size before harvesting everything.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ afii ni onibii lɛ eye (bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ be mli ni odu lɛ sɛɛ) ni okwɛ baai lɛ, be mli ni baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Tsɔɔmɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Dumɔ jogbaŋŋ koni okwɛ bulb lɛ dalɛ dani okpa nɔ fɛɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young maize seedlings wither easily in the hot sun while the adult ones stay strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni tso ni eda lɛ he wa lolo lɛ?

english: Young seedlings have very tender leaves and shallow roots that cannot reach deep underground water. Older plants have developed deep root systems and tougher leaves that help them endure high heat without drying out.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ baai ni bɛ hewalɛ waa kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ he. Tsei ni edara lɛ ená shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ baai ni mli wa ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni amɛgbiɛɛ.

english: Why is it better for me to plant out my fresh vegetable nursery shoots early in the morning or late in the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu mi-green shoots lɛ leebi loo shwane mli lɛ?

english: Transplanting during the cooler hours reduces heat shock and water loss from the young plants. It gives their tender roots time to adjust and settle into the new soil before facing the harsh midday sun.
ga: Kɛ́ atsake tsei lɛ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo kɛ nu ni jɛɔ tsei bibii amli lɛ aba shi. Enɛ haa shishifãi bibii lɛ náa be ni amɛkɛtsakeɔ amɛhe ni amɛhiɔ shikpɔŋ hee lɛ nɔ dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe.

english: Why does one cassava variety survive the dry harmattan season on my farm while another type dries up completely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei henɔ kome yeɔ wala yɛ harmattan be ni mli egbi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni henɔ kroko lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Different crop varieties have different natural strengths. Drought-resistant cassava varieties store more moisture in their roots and drop fewer leaves to conserve water, whereas softer varieties need constant water to stay alive.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi yɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛi srɔtoi. Cassava henɔi ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. ni eshiɔ baai fioo koni ekɛto nu he yɛ be mli ni henɔi ni mli jɔ lɛ biɔ nu daa koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do high-yielding cocoa seedlings from the nursery bear fruit much earlier than seeds I saved from my own harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni jɛɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ woɔ yibii oya fe dumɔwui ni mibuaa naa kɛjɛɔ mi diɛŋtsɛ mikpamɔ mli lɛ?

english: Nursery seedlings are often bred or grafted from mature, high-quality mother plants designed to produce early. Seeds saved directly from pods take a much longer natural path to reach maturity.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, afɔɔ dumɔwui ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ loo akɛwoɔ amɛmli kɛjɛɔ nyɛ tsei ni eda ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni afee koni amɛwo yibii mra lɛ amli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ɔ kwraa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my corn turning yellow and dying during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When water and nutrients are limited, the plant naturally sacrifices its older lower leaves by moving available moisture and food up to save the young, growing top leaves.
ga: Kɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ faaa lɛ Tsei kɛ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ shaa afɔle yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ koni amɛkɛbu ŋwɛi baai bibii ni miida lɛ ahe.

english: Why are all the flowers falling off my pepper plants instead of turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsei anɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when stressed by extreme heat or lack of water. The plant conserves its energy to survive the stress rather than spending it on developing new fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli lɛ he. Tsei toɔ hewalɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni amɛye nɔnyɛɛ mli moŋ fe ni amɛaafite koni amɛwo yibii heei.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide large leaves that act as temporary umbrellas, giving the cocoa the shade and cool soil it needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ be kukuoo mli ŋwɛi ŋwɛi. Enɛ haa kookoo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and aggressively steal nutrients and sunlight from the soil. Even with plenty of water, your crops remain starved of the essential food needed to grow tall and strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛkɛ ekãa juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ nu babaoo po Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa lɛ lolo.

english: Why should I put fertilizer right near the plant base instead of scattering it everywhere on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo he ni bɛŋkɛ mitsei lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ moŋ fe ni magbɛ eshwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli he fɛɛ he?

english: Applying fertilizer close to the base ensures the plant's roots absorb the nutrients directly, preventing the fertilizer from being washed away by rain or stolen by surrounding weeds.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnáa niyenii mli hewalɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haaa nugbɔ atsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ loo jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ akaju.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow small and crooked when planted in hard, unplowed soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ bibii ni ebɔle amɛhe kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni atsuko nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose soil to push through as they expand. Hard soil presses against the growing tuber, forcing it to bend or stop growing large altogether.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse koni amɛtsɔ mli be mli ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ nyɛɔ bulb ni miida lɛ nɔ. Ni anyɛɔ enɔ koni ebɔle ehe loo ekpa dalɛ kwraa

english: How long will it take for a newly planted coconut tree to start producing fruit on my farm?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani ŋmei tso ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Traditional tall coconut varieties usually take 6 to 10 years to start fruiting, but dwarf coconut varieties can begin producing fruit much faster, often within 3 to 4 years if properly watered and weeded.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, blema ŋmeii srɔtoi ni kɛlɛ lɛ heɔ afii 6 kɛyashi 10 dani amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi. Shi ŋmeii srɔtoi ni ji dwarf lɛ baanyɛ aje yibiiwoo shishi mra kwraa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ yeɔ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 kɛji akɛ awo nu jogbaŋŋ ni ajie jwɛi.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young coconut trees turning yellow and brown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmei bibii lɛ ashishigbɛ fãi lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves are usually a sign that the tree lacks key soil nutrients like nitrogen or potassium, or that the soil is waterlogged and preventing the roots from breathing.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hia yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen loo potassium. Aloo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu.

english: Can I grow food crops like cassava or maize between my rows of coconut trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmei tsei ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ?

english: Yes, because coconut trees are spaced wide apart, you can easily grow food crops like cassava, maize, or beans between the rows during the first few years before the tree canopy closes.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ akokoso tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ waa. Obaanyɛ okɛ niyenii tamɔ ŋmei, ŋmei loo ŋmei awo ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli dani tso lɛ ŋmei lɛ aŋmɛ.

english: Why do the small coconut flowers fall off before turning into real coconuts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akokoo fɔfɔi bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛtsɔɔ akokoo diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Young coconut flowers drop off mainly due to dry spells, lack of nutrients, or insect pests like bugs damaging the delicate flowers before they can develop into fruit.
ga: Kokoo fɔfɔi bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi babaoo yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ, loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ kooloi ni tutuaa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ dani amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ hewɔ.

english: How can I turn my harvested coconuts into flour that can be used for baking bread or biscuits?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsɔ ŋmei ni akpa lɛ mafee ashikishaŋ ni akɛshãa blodo loo biskit?

english: Coconut flour is made by grating fresh coconut meat, squeezing out the coconut milk, thoroughly drying the leftover solid coconut fiber, and then grinding it into a fine flour.
ga: Afeɔ akooshi ashikishaŋ kɛtsɔ akooshi loo hee ni ajieɔ, akooshi mliki lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli, kɛ akooshi fiji ni eshwɛ lɛ ni agbiɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, shwie nɔ ni etsɔ powda kpakpa.

english: Is leftover coconut waste after making oil good to feed to my farm animals like pigs?
ga: Ani ŋmeii ni eshwɛ yɛ mu sɛɛ lɛ feɔ niyenii kpakpa kɛhaa ŋmɔ mli kooloi tamɔ tsinai?

english: Yes, coconut cake—the solid material left after pressing out the oil—is rich in protein and energy, making it a valuable feed ingredient to help pigs grow healthy and strong.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmei keeki, ni ji nɔ ni wa ni eshwɛɔ beni ajie mu lɛ kɛjɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Eyɛ protein kɛ hewalɛ babaoo Enɛ haa efeɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yeɔ ebuaa tsinabii ni amɛdaraa kɛ hewalɛ.

english: Spreading dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, keeps the soil cool under the hot sun, holds water in the soil longer so you water less, and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Ale jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ha nu ahi sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ Obaaha nu fioo. ni etsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: Why do my crops dry up quickly during dry spells even when I give them a little water every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nu fioo daa gbi moŋ.

english: Giving crops only a little light water leaves moisture near the surface, forcing roots to stay shallow where the sun easily dries them out; deep watering encourages roots to grow deep into the cool, moist soil.
ga: Kɛ́ aha tsei lɛ nu fioo pɛ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ abɛŋkɛ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ shishifãi lɛ afee nɔ ni mli ekwɔɔɔ yɛ hei ni hulu la lɛ haa egbiɔ oya lɛ. Nu ni mli kwɔ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: How do I know if my soil needs organic manure before I plant my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia organic fertilizer dani madu dumɔwui?

english: If your soil turns hard and cracked when dry, looks pale, or does not hold water well after rain, it lacks organic matter and will benefit greatly from well-rotted animal manure or compost.
ga: Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛji egbi, etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo ehiɛɛɛ nu mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ mli, ni ebaaná ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ lɛ he sɛɛ waa.

english: Why do my vegetable seeds fail to come up after I sow them directly into the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds usually fail to sprout if they are buried too deep in the soil, if the ground dries out completely after planting, or if ants and birds carry the seeds away before they can germinate.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ kwɛŋ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa beni adu lɛ sɛɛ Aloo kɛji ŋmeii kɛ okpoi wo dumɔwui lɛ kɛtee dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is missing key food from the soil, especially nitrogen. It can also happen when the soil stays too wet for too long, preventing the roots from breathing and taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii titri ko bɛ sũ lɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛye niyenii.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season. It also gives pests and diseases that love maize a permanent home to multiply in your soil.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ yaa nɔ ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Ehaa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni sumɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ hu naa shihilɛhe ni hiɔ shi daa koni amɛshwere yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die if I grow them in direct sunlight without shade plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni tsei ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are soft and sensitive to harsh heat. Without shade crops like plantains or tree canopies to protect them, the intense sun burns their foliage and dries up the moisture in their leaves.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛnuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ dumɔwui bibii loo tsei ahe tsɔi ni buɔ amɛhe lɛ bɛ lɛ, Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ agbi.

english: When crops grow too closely, their roots compete for the same soil food and water, and their leaves block sunlight from each other. This results in thin, weak plants that yield very little produce.
ga: Kɛ tsei dara ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋshii mli yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ baa.

english: Weeds are fast growers that act like thieves in your farm. They drink the ground water and absorb the fertilizers meant for your crops, leaving your crops hungry and stunted.
ga: Jwɛi ji jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛnuɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni amɛjieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa onibii lɛ. Shi oŋmɔshi nii lɛ hɔmɔ kɛ shweremɔ.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they get stressed by high afternoon heat, lack of water, or when there are no insects around to help move pollen between the blooms.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ shwane mli latsaa, nu ni bɛ, loo kɛ́ kooloi bibii bɛ amɛhe. Koni eye ebua ni ajie pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi ateŋ

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and nutrients from the parent plantain. Removing all but one or two strong suckers directs all the plant's energy into producing a large, healthy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tsofai krɛdɛɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ajie tso lɛ mli ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja eko loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, etsɔɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ koni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji ni he wa aba.

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips feeding on the undersides of leaves and spreading plant diseases. The feeding damages the leaf tissue, causing it to wrinkle.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛgbɛɔ tsei ahe helai amɛshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Niyenii fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji, ni ekɛ ŋmɔlɔ baa.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground during heavy rainy seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when rainwater sits in the soil for too long without draining away. Excess water suffocates root tissues and attracts microscopic fungi that destroy the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejeee kpo. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ amli fãji lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbalaa ŋmeii bibii ni fiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop and wilt during the afternoon heat even when the ground is moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: During extreme afternoon heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull water from the soil. The leaves wilt temporarily to protect themselves and usually recover once the sun cools down.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi kɛ́ hulu lɛ mli jɔ.

english: Why is water so important for my crops even if I plant good seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu he hiaa midumɔ nii kɛji midu dumɔwui kpakpai po lɛ?

english: Water carries essential nutrients from the soil directly into the plant's roots. Without enough water reaching the roots, crops cannot feed themselves or grow, no matter how good the seeds are.
ga: Nu hiɛɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛyaa tsei ashishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ bɛ lɛ Dumɔwui nyɛɛɛ akwɛ amɛhe loo amɛdara. Bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ hi ha

english: Will any crop I plant grow successfully if I make sure water reaches my farm?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ baaye omanye kɛji mikwɛ koni nu lɛ ayashɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Water is the single most critical factor for farming success. While crops also need sunlight and soil nutrients, ensuring reliable water reaching the land dramatically increases the yield and survival of almost any crop you plant.
ga: Nu ji nɔ kome pɛ ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ kɛha okwaayeli omanyeyeli. Eyɛ mli akɛ hulu la kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii lolo moŋ. Kɛ́ okwɛ koni nu atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nɔ ni miihe ashɛ tso fɛɛ tso ni oduɔ lɛ yibiiwoo kɛ eshihilɛ aya hiɛ waa.

english: Why do my crops wither even when the top of the soil looks wet after I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni edɔ kɛji mikɛ nu wo amɛnɔ sɛɛ moŋ?

english: Crops need water to soak deep down into the ground to reach the root zone. If water only wets the surface layer, the roots underneath remain dry and the crop cannot absorb moisture.
ga: Nu he miihia tsei koni ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni eshɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛji nu pɛ shwieɔ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ nɔ lɛ Shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ baakã he ahi shi ni amɛgbi ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ nu.

english: How can I keep moisture in my farm's soil for longer so my crops do not suffer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi miŋmɔ lɛ mli be babaoo koni mikafite miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Covering the soil around your crops with dried leaves, grass, or straw acts like a shade cover. It blocks direct sunlight from drying out the ground, helping the soil hold onto water much longer.
ga: Mulching ni akɛbaa gboi, jwɛi, loo jwɛi tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why are my crops growing smaller on land I have farmed for many years compared to new land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni midu nɔ afii babaoo lɛ nɔ fe shikpɔŋ hee nɔ lɛ?

english: Land that has been farmed continuously for a long time loses its natural nutrients and its ability to hold water. Over time, the soil becomes exhausted, making it harder for new crops to get the nourishment they need.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni atsuɔ nii yɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛ nyɛmɔ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛhiɛɔ nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Be ni be shwieɔ mli lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi, ni no haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei heei akɛ amɛaana niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ.

english: How can I revive my old, tired farmland so that my crops will yield well again?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ momo ni etɔ lɛ lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ koni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee babaoo ekoŋŋ?

english: You can rebuild old land by adding organic matter like animal manure, crop waste, or compost. These materials restore lost nutrients and improve the soil's capacity to hold water for future crops.
ga: Obaanyɛ oma shikpɔŋ momo ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Nibii nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni elaaje lɛ baa ekoŋŋ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɛɔ nu mli kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Can I successfully farm two different plots of land at the same time?
ga: Ani manyɛ matsu ŋmɔji srɔtoi enyɔ yɛ be kome mli?

english: Yes, you can work multiple plots successfully as long as you ensure proper soil preparation and a reliable water supply for both pieces of land.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ otsu shikpɔji babaoo ahe nii yɛ omanyeyeli mli. Shii abɔ ni obaakwɛ koni asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni nu ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ yɛ kɛha shikpɔji enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I adopt a new farming system instead of sticking only to traditional methods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ okwaayeli gbɛjianɔtoo hee atsu nii moŋ fe ni makɛ mihe akpɛtɛ blema gbɛi lɛ ahe kɛkɛ?

english: Improved farming systems offer better ways to direct water to your land, protect your soil health, and manage crops, allowing you to get bigger harvests from the same piece of land.
ga: Okwaayeli gbɛjianɔtoo ni etee hiɛ lɛ haa gbɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ nu baa oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Buu shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛnamɔ he ni okwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ Koni onyɛ okpa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: Can I plant and harvest crops during the dry season if I bring water to my land?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ni makpa ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli kɛji mikɛ nu ba mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, crops do not strictly depend on rainwater to grow. As long as you have a system to deliver water to your land, you can plant and harvest successfully at any time of the year.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔɔ nugbɔ nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃. Shii abɔ ni oyɔɔ gbɛjianɔtoo ni akɛ nu baa oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Obaanyɛ odu ni okpa nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: What is the best way to prepare my land before planting so water reaches my crop roots easily?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani aduɔ nii koni nu lɛ ashɛ mitsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe oya?

english: Loosening hard soil by tilling or making raised soil beds helps water sink deep into the earth where the roots grow, rather than running off the surface and going to waste.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ajieɔ lɛ kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nɔ ni awoɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni nu lɛ abote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ. Mohu ɔ, e hoɔ kɛ jeɔ nu ɔ hɛ mi nɛ e siɔ jã.

english: Maize plants roll their leaves inward during extreme heat as a survival trick to reduce surface area, trap moisture inside, and prevent water loss from the hot sun.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛ baai lɛ amli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli akɛ wala yiwalaheremɔ gbɛ koni amɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ shi. Ha ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli ni otsi nu ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ naa

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without producing any tomatoes during the heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Excessive hot weather stresses tomato plants, causing their flowers to dry up and fall off because the plant cannot successfully pollinate or support fruit development under high heat.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tomato tsei nyɛŋ afee pollination loo amɛye amɛbua aduawai lɛ adalɛ yɛ la ni tsoɔ waa shishi.

english: Why does my cassava grow very tall with big leaves but produce very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baai ni kɛlɛ waa, ni dara waa shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves and stems above ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa kɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ starch toɔ tso ɔ sisi fã nɛ ngɛ sisi ɔ mi.

english: Why do I need to plant my cassava on soil mounds instead of flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji anɔ moŋ fe hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Mounds create loose, aerated soil that makes it easier for cassava roots to swell into large tubers while allowing heavy rainwater to drain away so the roots do not rot.
ga: Gɔŋ ko feɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ baafu ni amɛtsɔ ŋmei wuji. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha nugbɔ nu ni nɛɔ waa lɛ atsɔ mli koni shishifãi lɛ akafite.

english: Why do my pepper seeds take so long to come up when I bury them deep in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛ́ mifu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Pepper seeds have limited energy stored inside; if buried too deep, the young sprout exhausts its energy trying to push through the heavy soil before reaching sunlight.
ga: Pepper dumɔwui lɛ bɛ hewalɛ babaoo yɛ amɛmli. Kɛji akɛ afu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, tsei bibii lɛ ahewalɛ baaho kɛtsɔ sũ lɛ mli ni amɛtsiɔ waa dani amɛshɛɔ hulu la lɛ he lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is starving for nitrogen, an essential plant nutrient, or that excessive water in the soil is suffocating the roots and stopping them from absorbing food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei Aloo nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni no haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa niyenii ni haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up on the tree during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives and spreads rapidly when rain leaves standing water droplets on the cocoa pods for long periods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni daa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛji nugbɔ nɛ, ni no haa nu shwieɔ shi yɛ kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why are large holes suddenly appearing across my cabbage leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bulɛi wuji eba trukaa yɛ mi-cabbage baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Caterpillars and armyworms feed aggressively on fresh foliage, chewing through the leaves quickly if they are not spotted and managed early in the growing season.
ga: Kplukai kɛ ŋmeii yeɔ baai heei babaoo. Amɛyeɔ baai oya kɛji anaaa amɛ ni atsuuu he nii mra yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight; fast-growing plantains provide large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, shielding the cocoa with shade until it matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Okɛ shade aha kookoo lɛ he kɛyashi ebaada jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does planting beans alongside my maize help my maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Beans and legumes pull nitrogen from the air and naturally feed it into the soil, which acts as a free natural fertilizer for the neighboring maize crops.
ga: Beans kɛ legumes jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crops need to grow green and strong. Adding compost, animal manure, or a nitrogen fertilizer will help the maize regain its green color and grow healthy ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii tso titri ni he hiaa koni etsɔ eŋɔli ni ehe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛtoi hu ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I plant cowpeas together in the same field as my maize, and will it hurt my primary crop?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafee ekome kɛdu tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ? Ni ani ebaana miŋmɔ titri lɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, planting cowpeas alongside maize is very beneficial. Legumes like cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air into the soil, acting as natural fertilizer for your maize while giving you a second harvest from the same piece of land.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa o-corn lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa onáa kpamɔ ni ji enyɔ kɛjɛɔ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn easily under intense sunlight. Fast-growing plantains have wide leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa trees the shade and moist climate they need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or irregular watering. When temperatures are too high or water is scarce, the plant discards its flowers to save energy and protect its own survival.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu bɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala he.

english: How can I tell if my cassava tubers are fully grown and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmei lɛ shishifãi lɛ edara jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready 9 to 12 months after planting, when lower leaves turn yellow and drop off. You can also carefully dig up one test plant; if the tubers are thick, firm, and easy to break open, the rest of the farm is ready for harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsu kaa tso kome he nii. Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii lɛ mli tse, amɛhe wa ni amɛkuɔ oya lɛ, no lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Which leafy vegetables can I plant that will grow quickly and be ready for market within two months?
ga: Mɛɛ aduawai ni baai yɔɔ mli lɛ daa oya ni amɛfeɔ klalo kɛha jara yɛ nyɔji enyɔ mli?

english: Fast-growing vegetables like kontomire (cocoyam leaves), amaranth (aleefu), and spinach mature within 3 to 6 weeks. They require frequent watering but allow you to harvest and sell produce quickly.
ga: Aduawai ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ contomir (cacao baa), amaranth (alifoo) kɛ amaranth baakwɛ̃ yɛ otsii 3 kɛyashi 6 mli. Ehe miihia ni afɔ amɛ nu shii abɔ. Shi ehaa onyɛɔ okpaa onibii lɛ oya ni ohɔ̃ɔ.

english: Why is it important for me to tie my yam vines onto tall wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ makɛ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akpɛtɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to expose as many leaves to sunlight as possible. More sunlight helps the leaves make food, which flows down into the ground to build large, heavy yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni hulu la ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Hulu la babaoo yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. ni hoɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efeɔ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why should I heap my farm soil into mounds or ridges instead of planting on flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo miŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ mawo gɔji loo ŋshɔkei amli moŋ fe ni madu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Building mounds or ridges loosens the soil so roots can expand easily, and it protects topsoil from being washed away by heavy rains while ensuring good water drainage around plant roots.
ga: Gɔji loo ŋmeii ni afee lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi koni shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã oya. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ he koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akashwie nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu ni bɔleɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I prevent insects from eating up my harvested maize while it is stored in my room?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkaye ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ be mli ni akɛto mitsu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Insects thrive in damp grain, so you must dry your harvested maize in the sun until the seeds are hard and crack clean between your teeth. Storing dried grain in sealed, airtight bags prevents insects from entering and surviving.
ga: Kplukai shwereɔ yɛ dumɔwui ni mli efɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ baawa ni ŋmãa lɛ mli tse. Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui ni egbi lɛ wo kotoku ko ni akɛ vacuum ewo mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkabote mli ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes spoil so quickly on the long truck ride to markets in Takoradi or Accra?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ mitara lɔle mli kɛmiiya jara nɔ yɛ Takoradi loo Accra lɛ?

english: Tomatoes continue to breathe and produce heat after being picked. When tightly packed in hot, unventilated sacks or crates under the sun, heat builds up fast and causes the fruit to soften, bruise, and rot before arrival.
ga: Tomato yaa nɔ emuɔ ni ekɛ dɔlɛ baa beni ajie lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ akɛwo kotokui loo adekai ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu la shishi lɛ Dɔlɛ lɛ buaa ehe naa oya ni ehaa aduawai lɛ feɔ blɛoo, efoɔ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves that shade the young cocoa plants, keeping them cool and moist during their early stages.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni haa kookoo tso bibioo lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ha cacao tsei lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i yɛ shishijee mli.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin stalks and smaller cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii baa.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants turn yellow before the crop is mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani tso lɛ eda lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient plants need to produce chlorophyll and build strong green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji tso ni yɔɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni haa klorofil kɛ baai eŋɔli ni mli wa baa.

english: What does soil pH mean, and why does it matter for my farm?
ga: Mɛni shikpɔŋ pH tsɔɔ? Ni mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Soil pH indicates how acidic or alkaline your soil is. If the pH is outside a healthy range, your crops cannot draw up essential nutrients from the ground, even if fertilizer is present.
ga: Shikpɔŋ pH tsɔɔ bɔ ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ ji acidic loo alkaline. Kɛji pH lɛ je kpo yɛ he ni sa lɛ, Otsei lɛ nyɛŋ ajie niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ po.

english: Flowers often fall off when the plant experiences extreme heat or water stress, preventing proper pollination and fruiting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu he haomɔ. Etsiɔ pollination ni sa kɛ aduawai ni ato lɛ naa.

english: Why do weeds always seem to grow much faster than my main crops after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants with shallow root systems designed to grab surface water and sunlight faster than cultivated crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni afee koni amɛmɔmɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ hulu la oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I trim off extra branches from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Trimming unnecessary leafy stems helps the plant direct its energy and nutrients straight into developing bigger, healthier fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ yibii ni he ehiaaa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni etsɔɔ ehewalɛ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ mli koni ewo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upwards and stunted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni egbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Curled leaves are usually a sign of tiny pests like thrips or aphids feeding on the sap, which distorts leaf growth and slows down the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni yeɔ nu lɛ he okadi. Enɛ fiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ ni ehaa tso lɛ yaa hiɛ fioo.

english: Why do some of my bean seeds fail to sprout after I plant them in the wet ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-beans lɛ ekwɛɛɛ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Seeds can fail to sprout if the soil is overly saturated with water, causing the seed to rot before it can breathe and push roots out.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji nu babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ dani amɛmuɔ ni amɛtsiɔ shishifãi lɛ kɛjeɔ kpo.

english: How can I tell if my cassava crop has enough water during the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava tsei lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Cassava naturally drops some of its lower leaves to conserve water when it is dry, but if the main stem turns soft or leaves wilt completely, it needs additional moisture.
ga: Yucca shwieɔ eshishigbɛ baai lɛ ekomɛi yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛhiɛ nu mli kɛ́ egbi. Shi kɛji akɛ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ loo baai lɛ egbo lɛ, ehe miihia ni aná ŋmɔtɔ kroko.

english: Is it better to clear all the bush completely before I start planting my crops?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaajie jwɛi lɛ fɛɛ dani aje ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ shishi?

english: Clearing the land completely can actually destroy good topsoil and shade, wasting valuable land that could otherwise nourish your crops for many years.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ajieɔ lɛ kwraa lɛ baanyɛ afite shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ lɛ kɛ hulutsoo kpakpa diɛŋtsɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji shikpɔŋ ni jara wa ni kulɛ ebaanyɛ eye ebua oŋmɔshi nibii afii babaoo ni baa lɛ.

english: Why does my soil lose its strength so fast after I clear the farm plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ he waaa oya beni mijie miŋmɔ lɛ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When you clear too much vegetation, rain and hot sun strip away natural organic matter, making the land dry out and lose productivity much quicker.
ga: Kɛji ojie tsei babaoo lɛ Nugbɔ kɛ hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ jieɔ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbiɔ ni yibiiwoo lɛ laajeɔ oya kwraa.

english: How can I prepare my land for planting without wasting or ruining the soil?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ asaa shikpɔŋ kɛha dumɔ nii ni afiteee loo akpataaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he?

english: Avoid over-clearing or burning all trees and plants; clearing only what is necessary preserves soil moisture and nutrients so the land lasts longer.
ga: Tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsei kɛ tsei muu fɛɛ ni oootsi ohe fe nine loo oshã amɛ lɛ he. Nɔ ni he hiaa pɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaye abua ni sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ akahi shi bɔni afee ni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Should I plant all my crop seeds on the same day or spread the planting over time?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu midumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ yɛ gbi kome nɔ loo matsake midumɔwui lɛ amli yɛ be ni sa mli?

english: Planting continuously in batches ensures a steady supply of crops over time rather than having everything mature at once and risk going to waste.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ daa yɛ kui amli lɛ haa nibii ni aduɔ lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ahoo shikome ni okɛ ohe awo oshara mli akɛ ebaafite lɛ.

english: Can I get yields from the same crop field for several years without replanting every single season?
ga: Ani manyɛ mawo yibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afii babaoo ni ehe ehiaaa ni madu ekoŋŋ daa be mli?

english: Yes, if you manage the soil well and do not over-clear the land, certain long-term crops can continuously yield harvests for up to 5 or 6 years.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ okwɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛjieee mli tsɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ ekomɛi baanyɛ aha yibii ni yaa nɔ aahu kɛyashi afii 5 loo 6.

english: What happens to my farm if I do continuous sowing on my land?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji mitee nɔ midu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Continuous sowing allows you to make efficient use of the land so that mature crops keep yielding while younger ones grow, giving you continuous production.
ga: Kɛ́ oya nɔ odu nii lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni edara lɛ baaya nɔ awo yibii. yɛ be mli ni tsei bibii lɛ baakwɛ̃. Ehaa ofeɔ nii daa.

english: Is it good to grow other food crops on the same land where I have my cocoa trees?
ga: Niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi adumɔ Yɛ he ni miyɔɔ kookoo tsei lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ, ani ebaafee nɔ ni hi?

english: Growing other crops alongside cocoa protects the soil, provides shade and food, and helps you make full use of your farm's productivity.
ga: Nibii krokomɛi ni aduɔ Kɛfata kookoo he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Ha hulutsoo kɛ niyenii ni eye ebua bo ni okɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii atsu nii jogbaŋŋ

english: How do mixed crops on a cocoa farm help protect my land from going to waste?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfutuɔ nii yɛ kookoo ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ abu mishikpɔŋ lɛ he koni akashi lɛ?

english: Combining crops keeps ground cover healthy, preventing soil erosion and keeping the farm productive across multiple harvest cycles.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ. Tsi shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ naa ni oha ŋmɔ lɛ aya nɔ awo yibii yɛ kpamɔ bei babaoo lɛ amli fɛɛ.

english: What kind of assistance can I get from agriculture extension officers for my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ yelikɛbuamɔ manyɛ maná kɛjɛ okwaayeli he nitsumɔ he nitsulɔ ko dɛŋ kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Agricultural officers teach you best practices for land clearing, crop spacing, disease management, and getting high yields from mixed farms.
ga: Okwaafoi anitsulɔi lɛ baatsɔɔ nifeemɔi ni hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛbaatsu shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ahe nii. Tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ, helai ahe nitsumɔ, kɛ yibii babaoo ni jɛɔ ŋmɔji ni efutu mli lɛ amli

english: Who can I turn to if I am not sure how to manage cocoa mixed with other crops on my field?
ga: Namɔ manyɛ matswa lɛ? Ni kɛji akɛ mileee bɔ ni mafee matsu kookoo ni akɛfutu ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ahe nii hu? Ni miŋmɔ lɛ hu?

english: You can reach out to local agricultural extension officers (agric), who offer free guidance on managing mixed crop farms and protecting soil health.
ga: Obaanyɛ oya okwaayeli he nitsulɔ (Agriculture) ni baanyɛ aha bo ŋaa ni aheee nɔ ko yɛ ŋmɔji ni akɛfutuɔ nibii amli lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛnamɔ he bulɛ he.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant is starving for nutrients like nitrogen, or that the soil is too wet, which suffocates the roots and stops them from taking up food.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmã nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ kɛha niyenii, tamɔ nitrogen, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaaa amɛye nii.

english: This is caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly during rainy, humid weather when there is too much shade or poor airflow in the cocoa farm.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Beni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni ehiii yɛ kookoo ŋmɔ mli lɛ

english: What causes my cassava leaves to curl up, twist, and show yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni haa cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ?

english: Curled and twisted cassava leaves are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried and spread from plant to plant by tiny whiteflies that suck sap from the leaves.
ga: Kasava baai ni ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Whitefly ji nɔ ko ni hiɛɔ nibii ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ, ni ekɛ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: How can I tell if pests are eating my maize crop inside the central leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kooloi ni yeɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ miiye?

english: Pests like the Fall Armyworm leaves ragged holes in the leaves and wet, sawdust-like droppings inside the central funnel of the maize plant where they hide during the day.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ shiɔ baai ni mli ewo muji kɛ ŋmeii ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmeii tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli he ni amɛteeɔ amɛhe yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants keep falling off before turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛbatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat, dry soil, or when tiny insects attack the soft parts of the blossoms before fruit can form.
ga: Pepper tsei jieɔ fɔfɔii kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ latsaa ni naa wa he, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kɛji kooloi bibii ba tso lɛ nɔ. Tutua fɔfɔi lɛ fãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ dani aduawai lɛ aba.

english: Tomato plants can wilt in wet soil because of bacterial wilt or root rot, where invisible germs block the plant's internal tubes so water cannot travel up to the leaves.
ga: Tomato tsei baanyɛ agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ yɛ bacteria wilt loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ hewɔ. he ni helai ni anaaa lɛ tsiɔ tso lɛ mli tsɔnei lɛ anaa lɛ. Nu nyɛŋ aya baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow split open or misshapen under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔji lɛ mli egbala loo efite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Yam tubers split or deform when the soil is too hard and rocky, or when a dry period is suddenly followed by heavy rain, causing the tuber to swell too quickly.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baagbala loo amɛbaafite kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni eyɛ tɛi. aloo kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa nyiɛ sɛɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli ni eha yitso lɛ fũu oya tsɔ

english: When crops are planted too close together, they compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, which makes them grow tall and weak with small harvests.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ.

english: Why do my heavy plantain trees fall over so easily after a light wind or rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui ni tsii lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ loo nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees fall over when tiny pests like nematodes or banana weevils eat away their underground roots, leaving the plant without a strong grip in the soil.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji kooloi bibii tamɔ nematodes loo banana ŋmeii ye amɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, tsei lɛ nyɛŋ amɔ sũ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is my maize staying very short while a weed with pinkish flowers grows near its roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ feɔ kuku nɛkɛ yɛ be mli ni jwɛi ni fɔfɔii yɔɔ mli lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: That weed is Striga, a parasitic weed that attaches its own roots directly to the maize root to steal water and food, causing the maize to remain weak and stunted.
ga: Nakai jwɛi lɛ ji Striga, ni ji jwɛi ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni kɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ eshishifãi lɛ kpãa ŋmãa shishifãi ahe tɛ̃ɛ koni eju nu kɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ yaa nɔ egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds and fallen, rotten pods from under my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛ ŋmeii ni egboi ni shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: The ground under your trees is where they feed and live. Leaving rotten pods and weeds on the soil creates a dirty environment where fungal diseases like black pod disease grow and easily infect your healthy trees.
ga: He ni otsei lɛ yɔɔ lɛ ji he ni amɛyeɔ nii yɛ ni amɛhiɔ. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii kɛ jwɛi ni egboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa shihilɛ lɛ feɔ muji. Biɛ ji he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai, tamɔ black pod hela lɛ daa yɛ ni amɛyeɔ otsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ oya.

english: Why do my tomato plants keep getting sick even after I spray them with disease medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ yaa nɔ hela mɔɔ amɛ lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofa lɛ tsu nii moŋ.

english: Spraying medicine on tomato plants won't fully stop sickness if the ground around them is kept dirty with infected leaves and old plant waste. You must clean up diseased debris from the soil so the medicine can work properly.
ga: Tomato tsei ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ haaa hela lɛ akpa kwraa. Kɛji shikpɔŋ ni bɔle Tomato tsei lɛ ahe lɛ mli ewo muji kɛ baai ni hela emɔ amɛ kɛ tsei momo ni efite lɛ. Esa akɛ otsumɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni tsofa lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I cut off yellow and spotted leaves from my cassava plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ mi-cassava tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Diseased leaves act like a breeding ground for infections. Removing them keeps the plant's immediate environment clean and stops pests or viruses from spreading to the healthy leaves.
ga: Baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ he ni helai fɔɔ yɛ. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ he lɛ he atse ni ebaatsi tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize burning after I applied crop medicine to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ shãa beni mikɛ tso tsofa etsu nii yɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Applying too much crop medicine or spraying during the hottest part of the day can scorch maize leaves. Medicine must be measured carefully and applied during cool morning or evening hours.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii babaoo loo akɛshwie nɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha ŋmãa baa lɛ ashã. Esa akɛ asusu tsofa lɛ he jogbaŋŋ ni akɛwo mɔ he yɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ miitso.

english: Is it safe to spray pest medicine on my vegetables right before harvesting them for market?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ makɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ ashwie mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ dani makpã amɛ koni mahɔ̃ɔ?

english: No, crop medicines need time to wash out and break down inside the plant. Harvesting too soon after spraying leaves dangerous chemical residues that can make consumers sick.
ga: Dabi, tsofai ni akɛ tsofai tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ heɔ be dani ejieɔ ehe ni efiteɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akpa tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara ni baanyɛ aha mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ aná hela lɛ sɛɛ mra tsɔ yɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme sun heat, lack of soil moisture, or nutrient shortages in their root area.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛ kpe nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ hulu la ni naa wa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shishifã lɛ he lɛ

english: Why do my cowpea leaves fold up tightly during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ afolɔ tsina ŋmeii ahe tsei amli shiŋŋ yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas fold their leaves to reduce the surface area exposed to direct sunlight. This is a natural defense mechanism to save water and keep cool until the sun goes down.
ga: Cowpea shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shi. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ nu he ni ehaa hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: Why do my plantain suckers drop leaves and turn yellow during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have large leaves that lose water fast. When the soil becomes dry, the plant naturally drops its lower leaves to conserve water and protect its core stems.
ga: Plantains yɛ baai wuji ni nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ gbi lɛ, tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ shwieɔ eshishi baai lɛ koni ekɛhiɛ nu mli ni ebu eshishigbɛ fã lɛ he.

english: Yams need loose, soft soil to expand easily. If the soil floor is hard or filled with stones, the growing tuber twists to push past obstacles in its environment.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni egbɛ eshwa mlɛo. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa loo tɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ Yitso ni miida lɛ tsɔɔ ehe koni ekɛtsi gbɛtsii nii ni eho ni yɔɔ eshihilɛhe lɛ.

english: Why does planting my cassava too close together make the roots stay very thin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ he tsɔ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo waa lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are crowded, their roots are competing for the exact same spot in the soil for food and water, leaving none of them with enough room to expand into thick tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná he kome yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛna niyenii kɛ nu. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei lɛ eko kwraa bɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eda ni etsɔ yitsei ni mli tse.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of a maize stalk usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen. Maize moves available nutrients to its new upper leaves first, leaving the older lower leaves to turn yellow and die off when nutrients in the soil run low.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Abɛi tsiɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi baa heei anɔ klɛŋklɛŋ. Ha baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii lɛ faaa.

english: How do groundnut plants produce nuts underground when their flowers bloom above the soil?
ga: Te afeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei tsei woɔ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni fɔfɔii lɛ fɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: After groundnut flowers are pollinated above ground, their stems bend downwards and push sharp pegs into the soil. Once beneath the dirt, these pegs expand into the groundnut pods.
ga: Beni atswa ŋmeii fɔfɔi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ lɛ, Amɛtso lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa shishi ni amɛshwieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ eshɛ shikpɔŋ shishi pɛ Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ yaa ŋwɛi kɛyaa ŋmei ŋmei lɛ mli.

english: Yam vines need support to climb high and spread their leaves wide toward the sun. Exposure to sunlight allows the leaves to make plenty of food, which gets stored underground to build larger yam tubers.
ga: Yelikɛbuamɔ he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛkwɔ kɛya shɔŋŋ ni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã babaoo kɛya hulu lɛ he. Hulu la ni tsoɔ lɛ haa baai lɛ woɔ niyenii babaoo. Akɛ enɛɛmɛi toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi koni akɛfee sweet potato ŋmeii wuji.

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that do not go deep into the earth. As the bunch grows heavy, the root network cannot hold the weight, which is why farmers must prop up the stem with bamboo or wooden forks.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Beni kuu lɛ da lɛ Shishifã lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ shwiili lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ okwaafoi lɛ kɛ ŋmei tsei loo tsei ni akɛfee ŋmei lɛ afi tso lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why are my pepper leaves curling upwards and looking small and wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ bibii ni amɛhe efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Curled and twisted pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies, or a virus they carry. The insects suck the juices from the leaves, causing them to deform and stunt the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai ni ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. loo helai ni amɛhiɛɔ lɛ Kplukai nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai amli Enɛ haa amɛfiteɔ ni etsĩɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ naa.

english: Why are the blossoms on my tomato plants falling off instead of turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ tomato lɛ?
