english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather is extremely hot or when the soil gets too dry. High temperatures prevent pollination from happening, so the plant sheds the flower instead of producing fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. He ni mli edɔ waa lɛ tsiɔ pollination naa. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii.

english: Excessive foliage with low pod yield often happens when the soil has too much nitrogen or fertilizer. Cowpeas naturally pull nitrogen from the air, so extra nitrogen makes them put energy into leaves instead of flowers and pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ahe tsei ni fa fe nine kɛ pod ni baa shi lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ. Cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, nitrogen ni yaa hiɛ lɛ haa amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ woɔ baai lɛ amli moŋ fe fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do young cocoa trees need to be planted next to plantain plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu kookoo tsei bibii yɛ dumɔwui ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under strong direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide broad shade canopy and moisture to protect young cocoa until it is strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ haa hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa.

english: How can I tell if my cassava is ready for harvesting without digging up the whole farm?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa ni atsaaa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Cassava shows it is mature when its leaves start turning yellow and dropping, and cracks begin to form in the soil around the base of the stem as the swelling roots push the dirt upward.
ga: Yucca jieɔ dalɛ kpo kɛ́ baai lɛ je shishi amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli ŋmeii bɔi feemɔ beni shishifãi ni efuu lɛ tsiɔ sũ lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why does lowland rice need to stay flooded with water during most of its growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ nu awo ŋmãa folo mli yɛ edalɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Lowland rice thrives in flooded conditions because its roots can handle low oxygen while water prevents weeds from growing and competing with the rice for space and nutrients.
ga: Omɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ yeɔ omanye yɛ shihilɛi ni nu afua yɔɔ mli lɛ amli ejaakɛ eshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ akpee kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ faaa lɛ naa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu tsiɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni ekɛ ŋmãa lɛ akaŋ koni amɛná he ko kɛ niyenii kpakpai.

english: Why do I need to wait two weeks after spraying crop medicine before I can harvest my crops for the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ otsii enyɔ beni mikɛ tsofa ko ni akɛtsaa tso lɛ eshwie shi dani manyɛ makpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛya jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Crop medicines and pesticides take time to break down and leave the plant. Waiting two weeks allows the chemical to wash out so the food becomes safe for people to eat without causing sickness.
ga: Tsofai kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ heɔ be dani amɛfiteɔ ni amɛshiɔ tso lɛ mli. Otsii enyɔ ni akɛmɛɔ lɛ haa tsofai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni niyenii lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni gbɔmɛi baanyɛ aye ni hela baaa amɛnɔ.

english: Why do my crop leaves get burned when I spray chemicals on them in the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa kɛ́ mikɛ tsofai shwie amɛnɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: In the hot afternoon heat, plants are stressed and liquid sprays evaporate too fast, leaving behind strong concentrated chemical residues that burn the green leaves.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli dɔɔ ni edɔ waa. Tso lɛ miihao ni nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ. Eshiɔ tsofa ko ni mli wa ni shãa baai eŋɔli lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow very quickly and have large leaves that act like living umbrellas, protecting the young cocoa until it gets strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and thin with very small cobs when I plant seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa beni mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close, the plants compete for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Because no single plant gets enough food, they stretch upwards for light but lack the energy to produce large cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli ejaakɛ tso ko bɛ ni naa niyenii ni fa No sɛɛ lɛ tsei lɛ shwereɔ koni amɛná la shi amɛbɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaafee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why should I place fertilizer near the roots in the soil instead of pouring it directly on the plant leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mikɛbaawo tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Plants drink water and take in food through their roots underground. Pouring fertilizer on leaves can burn them, while placing it near the roots allows the plant to safely soak up the nutrients.
ga: Tsei nuɔ nu ni amɛyeɔ niyenii kɛtsɔɔ amɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha baai lɛ ashã. Shi kɛji akɛ akɛwo tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni eŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why does my land produce less maize when I plant it on the exact same spot every year without resting the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo beni miduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi ni mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ejɔɔɔ mihe lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil without giving it time to recover, making the soil weak and hungry.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsa ehe. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni hɔmɔ yeɔ lɛ.

english: Heavy rain creates high humidity and moisture, which helps a tiny plant sickness called Black Pod disease spread quickly from pod to pod through water droplets.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ kɛ hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo baa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ tsei bibii ahe helai anaa. Ale lɛ akɛ black pod hela, ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ pod mli kɛyaa pod mli kɛtsɔɔ nu mli nu mli.

english: Why do small caterpillars attack the tender leaves of my young maize right after the first rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii tutuaa mi-baby corn lɛ baai bibii lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Pest eggs hiding in the soil hatch as soon as the rains begin, and the young caterpillars target fresh maize shoots because the leaves are soft, sweet, and easy to eat.
ga: Pest wuji ni akɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baafɔ kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ pɛ. Ni ŋmeii bibii lɛ kwɛɔ ŋmãa tsei heei anɔ ejaakɛ baai lɛ ji bibii, amɛhe ŋɔɔ ni amɛyeɔ mlɛo.

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves in dry weather to conserve water and protect themselves from drying out; once the rains return, they will grow fresh leaves and keep growing.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni nu egbi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi. Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ, ebaana baai heei ni ebaaya nɔ eda.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster than my crop seeds after a rain shower?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe midumɔwui lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild native plants that are naturally stronger and better adapted to the local climate, so they can drink water and grow faster than cultivated crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji maŋ tsei ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ni amɛhe wa ni amɛnyɛɔ amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ, no hewɔ lɛ jwɛi baanyɛ anu nu ni amɛdara oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food crops use to stay green. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the soil feed the plant so the leaves stay healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn tso lɛ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni eha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, baai lɛ yɛ hewalɛ kpakpa.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts or cowpeas makes my soil richer for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei dumɔ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nii babaoo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas have small bumps on their roots filled with friendly bacteria that trap nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil, natural fertilizer for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni helai ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ eyi mli obɔ ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Eji adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so plant roots can drink it in. In dry soil, concentrated fertilizer sits around the roots and can actually burn them, causing the plant to wither.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ koni tso shishifãi lɛ anu. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi. shishifãi ni ebaanyɛ eshã diɛŋtsɛ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tso lɛ ni egboɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight because their tender leaves burn and dry out easily. Leaving shade trees or planting plantains keeps the soil moist and creates a cool environment for young cocoa to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ shãa oya ni amɛgbiɔ. Kɛ́ oshi tsei ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ loo plantains ni adu lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i, ni ebaaha shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ aba koni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahi shi.

english: Curled leaves are usually a sign of tiny insects like aphids or thrips hiding under the leaves and sucking out the plant sap, while spreading viruses that distort normal leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji koolooi bibii, tamɔ aphids loo thrips, ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛmiinu tso lɛ mli nu lɛ he okadi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, egbɛɔ hela ko ni fiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ ni sa lɛ eshwaa.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster and stronger on my farm than the crops I actually planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni miduɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally built to survive poor soil, dry weather, and pests. Because they are so tough, they steal water, light, and soil food away from your crops very quickly if you do not clear them early.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni abɔ amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ. kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui Ejaakɛ amɛhe wa waa. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛjuɔ nu, kane, kɛ sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli oya kɛji ojieee amɛ mra.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot inside the ground when heavy rains flood my field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyiɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay alive. When heavy rain leaves standing water for too long, the roots drown from lack of air, allowing rot-causing organisms in the wet mud to attack the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Ehaa bɔɔ nii ni miifite ni yɔɔ muji ni mli efɔ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa yitso lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without turning into actual tomatoes during very hot dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee anɔkwa tomato yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: When the air is extremely hot and dry, tomato plants get stressed and cannot pollinate their flowers properly. To save water, the plant drops its flowers instead of spending energy to grow fruits.
ga: Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ Tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni akɛ nu akafite Tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔii yɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛduɔ aduawai lɛ najiaŋ.

english: When crops are crowded, their roots and leaves compete fiercely with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Because no single plant gets enough food, they all produce smaller fruits or ears.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tso ko bɛ ni naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. No hewɔ lɛ tsei fɛɛ woɔ yibii bibii loo toi.

english: Yam leaves need full sunlight to produce the food that builds large tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground away from diseases and spreads them out to catch maximum sunlight.
ga: Hulu la ni fa babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni feɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ tsei ahe tsei lɛ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, kɛjɛɔ helai ahe, ni egbɛɔ eshwaa koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plants lack nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to stay green and grow fast. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara oya. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that easily burn under direct sunshine. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing necessary shade and cooling moisture until the cocoa plants grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa kɛ hulutsoo ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ.

english: When seeds are planted too close together in one hole, the plants fight each other for water, soil nutrients, and sunlight. This makes all the stalks thin and weak, resulting in small cobs with very few grains.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ Tsei baatswa amɛhe adafi koni amɛná nu. niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ amɛteŋ Enɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa anáa ŋmei bibioo ko. ni eyɛ dumɔwui fioo ko pɛ

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets extremely hot or when the soil dries out completely. Heat stress prevents the flowers from forming fruit, so the plant drops them to save water and energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Dɔlɛ tsiɔ fɔfɔi anaa koni amɛkawo yibii. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ nu koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Pepper plants curl their leaves in intense heat to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, which stops water from evaporating too quickly from the plant. Once the sun goes down and temperature drops, the leaves usually open back up.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa mli koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ baaha nu lɛ atsɔ tso lɛ mli oya tsɔ. Kɛ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi ni hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi lɛ Bei pii lɛ baai lɛ gbeleɔ amɛhe ekoŋŋ kɛyaa ŋwɛi.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are mature enough to dig up from the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ atsa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves on the stem turn yellow and drop off, and the ground around the base of the stem begins to crack as the swelling tubers push the soil upward.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni ŋmei ni efuu lɛ tsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why is it good for my soil if I plant cowpeas or beans alongside my main crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas are special plants that pull nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots. This leaves natural fertilizer in the ground that helps neighboring crops grow better.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii eshwɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so slowly even when I plant on time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ daa blɛoo nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ yɛ be naa moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are fast-growing plants that steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight directly from your crops. When weeds surround your plants, your crops starve because the weeds take the nutrients first.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni daa oya ni juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Beni jwɛi ebɔle otsei lɛ ahe lɛ Hɔmɔ baaye oŋmɔshi nibii ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ baaye niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Why are there ragged holes appearing in the middle whorl of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Holes in the center whorl of corn are typically caused by caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm. They crawl into the tight leaf funnel during the day to feed on the tender young leaves inside.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ feɔ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ. Amɛfoɔ amɛhe kɛyaa baai ni mli wa lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛye baai bibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why should I wait for the rains to fall consistently before I sow my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa dani madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: If you plant after just one early rain, the soil can dry out quickly if the rain stops for a week. Dry soil will scorch the germinating seeds before their roots are deep enough to find water.
ga: Kɛji odu nii yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ mra shikome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbi oya kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa nɛmɔ otsi kome. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ baashã dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ dani shishifãi lɛ mli aba bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛna nu.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and dying off before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen in the soil. The plant naturally moves nutrients from its old bottom leaves to feed the young growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Tsei jieɔ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are the tiny young pods on my cocoa tree turning black and shriveling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii bibii lɛ No hewɔ lɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ etsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbo lɛ?

english: This is called cherelle wilt. It happens naturally when the cocoa tree drops extra young pods it cannot feed due to dry weather, lack of soil nutrients, or general plant stress.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ tsɛnsi ni egbo. Ebaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛ́ cacao tso lɛ shwie ŋmeii bibii babaoo, ni shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ hewɔ lɛ, amɛnyɛŋ amɛhi shi. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo tso lɛ nɔnyɛɛ fɛɛ

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when temperatures get too high or when they experience irregular watering. High heat prevents proper pollination, so the plant drops the unpollinated flowers.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baafɔ̃ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ejaaa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa naa. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔi ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why does my cassava produce huge green bushes above ground but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ yɛ jwɛi wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ani yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil makes cassava focus all its energy on growing tall stalks and thick leaves instead of sending energy down to build big starch-filled root tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ tsei ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni mli tse ni miida lɛ ahe nii. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ he wami kɛ yaa si konɛ e kɛ pee sisi agbohi nɛ a kɛ starch e hyi ɔ.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the juices from young leaves, or by viruses spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ

english: What is the difference between buying certified seeds and using seeds I saved from last year's harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ ahemɔ kɛ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ teŋ?

english: Certified seeds are specially bred and tested to resist diseases, grow uniformly, and produce higher yields, whereas saved seeds often lose their vigor and disease resistance over time.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ ni akaa amɛ akwɛɔ koni ana kɛji amɛnyɛŋ amɛye helai. Kwɛmɔ daa ni owo yibii babaoo Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ ahewalɛ kɛ helai ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the seedlings compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, causing all of them to grow tall, thin, and weak.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ, amɛhe waaa ni amɛhe waaa.

english: Why does my plantain stem die after giving me only one bunch of plantains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ gbo beni ekɛ ŋmei kome pɛ ha mi lɛ?

english: A plantain stem is designed to produce fruit only once. After fruiting, the main stem naturally dies so its underground root system can direct food and energy into the side shoots (suckers) for the next harvest.
ga: Afee plantain tsei lɛ koni amɛwo yibii shikome pɛ. Kɛ́ ewo yibii sɛɛ lɛ, tso titri lɛ gboɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ kɛya sɛɛgbɛ ŋmeii (shishifãi) ​​lɛ anɔ kɛha kpamɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Maize leaves curl up during hot afternoons as a defense mechanism to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, helping the plant conserve water and prevent drying out.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ he koni akɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he ni ehaaa amɛgbi.

english: Why do people advise me to plant cowpeas or beans on my field before planting maize the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani madu be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas are legumes that fix nitrogen from the air into the soil. Planting them first enriches the soil naturally, helping the next maize crop grow better with less fertilizer.
ga: Peas kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni saa nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ adu amɛ mra lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ye obua ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmãa fioo pɛ.

english: Why do plants grow so much better on fresh land that hasn't been farmed in a long time compared to old land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ hee ni atsuko nɔ be kakadaŋŋ nɔ kɛ akɛto shikpɔŋ momo he lɛ?

english: Unused or long-fallowed land has accumulated rich organic matter and nutrients from rotting leaves and natural decay over many years. Old, continuously farmed land has had its nutrients drained away by previous harvests and needs organic matter or fertilizer to rebuild its strength.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akɛtsuuu nii loo efee ŋmɔshi nii be kakadaŋŋ lɛ ebua nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo naa kɛjɛ baai ni egboi kɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni egboi amli yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli. Shikpɔŋ ni etsɛ ni aduɔ nii yɛ nɔ ni yaa nɔ lɛ yɛ niyenii mli nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa tsutsu lɛ amli. ni ehe miihia nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii koni ekɛtswa ehewalɛ ekoŋŋ

english: Why do my crops dry up faster on high, hilly ground than down in the valley during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ ni gɔji yɔɔ lɛ fe jɔɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Water naturally flows downhill due to gravity, so soil on hills and slopes loses its moisture very quickly. Valley soil collects that runoff water and stays damp longer, meaning hill crops need extra mulching with dry grass to keep the soil moist.
ga: Nu hoɔ kɛjɛɔ gɔŋ lɛ shishi yɛ hewalɛ ni tsiɔ nii kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hewɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, sũ ni yɔɔ gɔji kɛ gɔji anɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ baa shi oya. Jɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ buaa nu ni hoɔ lɛ naa ni ehiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi babaoo awo gɔŋ nɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How can I stop heavy rains from washing away my fertilizer and topsoil when I farm on sloped land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekashwie ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ lɛ nɔ beni mitsuɔ okwaayeli yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: When farming on a slope, plant your crop rows across the hill (along the contour lines) rather than up and down. This creates natural barriers that slow down rainwater, preventing it from carrying away your fertile soil and fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji ootsu okwaayeli yɛ gɔŋji lɛ anɔ Dumɔ tsei ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ yɛ gɔŋ lɛ shishi. (yɛ ŋshɔ lɛ naa) yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni aaadu kɛya ŋwɛi kɛ shikpɔŋ Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ko ni haa nugbɔ nu lɛ baa shi lɛ baa. Etsiɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ naa.

english: Why do weeds grow so fast and aggressively right after I clear fresh bush to start my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛfeɔ basabasa beni mijie sũ jwɛi lɛ amli pɛ koni mije okwaayeli shishi lɛ?

english: Weed seeds can lie sleeping under the shade of trees for years. Once you clear the trees and open the land, direct sunlight and rain hit the ground, waking up those dormant seeds and causing them all to sprout at once.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui baanyɛ akã tsei ashishi afii babaoo. Kɛ́ ojie tsei lɛ ni ogbele shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Hulu kɛ nugbɔ lɛ tswa shikpɔŋ lɛ. Eteɔ dumɔwui ni ewɔ lɛ shi ni ehaa amɛ fɛɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: If I am starting a brand new farm, why should I plant food crops like cassava or plantain before planting cash crops like cocoa?
ga: Kɛji mije ŋmɔ hee shishi Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu niyenii nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo plantain dani madu shika nibii tamɔ kookoo?

english: Fast-growing food crops provide vital shade and wind protection for young cocoa seedlings, which die under direct hot sun. They also give you food to eat and crops to sell while you wait a few years for the cocoa to mature.
ga: Niyenii tsei ni daa oya lɛ haa kookoo tsei bibii ni gboiɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ hebuu ni he hiaa waa. Amɛhaa bo niyenii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii hu ni ohɔ̃ɔ yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ afii fioo komɛi dani kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why are my crops growing very tall and thin with weak stems under big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida ni amɛmiiya shɔŋŋ ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ yɛ tsei wuji ashishi lɛ?

english: Plants need sunlight to produce energy and grow strong. When they are trapped under dense shade, they stretch unnaturally high trying to reach light, making them weak, tall, and poor at producing fruit or tubers.
ga: Tsei hia hulu la koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Beni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa lɛ shishi lɛ Amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa hei ni nɔ kwɔ ni jeee adebɔɔ nɔ yɛ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbɔɔ koni amɛshɛ la lɛ he lɛ mli. Enɛ haa amɛgbɔjɔɔ, amɛkwɛɔ, ni amɛwoɔ yibii loo ŋmeii ni ehiii.

english: Since my share of land is small, how can I grow different crops together on the same plot without them damaging each other?
ga: Ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni miyɔɔ lɛ faaa Te mafee tɛŋŋ madu ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni mifiteee amɛhe?

english: You can combine crops that use soil differently, such as tall corn with low-growing beans or groundnuts. The beans capture nitrogen from the air to enrich the soil, while the corn grows upward, allowing both crops to share the small space peacefully.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ tsei ni kɛ shikpɔji srɔtoi tsuɔ nii, tamɔ ŋmãa kakadaŋŋ afata ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ fioo lɛ he. Beans lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo. be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ daa lɛ Enɛ haa tsei enyɔ lɛ jaa he bibioo ko. yɛ toiŋjɔlɛ mli

english: Why do my crops get small and yellow if I plant the exact same crop on the same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Every crop pulls specific nutrients from the soil. Planting the same crop repeatedly empties out those specific nutrients completely and allows pests that love that crop to multiply in the soil. Changing crops every season lets the soil recover.
ga: Tsei fɛɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni oookwɛ shii abɔ lɛ Ebaafite nakai niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ kwraa. ni ehaa kooloi ni sumɔɔ tsei lɛ ayiɔ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ daa be lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ehe feɔ fɛo.

english: Why do wild animals from the surrounding bush attack my farm crops more than wild forest plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli kooloi ni jɛ koo ni ebɔle mi lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa miŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fe koo mli tsei lɛ?

english: Farm crops like maize, cassava, and young shoots are bred to be sweet, soft, and easy to digest compared to tough forest plants. Animals naturally seek out these easy food sources, so planting boundary barrier crops like vetiver grass or pepper trees around your farm edge can deter them.
ga: Akwɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa bibii koni amɛfee nɔ ni ŋɔɔ, ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛyeɔ oya kɛ akɛto koo mli tsei ni wa lɛ ahe. Bei pii lɛ, kooloi taoɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ mlɛo nɛɛ, no hewɔ lɛ husu naa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ vetiver jwɛi loo pepper tsei ni aduɔ yɛ Oŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ amɛnaa.

english: What happens to my crops when strong dry winds blow across an open farm, and how can I protect them?
ga: Mɛni baa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi tswa yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni agbele mli lɛ nɔ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe?

english: Strong dry winds strip moisture directly from plant leaves faster than roots can drink from the soil, causing leaves to curl and dry up. Planting a hedge of tall trees or shrubs along your farm boundaries breaks the wind and protects your crops.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni naa wa lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ. Tsei kakadaji loo tsei bibii ni ooodu yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ baaye abua ni etsĩ kɔɔyɔɔ naa ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: How does spraying chemical medicine on my crops actually protect them from insects?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsofai ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ kooloi ahe?

english: Crop medicine works either by killing insects on contact or by making the plant leaves toxic and unpalatable to pests, stopping them from destroying your harvest.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛtsɔ kooloi bibii ni kɛ amɛhe kpeɔ lɛ agbemɔ nɔ loo kɛtsɔ tsei ahe tsei ahe tsei ahe tsei ahe tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ nyaaa he lɛ nɔ. Kɛtsɔ amɛ ni oootsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite onibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Is it safe for me to spray liquid medicine on my crops in the middle of a hot afternoon?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ makɛ nu lɛ afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli?

english: It is better to avoid spraying during hot daylight hours because strong sunlight makes the chemical evaporate too quickly and can cause the liquid droplets on leaves to act like magnifying glasses, scorching your crop leaves.
ga: Tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ŋmɛlɛtswai amli lɛ he. Ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baaha tsofai lɛ atsɔ la oya tsɔ. Ni enɛ baanyɛ aha nu ni hoɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ afee tamɔ glase ni haa nɔ ko feɔ bibioo. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ baai lɛ ashã.

english: Will heavy rain wash away the medicine if it falls shortly after I spray my farm?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaho tsofa lɛ kɛji egbee ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ beni afɔse tsofa lɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, rain within a few hours of spraying can wash the chemical off the leaves before it has time to work or be absorbed, making the application ineffective.
ga: Hɛɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni afɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ afɔ tsofai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ahe dani amɛná be ni amɛtsu nii loo amɛŋɔ amɛhe. Ha ni akɛtsu nii lɛ akafee nɔ ni mɔɔ shi

english: Can I mix fertilizer liquid together with insect medicine in one tank to spray my crops at the same time?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu ni ji ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ afutu tanki kome mli koni mikɛshwie ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ be kome mli?

english: Some chemicals can be mixed to save time, but combining incompatible liquids can damage your crop leaves or ruin the effect of the medicine, so you must always confirm compatibility first.
ga: Abaanyɛ akɛ tsofai komɛi afutu mli koni akɛ be akafite. Shi nu ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee ni okɛfutuɔ lɛ baanyɛ afite otso lɛ baai lɛ loo efite bɔ ni tsofa lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ehaa lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ oma nɔ mi akɛ ekɛ ehe kpãa gbee klɛŋklɛŋ be fɛɛ be.

english: Leaves curl during intense heat to shrink their surface area exposed to the sun, which helps the crop cut down on water loss and prevent drying out.
ga: Ha oyitsɔi lɛ abɔle ehe yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli koni ekɛba he ni hulu lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aka nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni amɛkagbi.

english: Why do my crops look yellow and weak during extended dry sunlight periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛhe waaa yɛ hulu la ni mli egbi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Without enough soil moisture during dry periods, crops cannot absorb nutrients effectively through their roots, causing leaves to turn yellow and growth to stall.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nyɛŋ atsɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdalɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Why do insect pests seem to multiply and attack my crops more during hot daylight weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo babaoo ni amɛtutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Warm temperatures speed up the life cycle of many farm pests, causing them to reproduce faster while crops are weakened by heat stress.
ga: He ni mli edɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔ mli kooloi babaoo ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ashihilɛ yaa oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛfɔɔ oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii amli gbɔjɔɔ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ.

english: How does using a knapsack sprayer help my crops better than just pouring chemical liquid by hand?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ sɛɛ mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ fe tsofai ni akɛ niji shwieɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: A sprayer turns liquid into a fine mist that covers every part of the leaves evenly, protecting the crop completely without wasting expensive medicine.
ga: Nɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nu lɛ nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ feɔ afua kpakpa ni haa baa lɛ fã fɛɛ fã nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe kwraa ni efiteee tsofai ni jara wa.

english: How do crop leaves soak up liquid food or medicine when I spray them from above?
ga: Te tso lɛ baai lɛ baafee tɛŋŋ amɛŋɔ niyenii loo tsofa ni mli ewo nu lɛ kɛji mikɛ ŋwɛi shwie nɔ?

english: Crop leaves have microscopic openings on their surfaces called stomata that open up to absorb liquid droplets directly into the plant system.
ga: Tse baai lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ amɛhiɛ ni atsɛɔ amɛ stomata. ni gbeleɔ ehe koni ekɛ nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ awo tso lɛ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why is it important to spray both the top and underside of my crop leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afɔse tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ kɛ amɛshishi fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Many harmful insects and disease spores hide on the undersides of leaves to stay out of direct sunlight, so spraying underneath ensures complete protection for the crop.
ga: Kplukai babaoo ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi koni hulu la akashɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, shishigbɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ahebuu kwraa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is lacking nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to grow green and strong. It can also happen if the roots are flooded with too much water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji shishifãi lɛ yɛ nu babaoo tsɔ.

english: Yam is a vine that naturally wants to climb. Staking holds the leaves up towards the sunlight so they can make food, which helps the tuber growing underground get bigger.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni adebɔɔ miisumɔ ni ekwɔ nɔ. Hiɛ baai ni kwɛɔ hulu la lɛ hiɛ lɛ yɛ tso ko nɔ koni akɛhoo nii. Enɛ baaye abua bulb ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ni amɛdara.

english: Cassava is usually ready around 9 to 12 months after planting when the leaves near the bottom turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base starts to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ, beni baai ni bɛŋkɛ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when planted under open sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and cannot handle direct heat from the sun. Planting shade crops like plantains nearby gives them shade and protection while their roots grow deep.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo kɛ hebuu aba be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: Should I plant my crop seeds right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: It is safer to wait until the rains are regular. The first rain often trickles away, and if a dry spell follows, your planted seeds will dry out in the hot soil and die.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ bɔ ni sa. Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be. Ni kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ko nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ Dumɔwui ni adu lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: How can I tell if the soil on my farm has enough nutrients for crops to grow well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha tsei akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Good, healthy soil is usually dark in color, crumbles easily in your hand, holds moisture without turning to mud, and contains small animals like earthworms.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni hi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ fɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Efoɔ oya yɛ oniji amli Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni etsɔɔɔ muji Ni kooloi bibii tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii hu yɛ.

english: Watering early gives plants time to absorb moisture before the hot afternoon sun causes the water to evaporate quickly from the dry ground.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ mra Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náa be ni amɛkɛbaaŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani shwane hulu lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ.

english: Curled leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking the plant's juices, or a plant virus spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ tsei amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. loo tsei amli helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ

english: Flowers fall off when the plant is under stress, which is usually caused by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of proper nutrients in the soil.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ yɛ haomɔ mli. Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni sa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that are better adapted to steal nutrients, water, and sunlight from the ground before your farm crops can reach them.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa waa, ni amɛhe esa jogbaŋŋ ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baashɛ.

english: Yellow leaves at the base of maize plants usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen gives plants their deep green color and helps them grow strong, so adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen haa tsei lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni tso lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they are stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch can prevent this.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ebaanyɛ etsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies spreading a plant virus, or by severe heat stress. Protecting young plants and managing insects keeps the foliage healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli Tsei bibii ahe ni abuɔ kɛ kooloi bibii akwɛmɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch enough sunlight to feed the underground tubers. Staking also keeps the leaves off the wet ground, preventing leaf diseases and leading to bigger harvest yields.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni ená hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei akwɛ̃. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ tso helai anaa ni ehaa yibiiwoo babaoo baa.

english: Too many shoots, or suckers, compete with the main plantain stem for water and nutrients. Removing extra suckers leaves only the strongest shoot, ensuring the main plant yields a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei loo tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛ plantain tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ ashiɔ. Enɛ baaha tso titri lɛ aná ŋmei agbo ni tsii.

english: Why do my groundnut plants need soil heaped around their bases when they start flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mi-peanut tso lɛ abua muji naa yɛ eshishigbɛ he beni ebɔi fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Groundnut flowers produce small pegs that must grow downward into soft soil to form the nuts underground. Heaping loose soil around the base makes it easy for these pegs to bury themselves.
ga: Peanut fɔfɔi lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii. ni esa akɛ ekwɛ̃ ni etsɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ mli koni efee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Shishitoo lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa pin lɛ ni ekɛ ehe awo mli.

english: Why are my cabbage heads cracking open before they are big enough to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage yitsei lɛ miigba dani amɛdara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa lɛ?

english: Cabbage heads split when they absorb too much water quickly after a dry spell. The inside grows faster than the outer leaves can stretch, so maintaining regular, balanced watering prevents splitting.
ga: Kaabaji yitsei lɛ baatswa kɛji amɛmu nu babaoo oya yɛ be mli ni nu egbi lɛ sɛɛ. Baai ni yɔɔ mli lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ amɛhe. No hewɔ lɛ, nu ni oooha amɛ daa ni sa lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ akakumɔ.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in damp, shady conditions. Pruning shade branches to let air and sunlight in and removing rotten pods quickly helps stop the spread.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Fuŋɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni edɔ kɛ shade yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ ni afolɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la abote mli. Ni ŋmeii ni efite lɛ ni ajieɔ oya lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 to 12 months after planting, when the bottom leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the ground around the base of the stem begins to crack from expanding roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu. Kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi ni he ni ebɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ shishifãi lɛ amlilɛɛmɔ hewɔ lɛ.

english: Why are tiny holes appearing in the leaves and pods of my cowpea crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ejieɔ ehe kpo yɛ mi-cowpea lɛ baai kɛ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ.

english: Holes in cowpeas are caused by insect pests like pod borers or caterpillars eating the crop. Planting early in the season or using eco-friendly pest controls protects the leaves and pods.
ga: Buji ni yɔɔ cowpea mli lɛ jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ pod borers loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli. Kɛ́ adu nii yɛ be lɛ mli mra loo akɛ nibii ni fiteɔ shihilɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii ahe.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed for leaf growth, or that heavy rains have washed away the nutrients in the topsoil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni baai lɛ adara Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do people tell me that planting groundnuts together with my maize will help my soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ko miikɛɛ mi akɛ kɛ́ mikɛ mi-ŋmã lɛ du ŋmei lɛ, ebaaye ebua mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which means they have tiny root nodules that pull natural nitrogen food from the air into the dirt, helping feed the maize growing next to them.
ga: Peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛyɛ shishifãi bibii. ni gbalaa adebɔɔ mli nibii ni ji nitrogen lɛ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eye ebua ni eha ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Cocoa trees shed their flowers when they are stressed by prolonged dry heat, lack of soil moisture, or when tiny insects called mirids bite the delicate flower stalks.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛbote hulutsoo be ni mli egbi mli be kakadaŋŋ. ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Aloo kɛ́ kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ mirids lɛ ŋmɔ fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to stretch their leaves high up on sticks to catch direct sunlight, which gives the plant the energy it needs to swell and form big tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni esa akɛ amɛgbala amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ koni hulu la lɛ aba amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛfu ni efee bulbs agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting under the ground before I am ready to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot underground when the soil holds too much water for too long without draining, allowing fungal diseases to drown and rot the tuberous roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ hela ni haa mɔ shwieɔ nu mli kɛ tuber shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ baa.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating the inside leaf folds of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ amli baai lɛ?

english: Those are Fall Armyworms, a pest that likes to hide inside the tender funnel of maize plants during the day and chew up the leaves before they fully unfold.
ga: Amɛji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni sumɔɔ ni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo amli. ni ji ŋmãa tsei lɛ yɛ gbi lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ dani amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ kwraa.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by microscopic insects like mites or whiteflies sucking the leaf juices, or by viral diseases spread by those insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛŋ, ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nakai kooloi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli

english: How deep should I bury my maize seeds in the soil when planting during the major rains?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli?

english: Maize seeds should be planted about 3 to 5 centimeters deep—deep enough to get steady moisture and stay hidden from birds, but shallow enough for the young shoot to easily push up into the light.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ mli aaafee sɛntimitai 3 kɛyashi 5, ni mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be, ni akɛtee okpoi ahe. Shi ekɔɔɔ he eko bɔ ni sa ni ŋmeii bibii baanyɛ ashɛ amɛhe kɛya la lɛ mli mlɛo.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so thin and weak even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds act like thief plants that quickly steal light, root space, and soil fertilizer away from your main crops, leaving your plants starving even with water.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ tsei julɔi, amɛjuɔ la, shishifãi ahe gbɛ, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ onibii titrii lɛ amli oya. Ha hɔmɔ aye otsei lɛ kɛ nu po.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomato fruits turning black and squishy while still growing on the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo be mli ni amɛdaraa yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil, usually caused by irregular watering during hot dry periods.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni afɔɔɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why do my stored maize seeds fail to grow well after being kept in a hot room for several weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ beni akɛto tsu ko ni mli edɔ mli otsii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds are living things that weaken or die if exposed to high heat for too long. Storing seeds in a cool, dry, and shaded place protects their inner energy so they can sprout strongly when planted.
ga: Dumɔwui ji nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni gbɔjɔɔ loo amɛgboiɔ kɛji akɛ amɛwo la ni mli edɔ waa mli be kakadaŋŋ. Dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni egbi, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu dumɔwui lɛ amli hewalɛ he. Koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ waa kɛ́ adu.

english: How can I test if my stored crop seeds are still strong enough to plant in my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji dumɔwui ni ato lɛ yɛ hewalɛ lolo bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You can test seed strength by placing ten seeds in a moist cloth for a few days. If most of them sprout quickly with strong shoots, the seeds have maintained their vitality and are good for planting.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka bɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ ahe wa ha lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui 10 ni okɛaawo mama ni mli efɔ mli gbii fioo komɛi lɛ nɔ. Kɛji amɛteŋ mɛi babaoo kwɛ̃ oya ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii ni wa lɛ, Dumɔwui lɛ baahi shi ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha dumɔ.

english: Why is it harmful to plant my seeds right on top of the dry soil under direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds left on top of dry soil get too hot and lose their moisture rapidly, which destroys the delicate life inside them before they can take root in the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ baadɔ oya ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni yɔɔ dumɔwu lɛ mli lɛ dani ewoɔ shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: How long does it normally take for maize seeds to sprout after planting them in wet soil?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ beni adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize seeds typically take between 4 to 7 days to sprout when given enough moisture and mild warm soil. During this critical time, the seed relies entirely on its internal energy store to push out roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ heɔ aaafee gbii 4 kɛyashi 7 dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛji akɛ aha amɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ fioo. Yɛ be ni he hiaa waa nɛɛ mli lɛ, Dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ amɛmli hewalɛ jɛɛhei lɛ anɔ kwraa koni amɛtsi amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛje kpo.

english: Why do my young pepper seedlings dry up and die when left under direct sunshine all afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ shwane muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young seedlings are very fragile and cannot withstand extreme sun heat. Harsh sunlight weakens their soft tissues and dries out their roots before they become established.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ waaa waa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa. Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa fãji bibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ dani amɛfeɔ.

english: Why do extension officers recommend building a palm frond shade over nursery beds for cocoa or vegetables?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛ ŋmei tsei awo hulutsoo mli fe kookoo loo aduawai ŋmɔji lɛ?

english: A palm frond shade shields young seedlings from intense direct sunlight and high heat, keeping them cool and strong until they grow hardy enough to face full sunlight.
ga: Shade palm baai buɔ dumɔwui bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Ha ohe afee fɛ̃i ni ofee hewalɛ kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ baadara ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkɛ hulu la ni fa lɛ akpee.

english: Why do my tomato plants look weak and droop right after I move them from the nursery to the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Moving seedlings causes transplant shock because roots are suddenly exposed to stronger sun and wind. Watering them well and transplanting in the late afternoon protects them from heat stress while they settle.
ga: Dumɔwui ni tsiɔ amɛhe lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ babaoo baa shishifãi lɛ anɔ trukaa. Nu ni awoɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ baaye abua ni aka dɔlɛ he haomɔ aba be mli ni akwɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass (mulching) acts as a protective shield against heat. It keeps the soil cool and preserves water so root systems stay healthy and strong.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni tsiɔ dɔlɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu hiɔ shi koni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves of my cassava plants curl or droop during the hottest hours of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ŋmɛlɛtswai ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Plants curl their leaves in intense heat to reduce water loss and protect their inner tissues. It is a natural self-defense behavior to survive the hottest part of the day.
ga: Tso lɛ shwieɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa mli koni nu ni elaaje lɛ aba shi ni ebu fãji ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe. Eji adebɔɔ mli hebuu subaŋ koni anyɛ aye wala yɛ gbi lɛ mli latsaa fe fɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why is it bad for me to water my vegetables in the middle of the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ oooha aduawai nu yɛ shwane hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Watering during high heat causes water droplets on leaves to act like small magnifying glasses that burn the plant tissues, and much of the water evaporates before roots can absorb it.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ haa nu ni hoɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ tamɔ glase bibii ni haa nɔ ko feɔ bibioo. ni shãa tso lɛ mli fãji Ni nu lɛ fa ko baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ.

english: How can proper land preparation help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni asaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Preparing your land properly loosens hard soil, makes it easier for plant roots to spread out, and improves the soil's ability to hold moisture and nutrients so whatever crop you plant can thrive.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni asaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa mlɛo. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli nibii amli lɛ yaa hiɛ Bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: What can I do to make sure my poor farm land is ready for planting?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni miŋmɔ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ afee klalo kɛha dumɔ?

english: You can improve poor farm land by thoroughly digging up the soil to break hard ground, turning it over, and covering it with organic matter or soil covers to restore its fertility before planting.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha okwaayeli shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ aya hiɛ kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oootsu jogbaŋŋ koni okɛgbala shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli, ni oootsɔ mli, ni okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔtɔ aha nɔ koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii aba ekoŋŋ dani okɛdu lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it important to cover the soil around my planted crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the soil helps trap moisture in the ground, protects the soil surface from harsh heat, and keeps weeds down so your crops have a stable environment to grow well.
ga: Mulching yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mɔ̃ɔ. Ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa he. ni ojie jwɛi lɛ koni eha onibii lɛ aná shihilɛ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does cassava need deep, well-dug soil to give a good yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni atsa jogbaŋŋ he hiaa koni ewo yibii kpakpai lɛ?

english: Cassava develops its heavy tubers underground. Deeply dug, loose soil allows the cassava roots to expand freely and grow large tubers without being restricted by hard earth.
ga: Cassava woɔ ŋmeii ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ amɛhaa amɛhe ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii wuji ni shikpɔŋ ni wa tsiii amɛ gbɛ.

english: Can I plant cassava on a large scale on my piece of land?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei tsei wuji yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, cassava is a tough and resilient crop. With good soil preparation and proper plant spacing, you can plant hundreds of stems and achieve a very high total yield.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei ji tso ko ni wa ni enyɛɔ ehiɔ shi. Kɛ shikpɔŋ he saamɔ kpakpa kɛ sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ ni sa ni yɔɔ tsei ateŋ lɛ nɔ. Obaanyɛ okwɛ tsei ohai abɔ ni okɛ yibiiwoo fɛɛ ni fa babaoo aba.

english: Why do some farmers cover their planted cassava cuttings with dirt or mulch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ sũ loo ŋmɔtɔ haa amɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Covering planted cassava cuttings protects them from drying out in the intense sun, holds moisture around the stem, and helps the cutting sprout roots faster.
ga: Kɛ́ oha o-cassava niji lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ tso lɛ he ni eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi ni afo lɛ ni amɛdaraa oya.

english: Will cassava do well on land that has been prepared for general crops?
ga: Ani ŋmei baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni asaa he kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, cassava is very versatile. Once the land is loosened and well prepared, cassava will grow easily and yield well just like most other basic crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei ji nɔ ni yɔɔ srɔtoi waa. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ etse ni asaa he jogbaŋŋ Tamɔ shishijee ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi lɛ, ŋmei kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni ewoɔ yibii kpakpai.

english: Is it better to use hand tools or heavy machines to prepare my land?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ akɛ nine dɛŋdadei loo tsɔnei ni tsii baatsu nii kɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Both have their advantages; heavy machines help clear and turn large areas quickly, while hand tools give you precision when digging specific spots and managing individual crop rows.
ga: Enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ yɛ amɛsɛɛnamɔi. Nibii ni tsii yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ hei wuji ni etsɔɔ mli oya. Nakai beaŋ lɛ, nine nitsumɔ dadei yeɔ ebua bo ni ogboɔ hei pɔtɛɛ ni otsuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eko fɛɛ eko he nii pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: How does digging the soil by hand help cassava plants?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ niji atsa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ŋmei tso lɛ?

english: Digging by hand breaks up clods of earth right where the stem is planted, creating a soft pocket of soil that helps the young roots establish quickly.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ niji tsu nii lɛ, ebaagbala shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he ni adu tsei lɛ ahe lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi bibii lɛ ni amɛmaa shi oya.

english: How does good soil management lead to a much bigger harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ nɔkwɛmɔ kpakpa haa ŋmaa babaoo baa?

english: Good soil management preserves underground moisture and nutrients, giving every single plant the strength to grow to its full potential and produce abundant crop yields.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔkwɛmɔ kpakpa haa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ hiɔ shi. Enɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hewalɛ ni edaa kɛyashɛɔ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean the maize plant is missing nitrogen. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen deep into the soil where young roots cannot reach it, leaving the plant hungry.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aho nitrogen lɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi bibii nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ tsei lɛ.

english: Why do my cowpea crops grow so many big green leaves but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or manure, cowpeas put all their energy into growing foliage and stems instead of producing flowers and bean pods.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen loo ŋmeii babaoo lɛ Cowpeas kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii

english: What causes my cassava roots to stay thin and woody instead of swelling big and fleshy?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ tso yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛfuu ni amɛdara ni amɛfee loo?

english: Cassava tubers stay thin if the soil is packed too hard or if plants are spaced too closely together, forcing the roots to compete for space, air, and nutrients.
ga: Cassava ŋmeii lɛ baakã he ahi shi bibii kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛji tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ tsɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ shishifãi lɛ atswa akaŋ koni amɛná he ko, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why are my sweet potato tubers cracking open underground before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miigba yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Tubers split open when the weather changes suddenly from dry to very wet. The sudden flush of water makes the inside of the root grow faster than the skin can stretch.
ga: Bulb lɛ tswaa kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛtee hulutsoo be mli waa. Flush ni baa trukaa lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants keep falling off before producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when temperatures get too high or when soil water drops suddenly, as the plant tries to save energy to keep itself alive.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ. aloo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ gbee shi trukaa Enɛ ji akɛ, tomato tso lɛ miitao ni ekɛ hewalɛ ato koni ehi wala mli.

english: Why is my yam crop taking so long to sprout even after I planted it in moist soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ɔ eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ moŋ?

english: Yam seed tubers have a natural resting period called dormancy. Until this internal biological clock finishes resting, the tuber will not sprout no matter how much water is in the soil.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy. Kɛyashi nɛkɛ mligbɛ wala yibii ahe ŋmɛlɛtswaa nɛɛ baagbe hejɔɔmɔ naa. Bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni nu babaoo yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, bulb lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves scorch and dry up when I cut down all the large shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ beni mifoɔ mi-shade tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Large trees act as living umbrellas that protect young cocoa leaves from heat and keep the surrounding air and soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei wuji lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ shade ni buɔ kookoo baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ latsaa he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why does my main plantain tree take so long to bear fruit when I leave all the small shoots growing around its base?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwu titri lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii beni mikɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwieɔ lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishitoo lɛ he lɛ?

english: All offshoots attached to the same root system drink water and feed on the same nutrients. Leaving too many shoots starves the main stem, delaying flower and fruit production.
ga: Tso lɛ shishifãi fɛɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpɛtɛɔ shishifã kome he lɛ nuɔ nu ni amɛyeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ ashi tsei bibii babaoo yɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ hɔmɔ aye lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai afeemɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Curled leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies feeding on the sap and injecting viruses that disrupt normal plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛwoɔ helai ni tsiɔ tso lɛ dalɛ ni sa lɛ naa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa.

english: Why do weeds growing near my young citrus trees slow down the trees' growth so drastically?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-orange tso lɛ masɛi lɛ miiha tso lɛ dalɛ miiba shi waa lɛ?

english: Weed roots spread very fast near the surface and steal fertilizer and water before the deeper roots of young fruit trees can drink them up.
ga: Jwɛi shishifãi gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ nu lɛ hiɛ lɛ. ni amɛju ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu dani tso bibioo lɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ anu lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that dry out and burn easily in full sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving young cocoa plants the shade and soil moisture they need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa oya. Dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ ambrela ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ náa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do I have to lift and tie my yam vines onto tall wooden stakes instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miwo sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ ni mikɛfi tso kakadaŋŋ ko he lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha efo kɛho shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Yam vines need to reach high into the air to catch maximum sunlight, which the plant uses to make food for growing large tubers. Keeping leaves off the damp ground also prevents leaves from rotting and spreading fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni awo sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe babaoo. Akɛ tsei lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii kɛha bulb agboi ni akwɛ̃ɔ. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa amɛfite ni amɛkagbɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ amɛshwãa.

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, their roots fight each other for water and nutrients in the soil, and their leaves block sunlight from one another. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room and food to grow big, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. ni amɛbaai lɛ haa hulu la lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe nɔ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmei agbo ni mli wa.

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves is a clear sign that your maize plant lacks nitrogen, which is essential for leaf growth and green color. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer near the base of the plant will help restore its healthy green color.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni he hiaa kɛha baa lɛ adalɛ kɛ eŋɔli su Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he ni bɛŋkɛ shishigbɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eŋɔlii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help make my soil better for other crops next season?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and store it in tiny bumps on their roots. When the crop is harvested, those roots decay and leave rich nitrogen in the soil for future crops like maize or vegetables.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ amli kɛ́ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Nakai shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛshiɔ nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai.

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water settles around them because the roots cannot breathe in waterlogged soil. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nu ni ekã shi ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi nyɛɛɛ amu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking juices from the undersides of young leaves. Spraying the leaves with soapy water or neem oil controls these pests and allows healthy leaves to grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli edɔ loo neem fɔ shwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaakudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ni ebaaha baai lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster and bigger than my planted crops right after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛdaraa fe tsei ni midu lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that naturally adapt to local soil conditions and absorb water and fertilizer much faster than domestic crops. Clearing weeds early prevents them from stealing food, water, and sunlight from your planted crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo shikpɔŋ ni amɛyɔɔ mli lɛ mli. ni ekɛ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ shi oya kwraa fe shia tsei Ojie jwɛi lɛ mra Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛ tsei ni oduɔ lɛ amli.

english: Tomato flowers drop when weather temperatures get too hot or when the soil dries out completely during flowering. Watering your plants consistently at root level early in the morning helps protect the flowers so they can set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli. Nu ni oooha tsei lɛ daa yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe leebi lɛ baaye abua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves droop and look lifeless in the hot afternoon sun even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni wala bɛ mli yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: During hot afternoons, plants lose moisture through their leaves faster than their roots can suck up water from the soil. As long as the soil remains moist, the leaves will stand back up in the evening once temperatures cool down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei lɛ fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ Baai lɛ teɔ shi ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ.

english: Why do my young maize leaves turn yellow at the bottom instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shishigbɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves on maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil. Planting leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts in rotation puts natural nitrogen back into the soil to keep leaves green and strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ, ehaa adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eha baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Pruning cocoa trees allows sunlight and fresh air to reach the lower branches and trunk. This keeps the tree dry enough to prevent black pod disease while directing energy into growing bigger pods.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shɛɔ tsei lɛ aniji kɛ amɛshishigbɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ mli egbiɔ bɔ ni sa koni ekɛtsi pod lɛ naa ni efee ediŋŋ yɛ be mli ni ekɛ hewalɛ yaa podi wuji lɛ amli.

english: Why do my yam vines need to climb up tall wooden poles instead of spreading on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooogbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight on their leaves to make food that feeds the tuber underground. Staking lifts the leaves into the sun and keeps them off the wet soil where diseases easily spread.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii ni yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ. Staking haa hulu la shɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe, ni ehaaa sũ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, he ni helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop when the weather gets too hot or the soil gets too dry. Regular watering at the base and placing dry grass around the plant helps keep the soil cool and moist so fruits can form.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. Okɛ nu awo shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ daa ni okɛ jwɛi ni egbi abɔle he. Tso lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ bɔni afee ni aduawai aba.

english: Curling leaves on cassava are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava stems provided by extension services stops this sickness from reducing your harvest.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmei nɔ lɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Kɛ́ odu ŋmei tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ kɛtsɔ sɛɛkuu nitsumɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekpa hela nɛɛ koni ekaha okpamɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the leaves right inside the center of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms that attack the growing heart of the maize plant. Inspecting your farm early and applying recommended treatments into the leaf funnels destroys them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms ni tutuaa ŋmei tso lɛ tsui ni miida lɛ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii yɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ baafite amɛ dani amɛbaafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant peppers or tomatoes in the exact same spot on my land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo tomato yɛ he kome yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting crops from the same family in the same place every season allows soil-borne pests and diseases to build up and drains the specific food those plants need. Rotating them with maize or grain crops starves pests and protects the soil.
ga: Tsei ni jɛ weku kome mli ni akwɛɔ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ buaa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni nakai tsei lɛ taoɔ lɛ anaa ni amɛjieɔ amɛ kɛjɛɔ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmaa tsake ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ebaaha hɔmɔ aye kooloi ni yeɔ awui lɛ, ni ebaabu shikpɔŋ lɛ he.

english: Why should I cover the dirt around my crops with dry bush grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the dirt with dry grass—called mulching—acts like a blanket that stops the sun from drying out the ground, prevents weeds from popping up, and turns into soft soil food as it rots.
ga: Mulch ni egbi - ni atsɛɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching - tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Tsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaje kpo. ni ebafeɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ nɔ kɛ́ egbo

english: Why shouldn't I throw fertilizer right against the main stem of my young plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mitsei bibii lɛ ashishifã titri lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Fertilizer placed directly against a stem can burn the soft tissue of the plant just like hot water. Placing it a small distance away in a ring allows the roots to safely search for and drink the nutrients.
ga: Nyɔŋtsere ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ baanyɛ ashã tso lɛ fãji ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ, taakɛ nu ni mli edɔ lɛ hu baanyɛ ashã lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛwo ŋwɛi ŋta ni kɛ shishifãi lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ fioo lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛnaa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni amɛnuɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do extension officers advise planting cover crops like mucuna on land I am leaving to rest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa he, tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ, yɛ he ni amɛbaaya hejɔɔmɔ yɛ lɛ?

english: Cover crops act like a carpet that smothers tough weeds, holds moisture in the earth during dry weather, and enriches the soil with plant food so your next main crop will grow much faster.
ga: Tsei ni haa shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kapɛti ni shwieɔ jwɛi ni mli wa. Ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ. ni okɛ tsei aniyenii afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he No hewɔ lɛ onibii titri ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya kwraa.
