english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen fertilizer or are getting too much water in the soil. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or well-rotted manure helps them turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo amɛyɛ nu babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava plants curl and droop their leaves during peak sunshine to conserve water and protect themselves from burning. As long as they bounce back in the cooler evening, it is just their natural way of surviving hot weather.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbee shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ shãa he. Shii abɔ ni amɛbaaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ. Eji adebɔɔ gbɛ kɛkɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if the brown spots on my cocoa pods are caused by a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hela ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ ba?

english: Black pod disease starts as small, hard brown spots on cocoa pods that quickly spread to cover the whole pod, making it turn black and rot. If you see spots spreading rapidly during wet weather, it is a fungal disease that requires removing infected pods and spraying recommended fungicides.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ he bibioo ko. Su ni mli wa ni ji ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔ lɛ nɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya koni eha ŋmɔtɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ. Etsɔɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ. Kɛji ona ŋmeii ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ ŋmeii hela ko ni biɔ ni ajie ŋmeii ni emɔ mli lɛ ni akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ afɔ nɔ.

english: What will happen to my crops if I plant them very close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ amɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli?

english: If crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in tall, thin, weak plants that produce much smaller fruits or smaller harvests.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ tsei bibii kwraa loo ni woɔ yibii fioo lɛ baa.

english: Why are extension officers telling me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni extension agent lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mikɛ mi-corn lɛ adu tsina loo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts trap nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil. Planting them with maize naturally feeds the soil and helps your maize grow stronger without needing as much expensive chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa du ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ni eye ebua ŋmãa lɛ ni ehiɛ wa ni tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm because their roots take up the water, fertilizer, and sunlight meant for your crops. Removing weeds early gives your crops all the nourishment they need to grow quickly.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ gbalaa nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya.

english: What is eating small ragged holes in my young maize leaves and how does it hurt the plant?
ga: Buji bibii ni ayeɔ Mɛni yɔɔ mi gbekɛ ŋmãa baa lɛ nɔ? Ni te eyeɔ tsei awui ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Ragged holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by fall armyworm caterpillars. If they eat the central growing funnel of the plant, it stops the maize from growing new leaves and producing ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baa. Kɛ amɛye tso lɛ teŋgbɛ faa lɛ Abele lɛ baakpa baai heei kɛ toi ŋmɔmɔ.

english: Planting maize continuously on the same plot drains the soil of the same nutrients every year and allows soil pests to build up. Rotating your plot with beans or groundnuts gives the soil a rest and restores its fertility naturally.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ daa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hejɔɔmɔ ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii aba ekoŋŋ.

english: How does covering the soil around my vegetables with dried grass help them grow?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa?

english: Covering the soil with dried grass or leaves, called mulching, keeps the ground cool under the sun, holds moisture in the soil longer so you water less, and prevents weeds from sprouting.
ga: Mulching kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi Atsɛɔ lɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ hulu la lɛ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. koni okɛ nu akashwie nɔ fioo ni otsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from severe heat, dry soil, or a lack of plant food. Keeping the soil consistently moist and feeding the soil with compost helps the plant hold onto its flowers and turn them into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo tsei niyenii ni bɛ lɛ miipiŋ amɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i be fɛɛ be ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni emɔ fɔfɔii amli ni etsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain trees on the same farm with my young cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-kookoo bibioo lɛ?

english: Plantains grow quickly and have broad leaves that provide essential shade to protect young cocoa seedlings from harsh sunlight, while also keeping the soil moist and giving you early food and income.
ga: Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa koni abu kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ, ni ehaa niyenii kɛ shika baa oya.

english: Will plantains steal nutrients away from my cocoa plants if I plant them together?
ga: Ani plantains baaju niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ amli lɛ kɛji mikɛ amɛ wo he kome?

english: If you space them correctly, plantains and cocoa share the soil well. Plantains help retain soil moisture and shelter cocoa root systems without harming the growth of your cocoa trees.
ga: Kɛji oto he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ Plantains kɛ cocoa baajara shikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Plantains yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ebuɔ kookoo shishifãi lɛ ahe ni efiteee kookoo tso lɛ dalɛ.

english: When should I start cutting down the plantains on my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mabɔi plantains ŋmɔmɔ yɛ kookoo ŋmɔ mli?

english: Once your cocoa trees grow a thick canopy (usually around 3 to 5 years), they no longer need heavy shade, so you can gradually remove plantains to let more sunlight reach the mature cocoa.
ga: Kɛji akɛ cacao tso lɛ da ni etsɔ ŋmei ni mli tse (bei pii lɛ, yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 5 mli) lɛ, ehe ehiaaa ni ená hulutsoo ni tsii dɔŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, ojieɔ plantains lɛ fiofio koni hulu la babaoo ashɛ kookoo ni eda lɛ he.

english: Should I cut down all the big trees on my land before planting cocoa?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo tsei ni eda ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ dani madu kookoo?

english: No, you should keep some mature forest trees. Leaving a few permanent shade trees protects your cocoa from extreme heat stress, improves soil fertility through falling leaves, and helps the farm live longer.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ okwɛ koo mli tsei ni eda lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ oshi tsei fioo komɛi ni haa hulu tsoɔ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu o-cocoa lɛ he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa he. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yaa hiɛ kɛtsɔɔ baai ni egbee shi lɛ nɔ. ni eye ebua ŋmɔ lɛ ni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ

english: What happens to my land if I clear the bush by burning everything?
ga: Mɛni baaba mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ? Kɛji mijie jwɛi lɛ kɛtsɔ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni mishãa lɛ nɔ?

english: Burning destroys rich organic matter and nutrients in the soil, kills friendly soil organisms, and exposes your land to heavy rain erosion, making it harder for cocoa seedlings to grow.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Ekpãtãa bɔɔ nii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni kɛ amɛhe feɔ naanyo lɛ ahiɛ. ni ehaa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ.

english: Why do the elders in my village advise keeping specific forest trees when clearing land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ onukpai ni yɔɔ mi akrowa lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ abu koo mli tsei titri lɛ ahe kɛji ajieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Certain traditional trees provide good high-canopy shade, drop nutrient-rich leaves that feed the soil, and act as windbreaks without competing directly with cocoa roots for water.
ga: Kusum tsei komɛi haa ŋwɛi ŋta ni kɛlɛ. Ejieɔ baai ni niyenii babaoo yɔɔ mli ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ. ni etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ni tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ kookoo shishifãi lɛ abɔi nu he akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Young cocoa leaves burn easily under direct sunlight. Yellowing usually means the plants are getting too much sun exposure and urgently need overhead shade from plantains or shade trees.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miiná hulu la babaoo tsɔ. ni ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei bibii loo hulutsoo tsei amli oya

english: Why do my plantains grow so much faster than my cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ miida oya fe mi kokoo dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Plantains are fast-growing soft plants that feed heavily on fresh land nutrients, whereas cocoa is a woody tree crop that spends its first months slowly developing strong deep roots.
ga: Plantains ji tsei bibii ni daa oya ni yeɔ niyenii kpakpai babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, kookoo ji tso ko ni yeɔ afii babaoo ni ekɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ daa fiofio. Tsɔɔmɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa

english: How many years must I wait after clearing land and planting before my cocoa yields pods?
ga: Kɛ́ ojie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni odu kookoo lɛ, afii enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ ajie amɛhe kpo?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa varieties usually begin producing pods within 2 to 3 years after planting if they are properly shaded, weeded, and protected from pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ cocoa hybrids lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ kɛji akɛ awo amɛ hulutsoo jogbaŋŋ, ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ amɛmli, ni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: Why do I need specific permission from the chief or landowner before planting permanent tree crops like cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni maná hegbɛ pɔtɛɛ kɛjɛ maŋ onukpa loo shikpɔŋtsɛ lɛ dɛŋ dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ afii babaoo tamɔ kookoo lɛ?

english: Tree crops like cocoa occupy land for decades, which creates long-term land ownership claims under customary law, so landowners must agree beforehand to avoid future legal disputes.
ga: Tsoi ni ji jwɛi, tamɔ kookoo, eye shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii nyɔŋmai abɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mɔ dɛŋ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ kusum mla shishi lɛ baa. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ shikpɔŋtsɛmɛi lɛ akpɛlɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ hiɛ koni mla naa béi aba wɔsɛɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and turn brown when I clear all the big trees away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants do not like strong direct sunlight because their foliage is soft and easily scorched. Keeping shade crops like plantains or shade trees around them acts like an umbrella, keeping the soil moist and protecting the leaves while they are young.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ sumɔɔɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛshãa oya. Shade tsei tamɔ dumɔwui bibii loo shade tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ akwɛmɔ Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebu baai lɛ ahe be mli ni amɛdarako lɛ.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each maize plant enough space and food to grow strong stalks and big cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa he lɛ haa ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ ŋmãa ni mli wa kɛ ŋmãa wuji.

english: How can I tell that my cassava stems are mature and ready for harvesting without digging up the whole farm?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be mli ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa ni okɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava shows maturity above ground when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, leaving a bare stem with leaves mostly at the top, and the soil around the base starts to crack as the roots expand beneath.
ga: Yucca daa yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ. Shi tso ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni baai babaoo yɔɔ nɔ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni shishifãi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ eshishi lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by heat stress or tiny insects like whiteflies that suck sap from the leaves and spread viruses. Giving plants adequate water and managing sap-sucking pests keeps leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo loo kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ hela lɛ amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ tomato mli. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛhaa tsei kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni nuɔ nu lɛ akwɛmɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do I need to erect wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe hiaa mi kɛha mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ ni mikɛkwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Yam vines need to reach sunlight to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the hot ground, increases sunlight exposure, and prevents leaves from rotting due to wet soil.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking woɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni edɔ lɛ, ehaa hulu la lɛ yaa hiɛ, ni ehaa baa lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow from the leaf tips down the center line?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ amɛnaa kɛyashi amɛteŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting at the tips of older lower leaves is a clear sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed for lush green foliage and fast growth.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anaa lɛ ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji tso niyenii titri ni he hiaa kɛha tsei ahe tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ amɛdalɛ oya.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience extreme heat, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Consistent watering and balanced plant food help the flowers stay on and turn into fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa, nu bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo mli. Nu ni akɛhaa fɔfɔi lɛ daa kɛ tso niyenii ni sa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: Why did my crop leaves scorch and dry up after I poured fertilizer directly around the base of the plant stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ebɔle tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Placing chemical fertilizer directly against a stem burns the plant's skin and roots like hot salt. Fertilizer should always be applied in a ring a few inches away from the stem where root tips can absorb it safely.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaashã tso lɛ hewolo kɛ eshishifãi lɛ, tamɔ ŋoo ni mli edɔ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋwɛi ŋta ni kɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko pɛ. ni shishifã lɛ naa baanyɛ aŋɔ shweshweeshwe

english: Why do my maiden plantain suckers grow faster and fruit better than the broad-leafed suckers I transplant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi klɛŋklɛŋ plantain tsei lɛ dara oya ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai fe broadleaf tsei ni midu lɛ?

english: Narrow-leafed 'maiden' suckers rely on strong root reserves and adjust quickly after transplanting, while broad-leafed suckers lose water quickly through their leaves and suffer transplant shock.
ga: Maiden’ suckers ni baai lɛ mli tseee lɛ kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ shishifãi ni ji enyɔ ni mli wa lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe oya beni ajie amɛ awo mli lɛ sɛɛ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, broadleaf suckers lɛ, nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ, ni amɛyeɔ amanehulu yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ amɛhe lɛ he shoofeemɔ hewɔ.

english: Is it better for my vegetable crops if I water them early in the morning or during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha mi-aduawai lɛ kɛji mikɛ nu wo amɛmli leebi loo shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning allows crop roots to absorb moisture before the sun gets hot, whereas afternoon watering causes quick evaporation and can shock hot plant tissues.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ni amɛheɔ nu dani hulu lɛ tsoɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu ni akɛhaa yɛ shwane mli lɛ baaha hulutsoo aya oya, ni ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ mli fãji lɛ atsɔ la.

english: Leaves turn yellow when the maize plant lacks nitrogen, which is its main food for leafy growth. This often happens when the soil is worn out from continuous farming or when heavy rain washes nutrients away from the root zone.
ga: Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii titri ni haa baa lɛ daa Enɛ fɔɔ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ efite kɛjɛ okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ lɛ mli. aloo beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ jeɔ shishifã lɛ he lɛ

english: Why are my yam vines growing very bushy with lots of green leaves, but the tubers underground stay very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: When yams get too much nitrogen fertilizer or soil nutrients early on, the plant uses all its energy to grow green leaves and vines above ground instead of sending energy down to build big tubers underground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ sweet potatoes nine shɛ nitrogen fertilizer loo niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli mra lɛ, Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛduɔ baai eŋɔli kɛ wain tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsu kɛba shi koni ekɛfee bulbs agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: This leaf curling is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, a sickness spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. The disease stops the leaves from making food properly, which reduces your total harvest.
ga: Yucca mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Hela nɛɛ haaa baai lɛ afee niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baaha nɔ ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ fɛɛ aba shi.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomato fruits turning black and rotten before they can ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot. It happens when tomato plants cannot get enough calcium from the soil, usually caused by irregular watering where the soil gets very dry and then very wet.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛ́ tomato tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baagbi waa, ni ebaatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ waa.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers keep falling off the tree stems without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi ni etsɔɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when tiny pollinating insects like midges are missing, or when the tree is stressed by excessive heat, dry spells, or a lack of plant nutrients.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ laajeɔ kɛji ŋmeii bibii ni haa ŋmeii tamɔ midges lɛ laaje, loo kɛji dɔlɛ ni fe nine, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi, loo tso lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ ha tso lɛ haoɔ.

english: Why do my mature plantain trees fall over easily during small winds before the fruits mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain ni eda lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli wa waa mli lɛ? Dani aduawai lɛ baakwɛ̃?

english: Plantain trees fall easily when tiny worms in the soil called nematodes eat away their root system, or because the heavy fruit bunch makes the tree top-heavy without proper wooden stakes to support it.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛji ŋmeii bibii yɛ jɛmɛ. Yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ nematodes lɛ yeɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ. Aloo akɛni aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ haa tso lɛ tsii ni tsei ni sa ni akɛfiɔ esɛɛ lɛ bɛ hewɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Big shade trees act like natural umbrellas, protecting seedlings from heat and keeping moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋtayaai. Buu dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he ni oha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ shishifãi ni wa

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers during the dry season even when I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fɔ̃ɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ moŋ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when afternoon temperatures get extremely high. The plant drops its flowers to save energy and water until the heat reduces.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ shwane mli latsaa lɛ mli wa waa. Tsei baashɛ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he kɛyashi hulutsoo lɛ baa shi.

english: Why does my maize grow stronger and greener when I plant cowpeas alongside it in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ he wa ni efeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ midu tsina ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This acts as natural food for the nearby maize plants.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ.

english: Why are my corn seeds failing to sprout even after good rain fell on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Corn seeds may fail to germinate if they were planted too deep where air cannot reach them, if the soil became too waterlogged and rotted the seed, or if soil insects ate the seeds before they sprouted.
ga: Ekolɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ he tsɔ. Kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ egbo, Aloo kɛji kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ye dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper space allows its roots to spread wide and leaves to catch enough light to grow large, heavy cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ehaa eshishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa babaoo, ni ebaa lɛ hu naa la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: If I plant maize on the exact same plot of land every year, why do my yields keep dropping?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi Mɛni hewɔ nibii ni miwoɔ lɛ yaa nɔ ebaa shi lɛ?

english: Repeatedly planting the same crop drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests that feed on that crop to build up in the field. Rotating your crop with legumes like beans or groundnuts puts nitrogen back into the soil and breaks the pest cycle.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni yeɔ tsei lɛ ni amɛbua amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ atsakeɔ kɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii Enɛ baaha nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni efo ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops stay green longer during dry spells when I cover the soil around them with dry leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ? Beni mikɛ baai ni egbi haa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Covering the soil with plant waste or dry grass acts like a blanket that shades the ground from hot sun. It slows down water evaporation from the soil and keeps the plant roots cool and hydrated.
ga: Nibii ni akɛ tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi loo jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ atade, ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nu ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees burn and turn brown when I cut down all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ mifo tsei ni eda ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under intense, direct sunlight. Shade trees act like living umbrellas, protecting young cocoa from direct heat and preserving the soil moisture they need while their roots develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ feɔ amɛnii tamɔ ambrela ni hiɛ ka. Ebuɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ he. ni ekwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa lɛ nɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground when there is too much continuous rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni nugbɔ ni yaa nɔ babaoo nɛɔ lɛ?

english: When soil stays soaked with water for too long without draining, oxygen cannot reach the tubers. Without air in the soil, roots suffocate, and soil fungi thrive, causing the roots to decay.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ ewo nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu hoɔɔɔ. Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ yitso lɛ he. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ adara ni eha shishifãi lɛ agbo

english: Weeds are naturally adapted to local conditions and have hardy root systems that quickly suck up available water and nutrients. Farm crops need extra space, clean land, and care to compete with wild weeds.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ tsakeɔ ehe ehaa shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ, ni eyɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni baanyɛ aŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ oya. Okwaayeli mli nibii ni aduɔ lɛ biɔ he kroko ni akɛfata he. he ni he tse kɛ hiɛdɔɔ ni akɛaaye akaŋ kɛ koo mli jwɛi

english: Why do the certified seeds I buy from the store yield more food than seeds I save from my own harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni miheɔ yɛ shwapoi amli lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni mikɛtoɔ kɛjɛɔ mi diɛŋtsɛ mikpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are developed through agricultural research to resist local diseases, withstand weather changes, and produce uniform fruit. Saved seeds lose these strong characteristics over successive generations.
ga: Atsɔ okwaayeli mli niiamlitaomɔ nɔ afee dumɔwui ni awo he hewalɛ koni ekɛte shi ewo maŋ lɛ mli helai. Dumɔwui ni ahere amɛyiwala lɛ laajeɔ sui ni mli wa nɛɛ yɛ wɔsɛɛ yinɔi amli.

english: Why should I trim off extra side branches and lower leaves from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo mi-tomato tsei lɛ ahe niji ni yɔɔ sɛɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Trimming removes extra leaves that consume food without contributing to fruit production. It redirects the plant's energy and nutrients straight into making fewer, larger, and healthier tomatoes.
ga: Trimming jieɔ baai ni fa fe nine ni yeɔ nii ni wooo yibii lɛ. Etsɔɔ tsei lɛ ahewalɛ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛwo tomatoi fioo, ni dara, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why does applying fertilizer right before a heavy downpour seem to waste my effort?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eji mɔdɛŋbɔɔ ni afiteɔ lɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash away loose fertilizer off the topsoil before the crop roots can drink it in. Applying fertilizer when the soil is damp—rather than during severe storms—allows the nutrients to sink in safely.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni etse ehe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani tsei shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛbaatsu nii yɛ ahum ni naa wa mli. Enɛ baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii lɛ ashɛ he shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my young maize leaves and powdery dust inside the growing tip?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ egbɛ eshwa kɛ sũ yɛ amɛyitsei ni miida lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This is typically caused by caterpillar pests like the Fall Armyworm feeding inside the leaves. Detecting this early and applying targeted treatments prevents the worm from destroying the growing center of the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworm ni yeɔ baai lɛ. mra ni anaa Ni tsofai ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ nii lɛ baatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite hei ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa lɛ.

english: How long does it usually take for garden eggs to mature and start producing fruit?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be enyiɛ eheɔ dani abɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi?

english: Garden eggs typically take about three months from planting to reach maturity, with nursery preparation taking about a month and a half before transplanting into the field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, abɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ heɔ aaafee nyɔji etɛ kɛjɛ be mli ni aduɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Hesaamɔ kɛha gbekɛbii askul lɛ heɔ aaafee nyɔji kome kɛ fã dani aya ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why shouldn't I stop harvesting my vegetable crops after just two months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikpaa aduawai akpamɔ yɛ nyɔji enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ?

english: Vegetable crops like garden eggs continue to flower and set fruit beyond two months if properly watered and weeded, allowing you to harvest continuously into the third month to get maximum yield.
ga: Aduawai tsei, tamɔ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii baanyɛ aya nɔ afɔlɔ ni amɛwo yibii fe nyɔji enyɔ kɛji akɛ awo amɛ nu jogbaŋŋ ni ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ amɛmli. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ oyaa nɔ okpaa nii kɛyashiɔ nyɔŋ ni ji etɛ lɛ nɔ koni oná yibii babaoo.

english: How do I know if my crops are strong enough to keep producing fruit into a third month?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni ebaaya nɔ ewo yibii kɛyashi nyɔŋ ni ji etɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: If your soil remains moist and fertile, and your plants continue to show healthy green leaves and new flowers, the crop has the energy to maintain production for three months or longer.
ga: Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo ni eyɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. ni otso lɛ yaa nɔ ejieɔ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ fɔfɔi heei akpo. No sɛɛ lɛ, tso lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛbaatsu nii nyɔji etɛ loo nɔ ni fe nakai.

english: Can I plant garden eggs together in the same row with my okra?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ abɔɔ lɛ mli yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ okra lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: It is better to keep garden eggs separate from okra because okra grows tall quickly and casts heavy shade, which blocks sunlight from smaller vegetable plants and stunts their growth.
ga: Esa akɛ ajie abɔɔ mli ŋmeii kɛjɛ okra mli ejaakɛ okra daa oya ni enáa hulutsoo ni tsii. Enɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni jɛɔ tsei bibii amli lɛ naa, ni ehaa amɛdalɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Why do crops with fine seeds like garden eggs need to be separated from other leafy crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie tsei ni yɔɔ dumɔwui kpakpai, tamɔ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ kɛjɛ tsei krokomɛi ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Crops with fine seeds grow delicately at first and need dedicated space so faster-growing neighboring crops do not choke them out or steal vital soil nutrients.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ dumɔwui kpakpai lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ shishijee mli ni amɛbiɔ he ko pɔtɛɛ. Enɛ ji koni tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ ni daa oya lɛ akafite dumɔwui lɛ loo amɛkaju niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: What happens if I crowd different types of vegetable crops together on the same farm plot?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mibua aduawai srɔtoi anaa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Overcrowding forces crops to compete intensely for sunlight, air, and ground nutrients, resulting in smaller fruits and higher spread of pests between plants.
ga: Mɛi ni eyi obɔ lɛ nyɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa aduawai bibii kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei lɛ ateŋ.

english: Is it better for me to plant only garden eggs on my land or mix it with other crops?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu abɔɔ mli ŋmeii pɛ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi afutu mli?

english: Planting only one crop makes land management and harvesting easier, but spreading your land across a mix of crops protects your farm income if pests or low market prices affect one crop.
ga: Nibii kome ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo. Shi kɛ́ okɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu oŋmɔ mli shika ni onáa lɛ he. Kɛji tsɛŋemɔ helai loo jara ni baa shi lɛ saa ŋmɔshi nibii kome he lɛ,

english: How do I check if my piece of land is right for planting garden eggs?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha abɔɔ mli ŋmeii akwɛmɔ?

english: Garden eggs grow best in rich, loose soil that receives full sunlight and drains water easily without creating standing puddles after heavy rain.
ga: Abɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni hulu lɛ fɛɛ shɛɔ nɔ ni nu hoɔ oya ni ekɛ nugbɔshiimɔi efeee ŋmeii yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: How far in advance should I start my seed nursery before moving crops to the main field?
ga: Te esa akɛ maje dumɔwui ashishi dani mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii aya ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli kɛyashi tɛŋŋ?

english: You should start your nursery about one and a half months before main field planting so that the seeds turn into strong seedlings capable of surviving field conditions.
ga: Esa akɛ oje ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ shishi aaafee nyɔŋ kome kɛ fã dani odu yɛ shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ. Bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ afee dumɔwui ni he wa ni baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli.

english: Why do fine vegetable seeds perform better when started in a nursery rather than planted straight into the farm soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai dumɔwui wuji tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ aje shishi yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ

english: Small seeds planted directly into open fields can easily wash away with rain, get eaten by insects, or struggle against aggressive weeds before they can establish roots.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii ni adu yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ nugbɔ nɔ, kooloi aye amɛ, loo jwɛi ni baa shi lɛ baanyɛ awuu amɛshi dani amɛfee shishifãi.

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves and tender roots that cannot handle intense, direct heat. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to them creates a protective canopy that reduces sunburn and retains soil moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii ni nyɛɛɛ adamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ehaa hulutsoo be baa shi ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are tiny ragged holes appearing in the central leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Ragged holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by caterpillars such as the Fall Armyworm feeding inside the central whorl. Catching them early with appropriate biological or chemical treatments protects the growing point of the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni yeɔ nii yɛ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baa. Amɛmɔmɔ mra Kɛ akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni sa tsu nii lɛ, ebuɔ he ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa lɛ he.

english: This condition is known as blossom end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit as it grows. It usually happens when watering is irregular or during dry spells, preventing roots from taking up enough soil nutrients.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ebaa kɛ́ nu lɛ hoɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ loo yɛ be mli ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ anine shɛɛɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my hot pepper plants twisting and curling upward during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl upward either to conserve water during dry weather or because tiny sucking insects like mites or aphids are feeding on the underside of the leaves. Inspecting under the leaves helps determine if pest control is needed.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛhiɛ nu mli yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ. Aloo akɛni kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii baa ni amɛbayeɔ baai lɛ ashishi hewɔ. Kɛ́ akwɛ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni anaa kɛji ehe miihia ni akudɔ kooloi ni yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my corn turning pale yellow while the top leaves remain light green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ shishi baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing of lower leaves usually indicates a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is essential for leafy growth, and adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer restores healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia kɛha baa lɛ adalɛ. Ni kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains specific soil nutrients and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts refills nitrogen naturally and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Ebaaha nitrogen lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ebaaku tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ amli.

english: Does allowing wild weeds to grow between my crops actually reduce my final harvest size?
ga: Ani koo mli jwɛi ni miŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa minaagbee ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ nɔ baa shi diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, weeds act as competitors that steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients directly from your crops. Keeping your field weed-free allows your plants to absorb maximum food and produce higher yield.
ga: Hɛɛ, jwɛi tsuɔ nii akɛ akaŋshilɔi ni juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ jwɛi bɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Multiple suckers growing together compete with the mother plant for food and water, leading to smaller fruit bunches. Pruning back excess suckers and keeping only two to three strong stems ensures larger, heavier plantain bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii babaoo ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he kome lɛ kɛ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ yeɔ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ. Enɛ haa aduawai bibii ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ ahe ni okɛ tsei 2-3 pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahi shi lɛ, ebaaha plantains lɛ afee wuji ni amɛhe afee mlɛo.

english: Why do I need to lift and tie my yam vines onto tall wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miwoɔ sweet potato wain tsei anɔ ni mikɛfiɔ tsei kakadaji ahe lɛ?

english: Staking exposes the maximum leaves of the yam vine to sunlight, which fuels tuber growth underground. It also keeps leaves off damp soil, preventing fungal diseases from spreading across the farm.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato wain tso lɛ baai lɛ aná hulu la ni fe fɛɛ. Enɛ woɔ ŋmeii lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni baai lɛ akajɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Tsi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ anaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Cassava plants show maturity when lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, leaving a mostly bare stem. You may also notice the ground around the base of the plant cracking open as the expanding tubers push against the soil.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shɛɔ dalɛ he beni amɛshishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ. Trunk lɛ mli babaoo bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko. Ekolɛ obaana shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ohe lɛ. Tso lɛ shishigbɛ mli gbalaa beni ŋmei ni egbɛ eshwa lɛ tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do experienced farmers build small shade shelters over their nursery beds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ maa tsũi bibii lɛ? Gbekɛbii askul saatso lɛ nɔ?

english: Shade shelters protect fragile young sprouts from harsh direct sunlight. They keep the soil cool and prevent the intense heat from burning delicate seedlings.
ga: Shade he lɛ buɔ dumɔwui ni waaa lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni amɛtsiɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa naa koni ekashã dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: What local materials can I use around my farm to make a shade cover for my young plants?
ga: Mɛɛ maŋ lɛ mli nibii manyɛ mikɛtsu nii yɛ he fɛɛ he? Miŋmɔ lɛ koni mikɛwo mi tsei bibii lɛ ahe shade

english: You can easily construct simple shade shelters using cheap, locally available materials like palm fronds or leafy branches placed over a basic wooden frame.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee shĩa ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Abaanyɛ akɛ nibii ni jara waaa ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ tamɔ ŋmei tsei loo tsei niji ni yɔɔ baai ni akɛwoɔ tso ni yɔɔ mlɛo nɔ lɛ atsu nii yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ.

english: Can I use palm fronds to shield my nursery beds from strong sunlight?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmei tsei ahe baai abu mi-nursery saatso lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he?

english: Yes, palm fronds are ideal for building crop shelters because they block the intense rays of the sun while allowing enough air to flow through to keep the area cool.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ahe tsei hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii afeemɔ. Ejaakɛ etsĩɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ lɛ naa yɛ be mli ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa tsɔɔ mli koni ŋwɛi lɛ mli ajɔ.

english: Will building temporary shelters over my nursery increase the number of seedlings that survive?
ga: Ani be kukuoo mli shĩa ni mikɛbaatsu nii yɛ mi-nursery lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha dumɔwui ni baahi shi lɛ ayi afa?

english: Yes, protecting tender sprouts from heat damage during their first days of growth significantly increases their chances of survival before they are ready for the open field.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui bibii ni abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni fiteɔ amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ gbii ni amɛdaraa lɛ amli lɛ haa hegbɛ ni amɛyɔɔ akɛ amɛbaahi shi lɛ yaa hiɛ waa dani amɛfeɔ klalo kɛha ŋmɔ ni agbele naa lɛ.

english: Why do my newly sprouted seedlings turn dry and burnt when the afternoon sun is very strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛshãa yɛ shwane hulu ni naa wa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tiny seedlings that have just sprouted have very delicate skin and roots. When the sun beats down too intensely, it scorches their soft leaves and dries them out before they can establish.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ yɛ hewolo kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa. Kɛ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi waa lɛ Ebaai bibii lɛ hu shãa ni amɛgbiɔ dani amɛfeɔ.

english: At what stage of growth are my crops most easily damaged by sunlight?
ga: Mɛɛ dalɛ mli hulu la lɛ fiteɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ oya?

english: Crops are most vulnerable right when they are sprouting out of the soil. As they grow bigger, their stems and leaves toughen up to handle full direct sun.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ yɛ oshara mli fe fɛɛ kɛ́ amɛje kpo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ amɛdara lɛ Eshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ anyɛ ashɛ he.

english: Is intense bright sunlight good for tender young sprouts just coming out of the ground?
ga: Ani hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ sa kɛha tsei bibii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛkɛ?

english: No, while mature crops need plenty of sunlight to grow, intense direct sunlight can easily kill tender young sprouts by burning them and overheating the soil.
ga: Dabi, eyɛ mli akɛ tsei ni eda lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara moŋ. Shi hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ agbe dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ oya kɛtsɔ shãa kɛ sũ ni edɔ fe nine lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell if the sunlight on my farm is too harsh for my tiny sprouts?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hulu ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa tsɔ kɛha mi ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: If your young seedlings look scorched, wilted, or crispy shortly after coming up, the sun is beating down too hard on them and they require temporary shade.
ga: Kɛji akɛ odumɔwui lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛshã, amɛgboi, loo amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛje kpo lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hulu lɛ miigbee shi waa tsɔ ni ebiɔ ni hulu lɛ miiho yɛ be kukuoo mli.

english: Does hot ground affect how my crop seeds sprout and grow?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ saa midumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ kɛ amɛdalɛ he?

english: Yes, when the sun beats down heavily, it makes the ground too hot for delicate young roots. Keeping the soil cool allows sprouts to grow safely without burning.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, beni hulu lɛ nyɔ shi waa lɛ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli adɔ tsɔ kɛha shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Kɛ́ oha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛdara shweshweeshwe ni amɛshãaa.

english: How does putting a shade cover over my farm plot keep the soil cool?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ?

english: A shade cover acts like an umbrella that blocks direct sunlight from hitting the ground, preventing the sun from heating up the top layer of dirt where the seeds are growing.
ga: Hulu tsɔne tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela, ni etsĩɔ hulu la ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Enɛ ji koni hulu lɛ akaha muji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ mli adɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants need partial shade because direct sunlight burns their tender leaves and dries out soil moisture rapidly. Planting shade crops like plantains provides a protective canopy that keeps young cocoa cool and humid.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hulutsoo fioo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo bibii lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: Planting trees too closely causes them to compete underground for soil nutrients and water, and overhead for sunlight. This results in tall, thin, weak trees that produce very few pods instead of short, bushy, high-yielding trees.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ kɛbɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ mli lɛ he. ni amɛyeɔ hulu la he akaŋ Enɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ baa. Yɛ tso kuku najiaŋ Eyɛ ŋmɔ mli ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why are my healthy green cocoa pods suddenly turning dark black and rotting on the branch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ trukaa ni amɛgboi yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in wet, overly shaded, or humid conditions. Clearing weeds and trimming extra leaves allows sunlight and fresh air to dry out the canopy and reduce fungal growth.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. ni ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ mli lɛ Shade babaoo yɛ. aloo hulutsoo be yɛ Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa haa ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli gĩɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do some of my cocoa trees have swollen stems and pale yellow patterns on their leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei komɛi ashishifãi ni efuu kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: This is a key sign of Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus Disease, which is spread between trees by tiny insects called mealybugs. Because there is no chemical cure for the virus, infected trees must be removed so the disease does not spread to neighboring healthy trees.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi ko ni he hiaa waa ni tsɔɔ Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, ni ŋmeii bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei anɔ lɛ. Atsɛɔ no akɛ ŋmeii. Enɛ ji akɛ tsofa ko bɛ ni baanyɛ atsa hela lɛ. Esa akɛ ajie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ koni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: What is causing small black spots and dry patches on my young cocoa shoots and pods?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmeii diji bibii lɛ baa? Kɛ hei ni egbi ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ kɛ mi-cocoa tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: These spots are typically caused by mirid insects (capsids) that pierce the plant skin to suck out sap. Their bites inject toxic saliva that kills the surrounding plant tissue, damaging new growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii babaoo (capsids) ni tsɔɔ tso lɛ hewolo mli koni amɛmu nu lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ baa. Amɛ ŋmei lɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni fiteɔ tso lɛ mli fãji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ woɔ mli. ni efiteɔ dalɛ hee.

english: Pruning removes weak, crowded, or unproductive branches so the tree directs its energy and nutrients into flower production and healthy pod development rather than growing unnecessary foliage.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ niji ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni mli ewo wu, loo ni tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookwɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ

english: How do weeds hurt my cocoa crop even when they are growing far below the leaves?
ga: Te jwɛi yeɔ mi kokoo tsei lɛ awui ehaa tɛŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ babaoo yɛ baai lɛ ashishi moŋ?

english: Weeds have fast-spreading roots that steal vital water and soil nutrients away from your cocoa trees before the crops can absorb them. Weeds also create damp hiding places for pests and fungal spores.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni juɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli nibii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ kookoo tso lɛ mli dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Jwɛi hu feɔ hei ni mli ejɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai shwieɔ amɛhe.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is losing its strength and needs fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ egbɔjɔ ni ehe miihia ni awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Signs of weak soil include pale yellow leaves on mature trees, slow overall growth, and a steady decline in the number of pods harvested each season even when rainfall is normal.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ hewalɛ he okadii lɛ ekomɛi ji baai ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ tsei ni eda lɛ anɔ. Dalɛ fɛɛ yaa hiɛ blɛoo. Ni ŋmeii ni akpaa lɛ ayibɔ yaa nɔ ebaa shi yɛ be fɛɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ daa moŋ.

english: Excess rain waterlogs the soil, pushing out air and suffocating the root system. When roots cannot breathe, they stop absorbing essential nutrients like nitrogen, causing the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ tsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ naa. Enɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu Ekpaa niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen lɛ ŋmɔmɔ, ni no haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do so many small cocoa flowers drop off the trunk without ever turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ amɛteŋ mɛi babaoo gbeeɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii kɔkɔɔkɔ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands more flowers than they can support as mature pods, dropping excess blossoms to save energy. However, extreme flower drop can also be caused by water stress, bad weather, or lack of pollination.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa, fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye amɛbua kɛji amɛdara kwraa. Amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. Shi kɛlɛ, fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi fe nine lɛ baanyɛ ajɛ nu mli haomɔ mli aba. kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni ehiii loo pollination ni bɛ

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly in the afternoon but open back up in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane mli shi amɛgbeleɔ amɛhe leebi lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up during the hottest hours to reduce surface area exposed to the sun, which conserves water and prevents the plant from drying out. If they stay rolled up even in the cool morning, it is a sign that the soil is critically low on moisture.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu hiɔ shi ni ehaaa tso lɛ agbi. Kɛji amɛtee nɔ amɛbɔle amɛhe yɛ leebi ni hulu lɛ miitso po lɛ Eji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ faaa kwraa.

english: Why shouldn't I walk through my pepper field to harvest when the leaves are still wet with morning dew?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ onyiɛɛɛɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ ŋmɔji lɛ amli ni okpa amɛ? Beni baa lɛ mli efɔ lolo kɛ leebi ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Moving through wet crops transfers water droplets from leaf to leaf via your hands, clothing, or tools. If fungal or bacterial diseases are present on one plant, wet conditions allow them to spread rapidly to healthy plants.
ga: Ni oootsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni efɔ lɛ amli lɛ tsɔɔ nu mli nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ baa nɔ kɛyaa baa kroko nɔ kɛtsɔɔ oniji, otadei loo nitsumɔ dadei anɔ. Kɛji fungal loo bacteria hela ko yɛ tso kome nɔ Shihilɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ baaha amɛgbɛ amɛshwã tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli oya.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cassava plants turning yellow and dropping off during a dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants naturally shed lower leaves during dry periods to conserve water and survive drought. As long as the top leaves remain green and healthy, the plant is simply protecting its root growth until rain returns.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Shii abɔ ni baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ baakã he afee eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa lɛ. Tso lɛ miibu eshishifãi lɛ ahe kɛkɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: How can I tell if my maize farm is being attacked by fall armyworms before I see the insects?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmeii eyi mli dani mana ŋmeii lɛ?

english: During your daily farm inspections, look inside the central leaf funnels for tiny, pin-sized holes or small patches of brownish, sawdust-like droppings. Catching these early signs means the caterpillars are small and easier to treat.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni okwɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa gbi lɛ Kwɛmɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ koni ona bu bibioo ko. Pin yitso loo ŋmɔtɔ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ dalɛ. Okadii ni anáa mra lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ daraaa ni etsamɔ waaa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are extremely sensitive to strong, direct sunlight and heat. Plantains grow quickly and produce broad leaves that act as living shade umbrellas, keeping the soil moist and protecting young cocoa plants from scorching.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ebuɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe koni amɛkashã.

english: Why is it beneficial for me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas between my rows of maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When planted alongside maize, they naturally feed the soil and supply nitrogen that helps the maize grow greener and stronger.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ adu kɛ ŋmãa lɛ Amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛhaa nitrogen ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni ekwɛ̃ɔ ni ehiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yam plants need sunlight on as many leaves as possible to create energy for tuber growth. Staking lifts the leaves into the air, preventing rot from moist ground and helping the plant produce bigger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha bulb lɛ dalɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Etsiɔ fitemɔ naa kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ bulbs wuji

english: Tomato blossoms drop when the plant is stressed by high temperatures, erratic watering, or an excess of nitrogen fertilizer, which causes the plant to produce thick leaves instead of setting fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be ni mli wa lɛ hao tsei lɛ. nu ni bɛ shiŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ baai ni mli tse yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava stems look twisted and crumpled with yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni efite ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Twisted leaves with light green or yellow patches indicate Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny whiteflies. Affected plants cannot photosynthesize properly, leading to small or soft roots.
ga: Baai ni etsɔ mli yɛ hei ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ Etsɔɔ akɛ ŋmei mosaic hela ni ji ŋmei bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ Tsei ni ena hela lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee fotosintɛsis jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shishifãi bibii loo blɛoo baa.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds from my farm while my crops are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa kwraa lolo lɛ?

english: Young crops have small, underdeveloped root systems. If weeds grow next to them early on, the weeds will steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, permanently stunting the crop's growth potential.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifã bibioo ko ni edako. Kɛji jwɛi kwɛ̃ yɛ emasɛi amɛ kɛjɛ amɛgbekɛbiiashi tɔ̃ɔ. Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ baatsi tso lɛ dalɛ naa kwraa.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to produce energy for the tubers growing underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground toward the light while protecting them from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsɔnei lɛ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa la lɛ he kɛ agbɛnɛ hu ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why should I plant my maize in straight rows instead of scattering the seeds randomly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa ni ja mli moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui trukaa?

english: Planting in neat rows ensures every plant gets equal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients without competing. It also makes weeding, fertilizing, and harvesting much easier.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛkɛ amɛhe etswaaa akaŋ. Ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ hu feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the bottom usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen. Maize needs plenty of nitrogen to stay green and produce big cobs, which you can fix by adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ewo ŋmeii wuji. Abaanyɛ asaa enɛ kɛtsɔ kooloi aŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ.

english: Maize uses up a lot of nutrients from the soil. Beans and groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and put it back into the earth, naturally restoring soil fertility for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beans kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater sits in the soil for too long, it smothers the roots and allows soil fungi to attack and rot the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ Efiteɔ shishifãi lɛ ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Curling leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips feeding on the undersides of the leaves. Spraying with neem oil or soap water helps get rid of these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo nu ni mli edɔ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ.

english: Why do my cowpea leaves get covered in a white powdery dust during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sũ yɛŋ ehà mi-cowpea baai lɛ anɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: That white dust is a fungal disease called powdery mildew, which spreads quickly in hot, dry conditions. Spacing your plants properly helps air circulate and reduces the moisture that feeds the fungus.
ga: Muji yɛŋ lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ tsei ateŋ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni ji niyenii ni ŋmei lɛ yeɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when daytime temperatures get too hot or when the plant doesn't get water consistently. Extreme heat stresses the plant, preventing the flowers from setting fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ ahaaa tomato tsei lɛ nu daa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ. Tsi fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkawo yibii

english: Why do the lower leaves of my oil palm tree turn brown and dry out during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During long dry spells, oil palms drop their older outer leaves to save water and energy for the young leaves and fruit bunches growing at the top center of the tree.
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ, Mu tsei lɛ shiɔ kponɔgbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ koni amɛkɛto nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛha baai bibii kɛ aduawai akui ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ yitso teŋgbɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle strong, direct sunlight. Without shade trees or plantain trees around them to block the intense sun, their leaves burn and dry out, preventing the crop from growing properly.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo plantains bɛ he ni ebɔle amɛhe ni baatsi hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa lɛ Amɛbaai lɛ baashã ni amɛbaagbi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei lɛ adalɛ ni ehiii.

english: What is eating small holes inside the middle leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Mi ŋmãa gbekɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ mli?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They hide inside the central leaf roll of the maize plant during the day and feed on fresh green leaves, leaving holes and waste that look like sawdust.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli. ni amɛye baai eŋɔlii heei Enɛ haa bu kɛ jwɛi ni tamɔ ŋmei baa.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from the underside of leaves, or by a leaf-curl virus spread by insects. This damages the leaf structure and stunts fruit growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. aloo kɛtsɔ hela ko ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ fiteɔ bɔ ni baai lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ, ni ehaa aduawai lɛ adalɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants have tall stems with plenty of green leaves but very small roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ shishifã kakadaŋŋ kɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi shishifãi bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or manure, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing big leaves above ground instead of sending nutrients down to build large starch tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo ŋmei babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ, ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsu niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛba shi koni ekɛfee starch yitsei wuji.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce energy for heavy tuber growth. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground so they capture maximum light and stay safe from soil-borne fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha ŋmeii wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Staking woɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni emɔ la ni fa fe fɛɛ lɛ ni eha amɛhi shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why is it helpful to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my land before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts are legumes that capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the crop dies, that stored nitrogen breaks down in the soil, acting as free fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii gboi Nitrogen ni abua naa lɛ baafite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my vegetable stems with dry grass and fallen leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbo kɛ baai ni egbee shi lɛ awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle aduawai tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass, known as mulching, protects the dirt from hot sun, traps moisture so you water less, and blocks sunlight so grass seeds cannot sprout into weeds.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching, shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu muji lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ŋmɛɔ bɔni afee ni oná nu fioo ni etsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ akakwɛ̃ ni amɛtsɔ jwɛi.

english: If too many suckers grow around one plantain, they fight the main plant for food, water, and sunlight. Pruning down to one or two shoots lets the main plant grow thick and produce heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ, Plantain kome Amɛkɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la. Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ mli lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaha jwɛi babaoo aba.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep dropping off the stems before turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi dani ebatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the air gets too hot, when soil dries out completely, or when the plant lacks nutrients. Proper watering and partial shade during hot days keep the flowers attached.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ Nu ni sa kɛ hulutsoo be fioo yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ akpɛtɛ amɛhe.

english: How does keeping shallow water in my lowland rice field help control weeds?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nu ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni akɛtoɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni akuɔ jwɛi lɛ anɔ?

english: Rice roots can breathe under shallow water, but most land weeds drown or cannot sprout without air. Holding a gentle level of water in the field smothers weeds without hurting the rice crops.
ga: Omɔ shishifãi baanyɛ amu yɛ nu ni mli ekɔɔɔ shishi. Shi shikpɔŋ nɔ jwɛi lɛ ateŋ babaoo baagbee nu mli loo amɛnyɛŋ amɛkwɛ̃ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ. Nu ni sa ni akɛtoɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ mli ni eyeee ŋmãa tsei lɛ awui.

english: Is it true that some well water can actually harm my crops instead of helping them grow?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ ŋshɔ mli nu baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui moŋ fe ni eeeye ebua amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Yes, some underground water contains high levels of minerals or salts, often called hard or salty water. This type of water can prevent your crops from absorbing nutrients properly, dry out their roots, or cause long-term damage to your soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, shikpɔŋ shishi nui komɛi yɛ mineral loo ŋmeii babaoo. Bei pii lɛ, atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ nu ni wa loo nu ni mli edɔ. Nu nɛɛ baanyɛ atsĩ ŋmɔshi nibii anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii mli hewalɛ nii jogbaŋŋ, eha shishifãi lɛ agbi, loo efite shikpɔŋ lɛ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: People in my community say our underground water is 'hard water'—does this affect how my crops absorb fertilizers?
ga: Mɛi ni yɔɔ mi akutso lɛ mli lɛ kɛɛ wɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ ji 'nu ni wa'. Ani enɛ saa bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe?

english: Yes, hard water contains high amounts of minerals like calcium and magnesium. When mixed with certain fertilizers or sprayed on crops, these minerals can react with the fertilizer, causing it to clump or settle so your crops cannot absorb the nutrients effectively.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni wa lɛ mli nibii babaoo tamɔ calcium kɛ magnesium yɔɔ mli. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi futu mli loo akɛshwie ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ Nɛkɛ sũ nɛɛ baanyɛ ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afee ekome. Enɛ haa efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ebɔleɔ ehe kɛyashɛɔ he ko ni otsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Before I spend money to dig a borehole on my farm, how can I know if the underground water will be suitable for my crops?
ga: Dani mafite shika koni mafo nu bu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ sa kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: You can test the water from nearby wells or ask an extension officer to test a water sample for saltiness, mineral hardness, and acidity before drilling. Testing prevents you from investing in a water source that might burn your plants or damage your soil.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka nu ni jɛ nu bu ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ mli lɛ okwɛ loo obi mɔ ko ni tsuɔ nii yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ ni eka nu lɛ mli nɔkwɛmɔnɔ ko akwɛ kɛji ŋmei yɛ mli. minerals lɛ mli wa kɛ acidity dani atswaa shikpɔŋ Kaa yeɔ ebuaa ni okɛ ohe wooo nu jɛɛhei ni baanyɛ ashã tsei loo efite shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops seem to grow much faster with rainwater than when I water them from my underground well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya kɛtsɔ nugbɔ nu ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ fe nu ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu bu mli lɛ?

english: Rainwater naturally picks up dissolved nitrogen from the air, which acts like a mild, natural fertilizer for your crops. Well water lacks this atmospheric nitrogen and may also contain minerals that slightly slow down root absorption.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ nitrogen ni egbɛ eshwa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli jɔ kɛhaa onibii lɛ Nu lɛ bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli nitrogen ni ekolɛ minerals ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli fioo lɛ yɛ mli.

english: What causes a white, chalky crust to form on top of my farm soil after I irrigate my crops?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ baa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ beni mikɛ nu eshwie ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: A white crust usually means the water you are using for irrigation contains heavy minerals or salts. As the sun evaporates the water from the ground, it leaves these minerals behind on the soil surface, which can harm plant roots if allowed to build up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii yɛŋ tsɔɔ akɛ nu ni okɛtsuɔ nii kɛshwieɔ nu lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ mineral loo ŋmeii. Beni hulu lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Nu shĩɔ nɛkɛ tɛi nɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aye tso shishifãi lɛ awui kɛji akɛ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni amɛbɔle amɛhe.

english: Is it better for my pepper plants if I water them in the early morning or during the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha mi-pepper tso lɛ kɛji mikɛ nu wo nɔ leebi loo shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Early morning is best because the water soaks deep into the roots before the heat evaporates it. Watering in the afternoon heat wastes water to evaporation and can scald leaves, while leaving wet leaves overnight can encourage fungal diseases.
ga: Leebi ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ nu lɛ baabote shishifãi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ dani la ni tsoɔ lɛ baaho. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo mli yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni efee nɔ ni he ehiaaa. ni ebaanyɛ eha baai lɛ ashã. Kɛ́ ashi baai lɛ ni edɔ nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela aba.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my vegetables turning yellow even though I am watering the farm every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Namɔ haa tsei lɛ nu daa gbi?

english: Giving crops too much water fills up all the air spaces in the soil, effectively drowning the roots. Without oxygen, roots begin to rot and can no longer transport food to the rest of the plant, causing the leaves to turn yellow and drop off.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ fe nine lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ eyiɔ sũ lɛ mli obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ boteɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ bɛ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ niyenii aya hei krokomɛi. of plants anymore Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my maize leaves curl up tightly like tubes during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ jwɛi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a crop's natural defense against heat and water loss. By rolling its leaves, the maize plant reduces the surface area exposed to the hot sun and retains water inside its tissues until the temperature cools down.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ nu ni laajeɔ lɛ he. Kɛ́ atsɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋmãa tso lɛ he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa nu hiɔ efãji lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why do some crops like sorghum survive long dry spells while my maize wilts and dies quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi, tamɔ ŋmei, hiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli yɛ be mli ni mi ŋmei lɛ shwieɔ oya ni egboɔ lɛ?

english: Sorghum has a deeper root system that reaches deep underground water, and its leaves have a natural waxy coating that seals in moisture. Maize has shallower roots and broader leaves that lose moisture much faster during dry periods.
ga: Sorghum yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni shɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Ni sorghum baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli waxy ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Abɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni nu fiteɔ oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli.

english: How can I tell if my crops are wilting because of hot weather or because the soil is completely dry?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ hewɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa?

english: If your crops wilt during the hot afternoon heat but bounce back standing straight by early morning, they are reacting to heat. If they remain wilted and weak in the cool early morning, the soil is dry and urgently needs water.
ga: Kɛji oŋmɔshi nibii miiho yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli, Shi ku osɛɛ kɛya shidaamɔ tɛ̃ɛ leebi. Etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miifee nɔ ko yɛ latsaa lɛ he. Kɛji amɛhe ejɔ lolo ni amɛgbɔjɔ yɛ leebi ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi, ni nu he miihia lɛ oya.

english: Why is it important for me to apply fertilizer to my crops early in the farming season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mawo ŋmɔshi nibii amli ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ okwaayeli be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Crops need nutrients most when their roots and leaves are developing rapidly. Applying fertilizer early ensures young plants build a strong root system to absorb water and food before flowering.
ga: Niyenii mli hewalɛ he miihia tsei fe fɛɛ beni amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ miiya hiɛ oya lɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli mra Enɛ baaha tso bibioo lɛ ama shishifã ni mli wa ni baaŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii dani ewo fɔfɔi.

english: Should I apply fertilizer to my crops right before a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli dani nugbɔ ni naa wa aba?

english: No, heavy rainfall will wash the fertilizer away from your crop roots and carry it off into streams before the plants have a chance to drink it in.
ga: Dabi, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ tsei shishifãi amli kɛyaa faai amli dani tsei lɛ náa hegbɛ amɛnuɔ.

english: What will happen to my crops if I put too much fertilizer on them at one time?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo mli shikome?

english: Applying too much fertilizer creates high salt levels in the soil, which burns the plant roots, turning the leaf tips brown and causing the crop to wither or die.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha ŋmei babaoo aya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ashã. Baai lɛ ashishigbɛi lɛ feɔ blɔfo. ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii agbi loo amɛgboi.

english: Why do my crops react faster to chemical fertilizer than to animal manure?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ tsuɔ nii oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Chemical fertilizer dissolves quickly in soil water, making nutrients available instantly to plant roots, while manure must break down slowly over time before crops can feed on it.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ mli lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ nu mli oya. Ehaa niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ baa tsei lɛ ashishifãi amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, esa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afite fiofio. Be ko baaho dani tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni ayeɔ.

english: Why do people advise that I test my soil before buying fertilizer for my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ maka mishikpɔŋ lɛ makwɛ dani mahe ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Soil testing acts like a health checkup for your land. It reveals which nutrients your soil is missing so you only spend money on the specific fertilizer your crops actually need.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ kaa tsuɔ nii tamɔ hewalɛnamɔ he kwɛmɔ kɛha oshikpɔŋ lɛ. Ejieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kpo. No hewɔ lɛ, ofiteɔ shika yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ pɛ he.

english: How can I tell if my crop leaves are yellowing because of missing plant food?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mitso lɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ tso niyenii ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ?

english: When crops lack major nutrients like nitrogen, older leaves at the bottom of the plant turn pale yellow first while the plant stays short and thin.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa, tamɔ nitrogen lɛ, baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ klɛŋklɛŋ. Yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ baafee kuku ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ.

english: Does every crop on my farm need the exact same type of fertilizer?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ biɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ?

english: No, crops have different nutrient needs. Leafy plants like cabbage need nitrogen to grow green, while fruiting crops like tomatoes need potassium and phosphorus to grow big, healthy fruit.
ga: Dabi, tsei yɛ niyenii he hiamɔ nii srɔtoi. Tsei ni yɔɔ baai, tamɔ kaabe lɛ he miihia nitrogen koni amɛdara. Yɛ be mli ni tsei ni woɔ yibii, tamɔ tomato lɛ he hiaa potassium kɛ phosphorus lɛ. Koni ewo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.
