english: Why do my crops dry up and lose food quickly when planted in sandy soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Sandy soil has large particles that allow water and nutrients to drain straight through past the root zone, making it harder for crops to retain moisture and fertilizer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ yɛ nibii bibii wuji ni haa nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii tsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei lɛ akɛ amɛaahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli.

english: Why do crops grow differently in forest zones like the Western Region compared to drier northern regions?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ yɛ kooi amli hei tamɔ Anaigbɛ kɛ akɛto kooyigbɛ hei ni egbi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Forest zones receive higher rainfall and have deeper topsoil, encouraging fast lush growth, but heavy rains can also leach nutrients deeper into the soil away from shallow roots.
ga: Kooi amli hei lɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo ni amɛyɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ. Ewoɔ dalɛ oya Shi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hu baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ, kɛjɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ he eko lɛ ahe.

english: Why did my maize plants produce small, empty cobs even though I used fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ miiwo ŋmeii bibii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii moŋ.

english: If fertilizer is given at the wrong time or lacks phosphorus during the cobs' formation stage, the plant will spend energy growing tall leaves instead of filling out grains.
ga: Kɛji akɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be ni esaaa mli loo fɔsfɔs faaa yɛ cob feemɔ be lɛ mli. Tsei kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo baai kakadaji moŋ fe ni amɛaawo ŋmaa mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when the dry season sun comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn under full direct sunlight. Planting plantains alongside young cocoa provides shade and keeps the surrounding air and soil moist while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni akɛ kookoo bibii duɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo baa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to clear tall sticks and stake my yam vines off the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie tsei niji ni kwɔlɔ lɛ ni madu sweet potato wain tsei kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to reach up high to gather sunlight through their leaves. Staking keeps leaves off the wet ground to prevent diseases and allows the plant to produce larger tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ashɛ he ko ni nɔ kwɔ koni amɛbua hulu la naa kɛtsɔ baai lɛ anɔ. Staking baajie tsei ahe tsei kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni helai akabote mli ni eha tso lɛ awo bulbs wuji.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to build strong leaves. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer restores green color and growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni he hiaa tsei lɛ koni amɛfee baai ni wa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ ni amɛdara ekoŋŋ.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, blocks the hot sun from drying out the dirt, traps moisture near the roots, and keeps weeds from growing.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi haa Atsɛɔ lɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni etsi hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa ni eha muji akagbi. Ha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shishifãi lɛ ahe. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: Is it good for my main crop if I plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same field with my maize?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ kɛji midu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ ŋmãa?

english: Yes, leguminous crops like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, which feeds the maize plants and improves soil richness naturally.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ niyenii ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yaa hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ

english: Should I cut away the small shoots growing at the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii bibii? Ani ajie nakai ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain wulu lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Yes, leaving too many shoots causes them to fight with the main plant for nutrients and water. Removing most shoots and leaving only one strong sucker ensures the main plant produces large bunches.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo yɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha amɛkɛ tso titri lɛ abɔi niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ babaoo ni ashi ŋmeii kome pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: What is causing holes in my maize leaves and leaving small dirt inside the plant funnel?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmãa baa mli bulɛ baa ni eshiɔ muji fioo ko yɛ sɛɛ? yɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the center of young maize plants and eat the leaves, but catching them early with recommended control measures stops them from destroying the farm.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ. Shi amɛmɔmɔ mra Gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ amɛ lɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite ŋmɔ lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies that spread plant viruses. Controlling these insects early keeps the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe awa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot underground when the heavy rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni naa wa lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Excess water sitting in heavy soil starves roots of air and causes fungal rot. Planting cassava on raised ridges or mounds allows surplus water to drain away safely.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni buaa ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat or irregular watering. Keeping soil moisture steady helps the flowers stay attached and turn into healthy tomatoes.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛfeɔ tomato ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can diseases from my neighbor's farm spread to infect my own crops?
ga: Ani hela ko ni jɛ akutsoŋnyo ko ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã mi diɛŋtsɛ midumɔ nii anɔ?

english: Yes, crop diseases and pests move easily through wind, soil, insects, and shared farm tools, which is why keeping your farm borders clean and spraying protective chemicals early helps stop infections from spreading across farm boundaries.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ahelai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ nyiɛɔ oya kɛtsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, shikpɔŋ, kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni ajaa lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni oha oŋmɔ lɛ husui lɛ ahe atse lɛ. kɛ tsofai ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni akpa helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔ lɛ husui lɛ amli lɛ.

english: If an outbreak of pests starts near my farm, what can I do immediately to protect my crops?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai bɔi gbɛfaŋnɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ miŋmɔ lɛ hu? Mɛni manyɛ mafee amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe?

english: You can create a protective barrier by clearing a wide boundary path around your farm and spraying approved chemicals along the edges to prevent crawling insects and diseases from crossing onto your land.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee gbogbo ni buɔ mɔ he kɛtsɔ gbɛ ni da ni bɔleɔ oŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ ni oootsi ni okɛ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ afɔ eshishigbɛ koni kooloi kɛ helai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ akashwie oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know if my crops are suffering from a pest attack or just lack of water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsɛŋemɔ helai egba miŋmɔshi nibii ahe loo nu efo mli kɛkɛ?

english: Water stress usually causes leaves to wilt evenly across the field, whereas pest attacks leave visible signs like chewed holes, spots, sticky residue, or yellow patches on specific leaves and stems.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu he haomɔ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ shiɔ okadii ni anaa tamɔ bu ni ashɛre, ŋmeii, ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi, loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ baai kɛ tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi anɔ.

english: Why is it dangerous to use any farm chemical I buy without proper guidance?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli ni miheɔ lɛ baatsu nii ni gbɛtsɔɔmɔ ni sa bɛ he lɛ?

english: Using the wrong chemical or incorrect dosage can burn your crops, damage your soil, leave harmful chemical residues on your food crops, and waste your money.
ga: Tsofai ni ejaaa loo falɛ ni ejaaa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii ashã. ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fitemɔ baa Eshiɔ tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara yɛ niyenii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔ ni efiteɔ bo shika

english: How often should I spray my crops with chemicals during the farming season?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai afɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ yɛ okwaayeli be lɛ mli?

english: Spraying depends on the specific crop type and the severity of pest threats; excessive spraying damages crops and costs too much, while spraying according to recommended schedules protects your yield safely.
ga: Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ damɔ ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ bɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ mli wa ha lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ fe nine lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ni ejara wa tsɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ yɛ gbɛjianɔtoo ni atsɔɔ lɛ naa lɛ, ebaabu onibii ahe shweshweeshwe.

english: Where can a small-scale farmer like me get affordable farm chemicals and expert advice?
ga: Nɛgbɛ okwaafoi bibii tamɔ mi baanyɛ ana ŋmɔ mli tsofai ni jara waaa kɛ ŋaawoo ni jɛ ŋaalɔi adɛŋ?

english: You can visit your local Ministry of Food and Agriculture (MOFA) extension office or join a local farmers' group to access subsidized farm supplies, expert training, and official support.
ga: Obaanyɛ oyasara Niyenii kɛ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe (MOFA) nitsumɔhe nine ni yɔɔ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ. Aloo okɛ ohe awo okwaafoi akuu ko ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli koni onine ashɛ okwaayeli he nibii ni akɛ shika yeɔ ebuaa lɛ anɔ. Tsɔsemɔ ni jɛ ŋaalɔi adɛŋ kɛ maŋ yelikɛbuamɔ

english: Why do large farms seem to get better crop yields than smaller farms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni ŋmɔji wuji woɔ yibii babaoo fe ŋmɔji bibii lɛ?

english: Large farms often yield more because owners have timely access to inputs like quality seeds, fertilizers, and protective chemicals, but small farms can achieve high yields too by using proper crop spacing and soil management.
ga: Okwaafoi wuji lɛ fɔɔ yibiiwoo babaoo ejaakɛ amɛnuŋtsɔmɛi lɛ náa nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli tamɔ dumɔwui ni hi, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ tsofai ni akɛbuɔ nii ahe lɛ yɛ be naa. Shi ŋmɔji bibii hu baanyɛ awo yibii babaoo kɛji akɛ akwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ ni akwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves often indicate that your crops lack vital soil nutrients like nitrogen, which happens when heavy rains wash away soil nutrients unless fertilizer or compost is applied.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, ni baa kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Ja okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and weak with few fruits when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, causing them to grow thin and produce small, poor-quality yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight, so fast-growing plantain trees act as living umbrellas that provide essential shade and moisture until the cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo, ni amɛhaa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa.

english: Groundnuts and beans are legumes that naturally trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. This naturally fertilizes the soil and helps your maize grow stronger.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eye ebua o-abele lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of a maize plant usually mean the soil is running low on nitrogen. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer, animal manure, or compost helps the leaves turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: When pepper plants are crowded, their roots and leaves compete for sunlight, water, and plant food. Giving them proper space lets each plant produce larger, healthier fruits.
ga: Beni pepper tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ tsei aniyenii ahe akaŋshii mli. He ni sa ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso fɛɛ tso ni ewoɔ yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Which direction should the buds point when I plant my cassava stem cuttings?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ ŋmeii lɛ atsɔɔ kɛ́ adu ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ?

english: The stem buds must always point upwards toward the sky. If you plant cassava stems upside down, the shoots and roots will struggle to grow, leading to a poor harvest.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmei lɛ shishifã lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi be fɛɛ be. Kɛji odu ŋmei tso ni okɛ ohiɛ fɔ shi lɛ, ewa akɛ eshishifãi kɛ shishifãi lɛ baakwɛ̃. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji kpamɔ ni ehiii.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to feed the tubers growing under the ground. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet soil, helping them catch maximum sunlight while protecting them from rotting.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni eye ebua ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa amɛnáa hulu la babaoo yɛ be mli ni ehaaa amɛfite.

english: Check for ragged holes eaten out of the leaves and yellowish-brown waste that looks like sawdust inside the central funnel of the plant. Seeing this early lets you treat the crop before it gets destroyed.
ga: Kwɛmɔ buji ni etse ni aye kɛjɛ baai lɛ ahe kɛ ŋmeii ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ ni ooona mra lɛ Ebaaye ebua bo ni ohere oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayiwala dani akpata amɛhiɛ.

english: Tomato leaves curl and drop flowers mainly because of extreme heat, lack of steady watering, or tiny insects like whiteflies sucking the plant's juices. Regular watering and insect protection will fix this.
ga: Tomato haa amɛbaai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛhaaa daa Aloo kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ ni nuɔ tsei amli nu lɛ yɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli daa kɛ kooloi ahebuu baatsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: What time of day is best for watering my garden egg and pepper plants?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha tsei ni yɔɔ ŋshɔŋlooi kɛ ŋshɔŋlooi abɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ nu?

english: Early morning is the best time to water. It gives the soil time to absorb the water before the hot sun causes it to evaporate, keeping the roots cool and hydrated throughout the afternoon.
ga: Leebi ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha nu. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa be ni ekɛmuɔ nu dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ nu lɛ nɔ. Ha shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i yɛ shwane lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do lowland rice farmers construct small soil walls around their plots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ ma shikpɔŋ gbogboi bibii kɛbɔle amɛshikpɔji lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: These low earth walls, called bunds, hold rainwater on the field. Lowland rice needs standing water to thrive, and flooded water also helps drown out unwanted weeds.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ nɛɛ akɛ bunds. Too nugbɔ nu yɛ ŋmɔ mli Lowland ŋmãa he miihia nu ni damɔ shi koni ekwɛ̃. Ni nu afua lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni efuɔ jwɛi ni ataooo lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plant is lacking nitrogen, which is the main food crop leaves need to stay healthy and green. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei ahe koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee eŋɔli. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants look like they are dying during the hot afternoon even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eegbo yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ leebi moŋ?

english: In intense sun, pepper leaves lose water faster than the roots can drink it from the dirt. The plant wilts slightly to protect itself from heat, but usually recovers in the evening when the air cools down.
ga: Yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Pepper baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baagbɔjɔ fioo koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. Shi bei pii lɛ, ehiɛɔ shi gbɛkɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. The plant gets stressed and drops its flowers to save energy to keep itself alive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ waa mli lɛ. Tsei lɛ haoɔ ni amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he koni amɛhi wala mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when planted in an open field with full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hulu tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under direct midday sun. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to them creates a umbrella that keeps them cool and moist while their roots grow deep.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shwane mli lɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ehaa shade ni haa tsei lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe jɔɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ lɛ baa.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava sticks very close together to get more crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛɔ he koni maná yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need space underground to expand into large tubers. If you plant them too close, the roots fight each other for water and plant food, resulting in many small, thin tubers instead of big ones.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi he ko he miihia cassava shishifãi koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji. Kɛji odu amɛ obɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa yitsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo baa yɛ yitsei wuji najiaŋ.

english: Why did some of the maize seeds I buried in the soil fail to shoot up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mifu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to sprout if they are buried too deep where air cannot reach them, if the soil dries out completely, or if insects eat the seeds before they can push out of the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ yɛ he ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ amɛhe. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa Aloo kɛji kooloi ye dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛtsi amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my soil turn hard and dry so quickly after rain falls on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni egbiɔ oya nɛkɛ beni nugbɔ enɛɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Bare soil exposed directly to the hot sun loses water fast and bakes into a hard crust. Covering the ground around your crops with dried grass or leaves keeps the soil shaded, soft, and moist for longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nu fiteɔ oya ni etsɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa. He ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ ni oooha Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi wo ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, efee blɛoo, ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops yield less harvest when I plant the exact same crop on the same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii beni miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop every season drains the exact same nutrients from the soil over and over, while allowing crop-specific pests and diseases to multiply in the ground. Rotating different crops keeps the soil balanced.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ daa afi lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shii abɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii srɔtoi ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ŋmɛɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to stay small and produce weak yields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibioo ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm—they aggressively drink the water, take the plant food from the soil, and block the sunlight that your crops need to grow big and strong.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛnuɔ nu waa. Tse niyenii ni oooŋɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni otsĩ hulu la ni he hiaa ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dara ni amɛhe wa lɛ naa.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my yam tubers so they do not rot in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ? koni ekafite yɛ sũ lɛ mli

english: Yam tubers are mature and ready for harvest when the leaves and vines start to dry up and turn yellow naturally. Harvesting too early yields small tubers, while leaving them in wet ground too long leads to rot.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ edara kwraa ni amɛfee klalo akɛ abaakpa beni baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ akpa mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii bibii aba. Shi kɛ́ ashi yɛ sũ ni mli efɔ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha egbo.

english: When is the best time for me to start clearing trees and weeds from my land before planting?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mabɔi tsei kɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ajiemɔ dani madu nii?

english: Land preparation like cutting trees and clearing weeds should be finished right before the main rainy season starts around May or June so your soil is clean and ready for immediate planting when the rains begin.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ saamɔ, tamɔ tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ Esa akɛ agbe enɛ naa dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ aje shishi yɛ May loo June aaafee. Enɛ baaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ atse ni efee klalo kɛha dumɔ kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ pɛ.

english: Why do I need to clear away all the tree stumps and bush debris before putting my seeds in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie tsei akutsei kɛ jwɛi amli ŋmeii fɛɛ dani mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Clearing all debris and stumps gives your crop seedlings direct access to sunlight, prevents pests from breeding in leftover dead wood, and makes it easier for young roots to spread in the soil.
ga: Nibii ni efite kɛ ŋmeii fɛɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa otso lɛ dumɔwui lɛ naa hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa koni amɛkafɔ yɛ tsei ni egboi amli. ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa shishifãi bibii lɛ akɛ amɛbaagbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: Is it safe for me to clear my land and plant my crops at the same time during the heavy rains?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mafo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni madu ŋmɔshi nii yɛ be kome mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: It is risky because land clearing takes a lot of time. If you spend your time clearing while it is already raining heavily, you will waste valuable growing days and end up planting your seeds too late.
ga: Oshara yɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni ajieɔ lɛ heɔ be babaoo. Kɛji okɛ be tsu nii ni okɛjie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be mli ni nugbɔ miinɛ waa lɛ Obaafite be ni okɛdu otsei lɛ ni obaagbe naa ni okɛ dumɔwui adu sɛɛ tsɔ.

english: Why do most farmers tell me to wait until June before I start planting my main crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi babaoo kɛɔ mi akɛ mamɛ kɛyashi June dani mije ŋmɔshi nibii titrii adumɔ shishi lɛ?

english: June usually marks the period when the rainy season becomes steady and reliable, giving your young seeds enough continuous water to germinate and build strong root systems.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, June ji be ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ yaa nɔ shiŋŋ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ. Kɛtsɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni oooha odumɔwui bibii lɛ daa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfee shishifãi ni mli wa lɛ nɔ.

english: What will happen to my crops if I plant them late in August or September instead of June?
ga: Mɛni baa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji midu yɛ August loo September naagbee gbɛ yɛ June najiaŋ?

english: Crops planted late in August or September will not get enough rainfall months to mature before the dry season starts, which can cause them to dry up, produce small fruits, or fail completely.
ga: Tsei ni adu yɛ August loo September naagbee lɛ naaa nugbɔshiimɔ nyɔji ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛshwere dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aje shishi. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ agbi. Fɔfɔi woɔ yibii bibii. loo eyeee omanye kwraa

english: How many continuous months of rain do my crops need after I plant them?
ga: Nyɔji enyiɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ he hiaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ?

english: Most common staple crops need about 3 to 4 months of reliable, regular rain from the month of planting to fully grow, flower, and produce healthy food.
ga: Nibii ni afɔɔ feemɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo biɔ aaafee nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 ni nugbɔ anɔ daa, ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ nyɔŋ ni aduɔ lɛ nɔ. Bɔni afee ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, fɔfɔi ni ewo niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa.

english: How do my young crops react if the rain suddenly stops for two weeks right after I plant them?
ga: Te miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ baafee amɛnii amɛha tɛŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa trukaa yɛ otsii enyɔ sɛɛ beni midu amɛ lɛ?

english: Young crop seedlings have short roots that stay near the surface, so if rain stops shortly after planting, the heat quickly dries out the topsoil and causes the delicate plants to wither and die.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi kukuji ni bɛŋkɛ nu lɛ hiɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa beni adu nii lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ, Dɔlɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gĩɔ oya. ni ehaa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Does the size of my farm change when I should start planting my crops?
ga: Ani miŋmɔ lɛ dalɛ tsakeɔ yɛ be mli ni esa akɛ mabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ?

english: Yes, because planting a large farm takes much more time and labor. If you don't start early in June, you will still be planting by August or September when the rains are already ending.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ ŋmɔ agbo ko ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ heɔ be kɛ nitsumɔ babaoo. Kɛji ojeee dumɔ shishi yɛ June shishijee mli Obaanyɛ odu amɛ lolo kɛyashi August loo September be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ eba naagbee lɛ.

english: If I have a large piece of land and fall behind schedule, should I still try to plant everything in August?
ga: Kɛji miyɛ shikpɔŋ agbo ko ni miba sɛɛ. Ani esa akɛ mabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni madu nɔ fɛɛ nɔ yɛ August mli?

english: It is better not to plant long-season crops late in August. Instead, focus on planting only what you can finish early, or switch the remaining land to short-duration crops that mature quickly with less rain.
ga: Ehi akɛ ooodu ŋmɔshi nibii kakadaŋŋ yɛ August naagbee gbɛ. Kɛ ojwɛŋmɔ ama nɔ ni obaanyɛ ofee oya lɛ pɛ ni ooodu lɛ nɔ. aloo atsake shikpɔŋ ni eshwɛ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kukuoo, ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ fioo.

english: Why do weeds grow faster than my planted crops when the early rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native plants with deep, established root systems that respond instantly to early rainfall, while crop seeds take extra time to absorb water, break open, and start growing roots.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji maŋ tso ni yɔɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni tsuɔ nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui heɔ be kroko dani amɛnuɔ nu, amɛkwɛ̃ɔ, ni amɛjeɔ shishifãi adalɛ shishi.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning brown and burning off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct sunlight and severe drought. Without shade trees or plantains grown beside them to block the intense heat, the delicate leaves dry out and burn.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo plantains ni adu yɛ emasɛi lɛ bɛ lɛ, Koni hulutsoo ni naa wa akafee lɛ Baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ baagbi ni amɛshã.

english: Why do I see small ragged holes in my young maize leaves and soft dirt inside the top leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii anɔ kɛ muji ni mli tseee yɛ jɛmɛ. yɛ baa lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ

english: This is a sign of Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They hide inside the central growing point of the maize plant during the day, eating the soft leaves before they unfold.
ga: Enɛ ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ahe okadi. Amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ baai bibii ni ayeɔ dani amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato fruits get a dark, flat rot at the bottom while the rest of the fruit is still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ mli edɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shishigbɛ yɛ be mli ni aduawai ni eshwɛ lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ lolo lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil, usually caused by irregular watering or dry spells while the fruit is forming.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni ashwieɔ shi yɛ be fɛɛ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbiɔ yɛ yibiiwoo be lɛ mli.

english: Why do my pepper leaves roll up tightly during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi waa yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plants curl their leaves during the hottest part of the day to reduce water loss through evaporation. It is a natural protection mechanism to survive heat stress.
ga: Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli koni nu ni fiteɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi. Eji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ayeɔ dɔlɛ mli haomɔ mli.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my field after harvesting my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots, which naturally restores soil fertility that maize feeds heavily on.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ ni akɛ ŋmãa babaoo yeɔ nɔ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow weak and small if I do not remove the weeds around them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe ehiaaa kɛji mijieee jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than main crops and steal the essential nutrients, water, and sunlight that your crops need to develop strong roots and stems.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa, nu, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛná shishifãi kɛ shishifãi ni wa.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves fully toward the sun. Sunlight allows the plant to make food, which flows down into the soil to build large tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛbaai lɛ ajie amɛhe kpo kwraa yɛ hulu la lɛ he. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. ni hoɔ kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni efeɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why shouldn't I let all the small shoots that sprout around my plantain tree grow at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mihaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ? Mɛi ni kwɛ̃ yɛ midumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ fɛɛ kwɛ̃ ekomekomei.

english: If too many shoots grow together on one plantain stem, they fight for nutrients and water, resulting in small, light bunches. Leaving only two or three shoots ensures bigger, healthier fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii babaoo ni miida yɛ ekomefeemɔ mli yɛ tso kome nɔ lɛ, Plantains baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei niji lɛ daraaa, ni amɛhe waaa. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni amɛhiɛɛɛ amɛhe lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ adara ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why do I get a much smaller harvest if I plant seeds saved from last season's hybrid maize harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ yibiiwoo bibioo kwraa nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ nyɔŋ ni ho lɛ mli ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for a single generation. The seeds harvested from that crop lose their original yield strength and disease resistance in the next season.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ krɛdɛɛ kɛha yinɔ kome. Dumɔwui ni akpa kɛjɛ nakai ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ baafite eshishijee yibiiwoo hewalɛ kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ helai yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are fully grown and ready to harvest without digging up the whole plant?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ edara kwraa ni amɛfee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni okɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ efooo?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to swell and crack open from the expanding tubers beneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi shwiemɔ ni egbɛ eshwa kɛjɛ bulb ni miigbɛ eshwa ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli.

english: How many days should I wait to see my maize seeds sprout after planting them in the ground?
ga: Kɛ́ amɛdu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ, gbii enyiɛ esa akɛ amɛmɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Under moist soil conditions, maize seeds usually sprout within 4 to 7 days. If they take longer than 10 days, the seeds may have rotted from excess water, been eaten by soil insects, or were planted too deep.
ga: Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gbii 4 kɛyashi 7 mli. Kɛji akɛ ehe fe gbii 10 lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ afite kɛjɛ nu babaoo mli. Kplukai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ loo aduɔ tsɔ

english: How can I test if my saved seeds are still good to plant before putting them in the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji midumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ hi lolo akɛ adu dani madu?

english: You can perform a simple float test in water—dead or insect-damaged seeds usually float while healthy seeds sink. Alternatively, wrap 10 seeds in a damp cloth for a few days to see how many germinate before planting your whole field.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka bɔ ni enyɛɔ efoɔ yɛ nu mli lɛ okwɛ. Dumɔwui ni egbo loo koolooi efite lɛ fɔɔ ŋshɔ hiɛ, yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɔ kroko hu ji akɛ, okɛ mama ni mli efɔ abɔ dumɔwui 10 he gbii fioo komɛi koni ona bɔ ni amɛyi fa ha dani odu ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upward and shrinking instead of growing flat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap from young leaves, or by a virus transmitted by these insects. It damages the leaf structure and slows growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛbaa lɛ nɔ Efiteɔ baa lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo ni ehaa edalɛ baa shi.

english: Why are my tomato plants growing very leafy and bushy but not producing any flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ yɛ baai kɛ ŋmeii babaoo shi fɔfɔi ko bɛ he lɛ?

english: Tomato plants often produce heavy foliage without flowers when there is too much nitrogen in the soil or fertilizer. Nitrogen encourages leaf and stem growth rather than flowering and fruiting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato tsei woɔ baai ni tsii ni fɔfɔi bɛ mli kɛ́ nitrogen babaoo yɛ sũ loo ŋmɔshi nibii amli. Nitrogen haa baai kɛ tsei lɛ daraa fe fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo.

english: Yellowing of lower leaves is a classic sign of nitrogen deficiency. The plant shifts available nitrogen from older lower leaves to nourish newer growth at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni ale waa ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi dalɛ hee lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why are my newly planted plantain suckers taking a very long time to shoot out new leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-banana tso ni midu ehee lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ baai heei lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers suffer from transplant shock as they re-establish roots. If the sucker roots were damaged or if the planting hole lacks sufficient moisture and compost, leaf emergence will be delayed.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ naa amanehulu yɛ be mli ni amɛtswaa amɛshishifãi lɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ. Kɛji akɛ sucker shishifãi lɛ efite loo kɛji akɛ dumɔ bu lɛ mli nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ, Baai lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Why do I see large holes and brown sawdust-like dirt inside the center of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji wuji kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmei ni tsuɔ nii yɛ mi-ŋmei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: This is characteristic damage caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central leaf whorl of young maize plants during the day, eating tender leaves and leaving behind waste material.
ga: Nɛkɛ ji bɔ ni Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ nii lɛ yɔɔ. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Ye baai bibii lɛ ni oshi fãi ni eshwɛ lɛ.

english: Why do the tiny flowers on my cocoa trees fall off without forming cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii ji No hewɔ lɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ gbeeɔ shi ni ebɔɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi?

english: Cocoa flowers often drop off due to lack of pollination by tiny biting midges, water stress from dry weather, or natural thinning when the tree has more flowers than its nutrients can support.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kooloi bibii ni shwieɔ mɔ lɛ ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ hewɔ. Nu mli haomɔ ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi loo adebɔɔ mli fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ mli beni tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi babaoo fe niyenii ni ebaanyɛ eye ebua lɛ.

english: What happens if I leave my cassava tubers in the ground long past their normal harvest time?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mishi ŋmei shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ be kakadaŋŋ fe be ni akɛkpaa ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Leaving cassava in the soil too long causes the roots to become woody, fibrous, and lose starch content. During heavy rains, older tubers are also more likely to rot in the ground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ashi ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ afee tsei, amɛhe afee ŋmeii ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baaje mli. yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa mli lɛ, ŋmeii ni egbɔ hu baanyɛ agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Yam rot in storage is usually caused by fungal or bacterial infections entering through small cuts or bruises sustained during harvest. Poor ventilation and hot conditions in the barn accelerate this decay.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela loo hela ko ni tsɔɔ pilamɔ bibioo ko mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sweet potatoes ni fiteɔ yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ baa. loo fãji ni baa yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be mli Kɔɔyɔɔ ni ehiii kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ haa nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ yaa oya.

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from direct heat and harsh sunlight. Leaving large shade trees or planting temporary shade crops like plantains keeps the soil cool and humid, helping the young cocoa survive its first few years.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Kɛ́ ashi tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo loo adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko tamɔ plantains lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Enɛ haa kookoo bibii lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow, twisted, and small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛmiitsake, ni amɛmiifee bibii lɛ?

english: Twisted and yellow leaves on cassava are signs of cassava mosaic disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. Planting improved, disease-resistant cassava stems helps protect your farm from this problem.
ga: Baai ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ yucca nɔ lɛ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Kɛ́ odu ŋmei tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ naagba nɛɛ he.

english: How deep into the soil should I place my maize seeds when planting?
ga: Te esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu?

english: Maize seeds should be planted about two to three fingers deep (around 3 to 5 centimeters). Planting too shallow lets birds eat the seeds or heat dry them out, while planting too deep makes it hard for the shoots to reach the surface.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ mli aaafee sɛntimitai 3-5. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha okpoi lɛ aye dumɔwui lɛ loo amɛkɛ dɔlɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛgbi dumɔwui lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ adu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ewa aha ŋmeii lɛ akɛ amɛaashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my plantain suckers too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Planting plantain suckers too close together forces them to fight for sunlight, water, and food in the soil. Proper spacing allows each plant to grow strong stems and produce larger bunches of plantain.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ teŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso fɛɛ tso ni ewoɔ shishifãi ni wa ni ewoɔ dumɔwui babaoo.

english: Crops remove natural plant food from the soil every season. Without resting the land, adding animal manure, or applying fertilizer, the soil becomes exhausted and cannot support high yields.
ga: Tsei jieɔ tso mli niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Kɛji akɛ aŋmɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hejɔɔmɔ, awooo mli ŋmɔshi nibii, loo awooo mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ yibiiwoo babaoo nɔ.

english: Why do people tell me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on my land before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ko baakɛɛ mi akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmei?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that naturally trap nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil. Planting them first acts as a natural fertilizer that helps the next maize crop grow better.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ebaatsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni baaye abua ni ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is making holes in my young maize leaves and leaving brown dirt inside the plant funnel?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli kɛ muji ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni miishiɔ yɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ baa?

english: This damage is caused by fall armyworms, which are caterpillars that hide in the center leaves of young maize. Catching them early and spraying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extract can protect your crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji cutworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa bibii amli baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ afɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ abu onibii ahe.

english: Is it better to water my pepper plants in the hot afternoon or in the early morning?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oooha ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ nu yɛ shwane mli loo leebi maŋkpa?

english: It is best to water early in the morning or late in the evening. Watering in the hot afternoon causes water to evaporate quickly before roots can absorb it, and hot water droplets can scorch tender leaves.
ga: Esa akɛ afɔ lɛ nu leebi loo gbɛkɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo mli yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ atsɔ oya dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Ni nu ni mli edɔ lɛ mli nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baanyɛ aha baai bibii lɛ ashã.

english: Why do my tomatoes get black, rotten spots on the bottom before they turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ dani etsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Black spots on tomato bottoms are known as blossom-end rot. This happens when the plant experiences irregular watering or lacks calcium in the soil while the fruit is forming.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tomato nɔ lɛ akɛ blossom end rot. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu ni ejaaa loo calcium ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli be mli ni aduawai lɛ miifee lɛ.

english: Why do my stored maize grains turn to dust and get full of insects after a few months in bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ mli eyi kɛ sũ ni ŋmeii eyi mli obɔ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi ni mikɛwo kotoku lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize grains spoil in storage if they are bagged while still damp or if small insects are already inside. Thoroughly drying your grain in the sun until it cracks sharply when bitten helps keep pests out during storage.
ga: Abele ŋmeii baafite yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ kɛji akɛ awo kotoku mli be mli ni amɛmli edɔ lolo loo ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli. Eyɛ mli momo Ehaa dumɔwui lɛ egbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛbaatse kɛji akɛ amɛye. Ebaaye ebua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai akabote mli yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: How do I know which crops will actually do well in my local district's soil and weather?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsei ni baatsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ mli?

english: Different crops prefer different soil types and rainfall levels. Testing your soil and observing what naturally thrives in your district prevents you from investing money in crops that will struggle and yield poorly in your local climate.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi biɔ shikpɔŋ henɔi srɔtoi kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ. Kaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ okwɛ ni okwɛ nɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ. Ebaatsi bo gbɛ ni okɛ shika awo ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛwooo yibii jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ lɛ mli.

english: Should I burn the cleared grass on my land before planting, or leave it on the soil?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashã jwɛi ni ajie yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ dani madu loo mashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Leaving cleared grass on the ground as mulch is usually better because burning destroys rich organic nutrients and dries out the soil. Covering the soil keeps it moist, cooler, and feeds future crops as it rots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, jwɛi ni he tse ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ la ni ashãa lɛ fiteɔ niyenii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ, ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli gĩɔ. Mulching yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii kɛji egbo.

english: Is it better for me to plant only one crop on my farmland or mix different crops together?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kome yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi ni akɛfutu mli?

english: Mixing crops, like planting cassava with groundnuts, protects your investment. Groundnuts feed the soil with nitrogen while cassava grows, and if pest or weather ruins one crop, you still have the other harvest to sell.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni akɛfutuɔ, tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ Ye obua ni obu oshika ni okɛwo mli lɛ he ŋmei kɛ nitrogen haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ be mli ni ŋmei miida lɛ. Ni kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kpata ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ ko hiɛ? Oyɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni obaahɔ̃ɔ lolo.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak plants and very small yields compared to crops given enough room to spread their roots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ baa, ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ kɛ akɛto tsei ni yɔɔ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amɛshwã lɛ ahe.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. Adding well-rotted manure or the right fertilizer early in the crop's life restores green leaves and boosts grain formation.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tsu nii yɛ tso lɛ wala shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha tso lɛ baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ ni eha ŋmaa ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil needs animal manure or chemical fertilizer to produce a good harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ koni ewo yibii kpakpai?

english: If your soil hardens easily, dries out fast, or crops grow slowly, organic manure helps build long-term soil structure and moisture holding. Chemical fertilizers give quick nutrient boosts but work best when combined with healthy soil.
ga: Kɛji akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ais oya, egbiɔ oya, loo oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa fiofio. Organic fertilizers yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ woɔ mli oya. Shi etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ akɛtsu nii kɛfata shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ he.

english: Why do my pepper plants look wilted in the afternoon sun even if I water them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbo yɛ shwane hulutsoo be mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: In strong heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than roots can take it up from the soil. Adding mulch around the base of the plant keeps the soil cool and root moisture stable throughout the hottest hours.
ga: yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mulching ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni shishifãi lɛ amli nu lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ bei ni mli edɔ waa lɛ amli.

english: How do I know the right time to start planting my seeds once the rainy season begins?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ aje dumɔwui ashishi beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the ground is thoroughly soaked by two or three heavy rains, not just the first light shower. Planting too early in dry, warm soil can cause young seeds to scorch and fail to sprout.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa shii enyɔ loo etɛ aaawo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Jeee klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ fioo lɛ pɛ ji no. Kɛ́ adu mra tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui bibii lɛ ashã ni amɛkakwɛ̃.

english: Flowers drop when the plant faces extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of specific nutrients like calcium. Keeping moisture consistent in the soil helps tomatoes hold their blossoms until fruit sets.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ kɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa kpe. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli daa loo niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ calcium ni bɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tomatoi ni amɛhiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: What causes small holes in my vegetable leaves, and how do I prevent insects from eating my harvest?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi-vegetable baa lɛ nɔ Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkaye mi-dubii lɛ?

english: Holes are made by pests like caterpillars and beetles feeding on leaf sap and tissue. Inspecting under leaves early and using natural neem sprays or safe targeted treatments keeps pest numbers down before they destroy your whole crop.
ga: Buji jɛɔ kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ baa mli nu kɛ fãji amli kɛbaa. Ni oookwɛ baai lɛ ashishi mra Ni okɛ adebɔɔ mli neem sprays loo tsofai ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛtoɔ he gbɛjianɔ lɛ atsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ayibɔ aba shi dani amɛfite onibii fɛɛ.

english: Why should I change the type of crops I grow on my farmland instead of planting the same food every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsake ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ moŋ fe ni madu niyenii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi?

english: Changing your crops prevents pests and diseases from building up in the soil and helps restore nutrients, which gives you better yields over time.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ lɛ haaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ baa ekoŋŋ. Enɛ baaha oná yibii kpakpai yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Which food crops grow better on sloping land compared to flat lowlands that hold a lot of water?
ga: Mɛɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ gɔŋji lɛ anɔ? Kɛ akɛto hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni nu babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe.

english: Sloping land suits crops like cassava and maize that need well-drained soil, while wet lowlands are better for crops like rice that can tolerate plenty of water.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ lɛ hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni biɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ kplanaa ni nɔ efɔ lɛ hi kɛha tsei tamɔ ŋmãa ni baanyɛ aŋmɛ nu babaoo gbɛ lɛ.

english: What causes my crops to dry up quickly when rains stop, and can changing my crop type help?
ga: Mɛni haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ gbiɔ oya kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa nɛ? Ni ŋmɔshi nibii ahe tsakemɔ baanyɛ aye abua.

english: Crops with shallow roots dry out fast when rain stops, so switching to deep-rooted crops like cowpeas helps them reach water stored deeper in the ground.
ga: Tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ baagbi oya kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ atsake kɛtee tsei ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ, tamɔ tsina ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná nu ni ato yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do crops at the top of my hill dry out faster than the crops growing at the bottom of the slope?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ migɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Water naturally flows downhill due to gravity, leaving the soil on hills drier while moisture settles in the lower land where roots can easily reach it.
ga: Nu hoɔ kɛjɛɔ gɔŋ lɛ shishi yɛ hewalɛ ni tsiɔ nii kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hewɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ gɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ po. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ buaa ehe naa yɛ shishigbɛ hei ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he oya lɛ.

english: Why do I have to dig deeper to find water on high ground than in the lower parts of my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo nu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni mana nu ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ fe ŋmɔ lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Underground water sits much lower beneath hills and high ground, whereas in valleys and low areas, the water level is naturally closer to the surface.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ baa shi yɛ gɔji ashishi kɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ waa nɔ. yɛ be mli ni yɛ jɔɔ lɛ mli kɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ Nu lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why does heavy rain wash away my soil and crops when I plant on a sloping hill?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ mishikpɔŋ kɛ miŋmɔshi nibii kɛji midu nii yɛ gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Rainwater moves very fast down slopes, carrying loose topsoil and fertilizer with it; planting across the slope instead of down it helps slow the water down.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ yaa oya waa kɛyaa ŋshɔ lɛ shishi. Kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu yɛ ŋshɔ lɛ naa moŋ fe ni ooodu shi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu lɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Why do my crops rot when I plant them in flat areas where water collects after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ midu yɛ hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nu buaa ehe naa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Standing water drowns crop roots by cutting off their air supply, which causes the roots to rot and the plant to yellow and die.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi lɛ shwieɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni tso lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egboɔ.

english: How deep do I need to dig into the soil to check if there is enough natural moisture for my crops?
ga: Te ehe baahia ni mafo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ koni mana kɛji adebɔɔ mli nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ?

english: Digging a small pit about arm-length deep allows you to see if the lower soil layers stay dark and moist, showing that water is available for deep crop roots.
ga: Bu bibioo ko ni ooofo ni mli kwɔ fe nine lɛ baaye abua bo ni ona kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli edɔ lolo ni edɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu yɛ kɛha tso lɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ.

english: How can I tell if there is underground water on my land before I decide where to plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi nu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani makpɛ miyiŋ yɛ he ni madu nii yɛ lɛ he?

english: Look for areas where grass and plants stay green during the dry season, or dig shallow test holes in low-lying spots to see if wet soil appears.
ga: Taomɔ hei ni jwɛi kɛ tsei hiɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. aloo atsa kaa bu ko ni mli ekwɔɔɔ yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ koni ona kɛji shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ jeɔ kpo.

english: Why does my soil dry out so fast under the sun even after a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ gbiɔ oya yɛ hulu lɛ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Bare soil loses moisture quickly through evaporation under direct heat; covering the soil around your crops with dry leaves or grass helps trap water in the ground longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwie Oŋmɔshinii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Can I plant corn and cowpeas in the same field during the same season?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ tsina ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ be kome mli?

english: Yes, planting corn and cowpeas together works very well. Cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil, which feeds the hungry corn plants and helps both crops produce a good harvest without exhausting your land.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ tsina ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa. Cowpeas mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ejieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni haa ŋmãa tsei ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ niyenii Ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai ni amɛfiteee oshikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Will planting beans alongside my corn help reduce weeds on my farm?
ga: Ani ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmeii ahe lɛ baaye abua ni jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi?

english: Yes, bean plants spread low across the ground and cover the bare dirt between corn rows. This living green cover blocks sunlight from reaching the soil, preventing weed seeds from sprouting easily.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ni ato lɛ ateŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni hiɛ ka nɛɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi dumɔwui anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ mlɛo.

english: What happens to the soil after I harvest a field of beans or cowpeas?
ga: Mɛni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mikpa ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli sɛɛ?

english: When bean or cowpea plants finish growing, their leftover roots and leaves break down into rich organic matter that leaves nitrogen behind, making the soil more fertile for the next crop you plant.
ga: Kɛji bean loo cowpea tso lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai ni eshwɛ lɛ mli fãa kɛfeɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa babaoo ni amɛshiɔ nitrogen yɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni baa shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my cowpeas grow so differently compared to my corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpeas lɛ miida yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ fe mi-corn lɛ?

english: Corn is a grass-family crop that grows straight up on a single tall stalk to reach full sunlight, while cowpeas are bushy legumes that spread wide along the ground to cover soil and make their own plant nutrients.
ga: Abɛi ji jwɛi weku ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ tso kakadaŋŋ kome nɔ koni enine ashɛ hulu la ni fa nɔ. Shi cowpea lɛ, eji ŋmei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli ni gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛfee lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehe niyenii.

english: Do cowpeas need the same amount of rainfall as corn to produce good food?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ he miihia tsina ŋmeii koni amɛná niyenii kpakpa?

english: No, cowpeas need less water than corn. Cowpeas have deep root systems and natural traits that help them tolerate dry spells, making them reliable even when rains are light or unpredictable.
ga: Dabi, tsina ŋmeii biɔ nu fioo fe ŋmãa. Cowpeas yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ adebɔɔ mli sui ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ nugbɔshiimɔ bei lɛ. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ nɛɔ fioo loo anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba po.

english: Why does my corn crop require so much sunlight and space between plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ he hiaa hulu la babaoo kɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ tsei ateŋ lɛ?

english: Corn leaves act like solar panels that need direct sunlight to build big cobs. If corn plants are crowded too close together, they shade each other out and produce small or empty cobs.
ga: Abɛi baai tsuɔ nii tamɔ hulu la, ni ebiɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni efee ŋmeii agboi. Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaafee amɛhe shade ni amɛbaawo dumɔwui bibii bibii. loo dumɔwui ni nɔ ko bɛ mli

english: Does the size of a crop's seed affect how deep I should plant it in the dirt?
ga: Ani dumɔwui lɛ adalɛ saa bɔ ni esa akɛ madu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he?

english: Yes, larger seeds like corn have more stored energy to push up through thick soil, while smaller seeds must be planted closer to the surface so they do not run out of energy before sprouting above ground.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui wuji, tamɔ ŋmãa, yɛ hewalɛ babaoo ni ato ni amɛkɛbaatsɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ amɛtsi amɛhe kɛya ŋwɛi. yɛ be mli ni ehe hiaa ni adu dumɔwui bibii ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ lɛ. Enɛ ji koni ehewalɛ akafite dani eda yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some bean varieties have large seeds while others have very small seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii komɛi yɛ dumɔwui wuji yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu yɛ dumɔwui bibii waa lɛ?

english: Seed size varies by crop variety based on how the plant adapted. Large seeds give young seedlings a stronger boost during early growth, while smaller seed varieties often mature faster and resist heat better.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ adalɛ srɔtoi yɛ tso henɔi lɛ anaa. Edamɔ bɔ ni tso lɛ tsakeɔ ehe ehaa lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui wuji yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛhe wa yɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee mli. yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui bibii lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛdara oya ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛshi dɔlɛ naa.

english: Why are cowpeas recommended for areas with poor or worn-out farm soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ akɛ tsina ŋmei atsu nii yɛ hei ni ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii loo efite lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are tough crops because their roots partner with natural soil bacteria to produce their own nitrogen fertilizer, allowing them to grow well in weak soil where other crops struggle.
ga: Cowpeas ji tsei ni wa ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ sũ mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ feɔ ekome yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛfee amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ haa amɛshwereɔ yɛ shikpɔji ni bɛ hewalɛ nɔ ni tsei krokomɛi bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ yɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why is it important to use different seed hole sizes when planting corn versus small beans?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ dumɔwui akui srɔtoi atsu nii kɛ́ adu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa?

english: Different seeds need different amounts of room to pass through planting tools without getting damaged or clustered together. Matching the hole size to the seed size ensures only one or two seeds drop at a time for proper spacing.
ga: Dumɔwui srɔtoi biɔ hei srɔtoi koni amɛtsɔ dumɔwui ahe nibii lɛ amli ni amɛfiteee loo amɛbuaa amɛhe naa. Kɛ́ akɛ bu lɛ dalɛ to dumɔwui lɛ adalɛ he lɛ, ehaa dumɔwui kome loo enyɔ pɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be kome mli koni aná gbɛ ni sa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil is low on nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding well-rotted animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do experienced farmers tell me to plant groundnuts together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ baakɛɛ mi akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ adu ŋmãa?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which naturally takes nitrogen gas from the air and puts it into the soil. Planting them alongside maize naturally feeds the soil, helping your maize grow better without needing as much expensive chemical fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts ji legume weku lɛ mlinyo, ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ejieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu ŋmã yɛ ŋmãa he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ye obua o-abele lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Why do my crops yield less when I plant seeds saved from my last harvest instead of buying certified seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni mihere kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Mohu ɔ, mo he dumɔwuhi nɛ a wo he odase ɔ.

english: Saved seeds lose their vigor over time and can carry diseases from the previous season into the new farm. Certified seeds are specially produced to resist common pests, withstand tough weather, and yield larger crops.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ he waaa yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli, ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ helai ni jɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ aya ŋmɔ hee mli. Afee dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ. Edamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai anaa ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo

english: Why should I avoid planting my corn seeds very close to each other in a line?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa mli lɛ ahe?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the grown plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough food and space to form full, healthy ears of corn.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ he ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmãa toi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the inside leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi-baby corn lɛ mli baai lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a pest that feeds on the soft growing core of young maize. Identifying them early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extracts into the funnel of the plant stops them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmãa bibii ni miida lɛ shishigbɛ. Amɛyoomɔ mra kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii. Tsi amɛ gbɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: How do I know when my groundnuts hidden underground are mature enough to dig up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-ŋmeii ni mikɛtee shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ atsa?

english: You can check by harvesting two or three test plants across your farm. Open the pods: if the inner shell wall has turned a dark brown or dark color and the seeds are firm and full, your crop is ready for harvest.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ enɛ kɛtsɔ kaa tsei enyɔ loo etɛ ni oookpa yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ nɔ. Gbelemɔ pods lɛ: Kɛji mligbɛ ŋmei lɛ gbogboi lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ. ni dumɔwui lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyi obɔ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eshɛ he kɛha kpamɔ.

english: What causes my cassava tubers to turn soft and rotten in the soil before harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpaa?

english: Cassava root rot happens when too much water settles around the roots, causing fungal infections. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the tubers stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji nu babaoo ba shishifãi lɛ ahe. kɛ fungal infection baa Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni yitso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why is it bad to plant tomatoes in the exact same spot on my land season after season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu tomato yɛ he kome yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be lɛ?

english: Planting tomatoes repeatedly in the same soil allows tomato-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground over time. Rotating your land with crops like maize or cassava breaks the life cycle of these diseases.
ga: Tomato ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, kooloi kɛ helai ni kɔɔ tomato he lɛ baabua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa Ebaatsake helai nɛɛ ashihilɛ.

english: Pepper flowers often drop off due to extreme heat stress, dry soil, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer that causes the plant to produce leaves instead of fruit. Regular watering during hot dry spells helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni haa tso lɛ woɔ baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ lɛ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ aduawai.

english: Why do weeds make my crops produce very small harvest even when there is good rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awo yibii babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than regular crops and aggressively steal the nutrients, water, and sunlight meant for your plants. Clearing weeds early in the plant's life ensures your crop gets all the nourishment it needs to yield well.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ daa lɛ, ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ aha otsei lɛ waa. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi yɛ gbekɛbiiashi lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ náa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize turning yellow even though I cannot see any insects on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? He ni anyɛɛɛ ana kooloi bibii komɛi yɛ?

english: Yellow leaves do not always mean pest damage; they often indicate that your soil is lacking essential nutrients like nitrogen, or that the plant is getting too much or too little water.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be baa ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fiteɔ nii. Bei pii lɛ, amɛtsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo akɛ tso lɛ miiná nu babaoo loo fioo pɛ.

english: If my cassava plants drop their leaves during the dry season, does it mean the crop is dead?
ga: Kɛji mi-cassava tsei lɛ baa lɛ fite yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ Ani no tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbo?

english: No, shedding leaves is a natural defense mechanism for cassava during dry weather to save water, and new leaves will sprout once the rains return.
ga: Dabi, baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ŋmei he yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ be mli koni ekɛbu nu he. Ni baai heei baakwɛ̃ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato leaves curl in intense heat to reduce their surface area and prevent water loss, which is normal as long as the plant recovers once temperatures cool down.
ga: Akɛ la shwieɔ tomato baai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛha ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ aba shi ni nu akafite. Enɛ ji nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa, be fɛɛ be ni tso lɛ he baajɔ lɛ beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ lɛ.

english: How can I tell if a dark patch on my cocoa pod is from black pod disease or just natural pod wilt?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cocoa ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ jɛ black pod hela loo adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii kɛkɛ?

english: Black pod disease creates a fast-spreading dark spot with a distinct white mold and foul smell, whereas natural wilt causes the young pod to simply shrivel and turn brown without mold.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ diji ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya baa. Eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ ni mli tse kɛ ŋmɔtɔ fɔŋ. Yɛ be mli ni adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔtɔ haa ŋmɔtɔ bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli lɛ.

english: Is it safe for me to use the same knapsack sprayer for weed killers and insect sprays?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ jwɛi kɛ kooloi anɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ baatsu nii?

english: It is risky because leftover traces of weed killer in the tank can burn or kill your crops when you later spray them for insects, even after rinsing.
ga: Oshara yɛ ejaakɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni ashi yɛ tanki lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã loo efite onibii kɛji okɛ ŋmeii lɛ shwie ŋmeii lɛ anɔ sɛɛ mli. Beni afɔ lɛ sɛɛ po

english: Can I mix two different farm chemicals together in my spraying tank to save time and work?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ ŋmɔ mli tsofai enyɔ afutu yɛ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ lɛ mli koni mikɛ be kɛ nitsumɔ akafite?

english: Mixing unapproved chemicals can cause a bad reaction that weakens their effectiveness, clogs your equipment, or burns your crop leaves.
ga: Tsofai ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ ni akɛfutuɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha nɔ ko ni ehiii aba ni baaha tsofa lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ. Etsiɔ otsɔne lɛ naa. loo eha tsei ahe baai lɛ ashã

english: Should I spray liquid fertilizer directly onto crop leaves or put dry fertilizer into the soil?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ nu ni ji ŋmɔshi nibii afɔ tso lɛ baai anɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he?

english: Soil fertilizer provides long-term feeding for roots, while leaf spraying is meant only for quick, temporary feeding when crops show urgent nutrient deficiencies.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ niyenii ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. Yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ yibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ koni akɛye niyenii oya yɛ be kukuoo mli beni tsei lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa oya lɛ kpo lɛ.

english: How long must I wait after spraying pest medicine before I can safely harvest and sell my vegetables?
ga: Kɛ́ mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ efɔ nɔ lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani manyɛ makpa aduawai ni mahɔ̃ɔ lɛ shweshweeshwe?

english: Every chemical has a specific pre-harvest waiting period listed on the bottle, usually between 3 to 14 days, which allows the poison to break down completely before harvest.
ga: Tsofai fɛɛ yɛ be ni akɛmɛɛɔ dani akpaa nibii ni atsɔɔ yɛ tɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ yaa nɔ yɛ gbii 3 kɛyashi 14 teŋ, ni no haa tsofa fɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ kwraa dani akpaa.

english: Why do I feel dizzy and get skin rashes after spraying my farm with crop chemicals?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mihe feɔ mi shoo ni mihewolo nɔ shwieɔ shi beni mikɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ shwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: These are signs of chemical poisoning caused by inhaling fumes or getting spray drift on your bare skin, which happens when you spray without protective clothing.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji tsofa ni gbeɔ mɔ ni lasu loo aerosol ni shwieɔ ohewolo ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ he okadii. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie shi ni owooo atadei ni buɔ mɔ he.

english: Could spraying my vegetables right before harvest cause health problems for the people who buy them at the market?
ga: Ani mi-aduawai lɛ ni mikɛshwieɔ shi dani akpaa lɛ baaha gbɔmɛi ni heɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ aná hewalɛnamɔ he naagbai?

english: Yes, harvesting too soon after spraying leaves toxic chemical residues on food, which can cause severe stomach illness or long-term health issues for consumers.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa mra tsɔ yɛ be mli ni ashwieɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ lɛ haa tsofai ni yɔɔ gbeyei shwieɔ niyenii lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ aná tsɛŋemɔ hela ni naa wa loo helatsamɔ mli naagbai ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Officer, why do my plantain leaves turn yellow and dry up during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Ofisa Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When temperatures rise, plantain leaves naturally curl or turn yellow to protect the plant from losing too much water. Ensuring your soil stays rich in organic matter helps the roots hold water longer during hot days.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ lɛ, Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni tso lɛ akafite nu babaoo. Kɛ́ oha oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi obɔ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛhiɛ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli.

english: Officer, why does my plantain tree produce so many smaller shoots around its base, and should I leave them all?
ga: Nitsulɔi Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii babaoo ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ, ni ani esa akɛ mashi ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ yɛ nɔ?

english: Plantain plants produce suckers to reproduce naturally. However, if you leave too many suckers attached, they will steal water and nutrients from the main stem, resulting in smaller plantain bunches. It is best to keep only two or three strong suckers per plant.
ga: Plantains woɔ ŋmeii yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛfɔ. Shi, kɛji oshi ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, Ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantains lɛ feɔ bibii. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookwɛ tso kome mli ŋmeii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Officer, why do my young crops wilt in the middle of the day even when the ground feels slightly moist?
ga: Ofisa Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ fioo moŋ?

english: In intense afternoon heat, young plants lose water through their leaves faster than their tender roots can pull it up from the soil. They usually recover in the evening once the sun cools down, but shade crops can help protect them.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Tsei bibii lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, amɛhe jɔɔ amɛ gbɛkɛ beni hulu lɛ edɔ lɛ. Shi tsei ni yɔɔ shade mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni abu amɛhe.

english: Officer, how can I get early warnings or signs about approaching droughts so I do not waste my seeds?
ga: Officer Te abaafee tɛŋŋ aná kɔkɔbɔɔi loo okadii ni kɔɔ hɔmɔ he mra? Bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ akafite?
