english: Extension offices and weather services monitor seasonal rainfall patterns and send out alerts. Paying attention to local radio farming updates and observing soil moisture trends helps you time your sowing right before stable rain arrives.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he nitsumɔhe lɛ kɛ Extension Office lɛ kwɛɔ bɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ kɔkɔbɔɔi majeɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ojwɛŋmɔ ma maŋ lɛ mli redio nɔ okwaayeli he saji heei anɔ ni okwɛ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ha lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni oto dumɔwui ahe gbɛjianɔ dani nugbɔ aba.

english: Officer, why do black spots suddenly appear on my plantain leaves after a long period of continuous rain?
ga: Ofisa, mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji je kpo trukaa yɛ mi plantain baai lɛ anɔ beni nugbɔ enɛ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: High moisture and damp air create the perfect conditions for fungal diseases like Black Sigatoka to spread. The fungus attacks the leaf surface, reducing the plant's ability to turn sunlight into food for the plantain bunch.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Black Sigatoka, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni tutuaa baai lɛ anɔ lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ. Ehaa tso lɛ nyɛmɔ ni ekɛtsakeɔ hulu la lɛ efeɔ niyenii kɛhaa plantains lɛ baa shi.

english: Officer, what causes my plantain stem to rot and break from the inside before the fruit is ready for harvest?
ga: Nitsulɔi Mɛni haa mi dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛtswaa kɛjɛɔ mli dani yibii lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa?

english: This is usually caused by crop pests like root nematodes or stem borers that burrow into the tissue, weakening the plant from within. Using clean planting material and practicing farm sanitation stops these pests from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ shishifã nematodes loo stem borers ni buɔ kɛboteɔ fãji lɛ amli lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛ emligbɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔ nii ni he tse tsu nii ni akɛ hetsemɔ kpakpa tsu nii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Officer, why is it recommended to plant plantains alongside young cocoa trees on fresh farmland?
ga: Amralofoi Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ adu plantains yɛ cocoa tsei bibii ahe yɛ sũ ŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot survive direct, harsh sunlight when they are small. Plantains grow fast with large leaves that create a cool canopy, giving the young cocoa shade while giving you food to harvest early on.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ tɛ̃ɛ beni amɛdarako lɛ. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli ejɔ. Ehaa kookoo ŋmɔlɔ ni mli tse yɛ be mli ni ehaa bo niyenii kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ mra.

english: Officer, is it safe to put chicken manure directly around my plantain crops, or will it damage the plants?
ga: Nitsulɔi Ani ehi akɛ akɛ tsina ŋmɔtɔ baabɔle he? Mi dumɔwui lɛ tɛ̃ɛ Aloo ebaafite tso lɛ.

english: Fresh chicken manure is very hot and rich in ammonia, which can burn plant roots if applied directly. You should let the manure decompose and mix with dried leaves or soil for a few weeks before applying it near the crop.
ga: Kooloo ŋmɔtɔ ni afee ehee lɛ mli edɔ waa ni ammonia babaoo yɛ mli. ni baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi kɛji akɛ akɛtsu nii tɛ̃ɛ Esa akɛ oha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbala ni ekɛ baai loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi afutu otsii fioo komɛi dani okɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Officer, why do plantain crops fall over so easily during heavy windstorms compared to other trees?
ga: Nitsulɔi Mɛni hewɔ tsei bibii lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa lɛ mli kɛ akɛto tsei krokomɛi ahe lɛ?

english: Plantains do not have deep taproots; instead, they have shallow roots that spread near the topsoil. When the soil becomes heavy with water during rainy weather, strong winds can easily pull up the shallow root base.
ga: Plantains bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ, shi moŋ eyɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala shishitoo ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ mlɛo.

english: Officer, how do I know if the very first rain of the season is enough to start planting my crops?
ga: Nitsulɔi Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni mikɛje miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishi?

english: The first rain often moistens only the very top surface of the soil, which dries out quickly if dry weather returns. It is best to wait for two or three steady rains so the deeper root zones hold enough moisture for seeds to germinate safely.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ yiteŋgbɛ pɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ. ni baagbi oya kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ ku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ koni eha shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my crops stop growing well after the heavy rains end around November in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekpaa shweremɔ jogbaŋŋ beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ba naagbee yɛ November mli yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Most crops rely heavily on consistent soil moisture. When the rainy season ends late in the year, high temperatures and dry Harmattan winds rapidly evaporate soil water, causing plants to wilt, stop growing, or die if extra water isn't provided.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ daa lɛ nɔ waa. Kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ ba naagbee yɛ afi lɛ naagbee lɛ, Harmattan latsaa ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ nɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ shi oya. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, tso lɛ baagbi, ebaakpa dalɛ, loo ebaagbo kɛji nu kroko fataaa he.

english: How can I prepare my farm in July so that my crops do not suffer when the dry season starts later in the year?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ July mli koni miŋmɔshi nibii akafite beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ afi lɛ naagbee gbɛ lɛ?

english: You can prepare by collecting and storing rainwater in tanks while it rains in July, applying thick organic mulch around crop roots to trap soil moisture, and setting up simple irrigation lines before the rains dry up around November.
ga: Obaanyɛ osaa ohe kɛtsɔ nugbɔ nu ni ooobua naa ni okɛto baagi mli be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ July mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛ organic mulch ni mli edɔ atsu nii. Abɔle tsei lɛ ashishifãi ahe koni akɛmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli ni ato nu ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he gbɛjianɔ mlɛo Dani nugbɔ lɛ agbi yɛ November he.

english: When is the best time of the year in Ghana to harvest and store water for dry season farming?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ Ghana ni akɛkpaa nu ni akɛtoɔ kɛha hulutsoo be mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: The best time to harvest rainwater is during the main peak of the rainy season, around May to July. Storing water in tanks or farm ponds during these heavy rains ensures you have a reliable supply when dry weather sets in from November onward.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akpa nugbɔ nu ji be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ. Aaafee May kɛyashi July Nu ni okɛtoɔ tanki loo nubui amli yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa nɛɛ mli lɛ haa onáa nu ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbiɔ kɛjɛɔ November mli lɛ.

english: Why are some crops like tomatoes so sensitive to water shortages compared to crops like cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi, tamɔ tomato, nuɔ nu he waa kɛ akɛto tsei tamɔ ŋmei he lɛ?

english: Vegetable crops like tomatoes have shallow roots and tender leaves that lose water very quickly in hot weather. Cassava has deeper root systems and tougher leaves designed to store water, making it much more resistant to drought.
ga: Aduawai tsei tamɔ tomato yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni nu lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ. Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ baai ni wa ni afee koni amɛhiɛ nu mli. Enɛ haa enyɛɔ eshiɔ hɔmɔ babaoo.

english: Why do my crop leaves wilt and drop off when there is a short break in the rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛɔ be kukuoo ko lɛ?

english: Wilting and dropping leaves is a plant's natural defense mechanism to stay alive. By shedding leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the sun, which stops it from losing too much water through evaporation.
ga: Baai lɛ gboɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi akɛ tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo kɛha wala. Kɛtsɔ baai ni amɛshwieɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tsei lɛ haa hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ amɛhiɛ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu ni hoɔ fe nine lɛ akafite kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: What happens to the soil on my farm when the rains stop completely in December?
ga: Mɛni baaba shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa kwraa yɛ December mli?

english: Without regular rainfall, topsoil loses its moisture and hardens into a tough crust. This makes it difficult for plant roots to breathe or absorb remaining nutrients, causing sensitive crops to dry up very quickly.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ daa lɛ Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ ni ehaa efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni wa. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaamu loo amɛŋɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ. Ehaa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ egbiɔ oya waa.

english: What is a greenhouse, and how does it actually protect my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji greenhouse ni te ebaafee tɛŋŋ ebu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe diɛŋtsɛ?

english: A greenhouse is a simple structure made of plastic or mesh netting that covers your crops. It creates a protected environment that shields delicate plants from excessive heat, dry winds, heavy downpours, and destructive insect pests.
ga: Greenhouse ji nɔ ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni akɛ plastic loo ŋtayaa fee ni haa oŋmɔshi nibii ahe. Feemɔ shihilɛ ko ni abuɔ he ni buɔ tsei ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ waa lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni fe nine, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do agricultural officers say that a greenhouse system is like gold for a farmer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he onukpai lɛ kɛɔ akɛ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai tamɔ shika tsuru kɛha okwaafoi lɛ?

english: Greenhouses allow you to grow delicate, high-value crops like sweet peppers year-round, even in the dry season. Because you control the water and environment, you get higher yields and can sell produce when market prices are highest.
ga: Greenhouses haa onyɛɔ oduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni jara wa waa tamɔ bell peppers afi muu lɛ fɛɛ, yɛ hulutsoo be mli po, ejaakɛ bo ji mɔ ni kudɔɔ nu lɛ kɛ shihilɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. Obaaná yibii babaoo ni obaanyɛ ohɔ̃ɔ onibii lɛ be mli ni jara lɛ nɔ jara wa fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: How does growing crops inside a greenhouse shelter help save water compared to open field farming?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa nu baa shi kɛ akɛto ŋmɔ mli okwaayeli he?

english: Inside a greenhouse, hot winds and direct sunlight are reduced. This slows down the rate at which water evaporates from the soil and plant leaves, meaning your crops need significantly less water to stay healthy.
ga: Yɛ greenhouse lɛ mli Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa nu ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ tsei ahe baai amli lɛ shwieɔ shi oya. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu fioo pɛ he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I still harvest fresh vegetables in Ghana during the dry season without relying on rain?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ akpa aduawai heei yɛ Ghana yɛ fɛ̃i be mli ni akɛ he fɔ̃ɔɔɔ nugbɔ nɔ?

english: Yes, you can harvest vegetables year-round by using protected structures like greenhouses or controlled drip irrigation systems, allowing you to feed crops with small amounts of stored water even when there is no rain.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okpa aduawai afi muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛtsɔ nɔ ko ni abuɔ he tamɔ greenhouse loo nu ni hoɔ ni akudɔ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa okɛ nu fioo ni ato lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii niyenii yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ po.

english: How do I know when my cocoa tree is ready to start producing pods?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni kookoo tso lɛ efee klalo akɛ ebaaje ŋmɔtɔ shishi?

english: Cocoa trees usually start flowering and bearing fruit about 3 to 5 years after planting, depending on the variety. You will notice small flowers growing directly on the trunk and main branches when the tree reaches maturity.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo tsei jeɔ fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 5 sɛɛ beni adu amɛ, ni enɛ damɔ henɔ ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ nɔ. Obaana fɔfɔi bibii. ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi kɛ eniji wuji lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ beni tso lɛ daa lɛ

english: Why are my cocoa trees growing so tall, and how does that affect my harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiya hiɛ waa lɛ? Ni te enɛ saa mikpamɔ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally reach upward to compete for sunlight if they are not pruned. Very tall trees make harvesting difficult and dangerous, while regular height control keeps pods within easy reach and encourages the tree to produce more branches and fruit.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ shɛɔ ŋwɛi yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la kɛji akɛ afolɔɔɔ amɛ. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ waa lɛ haa nikpamɔ feɔ nɔ ni wa ni eyɛ oshara. yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ haa pod lɛ shɛɔ he ni eshɛɔ he oya. ni ewo tsei hewalɛ koni amɛwo tsei niji kɛ aduawai babaoo

english: Why should I prune branches from my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maŋɔ ŋmeii kɛjɛ kookoo tso ni eda lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or overcrowded branches, allowing air and sunlight to move freely through the canopy. This reduces humidity that causes black pod disease and directs the tree's energy into producing bigger, healthier pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni eyi obɔ lɛ. Bɔni afee ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la anyɛ atsɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli oya. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ baa shi, ni ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Does cocoa grow better under big shade trees or in open sunlight?
ga: Ani kookoo kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ tsei wuji ashishi loo yɛ hei ni gbɛ yɔɔ?

english: Young cocoa trees need heavy shade to protect their young leaves from drying out, but mature cocoa needs a balance of light shade and controlled sunlight to produce abundant flowers and pods.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ni mli wa koni ebu baai bibii lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbi. Shi kookoo ni edara lɛ he miihia kane ni sa kɛ hulu la ni akudɔ lɛ koni ekɛ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii babaoo aba.

english: Ripe cocoa pods change color. Green pods turn bright yellow when ready, while red or purple pods turn orange-yellow. Harvesting pods when they are fully ripe ensures the beans inside have properly developed sugar and flavor.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛji amɛfee klalo. yɛ be mli ni pods tsuru loo purple lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ-ŋmei. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmeii lɛ beni amɛkwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ, ehaa kɔfi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ feɔ sugar kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni sa.

english: Are there modern tools or machinery that can help me harvest high cocoa pods easily?
ga: Ani ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ nibii loo tsɔnei komɛi yɛ ni baanyɛ aye abua mi ni makpa kookoo ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ lɛ mlɛo?

english: Yes, extension offices promote motorized pruning saws and extended telescopic harvesting poles. These tools allow you to cut pods high up in the tree cleanly from the ground without having to climb or strain.
ga: Hɛɛ, Extension Office lɛ woɔ tsɔnei ni akɛfoɔ tsei kɛ tsei ni akɛkpaa tsei ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ ahe hewalɛ. Nɛkɛ dɛŋdadei nɛɛ haa onyɛɔ ofoɔ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ yɛ gbɛ ni he tse nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni okɛ ohe wooo mli loo okɛ ohe wooo mli.

english: Why is it bad to twist or tear cocoa pods off the trunk with my bare hands?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ okɛ oniji ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko baatsɔ loo obaagbala kookoo ŋmeii kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Tearing pods off damages the small bump on the trunk called the flower cushion. Future flowers and pods only grow from this cushion, so damaging it means that part of the tree will never produce cocoa again.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii lɛ, efiteɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ. Atsɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ akɛ fɔfɔi akushin. Wɔsɛɛ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii baakwɛ̃ kɛjɛ kushin nɛɛ pɛ mli. Nɔ ni fiteɔ tamɔ nɛkɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ fã ko wooo kookoo dɔŋŋ.

english: Why do some of my small cocoa pods shrivel up and die before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii So mine lɛ gboɔ ni egboɔ dani edaa lɛ?

english: This is often 'cherelle wilt,' a natural reaction where the tree sheds excess young pods it cannot feed, or it can be caused by fungal diseases and insect pests. Keeping the farm clean and applying proper fertilizer helps save more pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji ‘cherel wilt’, ni ji adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni tso lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii ni fa fe nine ni enyɛŋ ekɛ niyenii aha amɛ lɛ. Aloo ekolɛ fungal helai kɛ kooloi bibii kɛbaa. Kɛ́ oha oŋmɔ lɛ mli tse ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ato.

english: How can I get my cocoa farm to produce more pods so I can make more money?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ awo pods babaoo koni maná shika babaoo?

english: You can boost your yield by applying recommended fertilizers, regularly clearing weeds, removing diseased pods quickly, and maintaining proper shade so the trees have the nutrients and strength to support a heavy crop.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha onibii lɛ aya hiɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ okɛbaatsu nii lɛ nɔ. Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ kɛjɛ ohe daa. Jiemɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya. ni ekwɛ hulutsoo ni sa nɔ koni eha tsei lɛ aná niyenii kɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛye amɛbua ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii.

english: Why does my cocoa tree produce lots of pods during one part of the year and very few during others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ afi lɛ fã ko mli, ni bei krokomɛi hu woɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowering follows the rainy and dry seasons in Ghana. The main rainy season triggers heavy flowering that leads to the main harvest, while lighter rains lead to a smaller mid-crop harvest later in the year.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ damɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be nɔ yɛ Ghana. Nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ kɛ fɔfɔi babaoo ni kɛ kpamɔ titri lɛ baa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be lɛ teŋgbɛ baafee bibioo yɛ afi lɛ naagbee gbɛ.

english: Why do my crops dry up faster when I plant them close to certain big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛ́ midu yɛ tsei wuji komɛi ahe lɛ?

english: Big trees have large root systems that actively draw water from deep and shallow soil, leaving very little moisture for smaller food crops planted nearby.
ga: Tsei ni eda lɛ yɛ shishifãi wuji ni gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa niyenii bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ fioo pɛ.

english: How do large trees steal food and nutrients away from my food crops?
ga: Te tsei wuji feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ mi niyenii ni miduɔ lɛ mli?

english: Tree roots spread wide under the ground to feed on the same soil nutrients that your food crops need, often consuming those nutrients faster than young crops can.
ga: Tso shishifãi gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi koni amɛye niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni he hiaa oniyenii tsei lɛ. Amɛfɔɔ nakai niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ yeli oya fe bɔ ni tsei bibii baanyɛ aye.

english: Why are the roots of my food crops struggling to grow near forest trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi niyenii tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ miitao ni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Large trees create a thick underground network of roots that physically blocks smaller crop roots from expanding and getting enough water and nutrients.
ga: Tsei wuji lɛ feɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni mli eyi obɔ ni tsiɔ tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛhe nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Is it better for me to leave large shade trees on my cocoa farm or cut them down?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mashi tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ loo mafo amɛ?

english: Leaving a few beneficial shade trees helps protect cocoa from harsh sunlight, but too many trees will compete with cocoa for water and nutrients, harming your pod yield.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi tsei fioo komɛi ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu kookoo lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Shi tsei babaoo tsɔ kɛ kookoo yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ náa o-pod yibiiwoo lɛ nɔ hewalɛ ni ehiii.

english: How do I know if a tree on my farm is good or bad for my cocoa trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hi loo ehiii kɛha mi cacao tsei lɛ?

english: Good trees usually drop beneficial leaf litter and don't drink excessive soil water, while bad trees have aggressive roots that steal water and cast too much dark shade.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ shiɔ baai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ amɛsɛɛ ni amɛnuuu nu babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsei ni ehiii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni kɛ nu he akaŋ ni amɛhaa hulutsoo be ni mli ewo duŋ fe nine baa.

english: Will tree shade help my cocoa survive the hot dry season?
ga: Ani tsei ahe hulutsoo baaye abua mikoo lɛ ni ehi shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli hɔmɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, moderate tree shade cools the farm and prevents young cocoa leaves from scorching, provided the tree doesn't suck up all the ground water during dry spells.
ga: Hɛɛ, tso ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni sa lɛ baaha ŋmɔ lɛ mli afee fɛ̃i. ni ehaaa kookoo baai bibii lɛ ashã. Kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ fɛɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli

english: Should I clear every single tree off my land before planting my food crops?
ga: Ani esa akɛ majie tso fɛɛ tso kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu niyenii?

english: You don't need to cut everything down; removing trees with wide, greedy roots helps food crops grow, while keeping selected trees can protect soil health.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa ni ofo nɔ fɛɛ nɔ mli. Tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ ni amɛyeɔ nii babaoo lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa niyenii tsei ni amɛdaraa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni ahala lɛ ni aaahi shi lɛ baanyɛ abu shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛnamɔ he.

english: Can I grow cassava and yam directly under big tree branches?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ tsei wuji aniji ashishi tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Most food crops need direct sunshine and free root space to produce heavy tubers, so planting them under dense tree canopies will make them weak and low-yielding.
ga: Niyenii tsei babaoo biɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ kɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hegbɛ koni amɛwo ŋmeii ni tsii. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ ni amɛbaawo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my crops stay small and weak when grown under dark tree leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ tsei ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Crops require light to process energy and grow; heavy shade from overhead leaves prevents them from making enough food to stay healthy.
ga: Dumɔwui he miihia la koni amɛtsu hewalɛ he nii ni amɛdara. Shade ni tsii ni jɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ amɛyiteŋ lɛ amli lɛ tsiɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafee niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Do food crops and cocoa trees need the same type of field conditions to grow well?
ga: Ani niyenii ni aduɔ kɛ kookoo tsei lɛ he miihia shihilɛi ni amɛdaraa yɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ?

english: No, many food crops prefer full sunlight and open land, whereas young cocoa trees prefer partial shade to protect them during their early stages.
ga: Dabi, niyenii tsei babaoo sumɔɔ hulu ni eyi obɔ kɛ he ko ni yɔɔ faŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kookoo tsei bibii sumɔɔ hulutsoo be fioo ko koni ebu amɛhe yɛ amɛshishijee bei amli.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow and die when water sits on my field for days after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ beni nu hiɔ miŋmɔji amli gbii babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When heavy rain floods your farm, water fills all the small spaces in the soil, pushing out air. Roots need oxygen to breathe and take up food; without air, the roots drown, rot, and cause the leaves to turn yellow and die.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi oŋmɔ lɛ mli Nu lɛ eyiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli hei bibii lɛ fɛɛ amli ni ekɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shwieɔ kpo. Shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa koni amɛmu ni amɛná niyenii. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛbaagboi, ni no baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboi.

english: How does making ridges or mounds on my farm help protect my crops during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni afee yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Building raised ridges or mounds lifts the crop roots above the standing water. Excess rain drains down into the channels between ridges, keeping the main root area moist but not waterlogged.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo gɔji ni afeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ tsei shishifãi anɔ kɛyaa nu ni damɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa ŋshɔkei ni yɔɔ gɔji lɛ ateŋ lɛ amli. Ha shishifã lɛ he titri lɛ afee fɛ̃i shi nu akabote mli.

english: Which crops are best to plant in low areas of my farm that flood easily every year?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei hi jogbaŋŋ ni abaanyɛ akwɛ yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni nu afua fɔɔ baa daa afi lɛ?

english: Crops like rice or sugarcane thrive in low-lying wet areas because their root systems are adapted to wet soil. Roots like cassava or sweet potato will quickly rot if planted in those flood zones.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ nɔ. Shishifãi tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei baafite oya kɛji akɛ adu yɛ hei ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ.

english: How do cover crops like cowpeas stop my topsoil from washing away when heavy rains come?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ tamɔ tsina ŋmei lɛ atsĩ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekaho yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Cover crops carpet the ground with leaves and roots, acting like a protective blanket. The leaves absorb the harsh impact of heavy raindrops, and the root network holds the soil tightly so rain cannot easily wash it away.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ tsei kɛ baai kɛ shishifãi haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he Baai lɛ shwieɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he hewalɛ ni naa wa lɛ. ni shishifãi lɛ hiɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shiŋŋ Nugbɔ nyɛŋ ashwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mlɛo.

english: How do I know if my crops actually need irrigation water during the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ he miihia mi diɛŋtsɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Dig about two to three inches into the soil with your fingers near the plant roots. If the soil feels completely dry and crumbles easily without sticking together when squeezed into a ball, it is time to irrigate.
ga: Kɛ oniji atsu nii ni okɛfo shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli 2-3 inch. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ egbi kwraa ni efoɔ oya ni ekɛ ehe kpaaa gbee kɛji akɛ ashɛre lɛ ni efee bɔɔlu. Etsɔɔ akɛ be eshɛ kɛha nu shwiemɔ.

english: Is it better for me to irrigate my vegetables early in the morning or late in the afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo aduawai anɔ nu leebi loo shwane?

english: Early morning is the best time to irrigate. Water reaches the roots before the hot sun can evaporate it, and any wet leaves dry quickly in the daylight, which stops fungal diseases from spreading on the leaves.
ga: Leebi ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha nu shwiemɔ. Nu lɛ shɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe dani hulu la lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ni baai ni efɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii helai akagbɛ ashwã baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Can using stream water for irrigation harm my crops or soil over time?
ga: Ani faa mli nu ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛshwieɔ nu nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nibii loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ awui yɛ be ni sa mli?

english: Stream water is usually fine for farming, but if it contains high levels of salt or mud washed from upstream, those salts can build up in your soil over time and hinder crop growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu ni yɔɔ faai amli lɛ hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ. Shi kɛji akɛ ŋmei loo muji ni fa babaoo ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ nu lɛ mli lɛ yɛ lɛ, Nakai ŋmei lɛ baanyɛ abua shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli ni etsĩ ŋmɔshi nibii adalɛ naa.

english: Why do my pepper plants curl up their leaves during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in high heat is the plant's natural defense mechanism. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces its exposure to direct sunlight, saving its inner moisture from evaporating too quickly.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Kɛ́ tso lɛ baa lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ehaa hulu la ni tsoɔ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baa shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ akashwie oya tsɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot under the ground when we get too much rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ wɔná nugbɔ babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need well-aerated soil to swell and store starch. Excess rainwater trapped underground creates a wet environment where rot-causing fungi thrive, invading and softening the tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ he miihia cassava shishifãi lɛ koni amɛfuu ni amɛhiɛ starch mli. Nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine ni emɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ baa. he ni ŋmei ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ daa lɛ boteɔ yitso lɛ mli ni ehaa egbɔjɔɔ

english: Why do my young tomato plants fall over after heavy rainstorms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young tomato plants have tender stems and shallow roots that cannot support the weight of heavy rainwater on their leaves or withstand strong ground surface currents. Supporting them with wooden stakes holds them upright until stems strengthen.
ga: Tomato tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ akwɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ baai lɛ anɔ loo amɛnyɛŋ amɛdamɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni hoɔ waa lɛ naa. Tso ni akɛfiɔ esɛɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ shishi baawa.

english: Why do my crops start wilting and dying just a few days after the rain stops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ ni egboɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa lɛ?

english: Crops rely on soil moisture to absorb nutrients and keep themselves cool through their leaves. When rain stops and the soil dries out, plants cannot drink water, causing them to lose their stiffness, wilt, and eventually dry up if the drought continues.
ga: Tsei kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ koni amɛŋɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ anu nu. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe waaa, amɛgboiɔ ni yɛ naagbee lɛ amɛgbiɔ kɛji hɔmɔ lɛ tee nɔ.

english: What happens to the fertilizer and money I put into my farm if the rain does not fall?
ga: Mɛni baa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ shika ni mikɛwoɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ?

english: Fertilizer requires water to dissolve so plant roots can absorb it. Without rain, the fertilizer stays dry in the topsoil or gets washed away by wind, meaning your crops cannot use it and the money spent on inputs is wasted.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ biɔ ni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tso shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Kɛ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii baagbi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ baaŋɔ amɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, anyɛɛɛ akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsu nii ni shika ni akɛwoɔ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ amli lɛ hu fiteɔ.

english: Is there a way I can keep moisture in my soil for longer when the rain fails?
ga: Ani gbɛ ko yɛ ni matsɔ nɔ maha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ?

english: Yes, practicing mulching—covering the soil around your crops with dried leaves, grass, or crop residues—helps trap moisture in the ground, shields the soil from hot sunlight, and reduces water loss.
ga: Hɛɛ, nifeemɔ ni ji mulching—ni ji sũ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli. Okɛ baai ni egboi, jwɛi, loo tsei ni afolɔ ashwie oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ atsu nii—ni eye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Buu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni eha nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi

english: Why are the leaves of my crops curling up and turning yellow during hot dry days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism where the plant shrinks its surface area to stop water from evaporating too quickly under extreme heat. Yellowing occurs when dry conditions prevent the plant from drawing essential nutrients from the soil.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe shi koni nu lɛ akatsɔ oya tsɔ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa shishi. Yellow baa kɛji shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ tsi tsei anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my maize plants produce empty cobs with no grains when there is dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni dumɔwui bɛ mli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize needs a lot of water when it is flowering and producing silks. If dry weather hits during this critical stage, heat and lack of water prevent proper pollination, resulting in empty or poorly filled cobs.
ga: Nu babaoo he miihia ŋmãa kɛ́ ewo fɔfɔi ni ekɛ siliki baa. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ba yɛ haomɔ be nɛɛ mli Dɔlɛ kɛ nu ni faaa lɛ baatsi pollination ni sa naa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ efolo loo amɛyiɔ obɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops completely stop growing during dry spells even though they are not fully dead?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ kwraa yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ amɛgbooo kwraa moŋ?

english: When water becomes scarce, crops enter a survival mode where they stop growing new leaves and stems to conserve the little energy and water they have left until rain comes.
ga: Kɛ nu faaa lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa wala mli, ni ekpaa baai kɛ tsei heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ koni ekɛto hewalɛ fioo kɛ nu fioo ni eshwɛ lɛ he kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ.

english: How can I tell the right time to plant my seeds so I don't lose my investment to early dry weather?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui? Bɔni afee ni mikafite mishika ni mikɛwo mli lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi mra?

english: It is best to wait until the rains become steady and consistent rather than planting after the very first heavy rain, as early false rains are often followed by hot dry spells that destroy young seedlings.
ga: Nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ ofee ji ni omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ be fɛɛ be. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, bei pii lɛ, ahum ni mli edɔ waa ni fiteɔ tsei bibii lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why does the soil on my farm crack open when it gets dry, and how does this harm my plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli fãa kɛ́ egbi lɛ? Ni te enɛ yeɔ mitsei lɛ awui ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Clay and heavy soils shrink and split as water evaporates out of them. These cracks tear fine root systems underground and allow hot air directly into the root zone, damaging the crop's ability to survive.
ga: Clay and heavy soils shrink and break apart as water evaporates. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ gbálaa shishifãi bibii lɛ amli. Go underground and allow hot air directly into the root zone. Efiteɔ nyɛmɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii yɔɔ ni amɛkɛhiɔ shi lɛ.

english: Are there specific crops I can grow in Ghana that do not easily die when rain is scarce?
ga: Ani tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi yɛ ni manyɛ makwɛ yɛ Ghana ni gbooo oya kɛji nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛ?

english: Yes, crops like cassava, millet, sorghum, and cowpeas have deep root systems or naturally low water needs, making them much more resilient to unpredictable rainfall and dry weather than maize or vegetables.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, ŋmãa kɛ tsina ŋmãa yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ loo nu ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ faaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa amɛnyɛɔ amɛshiɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi fe ŋmãa loo aduawai.

english: Why do my newly transplanted seedlings die much faster in dry weather than older plants on the same farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui heei ni midu lɛ gboiɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli fe tsei momo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Young seedlings have short, tender roots that only reach the top layer of soil, which dries out quickly. Older plants have longer, established root systems that reach deeper into the ground where moisture stays longer.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi kukuji ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni shɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yiteŋgbɛ pɛ, ni amɛgbiɔ oya. Tsei ni egbɔ lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni kɛlɛ, ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ. ni boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ

english: Which crop between maize, cassava, and yam will give me the fastest harvest if I need money quickly?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii—ŋmãa, ŋmãa, kɛ ŋmãa—baawo yibii oya fe fɛɛ kɛji akɛ shika he miihia mi oya?

english: Maize is your fastest option, maturing in just 3 to 4 months. Cassava takes 9 to 12 months, while yam takes about 7 to 9 months, making maize the quickest choice for fast financial returns.
ga: Abɛi ji nɔ ni obaanyɛ ohala oya fe fɛɛ. Amɛkwɛɔ yɛ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 pɛ mli, ŋmãa heɔ aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12, yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa ni ŋɔɔ lɛ heɔ aaafee nyɔji 7 kɛyashi 9, ni no haa ŋmãa ji nɔ ni ahala oya fe fɛɛ kɛha shika ni anáa oya.

english: Is it a good idea for me to plant maize and cassava together on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ makwɛ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, intercropping maize and cassava works very well because maize grows quickly and is harvested first, while cassava grows slower and takes over the space after the maize is removed.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa dumɔ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa. Ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya, ni akpaa lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ daa blɛoo ni eŋɔ he ko beni ajie ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves curl up into thin tubes during the hot afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Maize leaves curl up to reduce water loss through evaporation during intense heat; it is the plant's natural defense mechanism to conserve moisture during dry conditions.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni nu ni laajeɔ kɛtsɔ la ni shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ nɔ aba shi. Eji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehiɛɔ nu mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli.

english: Why are my harvested yams coming out small and twisted instead of big and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ ji bibii ni egbɛ eshwa moŋ fe ni eeefee agbo ni eja lɛ?

english: Yams need loose, deep soil and proper mounds to expand properly. Hard, compacted, or stony soil restricts tuber growth, causing them to deform and stay small.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli tse kɛ gɔŋ ni sa he miihia sweet potato koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni wa, ni mli edɔ, loo ni tɛi yɔɔ mli lɛ haaa tuber lɛ ada. ni haa efiteɔ ni efeɔ bibioo

english: How do weeds hurt my young cassava plants if cassava is known to be a tough crop?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aye mi-cassava tsei lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ? Beni ole akɛ ŋmei ji tso ko ni wa akɛ aaakwɛ?

english: While mature cassava is hardy, young cassava shoots grow slowly at first and cannot easily compete with fast-growing weeds for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, which reduces your final yield.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmei daa waa moŋ Shi ŋmeii bibii lɛ baakwɛ̃ fiofio yɛ shishijee mli. ni enyɛŋ ekɛ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ abɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ baaha naagbee nibii ni anáa lɛ aba shi.

english: Can I leave my cassava tubers in the ground if the current market price is too low?
ga: Kɛji akɛ jara ni yɔɔ amrɔ nɛɛ ba shi tsɔ Ani manyɛ mashi ŋmei shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: Yes, cassava can safely remain stored underground for several months after maturing, allowing you to hold off harvesting until market prices improve.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ akɛ ŋmei ato shikpɔŋ shishi shweshweeshwe nyɔji babaoo beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ. Ehaa otsiɔ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ naa kɛyashiɔ jara nɔ jara baaya hiɛ.

english: How can I stop my harvested yams from rotting quickly in storage before I can sell them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-sweet potato ni mikpa lɛ naa koni ekafite oya yɛ nitoohe lɛ dani mahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Store your yams in a shaded, well-ventilated barn off the ground, and handle them carefully during harvest to prevent cuts or bruises, which allow rot-causing fungi to enter.
ga: Kɛ sweet potatoes ato ŋmɔ ko ni yɔɔ hulutsoo, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli. ni okɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli koni akafo loo akatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ abote mli.

english: When is the best time to harvest my maize so I do not lose grains to pests in the field?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa koni ŋmɔ mli ŋmeii akafite ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Harvest your maize as soon as the cobs turn brown and the stalks dry out; leaving dry cobs standing in the field exposes them to insect infestation, mold, and bird damage.
ga: Kpaa ŋmãa kɛji ŋmeii lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ egbi pɛ. Kɛji akɛ ashi ŋmeii ni egbi yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii, ŋmeii kɛ okpoi yeɔ amɛ awui.

english: Why do market buyers offer me such low prices for my maize right at the main harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ haa mi jara ni baa shi nɛkɛ yɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ he yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ titri lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Prices drop during peak harvest because many farmers harvest and sell at the same time, creating an oversupply in the market that allows buyers to negotiate lower prices.
ga: Jara baa shi yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be mli ejaakɛ okwaafoi babaoo kpaa ŋmaa ni amɛhɔ̃ɔ yɛ be kome mli. Enɛ haa nibii ni fa fe nine baa jara nɔ ni haa mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ nyɛɔ amɛsusuɔ jara ni baa shi lɛ he.

english: Why does my land produce less maize every year when I plant it repeatedly on the same plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo daa afi kɛ́ midu shikpɔŋ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Maize consumes a lot of nutrients, especially nitrogen, from the soil. Planting it continuously on the same land without applying fertilizer or manure drains soil fertility and lowers your yield.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo, titri lɛ nitrogen, kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ aya nɔ adu nii yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fiteɔ, ni ehaa yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when the weather becomes very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive roots and delicate leaves that cannot handle direct, burning sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees planted beside them to shield them from high heat and retain moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo tsei ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Enɛ ji koni akafee dɔlɛ ni fe nine ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize crops full of tiny holes and ragged edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni ŋwɛigbɛi ni ekpɔtɔ lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm, which hide inside the central funnel of the plant and eat the tender green leaves. Inspecting the leaf funnels early allows you to spot these pests before they destroy the crop's ability to grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Baai lɛ agbɛi amli kwɛmɔ mra Ebaaye ebua bo ni ona nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ dani amɛfite nyɛmɔ ni odumɔ lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up and turning yellow instead of staying green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow, twisted leaves are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny flying insects called whiteflies. When a plant gets this virus, its leaves cannot capture sunlight properly, leading to much smaller roots beneath the ground at harvest time.
ga: Baai ni etse amɛhe lɛ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Kooloi bibii ni foɔ ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kɛ tsei ná nɛkɛ hela nɛɛ Ebaai lɛ nyɛŋ amɔmɔ hulu la lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli.

english: Why does my maize yield get smaller every time I plant it on the same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ baa shi be fɛɛ be ni madu shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Maize feeds heavily on plant food in the ground, especially nitrogen. Planting it repeatedly in the same spot drains the soil's natural strength, so rotating your plot with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts helps trap fresh nitrogen back into the soil for future crops.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ tsei niyenii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Titri lɛ kɛha nitrogen lɛ, dumɔ ni aduɔ shii abɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii atsake oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ nitrogen hee lɛ aku sɛɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni akɛdu nii wɔsɛɛ.

english: Why does putting too much fertilizer make my crops grow big green leaves but very small fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli fe nine lɛ baabii wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi ewoɔ yibii bibii waa lɛ?

english: Fertilizers high in nitrogen encourage the crop to put all its energy into growing thick stems and leafy foliage instead of setting fruit. Using a balanced fertilizer with phosphorus and potassium gives the plant the right signal to shift energy into flowering and making strong fruits.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ woɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ awo tsei ashishifãi kɛ tsei ahe tsei ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ amli yɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja ni phosphorus kɛ potassium yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ naa okadi ni sa ni amɛkɛtsakeɔ hewalɛ amɛwoɔ fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ mli.

english: Why do my yam vines need to grow up long wooden poles instead of spreading across the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni adu sweet potato wain tsei yɛ tsei kakadaji anɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines onto wooden stakes allows the leaves to spread out and catch as much sunlight as possible. Sunlight gives the vine energy to produce and store food underground, resulting in larger, heavier yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni amɛnáa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Sunlight gives the vines energy to produce and store food underground. As a result, the sweet potato tubers are larger and heavier.

english: These extra shoots, called suckers, compete with the main plantain tree for water and soil nutrients. Removing all but one or two strong suckers ensures the main tree gets enough nourishment to grow a big, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi nɛɛ akɛ suckers. Amɛkɛ plantain titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ yɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off the plant without turning into actual tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ tomato diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the plant suffers from extreme heat stress or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist and protecting plants from the hottest afternoon heat helps the flowers stay attached and form fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa kɛ tsei ahe ni abuɔ kɛjɛɔ shwane la ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛhiɛɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my seeds fail to grow when I plant them immediately after the first light rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first light rain often wets only the surface soil without providing enough deep moisture. If a dry spell follows, the hot ground dries out and kills the germinating seed, so it is safer to wait until the rains become steady before sowing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ hulutsoo ni fa bɔ ni sa haaa. Kɛji hɔmɔ ahum ko nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ, hei ni mli edɔ lɛ baagbi ni egbe dumɔwui ni miikwɛ̃ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ daa dani odu dumɔwui.

english: Why does spreading dry grass around the base of my pepper plants help them survive the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Spreading dry grass around your crops, known as mulching, forms a protective blanket over the soil that keeps the ground cool and slows down water evaporation, allowing plant roots to stay moist longer between waterings.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni ooogbɛ ashwã oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ehaa tsɔne ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ feɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso shishifãi ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ lɛ teŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants are like human babies—they burn easily under full sun and strong wind. Plantains grow fast and have huge leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving cocoa the shade and moisture it needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ adesai abifabii. They burn easily under strong sunlight and strong winds. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom mean the plant is starving for nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to stay green and grow leaves. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer early gives the maize the food it needs to make big corns.
ga: Yellow leaves on the underside mean the plant is lacking nitrogen. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛbaakwɛ̃. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer early on This will give the corn the food it needs to make large ears of corn.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot underground during the heavy rain season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water stays trapped around them in flat soil. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges lets extra rainwater drain away so the roots can breathe and stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bote shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ muɔ ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are small worms hiding inside the leaves of my young maize and eating holes through them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-baby corn lɛ baai amli ni amɛyeɔ bu kɛtsɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a pest that targets the soft center leaf funnel of young maize. Spraying recommended treatments directly into the center funnel early prevents them from destroying the plant's growing tip.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ anɔ. Nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsaa hela lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ ŋshɔ lɛ teŋgbɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni akafite tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ.

english: When pepper plants are crowded, they fight for light, water, and soil food, spending all their energy growing tall to reach the sun instead of making branches and fruits. Giving them enough space allows them to branch out and bear more peppers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ pepper tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ he kɛha niyenii. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛshɛ hulu la lɛ he moŋ fe ni eeefee tsei niji kɛ aduawai. Kɛ́ aha amɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛjeɔ niji amli ni amɛnáa ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers before forming tomatoes during hot dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani amɛwo tomato yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry soil cause stress to tomato plants, making them drop flowers to conserve water and stay alive. Covering the soil around the stems with dry grass keeps the roots cool and wet so flowers stay on.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei anɔ. Ha tomatoi ashwie fɔfɔi koni ekɛbu nu he ni ehi wala mli. Mulching around Dry stems lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why is it bad to plant my cowpeas during the period of heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmei dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli lɛ ehiii lɛ?

english: Cowpeas need dry conditions during flowering and harvesting; heavy rains rot the flowers and pods before the seeds can dry properly. Planting them towards the end of the rainy season gives the pods dry weather to mature.
ga: Cowpeas biɔ shihilɛ ni mli egbi yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ kpamɔ teŋ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ dani dumɔwui lɛ nyɛɔ amɛgbiɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ adu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ aná kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops stunted even when I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ sɛɛ foɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal fertilizer, water, and light away from your crops before the crop can reach it. Clearing weeds within the first month after planting lets your crop eat all the food provided.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ la kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli dani amɛshɛɔ amɛhe. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I cut off the extra shoots growing out from the base of my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ cacao tso ni eda lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Those extra shoots suck away food and water that the tree needs to feed its cocoa pods. Removing them keeps the tree clean, lets light into the canopy, and prevents diseases like black pod.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi nɛɛ shwieɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni he hiaa tso lɛ koni ekɛha kookoo ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ́ ojie lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ he atse. Ha la abote ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli. ni amɛtsi helai srɔtoi tamɔ black pods lɛ anaa

english: Why do grains I save from my previous harvest yield less corn than fresh certified seeds from the agrodealer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo fe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ okwaayeli mlijalɔ lɛ dɛŋ lɛ?

english: Many commercial crop seeds are specially bred for one-time high yields, but seeds saved from those crops lose their vigor and yield power in the next generation. Fresh certified seeds guarantee uniform growth and disease resistance.
ga: Akwɛɔ tsei babaoo ni akɛheɔ jara lɛ amli dumɔwui yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ saramɔ kome pɛ mli. Shi dumɔwui ni ahere amɛyiwala kɛjɛ nakai tsei lɛ amli lɛ baafite amɛhewalɛ ni amɛbaawo hewalɛ yɛ yinɔ ni baa lɛ mli. Dumɔwui heei ni ana he odaseyeli haa amɛ dalɛ daa kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to strong heat and direct sunlight. They require temporary shade crops, such as plantains, to shield their leaves from burning and keep the soil moist while their roots establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛbu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he, ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ tswaa lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the corn cobs are fully formed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tso ko shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a clear sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Maize requires a lot of nitrogen to build strong leaves; adding compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer restores healthy green growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni eha baai ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I protect my young maize farm from armyworms without spending too much money on chemicals?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-baby corn ŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ asraafoi akuu mli ŋmeii ahe ni mikɛ tsofai babaoo efiteee?

english: You can control fall armyworms naturally by checking your plants early, setting up simple traps, or dropping a small amount of wood ash or crushed neem leaf powder directly into the plant whorls where caterpillars hide.
ga: Obaanyɛ oye leaf fallworm lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔ tsei lɛ akwɛmɔ nɔ mra. Okɛ amale ni yɔɔ mlɛo ato Aloo, shwie tso sũ loo neem baa powda fioo ko awo tso lɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhe ewo mli lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Is it beneficial for me to plant cowpeas together on the same land as my maize?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ mafee ekome kɛdu tsina ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ ŋmãa?

english: Yes, planting cowpeas with maize is very helpful. Cowpeas grab nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, naturally improving soil fertility and helping your maize grow stronger.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweremɔ yaa hiɛ. ni oye obua o-corn lɛ ni ehiɛ wa.

english: Why do my cassava roots become tough, woody, and hard to cook if I leave them in the ground too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ wa, amɛfeɔ tsei, ni kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ahoomɔ wa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots reach peak starch quality between 10 to 12 months. If left in the soil past maturity, the roots convert their stored starch into woody fibers, making them hard and tough to eat.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ baashɛ amɛ starch ni nɔ kwɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ he yɛ nyɔji 10 kɛyashi 12 mli kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛho be nɛɛ he. Shishifãi lɛ tsakeɔ starch ni ato lɛ amɛfeɔ tso mli tsɔi. Ha niyeli wa ni ewa

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning black and rotting before they get a chance to ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This issue is called blossom-end rot and happens when tomato plants cannot absorb enough calcium from the soil, usually caused by uneven watering during hot weather.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ blossom end rot ni ebaa kɛ́ tomato tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni afɔɔɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: How can I prevent my harvested yams from sprouting and rotting while waiting to sell them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-sweet potato ni mikpa lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni efite be mli ni mimɛɔ ni ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Yams should be stored off the ground in a well-ventilated, shaded yam barn. Removing early sprouts by hand and avoiding damaged tubers during harvest keeps them fresh for longer.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ sweet potato ato shikpɔŋ yɛ tsũ ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ onine jieɔ ŋmeii lɛ ni otsiɔ ŋmeii ni efite lɛ ahe yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi ehee be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Which type of plantain suckers should I take from my old farm to start a new plantation?
ga: Mɛɛ plantain tsei esa akɛ mikɛtsu nii kɛjɛ miŋmɔ momo lɛ mli koni mikɛje tso hee shishi?

english: Look for 'sword suckers' that have narrow, spear-like leaves and a heavy base. They establish faster, produce deeper roots, and yield stronger plantain bunches than suckers with broad leaves.
ga: Taomɔ ‘klante tu’ ni baai lɛ mli tse ni tamɔ akpɔlɔ kɛ shishitoo ni tsii. Amɛto amɛhe gbɛjianɔ oya. Bɔɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni oha plantain kui ni he wa fe tsei ashishifãi ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ.

english: Why does clearing weeds early in the growing season make such a big difference to my crop yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ mli lɛ haa srɔtofeemɔ kpele baa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Young crops need maximum sunlight, soil nutrients, and water to establish. Clearing weeds during the first three to four weeks stops them from stealing vital resources from your main crops.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ hia hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni fa fe fɛɛ ni akɛbaafee Jwɛi ni agbeɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ lɛ mli lɛ haaa amɛju nibii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛ oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ amli.

english: The first rain is often brief and doesn't soak deep into the dry earth. Planting too early can cause seeds to sprout and quickly dry up if a hot, dry spell follows before the full rainy season begins.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ. ni eboteee shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli shɔŋŋ Dumɔwui lɛ mra tsɔ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi oya kɛji akɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ nyiɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ je shishi.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for green leaves. Heavy rains often wash nitrogen deep into the soil where young roots cannot reach it, so applying fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ nitrogen lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi bibii nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Curled leaves with yellow patches on cassava are typically caused by the Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. Planting certified disease-free stem cuttings and removing infected plants early stops the disease from spreading across your farm.
ga: Baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmei lɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Dumɔ tsei ni hela bɛ mli ni awo he odase akɛ ojie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni helai akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences heat stress, dry soil, or damage from tiny insects like thrips. Watering your plants regularly at the base and providing light shade during extremely hot afternoons helps the flowers stay attached and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips fite lɛ. Watering the plant regularly at the base and providing shade on hot afternoons will help the flowers stick and set fruit.

english: Why are my pepper plants growing very tall with thick green leaves, but no peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi chili bɛ?

english: When pepper plants receive too much nitrogen fertilizer, they focus all their energy on growing tall stems and lush leaves instead of flowers. Switching to fertilizers rich in phosphorus and potassium encourages the plant to stop growing leaves and start bearing fruit.
ga: Kɛji akɛ pepper tsei lɛ ná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ fɔfɔii najiaŋ lɛ, amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ tsei ni kɛlɛ ni miida kɛ tsei ahe tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ahe nii. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmɔshi nibii ni phosphorus kɛ potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ akpa baai lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ ni ebɔi yibiiwoo.

english: Yam tubers rot underground when soil stays waterlogged for too long, preventing oxygen from reaching the roots and allowing destructive fungi to thrive. Planting yams on raised mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa lɛ ayashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. ni oha ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ adara. Sweet potato ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my cocoa tree seedlings burn and die during the dry major season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo dumɔwui lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have shallow roots and sensitive leaves that burn easily under full sun and dry winds. Planting fast-growing plantains alongside young cocoa provides living shade umbrellas and retains soil moisture during their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi shishi. Dumɔwui ni daa oya ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ hiɔ shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: How can I prevent insects from destroying my harvested maize stored in the barn?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkafite ŋmãa ni akpa ni ato yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weevils and borers multiply in stored grain when moisture remains trapped inside or air flows freely around open bags. Drying maize thoroughly until the kernels break cleanly, then storing them in airtight or hermetic bags, starves pests of oxygen and keeps the grain fresh for months.
ga: Weevils and borers breed in stored seeds when moisture is trapped inside or air circulates freely around open bags. Okɛ ŋmãa lɛ agbi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi ŋmeii lɛ amli baatse jogbaŋŋ. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛto kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo kotoku ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli. Eshwieɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni ekɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ haaa. ni eha ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi ehee nyɔji babaoo

english: Why does my harvested cassava turn dark and spoil just two days after digging it up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ni mikpa lɛ mli edɔ ni egbo yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ beni atsa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots begin to spoil quickly after harvest because exposure to air triggers a rapid chemical breakdown inside the root. Storing fresh cassava tubers underground in trenches packed with moist sawdust or moist sand protects them from air and keeps them fresh for up to two weeks.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ oya kɛji akpa amɛ. This is because exposure to air will cause the chemicals within the roots to break down quickly. Kɛ́ akɛ cassava shishifãi heei to shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ bu ko ni ŋmeii loo ŋã ni mli edɔ eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaabu amɛhe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he, ni ebaaha amɛhi shi ehee kɛyashi otsii enyɔ.

english: Why is my garden egg yield so much smaller when I plant seeds closely together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kwraa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil food, resulting in small and weak fruits. Giving each plant proper space allows the roots to spread wide and absorb enough nutrients to produce large, healthy garden eggs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, yibii lɛ daraaa ni ebɛ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa babaoo ni amɛheɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why should I buy fresh certified hybrid maize seeds instead of planting seeds saved from last year's harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe ŋmãa dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase akɛ afee lɛ? Mohu ɔ, nyɛɛ du wuhi nɛ a bua naa ngɛ jeha nɛ be ɔ ngmami ɔ mi ɔ.

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for high yield, but the seeds harvested from them lose those high-performing traits in the next generation. Planting saved hybrid seeds results in uneven plant growth and much smaller cobs, whereas fresh certified seed guarantees strong yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Shi dumɔwui ni akpaa kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui nɛɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni aduɔ ni aŋmala ashwie shi lɛ haa tsei ni dalɛ ejaaa kɛ ŋmeii bibii babaoo baa. yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ haa yibiiwoo ni mli wa baa.

english: Why does a seed variety that yields heavily in South Africa struggle to produce well on my farm in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ South Africa dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛná yibii kpakpai yɛ miŋmɔ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops are adapted to specific local conditions like rainfall patterns, soil temperature, and daylight hours. A crop bred for South Africa's climate may feel stressed by Ghana's heat and humidity, making it hard for the plant to perform the same way.
ga: Atsakeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa shihilɛi pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔlɛ kɛ hulutsoo be. Tsei ni akwɛɔ amɛ kɛha South Africa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ lɛ baanyɛ anu he akɛ Ghana dɔlɛ kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ miigba amɛnaa. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei akɛ amɛaatsu nii yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ.

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves during dry periods to conserve water. By shedding leaves, the plant slows down its water loss and goes into a resting phase until the rains return to trigger new leaf growth.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛshwieɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso lɛ haa nu ni elaajeɔ lɛ baa shi ni eboteɔ hejɔɔmɔ be mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa koni eha baa heei akwɛ̃.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my maize turn yellow when I plant the seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Maize plants need space to absorb light and food from the soil. When crowded, they compete for nitrogen, causing the older bottom leaves to turn yellow as the plant starves for nutrients.
ga: Abɛi tsei taoɔ he ko ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ la kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni gbɔmɛi babaoo yɔɔ Amɛyeɔ nitrogen he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ niyenii ni tso lɛ bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas before maize make my next maize harvest grow stronger without adding artificial fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmãa ni aduɔ dani ŋmãa lɛ baaha mi ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli awa kɛji akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa fataaa he lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil. When the cowpea crop finishes, it leaves behind enriched soil that feeds the next maize crop naturally.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ adu cowpea agbe naa lɛ Ebaashi shikpɔŋ ni baa nii koni ekɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer pods after I cut down the tall shade trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa tsei lɛ miiwo ŋmɔtɔ fioo ko pɛ beni mifo tsei kakadaji ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Young and mature cocoa trees thrive in gentle shade. Direct, harsh sunlight stresses the trees, dries out the surrounding soil, and leaves the cocoa vulnerable to heat damage and pests like mirids.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii ni eda lɛ shwereɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Hulu la ni naa wa lɛ tswaa tso lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Ha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ agbi Ni enɛ haa kookoo lɛ nyɛɔ efiteɔ kɛjɛɔ latsaa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ pollen mli.

english: Why do my pepper flowers fall off without forming any peppers during very hot weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeee pepper ko yɛ otsi ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses pepper plants and dries out their pollen, preventing pollination. When temperatures get too high, the plant drops its blossoms to save its own energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa pepper tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa pollen lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Tsi pollination naa Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Why does removing the extra side shoots from my tomato plant result in bigger fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tomato tsei ahe lɛ, ehaa aduawai lɛ daraa lɛ?

english: Side shoots consume nutrients and water that would otherwise go into fruit development. Removing them directs the plant's energy straight into developing bigger, healthier tomatoes.
ga: Lateral shoots lɛ heɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni baanyɛ aná aduawai lɛ anɔ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ tomatoi lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ hewalɛ yaa tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ afeemɔ nɔ.

english: Why do seeds saved from last year's hybrid maize harvest produce weaker crops when I plant them again?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ́ midu amɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred from two unique parent plants to give maximum strength in the first generation. Seeds collected from that crop lose that special combination, resulting in uneven growth and lower yields in the second generation.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ fɔ̃ɔ fɔlɔi tsei enyɔ ni yɔɔ srɔtoi koni amɛná hewalɛ babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ nakai ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ laajeɔ nakai nibii krɛdɛɛi lɛ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli baa.

english: Why do tomato plants rot easily at the stem when planted in low land with poor drainage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei lɛ naa tsitsii ni fiteɔ lɛ he amanehulu kɛ́ adu yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Tomato roots need air just as much as they need water. Waterlogged soil smothers root systems and creates a damp environment where soil-borne fungi thrive and attack the stem.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ babaoo he hiaa tomato shishifãi tamɔ bɔ ni ehe hiaa amɛ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. kɛ nu he hiamɔ Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ baa. Biɛ ji he ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ mli lɛ daa ni amɛtutuaa tsei lɛ.

english: Why do insect pests spread less quickly when I plant different crops together instead of just one crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaaa oya kɛ́ mikɛ tsei srɔtoi wo he kome lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookwɛ tso kome pɛ

english: Pests usually target specific crops. Mixing different plants creates visual and physical obstacles that confuse insects, making it harder for pests to travel from one food source to another.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi anɔ. Tsei srɔtoi ni akɛfutuɔ amɛhe lɛ Amɛfeɔ ekome kɛfeɔ gbɛtsii nii ni anaa kɛ nɔ ni anaa ni haa kooloi lɛ ayiŋ feɔ amɛ kɔshikɔshi. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ akɛ amɛaajɛ niyenii he kome kɛya ekroko mli.

english: Potassium acts like a strength booster for crops, helping them build strong stems, fight off diseases, and produce larger, healthier fruits and flowers.
ga: Potassium tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni woɔ tso hewalɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni wa. Wuu helai srɔtoi ni owo aduawai kɛ fɔfɔii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do different fertilizer packages have different numbers or types listed on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ eko fɛɛ eko yɛ yibɔ loo henɔ sɔrɔto lɛ?

english: Those numbers show the varying strengths and mixtures of plant nutrients like potassium; different crops or growth stages need different strength levels to respond well.
ga: Yibɔi nɛɛ damɔ shi kɛha hewalɛi srɔtoi kɛ tsei amli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ potassium ni akɛfee ekome. Nibii ni aduɔ loo amɛdalɛ mli srɔtoi biɔ hewalɛ srɔtoi koni amɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my crop is reacting well to the fertilizer I applied?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miitsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ he?

english: A good response shows within a few weeks through greener leaves, stronger stems, and better flowering rather than yellowing or stunted growth.
ga: Hetoo kpakpa baaje kpo yɛ otsii fioo komɛi amli kɛtsɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ mli wa fe tsutsu lɛ. kɛ fɔfɔi ni hi fe tsutsu lɛ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee ŋmɔŋ loo ehiɛ aka shi

english: Should I dig chemical fertilizers into the soil or just sprinkle them around my plants?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo mikɛshwie tsei lɛ ahe kɛkɛ?

english: Digging solid fertilizer lightly into the soil near the plant base keeps rain from washing it away, while sprinkling works well if you water immediately so the roots can soak it up.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa blɛoo. Shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ mlibotemɔ baaye abua ni nugbɔ akashwie lɛ. Fertilizer tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛji okɛ nu wo nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ.

english: Is it better to use liquid fertilizers or solid ones on my farm?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mikɛ nu loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa baatsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Liquid fertilizers work faster because roots and leaves absorb them quickly, while solid fertilizers break down slowly to feed the plant over a longer period.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii oya ejaakɛ shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛ oya. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa lɛ baafite fiofio lɛ. Koni akɛ niyenii aha tsei be kakadaŋŋ

english: How far away from the main stem of my crop should I apply fertilizer?
ga: Te esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tso titri lɛ he kɛya he ko tɛŋŋ?

english: You should place fertilizer a few inches away from the stem around the root zone, as placing chemicals directly touching the main stem can burn the plant.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli 2-3 inches kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ he, ejaakɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã tso lɛ.

english: Can I pour liquid chemical treatments directly onto crop leaves without damaging them?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafɔse tsofai ni ji nu awo tsei ahe baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni mifiteee amɛ?

english: It depends on the chemical, but pouring strong mixtures directly on leaves in hot sun can burn them; it is often safer to apply diluted liquid around the base of the soil or during cool mornings.
ga: Edamɔ tsofai anɔ Shi kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni akɛfutu mli lɛ shwie baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã amɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ nu ni mli edɔ awo he ni oyɔɔ lɛ he. shikpɔŋ nɔ loo yɛ leebi ni hulutsoo be mli

english: What is paclo and how can it help my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji pacol ni te ebaanyɛ eye ebua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Paclo is a plant growth regulator chemical that slows down extra leaf growth and encourages crops to spend their energy producing more early flowers and uniform yield.
ga: Paclo ji tsofa ko ni haa tsei adalɛ yaa hiɛ ni haa tsei lɛ ahe baa ni fa fe nine lɛ yaa hiɛ fioo, ni ewoɔ tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ atsu nii koni amɛwo fɔfɔi babaoo mra ni amɛwo yibii babaoo ni yaa nɔ daa.

english: How should I apply paclo at the base of my plants so that it actually works?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ Pacol awo tso lɛ shishi koni etsu nii diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Paclo is usually mixed with water and applied directly to the soil around the base of the plant stem so the main roots can draw it up into the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, akɛ pacol futuɔ nu mli ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ ji koni shishifãi titrii lɛ anyɛ agbala lɛ kɛya ŋwɛi kɛya ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli.

english: How can I encourage my crops to produce more flowers instead of just growing taller with leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mawo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaakwɛ̃ kɛ baai?
