english: Using specific growth-regulating chemicals or potassium-rich feeds reduces excess stem growth and forces the plant to trigger strong flower production.
ga: Tsofai ni haa tso lɛ daa loo niyenii ni potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaha tso lɛ shishifãi ni fa fe nine lɛ aba shi, ni ebaanyɛ enyɛ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekanya fɔfɔi ni mli wa.

english: How do I know if the maize seeds I bought at the store are good quality and will actually sprout?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni miheɔ yɛ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Good quality seeds are uniform in size, clean, and free from insect holes or cracks. You can test them at home by dropping a handful into a bowl of water—seeds that sink are healthy and full, while seeds that float are usually dried out or damaged and will not sprout well.
ga: Dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ dalɛ tamɔ amɛhe, amɛhe tse, ni ŋmeii loo ŋmeii bɛ mli. Obaanyɛ oka enɛ okwɛ yɛ shia kɛtsɔ dumɔwui fioo ko ni oookɛwo nu tsɛnsi mli lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui ni ebote mli lɛ mli wa ni eyi obɔ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni hoɔ yɛ nu hiɛ lɛ mli egbi loo efite ni amɛkwɛ̃ŋ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves of my young cassava plants drop off during the long dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves naturally during very dry weather to save water and protect their underground roots from drying out. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh green leaves and continue growing normally.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi waa lɛ. Koni akɛbu nu he ni abu shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ahe koni amɛkagbi. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eda bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep falling off without growing into any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets too hot or doesn't get a steady supply of water. When the weather is very hot and dry, the plant gets stressed and drops its flowers to save energy; watering consistently at the roots helps the plant hold onto its flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo enáaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni egbi lɛ Tsei lɛ haoɔ ni amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ nu daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and turning small and twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bibii ni amɛmiitsake lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap from young leaves, or by a virus spread by whiteflies. Spraying the leaves early with neem oil mixture or recommended insecticide helps keep these insects away so new leaves can grow flat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akashɛ amɛhe bɔni afee ni baai heei lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in dark, overly wet, and cool conditions. Pruning excess branches to let sunlight and air into your cocoa farm and removing the infected black pods right away prevents the disease from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. ni ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni duŋ yɔɔ Fɛ̃i kɛ fɛ̃i tsɔ, ŋmɔmɔ niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote okokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Ni jiemɔ ŋmeii diji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why do my maize leaves have small holes and powdery dust that looks like sawdust inside them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa baa lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni sũ ni tamɔ ŋmei yɛ mli?

english: This is a clear sign of Fall Armyworm infestation. The young caterpillars hide inside the central leaves of the maize plant and eat them from the inside out, leaving behind sawdust-like waste; applying targeted bio-pesticides or recommended sprays into the leaf whorl early controls them.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ Fall Armyworm hela lɛ eba. Kplukai bibii kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ ni amɛyeɔ nii kɛjɛɔ emli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ. kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni ashiɔ yɛ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ nii loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ baai amli lɛ ni akɛbaatsu nii lɛ baaye amɛnɔ mra.

english: How do I know if my farm soil needs fertilizer before I start planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii dani mibɔi dumɔwui?

english: If your previous crops grew very slowly, produced pale yellow leaves instead of deep green ones, or yielded small harvests, your soil is likely exhausted. Planting a fast-growing green cover crop or adding well-rotted manure restores essential nutrients naturally.
ga: Kɛji onibii ni odu tsutsu lɛ dara blɛoo waa Eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse najiaŋ. loo ewo fioo pɛ Etamɔ nɔ ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ efo. Nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni aduɔ loo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fataa he lɛ baaha niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ aba ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when the fruit bunch grows big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya beni aduawai akuu lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have soft stems and shallow roots that do not reach deep into the ground. When the fruit bunch grows heavy, strong wind can easily pull the shallow roots out of wet soil, so propping up the trunk with a sturdy bamboo or wooden Y-fork stick gives it the support it needs.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛ aduawai akuu lɛ bafee tsiimɔ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ. Ejeɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ oya No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei loo tso ni akɛfee ŋmei ni wa fĩ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha ená yelikɛbuamɔ ni he hiaa lɛ.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot and turn watery underground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite ni shikpɔŋ shishi nu eyi mli obɔ dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot underground when water collects around them in heavy clay soil or when underground worms and beetles wound the tuber skin. Planting yams on tall, well-drained soil mounds prevents water from soaking the tubers and keeps them healthy.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu shwere yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa ni mli tse lɛ mli. aloo beni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii tutuaa yitso hewolo lɛ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii yɛ gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi nu naa koni ekabote ŋmeii lɛ amli, ni ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my harvested onions soft-rot so quickly before I can get them to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-onions ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya dani mikɛyaa jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Onions rot quickly if they are harvested while wet or not dried properly after harvest. Leaving harvested onions to dry in a warm, shaded, well-ventilated area for about a week hardens their outer skin and seals the necks, protecting them from rotting during storage and transport.
ga: Sabolai fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akpa lɛ ni efɔ lɛ loo egbiko jogbaŋŋ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ koni amɛgbi yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo yɔɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli aaafee otsi kome lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ mli awa ni ekɛtsi etsitsi lɛ naa. Etsiɔ fitemɔ naa yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ kɛ gbɛfaa mli.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and easily damaged by direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow very quickly and provide broad leaves that create natural shade, protecting the young cocoa trees and keeping the soil moist during their first few years.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni hulu la fiteɔ oya. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo baa. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Can I plant cassava and maize together on the same farmland?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Yes, planting cassava and maize together works well because maize grows quickly and is harvested within three to four months, leaving space and sunlight for the slower-growing cassava to expand afterwards.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ ŋwɛi kɛ hulu la ni ashiɔ koni eha ŋmei lɛ ada blɛoo ni eshwere sɛɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Maize leaves curl inward during hot afternoons to protect themselves from water loss. By rolling up, the leaf reduces its exposed surface area to the sun and retains moisture until the weather cools down.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli koni nu akafite. kɛji akɛ abɔle ehe Baai lɛ haa he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off before any fruit starts to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants often drop their blossoms when the weather gets too hot or when watering is irregular. The plant gets stressed by these rapid environmental changes and discards flowers it cannot support.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ afɔɔ amɛ nu be fɛɛ be. Tsei lɛ haoɔ kɛjɛɔ shihilɛ mli tsakemɔi ni baa oya lɛ amli ni amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛye amɛbua lɛ.

english: Yellowing on lower leaves usually indicates a lack of nitrogen in the soil. When nitrogen is low, the plant moves what little it has from older bottom leaves up to nourish the new, growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ nitrogen faaa Tso lɛ tsiɔ nɔ fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha baai heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow out small and twisted instead of long and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji bibii ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni ehiɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Yams require loose, deep, and well-aerated soil to stretch down smoothly. Compacted soil, heavy clay, or rocks beneath the mound block the tuber from expanding freely, resulting in stunted or misshapen yams.
ga: Sweet potatoes hia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni mli kwɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ koni ehi shi tɛ̃ɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ, shikpɔŋ ni mli wa. Aloo tɛi ni yɔɔ gɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ tsiɔ ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã amɛhe. Enɛ haa sweet potatoes lɛ shwieɔ shi loo efiteɔ.

english: Why are there white, powdery spots covering the leaves of my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ ni tamɔ powda ni ha mi-pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: This white coating is typically powdery mildew, a fungal infection that thrives when plants are crowded too closely together in humid conditions without enough airflow between them.
ga: Nɛkɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ futafuta nɛɛ jɛɔ powdery mildew lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛ́ tsei ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni sa hoɔ yɛ amɛteŋ.

english: Why are my cassava leaves turning yellow with patches and curling into distorted shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hei srɔtoi ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe kɛmiifee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: This is a key sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, a viral infection spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. It reduces the plant's ability to make food, resulting in smaller harvests.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi titri. Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Ehaa nyɛmɔ ni tsei yɔɔ ni amɛkɛfeɔ niyenii lɛ baa shi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ fioo.

english: How can I tell that my groundnuts are mature and ready to harvest from under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmeii lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Groundnuts are ready to dig up when the leaves begin to yellow and drop. You can pull up one test plant; if the inside of the pods shows dark brown markings and the seeds are firm, the crop is ready.
ga: Afee klalo akɛ abaakumɔ ŋmeii beni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Obaanyɛ ogbala kaa nitsumɔhe kome kɛya ŋwɛi. Kɛji akɛ pod lɛ mli yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ mli wa. Etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ efee klalo.

english: Why do my watermelons crack and split open on the farm before I pick them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon lɛ tswaa ni etswaa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mifoɔ lɛ?

english: Watermelons split open when they receive a sudden heavy intake of water—like a downpour after a dry spell. The inside of the fruit absorbs water faster than the outer rind can stretch, causing it to burst.
ga: Watermelon lɛ tswaa kɛji akɛ nu babaoo bote mli trukaa. Tamɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ. Yibii lɛ mligbɛ lɛ shwieɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ baanyɛ ashɛre. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋshɔŋloo lɛ mligbalamɔ.

english: Why do people say that planting beans makes the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Beans add natural nutrients like nitrogen into the soil through their roots, which makes the land richer and healthier for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ŋmeii kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nii babaoo ni eyɛ hewalɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: How do decaying plant leaves help my crops survive dry weather in Northern Ghana?
ga: Bɔ ni tsei ahe baai ni fiteɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli egbi lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Decaying leaves create a sponge-like organic layer in the soil that holds onto rainwater longer, keeping your crops hydrated during dry spells.
ga: Baai ni fiteɔ lɛ feɔ nɔ ko ni tamɔ sponge yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni haa nugbɔ nu lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. Ha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná nu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: I farm around Tamale where the soil gets tired easily; will planting beans help restore my land?
ga: Mitsuɔ ŋmɔ yɛ Tamale he ni shikpɔŋ lɛ fɔɔ shwiemɔ oya lɛ. Ani ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni aku sɛɛ akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ?

english: Yes, beans thrive in dry soil environments like Tamale because they fix nitrogen into poor soil and shed leaves that break down into natural fertilizer.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ, tamɔ tamale, ejaakɛ amɛsaa nitrogen lɛ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ mli. ni ejieɔ baai ni fiteɔ akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii

english: What simple crop can I plant that will naturally nourish my farm land for free?
ga: Mibaanyɛ makwɛ tsei mlɛo. Mɛni ji adebɔɔ naa nɔ ni baaha miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ yaka?

english: Legumes like beans or groundnuts are ideal because they trap nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the dirt to feed future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ amɛheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛkɛha tsei ni baaba wɔsɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Is it a good idea to leave fallen crop leaves on my farm, or should I sweep them away?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ mashi ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbee shi lɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli loo esa akɛ mafolɔ amɛ?

english: Leaving fallen leaves on your land is very good because as they rot, they turn into natural compost that feeds the soil and helps it stay moist.
ga: Baai ni egbee shi ni oooshi yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni hi waa. Ejaakɛ kɛ́ egbo lɛ Etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ ni ehaa efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow better in fields where crop leaves were left to rot in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔji ni ashiɔ tsei ahe baai koni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli lɛ?

english: As leaves break down, they release essential plant food and turn into organic matter, making it easier for new roots to absorb water and nutrients.
ga: Kɛji baai lɛ gbee shi Ejieɔ tsei niyenii ni he hiaa ni ebafeɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa shishifãi heei akɛ amɛaaŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Should I burn the leftover plant leaves on my field after harvesting my crops?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashã baai ni eshwɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ́ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: No, burning crop leaves destroys valuable nutrients. Letting the leaves decay naturally in the soil feeds your ground for the next planting season.
ga: Dabi, tso baai ni ashãa lɛ fiteɔ niyenii ni he hiaa waa. Kɛ́ oha baai lɛ fite yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ aye niyenii kɛha shweremɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do bean leaves shed and break down so easily in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkuɔ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Bean leaves are soft and high in natural nutrients, allowing them to decompose rapidly into rich topsoil that nourishes nearby plants.
ga: Bean baai lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo yɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa efiteɔ oya ni etsɔɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni haa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: How can I make my depleted farmland fertile again without spending a lot of money on chemical fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha ŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ ni mikɛ shika babaoo tsuuu nii yɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe?

english: You can plant beans and let their fallen leaves decompose on the land; this naturally improves soil fertility without the high cost of bought fertilizers.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu ŋmeii ni oha baai ni egbee shi lɛ agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yaa hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa.

english: Does growing legumes like beans actually save me money on buying bagged fertilizer?
ga: Ani ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha maná shika yɛ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ kotoku mli lɛ hemɔ mli diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, legumes fix nitrogen naturally in the ground and drop nutrient-rich leaves, reducing the amount of commercial fertilizer you need to purchase every season.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii lɛ saa nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ehaa baai ni niyenii mli hewalɛ eyi mli obɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa jarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii ni esa akɛ ohe daa afi lɛ baa shi.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight and dry soil. Leaving shade trees or planting plantains beside them creates a cool environment and retains soil moisture so the seedlings can survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Tsei ni ashiɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Ehaa shihilɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi koni dumɔwui lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: How do planting non-fruit forest trees along my farm boundary help my food crops grow better?
ga: Te tsei ni jeee yibii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ husu lɛ naa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi niyenii ni miduɔ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Boundary trees act as windbreaks to block heavy storms from breaking your crops. Their deep roots also bring up water from deep underground, and their falling leaves break down into free organic manure for your crops.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ husu lɛ naa lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsii koni ahum ni naa wa akafite onibii. Amɛshishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ hu gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. Ni amɛbaai ni egbee shi lɛ mli gbálaa kɛfeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my maize start turning yellow while the plant is still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni tso lɛ ji bibioo lolo lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of a maize plant mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green leaves. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer will restore green growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tso shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsei lɛ adara ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with bushy leaves but yielding very tiny roots inside the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni ebaa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli shi shishifãi bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When soil has too much leaf-building nutrient (nitrogen) and not enough root-building nutrient (potassium), the cassava puts all its energy into growing leaves above ground instead of swelling its tuber roots below.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ niyenii ni haa baai lɛ maa shi (nitrogen) babaoo tsɔ, ni niyenii ni haa shishifãi lɛ maa shi (potassium) lɛ faaa lɛ, ŋmei kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa baai ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, tuber ɔ sisije ɔmɛ fuɔ ngɛ sisi.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without forming any tomatoes during the heat of the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo tomato ko yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the pollen inside tomato blossoms, causing the flower to dry up and fall off. Mulching the soil around the plant with dry grass keeps the roots cool and helps the flowers form fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ gbiɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi. Mulching ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi ebɔle Tsei ahe lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai lɛ ni amɛwoɔ shi.

english: Is it helpful to plant groundnuts together on the same ridge with my cassava?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ni mikɛ mi-cassava lɛ yɔɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, groundnuts belong to a plant family that pulls nitrogen from the air and puts it into the ground. As the groundnut plants grow and decompose, they naturally feed the soil for the cassava plant.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii fata tsei aweku ko ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ sũ mli lɛ he. Kɛji ŋmei tso lɛ da ni egbo lɛ Amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii kɛha ŋmei tsei lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: What happens to my farm soil if I plant maize on the exact same plot every single year?
ga: Mɛni baaba shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi?

english: Planting maize repeatedly drains the same nutrients from the soil without giving it time to recover. Over time, the soil becomes weak, crop yields drop, and weeds and plant diseases build up in the field.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii momo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsa ehe. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbɔjɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ eba shi Jwɛi kɛ tsei ahelai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔji amli.

english: Why should I cut off extra branches from my mature cocoa trees if the tree looks green and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji krokomɛi ni fata he kɛjɛ kookoo tso ni eda lɛ nɔ kɛji tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ ni eyɛ hewalɛ?

english: Pruning removes hidden, unproductive branches so air and sunlight can flow through the tree. Good airflow prevents pod diseases like black pod and directs the tree's food into producing cocoa pods rather than excess leaves.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni wooo yibii lɛ ajieɔ. Bɔni afee ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la anyɛ atsɔ tsei lɛ amli. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ pod helai, tamɔ pod diji anaa, ni ekwɛɔ tso lɛ niyenii nɔ koni ekɛ cocoa pod aba yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do some of my seeds fail to sprout up when I plant them deep inside the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui komɛi kwɛ̃ɔɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Seeds only carry a limited amount of stored energy. If you plant them too deep, the sprout uses up all its energy pushing through heavy dirt before it reaches the light, causing it to die under the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ ni ato. Kɛji odu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ Tso bibioo lɛ baafite ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛtsiɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji lɛ mli dani eshɛɔ la lɛ he. ha egbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi

english: What causes the leaves of my young maize plants to get holes eaten through them almost overnight?
ga: Mɛni ha mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ ye bu aaafee nyɔɔŋ kome mli?

english: Holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by caterpillars like fall armyworms that hide inside the center of the plant during the day and eat the tender leaves at night. Catching them early with natural sprays like neem leaf extract or recommended treatments prevents total crop loss.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ yɛ shwane mli ni amɛyeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ gbɛkɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii baa bibii amli. Amɛmɔmɔ mra Kɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mɛi anɔ tamɔ neem tso lɛ mli nu. Aloo, gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsaa lɛ baatsi ŋmɔshi nibii muu lɛ fɛɛ ni baafite lɛ naa.

english: Why are my crop leaves suddenly being eaten and destroyed by insects in the middle of the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmeii yeɔ mi tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ trukaa ni amɛfiteɔ yɛ be ni amɛdaraa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Crops attract pests when they are vulnerable or during specific weather conditions. Insects attack leaves to feed themselves, which stops the plant from making food through sunlight and leads to severe crop damage if left untreated.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ gbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛji amɛhe waaa loo yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli. Kplukai tutuaa baai koni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtao amɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ atsɔ hulu la nɔ afee niyenii. ni ebaanyɛ efite tsei waa kɛji akɛ atsaaa amɛ.

english: How does a crop disease spread so quickly from my neighbor's farm to my own farm?
ga: Te fee tɛŋŋ ni tso hela ko gbɛ eshwa oya kɛjɛ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛtee mi diɛŋtsɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Crop diseases are caused by microscopic organisms that travel easily through the air on wind currents, water runoff, infected farm tools, or insects moving from one field to another.
ga: Nibii bibii ni baanyɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, kɔɔyɔɔ, nu ni hoɔ, kɛ okwaayeli nibii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ kɛ tsei helai baa. loo kooloi bibii ni fãa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛyaa ekroko mli.

english: What actually happens to my plants when I apply chemical medicine to protect them from insects?
ga: Mɛni baa mitsei lɛ anɔ kɛ́ mikɛ tsofai tsu nii koni mikɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ kooloi ahe?

english: Crop medicines, or pesticides, work either by coating the leaves to kill insects on contact or by being absorbed into the plant's system so that any pest taking a bite gets poisoned and dies.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ tsei, loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛtsɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ anɔ koni egbe kooloi kɛji amɛshɛ amɛhe loo kɛtsɔ amɛhe ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ nɔ koni kooloi ni shwieɔ mɔ lɛ aná poison ni amɛgboi.

english: If my neighbor's crop medicine worked well on his farm, can I use the exact same medicine on my crops?
ga: Kɛji okutsoŋnyo tso tsofa lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ eŋmɔ lɛ mli Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsofa nɛɛ nɔŋŋ atsu nii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: Not always. Different crops suffer from different types of pests, and using the wrong medicine or incorrect chemical dosage can burn your crop's leaves instead of curing the problem.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai srɔtoi ahe amanehulu. Ni tsofa ni ejaaa loo tsofa ni ejaaa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ baai ashã moŋ fe ni eeetsu naagba lɛ he nii.

english: Why do some pest medicines work quickly on caterpillars but fail to stop other destructive farm insects?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai komɛi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ tsuɔ nii oya yɛ ŋmeii anɔ shi amɛnyɛŋ amɛtsi kooloi krokomɛi ni fiteɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ anaa lɛ?

english: Farm chemicals are specifically formulated for targeted insect types; a medicine designed to destroy leaf-eating caterpillars may not affect tiny sap-sucking bugs or root-damaging worms.
ga: Afee tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni akɛtutua kooloi srɔtoi. Ekolɛ tsofai ni afee koni akɛfite ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ enaaa ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ anɔ hewalɛ. loo ŋmeii ni fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ

english: Should I wait until I see heavy damage on my farm before applying medicine to my crops?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mamɛ ni mana nɔ ko ni efite waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mikɛ tsofa awo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli?

english: No, you should act at the very first sign of damage. Waiting too long allows pests to multiply rapidly, destroying plant tissues beyond the point where medicine can save them.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ ofee nɔ ko kɛji ona klɛŋklɛŋ okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nɔ ko efite. Kɛ́ mɛɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ feɔ babaoo oya. Efiteɔ tsei ahe fãji fe bɔ ni tsofa baanyɛ atsa amɛ.

english: Why does spraying medicine on my crops right before a heavy rain ruin the treatment?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ tsofa shwie miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ, efiteɔ tsofafeemɔ lɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes the applied chemical off the plant leaves before it has time to work or be absorbed, wasting your money and leaving the crops unprotected against pests.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ tsofai ni akɛwo tsei ahe baai amli lɛ ahe dani amɛnáa be ni amɛkɛtsu nii loo amɛheɔ amɛhe. Eji oshika ni ofiteɔ ni ehaa oŋmɔshi nii lɛ bɛ hebuu kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: Can a crop plant recover and produce food after insects have eaten a large portion of its leaves?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aya hiɛ ni ewo niyenii beni kooloi bibii eye ebaai lɛ ateŋ babaoo sɛɛ?

english: Yes, if the main stem and root system remain healthy, treating the pests and providing proper soil nutrients will allow the plant to grow fresh leaves and still produce a harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ kɛ shishifã lɛ tee nɔ ehi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ atsa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ, ni akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni sa haa lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ tsei lɛ ahe tsei heei ni amɛya nɔ amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my crops look weak and stop growing properly even when there is enough rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po lɛ?

english: Water alone is not enough for growth. When soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen or phosphorus, or when hidden pests attack the plant's roots underground, the crop will stall and look sickly.
ga: Nu pɛ kɛkɛ faaa kɛha dalɛ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen loo phosphorus. aloo kɛ́ kooloi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ tutua tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ shishifãi. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baafee ais ni ebaafee nɔ ni ehiii.

english: How can I protect my harvested grains from pests when market disruptions prevent me from selling them immediately?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ ahe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe? Akɛni jarayeli mligbalamɔ lɛ tsi mi gbɛ koni mikahɔ̃ɔ nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ hewɔ lɛ.

english: Storing harvested crops in clean, airtight hermetic bags or cool, dry storage spaces keeps moisture out and suffocates any pest eggs, preventing insects from eating your stored produce.
ga: Kɛ nibii ni akpa lɛ ato kotokui ni he tse ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli. Aloo, he ko ni mli ejɔ ni egbi ni akɛ nibii toɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛtsi ŋmɔtɔ naa ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ atsu nii. Enɛ baatsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkaye nibii ni okɛto lɛ.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, their roots fight over the same water and food in the soil while their leaves block each other's sunlight. Giving each plant proper spacing allows them to grow strong, healthy stems and produce bigger, fuller ears of corn.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe hulu la lɛ naa. Kɛ́ okɛ gbɛ ni sa ha tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko teŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ená tso lɛ shishigbɛ ni wa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. ni amɛwoɔ ŋmãa toi ni dara ni yɔɔ nii babaoo.

english: Why do I need to clear all the big weeds around my crops in the very first month of planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi wuji ni ebɔle ehe lɛ? Nibii ni adu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ ni aduɔ lɛ mli?

english: Young crop seedlings are small and weak, so fast-growing weeds easily steal their soil food, water, and sunlight. Clearing weeds early ensures your crop gets all the nutrients it needs during its most critical growth stage.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe waaa. Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ juɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni onibii lɛ ana niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ yɛ amɛdalɛ be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits on flat ground for too long, it drowns the roots and causes fungal rot; planting your cassava on raised earth mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu hi shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli ni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbo. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why does putting dry grass on the soil around my pepper plants help them grow better in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mi-pepper tsei lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, acts like a protective blanket that keeps the sun from drying out the soil too quickly. It keeps the roots cool and preserves soil moisture so the plants do not wither.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya tsɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ koni tso lɛ akagbo.

english: Pale yellow leaves usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food crop leaves need to stay green and healthy. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-decomposed animal manure helps restore their green color and vigor.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei ahe koni amɛya nɔ amɛfee eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee eŋɔli kɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How do groundnuts and cowpeas make the soil better for maize when I plant them on the same plot later?
ga: Te ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii baafee tɛŋŋ amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmeii beni midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas have special root nodules that catch food from the air and store it in the ground. When you harvest them, that stored food remains in the soil, giving the next maize crop free nutrients to grow well.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ. Beni okpa niyenii ni ato lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ naa niyenii ni niyenii mli hewalɛ bɛ mli ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper flowers fall off the plant before growing into peppers during hot dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ pepper yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: When heat is too high and soil moisture is low, the plant gets stressed and drops its flowers to save energy and survive. Water the plants regularly and cover the root area with mulch to prevent flower drop.
ga: Beni latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ faaa lɛ. Tsei lɛ feɔ mɛi ni haoɔ ni amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛhi shi. Ha tso lɛ nu daa ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ aha shishifãi lɛ ahe koni fɔfɔi lɛ akafite.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they lack sufficient shade, are attacked by tiny sucking insects like mirids, or suffer from sudden dry periods. Maintaining good shade trees and protecting the farm from insects helps flowers turn into pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ. Kplukai bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ atatui tutuaa amɛ loo amɛyeɔ amanehulu yɛ hulutsoo be mli trukaa. Kɛ́ aha tsei lɛ yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni abu ŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ kooloi ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up tightly and the plant stops growing tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe shi shiŋŋ ni tso lɛ edaaa lɛ?

english: Curled leaves on tomatoes are often caused by tiny whiteflies that spread a virus to the plant as they feed on its sap. Controlling whiteflies early and removing infected plants stops the disease from spreading across your field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ tomato nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. ni gbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa tsei amli beni amɛyeɔ amɛ nu lɛ Early Whitefly Control ni ejieɔ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni helai akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔji lɛ amli fɛɛ.

english: Why do my harvested yam seed tubers refuse to sprout right away when I plant them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ kpooɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ kɛ́ midu amɛ mra lɛ?

english: Yam tubers enter a natural resting phase called dormancy right after harvest, during which they will not sprout regardless of soil conditions. They will naturally wake up and sprout roots once their internal biological clock detects the right humidity and warm soil conditions.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ boteɔ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy lɛ mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ. Yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛ ji lɛ, sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ kwɛŋ. Amɛbaate shi ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji amɛmli wala yibii ahe ŋmɛlɛtswaa lɛ na hulutsoo ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ shihilɛi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I plant them in an open field without any trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from direct sunlight because strong heat burns their delicate leaves and dries out the soil. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain alongside cocoa keeps the young trees cool and moist until they are strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ baashã baai bibii lɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye hulutsoo be lɛ fɛɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow while the crops are still short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ shi ŋmãa tso lɛ hiɔ shi kuku lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, which is a key nutrient plants need to grow dark green and healthy. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer early in the growing season helps the maize leaves turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛmɔ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot underground when there is heavy rainfall on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when too much water collects around them because the roots cannot breathe in soggy, waterlogged soil. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the roots stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu babaoo bua amɛhe naa, ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu kɛbote shikpɔŋ ni efɔ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ egbi ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why does my maize yield grow smaller every year when I plant it on the exact same plot of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ wooo yibii fioo daa afi kɛ́ midu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting maize on the same piece of land every season drains the exact same nutrients from the soil repeatedly and allows maize-specific pests to build up in the dirt. Rotating your maize with crops like groundnuts or beans restores nutrients back into the soil.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ be fɛɛ be ni Seasons lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shii abɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii pɔtɛɛ ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei tsakeɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the weather gets too hot, when the soil is too dry, or when small insects attack the delicate buds. Keeping the soil moist with mulch and protecting the plants from pests helps the flowers stay on and turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii tutuaa fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni abu tsei ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my cabbage plants look full of holes as if someone punched them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ eyi obɔ kɛ bu tamɔ mɔ ko etswa amɛ lɛ?

english: Holes in cabbage leaves are typically caused by small caterpillars like the diamondback moth larvae that feed on soft plant leaves. Applying safe insect treatments or neem leaf extract early in the morning can control these caterpillars before they destroy the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii, tamɔ diamondback moth larvae, ni yeɔ tsei bibii ahe baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni baa cabbage baai amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe loo leebi neem baa mli nu tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye kooloi nɛɛ anɔ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Spacing your plants properly gives each stalk enough room and food to grow thick and produce large, full cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa tso lɛ shishifã lɛ eko fɛɛ eko naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ ni ewo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do extension officers recommend planting cowpeas or beans to make my soil better for the next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni extension agent lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu tsina loo ŋmeii koni mikɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Leguminous crops like cowpeas and beans have natural bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil. When you harvest the beans, that trapped nitrogen stays in the soil to fertilize the next crop you plant.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ beans yɛ adebɔɔ mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni okpaa ŋmeii Nakai nitrogen ni aŋã lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛwo ŋmeii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up and look weak during the afternoon heat even when I watered them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ yɛ shwane mli kɛ́ awo amɛ nu po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl during hot afternoons as a natural defense mechanism to reduce water loss and protect themselves from burning. Covering the soil around the base of the plant with dry grass mulching helps keep the soil cool and traps moisture longer.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni haa nu ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ shãa he. Kɛ́ akɛ sũ ni egbi shwie tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why does a crop variety that grows very well in another village fail to produce well on my own farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ waa yɛ akrowai krokomɛi amli lɛ kwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Different crop varieties are suited to specific soil types, rainfall patterns, and temperatures. Soil that has too much clay, is too sandy, or lacks key minerals will prevent a crop from performing well, even if that same crop grows successfully in a neighboring area.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi lɛ sa kɛha shikpɔŋ srɔtoi. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ hulutsoo pɔtɛɛ Shikpɔŋ ni shikpɔŋ babaoo yɔɔ nɔ Ŋã babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ. Aloo shika tsuru ni he hiaa ni bɛ lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii akatsu nii jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ po.

english: Young cocoa plants get burned easily by direct, harsh sunlight and hot Harmattan winds. Without shade trees or nurse crops like plantains to cover them, the leaves lose water too fast and dry out.
ga: Hulu ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni jɛɔ harmattan mli lɛ shãa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ oya. Kɛji tsei ni baaha hulutsoo loo tsei tamɔ plantains ni baaha hulutsoo be lɛ bɛ lɛ, Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya tsɔ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Staking lifts yam leaves off the hot ground so they can catch more sunlight and fresh air. This helps the plant make food efficienty, which goes down into the soil to build bigger yam tubers.
ga: Staking jieɔ sweet potato lɛ kɛjɛɔ hei ni edɔ lɛ koni enine ashɛ hulu la babaoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baabote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛfee sweet potato ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my young maize leaves have small holes in them and look like something chewed them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Yɛ mli ni etamɔ nɔ ni nɔ ko miiye nɔ?

english: Small holes in maize leaves are usually caused by caterpillars like Fall Armyworm or stem borers. Moths lay eggs on the leaves, and when the caterpillars hatch, they feed on the soft green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworm loo stem borers lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii baai amli lɛ baa. Kplukai fɔɔ amɛwui yɛ baai anɔ. Ni kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ fɔ Eyeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli.

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up and developing yellow and light green patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and yellow patches are symptoms of Cassava Mosaic Disease. It is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies that carry a virus from infected cassava plants to healthy ones.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadii. Kplukai bibii ji mɛi ni gbɛɔ eshwaa. atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Eji mɔ ni kɛ hela lɛ baa kɛjɛɔ ŋmei tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋmei tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why are the top leaves of my pepper plants shrinking and twisting together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ekome lɛ?

english: Twisting leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny pests like mites or thrips hiding under the foliage. They suck the juices out of young leaves, causing them to curl up and stunt.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Amɛmuɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai bibii amli lɛ. Enɛ haa ebɔleɔ ehe ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Why should I wait until the soil is moist from rain before putting fertilizer on my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛ nugbɔ mli dani mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ amli?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so plant roots can absorb it. Applying fertilizer to dry soil under high heat can cause it to evaporate or burn the crop roots instead of feeding them.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni ekɛshwie shi bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa shishi lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ atsɔ la loo amɛshã yɛ niyenii najiaŋ.

english: Why do groundnut plants not require as much chemical fertilizer as my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ he ehiaaa mi ŋmãa lɛ tamɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family and can pull nitrogen gas directly out of the air and store it in small nodules on their roots, effectively making their own food.
ga: Peanuts fata legume weku lɛ he ni enyɛɔ ejieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛtoɔ ŋmeii bibii amli yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni no haa amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛfeɔ amɛ niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants instead of turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when temperatures get too high or when watering is irregular. Heat stress forces the plant to shed flowers to conserve water and survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu lɛ efɔɔɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be. Dɔlɛ haomɔ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛshwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why should I plant narrow sword suckers instead of broad-leafed suckers when starting a plantain farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu baai bibii ni mli tse yɛ baai bibii ni mli tse lɛ najiaŋ beni mijeɔ plantain ŋmɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Sword suckers have strong underground corms with plenty of food reserves, allowing them to establish roots fast, grow sturdy stems, and produce larger bunches than wide-leafed shoots.
ga: Sword suckers lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni mli wa ni niyenii babaoo yɔɔ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛtswaa shishifãi oya, amɛnáa tsei ni wa, ni amɛdaraa kui wuji fe baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ.

english: Why does my swamp rice field need standing water around the plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ŋmɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ yɛ nu ni damɔ shi ebɔle tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Standing water suffocates weeds that try to compete with the rice, keeps the soil consistently wet, and regulates the root temperature so the rice heads can fill out properly.
ga: Nu ni yɔɔ lolo lɛ tsiɔ jwɛi ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekɛ ŋmãa lɛ abɔ akaŋ lɛ naa. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be. ni akudɔ shishifãi lɛ amli latsaa lɛ koni ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ awo mli ekoŋŋ jogbaŋŋ

english: Why are the leaves of my young cocoa plants turning yellow and scorching in the middle of the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao baai bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiitso yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees planted next to them to filter the light and preserve soil moisture during their early growth.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo tsei ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Koni ajie kane lɛ ni ekwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i nɔ yɛ be mli ni edaa oya lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers before any peppers can start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ dani pepper lɛ baanyɛ ada lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when they experience heat stress, improper watering, or a lack of key nutrients like potassium, which prevents the plant from holding onto its flowers to produce fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛbote dɔlɛ he haomɔ mli. nu ni esaaa loo niyenii mli nibii titrii tamɔ potassium ni bɛ, ni haaa tsei afee fɔfɔi koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Can I prepare my own liquid fertilizer at home using a simple plastic bucket and animal manure?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafee nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yɛ shia kɛtsɔ plastic baagi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, you can make natural liquid fertilizer by stirring animal manure with water inside any rubber container or bucket and letting it steep for two weeks to release nutrients that feed your crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ ofee adebɔɔ mli nu ni ji ŋmɔshi nibii kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛ nu ni yɔɔ tsɛnsi loo rɔba baagi mli lɛ baafutu lɛ nɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, shi otsii enyɔ koni ejie niyenii ni haa onibii lɛ niyenii lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots become hard and woody if I do not harvest them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ wa ni amɛfee tsei kɛji mikpaaa amɛ mra lɛ?

english: As cassava plants age past maturity, the roots stop storing soft starch and begin developing tough plant fibers, turning the tubers hard and difficult to cook.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tso lɛ shɛ afii pɔtɛɛ ko he lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kpaɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ni amɛtoɔ ni amɛjeɔ tso lɛ mli tsɔi ni wa lɛ shishi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ wa ni ewa akɛ amɛhoomɔ.

english: Purple leaves on young maize usually signal a phosphorus deficiency in the soil or cold root conditions, preventing the crop from absorbing the energy it needs to build strong stems.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo shishifãi ni mli ejɔ. Ehaa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni ekɛma tso lɛ shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why do my tomato leaves wilt during the hot afternoon even when I watered the soil in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ amɛgboi moŋ? Higbɛ esa akɛ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu leebi?

english: In intense heat, tomato plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull water from the soil. They temporarily wilt to conserve moisture and usually recover when evening temperatures cool down.
ga: yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛbaagboi yɛ be kukuoo mli koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli, ni bei pii lɛ, amɛhe baajɔ amɛ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli ba shi.

english: Do I need special factory pots to start my vegetable seeds, or can I use local plastic containers?
ga: Ani tso krɛdɛɛ ko he miihia mi koni mabɔi aduawai dumɔwui adumɔ? Or can I use local plastic containers?

english: You do not need expensive pots; any clean rubber or plastic container from home will work as long as you poke holes in the bottom to allow extra water to drain out so the seeds do not rot.
ga: Tsɛnsi ni jara wa he ehiaaa bo. Rɔba loo plastic ni he tse fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shia lɛ baatsu nii kɛji ofo bu yɛ shishigbɛ koni nu babaoo atsɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ dumɔwui lɛ egbooo.

english: Why do I need to clear the vines and give my yam plants wooden stakes to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie wain tsei lɛ ni maha sweet potato tsei lɛ tso ni amɛkwɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need tall stakes to lift their leaves high into the sunlight, which helps the plant photosynthesize and generate enough energy to swell the tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso kakadaŋŋ ko ni baawó baai lɛ anɔ kɛya hulu lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ fotosintɛsis ni ekɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha tso lɛ yibii lɛ afuu.

english: Why should I pare and trim the outer roots of a new plantain sucker before I plant it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo ni mafolɔ dumɔwui heei asɛɛ shishifãi lɛ dani madu?

english: Trimming the outer layer and root base of a plantain sucker removes hidden weevils and harmful worm eggs, giving the new shoot a clean, pest-free start in the ground.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ plantain tsei lɛ asɛɛgbɛ kɛ amɛshishi lɛ, ebaajie ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ kɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii heei lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni he tse, ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bɛ mli.

english: How does planting cowpeas on my farm help the maize crop that I plant next season?
ga: Te tsina ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that naturally capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil through their roots, acting as a free, natural fertilizer for future crops like maize.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil or is getting logged with too much water. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure can help bring back the healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo ekɛ nu babaoo ewo mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Covering soil with dry grass or leaves (mulching) retains water in the soil, keeps plant roots cool during hot days, prevents weeds from growing, and rots over time to add rich nutrients to your farm.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (mulching) lɛ, ebaaha nu ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛkafite yɛ be ni sa mli koni ekɛ niyenii kpakpai afata oŋmɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so weak even when it rains heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your main crops. When weeds grow close to your plants, they take away the food your crops need to stay strong and produce big yields.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ tsei ni oyɔɔ mli lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji jwɛi kwɛ̃ yɛ otsei lɛ ahe Ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ koni tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: How do I know the right way to insert cassava stem cuttings into the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male bɔ ni akɛ ŋmei niji woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Plant cassava cuttings slanted at an angle or flat, ensuring the growth buds (nodes) point upwards toward the sky. Planting stem cuttings upside down causes weak sprouts and very poor tuber yield.
ga: Yucca tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi yɛ koŋ loo ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ haa ŋmeii ni miida lɛ (nodes) lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu tsei niji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha tuber yibii ni baa shi waa aba.

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a long hot, dry spell before the main rains start. Seeds planted too early will sprout and then dry up and die due to lack of continuous moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ be kakadaŋŋ, ni mli edɔ, ni mli egbiɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔi wuji lɛ jeɔ shishi. Dumɔwui ni adu mra tsɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛbaagbi ni amɛgboi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do I need to erect long wooden sticks next to my growing yam vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ato he lɛ? Amɛduɔ sweet potato wain tsei

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to produce food for big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the hot ground, exposes them to sunlight, and prevents fungal diseases caused by wet soil.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsɔnei lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni mli edɔ lɛ. hulu la lɛ nɔ ni etsi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ anaa.

english: Why are my ripe tomatoes developing dark, sunken rotten spots on the bottom of the fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ nii yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: This condition is blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit or uneven soil moisture. Keeping the soil consistently watered and adding agricultural lime or wood ash helps prevent it.
ga: Shihilɛ nɛɛ ji fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ejaaa. Kɛ́ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu daa ni akɛ okwaayeli mli ŋmei loo tso sũ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: What is causing ragged holes in the leaves and stems of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai kɛ amɛshishifãi amli lɛ baa?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding inside the plant's funnel. Checking your farm early and using recommended biopesticides or neem extract can protect your maize.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ tsei ashishifãi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni ajieɔ yi lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ abu oŋmɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before tiny pods start to form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani ŋmeii bibii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ? Ani ebaaje shishi efee?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when stressed by dry weather, lack of soil nutrients, or insect attack from sap-sucking pests like mirids (capsids). Managing shade and spraying for pests helps flowers develop into pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ hao amɛ. niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo kooloi ni yeɔ nu tamɔ mirids (capsids) lɛ tutuamɔ. Shade nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛfeɔ pods.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on the piece of land where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmeii yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ nɔ?

english: Maize uses up a lot of soil food, while legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts naturally capture nitrogen from the air and return it to the soil, restoring fertility for your next harvest.
ga: Abɛi kɛ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Koni okɛ babaoo aba ekoŋŋ kɛha okpamɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why does it take several years for cocoa trees to start producing good fruits after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ afii babaoo dani kookoo tsei jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ yibii beni adu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees spend their first three to five years establishing deep roots and strong branches to store energy. They need this foundation before they can support the heavy demand of producing quality pods season after season.
ga: Kakao tso bibioo ko heɔ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii etɛ kɛyashi enumɔ dani eshishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ niji ni mli wa baa koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato. Shishitoo nɛɛ he miihia amɛ dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛye amɛbua nibii babaoo ni ataoɔ yɛ be mli ni afeɔ pods ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my maize crops are getting enough nutrients from the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ miiná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛmiijɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Healthy maize plants have dark green, broad leaves and grow steadily. If the lower leaves start turning yellow or pale green, it is a sign that the plants are hungry for nitrogen and need nutrients.
ga: Abele tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ eŋɔli ni tsuɔ, baai ni mli kwɔ kɛ dalɛ ni yaa nɔ. Kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ bɔi ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse Etsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ he miihia nitrogen kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why should I keep some tall trees on my farm instead of cutting them all down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ tsei kakadaji anɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mafo tsei lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Large shade trees protect sensitive crops like cocoa from harsh sunlight and heat, reduce water evaporation from the soil, and drop leaves that decompose into natural fertilizer.
ga: Tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ kookoo he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ he. Ha nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. kɛ baai ni egbee shi ni fiteɔ ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily in direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains have wide leaves that create natural shade and hold soil moisture, helping the young cocoa survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Plantain ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo baa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Enɛ haa kookoo bibii lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants curl up and turn yellow during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava leaves curl to reduce water loss during hot, dry weather, but extreme curling and yellowing can also be caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that suck the sap from the leaves.
ga: Cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛba nu ni laajeɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ shi. Shi ŋmeii bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ baanyɛ aha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ fe nine ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: What causes my plantain trees to fall over easily when strong winds come?
ga: Mɛni haa plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi mlɛo kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miitswa?

english: Plantain stems usually fall over because soil pests like nematodes have damaged their roots, or because the fruit bunch has become too heavy for the shallow root system without a prop stick for support.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi tamɔ nematodes fiteɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ. Aloo akɛni aduawai akuu lɛ tsii tsɔ kɛha shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni sɛɛfimɔ bɛ he lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why does rain water stay on top of my land for days without soaking into the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ hiɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo ni ekɛ ehe wooo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Standing water means the soil is compacted or heavy in clay, which prevents drainage. Digging simple channels or adding organic material like compost helps open up the soil so water can sink in.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ loo eyɛ shikpɔŋ. ni tsiɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ naa Simple trenching Loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni agbele sũ lɛ mli koni nu lɛ abote mli.

english: How does clearing weeds right around the base of my crops help them grow bigger?
ga: Jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ajiemɔ Te mi tsei lɛ ashishitoo yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for groundwater and soil nutrients. Clearing them away ensures your crops get all the food and water they need without sharing.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ náa niyenii kɛ nu fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ, ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ amɛ aha.

english: Why do my pepper plants produce plenty of flowers but very few actual peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi pepper diɛŋtsɛ faaa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when exposed to intense heat stress, lack of water, or when there are not enough bees and insects around to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ amɛna nɔnyɛɛ kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli, nu ni bɛ, loo kɛ́ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi krokomɛi ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ bɛ.

english: Why is it good practice to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on the field after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ mli beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the ground, but crops like cowpeas and groundnuts put nitrogen back into the soil naturally, refreshing the land for the next planting season.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, shi ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina ŋmei kɛ ŋmei Ekɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I burn all the bush and weeds after clearing my farm land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishãa jwɛi kɛ jwɛi lɛ fɛɛ beni mijie he ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Burning destroys the naturally decaying leaves and soil organisms that feed your crops. Leaving cleared weeds to rot on top of the soil keeps it moist, cool, and rich in nutrients.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ baai kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni fiteɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni haa onibii lɛ niyenii lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi jwɛi ni ajie lɛ koni amɛgbo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i, edɔɔ, ni niyenii babaoo yɔɔ mli.

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves that easily burn in full sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains provides living cover that protects young cocoa from direct sun and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni buɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he lɛ yaa hiɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: When crops are too crowded, their roots fight over water, light, and soil food. Giving each plant proper distance helps them grow tall, stay healthy, and produce larger maize cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko kɛ ehe teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua lɛ ni ekwɛ̃. ehiɛ hewalɛ ni ewo ŋmãa ŋmeii wuji

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is losing its nutrients and needs help?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ faaa, ni kɛji akɛ yelikɛbuamɔ he miihia mi?

english: If your crops are growing slowly, have pale yellow leaves instead of deep green ones, or produce small yields, your soil is tired and needs compost, animal manure, or nutrient-restoring crops.
ga: Kɛji onibii lɛ daraa blɛoo Eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ najiaŋ. loo ewoɔ nibii fioo Oshikpɔŋ lɛ hu efite ni ehe miihia ni afee lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo tsei koni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ aba.

english: Leaf rolling is the plant's natural defense to save water. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface exposed to the sun and heat, keeping moisture trapped inside until weather cools.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu koni ekɛbu nu he. Tsei haa hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ amɛhe lɛ nɔ. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why do people encourage planting beans or groundnuts together with cassava or maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɔmɛi woɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni akɛfataa ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ahe lɛ he hewalɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and groundnuts capture natural nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil through their roots, which helps fertilize neighboring crops like maize naturally.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are my cassava leaves turning yellow and twisting with tiny white flies around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried and spread by whiteflies. Using disease-resistant cassava stems during planting keeps your crop healthy and high-yielding.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni whiteflies ji mɛi ni kɛ hela baa ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ Kɛ okɛ ŋmei tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ dumɔ be mli lɛ eyeɔ ebuaa ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why should I clear weeds early instead of waiting for them to grow tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi lɛ mra? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ ni amɛdara lɛ

english: Tall weeds steal light, rainwater, and plant food away from your crops before they can grow. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nutrients they need to establish strong roots.
ga: Jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ juɔ la, nugbɔ nu, kɛ niyenii ni aduɔ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli dani amɛdaraa. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛma shishifãi ni wa.

english: Plants drop blossoms when they experience stress from heat, dry soil, or a lack of soil food. Watering regularly and placing mulch around the roots keeps the soil cool so flowers can form fruit.
ga: Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nu lɛ daa ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ aha he ni oyɔɔ lɛ. Shishifãi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ awo yibii.

english: Why is it harmful to plant tomatoes in the exact same field spot every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu tomato yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously builds up specific soil pests and diseases in that spot. Rotating tomatoes with corn, beans, or cassava breaks the pest cycle and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aaaya nɔ akwɛ lɛ baaha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yɔɔ nakai he lɛ pɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa. Tomatoi ni akɛ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, loo ŋmãa baatsake lɛ Ebaaye ebua ni efo ŋmãa ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ mli ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turning yellow and burning under the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate strong direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantain or cassava planted next to them to act as living shade umbrellas until the cocoa trees grow stronger.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Koni etsu nii akɛ hulutsoo kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baaná hewalɛ.

english: Why is my maize crop turning pale yellow instead of deep green before it produces ears?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ dani ejeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Yellowing maize leaves are a sign that the soil lacks nitrogen or that heavy water logging is preventing the roots from absorbing nutrients properly.
ga: Abɛi baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo akɛ tso lɛ tsiimɔ miitsi shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain trees keep falling over whenever heavy winds blow across my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baatswa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots and heavy tops. Supporting the stems with sturdy wooden or bamboo stakes and mounding rich earth around the base keeps the plants upright.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse. Tso loo ŋmei tsei ni wa ni akɛfiɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ sɛɛ Kɛ shikpɔŋ ni jara wa ni abua naa ni ebɔleɔ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: My tomato plants produce many flowers, but the flowers drop off without turning into tomatoes. What is happening?
ga: Mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo. Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsɔɔɔ tomato. meni ba?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures are too high, when watering is inconsistent, or when there are not enough beneficial insects around to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Be mli ni nu ni akɛhaa lɛ bɛ daa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni baanyɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ lɛ faaa.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and looking tiny and twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bibii ni amɛfite lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking the plant's sap and transmitting viruses that prevent normal leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛhaa helai ni tsiɔ baa lɛ adalɛ naa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting underground before I get the chance to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani minine shɛɔ hegbɛ nɔ ni mikpaa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when planted in waterlogged soil that does not drain well. Wet, airless soil starves the roots of oxygen and allows soft-rot fungi to thrive.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ ni nu shwieee nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ aye hɔmɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ daa.

english: Why do I need to cut tall wooden sticks for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tsei kakadaji koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are vines that need to lift their leaves up toward direct sunlight to manufacture food, which then flows down to build large underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tso ji wain tso ni esa akɛ ewo ebaai lɛ anɔ koni hulu la ashɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni ewo niyenii. Kɛkɛ lɛ, efoɔ kɛyaa shi ni efeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: If I plant maize on the exact same piece of land year after year, will it affect my harvest?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ, Ani ebaana mikpamɔ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes specific soil nutrients and causes soil pests to multiply. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas restores nitrogen naturally.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. ni eha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ayi afa. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen baa ekoŋŋ

english: Why do my crop leaves get dark spots and white powdery coatings during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ powda yɛŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: High moisture and humidity during rainy periods create ideal conditions for fungal diseases to grow and spread spores across damp leaf surfaces.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni baa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ ashwaa baai ni mli efɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: How do I know if I am giving my newly planted seeds too much water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mikɛ nu babaoo eha midumɔwui ni midu ehee lɛ?

english: If the ground stays muddy and waterlogged, seeds cannot get air to breathe. They will turn soft, rot, and fail to sprout out of the ground.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ewo muji lolo ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ Dumɔwui nyɛŋ amu, amɛbaafee bɔdɔɔ, amɛbaagboi ni amɛkwɛɛɛ kɛjɛŋ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight because their tender leaves lose moisture too quickly. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain alongside young cocoa creates a living umbrella that keeps the plants cool and retains soil moisture.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kookoo tso lɛ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya tsɔ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, kɛ kookoo bibii lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo baa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do my yam vines need long wooden stakes to climb up instead of just growing along the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ lɛ? koni ekwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he?

english: Yam leaves need maximum sunlight to capture energy and transfer it down to grow thick tubers underground. Staking lifts the foliage off the soil, which also prevents ground dampness from causing leaf diseases.
