ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo koni amɛmɔ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛya shi koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni mli wa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking baaha baai lɛ ajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ baa helai hu baaa.

english: Why shouldn't I let all the small shoots grow around my main plantain tree at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii bibii shwereɔ yɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ he yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: When too many shoots (suckers) grow around the main plantain stem, they compete for nutrients and water. Pruning them down to leave only one or two strong suckers ensures the main plant gets enough food to produce big, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii (ŋmeii) babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ plantain tso wulu lɛ he lɛ Ebaatswa akaŋ kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo tsei niji wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my crop harvests keep getting smaller every year when I plant maize on the exact same plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Growing maize repeatedly on the same plot drains specific nutrients, especially nitrogen, from the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas puts nitrogen back into the dirt naturally and restores soil strength.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ, abaajie niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen, ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Abele ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ baaha nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ebaaha sũ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water settles around them without draining away, suffocating the tubers. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges of dirt allows excess rainwater to flow off, keeping the tubers safe underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu babɔle amɛhe. without draining out suffocate the head Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. ni oha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe

english: Why are my young maize leaves turning yellow from the tip downward during the middle of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ amɛnajiaŋ kɛmiiba shi yɛ be lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves are a sign that the crop has used up the available nitrogen in the soil. Applying proper nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost early in the growing cycle keeps the leaves deep green and active.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ efite nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ shishijee mli. Ebaaha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni yɔɔ wala.

english: This rot is caused by a fungal condition known as Black Pod disease, which thrives in cold, damp shade. Pruning excess tree branches allows airflow and sunlight to dry off the pods and reduce fungus growth.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ blackpod hela. Ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ko ni mli ejɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli. Tso lɛ niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli kɛ hulu la ni haa tsei lɛ amli tsei lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ ayibɔ baa shi.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up into tight balls and stop growing new shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ bɔɔlu ni mli wa ni ekpaa ŋmeii heei ni shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Curled leaves are caused by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies or aphids that feed on plant sap and pass viruses to the plant. Spraying neem oil extract or soapy water early keeps these sap-sucking pests off your crop.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. ni yeɔ tsei amli nu ni ekɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ yaa tsei lɛ anɔ Neem fɔ loo nu ni akɛ samla shwieɔ nɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni nuɔ nu nɛɛ akashɛ onibii ahe.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep falling off before producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat or erratic watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist and putting grass mulch around the stem keeps the root zone cool so the flowers stay on and form fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni ejaaa mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Tso lɛ baaha shishifã lɛ he lɛ afee fɛ̃i. Koni akɛ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai lɛ ahi shi

english: Why are there ragged holes chewed right through the central shoots of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji ni ekpɔtɔ yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Mikɛ mi-bibii ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ miiye nii?

english: This hole-chewing damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding inside the center funnel of the plant. Checking fields early and placing neem extract or recommended treatments into the funnel stops the worms before they destroy the crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ faa lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ bu ni shwieɔ nii amli nɛɛ fitemɔ baa. Hei ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ akwɛmɔ mra kɛ neem mli nu loo tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ ni akɛwoɔ ŋmei lɛ mli. Ehaa ŋmeii lɛ kpaa dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight because it scorches their delicate leaves and quickly dries out the soil moisture. Keeping some large shade trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantains around them provides the shade and cool air they need to survive while young.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Enɛ baashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ agbi oya. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ akwɛmɔ loo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ baaha amɛná hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛblahiiaŋ kɛ oblayeiaŋ.

english: Why do other farmers tell me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts together with my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi krokomɛi Ko ni amɛkɛɛ mi akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ adu tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into plant food in the soil through their roots. Planting them alongside maize helps feed the maize naturally and keeps your soil rich without relying completely on expensive chemical fertilizers.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ heɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmãa ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ehe afɔ̃ tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ anɔ.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with plenty of dark leaves, but the tubers underground are tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni tsuɔ babaoo lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen fertilizer or is planted in rich, leafy soil, the plant spends all its food energy growing big leaves and tall stems above ground instead of sending stored energy down to build heavy tubers below.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmei babaoo nɔ loo adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baai babaoo yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Tsei kɛ amɛ niyenii hewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo baai agboi kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsu hewalɛ ni ato lɛ kɛya shi koni ekɛfee yitso ni tsii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers usually drop off when the daytime temperatures become too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. When the plant gets stressed by hot weather or irregular watering, it drops its flowers to conserve energy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ waa mli lɛ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ hao tsei lɛ Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: What causes the leaves of my cassava plants to curl up, look twisted, and turn light yellow?
ga: Mɛni haa cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛtsakeɔ, ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ?

english: This symptom is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is a virus carried and spread from plant to plant by tiny whiteflies. The disease prevents the leaves from trapping sunlight effectively, which reduces your crop yield.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ okadi nɛɛ baa ji ŋmei mosaic hela. Enɛ ji hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ. Hela lɛ tsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkamɔ hulu la lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting green shoots even while they are resting inside my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔji ni ŋmɔji shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni amɛjɔɔ amɛhe yɛ mi ŋmɔ lɛ mli po lɛ?

english: Yam tubers are living plant parts that naturally go into a sleep period after harvest. Once warm, humid weather sets in, the tuber naturally wakes up and uses its internal food energy to grow new shoots so it can reproduce.
ga: Sweet potato tubers ji tso lɛ fã ni hiɛ ka ni yaa adebɔɔ mli wɔɔhe be mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo be je shishi ebaa lɛ Bulb lɛ teɔ shi yɛ ebɔɔ su mli ni ekɛ niyenii hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii heei koni amɛnyɛ amɛfɔ.

english: The very first rain is often followed by a long, hot dry spell before the main rainy season fully establishes. If you plant too early, the seeds will sprout, but the hot sun that follows will kill the young seedlings before the next rain arrives.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ nyiɛɔ latsaa be kakadaŋŋ ni mli edɔ, ni mli egbi lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi kwraa. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃. Shi hulu ni tsoɔ waa ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ gbeɔ tsei bibii lɛ dani nugbɔ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ baa.

english: Why does leaving weeds around my young maize cause the maize leaves to turn pale green and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ashi jwɛi yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ? Mi ŋmãa gbekɛ lɛ haa ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni ekpaa dalɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that steal food, water, and sunlight away from your crop. When weeds crowd around maize, the maize loses the battle for soil nutrients, causing its leaves to turn pale and its growth to stall.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Beni jwɛi ebɔle ŋmãa lɛ he lɛ ŋmãa lɛ yeɔ ta ni ewuɔ koni ená niyenii kpakpai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ kunim. Ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdalɛ kpaa.

english: Why are my young green oranges rotting and falling off the tree before they get fully ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tangerine bibii lɛ miifite ni amɛmiigbee shi kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛmiikwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ?

english: Young citrus fruits often rot and fall because fruit flies lay eggs underneath the skin of the fruit. When the eggs hatch into tiny maggots, they eat the inside of the orange, causing it to rot early and drop to the ground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, citrus aduawai bibii lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ejaakɛ aduawai amli ŋmeii woɔ amɛwui yɛ aduawai lɛ ahewolo lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ wɔɔji lɛ fɔ lɛ, amɛbatsɔmɔɔ ŋmeii bibii. Ebaaye ŋmei lɛ mli. Enɛ ɔ haa nɛ e puɛɔ mlamlaamla nɛ e gbeeɔ zugba.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during rainstorms when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plantain suckers are planted too close together, their roots crowd each other out near the surface and cannot spread wide or deep into the dirt. Without a deep root anchor, the heavy plants easily get pushed over by strong winds.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu plantain tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ feɔ ekome kɛbɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. ni enyɛŋ egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli babaoo loo ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ Kɛji ŋshɔkei ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ bɛ lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ shwieɔ tsei ni tsii lɛ anɔ oya.

english: Improved hybrid cocoa varieties typically start bearing pods within 2 to 3 years after planting, whereas older traditional varieties often take 4 to 5 years to produce their first harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jeɔ ŋmɔtɔ shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ, yɛ be mli ni kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ blema lɛ fɔɔ afii 4 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛshɛɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaa lɛ he.

english: Cassava is generally ready to harvest between 9 to 12 months after planting, which is usually indicated when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, leaving bare stems.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ajieɔ enɛ kpo kɛ́ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi, ni amɛshi tsei lɛ ahe nɔ ko nɔ ko.

english: Why should I plant plantains in the same field as my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-cocoa dumɔwui bibii lɛ duɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and easily damaged by direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have broad leaves that provide temporary shade and retain soil moisture for the cocoa trees during their early years.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni hulu la fiteɔ oya. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko mli, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛhaa kookoo tso lɛ yɛ eshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: My late father left me an old cocoa farm where trees produce very few pods; should I cut them down or keep tending them?
ga: Mitsɛ ni egbo lɛ shi mi yɛ kookoo ŋmɔ momo ko mli ni tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ. Ani esa akɛ mafo mli loo makwɛ nɔ?

english: Cocoa trees over 25 to 30 years old naturally decrease in yield. Cutting down old, unproductive trees and replanting with high-yielding hybrid varieties is recommended to restore the farm's productivity.
ga: Cocoa tsei ni eye fe afii 25 kɛyashi 30 lɛ baaná yibiiwoo ni baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Akɛ ŋaawoo ha akɛ afo tsei ni egbɔ ni wooo yibii lɛ amli ni akɛ tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo awo amɛ najiaŋ koni akɛku sɛɛ afee ŋmɔ mli nibii.

english: Is it good practice to burn grass and weeds on my field before planting seeds?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ mashã jwɛi kɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ dani madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Burning cleared weeds destroys valuable organic matter and kills useful soil organisms. Clearing without burning allows the plant material to rot into compost, which enriches the soil over time.
ga: Jwɛi ni ajie lɛ ni ashãa lɛ fiteɔ nibii ni jara wa ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ni egbeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie tso lɛ mli nibii lɛ ni ashãaa lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ mli nibii lɛ fiteɔ ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do extension officers advise planting legumes like cowpea alongside my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni extension agent lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa kɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpea have special roots that capture nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer that helps crops like maize grow better.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellowing leaves on maize plants usually signal a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which is an essential nutrient needed for plants to make food and grow healthily.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛɛmɛi ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves wilt in the hot afternoon sun even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai gboɔ yɛ shwane hulutsoo be mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: In high heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull it from the soil. They temporarily droop to conserve moisture and usually recover when temperatures drop in the evening.
ga: kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa Tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛbaatsi amɛhe be kukuoo ko koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. ni bei pii lɛ, ehaa ehe feɔ shoo kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi gbɛkɛ.

english: What causes tiny holes and chewed edges on the leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? kɛ ŋmeii ni ashɛreɔ yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: Holes in maize leaves are commonly caused by destructive pests like the Fall Armyworm, which feed on the growing shoots and leaves if they are not treated early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni yeɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni miida kɛji atsaaa amɛ mra lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni baa ŋmeii amli lɛ baa.

english: It is best to apply fertilizer early in the morning or late in the afternoon when the soil is moist, as heavy sun can evaporate or burn the nutrients before the roots absorb them.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli leebi loo shwane be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Yɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ hewɔ lɛ Amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo amɛtsake niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ.

english: If I cannot afford chemical fertilizer right now, can proper watering alone help my crops grow well?
ga: Kɛji minyɛɛɛ mahe tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ bianɛ Ani nu ni sa ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ pɛ baaye abua ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, consistent watering helps plants absorb the natural nutrients already present in the soil. While water does not add new chemicals, adequate soil moisture keeps soil organisms active and prevents plant stress, allowing your crops to make the best use of existing nutrients.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ nu lɛ kɛ tsofai heei komɛi fataaa he moŋ, shi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ehaaa tsei lɛ afee nɔ ni haoɔ. Ye obua onibii ni okɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know the right time of day to water my crops so the water does not go to waste?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛ nu awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli? Koni akafite nu lɛ?

english: The best time to water crops is early in the morning or late in the afternoon. Watering during these cooler hours allows the soil to absorb moisture deeply before the strong sun causes it to evaporate.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔ tsei anɔ nu ji leebi loo shwane. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli kwɔ dani hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: How does covering my soil with dry grass help my crops during hot weather?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Covering the soil around your crops with dry leaves or grass (mulching) acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool and stops water from evaporating quickly, helping your plants stay hydrated longer.
ga: Mulching around Nibii ni aduɔ ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: What is the most important thing I should do to nurture young crop seedlings right after transplanting them?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mafee koni manyɛ makwɛ dumɔwui bibii lɛ anɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni adu amɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Young seedlings need gentle watering immediately after transplanting and temporary shade from harsh afternoon sunlight so their delicate roots can settle into the new soil without drying out.
ga: Ehe miihia ni afɔ dumɔwui bibii lɛ anɔ nu blɛoo amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni adu amɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ. ni eha hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ aná hejɔɔmɔ be kukuoo ko. Enɛ haa shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ hee lɛ nɔ ni amɛgbiɛɛ.

english: Why do my crop roots need soft, loose soil instead of hard, packed soil to grow well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse he hiaa mi tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ? Mohu ɔ, e ji zugba nɛ mi wa, nɛ e mi mi wa nɛ haa nɛ e nyɛɔ waa wawɛɛ saminya.

english: Soft, loose soil contains tiny air pockets and allows crop roots to easily spread out deep into the ground to find water, anchor the plant firmly, and take in air to breathe.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni egbɔjɔ mli. ni ehaa tso shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛna nu Ha tso lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ. ni omu kɔɔyɔɔ koni omu

english: Can giving my crops too much water actually harm them?
ga: Ani nu ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ amli fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aye amɛ awui?

english: Yes, overwatering fills all the air spaces in the soil with water, which can drown the roots, cause them to rot, and turn the plant leaves yellow.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fe nine lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yiɔ kɛ nu. Enɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli, ni eha amɛ fite, ni eha tso lɛ baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: How can I tell if my crops are wilting because of heat or because of a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho yɛ latsaa loo hela hewɔ?

english: Crops wilting from heat will usually perk back up in the cool evening after watering, whereas crops suffering from disease will remain wilted, yellowed, or spotted regardless of water or time of day.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni hulutsoo lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ daa ekoŋŋ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli beni awo amɛ nu sɛɛ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ baaya nɔ agbɔjɔ, amɛfee ŋmɔŋ, loo amɛbaafee ŋmɔŋ ni nu loo gbi lɛ mli be kɔɔɔ he eko.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly into tubes during the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tsɔji yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up during hot afternoons as a natural defense to protect themselves from losing too much water to the hot air, unrolling once the temperature cools down.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni oootsɔ nɔ obu ohe kɛjɛ nu babaoo ni baafite yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ he. Ejieɔ ehe kpo kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli ba shi.

english: Why do my crops grow very tall and thin but fail to produce good fruit or yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ waa ni eyɛ mlɛo shi ewooo yibii kpakpai loo ewooo yibii kpakpai lɛ?

english: Crops often grow tall and weak when they are planted too close together or lack sufficient sunlight, causing them to stretch upward for light instead of spending energy on growing fruits or seeds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei daa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ amɛhe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ shwieɔ ehe koni ekɛ la lɛ atsu nii moŋ fe ni ekɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo yibii loo dumɔwui.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my plants turn yellow when rain has been sparse?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ashishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ fioo lɛ?

english: When water is scarce, plants automatically drop or sacrifice their older, lower leaves to conserve water and nutrients for the younger, growing leaves at the top.
ga: Kɛ nu faaa Tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ baashwie shi loo ekɛ ebaai bibii lɛ baashã afɔle koni ekɛto nu kɛ niyenii he kɛha baai bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and wither when there are no plantain trees planted next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui ko bɛ ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn under full direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains provides shade, acts like a protective umbrella, and keeps the soil moist so the young cocoa can survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains lɛ haa hulutsoo baa. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela ni buɔ mɔ he ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ bɔni afee ni kookoo bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cocoa trees very close to each other to get more pods on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni mafee ŋmeii babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When trees are planted too close together, they fight for sunlight, water, and soil food. Overcrowded farms also trap damp air, which allows diseases to jump quickly from tree to tree.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Okwaafoi ni eyi obɔ lɛ hu mɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli efɔ. ni kɛ helai srɔtoi baa Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ.

english: Why do so many flowers fall off my cocoa trees without turning into full pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shwieɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛfeee ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally grow thousands of flowers but can only support a small fraction into full pods. Flower drop happens naturally when the tree runs out of energy, lacks water, or when tiny insects fail to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ. Shi ebaanyɛ eye ebua fã bibioo ko pɛ. kɛyashi be mli ni pod lɛ eyiɔ obɔ pɛ Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛ́ tso ko bɛ hewalɛ, nu bɛ ehe, loo kɛ́ kooloi bibii bote mli. Enyɛɛɛ ekɛ fɔfɔii awo mli

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce a huge harvest in one year and very few pods the following year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo afi kome shi ewoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ yɛ afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees use up massive amounts of nutrients during a heavy harvest year and need time to rest and rebuild energy. Proper feeding with fertilizer and regular pruning help keep production steady every year.
ga: Cacao tsei yeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo yɛ amɛkpamɔ afii ni mli wa lɛ amli. ni ehe miihia be ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe ni ekɛ hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli jogbaŋŋ kɛ tsei ni afoɔ daa lɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ yaa nɔ daa afi fɛɛ afi.

english: Why are the pods on my cocoa tree turning black and rotting during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in damp, dark environments. Clearing weeds and harvesting pods as soon as they rot stops the fungus spores from splashing onto healthy pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ duŋ yɔɔ. Nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ jwɛi amli kɛ ŋmeii ni abua naa kɛji amɛgboi pɛ Ehaa fungal spores lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ.

english: Why do small insects like mirids make the leaves and branches of my cocoa trees turn brown and look burnt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ mirids lɛ haa mi-cacao tsei lɛ ahe baai kɛ amɛniji lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eshã lɛ?

english: Mirids bite into young shoots and branches to feed on sap, injecting poison that kills the plant tissue. The damaged branches dry up and look burnt, reducing the tree's ability to produce pods.
ga: Mirids ŋmɔɔ tsei bibii kɛ tsei aniji koni amɛnu nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Okɛ tsofa ni fiteɔ tso lɛ mli fãji lɛ awo mli. Niji ni efite lɛ baagbi ni etamɔ nɔ ni eshã. Enɛ haa nyɛmɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛbaawo ŋmeii lɛ baa shi.

english: Why is it necessary for me to cut off the fresh shoots growing directly out of the bottom of my cocoa trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ kookoo lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Those extra shoots, called chupons, suck away valuable food and water that the tree needs to grow pods. Removing them ensures all the tree's energy goes into producing healthy fruit.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ chupons nɛɛ shwieɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni jara wa ni he hiaa tso lɛ koni ekɛwo ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie lɛ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛwoɔ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ jeɔ kpo.

english: How does trimming the tall branches of my old cocoa trees help them bear more fruit?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ mi-cacao tso momo lɛ niji kakadaji ni afolɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua lɛ ni ewo yibii babaoo?

english: Trimming opens up the canopy so sunlight and air can reach all parts of the tree. Sunlight helps the tree make food, while good airflow dries out moisture that causes pod diseases.
ga: Edging gbeleɔ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ashɛ tso lɛ fãi fɛɛ ahe. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ hela baa lɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoa trees droop and dry up during the dry Harmattan wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The hot, dry Harmattan winds pull moisture out of the leaves faster than the roots can drink water from the soil. Placing dead leaves around the trunk base as mulch helps lock moisture into the ground during dry spells.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ anu nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nibii ni gboi ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ ahe Mulching lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: How do I know the exact time a cocoa pod is ready for me to pluck without damaging the beans inside?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be pɔtɛɛ ni kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ko efee klalo akɛ mafolɔ ni mifiteee kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: A pod is ripe when its color changes completely from green to yellow, or from red to orange/yellow. You can also tap the pod lightly; a hollow sound means the seeds inside have loosened from the outer skin.
ga: Pods lɛ ekwɛ̃ kɛji su tsake kɛjɛ eŋɔli kɛtee ŋmɔŋ. Aloo kɛjɛ red kɛtee orange/yellow kwraa. Obaanyɛ otswa pod lɛ hu fioo. Gbee ni mli ewo muji lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ egbee shi kɛjɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmei lɛ he.

english: Does planting my crops very close together give me a bigger harvest from my field?
ga: Ani tsei ni madu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ baaha maná ŋmaa babaoo?

english: No, planting crops too close together forces them to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Correct spacing gives each plant enough room to grow strong roots and produce bigger yields.
ga: Dabi, tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ he. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ shishifãi ni wa baakwɛ̃ ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Can I plant maize and beans together on the same land, or will they harm each other?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ loo amɛbaaye amɛhe awui?

english: Yes, you can plant them together safely. Beans take nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which helps the maize grow better, while the maize stalks give support to climbing beans.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ amɛ afee ekome shweshweeshwe. Beans jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa tsei yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛfiɔ ŋmãa ni kwɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when the hot season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni hulutsoo be lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate roots and soft leaves that burn under direct, harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to them acts like a canopy umbrella to shield them until they are strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe waɔ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do the leaves of my young maize plants have small holes in them like they are being eaten from the inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Tamɔ nɔ ni ayeɔ kɛjɛɔ emli?

english: Small holes in maize leaves are usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm feeding on the growing center of the plant. Checking your crops early helps you apply natural or approved treatments before the plant is destroyed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm ni yeɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ni edaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai amli lɛ baa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Ehaa okɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai loo tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii dani tso lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants turn yellow and stop growing after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean essential nutrients like nitrogen have been washed deep into the soil away from the plant's roots by rain. Adding compost or manure around the plant helps replace lost food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ afɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Away from the roots of plants by rainwater. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii wo Tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ niyenii ni elaaje lɛ ato najiaŋ.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller yields every year when I plant the same crop on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi be mli ni miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year and lets specific pests build up. Rotating different crops keeps the soil balanced and healthy.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. ni oha tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi abua amɛhe naa. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ mli srɔtoi ni atsakeɔ lɛ Yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist after light rain, but not during heavy downpours. Covering the fertilizer with a small layer of soil near the root zone protects it from running off.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Shi jeee yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ bibioo ko ni akɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nɔ Ebɛŋkɛɔ shishifã lɛ he lɛ, enɛ baatsi ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa koni ekajo foi.

english: Why does the soil on my farm dry out so fast during hot days, making my crops wilt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ? Mahã midumɔ nii lɛ agbi?

english: Bare soil loses water quickly through evaporation under direct sun. Covering the ground around your crops with dried grass or leaves traps moisture in the soil and keeps root temperature cool.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi lɛ nɔ. He ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ ni akɛhaa Nibii ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi baadu lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eha shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i.

english: Why are my cassava roots small and woody even though the plant leaves look big and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛji tsei eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ baai lɛ dara ni amɛji eŋɔli moŋ?

english: Hard or compacted soil prevents cassava roots from expanding into full tubers. Also, too much nitrogen makes the plant grow excessive leaf branches instead of storing food in the root tubers underneath.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo ni mli edɔ lɛ tsiɔ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛfee bulbs ni eyi obɔ. Kɛfata he lɛ, nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ haa tso lɛ niji kɛ baai babaoo shwereɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ niyenii baato shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why should I cut off extra suckers or stems growing out of my plantain or tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ plantains loo tomato tsei amli lɛ?

english: Extra suckers steal water and food away from the main plant. Cutting off weak extra stems ensures that all nutrients go directly into making larger fruits and heavier bunches.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ yaa aduawai wuji lɛ kɛ tsei akui ni tsii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crop plants need to grow green and strong. Adding compost, animal manure, or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea will help bring back the healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Nɔ ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ afee eŋɔli ni ehiɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Cocoa flowers often drop off when the tree is stressed by dry weather, poor soil nutrients, or insect pests like mirids. Keeping adequate shade trees, applying proper fertilizer, and managing pests before flowering helps the trees keep their flowers and form healthy pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ pollen Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ Ni akɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ Kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui dani amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛkwɛɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ni mli wa.

english: Why are my hot pepper plants dropping their blossoms during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-hot pepper tso lɛ fɔɔ yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat causes pepper plants to drop their blossoms to save water and energy. Watering your plants early in the morning and providing light shade during the hottest parts of the day helps the flowers stay on the plant to produce fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Nu ni oooha tso lɛ leebi ni oha hulutsoo yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the soil around them for too long without draining away. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the roots stay healthy and dry.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ wa ni amɛgbi.

english: How does covering the soil around my crops with dry grass help them survive dry weather?
ga: Mulching around Te ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛ jwɛi yeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like a blanket that traps moisture in the ground and shields plant roots from hot sunshine. As the dry grass decays over time, it also adds nutrients to enrich your soil.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli ni ebuɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Kɛ jwɛi ni egbi lɛ fite yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ Hay hu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ baafata oshikpɔŋ lɛ he.

english: Why is it good practice for me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas together with my main grain crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei kɛ mi ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. Planting them alongside grain crops like maize acts as a natural soil fertilizer, helping your main crop grow better while giving you an extra harvest.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa he lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa onibii titrii lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ kɛ agbɛnɛ hu ni amɛwoɔ nibii krokomɛi ni fata he.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when heavy wind or rain comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa loo nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems and carry heavy fruit bunches at the top, making them easy for strong winds to push over. Supporting the stems with strong wooden poles or bamboo forks helps bear the heavy weight and stops them from snapping.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akui ni tsii yɛ amɛyiteŋ, ni no haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baatsɔ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tso loo ŋmei ni wa fiɔ tsɔne lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsɔne ni tsii lɛ ni ebaatsi enaa koni ekakumɔ.

english: Why do I need to lift and stake my yam vines with wooden sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miwoɔ sweet potato wain tsei anɔ ni mikɛ tsei duɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally climb to catch as much sunlight as possible to produce energy. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, away from soil pests, and exposes them to sunlight so the plant can grow large tubers below the soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛkɛfee hewalɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe ni okɛwo hulu la mli bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ akwɛ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: What is causing small holes in my maize leaves and caterpillars eating inside the center shoot?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? yɛ mi-abɛi lɛ amli kɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that lays eggs on leaves and feeds inside the growing tip of the plant. Applying recommended organic or chemical sprays directly into the leaf center early in the morning will destroy the caterpillars before they destroy the crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ baai anɔ ni eyeɔ nii yɛ tsei ni miida lɛ ashishifãi amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ko ni akɛshwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ loo tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ wo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ tɛ̃ɛ leebi lɛ, ebaafite ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by heat stress or tiny insects called whiteflies that pass viruses to the plant. Keeping the soil moist with mulch and controlling whiteflies helps protect your tomato plants and keeps fruit growing properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo loo kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies ni kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛyaa tsei lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akudɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu tomato tsei ahe ni eye ebua aduawai lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves that provide living shade and keep the soil moist, protecting young cocoa trees until they grow strong enough to withstand direct heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Buu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ dɔlɛ ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Planting cassava stem cuttings at a slant helps the plant develop roots that spread wider and deeper into the soil, which leads to bigger cassava tubers and prevents the plant from falling over in heavy winds.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei ni afolɔ ashwie shi yɛ koŋ nɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ náa shishifãi ni gbɛɔ eshwaa babaoo ni eyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmei shishifãi lɛ feɔ agboi. ni otsi tsei anaa koni amɛkagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miitswa.

english: Why do I need to set up tall wooden sticks for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mato tso kakadaŋŋ ko koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines off the ground allows the leaves to catch maximum sunlight and fresh air. This improves growth, prevents leaf rot diseases from ground dampness, and helps the plant produce much larger underground tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ awó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa babaoo. Enɛ baaha dalɛ aya hiɛ. Tsi baa ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ naa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni dara kwraa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually show that the plant is hungry for nitrogen in the soil. The plant moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed new top leaves, indicating that your soil needs compost or nitrogen fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baa heei lɛ niyenii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts together with my corn will make my soil richer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ mikɛ mi-ŋmã lɛ du ŋmei lɛ, ebaaha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nii babaoo lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into natural fertilizer inside the soil. This feeds the soil naturally, helping companion crops like corn grow healthier without needing as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni etsakeɔ lɛ efeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni fata he, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ, ni amɛnáa hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ ni tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ he ehiaaa amɛ.

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when they experience extreme heat, irregular watering, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. When stressed, the plant drops flowers to save its energy rather than spending effort on growing fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛbote la ni naa wa mli. Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛfataa he Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei lɛ baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: These are fall armyworms, which target the soft, growing heart of the corn plant where it is moist and hidden from sun and birds. Treating them early with neem extract or recommended sprays prevents them from destroying the stalk.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji ŋmeii ni egbee shi ni kɛ amɛhiɛ fɔɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ tsui ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni miida lɛ nɔ yɛ he ni edɔ ni ekɛ ehe ewo hulu kɛ okpoi adɛŋ lɛ. Amɛtsamɔ mra Kɛ akɛ neem mli nu ni ajieɔ yi loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite tso lɛ yitso lɛ.

english: Why should I cut away the small extra stems growing at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii bibii ni fata he lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain tso lɛ shishi lɛ he

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and nutrients from the main plantain stem. Removing all but one or two strong suckers ensures the main stem gets enough food to produce a large, healthy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei krɛdɛɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ plantain tso titri lɛ mli. Ajieɔ ŋmeii fɛɛ ja ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ baaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee plantains ni wa ni dara.

english: Why does covering the dirt around my crops with dry leaves or grass help them survive the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mulching around Miŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Covering soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like a blanket that blocks the sun, keeps the soil cool, stops water from evaporating quickly, and keeps weeds from growing.
ga: Mulching kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi Atsɛɔ lɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃

english: Why is it better for me to water my vegetable garden early in the morning rather than in the afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miwoɔ mi aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu leebi moŋ fe shwane lɛ?

english: Watering in the cool morning allows the plant roots to absorb moisture deeply before heat sets in. In the hot afternoon, most water evaporates into the air before reaching the roots, and water droplets on hot leaves can burn the plant.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi yɛ leebi ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ mli lɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ dani hulutsoo be lɛ baa.Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ Nu babaoo shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani eshɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ni nu ni hoɔ yɛ baai ni mli edɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã tso lɛ.

english: Maize leaves roll up during extreme heat as a natural survival reaction to conserve moisture. By rolling up, the leaf exposes less surface area to the hot air, which reduces water loss through evaporation.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli wala nifeemɔ koni ekɛto fɛ̃i he. Kɛji okɛ ohe fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ shɛɛɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ he babaoo. Enɛ haa nu ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my corn plants turn yellow in a V-shape and dry up before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli ni amɛmiigbi dani akpa lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. When nitrogen is scarce, the maize plant moves the available nutrient from older leaves at the bottom to feed the new leaves growing at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛji nitrogen faaa lɛ, Abɛi tsiɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why is it not recommended for me to save seeds from my harvested hybrid maize to plant next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔɔ akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mi-hybrid corn harvest lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid maize seeds are specially produced by crossing two specific parent plants for high yield. If you replant seeds saved from your harvest, the second-generation crop loses that vigor, resulting in uneven growth and smaller cobs.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ tsuɔ nii krɛdɛɛ kɛtsɔ fɔlɔi tsei enyɔ ni akɛfoɔ mli koni amɛwo yibii babaoo lɛ nɔ. Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ Yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baafite hewalɛ. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa ni ekɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee, ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate harsh direct sunlight and will dry out. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide natural shade and conserve soil moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ, ni amɛbaagbi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ yaa hiɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa.

english: What causes black spots to spread rapidly across my cocoa pods during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii diji lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Black spots on cocoa pods are caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection. Rainy conditions and high humidity help the fungus spread easily through splashing rainwater and damp air.
ga: Black Pod hela, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ni baa kookoo tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ ŋmei lɛ baagbɛ eshwa kɛtsɔ nugbɔ nu ni shwieɔ shi kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ nɔ.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when stressed by extreme conditions, such as excessively high temperatures, irregular watering, or a lack of essential soil nutrients like phosphorus.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji shihilɛi ni mli wa waa, tamɔ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa lɛ hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ fɔsfɔs.

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is commonly caused by a plant virus transmitted by small insects like whiteflies. As the insects feed on plant sap, they infect the crop, leading to stunted and curled growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso mli hela ko ni kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies kɛbaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ baa, ejaakɛ kooloi lɛ yeɔ tso lɛ mli nu. Amɛbaatswa ŋmɔshi nibii ahe hela. Enɛ haa edalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni ebɔleɔ ehe lɛ baa.

english: Cassava is typically mature when the lower leaves on the stem turn yellow and shed, and the soil surrounding the base of the plant begins to crack upward as the roots expand beneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei eda kɛji tso lɛ shishi baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni shishifãi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ eshishi lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce very thin roots when I plant them too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ mlɛo waa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are crowded together, their roots compete heavily for limited soil nutrients, water, and sunlight, preventing each individual plant from swelling into large tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa koni amɛná niyenii ni faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli. Enɛ ji koni ŋmei tsei lɛ akafu ni amɛfee yitsei wuji.

english: Why should I avoid burning cleared grass and crop stalks on my land before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ jwɛi ni ajie kɛ tsei ahe tsei ni ashãa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe dani madu?

english: Burning destroys valuable organic matter and micro-organisms that keep the soil fertile. Letting cleared weeds rot back into the ground adds natural compost and helps the soil hold moisture.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni jara wa kɛ nibii bibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ ahiɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ jwɛi ni ajie lɛ gbɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ebaaye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my plantain shoots turning yellow and drying up before the fruit develops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ midumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani aduawai lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves often mean the plant lacks nitrogen or its roots are damaged by microscopic pests like nematodes. Proper soil care or targeted chemical treatments keep the leaves green so they can produce enough food for big plantain bunches.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli loo akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii, tamɔ nematodes efite shishifãi lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ ni sa loo tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli bɔni afee ni amɛwo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha plantains wuji lɛ.

english: Why do black spots appear on my plantain leaves, and will this hurt my crop yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji miije kpo yɛ mi plantain baai lɛ anɔ lɛ? Ni ani ebaana hewalɛ gbonyo yɛ minitsumɔ nɔ?

english: Black spots are caused by a fungal leaf disease that reduces the plant's ability to absorb sunlight and grow. Using fungicide sprays protects the leaves so the plantain plant has the energy to produce large, heavy bunches.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ ni haaa tso lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ hulu la ni eda lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ black spot baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii tsu nii lɛ, ebuɔ tsei lɛ ahe bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ aná hewalɛ ni amɛkɛfee fɔfɔi wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my crops rot or spoil quickly even after I harvest them carefully?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ fiteɔ loo efiteɔ oya eyɛ mli akɛ mikpaa lɛ jogbaŋŋ moŋ lɛ?

english: Rot often starts while the crop is still in the field due to hidden fungal or bacterial infections. Applying protective field chemicals before harvest helps kill these organisms so produce stays fresh longer after harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii jeɔ shishi be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo yɛ ŋmeii loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ ahewɔ. Tsofai ni buɔ mɔ he ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani akpaa nii lɛ baaye abua ni agbe nɛkɛ nibii nɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, nibii ni aduɔ lɛ hiɔ shi ehee be kakadaŋŋ yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why are my plantain bunches much smaller than the ones other farmers take to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ dara kwraa fe nɔ ni okwaafoi krokomɛi hɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Small bunches happen when crops don't get enough nutrients or when pests feed on their roots. Feeding the soil with fertilizer and controlling pests gives the plant the energy it needs to produce thick, high-value bunches.
ga: Kpoji bibii baa kɛji tso ko nine shɛɛɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ loo kɛji kooloi ni yeɔ eshishifãi lɛ yeɔ eshishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nibii ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ náa hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli tse ni jara wa waa.

english: Why shouldn't I allow all the young shoots to grow around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mihaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ fɛɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Mi plantain tso titri lɛ

english: Extra shoots act like extra mouths to feed, stealing nutrients and water from the main plant. Pruning excess suckers allows all the soil nutrients to go into making one strong plant and a larger fruit bunch.
ga: Tsoi ni fa lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ daaŋ krokomɛi kɛha niyenii. Kɛtsɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu ni ejuɔ kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ afo ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ jeɔ kpo ni ehaa tso kome ni he wa kɛ aduawai babaoo baa.

english: Why do my crop leaves curl up and droop during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiigbee shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl or droop to slow down water loss when temperatures rise. Ensuring plants have proper moisture and adequate soil nutrients helps them withstand heat stress without stopping their growth.
ga: Ha ni ebɔle ehe loo efolɔ ehe koni nu lɛ aya hiɛ fiofio be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ akwɛ koni tsei lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛŋmɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ naa ni amɛkpaaa amɛdalɛ.

english: Why is it necessary to spend money spraying chemical inputs on my crops if they look healthy right now?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afite shika koni akɛfɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ anɔ lɛ? Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ bianɛ

english: Agrochemicals often work as preventive medicine to protect plants before pests or fungi cause visible damage. Stopping pests early prevents crop loss and ensures your produce looks clean and attractive to buyers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ okwaayeli mli lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ tsofa ni tsiɔ hela naa koni akɛbu tsei ahe dani tsɛŋemɔ helai loo ŋmeii kɛ naagbai ni anaa aba. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni oookpa mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa onibii lɛ feɔ nɔ ni he tse ni mɛi ni heɔ lɛ sumɔɔ.

english: How do I know if my farm soil needs chemical fertilizer or if it is already rich enough?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ he miihia tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli loo eyɛ ŋmɔshi nibii jogbaŋŋ?

english: If your crops grow slowly, have pale leaves, or yield smaller fruits than normal, the soil is low on essential food like nitrogen or potassium. Adding fertilizer restores these nutrients so crops can reach their full size.
ga: Kɛji akɛ otso lɛ miida blɛoo, eyɛ baai ni tsuɔ, loo ewoɔ yibii bibii fe bɔ ni eji daa lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen loo potassium faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ niyenii nɛɛ aku sɛɛ aba koni eha tso lɛ ashɛ egbɔmɔtso lɛ he.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over during strong winds even when they look green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli eyɛ mli akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ moŋ?

english: Insects called stem borers or underground nematodes chew through the roots and base of the plant, weakening its foundation. Applying soil pest treatments strengthens the roots so the plant stands firm until harvest.
ga: Kplukai ni atsɛɔ amɛ stem borers loo shikpɔŋ shishi nematodes lɛ shwieɔ tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ eshishi. ni haa shishitoo lɛ gbɔjɔɔ Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛaatsu nii lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ aná hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ tsei lɛ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ nikpamɔ be mli.

english: Why do weeds harm my crops so much if they are just growing in the empty spaces between plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii awui waa kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ he ni nɔ ko bɛ ni yɔɔ tsei ateŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive roots that steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your crops. Removing weeds or using weed control chemicals ensures your main crops get 100% of the food they need to grow well.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa onibii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ loo tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ jwɛi lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa otso titri lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ 100% koni enyɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does fresh air blowing through my farm matter so much for my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni tswaa kɛtsɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he hiaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ waa lɛ?

english: Good air circulation cools your crops on very hot days and dries wet leaves quickly, which stops fungal diseases and rot from spreading among your plants.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee fɛ̃i yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ anɔ, ni ebaaha baai ni efɔ lɛ agbi oya. Enɛ baaye abua ni ekpa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ fitemɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa otsei lɛ ateŋ.

english: What happens to my crops if air cannot move freely between their leaves?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ aya baai lɛ ateŋ?

english: When air gets trapped, heat and dampness build up around the leaves, creating a wet environment where plant diseases and mold thrive.
ga: Kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe lɛ Dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i buaa ehe naa yɛ baai lɛ ahe, ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli efɔ ni tsei ahe helai kɛ ŋmeii baanyɛ aya hiɛ yɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Can strong wind hurt my crops, and how does letting breeze pass through help them?
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ aye midumɔ nii lɛ awui. Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa?

english: Harsh winds can break stems, but a gentle breeze passing through your crops strengthens their stems, cools them down, and keeps the field dry and healthy.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ akumɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi, shi kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli jɔ ni tswaa kɛtsɔɔ oŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ baawo amɛ hewalɛ, ebaaha amɛhe ajɔɔ, ni ebaaha ŋmɔ lɛ mli agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I check which direction the wind blows before building a nursery for my seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akwɛ he ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ yaa dani ama dumɔwui akwɛmɔhe lɛ?

english: Checking the wind direction helps you position the building so natural breeze flows right through it, keeping the interior cool and fresh for tender seedlings without damaging the structure.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni yaa nɔ lɛ he kwɛmɔ yeɔ ebua bo ni okɛ otsu lɛ toɔ he ko bɔni afee ni adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli. Ehaa mligbɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni efeɔ ehee kɛha dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni efiteee tsɔne lɛ.

english: How does building an open nursery shelter help protect my young vegetables?
ga: Te ŋmɔ ni agbele naa lɛ ni afee lɛ baanyɛ abu mi-aduawai bibii lɛ ahe aha tɛŋŋ?

english: A simple shelter shields delicate plants from harsh burning sun while letting the natural breeze pass through to keep them from overheating.
ga: He ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ buɔ tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, yɛ be mli ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ tsiɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkadɔ fe nine.

english: How should I set up shade structures on my farm so they do not get blown away by strong winds?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ mato shade ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa akatswa lɛ kɛya?

english: You should align shade structures with the main wind direction so air moves smoothly through the open sides instead of pushing hard against solid walls.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ o-shade structure lɛ ato kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ gbɛ titri lɛ he bɔni afee ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛtsɔ hei ni agbele lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ nɔnyɛɛ aba gbogbo ni wa nɔ lɛ

english: Can I use simple structures to create a better environment for crops that easily burn in the sun?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ gbɛjianɔtoo ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo atsu nii koni mikɛfee shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hulu lɛ shãa amɛ oya lɛ?

english: Yes, building light farm structures allows you to control how much sunlight reaches your plants while keeping them cool with natural air movement.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔ mli tsɔne ni mli tseee ni oootswa lɛ haa onyɛɔ okudɔɔ hulu la ni shɛɔ otsei lɛ ahe lɛ falɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsiɔ amɛhe lɛ nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my crops too close together just to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ koni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Planting too close blocks the wind from moving between plants, which traps moisture, promotes diseases, and makes plants fight each other for sun and nutrients.
ga: Kɛ́ adu kɛbɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekatsi lɛ kɛjɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ. Enɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ, ehaa helai baa, ni ehaa tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ.

english: How does leaving proper space between plant rows help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ tsei akutsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Leaving enough space between rows lets air move freely around every plant, lowers heat stress, and makes it easier for you to work on the farm.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ bɔleɔ amɛhe jogbaŋŋ. Nitsumɔhe fɛɛ nitsumɔhe Ha dɔlɛ he haomɔ aba shi ni eye ebua bo ni otsu nii yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mlɛo

english: How do I decide where to place new plants after setting up my farm structures?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpɛ miyiŋ yɛ he ni mikɛ tsei heei baawo yɛ beni ama ŋmɔ lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You should plant where there is enough open space for light and air to reach the plants, ensuring they are not crowded by structures or existing vegetation.
ga: Esa akɛ odu yɛ he ko ni gbɛ ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni kane kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ ashɛ tso lɛ he. Kwɛmɔ akɛ tsei lɛ eyimɔ obɔbɔ kɛ tsũi ni yɔɔ momo loo tsei.

english: Why should I plant my maize in straight rows instead of just scattering the seeds across my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa ni ja mli moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Planting maize in straight rows makes it much easier to walk through the farm to weed and apply fertilizer. It also ensures every plant gets equal space, sunlight, and soil nutrients to produce big cobs.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa akɛ aaatsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛya jwɛi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ mli. Ehaa tso fɛɛ tso hu náa he ko, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa tso lɛ mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: How deep into the soil am I supposed to bury my maize seeds when planting?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafu mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu?

english: You should bury maize seeds about two finger-joints deep (around 3 to 5 centimeters). If you bury them too deep, the seeds will run out of energy before reaching the surface, and if they are too shallow, birds or heat will ruin them.
ga: Esa akɛ ofu ŋmãa lɛ mli aaafee inchi enyɔ (3 kɛyashi 5 centimeters). Kɛji ofu amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, Dumɔwui lɛ ahewalɛ sɛɛ foɔ dani amɛshɛɔ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ. Ni kɛji akɛ dumɔwui lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ Okpoi loo latsaa baafite dumɔwui lɛ.

english: If I put three or four seeds in one hole, will I get more harvest?
ga: Kɛji akɛ okɛ dumɔwui 3-4 wo bu kome mli. Ani babaoo baahi ni abaakpa?

english: Putting too many seeds in one hole causes the crops to fight each other for food and water. This results in weak, thin stalks that produce tiny cobs or no food at all. It is better to plant one or two seeds per hole.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui babaoo wo bu kome mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awuu kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ feɔ ŋmeii bibii. loo niyenii ko bɛ kwraa Esa akɛ adu dumɔwui kome loo enyɔ yɛ bu fɛɛ bu mli.

english: Why do the lower leaves on my young maize plants turn yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is an important food plant needs to grow green and strong. Applying compost or the right fertilizer will help restore the green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Enɛ ji niyenii ko ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Groundnuts and beans are special crops that naturally put nitrogen food back into the soil. Planting them after maize refreshes the land so your next crop can grow better without using as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ji nitrogen lɛ kuɔ sɛɛ kɛbaa sũ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Abele ni ooodu lɛ baaha jɛmɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ bɔni afee ni oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ babaoo tsuuu nii.

english: Should I place fertilizer in the exact same hole with my fresh crop seeds?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo bu kome mli kɛ dumɔwui heei lɛ?

english: No, putting strong fertilizer directly touching a seed can burn and destroy it. You should place the fertilizer a few centimeters away from the seed or wait until after the seedling comes out of the soil.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni mli wa wo dumɔwui lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã dumɔwui lɛ ni efite amɛ. Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo he ko ni kɛ dumɔwui lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji sɛntimitai 2-3 loo omɛ kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ baajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: When planting cassava, does it matter if I stick the stem straight up, at an angle, or flat in the ground?
ga: Be ni esa akɛ adu ŋmei Ani ehe baahia ni adu tso lɛ tso lɛ shi shiŋŋ, ekɛ ehe awo mli, loo ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmei?

english: Planting cassava stems at a slanting angle or flat buried shallowly helps the stem sprout roots faster and produce more cassava tubers close to the surface, making harvesting easier.
ga: Cassava tsei ni aduɔ yɛ koŋ loo gbonyobu ni mli ekɔɔɔ he eko. Eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya. ni ehaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Ehaa ekpamɔ feɔ mlɛo

english: Why do my vegetable leaves curl up and droop during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl and droop during hot afternoons to protect themselves from losing too much water in the sun heat. If the plant does not stand up straight again by evening, it means the soil is too dry and needs watering.
ga: Ha oyitsɔi afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efo yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Enɛ ji koni obu ohe koni nu babaoo akafite yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Kɛji tso lɛ edamɔɔɔ shi tɛ̃ɛ ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ mli Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ ni ehe miihia ni awo nɔ nu.

english: The best time to weed is within the first two to three weeks after your crop comes up. Young crops are too weak to fight with fast-growing weeds for nutrients, water, and light.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ okɛjie jwɛi lɛ ji klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli beni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eje kpo lɛ sɛɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ darako tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwu amɛshi jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ koni amɛná niyenii, nu kɛ la.

english: Is it better to buy certified seeds from an agro-dealer or just plant seeds saved from my previous harvest?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ loo madu dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ mikpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli kɛkɛ?

english: Certified seeds from official stores are specially tested to resist local pests, survive heat better, and produce higher yields compared to seeds saved from an old harvest.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shwapoi ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli lɛ mli krɛdɛɛ koni ana kɛji amɛnyɛŋ amɛye maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ. Ehiɔ dɔlɛ naa jogbaŋŋ ni eyɛ yibiiwoo babaoo kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ blema ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ ahe.

english: Is it true that plantain crops need a lot of water to grow well?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ nu babaoo he miihia plantain tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, plantain plants have very broad leaves and thick stems that require constant moisture to build strong trunks and support heavy bunches of fruit.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔ waa kɛ tsei ni mli tse ni biɔ nu ni mli edɔ be fɛɛ be koni amɛfee tsei ni wa ni amɛye amɛbua aduawai ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ.

english: At what stage of growth does my plantain crop need the most water?
ga: Mɛɛ dalɛ mli mi dumɔwui lɛ nu he hiaa amɛ fe fɛɛ yɛ amɛdalɛ mli?

english: Plantains require continuous moisture throughout their lives, but they need water most critically during flowering and when the fruit bunches are forming and filling out.
ga: Plantains he miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ amɛshihilɛ be fɛɛ mli. Shi nu he miihia amɛ waa yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi kɛ be mli ni aduawai ahe fɔfɔi lɛ miifee ni amɛmiiyimɔ obɔbɔ lɛ.

english: Can plantain crops thrive in areas that get very little rainfall throughout the year?
ga: Ani dumɔwui baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ hei ni nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛɔ yɛ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: No, plantains naturally prefer hot and humid conditions with high rainfall; in dry areas, they will struggle unless you provide continuous irrigation water.
ga: Dabi, plantains sumɔɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli edɔ, ni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo yɛ mli lɛ. yɛ hei ni egbi lɛ Amɛbaabɔ mɔdɛŋ ja okɛ nu ni yaa nɔ lɛ ha.

english: What will happen to my plantain farm if the rains fail this season?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi plantain ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: If the rain fails, the plantain plants will slow down their growth, produce fewer leaves, and may fail to shoot out fruit bunches on time.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ baaha amɛdalɛ aya hiɛ. feɔ baai fioo ni ekolɛ ebaafee nɔ ni woɔ yibii niji yɛ be ni sa mli

english: Will my plantain crops be completely ruined if they do not get enough rainfall?
ga: Ani mi dumɔwui lɛ baafite kwraa kɛji amɛnáaa nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa?

english: They may not die immediately, but without enough water, the crop will yield very small, light bunches with poor-quality fingers that sell for very low prices.
ga: Eko ɔ, a be gboe amlɔ nɔuu. Shi kɛji nu bɛ lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni amɛhe ehiaaa ni ahɔ̃ɔ kɛ jara ni baa shi waa.

english: How do I recognize that my plantain plants are suffering from a lack of water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ nu ni faaa yɛ mi-plantain lɛ mli lɛ miipiŋ?

english: You will notice the broad green leaves starting to roll inward, turn yellow, droop, and dry up prematurely from the bottom of the plant.
ga: Obaana akɛ baai eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ kɛyaa mli. Etsɔ ŋmɔŋ, egbee shi, ni egbi mra kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi.

english: Why do my plantain leaves droop and dry up when the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: The plant naturally drops or droops its leaves to reduce water loss from the sun when there isn't enough moisture available in the soil.
ga: Tsei lɛ baagboi loo amɛbaagbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni nu ni hulu la lɛ fiteɔ lɛ aba shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ.

english: How can I help my plantain crops survive when there is no rain falling?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua midumɔwui lɛ ni amɛhi shi be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ?

english: You can protect your crop by mulching around the base with dry grass or crop leaves to keep the soil moist and reduce water loss from the sun.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu onibii ahe kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni egbi loo tsei ahe baai ni oookɛwo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishi lɛ he lɛ nɔ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni nu ni hulu la lɛ fiteɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Is there anything I can put on the ground to keep water in the soil for my plantains?
ga: Ani nɔ ko yɛ ni manyɛ mikɛwo shikpɔŋ koni nu ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛha mi plantains lɛ?

english: Yes, spreading a thick layer of organic mulch, such as dried leaves, weeds, or straw around the trunk, acts as a blanket that traps moisture in the earth.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai ni egboi, jwɛi, loo jwɛi fɔ̃ɔ tso lɛ he lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ni haa ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ sũ lɛ mli.

english: If the rain stops for weeks, how often should I manually water my plantain plants?
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa otsii babaoo Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mikɛ minine awo mi dumɔwui lɛ anɔ nu?

english: Providing a good soak of water at the base of each plant two to three times a week during dry spells will keep them healthy and productive.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso fɛɛ tso shishi shii 2-3 yɛ otsi mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni ewo yibii.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and weak root systems that cannot handle direct heat. Sunlight dries them out quickly, which is why they need shade trees or plantains to protect them while they grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Hulu lɛ haa amɛgbiɔ oya. Nɔ ni haa ehe hiaa ni amɛná tsei loo tsei bibii ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo be mli ni amɛdaraa waa lɛ.

english: Yellowing and curling leaves on cassava are usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, a virus spread by tiny whiteflies that feed on the plant's sap and weaken its growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmei nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ tsei amli nu ni amɛhaa amɛdalɛ baa shi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: How do I know if my soil lacks nutrients for growing maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ bɛ kɛha ŋmãa?

english: If your maize plants look pale yellow instead of dark green or remain very short despite getting enough rain, the soil is likely missing key nutrients like nitrogen.
ga: Kɛji akɛ o-abele tsei lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ loo amɛji kukuji waa lolo eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ. Ekolɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do armyworms keep attacking my maize leaves every planting season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tutuaa mi-abɛi lɛ daa be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Fall armyworm moths lay their eggs on young leaves because soft maize leaves are an easy food source for their hatching caterpillars, especially during warm weather.
ga: Katerpillar ŋmei lɛ woɔ ewui yɛ baai bibii anɔ ejaakɛ ŋmei bibii ji niyenii ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛha ŋmeii ni miifɔ lɛ. Titri lɛ, yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ

english: Pepper flowers fall off when the plant experiences stress, such as sudden hot dry spells or irregular watering, which prevents proper pollination and fruit set.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ kɛ haomɔi kpe, tamɔ hulutsoo ni fe nine trukaa. loo nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be Enɛ tsiɔ pollination kɛ yibiiwoo ni sa naa.

english: Fertilizer should be applied when the soil is moist and the plant is actively growing, usually a few weeks after germination and again during flowering, so roots can absorb it properly.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni tsei lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ otsii fioo komɛi yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ, kɛ agbɛnɛ hu yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli. koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ
