english: Why is it harmful for me to plant groundnuts in the exact same patch of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ makwɛ ŋmei yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting groundnuts in the same spot continuously allows crop-specific pests and fungal diseases to build up in the soil, leading to poorer yields over time.
ga: Kɛ́ oya nɔ adu ŋmeii yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ ŋmeii ahe helai babaoo aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do the leaves of my tomato plants curl upward during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl upward in intense heat as a natural defense mechanism to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun and conserve water.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni baaha hulu la ni shɛɔ nɔ lɛ aba shi ni ekɛbu nu he.

english: Will planting cowpeas alongside my cassava help or hurt my crop yield?
ga: Ani tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ mi-cassava lɛ masɛi lɛ baaye abua mi loo ebaana mi-cassava lɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Planting cowpeas with cassava helps because cowpeas naturally take nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil, which feeds the cassava and keeps weeds down.
ga: Cowpea ni akɛ cassava duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua. Ejaakɛ cowpea lɛ diɛŋtsɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni akɛduɔ ŋmei kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ

english: Why does my harvested maize develop mold and weevils in the storeroom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikpaa lɛ mli ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii yɛ nitoohe lɛ?

english: Maize rots and attracts weevils when it is put into storage before drying completely, as trapped moisture creates perfect conditions for fungi and pests to thrive.
ga: Abɛi fiteɔ ni egbalaa ŋmeii kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni akɛtoɔ nibii ahe dani egbi kwraa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmɔtɔ ni emɔ mli lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ adalɛ baa.

english: Can the floodwater that covers my low land during heavy rains actually help my soil in any way?
ga: Ani nu afua ni haa mishikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, floodwater carries rich mud, silt, and organic matter from higher ground and deposits it on your land. When the water settles, this fresh layer of sediment fertilizes the soil naturally for future planting.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu afua kɛ sũ, sũ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni jara wa baa kɛjɛɔ gɔŋji amli hei ni ekɛwoɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ nu lɛ ba shi lɛ, nɛkɛ sũ hee nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii wɔsɛɛ.

english: Why is the heavy rain washing away the good topsoil on my farm, and how can I stop it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa?

english: Heavy rainwater collects force as it flows down unprotected soil, carrying away top nutrients. Planting cover crops like cowpeas or making grass barriers along slopes slows down the water so it sinks into the ground instead of washing your soil away.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ buaa hewalɛ naa beni ehoɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni abuuu he lɛ nɔ lɛ. ni okɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ aya Dumɔ nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ tamɔ tsina ŋmei loo jwɛi ŋmeii ni afee yɛ gɔŋji lɛ ahe. Ebaaha nu lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. No hewɔ lɛ, efoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefo ehe.

english: Why do the leaves of my cassava and maize turn yellow when water sits on my farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Roots need air to breathe just like humans do. When excess rainwater floods the soil and stays there, it blocks oxygen from reaching the roots, causing the crop to starve, turn yellow, and rot.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Beni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehiɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. Etsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ji oxygen lɛ naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. hɔmɔ yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfiteɔ

english: Why do my maize plants fall over so easily after a very heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rains soften the earth so much that the roots lose their firm grip on the soil. Combined with strong winds, this soft soil allows the tall, top-heavy maize stalks to lean or fall over.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ aahu akɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɔmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dɔŋŋ. Kɛ akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa fata he Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa tsei ni kɛlɛ ni tsii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ni amɛfoɔ loo amɛgbeeɔ shi.

english: Why do damp rot and mold spread so fast among my crops right after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii gbɛɔ eshwaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Fungi and crop diseases thrive in wet, warm conditions. High moisture on leaves and saturated ground create the perfect home for these disease spores to multiply and attack weak crops.
ga: Fungal helai kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ omanye yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni eyi obɔ lɛ feɔ shia ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha nɛkɛ helai nɛɛ amli tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ koni amɛshwere ni amɛtutua ŋmɔshi nibii ni baanyɛ atswa amɛ.

english: Should I plant my crops on raised soil mounds or ridges if my land gets flooded often?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ kɛji nu hoɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shii abɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, building high ridges or mounds lifts the roots of your crops above the standing floodwater. This gives the roots access to air even when the paths between the mounds fill with water.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋshɔkpɔ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni ooofee lɛ baaye abua ni ewo oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛya nu ni damɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛji akɛ nu eyi gbɛjegbɛi ni yɔɔ gɔji lɛ ateŋ lɛ amli po.

english: Which crops can I grow in the swampy parts of my farm that always hold water during the wet season?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei srɔtoi manyɛ makwɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋshɔkpɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ nɔ?

english: Crops like rice, cocoyam (taro), and sugarcane love standing water and thrive in flooded soil where crops like maize or cassava would easily rot.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa, kookoo (taro) kɛ sugar cane sumɔɔ nu ni damɔ shi ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ, he ni nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa fiteɔ oya lɛ.

english: Is it a good idea to apply fertilizer to my crops right before a heavy rain is expected?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ anɛ waa?

english: No, heavy rainfall will wash away your expensive fertilizer before the roots can absorb it, wasting your money and polluting nearby streams.
ga: Dabi, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baajie o-fertilizer ni jara wa lɛ dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Shika ni afiteɔ kɛ faai ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ ni afiteɔ

english: How can I collect and store excess floodwater from the heavy rains to use during the dry season?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ abua nu ni fa fe nine ni jɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ naa ni akɛto koni akɛtsu nii yɛ hɔmɔ be mli?

english: You can dig simple water retention ponds or dugouts at the lowest points of your farm to catch runoff water, allowing you to irrigate vegetables when the dry season comes.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsa nu ŋtayaa loo nu ŋtayaa ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo. yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli he ni yɔɔ shishi fe fɛɛ lɛ koni omɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ. Ehaa okɛ nu shwieɔ aduawai anɔ kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shɛ.

english: What steps should I take to save my crops right after floodwater drains off my field?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee koni mahere miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayiwala amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni nu afua lɛ efo miŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Clear away weeds and debris trapped around the plants, gently loosen the hard surface crust of the dry mud so air can reach the roots, and cut off spoiled leaves to help the plant recover.
ga: Jiemɔ jwɛi kɛ sũ ni ebɔle tso lɛ he lɛ fɛɛ. Gbalamɔ sũ ni egbi lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ni wa lɛ blɛoo koni kɔɔyɔɔ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ni ofolɔ baai ni egbo lɛ koni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ ahi ehe nɔ.

english: Why does my fresh cassava become watery when I dig it up right after new leaves start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava hee lɛ mli nu yɔɔ beni mifoɔ mli beni baai heei jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: When rain falls and a cassava plant grows new leaves, it uses the starch stored in its underground roots for energy. Harvesting right at this moment results in watery, low-starch tubers, so you should wait a little while for the starch levels to build back up.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ ni ŋmei tsei lɛ ná baai heei Ekɛ ŋmeii ni ato yɛ eshishi shishi shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ hewalɛ. Nikpamɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii ni nu yɔɔ mli ni ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ baa. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ omɛ minitii fioo komɛi dani powda lɛ mli nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Is it bad to harvest my cassava immediately after the plant sprouts fresh green shoots?
ga: Ani ehiii akɛ abaakpa ŋmei amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni tso lɛ ewo ŋmeii heei ni eŋɔli lɛ?

english: Yes, harvesting immediately after new shoots appear is not ideal. The tubers lose quality during this sprouting phase, so letting some time pass allows the root quality to restore before you harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, nikpamɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni ŋmeii heei eje kpo lɛ jeee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Tubers lɛ sɛɛ foɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ oha lɛ be fioo lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ ahi jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ dani okpa amɛ.

english: Why does the quality of my cassava change if I leave it in the ground as the weather changes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ su lɛ tsakeɔ kɛji mishi yɛ shikpɔŋ mli beni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakeɔ lɛ?

english: As time passes and seasons change, the balance of starch and water inside the cassava root shifts. Tubers that were good for boiling or pounding earlier in the season may change texture, making them better suited for processing rather than immediate cooking.
ga: Beni be hoɔ ni bei lɛ tsakeɔ lɛ Starch kɛ nu ni yɔɔ ŋmei shishifã lɛ mli lɛ baatsake. Tubers ni sa kɛha ŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ baanyɛ atsake bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ nɔ ni sa kɛha nitsumɔ moŋ fe ni abaahoo amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: What can I do with cassava roots that are no longer suitable for making fufu?
ga: Mɛni abaanyɛ afee kɛ ŋmei shishifãi ni esaaa kɛha fɛ̃i dɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: When cassava roots lose the starch quality needed for good fufu, you can still grate or cut them up to process into gari or konkonte, ensuring that none of your harvest goes to waste.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ laaje starch su ni he hiaa kɛha fufu kpakpa lɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo ofolɔ mli lolo ni okɛfee gari loo conconte. Enɛ haa onibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ efiteee.

english: How can I preserve my harvested cassava so it doesn't go bad during the dry season?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ abu ŋmei ni akpa lɛ he koni ekafite yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: You can preserve cassava by converting it into dried products like konkonte. By cutting up and sun-drying the roots, you create shelf-stable dried pieces that can be safely stored until that lean season arrives.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmei akafite kɛtsɔ ŋmei ni oootsɔ nɔ ofee nɔ ko ni egbi, tamɔ conconte lɛ nɔ. Kɛtsɔ shishifãi lɛ ni ooofo ni ogbi amɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ofeɔ ŋmeii ni egbi ni abaanyɛ akɛto shweshweeshwe kɛyashi ŋmeii be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: What is the simple process for turning fresh cassava into konkonte?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsakeɔ ŋmei hee awoɔ konkonte mli?

english: To make konkonte, you dig up the cassava tubers, peel them, and cut them into smaller pieces. These pieces are then left to dry thoroughly in the sun so they can be stored and later ground into flour.
ga: yɛ con conte feemɔ mli Ebaabi ni otsa ŋmei shishifã lɛ, ofolɔ mli, ni ofolɔ mli bibii bibii. Kɛkɛ lɛ, agbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni akɛto ni agbɛɔ lɛ ashikishaŋ.

english: Why would I choose to grate my cassava instead of just cutting it into pieces?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mihala akɛ mafolɔ ŋmei moŋ fe ni mafolɔ mli bibii bibii lɛ?

english: Grating cassava is a key step used to make gari. Grating breaks down the root so moisture can be squeezed out and the mash fermented and roasted, whereas cutting the root into larger pieces is used for drying it into konkonte.
ga: Kasava ni atsɔ mli lɛ ji gbɛ ni he hiaa ni atsɔɔ nɔ afeɔ curry paste. Sive lɛ gbálaa shishifãi lɛ amli bɔni afee ni anyɛ ajie ŋmɔtɔ lɛ kɛjɛ mli ni atsɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ koni ekɛfee ŋmɔtɔ ni ashã. Yɛ be mli ni afoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli bibii wuji lɛ, akɛtsuɔ nii koni akɛgbi amɛ ni amɛfee conconte.

english: How do I know whether my harvested cassava is best used for fufu, gari, or konkonte?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-kasa ni mikpa lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha fufu, gari, loo konkonte?

english: Fresh, high-starch cassava harvested at the right time is ideal for fufu. If the cassava has sat in the ground through seasonal changes or has lower starch content, it is better used for grating into gari or drying into konkonte.
ga: Kasava hee ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ starch ni akpaa yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha fufu. Kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ kpɛtɛ shikpɔŋ he yɛ be tsakemɔi ahewɔ loo ashikiŋsha fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsɔ mli ni okɛfee gari loo ooogbi ni okɛfee conconte.

english: How long can dried konkonte last compared to fresh cassava tubers?
ga: Be enyiɛ Konkonte ni egbi lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi kɛ akɛto ŋmei shishifãi heei ahe?

english: Fresh cassava tubers spoil within a few days of being dug up, but properly cut and dried konkonte can be stored in a dry place for many months until you are ready to use it.
ga: Kasava shishifãi heei lɛ baafite yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli kɛji atsa amɛ. Shi abaanyɛ akɛ conte bulbs ni egbi jogbaŋŋ ni afolɔ mli lɛ ato he ko ni egbi nyɔji babaoo kɛyashi obaafee klalo akɛ okɛbaatsu nii.

english: What options do I have if I harvest more cassava than my family can eat fresh right away?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛi ni manyɛ matsɔ nɔ kɛji mikpa ŋmei babaoo fe bɔ ni miweku lɛ baanyɛ aye ehee shikome?

english: Instead of letting fresh cassava spoil, you can process the extra harvest into gari by grating and roasting it, or into konkonte by cutting and drying it, providing long-lasting food for your household.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha ŋmei hee lɛ agbo lɛ Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmei ni fa fe nine lɛ afee gari kɛtsɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei ni ashãa nɔ. Aloo feemɔ conconte kɛtsɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni oooha egbi lɛ nɔ. Koni okɛ niyenii ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ aha oshiabii lɛ

english: Why do my crops dry up and die so quickly whenever the rains stop for just two weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya ni amɛgboiɔ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ lɛ baakpa otsii enyɔ pɛ lɛ?

english: Crops need a steady supply of moisture in the soil to absorb nutrients. When rains are unreliable, shallow crop roots cannot reach deep underground water, causing the plants to wilt, stop growing, and eventually die unless artificial irrigation is used.
ga: Tsei hia shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ daa koni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛ́ anyɛɛɛ akɛ he afɔ̃ nugbɔ nɔ lɛ, tsei shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ he. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, tso lɛ baagbo, ebaakpa dalɛ, ni yɛ naagbee lɛ ebaagbo ja akɛ nu ni akɛfee lɛ tsu nii.

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn under strong, direct sunlight. Leaving shade trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantains nearby protects young cocoa from harsh sun and heat while keeping the soil moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa loo adu tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulutsoo kɛ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why does my cassava grow very big green leaves but produces tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli shi ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen and not enough potassium, the plant spends all its energy growing heavy leaves above ground instead of storing food in the roots to produce large tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ ni potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa ni tsii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ niyenii baato eshishifãi lɛ amli koni ekɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do armyworms destroy my maize far more during dry spells than during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ fiteɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli fe nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rains physically wash young caterpillars off maize leaves and drown them. In dry weather, pests multiply faster and feed aggressively on plants that are already weakened by heat.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ ni ehaa amɛshwieɔ nu mli. yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi mli lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo yaa hiɛ oya ni amɛyeɔ tsei ni latsaa ni naa wa lɛ egbɔjɔ lɛ.

english: When plants are crowded, they compete against each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. They stretch upward to reach light instead of growing thick stems and large cobs.
ga: Kɛ tsei ebɔle amɛhe babaoo Amɛbaatswa hulu la he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Amɛyaa shɔŋŋ koni amɛshɛ la he yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaaná tsei ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, stops hot sunlight from drying out the earth, keeps roots cool, and prevents weeds from stealing water from your crops.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi lɛ aju nu kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: Planting maize repeatedly drains the same specific nutrients from the soil and allows maize pests and diseases to build up in the dirt. Alternating with leguminous crops like cowpeas puts nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii wo mli lɛ, ebaaha nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my yam tubers end up short and bent when I plant them in hard soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛbɔleɔ amɛhe kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose earth to expand easily downward. Hard, compacted soil stops the roots from growing deep and straight, resulting in small, misshapen yams.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shi oya. Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ lɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee nɔ ni ja. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii ni efite.

english: Extreme heat, sudden dry weather, or lack of water causes severe stress to pepper plants, making them drop their flowers to save energy for survival rather than fruit production.
ga: latsaa ni naa wa, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi trukaa loo nu ni bɛ lɛ kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa baa pepper tsei anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ chili tsei lɛ ajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni amɛhi shi moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops turn brown and look burnt after I apply chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eshã beni akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ewo mli lɛ?

english: Applying too much chemical fertilizer or placing it too close to the plant stems draws water out of the roots, causing the plant to dry up and leaf edges to look scorched.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsu nii babaoo loo akɛma tso lɛ shishi tsɔ lɛ, ebaagbala nu kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ehaa tso lɛ gĩɔ ni eshãa baai lɛ ashishigbɛ.

english: Why should I clear away heavy wood and tree stumps from my land before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie tsei ni tsii kɛ tsei akutsei kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmãa?

english: Removing large wood and stumps frees up sunlight, prevents crop roots from being blocked, and eliminates rotting wood that can attract pests or fungal diseases to your young maize crops.
ga: Tsei wuji kɛ tsei akutsei ni ajieɔ lɛ baaye abua ni hulu la lɛ ajie kɛjɛ mli. Etsiɔ tso shishifãi lɛ anaa koni akatsi amɛnaa. ni ojie tsei ni egboi ni baanyɛ agbala tsɛŋemɔ helai loo tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛba o-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it important to level out my field soil properly before sowing vegetable seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afee shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ jogbaŋŋ dani adu aduawai dumɔwui lɛ?

english: A level field ensures rainwater spreads evenly across your plot. If the land is uneven, water gathers in low spots, rotting seeds, while seeds on higher ground dry out and fail to sprout.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ mlijaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ ehiɛɛɛ shi lɛ Nu baabua yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni dumɔwui lɛ baagboi, yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ baagbi ni amɛkwɛ̃ŋ.

english: Why do my tomato seeds sprout unevenly if my seedbed is not flat and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ kɛji midumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ ehiɛɛɛ shi ni ehiɛɛɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Uneven seedbeds cause seeds to be buried at different depths and receive unequal amounts of water. A flat bed makes sure all seeds sit at the right depth and get equal moisture to germinate at the same time.
ga: Dumɔwui ashishi ni ejaaa lɛ haa afuɔ dumɔwui yɛ hei srɔtoi ni mli kwɔ ni amɛnáa nu babaoo. Shishitoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ hiɔ he ni sa ni amɛnáa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ be kome mli.

english: Why do my groundnut plants produce very few pods when I plant them in hard, unworked soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ kɛ́ midu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni akɛtsuuu nii lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts need soft, well-turned soil because after flowering, the plant pushes shoots underground to grow nuts. Hard soil stops these shoots from entering the earth, reducing your total harvest.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ shihilɛ kpakpa mli lɛ he miihia ŋmeii. Ejaakɛ beni ewo fɔfɔi sɛɛ lɛ, tso lɛ tsiɔ eshishifãi lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi koni ekɛdu ŋmeii. Shikpɔŋ ni wa tsiɔ tsei nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkabote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, nɔ ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ fɛɛ baa shi.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate harsh direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains around them to block excessive heat and retain soil moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa tamɔ plantains ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ koni amɛtsi dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ naa ni amɛha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashi be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ baadara ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay thin and woody even when the leafy branches grow very tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛji tsei eyɛ mli akɛ niji lɛ kɛlɛ waa moŋ lɛ?

english: If the ground is packed hard or has too much nitrogen, the cassava plant puts all its strength into leafy top growth instead of storing energy in roots. Loose, properly prepared soil encourages big tuber growth.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ loo eyɛ nitrogen babaoo Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛkwɛɔ ebaa lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni asaa he jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and produce tiny cobs when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? When to plant seeds close together?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough food to grow tall and produce large cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni akɛtoɔ he ni sa lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ni ewo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains specific soil nutrients and allows maize pests to multiply in the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas restores nitrogen and keeps soil healthy.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi. ni ehaa ŋmãa mli tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen baa ekoŋŋ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds hurt my cassava crop more in the first three months than later in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ mi yucca tsei lɛ awui waa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji 3 lɛ amli fe sɛɛ mli yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cassava grows slowly at first and cannot shade out competing plants. Early weeds steal essential water and fertilizer, but once the cassava grows a thick leaf umbrella, it naturally blocks weeds from getting sunlight.
ga: Yucca bibioo lɛ daaa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli ni enyɛɛɛ ekɛ hulutsoo aha tsei ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ. Jwɛi ni shwereɔ mra lɛ juɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa waa. Shi kɛ́ ŋmei lɛ da ni etsɔ ŋmei ni mli edɔ ni baai yɔɔ mli lɛ Ebaatsi jwɛi lɛ anaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛkaná hulu la.

english: Why do my heavy pepper and tomato plants rot when their branches touch the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper kɛ tomato tsei lɛ fiteɔ kɛji amɛniji lɛ ta shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: When fruit-bearing branches rest directly on wet soil, soil-borne fungi and insects easily attack the plant. Tying branches to wooden stakes keeps the crop dry, clean, and healthy off the ground.
ga: Beni aduawai lɛ aniji lɛ tara shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ. Fungi kɛ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ sũ mli lɛ tutuaa tsei oya. Niji ni akɛfiɔ tsei ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbiɔ, amɛhe tseɔ, ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ kɛji amɛje shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell if the seeds I saved from my last harvest are still good enough to plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui ni mihere kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ hi lolo bɔ ni sa akɛ adu?

english: Good seeds are firm, heavy, and free from insect holes. You can test them by putting a few in a bowl of water; healthy seeds usually sink to the bottom, while weak or damaged seeds float to the top.
ga: Dumɔwui kpakpai yɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni mli wa, ni tsii, ni ŋmeii bu bɛ mli. Obaanyɛ oka enɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ nu fioo ni okɛbaawo nu tsɛnsi mli lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui kpakpai fɔɔ gbee kɛyaa shishi. yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ loo efite lɛ baafo kɛya ŋwɛi.

english: How should I store my seed stock so insects do not ruin them before the next rainy season?
ga: Te esa akɛ ato dumɔwui ni adu lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ aha tɛŋŋ koni kooloi akafite amɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aba?

english: Seeds should be dried properly until they are hard, then kept in airtight containers or sealed bags in a cool, dry place. Adding ash or approved grain storage dust helps keep insects away from eating your seeds.
ga: Esa akɛ agbi dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛto tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo kotoku ko ni atsĩ naa mli yɛ he ko ni mli ejɔ ni egbi. Kɛ́ okɛ sũ loo sũ fata dumɔwui atoohei ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kooloi akaye odumɔwui lɛ.

english: Why do my young seedlings wilt and die during their first few weeks in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni mikɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young plants have shallow roots and very tender leaves, making them weak against hot sun and dry soil. They need regular moisture and slight shade until their roots grow deeper to support themselves.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ baai bibii waa. Enɛ haa hulu la ni mli edɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛshɛɔ amɛhe oya. Ehe miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ hulutsoo fioo kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baatsɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛye amɛbua amɛhe.

english: How long does it usually take for young crops to get established enough to survive without daily attention?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be enyiɛ eheɔ dani tsei bibii lɛ hiɔ shi kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ amɛ daa gbi?

english: Most young crops need intensive care for the first three to four weeks. After this period, their root systems are established enough to pull moisture and nutrients from deeper in the soil.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ bibii lɛ ateŋ babaoo biɔ ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ lɛ mli. Yɛ be nɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ baafee nɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni amɛgbala ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ.

english: How can I protect my young crops from being eaten or destroyed by stray farm animals?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ ahe koni ŋmɔ mli kooloi akaye amɛ loo amɛkafite amɛ?

english: You can protect your field by erecting simple wooden or bamboo fences around the farm perimeter, or by planting thorny hedge plants along the borders to keep farm animals out.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu oŋmɔji lɛ ahe kɛtsɔ tso loo ŋmei gbogbo ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni oootswa yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ nɔ, loo kɛtsɔ ŋmeii tsei ni ooodu yɛ eshishigbɛ koni ŋmɔ mli kooloi akabote mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some of my crops rot on the farm right before I am ready to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi fiteɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mifeɔ klalo akɛ makpa lɛ?

english: Crops often rot before harvest due to excess water trapped around the roots, fungal diseases, or pest attacks. Proper spacing, good field drainage, and harvesting at the right time prevent this loss.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii fiteɔ dani akpaa yɛ nu ni fa fe nine ni ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe, tsɛŋemɔ helai, loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahewɔ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛaawo mli lɛ he miihia. nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ Ni kpamɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ nɛkɛ laajemɔ nɛɛ naa.

english: Why are my crop leaves turning yellow even though I gave them water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo enɔ po lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant is lacking essential plant food (nutrients like nitrogen) in the soil. Adding well-rotted manure or the right fertilizer will help the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa (nibii tamɔ nitrogen) yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin instead of producing heavy fruits or tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe ejɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii loo ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ?

english: Plants grow tall and weak when they are overcrowded or lack enough sunlight and proper nutrients. Giving crops enough space allows sun and air to reach them, making the stems thick and productive.
ga: Tsei baanyɛ adara ni amɛgbɔjɔ kɛji amɛyi obɔ kɛ hulu la ni sa kɛ niyenii kpakpai. He ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ baa. Ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops in the first month after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mitsei lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ ni mikɛduɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that adapt quickly to the soil and steal fertilizer and water intended for your crops. Clearing weeds early gives your young plants the space and nutrients they need to grow faster.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni tsakeɔ amɛhe oya kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu kɛhaa onibii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha odumɔwui lɛ aná hegbɛ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara oya.

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight underground for nutrients and water, while their leaves fight for sunlight. Spacing them correctly ensures every plant gets enough food to grow well.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu. yɛ be mli ni baai lɛ baawu koni amɛná hulu la He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade to survive because direct sunlight scorches their tender leaves and dries out the topsoil. Leaving larger shade trees or planting temporary crops like plantains creates a cool, moist microclimate that protects young cocoa during its early years.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ agbi. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ ni ashiɔ loo tsei ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains lɛ haa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli ejɔ ni mli edɔ baa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Does planting cassava stems close together give me more tubers at harvest time?
ga: Ani ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa ŋmeii babaoo baa yɛ kpamɔ be mli?

english: No, planting cassava too closely causes the roots to compete for space, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in many small, thin tubers. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to expand its root system and produce large, heavy tubers.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ abɔ he akaŋ koni amɛná he ko, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa yitsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo babaoo baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ teŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaagbɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli ni efee bulbs agboi ni tsii.

english: Why do my seeds fail to sprout when I push them deep into the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji mikɛ amɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Seeds buried too deeply exhaust their stored energy before the shoot can reach sunlight. Planting seeds at a shallow depth—usually about two to three times the width of the seed—helps them sprout faster and reach the surface easily.
ga: Dumɔwui ni afu amɛ tsɔ lɛ baafite hewalɛ ni amɛto lɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ ashɛ hulu la lɛ he. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni mli ekwɔɔɔ—bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ alɛɛmɔ toi enyɔ loo shii etɛ—yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛshɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mlɛo.

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed for leafy growth. Adding animal manure, compost, or a nitrogen-based fertilizer will restore the green color and encourage bigger corn cobs.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei, ŋmei, loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ afee ŋmeii ekoŋŋ ni eye ebua ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdara.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains the same specific nutrients from the soil and allows soil pests to multiply. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts rebuilds soil fertility naturally and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ baajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni amɛshwereɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni etswaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ emaa shi ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni efo tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe sɛɛkuu lɛ mli

english: How does planting beans or groundnuts alongside my crops help the soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Beans and groundnuts are legumes that capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant grows and decays, this nitrogen enters the soil, acting as a natural food source for nearby crops.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Beni tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ Nitrogen nɛɛ boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii jɛɛhe kɛha tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ.

english: What causes small holes in my corn leaves and brown powder inside the top stem?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ powda ni tsuɔ yɛ ŋwɛi ŋmãa lɛ mli

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that feeds on young foliage and hides inside the growing whorl of the plant. Spraying approved biological treatments or neem oil early in the morning helps protect the crops before major damage occurs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ baai bibii ni ekɛ ehe woɔ tsei ni miida lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni wala yɔɔ mli loo neem fɔ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe dani efiteɔ waa.

english: How do weeds hurt my crops if there is enough sunshine for all plants on the field?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha tso fɛɛ tso ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital water and soil nutrients directly from the ground before your crops can reach them. Clearing weeds early ensures that all the moisture and manure you apply goes directly to feeding your crops.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ shikpɔŋ nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baashɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni okɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yaa tɛ̃ɛ kɛhaa onibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Tomato plants shed their blossoms when they experience extreme heat or irregular watering during the flowering phase. Keeping the soil consistently moist and covering the ground with mulch protects the roots from heat and helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baawo fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ba. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha nɔ lɛ, ebaabu shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛjɛ latsaa he, ni ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is damp, but avoid applying it right before a heavy rainstorm. Placing the fertilizer in small holes or rings near the stem and covering it with soil prevents rain from sweeping it off your field.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Shi tsi ohe kɛjɛ he ni owoɔ dani nugbɔ ni naa wa aba lɛ he. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo bu bibii loo ŋmeii amli. Kɛ́ obɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi ni okɛ sũ aha nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ naa koni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akaje ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the tip usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green and leafy. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps restore green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Nɔ ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná baai. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How does planting cowpeas in the same field alongside my maize help my soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas belong to the legume family, which has special roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into soil food. This naturally fertilizes the soil and helps nearby maize grow stronger.
ga: Cowpeas yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni eyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ehaa efeɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eye ebua ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ waa.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines high up off the ground instead of letting them spread?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni mahã amɛgbɛ amɛshwã lɛ?

english: Staking lifts the yam leaves into direct sunlight so they can make maximum food for the plant. The extra light energy travels down to the roots, producing much larger and healthier tubers underground.
ga: Staking haa sweet potato baai lɛ shɛɔ hulu la lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná amɛ niyenii lɛ jogbaŋŋ amɛha tso lɛ. La hewalɛ kroko yaa shishi kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ babaoo baa.

english: If too many suckers grow at once, they steal food, water, and sunlight from the main mother plant. Removing extra suckers leaves only the strongest shoots, ensuring big, heavy bunches of plantain.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo yɛ be kome mli Ejuɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ ashiɔ. Kwɛmɔ akɛ plantains lɛ baafee agbo waa ni etsii.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips that suck sap from under the leaves and transmit viruses. Spraying neem oil or insecticidal soap controls these insects and stops the spread.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni shwieɔ baai lɛ ashishi nu lɛ ni amɛhaa hela lɛ baa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaakudɔ kooloi nɛɛ ni eha amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, often brought on by irregular watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist allows the roots to absorb calcium smoothly.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛjieɔ calcium lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or water, cassava focuses all its energy on leaf growth instead of root storage. Balancing the soil nutrients encourages the plant to direct its food down into expanding tubers.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen loo nu babaoo lɛ, Cassava kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ moŋ fe shishifãi ni ahiɔ shi lɛ. Niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii majeɔ shi kɛyaa bulbs ni miigbɛ eshwa lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa tree flowers keep dropping off without forming any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔ ko lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop when there is prolonged dry weather or a shortage of tiny pollinating insects like midges. Maintaining shade trees keeps the air humid and creates a good environment for pollinators to do their work.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi be kakadaŋŋ loo ŋmeii bibii ni haa fɔfɔi tamɔ ŋmeii bɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ otsei lɛ wo hulutsoo be mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli tseɔ ni ehaa shihilɛ kpakpa baa kɛha ŋmeii ni haa ŋmeii lɛ tsuɔ nii.

english: Why do my garden egg plants look wilted and droopy during hot afternoons even when the soil has moisture?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: On very hot days, leaves lose water through heat faster than roots can draw it from the ground, causing temporary afternoon wilting. Covering the soil with organic mulch keeps root temperatures cool so plants recover quickly.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ hulutsoo nɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, shwane lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko. Organic mulching yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifã lɛ mli fɛ̃i lɛ mli jɔɔ. Tso lɛ he waa oya.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily in direct sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains or cassava alongside cocoa provides a natural canopy that shelters the young plants until they are mature enough to withstand full heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ dumɔwui loo ŋmei dumɔ. Enɛ, kɛ kookoo lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ hulutsoo be lɛ fɛɛ naa.

english: How should I keep my cut cassava stems fresh before I plant them in my field?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mahã ŋmei tsei lɛ ahi shi ehee dani madu amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava stem cuttings should be stored vertically in the shade with their bottom bases resting in cool, moist soil. This keeps the stems alive and hydrated for several weeks until you are ready to plant.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ cassava ni afo lɛ ato shi shiŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Shishitoo lɛ damɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ otsii babaoo kɛyashi obaafee klalo akɛ obaadu amɛ.

english: Yam vines need tall stakes to elevate their leaves into the sunlight. Maximum light exposure enables the leaves to generate energy efficiently, which results in larger yam tubers growing underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso kakadaŋŋ koni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛya hulu la lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ajie lɛ kpo babaoo lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ feɔ hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii wuji kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why should I cover the ground around my vegetables with dry grass and leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi kɛ baai ni egboi aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-vegetables lɛ he lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry organic material, known as mulching, shields the ground from hot sun, slows down water evaporation, keeps the soil cool, and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ha nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye nɔ.

english: Is it better to put fertilizer on my crops when the ground is dry or after a rain?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nibii beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi loo beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ?

english: Fertilizer must be applied when the soil is moist after rain. Dry soil cannot dissolve the nutrients for the roots to absorb, and concentrated fertilizer on dry roots can burn and damage the plant.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nyɛŋ ajie niyenii mli nibii ni haa shishifãi lɛ aŋɔ. Ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi ni egbi lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã ni efite tsei lɛ.

english: Why is my maize field turning pale green and yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ miitsɔ eŋɔli ni mli tse kɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Pale or yellowing leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or Urea provides the essential food maize needs to develop dark green leaves and strong stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ni fa babaoo tamɔ NPK loo urea ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ baaha ŋmãa lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ená baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmãa ni mli wa.

english: What is causing small holes in the center leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi-baby corn tso lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ

english: Holes in the inner whorl of young corn are typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding inside the plant funnel. Treating the crop early with approved pest control products or neem leaf extracts destroys the worms before they ruin the yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ tso lɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe ŋmeii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ baa. Nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra Kɛtsɔ nibii ni akɛgbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo neem baa mli nu ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ, abaakpata tsɛŋemɔ helai ahiɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Leaf curl on pepper plants is commonly caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies feeding on the plant and spreading plant viruses. Controlling these insects early with neem oil or appropriate sprays protects your plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ pepper tsei lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ tsei lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Kɛtsɔ neem fɔ loo spray ni sa nɔ lɛ obaanyɛ obu otsei lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the blossoms on my tomato plants dropping off before producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani ewoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when plants experience extreme heat or irregular watering. Maintaining steady moisture in the soil and avoiding prolonged dry periods helps the flowers turn into fruit successfully.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ aduawai yɛ omanyeyeli mli.

english: Why should I trim off extra shoots growing at the base of my plantain trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi plantains lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, compete with the main plantain trunk for nutrients and water. Pruning them so only one main trunk and one follower remain ensures the tree directs its energy into making a large, heavy bunch of fruit.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei loo tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛ plantain tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli koni ashi tso lɛ shishifã titri kome pɛ kɛ esɛɛnyiɛlɔ kome pɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: How long does a cashew tree take from the day I plant it until it starts giving me nuts?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani cashew tso ko daa kɛjɛɔ be mli ni adu lɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ebɔi cashew ŋmeii feemɔ?

english: Grafted cashew trees usually start producing nuts in about 3 to 4 years, while trees grown directly from raw seeds take about 5 years to yield their first full crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cashew tsei ni akɛwo amɛmli lɛ jeɔ ŋmeii feemɔ shishi yɛ aaafee afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, yɛ be mli ni tsei ni akwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui ni akwɛɛɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ heɔ aaafee afii enumɔ dani amɛwoɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmeii ni yeɔ emuu.

english: Why do my cashew trees lose many of their leaves right before the flowering season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cashew tso lɛ baai babaoo miifite dani fɔfɔi be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Cashew trees naturally shed old leaves during the dry season to save water; this leaf drop triggers the tree to produce fresh leaves and flower clusters for the upcoming harvest.
ga: Cashew tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai momo lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ fɛ̃i be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Nɛkɛ baai ni egbee shi nɛɛ baaha tso lɛ awo baai heei kɛ fɔfɔi akui kɛha kpamɔ ni baa lɛ.

english: Can cashew trees grow well on dry or poor land where my maize usually fails?
ga: Ani cashew tsei baanyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni egbi loo hei ni mi-abele lɛ fɔɔ shweremɔ yɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, cashew trees are very tough and can grow in dry, sandy soils because they have deep taproots, but they still need well-drained soil and open sunlight to produce a high yield.
ga: Hɛɛ, cashew tsei lɛ wa waa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ hewɔ. Shi shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ hulu la babaoo he miihia lɛ lolo koni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why is it bad to plant cashew trees very close to each other like I do with corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu cashew tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Cashew trees develop wide branches that need full sunlight. If planted too close together, their branches shade each other out, which drastically reduces the total number of nuts the trees can produce.
ga: Cashew tsei yɛ niji ni mli kwɔ ni biɔ hulutsoo be fɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ adu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛniji lɛ haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii fɛɛ ni tso lɛ baanyɛ awo lɛ baa shi waa.

english: Can I grow food crops like groundnuts or cassava between my young cashew trees while waiting for them to mature?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei. Ani manyɛ madu mi-cashew tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni amɛdara lɛ?

english: Yes, during the first 3 to 4 years when cashew trees are still small, you can plant short crops like groundnuts, cowpeas, or maize between the rows to get food and income without damaging the young trees.
ga: Hɛɛ, yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 lɛ mli lɛ, cashew tso lɛ ji bibioo lolo. Obaanyɛ odu ŋmɔshi nibii kukuji tamɔ ŋmei, tsina ŋmei, loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmei teŋ koni oná niyenii kɛ shika ni okɛfiteee tsei bibii lɛ.

english: Do I need to trim or cut off the lower branches of my cashew trees as they grow?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mafolɔ loo mafolɔ mi-cashew tso lɛ niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli be mli ni edaa lɛ?

english: Yes, trimming the lower branches (pruning) during the first few years helps the tree form a single strong trunk, makes weeding easier, and opens up the tree for sunlight and airflow.
ga: Hɛɛ, niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ afolɔmɔ (afolɔ) yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ baaye abua tso lɛ ni efee tso kome ni mli wa. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ abaajie jwɛi kɛjɛ mli. ni ogbele tsei lɛ koni hulu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli

english: Why do the flowers on my cashew trees fall off without forming nuts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cashew tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: While dropping some flowers is natural, heavy flower loss is usually caused by sap-sucking pests like thrips or a lack of moisture in the soil during early flower development.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ fɔfɔi komɛi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ moŋ, shi bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔi wuji ni laajeɔ lɛ jɛɔ ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni bɛ yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ashishijee bei amli lɛ hewɔ.

english: What is the difference between the cashew apple and the nut, and do they grow together?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ cashew ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ateŋ? Ni ani wɔbaanyɛ wɔfee ekome kɛda?

english: The hard nut grows first on the outside bottom, and as it matures, the stem above it swells into a juicy red or yellow cashew apple; both mature together on the branch.
ga: Hardnuts lɛ daa klɛŋklɛŋ kɛjɛɔ kponɔgbɛ shishigbɛ. Ni kɛ́ eda kwraa lɛ, tso lɛ yiteŋgbɛ lɛ fũuɔ ni etsɔɔ cashew apple tsuru loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli ewo muji. Enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ feɔ ekome kɛdaraa yɛ tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cashew tree turning black and sticky?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cashew tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Black sticky leaves are caused by small insects like aphids sucking the plant sap and leaving a sweet liquid, which then grows a black fungus called sooty mold on the leaves.
ga: Kooloi bibii, tamɔ aphids, ni nuɔ tso lɛ nu ni amɛshiɔ nu ni ŋɔɔ yɛ sɛɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai diji ni kpɛtɛɔ lɛ baa. Kɛkɛ ni ŋmei diŋŋ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ sooty mold lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ baai lɛ anɔ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my cashew nuts from the tree?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa cashew ŋmeii kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: You should not pluck them from the tree; cashew nuts are fully mature only when the fruit naturally falls to the ground on its own.
ga: Kaafolɔ amɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ. Cashew ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ pɛ kɛji akɛ aduawai lɛ gbee shikpɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow fast. Heavy rains in northern Ghana can wash this food out of the soil, so adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores the plant's strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara oya. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ lɛ baanyɛ afɔ niyenii nɛɛ he kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do agricultural officers tell us to plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same farm with our maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔdu tsina loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni wɔduɔ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas have tiny natural powerhouses on their roots that take food from the air and store it in the soil. This enriches the earth with nitrogen, acting like free natural fertilizer for neighboring crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ adebɔɔ mli. Enaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ hãa nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do my crops give a poor harvest when I grow maize on the exact same plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekpaaa nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Maize consumes the same specific nutrients from the soil every season until the ground is completely drained. Rotating maize with crops like groundnut or soybean gives the soil time to rest and rebuild its natural plant food.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni sũ lɛ mli nu hoɔ kwraa. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo soybeans tsakeɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa be ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe ni ekɛ ehe woɔ tsei aniyenii ni ji adebɔɔ mli lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my sorghum and maize leaves curl up into tight tubes during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sorghum kɛ mi-corn baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tsɔji ni mli wa yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a natural survival defense crops use to protect themselves from intense heat. By rolling up, the leaf exposes less surface to the hot sun, which traps moisture inside and stops the plant from drying out.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ hebuu ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. kɛji akɛ abɔle ehe lɛ Baai lɛ shɛɛɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he tsɔ. Enɛ haaa nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ awo mli ni ehaaa tso lɛ agbi.

english: Why does covering the dirt around my crop stems with dry grass help them stay fresh during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mitsei lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dry grass acts like a protective blanket over the dirt, shading the soil from the hot sun. This prevents water from evaporating quickly into the air, keeping the crop roots moist and cool for much longer.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Buu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Enɛ ji koni nu akatsɔ oya kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Ehaa tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe jɔɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why is it dangerous for me to sow my seeds right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara kɛha mi akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain in northern Ghana is often a 'false rain' followed by weeks of hot, dry weather. If seeds sprout and the soil dries out completely before the main rains arrive, the intense sun will burn and kill the young seedlings.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ lɛ ji ‘nugbɔ ni bɛ amale’, ni otsii babaoo ni mli edɔ, ni mli egbi nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa dani nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã ni ekpata tsei bibii lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Why do my groundnut plants bend their flower stems down and push them into the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ ahe ni ekɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Unlike tomatoes or peppers, groundnut pods do not mature in the air. Once the flower is pollinated, the stem naturally grows downwards into the soil so the groundnut can safely swell and mature beneath the dirt.
ga: Nɔ ni tamɔɔɔ tomato loo ŋmɔtɔ lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ ŋmɔtɔi shwieee kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Kɛji akɛ fɔfɔi lɛ wo pollination lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmeii baanyɛ afu ni amɛkwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Yam leaves need sunlight to produce energy, which is sent underground to grow big yam tubers. Staking lifts the vines off the wet ground so the leaves get maximum sunlight and don't rot from ground moisture.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ. ni abaamaje shikpɔŋ shishi koni ekwɛ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. koni baai lɛ aná hulu la babaoo ni amɛkafite kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli

english: Why do my crop plants stay thin and weak when I put three or four seeds into one single hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni ebɛ hewalɛ beni mikɛ dumɔwui etɛ loo ejwɛ woɔ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, their roots compete heavily with each other for water, sunlight, and soil food. Giving each seed its own space allows the root system to grow large and feed a strong plant.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. Kɛ́ aha dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko lɛ diɛŋtsɛ egbɛhe lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ daraa ni amɛdaraa tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do armyworms hide deep inside the center whorl leaves of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The tender center leaves inside the leaf funnel are soft, moist, and easy for young caterpillars to chew. Hiding deep inside the funnel also protects the worms from harsh sunlight, rain, and birds that want to eat them.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ baa ŋmei lɛ mli lɛ ateŋ lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ oya. Kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhe tee ŋmeii lɛ amli shɔŋŋ lɛ hu buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa, nugbɔ, kɛ okpoi ni miisumɔ ni amɛye amɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green and strong. It can also happen when the soil has too much water, which prevents the roots from breathing and taking up food.
ga: Abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei lɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛná hewalɛ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛye nii.

english: It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist, usually a few weeks after planting or right after a good rain. Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so the roots can drink it; putting it on dry soil wastes the fertilizer and can burn the roots.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni adu nii loo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ jogbaŋŋ sɛɛ pɛ. Nu he miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ mli koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu. Kɛ́ okɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni ebaashã shishifãi lɛ.

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is usually caused by a virus spread by tiny white insects called whiteflies. As these insects feed on your tomato plant, they pass the sickness into the leaves, causing them to wrinkle up and stop growing properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii yɛŋ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Enɛ ji akɛ, nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ yeɔ o-tomato tsei lɛ. Amɛbaagbɛ hela lɛ amɛshwã baai lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa tsitsii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekpaa dalɛ kpakpa.

english: Is it better for me to spray my farm with insect medicine in the morning or during the afternoon heat?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mafɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ leebi loo shwane?

english: It is always best to spray early in the morning or late in the evening. In the hot afternoon sun, the liquid evaporates into the air too fast before it can work, and the hot sun on wet leaves can cause burns on your crops.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, okɛ tsofa lɛ afɔ nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ. Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Nui lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani amɛtsuɔ amɛnitsumɔ lɛ. Ni hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ baai ni efɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they get too hot or stressed by dry weather. Without enough water or relief from scorching sun, the plant drops its flowers to save energy so the whole plant doesn't die.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ edɔ tsɔ loo shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ miigba amɛnaa. Kɛ nu ni fa loo hejɔɔmɔ ni jɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli bɛ lɛ Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. koni tso muu lɛ fɛɛ akagbo.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers during the short dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ hulutsoo be kuku lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they do not get enough shade or soil moisture. High heat stresses the tree, causing it to shed its flowers to protect itself from drying out completely.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ efoŋ kɛji amɛnáaa hulutsoo loo ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa tsei haoɔ. Ha ejie efɔfɔi lɛ koni ebu ehe koni ekagbi kwraa.

english: Yam vines need to climb tall sticks so their leaves can spread out and catch as much sunlight as possible. The leaves use sunlight to manufacture food, which goes down to build large, heavy yam tubers in the soil.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei niji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Baai kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛ feɔ niyenii. No sɛɛ lɛ, yaa shi ni ofee sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: What causes my cassava roots to rot under the soil before I can dig them up?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani manyɛ mafo amɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot underground when rainwater collects in the soil and cannot drain away. Sitting in soggy dirt suffocates the tubers and allows tiny fungal germs in the mud to attack and rot the crop.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni anyɛɛɛ ajie kɛjɛ mli. Kɛ́ ota shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha bulb lɛ agbɔjɔ. ni amɛha ŋmeii bibii ni Yɛ muji lɛ mli lɛ amɛtutuaa ni amɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii fiteɔ.

english: Plantain trees fall easily because their roots are short and stay near the surface. Often, tiny invisible worms or beetle grubs in the dirt eat the roots, making the plant weak and unable to hold itself up.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ yɛ kuku ni amɛbɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii Anaaa amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, amɛyeɔ shishifãi Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni enyɛɛɛ efã ehe.

english: Weeds are like aggressive neighbors that steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients away from your crops. When weeds surround your plants, your crops cannot get enough food to grow thick stems or big fruits.
ga: Jwɛi tamɔ akutsoŋbii ni yɔɔ basabasa ni juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli lɛ. Beni jwɛi ebɔle otsei lɛ ahe lɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii nyɛŋ ana niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmeii ni mli tse loo aduawai wuji akwɛ̃.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa plants need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: The first rain is often followed by a long dry spell, known as a false start to the rainy season. If your seeds sprout and the soil dries out completely afterward, the young seedlings will wither and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Tswaa lɛ akɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee ni ji amale. Kɛji odumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ kwraa yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ, Tso bibioo lɛ baagbo ni ebaagbo.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize is lacking nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for plant growth. It can also happen when the soil is overly waterlogged, preventing the roots from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu.

english: Why do I have to tie my yam vines onto tall wooden sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ sweet potato wain tso lɛ fĩɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko he lɛ?

english: Yam vines are natural climbers that need to spread their leaves upward to catch sunlight for food production. Keeping the vines off the ground also protects the leaves from soil-borne fungal diseases and rot.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni esa akɛ amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni hulu la ashɛ amɛnɔ koni amɛkɛtsu nii akɛ niyenii. Wein tso lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu buɔ tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli kɛ fitemɔ he.

english: Why do some farmers cover the dirt around their crops with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ jwɛi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like a blanket. It stops soil moisture from evaporating in the sun, keeps the ground cool, and stops weeds from taking over your garden bed.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji hulu la lɛ shɛ enɔ. ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni otsi jwɛi anaa koni amɛkaye obɔɔ mli saatsoi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are the blossoms on my pepper plants curling up and dropping off without making any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ni amɛjieee pepper ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Flower drop and leaf curling are commonly caused by extreme heat or tiny sucking insects like aphids and mites. When these pests suck the sap out of the flower stems, the plant drops the flowers to save energy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids kɛ mites ji nɔ ni kɛ fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Kɛ́ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ nu fɔfɔi lɛ amli nu lɛ, Tsei lɛ jieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow so much faster than my crops even when I don't water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu efɔko amɛnɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild local plants that are naturally tougher and better adapted to poor soil and harsh weather. They aggressively pull water and food out of the ground before your planted crops get a chance to use them.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni amɛhe wa yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai amli. Amɛkɛ ekãa gbalaa nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ lɛ naa hegbɛ ni amɛkɛtsu nii.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when high afternoon temperatures dry up their pollen, preventing fruit formation. It can also happen if the plants do not get consistent watering while flowering.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ ha fɔfɔi lɛ mli fɔfɔi lɛ egbi. tsiɔ yibiiwoo naa Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji akɛ afɔɔɔ tso lɛ nu daa be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: How do I tell when my cassava tubers are ready to dig up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakumɔ?

english: Cassava is usually ready for harvest when the lower leaves start to turn yellow and drop off, and the soil surrounding the main stem begins to crack upward due to the expanding tubers underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni ŋmei ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains the specific food nutrients that maize relies on. Rotating your field with crops like groundnuts or beans helps put nutrients back into the soil naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni abɛi lɛ damɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Oŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii baatsake. Eyeɔ ebuaa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ekuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow before the corn is ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which gives plants their green color and strength. When soil nutrients run low, the maize moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves up to feed the young growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. Kɛji niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Abɛi tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do I need to prune tree branches above my mature cocoa farm when the weather is warm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mifoɔ tsei yɛ kookoo ŋmɔji ni eda lɛ anɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa needs heavy shade to survive, but mature cocoa needs moderate direct sunlight to produce plenty of flowers and pods. Excessive shade traps humidity, which creates a habitat for black pod disease and lowers overall harvest.
ga: Cocoo bibioo he miihia hulutsoo ni tsii koni enyɛ ehi shi. Shi hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he miihia kookoo ni eda lɛ bɔ ni sa koni ekɛ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii babaoo aba. Shade babaoo baamɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ. ni haa black pod hela lɛ feɔ shihilɛhe ni ehaa nibii fɛɛ ni afeɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting inside the ground during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When heavy rains leave standing water around the roots for too long, the roots drown and decay, which is why planting on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu lɛ shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛbaagboi. Enɛ hewɔ ni dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa lɛ.

english: Why does my farm yield less maize if I plant it in the exact same field every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ wooo ŋmãa fioo kɛji midu ŋmɔ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year. It also allows specific soil pests and diseases that feed on maize to build up in large numbers in that field.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. Ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ helai ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ hu buaa amɛhe naa babaoo yɛ nakai he lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat or drought stress. The plant sheds its flowers to conserve water and energy to protect itself from dying.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ he haomɔ he. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ gbele he.

english: Why should I leave measured space between my crops instead of planting many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ato he ko? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu dumɔwui babaoo lɛ Ha dumɔwui lɛ abɛŋkɛ amɛhe.

english: Crops planted too close together fight each other for limited sunlight, air, soil water, and nutrients. Giving each plant proper space allows it to grow thick stems and produce bigger yields.
ga: Tsei ni adu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ, shikpɔŋ nɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Weeds act like aggressive competitors on your farm. They grow fast and steal the water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your crops, leaving your crops hungry and weak.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akaŋshilɔi ni yɔɔ basabasa yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛdaraa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ onibii ni ogbɔjɔɔ.

english: Seeds contain a small, limited amount of stored energy to sprout. If buried too deep, the seed burns all its energy trying to push through the heavy soil and dies before reaching sunlight.
ga: Dumɔwui bɛ hewalɛ fioo ko ni ato koni amɛkɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji akɛ afu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ shãa amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ mli lɛ mli ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛshɛɔ hulu la lɛ he.

english: Why should I leave dry grass or leaves spread on top of the soil around my vegetables?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi jwɛi loo baai ni egbi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil with dried plant materials acts like a protective blanket. It keeps the soil cool, prevents water from drying out quickly under the hot sun, and breaks down into natural food for the soil.
ga: Mulching ni akɛ tsei ni egbi woɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekagbi oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ

english: Why should I cut off extra suckers growing around the base of my plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie mi plantain lɛ shishitoo lɛ.

english: Having too many shoots around one plantain stem means they all share the food and water coming from the ground. Cutting back extra suckers lets the main plant take all the food and grow a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Ni aaana ŋmeii babaoo ni ebɔle Plantain kome he lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛ fɛɛ amɛjaa niyenii kɛ nu ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aŋɔ niyenii lɛ fɛɛ ni ekwɛ dumɔwui babaoo ni tsii.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under strong sunlight. Leaving larger shade trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides a protective umbrella that keeps the soil cool and moist while the young cocoa grows.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ ni ashiɔ loo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi Ehaa nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa be mli ni kookoo bibioo lɛ miida lolo lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually show that the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrients crops use to build leaves. Adding animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant regain its dark green color and yield bigger cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ, ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi aŋmei, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do small caterpillars keep chewing holes in the center leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛyeɔ bu yɛ mi-ŋmei bibii lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars, known as fall armyworms, target the soft central leaves where they can hide and feed safely. Checking your field early and applying recommended treatments directly into the plant leaves stops them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ akɛ ŋmeii ni gbeeɔ shi. Tsɔɔmɔ baai bibii lɛ yɛ teŋgbɛ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛtee amɛhe ni amɛye nii shweshweeshwe lɛ. He ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Kɛ tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsuɔ he nii lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii tɛ̃ɛ yɛ tsei ahe baai lɛ haa amɛkpaa dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Does it matter which direction I point the stem buds when I plant cassava cuttings in the soil?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu ŋmei niji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ani etsɔɔ he ko?
