english: Yes, planting cassava stem cuttings with the leaf buds pointing upward ensures that the shoots grow directly up toward the sun while roots spread easily. Planting them upside down forces the plant to waste energy twisting around, resulting in smaller roots.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kɛ́ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ ni ŋmeii lɛ kwɛɔ ŋwɛi lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ daraa tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa hulu lɛ he yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa mlɛo. Tso lɛ ni edaa kɛyaa shishi lɛ haa ehewalɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ eshishijee ni ekɛbaabɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: How can I tell if the first rain of the season is enough for me to start sowing my maize seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi ŋmãa dumɔ?

english: Planting after just one early rain is risky because the ground can dry out quickly during a follow-up hot spell. It is safer to plant after two or three steady rains when the soil stays moist a few inches below the surface.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ leebi nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni yɔɔ oshara ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaadu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi inchi fioo komɛi.

english: Pepper blossoms drop off when the plant experiences stress from extreme heat or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist by placing dry grass around the base of the plants helps protect the flowers so they can form fruits.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ekɛhaaa lɛ be fɛɛ be. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni okɛaabɔle shishi lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛfɔ̃ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do the maize seeds I save from last year's harvest produce smaller ears than the original seeds I bought from the store?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni mijie kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ wo toi bibii fe shishijee ŋmãa ni mihe yɛ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Commercial hybrid seeds are specifically bred to give their highest yield in the very first season. Seeds saved from that crop lose their special strength in the next generation, resulting in smaller plants and lower yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ jarayeli dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ tsei amli lɛ laajeɔ amɛhewalɛ krɛdɛɛ lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei bibii kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi.

english: Is it really harmful if I leave wild grass growing close around the stems of my yam plants?
ga: Ani eji oshara diɛŋtsɛ kɛji mishi koo mli jwɛi yɛ ŋmei tso lɛ shishi?

english: Yes, tall grass competes directly with your yam plants for water, sunlight, and plant food in the soil. Clearing weeds away from the plant stems ensures your yams get all the nutrition they need to grow large tubers.
ga: Hɛɛ, jwɛi kakadaji kɛ o-sweet potato tsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la, kɛ tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ jwɛi kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ náa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why is my harvested corn molding in my storage barn even though I picked it when the leaves were dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ feɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mijie lɛ beni baai lɛ egbi lɛ moŋ.

english: Corn cobs can feel dry on the outside while still holding moisture deep inside the grains. Drying your shelled corn under the sun on a clean tarpaulin until the grains are very hard prevents mold and insects from destroying your store.
ga: Ekolɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ baanu he akɛ amɛgbi yɛ kponɔgbɛ shi amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ lolo yɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa ni ajie lɛ lɛ wo hulutsoo be mli yɛ tarp ni he tse nɔ kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli wa waa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmãa kɛ kooloi akafite oshwapo lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during heavy windstorms before the fruit is ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ ahum be mli dani aduawai lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and can struggle to support heavy bunches of fruit during storms. Cutting off extra shoots so only two or three stalks grow per mat, and using wooden poles to prop up fruiting trees, keeps them upright.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛye amɛbua aduawai ni tsii yɛ ahum be mli. Kpãa ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ mli bɔni afee ni ŋmeii 2-3 pɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ mat kome mli, ni okɛ tsei ni akɛwoɔ yibii lɛ atsu nii ni okɛfi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ asɛɛ koni amɛhi shi jaŋŋ.

english: If I harvest part of my crop and leave the rest in the ground, will the remaining part grow back on its own?
ga: Kɛ́ mikpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fã ko ni mishi fã ni eshwɛ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ Ani fã ni eshwɛ lɛ baakwɛ̃ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, many crops like cassava, sugarcane, and certain root vegetables can sprout new stems and leaves from roots or stems left in the soil after partial harvesting.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei babaoo, tamɔ ŋmei, ŋmei, kɛ shishifãi komɛi baanyɛ akwɛ̃ ŋmeii kɛ baai heei kɛjɛ shishifãi loo ŋmeii ni eshwɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ko sɛɛ.

english: Why do my yam tubers start growing leaves again if I leave them unharvested in the soil during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ baai shishi ekoŋŋ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni akpaaa amɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yam tubers are underground storage organs; when soil moisture and temperature are suitable, the tuber breaks dormancy and naturally uses its stored energy to produce fresh stems and leaves.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii ji shikpɔŋ shishi nibii ni akɛtoɔ nii ahe. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i kɛ latsaa lɛ sa Bulbs lɛ fiteɔ shihilɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi lɛ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛfee ŋmeii kɛ baai heei yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Can I cut my rice stems after harvest and expect a second crop to grow from the same roots?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafo ŋmãa tso ko yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ ni makpa gbɛ akɛ tso ni ji enyɔ lɛ baajɛ shishifãi kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ mli aba?

english: Yes, this practice is known as ratooning, where fresh shoots emerge from the main stem's base after cutting, producing a smaller secondary harvest if soil moisture and nutrients are sufficient.
ga: Hɛɛ, atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. he ni ŋmeii heei jeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ tso wulu lɛ shishi beni afo lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baaha nibii ni ji enyɔ lɛ aba shi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Is it good practice to leave some matured crops unharvested in my field, or should I clear everything at once?
ga: Ani eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ mashi ŋmɔshi nibii ni edara ni akpaaa yɛ miŋmɔji amli? Aloo esa akɛ majie nɔ fɛɛ nɔ shikome?

english: Staggering your harvest allows you to keep food fresh in the ground for longer, though leaving ripe crops too long can expose them to field pests, diseases, or rot.
ga: Nibii ni akpaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ haa niyenii lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Shi kɛlɛ, kɛ́ ashi ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tsɛŋemɔ helai, helai, loo fitemɔ aba amɛmli.

english: How do I pick peppers from my plant so that the main branch keeps producing more fruit?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafolɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ koni niji titrii lɛ awo yibii babaoo?

english: Harvest peppers gently by snapping or cutting the fruit stem without breaking the foliage stems, encouraging the plant to continue flowering and fruiting over an extended period.
ga: Kpaa ŋmeii lɛ blɛoo kɛtsɔ aduawai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ni ooofo loo ooofolɔ ni okɛ baai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ akumɔɔ lɛ nɔ. Tswaa tsei lɛ koni amɛya nɔ amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo yibii be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Should I leave leftover crop stalks in my field after harvesting, or burn them all?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashi tsei ahe tsei ni eshwɛ lɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛ́ akpa kpamɔ lɛ loo mashã fɛɛ?

english: Leaving non-diseased crop stalks on the field acts as mulch, retaining soil moisture and slowly decomposing into organic matter that improves soil fertility.
ga: Tso shishifãi ni hela bɛ mli lɛ ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baatsu nii akɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi fiofio ni efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, ni no haa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii babaoo.

english: Why do weeds come back so quickly after I cut them off at ground level during weeding?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa oya nɛkɛ beni mifo amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mifoɔ jwɛi lɛ?

english: Cutting only the top of the weed leaves the root system intact underground, allowing the weed to quickly push up new green shoots using energy stored in its roots.
ga: Kɛ́ afo jwɛi lɛ yiteŋ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ akafite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa jwɛi lɛ ni amɛtsiɔ ŋmeii heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ oya kɛtsɔ hewalɛ ni ato yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin when I plant too many seeds close together in my plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo beni miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the seedlings compete intensely for sunlight, forcing them to stretch upward quickly, resulting in weak, thin stalks.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ oya. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa.

english: Why do my crops look dry and dead during the harmattan season, and will they revive when rains return?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbi ni amɛgboi yɛ harmatta be lɛ mli lɛ? Ni ani ebaaku esɛɛ eba wala mli ekoŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ ekoŋŋ?

english: Many hardy plants enter a resting state and shed leaves during prolonged dry spells to save water; once rains return, dormant roots reactivate and sprout fresh leaves.
ga: Tsei babaoo ni wa lɛ yaa wɔɔhe ni amɛshwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ, shishifãi ni egbo lɛ tsuɔ nii ekoŋŋ ni baai heei kwɛ̃ɔ.

english: What happens to a green maize plant if I cut off its upper leaves before the cob fully forms?
ga: Mɛni baaba ŋmãa tso ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ nɔ kɛji mifo ŋwɛi baai lɛ dani ŋmãa lɛ gbe naa?

english: Leaves are the food factory of the plant; removing upper leaves reduces sunlight absorption, weakening the plant and lowering the ultimate yield of the maize cob.
ga: Baai ji tso lɛ niyenii nitsumɔhe. Kɛ́ ajieɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ, ehaa hulu la ni shɛɔ lɛ baa shi. Ha tso lɛ afee gbɔjɔmɔ ni oha ŋmãa ni fa fe fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ aba shi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which helps leaves grow big and healthy. It can also happen when heavy rains wash soil nutrients away or when excess water sits on the field for too long.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛhe wa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ loo kɛ́ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ta ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: Cassava roots rot underground when excess water stays in the soil without draining away. It can also be caused by fungal diseases that spread through infected stem cuttings used during planting.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ejeee kpo. Fungal hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ ni ajieɔ yɛ dumɔ be mli lɛ hu baanyɛ aha eba.

english: Why are my cocoa trees dropping their flowers without forming any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa kwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by prolonged dry weather, lack of shade, or insect pests like mirids. The tree drops flowers to save its energy when it lacks enough water or nutrients to support growing pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ, hulutsoo ni bɛ, loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ atatui ha amɛhe lɛ hao amɛ. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he beni amɛbɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua fɔfɔi ni miida lɛ.

english: This is known as blossom-end rot. It occurs when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil, usually because of irregular watering where the soil shifts from extremely dry to very wet.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. he ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ he ni egbi waa kɛyaa he ni edɔ waa lɛ

english: Plantain roots are shallow and often damaged by tiny soil pests like nematodes or root weevils. When roots are damaged, the heavy plant cannot hold itself firmly in wet, windy weather.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ nematodes loo shishifãi amli ŋmeii fiteɔ amɛ. Beni shishifãi lɛ efite lɛ Tsei ni tsii lɛ nyɛŋ ahi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: Why should I plant cowpea or groundnuts on my land after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mikpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts trap nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil through their roots. This naturally enriches the soil with food for your next maize crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii kɛha o-abele ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops even after I clear my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mifo ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Weed seeds can survive in the soil for years and sprout quickly once exposed to sunlight. They are naturally wild and tough, taking up water and soil nutrients much faster than planted crop seeds.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii babaoo ni amɛkwɛ̃ oya kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ. Amɛji adebɔɔ mli nibii ni amɛhe wa. Amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe dumɔwui ni adu lɛ.

english: Why do my yam plants grow long leafy vines but give me very small tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ woɔ baai kakadaji shi ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer makes the yam plant send all its energy upward into making leaves and vines, leaving little energy to store food down in the underground tuber.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaha sweet potato tso lɛ atsu ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛya ŋwɛi koni ekɛfee baai kɛ wain tsei. Hewalɛ fioo pɛ eshwɛ ni akɛtoɔ niyenii yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Leaf curling is caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips, mites, or aphids. These insects feed on the leaf sap and often spread viruses that stop the leaves from expanding properly.
ga: Kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, mites loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni bei pii lɛ amɛgbɛɔ helai ni haaa baa lɛ agbɛ ashwã jogbaŋŋ lɛ amɛshwãa.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and weak without good yield when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛwooo yibii kpakpai kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Instead of growing strong stems and large fruits, they stretch upward to fight for light.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ tsohi nɛ a he wa kɛ yiblii nguahi. Mohu ɔ, a kplɛɛ a he konɛ a hwu kɛ ha la a.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are missing nitrogen, which is the main food leaves need to stay healthy. When the soil lacks nutrients or gets washed out by heavy rain, the plant starves and turns yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa baa koni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ. Be mli ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ lɛ. Hɔmɔ baaye tso lɛ ni ebaatsɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do people tell me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my land before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ko baakɛɛ mi akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmãa?

english: Groundnuts and beans are special crops that pull food directly from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. When you harvest them, they leave behind rich soil that helps your next maize crop grow strong without needing as much expensive fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji okpa lɛ Ebaashi shikpɔŋ ni baaye abua bo ni oná ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ waa ni ŋmãa ni jara wa he ehiaaa bo.

english: How does adding dried chicken dung to my farm help my crops grow bigger?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛdaraa?

english: Chicken dung acts as natural plant food that slowly releases rich nutrients into the dirt while helping the soil hold onto water much longer during hot, dry days.
ga: Kooloo ŋmɔtɔ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli tso niyenii ni yaa hiɛ fiofio. Ejieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni fa babaoo kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ anɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to strong direct sunlight and hot winds. Leaving larger shade trees on the field creates a cool environment and keeps moisture in the soil so the young cocoa can survive.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ he waa. Kɛ́ ashi tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa shihilɛ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni cacao tsei bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when the rain falls heavily for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When water sits in the farm for too long without draining away, it drowns the roots and allows fungal rots to attack them.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nu hiɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ajieee kɛjɛɛɛ mli. Nu baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli ni eha ŋmeii ni egbo lɛ atutua amɛ.

english: This damage is usually caused by caterpillars known as Fall Armyworms. They hide deep inside the soft central leaves of the maize plant during the day and chew through them rapidly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ Fall Armyworms lɛ kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ nii oya.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites that hide under the leaves and suck out the juices, causing the leaves to twist and deform.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ ji kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛmuɔ nu lɛ mli lɛ. Ehaa baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efiteɔ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off the plant without turning into any tomato fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: When weather gets too hot or the soil dries out completely, tomato plants get stressed and drop their blossoms to save water and energy rather than feeding new fruit.
ga: Be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Tomato tsei lɛ feɔ mɛi ni haoɔ ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii heei.

english: Why do my crops grow so short and weak when I leave weeds around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛhe waaa beni mishiɔ jwɛi yɛ he lɛ?

english: Weeds act like greedy neighbors—they quickly drink up the water, soak up the sunlight, and steal the soil food that your main crops need to grow tall and strong.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akutsoŋbii ni hiɛ kɔ̃ɔ mɔ nɔ—amɛnuɔ nu oya, amɛmɔɔ hulu la, ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni he hiaa onibii titrii lɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during heavy rains right when the fruit bunches grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa mli beni ewo yibii wuji pɛ kɛkɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and do not grip deep into the soil. When the fruit bunch grows heavy, the top becomes heavy and wind can easily push the whole plant over unless you support it with wooden props.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛshɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Beni aduawai akuu lɛ mli tsii lɛ Yitsoŋgbɛ fã lɛ tsii ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ shi mlɛo. Ja okɛ tso ni akɛfee nibii fiɔ sɛɛ.

english: How far apart should I plant my cassava cuttings so that I get big tubers?
ga: Te esa akɛ adu amɛ kɛjɛ amɛhe teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ koni anyɛ ana bulbs wuji?

english: Cassava cuttings should ideally be planted about 1 meter apart in rows. Giving each plant enough space allows the underground roots room to expand into large tubers without competing with neighboring plants for water and soil nutrients.
ga: Esa akɛ adu tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ aaafee mita kome kɛjɛ amɛhe yɛ srɔtoi amli. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ shishi shishifã tsu lɛ daa ni etsɔɔ bulb agbo ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ abɔ akaŋ kɛha nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Yam vines are natural climbers that need to lift their leaves off the ground to catch sunlight. Staking exposes more leaves to direct sun, which allows the plant to produce more energy and grow bigger, healthier yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni ehe hiaa ni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ koni hulu la ashɛ amɛnɔ. Staking haa baai lɛ naa hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa hewalɛ babaoo. ni amɛkwɛ̃ sweet potato ŋmeii ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, a key plant food. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure around the plant will help restore its bright green color and improve cob development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso lɛ niyenii titri lɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli. Nitrogen ni fa babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ ni akɛbaabɔle Tso lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ su ni mli tse lɛ aba ekoŋŋ ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings wither and burn when there is too much sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshãa kɛ́ hulu la babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains or bananas alongside young cocoa provides living shade that keeps the soil moist and protects the seedlings until they grow stronger.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains loo banana ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo bibii ahe. Ehaa hɔɔŋ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ebuɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛwaa.

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is commonly caused by tiny pests like aphids or mites that suck juices from the leaves, or by a viral infection spread by insects. Spraying neem oil solution or an approved organic insecticide helps control these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli Kɛ akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ko ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ wala mli ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Why are small worms eating the leaves inside the centers of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These worms are likely Fall Armyworms, a common crop pest. They hide inside the central funnel of the plant to feed; applying recommended pesticides early in the morning or sprinkling clean ash/sand into the funnel can help clear them.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ namɔ. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli koni amɛye nii. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ wo mli leebi loo okɛ sũ/ŋã ni he tse shwie ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ejie amɛ.

english: Tomato plants often drop their flowers when temperatures are too high, when water is lacking, or when given too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil consistently damp with mulch and avoiding excessive fertilizer helps flowers turn into tomatoes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ, kɛ́ nu faaa yɛ amɛmli, loo kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen babaoo wo amɛmli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ba kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ tomatoi.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows pests to build up in the field. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas puts nitrogen back into the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and fertilizer nutrients. Clearing weeds early in the crop's growth ensures your crops get all the food and light they need to grow strong and yield well.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii baa. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Yɛ tsei adalɛ mli lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ niyenii kɛ la ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara waa ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: How can I tell if my soil has enough water for my crops without buying tools?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni miheee nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii?

english: You can dig down about hand-depth into the soil, grab a handful, and squeeze it tightly. If it forms a ball without dripping water, the soil is moist enough; if it crumbles dryly through your fingers, your crops need watering or rain.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ohe awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli aaafee bɔ ni onine lɛ mli kwɔ ha. Mɔ nine kome ni okɛmimɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji efee bɔɔlu ni nu shwieee shi lɛ, no lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa. Kɛji etsɔ oniji amli egbee shi Oŋmɔshi nibii ahe miihia nu loo nugbɔ.

english: Why should I mix different types of crop food or fertilizers together in one container instead of applying just one type?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tsei niyenii loo ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi afutu mli lɛ? ekome yɛ tsɛnsi kome mli Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ henɔ kome pɛ baafata he

english: Crops need a balanced diet to grow well, just like humans do. Mixing different fertilizers ensures your crops get all the necessary nutrients—like nitrogen for leaves, phosphorus for roots, and potassium for fruits—at the same time.
ga: Niyenii ni ja he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. tamɔ adesai nɔŋŋ Ni akɛfutuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ, tamɔ nitrogen kɛha baai lɛ. Fosfɔs kɛha shishifãi kɛ potasium kɛha aduawai yɛ be kome mli

english: Can putting too much plant food or fertilizer right next to the stem damage my crops?
ga: Ani tso niyenii loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni mikɛbaafata tso lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ baanyɛ afite miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Yes, plant food contains strong mineral salts. Putting it directly against the stem or roots can burn the plant tissue and suck water out of the roots, causing the crop to dry up and die.
ga: Hɛɛ, minerals babaoo yɛ tsei amli niyenii amli. Kɛ́ okɛwo tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ mli fãji ni ekɛnu nu kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Ebaanyɛ eha ŋmɔshi nibii agbi ni amɛgboi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential food for leaf growth, or that excess water around the roots is suffocating the plant so it cannot feed properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ loo nu ni fa fe nine yɛ he fɛɛ he Shishifãi lɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi aahu akɛ enyɛɛɛ ena niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants droop in the hot afternoon even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: On hot days, leaves lose water through evaporation faster than roots can drink it from the soil. The plant droops on purpose to hide its leaves from the sun and conserve moisture until the weather cools down.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei gboiɔ kɛ yiŋtoo akɛ amɛbaatee amɛbaai lɛ kɛjɛ hulu la he ni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience stress from high heat, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients, choosing to save their own lives rather than feeding new fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ hao amɛ. Ni ehala akɛ ebaahere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala yiwala moŋ fe ni eeeha lɛ aduawai heei.

english: If I plant my crop seeds very deep in the soil, will it help them grow stronger?
ga: Kɛji midu mi aduawai dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ waa Ani ebaaye ebua dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛdara waa?

english: No, planting seeds too deep starves them of air and forces them to waste all their stored energy trying to push through the soil, often causing them to rot before reaching sunlight.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui ni aduɔ kɛyaa shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ baaha amɛhe afee shoo ni enyɛ amɛnɔ ni amɛfite amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛto lɛ ni amɛkɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ haa amɛgboiɔ dani amɛshɛɔ hulu la lɛ he.

english: If I plant my crops very close together to fit more on my farm, will I get a bigger harvest?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni ekɛ miŋmɔ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ hu? Ani maná nitsumɔ babaoo?

english: No, planting too closely forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and plant food in the soil, resulting in weak, thin plants with small yields.
ga: Dabi, tso ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ hulu la, nu, kɛ tsei niyenii ni jɛ tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli lɛ abɔ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa lɛ baa, ni yibiiwoo hu baa shi.

english: Cassava cuttings fail if they are planted upside down, if the wood is dry or diseased, or if the stem buds are damaged during cutting and handling.
ga: Cassava ni afo lɛ baafee nɔ ni ehiii kɛji akɛ adu lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. Tso ni egbi loo hela emɔ lɛ loo kɛji hiŋmɛi tso lɛ efite yɛ be mli ni afoɔ lɛ ni akɛyaa he kroko lɛ

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Tall shade trees act as natural umbrellas, keeping the air cool and soil moist for the young seedlings.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulutsoo lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛha tsei bibii.

english: How do weeds growing near my crops actually stop my crops from growing well?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ atsĩ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa jogbaŋŋ?

english: Weeds act like aggressive neighbors—they steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight that your crops need, leaving your crops weak and stunted.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akutsoŋbii ni yɔɔ basabasa. Amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa onibii lɛ. Enɛ haa onibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ.

english: When maize lacks nitrogen fertilizer or stays in waterlogged soil, it pulls nutrients from its older, lower leaves to feed the young upper growth, causing the bottom leaves to turn yellow and dry up.
ga: Beni ŋmãa bɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo eyɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Egbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai bibii amli koni ekɛha tsei bibii lɛ. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why does my maize grow tall and thin with weak stalks instead of strong and thick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ daa ni ekwɛɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ fe ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Planting maize seeds too close together forces the plants to compete for sunlight, making them stretch tall and thin, which leaves them weak and easy for wind to push over.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la he akaŋ. Ehaa dumɔwui lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɔ amɛwoɔ amɛ oya.

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil encourages cassava to spend all its energy growing big leaves above ground, leaving little energy to expand the tubers hidden below.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaha ŋmei lɛ afite ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛwoɔ ebaai wuji lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni hewalɛ fioo pɛ eshwɛ ni ekɛgbala yitso ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Why do my yam vines wilt and dry up so quickly during short dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbiɔ oya yɛ be kukuoo mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ?

english: Yams have shallow feeding roots that struggle to reach deep moisture; without thick mulch around the mound to trap water, the roots dry out quickly when rain stops.
ga: Sweet potatoes yɛ shishifãi ni yeɔ niyenii ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛshɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli kwɔ he. without thick mulching Abɔle gɔŋ lɛ he koni nu ahi mli Shishifãi lɛ baagbi oya kɛ nugbɔ lɛ kpa.

english: Extreme heat, sudden dry conditions, or a lack of pollinating insects can stress tomato plants, causing them to drop their flowers before fruit can form.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shihilɛi ni mli egbi trukaa loo kooloi ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ faaa lɛ Baanyɛ ekɛ haomɔ aba tomato tsei anɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ kpo.

english: Leaf curl in peppers is usually caused by tiny pests like mites or thrips sucking the sap from young leaves, which deforms them as they grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baa lɛ baa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ náa su ko ni ejaaa beni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in damp, heavily shaded conditions where air cannot flow freely between cocoa trees.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli. he ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ atsɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ateŋ oya lɛ

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when the fruit starts to mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai lɛ bɔi kwɛ̃mɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems supporting heavy fruit stems; if microscopic worms called nematodes weaken the roots, or if the heavy stem isn't propped with a strong wooden pole, the tree easily topples.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni fiɔ aduawai ashishifãi ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ. Kɛji ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ ha shishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔ, Aloo kɛji akɛ tso lɛ shishi tsii Akɛ tsei ni wa fioo fiɔ sɛɛ. Tso lɛ baagbee shi mlɛo.

english: Cowpeas naturally create their own nitrogen in the soil, so adding extra nitrogen fertilizer makes them grow excessive leaves while suppressing flower and pod production.
ga: Cowpeas lɛ diɛŋtsɛ feɔ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, nitrogen ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ aná baai babaoo yɛ be mli ni etsĩɔ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii ni afee lɛ naa.

english: Why do my groundnut seeds rot in the soil before they even sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut dumɔwui lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ po lɛ?

english: Planting groundnuts in overly wet, unplowed soil deprives the seeds of oxygen and exposes them to soil fungi that rot the seeds before they can germinate.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni aduuu nɔ ni edɔ tsɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ baaná hɔmɔ, ni ebaaha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aba amɛnɔ ni haa amɛgboiɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why should I put manure or fertilizer into the soil before I put my seeds in, instead of waiting for them to sprout first?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he dani madu dumɔwui? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ ni ekwɛ̃ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ?

english: Adding nutrients at planting gives seeds the food they need the moment their first roots branch out, helping the seedling grow strong stems and leaves quickly right from the start.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ fata tso lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ kɛji klɛŋklɛŋ shishifãi lɛ kwɛ̃ pɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛdaraa ŋmeii kɛ baai ni wa oya kɛjɛɔ shishijee.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my growing maize turning yellow while the top leaves remain green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni miida lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow from the bottom up when the soil runs out of nitrogen, causing the plant to move its remaining food to the young top leaves to keep growing.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa baai bibii lɛ anɔ koni eya nɔ eda.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that burn easily in direct sun, so they need temporary shade trees like plantains above them to keep the soil moist and cool until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni nuɔ hulu he waa ni kɛ́ hulu lɛ tso amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, amɛshãa oya. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni kookoo tsei lɛ aná tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ kooyigbɛ tsei, koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni edɔ kɛyashi tsei lɛ baadara.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up tightly in the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants curl their leaves during intense heat to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, which helps them hold onto water and protect themselves from drying out.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafolɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ baaye abua ni amɛnu nu ni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when temperature spikes or water is inconsistent because the plant feels stressed and prioritizes saving its own life over producing fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ waa loo nu lɛ mli shwereɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tomato tso lɛ miihao ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala yiwalaheremɔ nɔ fe yibiiwoo ni ebaawo lɛ.

english: Why should I cut off the extra shoots growing around the bottom of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain wulu lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Extra shoots draw water and plant food away from the main stem, so removing them leaves more energy for the main plant to produce larger plantain bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii krokomɛi lɛ gbalaa nu kɛ tso lɛ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ, nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso titri lɛ naa hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii akui wuji.

english: Why do my yam vines produce bigger tubers when I give them tall wooden stakes to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ yɛ bulbs wuji fe tsutsu lɛ beni mikɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ ha amɛ lɛ? Ha amɛkwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves up off the ground so they catch maximum sunlight to manufacture food, which travels down to build larger tubers underground.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛná niyenii. Enɛ tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shi ni efeɔ ŋmei agbo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why does my maize yield get smaller every year if I plant it on the exact same land each season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛji midu he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains the specific nutrients maize relies on, but alternating with crops like cowpeas restores nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni abɛi lɛ damɔ nɔ lɛ. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaha nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why is it risky to plant my crop right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mitsei lɛ adumɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ ji oshara lɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a short dry spell, which can cause newly sprouted seeds to dry out and die before the main rainy season fully established.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ, ni baanyɛ aha dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ aba naagbee.

english: How long can I store cut cassava stems before planting them in the ground?
ga: Dani abaadu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, be enyiɛ abaanyɛ akɛ ŋmeii ni afo lɛ ato?

english: Cassava stems can sit in a shaded, well-ventilated spot for up to two weeks without dying, but planting them within a few days ensures faster root growth and sprouting.
ga: Kasava tsei baanyɛ ahi he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli kɛyashi otsii enyɔ ni amɛgbooo. Shi kɛ́ adu yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ adara ni amɛkwɛ̃ oya.

english: Why does my soil get so dry, hard, and cracked when the strong sun shines on it for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ, ewaa, ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛji hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shɛ enɔ lɛ? Gbii babaoo?

english: Extreme sun bakes bare soil and destroys organic matter, causing moisture to evaporate quickly. Without organic cover, the soil compacts and loses its ability to hold water and nutrients for plants.
ga: Hulu la ni fa fe nine lɛ baajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ebaafite nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ shwieɔ oya Kɛji akɛ nɔ ko bɛ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni enyɛŋ ehiɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa tsei lɛ.

english: How can I restore my farm land if it has become dry and unproductive from heat and continuous planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ ekoŋŋ? Ni kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi ni wooo yibii kɛjɛ latsaa kɛ okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ hu?

english: You can restore degraded soil by mixing in compost or animal manure, practicing crop rotation with leguminous plants like cowpeas, and keeping the ground covered with mulch to rebuild moisture and organic nutrients.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ aku sɛɛ aba kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsakeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ cowpeas ni okɛ mulch aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my crop plants turning yellow and looking burned under the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiifee tamɔ nɔ ni hulu lɛ etswa amɛ yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excessive heat and direct sunlight cause plants to lose water faster than their roots can pull it from the ground, causing sunburn and stress on delicate leaves.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa tsei lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ekɛ hulutsoo kɛ haomɔ baa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ anɔ.

english: How can I keep water in my soil for a longer time so my crops do not dry up during hot weather?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahã nu ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ koni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ akagbi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Covering the soil around your plant stems with dry grass, straw, or leaves—a method called mulching—blocks direct sunlight from reaching the soil and dramatically reduces water evaporation.
ga: Mulching around Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi, jwɛi, loo baai ha tso lɛ shishifãi ahe—gbɛ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ mulching—tsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa koni ekashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehaa nu ni hoɔ lɛ baa shi waa.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without forming any tomatoes during the hot dry period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, tomato pollen becomes inactive or dry, preventing pollination. Without pollination, the blossoms dry out and drop off before fruit can form.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Tomato pollen lɛ baafee nɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛtsu nii loo ebaagbi. Bɔni afee ni akafee pollination Kɛji pollination bɛ lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are the bottoms of my young tomatoes turning black and rotten while still on the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato bibii lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite be mli ni amɛyɔɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by irregular soil moisture which prevents the plant from taking up enough calcium to build strong fruit walls.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ejaaa lɛ kɛbaa. Enɛ haaa tsei lɛ aná calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛma aduawai gbogboi ni wa.

english: What basic steps do I need to follow to grow healthy tomatoes that sell well in the market?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛi titrii esa akɛ matsɔ nɔ manyɛ makwɛ tomato ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ahɔ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: To grow good market tomatoes, choose disease-resistant seeds, raise healthy seedlings in a nursery bed, space plants properly for airflow, water them consistently at the roots, and stake them to keep fruits off the damp ground.
ga: Koni adu tomato yɛ jara kpakpa nɔ Halamɔ dumɔwui ni helai nyɛŋ amɔ amɛ. Tsɔɔmɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ dumɔwui akwɛmɔhei. Too he ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli. Nu kɛyashɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ daa. ni okɛ tsei ama shi koni aduawai lɛ akashwɛ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ

english: Watering early in the morning is best because cooler temperatures allow the soil to absorb moisture deeply before the afternoon sun causes high evaporation.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ hulutsoo be ni mli ejɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ nu ni mli kwɔ dani shwane hulu lɛ haa hulutsoo babaoo baa.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops curl inward during the hottest hours of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa mli yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism where plants reduce the leaf area exposed to direct sunlight to slow down water loss and survive heat stress.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Tso lɛ baaha he ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baa lɛ aba shi. Koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni ekɛte shi ewo dɔlɛ he haomɔ.

english: Which food crops are naturally strong enough to survive in poor soil and dry conditions?
ga: Mɛɛ niyenii tsei ji nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa yɛ adebɔɔ naa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii kɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi nɔ?

english: Crops like cassava, cowpeas, millet, and sorghum have deep or hardy root systems that allow them to draw moisture and nutrients from dry or degraded soils far better than delicate vegetables.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa, tsina ŋmãa, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ loo ni wa ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛjieɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo efite mli jogbaŋŋ fe aduawai ni yɔɔ mlɛo fe tsutsu lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa tree leaves dry up and turn brown when there is direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ egbi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight because their leaves burn easily. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains next to them acts like a protective umbrella, keeping the soil cool and moist while the cocoa grows.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains ni bɛŋkɛɔ lɛ adumɔ Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ mɔ he Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa lɛ.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in dark, damp, and overly shaded environments. Clearing weeds around the base and pruning dense tree branches lets air flow and sunlight in, which helps stop the rot.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni edɔ, edɔ, ni shade babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ lɛ kɛ tsei niji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ ni hulu la boteɔ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni akpa fitemɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize field turning pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋma ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which maize relies on to build strong green leaves and stalks. Adding animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore the green color and food production.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi biɔ ni afee baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ niyenii ni afee lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my cassava produce huge bushy green leaves above ground but small, thin roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni ebɔle shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or very rich manure, cassava uses all its energy to grow top leaves instead of storing starch below ground. Balanced soil nutrients encourage root expansion instead of leafy growth.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei lɛ kɛ ŋmei baato shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ eŋwɛi baai lɛ anɔ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ mlilɛɛmɔ yaa hiɛ moŋ fe ni baa lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: Why are my pepper leaves curling tightly inward and stopping new branches from forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe waa kɛmiiya mli ni amɛmiitsi niji heei anaa koni amɛkafee lɛ?

english: Curling leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking plant juice from under the leaves, or a virus carried by whiteflies. Spraying organic solutions like neem seed oil can keep these pests away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ tso mli nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo helai ni ŋmeii hiɛɔ Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ neem dumɔwui amli fɔ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ etsi nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ anaa.

english: Why do the bottoms of my ripe tomato fruits turn black and sunken?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ shishi miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efo lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a shortage of calcium in the plant. It usually happens when watering is uneven—such as when soil dries out completely and is then suddenly flooded with water.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu lɛ hoɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ, tamɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa ni nu eyi nɔ trukaa.

english: Why do my cassava bushes drop all their leaves during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during long dry spells to protect itself from losing water through evaporation. This helps the plant survive underground in a sleeping state until the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaai lɛ shi yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli koni ekɛbu ehe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ yɛ la ni hoɔ lɛ hewɔ lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ shihilɛ ni mli wa mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: How do I know the exact right time to plant my maize seeds when rain begins?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ?

english: Wait until two or three deep, soaking rains have moistened the soil thoroughly, rather than planting right after the very first light shower. This ensures seeds do not germinate and dry up under returning hot weather.
ga: Mɛɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ enyɔ loo etɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Plantain roots grow close to the soil surface, and heavy fruit bunches make the plant top-heavy. When soil becomes soft from rain, strong wind easily pulls them down unless stems are propped up with strong bamboo poles.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Ni aduawai akutsei ni tsii baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ efee blɛoo yɛ nugbɔ hewɔ lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛba shi mlɛo. ja akɛ ŋmei tso ni wa fiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ

english: Why are the flowers on my cowpea plants dropping to the ground before forming bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ nɔ lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ dani pea ŋmɔtɔi lɛ feɔ lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when plants experience heat stress without enough soil moisture, or when tiny insect pests feed on the flower stems before the pods can form.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii Yeɔ fɔfɔii ahe dani ŋmeii feɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and die when there are no big trees growing around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ bɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the soil quickly. Planting plantains or shade trees alongside young cocoa acts as a natural shield against scorching heat while the cocoa gets established.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaatsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he beni kookoo lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning light yellow starting from the leaf tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛyitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves that start turning brown at the tips usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea helps restore healthy green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni miibɔi ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Biɛ ji he ni ehe hiaa ni tsei ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ yɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: How do I tell which way is up when I am planting cassava stem cuttings in my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mikɛ ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ miidu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Look closely at the small raised bumps or buds where leaves used to grow on the stem; these bumps should point upward toward the sky. Planting cassava stems upside down causes slow sprouting and very low root yields.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii bibii lɛ. Ehiɔ he ni tsutsu lɛ baai lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ kpaakpa. Esa akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Cassava ni akwɛɔ nɔ kɛyaa shishi lɛ baaha ekwɛ̃ blɛoo ni shishifãi lɛ hu baa shi waa.

english: Why do agricultural officers say planting groundnuts or cowpeas on my land will help my next corn crop grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ midu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua mi ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that fix nitrogen from the air into the soil. When the legume plants finish growing, they leave behind rich natural nutrients that feed the next crop like corn.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni fiɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ gbe amɛkwɛ̃mɔ naa lɛ Amɛshiɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni fa babaoo ni akɛbaatsu nii akɛ niyenii kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: What causes ragged holes in my maize leaves and small green caterpillars hiding deep inside the plant tops?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ baa? Ekɛ ehe ewo tsei lɛ ayiteŋ shɔŋŋ

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that feeds on the soft center leaf funnels of young maize. Checking your field early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extracts can protect your crop before severe damage occurs.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ ŋmãa bibii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ abu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe dani nɔ ko ni yɔɔ hiɛdɔɔ aba.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my crops with dry leaves or grass after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko he lɛ? Nibii ni baai loo jwɛi egbi yɛ amɛdumɔ sɛɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry plant material is called mulching. It acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool, slows down water evaporation during sunny days, and stops weeds from taking over your farm.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ tsei ni egbi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ha nu lɛ mli la ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ fioo yɛ gbii ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. ni otsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I need to lift my yam vines onto wooden stakes instead of letting them spread flat on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ sweet potato wain tso lɛ woɔ tso nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Staking lifts yam leaves into direct sunlight so the plant can make enough food to swell and produce large tubers underground. It also keeps leaves off wet soil, preventing diseases.
ga: Staking haa hulu la shɛɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ awo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha efuu ni ewo ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Ehaa baai lɛ hu shwieɔ shi, ni ehaaa helai aba.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning dark brown and rotten before the fruits even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni efiteɔ dani aduawai lɛ po shwereɔ lɛ?

english: This issue is called blossom-end rot, which happens when tomato plants don't get steady water or lack calcium in the soil while fruits are forming. Watering your tomatoes regularly and evenly prevents this bottom rot.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tomato tsei lɛ náaa nu babaoo be fɛɛ be loo calcium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo o-tomato lɛ nɔ daa kɛ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shishigbɛ fitemɔ akafee nɔ ko.

english: How can I tell if my harvested corn grains are dry enough to store safely in sacks without spoiling?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mikɛto kotokui amli shweshweeshwe ni efiteee?

english: You can test grain dryness by pressing your thumbnail hard into a corn kernel; if it leaves an indent or feels soft, it needs more sun drying. Storing fully dried, hard grains prevents mold growth and weevil damage.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka bɔ ni odumɔwui lɛ egbi lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ o-thumbnail lɛ nɔ nyɛmɔ waa nɔ. into corn seeds Kɛji eshi ŋmeii komɛi loo enuɔ he akɛ ebɛ hejɔɔmɔ lɛ, ekolɛ ebaafee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Dumɔwui ni wa lɛ ni oooha egbi kwraa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ ŋmeii ni shwereɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my crops wilt and droop in the afternoon sun even when it rained two days ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ gbii enyɔ ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Hot midday temperatures cause plants to lose moisture faster than roots can draw it from dry topsoil. Adding organic matter like compost to your soil helps it trap and hold rainwater longer for crop roots.
ga: Gbi mli latsaa ni mli edɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ agbala kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nugbɔ nu lɛ ahi tsei shishifãi lɛ amli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to plant plantain trees alongside young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔdu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily in direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and provide large leaves that act as natural shade umbrellas, keeping the young cocoa moist and protected during its early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni abuɔ he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize is starving for nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure early in the plant's growth helps fix this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo tso lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni asaa naagba nɛɛ.

english: What causes small holes in my young maize leaves and sawdust-like dirt inside the central leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii amli ni muji ni tamɔ ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ yɛ baai lɛ ateŋ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar feeding inside the growing shoot. Spraying approved control products early in the morning or late evening when the worms are active helps protect the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛyeɔ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ miitsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why should I wait for steady rains before planting instead of sowing seeds after the very first rain shower?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa dani madu nii? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaadu dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ

english: The first rain shower is often followed by a short dry spell that bakes the soil. If seeds germinate during this hot spell, the young roots will dry up and die before the main rainy season begins.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔɔ lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Shishifãi bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi.

english: Is it better for me to apply chemical fertilizer when the soil is dry or when it is wet?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baawo mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi loo kɛ́ edɔ?

english: Always apply fertilizer when the soil is moist after rain. Fertilizer applied to dry soil cannot dissolve for the roots to drink, and high heat can burn the plant roots.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Anyɛɛɛ ajie ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ mli koni shishifãi lɛ anu nu. Ni dɔlɛ ni naa wa baanyɛ aha tso shishifãi ashã.

english: Most cassava varieties mature between 9 to 12 months after planting. You will notice the lower leaves falling off, the remaining leaves turning slightly yellow, and cracks appearing in the soil around the base of the stem.
ga: Cassava henɔi babaoo hiɔ shi aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaana akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miiho. Baai ni eshwɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ fioo. ni ŋmeii je kpo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I measure space between my crop rows instead of planting them very close to get more yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu gbɛ ni kã ŋmɔshi nibii ni adu lɛ ateŋ lɛ he moŋ fe ni madu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ koni maná yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to grow strong stems and produce bigger fruits or grains.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ tso ni mli wa ni ewo yibii loo dumɔwui wuji.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce food that grows the tuber underground. Lifting the vines on stakes exposes the leaves to the sun and keeps them off the damp ground, preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ́ akwɛ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ awó wein tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ, hulu la shɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe, ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: Why does letting weeds grow around my vegetable crops reduce my total harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ oŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mi-vegetables lɛ miiha mi-yibiiwoo lɛ fɛɛ miiba shi?

english: Weeds act like food thieves in your farm, stealing water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your vegetables get all the nutrients they need to grow large fruits.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ niyenii julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli, ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa onibii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha o-vegetables lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ aduawai wuji.

english: This black rot at the base of tomatoes, called blossom-end rot, happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium from the soil, often due to irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the plant move calcium to the fruit.
ga: Rot diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ Atsɛɔ lɛ blossom end rot. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛjieɔ calcium kɛyaa aduawai lɛ amli.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa plants dry up and drop off during the Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During the Harmattan, dry winds and hot sun strip moisture from soil and leaves faster than young roots can drink it. Without shade trees or enough soil moisture, seedling leaves dry out, turn brown, and drop off to save the plant from dying.
ga: Yɛ harmattan beaŋ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛbaa lɛ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii baanyɛ anu lɛ. Kɛji tsei ni baaha hulutsoo loo ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baai lɛ baagbi. etsɔ blɔfo ni egbee shi koni ekɛhere tso lɛ yiwala koni ekagbo.

english: Why do my tomato plant leaves curl up tightly when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ waa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism where the plant rolls its leaves to reduce the surface area exposed to direct sunlight, helping it conserve internal water during hot and dry spells.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. He ni tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ aba shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hiɔ mli yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: What makes caterpillars suddenly appear and eat the middle of my young maize stems right after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni ha trukaa lɛ, etamɔ nɔ ni Caterpillars miiye nii yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ beni nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ sɛɛ?

english: Moist soil and fresh greenery after early rains trigger pests like the Fall Armyworm to hatch quickly from eggs hidden in soil or weeds, targeting soft, fast-growing young maize leaves for food.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ kɛ ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra sɛɛ lɛ haa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ fɔɔ oya kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni akɛtee shikpɔŋ loo jwɛi amli lɛ amli. Ekɛ ehiɛ fɔɔ ŋmãa baai bibii ni daa oya lɛ anɔ akɛ niyenii.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize crop turning yellow while the top leaves are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baa lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient plant food. The maize plant moves the remaining nitrogen from its older bottom leaves up to feed the new growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji tso niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ titri lɛ Abele tsei tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni etsɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha baai heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Maize feeds heavily on specific soil nutrients like nitrogen. Growing it repeatedly on the same plot drains the soil of those nutrients and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen. Kɛ́ adu nii shii abɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ, nakai niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni kɔɔ ŋmãa pɔtɛɛ he ni buaa ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why is it good practice to plant plantain trees alongside my newly transplanted cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ aaadu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that easily burn under full sun. Fast-growing plantain trees provide quick canopy shade and keep the air humid, protecting cocoa plants while they establish deep roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya kɛji akɛ hulu la ni naa wa shɛ amɛnɔ. Dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔ oya ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli fũuɔ. Ebuɔ kookoo tsei ahe yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ daraa lɛ

english: Yes, because maize grows quickly and is harvested in about three to four months, while cassava grows slowly at first and takes longer. By the time cassava leaves expand to cover the field, the maize is already harvested.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya, ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei daa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli ni ekɛ be babaoo tsuɔ nii lɛ. Beni ŋmãa baai lɛ mli lɛɛɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ Abaanyɛ akpa ŋmãa agbɛnɛ.

english: Why do my yam plants produce bigger tubers when I give the vines wooden stakes to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tsei lɛ yɛ bulbs wuji beni mikɛ tso haa wain tso lɛ koni ekwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make energy for growing large tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the shade of the ground, exposing more leaves to sunlight and preventing soil-borne leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha ŋmeii wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ ajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi. Ehaa baai lɛ naa hulu la babaoo. ni atsĩ fɔmɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ anaa

english: How can I tell if my cassava tubers are mature and ready for harvesting without digging up the whole plant?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo kɛha nikpamɔ ni okɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Mature cassava plants usually show yellowing and dropping of lower leaves, cracks appearing in the soil around the base of the stem, and a firm, well-developed root neck when slight topsoil is cleared away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei tsei ni eda lɛ jieɔ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ akpo. Gbɛjegbɛi je kpo yɛ sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli. kɛ shishifãi akuu ni edara jogbaŋŋ kɛji ajie sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ fioo.

english: How do I know the soil has enough water to safely plant my maize seeds after the dry season ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui shweshweeshwe beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eba naagbee lɛ?

english: Wait until you receive two or three heavy rains close together, then dig down about a hand's depth; if the soil stays moist and forms a ball when squeezed in your hand, it has enough water to germinate seeds safely.
ga: Mɛɛ kɛyashi obaaná nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa enyɔ loo etɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe. No sɛɛ lɛ, shwie shi aaafee onineshi fã kome. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo ni efee bɔɔlu kɛji okɛ onine mimɔ mli lɛ, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa baaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, which gives leaves their rich green color. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-decomposed animal manure will help the plant regain its strength and growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ kɛ amɛdalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and get white spots during the dry period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and white spots are usually caused by small sap-sucking insects like mealybugs or whiteflies that attack plants when water is scarce. Spraying the leaves with a light soapy water mixture or neem extract helps control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ mealybugs loo whiteflies lɛ kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni eyɛŋ. ni tutuaa tsei kɛji nu faaa Kɛ́ akɛ nu ni mli ejɔ loo neem mli nu ni ajieɔ lɛ shwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ lɛ.

english: How do I know if my soil has enough moisture before I plant my yam tubers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ fa bɔ ni sa dani madu sweet potato tubers?

english: Squeeze a handful of soil into a ball in your hand. If it holds its shape without dripping excess water or crumbling instantly into dust, the ground has enough moisture for planting yam mounds.
ga: Mimɔ shikpɔŋ sũ fioo ko ni okɛfee bɔɔlu yɛ onine mli. Kɛji ehiɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ mli ni nu ni fa fe nine shwieee shi loo efooo amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni etsɔɔɔ sũ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu ŋmɔtɔ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ.

english: Planting seeds too close forces the crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. This competition makes the stalks grow thin and weak, resulting in very small cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa, ni no haa ŋmeii bibii waa baa.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant experiences extreme heat, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil moist around the base using dry grass mulch helps the plant retain its blossoms.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi tsu nii ni akɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why does my harvested maize develop mold and spoil so quickly inside storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikpaa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya ni efiteɔ yɛ kotokui ni akɛtoɔ mli lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Maize spoils in storage bags when it is bagged before it is completely dry. Grains must be sun-dried until they are hard enough to make a sharp cracking sound when bitten before putting them in closed bags.
ga: Abɛi fiteɔ yɛ kotokui ni akɛtoɔ mli lɛ amli kɛ́ awo kotoku mli dani egbi kwraa. Esa akɛ agbi ŋmaa lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ebaawa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ efee gbee ni tswaa kɛji akɛ amɔ lɛ dani akɛwo kotoku ko ni aŋã mli.

english: Is it helpful to plant cowpeas in the same field alongside my maize crop?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ madu tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Yes, planting cowpeas with maize is beneficial because cowpeas naturally gather nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for the maize.
ga: Hɛɛ, sɛɛnamɔ yɛ tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he ejaakɛ tsina ŋmãa buaa nitrogen naa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmãa.

english: Why are my tomato plant stems turning soft and dark right near the soil surface?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛhe yɛ ediŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ lɛ?

english: Dark, soft stems near the soil line indicate a fungal disease called damping-off, which happens when the soil remains too wet for long periods without good drainage.
ga: Tsoi bibii ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ tsɔɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ dampening off, ni baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni nu kpakpa bɛ mli.

english: Should I start sowing my seeds right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mabɔi dumɔwui dumɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is safer to wait for the rains to become steady, because the very first rain is often followed by a hot dry spell that can dry out and kill new seedlings before the main season begins.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa. Ejaakɛ bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui heei agbi dani be titri lɛ aje shishi.

english: Young crops are weak and easily overshadowed by aggressive weeds. Clearing weeds early ensures your crop gets all the initial sunshine, water, and soil nutrients it needs to establish strong roots.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ bibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni jwɛi ni baa lɛ haa amɛhe feɔ shoo oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow and dying before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi dani akpa lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which maize needs to stay green and build strength. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps keep the leaves green so the plant can make big ears of corn.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni ŋmãa ahi shi eŋɔli ni etswa hewalɛ ema shi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔji bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná toi wuji.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on the same plot after harvesting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize takes away a lot of strength from the soil. Cowpeas and groundnuts put natural nitrogen back into the dirt through their roots, restoring soil fertility for the next season's crops without costing extra money.
