ga: Abɛi jieɔ hewalɛ babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Cowpeas kɛ peanuts kɛ nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi anɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni afiteee shika babaoo.

english: Why is it bad to apply fertilizer on my field when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, ani shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa?

english: Fertilizer needs moisture to dissolve so plant roots can absorb it. Applying it on dry soil during hot weather can burn the plant roots and waste the fertilizer as nutrients evaporate into the hot air.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe miihia ni nu atsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afite be mli ni niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have broad leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and cool soil moisture it needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Enɛ haa kookoo bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Yam leaves need maximum sunlight to make food that grows large tubers underground. Staking lifts the vines high off the damp ground, exposing leaves to sunlight while protecting them from soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo koni amɛfee niyenii kɛ́ amɛmiikwɛ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ naa hulu la ni ehaa helai hu baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking juice from under the leaves, or transmitting a plant virus. Controlling these pests early with neem water or insect spray prevents leaf twisting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo tso mli helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Neem nu loo kooloi ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ akatsɔ.

english: Why are my tomato plants producing many flowers, but the flowers keep falling off without growing into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛfeɔ tomatoi?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients like phosphorus and calcium needed to form the fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ hao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa waa mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli hewalɛ, tamɔ fɔsfɔs kɛ kalsium, ni he hiaa koni aduawai aba lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: How does my cassava crop manage to stay alive during long dry seasons when there is no rain?
ga: Te mi-cassava tso lɛ baafee tɛŋŋ ehi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava stores water and energy inside its thick roots underground, and it naturally sheds its leaves during dry spells to stop water from escaping, allowing it to rest until the rains return.
ga: Cassava kɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ toɔ eshishifãi ni mli tse ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli, ni ekɛ ebaa lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni nu akaje mli. ni oha ejɔɔ ehe kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when heavy rain and wind blow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miitswa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems and top-heavy fruit bunches. Supporting the main stem with strong bamboo forks or piling extra dirt around the base keeps the plants firmly anchored in the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akui ni tsii. Fi tso lɛ yitso lɛ sɛɛ kɛ ŋmei fɔk ni wa loo okɛ sũ kroko abɔ he. Shishitoo lɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds in my field make my main crops grow smaller and produce less harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ miifee bibii ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly away from your crops. When weeds grow close to your crops, the crops starve and cannot grow strong or yield heavy produce.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu ni he hiaa waa, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji jwɛi kwɛ̃ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ Hɔmɔ baaye ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkwɛ̃ waa loo amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow even when it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil has run out of nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green. It can also happen when heavy rains wash away nutrients from the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe nɔ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why does my land yield fewer crops every year even though I use the same seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii moŋ?

english: Crops pull food out of the soil every season. If you do not give the land a rest, rotate crops, or add manure and fertilizer, the soil becomes tired and loses its power to feed new plants.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Kɛji ohaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hejɔɔmɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nijiaŋ jeɔ wui ni ebɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛyeɔ ebuaa tsei heei.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when I clear all the big trees off the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei ni edara lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are like babies; direct hot sun burns their leaves quickly. Planting them under shade trees like plantains keeps the ground cool and moist until the cocoa grows strong.
ga: Kakao tso bibioo tamɔ abifao. Hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shãa baai lɛ oya. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ ashishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa waa.

english: Why should I wait for the steady rains before planting my pepper seeds instead of planting after the very first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa dani madu pepper dumɔwui lɛ moŋ fe ni madu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by many hot, dry days. If seeds sprout during that dry gap, the hot sun will dry out the weak roots and kill the young plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ gbii babaoo ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ ateŋ lɛ Hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ baaha shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ agbi ni ekpata tsei bibii lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Why is it bad to plant many maize seeds together in the same single hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni aduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui babaoo No hewɔ lɛ ani dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome yɛ bu kome mli lɛ ehiii?

english: When seeds are crowded in one hole, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves you with thin, weak stalks that produce very small cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ abu dumɔwui lɛ anaa awo bu kome mli lɛ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa onáa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa.

english: Yam leaves need to reach sunlight to make food for the tubers underground. Lifting the vines off the ground prevents diseases from wet soil and helps the plant build bigger yams.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la koni ekɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie wain tsei lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ anaa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with many bushy leaves but yield very small roots under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ miiya hiɛ waa lɛ? Baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli Shi shishifãi bibii waa ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or is packed too hard, the plant spends all its energy growing leaves on top instead of pushing energy down to expand the tubers below.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛkwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ. Mohu ɔ, a tsiɔ he wami kɛ yaa si konɛ e ha yi ɔ nɛ ngɛ sisi ɔ mi nɛ wa.

english: Extreme afternoon heat or a sudden lack of water stresses the plant, forcing it to drop its flowers to save energy rather than feeding new fruit.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ mli dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ trukaa lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei lɛ ajie fɔfɔii amɛshwie shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii heei.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so slowly even when I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ miwoɔ amɛ nu moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds have strong roots that drink up the water and fertilizer meant for your crops. Removing weeds early allows your main crop to get all the food it needs.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni wa ni nuɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa onibii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ.

english: Why do my stored maize grains turn into dust and get tiny holes after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ mli eyi kɛ sũ ni bu bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ? Yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli?

english: Insects called weevils hatch inside stored grain if it is not dried properly. Storing fully dried maize in airtight bags cuts off air so the pests cannot survive and destroy your harvest.
ga: Kplukai ni atsɛɔ amɛ weevils lɛ baafɔ yɛ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ amli kɛji akɛ agbiko amɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni egbi kwraa wo vacuum kotokui amli lɛ, efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ baatsi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa ni amɛkafite onibii lɛ.

english: How do I know which side of a seed should face down when I am planting it in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male dumɔwu lɛ fã ni esa akɛ makwɛ shi kɛ́ midu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Seeds have a root side (radicle) that needs to grow downward into the soil to gather water, and a shoot side (plumule) that carries leaves and grows upward toward the sun. Planting with the root side pointing down helps the plant emerge faster without wasting energy.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifã fã (radius) ni esa akɛ eda kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ebua nu naa, kɛ shishifã fã (plumule) ni hiɛɔ baai ni edaa kɛyaa hulu lɛ he. Kɛ́ adu ni shishifãi lɛ tsɔɔ shi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni edaa oya ni efiteee hewalɛ.

english: Why is it important to press the soil down gently after I place my seeds in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni manyɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ blɛoo beni mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pressing the soil gently ensures the seed makes firm contact with the moist dirt. This allows the seed to easily absorb water from the soil, which triggers it to wake up and start growing.
ga: Kɛ́ omi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ blɛoo lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ kɛ muji ni mli efɔ lɛ abɔ he jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ teɔ shi ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛdaraa.

english: What happens if I plant my crop seeds too deep or too close to the top of the soil?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsɔ loo mibɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsɔ?

english: If you plant seeds too deep, the young leaf shoot will run out of stored food energy before reaching the sunlight. If planted too close to the surface, the seed can dry out quickly or be eaten by birds.
ga: Kɛji odu dumɔwui lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ, niyenii hewalɛ ni ato lɛ baaho dani amɛshɛ hulu la lɛ he. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ agbi oya loo okpoi baanyɛ aye amɛ.

english: Should I pack the soil very tightly or just press it lightly around my newly planted crops?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ diɛŋtsɛ loo mafolɔ mli blɛoo kɛkɛ mabɔle mitsei ni midu ehee lɛ ahe?

english: You should press the soil gently to remove air gaps around the seed. Packing it too hard makes the soil too tough for delicate new roots to push through.
ga: Esa akɛ onyɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ blɛoo. Bɔni afee ni ajie kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ dumɔwu lɛ he lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa tsɔ ni shishifãi heei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ nyɛŋ abote mli.

english: How does a seed buried deep in the dark dirt know which way to grow up toward the sun?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni dumɔwu ni afu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo duŋ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ leɔ akɛ edaa kɛyaa hulu lɛ he?

english: Seeds naturally respond to gravity. The first root automatically senses gravity and grows downward to find water, while the stem and leaves grow upward away from gravity to find light.
ga: Dumɔwui tsuɔ hewalɛ ni tsiɔ nii kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Klɛŋklɛŋ shishifãi lɛ nuɔ hewalɛ ni tsiɔ nii kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛdaraa kɛyaa shikpɔŋ koni amɛyatao nu. yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai lɛ daa kɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ hewalɛ ni tsiɔ nii kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ koni amɛtao la.

english: What is the main difference between the first root and the first leaf shoot that emerge from my seed?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ titri ni yɔɔ klɛŋklɛŋ shishifã lɛ kɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ midumɔwu lɛ mli lɛ teŋ?

english: The first root grows downward to anchor the plant in the soil and drink water. The first leaf shoot grows upward to catch sunlight and start making food for the growing plant.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ shishifãi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ kɛyaa shi koni amɛkɛ tso lɛ ama shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛnu nu lɛ. Klɛŋklɛŋ tsei lɛ baakwɛ koni amɛmɔ hulu la lɛ ni amɛje niyenii feemɔ shishi amɛha tso ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do roots always grow under the soil before I see any leaves pushing above the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shishifãi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi be fɛɛ be dani ana baai ni miitsi amɛhe kɛmiijɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: A seed must establish its roots first to drink water and secure itself in the earth. Without a working root system underground, the leaf shoot above ground would dry up and die immediately.
ga: Esa akɛ dumɔwui awo shishifãi dani amɛnu nu ni amɛma shi yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛji shishifã ko bɛ ni tsuɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ Baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: How can I tell if my planted crop seeds are germinating properly under the dirt before they break through the surface?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui ni midu lɛ miikwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi dani amɛfo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Healthy germination begins when the seed swells with water, triggering a tiny white root tip to push downward out of the seed coat within a few days of planting in moist soil.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ kpakpa jeɔ shishi kɛ́ nu shwie nɔ. Wo shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ahe hewalɛ Tsi kɛjɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashishi yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my crop seeds require moist soil before they can start growing leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ he hiaa midumɔwui lɛ dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ baai lɛ?

english: Water softens the hard outer shell of the seed and activates the stored food inside. Without enough moisture in the soil, the seed remains asleep and cannot grow.
ga: Nu lɛ haa dumɔwu lɛ kponɔgbɛ fã ni wa lɛ feɔ blɛoo, ni ekanyaa niyenii ni ato yɛ mli lɛ. Kɛji ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baakã he amɛwɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why should I avoid leaving loose air pockets in the dirt around my seeds when planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni mashiɔ yɛ sũ ni bɔle dumɔwui ahe lɛ mli kɛ́ midu nii lɛ?

english: Air pockets prevent the seed from touching wet soil directly. If the seed hangs in an air pocket, it cannot absorb water and its tiny emerging root will quickly dry out and die.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui tsiɔ dumɔwui anaa koni amɛkashɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ fĩ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui lɛ amli lɛ Enyɛŋ eŋɔ nu ni eshishifãi bibii lɛ baagbi oya ni amɛgboi.

english: Yellowing starting from the leaf tips in a V-shape usually means the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. Maize needs nitrogen to stay green and build strong cobs, so applying compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer will help the plant recover.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai lɛ anaa yɛ V su mli lɛ fɔɔ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni efee ŋmãa ni mli wa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die during the harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have shallow roots and tender leaves that burn easily under intense sun and hot winds. They require shade plants, such as plantains or leguminous trees, overhead to shield them from high heat and retain soil moisture during dry months.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains loo legumes. amɛyiteŋ koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ahi shi yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli.

english: What is making small holes in the center leaves of my corn plants before they show tassels?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ miifee bu bibii? Yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ dani tsɔne ko yɔɔ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which burrows into the growing central funnel of the plant. Checking early and applying recommended biological or chemical treatments directly into the funnel prevents them from destroying the growing stem.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni shwieɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ nu ni daa lɛ mli lɛ. Kwɛmɔ kɛjɛ shishijee Ni kɛ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite tsei ni miida lɛ.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off instead of forming peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper blossoms drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat stress or erratic watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist and spreading dry grass or leaf mulch around the base cools the root area so the plant can hold onto its flowers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni okɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmɔtɔ ebɔle shishi lɛ he lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ ahiɛ fɔfɔii.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts between my cassava plants help the farm?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ mi-cassava tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔ lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts are legumes that capture nitrogen from the air and naturally store it in the soil through their roots. Intercropping them feeds nitrogen to your cassava without requiring extra synthetic fertilizer.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa nitrogen baa ŋmei lɛ mli ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmei ni akɛfee ŋmei krokomɛi afata he.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot underground when heavy rains come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess water sitting around cassava roots starves them of oxygen, causing waterlogged tubers to rot. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows water to drain away and keeps the roots healthy until harvest.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni bɔleɔ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa lɛ faaa. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ baagboi. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋmei ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ atsɔ mli ni eye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why shouldn't I allow all the small sucker shoots to grow around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii bibii shwereɔ yɛ midumɔwu titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: When too many suckers grow at once, they steal water, nutrients, and sunlight from the main stem. Removing extra suckers and keeping only one or two strong followers ensures the plant produces a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ shikome lɛ, amɛjuɔ nu, niyenii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni akwɛ sɛɛnyiɛlɔ kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni he wa lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ awo ŋmeii wuji ni tsii babaoo.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning dry, black, and sunken?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ egbi, eyɛ ediŋŋ, ni efo lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium uptake when soil moisture fluctuates too much between dry and wet spells. Regular watering and mulching keep moisture levels steady so the roots can feed calcium up to the growing fruits.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni anyɛɛɛ aŋɔ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsakeɔ tsɔ yɛ be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ teŋ lɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ daa. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aha calcium kɛyashi aduawai lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: Why do I need to clear tall trees and put tall wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie tsei kakadaji ni mikɛ tsei kakadaji ama shi koni mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines produce underground tubers using energy caught by their leaves in full sunlight. Staking gets the leaves high into the air and sunlight while keeping them off damp ground where fungal leaves diseases easily spread.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛtsɔ hewalɛ ni anáa kɛjɛɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ. Staking baaha baai lɛ aya ŋwɛi kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛya hulu la lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha ekɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni fungal leaf helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya lɛ akabɔ he.

english: Weeds grow faster than farm crops and compete aggressively for sunlight, soil nutrients, and root space. Clearing weeds while crops are young ensures all available water and plant food go directly toward crop growth instead of supporting weeds.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei ni amɛyeɔ hulu la he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ shishifãi ni mli wa lɛ Jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ darako lɛ kudɔɔ nu fɛɛ ni yɔɔ kɛ tsei lɛ amli niyenii lɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa tsei lɛ adalɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefi jwɛi sɛɛ

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants drying up and dying in the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting plantains or shade trees alongside cocoa creates a canopy that shields young trees from heat and retains soil moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he lɛ baa, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: How can I stop my plantain trees from falling over when the fruit bunches get heavy?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-plantain lɛ naa koni ekagbee shi beni aduawai lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain roots grow close to the surface, making heavy trees prone to wind damage. Pruning extra suckers so only two or three stems grow together, and propping the bearing stem with sturdy bamboo poles, prevents them from uprooting.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ daa kɛbɛŋkɛɔ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni tsii lɛ nyɛɔ amɛfiteɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Afoɔ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ ahe bɔni afee ni ŋmeii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ afee ekome kɛkwɛ̃. kɛ ŋmei tsei ni wa ni fiɔ bearing shaft lɛ sɛɛ Koni ekɛtsi shishifãi lɛ anaa

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the leaf tips usually mean the maize lacks nitrogen in the soil. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or Urea while the soil is moist will help the crop regain its deep green color and vigor.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK loo urea wo tso lɛ mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ená eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: What is eating small ragged holes into the leaf funnels of my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni yeɔ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Ragged holes in young maize funnels are typical signs of Fall Armyworm caterpillars. Checking the center funnel early and applying recommended biological or chemical controls prevents them from destroying the growing tip.
ga: Buji ni ekumɔ yɛ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ahe okadi ni afɔɔ namɔ. Kwɛmɔ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ teŋgbɛ mra. ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ baatsi ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ahe fitemɔ naa.

english: Growing maize repeatedly on the same land drains specific soil nutrients and allows maize pests and diseases to build up in the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas restores soil nutrients naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, abaajie shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the blossoms on my tomato plants dropping off before any fruit grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop when the plant experiences extreme heat, prolonged dry spells, or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist by mulching helps the plant retain its flowers and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ ná dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nuu be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ. loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why are the bottom tips of my young watermelons turning black and soft?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon lɛ naagbee lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ ni efee blɛoo lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium and uneven watering while the fruit is forming. Keeping soil moisture steady and adding agricultural lime helps protect developing watermelons.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ mli kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be be mli ni aduawai lɛ miikwɛ fɔfɔi lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni aaakwɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ okwaayeli mli lime ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni abu watermelon ni miiya hiɛ lɛ he.

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water collects around them in poorly drained soil during wet months. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows heavy rain to drain off, keeping the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu ni ekã shi lɛ shwie shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nyɔji ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. ni oha shishifãi lɛ awa

english: How does planting beans or groundnuts make my farmland better for future crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ lɛ haa miŋmɔ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their root nodules. When the plant decays, it releases free nitrogen into the soil, enriching it for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsei lɛ fite Ejieɔ nitrogen ni aheee nɔ ko kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Koni aha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ayibɔ aya hiɛ

english: Should I apply my fertilizer when the soil is completely dry or after it rains?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo ŋmɔshi nibii beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa loo beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ?

english: Fertilizer should always be applied when the soil is moist after rain. Placing chemical fertilizer on dry soil can burn plant roots and prevents the nutrients from dissolving into a form the crop can drink.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be fɛɛ be kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni etsĩ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ anaa koni ekafee nɔ ko ni tsei baanyɛ anu.

english: How do I know if my corn will finish growing before the dry season starts?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-abele lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aje shishi?

english: Every crop variety has a specific maturity period. You need to check how many months of rainfall your area gets and select a seed variety, such as an early-maturing maize, that finishes producing before the rain stops.
ga: Tso henɔ fɛɛ tso yɛ be pɔtɛɛ ko ni ekɛdaa. Esa akɛ okwɛ nyɔji enyiɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ. ni ohala dumɔwui srɔtoi tamɔ ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ mra ni baagbe yibiiwoo naa dani nugbɔ lɛ akpa.

english: What happens if I plant my crops several months before the rains actually begin?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ midu mitsei lɛ nyɔji babaoo dani nugbɔ lɛ je shishi diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Planting seeds in dry soil too long before the rains start can cause the seeds to dry out, get damaged by heat, or be eaten by insects and birds before they ever get the chance to sprout.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ dani nugbɔ anɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha amɛgbi. ni latsaa fiteɔ lɛ loo kooloi bibii kɛ okpoi yeɔ lɛ dani dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ.

english: How many months of rainy weather does maize need to give a good harvest?
ga: Nyɔji enyiɛ ehe hiaa ni nugbɔ anɛ ŋmãa koni ená ŋmaa kpakpa?

english: Most common maize varieties need about 3 to 4 months of reliable rainfall and sunlight to grow, flower, and produce full cobs ready for harvest.
ga: Abele henɔi ni afɔɔ namɔ babaoo biɔ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ kɛ hulutsoo be koni amɛkwɛ̃, amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ ni asaa he kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Why are my crops staying on the farm for months without growing any bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ehi ŋmɔ lɛ mli nyɔji babaoo ni nɔ ko nɔ ko ekwɛɛɛ dɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Crops usually stop growing when the soil lacks nutrients, water is scarce, or roots are damaged by disease. Under severe stress, the plant pauses its growth just to stay alive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei kpaa daamɔ kɛji niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, nu faaa, loo helai efite amɛshishifãi lɛ. yɛ haomɔ ni naa wa shishi Tsei baakpa dalɛ koni amɛhi shi kɛkɛ.

english: My crops have been in the field for over a year without yielding, what could be causing this?
ga: Miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ehi ŋmɔ mli nɔ ni fe afi ni amɛwooo yibii. Mɛni kɛ naagba nɛɛ baa?

english: When a plant remains stagnant for years without yielding, it is often due to poor soil fertility, severe disease, or planting a crop variety that is not suited for your area's climate.
ga: Beni tso ko ehi shi afii babaoo ni ewooo yibii. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji shikpɔŋ ni ehiii, helai ni naa wa, loo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ ni esaaa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ.

english: If my crops stop growing during a dry spell, will they start growing normally again when the rain returns?
ga: Kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpa shweremɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ Ani amɛbaabɔi shweremɔ bɔ ni sa lɛ ekoŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba?

english: If the dry period is short, plants can recover when the rain comes back. However, if the drought lasts too long, the crop suffers permanent damage and will not yield well even if it receives water later.
ga: Kɛji hɔmɔ be lɛ ji kuku lɛ Tsei baanyɛ aya hiɛ kɛji nugbɔ ku esɛɛ eba, shi kɛlɛ, kɛji hɔmɔ lɛ hi shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baafite kɛya naanɔ, ni amɛwoŋ yibii jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ awo amɛ nu sɛɛ mli po.

english: Is it normal for some local crops to stay in the ground for years without showing progress?
ga: Ani eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ akɛ maŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi baahi shikpɔŋ afii babaoo ni amɛyaaa hiɛ?

english: No, healthy crops should show steady growth throughout their active season. Stagnant growth over years means the plant is suffering from chronic nutrient deficiency, poor climate conditions, or root issues.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aya nɔ akwɛ̃ yɛ be lɛ mli fɛɛ. Nɔ ni tso lɛ yaa hiɛ fioo yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa lɛ miipiŋ. Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni esaaa loo tsei shishifãi ahe naagbai

english: Why do some corn varieties take much longer to harvest than others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa henɔi komɛi heɔ be babaoo dani akpaa fe ekrokomɛi lɛ?

english: Different corn varieties are bred for different purposes and climates. Short-duration varieties mature quickly for regions with short rainy seasons, while long-duration varieties take more months to mature but often produce heavier yields if water is plentiful.
ga: Abele henɔi srɔtoi Atsɔse amɛ kɛha yiŋtoi srɔtoi kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi. Henɔi ni hiɔ shi be kuku lɛ shwereɔ oya yɛ hei ni nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo yɔɔ lɛ. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii ni hiɔ shi be kuku lɛ heɔ nyɔji babaoo dani amɛshwereɔ lɛ. Shi amɛfɔɔ yibiiwoo ni tsii waa kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ.

english: Can crops survive dormant in dry soil for four or five months while waiting for rain?
ga: Ani tsei baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ nyɔji ejwɛ loo enumɔ be mli ni amɛmiimɛ nugbɔ?

english: Most food crops cannot survive four or five months in completely dry soil without dying. Only specialized or deep-rooted crops can handle long dry spells without water.
ga: Niyenii tsei babaoo nyɛŋ ahi shi nyɔji ejwɛ loo enumɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi kwraa nɔ ni amɛgbooo. Tsei pɔtɛɛ loo tsei ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ pɛ baanyɛ akpee hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni nu bɛ mli lɛ naa.

english: How can I protect my crops from failing during long dry periods before the rain starts?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe koni amɛkafite yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli dani nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi?

english: You can protect your crops by choosing drought-resistant or quick-maturing seed varieties, covering the soil with dry grass (mulching) to trap moisture, and planting at the very start of the reliable rains.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu onibii ahe kɛtsɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa loo ni shwereɔ mra lɛ ni ooohala lɛ nɔ. Kɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni emɔ ŋmɔtɔ. ni adu beni nugbɔ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ

english: Why do my young maize leaves turn yellow and stop growing when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When heavy rain leaves standing water in your farm, the plant roots cannot breathe or soak up nutrients like nitrogen from the soil, causing the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha nu lɛ ŋmɛ shi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli Tse lɛ shishifãi nyɛɛɛ amu loo amɛŋɔ niyenii tamɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni no haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers drop off without turning into pods during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop their blossoms when they lack enough water and shade, saving their strength to keep the main tree alive through the dry season.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji nu kɛ hulutsoo be ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ amɛhe. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo tsei lɛ ahewalɛ hiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do my cowpea plants make so many broad green leaves but very few pods during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ babaoo shi ŋmɔtɔi fioo pɛ yɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When beans get too much water and nitrogen in the soil early on, the plant spends all its food growing big leaves and vines instead of flowering and making seeds.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii lɛ ná nu kɛ nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ shishijee mli lɛ, Tso lɛ kɛ niyenii lɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo baai wuji kɛ wain tsei. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo fɔfɔi ni ewo dumɔwui lɛ

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and weak with tiny cobs when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ

english: When crops are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight and soil nutrients, causing them to stretch tall and thin instead of putting energy into growing big cobs.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛkwɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow much faster than my crops right after I put fertilizer on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo miŋmɔ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer feeds all plants in the dirt equally, so if you do not clear the weeds before applying fertilizer, the weeds will eat the food first and choke your crops.
ga: Okɛ niyenii ni falɛ kome pɛ awo tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji ojieee jwɛi lɛ dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ, Jwɛi lɛ baaye nii klɛŋklɛŋ ni ebaafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in cassava is caused by cassava mosaic disease, which is spread from plant to plant by tiny whiteflies that feed on the sap of young leaves.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmei mli lɛ baa ji ŋmei mosaic hela. Agbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmeii yɛji bibii ni yeɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants suddenly dry up and die even when the soil around them is moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ gbɛ́ɔ trukaa ni egboɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli edɔ moŋ?

english: This is often root rot caused by wet soil fungi that destroy the plant's underground roots, stopping water from reaching the stems and leaves above.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishifãi ni fiteɔ enɛ ji, ni ŋmei ko ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ mli ni fiteɔ tsei shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ kɛbaa. Enɛ haa nu nyɛɛɛ ashɛ tsei lɛ ashishi kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ahe.

english: Why does my tomato plant produce plenty of yellow flowers but fails to grow any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo shi ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: If the weather gets too hot or the plant lacks water, the flowers dry up and fall off before bees or wind can pollinate them into tomatoes.
ga: Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo nu bɛ tsei lɛ amli lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi dani ŋmeii loo kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ afee amɛ pollin ni amɛfee tomato.

english: Why are the edges of my plantain leaves turning brown and looking like they were burnt by fire?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ ashishigbɛi lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni etamɔ nɔ ni ashã amɛ lɛ?

english: Brown dry leaf borders usually show that the soil is running low on potassium, an essential plant food that helps plantains handle water and stay healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ potassium faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛji tsei niyenii ni he hiaa ni yeɔ ebuaa plantains ni amɛkwɛɔ nu nɔ ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does cassava planted from my old harvest stem take longer to swell tubers than the new stems from the agricultural officer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ be babaoo dani ŋmeii ni adu kɛjɛɔ tsei momoi amli lɛ shwereɔ fe tsei heei ni jɛ okwaayeli he onukpai adɛŋ lɛ?

english: Old cassava cuttings often carry hidden weakness or disease from past seasons, while improved new varieties are bred specifically to grow strong roots and yield tubers much faster.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, yucca tsei ni afolɔ momo lɛ yɛ bɔjɔmɔi loo helai ni jɛ bei ni eho lɛ amli ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, akwɛɔ tsei srɔtoi heei ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa ni amɛwo ŋmeii oya kwraa.

english: How many times in a year am I supposed to weed my cocoa farm?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli jwɛi yɛ afi mli?

english: Most cocoa farmers weed between two to four times a year. The right frequency for your farm depends on how fast weeds grow under your trees and how well your cocoa trees are producing.
ga: Kokoo okwaafoi babaoo shwieɔ jwɛi shii enyɔ kɛyashi shii ejwɛ yɛ afi mli. Shii abɔ ni sa kɛha oŋmɔ lɛ damɔ bɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya yɛ tsei lɛ ashishi kɛ bɔ ni o-cocoa tsei lɛ woɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What happens to my cocoa crop if I only weed my farm twice a year?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cocoa tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ jwɛi shwie miŋmɔ lɛ mli shii enyɔ pɛ yɛ afi mli?

english: Weeding twice a year can be enough if your cocoa trees have a thick canopy that blocks sunlight. However, if sunlight reaches the ground, weeds will grow fast, steal nutrients, and reduce your overall harvest.
ga: Shii enyɔ yɛ afi mli lɛ, jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ fa kɛji akɛ o-cocoa tso lɛ yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa. Shi, kɛji hulu lɛ shɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, Jwɛi lɛ daa oya, ni ejuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ehaa onibii fɛɛ ni onáa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do some cocoa farmers weed four times a year while others weed only twice?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo okwaafoi komɛi shwieɔ jwɛi shii ejwɛ yɛ afi mli lɛ? yɛ be mli ni mɛi krokomɛi jieɔ jwɛi lɛ shii enyɔ pɛ.

english: Farmers adjust their weeding based on sunlight, rainfall, weed growth speed, and pod production. A farm with high pod yields or sparse tree shade often needs more frequent weeding to maintain good harvests.
ga: Okwaafoi tsakeɔ jwɛi lɛ yɛ hulu la, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, kɛ bɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya lɛ naa. kɛ pod feemɔ Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔji ni pod yibii babaoo yɔɔ mli loo tsei ni bɛ ŋmɔlɔ babaoo lɛ biɔ ni ajie jwɛi shii abɔ koni anyɛ akwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai anɔ.

english: Is it necessary to clear all the weeds under my cocoa trees before harvesting?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni ajie jwɛi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ dani akpa?

english: Yes, clearing weeds around cocoa trees makes harvesting easier, prevents hidden pests like rodents from damaging pods, and keeps fungal diseases like black pod from spreading.
ga: Hɛɛ, jwɛi shwieɔ he fɛɛ he. Cacao tsei haa nikpamɔ feɔ mlɛo. Tsi kooloi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ tamɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ anaa. ni etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai diji lɛ anaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa

english: Does the amount of cocoa my trees produce affect how often I need to weed?
ga: Ani bɔ ni tso ko woɔ kookoo lɛ saa bɔ ni akwɛɔ jwɛi shii abɔ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, when your cocoa trees yield heavily, keeping the ground clean helps protect your pods from pests and diseases, justifying more frequent weeding to support your high production.
ga: Hɛɛ, beni o-cacao tsei lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ. Kɛ́ oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tse lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu o-pods lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kooloi kɛ helai ahe. Enɛ haa jwɛi ni ajieɔ shii abɔ lɛ baa koni eye ebua onibii ni fa babaoo lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow faster under some of my cocoa trees than under others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ kookoo tsei komɛi ashishi fe ekrokomɛi lɛ?

english: Weeds need sunlight to grow. If some of your cocoa trees are young, low-yielding, or have thin leaves, sunlight reaches the ground easily, causing weeds to grow much faster in those areas.
ga: Hulu la he miihia jwɛi koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji akɛ kookoo tsei komɛi yɛ bibii lolo Ewoɔ yibii fioo loo eyɛ baai bibii. Hulu la baanyɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, jwɛi lɛ daa oya kwraa yɛ nakai hei lɛ.

english: How do heavy weeds underneath my cocoa trees hurt my crop's yield?
ga: Te jwɛi ni eyi obɔ kɛ kookoo tsei ashishi lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds take away vital water and soil nutrients that your cocoa trees need to produce healthy pods, which leads to lower yields and weaker tree growth.
ga: Jwɛi jieɔ nu kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa o-cacao tsei lɛ koni amɛfee ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi ni tsei lɛ adalɛ baa shi.

english: How do I know if my cocoa farm needs extra weeding this season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ he miihia ni ajie jwɛi krokomɛi yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: Look at how much sunlight hits the soil and how healthy your cocoa pods look. If weeds are tall enough to compete with lower branches or harbour pests, it is time to clear them.
ga: Kwɛmɔ bɔ ni hulu la lɛ tswaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ehaa kɛ bɔ ni o-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ yɔɔ hewalɛ ha. Kɛji jwɛi lɛ kɛlɛ bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ tsei niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ loo kooloi krokomɛi ni yɔɔ lɛlɛdaamɔhe lɛ baaye akaŋ lɛ, Be eshɛɛ ni esa akɛ ajie nakai jwɛi lɛ.

english: Can mature, high-yielding cocoa trees naturally help control weed growth?
ga: Ani kookoo tsei ni edara ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ekwɛ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa?

english: Yes, mature cocoa trees with thick leaves create dense shade on the farm floor. This shade naturally prevents sunlight from reaching the ground, stopping weeds from growing quickly.
ga: Hɛɛ, kookoo tsei ni edara ni baai etsilɛi feɔ hulutsoo waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔlɔ nɛɛ baatsi hulu la naa koni ekashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ oya

english: Should every cocoa farmer follow the exact same weeding schedule?
ga: Ani esa akɛ kookoo okwaafoi fɛɛ anyiɛ jwɛi ŋmɔmɔ he gbɛjianɔtoo kome sɛɛ?

english: No, every farm is different. Your weeding schedule should be based on your specific farm conditions, such as the age of your trees, shade levels, weed growth, and how well your cocoa is yielding.
ga: Dabi, esoro ŋmɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔ. Esa akɛ ogbɛjianɔtoo ni okɛbaakpa jwɛi lɛ adamɔ shihilɛ pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ, tamɔ tso lɛ afii, shade, kɛ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ. Ni te o-cocoa yibiiwoo lɛ hi ha tɛŋŋ?

english: Why should I clear away fallen leaves and dead cocoa pods from around the bases of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie baai ni egbee shi kɛ kookoo tsei ni egboi lɛ kɛjɛ mikookoo tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Clearing farm debris and diseased pods removes hiding places for pests like mealybugs and stops fungal spores, such as black pod disease, from spreading through rain splashes to healthy trees.
ga: Okwaafoi amli jwɛi kɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ hei ni ŋmeii tamɔ mealybugs lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ ni ekpaa fungal spores tamɔ black pod hela lɛ gbɛ koni amɛkatsɔ nugbɔshiimɔi anɔ amɛgbɛ amɛshwã tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Can I reuse cocoa pod husks after harvesting instead of leaving them to rot in the field?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ atsu nii ekoŋŋ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbo yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Yes, cocoa pod husks can be processed into organic compost manure, turned into animal feed, or burned to extract potash for local soap making instead of wasting them.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ atsake kookoo pod lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli. tsakeɔ kɛyaa kooloi aniyenii nɔ loo ashãa koni ajie potash sũ ni akɛfeɔ maŋ lɛ mli samla. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite lɛ

english: Is it better to burn farm clearings or leave them to rot in the soil?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ abaashã shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ loo abaaha egbo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Leaving clearings to rot into compost adds natural organic matter back into your soil, whereas burning destroys helpful soil organisms and dries out the topsoil.
ga: Kɛ́ oŋmɛ gbɛ ni hei ni agbele lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ebaaha adebɔɔ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ. Yɛ be mli ni shãa lɛ kpataa shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ahiɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gĩɔ lɛ.

english: What happens if I cover the soil around my crops with dry leaves and farm waste?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ mulch wo he ni ebɔle ehe lɛ? Nibii ni aduɔ ni baai egbi kɛ ŋmɔ mli jwɛi?

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves, called mulching, keeps the soil moist during hot weather, prevents weeds from growing, and adds nutrients back into the dirt as it decays.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ baai ni egbi haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli beni efiteɔ lɛ

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees turn brown and dry during the sunny season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves burn under direct sunlight because their roots cannot pull enough water yet, which is why planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains nearby keeps them cool and protected.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ baashã yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ agbala nu ni fa bɔ ni sa lolo. Nɔ hewɔ ni shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa amɛhe jɔɔ ni abuɔ amɛhe lɛ.

english: Why is it bad to leave sickly or black pods hanging on my cocoa branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji nɔ fɔŋ akɛ mashi helatsɛmɛi loo ŋmeii diji yɛ mi-kookoo niji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Sickly pods carry fungal diseases that easily travel through rain drops and wind to attack good pods, reducing your harvest quality if you do not remove them early.
ga: Pods ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tsɔɔ ŋmeii kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya koni amɛyatutua pods ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, kɛ́ ojieee amɛ mra lɛ, okpamɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Pruning extra branches opens up the tree canopy so sunlight and air can flow through, which lowers moisture levels that cause mold and helps the tree focus energy on growing cocoa pods.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei krokomɛi ni afoɔ lɛ gbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Enɛ haa hulutsoo ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ baa shi. ni ehaa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ahe nii.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds in a ring around the base of each crop plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ajie jwɛi lɛ yɛ kooyigbɛ ni abɔle tso fɛɛ tso shishi lɛ he lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and plant food directly from the crop's feeding roots, so clearing space around each plant ensures it gets full nourishment.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ tso niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi ni yeɔ niyenii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, he ni ebɔle he lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ Abaanyɛ ana nɔmimaa akɛ tso fɛɛ tso baaná niyenii ni yeɔ emuu.

english: Where exactly around my crop plant should I place fertilizer?
ga: Nɛgbɛ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mitsei lɛ ahe?

english: Fertilizer should be placed in a circle beneath the outer edge of the crop's leaves where active feeding roots absorb it, rather than against the main stem where it can burn the trunk.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo tso lɛ baai lɛ kponɔgbɛ shishi yɛ he ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baaŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ lɛ. Mohu ɔ, mo ngɔ kɛ fɔ tso ngua a nɔ he nɛ e ma nyɛ maa sã tso ɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow better when I plant different types together on the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ tsei babaoo wo ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Mixing crops allows them to share farm space efficiently, as different plants feed at different soil depths, reduce soil erosion, and break pest lifecycles.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ haa amɛjaa ŋmɔ mli hei jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei srɔtoi naa niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ srɔtoi. Ha shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aba shi ni ofite kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ashihilɛ

english: Why do some farmers plant plantain suckers at an angle instead of planting them straight up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ plantain tsei lɛ yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛduɔ amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Planting plantain suckers at an angle encourages deeper root development and better stability, helping the plant absorb more nutrients from the ground to grow big and strong.
ga: Kɛ́ adu plantains lɛ yɛ koŋ nɔ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛheɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa.

english: Does changing the way I plant my plantains really make a difference in how big they grow?
ga: Ani gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ plantain lɛ tsakemɔ lɛ saa plantain lɛ dalɛ he diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, using proper planting orientation and depth allows roots to easily spread and capture the strength in the soil, leading to healthier plants and larger fruits.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ akɛ gbɛ ni ja kɛ dumɔ mlibotemɔ tsu nii lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ shishifãi lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛná hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ kɛ aduawai wuji.

english: When my plantains are ready, should I harvest everything or leave some plants behind?
ga: Beni ofee klalo lɛ Ani esa akɛ makpa nɔ fɛɛ nɔ loo mashi tsei komɛi?

english: You should harvest the mature fruit stem but leave healthy young shoots (suckers) growing at the base so your farm can continue producing food and income for the future.
ga: Esa akɛ okpa aduawai lɛ ahe tsei ni edara lɛ. Shi shi ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ (ŋmeii) ni miida yɛ shishigbɛ. Bɔni afee ni oŋmɔ lɛ aya nɔ ekɛ niyenii kɛ shika aba wɔsɛɛ.

english: Why do experienced farmers leave some plantain shoots behind instead of clearing the whole stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ shiɔ plantain lɛ yɛ amɛsɛɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaafɔ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ he lɛ?

english: Leaving strong follower shoots ensures continuous life for your farm without the cost and effort of buying new suckers and replanting from scratch.
ga: Nibii ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ ni he wa lɛ ni oooŋmɛɛ ohe lɛ haa oŋmɔ lɛ yaa nɔ ehiɔ shi ni shika kɛ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ ni akɛheɔ tsei heei ni aduɔ kɛjɛɔ shishijee lɛ fataaa he.

english: How can I make sure my plantain farm keeps producing good harvests as it grows older?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ koni mi-plantain ŋmɔ lɛ aya nɔ awo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai be mli ni edaa lɛ?

english: You can sustain your farm by pruning unwanted extra shoots, returning organic crop waste back to the soil, and allowing only one or two strong suckers to replace harvested trees.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛtsɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni ataooo lɛ ni oookpa lɛ nɔ. Okɛ tsei ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ aku sɛɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni oha ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aye tsei ni akpa lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why is my soil not producing big crops like it used to years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo ŋmɔshi nibii wuji tamɔ afii ni eho lɛ?

english: Continuous farming without replenishing the land drains the soil's natural strength over time, which reduces crop yields unless organic matter or fertilizer is added back.
ga: Okwaayeli ni aya nɔ ni awooo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ aba shi yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ aba shi. Ja akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii efata he ekoŋŋ.

english: What does it mean when people say the strength of the land is in the ground?
ga: Kɛ́ mɔ ko kɛɛ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, mɛni etsɔɔ?

english: It means plant health depends directly on the rich nutrients stored within the topsoil, which roots feed on to nourish the entire plant.
ga: Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ hewalɛnamɔ lɛ damɔ niyenii kpakpai ni buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. ni shishifãi lɛ yeɔ koni ekɛha tso muu lɛ fɛɛ niyenii

english: How do I know if the strength in my farmland is fading?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ he ni mitsuɔ nii yɛ lɛ hewalɛ miiba shi?

english: If your plants take longer to grow, look weak, and yield smaller fruits than in previous seasons, it means your soil nutrients are getting exhausted.
ga: Kɛji akɛ otsei lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛdaraa lɛ, kwɛmɔ akɛ amɛhe waaa ni amɛwoɔ yibii bibii fe nyɛsɛɛ be lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ miiho.

english: What makes plantain trees produce very big fruits while others stay small?
ga: Mɛni haa plantains woɔ yibii wuji waa yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ woɔ yibii bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Big plantain fruits come from planting in nutrient-rich soil, giving the roots enough room, and keeping only a few shoots per stand so all energy goes into the main fruit.
ga: Plantains wuji lɛ jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ mli. Ha gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa aha shishifãi lɛ. Ni okɛ ŋmeii fioo pɛ ato shidaamɔhe fɛɛ shidaamɔ he bɔni afee ni hewalɛ fɛɛ aya aduawai titri lɛ amli.

english: Planting plantains too close forces them to compete for sunlight, space, and soil strength, which leads to weak stems and smaller bunches.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛ shiɔ akaŋ kɛha hulu la, ŋwɛi kɛ shikpɔŋ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa tsei akui ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ jwɛi bibii baa.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight. Plantain trees grow quickly and provide tall, broad leaves that create protective shade and keep the soil moist while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai kakadaji ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo lɛ ŋmɛɔ ehe shi lɛ.

english: This is usually caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads in wet and cool weather. Clearing heavy shade and pruning branches lets air flow and reduces the moisture the fungus needs to spread.
ga: ni bei pii lɛ, black pod hela kɛbaa Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ hulutsoo be kɛ fɛ̃i be mli. Ni ajieɔ hulutsoo be ni mli ewo muji lɛ mli Ni ajieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ ni ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ agbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plant turning yellow during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, a key food crop plants need to stay green and grow well. Applying organic manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps restore healthy leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛɛmɛi ji niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa, ni esa akɛ amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: What is eating holes in the middle of my young maize leaves overnight?
ga: Mɛni oyeɔ ni haa bu ko shwieɔ ŋmãa bibioo ko teŋ nyɔɔŋ kome?

english: This damage is often caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide in the center whorl of young corn plants. Catching them early and spraying recommended bio-pesticides or neem leaf water protects your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋtayaai amli lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem baa mli nu ni atsɔɔ akɛ amɛshwie nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Which direction should I push cassava stems into the ground when planting?
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esa akɛ ashɛre ŋmei tso lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Plant cassava stems either slanted or upright with the small growth buds along the stem pointing upward toward the sky. Planting them upside down stops the plant from growing correctly.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ daa ni amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ loo amɛtsi amɛhe, ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ tso lɛ da ni etsɔ ŋwɛi lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekada jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to make food and grow large tubers underground. Staking lifts leaves off the hot ground, allowing them to catch sunshine and avoid soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Elevator lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ he ni edɔ lɛ. Okɛ amɛ awo hulu la mli ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas take nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in their roots. When the plant roots rot in the soil, they release natural fertilizer that feeds the crop planted there next.
ga: Akpɔlɔi kɛ tsina ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛmɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsei shishifãi fite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Amɛjieɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii koni akɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa nɔ lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow tall with lots of leaves but produce very few fruits after I fertilize them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi ewoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer makes plants put all their energy into leaf growth instead of flowers and fruits. Using balanced fertilizers rich in phosphorus encourages blooming and fruit production.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ afite ehewalɛ fɛɛ yɛ baai ni miida lɛ he moŋ fe fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja ni fɔsfɔs babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha fɔfɔi kɛ yibii aba.

english: How do I know if the soil has enough moisture to plant my seeds after the first rain of the season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu midumɔwui lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Squeeze a handful of soil into a ball; if it holds together without dripping water or crumbling away easily, it is ready. Planting after just one light rain can cause seeds to sprout and then die if dry weather returns.
ga: Mimɔ shikpɔŋ sũ fioo ko mli ni ofee bɔɔlu. Kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛ he ni nu shwieee shi loo egbeee shi oya lɛ, no lɛ efee klalo. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Saramɔ kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally suited to quick growth and quickly soak up surface water and nutrients. Weeding early prevents these wild plants from stealing food away from your growing crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni nyɛɔ amɛdaraa oya ni amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaatsi nɛkɛ koo mli tsei nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkaju niyenii kɛjɛ tsei ni oduɔ lɛ amli.

english: Why are many farmers in Ghana starting to grow sweet potatoes instead of relying only on traditional crops like cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi babaoo ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ amɛhe aaafɔ̃ blema ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei pɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Sweet potatoes mature much faster—usually within 3 to 4 months compared to cassava's 12 months. They require less rainfall, have strong market demand due to their high nutritional value, and allow farmers to harvest multiple times in a single year.
ga: Atomɔ baakwɛ̃ oya kwraa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4, ni akɛtoɔ nyɔji 12 he kɛha ŋmei. Amɛbiɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo. Eyɛ jarayeli nibii ni ataoɔ waa yɛ niyenii ni mli wa ni eyɔɔ lɛ hewɔ. ni ehaa okwaafoi kpaɔ nii shii abɔ yɛ afi kome mli.

english: How can I tell if a new crop variety being introduced in my district will actually make money for my household?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tso henɔ hee ko ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ baaha mishia lɛ aná shika diɛŋtsɛ?

english: A profitable new crop variety typically has high yield potential, matures quickly to reduce field risk, fits your local climate, and has an established buyer market or processing factory nearby before you start planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo. Eda oya koni oshara ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi. Ehi kɛha kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ. Ni oná jarayelɔ loo nitsumɔhe ko ni ato he gbɛjianɔ ni bɛŋkɛ bo dani obɔi dumɔwui.

english: Why do my potato tubers turn green if they sit uncovered on top of the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-potato tubers lɛ feɔ eŋɔli kɛji akɛ awooo amɛ mulch lɛ?

english: When potato tubers are exposed to direct sunlight, they produce chlorophyll for photosynthesis along with a natural chemical called solanine. Covering exposed roots with loose soil—a practice called hilling—keeps them safe and edible.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ Ejieɔ klorofil kɛha fotosintɛsis kɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofa ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ solanine. Kɛ́ akɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ha shishifãi ni eje kpo lɛ ahe—nifeemɔ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii—eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ ahiɔ shi shweshweeshwe ni ayeɔ.

english: Why are my root crops growing big leaves above ground but producing very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishishifãi lɛ yɛ baai wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi bulbs bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Giving plants too much nitrogen fertilizer causes them to use all their energy growing tall stems and bushy leaves instead of building tubers. Root crops need balanced nutrients with higher potassium and phosphorus to grow large tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen babaoo ha tsei lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛkwɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ moŋ fe ni eeefee bulbs. Shishifãi ni aduɔ lɛ biɔ niyenii ni ja ni potassium kɛ phosphorus babaoo yɔɔ mli koni amɛnyɛ amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do different varieties of potatoes spoil at different speeds after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi fiteɔ yɛ oyaiyeli srɔtoi amli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Potato varieties have different moisture, starch, and skin thickness levels. Varieties with softer skins or higher moisture retain more heat and rot faster if kept in warm, unventilated spaces, whereas high-starch varieties store longer in cool, dark conditions.
ga: Atomɔ henɔi lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ hewolo nɔ ŋmɔtɔ srɔtoi. Henɔi ni hewolo lɛ yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ loo hulutsoo be babaoo lɛ baahiɛ dɔlɛ babaoo mli ni amɛbaafite oya kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, starch henɔi ni fa babaoo lɛ baahi shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ ni duŋ yɔɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants drop their flowers or fail to form full cobs when the afternoon weather gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi loo amɛmiikwɛɛɛ kwraa beni shwane mli kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry air dry out the sticky silks on maize ears before pollen can fertilize them. Without fertilization, kernels cannot develop, leaving missing gaps on the corn cob.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ haa siliki ni shwieɔ ŋmãa toi lɛ anɔ lɛ gĩɔ dani ŋmãa lɛ baanyɛ afee amɛ fɔmɔ nii. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ lɛ Abele dumɔwui lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ̃. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni elaaje yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ baa.

english: What makes cassava leaves turn yellow and drop off during the dry season, and will the crop die?
ga: Mɛni haa cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli? Ni ani ŋmɔshi nii lɛ baagbo?

english: Cassava naturally sheds its leaves during dry periods to conserve water and survive drought. The plant is not dead; as soon as the rains return, it rapidly produces fresh leaves and continues growing.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hɔmɔ be mli koni ekɛhiɛ nu mli ni ehi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Beni nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ nɛ lɛ, oya nɔŋŋ ni ekwɛ baai heei ni etee nɔ eda.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up tightly during the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling during intense afternoon sun is a defense mechanism plants use to reduce the leaf surface exposed to heat and prevent excessive water loss. If they uncurl by evening, the plant is managing stress, but if they stay curled, they need water.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ ji gbɛ ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛba baa lɛ nɔ hulutsoo shi ni amɛtsi nu ni shwieɔ shi fe nine lɛ naa. Kɛji amɛkoto gbɛkɛ mli lɛ Tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ kɛ nɔnyɛɛ miikpe. Shi kɛji amɛku amɛhe lɛ Nu hu he miihia amɛ.

english: Why should I rotate my grain field with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsake ŋmaa ŋmɔji kɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ?

english: Grain crops like maize feed heavily on nitrogen in the soil. Legume crops like cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots, restoring fertility naturally for your next crop.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa mli tamɔ ŋmãa yeɔ nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Koni okɛ adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ aba ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: If I plant my seeds very close together to save space, how does it affect my final yield?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa koni mikɛha he ko akafee nɔ ko hu? Te ebaaná mi naagbee nibii lɛ anɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Planting too closely forces crops to compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak stems and small fruit or tubers, leading to a lower total harvest than properly spaced plants.
ga: Kɛ́ adu amɛ kɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ aduawai bibii loo ŋmeii baa. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, yibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ baafee nɔ ni baa shi fe tsei ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ.

english: Is it possible to get a heavy maize harvest without buying chemical fertilizer from the market?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ akpa ŋmãa babaoo ni aheee tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ kɛjɛɛɛ jara nɔ?

english: Yes, preparing and applying organic compost made from plant waste and animal manure feeds the soil naturally, helping you achieve high maize yields without needing expensive chemical fertilizers.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ tsei amli ŋmɔji kɛ kooloi aŋmɔji fee lɛ ahe saamɔ kɛ nitsumɔ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni onáa ŋmãa babaoo ni okɛ tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ tsuuu nii.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow even after applying chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji akɛ akɛ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ po?

english: Using wrong or excessive chemical fertilizers can burn plant roots, disturb soil nutrients, and stress the crop, which causes leaves to yellow instead of staying green and healthy.
ga: Tsofai ni ejaaa loo ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ ashishifãi ashã. Egbaa niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ naa ni ekɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛhiɛ hewalɛ.

english: What should I add to my soil before planting maize to help it grow strong?
ga: Dani abaadu ŋmãa lɛ, mɛni esa akɛ akɛfata he koni eye ebua ni ewaje shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Adding well-rotted compost or manure into the soil before planting gives young seeds natural nutrients and helps the soil hold moisture better during dry spells.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani adu lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui bibii lɛ aná adebɔɔ mli niyenii. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli

english: Can the store-bought sprays I put on my crops actually end up causing diseases?
ga: Ani tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ ni miheɔ yɛ shwapo mli lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ hela aba?

english: Yes, overusing or misusing harsh chemical sprays can destroy beneficial soil organisms and weaken the plant's natural defenses, making crops more vulnerable to diseases.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni mli wa ni akɛshwieɔ shi fe nine loo ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛ fɔŋ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ akpata shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ahiɛ. ni ehaa tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu nibii lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii nyɛɔ helai.

english: How can I protect my crops from sickness without using chemical sprays?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ hela he ni mikɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nibii anɔ lɛ tsuuu nii?

english: You can protect crops naturally by feeding the soil with well-prepared compost to build strong plant immunity, and using natural mixtures like neem leaf extract to deter pests.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni asaa he jogbaŋŋ ni okɛaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ koni eha tsei lɛ ahewalɛ ni tsiɔ hela naa lɛ ama shi lɛ nɔ. ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii tamɔ neem baa mli nu tsuɔ nii Koni ekɛtsi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa

english: Why do crops on neighboring farms look healthy while mine keep catching diseases?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ mli lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ be mli ni minɔ lɛ mli hela lɛ emɔ mi lolo lɛ?

english: Crops usually fall sick when soil nutrients are unbalanced or when harsh chemicals disrupt the farm environment; plants grown in balanced, naturally nourished soil are much tougher against sickness.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei yeɔ hela kɛ́ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ bɛ shiŋŋ loo kɛ́ tsofai ni mli wa gba ŋmɔ lɛ mli shihilɛ lɛ naa. Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ja ni nine shɛɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii mli hewalɛ nɔ lɛ nyɛɔ helai anaa kwraa.

english: How do I make my own natural fertilizer at home for my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ shia?

english: You can gather plant leaves, farm waste, kitchen scraps, and livestock dung into a pile, keep it moist, and let it decay into rich natural compost that safely feeds your crops.
ga: Obaanyɛ obua tsei ahe baai, ŋmɔ mli jwɛi, shĩa mli jwɛi. kɛ kooloi ashishifãi ni abua naa Kwɛmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni oha efite shweshweeshwe ni etsɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔtɔ ni jara wa ni okɛha onibii lɛ niyenii.

english: What makes maize grains turn out full, heavy, and high quality after harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmãa yibii eyiɔ obɔ, etsii, ni ehi jogbaŋŋ yɛ kpamɔɔ sɛɛ?

english: High-quality maize comes from plants that receive steady organic nutrients and moisture from rich soil throughout their growth without suffering chemical burns.
ga: Abɛi ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ jɛɔ tsei ni naa niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ be fɛɛ be kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni fa babaoo yɛ amɛdalɛ be fɛɛ mli ni tsofai shãaa amɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why do my maize plants produce tiny cobs even when the stalks grow very tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ miiwo ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ kwɔ waa moŋ

english: Tall stalks with small cobs often happen when a plant gets too much quick nitrogen from chemicals but lacks the balanced organic nourishment needed to form large, full grains.
ga: Tso lɛ kwɔ ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii. Bei pii lɛ, ebaa kɛji tsei lɛ ná nitrogen oya tsɔ kɛjɛ tsofai amli. Shi ebɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa ni he hiaa koni ekɛwo dumɔwui wuji ni eyi obɔ lɛ.

english: Why does food grown with natural compost taste better and last longer than chemically sprayed crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niyenii ni akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii duɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ ni ehiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ fe tsei ni akɛ tsofai shwieɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Natural compost nourishes the plant slowly with balanced nutrients, producing sturdy, chemical-free crops that store better and maintain natural flavor.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii haa tsei lɛ hewalɛ fiofio. kɛ niyenii ni ja Ha tsei lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ Tsofai bɛ mli Enɛ hiɛɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔlɔ lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen. Maize plants need nitrogen to stay green and produce big cobs, so applying well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer will restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ewo ŋmeii wuji. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ kooloi aŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha amɛfee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is my cowpea crop growing plenty of green leaves but producing very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen, cowpea plants spend all their energy making leaves instead of flowers. Cowpeas naturally make their own nitrogen, so adding extra nitrogen causes them to produce leafy foliage instead of food pods.
ga: When the soil has too much nitrogen Cowpea plants use all of their energy to create leaves instead of flowers. Cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ adebɔɔ mli. Therefore, adding additional nitrogen will cause the peas to produce leaves instead of food pods.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects and stays around them for too long. Cassava needs loose, well-draining soil so the roots can breathe and avoid fungal diseases caused by standing water.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa ni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ he miihia Cassava. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ muɔ ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni nu ni ekã shi lɛ kɛbaa lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my yam tubers crack open under the soil before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miigba yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani akpa lɛ?

english: Yam tubers crack when water levels change suddenly. A long dry period followed by heavy rainfall makes the inside of the tuber expand faster than its outer skin can stretch.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baatswa kɛji nu lɛ mli tsake trukaa. Hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ mli lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they suffer from prolonged dry weather, nutrient lack, or insect attacks. Keeping the tree base covered with organic mulch helps keep the soil moist so flowers stay on the branch.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli, niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa, loo kooloi bibii tutua amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tsuɔ nii yɛ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni fɔfɔii lɛ akpɛtɛ tsei lɛ aniji ahe.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their green fruits before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho aduawai eŋɔli dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop young fruit when the weather becomes too hot or when soil moisture jumps suddenly from very dry to very wet. Regular, balanced watering helps the plant hold onto its fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛyibii bibii lɛ anɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tee hiɛ trukaa kɛjɛ he ni egbi waa kɛtee he ni edɔ waa lɛ nɔ. Nu ni afɔɔ ashwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa ni ja lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehiɛɔ yibii.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my young maize leaves and green dirt inside the center leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu ni etse kɛ muji eŋɔli yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which burrows inside the tender center of young maize to feed. Removing them early or applying safe biological control saves the growing shoot.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli koni amɛtao niyenii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ajieɔ mra Aloo, kɛ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling tightly upward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Tight leaf curling is often a sign of heat stress or tiny whitefly insects transmitting a leaf curl virus. Providing light shade and keeping sap-sucking insects away keeps tomato leaves healthy.
