ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni etsilɛ waa lɛ ji dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ he okadi. ni gbɛɔ leaf curl virus lɛ eshwaa Shade ni mli tse kɛ hebuu kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tomato baa lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do wild weeds grow back much faster than my planted crops after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ yɛ nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild native plants that adapt easily and drink up water and soil food faster than farmed crops. Clearing weeds while they are small prevents them from robbing your crops of light and nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni tsakeɔ amɛhe oya ni amɛnuɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛ́ agbe jwɛi lɛ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli.

english: Plantains have shallow roots that can be destroyed by tiny soil worms called nematodes. Using clean, healthy suckers and propping heavy trees with strong wooden stakes stops them from uprooting.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii bibii baanyɛ akpata amɛhiɛ. ni atsɛɔ lɛ nematodes Akɛ ŋmei tsei ni he tse ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ tsei ni tsii ni fiɔ sɛɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii Kɛ tso ni wa Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛtsi enaa koni ekaje shishi.

english: When lower maize leaves turn yellow starting from the leaf tips in a V-shape, it usually means the plant lacks nitrogen. Adding fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure gives the plant the nutrients it needs to stay green.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ ashishigbɛ fãi lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ, ni ejeɔ shishi kɛ V-su yɛ amɛnaagbee lɛ, bei pii lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli.

english: What is causing small holes in my maize leaves and caterpillars hiding inside the center of the plant?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworms. They hide in the leaf funnel during the day to feed; catching them early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extract helps protect your harvest.
ga: Fall Armyworms ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai amli lasu tsuji amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛyatao niyenii. Mɔ amɛ mra. Ni kɛ́ okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni atsɔɔ akɛ amɛtsu nii loo neem mli nu lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Planting maize continuously in the same spot drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases to multiply. Alternating with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome be fɛɛ be lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai baa shi Enyɛɔ eshwereɔ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the soil for too long, especially in heavy rainfall areas. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the tubers stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Titri lɛ, yɛ hei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ lɛ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni yitso lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Yam vines need to reach high into the air to catch enough sunlight to produce food. Staking keeps the leaves off the hot ground and fully exposed to light, which directly helps the underground tubers grow bigger.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ahi kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaaye niyenii. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ waa yɛ, ni hulu lɛ hu baashɛ he fɛɛ he. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high, when the soil dries out completely, or if the soil lacks phosphorus. Regular watering and keeping the soil moist helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo kɛji akɛ fɔsfɔs bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from under the leaves. Spraying with neem oil or soapy water solution helps control these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo nu ni akɛ samla shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: How does putting dry grass around the base of my crops help them survive dry weather?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he fɛɛ he Te miŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil around your crops with dry grass, known as mulching, blocks direct sunlight. This keeps the soil cool and stops water from evaporating quickly, helping roots stay moist longer.
ga: Mulching around Okɛ jwɛi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ aha oŋmɔshi nibii ahe. Ebaaye ebua ni etsi hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and tall without yield when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛkwɛɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they shade each other and compete for sunlight, ground water, and soil food. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room to grow strong and yield well.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii he. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha dalɛ kpakpa kɛ yibii kpakpai.

english: Is it safe for me to buy crop seedlings from vendors selling by the roadside?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mahe tsei ahe dumɔwui kɛjɛ gbɛjegbɛ nɔ jarayelɔi adɛŋ?

english: Roadside seedlings often come from uncertified sources, meaning they might carry hidden diseases or produce low yields. It is safer to buy certified seedlings from approved agricultural officers or recognized research institutes so you know exactly what variety you are planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, gbɛjegbɛ he dumɔwui lɛ jɛɔ hei ni anyɛɛɛ ama nɔ mi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ekolɛ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ loo yibiiwoo ni baa shi. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooohe dumɔwui ni awo he hewalɛ kɛjɛ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko ni akpɛlɛ enɔ loo niiamlitaomɔ he ko ni akpɛlɛɔ nɔ lɛ dɛŋ. No hewɔ lɛ ole tso srɔtoi ni oduɔ lɛ.

english: My brother told me there is big profit in planting oil palm, so should I clear my farm and plant it too?
ga: Minyɛmi nuu lɛ kɛɛ akɛ, mu tsei ni aduɔ lɛ ji sɛɛnamɔ kpele. Ani esa akɛ majie ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni madu hu?

english: A crop that yields profit on one person's land might fail on yours because of differences in soil type, rainfall, and local climate. Before changing your crops based on trends, you need to check if your land's soil and weather support that specific crop.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he yɛ mɔ kome shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ afite yɛ srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ henɔ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ maŋ lɛ mli kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ahewɔ. Dani obaatsake ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ bɔ ni yaa nɔ ehaa lɛ naa Esa akɛ okwɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ asɛɛ.

english: Why do some crops grow very well in one region of Ghana but fail completely when I plant them in my area?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ waa yɛ Ghana kpokpaa ko nɔ shi amɛfiteɔ kwraa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Crops have specific natural requirements for rainfall, temperature, and soil conditions. For example, crops adapted to the wet forest zone will struggle in drier areas because their roots and leaves are built for high humidity and consistent water.
ga: Tsei yɛ adebɔɔ mli hiamɔ nii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛha nugbɔshiimɔ, latsaa kɛ shikpɔŋ shihilɛ. Akɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsake amɛhe amɛwo kooi ni mli efɔ lɛ amli lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ waa yɛ hei ni nu bɛ lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, abɔ eshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ koni amɛha hulutsoo babaoo kɛ nu ni yaa nɔ daa.

english: Why are my maize plants growing very tall with deep green leaves but failing to produce any cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni tsuɔ waa shi enyɛɛɛ ewo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: When crops get too much nitrogen fertilizer, they focus all their energy on growing tall leaves and stems instead of producing flowers and fruit. Plants need a balanced mix of nutrients and adequate water at the right stage to produce cobs.
ga: Kɛ tsei nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ maa baai kakadaji kɛ ŋmeii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ yiblii. Niyenii ni ja kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa he miihia tsei yɛ be ni sa mli koni amɛwo cob.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up and turn yellow during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl during extreme heat as a natural reaction to conserve moisture and protect themselves from heat stress. However, it can also be a sign of tiny pests like mites that attack crops when conditions are hot and dry.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. Shi kɛlɛ, ebaanyɛ efee okadi hu ni tsɔɔ kooloi bibii, tamɔ ŋmeii, ni tutuaa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji shihilɛi lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ.

english: Will a mango tree grown directly from a seed produce fruit as fast as a grafted mango seedling?
ga: Ani mango tso ni adu kɛjɛ dumɔwui amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baawo yibii oya tamɔ mango tso ni akɛwo tso mli lɛ?

english: Grafted seedlings mature much faster and usually bear fruit within 2 to 3 years because the branch used comes from a mature tree. Trees planted directly from seeds can take 5 to 7 years to fruit and may not taste as good as the parent tree.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛwo tso mli lɛ daa oya kwraa ni bei pii lɛ ewoɔ yibii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli ejaakɛ niji ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ jɛɔ tso ni eda mli. Tsei ni adu kɛjɛ dumɔwui amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahé afii 5 kɛyashi 7 dani amɛwo yibii, ni ekolɛ amɛmli ŋɔɔmɔ bɛ tamɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ.

english: Can I plant cassava and maize together on the same field without them stealing nutrients from each other?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni mikɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ he akaŋ akaŋ?

english: Yes, cassava and maize work well together because maize grows quickly and is harvested in a few months, while cassava grows slowly at first and matures much later, allowing both crops to share the land without heavy competition.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei daa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli ni sɛɛ mli lɛ edaa lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei enyɔ lɛ jaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni akaŋshii ni naa wa bɛ mli.

english: If I add double the amount of fertilizer to my land, will my crop yields also double?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ toi enyɔ Ani miŋmɔshi nibii hu baawo toi enyɔ?

english: No, putting too much fertilizer can burn plant roots, pollute the soil, and damage crop growth. Plants can only absorb a specific amount of nutrients at a time, so extra fertilizer is wasted and can harm your farm.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo baanyɛ ashã tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ. Mujiwoo ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ebaanyɛ efite tsei adalɛ Tsei baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii kpakpai fioo ko pɛ yɛ be kome mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa fe nine lɛ fiteɔ ni ebaanyɛ eye oŋmɔ lɛ awui.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants developing dark spots and dying starting from the bottom leaves upward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by a fungal disease that lives in the soil and splashes onto lower leaves during rainfall. Spacing plants properly and removing lower leaves helps air flow through the farm and stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni shwieɔ baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa kɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaye abua ni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ebaatsi ŋmei lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa.

english: Why does my land yield smaller harvests every year even though I plant the exact same crop on it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ moŋ?

english: Planting the exact same crop every season drains the exact same nutrients from the soil over and over while allowing specific pests to build up. Rotating your crop with legumes like cowpeas helps put nutrients back into the soil naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ be fɛɛ be ni Seasons lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shii abɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi buaa amɛhe naa. Nibii ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa tsakeɔ lɛ haa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Young cocoa plants have shallow root systems and delicate leaves that burn under direct, harsh sunlight. Plantain trees or shade trees act like natural umbrellas, keeping the air cool and soil moist so the young cocoa can survive its first two years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa shishi. Dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɛlɛtswai. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ hiɔ shi klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a clear sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is main food plants need to grow. When nitrogen is low, the maize plant starves its older bottom leaves to send the remaining food to the growing leaves at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ Kɛji nitrogen lɛ faaa Abele lɛ hɔmɔ yeɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi lɛ koni ekɛ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ amaje baai ni miida yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing tall with huge bushy leaves but giving me very small roots underground at harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai wuji shi ewoɔ shishifãi bibii waa kɛ́ akpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or lacks potassium, the cassava plant directs all its energy into growing big stems and leaves above ground instead of storing starch in the tubers underground.
ga: When the soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or lacks potassium. The cassava plant uses all of its energy to grow large trunks and leaves above the ground. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ ashikishaŋ lɛ baato ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ,.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture changes suddenly from dry to wet. Heat stress stops flower pollination, causing the plant to drop blossoms to conserve its water and energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ. Dɔlɛ haomɔ haa fɔfɔii lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpaa. Ha tsei afee fɔfɔi koni akɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and weak with small cobs when I put many seeds into one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni akɛ dumɔwui babaoo woɔ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Crowding plants forces them to compete closely for sunlight, soil food, and water. Instead of building strong stems and big ears, the crowded maize stretches tall and thin just to reach sunlight.
ga: Tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye akaŋ waa kɛha hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ nu, yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafee tsei ni wa kɛ toi wuji. Abɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baaku esɛɛ eda ni etsɔ shɔŋŋ ni efee bibioo koni enyɛ emɔ hulu la lɛ kɛkɛ.

english: Why do the inner leaves of my young maize plants look chewed up with tiny dark dirt inside the center fold?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ amli baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ashɛre ni muji bibii ni tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ? Yɛ teŋgbɛ fã lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which crawls into the deep center (funnel) of young maize during the day to hide from heat and eat the soft growing leaves before they unfold.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ (cones) ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛyatee amɛhe kɛjɛ latsaa lɛ he ni amɛye baai bibii lɛ dani amɛje kpo.

english: Why do I need to place tall wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on instead of leaving them on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama shi koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yam vines need to reach high into the sunlight to capture light and produce the energy required to swell tubers underground. Staking also keeps leaves off hot, moist soil, protecting them from fungal diseases.
ga: Hulu la ni fa babaoo he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛmɔmɔ la ni amɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛha ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ. Ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up inward during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ miihoso kɛmiiya mli yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism. By rolling its leaves, the plant reduces the leaf surface area exposed to direct heat, preventing water from evaporating out of the leaves too quickly.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. by rolling leaves Plants reduce the surface area of ​​their leaves exposed to direct heat. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekajɛ baai lɛ amli oya tsɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I spread dry fertilizer on my farm when the ground is completely dry and dusty?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmeii ni egbi shwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa ni sũ ebɔle he lɛ?

english: Fertilizers must dissolve in soil water before plant roots can drink them in. Applying dry fertilizer on parched soil leaves the salts sitting directly against roots, which can burn the roots and waste your money.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ mli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ anu. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli lɛ, ehaa ŋmei kpɛtɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ ashã shishifãi lɛ ni efite shika.

english: Weeds have faster-growing, aggressive root systems that steal essential nutrients and fertilizer out of the soil before your crops can reach them, leaving your crops starving despite receiving water.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni amɛfeɔ basabasa. Enɛ juɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baashɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye onibii lɛ kɛji amɛná nu po.

english: Pale yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for strong growth. Adding manure, compost, or a nitrogen fertilizer like urea helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ ni mli wa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: How does covering the ground with dry leaves help my vegetables grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ baai ni egboi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi-aduawai lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Covering soil with dry leaves or straw, called mulching, keeps moisture in the soil during hot days, stops weeds from growing, and cools the roots so your plants stay healthy.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ koni otso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do people say planting cowpeas makes my soil richer for the next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nii babaoo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans pull nitrogen from the air and store it in tiny lumps on their roots. When the plant harvest is finished, these roots decay and leave free fertilizer in the soil for future crops like maize.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi bibii amli kɛ́ akpa tsei lɛ. Nɛkɛ shishifãi nɛɛ fiteɔ ni amɛshiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ abele.

english: Why shouldn't I allow all the suckers growing around my plantain stem to stay?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mihaa ŋmeii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ shwereɔ lɛ? Mi plantain tsei lɛ ji nɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ.

english: When too many suckers grow around one plantain stem, they fight over soil food and water. Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two strong ones, resulting in much bigger plantain bunches.
ga: Beni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain kome he lɛ Amɛyeɔ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, eshiɔ ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni no haa ŋmeii babaoo feɔ ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers before producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop flowers when they get too hot, don't get steady water, or lack soil nutrients. Regular watering and keeping roots cool with mulch helps the flowers stay on and turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji edɔ tsɔ. Nu ni anáaa daa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa kɛ shishifãi ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ woɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tomatoi.

english: Why does my groundnut plant push long shoots into the soil after flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanuts lɛ tsiɔ ŋmeii kakadaji kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni ewo fɔfɔi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnut pods grow underground rather than on top. After flowering, the plant forms long stems called pegs that grow downwards into loose soil where the groundnuts actually swell and mature.
ga: Peanut pods lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi moŋ fe ŋwɛi. Kɛji tso lɛ wo fɔfɔi sɛɛ lɛ, ewoɔ tsei kakadaji ni atsɛɔ amɛ pegs. ni baakwɛ̃ kɛya shikpɔŋ ni nɔ etse lɛ mli Akpɔlɔi lɛ baafu ni amɛbaakwɛ̃.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites feeding on leaf sap and spreading plant viruses. Controlling these pests early keeps the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni yeɔ baa lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ tso lɛ helai lɛ amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe awa.

english: What is causing ragged holes and sawdust-like dirt inside the tops of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmei bibii lɛ ayiteŋ lɛ baa?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar hiding inside the leaves. Inspecting your field early and spraying neem water or recommended insecticides into the central leaf whorl protects your crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni odu lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Ni neem nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ okɛshwieɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil holds too much water or has fungal diseases. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away from the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo loo eyɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ amli.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves scorch and dry up during the sunny dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and cannot handle full direct sunlight or extreme dry heat. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains nearby shields young cocoa trees from sun burn.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo la ni mli egbi waa lɛ naa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he.

english: Why does a grafted mango seedling bear fruit much faster than one I grow directly from a seed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ woɔ yibii oya fe dumɔwui ni miduɔ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: A grafted seedling uses a branch taken from a mature tree that is already ready to produce fruit, so it skips the young growth stage. A seed-grown tree must start from scratch and can take up to seven years to reach maturity.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛwo tso mli lɛ kɛ niji ni ajie kɛjɛ tso momo ni efee klalo akɛ ebaawo yibii lɛ tsuɔ nii. No hewɔ lɛ, afoɔ tsei bibii lɛ adalɛ be lɛ mli. Esa akɛ aje tsei ni akɛ dumɔwui akwɛ̃ɔ lɛ shishi kɛjɛ shishijee ni ebaanyɛ ehe afii kpawo dani eshɛ shweremɔ he.

english: Why should I leave wide spacing between my mango trees when planting them on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafee mi mango tsei lɛ gbɛ kɛji mikɛ amɛ miidu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Proper spacing ensures that sunlight reaches all parts of the tree and air flows freely. This prevents fungal diseases from spreading and stops roots from fighting over water and soil nutrients.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa hulu la lɛ shɛɔ tso lɛ fãi fɛɛ ahe ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hu tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haaa ŋmeii helai agbɛ ashwã, ni ehaaa shishifãi lɛ awuu yɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he.

english: Why do my mango trees produce many flowers, but then almost all of them fall off before turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔii babaoo shi no sɛɛ lɛ, nɔ ni miihe ashɛ eyibii lɛ fɛɛ laajeɔ lɛ?

english: Flowers often fall off due to dry spells, insect pests like thrips, or a lack of nutrients in the soil. Protecting the flowers from pests and providing adequate water during fruit set helps them turn into mangoes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ thrips, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ abu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe, ni aha amɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ mango.

english: Why does my mango tree give me a huge harvest this year, but bears very little fruit the following year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango lɛ wo yibii babaoo nɛkɛ afi nɛɛ? Shi afi ni baa lɛ, ewoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ?

english: This natural behavior is called alternate bearing. Producing a huge crop uses up most of the tree's stored food reserves, so it needs a year to rebuild its energy before it can bear heavily again.
ga: Atsɛɔ adebɔɔ mli subaŋ nɛɛ akɛ tsakemɔ. Ni aaawo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ biɔ niyenii ni tso lɛ eto lɛ babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ, eheɔ afi dani enyɛɔ etswaa hewalɛ ekoŋŋ dani enyɛɔ etereɔ jatsu ni tsii lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Should I keep watering my mango trees heavily while they are blooming with flowers?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo mi mango tso lɛ nɔ nu babaoo be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: No, excessive watering while the tree is blooming can cause flowers to drop prematurely or trigger new leaves instead of fruit. It is better to hold back heavy watering until after the fruits have successfully formed.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ awo tso lɛ nu fe nine be mli ni efɔfɔi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha fɔfɔi lɛ agbo oya loo eha baai heei abaye aduawai lɛ najiaŋ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsi nu ni tsii ni oooha lɛ naa kɛyashi aduawai lɛ baaye omanye.

english: Why are the leaves on my mango trees turning black and sticky?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mango tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Black, sticky leaves are caused by black mold growing on the sugary liquid left behind by insects like mealybugs or aphids. Controlling these sap-sucking insects will prevent the leaves from turning black.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ baai diji ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa ji ŋmei diŋ ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nu ni mli ewo sugar ni kooloi bibii tamɔ mealybugs loo aphids shiɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akudɔ kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ, ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔ ediŋŋ.

english: What causes my mature mango fruits to split open while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni haa mi mango ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ shwereɔ be mli ni miyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Fruit splitting usually happens when heavy rain comes after a long dry period. The tree takes in a lot of water quickly, causing the inside of the fruit to expand faster than the skin can stretch.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, aduawai amli gbalamɔ baa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ. Tsei gbalaa nu oya. Enɛ haa tso yibii lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he.

english: Why is it important for me to cut off branches inside the middle of my mango tree canopy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ mango tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Pruning inner branches allows sunlight to penetrate the center of the tree and improves airflow. This keeps the inside dry, which prevents fungal diseases and encourages better fruit development.
ga: Kɛ́ afo emli lɛ, ehaa hulu la boteɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni emli lɛ mli egbiɔ. Enɛ tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ anaa, ni ehaa aduawai lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell that a green mango on the tree is ready to be harvested without cutting it open?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ mango ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa ni akpaaa amɛ?

english: A green mango is ready when the top part near the stem becomes full and rounded, the skin develops a slight sheen, and the sap flowing from a freshly picked stem turns thick and sticky.
ga: Mango eŋɔli lɛ efee klalo kɛji ŋwɛi fã lɛ bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi, ni eyi obɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Hewolo lɛ kpɛɔ fioo. kɛ latɛs ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni ajie ehee lɛ amli Ebaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young mango tree turning yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi mango tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the tree is lacking key nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, or that the roots are waterlogged from poor drainage, which stops them from taking up food properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii titrii, tamɔ nitrogen, yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo nu eyi shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haaa anyɛ aye niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I harvest or work in my vegetable farm early in the morning when there is still dew on the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ejeee jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ oookpa loo otsu nii yɛ aduawai ŋmɔ mli leebi beni ŋmɔtɔ kã baai lɛ anɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Wet leaves carry tiny fungi and germs easily. Walking through or touching wet crops spreads these hidden sicknesses from infected plants to healthy ones on your hands, clothes, and farm tools.
ga: Baai ni efɔ lɛ woɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai bibii oya. Kɛ́ onyiɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni efɔ lɛ anɔ loo ota he lɛ, ebaanyɛ egbɛ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ nɛɛ ashwã kɛjɛ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ kɛya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ oniji, otadei, kɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii anɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why is it bad to spray pesticides on my crop leaves while they are still wet with morning water drops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mafɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ anɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe be mli ni amɛmli edɔ lolo ni amɛmiiho leebi lɛ?

english: Water droplets already sitting on the leaves will wash away or dilute the chemical, making it too weak to kill pests and causing your costly spray to run off onto the ground uselessly.
ga: Nu ni shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ momo lɛ baaho tsofai lɛ loo ebaaha amɛfee mlɛo. Enɛ haa amɛgbɔjɔɔ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛgbe kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui. Ni ehaa o-spray ni jara wa lɛ feɔ nɔ ni he ehiaaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do dark spots and leaf rots spread so fast on my crops during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji kɛ baai ni fiteɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ anɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Disease germs love water. Constant wetness on leaves gives fungal spores the moisture they need to hatch, grow, and sink into the plant leaves to cause spots and rots.
ga: Muawai ni sumɔɔ nu Fɛ̃i ni yaa nɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ naa nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛfɔ, amɛdara, ni amɛbote tso lɛ baai lɛ amli ni ekɛ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii aba.

english: Why should I wait for the hot sun to dry the leaves before cutting off sick leaves from my plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ agbi baai lɛ dani mafo baai ni hela mɔ amɛ kɛjɛ tso ko mli lɛ?

english: Cutting wet stems leaves fresh open wounds that easily trap swimming disease germs from water drops. Dry weather helps plant wounds seal quickly without getting infected.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tsei ni efɔ lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha pilamɔ hee ni agbele naa lɛ ahi shi ni baanyɛ aŋɔ nu mli helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ amli tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa nu mli lɛ mli mlɛo. Shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei apilamɔi lɛ ŋmɛɔ oya ni hela ko bɛ mli.

english: Why does proper spacing between my maize plants prevent leaves from getting sick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ lɛ tsiɔ baa ni hela mɔ lɛ naa lɛ?

english: Good spacing allows wind and sunlight to blow through the farm easily. This dries morning dew off the leaves quickly before leaf-disease germs have time to grow.
ga: He ni jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ lɛ hi bɔni afee ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la anyɛ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli mlɛo. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ agbi oya dani baa hela lɛ mli helai lɛ aná be ni amɛkɛdara.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot when they grow too close to wet leaves or the moist ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ kɛ́ amɛdara ni amɛbɛŋkɛ baai ni efɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Trapped moisture between wet leaves and the pod creates the perfect home for the Black Pod fungus. Keeping air moving around the pods prevents this moisture buildup.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ baai ni efɔ lɛ kɛ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmeii diji ni yeɔ emuu lɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ebɔleɔ he lɛ Pods lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ akabɔle ehe.

english: Why do my pepper leaves turn yellow when water sits on the farm field for days after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air to breathe just like human beings do. Standing water drowns the roots, stopping them from taking up plant food, which makes the leaves turn yellow.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Nu ni ekã shi lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu. Etsiɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaye tsei aniyenii. Enɛ baaha baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants droop in the strong afternoon sun even when the ground has moisture?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulutsoo be mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Under intense heat, leaves lose water through breathing faster than roots can pump it up. The plant wilts slightly to protect itself from losing too much water until the sun goes down.
ga: yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa shishi lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔ mumɔ ni amɛmuɔ lɛ nɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu lɛ kɛya ŋwɛi. Tsei shwieɔ shi fioo koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe koni nu babaoo akafite amɛ kɛyashi hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: Why does clearing weeds around my crops help the leaves stay healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ haa amɛbaai lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Thick weeds trap cold damp air around the base of your crops. Clearing them lets air circulate and keeps the lower leaves dry so hidden pests and molds cannot thrive.
ga: Jwɛi ni mli tse lɛ mɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ. Otso lɛ shishitoo Kɛ́ ojie amɛ lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli ni ebaaha shishigbɛ baai lɛ agbi. Enɛ haaa ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I pour water directly onto my crop leaves in the middle of a hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ nu shwieɔ tsei ahe baai anɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Water drops on leaves act like tiny glass lenses under strong heat, magnifying the sun's rays and scorching tiny burnt spots onto the leaf surface.
ga: Nu ni hoɔ yɛ baai anɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ glase ŋmɛlɛtswai bibii. yɛ la ni naa wa shishi Ehaa hulu la kɛ shãa bibii ni shãa lɛ mli waa. ni shãa yɛ baa lɛ nɔ

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the base of the plant usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or well-rotted animal manure will give the plant the nutrients it needs to stay green and produce healthy cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it good to plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same farm with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts trap nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. This acts as a natural fertilizer that helps your maize grow better without needing as much expensive chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa o-ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ tsofai ni jara wa atsu nii.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees drying up and turning brown in the afternoon sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ egbi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive and cannot handle direct harsh sunlight before their roots fully develop. Planting shade plants like plantain or cassava around them creates protective shade that keeps them cool and moist.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ nuɔ he waa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ dani shishifãi lɛ adara. Dumɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo cassava yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ he. Ehaa hulutsoo ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i hiɔ shi lɛ baa.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up into small cups and looking wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ efolɔ amɛhe ewo kɔɔpoi bibii amli ni etamɔ nɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking the sap from under the leaves. Spraying an organic neem seed extract or recommended insecticide will stop the insects so new leaves can grow normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper leaf curl baa. Kɛ́ akɛ organic neem dumɔwui ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli loo tsofa ko ni akɛwo ŋaa akɛ gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie kooloi lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaatsi kooloi lɛ anaa koni baai heei lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is eating ragged holes in my young maize leaves and leaving small dirt inside the plant stems?
ga: Mɛni ji bu ni ekumɔ yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli lɛ ni ayeɔ ni ashiɔ muji bibii yɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the center of the plant. Applying recommended crop protection products or sprinkling clean dry wood ash into the leaf funnel early in the morning can control them.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni akɛbuɔ tsei ahe ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsu nii loo akɛ tso sũ ni mli tse ni egbi lɛ shwie baai lɛ amli leebi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye enɛɛmɛi anɔ.

english: Why do I need to clear the ground and put long wooden poles for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ wɔjie shikpɔŋ lɛ ni wɔkɛ tsei kakadaji awo mli lɛ? Ha sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food that grows big tubers under the ground. Staking lifts the vines off the damp ground into the light, which also prevents soil diseases from rotting the leaves.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛ́ amɛmiikwɛ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa la ni tsoɔ waa mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni helai akabote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite.

english: Covering soil with dry plant material (called mulching) keeps the ground cool, traps water in the soil during hot days, and prevents weeds from popping up and competing with your crops.
ga: Mulching kɛ tso nibii ni egbi Enɛ (ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching) yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i. Tsɔɔmɔ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni ekɛ oŋmɔshi nibii akaŋ akaŋ.

english: Having too many shoots (suckers) forces the mother plant to share its water and food. Pruning away smaller suckers and leaving only two or three healthy ones ensures your plantain tree produces large, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ tso lɛ ŋmeii (ŋmeii) babaoo yɛ lɛ, ebaaha ehe bahia ni tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ aja nu kɛ niyenii. ŋmeii bibii ni afoɔ lɛ Jiemɔ ni oshi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ 2-3 pɛ koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ oplantain tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Tomato flowers often drop when temperatures get too high or when the soil goes from completely dry to suddenly soaked. Watering your plants regularly at the root level keeps soil moisture steady and helps fruit set.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi kwraa kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ mli trukaa. Kɛ́ afɔ tsei anɔ nu daa yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa aduawai lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he.

english: How can I tell if my cassava tubers are ready to harvest without digging up the whole bush?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni mikɛ ŋmei muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava is mature when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, leaving a long stem, and the ground around the base of the plant starts to crack open as the tubers swell underground.
ga: Yucca lɛ eda beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ. Tso kakadaŋŋ ni eshwɛ ni he ni ebɔle shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn under harsh, direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides a living umbrella that shields them from heat and holds moisture in the soil.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo bibii ahe. Ehaa hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he ni ehaa nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning light green and yellowish instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaahi shi ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowish leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to build strong, green leaves. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer will help the leaves regain their rich green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua baai lɛ ni amɛná amɛsu ni mli kwɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller harvests when I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil without giving it time to recover. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas puts nitrogen back into the soil naturally and improves future yields.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsa ehe. Abele ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ baaha nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eha wɔsɛɛ be mli yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I apply fertilizer right when heavy rain is falling on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ miinɛ waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes away applied fertilizer before the crop roots have a chance to absorb it. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist, but not during downpours, so the nutrients stay in the root zone.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwo mli lɛ dani tsei shishifãi lɛ náa hegbɛ ni amɛŋɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo lɛ. Shi jeee yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ beaŋ. koni niyenii mli hewalɛ ahi shishifã lɛ he

english: Cassava roots rot in waterlogged soil because standing water blocks air from reaching the roots, causing fungal diseases to grow. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows extra water to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ha fungal hela aba. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to convert air and light into food energy. Staking the vines holds the leaves up off the ground, allowing them to catch maximum sunlight, which feeds the yams growing underground.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni etsake kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ la ni etsɔ niyenii hewalɛ. Wein tso lɛ ni akɛwoɔ tso mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Bɔni afee ni enyɛ ená hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ. ni ji niyenii kɛha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ

english: What causes small caterpillars to eat holes inside the fresh central leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ teŋ baai heei lɛ amli?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that targets the tender inner leaves of young maize plants. Finding them early and applying recommended neem-based sprays or bio-pesticides early in the morning can stop them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ naa yɛ ŋmei tsei bibii amli baai bibii lɛ anɔ. Amɛtaomɔ mra Ni akɛ tsofa ni akɛ neem fee loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛwoɔ mli leebi lɛ tsu nii lɛ baanyɛ akpa amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or lack of pollination. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch and watering regularly helps the flowers stay attached and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ hao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa waa mli. Irregular irrigation or insufficient pollination Keeping the soil evenly moist with mulch and regular watering will help the flowers stick and produce fruit.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing plants compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper spacing ensures every crop gets enough resources to grow thick stalks and full heads.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ba tso fɛɛ tso teŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ naa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do some of the crop seeds I planted fail to come up out of the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni midu lɛ ekwɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if they are buried too deep, if the soil is too dry, or if low-quality seed was used. Planting good seeds at the correct depth in moist soil ensures that most seeds sprout successfully.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ tsɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. or use low quality seeds Planting good seeds at the correct depth in moist soil will ensure that most seeds germinate successfully.

english: This yellowing is usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency. When a crop does not get enough nitrogen from the soil, it pulls nutrients out of its older bottom leaves to feed the fresh, growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ su ni ji ŋmɔŋ nɛɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Kɛ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ejieɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai ni etsɛ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Will applying a double dose of chemical fertilizer make my crops grow twice as fast?
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ni akɛfataa he Ani 2 ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ada oya shii enyɔ?

english: No, putting too much fertilizer at once can burn the crop's roots and damage the plant. Crops can only take up a specific amount of nutrients at a time, so extra fertilizer is wasted and can scorch the crop.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo tso lɛ mli yɛ be kome mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni efite tso lɛ. Tsei baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii kpakpai fioo ko pɛ yɛ be kome mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa fe nine lɛ fiteɔ, ni ebaanyɛ eha tsei lɛ ashã.

english: Why do the improved seeds I buy give a bad yield if I save them and replant them next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwu ni atsake lɛ ni miheɔ lɛ wooo yibii kpakpai kɛji mikɛto ni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Commercial high-yielding seeds are often hybrids designed to perform best only in the first generation. Replanting saved seeds causes the crop to lose its special traits, resulting in smaller harvests and weaker plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni akɛheɔ jara lɛ ji dumɔwui ni afee amɛ koni amɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli pɛ. Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ ni aduɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ afite amɛsui lɛ. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi ni tsei lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Cassava roots rot underground when soil holds too much water and lacks proper drainage. Excess water suffocates the roots and creates conditions for harmful soil fungi to attack and decay the crop.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Nu babaoo haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shihilɛi baa shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ koni amɛtutua ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛfite.

english: Why do caterpillars hide deep inside the center funnel of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-baby corn baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Pests like Fall Armyworms hide in the central funnel because the growing tissue there is soft, tender, and moist, while the surrounding leaves shield them from direct sunlight, heat, and birds.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworms lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli ejaakɛ fãji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔlɔ, ni amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔlɔ, yɛ be mli ni baai ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ. Ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ, dɔlɛ kɛ okpoi ahe.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers without forming pods during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛkuuu jwɛi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed their flowers during intense heat to conserve water and survive. Without enough soil moisture and shade, the tree prioritizes keeping itself alive over producing fruit.
ga: Kookoo tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi. Kɛji ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulutsoo ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa amɛhe ni amɛaaha amɛhi wala mli lɛ nɔ fe yibii ni amɛwoɔ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or beans between my maize rows make the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ mi ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ teŋ lɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas have natural root nodules that capture nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into plant food, which enriches the soil and nourishes the surrounding maize plants.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ adebɔɔ mli shishifãi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni etsakeɔ lɛ efeɔ tsei aniyenii. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa ŋmãa tsei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ náa niyenii.

english: Yam plants produce energy through their leaves using sunlight. Staking lifts the vines so all leaves catch maximum sunlight, which provides the energy needed to grow large underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ amɛnáa hewalɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ fɛɛ aná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Enɛ ji hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of yellow flowers but fail to grow any actual fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo shi ewooo yibii diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers without setting fruit when temperatures get too high or when there is too much nitrogen in the soil, which causes the plant to produce extra leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Tomato baajie fɔfɔi ni yibii bɛ mli lɛ ashwie shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ baai babaoo yɛ yibii najiaŋ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops look thin and stunted even when there is heavy rainfall on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that compete with crops for soil nutrients and light. Even with plenty of water, the weeds steal essential plant food before your crops can absorb it.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni kɛ tsei yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ la. Eyɛ mli akɛ nu babaoo yɛ moŋ, shi Jwɛi hu juɔ tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I burn the brush on my field when clearing the land for planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishãa jwɛi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mijieɔ shikpɔŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Burning destroys essential organic matter and beneficial insects in the topsoil that feed your crops. Leaving cleared weeds to decompose naturally coats the ground, retains soil moisture, and turns into free fertilizer.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni he hiaa ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni haa onibii lɛ niyenii lɛ mli lɛ ahiɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni jwɛi ni ajie lɛ lɛ fite yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ofee ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko

english: Why does rainwater wash away the rich topsoil on my hilly farm, and how can I stop it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ ni yɔɔ gɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa?

english: When rain falls on sloping ground, gravity pulls the water fast enough to carry away your fertile topsoil. Planting your crops in rows across the slope (contour planting) or building ridges acts as barrier walls to slow water down so it sinks into the ground instead.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ lɛ, Gravity lɛ gbalaa nu oya bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni jara wa lɛ aya. Tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔi lɛ anɔ (Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔi lɛ anɔ) loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ni haa nu lɛ baa shi kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass (mulching) acts as a protective blanket. It stops the hot sun from drying out the soil, keeps weeds from growing, and keeps the soil cool so roots can feed easily.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ Ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aye niyenii mlɛo.

english: Why is it good to add decomposed poultry manure to my soil before I plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ akɛ kooloi ashishifã ni egbo awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani adu lɛ?

english: Decomposed manure acts like long-lasting food for the soil. It improves the soil's structure so it holds water better and slowly releases essential nutrients that help crops grow strong green leaves and healthy fruits.
ga: Koolooi amli ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii lɛ feɔ fɛo bɔni afee ni ehiɛ nu mli jogbaŋŋ ni ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ fiofio. Koni eye ebua tsei ni amɛná baai eŋɔli ni mli wa kɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and thin with tiny ears when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ toi bibii babaoo beni adu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant its own space to spread roots and capture light to produce large ears.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa lɛ diɛŋtsɛ egbɛ ni ekɛgbɛɔ eshishifãi lɛ eshwaa ni emɔɔ la ni ekɛfeɔ toi wuji.

english: Why do my maize yields get smaller every year when I plant maize on the exact same plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize uses up specific nutrients from the soil every season. Planting it in the same spot repeatedly starves the ground of those nutrients and builds up pests; rotating with legumes like cowpeas restores balance to the soil.
ga: Abɛi kɛ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsuɔ nii daa be. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he kome shii abɔ lɛ, niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmei tsake lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ekome ekoŋŋ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts make my land better for other crops later?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have special roots that take nitrogen gas from the air and trap it inside the soil. When the crop finishes, this natural nitrogen stays behind to fertilize whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ agbe ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen nɛɛ baakã he ahi sɛɛ koni ekɛwo tsei fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide large leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and humidity needed to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantains ni shwereɔ oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Cassava roots need air to breathe underground. When water collects in heavy, flat land without draining away, it drowns the roots and causes rot; planting on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain off.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia cassava shishifãi koni amɛmu yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Beni nu buaa ehe naa babaoo yɛ hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ ashwie shi ni eha amɛgboi. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Cutting off extra or dead branches (pruning) allows sunlight and fresh air to pass through the trees. This prevents humidity from building up, which stops black pod disease and encourages the tree to produce more pods.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine loo ni egboi lɛ ni afoɔ (Pruning) lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni ŋmɔtɔ akabua ehe naa Enɛ haa black pod hela lɛ kpaa ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ewo ŋmɔtɔ babaoo.

english: How do I know if my cocoa plot is large enough to be run as a full commercial farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-kokoo shikpɔŋ lɛ da bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ matsu jarayeli ŋmɔ ni fa babaoo he nii?

english: A commercial farm is defined by how you manage it rather than just its size. If you plant with proper spacing, maintain regular weeding and pest control, and produce cocoa primarily for sale to buying companies rather than just home use, you are running a commercial enterprise.
ga: Bɔ ni okwɛɔ nɔ ohaa lɛ ji nɔ ni tsɔɔ jarayeli ŋmɔ. Jeee bɔ ni edara ha lɛ pɛ he ewieɔ. Kɛji okɛ gbɛ ni sa du lɛ Tsa jwɛi kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nii daa. ni efeɔ kookoo ni ekɛhɔ̃ɔ nitsumɔhei ni heɔ nii lɛ titri Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni okɛbaatsu nii yɛ shia kɛkɛ Otsuɔ jarayeli nitsumɔ ko he nii.

english: Are there specific rules about what crops I am allowed to mix with cocoa on my farm?
ga: Ani mlai pɔtɛɛ komɛi yɛ ni kɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aŋmɛ mi gbɛ akɛ mikɛ kookoo afutu mli yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he?

english: Yes, agriculture officers guide farmers on intercropping. While temporary shade crops like plantain or food crops like cocoyam are allowed when cocoa is young, heavy root crops or too many timber trees are restricted because they compete with cocoa for water and soil nutrients.
ga: Hɛɛ, okwaayeli he onukpai lɛ baawo okwaafoi lɛ ŋaa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ he. Eyɛ mli akɛ kookoo haa anáa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains loo niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo yɛ be kukuoo mli be mli ni kookoo lɛ ji gbekɛ lolo moŋ. Shi tsei ni shishifãi ni tsii loo tsei babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ faaa ejaakɛ amɛkɛ kookoo yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli.

english: What should I do if my farm produces more cocoa pods than my drying mats can hold during peak harvest?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ kookoo ŋmeii babaoo fe bɔ ni ŋmeii ni akɛgbiɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ mli?

english: When you have a surplus yield, you should stagger your harvesting schedule so pods do not spoil on the tree, construct additional raised bamboo drying fermentation trays, or work with local farmer cooperatives to manage excess pods.
ga: Beni oyɛ nibii ni fa fe nine Esa akɛ oja okpamɔ be lɛ mli koni okafite tso lɛ nɔ ŋmeii lɛ. Bɔɔ ŋmei ni awo nɔ lɛ kroko ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Aloo okɛ maŋ lɛ mli okwaafoi akuu ko atsu nii koni okwɛ pods ni fa fe nine lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it important for an agricultural extension officer to physically visit my farm before I expand my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko ayasara miŋmɔ lɛ dani magbɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: An extension officer visits your farm to check soil quality, slope, and land suitability. They ensure you follow proper spacing rules and do not clear protected forest areas, helping you avoid losses before you invest money.
ga: Extension officers lɛ baa oŋmɔ lɛ mli koni amɛkwɛ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ha, bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi kɛ bɔ ni ehi ha. Amɛkwɛɔ koni onyiɛ mlai ni sa ni kɔɔ he ni esa akɛ okɛ ohe akabɔ he lɛ sɛɛ, ni okajie kooi ni abuɔ he lɛ amli. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni otsiɔ ohe kɛjɛɔ nibii ni elaaje lɛ ahe dani okɛ shika woɔ mli

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and burning in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand harsh direct sunlight. They need temporary shade plants like plantains or specific shade trees to protect their delicate leaves from sun scorching and to keep moisture in the soil.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ dumɔwui loo tsei pɔtɛɛ ni haa hulutsoo. Bɔni afee ni abu baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What happens to my yield if I plant cocoa trees very close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni ekɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ?

english: Planting cocoa too close together causes the branches to overlap and block sunlight. This creates damp conditions that encourage black pod disease and forces trees to compete for soil nutrients, leading to fewer and smaller pods.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ aniji lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe nɔ ni amɛtsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa. Enɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni woɔ black pod hela lɛ he hewalɛ baa. kɛ tsei ni nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ baa shi fioo ni amɛfeɔ bibii.

english: Why do many of the small cocoa flowers fall off my trees without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ fɔfɔi babaoo shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ?

english: It is natural for a cocoa tree to drop many flowers it cannot support. However, excessive flower drop can be caused by dry weather, lack of soil nutrients, or damage from insects like mirids (akate).
ga: Eji adebɔɔ naa nɔ akɛ cacao tsei baashwie fɔfɔi babaoo ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛye amɛbua. Shi kɛlɛ, shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ hu baanyɛ aha fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi fe nine lɛ aba. niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nibii ni kooloi bibii tamɔ mirids (akate) fiteɔ.

english: Will cutting off extra branches from my cocoa tree reduce the amount of cocoa I harvest?
ga: Ani niji krokomɛi ni mifoɔ yɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ baaha kookoo ni mikpaa lɛ aba shi?

english: No, proper pruning actually increases your harvest. Removing dead, diseased, or extra non-producing branches (chupons) allows air and sunlight to reach the trunk, helping the tree focus its energy on growing healthy pods.
ga: Dabi, tsei ni afoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa onibii ni owoɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Kɛ́ ajie tsei niji ni egboi, ni hela emɔ amɛ, loo ni wooo yibii (chupons) lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la ashɛ tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do cocoa pods turn black and hard on the tree during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛhe wa yɛ tsei anɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in high humidity and wet conditions. Clearing weeds, pruning branches for better airflow, and picking infected pods early helps stop it from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ kɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ. weeding Tsei ni afolɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anaabuamɔ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni akpa gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: How can I tell if the soil on my old cocoa farm is tired and needs support?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ momo lɛ nɔ lɛ efite ni ehe miihia ni aye abua mi?

english: Signs of poor soil include slow tree growth, pale or yellowing leaves, and trees producing very few pods even after flowering. Adding organic compost or recommended cocoa fertilizers helps restore soil nutrients.
ga: Nɔ ni fata okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii lɛ he ji tsei ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo. Baai ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔŋ Ni tso lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ fioo ko pɛ eyɛ mli akɛ ewo fɔfɔi moŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Is it better to burn the bushes after clearing my farmland or leave them to rot on the ground?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mashã jwɛi lɛ beni mijie midumɔi lɛ loo mahã amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Leaving cleared vegetation to rot on the field acts as natural mulch, which protects the soil from heat, holds water, and adds organic plant food back into the soil as it breaks down. Burning destroys these good nutrients and kills helpful soil organisms.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛ tsei ni ajie lɛ lɛ gbɛ ni amɛgboi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsu nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he, ehaa nu hiɔ shi, ni ekɛ tsei aniyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni efiteɔ lɛ. Shãa fiteɔ nɛkɛ niyenii kpakpai nɛɛ ni egbeɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why does planting my crops too close together cause them to produce smaller harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mitsei lɛ ni miduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii baa lɛ?

english: When crops are packed tightly together, their roots and leaves fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil food. Giving each plant proper space ensures it gets enough light and nutrients to produce big fruits and heavy yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ebɔ he lɛ, Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso gbɛ ni sa lɛ, ehaa enáa la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ yibii wuji ni woɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with thick leaves but give me very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni mli tse lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shishi?

english: This usually happens when the soil has too much nitrogen and not enough potassium. High nitrogen forces the cassava plant to spend all its energy growing big leaves on top instead of feeding and growing the tubers underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ ni potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Nitrogen ni fa babaoo lɛ haa ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛtsɔ baai wuji ni ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaaye niyenii ni amɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ

english: Why are my young maize leaves turning yellow shortly after planting in my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are a classic sign that your crop is hungry for nitrogen, which helps plants stay green and grow strong. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer will restore their deep green color and boost growth.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni ale jogbaŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔtɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaha ehiɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni mli kwɔ ekoŋŋ, ni ebaaha edalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Maize feeds heavily on soil nitrogen, leaving the soil tired. Cowpeas and groundnuts are special crops that take nitrogen from the air and fix it back into the soil, restoring fertility naturally for the next season.
ga: Abele haa nitrogen babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, etɔ sũ lɛ. Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Koni akɛ adebɔɔ mli babaoo aba ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn easily in full sunlight. They need fast-growing shade plants, like plantains or cassava, planted alongside them to act as living shade umbrellas during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa oya, tamɔ plantains loo yucca. adu yɛ masɛi Koni ekɛ wala aha yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without producing any tomatoes during the dry, hot months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato ko yɛ nyɔji ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Extreme hot and dry conditions stress tomato plants, causing the pollen inside the flowers to dry up. When flowers fail to pollinate, the plant drops them to save energy and water.
ga: Shihilɛi ni mli edɔ waa ni egbi lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ. Enɛ haa pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Beni anyɛɛɛ afee fɔfɔii lɛ pollen lɛ Ashwieɔ tsei koni akɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he.

english: How can I tell if my farmland has healthy soil before I begin planting my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa dani mabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ?

english: Healthy soil is dark in color, crumbly to the touch, and smells like fresh earth. Seeing living earthworms digging in your soil is a great sign that the ground is alive and full of nutrients for your crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Efoɔ kɛji ota he ni eŋɔɔɔ tamɔ shikpɔŋ hee Kɛ́ ona shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka ni miifo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, eji okadi kpakpa ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ wala mli ni eyi obɔ kɛ niyenii ni haa oŋmɔshi nii lɛ.

english: Why are my plantain trees falling over easily even when there is no strong wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ko bɛ po lɛ?

english: Plantain stems usually tip over because tiny underground worms called nematodes or root-boring insects are eating away the root system. Without a strong root network anchoring it to the soil, the heavy plant collapses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, plantain tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii ahewɔ. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ nematodes loo kooloi ni shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ miiye shishifãi lɛ. Kɛji shishifãi ni mli wa ko bɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpɛtɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ Tsei ni tsii baagbee shi.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites living under the leaves. Spraying your plants with neem oil mixture helps clear these pests so healthy, flat leaves can grow again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni hiɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ ni akɛfutu mli lɛ shwie tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ. Bɔni afee ni baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: Leaves usually turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green and strong. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer will help your maize regain its green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is my farmland producing fewer cassava tubers now than it did three years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ miiwo ŋmei shishifãi fioo fe afii etɛ ni eho lɛ?

english: Planting cassava on the exact same piece of land continuously drains nutrients without giving the soil time to rest. Rotating your crops with beans or leaving the land fallow restores soil fertility so crop yields can increase again.
ga: Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ yaa nɔ etsɔɔ mli ni ehaaa sũ lɛ be ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii tsake oŋmɔshi nibii loo oshi hei ni ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ. koni ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die shortly after I transplant them into the open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ beni mikɛ amɛ tee ŋmɔ mli etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot handle full, direct sunlight and heat. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains first provides a protective living umbrella that keeps the seedlings cool and moist while they grow.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa kwraa. Shade tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ ehaa shade ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants droop and dry up even when it rains heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When water sits on the farm without draining, the roots rot from waterlogging. Without healthy roots, the plant cannot absorb water or food, causing it to wilt and die even during the rainy season.
ga: When water is stuck in the farm without drainage. Shishifãi lɛ baagboi kɛjɛ nu ni hoɔ lɛ mli. If there are no strong roots The plant will not be able to absorb water or food. This causes them to wither and die even during the rainy season.

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when temperatures get too high or when the plant does not receive consistent water. Giving the plants steady water at the root level and light shade helps flowers develop into fruit.
ga: Tomatoi baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ afɔɔɔ tsei lɛ nu daa. Kɛ́ aha tsei lɛ nu yɛ amɛshishifã lɛ he, ni aha amɛ hulutsoo fioo lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ aduawai.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and rotting on the tree before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Black pod is a fungal disease that spreads rapidly in damp, dark farms. Pruning overgrown tree branches lets in sunlight and fresh air, which prevents the fungus from surviving and spreading.
ga: Black pods ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli efɔ ni mli ewo duŋ lɛ amli. Tsei ni edara fe nine lɛ ni afolɔ ashwie shi kɛyashi amɛbaaná hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Enɛ baatsi ŋmei lɛ naa koni ekahi shi ni egbɛ eshwa.

english: Planting seeds too close together forces the plants to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to grow thick stalks and large cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space to grow thick stems and large cobs.

english: Why are insects damaging my cabbage leaves much more during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii babaoo tutuaa mi-cabbage baai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pests multiply much faster in warm, dry weather and attack leafy crops to get water. Watering your crops regularly and spraying neem leaf solution keeps pests away safely.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ faa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ mli. ni etutuaa tsei ahe baai koni ená nu Nu ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ daa kɛ neem baai ahe tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaha abu he shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: How do I know if my soil is healthy enough to start growing vegetables?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi aduawai adumɔ?

english: Healthy soil is dark, crumbles easily in your hand, holds moisture well, and contains earthworms. If your soil is hard clay or dry sand, mixing in dry leaves and manure will improve its quality.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su yɛ ediŋ, efiteɔ oya yɛ nine mli, ni ehiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ. ni eyɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ ji shikpɔŋ ni wa loo ŋã ni egbi Kɛ́ okɛ baai ni egbi kɛ ŋmeii futu mli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo.

english: Why are my plantain suckers growing very slowly compared to the ones on my neighbor's farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ miida blɛoo nɛkɛ kɛ akɛto nɔ ni yɔɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he lɛ?
