english: Weeds surrounding your plantain suckers steal the food, water, and sunlight meant for the crop. Clearing weeds regularly and placing dry grass around the plant base as mulch speeds up their growth.
ga: Jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ juɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Tsɔɔmɔ jwɛi lɛ daa ni okɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo tso lɛ shishigbɛ he ejaakɛ ŋmɔshi nibii haa tso lɛ daa.

english: Which fast-growing crops can I plant right now to harvest food within three to four months?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei ni daa oya manyɛ madu bianɛ koni manyɛ makpa niyenii yɛ nyɔji etɛ loo ejwɛ mli?

english: Crops like maize, cowpeas, and leafy vegetables grow rapidly and can be harvested in 90 to 120 days. Cowpeas are especially good because they mature quickly and also enrich the soil with nitrogen for future crops.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa, tsina ŋmãa, kɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ daa oya, ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ gbii 90 kɛyashi 120 mli. Cowpeas hi jogbaŋŋ titri ejaakɛ edaa oya, ni ehaa nitrogen babaoo hu baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Cassava naturally sheds its leaves during dry spells to save water and stay alive. The root tuber under the ground stops growing temporarily, but once the rains return, the plant will sprout new leaves and resume growing.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hɔmɔ be mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ehi wala mli. Shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ kpaɔ amɛdalɛ be kukuoo ko. Shi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ ŋmeii heei ni ebaakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil. Applying manure or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer will help the leaves turn green and give the plant strength to grow big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni eha tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow tall and thin with small tubers when I plant them under big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii kɛji akɛ adu lɛ yɛ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava needs direct sunlight to manufacture food in its leaves and store energy in its root tubers. Under shade, the plant wastes energy stretching upward to reach the light instead of swelling its tubers.
ga: Cassava he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni enyɛ efee niyenii yɛ ebaai lɛ amli ni ekɛ hewalɛ ato eshishifãi lɛ amli. Yɛ hulutsoo shishi lɛ, tsei fiteɔ hewalɛ kɛtsɔ amɛhe ni amɛkpãa kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛná la lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha yitso lɛ agbɔjɔ

english: How can I protect my harvested maize grains from weevils without using expensive chemicals?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ he kɛjɛ ŋmeii ahe ni mikɛ tsofai ni jara wa tsuuu nii?

english: You can store well-dried maize in airtight triple-layer storage bags (PICS bags) or mix clean wood ash with the grains in sealed drums. Removing air and keeping moisture out prevents insects from surviving and reproducing.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmãa ni egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ awo vacuum triple-layer storage bags (PICS kotokui) amli loo okɛ tso sũ ni he tse afutu ŋmãa lɛ yɛ baagi ko ni atsĩ naa mli. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni ajieɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ mli lɛ haaa kooloi ahi shi ni amɛfɔ bii.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests every year when I keep planting maize in the exact same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the specific nutrients that crop uses most. Alternating maize with legumes like groundnuts or beans gives the soil a break and naturally restores nutrients.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni tsei lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii fe fɛɛ lɛ hoɔ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa lɛ, ebaagbala shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without producing any fruit during very hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Excessive heat causes stress to tomato plants, making the pollen dry out so flowers cannot develop into fruit. Spreading dry grass mulch around the base of the plant keeps the roots cool and helps fruit set.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei anɔ. dry out pollen Fɔfɔi nyɛŋ atsɔ aduawai. Okɛ jwɛi ni egbi afɔ shi. shishi koni shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni eye ebua ni ewo yibii

english: Why do my plantain trees produce small, light bunches when weeds grow around their bases?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ feɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Eyɛ mlɛo ni jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ he?

english: Weeds have aggressive roots that steal water and nutrients meant for your plantain trees. Clearing a wide ring around the base of each plantain tree allows it to absorb the food it needs to produce large bunches.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛhaa o-plantain lɛ. wide separation around Dumɔwu lɛ eko fɛɛ eko shishitoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwu lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: How do I know if the very first rain of the season means it is time to sow my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui?

english: It is best to wait until the ground stays consistently moist after a few rains before sowing. Planting after just one early rain can cause seeds to sprout and then die if a dry spell follows immediately.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ dani odu dumɔwui. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji akɛ nugbɔshiimɔ nyiɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my harvested sweet potatoes spoil much faster than my harvested yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya fe mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ?

english: Sweet potatoes have thin, delicate skin and high water content, making them easy to bruise and decay. Yams have thicker skins that act as a protective layer, allowing them to last longer in storage if kept cool and dry.
ga: Sweet potatoes yɛ hewolo ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni nu babaoo yɔɔ mli. Efoɔ ni egboɔ oya. Sweet potatoes yɛ hewolo ni mli tse ni tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Abaanyɛ akɛto be kakadaŋŋ kɛji akɛto he ko ni mli ejɔ ni egbi.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plants lack nitrogen in the soil or are getting too much water around their roots. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-decomposed manure helps them regain their green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu babaoo yɛ eshishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛná amɛhe ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ ni amɛdara waa.

english: Maize takes a lot of nitrogen out of the soil to grow. Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts draw nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground, naturally restoring soil nutrients for the next crop.
ga: Abɛi kɛ nitrogen babaoo ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛkwɛ̃. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ. Enɛ haa niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I clear all the large shade trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijieɔ cacao tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense direct sunlight. Leaving selected shade trees or planting plantains alongside cocoa provides a natural leaf umbrella that protects young cocoa roots and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ehaa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo baa ni buɔ kookoo shishifãi bibii ahe ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why should I remove some of the extra shoots growing around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ ekomɛi? Ajieɔ midumɔwu titri lɛ shishitoo lɛ.

english: When too many shoots grow from the bottom of one plantain plant, they compete with the main stem for water and nutrients. Pruning extra shoots leaves one or two strong stems, resulting in larger and heavier plantain bunches.
ga: Beni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu kome shishi. Nakai ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni oookpa lɛ baaha tso lɛ yitso kome loo enyɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, plantain tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when heavy rains fall continuously?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ miinɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot in waterlogged soil because standing water cuts off oxygen to the root system, causing fungal diseases to multiply. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ. Ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli baa lɛ fa babaoo Ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Yam leaves need to climb high on stakes to catch maximum direct sunlight. Exposure to sunlight allows the leaves to produce more plant food, which moves down into the soil to build bigger yam tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato baai lɛ akwɔ tso kakadaŋŋ nɔ koni amɛna hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ. Hulu la ni tsoɔ lɛ haa baai lɛ woɔ tsei niyenii babaoo. Enɛ tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni efee sweet potato ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do flowers fall off my tomato plants without turning into fruits during hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop off when soil temperatures rise too high or when plants experience sudden dryness. Mulching the soil with dried grass keeps the root zone cool and moist, helping flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ latsaa lɛ fa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ egbi trukaa. Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and remaining tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Curled, dwarfed leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips sucking plant sap and transmitting viruses. Controlling these pests early with neem oil or suitable sprays protects leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni yɔɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Kɛtsɔ neem fɔ loo spray ni sa nɔ lɛ, ebuɔ baai lɛ adalɛ he.

english: Why do my watermelons split open on the farm before they are mature enough to pick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon lɛ miitswa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani amɛdara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mafo lɛ?

english: Watermelons crack open when they receive a sudden abundance of water after a dry period, causing the inside to grow faster than the outer skin can stretch. Watering plants consistently prevents sudden fruit bursting.
ga: Watermelon baatswa kɛji akɛ nu babaoo bote mli trukaa yɛ be ko sɛɛ. Enɛ haa watermelon lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni ehewolo ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo otsei lɛ amli daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni aduawai lɛ akafo trukaa.

english: Why does swamp rice grow much better when there is standing water on the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋshɔ mli ŋmãa lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ waa yɛ be mli ni nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Lowland rice varieties are adapted to flooded soil, which smothers competing weeds and keeps nutrients dissolved so the roots can easily absorb them to fill out the grain heads.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛhaa shikpɔji ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni egbeɔ jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ lɛ mlɛo kɛyashi ŋmãa yitso lɛ eyi.

english: If imported feed or maize becomes hard to get, what crops can I easily grow to feed my farm animals?
ga: Kɛji kooloi aniyenii loo ŋmãa ni jɛ maŋsɛɛ lɛ namɔ wa Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo nɔ koni mikɛha miŋmɔ mli kooloi lɛ niyenii?

english: Crops like cassava, sorghum, and sweet potatoes grow very well in local soils and produce high yields. Cassava roots provide energy while sorghum grain can be ground down to make rich feed for poultry and livestock.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei, ŋmei kɛ ŋmei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ waa yɛ maŋ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo. Cassava shishifãi haa hewalɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, abaanyɛ atsɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui babaoo nɔ afee kooloi kɛ kooloi aniyenii.

english: What crops can I plant that grow very fast so I can harvest food without waiting many months?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei manyɛ makwɛ ni amɛdaraa oya bɔ ni abaanyɛ akpa niyenii ni amɛmɛɛɛɛ nyɔji babaoo?

english: Vegetables like amaranth (aleefo), okra, and cowpeas grow rapidly and can be harvested in just 30 to 60 days, giving you quick food and income while longer-term crops are still growing.
ga: Aduawai tamɔ amaranth (alifo), okra kɛ cowpea daa oya ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ gbii 30 kɛyashi 60 pɛ mli, ni ehaa onáa niyenii kɛ shika oya yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ lolo lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested grains like maize and beans rot or get spoiled by insects so quickly after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmaa ni mikpa, tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa lɛ fiteɔ loo kooloi bibii fiteɔ amɛ oya yɛ ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Grains spoil because of moisture left inside them and pests like weevils. Drying your grains completely in the sun and storing them in sealed, airtight bags (like PICS bags) starves insects of air and protects your crop for months.
ga: Nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ fiteɔ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni eshwɛɔ yɛ mli ni kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ebɔle amɛhe lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmaa lɛ gĩ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni okɛto kotokui ni akɛ vacuum ewo mli (tamɔ PICS kotokui) lɛ, ebaaha hɔmɔ aye kooloi lɛ ni ebaabu onibii ahe nyɔji babaoo.

english: How can I keep my cassava roots fresh after digging them out of the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ ahi shi ehee beni mifo amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli sɛɛ?

english: Cassava roots spoil within two to three days after harvest because they react to air. Processing them quickly into gari, flour, or drying them into kokonte preserves them for a long time.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ mli yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ yɛ bɔ ni ekɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsuɔ nii eha lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ afee amɛ oya ni afee amɛ gari, ashikishaŋ loo agbi amɛ awo kokonte mli lɛ, ebaaha amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants turn yellow and stop growing tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, a key plant food. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the leaves stay green and healthy so the plant can grow big ears of corn.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji tsei aniyenii titri Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ. Tso lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ ŋmãa toi agboi.

english: Why do my crop plants wither and yellow when water sits on my field for too long after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ beni nu hiɔ miŋmɔji amli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air to breathe just like humans do. When water covers the soil for too long, it cuts off air to the roots, causing them to rot and preventing the crop from taking up food.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ Efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaaa tso lɛ aye niyenii.

english: Can I plant beans together in the same field with my maize plants?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafee ekome kɛdu ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ mi-ŋmei tsei lɛ?

english: Yes, planting beans alongside maize helps both crops. Beans naturally pull nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which helps the maize grow stronger without exhausting the land.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmeii ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ. Beans jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ daa waa ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteee.

english: Which crops survive best in my field when the rains are late or irregular?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛɔ fioo loo enɛɛɛ be fɛɛ be?

english: Crops like millet, sorghum, and cassava have deep or efficient root systems that search for underground water, allowing them to withstand dry spells better than maize or fresh vegetables.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, kɛ ŋmãa Eyɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ loo ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu taomɔ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ hɔmɔ shihilɛi jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmãa loo aduawai heei.

english: Why do small worms suddenly show up and eat the leaves inside my young maize stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ba trukaa ni amɛye baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are likely fall armyworms, which hatch from eggs laid by moths on young, soft maize leaves. Checking your farm early and applying organic or recommended sprays into the plant whorls controls them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni ŋmeii fɔɔ ŋmeii bibii ni ji ŋmeii bibii anɔ lɛ amli. Oŋmɔ lɛ mli kwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ atsu nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akuu lɛ mli lɛ baakudɔ amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Can I save the seeds from the crops I harvest this season to plant again next year?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni mikpa yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ afi ni baa lɛ?

english: You can save seeds from traditional varieties, but if you bought high-yielding hybrid seeds, saving them for the next season will result in much smaller yields and weak plants. It is better to buy fresh hybrid seeds each season.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ shishijee henɔi lɛ amli lɛ ato. Shi kɛji akɛ ohe dumɔwui ni akɛfee hybrid ni woɔ yibii babaoo hu? Kɛ́ akɛ amɛ to kɛha be ni baa lɛ, ebaaha yibiiwoo fioo pɛ aba, ni tsei lɛ hu bɛ hewalɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui heei ni akɛfee hybrid lɛ daa afi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, an essential plant food in the soil, or that the soil has too much water. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or compost helps the leaves turn green and produce strong ears of corn.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu babaoo Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni ŋmãa toi lɛ aná hewalɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when there are no plantain trees planted next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso bibioo lɛ gbo beni aduko dumɔwui yɛ emasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that burn and dry out quickly under direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide broad leaves that create necessary shade and keep the soil moist for cocoa to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Plantain tsei ni daa oya lɛ haa baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa lɛ baa, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni kookoo lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the weather gets too hot, when the plant lacks water, or when insects fail to transfer pollen between flowers. Keeping the soil consistently moist during hot weather helps flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni tsei lɛ bɛ nu loo be mli ni kooloi bibii nyɛɛɛ ajie pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi ateŋ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha ehi shi pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains leave standing water around the roots without draining, soil organisms cause the tubers to suffocate and rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ha nu lɛ ata shi ebɔle he. shishifãi ni nu bɛ mli Nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baafo ni amɛbaafite ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Planting maize on the same soil every year drains all the specific nutrients maize relies on and allows pests to multiply. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni abele lɛ damɔ nɔ lɛ hoɔ, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai fɔɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds from around my crop plants as soon as they sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ? Nibii ni aduɔ kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ pɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal sunlight, water, and soil food from your crop plants. Removing weeds early allows your crop seedlings to grow big and strong without fighting for resources.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ye obua otso lɛ dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa ni okɛ nibii ahe akaŋshii akafee nɔ ko.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves in direct sunlight, which gives the plant energy to feed the growing tuber below. Staking also keeps leaves off damp soil, preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛbaai lɛ ashɛ hulu la lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ náa hewalɛ ni ekɛhaa ŋmeii ni miida yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ niyenii. Staking hu buɔ tsei ahe tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akamɔ amɛ.

english: What causes the leaves on my pepper plants to curl up and shrink?
ga: Mɛni miiha baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ?

english: Leaf curling is typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking sap from the leaves, or by a virus spread by these insects. Controlling these pests with mild sprays keeps leaves healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛjɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Kɛtsɔ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ blɛoo nɔ ni akɛyeɔ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baa lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do holes appear in the leaves and stems of my maize plants while they are growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ahe be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Holes in maize leaves are caused by pests like the fall armyworm caterpillar eating through the plant tissue. Applying recommended treatments into the growing tip of the plant destroys the caterpillars before they ruin the crop.
ga: Buji ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa mli lɛ ji nɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ fall armyworms ni yeɔ tsei ahe fãji lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ tsu nii yɛ tso lɛ naagbee ni miida lɛ he lɛ, ebaakpata ŋmeii lɛ ahiɛ dani amɛbaafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested vegetables spoil quickly before I can sell them at the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya dani ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Vegetables spoil fast if harvested during the heat of the day, stacked tightly in unventilated sacks, or bruised during transport. Harvesting early in the morning and storing crops in cool, shaded spaces preserves their freshness for buyers.
ga: Aduawai fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akpa yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ. Akɛto kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ amli. loo egbɔjɔ yɛ gbɛfaa mli Nikpamɔ leebi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtoɔ he ko ni hulutsoo yɔɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa efeɔ ehee kɛhaa mɛi ni heɔ lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize crop roll up tightly during the dry afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe waa yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up during extreme heat as a natural defense mechanism to reduce their surface area, which slows down water evaporation and protects the plant from drying out.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he lɛ aba shi. Enɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo, ni ebuɔ tsei ahe koni amɛkagbi.

english: Why are my young cocoa trees dropping their flowers before turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers when stressed by extreme sunlight, sudden dry weather, or poor shade. The tree sacrifices its flowers to save energy and water to stay alive.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ. trukaa kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi loo hulutsoo be ni ehiii Tsei kɛ amɛfɔfɔi shaa afɔle koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu ato koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my pepper plants stop setting fruit when the temperature gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ kpaɔ yibii beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ?

english: High temperatures cause pepper pollen to become sterile and blossoms to drop. The plant delays fruit production until cooler weather returns so it does not exhaust its water reserves.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa pepper pollen lɛ feɔ nɔ ni bɛ fɔmɔ nii ni fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Tso lɛ baaha yibiiwoo lɛ asɛɛ afo kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ. bɔni afee ni nu ni ato lɛ akafite

english: How do fast-growing, improved crop varieties behave differently from traditional seeds in terms of fertilizer needs?
ga: Te tsei srɔtoi ni etee hiɛ ni daa oya lɛ feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa tɛŋŋ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ yɛ dumɔwui ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ ahe yɛ amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe hiamɔ nii ahe?

english: Fast-growing hybrid varieties feed much more aggressively than traditional crops. Because they reach maturity quickly, they require early and consistent fertilizer to produce full yields without starving the soil.
ga: Hybrid tsei ni daa oya lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ niyenii yeli mli fe blema tsei. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛdaraa oya. No hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia ni amɛwo amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya ni afeɔ amɛ daa koni amɛná ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa ni hɔmɔ akaye shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow tall with lots of leaves but yield very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi ewoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil or heavy rainfall early on causes cassava to send all its energy into stem and leaf growth instead of storing carbohydrates in its roots.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa mra lɛ haa ŋmei tsɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa tsei kɛ baai ni miida lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ carbohydrates ato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn under direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains act as natural shade umbrellas, keeping the soil cool and moist while the young cocoa roots establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ baashã yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa yɛ be mli ni kookoo shishifãi bibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Staking lifts yam leaves off the hot ground and spreads them out toward sunlight. Maximum sun exposure allows leaves to manufacture more food to swell the tubers underground.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato lɛ ajo foi kɛjɛ he ni edɔ lɛ ni egbɛ eshwa hulu la lɛ mli. Hulu la ni fa babaoo lɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ niyenii babaoo ni baaha ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why does planting my cowpea seeds too close together reduce the number of pods I harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni cowpea dumɔwui ni miduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii ni mikpaa lɛ ayibɔ baa shi lɛ?

english: When cowpea seeds are crowded, the plants shade each other out and compete for soil moisture, leading to weak stems, foliage disease, and fewer pods.
ga: Kɛji akɛ cowpea dumɔwui lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ feɔ amɛhe shade ni amɛyeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, baa helai kɛ ŋmeii fioo komɛi baa.

english: Sudden wilting in moist soil is often caused by bacterial wilt or root rot. The disease blocks the water-carrying tubes inside the stem, preventing water from reaching the upper leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa. Hela nɛɛ tsiɔ paipii ni kɛ nu yaa lɛ anaa yɛ tsɔne lɛ mli. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekashɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my plantain trees turning yellow and hanging down during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains naturally drop their older, bottom leaves during dry conditions to conserve water for the growing main stem and emerging bunch.
ga: Plantains lɛ shwieɔ amɛshishi baai ni egbɔ lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni ekɛto nu he kɛha tso lɛ shishifãi ni miida kɛ ŋmeii ni miiba lɛ.

english: No, planting seeds too close causes overcrowding. The maize plants will fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in tall, thin stalks with very small or empty cobs.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa mɛi ayiɔ obɔ fe nine. Abɛi tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa loo nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is hungry and lacks nitrogen, which is the food plants use to build green leaves. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure will turn them green and strong again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye shikpɔŋ lɛ ni nitrogen bɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaha amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and lets specific pests build up in the ground. Rotating with crops like beans or peanuts restores the soil naturally.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ be fɛɛ be lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii Yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baa ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, steal water and plant food from the main mother tree. Leaving only one or two strong shoots ensures the main tree gets enough energy to produce a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei loo tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ nu ni amɛduɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso niji kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo ŋmeii wuji babaoo ni tsii.

english: Will cutting off some side branches on my tomato plants help me get bigger fruit?
ga: Ani tomato tso lɛ niji ni yɔɔ esɛɛ lɛ ni afolɔ lɛ baaye abua ni eha aduawai lɛ adara?

english: Yes, removing extra leafy branches allows the plant to focus its energy and nutrients directly on growing bigger, healthier tomatoes instead of wasting strength on growing excess leaves.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei niji ni baai babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii tɛ̃ɛ yɛ tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni miida lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ kɛtsɔ baai ni fa fe nine ni oookwɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do we need to heap up soil into high mounds before planting yam seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ wɔto shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ dani wɔdu ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow underground and need soft, loose earth to expand easily. High mounds prevent the soil from packing hard and allow water to drain away so the yams don't rot.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni ehe hiaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli edɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã oya. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ tsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekafee ais ni ehaa nu hoɔ kɛyaa koni ŋmeii lɛ akafite.

english: Does it matter which part of the cassava stem I choose to plant in my field?
ga: Ani mihalaa ŋmei tso lɛ fã ni mikɛbaadu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, using the hard, mature middle part of the stem works best because it contains stored food and strong buds. Very soft stem tops dry out easily, and overly woody bases sprout slowly.
ga: Hɛɛ, tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ni wa ni eda lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ niyenii ni ato kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɔɔ mli. Tso lɛ yibii bibii waa lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Ni shishitoo ni fa fe nine lɛ baakwɛ̃ fiofio.

english: Is it better for me to water my pepper plants during the hot afternoon or in the early morning?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ nu yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli loo leebi maŋkpa?

english: Watering in the early morning allows the roots to absorb water before the sun gets too hot. Afternoon watering causes most of the water to evaporate quickly into the air before the plant can use it.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli leebi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛmɔɔ nu dani hulu lɛ mli woɔ la tsɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli shwane mli lɛ haa nu lɛ fa ko shwieɔ oya kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani tso lɛ baanyɛ ekɛtsu nii.

english: Why are small worms eating holes in the middle of my maize leaves right after the rain starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-abele baai lɛ ateŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ pɛ kɛkɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, which hatch quickly when rainy conditions arrive to feed on soft new leaves. Catching them early by inspecting the leaves and applying ash or recommended sprays protects your crop.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni fɔɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ nɛ koni amɛye baai heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Amɛmɔmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni oookwɛ ni okɛ sũ loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwie nɔ lɛ atsu nii lɛ nɔ lɛ, obaaye obua ni obu onibii ahe.

english: What causes my maize leaves to have small holes and look chewed up?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-abɛi lɛ amli ŋmeii bibii lɛ miifee? ni ekwɛɔ akɛ eshɛre?

english: Chewed leaves and small holes are usually caused by crop pests like the Fall Armyworm or caterpillars that feed on young, soft leaves before the maize can mature.
ga: Baai ni ashɛreɔ kɛ buji bibii Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm, loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai bibii dani ŋmãa lɛ shwereɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa.

english: How can I tell if my maize plant is dying from lack of rain or from insect attack?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-abele tsei lɛ miigboi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɛɛ loo kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ ahewɔ?

english: Lack of water causes the whole plant to wilt and turn pale evenly, whereas pest damage shows clear signs like chewed holes, broken stems, or visible insects and their droppings in the leaf funnels.
ga: Nu ni bɛ lɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gbɛ ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ nɔ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baatsɔɔ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ tamɔ bu ni atsɔ mli, tsei ni ekumɔ, loo kooloi ni anaa kɛ amɛmli ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do pests show up on my maize farm during certain times of the farming season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-abele ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ bei komɛi amli yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pests often multiply when young, tender crops grow after the early rains or during dry spells, as these conditions provide abundant food and ideal temperatures for them to breed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai fɔɔ kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii shwere yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ni nɛ mra lɛ sɛɛ loo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shihilɛi nɛɛ haa niyenii babaoo kɛ hulutsoo be ni sa kɛha fɔmɔ.

english: How do pest control chemicals work to protect my maize crops?
ga: Te tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tsuɔ nii amɛhaa tɛŋŋ koni ebu mi-abele tsei lɛ ahe?

english: Some chemicals act as repellents that drive pests away from your farm, while others directly eliminate destructive insects when sprayed on the affected parts of the plant.
ga: Tsofai komɛi tsuɔ nii akɛ tsofai ni shwieɔ kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Yɛ be mli ni tsofai komɛi tsuɔ nii akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi tɛ̃ɛ kɛ́ akɛshwie tso lɛ fãi ni hela lɛ emɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ,.

english: How do I choose the correct chemical to buy when insects attack my maize field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahe tsofai ni sa be mli ni kooloi bibii miitutua mi ŋmɔji lɛ?

english: Different pests require specific chemical formulas, so you should describe or show the pest to an agricultural extension officer to get the right approved product for your maize.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko biɔ tsofa pɔtɛɛ ko. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ogbala tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ mli loo otsɔɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ lɛ koni enine ashɛ nɔ ni sa ni akpɛlɛ nɔ kɛha o-ŋmãa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it important to spray chemical directly into the center of the young maize plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afɔ tsofai awo ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Many destructive caterpillars, such as Fall Armyworms, hide deep inside the central leaf funnel of the maize plant where normal surface spraying cannot reach them.
ga: Kplukai srɔtoi babaoo ni fiteɔ nii, tamɔ Fall Armyworms lɛ, kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ baai amli shɔŋŋ. ni ŋwɛi shwiemɔ ni afɔɔ feemɔ lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ he.

english: How can I apply pest control chemicals safely without harming my crops or myself?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ atsu nii shweshweeshwe ni miyeee miŋmɔshi nibii loo mi diɛŋtsɛ mihe awui?

english: You should wear protective gear like boots and gloves, mix the chemical strictly according to the recommended dose, and spray during cool hours when the wind is low.
ga: Esa akɛ owo nibii ni buɔ mɔ he tamɔ atadei kɛ glɔvs. Futumɔ tsofai lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ taakɛ bɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ. Ni okɛshwie nɔ gbɛkɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miitswa.

english: Where can I go in my district to get expert help when my maize crops have a disease?
ga: Nɛgbɛ manyɛ maya yɛ mikpokpaa lɛ nɔ koni mayahe ŋaalɔi ayelikɛbuamɔ kɛji mi-abele lɛ emɔ hela?

english: You can visit your local Ministry of Food and Agriculture (MoFA) office or contact a community agricultural extension officer to receive free guidance and diagnostic support.
ga: Obaanyɛ oyasara Niyenii kɛ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe (MoFA) nitsumɔhe ni yɔɔ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ. Aloo okɛ oakutsoŋ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ lɛ agba hela he ŋaawoo kɛ yelikɛbuamɔ ni aheee nɔ ko.

english: Can agricultural extension officers come to my farm to teach me how to manage crop pests?
ga: Ani okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko baaba miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ebatsɔɔ mi bɔ ni akwɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anɔ?

english: Yes, extension officers regularly conduct field visits and demonstrations to train farmers directly on identifying pests, safe chemical handling, and effective crop protection techniques.
ga: Hɛɛ, mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔ mli saramɔi kɛ nifeemɔi daa koni amɛkɛtsɔse okwaafoi lɛ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe. Tsofa ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahebuu ŋaai ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ

english: What simple steps can I take on my farm to reduce pests before needing to buy expensive chemicals?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mafee nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Mɛni ji nibii komɛi ni obaanyɛ ofee yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli koni oha tsɛŋemɔ helai aba shi dani ehe bahia ni ohe tsofai ni jara wa?

english: You can reduce pests naturally by rotating your crops each season, clearing weeds around field borders where insects hide, and checking your farm regularly to catch early attacks.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii aba shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni oootsake yɛ bei lɛ ateŋ lɛ nɔ. Jiemɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle ohe lɛ. Gbɛjegbɛ ni kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe ewo mli lɛ naa Ni okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa koni onyɛ omɔ tutuamɔi mra.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and wither when there is direct sunlight on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to intense sunshine and dry soil. Without shade crops like plantain or cassava grown nearby to shield them, the harsh heat burns their tender leaves and dries out their shallow roots before they can establish.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ he waa. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ koni ebu amɛhe lɛ bɛ lɛ, Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ shãa baai bibii lɛ ni ehaa shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ baa. Egbiɔ dani edaa.

english: How does covering the bare soil around my crops with dry leaves or grass help them survive dry weather?
ga: Mulching bare soil around Te mafee tɛŋŋ madu miŋmɔshi nibii kɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: Covering the ground with organic material, called mulching, blocks direct sunlight from heating the earth. This holds moisture in the soil longer, stops weeds from growing, and keeps the roots cool during hot dry spells.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛhaa lɛ akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni etsĩ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa ni etsi jeŋ dɔlɛ naa. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: When maize leaves turn yellow starting from the tips down the center, it usually means the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to make green leaves. Adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help restore their green color and growth.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛyitseiaŋ kɛtee teŋgbɛ lɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛbaai lɛ afee eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ dalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences heat stress or uneven watering. When the soil gets too dry during warm periods, the plant sheds its flowers to save water rather than spending energy growing fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ekɛhaaa lɛ be fɛɛ be. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii kɛwo yibii.

english: Which direction should I stem-plant my cassava cuttings into the soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esa akɛ adu ŋmei tso lɛ yɛ?

english: Always plant cassava stem cuttings with the leaf buds or nodes pointing upward toward the sky. Planting stems upside down causes the buds to struggle to sprout, leading to weak shoots and much smaller tuber yields.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, dumɔ ŋmei ni afo lɛ ni ŋmeii loo ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ shishi kɛtee shishi lɛ, ebaaha ewa aha ŋmeii lɛ akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni baa shi kwraa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my plantain trees keep falling over before the fruit bunches are ready for harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains lɛ miigbee shi dani aduawai akui lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots and carry heavy fruit, making them easy for strong winds to blow over. Pruning extra sucker shoots, planting at proper depth, and propping heavy bunches with strong wooden sticks prevents them from falling.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni tsii. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baatsɔ mli. Krɛdɛɛ ni afoɔ tsei ahe ni aduɔ yɛ he ni sa Kɛ tsei ni wa ni akɛtsuɔ nii koni akɛfi tsei niji ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ lɛ baaye abua ni amɛkagbee shi.

english: Why are ragged holes suddenly appearing in the center leaves of my young maize stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bu ko ni etse ehe banee trukaa yɛ mi-abɛi bibi lɛ tso lɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Holes inside the center leaves of maize are caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars eating the fresh growing stem. Inspecting your farm early in the morning and treating the central leaves early will stop them from destroying the growing shoot.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmeii baa teŋ lɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli leebi ni otsa baai ni afɔɔ namɔ mra. Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: What causes the pods on my cocoa trees to turn dark brown or black and rot during the heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ ni egboɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Black pod is a fungal disease that spreads rapidly in damp, shady, and overly wet conditions. Clearing weeds and pruning thick tree branches allows sunlight and dry air to flow through the farm, keeping the cocoa pods dry and healthy.
ga: Black pod ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ fe nine. Tso niji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ ahe jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ amɛhe ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Ehaa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my ripening green tomatoes turning black and soft on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato eŋɔli ni miikwɛ̃ lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni eyɛ blɛoo yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This soft rot at the bottom of tomatoes is called blossom-end rot, caused by a shortage of calcium and irregular watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist throughout the flowering and fruiting stages stops this rot from developing.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ akɛ blossom end rot. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni faaa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo be lɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekafite.

english: Is it better for me to apply granular fertilizer right before a heavy rain or after the rain stops?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oookɛ granular fertilizer awo mli dani nugbɔ anɛ waa loo beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa sɛɛ?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist after rain or before a very light drizzle. Heavy downpours will wash the fertilizer off the top layer of soil before the crop's roots have a chance to drink it in.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ loo dani nugbɔshiimɔ fioo ko baa. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ tsuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani tsei shishifãi lɛ náa hegbɛ amɛnuɔ.

english: This usually happens when your soil is short on nitrogen. The maize plant naturally pulls whatever nitrogen it has from its older lower leaves and sends it up to feed the young growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi gbalaa nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli ni etsuɔ ​​kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni eyaha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up into little cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi efeɔ kɔɔpoo bibioo ko lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is commonly caused by tiny pests like aphids or thrips feeding on the undersides of leaves, or by a viral infection spread by insects when the weather is very dry and hot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni edɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: This is your crop's natural way of saving water. When the sun is very hot, the plant loses water faster than the roots can absorb it, so it temporarily wilts to shade itself and reduce water loss until temperatures cool down.
ga: Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ nu toɔ onibii ahe. Kɛ hulu lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be kukuoo mli ni amɛhaa nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ baa shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when the soil gets too dry, which stops pollen from fertilizing the flowers. Giving the plants consistent moisture and shade during peak heat helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. Enɛ baatsi pollen lɛ naa koni ekawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔ. Fɛ̃i kɛ shade ni akɛhaa tsei yɛ dɔlɛ be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads rapidly during rainy or humid weather when water stays on the pods for too long without enough sunlight and air movement.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela. Fungal hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ loo hulutsoo be mli. Beni nu hiɔ pod lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli.

english: Why does my cassava plant drop almost all its leaves during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yibii babaoo fiteɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry spells to protect itself from dying. By losing its leaves, it stops losing precious water to the dry air and survives off the energy stored inside its underground roots.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaa lɛ shi yɛ fɛ̃i be mli koni ekɛbu ehe kɛjɛ gbele he. Baai ni laajeɔ lɛ haaa nu ni jara wa lɛ aya kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi mli, ni ehiɔ shi kɛtsɔ hewalɛ ni ato yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi amli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do yam vines try to wrap around sticks and climb upward instead of trailing on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tso lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekɛ ehe abɔle tso lɛ nine lɛ he ni ekwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants naturally reach up to catch as much sunlight as possible. Climbing stakes helps the leaves spread out into the light, which allows the plant to manufacture more energy to build big, heavy tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ baashɛ he koni emɔ adebɔɔ mli hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Tso lɛ nɔ kwɔɔ haa baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa la lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛfeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and produce large leaves that act as living shade umbrellas to keep the soil moist and protect the young cocoa during its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why is it beneficial to plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same field with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen gas from the air and feed it into the soil through their roots. This enriches the soil naturally, providing free fertilizer for your heavy-feeding maize crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ heɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli amɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa oŋmãa ni oyeɔ nii waa lɛ.

english: Why should I plant my seeds in straight rows with spaces between them instead of scattering them across the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni gbɛ ahi dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooogbɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ

english: Planting in spaced rows prevents plants from fighting each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, while also making it much easier for you to walk through the farm to weed and harvest.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ tsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaye hulu la he akaŋ. nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ, yɛ be mli ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa bo hu akɛ oootsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛyajie jwɛi kɛ nibii ni akpa.

english: Is it safe for me to use tap water from the pipe to water my vegetable farm?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ nu ni jɛɔ hose mli lɛ baatsu nii kɛwo mibɔɔ lɛ mli nu?

english: Pipe water is filtered and treated with chemicals like chlorine to make it clean for drinking, which generally won't harm mature plants, but natural rainwater or well water is cheaper and better for beneficial soil micro-organisms.
ga: Afolɔ nu ni jɛɔ pɔmpi mli lɛ mli ni akɛ tsofai tamɔ klorin tsuɔ he nii koni ehe atse kɛha nu ni anuɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ yeee tsei ni eda lɛ awui. Shi adebɔɔ mli nugbɔshiimɔ loo nu bu mli nu lɛ jara waaa ni ehi kɛha sũ mli nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ.

english: Why do white crusts form on top of my soil after I water my crops repeatedly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ ko baa mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mikɛ nu ewo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ amli shii abɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When water evaporates in the heat, it leaves behind dissolved minerals and salts. Over time, these build up on top of the soil and can prevent young crop roots from absorbing moisture properly.
ga: Kɛ nu kɛ dɔlɛ shwie shi Eshiɔ shika tsuru kɛ ŋmeii ni egbɛ eshwa. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, enɛɛmɛi buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsi tsei bibii ashishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaŋɔ nu jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow even after I applied fertilizer to the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Plants cannot drink fertilizer dry; they need moisture to dissolve nutrients. If the soil lacks water, the crops cannot absorb the fertilizer, causing leaves to turn yellow from nutrient starvation.
ga: Tsei nyɛŋ anu ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi. Amɛmiitao ŋmɔtɔ koni amɛjie niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Kɛji nu bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii nyɛŋ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: How can I tell if my crop is suffering from lack of water or lack of fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu efo miŋmɔshi nibii amli loo ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ mli?

english: When a plant lacks water, the whole plant droops and leaves wilt. When it lacks fertilizer, the plant remains standing upright, but the lower leaves slowly turn yellow or light green.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ nu Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ lɛ, tso muu lɛ fɛɛ baagbo ni ebaagbɔjɔ. Kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ lɛ, tso lɛ baadamɔ shi shiŋŋ. Shi shishigbɛ baai lɛ baatsake fiofio kɛbatsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse

english: Will adding extra fertilizer make my crops yield twice as much harvest?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni mikɛbaafata he lɛ baaha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná yibiiwoo lɛ toi enyɔ?

english: No, applying too much fertilizer creates a salty environment in the soil that burns the roots, drying out the plant and reducing yield rather than increasing it.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmei baa. Enɛ shãa shishifãi lɛ, egbiɔ tso lɛ, ni ehaa yibiiwoo baa shi moŋ fe ni eeeha eya hiɛ.

english: Can heavy downpours wash away the fertilizer I just applied to my crops?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwo miŋmɔshi nibii amli amrɔ nɛɛ?

english: Yes, heavy rains can wash away surface fertilizer before it melts into the ground. It is best to cover fertilizer with a thin layer of soil after application so rain doesn't carry it away.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ dani etsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli ogbe naa lɛ, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli tseee aha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe. Koni nugbɔ lɛ akashwie shi

english: In intense midday heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can suck it up from the wet soil, causing temporary wilting to protect themselves until temperatures drop in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane gbi lɛ mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ tso lɛ agbi yɛ be kukuoo mli koni ebu ehe kɛyashi hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ.

english: Early morning is best because it prepares the soil with moisture before the hot afternoon sun, and leaves dry off quickly during the day, preventing fungal diseases from growing.
ga: Leebi ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ saa shikpɔŋ lɛ he dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ baa. Ni baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Koni fungal helai akaya hiɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce small tubers when there is prolonged drought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava needs adequate soil moisture in its early stages to build strong roots; during a drought, the plant saves its energy to keep leaves alive rather than growing big roots underground.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa he miihia Cassava shishijee mli koni shishifãi ni wa aba. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ Tsei toɔ hewalɛ he koni amɛkɛkwɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaawo shishifãi wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl upwards during very dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi waa lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl up during dry periods as a natural survival trick to shrink their leaf surface area exposed to the hot sun, trapping moisture and stopping water loss.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ hulutsoo be mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ gbɛ ni akɛbaa baai lɛ anɔ he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Retains moisture and stops water loss

english: How can I get a big harvest if I only have a small piece of land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná ŋmaa babaoo kɛji shikpɔŋ bibioo ko pɛ miyɔɔ?

english: You can get high yields on small land by using improved seeds, planting in neat rows with proper spacing, and applying organic manure or fertilizer at the right times so every plant gets full nutrients without competing.
ga: Obaanyɛ oná yibii babaoo yɛ shikpɔji bibii anɔ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Plant in neat rows with appropriate spacing. Ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli atsu nii yɛ be ni sa mli bɔni afee ni tso fɛɛ tso aná niyenii ni yeɔ emuu ni ekɛ ehe akatswa akaŋ.

english: Can I plant crops on farmland that was previously damaged by illegal mining?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ ŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ ni tsutsu lɛ shika tsuru ni ajieɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ efite lɛ nɔ?

english: Damaged land loses its topsoil and good nutrients, but you can rebuild it over time by clearing debris, adding fresh compost or manure, and planting nitrogen-fixing cover crops like legumes before putting in main crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ baafite sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi kɛ niyenii kpakpai. Shi obaanyɛ oma ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni sa mli kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni ooojie lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii hee afata he. ni amɛduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni saa nitrogen, tamɔ ŋmeii. Dani akɛ tso titri lɛ baafata he

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient that gives plants their green color and energy to grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Eji niyenii titri ni haa tsei lɛ amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ hewalɛ koni amɛdara waa.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they get stressed by sudden heat, a lack of regular water, or a shortage of soil nutrients needed to support fruit development.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni baa trukaa lɛ hao amɛ. nu ni hoɔ daa loo niyenii ni he hiaa koni aduawai akwɛ̃ lɛ bɛ sũ lɛ mli

english: Weeds are wild plants with very strong roots that are naturally aggressive at grabbing water, sunlight, and soil food before your planted crops can get them.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni shishifãi lɛ wa waa. Taakɛ eji lɛ, egbɛɔ eshwaa oya koni ekɛ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ abɔ he akaŋ dani otso lɛ anyɛ aná.

english: Is it good to plant cowpeas together with my maize on the same plot?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu tsina ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, cowpeas naturally pull nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which acts as free food for your maize while covering the earth to keep it moist.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsina ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa o-corn lɛ yɛ be mli ni okɛ muji woɔ mli koni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves and weak roots that dry out quickly in direct sun, which is why they need fast-growing shade crops like plantains planted beside them to act as living umbrellas.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Enɛ hewɔ ni kookoo tsei he hiaa ni amɛná hulutsoo tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ. Koni etsu nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka

english: Why do crops like maize stretch tall and thin without fruiting when planted under big shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ ni ewooo yibii kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Maize needs direct, full sunlight to make energy for growing ears, so when stuck in heavy shade, it wastes all its strength stretching upward toward the light and leaves no energy for yield.
ga: Hulu la he miihia ŋmãa tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha toi ni miida lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ laajeɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛtsɔ ŋwɛi ni ekpãa kɛyaa la lɛ he lɛ nɔ, ni ebɛ hewalɛ ko ni ekɛbaatsu nii.

english: Why is it harmful to plant cassava on the exact same spot on my land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu ŋmei yɛ he kome yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the exact same crop repeatedly drains the same nutrients from the soil every season and lets crop-specific pests and diseases multiply in the ground.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. ni eha tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo aya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell if my soil has enough moisture for my seeds to sprout?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha midumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃?

english: Dig down a few inches and squeeze a handful of soil; if it forms a soft ball in your palm without dripping water or crumbling into dry dust, it has enough moisture for seeds to germinate.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ shi inchii fioo komɛi ni okɛmimɔ shikpɔŋ ni fa fioo. Kɛji efee bɔɔlu ni yɔɔ blɛoo yɛ onine nɔ ni nu shwieee shi loo efoɔ kɛfeɔ sũ ni egbi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Is it better for me to test a new crop on a small piece of land first before planting my whole farm with it?
ga: Ani ebaafee nɔ ni hi akɛ maka ŋmɔshi nibii hee ko makwɛ yɛ he bibioo ko? Dani abaakwɛ nakai tso lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli?

english: Yes, starting with a small test plot lets you see how the crop performs in your local soil and weather without risking all your money. Once you get a good harvest and learn how it grows, you can safely clear more land and expand in the following seasons.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛjɛ kaa he gbɛjianɔtoo bibioo ko nɔ. Ehaa ona bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii amɛhaa yɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ nɔ ni okɛ oshika fɛɛ wooo oshara mli. Beni onine shɛɔ ŋmaa kpakpa nɔ ni okaseɔ bɔ ni edaa lɛ. Obaanyɛ ojie he babaoo ni okɛgbala mli shweshweeshwe yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Why would I need a harvesting machine instead of just hiring people to harvest my farm by hand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi nikpamɔ nii yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mahe mɔ ko ni ekɛ enine akpa miŋmɔ lɛ mli nii lɛ?

english: Harvesting machines allow you to collect crops from very large fields in a few hours, which saves time and prevents crops from spoiling in the sun. Manual harvesting works well for small plots, but as your farm grows larger, finding enough hand labor quickly becomes difficult and expensive.
ga: Nikpamɔ tsɔne lɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa ŋmɔji wuji amli yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai fioo komɛi amli. Enɛ haaa be afite, ni ehaaa ŋmɔshi nibii afite yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Nine ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛha shikpɔji bibii. Shi beni oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛɛ lɛ Nine nitsumɔ ni sa ni anáa lɛ bafee nɔ ni wa ni jara wa oya.

english: Why do my crops grow poorly if I burn all the bushes on my land before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ jogbaŋŋ kɛji mishã tsei bibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani midu lɛ?

english: Burning destroys the natural compost, beneficial insects, and nutrients in the topsoil that your crops need to grow. Clearing the land without burning helps the soil hold moisture better and keeps it fertile for your crops.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. ŋmeii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ojie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oshãaa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa onibii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen in the soil or that heavy rains have washed away the nutrients. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or compost helps the leaves turn green so the plant can make food and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo akɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea loo compost tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli. No sɛɛ lɛ, tsei baanyɛ awo niyenii ni amɛdara waa.

english: Planting seeds too close together makes the crops compete with one another for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in weak, thin plants with very small yields instead of healthy plants with big harvests.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa lɛ baa, ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ. Mohu ɔ, e ji tso nɛ he wa nɛ e woɔ yiblii.

english: Why is extension officers telling me not to plant cassava on the exact same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔkadu ŋmei yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop on the same land every year drains specific soil nutrients and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the dirt. Rotating your cassava with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores nutrients and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kpo. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai pɔtɛɛi kɛ tsei ahe helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei tamɔ tsina loo ŋmei tsake ŋmei lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni ewaje shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers when the sun gets too hot and there is no rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi beni hulu lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers during dry spells to protect themselves from water loss and heat stress. The plant sheds the flowers to save its limited energy and survival resources until moisture returns.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nibii fioo ni amɛyɔɔ ni amɛkɛhiɔ shi lɛ ahe kɛyashi be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so slowly during the first month after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mitsei lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ ni mikɛduɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than young crops and steal the water, fertilizer, and sunlight your crops need to establish roots. Removing weeds within the first few weeks gives your crops full access to nutrients so they can grow rapidly.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya kwraa fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛná shishifãi. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha otsei lɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ. koni amɛnyɛ amɛdara oya

english: What main things do I need to prepare if I want to increase my farm size from two acres to twenty acres?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii ni he hiaa esa akɛ masaa mihe kɛji miisumɔ ni mafee miŋmɔ lɛ dalɛ kɛjɛ acre enyɔ kɛyashɛ acre nyɔŋmai enyɔ?

english: Expanding requires secured access to tractor services for plowing, enough capital for seeds and fertilizer, reliable labor or machinery for harvesting, and a guaranteed buyer so your larger harvest does not go to waste.
ga: O nitsumɔ lɛ mlilɛɛmɔ biɔ ni onine ashɛ traktɔ nitsumɔi anɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe. Shika ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha dumɔwui kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii Nitsumɔ loo tsɔnei ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ kɛha nikpamɔ kɛ mɛi ni heɔ nii ni yɔɔ nɔmimaa koni okpamɔ ni da fe fɛɛ lɛ akafite.

english: Why do my harvested grains get insects and rot even after I have put them inside bags in my storehouse?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni midumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ mli ŋmeii ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifite eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛwo kotokui amli yɛ nitoohe lɛ moŋ?

english: Grains rot and attract weevils if they are not properly dried to low moisture levels in the sun before bagging. Storing damp grain creates heat and humidity inside the bag, which makes molds grow and attracts insect pests.
ga: Nibii ni ŋmaa baafite ni ebaagbala ŋmeii kɛji akɛ agbiko lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashɛ he ko ni hulu la lɛ mli edɔ fioo dani akɛwo kotoku mli. Dumɔwui ni mli efɔ ni akɛtoɔ lɛ haa dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i baa kotoku lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ daa ni egbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees are very sensitive to direct sunlight and high heat. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside them provides living shade, keeping the air cool and preserving soil moisture so the cocoa seedlings survive.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ lateral plantains ni aduɔ lɛ baaha hulutsoo aba. ha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ajɔɔ ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize needs to grow green leaves. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure helps the plants turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni baai eŋɔli lɛ akwɛ̃. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava is usually ready 9 to 12 months after planting. You will know it is time when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the ground around the stem begins to crack open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ. Obaale be ni shishigbɛ baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. kɛ hei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso lɛ shishifã lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes inside the funnel leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai ni tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This is typically caused by Fall Armyworm, a common pest that feeds on young corn leaves. Finding them early and applying safe control measures like ash, neem extract, or approved pesticides prevents them from destroying the harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Amɛtaomɔ mra ni akɛ gbɛi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛkwɛɔ amɛ nɔ tamɔ sũ, neem mli nu loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii. Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite nibii ni amɛdu lɛ.

english: Covering soil with dry grass or leaves (mulching) acts like a blanket that traps moisture in the ground, stops weeds from growing, and protects crop roots from extreme sun heat.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ sũ mli (mulching) lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ sũ mli, ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni ebuɔ tsei shishifãi ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he

english: Why do I need to cut away some of the extra shoots growing at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain lɛ shishi lɛ ekomɛi?

english: Extra shoots (suckers) compete with the main plantain tree for water and plant food. Pruning away weaker suckers allows the main tree to put all its energy into producing large bunches of fruit.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei krɛdɛɛi (tso lɛ) kɛ plantain titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛhaa nu kɛ tsei aniyenii. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei bibii lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or groundnuts make my soil better for future crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have roots that naturally trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, leaving free fertilizer behind for the next crop planted in that field.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛshiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni aduɔ yɛ nakai ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when plants suffer from water stress during very hot weather or when there is too much nitrogen fertilizer. Regular watering during flower formation helps tomatoes set fruit properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na naagba yɛ nu he yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli loo kɛ́ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nu wo tomato nɔ daa yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Staking yam vines allows leaves to spread out and catch more sunlight to make food, which encourages the plant to grow much bigger tubers under the ground.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ sweet potato wain tso lɛ wo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni enáa hulu la babaoo kɛha nihoomɔ. Enɛ woɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekwɛ̃ bulbs wuji babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why shouldn't I apply fertilizer when the ground is completely dry and there is no rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa ni nugbɔ enɛko lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so roots can absorb it safely; if put on bone-dry soil, concentrated chemical fertilizer stays near roots and can burn or destroy them.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛshwie shi bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ shweshweeshwe. Kɛji akɛ okɛ sũ ni egbi ni wu fata he lɛ Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni ebaanyɛ eshã loo efite amɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning pale yellow from the middle instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛjɛ teŋgbɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your crop lacks Nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green leaves. Applying urea or balanced NPK fertilizer near the roots gives the crop the nutrients it needs to turn healthy green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli Kɛ́ akɛ urea loo NPK ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛtsɔmɔ eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn dark brown and rotten before they are even ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni efiteɔ dani efee klalo po akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: This problem is called blossom end rot, which happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium or when watering is irregular. Keeping the soil consistently damp and adding agricultural lime or wood ash to the soil helps the fruits develop cleanly.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa loo kɛ́ nu lɛ haaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni okɛ lime loo tso sũ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua aduawai lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my mature cocoa trees dropping many of their young flowers without turning them into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso ni eda lɛ miiho fɔfɔi bibii babaoo ni etsɔko ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they experience stress from prolonged heat, dry soil, or attack by pests like mirids. Providing light shade, keeping soil covered with mulch, and treating pests promptly helps flowers develop into pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ pollen he. ni haa hulutsoo be mli Okɛ ŋmɔtɔ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ni ejieɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kɛyaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Leaving too many young shoots creates competition for water and food underground. Keeping only two or three healthy shoots ensures the main plant gets full nourishment to bear a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii bibii babaoo tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha akaŋshii aba kɛha nu kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ hi shi lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii babaoo ni ekɛwo tsei babaoo ni tsii.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot under the ground during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water builds up in the soil around them for too long. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ni ekã shi lɛ bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: Why do my freshly harvested seed yams refuse to sprout even when I plant them in wet soil right away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa ehee lɛ ekwɛɛɛ eyɛ mli akɛ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ moŋ?

english: Yams go through a natural rest period called dormancy after harvest. The seed yam needs a few months in a cool, dark storage barn before its internal clock wakes up and starts growing new shoots.
ga: Sweet potatoes yɛ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ he miihia nyɔji fioo komɛi yɛ shĩa ni mli ejɔ ni mli ewo duŋ mli dani amɛmli ŋmɛlɛtswaa lɛ ateshi ni ŋmeii heei aje shishi amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and looking small and twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bibii ni amɛfite lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is typically caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites feeding on the undersides of the leaves. Spraying with neem leaf extract or insecticidal soap removes these pests so new leaves grow out flat and broad.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ numɔ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ okɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie kooloi nɛɛ kɛjɛ ohe. Enɛ baaha baai heei lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.
