english: Why do weeds make my crops grow weak and thin even if my crops are taller than the weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ fe jwɛi lɛ moŋ

english: Weed roots spread aggressively underground and secretly steal water and fertilizer meant for your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures that all nutrients you put into the farm go directly to feeding your crop.
ga: Jwɛi shishifãi gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛjuɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ yɛ teemɔŋ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni okɛwoɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yaa tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛha onibii lɛ niyenii.

english: How does planting cowpeas on my farm help make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans have natural nodules on their roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When the cowpea plant decays, it leaves behind natural fertilizer that nourishes the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans yɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji cowpea tso lɛ fite Ebaashi adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekɛbaakwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ anɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my rice plants fall over flat into the mud right before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ miigbee muji lɛ mli dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Rice plants fall over, or lodge, when their stems are too weak to support heavy grain heads, often due to applying too much nitrogen or planting seeds too close together. Adding potassium fertilizer strengthens the stems so they stand upright.
ga: Omɔ tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi loo amɛkuɔ shi kɛ́ amɛshishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛfi dumɔwui ayitsei ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nitrogen babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ potassium ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaawo tsei lɛ ahe hewalɛ koni amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to intense heat and need shade to protect their tender leaves from burning and to keep the soil moist while their root systems develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa, ni amɛbiɔ hulutsoo koni amɛbu baai bibii lɛ ahe koni amɛkashã. kɛ koni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why do I need to heap soil into high mounds before planting my seed yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibuaa sũ naa yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ dani miduɔ ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Yams require loose, soft soil to expand their tubers freely, and raised mounds improve drainage to prevent waterlogging, which can rot the tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ he miihia sweet potato koni enyɛ ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Ni gɔŋ ni awó nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni nu lɛ aya hiɛ koni nu akabote mli. Enɛ baanyɛ aha yitso lɛ agbo.

english: Why are there small worms eating the inside leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ amli baai lɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that feeds on the central growing leaves of young maize and requires early intervention to protect crop yields.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ ŋmãa bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni ebiɔ ni akɛ he awo mli mra. Koni abu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe

english: This is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, a virus spread by tiny whiteflies that weakens the plant and reduces the size of the cassava roots.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Enɛ ji hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni haa tsei gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ daraaa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants shrinking and twisting together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Tiny sap-sucking pests like thrips or mites are feeding on the soft leaves, causing them to curl, harden, and stunt the overall growth of the plant.
ga: Kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites. baai bibii ni ayeɔ Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni etsĩɔ tso lɛ fɛɛ dalɛ naa.

english: Why should I wait until the ground is wet from rain before putting fertilizer on my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ amli?

english: Fertilizer requires water to dissolve so roots can absorb it, and applying fertilizer to dry soil can scorch and destroy the plant's root system.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ biɔ nu koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Ni shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã ni efite tsei lɛ ashishifãi.

english: How does planting groundnuts or beans help improve my soil for maize in the next season?
ga: Te ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ ni akɛbaadu ŋmãa yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, which acts as a natural fertilizer for heavy-feeding crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha niyenii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures are extremely hot or when plants experience water stress, both of which prevent successful pollination.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ na nu he haomɔ. Nibii enyɔ nɛɛ fɛɛ tsiɔ pollination naa koni ekaye omanye.

english: Extra shoots, known as suckers, compete with the main plant for nutrients and water, which results in smaller bunches and lower fruit quality.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ aniji feɔ bibii ni aduawai lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Why is my oil palm tree producing small bunches filled with empty fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ woɔ yibii bibii lɛ? Eyi obɔ kɛ aduawai ni bɛ nɔ ko?

english: Empty palm fruitlets usually occur due to insufficient pollination or a shortage of essential soil nutrients, particularly potassium.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni jɛɔ ŋmei yibii ni bɛ nɔ ko mli baa ji ŋmeii ni fa bɔ ni sa loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. titri lɛ, potasium

english: How do I know the right time to plant my seeds when the rains keep starting late every year?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui beni nugbɔ jeɔ shishi daa afi lɛ?

english: When rainfall patterns change, wait until the rains become steady for at least two weeks before planting, or switch to fast-maturing seed varieties that require shorter rainy seasons to grow fully.
ga: Beni nugbɔ lɛ tsakeɔ lɛ Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ aba shi kɛ hoo lɛ otsii enyɔ dani odu. aloo otsake kɛya dumɔwui srɔtoi ni daa oya ni biɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku dani amɛdara lɛ anɔ.

english: Why did my young corn plants wither when a strong sun came right after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulu lɛ ba yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Rapid shifts from heavy rain to intense heat cause thermal shock. The high sun quickly evaporates surface water and scorches tender foliage before weak young roots can absorb enough groundwater.
ga: Tsakemɔ ni baa oya kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛyaa latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ haa latsaa baa oya. Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ oya ni eshãa baai bibii dani shishifãi bibii lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why does my farm produce a small harvest compared to what other farmers get on the same size of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo pɛ kɛ akɛto okwaafoi krokomɛi ni yɔɔ he ni dalɛ tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Low harvest yields usually result from depleted soil nutrients, using low-quality seeds, improper crop spacing, or failing to protect crops from pests and heat stress early in their growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa lɛ mli baa ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa shi lɛ. Dumɔwui ni bɛ sɛɛnamɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii Tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni esaaa loo ni abuuu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he yɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee mli.

english: How can I grow crops so that I have produce to sell even during the long dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ madu ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛhɔ̃ɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ po mli?

english: You can farm through the dry months by using simple water conservation tools like drip irrigation or treadle pumps, combined with drought-tolerant crop varieties.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsu okwaayeli yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli kɛtsɔ nu he nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ drip irrigation loo pedal pump nɔ. kɛ tsei srɔtoi ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa lɛ fata he

english: Why do improved seed varieties cost more than the seeds I save from my own harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni asaa amɛhe lɛ jara wa fe dumɔwui ni mikɛtoɔ kɛjɛɔ mi diɛŋtsɛ mikpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Improved seeds are specially bred to fight off local diseases, endure harsh sun, and produce much higher yields, making the upfront cost worth the extra profit at harvest.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni akɛwu ashi maŋ lɛ mli helai. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ ni ehaa yibii babaoo baa Enɛ haa shika ni akɛwoɔ hiɛ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni sa sɛɛnamɔ kroko ni anáa yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ.

english: Why do crops grown from my local saved seeds produce uneven sizes during harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni mikɛto yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ amli lɛ wooo yibii ni dalɛ tamɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmaakpamɔi lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Saved seeds carry mixed genetic traits from previous seasons, causing individual plants to react differently to soil nutrients and sunshine, leading to non-uniform produce sizes.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ yɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ni jɛ be ni eho lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tso henɔ fɛɛ tso yɛ bɔ ni etsuɔ ​​niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la lɛ he nii eha. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ dalɛ jeee ekome.

english: What can I do to keep my farm soil from drying out too fast under the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ akagbi oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi?

english: Covering the ground around your plants with dry grass or leaves—a method called mulching—blocks direct heat, reduces water evaporation, and keeps the soil cool.
ga: Ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ nɔ. Atsɛɔ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ he nii lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ naa. Ehaa nu ni hoɔ lɛ baa shi ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ

english: Why do the leaves on my vegetable crops turn soft and droop during the hot afternoon hours?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-vegetables lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plants lose water rapidly through their leaves in high heat. They droop naturally to reduce their exposure to direct sunlight and conserve moisture until temperatures drop in the evening.
ga: Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli. Amɛbaa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ aba shi ni amɛha hulutsoo be lɛ ahi shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do market traders pay less money for my produce compared to crops brought from elsewhere?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jarayeli jarayelɔi woɔ mi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ ahe nyɔmɔ fioo kɛ akɛtoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛjɛɔ hei krokomɛi kɛbaa lɛ he lɛ?

english: Traders pay higher prices for uniform sizes, clean appearance, and defect-free crops. Improving your planting techniques and pest management helps meet these market quality standards.
ga: Nihɔɔlɔi woɔ jara ni nɔ kwɔ kɛha dalɛi ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ. hiɛ ni he tse kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ muji Nɔyaa ni yaa hiɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ he ŋaai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ashɛɔ nɛkɛ jarayeli hei nɛɛ ashishitoo mlai ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahe.

english: Will planting my seeds very close together give me more total harvest from my small plot of land?
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ni mikɛduɔ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ baaha maná yibii fɛɛ ni fa babaoo kɛjɛ he bibioo ko. mi nɔ loo daabi

english: No, planting too closely forces crops to fight each other for sunshine, soil food, and water, resulting in stunted, weak plants that produce a much smaller total yield.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛná hulu la, sũ mli niyenii, kɛ nu, ni no haa tsei ni egbɔjɔ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛwoɔ yibii fɛɛ ni baa shi kwraa lɛ baa.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow during the heavy rain season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes away nitrogen—the main food plants need to stay green—deeper into the soil where young roots cannot reach it. When the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil, it pulls nutrient reserves from its oldest lower leaves to keep the top growing, causing those lower leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ nitrogen—ni ji niyenii titri ko ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli lɛ—kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi bibii nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Kɛ tsei bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ejieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni etsɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ amli koni eha ŋwɛi tsei lɛ adara. Enɛ haa nakai baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do agricultural officers advise me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on the same land before planting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ dani madu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Beans and groundnuts are part of the legume family, which have small nodules on their roots that take nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into plant food. When the bean plants decay, they leave this free fertilizer in the soil, making it richer for the next crop like maize.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts fata legume weku ni yɔɔ shishifãi bibii lɛ ahe. Eheɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni etsakeɔ lɛ efeɔ tsei aniyenii. Beni ŋmei tso lɛ miifite lɛ Amɛshiɔ nɛkɛ ŋmei ni aheee nɔ ko nɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ewoɔ yibii kpakpai kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop so many tiny young pods before they can mature into big pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ? Mɛi babaoo dani amɛdara ni amɛtsɔmɔ ŋmeii wuji?

english: This natural process is called 'cherelle wilt.' The tree produces far more flowers and tiny pods than it has energy, water, or nutrients to feed, so it deliberately sheds a portion of them to ensure the remaining pods grow healthy and full.
ga: Atsɛɔ adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ ‘Cherelle Wilt’ Tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii bibii. Nɔ ni fe hewalɛ, nu loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ji niyenii. No hewɔ lɛ, ejɛ etsuiŋ eshi ekomɛi koni ekwɛ akɛ ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my plantain farm yield small bunches if I leave all the young shoots growing around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Kɛji mishi tsei bibii komɛi ni bɔle tso wulu lɛ he lɛ

english: Each young sucker shoot growing at the base acts like an extra mouth to feed. They drain water, soil nutrients, and sunlight away from the mother plant, so removing extra suckers leaves all the energy for the main stem to build a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Tso bibioo fɛɛ tso bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ naabu krɛdɛɛ ko ni atsɔɔ nɔ ayeɔ niyenii. Amɛjieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ mli. niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ mli No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, eshiɔ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ náa koni efee ŋmeii agbo ni tsii.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up tight during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a survival mechanism where the plant rolls its leaves to reduce the surface area exposed to the hot sun, preventing precious water from evaporating too quickly from its pores.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa wala. Tsei lɛ baafolɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛha he ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ ji koni nu ni jara wa lɛ akajɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli oya tsɔ.

english: Why do my harvested seed yams start sprouting in the barn even before I take them to the field to plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ bɔi shweremɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mikɛtee ŋmɔ mli po koni miyadu lɛ?

english: Yams have an internal biological clock called dormancy. Once a yam tuber rests for a set period after harvest, it automatically senses changes in temperature and air humidity, signaling that it is time to wake up and grow new vines.
ga: Atomɔ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswaa ko ni yɔɔ mli ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy. Kɛji akɛ sweet potato tubers lɛ jɔɔ amɛhe yɛ be pɔtɛɛ ko mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ Eyɔseɔ tsakemɔi ni baa yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli latsaa kɛ latsaa mli lɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Etsɔɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ ate shi ni adu wain tsei heei.

english: Why do my cassava tubers become hard and woody to boil if I leave them in the ground for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ wa ni amɛfee tsei waa akɛ amɛbaashã kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots are storage organs for starch, but as the plant gets past its ideal harvest age, it begins converting that soft starch into tough woody fibers to support its expanding heavy branches above ground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ji nibii ni akɛ starch toɔ. Shi beni tsei lɛ ho kpamɔ be ni sa lɛ he lɛ Ebɔi ŋmei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ tsakemɔ ewo tso mli tsɔi ni wa mli koni ekɛfi tsei niji ni tsii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ asɛɛ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning black and rotting while still on the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ be mli ni eyɔɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium while the fruit is growing rapidly. It usually happens when watering is irregular, preventing the plant roots from taking up continuous calcium from the soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida oya lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Enɛ haa tsei shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do weevils destroy my stored dried maize even when the cobs looked completely clean when I harvested them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii miifite mi-ŋmãa ni egbi ni mikɛto lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋshɔŋloo lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ehe tse beni mikpa lɛ moŋ.

english: Weevil insects often lay microscopic eggs inside the soft grain kernels while the maize is still standing in the field. When you store the grain in a warm storehouse, those hidden eggs hatch into larvae that eat the grain from the inside out.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ woɔ amɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli yɛ ŋmeii bibii amli be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ dumɔwui to nitoohe ko ni mli edɔ Nakai ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ fɔɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ.

english: Why do armyworms prefer attacking the dark central funnel of my young maize plants instead of the outer leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii sumɔɔ ni amɛtutua mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ duŋ lɛ moŋ fe kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ?

english: The central funnel (or whorl) contains the youngest, most tender leaves rich in moisture and nutrients, and it offers the worms a shaded, protected hiding spot away from predatory birds and direct sunlight.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ (loo whorl) lɛ mli ji baai bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo fe fɛɛ, ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii kpakpai babaoo yɔɔ mli. Ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ naa he ko ni yɔɔ hulutsoo, ni abuɔ he koni amɛtee amɛhe kɛjɛ okpoi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he.

english: Why do my maize leaves curl up and roll like tubes during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe tamɔ jwɛi kɛji akɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants roll their leaves during intense heat to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun. This helps the plant trap moisture inside and prevent water loss, acting like a natural defense mechanism against heat stress.
ga: Abele tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛmɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ amɛmli ni amɛtsiɔ nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ naa. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he.

english: Extreme heat damages the delicate pollen inside tomato flowers, making it impossible for the flowers to fertilize properly. When the plant senses it is too hot to sustain fruit growth, it drops its flowers to save energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɛɛ awo fɔmɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ tso lɛ nu he akɛ edɔ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ yibii lɛ adalɛ nɔ Ebaajie fɔfɔii koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Can the topsoil get too hot for my seeds to sprout after I plant them?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ baanyɛ adɔ tsɔ ni dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yes, direct heat from intense sunlight can overheat the top layer of soil, drying out the moisture required for germination and effectively baking sensitive seeds before they can break through the ground.
ga: Hɛɛ, dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli adɔ tsɔ. Enɛ haa nu ni he hiaa koni ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛ̃ lɛ agbi. ni ehaa dumɔwui ni nuɔ la he lɛ gboiɔ jogbaŋŋ dani amɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my harvested cocoa beans get very hot and produce a strong smell when covered under plantain leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa yibii ni mikpa lɛ mli edɔɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ waa kɛ́ mikɛha plantain baai ashishi lɛ?

english: Covering wet cocoa beans traps heat and gases created by tiny natural microbes breaking down the sweet pulp around the beans. This process, called fermentation, generates high heat which kills the bean seed and unlocks the rich chocolate flavor.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ ahe ni akɛhaa lɛ mɔɔ dɔlɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni adebɔɔ mli nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ jieɔ lɛ. No fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ŋɔɔ ni ebɔle kɔfe ŋmɔtɔ lɛ he lɛ. Atsɛɔ gbɛ nɛɛ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni fiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ ni ejieɔ amɛ tsokolate ni mli wa lɛ kpo.

english: If I place one ripe banana inside a closed basket of green mangoes, why do all the mangoes turn yellow so quickly?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ banana ni ekwɛ̃ wo mango eŋɔli ni atsĩ naa lɛ mli lɛ, Mɛni hewɔ mango lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ oya nɛkɛ?

english: Ripe fruits naturally produce an invisible gas called ethylene. When trapped inside a container, this ripening gas acts as a signal to surrounding green fruits, causing them to soften, turn yellow, and mature faster.
ga: Yibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ jieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ko ni anaaa ni atsɛɔ lɛ ethylene lɛ kpo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛji akɛ akɛwo tsɛnsi lɛ mli Nɛkɛ gas ni shwereɔ nɛɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ okadi kɛhaa aduawai eŋɔli ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, aduawai lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ. tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekwɛ̃ oya

english: Why is it necessary to dry my harvested cocoa beans in the sun heat before taking them to the buying clerk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni agbi kookoo ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani akɛha nitsulɔi ni heɔ nii lɛ?

english: Sunlight heat evaporates the deep moisture inside the bean, stopping bad gases, mold, and rot from developing, which keeps the cocoa good for storage and transportation.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli lɛ haa nu ni yɔɔ kɔfe yibii lɛ amli lɛ shwieɔ shi. Etsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fiteɔ nii, ŋmɔtɔ kɛ fitemɔ naa. Enɛ haa kookoo feɔ nɔ ni sa kɛha nitoo kɛ gbɛfaa.

english: How does spreading dry grass over my garden bed protect my crops from heat?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ abɔɔ mli saatso nɔ lɛ buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he?

english: Dry grass acts as mulch, serving as a protective shield between the hot sun and the soil. It lowers soil temperature and stops heat from quickly evaporating the groundwater away from crop roots.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ mulch. Etsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ni buɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ teŋ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dɔlɛ baa shi, ni ehaa dɔlɛ ni haa shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛjɛɔ tsei shishifãi amli lɛ kpaa.

english: When I pile up dry leaves and manure to make compost, why does the inside of the heap become hot?
ga: Kɛ́ mikɛ baai ni egbi lɛ to ŋmɔshi nibii ahe koni mikɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli dɔɔ lɛ?

english: Microorganisms like bacteria generate natural heat and gas as they eat and digest the organic matter inside the pile. High heat inside a compost heap shows that the waste is breaking down into rich fertilizer correctly.
ga: Nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli, tamɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ, feɔ dɔlɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ be mli ni amɛyeɔ ni amɛyeɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni yɔɔ ŋtayaa lɛ mli lɛ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato lɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ abaanyɛ afite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni afee ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why does my stored corn feel hot inside the sack when I open it after a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ nuɔ he akɛ edɔ yɛ kotoku lɛ mli kɛ́ agbele yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: If corn is stored with too much moisture, the grains continuing to breathe along with mold activity generate trapped heat and moisture gases, which can quickly spoil the whole bag if not re-dried.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmãa to he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baaya nɔ amɛmu be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ, ni ekɛ dɔlɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔi baa. Enɛ baanyɛ afite kotoku lɛ oya kɛji akɛ egbiko ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do young pepper plants grow faster under a clear plastic sheet than out in the open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsei bibii lɛ daa oya yɛ plastic ni mli tse shishi fe ŋmɔji ni mli tse lɛ amli lɛ?

english: The plastic cover traps the heat from sunlight and keeps warm air and humidity inside around the young seedlings, creating a cozy environment that speeds up their growth.
ga: Plastic ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ mɔ̃ɔ dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu la mli lɛ. ni emɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebɔleɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ, ni ehaa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni haa amɛdaraa oya lɛ baa.

english: Why do my crops start rotting when weeds grow too tall around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ be mli ni jwɛi kakadaji babaoo ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Tall weeds trap excessive moisture and block sunlight around your crops. This damp, dark environment creates perfect conditions for fungal diseases and bacteria to grow, causing stems and low-hanging fruits to rot.
ga: Jwɛi kakadaji lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nu ni fa fe nine ni amɛtsiɔ hulu la ni bɔleɔ onibii lɛ ahe lɛ naa. Nɛkɛ shihilɛ ni mli efɔ ni mli ewo duŋ nɛɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli baa lɛ baa. Enɛ haa tsei kɛ aduawai ni shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ lɛ fiteɔ.

english: How do weeds affect the growth of my young crops if I don't clear them early?
ga: Te jwɛi lɛ baaná miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ nɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ kɛji mijieee amɛ mra?

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that steal vital water, sunlight, and soil nutrients from your young crops. If left uncleared, they stunt crop growth and make the plants weak and prone to dying early.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ otsei bibii lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ ashi lɛ ni mli kãaa shi faŋŋ Ebaatsi tsei adalɛ naa. ni ehaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ekolɛ ebaagbo oya.

english: Why is it bad to wait until the farm is completely bush before I begin weeding?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi ŋmɔ lɛ mli eyi kɛ jwɛi dani obɔi jwɛi shwiemɔ lɛ?

english: When a farm becomes overgrown, thick weed roots drain the soil of essential plant food, and clearing them later damages the shallow roots of your crops, leading to weak growth and lower yields.
ga: Beni ŋmɔ lɛ ji ŋshɔkpɔ lɛ nɔ jwɛi shishifãi ni mli tse lɛ shwieɔ tsei lɛ amli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. ni kɛ́ ajie lɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaakpata ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ ahiɛ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo baa shi.

english: Does letting wild bushes grow near my farm attract pests that ruin my crops?
ga: Ani koo mli tsei bibii ni mihaa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ masɛi lɛ gbalaa kooloi ni fiteɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yes, wild bushes act as breeding grounds and hiding spots for farm pests like grasshoppers, rodents, and sap-sucking insects that travel into your farm to feed on your crops.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, koo mli jwɛi tsuɔ nii akɛ he ni ŋmɔ mli kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii, ŋmeii, kɛ kooloi ni nuɔ nu ni baa oŋmɔ lɛ mli koni amɛbaye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɔɔ yɛ kɛ he ni amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ.

english: Black pod rot is caused by a fungal mold that spreads quickly in cool, wet weather. Excessive shade, damp ground, and overgrown weeds make it easier for rainwater to splash these fungal spores onto healthy pods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod rot baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ lɛ. Shade ni fa fe nine, hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, kɛ jwɛi ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ nugbɔ nu lɛ baashwie nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ anɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: What causes cassava and other root crops to rot underground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni haa mɛi sumɔɔ cassava kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi waa? Ani ebaagbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani kpamɔ be lɛ aba?

english: Underground tuber rot usually happens when water gets trapped in waterlogged, uncleared soil. Excess water cuts off oxygen to the roots and lets soil bacteria break down and rot the tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tuber rot baa kɛji nu tsɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ ni mli tseee lɛ nɔ. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli. kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni eha ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ

english: Why does leaving spoiled or rotten crops on the farm affect my healthy plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite loo ni efite ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ saa mi tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Rotten plants carry infectious fungal spores and bacteria. Leaving them in the field allows rain and wind to carry these germs directly to your healthy standing crops, spreading the disease further.
ga: Fungal spores kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ tsei ni egboi amli. Kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ, ehaa nugbɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ helai nɛɛ yaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. ni amɛya nɔ amɛgbɛ hela lɛ amɛshwã

english: Why do my crops rot faster when they are planted too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Planting crops too close together cuts off fresh airflow between the leaves. Moisture stays trapped on the plant surface for too long after rain, giving rot-causing fungi the wet environment they need to spread.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ yɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Fɛ̃i hiɔ tsei lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmei ni egbo lɛ baa he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ he ni esumɔɔ ni egbɛ eshwa lɛ.

english: How often should I clear my farm to prevent crops from failing?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mafo miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni ŋmɔshi nibii akafite?

english: Clearing weeds at least two to three times during the growing season—especially right after the rainy season starts—keeps moisture levels balanced, improves sunlight exposure, and protects crops from disease.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, jwɛi ni ajieɔ shii enyɔ loo shii etɛ yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ—titri lɛ beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eje shishi lɛ—yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ feɔ ekome, ehaa hulu la lɛ yaa hiɛ, ni ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ahe.

english: Why do my crops look yellow and produce small fruits when the farm ground is covered in dense weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ewoɔ yibii bibii lɛ? Beni jwɛi eyi ŋmɔ lɛ mli babaoo lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves mean your crops are starving for nitrogen and sunlight because surrounding weeds are absorbing all the plant food from the soil and blocking the sun.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen kɛ hulu la bɛ onibii amli. Yɛ jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ahewɔ Ejieɔ tsei lɛ amli niyenii fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni etsĩɔ hulu la naa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to build strong, green leaves. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts on my farmland makes the soil better for other crops later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ midu ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which has tiny bumps on its roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil. When the crop is harvested, this stored nitrogen acts as natural fertilizer for your next crop, such as maize.
ga: Peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni mɔɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Beni akpaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Nitrogen ni ato nɛɛ baatsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why are there small holes on my young maize leaves and tiny caterpillars hiding inside them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ji ŋmeii lɛ? Mi nɔ lɛ yɛ bu bibioo ko. Akɛtee mli?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that feeds on the tender growing center of maize plants. Spraying recommended biopesticides early in the morning or late evening when the worms are active helps prevent total crop loss.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa titri ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ ateŋ lɛ. Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni kooloi lɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ akafite.

english: Why does leaving weeds in my crop field reduce the amount of harvest I get at the end of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mishiɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmaa ni minine shɛɔ nɔ yɛ be lɛ naagbee lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, soil nutrients, and sunlight. Clearing weeds early ensures your crop plants get all the nourishment they need to grow big and produce a rich yield.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la, ni jieɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive, tender leaves that dry out and burn easily in strong heat. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains protects the young cocoa from harsh sunlight during its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni nuɔ he waa ni amɛgbiɔ ni amɛshãa oya yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa yɛ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Yam leaves need to spread out high off the ground to catch as much sunlight as possible. The leaves use sunlight to manufacture food, which travels down to swell the underground tuber.
ga: Ehe miihia ni agbɛ sweet potato baai lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni hulu la ashɛ amɛhe bɔ ni aaanyɛ. Baai kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛ feɔ niyenii. ni fãa gbɛ kɛyaa shi ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ

english: Why should I cut down some of the small shoots growing around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he Ajie midumɔwu titri lɛ shishi.

english: Having too many shoots around one plantain tree causes them to steal food and water from each other. Removing extra suckers leaves only the strongest shoot, allowing it to grow a larger and heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: Ni aaaná dumɔwui babaoo ni ebɔle amɛhe Dumɔwui kome pɛ baaha amɛju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ amɛhe. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ ashiɔ. Ehaa plantain ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ agboi ni amɛhe wa.

english: Flower dropping is usually caused by environmental stress, such as extreme heat, poor watering, or lack of insect pollinators. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch helps the plant hold onto its flowers and form fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shihilɛ mli haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni ehiii ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ fiteɔ lɛ baa. aloo kooloi bibii ni haa fɔfɔii lɛ faaa lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ muji wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why are my cassava plants producing long, thin roots instead of big, thick cassava tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ shishifãi kakadaji ni yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ shishifãi wuji ni mli tseee lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots stay thin if the soil is too hard and compact for them to expand, or if the soil lacks potassium. Softening the soil during land preparation and ensuring balanced nutrients allows the roots to swell properly.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ baafee bibioo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa ni ebɔle ehe tsɔ ni enyɛŋ egbɛ eshwa. Aloo kɛji akɛ potassium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni afee lɛ blɛoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ be mli ni akwɛ koni niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ afee nɔ ni sa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛshwereɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl during hot hours as a natural defense mechanism to reduce their surface area and save water from evaporating too fast. Providing adequate irrigation and mulching around the roots helps keep the plants hydrated.
ga: Ha ni ebɔle ehe yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni baaha ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ aba shi ni ekɛtsi nu lɛ naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ sũ ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ mli fũuɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting if I leave them in the ground too long after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots absorb excess water during heavy rains. If left in waterlogged soil, oxygen is cut off, causing soil fungi and bacteria to multiply and rot the underground tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu ni fa fe nine yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, afoɔ Oxygen lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ faa babaoo ni amɛfiteɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ.

english: How do I select the best cassava stems for planting to get big, healthy tubers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei tso ni hi fe fɛɛ ni madu koni maná ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ?

english: Select cuttings from the middle section of mature, healthy cassava plants that are 8 to 18 months old. Middle stems sprout faster and produce stronger roots than soft green tops or dry bases.
ga: Halamɔ ŋmeii ni afolɔ kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eda ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 18 lɛ teŋgbɛ. Teŋgbɛ tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya ni ebaawo shishifãi ni mli wa fe ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli loo shishifãi ni egbi lɛ.

english: Why do some cassava varieties produce plenty of gari while others yield very little solid product?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi komɛi woɔ gari babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni kooloi srɔtoi komɛi jieɔ nibii ni wa fioo ko pɛ kpo lɛ?

english: Different cassava varieties have varying starch and water content. Varieties with high starch yield more dry gari or flour, while high-moisture varieties carry more water and yield less solid food after processing.
ga: Kasava henɔi srɔtoi Ashikiŋsha kɛ nu falɛi srɔtoi yɛ. Starch henɔi ni fa babaoo lɛ haa gari loo starch ni egbi babaoo baa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii srɔtoi ni mli edɔ waa lɛ hiɛɔ nu babaoo ni amɛhaaa niyenii ni wa babaoo aba beni atsu he nii agbe naa lɛ.

english: Why does cassava stored in the ground lose its quality when the new rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei ni akɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: When the rainy season begins, the cassava plant starts growing new branches and leaves. To do this, it draws energy and starch directly out of its underground roots, making the tubers watery and light.
ga: Kɛji akɛ abote nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmei tso lɛ baabɔi niji kɛ baai heei kwɛ̃mɔ. Bɔni afee ni efee enɛ Ejieɔ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi amli tɛ̃ɛ. Ha yitso lɛ mli ajɔ ni efee mlɛo.

english: Yellowing starting from the bottom leaves upward is a sign of nitrogen deficiency. The plant shifts the limited nitrogen it has from older leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen fioo ko kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi shweremɔ hee lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or beans next to my maize make the maize stalks greener and stronger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and cowpeas pull nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots, naturally feeding neighboring crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ ŋmãa

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist after a gentle rain, but not right before heavy downpours. Granules need moisture to dissolve into the soil where roots can reach them before heavy rain washes them away.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Shi kaafee nakai pɛpɛɛpɛ dani nugbɔ nɛ waa. Fɛ̃i he miihia pellets lɛ koni amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, he ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ amɛhe dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ahoɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin without producing heavy fruits when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛwooo yibii ni tsii beni midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, they compete for sunlight and stretch upward instead of developing thick stems and strong fruit. Proper spacing allows sunlight and air to reach the whole plant.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛbaatswa hulu la he akaŋ ni amɛbaafee kakadaŋŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaana tsei ni mli tse kɛ aduawai ni mli wa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ he.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers without forming peppers during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni efeee pepper yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses pepper plants, causing them to drop flowers to conserve water and survive rather than spending energy to feed new fruits.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ nyɛɔ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛshwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni akɛye aduawai heei

english: Why do weeds make my main crops stay small even when there is enough soil in the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ feɔ bibioo eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than most cultivated crops, taking up water, soil nutrients, and root space before your main crop roots can reach them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni aduɔ lɛ babaoo, ni amɛmɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. kɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe dani tso lɛ shishifãi titri lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he.

english: Why are some sweet potatoes orange inside while others are white or yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii komɛi yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu ji ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Different sweet potato varieties have different nutrients inside them. Orange sweet potatoes are rich in Vitamin A, which is good for eyes and general health, while white and yellow varieties usually have more starch but less Vitamin A.
ga: Sweet potato henɔ fɛɛ henɔ yɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ srɔtoi. Orange sweet potatoes lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ vitamin A. ni hi kɛha hiŋmɛii kɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ hewalɛnamɔ fɛɛ yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ henɔi lɛ fɔɔ starch babaoo shi vitamin A faaa.

english: How do I choose between planting white sweet potatoes and orange sweet potatoes on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ateŋ?

english: It depends on what your market wants and your soil conditions. White sweet potatoes often store longer and have high starch, while orange ones grow fast, fetch good prices due to high nutritional value, and are popular for feeding children.
ga: Edamɔ nɔ ni he hiaa ojarayelihe lɛ kɛ bɔ ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ nɔ. Sweet potatoes yɛŋ lɛ fɔɔ shihilɛ be kakadaŋŋ ni starch fa yɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ ni ji ŋmɔtɔ ni ji ŋmɔtɔ lɛ daa oya. Ekɛ jara kpakpa haa yɛ niyenii ni mli wa ni eyɔɔ lɛ hewɔ. ni ehe gbɛi waa kɛha gbekɛbii atsɔsemɔ

english: Why are the leaves on my crop turning pale yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Leaves turn pale yellow when the plant lacks important soil nutrients like nitrogen, or when the roots are getting too much water and cannot breathe properly.
ga: Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, loo kɛji shishifãi lɛ ná nu babaoo ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu jogbaŋŋ.

english: What happens if I plant my sweet potato vines too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu sweet potato wain tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: If you plant them too close, the vines will fight for sunlight and soil nutrients. The plant will grow plenty of green leaves on top, but the tubers underground will stay very small and thin.
ga: Kɛji odu amɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Wein tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Tso lɛ baaná baai eŋɔli babaoo yɛ ŋwɛi. Shi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ daraaa kwraa ni amɛhe yɛ mlɛo.

english: Should I plant the sweet potato tuber itself into the ground, or should I use the green vines?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ loo mikɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ atsu nii?

english: It is best to plant fresh vine cuttings from healthy plants rather than the tuber. Vine cuttings grow faster, produce healthier roots, and yield bigger tubers than planting the potato directly.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu wain tsei heei ni afolɔ kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ mli moŋ fe bulbs. Kɛ́ afo wain tso lɛ, ebaada oya. Ha shishifãi lɛ awa ni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji fe ŋmeii ni aduɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do farmers make mounds or ridges before planting sweet potatoes instead of planting on flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi maa gɔji loo ŋmeii dani amɛduɔ ŋmeii yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaadu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Mounds and ridges create soft, loose soil that allows sweet potato roots to easily expand into big tubers. It also helps excess rainwater drain away so the roots do not rot.
ga: Gɔji kɛ ŋshɔkei lɛ feɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni etse ehe ni haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ sweet potato shishifãi lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛtsɔ bulbs agboi. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ koni shishifãi lɛ akafite.

english: Why do my sweet potato tubers come out with small holes and black marks inside them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔji lɛ amli buji bibii lɛ? ni okadii diji yɛ mli

english: This is caused by sweet potato weevil insects. Piling soil high around the base of the plant (earthing up) covers soil cracks so the insects cannot reach the tubers.
ga: Atomɔ ŋmei kɛ enɛ baa. Okɛ sũ lɛ ato shishigbɛ lɛ he kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ (muji) koni eye ebua ni ekɛtsi sũ lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ anaa ni eha kooloi akashɛ bulb lɛ he.

english: How can I know that my sweet potatoes under the ground are ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potatoes ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ eshɛ he koni akpa?

english: Sweet potatoes are usually ready 3 to 4 months after planting. You will notice the green vines starting to dry out and turn yellow, but you can also dig up one test plant to see if the tubers are big enough.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ, sweet potato lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu. Obaana akɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgbiɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ. Shi obaanyɛ okɛ kaa tso kome atsu nii ni okwɛ kɛji bulb lɛ da bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my sweet potatoes spoil quickly after I dig them out of the earth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ fiteɔ oya beni mifo amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Sweet potatoes rot quickly if their skin gets bruised or cut during harvesting. Handling them carefully and letting them dry in a shady, well-ventilated area for a few days cures the skin and makes them last longer.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ atswa hewolo lɛ loo afo lɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli. Kɛ́ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ tsu he nii ni oha egbi yɛ he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ gbii fioo komɛi lɛ, ebaaye ebua hewolo lɛ ni etsa ni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Does the color of the sweet potato change how long I can keep it after harvesting?
ga: Ani ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ahe su tsakeɔ beni akpa lɛ sɛɛ? Be enyiɛ manyɛ mikɛto?

english: Yes, white and light yellow sweet potatoes generally have thicker skins and higher starch, making them last longer in storage than orange varieties, which have softer flesh and require gentler handling.
ga: Hɛɛ, bei pii lɛ, sweet potatoes yɛŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ hewolo ni mli tse ni starch fa yɛ mli. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ akɛ amɛ toɔ be kakadaŋŋ fe ŋmeii srɔtoi ni yɔɔ loo ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni biɔ ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why is the government asking us to cut down our cocoa trees when some of them are still bearing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nɔyeli lɛ biɔ ni wɔfolɔ kookoo tsei lɛ be mli ni ekomɛi woɔ yibii lolo lɛ?

english: Trees infected with Swollen Shoot disease or old viral infections carry diseases that spread through insects to healthy farms nearby. Cutting down affected trees stops the spread and allows you to replant healthy seedlings that will yield more in the long run.
ga: Tsei ni bud swelling loo virus hela momo ko emɔ amɛ lɛ hiɛɔ hela lɛ, ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ kooloi bibii amli kɛyaa ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ ni oookpa lɛ baaha egbɛ eshwa, ni ebaaha okwɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni baawo yibii babaoo yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa tree is sick from swollen shoot disease just by looking at the leaves and stems?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ kookoo tso ko miipiŋ yɛ ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ ahe kɛtsɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛkɛ nɔ?

english: Infected trees usually show swollen nodes on young shoots, clear yellow patterns along leaf veins, and stunted pods that fail to grow to normal size before dying back.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ jieɔ ŋmeii ni efuu yɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ kpo. Ayɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni mli tse yɛ baa lɛ fãji lɛ ahe. kɛ dwarfed pods ni edaaa kɛyashɛɛɛ bɔ ni sa dani amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do crops planted close to rivers and streams grow differently than those planted on top of hill slopes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni aduɔ yɛ faai kɛ kpaakpoi ahe lɛ daraa yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ fe tsei ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji anɔ lɛ?

english: Soils near riverbanks retain moisture longer and contain rich washed-down nutrients, but too much trapped water can cause root rot, whereas hilltop soils dry out faster during hot dry seasons.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ faa lɛ naa lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ, ni niyenii ni mli ewo muji babaoo yɛ mli. Shi nu babaoo baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ agbo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ gɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why does my cocoa farm produce smaller pods after several years of farming on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii beni ekwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Over time, crop harvests remove key plant nutrients from the soil; without replenishing the land with nutrients or organic compost, the soil gets exhausted and trees produce smaller fruits.
ga: Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa lɛ jieɔ tsei amli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni akɛ niyenii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fataaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ewo wu ni tso lɛ woɔ yibii bibii.

english: How long does a new hybrid cocoa seedling take to start bearing pods after planting?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani hybrid cocoa dumɔwui heei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii beni adu amɛ sɛɛ?

english: Improved hybrid cocoa varieties are bred to grow faster and typically produce their first pods within two to three years under good shade and regular weeding.
ga: Akwɛ kookoo henɔi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ koni amɛdara oya. ni bei pii lɛ ebaawo eklɛŋklɛŋ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ afii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ mli yɛ hulutsoo kpakpa kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa lɛ shishi.

english: Overcrowding prevents sunlight from reaching lower branches and reduces airflow, creating excessive humidity that allows fungal diseases like black pod to spread quickly.
ga: Nibii ni eyi obɔ lɛ haaa hulu la ashɛ tsei niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ahe, ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ babaoo baa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji black pods lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: Is it safe for my young cocoa trees if I plant cassava on the same farm during the first year?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli?

english: Cassava roots grow very large and aggressive, taking away essential nutrients and water from young cocoa seedlings; temporary food crops like plantain or cocoyam provide better shade without killing the seedlings.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ daa ni amɛhe wa. Ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ cacao tsei bibii amli. Niyenii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains loo cocoa haa hulutsoo kpakpa ni egbeee dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn yellow and drop off during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa leaves turn yellow and drop off when intense heat and direct sunlight dry out the moisture inside the plant; maintaining temporary shade trees reduces sun stress.
ga: Cocoa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ ha nu ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ gĩ. Tsei ni akɛhaa amɛ be kukuoo mli hulutsoo lɛ haa nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛɔ hulu la mli baa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why does cutting off water sprouts and excess branches help my cocoa tree yield more pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni tso lɛ mli nu ni fa fe nine kɛ eniji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-cacao tso lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii babaoo lɛ?

english: Water sprouts and crowded branches consume water and food from the soil without producing fruit; pruning them directs nutrients straight into pod development.
ga: Nu tsei ni mli eyi kɛ tsei aniji lɛ yeɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni amɛwooo yibii. Pruning kudɔɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛyaa pod lɛ shweremɔ he.

english: Why do cocoa pods rot and turn black when heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall causes fungal spores in the soil to splash onto low-hanging pods, and high moisture levels allow the black pod fungus to infect and destroy the fruit rapidly.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. Ni hulutsoo ni fa babaoo lɛ baanyɛ aha black pod fungus lɛ atswa aduawai lɛ oya ni efite.

english: Why should I buy plant seedlings from a certified lab nursery instead of using seeds from my own harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe tsei dumɔwui kɛjɛ laboratori ni yɔɔ hegbɛ ni akɛkwɛɔ tsei amli lɛ mli? Mohu ɔ, i kɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mikpamɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii.

english: Certified lab seedlings are carefully bred and tested to be free from hidden diseases. They grow into stronger plants, resist local pests better, and yield far more crop than seeds saved from previous harvests.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ laboratorii ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ amli lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni akaa amɛ akwɛɔ koni helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ bɛ mli. Amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ tsei ni he wa. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni aŋmala ashwie shi kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ.

english: How can I test if a batch of seeds will actually sprout before I waste time planting them in my big field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji dumɔwui komɛi baakwɛ̃ diɛŋtsɛ dani mafite be kɛdu amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ agbo lɛ mli?

english: You can place ten seeds in a wet cloth inside a plastic bag for three to five days; if at least eight sprout, the seed batch is healthy and ready for planting.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ dumɔwui 10 awo plastic kotoku mli gbii etɛ kɛyashi enumɔ. Kɛji kɛ hoo lɛ tsei kpaanyɔ yɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni esa akɛ adu.

english: Why do the leaves on my vegetable crops droop during the hot afternoon but stand up straight again by morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, shi amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ ekoŋŋ leebi lɛ?

english: In the hot afternoon sun, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it from the soil. Overnight, when it cools down, the roots catch up and refill the plant with water.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Gbi gbɛkɛ beni edɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baaje kpo ni amɛkɛ nu baafata tso lɛ he.

english: Yellowing lower leaves mean your soil is low on nitrogen, which is the main food crops use to grow green leaves. Adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer will restore their healthy color.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii tso titri ni akɛduɔ baai eŋɔli lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha ehiɛ afee fɛo ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the blossoms falling off my tomato plants without turning into any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ tomato tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they are stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients, choosing to save their energy rather than produce fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ hao amɛ. Amɛhalaa akɛ amɛbaakwɛ hewalɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when there are no taller shade plants around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ be mli ni cacao tsei ni kɛlɛ fe no bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under intense sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain beside them protects them from harsh sun and keeps moisture in the ground.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ Emasɛi lɛ baabu tsei ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa he ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Why do my cassava plants stay thin with small tubers when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Ani ekomɛi yɛ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When crops are crowded together, their roots fight each other for limited water and soil food. Giving each plant proper distance allows roots to expand and grow thick tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni fa fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni sa yɛ tso fɛɛ tso teŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni mli wa.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and turning thick and bumpy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Curling leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites hiding underneath and sucking out the plant's sap, which deforms the new growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo shishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Enɛ baaha dalɛ hee lɛ afee nɔ ni efite.

english: Why do my tomato seedlings wilt and rot right at the soil line a few days after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni midu lɛ?

english: This is caused by soil fungi attacking young stems, often due to excess water around the stem base or planting in infected soil.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni tutuaa tsei bibii lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni fa fe nine ni ebɔle he lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Stem base loo dumɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni hela emɔ nɔ

english: What basic routine should I follow when walking through my field to spot crop problems early?
ga: Mɛɛ shishijee nifeemɔi esa akɛ mafee kɛji minyiɛ ŋmɔji amli koni mana ŋmɔshi nibii amli naagbai mra?

english: Walk through your farm every few days in a zig-zag pattern, checking under leaves for insects and examining stems and new leaves for unusual spots or color changes so you can treat problems before they spread.
ga: Nyiɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa gbi. Gbii fioo komɛi yɛ zigzag gbɛ nɔ Kwɛmɔ baai shishi kɛji ŋmeii yɛ. ni okwɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai heei lɛ amli kɛji nɔ ko ni yɔɔ srɔto loo amɛhe su tsake. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ otsa naagbai dani amɛgbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why does it take so long to pluck oil palm nuts off the bunch one by one?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ be babaoo dani ajieɔ mu tso mli ŋmeii kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ?

english: Picking oil palm nuts individually by hand is very slow because the fruits are tightly bound to the tough stalks. Using bulk separation techniques like covering the bunch allows the nuts to loosen naturally, saving time and labor.
ga: Oil palm aduawai ashishifãi ni akɛ niji shwieɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ fioo ejaakɛ aduawai lɛ kpɛtɛɔ tso lɛ shishi ni wa lɛ he. Kɛ akɛ mass separation technique tamɔ ni akɛfiɔ nii ahe lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha nut lɛ agbɔjɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Okɛ be kɛ nitsumɔ ato

english: What happens to palm fruit bunches when I cover them with tarpaulins or leaves after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni baa palm aduawai akui anɔ kɛ́ mikɛ tarpaulin loo baai ha amɛhe beni akpa amɛkpamɔ sɛɛ?

english: Covering harvested palm bunches traps heat and moisture, which weakens the stalks connecting the nuts to the bunch. This softens the attachment points so most of the nuts naturally fall off quickly.
ga: Palm tso ni akpa lɛ nɔ ni akɛhaa lɛ haa dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i hiɔ shi. Enɛ baaha tso ni kɛ nut lɛ tsaa tso lɛ he lɛ agbɔjɔ. Enɛ baaha ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ afee blɛoo. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmeii babaoo shwieɔ shi oya yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why don't all the palm nuts fall off the bunch even after I leave them covered for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei dumɔwui lɛ gbeeee shi kɛjɛɛɛ ŋmei lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ amɛhe eha amɛhe gbii babaoo moŋ?

english: Nuts tucked deep inside the center of the bunch or those harvested slightly underripe hold on tighter to the stalk. These stubborn remaining nuts need a light manual shake or stripping after the main batch falls off.
ga: Beans ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ loo ŋmeii ni akpaa lɛ eshɛko fioo, amɛmɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ. Ehe miihia ni akɛ niji akpokpo loo ajie nɛkɛ ŋmeii ni eshwɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɛɛ fioo beni ŋmeii titri lɛ egbee shi lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do some oil palm fruits loosen easily from the stalk while others stay stuck hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mu tso yibii komɛi jeɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli oya shi ekrokomɛi hu hiɔ shi shiŋŋ lɛ?

english: Fully ripe palm nuts naturally form a weak layer at their base as they mature, while less ripe or tightly packed inner nuts retain strong fibers that keep them stuck to the stalk.
ga: Palm ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ feɔ fã ko ni bɛ hewalɛ yɛ amɛshishigbɛ, yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii ni eshɛko loo ni ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa ni kpɛtɛɔ tso lɛ he lɛ.

english: How can I speed up the process of separating my harvested oil palm nuts from the heavy bunches?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafee nibii ni akɛgbalaa mu ni akpa kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni tsii amli lɛ oya?

english: Instead of cutting nuts individually, covering the bunches for a short period lets natural warmth loosen the fruit. You can then easily shake or thrash the bunch to collect the nuts much faster.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofolɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli bibii bibii Oha ŋmeii lɛ anɔ be kukuoo ko Enɛ baaye abua ni adebɔɔ mli latsaa lɛ aha aduawai lɛ ajɔɔ amɛhe. No sɛɛ lɛ obaanyɛ okpokpo loo otswa ŋmeii lɛ koni obua ŋmeii lɛ anaa oya kwraa.

english: How do I make sure I do not waste palm nuts when separating them from the main bunch?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ mifiteee ŋmei ŋmeii beni migbalaa amɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmei wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the bunches on a clean mat or tarpaulin allows most nuts to drop off without getting lost in the soil, making it easy to gather the loose ones and clean up the few that stay attached.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tsɔne ni he tse loo tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli lɛ ha dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ babaoo ajo foi ni amɛgbeeee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ abaabua dumɔwui ni etse lɛ anaa ni ajie nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni etsi ehe lɛ.

english: Does trapped heat really help in separating harvested fruits from crop stalks?
ga: Ani la ni mli edɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa diɛŋtsɛ yɛ yibii ni akpa lɛ mligbalamɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ mli?

english: Yes, trapped heat speeds up natural biochemical changes in the plant tissue connecting the fruit to the stalk, causing the joint to soften and release the fruit cleanly.
ga: Hɛɛ, la ni mli edɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ amli tsakemɔi ni yaa nɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli fãji ni kɛ tso lɛ yibii lɛ tsaa lɛ mli lɛ yaa oya. Enɛ haa fãji lɛ feɔ blɛoo, ni ehaa aduawai lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ gbɛ ni he tse nɔ.

english: At what point in handling my oil palm nuts should I start using a processing machine?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mabɔi tsɔne ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ mu mli lɛ he nitsumɔ?

english: You should bring in a machine after the nuts have been separated from the large stalks and gathered, as the machine is designed to process loose nuts efficiently rather than whole, bulky bunches.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ tsɔne lɛ aba beni ajie ŋmeii lɛ kɛjɛ ŋmeii wuji lɛ amli ni abua naa lɛ sɛɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, afee tsɔne lɛ koni ekɛ ŋmeii ni etse ehe lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ kuu agbo muu fɛɛ najiaŋ

english: Why is it important to separate palm nuts from the main stalk before putting them into a machine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie ŋmei ŋmeii kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ mli dani akɛwo tsɔne lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Processing machines work best on loose nuts. Feeding large, hard stalks into the machine can clog the mechanism, damage the blades, and reduce the amount of oil you extract.
ga: Nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmeii ni etse amɛhe. Kɛ́ okɛ tso agbo ko ni wa wo tsɔne lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ etsi tsɔne lɛ naa, efite tsɔne lɛ mli tsɔnei lɛ, ni eha mu ni ojieɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Will leaving harvested oil palm bunches covered in the sun spoil the oil inside the nuts?
ga: Ani mu tsei ni akpa lɛ ni ashiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ baafite mu ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Covering bunches for a short period of 1 to 3 days safely loosens the fruit, but leaving them covered for too long can cause over-fermentation, which increases acidity and lowers oil quality.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ha aduawai lɛ ahe yɛ kui amli gbii 1 kɛyashi 3 be kukuoo ko lɛ, ebaaha aduawai lɛ agbɔjɔ shweshweeshwe. Shi kɛ́ ashi ni aha nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha edɔ fe nine. Enɛ haa acidity lɛ yaa hiɛ ni ehaa mu lɛ mli ehiii.

english: Why do I need to clear thick weeds and bushes from my land before planting cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛ jwɛi bibii kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu kookoo dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Overgrown weeds and bushes steal water, sunlight, and nutrients from young cocoa seedlings. Clearing the land ensures your new plants get enough resources and aren't choked out or damaged by pests hiding in the bush.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ juɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ cacao tsei bibii amli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oootsi lɛ haa otsei heei lɛ náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa. ni kooloi bibii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo jwɛi lɛ amli lɛ akagbala amɛ loo amɛkafite amɛ.

english: What is the best time of the year for me to plant cocoa seedlings on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ afi lɛ mli be ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu kookoo dumɔwui yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: The best time to plant is at the beginning of the main rainy season (usually around May or June in Ghana). This allows the young seedlings to get plenty of rain to build strong roots before the dry season arrives.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu ji nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee. Nugbɔshiimɔ be (bei pii lɛ, aaafee May loo June yɛ Ghana) lɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ naa nugbɔ babaoo koni amɛma shishifãi ni wa dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baashɛ.

english: Why must I leave proper space between cocoa trees instead of planting them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ashi gbɛ ni sa yɛ kookoo tsei lɛ ateŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Spacing cocoa trees properly (typically 3 meters by 3 meters) gives their roots and leaves room to spread. It also allows air to flow through the farm, which reduces fungal diseases like black pod.
ga: Kookoo tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa (bei pii lɛ mitai 3 x mitai 3) baaha shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ hu tsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji black pods lɛ baa shi.

english: What will happen to my cocoa seedlings if I plant them in full sun without any shade?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily in harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains or cassava alongside cocoa protects the young seedlings until they grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya kɛji akɛ hulu la ni naa wa shɛ amɛnɔ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo cassava yɛ cocoa masɛi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la lɛ fɛɛ.

english: How should I care for my cocoa seedlings if I cannot plant them into the soil immediately after receiving them?
ga: Te esa akɛ makwɛ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ anɔ aha tɛŋŋ? Ni kɛji akɛ anyɛɛɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni aná dumɔwui lɛ hu?

english: Keep the seedlings in a cool, shaded area protected from strong winds, and water them every day so the soil in their bags stays moist until you are ready to plant them.
ga: Ha dumɔwui lɛ ahi he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni shade yɔɔ koni abu he kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he. Ni okɛ nu awo mli daa gbi koni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi obaafee klalo akɛ obaadu.

english: How do I know if the soil on my land is good enough to grow cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu kookoo?

english: Good cocoa soil should be deep, dark, rich in decayed leaves, and well-drained so water does not sit on top like a swamp, as standing water can rot the tree roots.
ga: Esa akɛ kookoo shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ afee nɔ ni mli kwɔ, ni edɔ, ni baai ni fiteɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli. ni etsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ Bɔni afee ni nu lɛ akatara nɔ tamɔ ŋshɔ. Ejaakɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei ashishifãi agbo.

english: How long will it take for my new hybrid cocoa seedlings to start giving me pods?
ga: Be enyiɛ ebaahe dani mi-hybrid cocoa dumɔwui heei lɛ aje shishi amɛfee pods?

english: With good care, weed control, and proper shade management, modern hybrid cocoa varieties usually start flowering and producing pods within 2 to 3 years after planting.
ga: kɛ jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ hulutsoo be ni sa Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo ni akɛfee tsofai lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔii ashishi ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ.

english: Yellow, dry leaves are usually a sign that the plant is getting too much direct sunlight, lacks water, or is missing nutrients in the soil. Adding shade and watering during dry spells helps them recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni egboi ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miiná hulu la babaoo tɛ̃ɛ, nu efo emli, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo be kɛ nu fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhe waaa.

english: Why is regular weeding so important even after my cocoa trees have started growing tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ daa yɛ be mli ni mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ebɔi shweremɔ po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds harbor insect pests and diseases that can climb onto your cocoa trees. Regular weeding keeps the farm clean, makes harvesting easier, and ensures fertilizer goes directly to your cocoa trees.
ga: Jwɛi ji he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai fɔɔ yɛ. ni baanyɛ akwɔ o-cacao tso lɛ nɔ Jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔ lɛ mli tseɔ. Ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii akpamɔ feɔ mlɛo ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa o-cocoa tsei lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How can I tell when a cocoa pod on my tree is fully ripe to pick?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ kookoo ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: A cocoa pod is ready to harvest when its color changes completely—usually turning from green to bright yellow, or from red to an orange-yellow color. Unripe green pods will spoil the beans if picked too early.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji amɛhe su etsake kwraa. Bei pii lɛ, etsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. aloo kɛjɛ red kɛyashi yellow-orange Pods ni ji eŋɔli ni eshɛko lɛ baafite ŋmeii lɛ kɛji akɛ ajie amɛ mra tsɔ.

english: Why do the maize seeds I brought from another region grow differently on my land here?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛbaa kɛjɛɔ kpokpai krokomɛi anɔ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ biɛ lɛ?

english: Crops react to local soil composition, rain patterns, and temperatures. Seed varieties adapted to one region may need time to adjust or may require different fertilizer and water management to thrive in a new environment.
ga: Dumɔwui haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, kɛ dɔlɛ. Dumɔwui srɔtoi ni atsake amɛhe kɛtee kpokpaa kome nɔ lɛ baanyɛ ahe be dani amɛtsake amɛhe loo amɛbaanyɛ amɛbi ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu he gbɛjianɔtoo srɔtoi koni amɛshwere yɛ shihilɛ hee mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither when exposed to full sunlight during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and delicate root systems that burn easily under direct heat. They require partial shade from nurse crops like plantains or shade trees to retain moisture and survive their initial growth phase.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be ko kɛjɛ nurse tsei tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Bɔni afee ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi ni ehi shi yɛ shishijee dalɛ fãi lɛ amli.

english: Why does my cassava produce a lot of tall leaves during heavy rains but small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwereɔ waa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Excessive water and high nitrogen levels encourage plants to direct energy into leaf and stem growth above ground instead of storing starch in root tubers below ground.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine kɛ nitrogen ni fa babaoo woɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ aya baai kɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ starch kɛ woɔ tso sisifãhi nɛ a ngɛ zugba a sisi ɔ a mi.

english: Why do my maize plants grow greener and stronger when I plant cowpeas between the rows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe waaa kɛ́ midu tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and other legumes capture nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil through their roots. This natural fertilizer feeds neighboring maize crops, boosting their foliage and growth.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi Mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ejieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ niyenii. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei ahe tsei kɛ amɛdalɛ yaa hiɛ

english: Why do my tomato plant leaves curl up during the hot afternoon even after I water them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: Leaf curling is a defense mechanism plants use in intense heat to reduce surface area and minimize water evaporation. Leaves usually recover in the cooler evening once heat stress drops.
ga: Leaf curling ji tso hebuu gbɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli koni akɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni nu lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ shi. Bei pii lɛ, tsei lɛ ahe baa shi yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli beni dɔlɛ he haomɔ lɛ baa shi lɛ.

english: Why do crops grow faster in dark organic soil than in heavy reddish clay soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei daa oya yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ fe shikpɔŋ tsuru ni tsii nɔ lɛ?

english: Dark soils contain rich organic matter that holds water and nutrients loosely, making them easy for young roots to absorb. Clay soil packs tightly when dry, making it harder for roots to spread and find nutrients.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo duŋ lɛ yɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo ni haa nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ hiɔ shi mlɛo. Ehaa shishifãi bibii lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ lɛ oya Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee ekome beni egbiɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛna niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow tall and thin and fall over easily when planted close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ bibioo ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, plants compete for sunlight and stretch upward instead of building thick, sturdy stalks. Proper spacing ensures each stalk receives enough light and air to grow strong roots and stems.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ ni ebaafee kakadaŋŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee ŋmeii ni mli wa ni mli wa. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ eko fɛɛ eko naa la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha shishifãi lɛ kɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my crop turning pale yellow while the top leaves remain green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves typically indicate a lack of nitrogen. The plant moves available nitrogen from its older, lower leaves to feed new growth at the top, showing it needs soil replenishment.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ mli. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli koni amɛha gbɛ aha dalɛ hee ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ. Etsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni akɛ shikpɔŋ afata he.

english: Why are the flowers on my garden egg plants dropping off without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?
