english: Flowers drop when plants face stress from extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of pollinating insects like bees. Maintaining steady soil moisture helps flowers stay attached long enough to form fruits.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nibii ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ ŋmeii ni bɛ lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni amɛwo yibii.

english: How do small weeds in my field stunt the growth of my pepper plants so quickly?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni jwɛi bibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ atsĩ mi-pepper tsei lɛ adalɛ oya lɛ naa?

english: Weeds have fast-growing root systems that aggressively absorb moisture and nutrients from the soil before crop roots can reach them, leaving crops undernourished even if the weeds look small.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa eyɛ mli akɛ jwɛi lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛji bibii moŋ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually show that the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil, which is the main nutrient crops use to build healthy green leaves and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛfee baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ dalɛ ni mli wa.

english: Why do my crops yield much less food when I plant the seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ naa niyenii fioo kwraa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close to each other, the crops compete against one another for sunlight, ground water, and soil nutrients, leaving every plant weak and underdeveloped.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei fɛɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛdarako jogbaŋŋ.

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves acts like a blanket that keeps the ground cool, prevents water from evaporating quickly in the hot sun, and stops weeds from growing.
ga: Mulching ni akɛ baai ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ blanket ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear away all the big tall trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei kakadaji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves and shallow roots that burn and dry out quickly under direct hot sunlight; big trees provide the gentle shade young cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni shãa ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei wuji haa hulutsoo blɛoo. Ehe miihia ni kookoo bibioo lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do I need to set up wooden sticks for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mato tso kɛha sweet potato wain tso lɛ koni ekwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves out in the sunlight, which allows the plant to make enough food to grow big, healthy tubers underground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã koni amɛkɛ hulu la lɛ akpee. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: Weeds act like thief plants that quickly drink up the water and eat up the soil nutrients before your main crops have a chance to take them.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ tsei julɔi ni nuɔ nu lɛ oya ni amɛyeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ dani onibii titri ni oduɔ lɛ naa hegbɛ ni ekɛyeɔ nɔ.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually a sign that tiny insects like aphids or mites are hiding under the leaves and sucking out the plant juices, causing damaged growth.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ koolooi bibii, tamɔ aphids loo mites, kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛmiinu tso lɛ nu. Ekɛ fitemɔ aba dalɛ nɔ

english: Cassava roots rot in the ground when the soil holds too much water after heavy rains, which suffocates the roots and encourages rot diseases to attack.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ahe hewalɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off the plant before any tomatoes start forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani tomato lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they suffer stress from sudden hot temperatures or irregular watering, causing the plant to save energy by letting go of blossoms.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ hao amɛ. Ehaa tomato tsei lɛ kɛ hewalɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛjieɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots near the soil surface, so when the heavy fruit bunches make the plant top-heavy, wet ground allows wind to pull the roots right out of the soil.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ aduawai akui lɛ tsii lɛ, tso lɛ baaná ŋmeii ni tsii. He ni nu yɔɔ lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ agbala shishifãi lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Yellowing of lower leaves usually means your maize lacks nitrogen, a key plant food. When nitrogen is low, the plant takes whatever food it has left from its older lower leaves and sends it up to support the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii titri ko bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Kɛji nitrogen lɛ faaa Tso lɛ yeɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ, ni egbɔ lɛ amli ni etsuɔ ​​kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni eye ebua dalɛ hee ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to plant groundnuts or beans on my field after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ mɛi akɛ amɛdu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔji amli beni akpa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans have special roots that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. Planting them after heavy-feeding crops like maize naturally refills the soil's food reserves for your next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ odu nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmãa sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni ato kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle strong sunlight directly. Their tissues dry out quickly, so they need shade crops like plantains or tall trees to block harsh sun rays and preserve soil moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛ fãji lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa amɛnáa hɔnɔ, tamɔ plantains loo tsei kakadaji. Koni abu he kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants, causing them to drop their flowers to save water and survival energy. Without flowers staying attached to get pollinated, the plant cannot produce fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he. Kɛji fɔfɔii ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni baaha pollinate lɛ bɛ lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ awo yibii.

english: Why are the leaves of my hot pepper plants curling upwards and looking wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi chili baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni etamɔ nɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Upward curling leaves are usually a plant's response to tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies, or a virus spread by them. The curling is the leaf's defense and reaction to having its juice drained.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso lɛ baai ni efoɔ lɛ ji bɔ ni tso lɛ tsuɔ nii ehaa yɛ kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies lɛ ahe. loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ Curling ji hebuu kɛ bɔ ni baai lɛ feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa kɛ́ ajie nu lɛ kɛjɛ mli.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and thin with tiny cobs when I plant many seeds close together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Be ni miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo Dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli?

english: When seeds are crowded together, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Instead of growing thick stems, they stretch tall searching for light, leaving little energy to build big cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ abua dumɔwui lɛ anaa lɛ Tsei lɛ wuɔ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeedu tsei ni mli tse lɛ Moŋ lɛ, ekpã mli kɛtee ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni eyatao la. Kɛ hewalɛ fioo pɛ ni eshwɛ ni akɛbaafee ŋmei agbo ko.

english: Why should I cut off the extra shoots coming up around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni ebɔle ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ plantain tsei titrii lɛ.

english: The extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and nutrients from the main stem. Removing all but one or two strong suckers ensures the main stem gets enough food to produce large, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ, juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ ajie tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ fɛɛ, ja eko loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo plantain tsei wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very bushy with plenty of leaves but give me very small roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi shishifãi lɛ daraaa lɛ?

english: If the soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or manure, the cassava plant spends all its food making green leaves above ground instead of sending that energy downward to build thick root tubers.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo Yucca tso lɛ kɛ eniyenii fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, moŋ fe ni eeetsu nakai hewalɛ lɛ kɛba shi ni ekɛfee shishifãi ni mli tse.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce food for the underground tubers. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground so they capture more light and stay clear of soil-borne rot and diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmeii lɛ. Staking baawó tso lɛ yibii lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni ená la babaoo ni ehiɛ akafee ŋmɔtɔ kɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes rot so fast when I stack them in deep wooden crates?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ mikɛto tso adekai ni mli kwɔ amli lɛ?

english: Tomatoes continue to breathe and produce heat after harvest. Deep crates crush the bottom fruits under heavy weight, breaking their skin and trapping heat, which speeds up rotting.
ga: Tomato yaa nɔ emuɔ ni ekɛ dɔlɛ baa beni akpa lɛ sɛɛ. Adeka ni mli kwɔ lɛ kɛ amɛtsiimɔ kpeteŋkpele lɛ shwieɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ anɔ. Efiteɔ hewolo lɛ ni ehiɛɔ dɔlɛ mli. Enɛ baaha egbo oya.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the plant is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient it needs from fertilizer or compost to build strong, green foliage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛɛmɛi ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii amli koni akɛfee baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji.

english: Why does planting the exact same crop on the same piece of land every season cause my harvest to get smaller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ midu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ, ehaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the soil of specific nutrients and allows crop-specific pests and soil diseases to multiply in your field.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eye ebua tsei pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ mli lɛ ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa lɛ babaoo yɛ oŋmɔji amli.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller fruits when I plant the seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii bibii kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing plants fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, leaving none of them with enough food to produce large yields.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei komɛi bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛdu nii babaoo.

english: Why should I plant beans alongside my maize farm instead of growing only maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ masɛi moŋ fe ŋmãa kɛkɛ?

english: Beans pull nitrogen from the air and feed it into the ground, acting as a natural fertilizer that helps neighboring maize grow bigger and healthier.
ga: Beans gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni edara ni enáa hewalɛ.

english: What causes the leaves on my pepper plants to curl up and stop producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekpaa yibiiwoo?

english: Leaf curl on pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or mites carrying plant diseases, or by stress from intense heat and poor watering.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo mites ni kɛ tsei ahelai baa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni ehiii mli baa lɛ kɛbaa.

english: Why are my cassava leaves wilting and dying even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Wilting during rainy periods usually means rot fungi or underground pests are damaging the cassava roots, preventing the plant from taking up water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii loo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii miifite ŋmeii lɛ shishifãi lɛ. Ehaa tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before any cocoa pods actually form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho amɛfɔfɔi lɛ dani cacao ŋmɔji lɛ eba diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by drought, poor soil nutrients, or insect pests like capsids, which stops the flowers from turning into pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hɔmɔ hao amɛ. shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ capsids, ni tsiɔ fɔfɔi anaa koni amɛkatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why should I cut off extra small shoot suckers growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Ajieɔ Mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Extra suckers steal water and soil nutrients from the main plantain tree; cutting them off allows the main tree to focus its strength on growing a large bunch.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi juɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Tso lɛ mli tsei ni afoɔ lɛ haa tso titri lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ maa tso agbo ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal fertilizer and soil moisture long before your crops have a chance to absorb them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu be kakadaŋŋ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa hegbɛ ni amɛŋɔ amɛ.

english: How does spreading dry grass around the base of my crops help them during hot sunny days?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he fɛɛ he Te miŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa amɛ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass (mulching) acts as a shield that keeps the soil cool and stops water from evaporating away from the plant roots.
ga: Mulching (mulching) tsuɔ nii akɛ tsɔne ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ahe.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow and die whenever water sits on my land for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nu ta mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Most crops need air in the soil to breathe through their roots. When water covers the ground for too long, it drowns the roots and stops them from taking up nutrients, causing the plant leaves to turn yellow and eventually rot.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu kɛtsɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ nu ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ shishi ni eha amɛkaná niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ haa tso baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni naagbee lɛ amɛgboiɔ.

english: Is there any crop I can plant on the swampy part of my land where my normal crops refuse to grow?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi yɛ ni manyɛ madu yɛ mimaŋ ŋshɔkpɔ lɛ nɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ daa lɛ kpooɔ akɛ amɛbaadu?

english: Yes, crops like swamp rice, taro (cocoyam), and sugarcane naturally love wet ground because their roots can survive and feed easily in waterlogged soils that would kill other crops.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa, taro (kookoo) kɛ ŋmãa sumɔɔ hei ni nu yɔɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi ni amɛye nii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ ni baanyɛ afite ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi lɛ nɔ mlɛo.

english: Should I burn all the grass and bushes after clearing my land before planting?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashã jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii fɛɛ beni mijie he ni miyɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani madu?

english: Burning destroys the good organic matter and beneficial insects in the soil that naturally feed your crops. It is better to clear the land and allow the cleared leaves and grass to rot naturally into the dirt to build richer soil.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii kpakpai ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni haa adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛhaa onibii lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oha baai kɛ jwɛi ni ajie lɛ lɛ afite yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛfee shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ nii babaoo.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up like tubes when the afternoon sun becomes very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rolling leaves is a protective behavior. The plant rolls its leaves tightly to reduce the surface area exposed to the hot sun, which keeps its internal water from evaporating too quickly during the heat of the day.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji subaŋ ni buɔ mɔ he. Tso lɛ shwieɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ koni ekɛba he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ haaa nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ atsɔ oya tsɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my crops are struggling because the soil lacks nutrients?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ he miipiŋ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe?

english: When soil lacks nutrients, crops will grow very slowly, look pale green or yellowish instead of deep green, have thin stems, or flower late without producing big fruits or tubers.
ga: Beni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tso lɛ daa blɛoo waa. Amɛji eŋɔli ni mli tse loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ najiaŋ, amɛyɛ tsei bibii, loo amɛfɔɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli ni amɛwooo yibii loo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do crop roots struggle to grow when the ground is very hard and compact?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Soft young roots cannot push through hard, packed dirt to find water and food deeper down. Loosening the topsoil with a hoe allows the roots to expand widely and build a strong foundation for the plant.
ga: Shishifãi bibii nyɛŋ atsɔ muji ni eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli koni amɛyana nu kɛ niyenii yɛ shishigbɛ shɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei ŋmɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ alɛɛ mli ni efee shishitoo ni wa aha tso lɛ.

english: Why am I getting only a few bags of harvest even though my farmland is very large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kotokui fioo pɛ nɔ eyɛ mli akɛ he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ da waa moŋ lɛ?

english: A large farm does not guarantee a high harvest if plants are spaced too far apart, weeds steal nutrients, or the soil is tired. Proper plant spacing and soil fertilization can produce more bags of crops on a smaller plot than on a big uncared-for field.
ga: Okwaafoi wuji haaa ana ŋmaa babaoo kɛji tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ tsɔ. Jwɛi juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ efite Tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo aba yɛ he ko bibioo fe he ko ni da ni atsuuu he nii.

english: Can I plant cassava and maize on the same plot of land without them damaging each other?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni mifiteee amɛhe?

english: Yes, planting them together works well because maize grows fast and is harvested in a few months, while cassava grows slowly at first and takes over the field only after the maize has been harvested.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya, ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli ni eŋɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ pɛ.

english: If my neighbor plants tall crops right next to my farm boundary, will it affect my plants?
ga: Kɛji mikutsoŋnyo lɛ du tsei kakadaji ni bɛŋkɛ miŋmɔ lɛ husu lɛ Ani ebaana mitsei lɛ anɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, tall crops can block essential sunlight from reaching your shorter crops and their long roots can steal water and soil food from your side of the boundary line.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ otsei kukuji lɛ ahe. Ni amɛshishifãi kakadaji lɛ baanyɛ aju nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛjɛ ohusu lɛ mli.

english: Which food crops can I plant that allow me to harvest gradually over time so my family doesn't run out of food?
ga: Mɛɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu koni manyɛ makpa fiofio yɛ be ni sa mli koni niyenii akaha miweku lɛ kɔkɔɔkɔ?

english: Crops like cassava, sweet potatoes, and leafy green vegetables can be harvested bit by bit in small amounts as you need them, keeping food available in the ground over a long period.
ga: Abaanyɛ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei, ŋmei, kɛ ŋmei ni yɔɔ baai bibii bibii bɔ ni he hiaa bo lɛ. koni niyenii ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen, which is essential for healthy green growth. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure helps restore leaf color and improves cob growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ mli. ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha baai lɛ ahe afee fɛo ekoŋŋ ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant peppers on the same piece of land where I just harvested tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa tomato lɛ nɔ kɛkɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Tomatoes and peppers belong to the same plant family and share the same soil pests and diseases. Rotating them with a different crop family, like maize or beans, breaks disease cycles and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Tomato kɛ pepper yɛ tso weku kome mli ni amɛ fɛɛ amɛyɔɔ sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai kome. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ awekui srɔtoi, tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni atsakeɔ lɛ Enɛ haa helai ni yaa nɔ lɛ kpaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees get scorched easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and provide large leaves that act as living shade umbrellas, giving young cocoa trees the moist, protected environment they need to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa cacao tsei bibii lɛ naa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni abuɔ he ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, their roots and leaves compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives every plant enough resources to form full, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni akɛtoɔ he ni sa lɛ baaha tso fɛɛ tso aná nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha efee ŋmei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves curl up in the afternoon even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: Leaves curl up during hot afternoons to reduce the amount of water they lose to the hot sun. If the soil is moist, the leaves will normally unroll and recover once the temperature cools down in the evening.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛba nu ni amɛfiteɔ kɛjɛɔ hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ shi. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, baai lɛ baagbala ni amɛhe baajɔ amɛ bɔ ni sa kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli ba shi gbɛkɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long, starving the roots of air and encouraging fungal growth. Planting cassava on raised ridges or mounds helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. ni eha ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves in direct sunlight to create food for the tubers growing underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet ground where diseases spread and ensures maximum sun exposure for bigger tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ shɛɛɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ, ni ehaa hulu la ni fa babaoo baa bulbs wuji lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow thin and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifee mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crops. Clearing weeds early leaves all the soil nourishment for your crops, helping them grow tall and produce good yields.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu ni he hiaa waa, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ aha oŋmɔshi nibii. Eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Tomato flowers drop when plants suffer from extreme heat stress or erratic watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist and applying grass mulch around the base helps cool the soil so flowers can set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ naa amanehulu yɛ dɔlɛ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ ni ejaaa hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha efee ŋmɔtɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ awo shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ awo yibii.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my maize leaves with small caterpillars hiding inside the stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Ani akɛtee tsɔne lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that feeds on young crop foliage. Inspecting your field early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or organic neem sprays prevents them from destroying the growing tips.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ tsei bibii ahe baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo organic neem spray ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni akafite ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do many farmers in Ghana plant plantains alongside young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi babaoo ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ miidu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow rapidly and provide broad leafy shade to protect the young cocoa plants while also giving you food and extra income before the cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ehaa baai ni mli kwɔ ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa koni ebu kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe. Yɛ be nɛɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ, ekɛ niyenii kɛ shika kroko haa dani kookoo lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Spacing your plantain suckers about 3 meters (10 feet) apart gives each plant enough room for its leaves to spread, catch sunlight, and absorb soil nutrients without competing with neighboring plants.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ plantain tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mitai 3 (naji 10) lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ egbɛ eshwa, ená hulu la, ni ekɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ akaŋ.

english: Which type of plantain sucker is best for me to plant if I want strong growth?
ga: Mɛɛ plantain sucker tso ni hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ madu kɛji miisumɔ ni eda waa?

english: Sword suckers—which have narrow, spear-shaped leaves and a strong bulb base—are best because they have strong root systems and grow much faster than suckers with broad, weak leaves.
ga: Sword shoots, ni yɔɔ baai bibii ni tamɔ lance kɛ shishitoo ni mli wa ni tamɔ bulbous. Ehi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ eyɛ shishifãi ni mli wa, ni edaa oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ.

english: Why are too many small shoots growing around my main plantain stem, and should I remove them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii babaoo miida yɛ mitso titri lɛ he lɛ? Ni ani esa akɛ majie loo esaaa akɛ majie?

english: Those small shoots are called suckers, and if you leave too many, they steal water and nutrients from the main stem. You should cut them back so only one or two strong ones remain to replace the main plant after harvest.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii bibii nɛɛ akɛ suckers. Ni kɛji oshi lɛ yɛ nɔ babaoo Ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Esa akɛ ofolɔ amɛ koni amɛshi tso ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni baaye tso titri lɛ najiaŋ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Plantains have large leaves that lose water quickly in hot weather. During the dry season, mulching the base of the plant with dry leaves or grass helps keep moisture in the soil and prevents the leaves from yellowing.
ga: Plantains yɛ baai wuji ni nu fiteɔ oya kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Kɛ́ okɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi ha tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi ni ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: What kind of manure or fertilizer is best to help my plantains produce big bunches?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii baaye abua mi plantains lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni ewo jwɛi wuji?

english: Plantains grow best when fed with rich organic manure, such as decomposed poultry dung or cow manure, mixed into the soil around the plant to provide steady nitrogen and keep the soil moist.
ga: Plantains daa jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ kooloi loo tsina ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo lɛ ha amɛ. Okɛfutu shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ mli. tsei koni ekɛha nitrogen lɛ ahi shi ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: What causes my plantain tree to suddenly fall over even when there is no strong wind?
ga: Mɛni haa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa lɛ? He ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa bɛ lɛ?

english: This usually happens when tiny pests like plantain root nematodes or stem borers attack the roots and lower trunk, damaging the base until the plant can no longer support its own weight.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa kɛji kooloi bibii tamɔ plantain shishifãi nematodes loo stem borers tutua shishifãi lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ. Kpatamɔ shishitoo lɛ hiɛ kɛyashi tso lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ egbɔjɔmɔ lɛ nɔ dɔŋŋ.

english: How can I prevent strong winds from snapping my plantain trees when they carry heavy bunches?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa naa koni ekakumɔ mi-plantains lɛ beni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: You can support fruiting plantain trees by placing a sturdy wooden stake or a branched bamboo pole under the neck of the heavy bunch to brace it against the wind.
ga: Obaanyɛ oye obua dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii lɛ kɛtsɔ tso loo ŋmei tso ni wa ni niji yɔɔ mli ni okɛaawo tso ni tsii lɛ kuɛ shishi koni ekɛfi ehe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ he lɛ nɔ.

english: How does clearing weeds regularly around my plantain plants help them produce better food?
ga: Jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli Te plantains ni afeɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ niyenii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds compete directly with plantains for soil nutrients, fertilizer, and water. Keeping a clear circle around the base of each plant ensures the plantain gets all the nourishment it needs.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ plantains yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu. Ni aaana kooloo ni mli ka shi faŋŋ ni ebɔle tso fɛɛ tso shishi lɛ haa plantain lɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest my plantain bunch before it ripens on the tree?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa plantain ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: A plantain bunch is ready to harvest when the individual fingers become plump and full, and the sharp edges or ridges along the sides of the green fruit start to smooth out.
ga: Plantains kuu ko efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji nine fɛɛ nine egbɔ. ni ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ aduawai eŋɔli lɛ afãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Yellowing starting at the tip and moving down the leaf center in a 'V' shape means your soil is lacking nitrogen. The plant is stealing nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the newer top leaves.
ga: Yellow jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni eyaa baa lɛ teŋgbɛ yɛ ‘V’ su mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei miiju nitrogen kɛmiijɛ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ niyenii.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids, thrips, or mites feeding on the undersides of leaves, or by a virus they transmitted to the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa tsei anɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot, when the plant experiences extreme dry spell stress, or when there is too much nitrogen fertilizer causing leaf growth instead of fruit growth.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛ tsei kɛ hɔmɔ he haomɔ ni naa wa kpe Aloo kɛji akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ mli lɛ, ehaa baa lɛ daa yɛ aduawai ni baa lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide leafy shade to act as umbrellas, keeping the soil moist and protecting young cocoa until it matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ haa hulutsoo tamɔ ambrela. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why does my plantain stand produce smaller fruits if I leave all the shoots growing around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ woɔ yibii bibii kɛji miha ŋmeii ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ fɛɛ kwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Leaving too many young shoots (suckers) forces them to compete with the main mother plant for water and soil nutrients, leaving less energy for building big fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii bibii (ŋmeii) babaoo tsɔ lɛ, enyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛkɛ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ abɔi nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haaa hewalɛ babaoo ahi shi ni akɛfee aduawai akui wuji.

english: Lifting yam vines on stakes helps leaves capture maximum sunlight to feed the tuber underground, while keeping leaves off wet ground prevents soil-borne fungal diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ awó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnáa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛkɛha tsei lɛ amli tsei lɛ niyenii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa sũ lɛ mli lɛ akabote mli.

english: When planted too close, maize stalks compete aggressively with each other for sunlight and soil nutrients, growing spindly instead of thick and strong enough to produce big cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, Abele tsei lɛ kɛ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ waa. Ekwɛɔ ŋmeii moŋ fe ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehe wa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji baa.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. In waterlogged soil, water fills all the air spaces, causing the roots to drown and decompose.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ Nu baayi kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly like green straws during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ jwɛi eŋɔli yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a survival trick. Maize plants curl their leaves to hide their surfaces from hot sun and wind, reducing water loss through evaporation during dry afternoon heat.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji yiwalaheremɔ he ŋaa. Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛtee amɛhiɛ kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nu ni laajeɔ kɛjɛɔ la ni hoɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do groundnut plants flower above the ground but produce nuts under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii fɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ shi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: After groundnut yellow flowers are pollinated, they grow long stalks called 'pegs' that push downward into the earth, where the pods can develop safely hidden from sun and heat.
ga: Beni afee ŋmɔtɔ fɔfɔi ni ji ŋmɔtɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, fɔfɔi tso kakadaŋŋ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ ‘peg’ lɛ daa ni tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ aya hiɛ shweshweeshwe, ni akɛtee hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ he.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade from bigger trees or shade crops like plantains because harsh, direct sunlight scorches their soft leaves and dries out the topsoil before their roots grow deep enough.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains adɛŋ, ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ agbi dani shishifãi lɛ mli aba mli bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do the broad leaves of my plantain plants dry up and drop during the dry harmattan wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dry harmattan winds pull water out of plantain leaves faster than roots can draw it from the soil. The plant naturally sheds its older outer leaves to conserve water and protect its central stem.
ga: Harmatta kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ plantain baai amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛ kponɔgbɛ baai momo lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛhiɛ nu mli ni amɛbu amɛteŋgbɛ tso lɛ he.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the corn even comes out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ po jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need for healthy green growth. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or planting legumes like beans before maize helps supply this missing plant food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni tsei he hiaa koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii, dani ŋmeii baanyɛ aye abua ni akɛ tso niyenii ni elaaje nɛɛ awo mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts in the same farm as maize makes the maize yield better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ ŋmei lɛ, ehaa ŋmei lɛ yibiiwoo yaa hiɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants pull nitrogen from the air into the soil through tiny nodules on their roots. This naturally enriches the soil with nutrients that feed the neighboring maize plants.
ga: Peanut tsei gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ niyenii ni haa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do I have to make high soil mounds before planting my yams instead of just planting on flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ofee shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ dani odu sweet potatoes yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Loose, raised soil mounds make it easy for yam tubers to expand long and thick underground without hitting hard dirt, while also helping excess rainwater drain away so the tubers do not rot.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni awó nɔ lɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛnáaa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ nɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ koni tsɔnei lɛ akafite.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and stopping flowers from forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiikpa fɔmɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the plant's sap and spreading viruses. Spraying natural solutions like neem oil early protects the plants from these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso lɛ nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ kɛ baa lɛ baa. Kɛji akɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofa tamɔ neem fɔ shwie nɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni ebu tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ ahe.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the soil if I leave them buried during heavy rainy seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji akɛ afu amɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni naa wa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When heavy rain leaves standing water in the soil, air cannot reach the cassava roots. The roots drown and rot because soil fungi and bacteria thrive in waterlogged, airless soil.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu kpɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ahe. Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ ejaakɛ sũ mli ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ yeɔ omanye yɛ sũ ni nu eyi mli obɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: The first rain is often followed by a heatwave or dry spell. If you plant too early, the seeds will sprout but then scorch and die in the hot, dry soil before the main rainy season truly begins.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, latsaa loo nugbɔshiimɔ be nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ shi amɛbaagboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi nɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ baaje shishi.

english: Why do weeds make my crops produce small fruits even if I water the farm regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ woɔ yibii bibii lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa moŋ.

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that steal fertilizers, minerals, and sunlight away from your crops. Even with enough water, your crops remain starved of key food taken by the weeds.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, shika tsuru, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa po lɛ, jwɛi baaye Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ lolo.

english: Why should I pinch off extra shoots from my tomato stems when they start growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ tomato tsei lɛ amli lɛ beni tomato lɛ jeɔ shishi edaa lɛ?

english: Trimming unnecessary side branches directs the plant's energy and soil nutrients into producing larger, healthier fruits rather than wasting energy on growing excess leaves and stems.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ tso lɛ niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ naa hewalɛ kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ewo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ lɛ, obaakwɛ baai kɛ tsei krokomɛi.

english: How can I tell if my young crop seedlings are healthy enough to be moved from the nursery to my main farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji midumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛya miŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli?

english: Healthy seedlings have firm, upright stems, dark green leaves, and well-formed root systems. If they look strong and actively growing rather than weak or drooping, they are in good condition to survive being transplanted.
ga: Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ yɛ tsei ni ja. baai ni tsuɔ waa kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ fɛo Kɛji amɛtamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa ni amɛdaraa oya Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee gbɔjɔmɔ loo amɛgbee shi Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛyɛ shihilɛ kpakpa mli ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi kɛji akɛ atsake amɛ.

english: Why do my seeds take much longer to sprout during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Seeds need a steady supply of moisture and warm soil to break their resting state. When the soil is dry, the seed delays germination to protect itself until enough water is available to support early root growth.
ga: Dumɔwui hia shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni mli edɔ be fɛɛ be koni amɛfo amɛ wɔɔhe lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛyashi nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua shishifãi lɛ adalɛ mra lɛ baa.

english: Why do I need to leave specific distances between my plants instead of putting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mitsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe shi moŋ ni mikɛ amɛ aaabɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough sunlight, water, and soil nutrients without competing with its neighbors. It also allows air to circulate between plants, which keeps diseases from spreading quickly.
ga: He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ekutsoŋbii lɛ yeee akaŋ. Eha kɔɔyɔɔ hu tsɔɔ tsei ateŋ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaaa oya.

english: Why is it recommended to plant cassava cuttings at an angle instead of planting them completely flat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ adu ŋmei niji yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeefee ŋmei kwraa lɛ?

english: Planting cassava cuttings at an angle positions the growing buds properly toward the surface for easy sprouting while placing the root nodes deep enough to anchor firmly and grow big tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ adu cassava niji yɛ koŋ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya. Okɛ shishifãi lɛ awo mli bɔ ni sa koni amɛma shi shiŋŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs agboi.

english: Why do the leaves of my young cocoa plants turn yellow and dry up during the hot months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ nyɔji ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under full sun and high heat. Without shade trees like plantains nearby to block harsh light and hold soil moisture, the leaves turn yellow from stress.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ la ni mli edɔ waa shishi. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains ni bɛŋkɛ ni baatsi hulutsoo naa ni ehiɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ bɛ lɛ, Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ haomɔ mli.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when stressed by extreme heat, prolonged dry soil, or a sudden lack of nutrients. The plant drops flowers to conserve energy for survival.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi be kakadaŋŋ. loo niyenii ni esaaa ni baa trukaa lɛ Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Why do yam vines require tall wooden stakes to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ koni enyɛ ekwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally climb to expose as many leaves as possible to sunlight, which powers root tuber growth underground. Staking also lifts leaves off wet soil, protecting them from fungal rot.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛha hulu la babaoo aba tsei lɛ ahe bɔ ni eeenyɛ. ni tsirɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ adalɛ Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ koni ŋmeii akafite.

english: Why should I wait for the major rains to settle before planting my main maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa dani madu mikooloo niyenii titri, ni ji ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Seeds need continuous soil moisture after germination. Planting after a single rain when the soil may dry out again causes sprouted seeds to wither and die underground.
ga: Dumɔwui hia shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ daa yɛ amɛkwɛ̃mɔ sɛɛ. Dumɔ ni aaadu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kome sɛɛ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi ekoŋŋ lɛ baaha dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why does planting beans or cowpeas make my soil better for future crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans work with natural soil microbes to capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant naturally decays, that nitrogen stays in the soil as free food for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ sũ mli nibii bibii tsuɔ nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Beni tsei fiteɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe Nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How does well-rotted animal manure help my crops differently than chemical fertilizer?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ ni etamɔɔɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizers feed the plant directly for a short time, while organic manure feeds the soil itself. Manure improves the soil's structure, helping it hold onto water and plant food for a much longer period.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei niyenii tɛ̃ɛ yɛ be kukuoo mli. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ niyenii. Manure haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii feɔ fɛo. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɛɔ nu mli ni eduɔ niyenii be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How do I pick mature fruits or pods from a plant without causing the main plant to die?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafolɔ aduawai loo ŋmeii ni eda kɛjɛ tso mli ni migbeee tso titri lɛ?

english: Using clean, sharp tools to cut only the mature parts leaves the plant's roots and main stem intact. This allows water and nutrients to keep flowing to the remaining unripened fruits so they can continue growing.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni he tse ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ tsu nii ni akɛfolɔ fãi ni edara lɛ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ eshishifãi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai hoɔ kɛyaa aduawai ni eshwɛ ni ekwɛko lɛ anɔ koni enyɛ eya nɔ eda.

english: Why do my crops dry up and die after I harvest the lower parts of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni egboɔ beni mikpa tso lɛ shishigbɛ fãi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Roughly tearing or breaking the bottom parts damages the plant's stem tissues, cutting off food and water to the rest of the plant. Careful cutting protects the stem so the upper parts stay alive.
ga: Shishigbɛ fã lɛ mligbalamɔ loo gbee ni mli wa Ebaafite tso lɛ shishi fã lɛ. Enɛ haa niyenii kɛ nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ kɛyaa tso lɛ fãi krokomɛi anɔ. Kɛ́ afolɔ tso lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tso lɛ he bɔni afee ni ŋwɛi fã lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I harvest my crop in stages instead of pulling up everything at once?
ga: Makpa ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Ni yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ato shikome hu?

english: Selective harvesting involves identifying which individual fruits or roots are fully mature while leaving younger ones attached. This gives smaller produce time to reach full size, giving you multiple harvests from one planting.
ga: Nɔ ni fata nikpamɔ ni ahalaa lɛ he ji ni ayɔse aduawai loo shishifãi lɛ eko fɛɛ eko ni eda, ni ashi bibii lɛ. Enɛ haa be ni akɛfeɔ nii lɛ faaa dani eshɛɔ elɛɛmɔ he. Enɛ haa onáa ŋmaa babaoo kɛjɛɔ dumɔ kome pɛ mli.

english: Why do agricultural officers tell us to wait six full months before harvesting this crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ miikɛɛ wɔ akɛ wɔmɛ nyɔji enumɔ muu fɛɛ dani wɔkpa nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ?

english: Crops need a specific amount of time to build up starch, yield weight, and internal nutrients. Harvesting before the recommended six months results in smaller yields and lower market value even if the crop looks big on the outside.
ga: Tsei he miihia be fioo dani amɛfee starch. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ amli tsiimɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ Nibii ni akpaa dani nyɔji 6 ni atsɔɔ akɛ ashɛɔ lɛ baaha yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi ni jara hu baa shi. Eyɛ mli akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni eda kɛjɛ kponɔgbɛ moŋ

english: What happens if I rush and harvest my crops early because I need food or money?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ mikɛ oyaiyeli kpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ mra ejaakɛ niyenii loo shika he miihia mi hu?

english: Harvesting too early reduces your overall yield because the produce has not finished growing. Waiting until full maturity yields heavier, better-quality crops that sell for higher prices.
ga: Kɛ́ okpa ŋmɔshi nii lɛ mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaakpa lɛ aba shi ejaakɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbeko ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛmɔ naa lolo. Nibii ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii, ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ahɔ̃ɔ kɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ.

english: How can I tell if my crop is ready to harvest without cutting it open to check inside?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa ni mifolɔɔɔ mli koni mikwɛ emli?

english: You can judge ripeness by counting the months since planting and checking external signals like changes in skin color, foliage drying, or firmness, rather than wounding the crop to look inside.
ga: Obaanyɛ okojo tso lɛ shweremɔ kɛtsɔ nyɔji ni eho kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ lɛ akanemɔ nɔ ni okwɛ kɛji okadii ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ, tamɔ hewolo nɔ su tsakemɔi, baai ni egboi, loo bɔ ni eyɔɔ shiŋŋ lɛ, moŋ fe ni ooopila tso lɛ koni okwɛ emli.

english: If the bottom shell of my crop cracks open on the farm, does it mean it is ready to pick?
ga: Kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishigbɛ fã lɛ mli fã yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Ani enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔ lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa?

english: Splitting at the bottom can mean maturity, but it often signals over-ripeness or water stress. Leaving cracked crops on the farm exposes the inside to pests and rot, so they should be harvested immediately.
ga: Mligbalamɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baanyɛ atsɔɔ dalɛ. Shi bei pii lɛ amɛtsɔɔ akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ fe nine loo nu mli haomɔ. Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni ekumɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔ lɛ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ ŋmeii aba. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ akpa lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: How do I prevent insects from ruining my crops when the outer skin breaks open before harvest time?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkafite miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni hewolo lɛ kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ fãa dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ shɛɔ lɛ?

english: Cracks expose the inner flesh to flies and fungi. Harvesting slightly before severe cracking occurs—based on recommended timing—keeps the protective outer layer whole and safe from pests.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi lɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii baa emli. Nikpamɔ fioo dani gbee ni naa wa baa. Edamɔ be ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ nɔ Enɛ baaha kponɔgbɛ hebuu fã lɛ fɛɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehi shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: Why did my field yield nothing at all when I planted this crop for the very first time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ wooo ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi beni midu ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ?

english: First-time failures usually happen due to planting at the wrong depth, harvesting prematurely, or using improper techniques. Learning proper planting intervals and care methods prevents zero-yield seasons.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ shishijee shigbeemɔ baa ji dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ he ni esaaa lɛ. ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaaa mra loo gbɛi ni esaaa ni akɛtsuɔ nii Dumɔ bei ni sa kɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ kasemɔ baaye abua ni atsĩ be ni yibiiwoo bɛ mli lɛ naa.

english: Why is it important to follow proper harvesting methods taught by extension officers rather than doing it by trial and error?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni anyiɛ ŋmaakpamɔ gbɛi ni sa ni extension nitsulɔi lɛ tsɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Yɛ kaa kɛ tɔmɔ najiaŋ?

english: Trial and error often leads to ruined plants, damaged yields, or premature harvesting. Proper extension methods teach you the exact growth duration and picking techniques to maximize yield without destroying your farm investment.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kaa kɛ tɔmɔ haa tso lɛ fiteɔ. Nibii ni adu lɛ fite. loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa oya Proper Propagation Methods lɛ tsɔɔ bo be pɔtɛɛ ni esa akɛ okwɛ̃ kɛ gbɛi ni oootsɔ nɔ ohala ŋmɔshi nii lɛ koni oná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni okpãtãaa oŋmɔ mli shika ni okɛwo mli lɛ hiɛ.

english: I keep hearing about pheromone traps for my farm, but how do they actually work to catch insect pests?
ga: Miyaa nɔ minuɔ pheromone tsɔnei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe, shi te amɛtsuɔ nii amɛhaa tɛŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ koni amɛmɔmɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai?

english: Pheromone traps use special scents that mimic the natural smells female insects release to attract males. The male pests smell the lure from far away, fly into the trap expecting to find a mate, and get trapped inside before they can reproduce.
ga: Pheromone tsɔnei lɛ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ krɛdɛɛ ko ni kaseɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔlɔ ni kooloi yei jieɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛgbala hii. Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ anu ŋshɔŋloo lɛ he kɛjɛ shɔŋŋ. Fɔ̃ɔ kɛboteɔ tsɔne lɛ mli kɛ hiɛnɔkamɔ akɛ obaana hefatalɔ. ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ mli dani amɛfɔɔ bii.

english: If I put a scented pest trap on my farm, won't it draw all the insects from my neighbor's farm onto my crops?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmeii ni he yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ wo miŋmɔ lɛ mli Ani egbalaŋ ŋmeii fɛɛ ni jɛ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ kɛbaaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ?

english: The traps use a controlled, mild scent lure that mainly attracts insects already flying around or near your field. Instead of bringing new swarms, it tricks the local pests into landing inside the trap rather than onto your crops.
ga: Amale lɛ kɛ ŋshɔŋloo ko ni he yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ fioo tsuɔ nii. ni abaanyɛ akudɔ Amɛgbalaa kooloi bibii ni foɔ kɛbɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ babaoo. loo yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ oŋmɔ lɛ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ ŋmeii heei baaba lɛ, elakaa he ni oyɔɔ lɛ koni amɛgbee tsɔnei amli moŋ fe ni amɛaagbee oŋmɔshi nibii anɔ.

english: How does catching only male insects in a trap stop pests from destroying my tomato farm?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni kooloi hii ni amɔmɔ amɛ yɛ tsɔnei amli lɛ aaatsi kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite mi-tomato ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: If male insects are caught in traps before they can meet the females, the females cannot lay fertile eggs. Fewer eggs mean fewer caterpillars or larvae hatching to eat your crops in the next generation.
ga: Kɛji akɛ amɔ ŋmei nuu lɛ yɛ tsɔne lɛ mli dani ekɛ yoo lɛ kpe lɛ, Yei nyɛŋ awo ŋmeii ni fɔɔ bii. Akpɔlɔi fioo tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni baaye onibii yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ faaa.

english: Does a sticky insect trap kill pests immediately, or is it just meant for counting them?
ga: Sticky insect trap Gbeɔ kooloi bibii amrɔ nɔŋŋ loo eji kɛha amɛkanemɔ pɛ?

english: Most insect traps serve as an early warning system. They hold the insects fast so you can see which pests have arrived on your farm and how many there are, helping you decide if you need to spray or use other controls.
ga: Koolooi amli tsɔnei babaoo tsuɔ nii akɛ kɔkɔbɔɔ gbɛjianɔtoo mra. Amɛmɔɔ kooloi bibii oya bɔni afee ni ona kooloi bibii ni eshɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛ amɛyibɔ ​​fɛɛ. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni okpɛɔ oyiŋ kɛji akɛ ehe miihia ni okɛ tsofa afɔ nɔ loo nibii krokomɛi ni akɛkwɛɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: How do insect pests manage to find my maize farm even when it is hidden far inside the bush?
ga: Te afeɔ tɛŋŋ ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ naa mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ? Kɛji akɛ akɛtee jwɛi komɛi ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ amli po?

english: Insects have an extremely sharp sense of smell and can detect the natural chemicals and scent released by healthy crop leaves from miles away, guiding them directly to your farm.
ga: Kplukai yɛ henumɔ ni yɔɔ srɔto kwraa ni haa amɛnuɔ nii ahe. ni ebaanyɛ ena adebɔɔ mli tsofai kɛ ŋmɔlɔi ni jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli lɛ amli kɛjɛɔ he ko ni kɛ jɛmɛ jɛkɛmɔ ji kilomitai babaoo. koni otsɔɔ amɛ gbɛ kɛya oŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How do male and female crop pests find each other in a large field to multiply?
ga: Te afeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii hii kɛ yei kpeɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli koni amɛshwere?

english: Female insects release invisible scent chemicals called pheromones into the air. Male insects follow these scent trails through the wind until they locate the female on a plant leaf.
ga: Kplukai yei jieɔ tsofai ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ ni anaaa ni atsɛɔ lɛ pheromones lɛ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Kplukai hii nyiɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ asɛɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛnaa yei yɛ tsei ahe baai anɔ.

english: Why do pests seem to suddenly appear on my farm in large numbers all at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo miiba trukaa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli shikome lɛ?

english: Insects often travel in search of food or mates when weather conditions change. A few adult insects can arrive undetected, mate quickly, and lay hundreds of eggs that hatch together a few days later.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii fãa gbɛ kɛyaa niyenii loo hefatalɔi kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ tsake. Kplukai komɛi ni eda lɛ baanyɛ aba ni mɔ ko mɔ ko enaaa amɛ. Fɔmɔɔ oya ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ohai abɔ, ni gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ amɛfeɔ ekome kɛfɔ̃ɔ.

english: How can I tell if pests have entered my farm before I start seeing eaten leaves and destroyed fruits?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsɛŋemɔ helai miiba miŋmɔ lɛ mli? Dani obaaje baai ni aye kɛ aduawai ni efite lɛ shishi?

english: You can place monitoring traps around your field boundary. Checking these traps regularly reveals when adult pests first arrive in your area, long before their offspring start chewing your plants.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ tsɔnei ni akɛkwɛɔ nɔ lɛ awo he. Oŋmɔ mli husui Nɛkɛ tsɔnei nɛɛ akwɛmɔ daa lɛ baatsɔɔ be mli ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni eda lɛ baabote he ni oyɔɔ lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa. Dani seshibii lɛ baabɔi otsei lɛ ŋmɔmɔ

english: Why do insects attack my crops more during certain weather conditions or months of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii babaoo tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi komɛi loo afi lɛ mli nyɔji komɛi amli lɛ?

english: Insects depend on temperature and moisture to survive and reproduce. Warm, humid weather speeds up their life cycle, causing them to mate faster and search actively for host plants.
ga: Kplukai damɔɔ dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i nɔ koni amɛhi shi ni amɛfɔ bii. Shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ haa amɛshihilɛ yaa oya. Enɛ haa amɛfɔɔ oya ni amɛtaoɔ tsei ni amɛbaahere amɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is the best way to stop insects from mating and laying eggs on my cabbage crop?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni aaatsɔ nɔ atsĩ kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkabote gbalashihilɛ mli ni amɛkawo mi-cabbage tsei lɛ anɔ?

english: Combining lure traps to capture adult insects with clean farming practices—like clearing weeds where insects hide—disrupts their mating cycle and keeps egg counts low.
ga: Amalei ni akɛaafee ekome koni akɛmɔmɔ kooloi bibii ni eda lɛ kɛ okwaayeli gbɛi ni he tse, tamɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ he ni kooloi bibii lɛ ehiɛ amɛhe lɛ. Ebaafite fɔmɔ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ ni eha ŋmeii ayibɔ aba shi.

english: How does plowing my land with a tractor help my crops grow better compared to just clearing the weeds with a cutlass?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni mikɛ traktɔ tsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ? Kɛ akɛto jwɛi ni akɛ tsɔne kuku tsuɔ nii kɛfoɔ lɛ he

english: Plowing breaks up hard, compacted soil so your crops' roots can easily push deep underground to find water and nutrients. Loose soil also allows rainwater to sink in deeply rather than washing away your valuable topsoil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ gbálaa shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli bɔni afee ni otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ oya koni amɛyatao nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ hu haa nugbɔ nu lɛ boteɔ mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni jara wa lɛ nɔ.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot rapidly drains the specific nutrients maize needs from the soil and allows soil pests to multiply. Rotating with crops like groundnuts or cowpeas returns nitrogen to the soil naturally and starves out maize pests.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa abele lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya. ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni amɛshwereɔ Nibii ni aduɔ ni tsakeɔ amɛhe tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii lɛ haa nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa sũ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni hɔmɔ aye kooloi ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate direct, harsh sunlight and hot winds. Leaving some tall trees or planting temporary shade crops like plantains creates a cool shelter that keeps the soil moist and protects fragile cocoa leaves from burning.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ gbɛ tɛ̃ɛ. tsei kakadaji ni ashiɔ Aloo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo baa ni ehaa kookoo baai ni waaa lɛ shãaa.

english: Why do my crops grow poorly if I plant immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛji midu amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The season's first rain often creates a brief burst of hot, damp soil that can heat up and kill newly germinated seeds. Waiting until the rains become steady ensures the ground stays cool and moist enough for seeds to establish strong roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni edɔ lɛ mli fãa yɛ be kukuoo mli. Enɛ baanyɛ adɔ ni egbe dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ. Mɛ ni aaamɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni edɔɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ aná shishifãi ni wa.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, soil food, and water. This competition results in tall, thin, weak stalks that produce very small ears of corn.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ nu he akaŋshii mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ akaŋshii nɛɛ mli baa ji tsei ni kɛlɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ ŋmãa toi bibii waa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, an essential plant food. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or NPK at the right stage keeps the leaves green so the plant can feed its growing corn cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa Kɛ akɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo NPK wo mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ aha ŋmãa ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients like phosphorus. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to conserve energy for its own survival.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Nu ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ fɔsfɔs, kɛ́ haomɔ Tsei baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips sucking the sap from young leaves, or by a virus carried by insects. Spraying early protects the leaves so they can spread out and catch sunlight to make food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ mites loo thrips ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni kooloi kɛbaa lɛ anɔ Ashwieɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ mra Enɛ baabu baai lɛ ahe koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛná hulu la ni amɛkɛtsu nii yɛ niyenii homɔ mli.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the ground if I leave them too long after they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ beni amɛdara sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Once cassava reaches full maturity, the roots stop growing and begin to absorb excess water from heavy rains. This extra moisture causes the roots to break down underground and rot before you can harvest them.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ eda kwraa lɛ, shishifãi lɛ kpaɔ dalɛ ni amɛjeɔ nu ni fa fe nine ni jɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ shishi. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa nɛɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛgboiɔ dani obaanyɛ okpa amɛ.

english: Why do I need to put up wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafee tsei kɛha mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ koni makwɔ nɔ beni edaa lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves out high in the air to catch maximum sunlight, which provides the energy needed to swell the tubers underground. Lifting the leaves off the damp ground also prevents leaves from rotting and spreading disease.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ haa hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛwo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa amɛgboi ni helai akagbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I plant them in an open field without tall trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei kakadaji bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to direct sunlight and intense heat. Without shade trees or plantain plants to protect them, their young leaves burn and lose moisture faster than their roots can absorb water.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Kɛji tsei ni baaha hulutsoo loo plantains ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ bɛ Amɛbaai bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants developing tiny holes and looking chewed up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? ni ekwɛɔ akɛ eshɛre?

english: This damage is usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm. They hide inside the growing center (funnel) of young maize during the day and feed on the leaves, which weakens the plant's growth if not managed early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ adalɛ hei (cones) lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ dalɛ agbɔjɔ kɛji akɛ atsuuu he nii mra.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava stems turning yellow and curling up tightly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpɛɔ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: This is a common sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried and spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. The disease stops the plant from making food properly, leading to very small or low-yield cassava tubers.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi ni afɔɔ naa yɛ ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he. ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ woɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa Hela nɛɛ haaa tsei afee niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii shishifãi bibii waa loo yibiiwoo ni baa shi lɛ baa.

english: How do I know if my land needs fertilizer or manure before I plant my next crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii dani madu miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: If your previous crops grew slowly, had pale green or yellow leaves, or gave very small yields, your soil is running low on essential nutrients like Nitrogen and Phosphorus and needs organic manure or chemical fertilizer to recover.
ga: Kɛji oŋmɔshi nibii ni eho lɛ dara blɛoo Eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. loo ewoɔ nibii fioo ko pɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ asaa

english: Why do agricultural officers tell me to plant groundnuts or beans on the plot where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmã yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops like groundnuts and beans are legumes, which pull nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots. Growing them after heavy-feeding crops like maize naturally refills the soil's strength for future crops.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei ji ŋmei. Egbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Nibii nɛɛ ni aduɔ yɛ kooloi aniyenii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa sɛɛ lɛ, baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why should I remove the extra small suckers growing at the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maŋɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Aduɔ krɛdɛɛ yɛ plantain wulu lɛ shishi.

english: If you leave too many suckers growing together, they compete with the main tree for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Leaving only one or two healthy suckers allows the mother plant to produce a bigger and heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛji oŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii bibii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ he kome lɛ, Amɛkɛ tso ni hereɔ amɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔlɔ tso lɛ ni ewoɔ tso wuji ni tsii.

english: Tomato plants shed flowers when temperatures get too high, when water supply is irregular, or when they lack key nutrients. Watering consistently during hot spells helps the flowers stay attached and turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Be mli ni nu lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni niyenii mli nibii titrii lɛ faaa Nu ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli daa yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are the bottoms of my pepper fruits turning dark brown and rotting before they turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper aduawai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni efiteɔ dani etsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called Blossom End Rot. It happens when the soil lacks sufficient calcium or when watering goes from very dry to very wet while the peppers are developing on the branch.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ Blossom End Rot. Ebaa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa loo kɛ́ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ waa nɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔtɔi lɛ miiya hiɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves look wilted in the afternoon heat even though I watered the soil in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ baai lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ amɛkwɛɛɛ moŋ lɛ? Higbɛ esa akɛ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu leebi?

english: During hot afternoons, leaves lose moisture into the air faster than the roots can drink water from the soil. The plant temporarily wilts to save water, but it usually bounces back by evening once the sun sets.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, baai lɛ fiteɔ nu ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ anu nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei sumɔɔɔ ni amɛbuɔ nu he be kukuoo ko. Shi bei pii lɛ, efoɔ esɛɛ gbɛkɛ beni hulu lɛ nyɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why do wild weeds grow back so quickly after I cut them down with a cutlass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ekoŋŋ oya nɛkɛ beni mikɛ dade shwieɔ amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Clearing land with a cutlass only removes the top stems of the weeds, leaving their underground root systems and buried seeds alive. Tilling the soil or applying mulch covers helps stop roots and seeds from shooting up again.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ nii lɛ shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, jwɛi lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ baajie. Ashiɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ kɛ dumɔwui ni afu lɛ ni amɛhiɛ kã. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni shishifãi kɛ dumɔwui lɛ akakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees are very delicate and burn easily in full sunlight. Plantains or shade trees act like living umbrellas, providing the cool shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa waa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa kookoo bibii koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ haa.

english: Why do my plantain plants keep falling over right before the fruit is ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains lɛ miigbee shi dani aduawai lɛ baafee klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: Plantain trunks are made of soft leaves rather than solid wood, and their roots are shallow. Supporting the plant with strong wooden poles or bamboo prevents the heavy bunch of fruit and high winds from pulling the plant down.
ga: Akɛ baai bibii feɔ plantain tsei lɛ, shi jeee tso ni wa. ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei loo ŋmeii ni wa fi tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi aduawai akui ni tsii kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa naa koni amɛkagbala tso lɛ shi.

english: Why do I need to spend time putting long sticks for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kakadaŋŋ he hiaa mi lɛ? Ba ni okpa koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam vines produce tubers by converting sunlight through their leaves. Lifting the vines up on stakes spreads out the leaves so they catch maximum sunlight, which results in larger yam tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii kɛtsɔ hulu la ni amɛtsakeɔ kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. Wein tso lɛ ni ooowo nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ baaha baai lɛ agbɛ ashwã koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ enɔ babaoo. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow in the middle of the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be ni amɛdaraa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. When nitrogen is low, the maize plant takes whatever is left in its older lower leaves and sends it up to feed the new top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji nitrogen lɛ faaa lɛ Abele lɛ baaŋɔ nɔ ni eshwɛ yɛ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ amli lɛ ni ekɛmaje ŋwɛi koni eyaye ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ.

english: How does leaving dried grass and dead leaves on top of my soil help my crops stay alive during dry spells?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi kɛ baai ni egboi ni mishiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves creates a protective blanket called mulch. Mulch stops the hot sun from evaporating water from the soil, keeps root zones cool, and slowly breaks down into crop food.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch lɛ baa. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni hulu ni tsoɔ lɛ akajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ tsei aniyenii.

english: Why shouldn't I apply my chemical fertilizer when the ground is completely dry and rain hasn't fallen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ okɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer requires water to dissolve so that roots can drink it in. Placing fertilizer on dry soil sits uselessly on top, can burn plant roots, or can easily blow away in the wind.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ biɔ ni etsɔ mli koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu. Sɛɛnamɔ ko bɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Ebaanyɛ eha tso shishifãi ashã. loo kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ shwieɔ lɛ oya

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas on my plot make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Te ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ aha tɛŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that work with helpful soil microbes to pull nitrogen gas out of the air and store it in the ground, leaving natural fertilizer behind for whatever crop you plant next.
