ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen gas kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto sũ lɛ mli. Eshiɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers become soft, watery, and light when I leave them in the ground for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ, nu, ni amɛhe waaa kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots reach maximum starch content at full maturity. If left in the soil past their prime, the plant starts consuming its own stored energy, making the tubers woody, watery, and low in starch.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ ji nɔ ni starch fa fe fɛɛ kɛji amɛdara kwraa. Kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛteke he ni eshɛɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baabɔi amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ hewalɛ ni ato lɛ kɛ nitsumɔ. Ehaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ tsei, amɛfeɔ nu ni amɛmli ŋmei faaa.

english: Why are all the flowers on my pepper plants falling off without turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when stressed by extreme weather heat, irregular watering, or a shortage of essential plant food like calcium and phosphorus needed to form fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa loo tsei amli niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ calcium kɛ phosphorus ni he hiaa koni aná aduawai lɛ ni bɛ.

english: Why are small caterpillars attacking the inner leaves at the very center of my young maize plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ tutuaa mligbɛ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms that target the softest, newest central growth of the maize plant. Catching them early prevents them from destroying the growing tip, which would stop the plant from forming grain.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms ni kwɛɔ ŋmãa tso ni ji gbekɛ fe fɛɛ, ni eda ehee fe fɛɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmɔmɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite ŋmeii ni miida lɛ. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ awo dumɔwui.

english: Maize leaves curl up during hot afternoons as a natural defense mechanism to reduce exposed surface area and stop water from evaporating too quickly from the plant.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni baaha ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ aba shi ni ekɛtsi nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli oya lɛ naa.

english: Why do my pepper plants rot at the roots when water stays on top of the soil for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shishifã lɛ fiteɔ beni nu lɛ ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli gbii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: When water sits in shallow or poorly drained soil, plant roots get flooded and cannot absorb oxygen from the air in the dirt, causing root rot and killing the plant.
ga: Kɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ekwɔɔɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tso shishifãi lɛ eyi obɔ kɛ nu ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛjie kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni efiteɔ tso lɛ.

english: Twisted and yellowing cassava leaves are usually caused by cassava mosaic disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies that feed on the sap of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei baa ni etsake ni efee ŋmɔŋ lɛ baa. Whiteflies bibii ni yeɔ tsei amli nu lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: What is making small ragged holes in the leaves inside the central whorl of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ baa ni yɔɔ mibi lɛ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋtayaa lɛ mli lɛ nɔ?

english: This leaf damage is typically caused by fall armyworms, which crawl into the growing center of young corn plants to feed on the tender new leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni egbee shi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛkpãa kɛboteɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii ni miida lɛ amli koni amɛye baai heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops compete against each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, resulting in weak stems and poor yield.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: How deep should I build my soil mounds when I want to plant yams?
ga: Kɛ́ oosumɔ ni odu sweet potato lɛ, te esa akɛ afee gɔŋ lɛ mli kwɔ ha tɛŋŋ?

english: Yams need deep, loose soil mounds so the roots can expand easily underground without running into hard, shallow soil that stops tuber growth.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli tse he miihia sweet potatoes bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi oya ni amɛka shi kɛya shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli ekwɔɔɔ nɔ, ni baaha tuber lɛ akakwɛ̃.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my corn turning yellow at the tips and dying off first?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛyitseiaŋ ni amɛgboiɔ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing that starts at the tips of lower leaves indicates a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which is the main food crops need to keep leaves green and growing.
ga: Su ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛ baai lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni amɛdara.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping all their flowers before any fruit forms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miishwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop flowers when exposed to sudden heat stress, dry soil, or a lack of soil nutrients, causing the plant to save its energy instead of fruiting.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni baa trukaa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hao amɛ. Ehaa tsei kɛ hewalɛ toɔ yibii moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay very small when I plant them under big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii waa kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava needs full, direct sunlight to make food through its leaves and store energy in its tubers, so shade prevents the roots from growing large.
ga: Cassava he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni etsɔ baai lɛ anɔ eye nii ni ekɛ hewalɛ ato tuber lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, shade lɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkadara.

english: Why is it beneficial to plant groundnuts on my land after harvesting a heavy crop like maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni akpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that naturally capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, helping to restore nutrients that maize took away.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii ni ŋmãa lɛ ejie lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that burn easily under direct intense sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with broad leaves, providing necessary shade and preserving soil moisture to help young cocoa survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Plantains daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ. Ha hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni okwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i nɔ koni eye ebua kookoo bibii lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my maize crops yield better when I plant cowpeas on the land during the season before?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ woɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu tsina ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli mra yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and other leguminous crops pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When you plant maize afterward, it feeds on this natural nutrient boost to grow stronger stems and larger cobs.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi Ejieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji odu ŋmãa sɛɛ mli lɛ Ebaaye nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii nɛɛ koni ekwɛ̃ ŋmãa ni wa kɛ ŋmãa wuji.

english: Why does my groundnut plant push stalks into the dirt after the flowers bloom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ tsiɔ eshishifã lɛ ewoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni ewo fɔfɔi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants form their pods underground. After pollination occurs above ground, the plant grows small stalks called pegs that naturally extend downwards into the soil where the nuts mature safely.
ga: Peanut tsei feɔ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Beni pollination baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ. Tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ tso bibioo ko. atsɛɔ lɛ pins Enɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ he ni ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shweshweeshwe lɛ.

english: Yellowing leaf tips on maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. When nitrogen is low, the plant pulls available nutrients from older lower leaves to support new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛji nitrogen faaa Tsei lɛ gbalaa niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni eye ebua dalɛ hee ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines dry up and turn brown at the end of the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Drying yam vines are a natural sign of maturity rather than a disease. The plant stops growing leaves and transfers all remaining energy into the underground tuber, signaling it is ready for harvest.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni egbi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ amɛmiida moŋ fe hela. Tso lɛ haa baai lɛ dalɛ kpaa ni ekɛ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ yaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amli. Etsɔɔ akɛ eshɛ he kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants dropping off without setting any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when day or night temperatures get too high, or when soil water levels fluctuate dramatically. Extreme heat stresses the plant, preventing pollen from fertilizing the flower.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji shwane loo gbɛkɛ mli latsaa lɛ fa tsɔ. aloo be mli ni nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsakeɔ waa lɛ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ. Etsiɔ pollen naa koni ekawo fɔfɔi amli fɔ.

english: Why do my watermelons taste watery and plain if heavy rain falls right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon lɛ ŋɔɔ tamɔ nu ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa dani akpa kpamɔ lɛ?

english: Watermelon plants absorb excess water very quickly near harvest, which dilutes the natural sugars inside the fruit. Reducing water right before picking allows sugars to concentrate for a sweeter taste.
ga: Watermelon tsei lɛ gbalaa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ oya beni ebɛŋkɛ nikpamɔ be lɛ. Enɛ baaha adebɔɔ mli sugars ni yɔɔ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ afee mlɛo. Nu ni ajieɔ lɛ shi dani ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sugar lɛ feɔ ekome koni ehiɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Curled pepper leaves are typically caused by tiny sucking insects like mites, thrips, or aphids feeding on leaf sap, or by a viral infection spread by these insects as they feed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ mites, thrips, loo aphids ni yeɔ baa lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛjɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa beni amɛyeɔ niyenii lɛ mli

english: Why do my cassava roots rot quickly underground if left in the soil during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Waterlogged soil cuts off oxygen to cassava roots. Excess stagnant water creates ideal conditions for soil-borne fungi and bacteria to attack the root tissues, causing rapid decay.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ amli. Nu ni damɔ shi fe nine lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha ŋmeii kɛ helatsɛmɛi ni yɔɔ sũ mli lɛ koni amɛtutua shishifãi lɛ. ni kɛ fitemɔ baa oya

english: Why do my tall maize plants fall over easily during light winds when the cobs start forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei kakadaji lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli wa waa mli lɛ? Mɛɛ be ŋmei lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ?

english: Maize plants fall over, or lodge, when root systems are too shallow or when high nitrogen makes stems tall and weak. Mounding soil around the plant bases during early growth helps anchor them against heavy cobs.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi loo amɛhiɔ shi kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ. Aloo kɛ́ nitrogen fa lɛ, tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ kɛlɛɔ ni amɛhe waaa. heaping dirt around Tso lɛ shishitoo yɛ be mli ni edaa mra lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ŋmɛɔ ŋmeii ni tsii waa lɛ ahe.

english: This usually means the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to grow green and strong. When the plant runs short of nitrogen, it steals it from its older lower leaves to keep the young top leaves growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ tsei bɛ nitrogen Ejuɔ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli koni baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anyɛ adara.

english: Why do I need to clear all the weeds before putting fertilizer around my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi fɛɛ dani mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster and steal fertilizer much quicker than your crops can. If you do not weed first, you end up feeding the weeds instead of your crops, causing the weeds to choke your harvest.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Kɛji ojieee jwɛi lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, Ebaabi ni okɛ jwɛi lɛ aye niyenii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ najiaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ oŋmɔshinii lɛ anɔ.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves and sucking out the plant sap. They can also pass small diseases to the plant that prevent the leaves from opening properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ nu lɛ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ helai bibii hu amɛshwã tsei ni haaa baai lɛ agbele jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ.

english: Plantain trees fall easily because tiny underground worms or root weevils eat away their weak roots. Without a strong root grip in the soil, the weight of the heavy bunch combined with wind tips the plant over.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii loo shishifãi ahewɔ. eyeɔ eshishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ Kɛji shishifãi ni wa bɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpɛtɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he Tso ni tsii lɛ tsiimɔ ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ fata he lɛ ha tso lɛ gbee shi.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by too much heat, lack of water, or when there are not enough tiny beneficial insects in the shade to pollinate the flowers so they turn into pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni fe nine, nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli, loo kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ hao amɛ. Shade ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ bɛ kɛyashi amɛbaafee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are my tomatoes developing black rotten patches at the bottom before they turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ dani etsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot and happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium from the soil. It is usually caused by irregular watering—either letting the soil dry out too much or flooding it with water.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ blossom end rot ni ebaa kɛji tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni afɔɔ nɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli, tamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni egbiɔ tsɔ loo nu lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi.

english: No, planting too close together causes crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in weak, thin stalks and very small fruits or ears, giving you a smaller overall harvest.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ aduawai loo toi bibii waa baa. Enɛ haa okpamɔ fɛɛ baa shi.

english: Why do young cocoa plants die if I clear away all the big trees from the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛji mijie tsei wuji kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that scorch easily under direct sunlight. Tall trees provide necessary shade and cool moisture that protect young cocoa trees until they are strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Yam leaves need plenty of sunlight to produce the food that grows big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves into the air to catch light and keeps them away from pests and rot on the ground.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ́ akwɛ bulb lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking woɔ tsei lɛ anɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni emɔ la ni ekɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ fitemɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he.

english: Will my cassava tubers spoil if I leave them in the ground during the rainy season?
ga: Ani mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ baafite kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ be mli?

english: If the soil gets flooded or stays soaked with water for too long, air cannot reach the roots, which causes the cassava tubers to rot quickly in the ground before you can harvest them.
ga: Kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu ewo mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ sũ lɛ mli dani abaanyɛ akpa amɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant is starving for nitrogen, an essential nutrient in the soil. This often happens when the soil is worn out from continuous farming or when heavy rains wash away nutrients, which can be fixed by adding organic manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ fɔɔ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ efite kɛjɛ okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ lɛ mli. Aloo be mli ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ laajeɔ. Abaanyɛ atsake enɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt and dry up even when the ground around them is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho ni amɛmiigbi eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by soil-borne fungal or bacterial wilt diseases. Excessive water in poorly draining soil rots the roots and blocks the tubes inside the stem, preventing water from reaching the upper leaves regardless of how wet the soil is.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Nu babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbo ni etsi tsɔnei ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ anaa. Enɛ haaa nu ashɛ baai lɛ anɔ, bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ha.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly during rainy seasons when humidity is high. Excess shade and overcrowded branches trap moisture, allowing the disease to ruin the pods if the farm is not cleared and pruned.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ. Shade babaoo kɛ tsei niji ni eyi obɔ lɛ baamɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Ha helai akpata ŋmeii lɛ ahiɛ kɛji ajieee ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ ni afolɔɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why do small caterpillars start eating the very center of my young corn plants right after they sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii jeɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ fã lɛ yeli shishi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, which hatch from eggs laid by moths inside the tender leaves of young corn. They target the funnel of the plant because the fresh, soft leaves inside provide easy food before the crop hardens.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni ŋmeii woɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ amli lɛ amli. Amɛtutuaa tso lɛ ŋmeii lɛ ejaakɛ baai heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ haa niyenii yeɔ mlɛo dani tso lɛ mli waɔ.

english: When cassava plants are crowded, their roots fight each other underground for nutrients and space, while their leaves block sunlight. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to develop thick, heavy tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Eshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná niyenii kɛ he ko. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ amɛhe lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni mli wa ni tsii lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: Why is it beneficial for me to plant cowpeas together on the same land with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ feɔ ekome kɛduɔ tsina ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas belong to the legume family, which pulls nitrogen from the air and fixes it into the soil. Planting them with maize naturally feeds nitrogen to the corn plants while shading the soil to retain moisture.
ga: Cowpeas yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni amɛgbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛsaa lɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nibii ni akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa duɔ lɛ haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ nitrogen yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo baa koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience extreme heat, drought, or poor soil nutrients like phosphorus. To survive the stress, the plant drops its blossoms to save energy rather than spending it on fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa, hɔmɔ, loo sũ mli niyenii ni ehiii, tamɔ fɔsfɔs lɛ he, koni amɛye amɛhe kɛjɛ haomɔ mli. Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaafite yɛ aduawai ahe.

english: Watermelons burst open when there is a sudden heavy rain after a dry spell. The plant absorbs water too quickly, causing the inside fruit to expand faster than the outer skin can stretch.
ga: Watermelons tswaa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa trukaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ. Tsei shwieɔ nu oya tsɔ. Enɛ haa tso yibii lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Yams need loose, deep, and well-mounded soil to expand downward smoothly. If the soil is hard, stony, or compacted, the growing tuber struggles to push through the dirt, resulting in small or misshapen yams.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni mli kwɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mlɛo. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa, tɛi yɔɔ nɔ, loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, ŋmeii ni miida lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during rainstorms even when the trunk looks healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems that stay near the top layer of soil. When heavy bunches grow at the top, the plant becomes top-heavy, making it easy for rainwater to soften the soil and wind to pull the shallow roots right out.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ he. Kɛji fɔfɔi lɛ shwere yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ Tso lɛ baaná muji babaoo yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. Nugbɔ nu haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ ajie shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ oya.

english: How long does a new cocoa tree usually take before it starts producing pods?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be enyiɛ eheɔ dani cacao tso hee ko jeɔ shishi ewoɔ ŋmeii?

english: With proper care and modern hybrid varieties, cocoa trees typically start bearing pods within 2 to 3 years, but full harvest production usually peaks around 5 to 6 years after planting.
ga: Kɛtsɔ hiɛdɔɔ ni sa kɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ hybrid henɔi anɔ. Bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli, shi bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa lɛ fɛɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ afii 5 kɛyashi 6 sɛɛ beni adu amɛ.

english: How far apart should I space my cocoa seedlings when expanding my farm?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo kookoo dumɔwui lɛ amli beni mikɛ miŋmɔ lɛ miigbɛ mishwa lɛ?

english: The standard spacing for cocoa trees is 3 meters by 3 meters (10 feet by 10 feet). Proper spacing ensures every tree receives adequate sunlight, nutrients, and airflow to prevent overcrowding and reduce disease spread.
ga: Gbɛ ni ato kɛha kookoo tsei lɛ ji mitai 3 x mitai 3 (naji 10 x naji 10). Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa hulu la, niyenii, kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ ji koni mɛi akayimɔ obɔbɔ fe nine, ni helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ hu aba shi.

english: How can I tell if my piece of land has good soil for cocoa farming?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni akɛduɔ kookoo?

english: Good cocoa soil should be deep, dark, well-drained, and rich in decaying plant matter. Avoid swampy land where water stands for days, as well as rocky or pure sandy soil that cannot hold nutrients.
ga: Esa akɛ kookoo shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ afee nɔ ni mli kwɔ, ni ehiɛ edɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. ni tsei ni fiteɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli Tsi ohe kɛjɛ hei ni nu ehi shi gbii babaoo lɛ ahe. Nɔ ni fata enɛ he ji tɛi loo ŋã shikpɔŋ krɔŋŋ ni nyɛɛɛ ahiɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: What other crops can I plant alongside my cocoa trees to earn extra income while waiting for them to grow?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ madu ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi yɛ cacao tso lɛ masɛi koni maná shika kroko yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: You can plant food crops like plantains, cassava, or maize alongside young cocoa. Plantains provide helpful shade for young trees, while short-term crops like cassava give you quick household income while cocoa matures.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu niyenii nibii tamɔ plantain, cassava loo ŋmãa yɛ kookoo bibii ahe. Plantains haa tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. Yɛ be mli ni be kukuoo mli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei haa onáa shia shika oya be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: What additional cash crops can I grow on my land to support my family during the cocoa off-season?
ga: Mɛɛ shika ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi manyɛ madu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni mikɛkwɛ miweku lɛ yɛ be mli ni kookoo lɛ bɛ lɛ?

english: Growing crops like oil palm, citrus, cashew, or maintaining economic shade trees like coconut and avocado on farm edges provides secondary harvests and steady income during non-cocoa months.
ga: Nibii tamɔ oil palm, akutu, kɛ cashew nuts ni aduɔ. aloo shika helɛtemɔ mli shade tsei tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ avocado ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ ahe lɛ akwɛmɔ. Ebaaha aná ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji enyɔ kɛ shika ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ yɛ nyɔji ni kookoo bɛ mli lɛ amli.

english: Young cocoa leaves burn easily under intense heat. Seedlings require shade canopy—often provided by temporary plantain plants or natural forest trees—to retain moisture and survive their first two years.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ la ni naa wa waa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ hia hulutsoo. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ jɛɔ be kukuoo mli dumɔwui loo tsei ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli kooi amli lɛ amli. Bɔni afee ni hulutsoo be lɛ ahi shi ni ehi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why is it important for me to regularly prune my cocoa branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ kookoo niji daa lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead, unwanted, or diseased branches, allowing light and air to penetrate the center of the tree. This reduces fungal growth, prevents shade overload, and encourages the tree to produce more cocoa pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni egboi lɛ. niji ni ataooo loo niji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ Enɛ haa la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ aba shi. Tsi hulutsoo ni fe nine lɛ naa. ni ekanyaa tsei lɛ koni amɛwo kookoo ŋmeii babaoo

english: How do I rehabilitate an old cocoa farm that is no longer producing enough pods?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mawo kookoo ŋmɔ momo ko ni wooo ŋmeii ni fa bɔ ni sa dɔŋŋ lɛ shi ekoŋŋ?

english: You can rejuvenate an unproductive farm by coppicing (cutting back old trunks to let fresh shoots grow) or gradually replacing old trees with high-yielding hybrid seedlings while maintaining temporary shade.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmɔ ni wooo yibii aba ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ tsei ni oookpa lɛ nɔ. (Fomɔ tsei akui momo koni ŋmeii heei akwɛ̃) loo fiofio lɛ, okɛ tsei momo ni ji hybrid dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ ato najiaŋ yɛ be mli ni ohaa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko hiɔ shi.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and rot before harvest, and how do I prevent it?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ dani akpaa? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu he?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in excessive moisture and dark shade. You can prevent it by clearing weeds around the base, pruning for good ventilation, and removing affected pods immediately.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ fɛ̃i fe nine kɛ duŋ mli ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Obaanyɛ otsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle shishi lɛ ni ooojie kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni oookpa koni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa abote mli lɛ nɔ. ni ojie pods ni ena hela lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: When is the best time of year to apply fertilizer to my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaawo mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Apply fertilizer at the beginning of the rainy season when the soil is moist. This allows the roots to absorb nutrients effectively; avoid fertilizing during severe dry spells or heavy downpours that wash nutrients away.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii jogbaŋŋ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ he yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni shwieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees turn yellow and die when there are no bigger trees planted around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to protect their delicate leaves from hot sunlight and to keep soil moisture from drying out quickly. Planting shade trees or plantains alongside young cocoa provides a protective canopy until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ taoɔ hɔɔŋ koni amɛbu amɛbaai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni koni ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ akagbi oya Tsei loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsei bibii ahe lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmɔtɔ he kɛyashi ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the soil is low in nitrogen, which maize needs in large amounts to grow. The plant moves nitrogen from older lower leaves to feed newer top leaves, so adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehe hiaa ni ŋmãa akwɛ̃ babaoo Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni etsɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baa heei lɛ niyenii. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or beans on a piece of land after harvesting maize from it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mikpa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize takes up a lot of nutrients from the soil, but legumes like beans and groundnuts capture nitrogen from the air and put it back into the ground. Rotating crops this way naturally restores soil fertility for future crops.
ga: Abɛi shwieɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ ni atsakeɔ yɛ nɛkɛ gbɛ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ekoŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Does it matter which direction the buds point when I stick my cassava stem cuttings into the soil?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ Mɛɛ gbɛ ŋmei niji lɛ baatsɔɔ?

english: Yes, cassava stem buds must point upward toward the sky. Planting stems upside down forces the new sprouts to bend down first before growing up, which wastes the plant's energy and lowers your root harvest.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ cassava tsei lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwu hee lɛ atsɔ ŋwɛi dani eda. Enɛ fiteɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ehaa shishifãi ni akpaa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why does planting my crops too close together cause them to grow tall and thin with very small harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ ni miduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa amɛfeɔ kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ kukuji ni yibiiwoo fioo pɛ amɛwoɔ lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, their roots and leaves compete against each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough food and light to grow sturdy stems and produce good yields.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu. He ni akɛtoɔ he ni sa lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ tsei ni wa ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Excessive moisture and poor airflow during rainy weather encourage a fungus called Black Pod to spread rapidly. Pruning extra cocoa branches and clearing weeds allows sunlight and wind to dry the farm and reduce fungal infection.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni eyaaa jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ blackpod lɛ agbɛ ashwã oya. Cocoa ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli egbiɔ kɛjɛɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa tsɛŋemɔ helai anɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do I see small holes in my young maize leaves and small caterpillars hiding inside the center shoot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii amli Ekɛtee ŋmãa ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworms feeding on the tender inner leaves of young maize plants. Inspecting fields early and applying appropriate natural or recommended treatments directly into the plant funnel stops them before severe damage occurs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ he lɛ mra ni akɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai loo tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ awo tso lɛ ŋmei lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Ekpaa nibii nɛɛ dani amɛfiteɔ nii waa.

english: Why shouldn't I allow all the young shoots to keep growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mihaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ fɛɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Mi plantain shishitoo titri lɛ

english: Allowing too many suckers to grow forces them to steal food and water from the main mother plant, resulting in smaller plantain bunches. Pruning away excess suckers leaves the strongest one for future growth while keeping the main bunch large.
ga: Suckers babaoo ni ashiɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantains lɛ feɔ bibii. Ni aaafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ amli lɛ haa tsei ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ baa kɛha wɔsɛɛ dalɛ yɛ be mli ni ehaa tsei akuu titri lɛ feɔ agbo lolo.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds and lift my yam vines onto wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi kakadaji ni mawo sweet potato wain tsei yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to reach open sunlight to produce the food required to swell their underground tubers. Raising the vines on stakes keeps leaves off hot, damp soil where diseases spread and improves tuber growth.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni agbele naa koni amɛná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii. Wein tsei ni aduɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ baabu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he. Biɛ ji he ni hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni ehaa tuber lɛ daalɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plant flowers fall off without growing into fruits when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ aduawai yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: High heat stresses tomato plants and dries out the pollen, preventing flowers from setting fruit. Covering the soil around the plant base with mulch helps keep root temperatures cool and retains soil moisture during hot spells.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa pollen lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Tsi fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkawo yibii Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ.

english: Why should I plant plantains alongside my newly planted cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving young cocoa trees the shade and moist climate they need to survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ mi akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-ŋmãa lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts extract nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. Planting them with maize acts as a natural fertilizer, feeding your maize plants and making the soil richer for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abele ni aduɔ lɛ baatsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Ha ŋmãa tsei lɛ niyenii ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛo kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, which it needs to grow green and healthy. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients out of the soil or leaves the roots waterlogged.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Ehe miihia ni amɛdara ni amɛfee eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli loo eha shishifãi lɛ amli eyi kɛ nu.

english: Tomato flowers drop off without setting fruit when temperatures are too high, when water is inconsistent, or when there are no insects around to pollinate them. Regular watering and gentle shade during extreme heat can help flowers turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Kɛ nu lɛ mli ebɔle ehe Aloo kɛji kooloi bibii bɛ he ni amɛbaawo fɔfɔi lɛ, nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ tomato.

english: Yam plants rely on their leaves receiving maximum sunlight to generate energy to grow heavy tubers underground. Staking lifts the vines off the damp ground, increasing sunlight exposure and preventing leaf rot.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ baai ni naa hulu la babaoo lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛfee hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Ha hulu la lɛ aya hiɛ ni otsi baai ni fiteɔ lɛ naa.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is typically caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or mites, or viruses spread by whiteflies. Treating these pests early prevents the leaves from twisting and keeps the plant growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. loo helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Tsa nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ mra. Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni eda.

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil holds too much water and roots cannot get air, allowing water fungi to infect them. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo. ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ Ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela aba nu lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: It is best to water early in the morning because the cool soil absorbs water before the sun can evaporate it. Watering in the afternoon heat can shock the leaves, while evening watering leaves plants wet overnight, causing leaf disease.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha nu leebi maŋkpa ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ lɛ baaŋɔ nu dani hulu la lɛ atsɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shwane mli latsaa be mli lɛ baanyɛ aha baai lɛ akpokpo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu ni oooha tso lɛ gbɛkɛ lɛ baaha tso lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nyɔɔŋ kome. Ebaanyɛ ekɛ baa hela aba.

english: Why does leaving my farmland unplanted for a year make my crops grow better when I return to it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ mishi miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi kome ni miduko nɔ ko lɛ, ehaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ miku misɛɛ kɛba lɛ?

english: Leaving land to rest gives the soil time to naturally replenish missing nutrients, organic matter, and moisture. It also starves out crop-specific pests and diseases that were living in the field.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ejɔɔ ehe lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa be ni ekɛ niyenii, nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni efite lɛ baa ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ejieɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ tsei ahe helai ni hiɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my dried maize grains develop small holes and turn to white powder inside my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni etsɔ powda yɛŋ yɛ mi ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by small insects called grain weevils that lay eggs inside dried maize. The larvae hatch and eat the inside of the grain. Drying maize thoroughly and storing it in airtight bags suffocates the insects and protects your yield.
ga: Koolooi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ seed moths ni woɔ wɔji yɛ ŋmãa ni egbi mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Lala lɛ fɔɔ ni eyeɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ogbi ŋmãa lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛwo kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaabu oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Which crops can I plant on my farm in Ghana that can survive long dry seasons without dying easily?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei manyɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ Ghana ni baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli ni amɛgbooo mlɛo?

english: Crops like cassava, sorghum, and cowpea are naturally tough and drought-tolerant. They have deep root systems or leaves that conserve water, making them far better suited to survive dry spells than delicate vegetable crops.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa kɛ tsina ŋmãa lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nibii ni wa ni amɛnyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa. Amɛ yɛ shishifãi loo baai ni mli kwɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hiɔ shi. Enɛ haa amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli fe aduawai ni mli wa waa.

english: How do I choose crop seeds that will not catch diseases easily on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala dumɔwui kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ ni hela tsɛŋeɔ mɔ oya?

english: You should look for certified seeds labeled as 'disease-resistant' or ask your local extension officer for recommended native varieties. These seeds produce stronger plants that can naturally defend themselves against common leaf and root illnesses.
ga: Esa akɛ otao dumɔwui ni yɔɔ odaseyeli akɛ ‘enyɛɔ helai anaa’ loo obi o-extension agent lɛ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui srɔtoi ni ajieɔ yi lɛ ahe. Nɛkɛ dumɔwui nɛɛ woɔ tsei ni he wa ni baanyɛ abu amɛhe kɛjɛ baa kɛ shishifãi ahe helai ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually show that the plant is hungry for nitrogen or that too much water around the roots is stopping the plant from taking up food from the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ loo nu yɛ ehe. Shishifãi babaoo haa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: During extreme heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can suck it out of the ground. The plant wilts temporarily to protect itself from losing more water and usually recovers when the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baagbo be kukuoo ko koni ebu ehe koni nu babaoo akafite. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants keep dropping their flowers before any peppers start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ miiho amɛfɔfɔi lɛ dani pepper lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they experience heat stress, irregular watering, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil consistently moist and providing shade during midday heat helps flowers stay on the stem.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. Nu ni afɔɔɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell if my crops are suffering from an insect attack or a plant disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kooloi loo tsei ahe helai emɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Insect attacks usually leave visible chewed holes on leaves or stems, while diseases show up as brown spots, powdery patches, wilting, or unusual yellow patterns on the leaves without any visible bugs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni tutuaa mɛi lɛ haa ŋmeii ni amɛyeɔ lɛ shwieɔ baai loo amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Yɛ be mli ni hela lɛ jeɔ kpo akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Powder spots, wilted, loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ baai ni kooloi bibii ni anaaa bɛ mli lɛ anɔ.

english: Is it good practice to spray chemical medicine on my crops every week even when I don't see pests?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ makɛ tsofai afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ daa otsi kɛji minaaa tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi po?

english: No, spraying chemicals unnecessarily wastes money and can kill beneficial insects like bees while making pests stronger and resistant to the medicine over time. You should only apply treatments when you see clear signs of pests or disease.
ga: Dabi, tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mɔ nɔ lɛ ji shika fitemɔ ni he ehiaaa, ni ebaanyɛ egbe kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ ŋmeii yɛ be mli ni ehaa kooloi bibii lɛ hu he wa ni amɛnyɛɔ amɛyeɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli. Esa akɛ okɛ tsofa lɛ atsu nii pɛ kɛji ona tsɛŋemɔ hela loo tsɛŋemɔ hela he okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ.

english: What happens to my crop yield if I plant my cassava sticks too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ he tsɔ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots and leaves fight each other for water, sunlight, and nutrients. This competition leads to tall, skinny plants with very small roots beneath the ground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii kpakpai. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni amɛhe tseee ni shishifãi bibii waa yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ baa.

english: Beans and cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil through their roots. This acts as natural fertilizer, making the soil richer and helping the maize plants grow stronger.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔshi nii ni eye ebua ŋmãa tsei lɛ ni amɛdara waa

english: How can I help my young cocoa plants develop deep, strong roots that will keep them alive for many years?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛná shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa ni baahi shi afii babaoo?

english: Covering the ground around young cocoa trees with dry leaves or straw (mulching) keeps the soil cool and moist. This encourages the plant's taproot to grow deep into the earth searching for nutrients instead of staying shallow.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi (mulching) ha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Enɛ woɔ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ hewalɛ koni ekwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni eyatao niyenii mli hewalɛ moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ.

english: Why are my young cocoa trees failing to grow well after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings struggle to grow if they receive too much direct sunlight, lack sufficient soil moisture, or are planted in hard, poor soil. Protecting young plants with shade crops like plantain gives them the sheltered environment they need to establish strong roots.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui bibii lɛ baaná naagba akɛ amɛaada kɛji hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo ba amɛnɔ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni bɛ loo adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni bɛ hewalɛ nɔ Tsei bibii ni akɛ hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains buɔ he lɛ haa amɛ shihilɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa.

english: Does the spacing between cocoa trees affect how fast they grow and produce?
ga: Ani gbɛ ni kã kookoo tsei ateŋ lɛ saa bɔ ni amɛdaraa oya ni amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ he?

english: Yes, planting cocoa trees too closely together causes them to compete for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, leading to weak growth and low yields. Proper spacing gives each tree enough room to develop a healthy canopy and root system.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ adu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ehaa amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa kookoo tso lɛ daaaa jogbaŋŋ, ni yibiiwoo hu faaa. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi ni mli wa kɛ shishifãi ahe gbɛjianɔ.

english: Why do extension officers advise leaving certain big trees standing in my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nitsulɔ ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ wo ŋaa akɛ ashi tsei wuji yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Large shade trees protect cocoa plants from extreme sun heat, help maintain humidity on the farm, prevent soil erosion, and drop leaves that rot into rich organic manure for the cocoa roots.
ga: Tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli Etsiɔ shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ naa ni ehaa baai ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa kɛha kookoo shishifãi.

english: Do mature cocoa trees need full sun or shade to produce good yields?
ga: Ani hulu loo hulutsoo he miihia kookoo tsei ni edara lɛ koni amɛwo yibii kpakpai?

english: Mature cocoa trees grow best under light, filtered shade (about 30-40% shade). Too much shade reduces flowering and yields, while no shade at all can stress the tree and shorten its lifespan.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ kane ni ajieɔ mli (aaafee 30-40%) shishi. Shade babaoo baaha fɔfɔi kɛ yibiiwoo aba shi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, hulutsoo ko kwraa bɛ ni baanyɛ aha tso lɛ aná nɔnyɛɛ ni eha ewala be lɛ afee kuku.

english: How can I stop monkeys and other wild animals from destroying my cocoa pods?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi ŋmeii kɛ koolooi krokomɛi ni yɔɔ ŋa nɔ lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ?

english: Wildlife can be managed by regularly harvesting ripe pods so they do not attract animals, clearing thick brush along farm boundaries to reduce animal cover, and using boundary deterrents or traditional scare tactics.
ga: Abaanyɛ akwɛ koo mli kooloi anɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ ni akpaa daa koni amɛkagbala kooloi. Tsɔɔmɔ jwɛi ni mli tse. yɛ ŋmɔ mli husui lɛ ahe koni akɛba kooloi ni ha amɛhe lɛ shi ni akɛ husui ahe nibii ni tsiɔ mɔ naa loo blema gbɛi ni akɛwoɔ mɔ he gbeyei lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why are insect pests worse on some cocoa farms than on others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ehiii kwraa yɛ kookoo ŋmɔji komɛi amli fe ekrokomɛi lɛ?

english: Pests thrive on farms with dense overgrown branches, excessive shade, or neglected weeds. Regular pruning allows sunlight and air to pass through the tree canopy, creating an environment that deters major cocoa pests like mirids.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yeɔ omanye yɛ ŋmɔji ni niji babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Shade babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ tsɔ. loo jwɛi ni aku hiɛ ashwie nɔ Tso lɛ ni afoɔ daa lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ko ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ kookoo mli nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ pollen lɛ ahe lɛ baa.

english: Why am I putting in so much hard labor on my farm but getting very few cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsuɔ nii waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli shi minine shɛɛɛ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi fioo pɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Low yield despite high labor usually happens when trees are unpruned, diseased, growing in nutrient-depleted soil, or affected by black pod disease. Focusing labor on proper pruning, pest control, and soil fertility converts hard work into actual harvest.
ga: Nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ nitsumɔ hewalɛ ni fa babaoo lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ Bei pii lɛ ebaa kɛji afooo tsei, hela mɔ amɛ, amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. loo black pod hela lɛ ena enɔ Okɛ ojwɛŋmɔ ama ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ nii kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa lɛ nɔ Ebaatsɔ onitsumɔ ni wa lɛ nɔ etsɔ ŋmaa diɛŋtsɛ.

english: What benefits will I see if I prune my cocoa trees regularly?
ga: Mɛɛ sɛɛnamɔi maná kɛji mifo mi-cacao tsei lɛ daa?

english: Pruning removes dead or non-producing branches, directing the tree's energy into growing healthy cocoa pods. It also increases airflow and sunlight, which dramatically reduces fungal diseases like black pod.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ hewalɛ yaa ni ekɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni mli wa. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛ hulu la hu yaa hiɛ. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji black pods lɛ baa shi waa.

english: Why is one of my cocoa trees wilting and drying up while the others nearby look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ eko miigbo ni eegbi yɛ be mli ni cacao tsei krokomɛi lɛ miigboi lɛ? Mɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ tamɔ mɛi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: A single cocoa tree dying amidst healthy ones often indicates a root infection, attack by stem borers, or Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus disease. Unhealthy trees should be inspected early to stop diseases from spreading to surrounding plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo tso kome ni gboɔ yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ateŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hela ko emɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Stem borer tutuamɔi loo cocoa bud virus hela Esa akɛ akwɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ mra. Enɛ baatsi hela lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ amli.

english: Why do flowers appear on my cocoa trees but drop off without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii jeɔ kpo yɛ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ shi amɛgbeeɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop without developing into pods if the tree is stressed by drought, lacks essential nutrients, suffers from pest damage, or lacks beneficial insects like midges that pollinate the flowers.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛtsɔko ŋmɔtɔ kɛji hɔmɔ ha tso lɛ hao. Niyenii ni he hiaa ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fiteɔ lɛ ni bɛ loo kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ, tamɔ midges, ni haa fɔfɔii amli ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ ni bɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are missing nitrogen, which is an essential plant food, or the roots are sitting in too much water and cannot breathe or absorb nutrients properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Aloo shishifãi lɛ yɛ nu babaoo mli ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu loo amɛhe niyenii kpakpai jogbaŋŋ.

english: Spreading dry grass or leaves on top of the soil helps trap moisture, keeps the ground cool during hot sunny days, and prevents weeds from growing and taking nutrients away from your crops.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ waa lɛ amli. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛkajie niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and can easily burn or dry out under full sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide big leaves that act as shade umbrellas to protect the cocoa until it grows stronger.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛshã loo amɛgbi yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi oya. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo ni buɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni enáa hewalɛ.

english: Why should I leave distance between my cassava cuttings instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mi-cassava tsei lɛ ato he ko moŋ fe ni madu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots compete with each other for space, water, and nutrients in the soil, resulting in smaller tubers than if they had enough room to grow.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ he ko, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii feɔ kɛji amɛyɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdara.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects and stays in the soil for too long without draining properly, causing fungal diseases that destroy the roots before harvest.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa ni ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ dani akpaa.

english: How do I know the soil is ready for me to sow my maize seeds after the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the ground has received two or three good, heavy rains so the soil is thoroughly moist down deep, giving the seeds enough water to germinate and grow without drying out.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná nugbɔshiimɔi kpakpai fioo komɛi ni naa wa koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛdara ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips feeding on the sap under the leaves, or by viral sicknesses spread by those insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies kɛ thrips ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nakai kooloi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli

english: What is making small holes in my maize leaves and leaving powdery dirt in the central shoot?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ ni eshiɔ muji ni tamɔ powda yɛ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ.

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central growing tip of young maize plants and eats the leaves before they open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ashishifãi amli yɛ ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa, ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ dani amɛgbeleɔ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the sunlight to make energy for growing large tubers underground; letting them trail on the ground keeps them in the shade and reduces yields.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã hulu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs wuji ni baakwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ oŋmɛ amɛ gbɛ ni amɛnyiɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛhi hulutsoo be mli, ni ebaaha yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when temperatures get too high, when the plants do not get consistent water, or when bees and insects fail to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni tsei lɛ náaa nu daa Aloo be mli ni ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii nyɛɛɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii.

english: How do I know if the seeds I saved from my own last harvest are good enough to plant again?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ dumɔwui ni mikpa kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ hi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu ekoŋŋ?

english: Look for large, plump, and healthy seeds without holes or mold. Sorting out the tiny or damaged ones ensures your new crops grow strong and give you a good yield.
ga: Taomɔ dumɔwui ni dara, ni egbɔjɔ, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni bu loo ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli. Kɛ́ ojie tsei bibii loo ni efite lɛ, ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ adara waa ni ewo ŋmaa kpakpa.

english: Does planting larger seeds mean I will get a bigger crop yield at the end of the season?
ga: Ani dumɔwui wuji ni aduɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ maná ŋmaa babaoo yɛ be lɛ naagbee?

english: Yes, larger and fuller seeds usually contain more food reserves for the young plant, giving the seedling a stronger start and leading to healthier, higher-yielding crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ni dara ni eyi obɔ lɛ fɔɔ niyenii babaoo ni ato kɛha tso bibioo lɛ. Ehaa dumɔwui jeɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni woɔ yibii babaoo baa.

english: Why should I spend money to buy certified seeds instead of using seeds from my previous harvest for free?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafite shika kɛhe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ? Mohu ɔ, i kɛ dumɔwuhi nɛ i je ye kpami nɛ i kpa ye nɛ i kpata nɛ i kɛ tsu ní ɔ tsu ní.

english: Certified seeds are specially tested to resist local pests, handle dry weather better, and produce much higher yields than recycled seeds, which lose their strength over time.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ mli krɛdɛɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛte shi amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai. Etsuɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ he nii jogbaŋŋ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni akɛtsuɔ nii ekoŋŋ, ni hewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ.

english: How much water do my crops actually need when I am using manual irrigation during the dry season?
ga: Nu enyiɛ he hiaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ kɛ́ mikɛ niji shwieɔ nu nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Crops need enough water to soak deep into the root zone rather than just wetting the surface. Watering thoroughly two to three times a week is usually better than giving a light splash every day.
ga: Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa he miihia tsei koni amɛbote shishifãi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ moŋ fe ni amɛaaha amɛhiɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ. Nu ni oooha shii 2-3 yɛ otsi mli lɛ hi lolo fe nu fioo ni oooha daa gbi.

english: Is it better to water my crops in the middle of the day when the heat is strong or early in the morning?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oooshwie ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ nu yɛ gbi ni mli edɔ lɛ mli loo leebi?

english: It is best to water early in the morning because mid-day heat causes most of the water to evaporate into the air before the plant's roots can drink it.
ga: Okɛ nu awo mli leebi maŋkpa ejaakɛ gbi lɛ mli latsaa lɛ baaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anu.

english: If I am planting a field of about 2.5 acres, how do I figure out the right space to leave between my crops?
ga: Kɛ midu aaafee acre 2.5 lɛ, te mafee tɛŋŋ mana he ni sa ni mashi yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ?

english: Proper spacing depends on the crop type, but leaving enough room allows each plant to get equal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients without fighting its neighbors.
ga: He ni sa ni jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ lɛ damɔ tso henɔ lɛ nɔ. Shi kɛ́ ashi he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ ekutsoŋbii lɛ awuu.

english: What happens if I plant too many seeds close together in a single hole?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ bu kome mli?

english: If you plant too many seeds together, the growing plants will compete with each other for food and light, resulting in weak, thin stems and very small fruits.
ga: Kɛji odu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ he kome lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii kɛ la. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, tsei lɛ ahe tsei bibii, kɛ aduawai bibii waa.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow even though I am giving them enough water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil has run out of vital nutrients like nitrogen. Adding compost or the right fertilizer gives the plant the energy it needs to turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaha otsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛtsɔmɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I protect my stored seeds from insects before the next planting season starts?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu midumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ahe dani be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aba?

english: Make sure your seeds are completely dried in the sun, treat them with recommended seed protection powder or neem oil, and keep them sealed in airtight containers.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ni odumɔwui lɛ agbi kwraa yɛ hulu lɛ mli. Kɛ dumɔwui ahebuu powda loo neem fɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ atsu nii. ni akɛwo tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli.

english: How can I estimate how much harvest I will get from my farm before the season even ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu nibii ni manyɛ makpa kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ayibɔ he akɔntaa dani be lɛ aba naagbee?

english: You can estimate your yield by counting the healthy plants in a small section of your farm, checking the size of the developing fruit or grains, and multiplying that across your total field size.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu yibiiwoo ni obaaná lɛ he akɔntaa kɛtsɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ fã bibioo ko nɔ lɛ akanemɔ nɔ, ni okwɛ bɔ ni aduawai loo dumɔwui ni miiya hiɛ lɛ dara ha lɛ nɔ. ni okɛ ogbɛhe lɛ fɛɛ abɔ he.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings burn and turn brown when planted in the open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very delicate and cannot handle direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains planted alongside them to shield their leaves from intense heat and keep the soil moist while they establish roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa kwraa, ni amɛŋmɛɛɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Bɔni afee ni abu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛfeɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. The maize plant moves the remaining nitrogen from its older bottom leaves up to support the new growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi tsei tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni eye ebua dalɛ hee ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: The young shoots, called suckers, compete with the main plant for soil nutrients and water. Pruning away weaker suckers ensures the main plant gets enough food to grow large, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Tso bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ kɛ tso ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Kɛ́ afo tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ plantain tsei wuji ni tsii lɛ anɔ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences extreme afternoon heat, irregular watering, or excess nitrogen fertilizer. The heat stresses the plant, causing it to drop flowers to preserve its own survival.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na shwane mli dɔlɛ ni naa wa. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa loo nitrogen ni fa fe nine Dɔlɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛbu lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala he.

english: Why do I need to heap loose soil around the base of my cassava plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ sũ ni mli ewo muji lɛ toɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ?

english: Heaping loose soil protects expanding cassava tubers from exposure to direct sunlight and pests, while also making it easier for roots to swell and grow large beneath the ground.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni aaabɔ he lɛ baaye abua ni ebu ŋmeii shishifãi ni miiya hiɛ lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ shishifãi lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛdara babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are typically caused by tiny sucking insects like mites or thrips feeding on the undersides of the leaves, which damages the leaf tissue and distorts growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ mites loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ni amɛnuɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. ni fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji ni efiteɔ dalɛ

english: What happens if I leave my yam vines to spread on the bare ground instead of using sticks for them to climb?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mishi sweet potato wain tso yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni mikɛ tso nine baakwɔ nɔ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch enough sunlight for making food. Leaving vines on the damp ground exposes leaves to soil diseases and reduces sunlight, resulting in much smaller tubers at harvest.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha nihoomɔ. Kɛ́ ashi wain tso lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baa lɛ aba tsei lɛ ahe, ni ebaaha hulu la lɛ aba shi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, kɛ́ akpa ŋmeii lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii kwraa.

english: Why is it good practice for me to plant groundnuts or beans on my land after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans are legumes that capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When harvested, they leave this nitrogen behind, naturally feeding the soil for the next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Be ni esa akɛ akpa Amɛshiɔ nitrogen yɛ amɛsɛɛ. koni akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii aha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ

english: Why do my vegetable plants droop in the middle of the day even when the soil was watered in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ gboɔ yɛ gbi mli lɛ? Higbɛ esa akɛ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu leebi?

english: On very hot afternoons, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can draw water from the soil. Drooping is a temporary defense mechanism to reduce leaf surface area and hold onto moisture.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Defoliation ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ mɔ he yɛ be kukuoo mli koni akɛba baa lɛ hiɛ shi ni akɛha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: How can I tell if a cassava stem cutting is good enough to plant on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmei tso lɛ mli tsei ni afo lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: A good cassava cutting should come from a healthy, mature plant, feel firm, have visible raised buds (eyes) along the stem, and show no signs of insect damage or stem drying.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmei kpakpai ni afo lɛ ajɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eda lɛ amli. Eyɛ hiɛ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni ŋmeii (hiŋmɛii) ni etee ŋwɛi faŋŋ yɛ tso lɛ he. Ni okadi ko bɛ ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi efite loo tsei lɛ egbi.

english: What is mixed farming, and how can combining crops with other farm activities help my land?
ga: Mɛni ji okwaayeli ni akɛfee ekome? kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ okwaayeli nitsumɔi krokomɛi feɔ ekome. Te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Mixed farming means growing crops while also raising farm animals or keeping fish on the same farm. The manure from animals feeds your crops as natural fertilizer, and leftover crop stems feed the animals, saving you money and making your land produce more overall.
ga: Okwaayeli ni akɛfee ekome lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ aduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be kome mli. kɛ kooloi akwɛmɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli loo loo ni akwɛɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli Kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii haa onibii lɛ niyenii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. ni tso lɛ shishifãi ni eshwɛ lɛ ji kooloi aniyenii. Ehaa onáa shika ni ehaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: Why do many farmers in my area plant cassava and maize together on the same plot of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi babaoo ni yɔɔ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ feɔ ekome kɛduɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize grows fast and is harvested within three to four months, while cassava grows slowly underground over a full year. Planting them together gives you a quick harvest of maize first, while leaving space for the cassava to mature later on the same land.
ga: Abɛi daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa daa blɛoo Shikpɔŋ shishi afi muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ Companion dumɔ baaye abua bo ni okpa ŋmãa oya klɛŋklɛŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eshiɔ gbɛ ehaa ŋmeii ni baakwɛ̃ yɛ sɛɛ mli yɛ nakai he lɛ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my corn plants grow thin and weak when I put many seeds together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa beni mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo woɔ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the young plants end up fighting each other for sunlight, water, and food in the soil. Spacing seeds properly ensures every plant gets enough nutrients to grow thick stems and big cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei bibii lɛ baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers without producing any fruit when the weather becomes very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni ewooo yibii be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: When heat is too intense, pepper plants get stressed and drop their flowers to conserve water and survive. Giving them shade or watering them regularly during hot spells keeps the plant cool enough to hold its flowers and turn them into peppers.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ haoɔ ni amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ okɛ hulutsoo loo nu wo tso lɛ nɔ daa yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ mli jɔɔ bɔ ni sa koni ehiɛ efɔfɔi lɛ amli ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize are usually a sign that the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the food plants need to stay green and grow strong. Heavy rains can also wash nitrogen deep into the ground where small roots cannot reach it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hu baanyɛ afɔ nitrogen lɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi bibii baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ lɛ. anyɛɛɛ ashɛ he

english: Why does putting dry grass or leaves around the base of my crops help them stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ mitsei lɛ ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry leaves or grass (called mulching) acts like an umbrella for the soil. It blocks the hot sun from drying out the ground, keeps the soil cool, and traps moisture so your crops stay hydrated longer.
ga: Ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ mulching.) Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ. Etsĩɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli bɔni afee ni onibii lɛ ahi shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants curling up and looking twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle ehe ni efee tamɔ nɔ ni efite lɛ?

english: Curling and twisted leaves on cassava are caused by a sickness called Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny white insects called whiteflies. Using healthy, disease-free stems for planting helps protect your crop from this problem.
ga: Hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ cassava mosaic disease lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei baa ni ebɔle ehe ni etsɔ ŋmei lɛ baa. Kplukai bibii yɛŋ ji nɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Kɛ́ okɛ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni hela bɛ mli lɛ tsu nii kɛ́ oodu lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu onibii ahe kɛjɛ naagba nɛɛ he.

english: Why is it bad for me to plant tomatoes on the exact same spot where I just harvested garden eggs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ madu tomato yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni mifo ŋmeii lɛ yɛ abɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomatoes and garden eggs (eggplants) belong to the same plant family and share the same pests and soil diseases. Planting them in the same spot season after season lets pests and diseases build up in the soil and attack your new plants immediately.
ga: Tomato kɛ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii (eggplant) yɛ tso weku kome mli ni amɛ fɛɛ amɛyeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ helai kome. Tsei ni ooodu yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ baaha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛtutua otsei heei lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why are my yam tubers growing small even though the vines and leaves on top look long and very green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tsei lɛ bibii waa lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ wain tso lɛ kɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni kɛlɛ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ moŋ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer, the yam plant uses all its energy to grow big leaves on top instead of sending energy underground to swell the tuber. Yam needs balanced soil food and soft, deep soil to produce large tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ Sweet potato tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai wuji yɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsu hewalɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ shishi koni eha yitso lɛ ada lɛ. Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni mli kwɔ koni ekɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: How do I know if the first rains of the season are enough for me to start planting my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ?

english: Do not plant after just one short rainfall, because the dry soil will quickly soak up the water and leave your seeds to dry out. Wait until the rain falls steadily for a few days and the soil stays wet up to your finger's depth before planting.
ga: Kaadu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ be kukuoo ko pɛ sɛɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ gbalaa nu oya, ni no haa dumɔwui lɛ gbiɔ. Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ be fɛɛ be gbii fioo komɛi. Ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ kɛyashɛɔ inchii dani aduɔ nii.

english: Why do the leaves on my young plantain trees dry up and turn yellow during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have broad leaves that lose water very quickly in high heat. During dry months in Ghana, the plant naturally drops its outer leaves to conserve moisture and protect its main stem.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni nu fiteɔ oya waa kɛji akɛ amɛwo la ni mli edɔ waa mli. Yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ yɛ Ghana lɛ amli lɛ, Tsei shwieɔ amɛ kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he ni amɛbu tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ he.

english: Why does my plantain plant take more than a year to produce its first bunch of fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ heɔ nɔ ni fe afi dani ekɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ ŋmeii lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Plantains normally take between 12 and 15 months to fruit. If the soil lacks key nutrients like potassium or does not get enough water during its early growth stage, the plant will take even longer to mature.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, plantains heɔ nyɔji 12 kɛyashi 15 dani ewoɔ yibii. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium loo enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ yɛ shishijee be mli ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Tsei baahe be babaoo dani amɛdara.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when strong winds blow through the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa kɛfo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems that stay close to the topsoil. When the soil becomes very wet or when the heavy weight of a growing bunch pulls the plant down, strong winds can easily tip the entire tree over.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa loo be mli ni tso lɛ kuu ni miida lɛ tsiimɔ ni tsii lɛ gbalaa tso lɛ kɛyaa shi lɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ aha tsei akumɔ shi mlɛo.
