english: Why do I need to cut off the extra shoots growing around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie plantain tso lɛ tso lɛ

english: The small shoots, called suckers, compete with the main plant for water, sunlight, and soil food. Pruning away the excess shoots leaves only the strongest stem, which results in a bigger and healthier harvest.
ga: Tso bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaashi tsei ni wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa.

english: Can I grow food crops like cassava or vegetables on the same plot where I plant my plantains?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmei loo aduawai yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ plantains yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, intercropping is common in Ghana, but crops must be spaced properly. Planting tall or heavy-feeding crops too close to plantains can cause them to fight for light and soil nutrients, lowering the yield of both crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni afɔɔ feemɔ yɛ Ghana. Shi esa akɛ atse tsei lɛ ateŋ jogbaŋŋ. Tsei ni yeɔ niyenii ni nɔ kwɔ loo ni tsii ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ plantains tsɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ abɔi niyenii ni mli tse kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei sɔrɔtoi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ yibii lɛ ba shi.

english: How can I tell if a plantain shoot is healthy enough to plant in a new field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi plantain tsei lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu yɛ shikpɔŋ hee nɔ?

english: A good shoot, known as a maiden sucker, has narrow sword-shaped leaves, a firm bulb at the bottom, and clean roots without dark spots, soft rotting areas, or holes caused by pests.
ga: Sucker wulu, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ Maiden Sucker lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni tamɔ klante. Eyɛ bulb ni mli wa yɛ shishigbɛ. kɛ shishifãi ni he tse ni ŋmɔtɔ diji bɛ mli He lɛ egbo blɛoo. aloo buji ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛbaa lɛ yɛ jɛmɛ

english: How does covering the soil around my plantain roots with dry leaves help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi plantain shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ ni mikɛ baai ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Covering the ground around your crop with dry grass or leaves is called mulching. It keeps the soil cool, prevents moisture from evaporating quickly in the hot sun, and stops weeds from growing around your crops.
ga: He ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ ni akɛhaa Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. ni otsi jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ naa.

english: Is it really necessary to spend money on fertilizer for plantains, or will they yield well on their own?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni afite shika ni akɛhe ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha plantains loo ebaawo yibii kpakpai kɛjɛ ehe?

english: While plantains can grow naturally, they feed heavily on soil nutrients like potassium and nitrogen. Adding manure or fertilizer helps them develop thick stems, resist diseases better, and yield much heavier bunches.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ plantains baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ adebɔɔ naa moŋ, Shi amɛyeɔ sũ mli nibii babaoo tamɔ potassium kɛ nitrogen. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Helai ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ helai ni ekɛ kui ni tsii fe tsutsu lɛ baa

english: How do improved crop seed varieties help my farm compared to the traditional seeds I usually save?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei dumɔwui ni atsake lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ lɛ? Kɛ akɛto blema dumɔwui ni mifɔɔ kɛtomɔ he lɛ he

english: Improved crop varieties are selected to grow faster, withstand dry conditions better, and resist common plant diseases that often reduce harvests from traditional local seeds.
ga: Ahalaa tsei srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ koni amɛdara oya. Shihilɛi ni mli egbi ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ tsei ahe helai ni afɔɔ namɔ ni bei pii lɛ ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni jɛɔ blema maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui amli lɛ baa shi lɛ ahe shiwoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What causes black spots to appear on crop leaves, and how can I keep them from spreading?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tsei ahe baai anɔ lɛ baa? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ oootsɔ otsĩ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa?

english: Black spots are usually fungal infections caused by high humidity and leaves staying wet for too long. Clearing weeds around your crops and cutting off infected leaves improves air movement and stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni jɛɔ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo kɛ baai lɛ ni haa efɔ̃ɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ kɛbaa. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi ni bɔle oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ni ofolɔ baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ni ebaaha helai agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do people tell me to plant plantains on the same land where I just planted young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ko baakɛɛ mi akɛ midu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni midu kookoo tsei bibii amrɔ nɛɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are delicate and burn under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce large leaves that provide essential shade and protect the soil's moisture while your cocoa trees are establishing themselves.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai agboi ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ hebuu yɛ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ miida lɛ.

english: Why do we make high earth mounds before planting yam seeds instead of planting them in flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wɔmaa gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ dani wɔduɔ sweet potato dumɔwui yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni wɔbaadu yɛ shikpɔŋ kplanaa nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need loose, deep soil to grow long, thick, and healthy. High mounds prevent the soil from compacting, improve drainage during heavy rains, and make harvesting easier without breaking the tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni mli tse koni amɛdara kakadaŋŋ, amɛmli, ni amɛhe wa. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ tsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ha nu ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli. ni ehaa ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo ni akuuu bulb lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize are usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil or heavy rain washing away nutrients. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or Urea helps restore their green color and growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ efo. Nitrogen babaoo ni yɔɔ mli tamɔ NPK loo urea ni akɛaatsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ dalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: The first application should be done about 1 to 2 weeks after planting when seedlings emerge. A second top-dressing application should be done around 4 to 6 weeks after planting when the stalks grow rapidly.
ga: Esa akɛ afee klɛŋklɛŋ tsofa lɛ aaafee otsi 1 kɛyashi 2 yɛ dumɔwui lɛ adumɔ sɛɛ beni dumɔwui lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Esa akɛ afee ŋwɛi atadewoo ni ji enyɔ aaafee otsii 4 kɛyashi 6 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Be mli ni tso lɛ daa oya

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains specific soil nutrients and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like beans or groundnuts naturally enriches the soil with nitrogen.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa ŋmãa nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ. Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná nitrogen babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why does allowing weeds to grow around my crops reduce the size of my harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ oŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ haa mikpamɔ lɛ dalɛ baa shi?

english: Weeds steal essential water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crops. When crops have to compete with weeds, they cannot grow strong enough to produce high yields.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Beni esa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ jwɛi abɔ akaŋ lɛ Amɛnyɛŋ amɛdara ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: How do I control the small caterpillars that are eating the middle leaves of my young corn?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makudɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ mi-ŋmei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms. You can control them by applying approved pesticides early in the morning or late evening, or by sprinkling clean neem leaf powder or wood ash into the plant funnels.
ga: Ekolɛ Fall Armyworms ji enɛɛmɛi. Obaanyɛ okudɔ amɛ kɛtsɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni okɛbaatsu nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ nɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ neem baa powda loo tso sũ ni he tse ni akɛshwieɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ nɔ.

english: Cassava is typically ready 9 to 12 months after planting. Indications include the lower leaves turning yellow and falling off, and the soil around the stem base cracking as the tubers expand.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ. Nɔ ni tsɔɔ akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli fãa be mli ni tuber lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes rotting and turning black before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifite ni etsɔ ediŋŋ dani eshɛ po lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot. It is usually caused by irregular watering, which prevents the tomato plant from absorbing enough calcium from the soil while the fruit is growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ haaa tomato tso lɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ.

english: Why do my crops wilt during the afternoon heat even if it rained two days ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ gbii enyɔ ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Hot afternoon weather causes water to evaporate rapidly from plant leaves faster than roots can absorb it from drying topsoil. Placing dead grass or mulch around crop bases helps trap soil moisture longer.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi gbohii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ he. Tso lɛ shishitoo lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Maize leaves usually turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen or when too much standing water around the roots prevents the plant from breathing and absorbing nutrients properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni damɔ shi babaoo ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni no haaa tso lɛ amu jogbaŋŋ ni enyɛŋ eŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cowpea crops grow so well without me adding synthetic nitrogen fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ nitrogen ni akɛfee ŋmɔshi nii lɛ fataaa he lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes, which means their roots work together with good bacteria in the soil to pull nitrogen directly from the air and turn it into food for the plant.
ga: Cowpea ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ helatsɛmɛi ahe nibii kpakpai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛtsake lɛ amɛfee tsei aniyenii.

english: Why does an orange tree planted directly from a seed take so many years to bear fruit compared to a grafted tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ citrus tsei ni akwɛɔ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii kɛ akɛto tsei ni akɛwo amɛhe lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: A tree grown from a seed has to go through a long juvenile phase where it focuses purely on building strong roots and branches, whereas a grafted tree uses a branch taken from an already mature tree that is ready to produce fruit right away.
ga: Tsei ni jɛ dumɔwui amli akwɛ̃ lɛ tsɔɔ oblahiiaŋ ŋmɔnɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli. Ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa shishifãi kɛ niji ni wa amamɔ pɛ nɔ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsei ni akɛ tsei ebɔ he lɛ kɛ tsei niji ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni edara ni efee klalo akɛ amɛbaawo yibii amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when strong winds and heavy rains come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that stay near the surface, so when the heavy bunch of plantains grows at the top, the plant becomes top-heavy and easily gets pulled out of soft, wet soil.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛbɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ plantains babaoo yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ, Tsei lɛ feɔ ŋwɛi-tsiimɔ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ oya.

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when temperatures get too high or when there is irregular watering, as heat and water stress prevent the flowers from pollinating and setting fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baafɔ̃ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu lɛ haaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Yɛ dɔlɛ kɛ nu he haomɔ hewɔ lɛ, fɔfɔi nyɛɛɛ afee pollination ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why does my maize crop start producing flowers early when there is a long period without rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔi shishi oya be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When crops face extreme dry weather, they sense danger and try to produce seeds as quickly as possible to ensure their survival before the plant dies.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli egbi waa kpe lɛ Amɛnuɔ oshara he ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛwo dumɔwui oya bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛhi shi dani tso lɛ agbo.

english: Why do my cassava plants have huge green leaves on top but very small tubers underneath the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ hiɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi?

english: If cassava receives too much nitrogen or excessive water, it spends all its energy growing leafy stems above ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers below.
ga: Kɛji ŋmei lɛ nine shɛ nitrogen loo nu babaoo nɔ Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ starch toɔ tso ɔ sisi fã nɛ ngɛ sisi ɔ mi.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves up toward the sun to capture light and make food; keeping the leaves off the damp ground also protects the plant from diseases and helps build larger tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã hulu lɛ he koni amɛmɔ la lɛ ni amɛfee niyenii. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu buɔ tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ helai ahe, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔi wuji baa.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking the plant juices, or by a virus carried by whiteflies that distorts normal leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛji kɛbaa ni fiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ ni sa lɛ nɔ

english: Should I clear five acres of land with the little money I have, or focus on doing just one acre very well?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ shika fioo ko pɛ ajie shikpɔŋ ni dalɛ ji acre 5 lɛ nɔ loo mikɛ mijwɛŋmɔ ama ekpakpafeemɔ nɔ yɛ acre 1 pɛ nɔ?

english: It is much better to start small and manage one acre with high quality seeds, proper fertilizer, and regular weeding. A well-managed small farm will produce higher yields and profit than a large, neglected farm where crops suffer from poor care.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooobɔi bibioo. ni ekwɛ shikpɔŋ acre kome ni dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ daa Okwaafoi bibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo ni amɛnáa sɛɛnamɔ fe ŋmɔji wuji ni akuɔ hiɛ ashwieɔ nɔ ni akwɛɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii jogbaŋŋ yɛ mli lɛ.

english: Certified seeds are specially bred to resist common diseases, tolerate drought better, and grow uniformly. Saved seeds from previous harvests lose their vigor over time, leading to weaker plants and lower yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni afɔɔ namɔ. Hɔmɔ he tsuishitoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ daa Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ kpamɔ ni eho mli lɛ baafite hewalɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo lɛ hu baa shi.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close together, won't I get more corn harvested from my farm?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani maná ŋmãa babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting too close causes crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This stress results in thin, weak stalks and very small or empty cobs, ultimately reducing your total harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ wuɔ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Nɔ ni jɛɔ nɔnyɛɛ nɛɛ mli baa ji tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ. kɛ cobs bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli Enɛ haa yɛ naagbee lɛ, onibii fɛɛ ni okɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baa shi.

english: Why shouldn't I leave all the young plantain shoots growing around the main mother plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mashɛrɛɔ plantain tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ ashwieɔ lɛ? Tso titri

english: Too many shoots (suckers) steal food and water from the main plantain tree. Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two strong ones, ensuring the main tree produces a much larger, heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: Suckers (shoots) babaoo tsɔ juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni no baaha tso titri lɛ awo ŋmeii ni dara ni tsii babaoo.

english: Staking lifts the yam leaves up into the sunlight so the plant can produce more energy. Sunlight exposure allows the plant to send food down into the ground, producing much bigger and healthier tubers.
ga: Staking haa hulu la shɛɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ ajie hewalɛ babaoo. Hulu la ni tsoɔ lɛ haa tsei kɛ niyenii yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ feɔ agbo babaoo ni ehaa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn brown and die when I remove all the shade trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijieɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to heat and direct sunlight. Without shade trees like plantains or forest trees to shield them, the intense sun burns their delicate leaves and dries out the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Kɛji tsei ni baaha hulutsoo aba, tamɔ tsei bibii loo koo mli tsei bɛ lɛ, Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ baashã ebaa ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off without producing fruit during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes away pollen and high humidity prevents insects from pollinating the flowers properly. Excessive moisture also encourages fungal diseases that weaken the stems holding the flowers.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ ahe ni hulutsoo ni fa babaoo lɛ haaa kooloi bibii lɛ aná fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine lɛ hu woɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa tsei ni hiɛ fɔfɔi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ lɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot inside the soil before I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ŋmeii lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani mikɛ amɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects and sits around the roots for too long without draining. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water flow away, keeping the tubers healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛ amɛhe. Shishifãi lɛ yaa shɔŋŋ tsɔ ni nu shwieee. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. ni eha yitso lɛ aná hewalɛ

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites feeding on the sap under the leaves, or by a virus spread by these insects. Controlling these pests early stops the leaves from curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Kudɔmɔ kooloi nɛɛ mra Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkabɔle amɛhe.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow much faster than my crops after I apply fertilizer to the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni mikɛ ŋmɔji lɛ ewo ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: Fertilizer acts as food for all plants in the soil, including weeds. If you do not clear the weeds before applying fertilizer, the weeds will steal the food first and choke your crops.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii kɛhaa tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni jwɛi fata he. Kɛji ojieee jwɛi lɛ dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli lɛ, Jwɛi lɛ juɔ niyenii klɛŋklɛŋ ni efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce flowers, but the flowers just fall off without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny insects called midges to transfer pollen from flower to flower. If these pollinators are absent or cannot reach the flowers, the flowers drop off without developing into cocoa pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii. Atsɛɔ amɛ midges koni amɛkɛ pollen ajɛ fɔfɔi kome mli kɛya ekroko mli. Kɛji akɛ nɛkɛ pollinators nɛɛ bɛ loo amɛnyɛŋ amɛshɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe lɛ, Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛbaafee kookoo ŋmeii.

english: What brings beneficial insects like pollinators to my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni kɛ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ, tamɔ pollinators baa mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Pollinators like cocoa midges thrive in cool, moist environments with rotting organic matter, such as damp fallen leaves and banana stumps, which give them safe places to breed and live.
ga: Pollinators tamɔ kookoo yibii yeɔ omanye yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Nibii ni fiteɔ tamɔ baai ni egbee shi kɛ banana tsei ni efɔ lɛ yɛ mli. Enɛ haa amɛnáa he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni amɛfɔɔ bii ni amɛhiɔ shi.

english: How does pollen actually help my cocoa trees produce pods?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ pollen yeɔ ebuaa mi-cacao tso lɛ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa?

english: Pollen is the fine powder inside a flower. When pollinating insects carry this pollen to the female part of another flower, it fertilizes the plant so it can grow into a healthy cocoa pod.
ga: Pollen ji powda kpakpa ko ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ pollinators lɛ kɛ pollen nɛɛ tee fɔfɔi krokomɛi ahe yei ahe lɛ, Ebaaha tsei lɛ aná fɔ bɔni afee ni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔmɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: What should I do on my farm when my cocoa trees start flowering heavily?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli beni kookoo tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ babaoo lɛ?

english: When trees are flowering, avoid spraying harsh chemical insecticides that kill friendly pollinators, and keep the farm ground shaded and rich with natural leaf litter to support pollination.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ Tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi ni kɛ amɛhe feɔ naanyo lɛ ahe. kɛ ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ ni aaaha efee hulutsoo ni adebɔɔ mli baai amli jwɛi babaoo aba mli koni eye ebua pollination.

english: Does the overall environment and care of my farm really change how well my crops produce?
ga: Ani shihilɛ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛ bɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ ahaa lɛ tsakeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli yibiiwoo lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, maintaining a calm, well-kept environment with proper shade, weed management, and rich soil encourages beneficial insects to stay on your farm and helps plants use their energy to make fruit.
ga: Hɛɛ, shihilɛ ni yɔɔ kpoo ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni hulutsoo ni sa yɔɔ mli lɛ mlihiɛmɔ. jwɛi nɔkwɛmɔ Ni shikpɔŋ ni nɔ eyi obɔ lɛ woɔ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛhi oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ yibii.

english: How do shade and ground cover affect the insects that help my crops?
ga: Te hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii náa kooloi bibii ni yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ hewalɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Moderate shade and ground mulch keep the soil cool and moist. This creates an ideal habitat for pollinators while protecting the soil from drying out under strong sunshine.
ga: Shade ni sa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ he ko ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ, ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hu he koni ekagbi yɛ hulu ni naa wa lɛ shishi.

english: Why do some of my young cocoa pods turn black and dry up before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Young pods may dry up due to incomplete pollination, nutrient competition, or fungal diseases like black pod. Maintaining clean farm habits and good airflow helps pods grow safely.
ga: Pods bibii lɛ baanyɛ agbi yɛ pollination ni eshɛɛɛ he lɛ hewɔ. Niyenii mli hewalɛ akaŋshii loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai diji. Okwaafoi ashihilɛ mli sui ni he tse kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ mlihiɛmɔ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa shweshweeshwe.

english: How can I estimate how many cans or bags of cocoa my farm can produce?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu kookoo kans loo kotokui enyiɛ ni miŋmɔ lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ he akɔntaa?

english: Yield depends on tree age, soil quality, shade level, and pollination success. Counting the number of healthy, pollinated pods per tree during flowering gives you an early idea of your total harvest.
ga: Yibiiwoo damɔ tso lɛ afii abɔ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, bɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ ha kɛ pollination omanyeyeli nɔ. Kɛ́ okane tso kome mli ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ fɔfɔii amli lɛ ayibɔ yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha oná susumɔ ko ni mli wa. Yɛ okpamɔ lɛ fɛɛ he

english: Why is one of my cocoa trees full of pods while the tree right next to it has almost nothing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ eko mli eyi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ? be mli ni tso ni bɛŋkɛ Hardly nɔ ko kwraa?

english: Individual trees vary based on their health, soil nutrients, shade exposure, and whether pollinating insects happened to visit that specific tree's flowers during blooming.
ga: Tso fɛɛ tso baafee srɔto yɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ hewalɛ ha lɛ naa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii, hulutsoo, kɛji akɛ ŋmeii ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ yaa tso lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: How does heavy rainfall or dry weather affect how my crops set fruit?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ saa ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Heavy rain can wash away pollen and stop tiny insects from flying, while severe dry weather causes flowers to dry up. Gentle rain and humid, shaded conditions are best for pollination.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe ni etsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkafo, yɛ be mli ni shihilɛi ni mli egbi waa lɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ agbiɔ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo kɛ hulutsoo be ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha pollination.

english: How deep into the soil am I supposed to plant my crop seeds?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu midumɔwui lɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ?

english: Most seeds should be planted shallowly, around 5 centimeters deep. Planting at this depth ensures the seed gets enough soil moisture while still allowing the young sprout to easily push through to the surface and reach sunlight.
ga: Esa akɛ adu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ, aaafee sɛntimitai enumɔ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nɛkɛ shɔŋŋ nɛɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ aná shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa dumɔwui lɛ boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya ni amɛnaa hulu la.

english: What will happen to my crop if I plant the seeds too deep in the soil?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ?

english: If you bury seeds too deep, the young sprout uses up all its stored energy trying to push through the heavy soil and may die before reaching the surface, leading to poor crop growth or failed seeds.
ga: Kɛji ofu dumɔwui lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ Tsei bibii lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛto lɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ mli ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi dani amɛshɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ loo dumɔwui lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ.

english: Does it matter which side or direction I place a seed or cutting when planting it in the ground?
ga: Mɛɛ he loo gbɛtsɔɔmɔ mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ woɔ loo mifoɔ kɛji midu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, placing the root or stem part facing downwards correctly in the soil allows the plant to anchor its roots quickly and direct its shoots upward without wasting energy turning itself around.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ akɛ shishifã lɛ fã loo shishifã lɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ ŋmɛɔ eshishifãi lɛ ahe oya ni ekɛ shishifã lɛ baa ŋwɛi ni efiteee hewalɛ ni ekɛtsakeɔ ehe lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my seeds are planted shallow enough to sprout easily?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ adu midumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya?

english: A simple guide is to plant seeds at a depth about 2 to 3 times their size, usually around 5 centimeters for standard seeds, so the soil layer above them stays light and easy for shoots to break through.
ga: Yiŋtoo ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo ji ni adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ aaafee amɛdalɛ toi 2 kɛyashi 3. Enɛ feɔ sɛntimitai enumɔ kɛha dumɔwui ni afɔɔ namɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, sũ ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ mli waaa ni eboteɔ mli oya.

english: What should I do if my crop plants become extremely bushy and overgrown in the field?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ebɔle ŋmɔ lɛ he waa ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When plants become too bushy, you should prune or thin out extra leaves and stem branches so that sunlight and air can reach all parts of the crop, reducing disease and focusing energy on yield.
ga: Beni tso lɛ egbɔjɔ tsɔ Esa akɛ ofolɔ loo ofolɔ baai kɛ eniji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ashɛ tso lɛ fãi fɛɛ ahe. Tsɔɔmɔ helai anɔ ni okɛ ojwɛŋmɔ ama nibii ni anáa lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my crops produce so many leaves but very few fruits or seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ woɔ baai babaoo shi ewoɔ yibii loo dumɔwui fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Excessive leafy growth often happens when plants get too much nitrogen or are left unpruned, causing the crop to spend all its energy growing big and bushy rather than producing flowers and fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yaa hiɛ fe nine lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ ná nitrogen babaoo loo afolɔɔɔ amɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai moŋ.

english: Will a plant being very bushy harm the final harvest of my field?
ga: Ani tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ baawo naagbee kpamɔɔ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he gbeyei?

english: Yes, if a plant becomes too dense and bushy, it creates shade over itself, traps humidity that attracts pests, and wastes nutrients on leaves instead of swelling fruits or tubers.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji tso lɛ mli eyi tsɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔji. Ebaafee hulutsoo eha ehe. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni gbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baa Ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ laajeɔ yɛ baai lɛ amli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha aduawai loo ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: How does managing overgrown branches and leaves help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei niji kɛ baai ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ akwɛmɔ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Trimming extra growth reduces overcrowding, allows airflow to dry wet leaves, and directs water and soil nutrients straight into fruit and root development instead of excess foliage.
ga: Kɛ́ afo dalɛ kroko mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni gbɔmɛi ni eyi obɔ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tsɔɔ baa ni efɔ lɛ mli ni egbiɔ. ni etsɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ koni aduawai kɛ shishifãi lɛ aya hiɛ. yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ najiaŋ

english: Why are my seeds taking so long to push through the soil after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni adu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Delayed emergence usually happens if the soil above the seed is hard and compacted or if the seed was buried too deep for the sprout to push through easily.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kwɛ̃mɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ mli wa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Aloo kɛji akɛ afu dumɔwui lɛ amli tsɔ bɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ nyɛŋ atsɔ mli oya.

english: How does soft, loose soil around the planting hole help my young seeds grow?
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni ebɔle he Te dumɔ bu yeɔ ebuaa midumɔwui bibii lɛ ni amɛdaraa tɛŋŋ?

english: Loose soil around the top 5 centimeters allows delicate shoots to break through quickly and gives early roots easy access to air, water, and nutrients needed for strong early growth.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni shɛɔ sɛntimitai 5 lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya. ni ehaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ mra lɛ náa kɔɔyɔɔ, nu, kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa koni amɛdara mra lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my crop yield get smaller every year if I keep planting on the same land my family left for me?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛji mitee nɔ midu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miweku lɛ shi mi lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Crops pull food and nutrients out of the ground every season. If you do not give the soil time to rest or put nutrients back using manure or fertilizer, the soil becomes exhausted, leading to smaller harvests.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Kɛji akɛ ohaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe loo okɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ tsuuu nii ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baaho, ni no baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa lɛ baafee bibioo.

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crops. Even if the farm looks large, the roots underground compete for the exact same food, leaving your crops weak.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni da moŋ Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ he akaŋ. Ha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee gbɔjɔmɔ

english: Tree crops like cocoa spend their first few years building deep root systems and strong trunks so they can support heavy fruit later. They need time to mature before they have enough energy to produce pods.
ga: Tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo tamɔ kookoo lɛ kɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ maa shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ tsei ni wa koni amɛnyɛ amɛye amɛbua aduawai ni tsii yɛ sɛɛ mli. Ehe miihia ni amɛná be dani amɛdara dani amɛná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛfee pods.

english: Why does cassava manage to stay green and alive even when the dry season lasts very long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ehiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ waa po mli lɛ?

english: Cassava stores water and food reserves deep inside its underground tubers. It can also drop some leaves during dry periods to save water, making it very tough in hot weather.
ga: Cassava kɛ nu kɛ niyenii toɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli shɔŋŋ. Kɛfata he lɛ, abaanyɛ ashɛrɛ baai komɛi ashwie yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni akɛbu nu he. Enɛ haa ehiɔ shi waa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning light yellow from the bottom up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main plant food that keeps leaves green. Heavy rains can wash this nutrient out of the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii titri ni jɛɔ tsei amli ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do coconut trees take so many years to bear fruit compared to maize that finishes in a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akokoshi tsei heɔ afii babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ? Kɛ akɛto ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli lɛ he?

english: Maize is a short-term plant designed to grow, produce seed, and die in one season. A coconut tree is a perennial plant that spends years building a permanent trunk and deep roots so it can keep producing for decades.
ga: Abɛi ji be kukuoo mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ koni ekwɛ̃, ewo dumɔwui, ni egbo yɛ be kome mli. Kokoo tsei ji tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo ni amɛheɔ afii babaoo dani amɛfeɔ tso ni hiɔ shi daa, ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ ni haa anyɛɔ atsuɔ nii afii nyɔŋmai abɔ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants drop off during heavy rains instead of turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee pepper lɛ?

english: Heavy rain can knock fragile blossoms off physically, and too much water in the soil stresses the plant's roots, causing it to drop flowers temporarily until conditions improve.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ agbee shi. Ni nu babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baaha tsei shishifãi lɛ afee nɔ ni wa. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ laajeɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shihilɛi lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and tall without bearing fruit when I plant seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛkwɔ ni amɛwooo yibii beni midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crowded plants fight each other for sunlight. They waste all their energy growing upward to reach the light instead of putting energy into making fruit.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ hulu la lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Amɛfiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ koni amɛshɛ la lɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛkɛbaabɔ aduawai.

english: Can I put all my crop fertilizer into the soil at once during planting to save time?
ga: Ani manyɛ mawo miŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be kome mli yɛ dumɔ be mli koni mikɛ be akafite?

english: Young plants cannot absorb a large amount of fertilizer at once. If you apply it all at the start, heavy rains will wash most of it away before the plant's roots grow big enough to use it.
ga: Tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo shikome. Kɛ okɛ fɛɛ tsu nii kɛjɛ shishijee Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ emli babaoo dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ daraa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akɛtsu nii.

english: Why should I trim or cut off some branches from my fruit trees when I want them to grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ loo mafolɔ niji komɛi ni yɔɔ mi tso lɛ nɔ lɛ? Be ni miisumɔ ni eda?

english: Trimming off weak or extra branches stops the tree from wasting food on parts that do not produce good fruit. It sends all the water and nutrients directly to the healthiest fruit-bearing branches.
ga: Kɛ́ ofolɔ niji ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekaye nii yɛ hei ni etsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ yaa tso yibii niji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Tomato flowers usually drop when temperatures are too high or when watering is irregular. Giving the plants consistent water at the root and providing shade during extreme heat helps the flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu lɛ efɔɔɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ aha tsei lɛ nu ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Leaf curling and yellowing are often a crop's reaction to extreme heat stress, water loss, or small sucking pests like aphids. Mulching the root area with dry grass keeps the soil cool and retains moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni shwieɔ shi kɛ ŋmɔŋ ji nɔ ni tso lɛ feɔ kɛji edɔ waa. nu ni laajeɔ loo kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi ha shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why are my young cocoa seedlings turning brown and drying up in full sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that cannot handle direct midday heat. Planting shade crops like plantains next to cocoa trees acts like a natural umbrella, protecting the seedlings until their roots grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ adamɔ hulutsoo be ni baa shwane mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ Cocoa tso lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the maize plants fight each other for sunlight and soil nutrients. Spacing seeds properly gives each plant enough food and light to develop thick stems and full cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Abɛi tsei wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ he jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Yellowing from the bottom up means the plant is hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient for growth. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves stay green and healthy.
ga: Yellow kɛjɛ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why are my cassava tubers small and woody instead of large and soft?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛji tsei moŋ fe ni amɛaafee wuji ni amɛhe yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots become thin and tough if planted in hard, compacted soil or harvested too late during a dry spell. Loosening the soil before planting helps the tubers expand easily.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe wa kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ nɔ loo akpa amɛ sɛɛ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ dani adu lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya.

english: Why do my okra leaves have small holes all over them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii yɛ amɛhe fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Holes in okra leaves are caused by leaf-eating insects like flea beetles feeding on the plant. Spraying the leaves with organic neem oil solution protects the foliage so the plant can grow normally.
ga: Koolooi ni yeɔ baai tamɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ tso lɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ okra baai lɛ amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ organic neem oil solution shwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaabu baai lɛ ahe koni tso lɛ anyɛ ada jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my yam leaves turning black and the vines dying before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni wain tsei lɛ miigboi dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ?

english: Yam leaves turn black when affected by a fungal disease called anthracnose, which spreads quickly in wet weather. Clearing surrounding weeds and planting resistant varieties helps keep the vines green until maturity.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ anthracnose lɛ ye amɛnɔ. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ni ajieɔ Kɛ henɔi ni nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni wain tsei lɛ feɔ eŋɔli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes spoil and go soft before I can take them to market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani akɛwoɔ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes ripen and soften very quickly when exposed to heat after harvest. Harvesting early in the cool morning and storing them in ventilated crates in the shade preserves their firmness much longer.
ga: Tomatoi lɛ shwereɔ ni efeɔ blɛoo oya waa yɛ latsaa be mli beni akpa lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ okpa amɛ yɛ leebi ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli ni okɛwo adeka ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaaha amɛhi shi shiŋŋ be babaoo.

english: How do I know if my harvested maize is dry enough to store without molding?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-abele ni mikpaa lɛ mli egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mikɛto ni mikɛ ŋmɔtɔ akafee nɔ ko?

english: Maize is dry enough for storage when the grains make a sharp cracking sound when bitten, rather than denting. Thorough sun-drying prevents mold and insects from ruining the grain, preserving its quality for market.
ga: Abɛi lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akɛto beni ŋmeii lɛ feɔ gbee ni tswaa kɛji akɛ amɛye lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee ŋmeii lɛ, hulutsoo be mli ni agbiɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii akafite dumɔwui lɛ. ni ekwɛ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ nɔ kɛha jarayeli lɛ.

english: Why does my locally planted rice taste different or take longer to cook compared to imported rice from Thailand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ ŋɔɔ yɛ srɔto loo ekɛ be babaoo hoɔ fe ŋmãa ni akɛjɛɔ Thailand lɛ?

english: Local Ghanaian rice varieties often contain higher natural nutrients and fresh oils depending on soil conditions, whereas imported rice is heavily polished and processed for long ocean travel, which changes its texture and cooking behavior.
ga: Ghana ŋmãa henɔi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ fɔɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛ fɔ hee babaoo. Edamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛ nɔ Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ajieɔ ŋmãa ni akɛbaajɛ maŋsɛɛ aba lɛ waa ni atsuɔ he nii kɛhaa ŋshɔ hiɛ gbɛfaa kakadaŋŋ. Enɛ tsakeɔ bɔ ni afeɔ lɛ ahaa kɛ bɔ ni ahoɔ nii ahaa lɛ.

english: How can I get my local Ghanaian rice farm to yield as many bags as foreign production standards?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mimaŋ Ghana ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ awo baagi babaoo tamɔ maŋsɛɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ?

english: Achieving high yields requires using certified high-yielding seed varieties suited for Ghanaian weather, maintaining precise planting distances, controlling weeds early, and applying the right fertilizer at key growth stages.
ga: Bɔni afee ni aná yibii babaoo lɛ, ehe miihia ni ana dumɔwui srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni sa Ghana kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ lɛ he odaseyeli. Dumɔ he jɛkɛmɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni akwɛɔ Jwɛi lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ dalɛ bei ni he hiaa lɛ amli

english: Why does rice need standing water in the field to grow well compared to crops like maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni damɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Rice plants are naturally adapted to aquatic conditions. Maintaining shallow standing water smothers weeds and creates a stable root environment that helps the plant absorb nutrients continuously.
ga: Omɔ tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ nu mli shihilɛi amli. Nu ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni jwɛi lɛ akabote mli, ni ehaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni haa tsei lɛ yaa nɔ amɛnáa niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why are my rice leaves turning yellow before the crop is mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani aduɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves early in the season usually indicate a nitrogen deficiency in the soil or water balance issues. Applying balanced nitrogen fertilizer early keeps leaves green so they can feed the developing grain heads.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu lɛ he naagba ko yɛ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra Enɛ baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji koni ekɛ niyenii aha dumɔwui ni miiya hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why are weeds growing faster than my young rice plants in the swamp area?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe mi ŋmãa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ ŋshɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds thrive in warm, wet soil and grow aggressively. Keeping a controlled water depth of 5 to 10 centimeters after rice seedlings establish will drown out emerging weeds while allowing the rice to grow tall.
ga: Jwɛi shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ, ni efɔ lɛ nɔ ni amɛdaraa oya. Akwɛɔ nu lɛ mlibotemɔ nɔ yɛ sɛntimitai 5 kɛyashi 10 mli beni ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ. Enɛ baaha jwɛi ni jeɔ kpo lɛ agbɔjɔ yɛ be kome too mli. ni eha ŋmãa lɛ aya hiɛ

english: Why are small brown spots appearing across my rice leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ? Ejeɔ kpo yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ?

english: Brown spots are typically caused by fungal infections like rice blast, which attack plants under nutrient stress. Using clean certified seeds and maintaining healthy soil nutrients helps prevent this disease.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko, tamɔ ŋmãa tsɛŋemɔ hela, ni tutuaa tsei yɛ niyenii mli hewalɛwoo shishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ brown spot baa. Dumɔwui ni he tse ni awo he odaseyeli ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ akwɛmɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ hela nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do some plants in my rice field produce grains earlier than others planted on the same day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ dumɔwui mra fe ekrokomɛi lɛ? Adu yɛ gbi kome nɔ?

english: Uneven flowering happens when seeds are mixed with different varieties or when soil nutrients and water levels are uneven across the field. Planting pure, single-variety certified seeds ensures uniform crop growth.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni bɛ gbɛjianɔtoo mli lɛ baa kɛji akɛ akɛ dumɔwui kɛ srɔtoi srɔtoi ebɔ he. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ nu lɛ mli nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ejaaa. Dumɔwui krɔŋŋ ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ tso kome mli lɛ dumɔ haa tsei lɛ daa daa.

english: Why do my rice grains break into small pieces during milling after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ mli fãi bibii lɛ? Yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Rice breaks during milling if it was harvested when overly dry in the field or dried too rapidly under intense direct sun. Harvesting when 80-85% of grains turn golden yellow prevents kernel breakage.
ga: Omɔ baatse yɛ be mli ni akpaa lɛ kɛji akɛ akpa lɛ beni egbi tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli loo egbi oya tsɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi lɛ. Kpamɔ be mli ni ŋmaa lɛ mli 80-85% etsɔ shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ. Ebaaye ebua ni dumɔwui lɛ akafite.

english: Why do extension officers advise us to parboil harvested rice before milling it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔkɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ awo la mli dani wɔkɛ ŋmɔtɔ awo mli lɛ?

english: Parboiling involves soaking and steaming raw paddy rice before drying. This process hardens the rice grain to prevent breakage during milling and preserves essential vitamins inside the grain.
ga: Nɔ ni fata blenching he ji ŋmãa ni ahoko lɛ ni akɛwoɔ nu mli ni ashãa lɛ dani agbiɔ. Nɛkɛ gbɛ nɛɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ mli wa koni ekakumɔ beni ashɛreɔ lɛ, ni ehaa vitamini ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why does locally produced rice sometimes contain small stones after processing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, ŋmãa ni afeɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ hiɛ tɛi bibii lɛ? Beni atsu he nii sɛɛ?

english: Stones get mixed into the harvest when harvested rice is laid directly on bare soil or concrete floors to dry. Drying harvested rice on clean tarpaulins or raised drying racks keeps the grain clean and market-ready.
ga: Akɛ tɛi futuɔ mli yɛ kpamɔ be mli beni akɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ fɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ loo kɔnkrit nɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni egbi lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ agbi yɛ tarp ni he tse nɔ loo ŋmãa ni awo nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmãa lɛ he atse ni efee klalo kɛha jarayeli.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning yellow and drying up during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate direct sunlight. Without temporary shade crops like plantains to block the harsh sun, the hot heat burns their delicate leaves and dries out the topsoil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko tamɔ plantains bɛ ni baatsi hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ gĩɔ.

english: Why does my maize grow very tall and green in one part of my field, but stays short and yellow in another part?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ miiya hiɛ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fã ko mli lɛ? Shi fã kroko lɛ yɛ kuku ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo?

english: Soil nutrients are not always spread evenly across a field. Short, yellow maize usually means that specific patch of land lacks nitrogen, which the crop needs to grow strong and green.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ ejaraaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa kuku ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ he pɔtɛɛ ko. Biɛ ji he ni ehe hiaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛ̃ waa ni amɛfee ŋmɔji.

english: Is it safe for me to plant cassava together with maize on the same plot of land?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ makwɛ ŋmãa kɛfata ŋmãa he yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting cassava and maize together works well because maize grows quickly and is harvested early, leaving the land free for the slower-growing cassava to expand its roots.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya, ni akpaa lɛ mra. Shi he ko koni ŋmei ni daa blɛoo lɛ agbɛ eshishifãi lɛ ashwã.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly in damp, shaded conditions. Clearing weeds and trimming overgrown branches allows air and sunlight to dry out the trees and stop the fungus.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ tsei ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la haa tso lɛ gĩɔ ni etsiɔ ŋmeii lɛ anaa.

english: Why do the leaves of my tomato plants curl tightly inwards during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in hot weather is a plant's natural defense to protect itself from losing water through evaporation. The leaves curl up to reduce surface area until the air cools down.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ nu ni fiteɔ yɛ la ni hoɔ lɛ hewɔ lɛ he. Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛha ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ aba shi kɛyashi kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my pepper plants before any peppers actually start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ dani pepper lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience stress, usually from extreme heat, dry soil, or lack of soil nutrients. The plant drops flowers to save its energy until conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ kɛji amɛmiihao. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛyashi shihilɛi lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know when my cassava crop is fully ready under the ground to be dug up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-cassava tsei lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakumɔ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is ready for harvest when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, leaving a bare stalk, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to bulge or crack open.
ga: Cassava efee klalo akɛ ebaakpa kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Eshwɛ tso ko ni nɔ ko bɛ mli. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ loo egbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why does my land produce fewer bags of maize when I plant maize on the exact same farm every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas restores nitrogen to the soil naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Enɛ baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ kome lɛ nɔŋŋ afite kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers start sprouting green shoots even while stored inside my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛji akɛ akɛto mi-ŋmɔ lɛ mli po lɛ?

english: Yam tubers naturally go through a resting period after harvest called dormancy. Once that resting phase ends, humidity and warmth trigger the tuber to sprout and try to grow a new plant.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy. Beni hejɔɔmɔ be lɛ ba naagbee lɛ, hulutsoo kɛ latsaa lɛ baaha bulb lɛ akwɛ̃ ni ebɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekwɛ tsei heei.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my planted crop right after the first rains arrive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants adapted to take immediate advantage of water and topsoil nutrients. They grow faster than young crops until your crop establishes strong root systems.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni atsake amɛ koni amɛkɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii oya. Amɛdaraa oya fe tsei bibii kɛyashiɔ be mli ni otso lɛ etswa shishifãi ni mli wa ema shi.

english: Can I plant cocoyam on the same land as my young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu kookoo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikookoo tsei bibii lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, planting cocoyam with young cocoa trees is a great practice. The broad leaves of the cocoyam provide temporary shade to protect young cocoa seedlings from harsh sunlight, while also supplying your family with food while you wait for the cocoa to mature.
ga: Hɛɛ, kookoo ni akɛ kookoo tsei bibii duɔ lɛ ji nifeemɔ kpakpa. kookoo baai ni mli kwɔ Haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko baa koni ebu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ha oweku lɛ niyenii be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni kookoo lɛ agbɔ lɛ.

english: Will growing food crops like cocoyam alongside my cocoa trees reduce my cocoa harvest?
ga: Ani niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo ni miduɔ yɛ mi kookoo tsei lɛ ahe lɛ baaha mi kookoo ni mikpaa lɛ nɔ aba shi?

english: If planted with proper spacing, food crops won't harm young cocoa. However, as cocoa trees grow larger, their roots and shade will outcompete crops like cocoyam, so food crops should be phased out once the cocoa canopy closes.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu kɛ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa Niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii yeŋ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ awui. Shi, beni cacao tsei lɛ daraa lɛ, Tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ eshishifãi lɛ daraa fe ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ cacao. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii akpa kɛji kookoo ŋmei lɛ ŋmɛ pɛ.

english: Why are the cocoa pods on my trees so few and small this season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ faaa ni amɛhe ehiaaa yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Low pod count can be caused by several factors, including poor soil nutrients, prolonged dry weather, lack of proper pruning, or pests and diseases attacking the flowers. Regular pruning and balanced fertilizer application help trees produce more and larger pods.
ga: Nibii babaoo baanyɛ aha pod yibɔi ni baa shi lɛ aba. nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fata he Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ Tso lɛ ni afolɔ jogbaŋŋ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni bɛ Tso lɛ ni afoɔ daa kɛ fɔfɔi ni akɛwoɔ mli ni ja lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ fɔfɔii babaoo ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why are my cocoyam tubers rotting in the ground before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo yitsei lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoyam tuber rot is usually caused by fungal infections in soil that stays waterlogged for too long, or by poor quality seed tubers. Ensuring good land drainage and planting healthy, disease-free suckers prevents rot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ cocoyam tuber rot lɛ baa. loo dumɔwui ayitsei ni ehiii lɛ kɛbaa Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni hela bɛ mli lɛ ni baaye abua ni akafite.

english: Why do the leaves of my young cocoa trees turn brown and dry up during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have shallow roots and tender leaves that lose water rapidly in intense heat. Without adequate shade trees or plantain plants nearby to shield them, heat stress causes the leaves to scorch and dry up.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛbaai bibii ni nu lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa he. Kɛji akɛ tsei loo tsei bibii ni haa hulutsoo lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni bɛŋkɛ ni baanyɛ abu he lɛ bɛ lɛ, Heat stress haa baai lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and rot directly on the tree?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: This is typically caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly during rainy conditions and high humidity. Clearing weeds, pruning dense branches to let air flow, and removing infected pods early helps control its spread.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. weeding Dense pruning koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli ni ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ egbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow when the soil stays wet for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When soil is constantly waterlogged, plant roots cannot breathe because air pockets in the dirt are filled with water. Suffocated roots cannot absorb nutrients properly, causing the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Beni nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ Tso shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ eyi kɛ nu. Shishifãi ni egbɔjɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: Signs of poor soil include stunted crop growth, pale or yellowish leaves, low yields, and crops succumbing easily to minor pests. Adding organic compost or appropriate fertilizers restores vital nutrients.
ga: Nɔ ni fata okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii lɛ he ji tsei ni edaaa jogbaŋŋ. Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔŋ, yibiiwoo faaa, ni ŋmɔshi nibii bibii yeɔ amɛ oya. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: How do I know when it is time to ask an agricultural extension officer to inspect my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni esa akɛ mabi okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko ni ekwɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You should request an inspection whenever you notice strange pests, rapid crop decay, unexplained low yields, or when preparing new land. Extension officers can diagnose hidden issues early before you suffer total crop failure.
ga: Esa akɛ obi ni akwɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni obaana kooloi ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fiteɔ oya Nibii ni anáa lɛ faaa ni atsɔɔɔ mli loo beni asaa shikpɔŋ hee Extension nitsulɔi baanyɛ ana naagbai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ mra. Dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ kwraa baakpe lɛ,

english: How will attending farmer training classes help me get better yields on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ okwaafoi atsɔsemɔ klas ni mikɛ mihe aaawo mli lɛ baaye abua mi ni maná yibii kpakpai yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Farmer field schools teach modern techniques such as proper pruning, correct chemical application, pest management, and soil preservation. Learning these practices helps you grow healthier crops and harvest more while spending less money on trial-and-error.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛ nɔ skul tsɔɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋaai tamɔ tsei ni afoɔ. Tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ Nifeemɔi nɛɛ akasemɔ baanyɛ aye abua bo ni odu ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmaa wuji yɛ be mli ni okɛ shika fioo pɛ tsuɔ kaa kɛ tɔmɔ he nii.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees turn brown and dry up when there are no big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because their leaves are tender and easily damaged by direct sun and heat. Shade trees or tall plants like plantains reduce heat stress, keep the soil moist, and protect the young cocoa until it grows strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii biɔ hulutsoo ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ fiteɔ amɛ oya. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantains yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa shi. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni obu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ.

english: This yellowing usually means the soil lacks nitrogen, which maize needs to grow green leaves and strong stalks. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure will help restore the green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ su ni ji ŋmɔŋ nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni ŋmãa lɛ akwɛ baai eŋɔli kɛ ŋmeii ni wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Does it matter which way I point the cassava stem when I stick it into the ground?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ otsɔɔ ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, cassava stems must be planted with the raised leaf buds pointing upward toward the sky. If planted upside down, the plant will struggle to sprout, grow roots sideways, and give you much smaller tubers.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ adu ŋmei tsei ni baai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ Tso lɛ baaná naagba yɛ ekwɛ̃mɔ he. Shishifãi lɛ daa yɛ afã. ni ehaa yitso bibioo kwraa

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the sunlight to produce food for the underground tubers. Staking also keeps the leaves off the wet ground, preventing rot and fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã hulutsoo be lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ naa.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts alongside my corn makes the soil better for future crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ midu ŋmeii yɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ masɛi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the groundnut roots decay in the soil, they release this natural plant food, which fertilizes the next crop.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Amɛjieɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii kpo. ni baafee ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha tso henɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ

english: Why do the blossom flowers on my pepper plants keep falling off without forming any pepper pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni ekɛ pepper ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa baaa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when the soil gets too dry, when temperatures get extremely hot, or when tiny pests feed on the flower stems. Keeping the soil consistently moist and protecting plants from heat or pests helps the pods set.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. Kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa Aloo kɛ́ kooloi bibii ye fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni obu tso lɛ he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ loo kooloi ni yeɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ.

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, which target the tender central leaves of maize. Clearing them early by applying approved control methods or putting neem solution or ash into the plant funnel prevents them from destroying the crop.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni kwɛɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ anɔ. Tsei ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Kɛ akɛ gbɛi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛkwɛɔ nɔ lɛ tsu nii loo akɛ neem solution loo sũ fata dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to clear weeds from my crop field early instead of waiting until the crops grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔji amli mra? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ ni tso lɛ atsɔ agbo lɛ

english: Young crops grow slowly and easily lose the fight against fast-growing weeds for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Weeding early ensures your young plants get all the nourishment they need to build strong roots.
ga: Nibii bibii ni aduɔ lɛ daa blɛoo ni ehiɛɛɛ mlɛo, ni amɛyeɔ ta ni amɛwuɔ amɛshiɔ jwɛi ni daa oya koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii lɛ nɔ kunim. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni otsei bibii lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa.

english: Too many side shoots (suckers) steal nutrients and water from the main mother plantain. Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two strong ones, allowing the main plant to produce a bigger and heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: Side shoots (shoots) babaoo tsɔ juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni no baaha tso titri lɛ awo ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my harvested grains like maize turn to powder and get small holes after sitting in storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmaa ni mikpa, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni eyɛ bu bibii lɛ? Beni eta nitoohe kotoku lɛ mli sɛɛ

english: Small insects called weevils eat the grains from the inside out when stored in normal bags. Drying grains until they are very dry and storing them in sealed, airtight bags (like PICS bags) suffocates the bugs and keeps the grain safe.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ weevils lɛ yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ kɛ́ akɛwo kotokui ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ amli. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmaa lɛ aahu kɛyashi ebaagbi waa ni akɛwo kotokui ni akɛ vacuum tsiɔ mli (tamɔ PICS kotokui) amli lɛ, ebaaha kooloi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha ŋmaa lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow when the soil stays waterlogged for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Excess water drowns the crop's roots by pushing out air, preventing them from taking up essential nutrients like nitrogen, which causes the leaves to lose their green color and turn yellow.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ shwieɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni etsiɔ kɛyaa he kroko lɛ nɔ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ anine shɛɛɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen nɔ, ni no haa baai lɛ ahe feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Legumes like cowpeas naturally fix nitrogen from the air into the soil through their roots, restoring fertility that heavy-feeding crops like maize took away.
ga: Legumes, tamɔ cowpeas, kɛ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Nibii babaoo ni kooloi aniyenii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ jie lɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt during the hot afternoon sun even when the soil has moisture?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: During intense heat, tomato leaves lose water faster than the roots can drink it up, causing temporary wilting to protect themselves; they usually recover once the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ, Tomato baai lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛgbiɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe. Bei pii lɛ, amɛhe waaa kɛji hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: Pepper plants shed flowers when stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients like calcium in the soil.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ calcium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: How does early rain after a long dry spell affect my cassava plants?
ga: Te leebi maŋkpa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ saa mi-cassava tsei lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: The sudden water triggers the cassava to rapidly grow new stems and green leaves, temporarily pulling energy away from root growth until the leaves fully develop.
ga: Nu ni hoɔ trukaa lɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji kwɛ̃ɔ oya. Ejieɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ adalɛ mli yɛ be kukuoo mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni baai lɛ daraa kwraa.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crop shoots at the start of the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi ŋmeii lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild and aggressive plants adapted to quickly soak up early rainfall and soil fertilizers before farm crops can establish strong roots.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa waa ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛŋɔ nugbɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya dani ŋmɔ mli nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aná shishifãi ni wa.

english: What causes tiny holes to suddenly appear all over my cabbage leaves?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii jeɔ kpo trukaa yɛ mi-cabbage baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ?

english: Those holes are caused by tiny caterpillars, like the diamondback moth larvae, which feed on the leaves shortly after hatching.
ga: Buji nɛɛ ji nɔ ni ŋmeii bibii, tamɔ daimondback ŋmei lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ feɔ. ni yeɔ baai lɛ beni efɔ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ

english: Why do my yam vines produce smaller tubers when I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ náa bulbs bibii beni midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Planting too closely forces the yam plants to compete for sunlight, space, and soil nutrients, leaving less energy for each plant to build large tubers underground.
ga: Kɛ́ adu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ehaa sweet potato tso lɛ kɛ hulu la, he ko kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Enɛ haaa tso fɛɛ tso aná hewalɛ fioo ni ekɛfee bulb agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: It is best to buy fresh hybrid seeds each season because seeds saved from hybrid harvests lose their strength, resulting in weaker plants and smaller cobs.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui heei ni akɛfee hybrid lɛ daa afi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa lɛ amli lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: How do I know the exact right time to dig up my groundnuts so they do not rot in the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii? Koni ŋmeii lɛ akafite yɛ sũ lɛ mli?

english: Groundnuts are ready to harvest when the leaves turn yellow and dry up, and the inside of the pods shows dark brown or black marks when cracked open.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa kɛji baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi. Ni pod lɛ mli baaná okadii ni tsuɔ loo ediŋŋ kɛji efo.

english: Tomatoes continue to breathe and ripen fast after picking, especially in hot weather. Harvesting them when they just start turning pink and keeping them in a cool shade slows down spoilage so they survive long transit times.
ga: Tomato yaa nɔ emuɔ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ oya beni ajie lɛ sɛɛ. Titri lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akpa amɛ be mli ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ pinki kɛkɛ ni akɛtoɔ he ko ni mli ejɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛfitemɔ asɛɛ afo bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ gbɛfaa mli.

english: Why does putting harvested mature mangoes inside a closed sack make them soften faster?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango ni akpa ni ekwɛ̃ ni akɛwoɔ kotokui ni aŋã mli lɛ haa amɛfeɔ blɛoo oya lɛ?

english: Mangoes release a natural ripening gas called ethylene. Trapping this gas inside a closed bag concentration speeds up the softening and sweetening process of all the fruit inside.
ga: Mango jieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ko ni haa mɔ shwereɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ ethylene lɛ kpo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛ́ akɛ gas nɛɛ wo kotoku ko ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa aduawai lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni ehaa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔ oya.

english: Why do my maize leaves curl up and turn yellow when rain does not fall for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛko gbii babaoo nɛ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl to reduce their surface area and stop water from evaporating off the plant during hot days. The yellowing shows the crop is under heat stress and struggling to draw nutrients from dry soil.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛha ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ aba shi ni ekɛtsi nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ naa yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Yellow tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ shishi ni eebɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ejie niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture swings from too wet to too dry. This heat stress causes the plant to protect itself by shedding flowers it cannot support.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsake kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ mli kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ mli. Nɛkɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ nɛɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ebu ehe kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ nɔ lɛ ni ekɛshwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce thin, watery roots when I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ nu yɔɔ mli beni midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need room underground to expand and store starch. When planted too close, their roots compete heavily for soil space, water, and light, resulting in small, thin tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi he ko he miihia cassava shishifãi koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛkɛ starch ato. Kɛji akɛ adu he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ he ko, shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ la he akaŋshii mli, ni no haa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo baa.

english: Why do plantain trees easily fall down during heavy storms when they are full of fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ ahum ni naa wa mli eyɛ mli akɛ aduawai lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that spread out near the surface rather than deep down. When the heavy bunch forms at the top, the whole plant becomes top-heavy and easily pulls out of wet soil.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛbɛŋkɛɔ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ moŋ fe ni eeeshɛ he ni mli kwɔ. Kɛji ŋmeii ni tsii fee yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ Tso muu lɛ fɛɛ tsii yɛ ŋwɛi ni ejieɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ oya.

english: Why does planting cowpeas in my farm make my maize grow stronger in the next planting season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa mi-ŋmãa lɛ daa waa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpea plants capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the cowpea plants die and rot, that stored nitrogen stays in the earth as natural food for future crops like maize.
ga: Cowpea tsei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Beni tsina tsei lɛ gboi ni amɛgboi lɛ Nitrogen ni ato lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do my garden eggs become bitter when I leave them on the plant for too long before harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ ŋɔɔ waa kɛ́ mishi amɛ yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ dani mikpa lɛ?

english: As garden eggs stay longer on the stem, the seeds inside harden to prepare for reproduction. The plant produces natural bitter defense chemicals to protect those maturing seeds from animals.
ga: Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ abɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ baahi tso lɛ shishi be kakadaŋŋ. Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ mli waa koni amɛkɛsaa amɛhe kɛha fɔmɔ. Tso lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni gbeɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebuɔ dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ kooloi ahe.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my young yam sprouts in the early season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe mi sweet potato tsei lɛ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Weeds have hardy, wild seeds that sprout instantly to grab early sunlight and nutrients, whereas yam setts take longer to build underground roots before sending up green vines.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ koo mli dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni kwɛ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la kɛ niyenii kpakpai yɛ shishijee mli. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, sweet potato heɔ be babaoo dani ekɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ feɔ dani wain tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why do black spots appear and spread on my cocoa pods during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji jeɔ kpo ni egbɛɔ eshwaa mi-kokoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?
