english: Rainy weather creates high humidity and wet surfaces where fungal spores thrive. The moisture allows the black pod fungus to easily swim across the pod skin, rotting the crop if shade isn't managed to allow airflow.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ haa hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ baa he ni ŋmeii baanyɛ ada yɛ lɛ. Fɛ̃i haa pod fungus diŋ lɛ shwieɔ pod hewolo lɛ nɔ mlɛo. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii fiteɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ nyɛɛɛ aha kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli.

english: Leaf curling and yellow patches on cassava are typically caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. Using disease-resistant cassava stem cuttings from agricultural extension officers is the best way to prevent this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi kɛ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmei nɔ lɛ baa. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Akɛ ŋmei niji ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ kɛjɛɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi adɛŋ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ naa.

english: Black and rotting cocoa pods are caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungal infection that thrives in wet, overly shaded, and humid farms. Pruning tree branches to let in sunlight and clearing weeds around the trunk helps prevent the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ cocoa ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ kɛ nɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli efɔ lɛ amli. Shade babaoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei aniji koni hulu la abote mli ni ojie jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ. Tsoi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ akagbɛ eshwa.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn yellow and the whole trunk collapses before producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tso muu lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi dani ewoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by Panama disease or root damage from microscopic worms called nematodes. You can prevent this by planting clean, disease-free suckers and avoiding planting in areas where infected plantains previously grew.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Panama hela loo shishifãi ni ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ fiteɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Obaanyɛ otsi enɛ naa kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni he tse ni hela bɛ mli lɛ ni oookwɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Ni tsi ohe kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ hei ni tsutsu lɛ aduɔ dumɔwui ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ahe lɛ he.

english: Why are there white powdery spots all over my garden egg leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant baai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ lɛ?

english: These white spots are a fungal disease called powdery mildew, which happens when plants are packed too closely together in humid weather. Spacing your plants properly allows air to blow through and keeps the leaves dry.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii yɛŋ nɛɛ ji ŋmeii hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ akɛ tsei bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli ni egbiɔ baai lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen or is flooded with water. Nitrogen gives plants their green color and strength, so adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer like urea will help them green up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ. Nitrogen haa tsei feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛnáa hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmeii tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛhi shi eŋɔli.

english: Tomatoes shed their flowers when the weather is too hot or when the soil dries out during flowering. Keeping the soil moist by watering regularly and putting dried grass or mulch around the base of the plant helps keep the soil cool.
ga: Tomato fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ba kɛtsɔ nu ni oooha lɛ daa kɛ jwɛi loo ŋmɔtɔ ni okɛwo tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i.

english: Why do my pepper seedlings look weak and stop growing after I move them to the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ beni mikɛ amɛ tee ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper seedlings get shocked when moved under direct afternoon sun or if their roots break during transplanting. Moving them late in the afternoon when it is cooler and watering them right away helps them settle and grow fast.
ga: Pepper dumɔwui lɛ baaya shoofeemɔ mli kɛji akɛ ajie amɛ kɛjɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shwane mli. aloo kɛji shishifãi lɛ fã yɛ be mli ni aduɔ lɛ Kɛ́ otsi amɛ shwane mli beni hulu lɛ miitso ni okɛ nu awo amɛmli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛdaraa oya.

english: Yams need soft, deep, and well-aerated soil to grow long and straight. If the soil is hard, stony, or compacted, the tuber cannot push downward easily, causing it to stay short and twist.
ga: Sweet potato he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli kwɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ koni ekwɛ̃ kakadaŋŋ ni efee tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa, eyɛ tɛi, loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ shi mlɛo. Abaanyɛ afee lɛ kuku ni atsɔ mli.

english: Why do the stems of my bean seeds rot right at the ground level soon after sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: This rotting is called damping-off, which happens when the soil is too wet and fungus attacks the young stem. Planting in well-drained soil and avoiding overwatering early on keeps young sprouts healthy.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ akɛ damping off, ni baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ tutua tsei bibii lɛ. Dumɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ nɔ ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ he mra. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei bibii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cabbage heads stay soft and loose instead of forming a hard ball?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage yitsei lɛ yɔɔ blɛoo lolo ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ fe ni eeefee shiŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to form hard heads when they don't get steady water or enough plant food during early growth. Providing constant moisture and balanced nutrients helps the leaves wrap tightly into a firm head.
ga: Kaabaji lɛ ewaŋ kɛji enine shɛɛɛ nu nɔ daa loo tsei niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni edaa mra lɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ niyenii ni sa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ amɛhe shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ yitso ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants turn yellow and dry up when I clear all the big trees off my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive full, harsh sunlight because their leaves burn easily. Keeping larger trees on the farm provides gentle shade and keeps the soil cool and moist so the cocoa can grow safely.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya. Tsei wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ akwɛmɔ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ koni kookoo lɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, steal water and food from the main plant. Pruning them away leaves more nutrients for the main plantain stem to produce a bigger, heavier bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei krokomɛi loo tsei lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ, ebaaha plantain tsei titri lɛ aná niyenii babaoo. Koni aná kuu ni da ni tsii

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning pale yellow from the middle out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛjɛɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to make food and grow strong. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer will make the leaves green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛdara waa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do people tell me to plant beans or cowpeas on my land before I plant maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ mi akɛ madu ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas pull good food (nitrogen) out of the air and put it deep into the soil through their roots. When you harvest them, the soil is left richer for crops like maize.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas gbalaa niyenii kpakpa (nitrogen) kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛfuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Beni okpaa nii lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ hu baafee nɔ ni baa shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why shouldn't I put chemical fertilizer on my soil when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs soil moisture to dissolve so plant roots can safely drink it. Placing fertilizer on hot, dry soil can burn the crop roots and cause the crop to wither.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anu lɛ shweshweeshwe. Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni eha tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, hot dry winds, or irregular watering. Giving tomatoes regular water keeps the flowers healthy so fruit can form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli. kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni egbi loo nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be Nu ni okɛhaa o-tomatoi lɛ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and twisting into tight bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni etsɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like aphids feeding on the juice inside young leaves. Spraying the leaves with simple neem oil solution or soapy water helps clear those pests away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids ni yeɔ baai bibii amli nu lɛ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo nu ni mli edɔ shwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ.

english: Yam vines need sunlight on all their leaves to make energy. Staking keeps the leaves high in the air off wet dirt, which protects the plant from rot and helps big tubers grow underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la yɛ amɛbaai lɛ fɛɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ hiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni muji ni efɔ lɛ bɛ mli. Enɛ buɔ tso lɛ he koni ekafite, ni eyeɔ ebuaa bulb agboi ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Cassava roots rot when water stays trapped around them for too long in heavy, soggy soil. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps rainwater drain away quickly.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu tsɔ amɛhe. Etsɛ tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ, nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ oya.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than my crops right after the rainy season begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are extremely tough and sleep deep in the soil during dry times, waking up instantly with rain. Removing weeds early prevents them from stealing water and plant food from your young crops.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ wa waa ni amɛwɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ. ni te shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛha nugbɔ lɛ Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju nu kɛ niyenii ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ otsei bibii lɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to cover my tomato seedbed with palm fronds until the seeds sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ ŋmei tsei haa mi tomato dumɔwui saatso lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Palm fronds protect tender seeds from direct hot sunlight and heavy rain that can wash them away. The cover keeps the soil warm and moist, creating the ideal conditions for seeds to germinate safely before they are exposed to full sun.
ga: Palm tsei ahe baai buɔ dumɔwui ni mli tse lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, ni baanyɛ ahoo dumɔwui lɛ ahe. Nɔ ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔɔ ni edɔɔ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni sa baa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe dani amɛshɛ hulu la lɛ he kwraa.

english: Seeds need air, warmth, and a little moisture to sprout. If planted too deep, the soil is too cool and lacks air, and the young shoot burns all its stored energy trying to push through the heavy dirt before reaching light.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, dɔlɛ, kɛ nu fioo dani amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji adu lɛ mli tsɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee fɛ̃i tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli. Ni ŋmeii bibii lɛ baashã amɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛto lɛ ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ nɔ dani amɛyashɛ la lɛ he.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my young crops with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei bibii ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like a shade cover for the earth. It traps moisture in the soil, keeps the root zone cool during hot sunny days, and stops weeds from growing and taking food from your crops.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo kɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ha shishifã lɛ he afee fɛ̃i yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛkaye oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why is it important to heap soil high into mounds before planting yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ato shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ naa dani adu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Mounding loosens the soil so yam tubers can expand easily without pushing against hard earth. It also keeps the root area cool and prevents water from pooling around the tubers during heavy rains, which causes rotting.
ga: Mounding haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo ni amɛtsiii shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ nɔ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ hu feɔ fɛ̃i, ni ehaaa nu akabɔle bulb lɛ he yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli, ni no haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry periods as a natural defense to protect itself from drying out. Without leaves, the plant loses very little water through heat, allowing it to stay alive underground until the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛ́ baai bɛ lɛ, nu fioo pɛ tso lɛ laajeɔ kɛjɛɔ latsaa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa amɛhiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: Why do my cowpea leaves curl up or droop during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea baai lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpea leaves turn or curl in intense afternoon heat to reduce the amount of leaf surface directly hit by the sun. This smart behavior helps the plant conserve moisture until the temperatures drop in the evening.
ga: Cowpea baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe loo amɛfoɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ mli koni ekɛba baa lɛ hiɛ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ aba shi. Nɛkɛ ŋaa gbɛ nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my pepper plants turning yellow and falling off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves often mean the plant is stressed by heat, bad watering, or a lack of nutrients like nitrogen. The plant sacrifices its older bottom leaves to send remaining energy and food to the growing top leaves and fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miiye latsaa. nu ni ehiii loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tamɔ nitrogen bɛ mli lɛ, tsei kɛ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ shaa afɔle koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ amaje baai kɛ aduawai ni miida yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt and die when the Harmattan dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ Harmattan fɛ̃i be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate roots and thin leaves that lose water very quickly in direct sun and dry wind. Without shade crops like plantains to block the heat, the sun dries out the seedlings faster than their roots can drink water.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ baai bibii, ni nu fiteɔ oya kɛji hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi tswa. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains ni tsiɔ latsaa naa lɛ bɛ lɛ, Hulu lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu nu lɛ.

english: Why should I cut away extra suckers growing at the base of my plantain trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-plantain lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: If too many suckers grow around one mother plantain, they fight for the same soil food, water, and sunlight. Pruning extra suckers leaves only one or two strong stems, ensuring the plant has enough energy to produce big, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ, dumɔwu kome Amɛyeɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ yibii lɛ amli babaoo lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ, ni ebaaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee kui wuji ni tsii.

english: Can I grow tomatoes under the heavy shade of large trees on my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tomato yɛ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ashishi?

english: Tomatoes need direct sunlight for most of the day to produce flowers and ripen fruit. If planted under dense tree shade, the stems grow tall, weak, and thin as they search for light, resulting in very few or no tomatoes.
ga: Tomato he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ yɛ gbi lɛ mli babaoo koni ewo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ni ekwɛ̃. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ashishi lɛ, tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ baafee kakadaŋŋ, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛhe baajɔ kɛji amɛmiitao la. Enɛ haa tomato fioo ko pɛ baa loo ebɛ kwraa.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow before the corn is ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen or lacking water. When plants do not get enough nutrients from the soil, they draw stored food from their older lower leaves first to survive, causing those leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-corn tsei lɛ miiye nitrogen loo nu efo amɛmli. Kɛ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Amɛgbalaa niyenii ni ato kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli klɛŋklɛŋ bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nakai baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why is my pepper plant growing very big green leaves but not producing any flowers or peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi waa shi ebɛ fɔfɔi loo pepper lɛ?

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer causes pepper plants to grow heavy green foliage instead of flowers. The plant spends all its energy on leaf growth rather than shifting into its reproductive stage to form fruits.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ haa pepper tsei lɛ woɔ baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ baai yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaabote fɔmɔ be lɛ mli koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by severe heat, lack of water, or attacks from sap-sucking pests like mirids. The tree drops its flowers to conserve energy so it can stay alive during tough conditions.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni nuɔ nu tamɔ pollen lɛ tutua amɛ. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli.

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up with yellow and light green patches on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Curled and patchy leaves are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is carried from plant to plant by tiny whiteflies. The virus damages the leaves so they cannot trap sunlight efficiently, resulting in smaller root harvests.
ga: Baai ni ekpɔtɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ woɔ kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ Virus lɛ fiteɔ baai lɛ bɔni afee ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛmɔmɔ hulu la lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shishifãi ni akpaa lɛ baa shi fioo.

english: Yam vines are climbing plants that need support to spread their leaves fully toward the sun. When leaves receive full sunlight, they manufacture more food to send underground, creating larger yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ yelikɛbuamɔ koni amɛjie amɛbaai lɛ kpo kwraa kɛya hulu la lɛ he. Kɛji baai lɛ ná hulu la ni fa lɛ Ebaaha niyenii babaoo aba ni ekɛmaje shikpɔŋ shishi. Ha sweet potato lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ afee wuji.

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots and carry heavy bunches at the top. Soil pests like root nematodes or weevils often destroy the underground roots, leaving the top-heavy plant with weak support against strong winds.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ panicle ni mli wa yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ shishifãi ni ji nematodes loo ŋmeii. Bei pii lɛ, efiteɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi. Enɛ haa tsei ni tsiimɔ yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nyɛɛɛ adamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa naa.

english: Why is it good for me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts together with my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ duɔ tsina loo ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts belong to the legume family, which can capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. This naturally enriches the soil and provides extra food for neighboring crops like maize.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni baanyɛ amɔmɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ niyenii babaoo.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than my planted crops after a rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni midu beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that are adapted to jump into action immediately after rain. Their seeds can rest in the soil for years and germinate faster than crop seeds to steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛtsu nii kɛji nugbɔ enɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Amɛ dumɔwui baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii babaoo ni amɛ kwɛ̃ oya fe dumɔwui ni amɛ ju hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why are my tomatoes turning black and soft at the bottom while still on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomatoi lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifee blɛoo yɛ shishigbɛ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit, often due to irregular watering. When soil moisture fluctuates rapidly, the plant cannot move calcium from the soil into the developing fruit properly.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsake oya lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ ajie calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛya aduawai ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do some of my cassava roots turn hard and woody instead of soft when I harvest them late?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ekomɛi wa ni amɛfeɔ tsei moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee blɛoo beni mikpaa amɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaving cassava in the ground too long past maturity causes the plant to convert stored starch into tough plant fiber. When dry weather sets in, the roots dry out and turn hard, making them tough to cook and consume.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ tsakeɔ ŋmeii ni ato lɛ ewoɔ tso mli ŋmeii ni wa amli. Kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaafee shiŋŋ. Enɛ haa ewaa akɛ aaaho ni aye.

english: If I spray my tomatoes with pest medicine today, can I harvest and sell them at the market tomorrow?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie tomato nɔ ŋmɛnɛ Ani manyɛ makpa ni mahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ wɔ?

english: No, every chemical has a required waiting period called a Pre-Harvest Interval listed on the label. If you harvest too early, the chemical poison stays inside the food, which can make the consumers sick and cause long-term health problems.
ga: Dabi, tsofai fɛɛ yɛ be ni akɛmɛɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ pre-harvest ni aŋmala awo nɔ. Kɛji okpa mra tsɔ Tsofai ni yɔɔ gbeyei hiɔ niyenii mli. Enɛ baanyɛ aha mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ aná hela ni ekɛ helatsamɔ mli naagbai ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ aba.

english: How do I know if the pesticide or weedkiller I am buying at the store is safe to use on my food crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo jwɛi ni ahe yɛ shwapo mli lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛbaatsu nii yɛ miniyenii tsei lɛ anɔ?

english: Always buy from registered agro-dealers and check that the bottle has an official registration number from the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA). Avoid unlabelled liquids or cheap mixtures, as fake chemicals can ruin your soil, burn your crops, or contaminate your harvest.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, hemɔ kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ ko ni aŋma egbɛi awo wolo nɔ lɛ dɛŋ. Ni kwɛmɔ ni tsɛnsi lɛ aná nɔmba ni jɛ Shihilɛ He Buumɔ Nitsumɔhe (EPA) lɛ ŋɔɔ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ nu ni aŋmalako nɔ loo nibii ni jara waaa lɛ ahe. Enɛ ji akɛ, tsofai amalei baanyɛ afite shikpɔŋ, ashã ŋmɔshi nibii, loo amɛfite onibii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen or the soil is too waterlogged for the roots to breathe. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or Urea when the soil is moist will help the leaves turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli loo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ NPK loo urea wo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Is it better to apply fertilizer to my crops when the ground is dry or after rain has fallen?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nibii beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi loo beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer right after rain when the soil is damp. Dry soil cannot dissolve the fertilizer for the roots to absorb, but heavy rain right after application can wash all your fertilizer away.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni nugbɔ enɛɔ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nyɛŋ atsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli koni shishifãi lɛ aŋɔ. Shi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo mli lɛ baanyɛ afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ kɛya.

english: Why does my cassava grow huge green stems and leaves but produces very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kɛ baai wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Excessive leaf growth with small roots happens when the soil has too much nitrogen or when plants are spaced too closely. The plant spends all its energy feeding the leaves on top instead of storing food in the root tubers.
ga: Baai ni yaa hiɛ fe nine ni shishifãi bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyeɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shishifã lɛ mli lɛ

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants dropping off without turning into pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ pepper aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant suffers from heat stress, dry soil, or an imbalance of nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist and avoiding excessive nitrogen fertilizer during the flowering stage helps fruits form.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ faaa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ he yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni aduawai aba.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and dry up after I clear away all the big trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ beni mijie tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under full sun. They need shade crops like plantains around them during their first few years to protect them from direct sun rays and keep moisture in the soil until they grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo tamɔ plantains ni ebɔle amɛhe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Enɛ ji koni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: Why are my tomato plants wilting and dying even though I give them plenty of water every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nu babaoo daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: This is often caused by bacterial wilt or root rot from overwatering. Small organisms in the soil block the water tubes inside the stem, causing the leaves to collapse even when the soil around the roots is wet.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji helai ni gbeɔ mɔ loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ nu ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli fe nine lɛ mli. Nibii bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsiɔ nu paipii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ anaa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli ewo ŋmɔtɔ po.

english: Can I save seeds from the hybrid maize I harvested this season to plant again next year?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ hybrid corn ni mikpaa yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ afi ni baa lɛ?

english: It is not advisable to plant saved seeds from hybrid crops. The second generation will grow unevenly, be more vulnerable to pests, and produce a much smaller yield compared to buying fresh certified hybrid seeds.
ga: Akɛ ŋaawoo haaa akɛ adu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli. Yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ baadara yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Ehe waaa kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai Ni yibiiwoo lɛ faaa kwraa fe dumɔwui heei ni akɛwo mli ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ ahemɔ.

english: What will happen if I plant my maize seeds very close together to fit more plants on my plot?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni tsei babaoo akwɛ̃ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting too closely forces the maize plants to compete for sunlight, water, and plant food. This results in thin, tall stalks that fall easily and small, poorly filled cobs, giving you less total grain at harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ adu amɛ kɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmãa tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu, kɛ tsei aniyenii he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ kɛlɛ, amɛhe tseee ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya. Kob lɛ ji bibioo. Akɛwoɔ mli jogbaŋŋ Enɛ haa dumɔwui fɛɛ ni yɔɔ kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ faaa.

english: How do I know if a piece of land is suitable for planting cassava?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale kɛji shikpɔŋ ko hi kɛha ŋmei ŋmɔ loo esaaa?

english: Cassava needs well-drained, loose soil to allow its tuberous roots to expand properly. If the land holds stagnant water or is made of heavy clay, the roots will rot in the wet soil before harvest.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni mli tse he miihia cassava koni eshishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu ni ekã shi loo akɛ shikpɔŋ fee. Shishifãi lɛ baagboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ dani akpa.

english: Why do my crops grow very well on one side of my field but struggle on the other side?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ fa kome shi amɛmiibɔi ŋmɔlɔ yɛ fa kroko lɛ?

english: Soil quality and water drainage can change across a single field. Areas with shallow soil or poor drainage hold excess water and choke roots, while deeper, loose soil allows crops to feed and grow easily.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su kɛ nu ni hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ atsake yɛ he kome fɛɛ. Hei ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ loo nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahi nu ni fa fe nine lɛ mli ni ekɛtsi shishifãi lɛ anaa. Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli tse lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa tsei akɛ amɛaana niyenii ni amɛdara.

english: Which crops are safe to plant on low-lying land near a stream that floods easily?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei abaanyɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni bɛŋkɛ faai ni nu hoɔ oya lɛ anɔ?

english: Crops like rice and sugar cane thrive in wet or waterlogged land, while crops like maize, cassava, and cocoa will rot and die because their roots cannot tolerate standing in water.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni nu yɔɔ loo nu yɔɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa fiteɔ ni amɛgboiɔ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛŋmɛ amɛtsui shi yɛ nu mli.

english: Why do my crop roots rot when water stays on my farm for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nu hi miŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Excess water chokes plant roots by cutting off oxygen in the soil. This weakens the plant and allows water-borne fungi and bacteria to multiply and attack the roots with diseases like root rot.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii kɛ helatsɛmɛi ni yɔɔ nu mli lɛ ayiɔ babaoo ni amɛkɛ helai tamɔ shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ tutuaa shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato plants wilting and dying after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants are sensitive to waterlogged soil. Heavy rain and poor drainage create wet soil conditions where fungal diseases and bacterial wilt spread quickly to attack the roots.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ nuɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ he waa. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ baa he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ bacteria wilt gbɛɔ eshwaa oya koni amɛtutua shishifãi lɛ.

english: Does using stagnant or dirty water to irrigate my vegetables cause plant diseases?
ga: Ani nu ni ekã shi loo nu ni mli ewo muji ni mikɛwoɔ mi-aduawai lɛ amli lɛ kɛ tsei ahelai baa?

english: Yes, stagnant or dirty water often carries disease-causing fungi and bacteria. When sprinkled on crops, this water can infect leaves and roots, leading to spots, rot, and crop failure.
ga: Hɛɛ, bei pii lɛ, nu ni ekã shi loo nɔ ni mli ewo muji lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ helai ni kɛ hela baa. Kɛji akɛ afɔse tsei anɔ Nu nɛɛ baanyɛ atswa baai kɛ shishifãi, ni ekɛ ŋmeii, ŋmeii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ aba.

english: Why do crops need water to survive, but too much water kills them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛhi shi lɛ? Shi ani nu babaoo gbeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Roots need water to drink soil nutrients, but they also need air in the soil to breathe. Too much standing water fills all the air spaces in the dirt, drowning the roots and causing them to rot.
ga: Nu he miihia shishifãi koni amɛnu niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Shi kɔɔyɔɔ hu he miihia amɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Nu ni ekã shi babaoo lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ hei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. Ekɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ.

english: What can I do to protect my crops if my farm holds too much water after it rains?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛji nu babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ?

english: You can construct raised soil beds and dig drainage channels across your farm so excess rain water flows away quickly, keeping crop roots safe from drowning and water-borne diseases.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee saatsoi ni awó nɔ ni otsa nu ni hoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya. Ha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ nu mli gbee kɛ helai ni jɛɔ nu mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why is it important to seek guidance on soil quality before clear-cutting land for planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ana ŋaawoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani afo nibii ni adu lɛ?

english: Getting expert advice helps you select crops that match your specific soil type and water drainage, preventing you from wasting money and effort on crops that cannot grow well there.
ga: Kɛ́ onine shɛ ŋaawoo ni jɛ ŋaalɔi anɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ohala ŋmɔshi nibii ni kɛ shikpɔŋ pɔtɛɛ ni oyɔɔ lɛ kɛ nu ni hoɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ kpãa gbee. Etsiɔ bo gbɛ koni okafite shika kɛ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ yɛ tsei ni nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ ahe.

english: How does proper crop spacing help prevent plant diseases on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni akɛtoɔ he ni sa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsĩ tsei ahe helai anaa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Giving plants enough room allows sunlight and air to move freely between them. This dries out wet leaves quickly after rain, making it harder for water-loving fungal diseases to spread.
ga: Kɛ́ aha tsei lɛ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baaha baai ni efɔ lɛ agbi oya yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa ewaa waa akɛ hydrophilic fungal helai lɛ baagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why are my neighbour's tomatoes growing so big, but when I planted the exact same seed on my farm, they stayed small and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ tomatoi lɛ miida waa nɛkɛ? Shi beni midu dumɔwui nɛɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, no mli lɛ tomato lɛ ji bibioo lolo ni ebɛ hewalɛ.

english: Crops behave differently depending on the soil quality, water levels, and nutrients available in that specific piece of land. Planting the same crop as someone else does not guarantee the same results unless your soil has the right food and care the crop needs.
ga: Tsei feɔ amɛnii yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, nu lɛ mli, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ nɔ. Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni mɔ kroko duɔ lɛ haaa nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ nɔŋŋ aba. Ja okɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ ewo niyenii kpakpa mli ni okwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahiamɔ nii anɔ.

english: Excess water drowns the crop's roots by pushing out all the air in the soil. Without air, the plant cannot absorb food like nitrogen, causing its leaves to turn yellow and its growth to stall.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni ekɛshwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii tamɔ nitrogen, ni no haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdalɛ kpaa.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my cassava plants after I clear the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi yucca tsei lɛ beni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants naturally adapted to fight aggressively for light, water, and nutrients. Young cassava takes time to establish root systems, so weeds will quickly steal sunlight and soil food unless you clear them early.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo la, nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Cassava bibioo lɛ heɔ be dani enáa shishifãi. No hewɔ lɛ, jwɛi lɛ juɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ oya. Ja ojie amɛ oya.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they suffer stress from extreme heat, lack of water, or too much fertilizer. The plant drops blossoms as a survival tactic to conserve its remaining energy.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ha amɛ. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi akɛ wala gbɛ koni amɛbu hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close to each other, won't I get a larger harvest from my farm?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe Ani maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting crops too close together forces them to compete against each other for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. This leaves every plant weak and thin, resulting in small cobs or no fruit at all.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei fɛɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe ejɔ. Enɛ haa anáa ŋmei bibioo ko. loo ebɛ hewalɛ ko kwraa

english: Why is my farm yielding less cassava every year even though I plant on the exact same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmei fioo daa afi lɛ? Akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Soil acts like a food store; every harvest removes nutrients from the ground. Growing the same crop continuously without adding manure, organic matter, or allowing the land to rest drains the soil completely.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii atoohe. Nikpamɔ fɛɛ kpamɔ jieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ aduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ be fɛɛ be ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, loo ahaaa sũ lɛ gbɛ ni ejɔɔ ehe lɛ, ebaaha sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ atsɔ mli kwraa.

english: Why are the leaves of my young cocoa trees turning brown and dry as if fire burnt them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ ji ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbi tamɔ nɔ ni ashã lɛ?

english: This damage is often caused by tiny sucking insects like mirids (capsids) or severe sun exposure. These insects suck sap from the shoots, causing patches of tissue to die and turn dark brown.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ mirids (capsids) loo hulu la ni naa wa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ mli. ni haa fãji lɛ gboiɔ yɛ hei srɔtoi ni etsakeɔ efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ

english: Why do my plantain trees keep falling over before the fruits are big enough to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ miigbee shi dani aduawai lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots and carry heavy fruits. Strong winds or root damage from soil pests can easily push them over unless you support the stem using a strong branched prop stick.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni tsii. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi adɛŋ lɛ baanyɛ ashɛre amɛ oya kɛho ja okɛ tso ni fiɔ shishifãi lɛ asɛɛ ni niji ni mli wa yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Can I put a large amount of chemical fertilizer on my crops at once so they grow much faster?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsofai babaoo awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli shikome koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya?

english: Applying too much fertilizer at once can 'burn' plant roots by drawing water out of them, causing the crop to dry up and die. Fertilizer must be applied in small, controlled amounts at the right times.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo mli yɛ be kome mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ ‘eshã’ tso lɛ shishifãi kɛtsɔ nu ni ejieɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. Ehaa tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli fioo, ni akudɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil. This acts as free, natural food that feeds the nearby maize and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛmɔɔ lɛ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko ni haa ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ niyenii ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive strong, direct sunlight. They need partial shade from taller trees or shade crops like plantain to protect their leaves from scorching and keep the soil moist during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo fã ko kɛjɛ tsei kakadaji loo hulutsoo tsei, tamɔ plantains, amli koni ebu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ la ni tsoɔ lɛ he, ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Planting cocoa trees too close causes them to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing allows roots to spread and ensures good air movement, which stops diseases from spreading easily.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa, ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa tsɔɔ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ eshwa mlɛo.

english: Cassava has deep, heavy roots that absorb a lot of water and food from the soil, which starves young cocoa trees. It is better to plant shade crops like plantain or nitrogen-fixing leguminous plants instead.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ, ni tsii ni gbalaa nu kɛ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ kookoo tsei bibii. Mohu ɔ, duɔ tsohi nɛ a haa nɛ hɛ mi jɔɔ kaa plantains loo tsohi nɛ haa nɛ nitrogen hiɔ si ɔ.

english: How do I know if my cocoa farm soil lacks nutrients for the trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni haa tsei lɛ yeɔ hewalɛ?

english: When soil lacks nutrients, leaves often turn pale yellow, growth slows down, and trees fail to produce pods. Adding organic compost or appropriate cocoa fertilizers restores essential plant food to the soil.
ga: Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii bɛ lɛ Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ. shweremɔ blɛoo ni tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie ŋmeii. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Cocoa trees naturally shed extra flowers if they lack water, proper soil food, or pollination by tiny insects. Keeping the soil moist and well-nourished helps more flowers turn into mature cocoa pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ baafɔ̃ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji nu bɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni sa loo kooloi bibii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni niyenii kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi babaoo ni amɛtsɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni eda.

english: Why is it important to cut off the extra branches and suckers growing on my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei niji kɛ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mikoko tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Extra branches and suckers consume food and water that should go into making fruit. Pruning them off directs energy back to the main tree so it can produce bigger and healthier cocoa pods.
ga: Niji kɛ tsei ashishifãi ni fa fe nine lɛ yeɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni esa akɛ akɛtsu nii kɛwo aduawai. Nibii ni afolɔ lɛ kɛ hewalɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa tso titri lɛ mli koni ekɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in cool, dark, and wet conditions. Pruning extra leaves and clearing weeds lets sunlight and air into the farm to dry out and kill the fungus.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, duŋ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Baai ni afolɔ ashwie shi kɛ jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ baaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni egbi ni egbe ŋmeii lɛ.

english: What causes the leaves of my young cocoa trees to look dry, twisted, and full of small holes?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbi, amɛtsake, ni bu bibii eyi mli obɔ?

english: This damage is usually caused by pests like mirids or capsids that suck sap from young leaves and stems. Applying recommended bio-pesticides or approved insecticides at the right time protects the foliage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi tamɔ mirids loo capsids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai kɛ tsei bibii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi loo tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ baaye abua ni abu tsei lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my cocoa tree leaves turn yellow and drop during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop leaves in severe dry weather to conserve water and prevent themselves from drying out completely. Covering the soil with organic mulch keeps the ground cool and retains moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi waa mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛtsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi kwraa. Kɛ́ akɛ organic mulch wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: A cocoa pod changes color when fully ripe—green pods turn bright yellow, while red or purple pods turn orange-yellow. Harvesting at full color change ensures the beans inside are fully developed.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ kwraa. Pods eŋɔli lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. yɛ be mli ni pods tsuru loo purple lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ-ŋmei. Nikpamɔ kɛ sui tsakemɔi fɛɛ lɛ haa kɔfi yibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain trees in the same field as my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ kookoo dumɔwui heei lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under strong direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees produce large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing necessary shade and preserving soil moisture for the cocoa to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni okwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i nɔ koni kookoo ahi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my plantain plants produce very small bunches even when the land looks rich?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ miiwo ŋmeii bibii waa eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔshi nibii moŋ?

english: When a plantain plant produces too many side shoots (suckers), it splits its food and water among all of them. Cutting away extra suckers leaves only one or two strong shoots, allowing the main plant to put all its energy into growing large fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwu ko wo sɛɛgbɛ ŋmeii (ŋmeii) babaoo tsɔ lɛ, ebaatse ehe kɛjɛ niyenii kɛ nu he. Kɛ́ afo ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ shwɛɔ, ni no haa tso titri lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ yibii wuji ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are my cassava plants producing tall leafy stems above ground but only tiny roots underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ baai lɛ nɔ kwɔ fe shikpɔŋ lɛ shi shishifãi bibii yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil contains too much nitrogen or gets excessive rain, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves and branches instead of storing food in its underground tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo nugbɔ enɛ babaoo. Kasava tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛbaa kɛ eniji fɛɛ kwɛ̃ɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato ŋmeii amli lɛ,.

english: Lifting yam vines on stakes allows the leaves to catch maximum sunlight for making plant food. It also keeps the leaves off damp soil, preventing fungal diseases and rotting.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ yibii lɛ naa hulu la babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ tsei ahe niyenii homɔ mli. Ehaa baai lɛ hu ehiɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ. Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela naa.

english: Why do my sweet potato tubers have dark tunnels and small holes inside them when I harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Hii mli kɛ́ mikpa nii

english: Small holes inside tubers are caused by sweet potato weevils, tiny insects that lay eggs near the base of the stem. The hatched grubs burrow into the roots to feed as the tubers grow.
ga: Buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ jɛɔ ŋmeii ni ji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ amli. ni ji kooloo bibioo ko Akɛ ŋmeii lɛ woɔ tso lɛ shishigbɛ. Kplukai ni efɔ lɛ shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ amli koni amɛye nii be mli ni bulb lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow in the middle of the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be ni amɛdaraa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil has run out of nitrogen, which is the essential food maize needs to stay green and build leaves. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa ni ŋmãa ahi shi eŋɔli ni ewo baai. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my cowpea leaves developing white powdery patches during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: High air humidity and damp leaves during rainy periods create ideal conditions for powdery mildew, a fungal disease that spreads across foliage and blocks sunlight from reaching the leaves.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa kɛ baai ni mli efɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha powdery mildew baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa baai lɛ fɛɛ mli ni etsĩɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ baai lɛ ahe.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when stressed by extreme heat, dry soil, or sudden changes in moisture. Without steady water and shade from extreme midday sun, the plant sheds flowers to save energy.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo hulutsoo tsakemɔi ni baa trukaa lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛji nu kɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane teŋ lɛ bɛ. Tsei baafɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling upward and drying out during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a defense mechanism tomatoes use to prevent water loss during dry, hot weather, but it can also be caused by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies that transmit leaf-curl viruses.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ni atoma kɛtsuɔ nii koni ekɛtsi nu ni elaaje yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ naa. Shi kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies, ni ji helai ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ hu baanyɛ ekɛba.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my planted crops right after the early rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni midu beni nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds sit dormant in the soil surface and are naturally adapted to germinate instantly with the first drop of moisture, while cultivated crop seeds take longer to establish roots and build strength.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ ehi shi. yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni etsakeɔ ehe yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔtɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, dumɔwui ni adu lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛshishifãi lɛ tswaa shi ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when there are no bigger trees growing near them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei wuji komɛi bɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that scorch easily in intense sunlight. Larger shade trees or plantain plants block the direct midday heat, keeping the air cool and soil moist so the cocoa can establish strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shãa oya. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo plantains wuji tsiɔ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shwane mli lɛ naa. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hu feɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Bɔni afee ni kookoo lɛ anyɛ ama shishifãi ni wa.

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for water, soil nutrients, and sunlight. This causes the maize plants to grow thin and produce tiny cobs, leading to a smaller overall harvest than properly spaced plants.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei baatswa akaŋ kɛha nu. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ amɛteŋ Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni ehaa ŋmãa bibii baa. Enɛ haa ŋmaa fɛɛ ni akpaa lɛ baa shi fe tso ni akɛtoɔ he ko ni sa.

english: Why is my farm giving me less food every harvest even though I use the same piece of land and work just as hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ haaa mi niyenii fioo be fɛɛ be ni abaakpa lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mi fɛɛ miyɔɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni mitsuɔ nii waa nakai nɔŋŋ moŋ.

english: Crops pull nutrients out of the soil as they grow. If you plant the same crop on the same plot season after season without adding manure, organic compost, or letting the soil rest, the earth becomes exhausted and loses its nutrients.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Kɛji odu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo ohaa shikpɔŋ lɛ jɔɔɔ lɛ fataaa he lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite ni niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ baaje mli.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating the inner leaves of my young maize as soon as the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ je shishi pɛ?

english: These pests are likely Fall Armyworms, which hatch quickly in warm, humid weather and target soft growing leaves. Identifying them early allows you to use recommended pest control remedies before they destroy the center of the plant.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni fɔɔ oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. ni akɛma baai bibii ni miida lɛ anɔ. Amɛyoomɔ mra Enɛ baaha okɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii kɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ atsu nii dani amɛfite tso lɛ mli fã lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato leaves turning yellow and curling up into tight tubes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe kɛmiifee tsɔji ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and yellowing in tomatoes is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies carrying a plant virus, or severe stress from heat and uneven watering. Protecting plants from pests early keeps the leaves green and open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni hiɛ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ tomato mli. loo haomɔ ni naa wa ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa mli baa. Abuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe mra Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeleɔ amɛhe.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they experience heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients in the soil. Consistent watering and adding compost during flowering helps the blossoms develop into healthy pepper fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ pepper aduawai ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when heavy rains fall right before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa dani kpamɔ lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots require well-drained soil to breathe. When water sits in flat soil without proper drainage, the roots suffocate and decompose. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds helps excess water flow away safely.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ he hiaa cassava shishifãi koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse nɔ lɛ, nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ bɛ. Shishifãi lɛ baafo ni amɛbaagboi. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Can I save seeds from the maize I harvested last season to plant again this year?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni mikpa yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ afi nɛɛ?

english: If your previous harvest came from hybrid seeds, saving those seeds will yield weaker plants and much less food. While traditional open-pollinated seeds can be saved, buying fresh certified seeds each season guarantees strong crop growth.
ga: Kɛji akɛ okpamɔ ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ jɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ mli Nakai dumɔwui lɛ ni ooohere lɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ faaa kwraa. Eyɛ mli akɛ abaanyɛ ato blema dumɔwui ni agbele naa lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ moŋ, shi kɛ́ ahe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ adara waa.

english: Why do weeds always grow so much faster than my crops after the first rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii be fɛɛ be yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Wild weeds are naturally suited to local conditions and have deep root systems that consume water and soil food instantly. Clearing weeds early prevents them from stealing light and food away from your growing crop plants.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi lɛ ji nɔ ni sa kɛha shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ, ni eyɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni yeɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Jwɛi ni ooojie mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju la kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ otsei ni miida lɛ amli.

english: How do I know if the ground is truly ready for planting right after the dry season ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo diɛŋtsɛ kɛha dumɔ beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eba naagbee lɛ?

english: Planting after the very first rainfall is risky because dry soil swallows initial rain quickly and remains hot underground. You should wait until the rainfall is steady enough to moisten the top layer of soil down to the depth of your hand.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ yɛ oshara ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ miɔ shishijee nugbɔ lɛ oya ni ehaa edɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Esa akɛ omɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ ashɛ shi shiŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashɛ onine mli.

english: When maize plants are crowded together, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Giving each seed proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough food and sunlight to produce large, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ abua ŋmãa tsei anaa yɛ kui amli lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ kɛha amɛhe He ni sa ni akɛhaa yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa niyenii kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛwo ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yam vines need maximum exposure to sunlight so their leaves can manufacture food to feed the tubers underground. Staking lifts leaves off the damp ground, improving sunlight exposure and protecting the vines from fungal rot.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ afee niyenii ni baaye abua ŋmeii lɛ. Elevator lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Ehaa hulu la lɛ yaa hiɛ ni ebuɔ wain tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ ahe.

english: When is the right time for me to put fertilizer on my maize farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Maize needs nutrients at key growth stages. The first application should be done about two weeks after germination when green shoots appear, and the second when the plants are knee-high right before producing tassels.
ga: Niyenii mli hewalɛ he miihia ŋmãa yɛ dalɛ bei ni he hiaa waa lɛ amli. Esa akɛ afee klɛŋklɛŋ tsofa lɛ aaafee otsi enyɔ sɛɛ beni ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃, beni ŋmeii eŋɔlii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ. kɛ shi ni ji enyɔ lɛ beni tso lɛ shɛɔ enaji ahe dani enáa ŋmeii.

english: How does planting groundnuts alongside my corn help my soil and crops?
ga: Te ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull natural nitrogen out of the air and deposit it into the soil through their roots. Maize needs nitrogen to grow strong, so intercropping with groundnuts acts like a continuous, natural fertilizer source.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ nitrogen mli kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃, no hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa wo mli lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa jɛɛhe ni yaa nɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are fragile and easily scorched by strong sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide big leafy canopies that shield young cocoa plants from heat while keeping moisture in the soil.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shãa amɛ oya. Tsei bibii ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai agbo ko ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he, yɛ be mli ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my vegetable plants wilting during the hottest part of the afternoon even when the ground was watered?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli beni mikɛ nu ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ po lɛ?

english: During intense afternoon heat, leaves lose water through evaporation faster than the roots can suck it up from the soil. The leaves temporarily wilt to protect the plant from drying out, usually recovering by evening when temperatures drop.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ baagbee shi be kukuoo ko koni tso lɛ akagbi. Bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ beni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi lɛ.

english: Why are caterpillars eating tiny holes into the center whorl of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii yeɔ buji bibii lɛ? Yɛ mi gbekɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworms, which lay eggs on tender leaves. The hatching caterpillars crawl into the central heart of the plant where it is moist and dark, eating the young leaves before they open up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ baai bibii anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kplukai ni efɔ lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ni mli ewo duŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ mli. Ye baai bibii dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies feeding on the underside of leaves. As they suck the plant juices, they weaken the leaves and can transmit viruses that stunt growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛŋ ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. beni amɛmuɔ tso mli nu lɛ Amɛhaa baai lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ helai ni tsiɔ dalɛ naa lɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn hard and woody if I leave them in the ground too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tso kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots store starch for the plant's food reserves. If left unharvested past full maturity, the plant converts that soft starch into tough woody fibers to support stem growth, making the root tough and poor for cooking.
ga: Cassava shishifãi toɔ starch akɛ tso lɛ niyenii ni akɛtoɔ. Kɛji akɛ ashi lɛ kɛyashi eda kwraa Tso lɛ tsakeɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ewoɔ tso mli ŋmɔtɔ ni wa mli koni eye ebua tso lɛ shishifã lɛ dalɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni esaaa akɛ ahoɔ nii.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium reaching the fruit. Irregular watering causes uneven nutrient flow in the plant, leading to cell breakdown at the base of the tomato.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni faaa. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ daa lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni yɔɔ tsei amli lɛ hoɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, wala yibii ni yɔɔ tomato lɛ shishi lɛ baafite.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains on the same land where I am planting young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ kookoo tsei bibii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily in direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow very quickly and produce large leaves that provide essential shade and moisture, acting as a shelter for cocoa during its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya waa ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ. Eji he ni Cocoa hiɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Will planting plantains on my cocoa farm take away nutrients and hurt the growth of the cocoa?
ga: Ani plantains ni miduɔ yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baajie niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛjɛ mli ni ebaafite kookoo lɛ dalɛ?

english: No, if spaced properly, plantains and cocoa complement each other because plantain roots are shallow while cocoa roots grow deeper, allowing them to draw nutrients from different soil levels without competing.
ga: Dabi, kɛji akɛ ato he gbɛjianɔ bɔ ni sa. Plantain kɛ cocoa kɛ amɛhe feɔ ekome jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, yɛ be mli ni cocoa shishifãi lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa amɛgbalaa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ srɔtoi anɔ ni amɛkɛ amɛhe etswaaa akaŋ.

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots and tall, heavy stems filled with water. When the soil becomes soft from rain and the heavy fruit bunch weighs the plant down, strong winds can easily pull the shallow roots out of the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ tsei kakadaji ni tsii ni nu eyi mli obɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ fee blɛoo yɛ nugbɔ kɛ aduawai akui ni tsii hewɔ lɛ, tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ. Shi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mlɛo

english: Why are the leaves on my plantain tree turning yellow before the fruits are fully mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani aduawai lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the plant lacks water or key nutrients like potassium, or it is being attacked by underground root pests like plantain nematodes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu loo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium bɛ tso lɛ mli, loo shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, tamɔ plantain nematodes lɛ miitutua lɛ.

english: How can I tell when a bunch of plantain is ready for me to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni plantains lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Plantain is ready to harvest when the individual fingers swell up and lose their sharp edges, becoming rounded, and the small leaf at the top of the bunch turns yellow.
ga: Plantains lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji nineshi nine lɛ eko fɛɛ eko fũu ni eshishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ sɛɛ fo, ni ebatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni baai bibii ni yɔɔ panicle lɛ yiteŋ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce many flowers, but most of them drop off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi amɛteŋ mɛi babaoo gbeeɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ pods?

english: Cocoa flowers require tiny insects called midges for pollination; if these insects are missing, or if the tree is stressed by dry weather or poor soil nutrients, the flowers fall off without forming pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii. Atsɛɔ nakai midge kɛha ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛji akɛ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ laaje loo kɛji akɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. No sɛɛ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii.

english: Why do young cocoa pods on my trees turn black and dry up before they fully grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This is typically caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in cool, overly shaded, and very humid environments where air cannot flow freely between trees.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ. Shade babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ ni hulutsoo hu fa babaoo aahu akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ oya.

english: How long does a newly planted cocoa tree take before it begins to yield pods?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani cacao tso ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ shishi ewoɔ ŋmeii?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa varieties usually begin producing pods within 2 to 3 years under good care, whereas older traditional varieties take about 4 to 5 years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo ni akɛfee tsofai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmeii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli yɛ kwɛmɔ kpakpa shishi. Yɛ be mli ni blema kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ baahe aaafee afii 4 kɛyashi 5 lɛ.

english: Why do mature cocoa trees need less shade than young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei ni eda lɛ biɔ hulutsoo fioo fe cacao tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves are delicate and scorch easily, but mature trees need direct sunlight on their canopy to generate the energy required to yield large amounts of cocoa pods.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya. Shi tsei ni eda lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛmli lɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛfee kookoo ŋmeii babaoo.

english: How far apart should I space my cocoa trees when planting them for the first time?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ato he ko beni miduɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees should generally be planted 3 meters apart from each other so their roots and branches have sufficient room to expand without competing for sunlight and nutrients.
ga: Esa akɛ bei pii lɛ, adu cocoa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ ji mitai 3 koni eha shishifãi kɛ eniji lɛ aná hegbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛkaye akaŋ yɛ hulu la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he.

english: How can I tell if my maize crops are dying from lack of water or from a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu ni faaa loo hela miigbo yɛ mi-abele lɛ mli?

english: When maize lacks water, the leaves roll up tightly like fingers during the hottest part of the day to save moisture, and they turn yellow evenly from the bottom of the plant upwards. Disease usually causes irregular spots, strange colors, or rotting regardless of how hot the sun is.
ga: Beni nu bɛ ŋmãa lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe shi shiŋŋ tamɔ niji yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli koni eye ebua ni ŋmãa lɛ ahi shi. ni kɛjɛ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ, ebaatsɔ ŋmɔŋ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Bei pii lɛ, hela kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ejaaa, sui ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ, loo ŋmɔtɔ baa. Bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni hulu lɛ mli edɔ ha

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants droop down in the hot afternoon sun even though they look healthy in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shwane hulu lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ? Ani baai lɛ yɛ hewalɛ lolo?

english: Pepper plants lose water rapidly through their leaves when the sun is extremely hot. Drooping is the plant's natural self-defense to reduce the leaf area exposed to direct sunlight so it doesn't dry out before evening.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulu lɛ miitso waa. Foji ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu. Koni akɛba he ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ shi. No hewɔ lɛ, egbiɛɛ dani gbɛkɛ shɛɔ.

english: What crops can I plant on my farm if my land is far from any river or stream and relies only on rain?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ faa loo faa ko teŋ jɛkɛ ni ekɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ nugbɔ pɛ nɔ?

english: Crops like cassava, cowpeas (beans), sorghum, and millet do very well in dry areas. Their root systems grow deep to search for underground moisture, and they can pause their growth during dry spells without dying easily.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei, tsina ŋmei, ŋmei kɛ ŋmei tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa yɛ hei ni nu bɛ. Amɛshishifãi lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ koni amɛtao shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmɔtɔ. Ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkpa dalɛ be kukuoo ko yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli ni amɛgbooo oya.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die during long dry spells while the plantains next to them stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli yɛ be mli ni cacao tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ? eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo

english: Plantain stems act like giant sponges that store soft stem tissue filled with water, whereas young cocoa trees have tender, woody roots and small stems that cannot hold water for long periods without rain.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji wuji ni hiɛɔ tso lɛ mli fãji ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, kookoo tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ tsei bibii ni nyɛɛɛ ahiɛ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ.

english: How can I keep the soil around my tomato plants from drying out quickly when the sun is very hot?
ga: Mibaafee shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ Te fee tɛŋŋ ni mi tomato tsei lɛ egbiŋ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: You can cover the soil around the stem with dried grass, leaves, or cocoa pod husks (a practice called mulching). This organic blanket blocks direct sunlight from hitting the bare earth, keeping the root area cool and holding moisture much longer.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Tso ni jwɛi ni egbi, baai, loo kookoo ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli. (Gbɛ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ mulching.) Nɛkɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli nɛɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Enɛ haa shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why does the soil on the top of the hill on my farm dry out much faster than the soil in the lowland valley?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ gɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbiɔ oya fe shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ jɔɔ lɛ mli ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ waa lɛ?

english: Rainwater naturally drains downward due to gravity and gathers in low valley soils. High ground loses water quickly to drainage, wind exposure, and intense sun, making the top layer of soil dry out faster.
ga: Nugbɔ nu hoɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hewalɛ ni tsiɔ nii kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hewɔ, ni ebuaa ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ jɔɔ lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ nu fiteɔ oya yɛ nu ni hoɔ, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ hewɔ, ni no haa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya.

english: Is it better for me to give my vegetable crop a little water every day or a lot of water just twice a week?
ga: Ani ebaafee nɔ ni hi akɛ mahã mitsei lɛ nu fioo daa gbi? Aloo ehi akɛ oooha lɛ nu babaoo kɛkɛ shii enyɔ yɛ otsi mli?

english: Watering deeply a few times a week is much better. Deep watering encourages roots to grow downward into the cooler soil where water stays longer, whereas light daily watering keeps roots near the surface where the hot sun quickly dries them out.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli shii 2-3 yɛ otsi mli lɛ hi kwraa. Nu ni mli kwɔ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ nɔ. he ni nu hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ Be mli ni afɔɔ nu blɛoo Daa gbi yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baaha amɛgbi oya lɛ.

english: Is it safe for me to plant my cassava cuttings right after the very first rain of the year falls?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is risky because the first rain only wet the top surface while the ground underneath remains hot and dry. It is best to wait for two or three heavy rains so the deeper soil absorbs enough water to help the stem cuttings sprout roots safely.
ga: Oshara yɛ ejaakɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa ŋwɛi ŋshɔ lɛ nɔ pɛ fɔ̃ɔ. yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ lolo lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa shii enyɔ loo etɛ koni shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: Will hot weather with no rain cause my maize cobs to remain small or have missing seeds?
ga: Ani kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ baaha ŋmãa lɛ ahi shi bibii loo dumɔwui lɛ baaje mli?

english: Yes, if maize plants lack water while flowering, the silk threads dry up before pollen can touch them. Without proper pollination, many kernels will not form, leading to small cobs with missing seeds.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ nu bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Siliki lɛ gbɛ́ɔ dani pollen lɛ kɛ lɛ kpeɔ. Kɛji akɛ pollination ni sa bɛ lɛ Dumɔwui babaoo efeŋ. ni ekɛ ŋmei bibioo ko ba he ni dumɔwui lɛ laaje yɛ lɛ

english: Why are my yam vines turning yellow and remaining very small when there has been no rain for weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛji bibii waa lolo yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛko otsii babaoo nɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need continuous moisture to push nutrients up to form green leaves. When water is scarce, the plant stops growing new leaves and saves its remaining energy underground inside the seed tuber until moisture returns.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia nu ni mli edɔ daa koni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ awo baai eŋɔli amli. Kɛ nu faaa Tso lɛ haa baai heei lɛ shwereɔ ni ekɛ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ayitso lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Officer, what exactly is the Fall Armyworm that everyone in Ghana is talking about?
ga: Ofisa, mɛni tuuntu ji Fall Armyworm ni mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ wieɔ he lɛ?
