english: The Fall Armyworm is a destructive caterpillar that feeds heavily on maize plants. It chews through leaves and stalks, leading to severe damage across fields if left unchecked.
ga: Fall Armyworm ji ŋmei ni fiteɔ nii ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei babaoo. Eyeɔ baai kɛ tsei ashishifãi. Ekɛ fitemɔ ni naa wa baa ŋmɔji amli kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does the Fall Armyworm manage to spread so quickly from farm to farm?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni Fall Armyworm lɛ agbɛ ashwã oya kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛya ŋmɔ mli?

english: The adult form of the Fall Armyworm is a moth that can fly long distances overnight on wind currents, laying hundreds of eggs on healthy maize crops across wide areas.
ga: Fall Armyworm ni eda lɛ ji ŋmei ni baanyɛ afã gbɛ kakadaŋŋ nyɔɔŋ kome yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ nɔ. Amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ohai abɔ yɛ ŋmãa tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahe hei wuji.

english: Why does maize seem to attract so many pests and diseases all at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa gbalaa kooloi kɛ helai babaoo yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: Maize is a sweet, nutrient-rich crop that attracts many insects. When weather conditions or pests stress the plant, its natural defenses weaken, making it vulnerable to multiple diseases at once.
ga: Abɛi ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni ŋɔɔ, ni niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo yɔɔ mli ni gbalaa koolooi babaoo. Kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ haomɔ ba tsei anɔ lɛ Ebɔɔ su mli hebuu lɛ baagbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa helai babaoo nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ shikome.

english: Why are ragged holes suddenly appearing in the leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji ni etse ehe lɛ miije kpo trukaa yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Holes and ragged edges on maize leaves are usually caused by feeding caterpillars, such as the Fall Armyworm, which eat the tender young leaves from the central whorl outward.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni yeɔ baai bibii kɛjɛɔ teŋgbɛ kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni etse ehe lɛ baa.

english: How can I inspect my maize field to catch pest damage early before it gets bad?
ga: Makwɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ amli kɛji tsɛŋemɔ helai efite mra. Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmãa lɛ agbo?

english: Look inside the central funnel (whorl) of young maize plants for ragged leaf holes and small yellowish-brown waste material, which indicate active caterpillars hiding inside.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmãa tso bibioo lɛ teŋgbɛ faa (ring) lɛ mli. koni ana baai ni etsilɛ kɛ nibii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmei ko ni tsuɔ nii ehiɛ ehe yɛ mli.

english: Why do pests seem to cause much worse damage when my maize plants are already struggling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fiteɔ nii waa fe tsutsu lɛ yɛ be mli ni mi-abele tsei lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔ momo lɛ?

english: A weak or stressed plant cannot grow fast enough to replace destroyed leaves or produce natural defense chemicals, allowing pests to eat through the plant faster than it can recover.
ga: Tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni haoɔ amɛhe lɛ nyɛŋ adara oya bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaato baai ni efite lɛ najiaŋ loo amɛfee adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni buɔ mɔ he. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai yeɔ tso lɛ oya fe bɔ ni ebaanyɛ ehiɛ ahi ehe nɔ.

english: If worms eat the leaves of my maize, will it really stop the plant from producing good cobs?
ga: Kɛji ŋmei ko ye mi ŋmãa lɛ Ani ebaatsi tso lɛ naa diɛŋtsɛ koni ekawo ŋmãa kpakpai?

english: Yes, leaves are like the factory of the plant that makes food for cob development. If caterpillars destroy the leaves, the maize plant cannot produce energy to grow healthy, full cobs.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, baai lɛ tamɔ tso ko nitsumɔhe ni feɔ niyenii kɛha cob lɛ shweremɔ. Kɛji ŋmeii lɛ fite baai lɛ, Abele nyɛŋ ajie hewalɛ ni baaha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ ni eye emuu.

english: What will happen to my total harvest if I do not take action when pests attack my maize?
ga: Mɛni baaba mikpamɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ kɛji mifeee nɔ ko beni tsɛŋemɔ helai tutua mi ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Without control measures, pest infestations can completely ruin the leaves and stalks, resulting in stunted plants, empty cobs, or total crop failure with very little to harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ gbɛjianɔtoo ko bɛ ni akɛbaatsu he nii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ afite baai kɛ tsei lɛ kwraa. Enɛ haa tsei ni egbɔjɔ, ŋmeii ni efee efolo loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite ni be fioo pɛ yɔɔ ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ baa.

english: Is this Fall Armyworm threat just on my farm, or is it a general problem across Ghana?
ga: Ani Fall Armyworm he gbeyeishemɔ lɛ ji nɔ ko ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli pɛ loo eji naagba ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana fɛɛ?

english: It is a nationwide issue in Ghana affecting maize farmers across many regions, which is why agricultural officers and communities are taking urgent joint action to control it.
ga: Enɛ ji maŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ naagba ko ni yɔɔ Ghana ni saa ŋmãa okwaafoi ni yɔɔ kpokpai babaoo anɔ lɛ ahe. Enɛ hewɔ ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi kɛ akutsei lɛ miitsu nii oya koni amɛkɛkudɔ naagba nɛɛ.

english: Why is it risky to ignore a pest problem when it is just starting on a few of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaaku hiɛ ashwie tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe naagbai anɔ lɛ? Akɛni eje shishi kɛkɛ kɛ mi ŋmãa tsei fioo komɛi pɛ hewɔ lɛ?

english: Pests multiply extremely fast. A small infestation on a few plants can quickly explode into thousands of caterpillars that destroy your entire field within days if not controlled early.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fɔɔ oya waa. small spread Tsei fioo komɛi pɛ baanyɛ atswa oya ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii akpei abɔ. Enɛ baafite he ni oyɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli kɛji akɛ akudɔɔɔ mra.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct heat from the sun. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide shade, keeping the young cocoa plants cool and moist until they grow strong enough to withstand direct sunlight.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo. Ha cacao tsei bibii lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning light yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient responsible for leaf growth and green color. This happens when the soil is exhausted or when heavy rains wash away soil nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni haa baa lɛ daa kɛ eŋɔli su. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ sũ lɛ mli ewo wu loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fite niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why is it good for me to plant groundnuts or beans in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When left in the ground, they feed the soil naturally, helping nearby maize plants grow stronger without needing as much artificial fertilizer.
ga: Akpɔlɔi kɛ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa babaoo awo mli.

english: What causes small holes in the leaves at the center of my young maize stalks?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ baa ni yɔɔ mibi lɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the growing center of the maize plant and eats the delicate new leaves before they open up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ni amɛyeɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ dani amɛgbeleɔ lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips feeding on the underside of the leaves, or by a virus these insects carry that disrupts leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ hiɛɔ ni tsiɔ baa lɛ naa lɛ nɔ

english: How does placing dry leaves around the base of my tomato plants help them during hot days?
ga: Baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te mi-tomato tsei lɛ ashishitoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tɛŋŋ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli?

english: Placing dry grass or leaves around plants is called mulching. It acts like a blanket over the dirt, stopping the sun from drying out soil moisture and keeping the crop roots cool.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛbɔleɔ Tsei ahe lɛ akɛ mulching. Efeɔ enii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekagbi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni eha tso shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when left in wet soil during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When soil stays completely soaked with water, oxygen cannot reach the cassava roots. Starved of air, the roots weaken and rot easily due to soil fungi thriving in damp conditions.
ga: Kɛji nu shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ahe. kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ hewɔ Shishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛgboiɔ oya ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ omanye yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ mli.

english: Why should I stick tall wooden poles into the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama shi lɛ? Okɛwo shikpɔŋ koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can trap as much sunlight as possible to make energy, which goes directly into producing larger underground tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ amɔmɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛkɛfee hewalɛ. ni baaha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji aba tɛ̃ɛ

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when temperatures become too hot or when water is irregular, because the stress prevents proper pollination and fruit development.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛji nu lɛ ejaaa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nɔnyɛɛ tsiɔ pollination kɛ aduawai lɛ akwɛmɔ ni sa naa.

english: The first rain is often followed by several hot, dry weeks before the real rainy season sets in. Seeds planted too early may sprout and then dry up and die from lack of follow-up rain.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, otsii babaoo ni mli edɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be diɛŋtsɛ lɛ baashɛ. Dumɔwui ni adu mra tsɔ lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgbi ni amɛgboi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ hewɔ.

english: Heavy rainfall washes away nitrogen from the soil, which is the key nutrient maize plants need to stay green and grow strong.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my maize when the rainy season begins?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ bote mli lɛ?

english: Planting should be done after the soil receives one or two deep rains so the ground retains enough moisture for the seeds to germinate properly.
ga: Esa akɛ adu beni shikpɔŋ lɛ ená nugbɔ ni naa wa shikome loo enyɔ sɛɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the flowers on my cocoa tree falling off instead of turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaatsɔ cacao ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop when the plant suffers from water stress during dry spells or when there are not enough tiny insects called midges to pollinate them.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Aloo kɛ́ kooloi bibii yɛ Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ midge lɛ faaa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ pollination baa.

english: Why do young green cocoa pods turn black and dry up while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ be mli ni amɛkã tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast in cool, wet, and shady farm conditions.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava stems growing tall with lots of leaves, but the tubers underground are small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso lɛ kɛlɛ shi eyɛ baai babaoo shi ŋmei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ji bibioo lɛ?

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil causes the cassava plant to spend its energy producing leafy top growth instead of storing starch in the root tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei tsei lɛ kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ baa ŋmeii amli moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ ŋmei baato amɛshishifãi lɛ amli.

english: How can I prevent my cassava roots from rotting in the ground during heavy rains?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ atsĩ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess water to drain away, keeping the roots from sitting in waterlogged soil.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. Etsiɔ shishifãi anaa koni amɛkatara shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my farmland produce fewer crops each year even when I clean and weed the farm well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo daa afi lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mile ŋmɔ lɛ mli saamɔ kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ moŋ.

english: Growing crops on the same land season after season exhausts soil nutrients, so the land needs crop rotation or manure to rebuild its fertility.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ haa niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ atsake shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii koni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni baa lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it harmful to burn the bushes on my land before I plant my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mashã tsei bibii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani adu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Burning destroys organic matter and kills beneficial earthworms and soil organisms that help keep the soil fertile and moist.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ahiɛ ni egbeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛ sũ mli nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ŋmɔshi nibii yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up tightly during the sunny afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli shwane mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl inward to reduce water loss through their surface when the weather is too hot and dry.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli koni nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ.

english: Why do my pepper seedlings collapse and die at the stem level right after I put them in the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ stem level nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is called 'damping-off,' a soil fungus attack that happens when seedling beds stay too wet and poorly ventilated.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ ‘Damping’, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni baa kɛji dumɔwui asaji lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my land's soil is actually good for growing crops before I plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hi diɛŋtsɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ? Dani abaadu loo aduuu

english: You can send a sample of your soil to an agricultural laboratory for testing. The lab checks the nutrients, acidity, and soil type to tell you exactly which crops will grow successfully on your land.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ amaje okwaayeli he ko koni aka lɛ akwɛ. Lab lɛ baakwɛ niyenii mli nibii, acidity, kɛ shikpɔŋ henɔ. Koni ekɛɛ bo ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ ni baaye omanye yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some crops grow very well on my neighbor's farm but fail completely on mine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ mli, shi amɛshwereɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Soil can change drastically even over short distances. Your neighbor's land might have different soil depth, nutrient levels, or water drainage than yours, making it suitable for different crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ atsake kwraa yɛ gbɛ kukuji po amli. Ekolɛ okutsoŋnyo lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ. Nutrient level Aloo nu ni hoɔ lɛ yɛ srɔto yɛ onɔ̃ lɛ he? Enɛ haa ehi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi.

english: How does sending my farm soil to a laboratory save me money?
ga: Te ebaafee tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni mikɛbaatsu nii yɛ laboratori lɛ mli lɛ baaha maná shika?

english: Testing your soil prevents you from spending money on seeds that won't grow on your land or buying expensive fertilizers that your soil does not actually need.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ kaa baatsi bo gbɛ koni okafite shika yɛ dumɔwui ni baakwɛ̃ yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe. Aloo hemɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa ni he ehiaaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants turn yellow and dry up before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi dani akpa lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your crop is starving for key soil nutrients like nitrogen, or it is not getting enough water. A soil test shows what fertilizer your land needs to keep crops healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ onibii lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo amɛnáaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Shikpɔŋ nɔ kaa tsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ koni enyɛ ekwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my tomato plants producing plenty of yellow flowers but no fruits are forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi ŋmɔŋ babaoo shi ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: Extreme heat, lack of water, or missing nutrients like phosphorus can cause plant flowers to drop off before turning into fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni faaa yɛ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha tso fɔfɔii lɛ agbɔjɔ dani amɛbatsɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up and stop growing during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛkpaa shweremɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids, or by heat stress when the soil loses all its moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ mli haomɔ mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu lɛ fɛɛ fiteɔ lɛ.

english: What causes crop roots to rot and turn soft after heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni haa tsei ashishifãi fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: When soil has too much clay or poor drainage, rainwater gets trapped around the roots. Without air in the soil, the roots drown and rot.
ga: Be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ fa babaoo loo nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Nugbɔ nu baakpɛtɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛbaagboi.

english: Why does my land become very hard and cracked when it does not rain for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ais ni egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni nugbɔ enɛko otsii fioo komɛi nɛ lɛ?

english: Soil gets hard when it lacks organic matter like dried leaves or compost. Adding manure or compost helps soil stay loose and hold onto water longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai ni egboi loo ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha sũ lɛ mli agbɔjɔ ni nu lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall and thin instead of forming big tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni efeɔ mlɛo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight for sunlight and soil food. The plants stretch upward for light instead of putting energy into growing big underground roots.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Tsei lɛ tsɔɔ amɛhe koni amɛhe la lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaaha hewalɛ koni shishifãi wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Is it good to plant groundnuts on the same piece of land where I grow corn?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmei yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and naturally put it back into the soil, which helps feed heavy-eating crops like corn.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli nitrogen ni amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa sũ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ. ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei ni ayeɔ amɛ waa, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ niyenii

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crops lack nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to grow green leaves. This happens when the soil is exhausted or when heavy rains wash away soil nutrients, so adding fertilizer or compost helps them turn healthy green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai eŋɔli Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ loo kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni etsɔ eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my corn leaves curl up tightly like drinking straws during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ jwɛi ni anuɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is the plant's natural trick to protect itself from heat. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface exposed to the hot sun, which keeps water from evaporating out of the plant too quickly.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli ŋaa ni ekɛbuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he. Kɛ́ okɛ baai lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ hiɛ ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi. Enɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli oya tsɔ.

english: Yams produce big tubers underground when their leaves get plenty of direct sunlight. Staking keeps the leaves off the hot ground, allows maximum sun exposure, and prevents wet ground rot from damaging the foliage.
ga: Sweet potatoes woɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji kɛji amɛbaai lɛ ná hulu la babaoo tɛ̃ɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni enine shɛɔ hulu la ni fe fɛɛ nɔ. ni etsĩɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekafite baai lɛ.

english: What happens to my crops if I sow seeds very close together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ bu kome mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crowded plants compete with each other for limited water, light, and soil nutrients. This causes them to grow thin and weak, resulting in very low harvests.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei ni mli wa lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná nu, la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛhe tsɔi ni amɛgbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi kwraa.

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves start turning yellow and dropping off, and tiny cracks appear on the topsoil around the stem base, showing that tubers have expanded underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. ni ŋmeii bibii yɛ Ejeɔ kpo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ. Etsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ miigbɛ amɛshwã yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why is it good practice to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on land where I previously harvested maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ madu ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpaa ŋmeii yɛ nɔ tsutsu lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have special roots that grab nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the earth. Rotating crops this way naturally restores soil fertility for the next season's grain crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛgbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ nɛkɛ gbɛ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ekoŋŋ kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Weeds have aggressive roots that steal water and fertilizer nutrients faster than your main crops can reach them. Clearing weeds early ensures all applied fertilizer goes directly into feeding your crop.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe bɔ ni otso titri lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yaa onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my maize leaves and light dust inside the central shoot?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? Yɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ kɛ sũ fioo ko ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli lɛ

english: This damage is typically caused by hungry caterpillars like fall armyworms feeding inside the leaf whorl. Spraying approved biopesticides or plant extracts early protects the growing shoot before serious damage is done.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ, tamɔ asraafoi ŋmeii ni egbee shi, ni yeɔ baai ŋmeii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo tsei amli nibii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra Ebuɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ahe dani fitemɔ ni mli wa baa.

english: Flowers fall when plants get stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to save energy rather than using it to build fruits.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛkɛbaatsu nii ni amɛkɛwo yibii.

english: Why is it better to buy certified hybrid seeds instead of planting seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially tested and bred to grow uniformly, resist common local plant diseases, and produce higher yields compared to old seeds that gradually lose their strength over generations.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ akwɛɔ krɛdɛɛ ni akwɛɔ amɛ koni amɛdara daa. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ tsei ahe helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ ni ehaa yibiiwoo babaoo kɛ akɛto dumɔwui momo ni hewalɛ baa shi fiofio kɛjɛɔ yinɔ kome mli kɛyaa yinɔ kroko mli lɛ ahe.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct sunlight because their roots are shallow and leaf tissues burn easily. Planting shade crops like plantains or leaving canopy trees shields young cocoa from heavy heat and keeps moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛbaa lɛ mli fãji lɛ shãa oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo ashi ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni ebaaha sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Why do my maize leaves have ragged holes in them with tiny caterpillars hiding inside the center of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Ni okɛ ohe ewo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworms, which target the tender central leaves (the funnel) of maize. Finding them early and applying organic treatments like neem oil or recommended sprays into the leaf funnels stops them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmãa ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ ni yɔɔ blɛoo (cones) lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Taomɔ amɛ mra. kɛ tsofai ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli tamɔ neem fɔ loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii. Tsi amɛ gbɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling tightly upwards and stopping the plant from growing tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso kɛmiiya ŋwɛi ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids that live on the underside of leaves and transmit viruses. Controlling these pests early prevents the virus from spreading and stunting the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. ni hiɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛhaa helai baa Helai nɛɛ anɔ kudɔmɔ mra Ebaatsi helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ anaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa ni eha tsei lɛ akagbɔjɔ.

english: Cassava roots need oxygen in the soil to stay healthy. In waterlogged soil, roots drown and harmful fungal diseases thrive, causing rot; planting cassava on raised ridges or mounds allows excess water to drain away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ daa. kɛ fitemɔ baa Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Why should I spread dry grass or straw on the bare ground around my vegetable crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbɛ jwɛi loo jwɛi ashwã shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ mabɔle mi-aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass is called mulching. It acts as a blanket that protects the soil from the hot sun, keeps water from evaporating quickly, stops weeds from growing, and decomposes into natural nutrients.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekafee lasu oya Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa ni efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii

english: Why do experienced farmers tell me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ baakɛɛ mi akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ ni mikɛ mi-ŋmã lɛ duɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots, which naturally enriches the soil with free fertilizer that nearby maize plants use to grow strong.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa ŋmɔshi nibii ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli ni aheee nɔ ko ni ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Extremely high heat dries out tomato pollen, preventing flowers from successfully pollinating and forming fruit. Watering early in the morning and providing soil shade through mulching helps keep root zone temperatures cool enough to support fruiting.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baaha tomato pollen lɛ agbi. Etsiɔ fɔfɔii lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye omanye ni amɛkawo yibii. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ leebi ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo ni bɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli jɔɔ bɔ ni sa ni ewoɔ aduawai ahe hewalɛ.

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight on their leaves to produce energy for growing big underground tubers. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground where diseases live and exposes them to sunlight.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni baa lɛ. Staking baajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ he ni hela lɛ yɔɔ lɛ, ni ebaaha hulu la lɛ aba amɛnɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily during strong winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems that can be weakened by stem borers or underground worm pests (nematodes). Leaving too many suckers growing around one mother plant also weakens its anchor in the soil.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni stem borers loo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii baanyɛ aha amɛgbɔjɔ. (Nematodes) Eshiɔ ŋmeii babaoo ni ebɔleɔ he. Tso ni ji nyɛ kome lɛ hu haa e-ankɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why do my cabbage plants stay open and leafy instead of forming a hard, round head?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ miigbele ni eyɛ baai yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee yitso ni wa ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ?

english: Cabbage requires cool root temperatures, steady watering, and balanced nutrients to form a solid head. Applying too much nitrogen fertilizer causes excess leaf growth without the central head tightening up.
ga: Kaabaji he miihia shishifãi ni mli ejɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ niyenii ni sa ni akɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ Nitrogen ŋmeii ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ baaha baai lɛ adara fe nine ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ bɛ mli.

english: This is usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting improved, disease-resistant cassava stems provided by agricultural extension officers is the best way to keep your farm healthy and ensure a strong harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Okwaayeli mli nitsulɔi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ni amɛduɔ ŋmei tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ oha oŋmɔ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni okwɛ koni ŋmaa ni mli wa aba.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers and look unhealthy when the big forest trees around them are cut down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa tsei lɛ amli fɔfɔii lɛ miiho ni amɛmiifee tamɔ mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ beni afolɔ tsei ni eda ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally thrive under canopy shade. Without shade trees, the intense sun dries out the soil, scorches the cocoa leaves, and makes the trees weak and vulnerable to insect attacks like mirids (capsids).
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ tsei ni akɛwoɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ashishi. Kɛji tsei ni baaha hulutsoo be lɛ bɛ Hulu ni naa wa lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. shãa kookoo baai lɛ ni ehaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni kooloi tamɔ mirids (capsids) lɛ baanyɛ atutua lɛ.

english: How do I know if my maize plants are lacking nutrients in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-abele tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: If your maize plants have thin stems and lower leaves that turn yellow starting from the tip down the middle rib, the soil lacks nitrogen. Applying NPK fertilizer or well-rotted manure early in the plant's life restores green foliage and boosts cob size.
ga: Kɛji akɛ o-abele tso lɛ yɛ shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ eshishigbɛ kɛyashiɔ teŋgbɛ tsitsii lɛ, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. NPK ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shihilɛ mli mra lɛ baaye abua ni eha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Maize leaves roll up to conserve water during high heat. By rolling their leaves, the plants reduce the leaf area exposed to the hot sun, preventing evaporation and saving moisture inside the stalk until the cooler evening.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛhiɛ nu mli yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ baai lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ebaaha he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ yɔɔ baa lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Etsiɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ naa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ tso lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Is it better to plant my yams on high mounds rather than on flat ground?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu sweet potatoes yɛ gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ moŋ fe nɔ ni aaadu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ?

english: Yams grow much better on raised soil mounds because loose, mounded soil allows the tubers to expand freely underground while preventing heavy rainfall from settling around the roots and causing tuber rot.
ga: Sweet potatoes kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ kwraa yɛ gɔji ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi amɛhaa amɛhe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekabɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe ni ehaa bulb lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for a single high-yielding harvest. If you plant the seeds saved from that harvest, the new crop will grow unevenly, produce smaller cobs, and yield much less grain than the original seed.
ga: Atsɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ anɔ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ kome ni woɔ yibii babaoo. Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ nakai kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ Nibii heei kwɛ̃ŋ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Ehaa cob yibii bibii ni ehaa dumɔwui fioo kwraa fe shishijee dumɔwui lɛ

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the weather becomes too dry and hot, or when the plant gets too much nitrogen fertilizer without enough phosphorus. Keeping the soil evenly moist and using balanced fertilizer helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji shihilɛi lɛ mli egbi tsɔ ni edɔ. aloo kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen babaoo wo tsei amli ni phosphorus ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Spear grass has aggressive underground stem networks called rhizomes that remain alive beneath the soil after cutting. To eliminate it, you must dig up the deep underground root networks or treat the green leaves with a systemic herbicide that reaches the roots.
ga: Spear jwɛi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni atsɛɔ amɛ rhizomes ni hiɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji afo lɛ sɛɛ. Bɔni afee ni ojie lɛ, ehe miihia ni otsa shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni mli kwɔ loo okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni shɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ atsa baai eŋɔlii lɛ.

english: Why do my stored maize grains turn into powder and get full of small insects after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ bafee powder ni ŋmeii bibii eyi mli obɔ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli lɛ?

english: This destruction is caused by grain weevils that hatch from tiny eggs inside dry seeds. Drying your maize thoroughly until it clicks between your teeth and storing it in airtight PICS bags starves the insects of air and preserves your harvest without chemicals.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ hiɛkpatamɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmei ŋmeii ni jɛɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ. inside dry seeds Gbimɔ o-corn lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi ebaashɛ onyanyɔji ateŋ. Ni kɛ́ akɛto kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli lɛ, PICS lɛ baaye abua ni eshi kooloi ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ, ni ebaaha tsofai akafee onibii lɛ.

english: Why will planting my plantain suckers too close together give me small bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ banana ŋmeii ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa mifeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Planting plantains too close forces their large leaves to shade one another, cutting off essential sunlight. Their roots also compete for water and soil nutrients, leading to slender stems and smaller, lighter fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛbaai wuji lɛ afee amɛhe ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni amɛfoɔ hulu la ni he hiaa lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ hu kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo kɛ aduawai akui bibii ni waaa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep drying up and dying when I plant them out in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct, harsh sunlight and hot winds. They need temporary shade plants like plantain or cocoyam planted beside them to shield their delicate leaves and keep the soil moist while they grow.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ he waa. Tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo cocoa ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Enɛ buɔ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why are tiny green caterpillars eating the leaves inside the center whorl of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miiye baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that loves feeding on the soft tender center of maize leaves. Catching them early and applying approved insecticides or putting clean sand/ash into the leaf funnel helps stop them before they destroy the whole plant.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni sumɔɔ ni eye ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ ateŋ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii Loo okɛ ŋã/ashwishwɛ ni he tse awo baa lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni akpa amɛ dani amɛfite tso muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with lots of green leaves, but the tubers underground remain tiny and watery?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmei lɛ ji bibioo lolo ni nu yɛ mli?

english: This usually happens when the soil has too much nitrogen or if the field is heavily shaded. The cassava plant puts all its energy into growing tall stem and leaves above ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo kɛ́ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ewo hulutsoo waa. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ eshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ amli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ starch baato shishifã lɛ mli lɛ

english: My pepper plants are flowering heavily, but why do all the flowers drop off without turning into peppers?
ga: Mi pepper tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi waa. Shi mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat stress, severe dry spells, or lack of soil nutrients. Providing consistent water during dry periods and adding compost or balanced fertilizer helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Hɔmɔ shihilɛi ni naa wa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa yɛ hɔmɔ be mli kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfutuɔ mli ni sa lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Do I really need to put wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb, or can I just let them spread on the ground?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni makɛ tso ko ama shi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ nɔ diɛŋtsɛ, aloo manyɛ mashi lɛ kɛkɛ ni egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high on stakes so their leaves can capture sunlight properly to make food. When vines trail on the hot ground, leaves get scorched and disease spreads easily, resulting in much smaller tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ hulu la lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛha nihoomɔ. Kɛ wain tsei lɛ tsɔ hei ni mli edɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ Baai lɛ shãa ni hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, yitso lɛ feɔ bibioo kwraa.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests every year even though I plant the exact same crop on it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ moŋ?

english: Planting the exact same crop in the same spot season after season drains specific soil nutrients and allows pests to build up in the dirt. Rotating your crops—like planting cowpeas or groundnuts after maize—helps restore nutrients back into the soil naturally.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ aba shi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Oŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛbaatsake, tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni ooodu yɛ ŋmãa sɛɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Too many shoots, called suckers, compete directly with the main plant for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Removing extra suckers and keeping only one or two strong ones allows the mother plant to produce a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso ni shwereɔ fe nine, ni atsɛɔ lɛ shoots lɛ kɛ tso ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajie ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha fɔlɔ tso lɛ awo ŋmeii wuji ni tsii babaoo.

english: Is it better for me to water my garden vegetables in the middle of the hot afternoon or early in the morning?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mibɔɔ lɛ mli nu yɛ shwane mli loo leebi maŋkpa?

english: Watering early in the morning is best because the cool soil absorbs water deeply before the hot sun turns it into vapor. Afternoon watering causes water to evaporate quickly and can heat up wet leaves, stressing the plants.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ lɛ shwieɔ nu lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ dani etsɔɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli shwane mli lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya ni ehaa baai ni efɔ lɛ mli dɔɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ haoɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I place fertilizer directly touching the stem of my maize or vegetable plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai ashishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer contains concentrated salts that draw moisture out of plant tissues. Placed directly against the main stem, it causes 'fertilizer burn' that can kill the plant; it should always be placed a few inches away in a ring or band.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yɛ ŋmei ni mli eyi obɔ ni gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe fãji amli. Kɛ akɛwo tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ masɛi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ehaa ‘ŋmei shãa’ ni baanyɛ agbe tso lɛ. Esa akɛ akɛto he ko ni kɛ ŋmɛlɛtswaa loo ŋmɛlɛtswaa lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo komɛi be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn black and mushy before they get a chance to ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called Blossom End Rot, caused by irregular soil moisture or lack of calcium in the plant. Keeping the soil evenly damp with mulch and adding wood ash or lime to the soil helps prevent the bottoms from rotting.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ Blossom End Rot, ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shiŋŋ loo calcium ni bɛ tsei amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni okɛ tso ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ akafite.

english: Young cocoa leaves burn easily under direct sunlight and lose too much water. Shade trees protect fragile seedlings from sun scorch and extreme heat until their root systems grow strong enough.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ ni nu babaoo fiteɔ amɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ dumɔwui ni waaa lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ kɛ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do plantain plants fall over easily during heavy rains and wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems and heavy stems filled with water. When soil gets saturated and soft during heavy rains, wind easily pushes over the top-heavy plants unless they are propped up with wooden stakes.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli tse ni nu eyi mli obɔ. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi ni efee blɛoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ atsɔ tsei ni yitsei ni mli wa lɛ amli oya. ja akɛ tso ko efi sɛɛ

english: Yellowing starting at the leaf tips usually means the maize plant is starving for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient needed for leaves to stay green and food production to occur.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ anaa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmei tso lɛ mli. Enɛɛmɛi ji niyenii ni he hia yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eha baai lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni amɛwo niyenii.

english: How can I tell if fall armyworms are destroying my young maize plants?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ fall cutworms lɛ miigbe mi-ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Fall armyworms leaves large ragged holes in the leaves and leave moist, sawdust-like droppings inside the central funnel (whorl) where young leaves emerge.
ga: Fall cutworms lɛ shĩɔ buji agboi ni ekpɔtɔ yɛ baai lɛ amli kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ yɛ funnel (ring) ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli he ni baai bibii lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the soil when it rains too heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Excess water trapped in heavy soil cuts off oxygen to cassava roots, causing root suffocation and allowing fungal rot organisms to thrive and decay the tubers.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni ekpɛtɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii mli lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ daa ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves toward sunlight for better photosynthesis, while keeping the leaves off damp soil where fungal diseases breed.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã kɛya hulu la lɛ he koni amɛná fotosintɛsis ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ, ni ji he ni ŋmeii fɔɔ yɛ lɛ he.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts add nitrogen back into the depleted soil through their roots, restoring fertility naturally for the next season's crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts kɛ nitrogen kuɔ sɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni faaa lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Koni akɛ adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ aba ekoŋŋ kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How does spreading dry grass on top of my soil help my crops during dry periods?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hɔmɔ be mli?

english: Dry grass acts as mulch, blocking hot sunlight from baking the bare soil. This keeps moisture from evaporating quickly and keeps the roots cool.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ mulch. Etsiɔ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni egbiɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haaa nu ni hoɔ oya lɛ aya, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ.

english: Why do my plants grow thin and produce tiny harvests when I plant seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Crops planted too tightly compete with each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, causing all plants to starve and yield smaller fruits.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ waa tsɔ lɛ kɛ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Ehaa hɔmɔ yeɔ tsei fɛɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii bibii.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers before setting fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani ewo yibii lɛ?

english: Extreme daytime heat, dry soil, or a lack of specific nutrients like phosphorus causes stress in tomato plants, forcing them to shed blossoms instead of growing tomatoes.
ga: Gbi mli dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii pɔtɛɛ tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei anɔ. Enɛ haa ehe bahiaa ni tomato tsei lɛ afɔ fɔfɔi moŋ fe ni amɛaakwɛ tomato.

english: When maize leaves turn yellow starting at the tip and moving down the middle vein, it means the soil is short on nitrogen. The crop is pulling nitrogen out of its older leaves at the bottom to send food up to the young, growing top leaves.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ejeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baa lɛ naa kɛyaa shishigbɛ kɛyaa shishigbɛ. Etsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ miigba nitrogen kɛmiijɛ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛ niyenii aha baai bibii ni miida yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why does my plantain crop yield much smaller bunches if I leave all the young shoots growing around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii babaoo kɛji mishi ŋmeii bibii ni bɔle tso lɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: All the shoots (suckers) growing around a plantain mother plant share the same root system and food supply. If you leave too many suckers, they steal water and nutrients from the mother plant, leaving her with too little energy to produce a large bunch.
ga: Tsoi (tsoji) fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ Mae Klai tsei lɛ ahe lɛ kɛ shishifã gbɛjianɔtoo kɛ niyenii jɛɛhe kome tsuɔ nii. Kɛji oshi ŋmeii babaoo lɛ Ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, hewalɛ fioo pɛ eyɔɔ ni ekɛbaafee kui wuji.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize crop roll up tightly like green pencils during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ pensil eŋɔli yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up tight to protect themselves from losing water through evaporation in intense heat. By reducing the leaf surface exposed to the hot sun, the plant conserves water until cooler evening temperatures arrive.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa baai shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ koni nu akafite yɛ la ni shwieɔ shi yɛ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. Kɛtsɔ baai ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe lɛ anɔ lɛ ni abaajie lɛ nɔ. Tsei lɛ hiɛɔ nu mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow so much bigger when I give the vines wooden stakes to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ daraa babaoo waa beni mikɛ wain tso ha amɛ koni amɛkwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make the food that expands the underground tuber. Staking lifts the leafy vines off the ground so every leaf catches maximum sunlight, creating more energy to feed a bigger yam.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking woɔ wain tsei ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni baa fɛɛ baa aná hulu la ni fe fɛɛ. Enɛ haa anáa hewalɛ babaoo ni akɛduɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are my pepper plant leaves curling upward and getting crinkled instead of spreading wide?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã babaoo lɛ?

english: Upward curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking sap from the undersides of young leaves. As the damaged leaves continue to grow, the wounded sap channels cause them to twist and warp.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. yɛ be mli ni baai ni efite lɛ yaa nɔ edaa lɛ. Sap channels ni pila lɛ haa baai lɛ tsɔɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ srɔtoi.

english: Tomato flowers drop without forming fruit when air temperatures get too hot or the plants get stressed by irregular watering. Extreme heat damages the flower pollen, preventing proper pollination so the flower simply dies and falls off.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Aloo tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baafite pollen lɛ. Ehaa enyɛɛɛ ekɛ fɔfɔii awo mli No sɛɛ lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ gboiɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi.

english: Why did my cowpea crop grow lots of lush leaves but very few pods after I put chemical fertilizer on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpeas lɛ hiɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi pods fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli beni mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ efata he sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas make their own nitrogen in the soil through their roots. Adding high-nitrogen fertilizer tricks the plant into using all its energy to build tall, soft green leaves instead of switching to flowering and pod building.
ga: Cowpeas lɛ feɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Nitrogen ni fa babaoo ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ lakaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kakadaji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsake ni efee fɔfɔi ni efee pods lɛ

english: Why do young cocoa trees turn brown and dry up when planted in open, sunny fields without cover trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hei ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ yɛ ni tsei bɛ hulutsoo be lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft, sensitive leaves that scorch under strong, direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain beside young cocoa acts like an umbrella, shielding delicate leaves from heat while keeping moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli tɛ̃ɛ. Shade tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo bibii ahe lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta. Buu baai bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots go soft and rot under the ground when heavy rains stay on the farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ shishi be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo nɛ lɛ?

english: Roots need air inside the soil to stay alive. When heavy rain stays stagnant on your farm, it pushes all the air out of the soil spaces, causing living cassava roots to suffocate, die, and attract rotting microbes.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he hiaa shishifãi yɛ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ yaa nɔ ehaa ais feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ. Ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmei shishifãi ni hiɛ ka lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛgboiɔ, ni amɛgbalaa nibii bibii ni fiteɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops stop growing and look weak when weeds grow tall right beside their roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ beni jwɛi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive roots that steal water, fertilizer, and soil food before your crops can reach them. Removing weeds leaves all the food in the ground exclusively for your crops to drink and grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baashɛ. Jwɛi ni agbeɔ lɛ haa niyenii fɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni onibii lɛ anu ni amɛdara waa.

english: Is it dangerous if the liquid from my knapsack sprayer leaks onto my back while I am spraying my farm?
ga: Ani eyɛ oshara kɛji nu ni jɛ misɛɛgbɛ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ lɛ mli lɛ ho kɛba misɛɛ be mli ni mikɛshwieɔ nii anɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yes, farm chemicals can easily soak through your shirt and absorb into your skin, causing rashes, poisoning, or long-term health problems. Always repair leaking equipment immediately and wear protective gear like water-resistant clothing.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ abote atadei amli ni ebote hewolo lɛ mli oya. Ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai, tsofa fɔŋ, loo helatsamɔ mli naagbai ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ baa. Saamɔ nibii ni hoɔ nu lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ be fɛɛ be ni owo nibii ni buɔ mɔ he, tamɔ atadei ni nu nyɛɛɛ abote mli.

english: Why did the chemical I sprayed to kill weeds end up destroying my growing maize crop as well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni mikɛshwieɔ mijwɛi lɛ anɔ koni mikɛgbe mijwɛi lɛ miifite mi-abele ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Some weedkillers are non-selective, meaning they kill any green plant they touch. You must use selective herbicides made specifically for maize, or use a shield on your nozzle to prevent the chemical from touching crop leaves.
ga: Tsofai komɛi ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ halaaa mɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛbaagbe tsei eŋɔli fɛɛ ni amɛkɛbaakpe lɛ. Esa akɛ okɛ tsofa pɔtɛɛ ko ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni afee aha ŋmãa pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ atsu nii. Aloo okɛ shield ni yɔɔ nozzle lɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii koni tsofai akashɛ tso baai ahe.

english: Why does my harvested maize turn moldy and spoil when stored inside bags in my shed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikpaa lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efiteɔ kɛ akɛto kotokui amli yɛ mi-shĩa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize rots when it is bagged before being fully dried, or if water leaks into the storage area. High moisture allows fungi and mold to grow fast, which ruins the grain and makes it unsafe to eat.
ga: Abɛi baagbo kɛji akɛ awo kotoku mli dani egbi kwraa. aloo kɛji nu ho kɛtee he ni akɛ nibii lɛ toɔ lɛ mli Fɛ̃i ni mli wa lɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ yaa hiɛ oya. Enɛ baafite ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ ni ebaaha amɛfee nɔ ni esaaa akɛ ayeɔ.

english: How do I know the exact time my yam is mature enough to be dug out of the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-sweet potato lɛ da bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Yam is ready for harvest when the leaves and vines on top of the soil stop growing, turn yellow, and begin to dry up naturally. Digging too early results in watery tubers that spoil quickly.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kpa kwɛ̃mɔ. etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔi ŋmɔlɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa Kɛ́ atsa oya tsɔ lɛ, no haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ nu oya.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle strong, direct sunlight because their roots and leaves are delicate. Planting temporary shade trees like plantains protects them from sunburn and keeps the soil moist until the cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, eshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ waaa. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ.

english: What happens if I put three or four maize seeds in one small planting hole instead of spacing them?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii etɛ loo ejwɛ wo ŋmãa bu bibioo ko mli? Bu kome moŋ fe ni amɛaajɛ amɛhe

english: Placing too many seeds together causes the plants to fight with each other for food, water, and sunlight. This results in weak, thin stalks that produce small cobs or no grains at all.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui babaoo fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe abɔi niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ ahe tseee ni egbɔjɔ, ni no haa tsei bibii baa. loo dumɔwui ko kwraa bɛ mli

english: Why do my tomato leaves drop and wilt during the hot afternoon even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ amɛdaraaa moŋ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: In intense midday sun, tomato leaves lose water faster through evaporation than the roots can suck up from the soil. As long as the soil has water, the plants usually recover in the cool evening.
ga: Yɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shishi yɛ shwane mli lɛ Tomato baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ nu lɛ Tsei hu sumɔɔ ni amɛhe ajɔ amɛ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants turning yellow and dropping off early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tsei ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi oya lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen nutrients in the soil, is receiving too much water around its roots, or is being attacked by tiny pests under the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nu babaoo ni bɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe loo tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ tutuaa amɛ.

english: Why does my cassava crop grow very tall with many leaves but gives me very small tubers beneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ tuber bibioo ko yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer makes cassava focus all its energy on building leafy green top-growth. To get big tubers, the plant needs potassium-rich soil or specialized fertilizers.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo haa ŋmei lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa shweremɔ ni eeefee yɛ baai eŋɔli lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni potassium eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ he miihia tso lɛ koni ekɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Can I apply chemical fertilizer directly against the stem of my young crop plants?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ awo mitsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ?

english: No, putting chemical fertilizer directly against the plant stem can burn and kill the plant. Fertilizer should be placed in a small ring or hole a few inches away from the stem so the roots can draw it safely.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ ashã ni egbo. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmeii bibii amli. Aloo bu lɛ kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko. Enɛ baaha anyɛ ajie shishifãi lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: A greenhouse is a covered structure made of clear plastic or glass that protects crops from extreme heat, heavy rain, pests, and diseases. It creates a controlled environment where plants like tomatoes and peppers can grow faster, stay healthy, and produce higher yields all year round.
ga: Greenhouse ji tsu ko ni akɛ plastic loo glase ni mli tse fee ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kooloi kɛ helai ahe, ni ehaa shihilɛ ko ni akudɔɔ ni tsei tamɔ tomato kɛ pepper baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ mli. baanyɛ adara oya Hiɛ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ewo yibii babaoo yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ

english: I heard people talking about using net structures on farms; how does putting a net over my crops help them grow?
ga: Minu ni mɛi miiwie trellis tsɔnei ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ he. Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ tsɔne mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa?

english: Net structures, often called shade net houses, block strong sunlight, heavy winds, and large insect pests while allowing air and rain to pass through. This keeps delicate crops like vegetables cooler and safe from damage without needing heavy chemical spraying.
ga: Trellis tsũ, ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ lɛ trellis shia lɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni naa wa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa, kɛ kooloi wuji ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ tsɔɔ mli. Ehaa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ aduawai lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe ejɔɔɔ kɛjɛɔ nɔ ni efiteɔ lɛ he ni tsofai ni tsii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Heavy rains always ruin my tomato flowers and spoil the fruits; is there a farming method that protects crops from too much rainfall?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ gbeɔ mitato fɔfɔi lɛ ni efiteɔ aduawai lɛ. Ani okwaayeli gbɛi komɛi yɛ ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ he?

english: Growing crops inside plastic greenhouses shields them from direct, heavy rainfall that washes away flower blossoms and spreads fungal diseases. The roof keeps water off the leaves while drip lines feed water safely to the soil.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ plastic tsũi amli lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa tɛ̃ɛ he. ni shwieɔ fɔfɔii anɔ ni egbɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai eshwaa. Kpoji lɛ haa nu hoɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ anɔ. yɛ be mli ni tsɔne ni hoɔ nu lɛ haa nu lɛ yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shweshweeshwe.

english: How do protected structures keep insects away from my vegetables without using too much chemical spray?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni nɔ ko ni abuɔ he lɛ aha kooloi akabɛŋkɛ mi-aduawai lɛ ahe ni akɛ tsofai babaoo ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Structures like net houses physically block insects from reaching the crops to lay eggs or feed. Because pests cannot easily get inside, plants stay healthier, and you do not need to buy or apply as many expensive chemical sprays.
ga: Gbɛjianɔtoi tamɔ trellis tsũi tsiɔ kooloi anaa koni amɛkabote ŋmɔshi nibii amli koni amɛwo amɛwui loo amɛye niyenii. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai nyɛŋ abote mli mlɛo. No hewɔ lɛ tso lɛ yɛ hewalɛ fe tsutsu lɛ. Ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohé loo okɛ tsofai ni jara wa babaoo atsu nii.

english: Why do my vegetables wither so quickly during the hot dry season, and how can modern farming methods prevent this?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ okwaayeli gbɛ̀i baanyɛ atsĩ enɛ naa?

english: Vegetables wither in the dry season because intense sunlight and low soil moisture make plants lose water faster than their roots can drink. Covered farming methods like greenhouses or shade nets reduce direct heat and retain moisture, keeping crops green and active.
ga: Aduawai shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ fioo lɛ haa tsei lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ okwaayeli he nii tamɔ greenhouses loo shade nets haa dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baa shi ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Ha ŋmɔshi nibii afee eŋɔli ni amɛhiɛ ahi amɛhe nɔ.

english: Is it possible for me to harvest vegetables like tomatoes all year round instead of waiting for the rainy season?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ makpa aduawai tamɔ tomato afi muu lɛ fɛɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mamɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ?

english: Yes, by using protected structures like greenhouses combined with drip irrigation, you control the water, sun, and nutrients your crops receive. This allows you to grow and harvest crops continuously regardless of the weather season.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛtsɔ nɔ ko ni abuɔ he tamɔ greenhouse ni akɛ nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ nu mli lɛ fataa he lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Obaanyɛ okudɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni otsei lɛ náa lɛ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ oyaa nɔ oduɔ nii ni okpaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli shihilɛi kɔɔɔ he eko.

english: Do crops grown under covered farm structures require more water or less water than crops in open fields?
ga: Ani tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋtayaai ashishi lɛ biɔ nu babaoo loo fioo fe tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni mli tse lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Crops under covered structures usually need less water because the cover shades the soil from direct sunlight, greatly reducing evaporation. When combined with drip irrigation, water goes straight to the roots with very little waste.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ tsɔne ni akɛ nɔ ko eha nɔ lɛ shishi lɛ biɔ nu fioo ejaakɛ nɔ ni akɛha nɔ lɛ buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Enɛ haa la ni hoɔ lɛ baa shi waa. Kɛ akɛ drip irrigation fata he Nu lɛ hoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ anɔ ni jwɛi fioo ko pɛ shwieɔ nɔ.

english: Will using modern structures like greenhouses produce a higher yield from a small plot of land compared to open-field farming?
ga: Kɛ akɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ nibii, tamɔ tsũi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha aná shika babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔji bibii anɔ. Ani akɛtoɔ ŋmɔ mli okwaayeli he?

english: Yes, protected environments shield crops from harsh weather and pests, allowing plants to grow taller, stay healthy longer, and produce significantly more fruit per square meter than traditional open-field farming.
ga: Hɛɛ, shihilɛ ni abuɔ he lɛ buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa babaoo Enáa hewalɛ kpakpa be kakadaŋŋ. ni ewoɔ aduawai babaoo kwraa yɛ sqɛɛ mita kome mli fe blema ŋmɔ mli okwaayeli ni agbele naa lɛ.

english: Can I grow any crop inside a greenhouse or net house, or are there specific crops that perform best in them?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ. Ani ebaanyɛ ehi ŋmɔ mli loo ŋmɔ mli? Aloo ani tsei komɛi yɛ ni woɔ yibii ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ amɛteŋ?

english: High-value vegetables like tomatoes, sweet peppers, cucumbers, and leafy greens perform best inside greenhouses and net houses. Field crops like maize, cassava, or cocoa need too much space or height and are better suited for open fields.
ga: Aduawai ni jara wa waa tamɔ tomato, bell peppers, kukumba kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔji kɛ ŋmɔji amli. Gbɛjegbɛ nɔ nibii tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa loo kookoo biɔ he ko loo ŋwɛi ŋta babaoo. ni ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔji ni mli tse.

english: How do I know which new farming method or technology is best suited for my land and the crops I want to plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male okwaayeli gbɛ loo ŋaa hee ni sa jogbaŋŋ kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni misumɔɔ ni madu lɛ?

english: Agricultural extension officers can help assess your soil, water availability, budget, and local market demand. They provide guidance on whether open-field improvements, shade nets, or full greenhouses will give you the best return on your investment.
ga: Okwaayeli he nitsulɔi baanyɛ aye abua ni akwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. nu ni yɔɔ, shika ni akɛbaatsu nii, kɛ maŋ lɛ mli jarayeli he hiamɔ nii Amɛbaawo ŋaa yɛ kɛji akɛ he ko ni agbele, shade net loo greenhouse muu lɛ fɛɛ ni asaa lɛ baaha shika ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ aná sɛɛnamɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ.

english: Why are my crops failing even though I planted them in the same month I always do every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ yɛ nyɔŋ ni miduɔ daa afi lɛ nɔŋŋ mli moŋ?

english: Rainfall patterns across Ghana have become unpredictable due to changing weather cycles. Planting strictly by traditional calendar months can cause seeds to dry out if the rains arrive late or stop suddenly, so it is better to wait until the soil stays consistently moist before planting.
ga: Anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ Ghana fɛɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ahewɔ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ kusum kalanda nyɔŋ lɛ naa lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛ loo ekpa trukaa. No hewɔ lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ dani odu.

english: If the rainy season starts late this year, should I still plant my usual maize seeds or switch to something else?
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ lɛ je shishi yɛ afi nɛɛ naagbee Ani esa akɛ madu ŋmãa bɔ ni sa loo matsake kɛya nɔ kroko nɔ?

english: When rains start late, standard maize varieties may not have enough time to mature before the rain stops. Switching to early-maturing or short-duration seed varieties ensures your crops mature quickly before the dry spell begins.
ga: Be ni nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ Ekolɛ Standard corn henɔi lɛ bɛ be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ̃ dani nugbɔ lɛ akpa. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee dumɔwui srɔtoi ni kwɛ̃ɔ mra loo ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ daa oya dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi.

english: What can I cover my soil with to keep it from drying out so quickly when the sun is very hot?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mawo mli koni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akagbi oya?

english: Covering the soil around your crops with dry grass, straw, or leaves—a practice called mulching—acts as a protective shield against the sun, slowing down water evaporation and keeping the root area cool and moist.
ga: Mulching ni bɔleɔ he lɛ Akɛ jwɛi, jwɛi, loo baai duɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii akɛ tsɔne ni tsiɔ hulu la naa. Ha nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. kɛ shishifã lɛ he ni aaaha afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ

english: How do I know if my soil actually has enough water in it for my seeds to sprout properly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha midumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Grab a handful of soil from a few inches deep and squeeze it in your palm. If it forms a ball that holds together without dripping water, the soil has the right amount of moisture for planting.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni ji inchi fioo ko ni okɛmimɔ onine mli. Kɛji akɛ etamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ko ni yɔɔ kokroo ni kpɛtɛɔ he ni nu shwieee shi. Etsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha dumɔwui.

english: How does digging a small pit or farm pond on my land help my crops when the rain pauses?
ga: Bu bibioo ko ni mifoɔ Aloo te nubu ko ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa?

english: A small farm pond captures rainwater runoff during heavy downpours so it doesn't wash away. You can then use this trapped water to manually water your crops during dry weeks when the rain stops unexpectedly.
ga: ŋshɔ bibioo Etsuɔ nii kɛtoɔ nugbɔ nu ni hoɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ekɛ ehe wooo mli. No sɛɛ lɛ obaanyɛ okɛ nu ni emɔ mli nɛɛ atsu nii ni okɛ onine awo onibii amli nu yɛ otsii ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ amli beni nugbɔ lɛ kpaɔ trukaa lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my plants are rolling up their leaves because of lack of water or because of a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mitso lɛ miifo baai lɛ yɛ nu ni bɛ hewɔ loo hela emɔ lɛ?

english: When crops like maize lack water, their leaves roll tightly upward during the hottest hours of the day to save moisture and unfold again in the cooler evening. Disease usually causes permanent discoloration, spots, or wilting that does not change with the heat of the day.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa bɛ nu lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ gbi lɛ mli bei ni mli edɔ waa lɛ amli. koni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni ebaajie ehe kpo ekoŋŋ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, hela lɛ haa mɔ he su tsakeɔ daa. Ayɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni egbɔjɔ ni kɛ gbi lɛ mli latsaa lɛ tsakeee.

english: Which food crops grow best in areas where rain is very small and hard to predict?
ga: Mɛɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ fioo ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ?

english: Crops like sorghum, millet, cassava, and cowpeas have deep root systems or tough leaves that allow them to draw water from deep underground and survive long periods without rain much better than crops like maize or vegetables.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, ŋmãa, kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ loo baai ni mli wa ni haa amɛgbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni mli kwɔ ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ fe nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai.

english: Why do my crops stop growing and turn yellow after a sudden heavy rainfall followed by intense hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpaɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Heavy rain can flood the ground and suffocate plant roots by cutting off oxygen. When the hot sun returns immediately after, the damaged roots cannot absorb nutrients from the soil, causing the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ atsɔ nu afua ni eha tsei shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ baafo mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛ hulu ni tsoɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba amrɔ nɔŋŋ Shishifãi ni efite lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetables early in the morning or in the afternoon when the sun is hottest?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ nu leebi loo shwane be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning gives roots plenty of time to absorb water before heat sets in. Afternoon watering causes most of the water to evaporate into the hot air before the roots can take it up.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli leebi lɛ haa amɛnáa be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaaŋɔ nu dani hulutsoo be lɛ baa, ni kɛ́ afɔ amɛ nu shwane lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ fa babaoo atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu.

english: If I get water from a nearby dam or river during the dry season, how should I apply it to my crops?
ga: Kɛji minine shɛ nu nɔ kɛjɛ faa loo faa ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli Te esa akɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Pour water directly at the base of the plant around the roots rather than spraying it over the leaves. Watering the leaves directly under hot sun can cause leaf burn and encourage fungal diseases.
ga: Okɛ nu lɛ awo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ, yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe, moŋ fe ni oookɛwo baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ afɔ baai lɛ anɔ nu yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã baai lɛ ni ewo tsɛŋemɔ hela he hewalɛ.

english: Why are there tiny holes in my young maize leaves and light green dust inside the plant tops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni sũ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tso lɛ yiteŋgbɛ.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a very common pest in Ghana that feeds on young maize foliage. Applying recommended organic neem extracts or approved target insecticides early in the morning before heat rises will help control them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmei, ni ji ŋmei ko ni afɔɔ namɔ waa yɛ Ghana ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ organic neem extract ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ loo tsofa ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ tsu nii leebi dani hulutsoo be lɛ aba lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: Tomato flowers usually drop off when the soil suffers from extreme dryness or excessive afternoon heat. Keeping the soil consistently moist through morning watering and applying dry grass mulch around the base protects the roots and preserves the flowers.
