ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi waa loo yɛ shwane mli latsaa be mli. Ni aaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi kɛ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛbaabɔle he lɛ nɔ. Shishitoo lɛ baaye abua ni ebu shishifãi lɛ ahe ni ekwɛ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my growing maize plants turn yellow and dry up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi lɛ?

english: Yellowing of the lower leaves indicates that the plant lacks nitrogen, which is essential for green leaf growth. Applying balanced NPK or urea fertilizer around the base when the plant reaches knee height gives it the nutrients it needs to recover.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen, ni he hiaa koni baa lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ. Kɛ NPK loo urea ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja atsu nii yɛ tso lɛ he. base beni tso lɛ shɛɔ enaji ahe Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do extension officers recommend planting beans or groundnuts on my farm after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni extension agent lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like beans, groundnuts, and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil. Planting them restores natural soil fertility that heavy crops like maize consume.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei, ŋmei, kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ adumɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmãa yeɔ lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I spread dry grass around the roots of my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbɛ jwɛi ni egbi mashwã mi-pepper tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Spreading dry grass, known as mulching, stops sunlight from evaporating soil moisture during hot days, keeps root zones cool, and slows down weed growth, allowing pepper plants to grow steadily.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ehaa hulu la lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ. ni eha jwɛi ni shwereɔ lɛ aba shi Ehaa pepper tso lɛ daa be fɛɛ be.

english: How do I know the exact right time to sow my seeds when the rainy season starts late?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: You should wait until the soil is thoroughly wet to about a hand-depth level after steady rain, rather than planting after a single short drizzle, which can trick seeds into germinating only to wither from hot ground.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ kwraa kɛyashɛ onine mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ sɛɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. shikome pɛ Enɛ baanyɛ alaka dumɔwui ni amɛkwɛ̃, shi amɛgboɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my cassava tubers turning soft and rotting in the ground before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when trapped water starves them of oxygen, usually during heavy rainfall in flat, hard soil. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away naturally.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ni emɔ mli lɛ ha kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ faaa. Bei pii lɛ, yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in direct sunlight to create food for the plant. Staking the vines ensures leaves get full light, which directly encourages large tuber growth under the ground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha tso lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ wain tso lɛ wo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yibii lɛ aje kpo yɛ la fɛɛ mli. Enɛ woɔ bulbous tsei lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and dry out easily under strong afternoon sun. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain beside young cocoa provides living umbrellas that shield seedlings until they are old enough to handle sunlight.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la.

english: Why do my orange tree fruits turn yellow and drop off early when they are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ eji gbekɛbii lɛ?

english: Premature fruit drop in citrus is often caused by fruit fly attacks or sudden swings between dry soil and heavy rain. Keeping soil moisture steady and placing simple fruit-fly traps in the branches prevents early fruit loss.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ citrus aduawai ni shwieɔ shi oya lɛ baa ji aduawai amli ŋmeii ni shwieɔ mɔ loo tsakemɔi ni baa trukaa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ teŋ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni aaakwɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ tso yibii amli ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni akɛwoɔ tsei aniji anɔ lɛ baaye abua ni tso yibii lɛ akafite mra.

english: Officer, how do I know the right time to start planting my crops when the rainy season begins?
ga: Official Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu tsei kɛji nugbɔ be lɛ bashɛ?

english: You should wait until the first two or three heavy rains have thoroughly soaked the ground before planting. Planting immediately after a light, early shower can cause your seeds to sprout and then dry up if the rain stops for several days.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔi fioo ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani okɛdu. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ leebi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa gbii babaoo.

english: Can I mix river sand or beach sand into my soil to help my young nursery plants grow better?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ faa mli ŋã loo ŋshɔnaa ŋã afutu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eye ebua midumɔwui lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ?

english: River sand is good for nursery beds because it loosens heavy soil so water passes through easily and roots can breathe. However, beach sand should never be used because the salt in it will burn your seeds and kill them.
ga: Faa mli ŋã hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ejaakɛ ehaa shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni nu atsɔ mli oya ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ amu. Shi kɛlɛ, esaaa akɛ akɛ ŋshɔnaa ŋã tsuɔ nii. Ejaakɛ ngo ni yɔɔ ŋã lɛ mli lɛ baaha wui lɛ ashã ni amɛgboi.

english: Sandy soil has large spaces between its grains, which allows water to drain away very fast rather than staying near the roots. To fix this, you need to mix organic manure or compost into the soil to help it hold onto moisture longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ yɛ gbɛjegbɛi wuji yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ. Enɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya waa. yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeebɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ Bɔni afee ni otsu naagba nɛɛ he nii Ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afutu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eye ebua ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How can I test my land to see if water drains through the soil easily before I plant?
ga: Ani manyɛ maka mishikpɔŋ lɛ makwɛ kɛji nu hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mlɛo dani madu nii?

english: You can dig a small hole about a foot deep, fill it with water, and watch how fast it sinks. If the water stays standing in the hole for many hours, the soil drains poorly and may rot your crop roots during heavy rains.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsa bu bibioo ko ni mli kwɔ aaafee ninetalɔ kome, ni okɛ nu awo mli, ni okwɛ bɔ ni efoɔ oya. Kɛji nu hi bu lɛ mli ŋmɛlɛtswai babaoo Shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieŋ nu jogbaŋŋ ni ebaanyɛ eha otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ agbo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why is it dangerous for my crops if water collects and stays standing around their stems after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ nu bua ehe naa ni ehi shi yɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui lɛ? Trunk yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ?

english: Crop roots need to breathe air just like human beings do. When water stays trapped around the stems for too long, it drowns the roots, stops them from taking in food, and causes root rot disease.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, ehe miihia ni tsei shishifãi amu kɔɔyɔɔ. Kɛ́ nu hi tso lɛ he be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli, ni no haaa amɛye nii. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ shishifãi ni fiteɔ hela aba

english: How often should I water my young nursery plants if the soil drains water very fast?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mawo mi dumɔwui lɛ nu kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu hoɔ oya waa?

english: When soil drains quickly, you should water your young plants gently twice a day—once early in the morning before the sun gets hot, and once in the late afternoon. This keeps the soil constantly moist without washing the seeds away.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu hoɔ oya Esa akɛ Oha tsei bibii lɛ nu blɛoo. shii enyɔ daa gbi Klɛŋklɛŋ nɔ ni esa akɛ afee leebi dani hulu lɛ adɔ. Ni agbɛnɛ hu yɛ shwane mli Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be ni ekɛ dumɔwui lɛ efɔɔɔ.

english: What basic materials do I need to gather before I start making a seed nursery bed?
ga: Mɛɛ shishijee nibii ehe hiaa ni mabua naa dani mabɔi dumɔwui akwɛmɔ?

english: To start a nursery bed, you need good fertile soil mixed with compost or well-rotted manure, fine sand to improve drainage, clean water, and dry grass or palm fronds to shade the tender young seedlings from strong sunlight.
ga: Kɛji oooje gbekɛbii askul saatso shishi Ohe miihia shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni baa nii ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ efutu mli. Ŋã ni akɛ ŋã kpakpa ewo mli koni nu lɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ, nu ni mli tse, kɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo tsei ahe tsei ni haa dumɔwui bibii lɛ shwieɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do small seeds struggle to sprout if the top layer of soil becomes hard after watering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui bibii lɛ No hewɔ lɛ ebɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ fee ais yɛ nu ni awo lɛ sɛɛ?

english: When heavy clay soil dries out, it forms a hard crust that young, delicate shoots cannot push through. Mixing sand or organic matter into the topsoil keeps it loose so tiny seedlings can easily emerge into the light.
ga: Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa ni akɛ shikpɔŋ sũ fee lɛ gĩ lɛ Efeɔ ŋmei ni wa ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ nyɛŋ abote mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋã loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli futu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni dumɔwui bibii anyɛ ahi shi. Ejeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ la mli oya

english: Why is it better for me to plant my seeds in straight line rows instead of scattering them by hand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ moŋ fe ni mikɛ nine baadu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Planting in straight rows gives each plant enough space to get light and nutrients, makes it easy to walk between crops to remove weeds, and helps you know exactly how many plants are on your farm.
ga: Tso ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa koni enyɛ ená la kɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ oooya tsei lɛ ateŋ koni ojie jwɛi lɛ. Ni eyeɔ ebua bo ni oleɔ tsei enyiɛ pɔtɛɛ ni oyɔɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Do plant roots need air inside the soil to survive, or do they only need water?
ga: Ani kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi loo nu kɛkɛ he miihia amɛ?

english: Roots need both air and water to stay healthy. Loose soil that lets excess water pass through leaves tiny air pockets that roots use to take in oxygen, which gives the plant energy to grow strong.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nu fɛɛ he miihia shishifãi koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ mli. Enɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii aba. Akɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛdara waa.

english: Can I plant food crops like maize on the same field where I just planted my young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii, tamɔ ŋmãa, yɛ shikpɔŋ ni midu kookoo tsei bibii yɛ nɔ amrɔ nɛɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, planting maize alongside young cocoa trees is a great practice. It gives you quick food and income while the cocoa is still young, and the tall maize plants provide temporary shade to protect young cocoa seedlings.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ cacao tsei bibii ahe lɛ ji nifeemɔ kpakpa. Ehaa onine shɛɔ niyenii kɛ shika nɔ oya be mli ni kookoo lɛ ji gbekɛ lolo lɛ. Ni ŋmãa tsei kakadaji haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko koni ebu kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe.

english: At what point should I stop growing maize among my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ makpa ŋmãa dumɔ yɛ kookoo tsei lɛ ateŋ?

english: You should stop growing maize after 2 to 3 years, once the cocoa trees start growing bigger and expanding their branches. At that stage, maize will compete with cocoa for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water.
ga: Esa akɛ okpa ŋmãa dumɔ yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 sɛɛ, beni kookoo tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa ni amɛwoɔ niji babaoo lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, Abɛi kɛ kookoo yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings need shade plants or trees over them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni tsei loo tsei aha mi-kookoo tso bibioo lɛ he ŋmɔlɔ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and easily damaged by harsh sunlight. Shade plants act like umbrellas, keeping the soil moist and protecting young seedlings from drying out in direct heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa, ni hulu la ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ amɛ oya. Shade tsei tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ tsei bibii ahe koni amɛkagbi yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ mli.

english: Will having too much bush or shade trees hurt my cocoa farm?
ga: Ani jwɛi loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ babaoo ni miyɔɔ lɛ baaye mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ awui?

english: Yes, while young cocoa needs shade, thick bush or overly dense shade trees block necessary sunlight, which cocoa needs to produce food, grow strong trunks, and bear pods.
ga: Hɛɛ, yɛ be mli ni kookoo bibioo he hiaa hulutsoo. Tsei bibii loo tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be babaoo lɛ he miihia hulu la. ni kookoo he hiaa yɛ niyenii feemɔ mli Ekwɛ̃ɔ tsei ni wa ni ewoɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees turn brown and drop during the dry season when exposed to full sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛ́ hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Direct sunlight without shade dries out moisture from cocoa leaves faster than the roots can take up water from the soil, causing leaf burn and stress.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni hulutsoo bɛ mli lɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ kookoo baai lɛ amli lɛ agbi oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa baa lɛ shãa kɛ haomɔ.

english: How far apart should I space my cocoa trees when measuring my land for planting?
ga: Te esa akɛ mikɛ kookoo tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ahi tɛŋŋ beni misusuɔ he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees are typically spaced about 3 meters (10 feet) apart in straight rows. Proper spacing ensures each tree gets enough room, soil nutrients, and light to grow without overcrowding.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, akɛ kookoo tsei lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mitai 3 (naji 10) yɛ sɛɛgbɛ ni ja. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ. niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ekwɛ̃ ni ekɛ ehe ewooo mli tsɔ.

english: How can I mark out my land correctly so that my tree crops are neatly arranged?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makadi mishikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni mitsei lɛ ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: You can use a long rope marked at equal distances (like 3 meters) and wooden pegs to outline straight rows across your farm before digging planting holes.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ kpãa ni kɛlɛ ji ekome (nɔkwɛmɔnɔ mitai etɛ) kɛ tsei ni akɛtswaa amɛhe lɛ atsu nii ni okɛto amɛhe yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli dani otsa dumɔ bui lɛ.

english: How high do cocoa trees need to grow before they start producing fruit?
ga: Te esa akɛ cacao tso lɛ adara aha tɛŋŋ dani ebɔi yibiiwoo?

english: Cocoa trees usually grow to a height of about 1.5 to 2 meters before branching out into a canopy, which allows the tree to build enough strength to carry heavy cocoa pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo tsei lɛ daa kɛyashɛɔ mitai 1.5 kɛyashi 2 dani amɛwoɔ niji amli ni amɛfeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta. Enɛ haa tso lɛ naa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ.

english: Should I clear all the existing big trees on my land before I plant my crops?
ga: Ani esa akɛ majie tsei ni eda ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: No, it is best to leave a few scattered, beneficial shade trees on your land. Completely bare land leaves young crops exposed to strong winds and hot sun.
ga: Dabi, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshi tsei fioo komɛi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ efee efolo kwraa, ni eshiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ yeɔ amɛnɔ.

english: What happens if weeds and tall bushes grow too close to my young trees?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii ni kwɔlɔ lɛ kwɛ̃ ni ebɛŋkɛ mi tsei bibii lɛ tsɔ hu?

english: Tall weeds and bushes steal water, light, and soil nutrients from your young trees, and they can also harbor dangerous pests and plant diseases.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii ni kɛlɛ lɛ juɔ nu, la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ otsei bibii lɛ amli. Eji shihilɛhe hu kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ oshara kɛ tsei ahelai.

english: Why are the leaves on my rice plants turning yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-rice tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Rice leaves usually turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen nutrients or when stagnant water has stayed on the field for too long without fresh air. Adding a small amount of nitrogen fertilizer or draining excess water helps the leaves turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ bɛ. aloo be mli ni nu lɛ ehi shi yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmãa fioo ko fata he loo nu ni fa fe nine lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops curling up during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism. When the sun is too hot, the plant rolls its leaves inward to hide from the harsh direct light and reduce the amount of water escaping through its pores.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Kɛ hulu lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli koni amɛkɛ amɛhe akaje la ni tsoɔ waa ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni eha nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ aba shi

english: Why do my crops become tall, thin, and pale if I plant the seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛlɛ, eyɛ mlɛo, ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the growing plants shade each other from sunlight and their roots fight for the same limited nutrients in the soil. This forces them to stretch upward for light, making them weak.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ haa amɛhe feɔ hulu la. Ni amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa fioo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ nyɛ amɛnɔ koni amɛjaje amɛhe koni amɛná la lɛ. ha amɛgbɔjɔ

english: Why does my rice crop need so much water compared to my maize farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ he hiaa nu babaoo kɛ akɛto mi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Rice plants have shallow root systems and natural air channels in their stems that allow them to thrive in saturated, watery soil. Maize roots need oxygen from dry soil pockets and will rot if flooded for long periods.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli ni haa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ, ni amɛbaafite kɛji akɛ nu shwie amɛnɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: What makes the soil on one side of my farm dry out much faster than the other side after it rains?
ga: Mɛni haa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ fã kome lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya fe fã kroko lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Soil made of large sand particles cannot hold onto moisture and allows water to drain away quickly. Soil made of fine clay particles holds water tightly like a sponge, keeping the ground wet for days.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã bibii wuji yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ ahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli, ni ehaa nu lɛ hoɔ oya. Shikpɔŋ ni akɛ sũ bibii bibii fee lɛ ŋmɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ tamɔ sponji. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ gbii babaoo.

english: Why do my crops grow better when I plant them in straight lines instead of scattering seeds everywhere?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ moŋ fe ni magbɛ dumɔwui ashwã he fɛɛ he lɛ?

english: Planting in straight rows ensures every plant gets equal space, sunlight, and air. It also leaves clear pathways for you to remove weeds and apply fertilizer without crushing your young crops.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ náa he ko ni tamɔ amɛhe, hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ. Ehaa gbɛ ni yɔɔ faŋŋ hu ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ okɛ jwɛi awo mli ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli ni okɛ otsei bibii lɛ akumɔɔɔ.

english: Why is it important for me to remove weeds while my rice plants are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi lɛ be mli ni mitsei lɛ darako kwraa lolo lɛ?

english: Young crops grow slowly at first and cannot win against fast-growing weeds. Clearing weeds early ensures the young crops get all the fertilizer, soil food, and sunlight needed to establish strong stems.
ga: Tsei bibii daaa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛye jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ anɔ kunim. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tso bibioo lɛ naa ŋmɔshi nibii, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ hulu la fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ tso ni wa.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my rice so the grains do not fall off on the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa? No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ shwieee shikpɔŋ?

english: You should harvest when about 80 to 85 percent of the seed heads turn golden yellow while the lower stem remains slightly green. Waiting too long makes the grains dry out, brittle, and drop to the ground.
ga: Esa akɛ okpa be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ ayitsei lɛ aaafee oha mlijaa 80 kɛyashi 85 etsɔ shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ. yɛ be mli ni shishigbɛ tso lɛ kã he efee ŋmɔŋ fioo. Kɛ́ mɛ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi, amɛbaatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ, ni amɛgbee shikpɔŋ.

english: What causes the hulls on my harvested rice to be empty with no solid grain inside?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ feɔ efolo ni ŋmãa ni wa bɛ mli?

english: Empty rice grains happen when the crop suffers from severe drought, extreme heat, or pest damage while it is flowering. This stress stops the plant from filling the grain pods with starch.
ga: Nibii ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko baa kɛji tsei lɛ na hɔmɔ ni naa wa, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Nɛkɛ haomɔ nɛɛ tsiɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekakɛ starch awo dumɔwui lɛ amli.

english: Why do my crops dry up so fast when the Harmattan wind starts blowing in the northern region?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛ́ Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ je shishi etswa yɛ kooyigbɛ lɛ?

english: The Harmattan brings extremely dry air that sucks moisture directly out of plant leaves at a very fast rate. Even if the soil has some water, the roots cannot suck up water fast enough to match what the dry air takes from the leaves.
ga: Harmattan kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi waa ni gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli tɛ̃ɛ oya waa baa. Eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu fioo moŋ Shi shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu oya bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛjie kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi kɛjɛ baai lɛ amli.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn pale and yellow after I clear dense bush and plant immediately?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni mijie jwɛi ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ ni midu amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: When you clear thick bush, decaying organic matter temporarily locks up nitrogen in the soil. Giving the soil a short rest or adding manure restores available nitrogen so young crop leaves stay green and healthy.
ga: Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni egbo lɛ kɛ nitrogen toɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kukuoo ko. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha ejɔɔ ehe kuku Loo ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he lɛ baaye abua ni nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ. Koni baai bibii lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ

english: Why does heavy rain wash away the rich topsoil on my hilly farm land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii jogbaŋŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ gɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Unprotected soil on slopes gets swept away by fast-running rainwater. Planting crops in ridges along the slope's contour slows down the water and keeps rich topsoil and fertilizer right at the crop roots.
ga: Nugbɔ nu ni hoɔ oya lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ ni abuuu he ni yɔɔ gɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ. Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔi ni yɔɔ ŋshɔkpɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ fioo ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi kɛ sũ ni mli ewo ŋmɔshi nii lɛ hiɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my maize crops grow tall and thin with very small cobs when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Crowded crops fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough light and food to build strong stems and full cobs.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni eyi obɔ lɛ kɛ hulu la he akaŋ. shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ nu Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛná tsei akutsei ni wa kɛ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do my vegetable crops grow lots of leaves but refuse to produce fruit under big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ yɛ baai babaoo shi amɛwooo yibii yɛ tsei wuji ashishi lɛ?

english: Fruiting crops need direct sunlight to produce flowers and fruit. In deep shade, plants spend all their energy growing long stems and leaves searching for light instead of producing yield.
ga: Tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi kɛ yibii. Yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, tsei baafite amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ tsei kɛ baai kakadaji. Koni atao la yɛ yibiiwoo najiaŋ

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on land where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmeii yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ nɔ?

english: Maize consumes a lot of nitrogen from the soil. Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts trap nitrogen from the air and put it back into the earth, making the soil fertile for the next crop.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni baa nii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How does adding dried poultry manure help my cassava farm during dry spells?
ga: Te kooloi ashishifã ni egbi ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-cassava ŋmɔ lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Poultry manure acts like a sponge in the soil. It improves the soil's structure so it holds moisture longer, allowing cassava roots to survive hot, rainless periods.
ga: Kooloi afɔfɔi tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii lɛ feɔ fɛo koni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmei shishifãi ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my crop seedlings after the early rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe midumɔwui lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to steal water and nutrients instantly. Clearing them early prevents them from choking seedling roots and taking away the sunlight your crops need.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛju nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii yɛ fɛ̃i mli. Ni aaatsi mra Enɛ baatsi dumɔwu lɛ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsi tso lɛ hulu la ni he hiaa lɛ lɛ naa.

english: Why do worms attack my maize leaves more during a short drought in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii babaoo tutuaa mi-abele baa lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Warm, dry spells cause pest populations like fall armyworms to multiply quickly, while crops become weaker from thirst. Early farm checks help catch pests before they destroy leaves.
ga: Be ni mli edɔ, ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ haa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ fall armyworms lɛ ayibɔ yaa hiɛ oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii baagbɔjɔ yɛ kumai hewɔ. Okwaafoi lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni emɔɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui dani amɛfiteɔ baai lɛ.

english: Is it better to plant seeds saved from my last harvest or buy certified seeds for planting?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli loo aaahe dumɔwui ni awo he odase akɛ abaadu?

english: Saved seeds from hybrid crops lose vigor and disease resistance over time. Certified seeds are bred for uniform growth, pest resistance, and reliable yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ hewalɛ kɛ helai ahewalɛ baaje mli yɛ be ni sa mli. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ koni amɛdara daa. Pest ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ ni ekɛ yibii ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ baa

english: Why do my crop seedlings die shortly after sprouting when the top layer of soil forms a hard crust?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ dumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ? Mɛɛ be shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni wa?

english: A hard soil crust blocks oxygen from reaching the seed and physically traps fragile shoots beneath the surface. Lightly breaking the topsoil surface allows sprouts to break through safely.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli wa lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ naa, ni emɔɔ ŋmeii ni waaa lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛkpatamɔ fioo ko haa dumɔwui lɛ boteɔ mli shweshweeshwe.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to build leaves. Applying nitrogen-based fertilizer like Urea or NPK after a good rain helps the plants recover their healthy green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli tamɔ urea loo NPK wo mli yɛ nugbɔ kpakpa sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná su ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why do the new hybrid cocoa varieties yield pods much faster than the old cocoa trees on my father's farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei heei ni akɛfutu mli lɛ woɔ ŋmeii oya fe kookoo tsei momo ni yɔɔ mitsɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid cocoa trees are specially bred by scientists to mature quickly and resist local stress. Unlike older varieties that take up to five years to produce, hybrids start producing pods within two to three years.
ga: Jeŋ nilelɔi ekwɛ cacao tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ anɔ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛdara oya ni amɛte shi amɛwo he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ mli haomɔi. Enɛ yɛ srɔto yɛ tsofa momo ni he afii enumɔ ni akɛfee lɛ he. Hybrids baabɔi pods feemɔ yɛ afii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ mli.

english: Flower drop happens when pepper plants experience extreme heat or do not get enough water during flowering. Keeping the soil moist around the root area helps the flowers stay attached and form peppers.
ga: Blossom drop baa kɛji akɛ pepper tsei lɛ shɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa waa he loo amɛnáaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha ebɔle he lɛ shishifãi lɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ kpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot right on the branch before they get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, wet, and humid conditions. Pruning extra shade trees to let sunlight into the farm and clearing infected pods helps stop the rot from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni efɔ, kɛ hei ni edɔ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ babaoo lɛ afolɔmɔ koni hulu la abote ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni akpa ŋmeii ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the leaves in the center of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, destructive pests that hide in the center leaves of maize. Spraying recommended treatments early in the morning or late evening directly into the plant center stops them from destroying the growing crop.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni fiteɔ nii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ afɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekafite tsei ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do my mature plantain trees fall over easily whenever there is a strong wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui ni eda lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baa lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are often eaten and weakened underground by tiny pests called nematodes or stem borers. Propping heavy plants with bamboo sticks and planting clean, healthy suckers keeps the stand firm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii yeɔ plantain shishifãi ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo stem borers. Tsei ni tsii ni akɛ ŋmeii tsei toɔ he kɛ ŋmeii ni he tse ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdamɔ shi.

english: Why should I wait until the soil is wet from rain before putting fertilizer around my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs moisture to dissolve so plant roots can absorb it. Applying fertilizer on dry ground can burn the plant roots and cause the nutrients to evaporate into the air.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe miihia ni nu atsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni eha niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: Why does planting cowpeas together with my cassava help the cassava grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ mi-cassava lɛ du tsina ŋmei lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes, which means they naturally trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. As cowpeas grow, they share this natural fertilizer with the neighboring cassava plants.
ga: Cowpea ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmɔɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji tsina ŋmei kwɛ̃ lɛ Amɛjaa adebɔɔ mli ŋmei nɛɛ kɛ ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to clear weeds away from my yam mounds early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ mi-sweet potato ŋmɔji lɛ amli mra yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young yam sprouts grow slowly at first and cannot fight off fast-growing weeds for water and sunlight. Clearing weeds early ensures all the soil nutrients go directly into forming big yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ daaa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ abɔ akaŋ kɛha nu kɛ hulu la. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ yaa tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛfeɔ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are my harvested cassava tubers tough and woody instead of soft when boiled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ni mikpa lɛ shishifãi lɛ wa ni amɛfeɔ tso moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee blɛoo kɛ́ ahoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots become hard and woody if left in the ground too long past their mature harvest date or if grown in poor soil without enough nutrients. Harvesting on time ensures the tubers remain soft for eating.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ baafee nɔ ni wa ni ebaafee tso kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. aloo kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ ni niyenii kpakpai ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ Nikpamɔ yɛ be naa lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ ahiɔ shi bɔdɔɔ kɛha niyeli.

english: Why did some of the crop seedlings I planted fail to grow while others survived?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ ekomɛi edaaa yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hiɔ shi lɛ?

english: Seedlings often fail to establish if they suffer root damage during planting, lack steady soil moisture, or are buried too deep. Ensuring gentle handling, soft soil, and consistent water helps more seedlings take root successfully.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ kɛji amɛshishifãi lɛ fite yɛ be mli ni aduɔ lɛ. shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni bɛ loo afu lɛ mli tsɔ Nɔkwɛmɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo, kɛ nu ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ baaye abua ni dumɔwui babaoo atswa shishifãi.

english: Why do my young crops die shortly after I move them into the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ gboiɔ beni mikɛ amɛ tee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Transplanting causes shock to young plants if their roots dry out in the hot sun or break during moving. Planting early in the morning or late in the afternoon and watering immediately helps them settle into the soil.
ga: Tso bibioo lɛ ni aaawo lɛ baaha eshishifãi lɛ agbi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli loo efo yɛ be mli ni aduɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ adu amɛ leebi loo shwane ni awo amɛ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know if my seeds in the ground are dead or just taking time to sprout?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji midumɔwui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ egbo loo amɛmiihe be kɛkɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Most healthy crop seeds sprout within 7 to 14 days if the soil is moist. If nothing emerges after two weeks, carefully dig up a seed; if it feels soft, dark, or rotted, excess water or bad seeds prevented germination.
ga: Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ babaoo baakwɛ̃ yɛ gbii 7 kɛyashi 14 mli kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Kɛji nɔ ko baaa yɛ otsii enyɔ sɛɛ Tsɔɔmɔ dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji enu he akɛ eyɛ bɔdɔɔ, eyɛ ediŋŋ, loo egbo Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu ni fa fe nine loo dumɔwui ni ehiii lɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkakwɛ̃.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops turn yellow when rain water gathers on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nu bua ehe naa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Standing water blocks air from reaching crop roots, essentially suffocating them. When roots cannot breathe, they stop taking up food, which causes the leaves to turn yellow and growth to stall.
ga: Nu ni ato lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmɔlɔ Beni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu Ebaakpa niyenii yeli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdalɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Can heavy rain water staying on my land kill my crops completely?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ akpata midumɔ nii lɛ ahiɛ kwraa?

english: Yes, water left standing on fields for several days causes root rot due to fungal growth in oxygen-starved soil. Digging simple drainage pathways allows excess rain to flow away and saves crop roots.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli gbii babaoo lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni yaa hiɛ yɛ sũ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. Nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ nu mli ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni aaafo Enɛ haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei shishifãi ahe.

english: How does wet, flooded soil affect how my crop roots grow underground?
ga: Te shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ saa bɔ ni mitsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ daa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Excess water forces crop roots to stay shallow near the top of the soil where air is available. These shallow roots make the crop weak and easily knocked over by wind once the soil dries.
ga: Nu babaoo haa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yiteŋ he ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Nɛkɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ nɛɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ, ni kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ tswaa amɛ oya.

english: Why do crops grow poorly near big wood logs and old tree stumps on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ tsei wuji kɛ tsei akui momo ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Old stumps and heavy logs hide pests like termites and diseases, while underground tree roots steal moisture and nutrients away from your planted crops, weakening their growth.
ga: Tsoi ni egbɔ kɛ tsei ni mli tse lɛ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ helai teeɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ juɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ lɛ amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dalɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ.

english: Does leaving tall trees on my land prevent my crops from growing well?
ga: Ani tsei kakadaji ni mashi yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, heavy tree canopy blocks sunlight, which crops need to make food. Crops grown in deep shade usually become tall, thin, and yield very little food.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa. ni ji tso ni he hiaa kɛha niyenii feemɔ Tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ fɔɔ shweremɔ, ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ.

english: Why is it hard for my crop roots to spread when I do not break the soil well before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa akɛ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ miigbɛ amɛshwã lɛ? Akɛni migbalaaa sũ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ dani miduɔ nii hewɔ lɛ?

english: Hard, compacted soil acts like concrete, stopping young roots from stretching deep to find moisture. Loosening the soil before planting lets roots grow easily and anchor the plant.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kɔnkrit. Etsiɔ shishifãi bibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkashɛ amɛhe kɛya shɔŋŋ koni amɛyatao ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ dani adu lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ adara oya ni ekɛ tso lɛ ama shi.

english: Why do my crops grow fast on one side of my land but stay small on the other side?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida oya yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ fã kome shi amɛhe ehiaaa yɛ fã kroko lɛ?

english: Soil quality changes across a farm; areas with poor drainage, hard soil, or shade will hold crops back, while well-drained, sunny spots allow crops to grow strong.
ga: Tsakemɔi ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ Hei ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ, shikpɔŋ ni wa, loo hulutsoo be lɛ baatsi ŋmɔshi nibii anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃. Nakai beaŋ lɛ, he ko ni nu hoɔ yɛ jogbaŋŋ, ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ yɛ lɛ baawo tsei adalɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. This feeds the neighboring maize plant naturally, making the soil richer without needing to buy as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Gbɛ nɛɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the specific nutrients that crop needs and allows soil pests and diseases that attack maize to build up in the ground year after year.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ pɛ. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my maize start turning yellow in a V-shape down the center?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baai lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔŋ ni V su yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This yellowing means your soil lacks nitrogen. Maize needs plenty of nitrogen to stay green and build large cobs, so seeing this symptom means it is time to feed the soil with nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea.
ga: Nɛkɛ su ni ji ŋmɔŋ nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ewo ŋmeii wuji. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ona okadi nɛɛ, no lɛ be eshɛɛ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ urea lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under strong sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide big leaves that shield the young cocoa plants from the sun and keep the soil moist during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ woɔ baai wuji ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do we build big earth mounds to plant yams instead of planting them directly into flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wɔmaa muji gɔji wuji koni wɔkɛdu ŋmeii yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni wɔbaadu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose earth so they can expand downward without resistance. High mounds keep the soil loose, improve drainage, and stop heavy rains from rotting the growing yam.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse bɔni afee ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã kɛya shi ni nɔ ko nɔ ko akatsi amɛnaa. Gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ha nu ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ ni otsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafite ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: How do I know which way to stick cassava stems into the ground when planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji midu ŋmei akɛ ebaakpɛtɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he?

english: You must check the small growth buds along the stem and make sure they point upward toward the sky. Planting cassava stems upside down forces the shoots to grow backward, leading to weak plants and small yields.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ hiŋmɛii bibii lɛ. yɛ tso lɛ shishi ni okwɛ koni amɛtsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Cassava ni akwɛɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ kɛyaa shishi lɛ baaha ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi.

english: Why do the blossoms on my pepper plants drop off without forming any peppers during very hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeee pepper ko yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high and water is scarce, pepper plants get stressed. They drop their flowers to conserve water and protect themselves instead of using energy to grow fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni nu faaa lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ baaná haomɔ. Amɛkɛ fɔfɔii woɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii kɛdu aduawai.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow thin and produce small harvests even when it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibioo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that aggressively steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your main crop, leaving your plants starved of the food they need to produce a good harvest.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni jɛɔ onibii titrii amli lɛ amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei náaa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why are there holes in my young maize leaves and small dirt-like powder inside the leaf funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu kɛ nibii bibii ni tamɔ muji lɛ? yɛ baa lɛ mli

english: This is a sign of Fall Armyworm damage. The caterpillars hide inside the central funnel of the young maize plant and chew through the new leaves before they fully unfold.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ Fall Armyworm lɛ efite nii. Kplukai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ baai heei dani amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa kwraa.

english: Why should I trim off some of the lower branches and extra leaves from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ kɛ baai ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Trimming extra leaves directs the plant's energy into producing bigger, healthier tomatoes rather than wastefully feeding unnecessary foliage. It also improves air circulation around the stem, which prevents fungal diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ afo baai ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ hewalɛ afee tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ moŋ fe ni eeefite baai ni he ehiaaa. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ tso lɛ he lɛ hu yaa hiɛ, ni no haaa ŋmeii helai aba.

english: Why are my crops turning yellow and dying ever since people started digging for gold near my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboi kɛjɛ be mli ni gbɔmɛi bɔi shika tsuru taomɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Mining activities disturb deep soil layers and wash away healthy topsoil. This removes the nutrients crops need to feed on and exposes roots to harsh subsoil, causing leaves to turn yellow and plants to stunt or die.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ gbaa shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ naa ni efoɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ jieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tso lɛ ni eyeɔ lɛ, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ yaa shikpɔŋ shishi shikpɔŋ ni mli wa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛgboiɔ.

english: What naturally happens to my farm soil when the dark top layer is scraped away?
ga: Mɛni baa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛ́ ajie ŋwɛi fã ni yɔɔ duŋ lɛ?

english: The dark top layer of soil contains almost all the organic food, microbes, and earthworms that crops need to grow. When it is scraped off, only hard, nutrient-poor subsoil remains, making it very difficult for plant roots to spread or find food.
ga: Niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli, nibii bibii, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara lɛ ateŋ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni yɔɔ duŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji ajie lɛ, shikpɔŋ shishi shikpɔŋ ni wa ni niyenii mli hewalɛ bɛ mli lɛ pɛ eshwɛɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei shishifãi akɛ amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã loo amɛna niyenii.

english: Why does my farmland flood so easily now whenever it rains, even though it never used to?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, nu hoɔ yɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli oya lɛ? Akɛ jeee nakai kɔkɔɔkɔ?

english: Heavy digging and machinery flatten and pack the soil very tightly while destroying natural water pathways. Because the hard ground can no longer absorb rainwater like a sponge, water pools on the surface and drowns crop roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni atsaa kɛ tsɔnei ni tsii baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa yɛ be mli ni efiteɔ adebɔɔ mli nu gbɛi lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nugbɔshiimɔ tamɔ sponji dɔŋŋ. No sɛɛ lɛ, nu buaa ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: How do I know if the river water near my farm is still safe to water my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu ni yɔɔ faa ni bɛŋkɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hi lolo kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ anɔ nu?

english: If the water is muddy brown, thick with silt, or smells unusual, it is polluted. Using this water coats crop leaves with mud, preventing them from catching sunlight, and can introduce dangerous mud that smothers plant roots.
ga: Kɛji nu lɛ ji ŋmɔtɔ, atatu, eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ, loo eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ srɔto. tsɔɔ akɛ eji nu ni fiteɔ nii Nu nɛɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaha tso lɛ baai lɛ afee muji. Buu he kɛjɛ hulu la he. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ muji ni yɔɔ oshara ni fiteɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ aba.

english: Is it safe for my family to eat cassava or yams grown on land that was affected by chemical mining runoff?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ miweku lɛ baaye ŋmei loo ŋmei ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋtayaai amli lɛ efite nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Crops grown in chemical-polluted soils can absorb harmful substances through their roots directly into the food you eat. It is best to have an agricultural officer inspect the soil before eating root crops grown on affected land.
ga: Tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsofai ewo mli lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ amɛshishifãi anɔ aŋɔ nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui awo niyenii ni oyeɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ baakwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani amɛye shishifãi ni adu yɛ he ni hela lɛ emɔ lɛ.

english: Can I plant cassava or maize directly on land that was previously dug up by galamsey workers?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni galamsey nitsulɔi efo tsutsu lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting immediately on freshly mined land usually leads to crop failure because the fertile topsoil is gone and the ground is too hard. The land must first be leveled and improved with organic matter before crops can grow well.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni atsa ehee nɔ ni aduɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii baa shi ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ nɔ efoɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ. Esa akɛ afee shikpɔŋ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli awo mli klɛŋklɛŋ dani ŋmɔshi nibii abakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What fast-growing plants can I sow to help heal and fix my spoiled farm soil?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya manyɛ madu koni eye ebua ni etsa shikpɔŋ ni efite yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni esaa?

english: Leguminous plants like mucuna, pigeon pea, or cover grasses help heal damaged soil. They pull nitrogen from the air into the ground, drop leaves that rot into rich topsoil, and break up hard earth with their roots.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli tamɔ mucilagina, pigeon pea loo mulch baanyɛ aye abua ni etsa shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ. Amɛgbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Jiemɔ baai ni egboi lɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ nɔ. ni ekɛ eshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ nɔ.

english: How long does damaged farmland usually take to become good for growing crops again?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be enyiɛ eheɔ dani ŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ ekoŋŋ?

english: Left alone, damaged soil can take tens of years to recover. However, if you actively fill in pits, add animal manure or compost, and plant soil-rebuilding cover crops, you can start growing simple crops within 2 to 5 years.
ga: Shi kɛlɛ, kɛji akɛ ashi lɛ pɛ Shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ baanyɛ ahé afii nyɔŋmai abɔ dani etsa, kɛji otsa shi waa. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi aŋmɔji afata he. ni amɛdu ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛkɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ. Obaanyɛ oje tsei foloi akwɛmɔ shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 5 mli.

english: How does adding animal manure or compost help bring back crops on damaged farm ground?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii aku sɛɛ aba ŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ?

english: Manure and compost act like medicine for poor soil by feeding good soil bugs, adding missing plant food, and helping the ground hold moisture so new crop roots can easily take hold.
ga: Manure kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsofa kɛha shikpɔŋ ni ehiii kɛtsɔ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni amɛhaa lɛ nɔ. Okɛ tso niyenii ni elaaje lɛ afata he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli bɔni afee ni tso shishifãi heei anyɛ amɔmɔ mli mlɛo.

english: What basic steps should I take if I want to turn land filled with deep pits back into a cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛi titrii esa akɛ matsɔ nɔ kɛji miisumɔ ni maku misɛɛ mafee mishikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bu mli lɛ ekoŋŋ mafee kookoo ŋmɔ?

english: First, you must fill the pits with dirt and level the ground so water doesn't create ponds. Next, plant cover crops and fast-growing shade trees like plantain to restore soil moisture and shade before planting young cocoa seedlings.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, esa akɛ okɛ sũ awo bu lɛ mli ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee pɛpɛɛpɛ koni nu akafee nubu. Nɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ji, dumɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ hulutsoo tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains, koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulutsoo aba ekoŋŋ dani odu kookoo dumɔwui bibii.

english: I heard people talk about spraying green tea or leaf extracts on crops. What does adding plant liquids to my farm actually do?
ga: Minu ni mɛi wieɔ green tea loo tsofa ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ baa mli lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ he. Ani tsei amli nu ni mikɛfataa miŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Soaking beneficial leaves or compost in water creates liquid food called 'plant tea.' When sprayed on crops, it delivers quick nutrients directly through the leaves and roots, helping the plant grow stronger and resist diseases.
ga: Baai loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni akɛwoɔ nu mli lɛ feɔ nu ni atsɛɔ lɛ ‘tso tii’ kɛji akɛ afɔ tsei anɔ. Ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ oya kɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛtsɔɔ baai kɛ shishifãi anɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa waa ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ helai.

english: How do my crops actually 'eat' the food and fertilizer I put in the soil?
ga: Te feɔ tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ‘yeɔ’ niyenii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops do not eat like animals; they absorb liquid nutrients through very fine hair roots in the soil. When soil moisture dissolves fertilizers or plant extracts, the roots drink it up to build leaves and stems.
ga: Ayeee ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kooloi. Amɛtsɔɔ shishifãi ahe yitsɔi bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amli amɛheɔ niyenii ni ji nu. Kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu lɛ shwie ŋmɔshi nibii loo tso mli nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ mli lɛ Shishifãi lɛ nuɔ lɛ koni amɛfee baai kɛ ŋmeii.

english: If I spray a bitter plant extract on my crops, will that stop insects from eating the leaves?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ tso mli nu ni mli edɔ shwie miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ Ani ebaatsi kooloi ni yeɔ tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ anaa?

english: Yes, bitter natural sprays made from local plants like neem make the crop leaves taste bad to insects. This deters pests from feeding on your crop without harming the plant itself.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni mli edɔ ni jɛ maŋ lɛ mli tsei tamɔ neem mli lɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ nɔ ni ŋɔɔ kɛha kooloi bibii. Enɛ baatsi kooloi ni yeɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa ni amɛyeee tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ awui.

english: Does putting sweet things in the soil make my harvested fruits taste sweeter?
ga: Ani nɔ ko ni ŋɔɔ ni akɛaawo sũ lɛ mli lɛ baaha aduawai ni akpa lɛ afee ŋɔɔ?

english: Crops make their own sugars naturally using sunlight, water, and soil minerals like potassium. Adding sugar directly to the soil doesn't work, but giving plants balanced nutrients helps them produce their own natural sugars.
ga: Tsei kɛ hulu la, nu kɛ nibii ni yɔɔ sũ mli, tamɔ potassium tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ sugar yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Sugars ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ. Shi kɛ́ akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni sa ha tsei lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛfeɔ sugar yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves taste bitter when I harvest them during very hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ akpa amɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: When crops experience heat stress and lack of water, they produce protective chemicals that make their leaves bitter. Watering regularly and providing light shade helps keep vegetables tasting good.
ga: Kɛ tsei kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ kɛ nu ni bɛ kpe lɛ, Tso lɛ jieɔ tsofai ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ hulutsoo yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa aduawai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Is it better to give liquid nutrients to the plant leaves or directly to the soil?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ji nu lɛ aha tsei ahe baai loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Soil application feeds the main root system for steady long-term growth, while spraying liquid nutrients onto leaves acts like a fast boost when the plant is weak, stressed, or showing quick yellowing.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ niyenii kɛha dalɛ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ, ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, niyenii mli nu ni akɛshwieɔ baai anɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni woɔ mɔ hewalɛ oya kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, amɛmiihao loo amɛmiitsɔɔ okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ amɛmiifee ŋmɔtɔ oya.

english: Can I mix local herbs and plant leaves into water to protect my vegetables from sickness?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ maŋ lɛ mli tsofai kɛ baai afutu nu lɛ mli koni mikɛbu mi-aduawai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hela he?

english: Many local plants have natural defensive compounds that fight off fungi and bacteria. Soaking them in water creates a natural protective coat for your crops, though it must be diluted properly so it doesn't burn the leaves.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli hebuu nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ wuɔ yɛ tsei babaoo amli. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ wo nu mli lɛ, ehaa adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ko ni buɔ onibii ahe lɛ baa. Eyɛ mli akɛ esa akɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ koni akashã baai lɛ moŋ.

english: Do crops take in food at night or do they only feed during the daytime?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ niyenii gbɛkɛ loo shwane pɛ?

english: Crops collect sunlight and water to create food during the day. At night, when it is dark, they use that stored energy to expand their roots, grow new stems, and develop flowers or fruits.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ buaa hulu la kɛ nu naa koni ekɛfee niyenii yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Gbi gbɛkɛ beni edɔ Amɛkɛ nakai hewalɛ ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo shishifãi. Bɔɔ tso hee ni okɛ fɔfɔi loo aduawai aba

english: Will adding a extra large amount of plant food or fertilizer make my crops grow twice as fast?
ga: Ani tsei aniyenii loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni mikɛfataa he lɛ baaha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adara oya fe tsutsu lɛ shii enyɔ?

english: Too much fertilizer or strong plant extracts can overload the crop and 'burn' the roots, causing leaves to turn yellow or brown. It is better to apply smaller, correct amounts regularly.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli loo tso mli nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ babaoo baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ fe nine ni ‘eshã’ shishifãi lɛ, ni eha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ. Esa akɛ akɛwo mli fioo fioo kɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my crops become greener when I mix decaying plant waste into the dirt before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ eŋɔli kɛ́ mikɛ tsei amli jwɛi ni egboi futu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani midu lɛ?

english: Decaying plant waste breaks down into nitrogen and rich organic matter. This provides the exact building blocks plants need to create chlorophyll, the green material inside leaves that turns sunlight into energy.
ga: Tsei amli jwɛi ni egbo lɛ mli gbalaa ni etsɔɔ nitrogen kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa babaoo. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛfee klorofil. Enɛ ji nibii ni yɔɔ baai amli ni tsakeɔ hulu la lɛ ewoɔ hewalɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to build green leaves. It can also happen if heavy rains wash away soil nutrients or if waterlogged soil prevents roots from taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ loo sũ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye nii.

english: Why do my crops wither during hot afternoons even when the soil has moisture?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: On very hot days, leaves lose water through evaporation faster than the roots can drink it up from the soil. The plant temporarily wilts to close its pores and conserve moisture until the heat cools down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni mli edɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ, baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛŋa eshishifãi lɛ be kukuoo ko ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni latsaa lɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too high or when rainfall is unpredictable. Extreme heat dries out the pollen inside the blossom, preventing fertilization, so the plant sheds the flower to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nugbɔ baanɛ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baaha pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ agbi. Etsiɔ fɔmɔ naa No hewɔ lɛ, tsei gbalaa amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amli koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why does my maize produce small cob heads with missing kernels instead of full cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ miiwo ŋmeii bibii shi ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Missing seeds on a maize cob happen because of poor pollination, which often occurs if there is a drought when the silk emerges. If the silk dries out too fast, pollen cannot fertilize the cob properly.
ga: Abɛi dumɔwui ni elaaje lɛ baa yɛ pollination ni ehiii lɛ hewɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛji hɔmɔ ba beni siliki lɛ miida lɛ. Kɛji akɛ siliki lɛ gĩ oya tsɔ lɛ, Pollen nyɛŋ afee ŋmeii lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my cassava tubers small and woody even though the branches and leaves are growing very big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛji tsei lɛ? He ni tsei niji kɛ baai lɛ dara waa yɛ lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or water, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing tall stems and leafy foliage above ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers down below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo nu babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ starch toɔ tso ɔ sisi fã nɛ ngɛ sisi ɔ mi.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow tall and thin with few fruits when planted under big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ ni ewoɔ yibii fioo pɛ kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ?

english: Pepper plants need direct sunlight to produce energy for flowers and fruits. When shaded by tall trees, the pepper plant stretches upward searching for light, making it weak and unable to bear heavy fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha amɛfɔfɔi kɛ amɛyibii lɛ. Beni eyɔɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko shishi lɛ Pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ ehe kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ena la lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ewo yibii ni tsii.

english: Why do I get smaller total yields when I plant my seeds very close together to squeeze more onto my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ yibiiwoo fɛɛ nɔ bibioo nɔ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni mikɛmi dumɔwui babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops struggle like too many people sharing one small plate of food. Every plant competes for the same limited sunlight, water, and soil food, resulting in weak plants and tiny harvests.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ wuɔ tamɔ mɛi babaoo ni jaa tsɛnsi bibioo ko. Tsei fɛɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ falɛ kome. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, ni ŋmaa fioo pɛ kpaɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up tight like tiny cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is typically caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites feeding under the leaves, or by a virus transmitted by insects that disrupts the plant's normal leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni kooloi bibii ni tsiɔ baai lɛ adalɛ ni sa lɛ naa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds on my farm grow much faster than the food crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida oya fe niyenii ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally suited to tough local soil conditions, so their roots grow very fast to capture sunlight, water, and nutrients before your crops have time to establish themselves.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji koo mli tso ko ni sa jogbaŋŋ kɛha shikpɔŋ ni wa ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ daa oya koni amɛhe hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii kpakpai dani onibii lɛ aná be ni ekɛbaatswa shi.

english: Why did my young crops burn and dry up right after I applied chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ wo midumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer behaves like salt; if applied directly against plant stems or put on dry soil without water, it pulls moisture straight out of the plant's roots, causing root burn and wilting.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ feɔ amɛnii tamɔ ŋmei. Kɛji akɛ akɛwo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ loo akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ ni nu bɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni ejie nu kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why do my maize leaves curl up tightly into thin tubes during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Maize leaves roll up during intense heat as a natural defense mechanism to reduce their surface area, which helps the crop conserve water by reducing evaporation.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he lɛ aba shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he kɛtsɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell if my tomato plants are receiving too much water when I irrigate them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiná nu babaoo kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo amɛnɔ?

english: Overwatered crops usually show pale yellowing leaves, slow growth, and soft roots, because excess water pushes oxygen out of the soil and starves the root system.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni nu babaoo náa amɛ lɛ jieɔ baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ, amɛdaraa blɛoo, ni amɛshishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ejaakɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ jeɔ sũ lɛ mli ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves turn pale brown and dry up when exposed to strong sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young pepper leaves can suffer from sunburn when direct heat dries out tender leaf tissues faster than roots can draw moisture from the ground.
ga: Pepper baai bibii lɛ baanyɛ ashã hulu kɛji la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ ha baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ agbi oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my plantain shoots grow very tall and slender when I plant them close under big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains lɛ daa ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ?

english: Plantains stretch upward rapidly toward sunlight when shaded, producing thin, weak stems that struggle to support heavy fruit later on.
ga: Plantains lɛ baashɛ ehe oya kɛya hulu la lɛ he kɛ́ eyɛ hulutsoo be mli. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛfi aduawai ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Extreme daytime heat or erratic moisture levels cause plant stress, which stops tomato blossoms from self-pollinating and forces the plant to drop its flowers.
ga: Gbi mli dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo latsaa ni bɛ shiŋŋ kɛ tsei haomɔ baa. Enɛ haaa tomato fɔfɔi lɛ afee amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ŋmɔtɔ, ni enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni efoɔ shi.

english: Why do my sweet potato vines produce heavy leafy stems but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ baai ni tsii shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil encourages sweet potatoes to direct energy into growing leaf foliage rather than developing thick, food-storing roots.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ sweet potatoes hewalɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aya baai lɛ adalɛ mli. Mohu ɔ, e peeɔ sisi nɛ mi wa nɛ e ngɔɔ niye ní kɛ toɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize turning yellow starting from the leaf tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing that moves from the leaf tip down the main vein signals a nitrogen shortage, prompting the plant to move remaining nitrogen from older leaves to feed new growth.
ga: Su ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ baa lɛ naagbee kɛyaa fã titri lɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Wo tsei hewalɛ ni amɛjie nitrogen ni eshwɛ kɛjɛ baai momoi lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do the edges of my cassava leaves look scorched like they were burned by fire?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei baai lɛ ahe shãa tamɔ nɔ ni ashã amɛ lɛ?

english: Scorched leaf edges typically point to a potassium deficiency, a key nutrient crops use to regulate water movement inside their tissues.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ashã lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ potassium faaa. ni ji tso titri ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii koni akɛkudɔ nu ni hoɔ yɛ fãji amli lɛ

english: Why do my cassava bushes shed most of their bottom leaves during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baa lɛ babaoo shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants shed lower foliage in dry weather to conserve stored water and nutrients inside their underground roots until rain returns.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi koni amɛkɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ato amɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my cowpea crop leaves fold upward close together when the sun sets?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛbɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe kɛ́ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Cowpea leaves fold at night to keep tender tissues warm and minimize night-time water loss while photosynthesis is paused.
ga: Cowpea shwieɔ ebaa lɛ nɔ gbɛkɛ koni egbɔmɔtso ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ mli adɔ. ni ehaa nu ni laajeɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ baa shi yɛ be mli ni fotosintɛsis lɛ ekpa nitsumɔ lɛ.

english: Why are my crops turning yellow and growing slowly when tall weeds surround them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdaraa blɛoo kɛ́ jwɛi kakadaŋŋ abɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Tall weeds cover your crop's leaves and block them from catching sunlight. They also steal water and food from the soil, preventing your plants from getting the nutrients they need to stay green and healthy.
ga: Jwɛi kakadaji haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu la he. Amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii hu kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Ehaa tsei lɛ náa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why do climbing vines covering my cocoa trees cause them to produce fewer cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wain tsei ni ha mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ akwɔɔ lɛ haa amɛwoɔ cocoa ŋmeii fioo lɛ?

english: When climbing vines spread across the top of a cocoa tree, they cover the tree's leaves and block sunlight. Without light, the tree cannot make enough food or absorb nutrients properly to grow pods.
ga: Kɛji okwɔ wain tsei ni gbɛ eshwa cacao tsei lɛ ayiteŋ lɛ Ebaaha tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ ni ebaatsi hulu la lɛ naa. Kɛji la bɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ afee niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa loo eŋɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why are the vegetable crops I planted under a big mango tree not growing well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai ni midu yɛ mango tso agbo lɛ shishi lɛ ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: The thick leaf canopy of the big mango tree blocks sunlight from reaching your lower crops, and the large tree roots steal most of the nutrients and water in the ground.
ga: Mango tso agbo ko ni yɔɔ baai ni mli tse lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ahe. Ni tsei wuji ashishifãi juɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ babaoo.

english: When maize plants grow too close together, their leaves overlap and block sunlight from one another. Their roots also fight for the same soil nutrients, causing all the plants to stay small and weak.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe nɔ ni amɛtsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Amɛshishifãi lɛ hu wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii kpakpai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ feɔ bibioo ni egbɔjɔ.

english: When my plantain sucker grows many extra shoots around it, should I leave all of them?
ga: Kɛ́ mi plantain tsei lɛ amli tsei lɛ yɛ tsei babaoo ni miida yɛ tso lɛ he lɛ, ani esa akɛ mashɛ tsei lɛ fɛɛ ashwie?

english: No, you should cut off the extra shoots and keep only the strongest one. Leaving all shoots causes them to fight for nutrients, which results in smaller bunches of plantains.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ ofolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ ni okɛ tsei ni wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ ahi shi. Kɛ́ ashɛrɛ ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ ashwie lɛ, ebaaha amɛwuu yɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he. Enɛ haa plantain lɛ feɔ bibioo.

english: Why should I remove some small, weak fruits from my pepper plant while it is growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie aduawai bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsei amli be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Removing the extra small fruits allows the plant to send all its gathered soil nutrients and water into the remaining peppers, helping them grow much larger and stronger.
ga: Yibii bibii ni fa lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ekɛ sũ mli niyenii kɛ nu ni ebua naa lɛ fɛɛ yaa ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ amli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ feɔ agboi babaoo ni amɛhe wa.

english: Will trimming off some extra leafy branches from my tomato plants help them yield better?
ga: Ani mi-tomato tsei lɛ ahe baai ni fa fe nine ni mifoɔ lɛ baaye abua mi yibiiwoo lɛ?

english: Yes, trimming away overgrown leaves and extra branches helps sunlight reach the main stems and stops the plant from wasting nutrients on useless leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ afo baai ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine kɛ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ he, ni ehaa tso lɛ fiteɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: What happens to my crop if I do not pluck off dead or diseased leaves?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji mijieee baai ni egboi loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Dead and diseased leaves can block healthy leaves from sunlight, waste the plant's energy, and spread sickness to the rest of the crop.
ga: Baai ni egboi ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ baa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anaa koni hulu la akashɛ amɛnɔ. efiteɔ tsei ahewalɛ ni egbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why do my crops need open sunlight on their leaves to absorb nutrients properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ hulu la he hiaa mi tsei lɛ koni amɛshɛ amɛbaai lɛ ahe koni amɛnyɛ amɛŋɔ niyenii kpakpai lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leaves catch sunlight to power the plant, acting like an engine that draws water and nutrients up from the soil through the roots.
ga: Baai mɔɔ hulu la koni eha tso lɛ hewalɛ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ko ni gbalaa nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ.

english: When my cassava plant grows too many thick leaves on top, why don't the roots grow big underneath?
ga: Beni mi yucca tso lɛ hiɛ baai ni mli tse tsɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ. Mɛni hewɔ anaigbɛ shishifãi lɛ daraaa lɛ?

english: If a plant spends all its nutrients building heavy leaves on top, it does not have enough extra food left over to feed and swell the cassava roots under the soil.
ga: Kɛji tso lɛ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ fɛɛ tsu nii ni ekɛfee baai ni tsii yɛ nɔ lɛ, Niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni eshwɛɛɛ ni ebaaye ni ebaaha ŋmei shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and easily damaged by direct hot sunlight. Plantain plants grow quickly and produce large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing necessary shade and cooling the surrounding soil while the cocoa trees mature.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ fiteɔ amɛ oya. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli akpɔlɔi. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa lɛ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli jɔɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to catch direct sunlight to produce energy for underground tuber growth. Raising the vines on stakes exposes more leaves to sunlight, prevents leaves from rotting on wet soil, and reduces crop losses caused by ground pests.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tuber dalɛ. Wein tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ baaha baai lɛ aná hulu la babaoo. Etsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ. ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛbaa lɛ aba shi.

english: Maize heavily uses up specific nutrients like nitrogen from the soil. Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot weakens the soil quality and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to multiply in that ground, resulting in poorer harvests each year.
ga: Abele kɛ niyenii pɔtɛɛi babaoo, tamɔ nitrogen, ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii.
