Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ aba shi. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa ŋmãa nɔ lɛ ayi fa babaoo yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nikpamɔ yibii lɛ fiteɔ daa afi.

english: When is the best time to put chemical fertilizer on my field so it doesn't go to waste?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ awo ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni ekafite?

english: Fertilizer should be applied when the soil is moist but not during heavy rains. Applying fertilizer when the soil is slightly damp allows plant roots to soak up nutrients, whereas applying it right before a heavy downpour causes the rain to wash the expensive fertilizer away.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi esaaa akɛ akɛwoɔ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ fioo lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei shishifãi lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii mli hewalɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛwo mli dani nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ lɛ ajie ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize plant turning yellow instead of staying green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the plant is starving for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient responsible for leaf growth and green color. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure helps restore green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni haa baa lɛ daa kɛ eŋɔli su. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is frequently caused by viruses spread by tiny insects like whiteflies, or by extreme heat and uneven watering. Keeping the farm clean of weeds and spraying early against sap-sucking insects helps protect the plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi, loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ ni eyaaa nɔ. Kɛ́ ŋmɔ lɛ mli tse kɛjɛ jwɛi ahe kɛ kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu tsei ahe

english: What is making small holes in my maize leaves with sticky, sawdust-like dirt inside the growing tip?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-abɛi lɛ amli ŋmeii bibii lɛ miifee? Ni muji ni tamɔ ŋmei ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmei ni miida lɛ mli.

english: This damage is caused by caterpillars such as the Fall Armyworm feeding inside the heart of the plant. The sawdust-like dirt is their droppings. Early treatment with recommended pesticides or applying clean sand/ash into the whorl can kill the caterpillars.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni yeɔ nii yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ. Muji ni tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ ji amɛ ŋmeii. Tsamɔ mra Kɛtsɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii loo ŋã/ashwishwɛ ni he tse ni yɔɔ ring lɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbe kooloi lɛ.

english: Why are the blossoms on my pepper plants dropping off before any peppers can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani pepper lɛ baanyɛ afee lɛ?

english: Flowers drop when the plant undergoes stress from sudden hot dry spells, irregular watering, or insect attacks on the delicate flower stems. Consistent watering during flowering and managing insect pests keeps the flowers attached so fruit can develop.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ miigba tso lɛ naa. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa Aloo kooloi bibii tutuaa fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa yɛ fɔfɔii akwɛmɔ be mli kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔii lɛ ahiɔ shi bɔni afee ni aduawai anyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: How do I choose the best plantain suckers from an existing farm to start my new field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantain tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ ni miyɔɔ mli momo lɛ mli koni mikɛje ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: Select 'maiden' or 'sword' suckers, which are young shoots with narrow, spear-shaped leaves and a broad base bulb. These produce stronger root systems and larger fruit bunches compared to shoots with broad, floppy leaves ('water suckers').
ga: Halamɔ ‘maiden’ loo ‘sword’ tsei, ni ji tsei bibii ni baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni tamɔ lance kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli lɛɛ. Enɛɛmɛi haa shishifãi ni mli wa kɛ aduawai akui wuji baa kɛ akɛto ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni shwieɔ shi (‘nu ŋmeii’) ahe.

english: How do I know when my cassava underground tubers are mature enough to dig up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ atsa?

english: Most cassava varieties mature between 9 to 12 months after planting when lower leaves begin turning yellow and shedding naturally. You can test maturity by carefully digging around one plant to check if the roots have expanded into thick, firm tubers.
ga: Cassava henɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo daa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ je shishi amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ Obaanyɛ oka ehewalɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ tso lɛ he ni ooofo lɛ nɔ. Dumɔ eko jogbaŋŋ koni okwɛ kɛji shishifãi lɛ egbɛ eshwã ni etsɔ ŋmeii ni mli tse ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have broad leaves that provide essential shade and moisture, protecting young cocoa trees until they are strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la he tɛ̃ɛ. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa. Buu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why is it helpful for me to plant groundnuts or beans on the same land where I grow maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmei yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans are legumes that capture nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil through their roots. This naturally fertilizes the soil and helps your maize grow healthier without relying entirely on chemical fertilizers.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eye ebua o-abele lɛ ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ ohe afɔ̃ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ anɔ kwraa.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to build green leaves. It can also happen when the soil is waterlogged, preventing the roots from taking in air.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni tsei lɛ he hiaa koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off before any tomatoes actually start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani tomato lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off without setting fruit when the plant gets stressed by extreme afternoon heat, irregular watering, or a lack of essential soil nutrients.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ shwane mli latsaa lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: Why do my cassava roots become soft and rot inside during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water stays trapped in the soil for too long without proper drainage. Excess water suffocates the roots and creates favorable conditions for soil fungi to attack the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shihilɛ ni hi baa shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ koni amɛtutua ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that suck plant sap and spread plant viruses. Controlling these insects early prevents the damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ mra lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni akafite.

english: How can I prevent caterpillars from chewing big holes in my cabbage leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi ŋmeii anaa koni amɛkaye buji wuji ni yɔɔ kaabe baa mli lɛ?

english: Caterpillars target leafy crops like cabbage. You can control them by inspecting leaves regularly to pick them off, using natural extracts like neem oil, or applying recommended crop protection sprays.
ga: Katɛji lɛ kwɛɔ tsei ni yɔɔ baai tamɔ kaabeji. Obaanyɛ okudɔ enɛ kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni oookwɛ daa koni ojie amɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli tamɔ neem fɔ loo tsofai ni akɛbuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers develop dark, rotten spots inside while in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tubers ni akpa lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diji kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ mli beni akɛtoɔ lɛ?

english: Dark spots in stored yams are often caused by microscopic soil worms called nematodes that infected the tuber before harvest, or by fungi that entered through small cuts made during harvesting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sũ mli ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes ni tsɛŋeɔ ŋmeii lɛ dani akpaa ŋmeii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ni ato lɛ anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni boteɔ mli kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ nɔ. ni baa yɛ nikpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ

english: How can I easily tell if my farm soil has lost its nutrients and needs fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ faaa, ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli?

english: Exhausted soil shows signs like slow crop growth, pale or yellowing leaves, significantly smaller harvests than usual, and an increase in stubborn weeds like Striga.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ baatsɔɔ okadii tamɔ tsei ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo. Baai ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔŋ Nikpamɔ lɛ faaa kwraa fe bɔ ni eji daa lɛ. kɛ jwɛi ni yitsoŋ wa tamɔ Striga lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to grow aggressively in harsh conditions. They absorb water, light, and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crops, which is why early weeding is necessary.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Amɛheɔ nu, la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants keep dying when I clear all the tall trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ mijie tsei kakadaji fɛɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct sunlight and high heat. They need shade from larger trees or fast-growing plants like plantains to protect their delicate leaves and keep the soil moist while their roots develop.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛbu amɛbaai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Can I leave all the young shoots growing at the base of my plantain tree, or should I cut some away?
ga: Ani manyɛ mashi tsei bibii ni miida yɛ mi-plantain lɛ shishi lɛ? Aloo esa akɛ afolɔ fãi komɛi ni ashɛrɛ ashwie?

english: You should remove most shoots and leave only two or three healthy ones of different ages. Leaving too many shoots creates competition for nutrients and water, which results in smaller plantain bunches.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ babaoo ni ashi ŋmeii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eye afii srɔtoi. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo yɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ekɛ akaŋshii baa kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Enɛ haa plantain lɛ feɔ bibioo.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of the stalk usually mean the soil is lacking nitrogen. Adding compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the plant stay green and grow full ears of corn.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How do I pick the right cassava stems from my old farm to plant a new field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei tsei ni sa kɛjɛ miŋmɔ momo lɛ mli koni mikɛdu yɛ miŋmɔ hee lɛ mli?

english: Choose straight, healthy stems from mature plants that showed no signs of disease or pest damage. Cut pieces from the middle part of the stem with active buds, as top soft parts and bottom woody parts do not sprout as well.
ga: Halamɔ tso ni ja ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni jɛ tso ni eda ni hela loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko bɛ he okadi ko mli. Okɛ fã ko kɛjɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ni ŋmei ni tsuɔ nii yɔɔ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, fãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ kɛ fãi ni yɔɔ shishi ni tsei yɔɔ mli lɛ hu edaŋ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up into small cups instead of spreading flat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi efeɔ kɔɔpoo bibioo ko lɛ? yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from the leaves, or by a virus spread by whiteflies. Inspect under the leaves and treat with neem oil or appropriate sprays.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni okɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni sa awo mli.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce a lot of flowers, but the flowers just drop off without growing tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni aduuu tomato?

english: Tomato flowers fall off without forming fruit when temperatures get too high, when water is inconsistent, or when there are no bees or wind to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu lɛ ejaaa Aloo be mli ni ŋmeii loo kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ ni baaha fɔfɔii lɛ afee ŋmeii.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains the soil of the specific nutrients maize needs and allows pests that feed on maize to multiply. Rotating with beans or groundnuts restores nitrogen to the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baaná niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa abɛi lɛ. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ ni amɛshwereɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake amɛhe lɛ, ehaa nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Planting too close forces crops to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in weak, thin plants with small yields. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space to produce a full harvest.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa lɛ baa, ni yibiiwoo hu baa shi. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo ekpamɔ lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my crops look weak and pale even after heavy rain falls on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Excessive rain in poorly drained soil fills all the air pockets in the earth with water, suffocating root systems so they cannot absorb nutrients properly. Digging drainage channels helps excess water flow away.
ga: Nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ, ni no haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui fɛɛ ni yɔɔ je lɛŋ lɛ eyiɔ kɛ nu. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyashɛɔ he ko ni enyɛɛɛ eŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ. Nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ nu mli lɛ mli ni akuɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to quickly steal available water, light, and nutrients from the soil. Early and regular weeding prevents them from crowding out your crops before the crops grow strong enough to compete.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛju nu, la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ni ooofee nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ baatsi oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee mɛi babaoo dani amɛdara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye akaŋ.

english: How do I know how many days my maize variety takes before it is ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male gbii enyiɛ ni ebaahe mi-ŋma henɔ lɛ dani efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ?

english: Different crop varieties have specific maturity periods set by breeders. For instance, improved maize varieties like Obatampa take about 110 days from planting to full maturity, which helps you predict your harvest timeline.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi yɛ dalɛ be pɔtɛɛ ni mɛi ni kwɛɔ amɛ lɛ toɔ. Akɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, ŋmãa henɔi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ tamɔ Obatampa lɛ heɔ aaafee gbii 110 kɛjɛ be mli ni aduɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa. Enɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni otsɔɔ kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why is it important for me to record the exact date I plant my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni maŋma gbi pɔtɛɛ ni midu midumɔwui lɛ?

english: Tracking your planting date helps you follow a precise schedule for critical farm activities like weeding, applying fertilizer, and harvesting at the peak time before pests or late rains spoil the crop.
ga: Gbii ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ asɛɛdii yeɔ ebua bo ni onyiɛɔ gbɛjianɔtoo ni ja sɛɛ kɛha ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔi ni he hiaa tamɔ jwɛi shwiemɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ yɛ bei ni fa babaoo mli dani tsɛŋemɔ helai loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ lɛ yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ.

english: What happens to my crops if I do not follow the recommended planting dates given by extension officers?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ gbi ni mi-extension officer lɛ wo he ŋaa lɛ tsuuu nii?

english: If you plant off-schedule, your crops may run out of rain during crucial growth periods like flowering or grain filling, leading to smaller yields or total crop failure.
ga: Kɛji odu nii yɛ grid lɛ kponɔ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni nugbɔ bɛ yɛ dalɛ bei ni he hiaa tamɔ fɔfɔi loo dumɔwui ni eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi loo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fiteɔ kwraa.

english: How do agricultural experts decide the exact planting dates for crops in my area?
ga: Te okwaayeli he nilelɔi feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛkpɛɔ amɛyiŋ yɛ gbii ni abaadu nii yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ he?

english: Experts study historical weather patterns, soil moisture levels, and seasonal rain forecasts for your region to set planting dates that give crops the maximum chance of thriving.
ga: Nileelɔi kaseɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni eho lɛ ahe nii. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be mli ni awieɔ yɛ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ. Koni ana gbi ni abaadu ni baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni amɛdara.

english: When a seed package says a crop matures in 110 days, does the counting start from planting day or when the shoots appear?
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui ahe wolo ko tsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ daraa yɛ gbii 110 mli lɛ, ani akanemɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ gbi ni adu lɛ nɔ loo be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: The maturity timeframe usually begins on the exact day you plant the seed in the ground, allowing you to count forward and estimate when the crop will complete its life cycle.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be ni dumɔwui lɛ shwereɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ gbi ni oduɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okane kɛtsɔ hiɛ ni osusu be ni tso lɛ baagbe ewala shihilɛ naa lɛ he.

english: Why do some types of maize mature faster than other types?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa henɔi komɛi daa oya fe ekrokomɛi lɛ?

english: Breeder varieties are developed for different conditions; short-duration varieties mature quickly to survive short rainy seasons, while long-duration varieties take longer to yield heavier crops in areas with extended rain.
ga: Afee tsɔnei ni akɛkwɛɔ kooloi anɔ kɛha shihilɛi srɔtoi. Henɔi ni hiɔ shi be kuku lɛ daa oya koni amɛhi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ mli. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsei srɔtoi ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii waa yɛ hei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my maize is ready for harvest if I lost track of the day I planted it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmãa lɛ eshɛ ŋmaa lɛ he? Ni kɛji akɛ mihiɛ kpa gbi ni adu lɛ nɔ hu?

english: While keeping track of days is best, you can check for physical signs such as the leaves turning yellow-brown, the husks drying up, and a tiny black layer forming at the base of the maize kernels.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ gbi lɛ he saji ni aŋmala ashwie shi lɛ ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ moŋ. Obaanyɛ okwɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii tamɔ baai ni miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ-ŋmɔŋ, ŋmɔŋ ni egbi, kɛ ŋmɔŋ bibii ni yɔɔ diŋ. Efeɔ yɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ ashishi.

english: How does tracking my planting schedule help me apply fertilizer at the right time?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ be ni mikɛduɔ nii lɛ sɛɛnyiɛmɔ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni mawo ŋmɔshi nii yɛ be ni sa mli?

english: Crops require specific nutrients at key growth stages, such as two to three weeks after planting; keeping track of days ensures you feed the crop when its roots can best absorb the nutrients.
ga: Tsei biɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa waa pɛ, tamɔ otsii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ sɛɛ beni adu amɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ gbii lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni oha tso lɛ niyenii yɛ be mli ni eshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Can I leave mature maize in the field past its target maturity days if I am busy with other farm tasks?
ga: Ani manyɛ mashi ŋmãa ni eda yɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛho be ni ato akɛ ebaakwɛ lɛ he? Kɛji akɛ mikɛ nitsumɔi krokomɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ deka

english: Leaving ripe crops in the field beyond their maturity timeframe exposes them to weaver birds, grain borers, mold, and rot, which lowers the quality and market value of your harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛho amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe be lɛ he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná okpoi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ. Dumɔwui ni shwieɔ shi, ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ baaha okpamɔ lɛ mli nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ jarayeli jara aba shi.

english: Can I plant two different crops together if they take different amounts of time to mature?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ tsei enyɔ yɛ he kome kɛji amɛhe be srɔtoi ni amɛkɛdaraa?

english: Yes, intercropping crops with different growth timelines works well because you can harvest the fast-maturing crop first, giving the slower crop extra room and sunlight to finish growing.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfutuɔ nibii ni shwereɔ bei srɔtoi yɔɔ mli lɛ ni ooodu lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ obaanyɛ okpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwereɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni daraa blɛoo lɛ naa gbɛ babaoo kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara.

english: How can I tell if my young cocoa trees are getting enough water during the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ miiná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Look at the leaves and topsoil. If leaves remain green and firm, the cocoa tree is healthy. If the leaves turn yellow, droop, or crisp up, and the soil feels like dry dust, your tree needs water or extra shade to survive.
ga: Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ. Kɛji baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo ni amɛyɛ hewalɛ Tsɔɔ akɛ kookoo tso lɛ yɛ hewalɛ. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ, amɛgbeeɔ shi loo amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nuɔ he tamɔ sũ ni egbi. Nu loo hulutsoo babaoo he miihia otsei lɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why is it helpful to cover the soil around my plantain stems with dry leaves and palm fronds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mulching ni bɔleɔ Mi plantain tsei lɛ ahe kɛ baai ni egbi kɛ palm baai lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ.

english: Covering soil with organic material, known as mulching, stops moisture from evaporating under the hot sun, keeps the ground cool, and slowly rots to feed the soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛhaa lɛ akɛ mulching. Enɛ baatsi ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni efiteɔ fiofio koni ekɛ niyenii aha shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetable crops early in the morning or during the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo aduawai anɔ nu leebi loo shwane?

english: Watering early in the morning is best because the soil absorbs the moisture before heat sets in. Afternoon sun evaporates most of the water before plant roots can drink it.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani hulutsoo be lɛ baa, ni hulu lɛ shɛɔ shwane mli lɛ haa nu lɛ fa ko shwieɔ shi dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nuɔ.

english: How do deep roots help big trees like mangoes stay green when there has been no rain for months?
ga: Te shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso agbo ko tamɔ mango lɛ ni ekwɛɔ eŋɔli yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛko nyɔji babaoo lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Deep roots act like deep straws, reaching down into underground water reserves far below the surface long after topsoil has dried out completely.
ga: Shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ jwɛi, ni amɛshɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu jɛɛhei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi shɔŋŋ lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do extension officers advise using small nursery bags to raise seeds before transplanting them to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii bibii atsu nii ni akɛdu dumɔwui dani akɛwo ŋmɔ titri lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Nursery bags protect young seeds from strong heat, weeds, and pests while their roots are small, giving them a strong start before they move to the harsh field.
ga: Grow bags buɔ dumɔwui bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ, jwɛi kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ahe. yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ ji bibii Enɛ haa amɛjeɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ dani amɛyaa ŋmɔji ni hiɛdɔɔ yɔɔ mli amli.

english: Why do my young pepper seedlings burn and look weak when planted in full sunshine without cover?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby pepper dumɔwui lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tender young leaves burn easily under strong sunlight. Giving seedlings light shade for their first few weeks protects them while they build strong roots.
ga: Baai bibii ni darako lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Kɛ́ okɛ hulutsoo wo dumɔwui lɛ anɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe be mli ni amɛwoɔ shishifãi ni wa lɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly into tubes when the afternoon sun becomes very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tsɔnei yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up to protect themselves from intense heat. By rolling up, the plant reduces the leaf surface exposed to the sun and saves water.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa baai shwieɔ shi koni hulutsoo ni fe nine akafee. Kɛtsɔ Tsei ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa baai ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ lɛ anɔ baa shi ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my cassava plants turn yellow and fall off during long dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its lower leaves to reduce water loss when ground is dry. This natural behavior saves energy so the plant roots stay alive until rains return.
ga: Akɛ ŋmei shwieɔ shishigbɛ baai lɛ anɔ koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli subaŋ nɛɛ haa hewalɛ hiɔ shi koni tsei shishifãi ahi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baashɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants collapse and rot on the ground if I do not tie them to wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kɛji mikɛ amɛ fĩii tsei ahe lɛ?

english: Tomato stems are soft and cannot bear the weight of heavy fruits alone. Tying them to wooden stakes keeps leaves and fruit off wet ground, preventing rot and disease.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo aduawai ni tsii lɛ pɛ. Kɛ́ akpɛtɛ tso he lɛ, ebaabu baai kɛ aduawai lɛ ahe koni amɛkatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Etsiɔ fitemɔ kɛ helai anaa

english: What happens to my farm produce if I plant my yam mounds too close together?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji midu ŋmeii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When yam mounds are too close, roots compete with each other for water and soil nutrients, resulting in smaller tubers at harvest time.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii akuu ko bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii baa yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow and curling up during the dry weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔleɔ ehe yɛ otsii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Yellowing and curling leaves are a clear sign that your maize is suffering from heat and lack of moisture. When plants do not get enough water, they cannot pull nutrients from the soil, causing their leaves to dry out and turn yellow to protect themselves.
ga: Yellowing and curling leaves are a clear sign that your corn is suffering from heat and a lack of moisture. Kɛ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ lɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛjie niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ haa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe.

english: Is it better for me to water my tomato crops early in the morning or during the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ nu leebi loo shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: It is much better to water early in the morning because the cool ground allows the roots to absorb water before the sun rises high. Watering in the hot afternoon causes most of the water to evaporate quickly into the air before the plant can drink it.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha nu leebi ejaakɛ he ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu dani hulu lɛ yaa ŋwɛi. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha nu lɛ fa oya kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani tso lɛ anu.

english: Why do my crops rot and die in fields where rainwater stays standing for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ ŋmɔji ni nugbɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ shi gbii babaoo lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air to breathe just like humans do. When water sits on top of your land for days without draining away, it chokes the roots under the soil, causing them to rot and die from lack of oxygen.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Beni nu ta oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo ni ehooo. Ebaatsi shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ anaa. Enɛ haa egboɔ ni egboɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with many leaves but end up with very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi ŋmeii bibii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are planted too close together or get too much nitrogen from leafy manure, they waste all their energy growing tall stems and thick leaves instead of sending food down to grow big tubers in the ground.
ga: Beni adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo enine shɛɔ nitrogen babaoo nɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmei mli. Ebaafite ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛmiida tsei kakadaji kɛ baai ni mli tse lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsu niyenii kɛba shi koni amɛdu bulb agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why are my young cocoa trees dropping their flowers before any pods start forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ miigbee shi dani ŋmeii lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they are stressed by extreme hot sun, prolonged dry weather, or insect attacks. Keeping good shade trees on your farm helps protect the cocoa trees from direct heat so flowers can turn into pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi be kakadaŋŋ. loo kooloi ni baatutua amɛ Kɛ́ okwɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu kookoo tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. koni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ

english: Why do my pepper plants stop producing fruits and stay small when I don't weed around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ kpaɔ yibiiwoo ni ehiɔ shi bibioo beni mikɛ jwɛi shwieee he ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are like greedy neighbours on your farm—they steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients that your pepper plants need to grow big and bear fruit.
ga: Jwɛi tamɔ akutsoŋbii ni hiɛ kɔ̃ɔ mɔ nɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa o-pepper tsei lɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do extension officers tell me not to plant tomatoes on the exact same plot every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔkadu tomato yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting tomatoes in the same spot every year allows soil pests and diseases that attack tomatoes to build up in that ground. Changing the crop to something like maize or beans starves those pests and keeps your soil healthy.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tomato yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ, ebaaha sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa tomato lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ nakai sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaha nakai ŋmãa lɛ aye hɔmɔ, ni ebaaye ebua ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does adding dried chicken manure help my crops produce better yields?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni egbi ni mikɛfataa he lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai?

english: Chicken manure acts like rich food for the earth by adding vital nutrients like nitrogen back into the soil and helping the ground hold water longer, which makes your crops grow greener and produce heavier harvests.
ga: Kooloo ŋmei tsuɔ nii akɛ sũ mli niyenii ni fa babaoo kɛtsɔ niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, ni ekɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ lɛ nɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do people advise me to plant pepper together in the same field with my cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu pepper kɛ cassava yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Mixing pepper with cassava is a smart practice called intercropping. The strong smell of pepper plants can naturally keep certain harmful insects away, and you can harvest pepper quickly while waiting for the cassava to mature.
ga: Pepper kɛ ŋmei ni akɛfutuɔ lɛ ji nifeemɔ ko ni yɔɔ ŋaa ni ale lɛ akɛ intercropping. Pepper tsei lɛ ahe ŋmɔlɔ ni naa wa lɛ baanyɛ aha kooloi bibii komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akabote mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ni obaanyɛ okpa ŋmɔtɔ oya be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ agbɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I buy fresh certified seeds from an input dealer instead of planting seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ kɛjɛ jarayelɔ dɛŋ? Mohu ɔ, i du duwuhi nɛ a yi wami kɛ je ye nyagbe kpami ɔ mi ɔ.

english: Certified seeds are specially tested to resist common plant diseases, grow uniformly, and produce much higher yields than seeds saved from old crops, which naturally lose their vigor and strength over time.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ mli krɛdɛɛ koni ana kɛji amɛnyɛŋ amɛye tsei ahe helai ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ anɔ. Ekwɛ̃ɔ daa ni ehaa yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ tsei momoi amli ni fiteɔ ebɔɔ su hewalɛ kɛ shifimɔ yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of a maize stalk usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, a vital plant food. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps the plant recover its healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua tsei lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without growing into fruit during very hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ aduawai yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages tomato pollen, making it impossible for flowers to fertilize and form fruit. The plant naturally sheds these unfertilized flowers to conserve its remaining water and energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ fiteɔ tomato mli ŋmeii. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɛɛ afɔ ni amɛwo yibii. Tsei shwieɔ nɛkɛ fɔfɔi ni awooo amɛ fɔ nɛɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting in the ground when it rains heavily for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa gbii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater sits on the farm, it suffocates the roots and encourages soil fungi to attack and rot the tubers before harvest.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ewo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛtutua ni amɛfite ŋmeii lɛ dani akpa.

english: Why do I see ragged holes and brown dirt inside the center leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji ni etse kɛ muji ni tsuɔ yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which crawls deep inside the growing funnel of the maize plant during the day to feed safely on tender new leaves.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni shwereɔ kɛboteɔ ŋmei tsei ni miida lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛye baai heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ shweshweeshwe lɛ.

english: How does putting dry grass on top of the soil help my vegetables grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-aduawai lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, called mulching, acts as a blanket that traps soil moisture, keeps roots cool during hot days, stops weeds from growing, and adds plant nutrients as it decays.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni ŋmɛɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni ehaa tso lɛ mli niyenii babaoo yaa hiɛ kɛji efite

english: Groundnut plants have special root nodules that pull nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil. When the groundnuts are harvested, that extra nitrogen stays behind to feed your next crop.
ga: Peanut tsei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Be ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmeii Nakai nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ hiɔ sɛɛ koni ekɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do I need to tie my yam vines to tall sticks instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ sweet potato wain tsei fĩɔ tsei kakadaji ahe lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking holds yam leaves up in the air where they can catch maximum sunlight to manufacture food for big tubers, while also keeping the leaves off damp soil where fungal diseases spread.
ga: Staking hiɛɔ sweet potato baai lɛ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Biɛ ji he ni amɛnáa hulu la babaoo yɛ koni amɛkɛfee niyenii amɛha amɛ bulb agboi lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ, he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he.

english: Why are my plantain leaves turning yellow and drying up even when the ground is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po lɛ?

english: Fungal diseases like Panama disease attack the internal water channels inside the trunk, blocking water from travelling up from the roots to the leaves and causing them to dry out.
ga: Fungal helai tamɔ Panama hela lɛ tutuaa nu gbɛi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekajɛ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛya ŋwɛi kɛya baai lɛ amli ni ehaa amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why is it better to water my pepper garden early in the morning instead of at midday?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mawo mi-pepper abɔɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ leebi moŋ fe shwane mli lɛ?

english: Watering early lets plants drink before the sun gets too hot. Midday watering leads to fast evaporation, wastes water, and cold water on scorching leaves can shock and stress the plants.
ga: Nu ni awoɔ mra Enɛ haa tsei lɛ nuɔ nu dani hulu lɛ mli woɔ la tsɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi oya, nu fɔŋ, kɛ nu ni mli ejɔ ni yɔɔ baai ni eshã lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ he afee shoo ni ehao.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains or cassava next to them provides living shade and keeps the soil moist, helping the cocoa survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains loo cassava, yɛ amɛhe lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eye ebua kookoo ni ehi shi yɛ eshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to put tall wooden stakes next to my yam vines as they start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama emasɛi lɛ? Sweet potato wain tso beni ebɔi edamɔ

english: Yam vines need tall stakes to climb so their leaves can capture plenty of sunlight. Sunshine helps the plant make food, which results in much larger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso kakadaŋŋ ni amɛkɛkwɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ aná hulu la babaoo. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraa kwraa.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over whenever a strong wind blows through my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baatswa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain roots grow close to the surface, making heavy bunches top-heavy. Propping up the stems with strong, forked wooden poles once fruit bunches appear prevents wind from knocking them down.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Ha kuu lɛ afee nɔ ni tsii, nɔ ni tsii. Okɛ tso ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ ato tso lɛ he kɛji aduawai akui je kpo. Ebaaye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ akatswa lɛ shi.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites. Spraying recommended organic or chemical insecticides controls these pests and allows healthy new leaves to unfold.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaye kooloi nɛɛ anɔ ni eye ebua baa heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes inside the middle of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-babi corn tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that destroys young maize. Spraying an approved pesticide directly into the plant's central growing leaf (the funnel) early in the morning or late evening controls them.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ namɔ ni fiteɔ ŋmeii bibii. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie tso lɛ baai (cones) ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaakudɔ amɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water builds up around them in flat or poorly drained soil. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows heavy rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nu ni ekã shi ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ. Anaa amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize crop turning light yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves indicate a lack of nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient needed for leaf growth. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or Urea around the base of the crop restores their green color and vigor.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Nitrogen ni fa babaoo tamɔ NPK loo urea ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ he fɛɛ he Tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ baaha ehiɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when plants suffer heat stress, irregular watering, or excess nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping soil moisture consistent by watering early in the morning helps the blossoms stay attached and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen ni fa fe nine Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my harvested watermelons taste watery instead of sweet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon ni mikpa lɛ ŋɔɔ tamɔ nu moŋ fe nɔ ni ŋɔɔ lɛ?

english: Watermelons lose their sweetness if they receive too much water right before harvest. Reducing watering as the fruits reach full size allows natural sugars to build up inside the fruit.
ga: Watermelon lɛ baafee nɔ ni ŋɔɔ kɛji akɛ enine shɛ nu babaoo nɔ dani akpa. Kɛ́ ajie nu ni akɛhaa lɛ nɔ kɛji aduawai lɛ shɛ egbɔmɔtso lɛ he lɛ, ebaaha adebɔɔ mli sugars lɛ abua aduawai lɛ amli.

english: Why do weeds grow back so quickly on my land even after I clear them with a hoe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miikwɛ̃ oya yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nɛkɛ? Kɛ mikɛ shɔvel jie lɛ po?

english: Hoeing turns over the soil and exposes buried weed seeds to sunlight, causing them to germinate quickly. Covering bare soil with dry grass or mulch blocks sunlight and keeps weed seeds from sprouting.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nitsumɔ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ ni ehaa jwɛi dumɔwui ni afu lɛ shɛɔ hulu la nɔ. Ehaa jwɛi dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ oya Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ha shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi hulu lɛ naa ni ebaatsi jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃.

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to strong, direct heat and lose water faster than their small roots can drink. Planting shade crops like plantains nearby creates a living umbrella that protects the young cocoa until its roots grow strong.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ he waa. ni nu lɛ fiteɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii baanyɛ anu. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ Ehaa hulutsoo baa ni buɔ cacao tso bibioo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ shishifãi lɛ amli waa.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce energy to grow large underground tubers. Staking lifts the vines off the damp ground, exposing leaves to full light while preventing fungal diseases caused by splash-back from the soil.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni oooha amɛná la ni fa babaoo lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ naa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize lacks nitrogen, an essential plant food. The plant moves available nitrogen from its older bottom leaves up to feed new top leaves, causing the bottom ones to turn yellow and dry up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛye ŋwɛi baa heei lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why do extension officers recommend planting cowpeas or groundnuts in the same field with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu cowpeas loo peanuts yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-corn lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts naturally pull nitrogen gas out of the air and put it back into the soil through their roots. Planting them alongside maize helps naturally feed the soil and improves maize yields without using extra fertilizer.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ abɛi ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehaa abele yibiiwoo yaa hiɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi afata he.

english: Why do my crop leaves burn and dry up if I put chemical fertilizer directly against the plant stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ baai lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ kɛji akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer contains concentrated salts that pull water out of plant roots if placed too close. Applying fertilizer a few inches away from the stem allows the plant to safely drink up the nutrients through moist soil.
ga: Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni baajie nu kɛjɛ tsei shishifãi amli kɛji akɛ akɛwo he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi yɛ he ko ni kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ nyɛɔ enuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ nɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are small holes appearing in the center funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Eje kpo yɛ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Holes in the center leaves are typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the whorl and eating the tender leaves. Checking crops early helps catch the caterpillars before they destroy the main growing tip of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fall armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmeii amli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ baa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni amɔmɔ ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛfite tso lɛ naagbee titri ni miida lɛ.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips sucking the juice from the underside of leaves. This sap loss weakens the leaf tissue, causing it to curl up and stunt the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo thrips ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ nu ni laajeɔ nɛɛ haa baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛtsiɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ naa.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when temperatures get too high or water is scarce. Heat stresses the plant, forcing it to shed flowers to conserve water and energy rather than setting new fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ. Dɔlɛ haa tsei haoɔ Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛshwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo yibii heei

english: When heavy rains flood the soil, water displaces the oxygen that cassava roots need to stay healthy. Without air, the buried tubers suffocate and soft rot bacteria quickly attack them.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Nu lɛ yeɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ najiaŋ. Kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ lɛ, ŋmeii ni afu lɛ nyɛŋ amu ni helai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ tutuaa amɛ oya.

english: How does planting my crops right after the first major rain help them grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ mitsei lɛ ni miduɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ?

english: The first rain triggers a natural release of trapped nitrogen and nutrients in the warm, dry soil. Planting right away lets seedlings absorb this quick boost of nutrients, helping them establish strong roots before dry spells return.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa nitrogen kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ ni mli edɔ kɛ egbi mli lɛ jeɔ kpo. Dumɔwui lɛ ni aduɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii ni fa babaoo lɛ oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni wa dani hulutsoo be lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize turning yellow and curling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that your maize is starving for nutrients like nitrogen or suffering from drought stress. When water or plant food is scarce, the crop starves its bottom leaves to keep the top growing leaves alive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli, loo hɔmɔ he haomɔ miipiŋ lɛ. Kɛ nu loo tsei aniyenii faaa lɛ, hɔmɔ yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ koni eha baai ni miida yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ ahi shi.

english: How can I tell if my tomato plants are getting sick before the whole field gets ruined?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-tomato tsei lɛ hela mɔ amɛ dani jɛmɛ fɛɛ akpata?

english: Check your plants every morning for early signs like leaves drooping while the soil is still wet, dark spots forming on stems, or white leaf undersides. Seeing these unusual behaviors early allows you to treat disease before it spreads.
ga: Kwɛmɔ tsei lɛ amli daa leebi koni ona mra be mli okadii, tamɔ baai ni gbeeɔ shi be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo lɛ. Ayɛ ŋmeii diji yɛ tso lɛ nɔ. loo baa yɛŋ lɛ shishi Sui ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ nɛɛ ni onaa mra Ehaa onyɛɔ otsaa hela dani egbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under strong direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast with wide leaves that act like broad umbrellas, giving cocoa seedlings the soft shade and cool moisture they need to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi lɛ oya. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela ni mli kwɔlɔ. Enɛ haa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ naa hulutsoo ni mli jɔ kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why are my pepper plants growing tall and thin instead of producing bushy branches and fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ daa ni efeɔ mlɛo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ehiɛ niji kɛ aduawai akui lɛ?

english: When pepper plants do not get direct sunlight, they put all their energy into stretching upwards to search for light. This leaves them tall, weak, and without enough strength to grow fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ pepper tso lɛ nine shɛɛɛ hulu la nɔ tɛ̃ɛ Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ ŋwɛi ni amɛkpãa mli koni amɛtao la. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, amɛdara, amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛbɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaawo yibii.

english: How do I know if my cassava crop is receiving too much rain water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava tsei lɛ miiná nugbɔ babaoo?

english: If soil stays soaked for too long, cassava leaves will turn yellow and fall off, and the stem base will feel soft. Too much standing water drowns the roots, causing the tubers under the ground to rot.
ga: Kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ewo nu be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, Cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi. ni tso lɛ shishi lɛ baanu he akɛ eyɛ blɛoo Nu ni damɔ shi babaoo lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my crops produce much smaller harvests when I plant them on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kwraa beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Crops feed on specific nutrients in the dirt. Planting the same crop in the same soil season after season completely drains those specific nutrients, leaving the soil tired and unable to feed new crops properly.
ga: Tsei yeɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nakai niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ fɛɛ ajɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɔɔ ni enyɛɛɛ eye ebua tsei heei jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant multiple maize seeds right next to each other in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii babaoo ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Seeds planted too closely fight each other for the same water, soil food, and sunlight. Because they are competing, all the plants remain thin and weak, producing tiny cobs instead of large ones.
ga: Dumɔwui ni adu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa. Ejaakɛ amɛkɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ. No hewɔ lɛ tsei lɛ fɛɛ tee nɔ amɛfee mlɛo ni amɛgbɔjɔ. ni kɛ cob bibioo baa Yɛ ŋmɔtɔ agbo najiaŋ

english: Why do weeds stop my yam vines from growing big leaves even when it rains heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi tsiɔ mi sweet potato tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ baai wuji yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that drink the water and steal the fertilizer meant for your crops. They crowd out your crop's roots under the ground, starving your yam of nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ basabasa ni nuɔ nu ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa onibii. Amɛmiimiɔ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Enɛ haa niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ faaa.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme hot dry weather or a lack of water. Dropping flowers is the plant's way of conserving energy to survive harsh conditions.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ nɔ ko tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ loo nu ni bɛ lɛ kpe. Fɔfɔi ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni tso tsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ hewalɛ toɔ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli.

english: Why do the leaves of my cowpea plants have a white powder on them and dry up early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea baai lɛ yɛ powda yɛŋ ni amɛgbiɔ oya lɛ?

english: The white powder is a common fungal disease called powdery mildew that thrives in warm, humid weather. It covers the leaf surface and blocks the crop from drinking in sunlight, causing leaves to dry and die.
ga: Pauda yɛŋ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew ni yaa hiɛ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Ehaa baa lɛ nɔ ni ehaaa tso lɛ anu hulu la. Ehaa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: What is a liquid foliar spray, and how does it help my crops grow better than regular soil fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni ji nu ni akɛshwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ eyeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ fe shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ?

english: Foliar spray is liquid plant food that you spray directly onto the leaves rather than putting into the soil. Leaves absorb nutrients much faster than roots, giving your crops a quick boost of energy and health, especially when the soil is poor or very dry.
ga: Foliar sprays ji tso niyenii ni ji nu ni okɛshwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ shwieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe shishifãi lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa hewalɛ kɛ hewalɛ oya. Titri lɛ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii loo edɔ waa.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant lacks essential nutrients in the soil, particularly nitrogen. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or foliar spray restores their green color, allowing the leaves to absorb sunlight and produce good corn yields.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ wo mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ ekoŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛŋɔɔ hulu la ni amɛwoɔ ŋmãa kpakpa.

english: When crops receive too much nitrogen, they put all their energy into growing tall stems and big leaves instead of tubers. Using a balanced fertilizer that contains phosphorus and potassium encourages the plant to direct its energy into expanding the tubers underground.
ga: Kɛ tsei nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ tsei ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai wuji ni amɛkwɛɔ lɛ ahe nii moŋ fe ni amɛbaakwɛ bulbs. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja ni phosphorus kɛ potassium yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ewoɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛwo bulbs yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that dry out and burn under direct hot sunlight. Plantain trees grow fast and have large leaves that act like umbrellas, providing the shade and humidity cocoa trees need during their first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli egbiɔ ni amɛshãa. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ha kookoo tso lɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops curl up and droop during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plants curl their leaves in intense afternoon heat to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun and prevent water loss. If the leaves recover by evening, it is a normal protective response, but if they stay limp, the plants need watering or soil moisture protection.
ga: Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ shwane latsaa ni naa wa lɛ mli koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi ni ekɛtsi nu ni elaaje lɛ naa. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ he wa amɛ yɛ gbɛkɛ mli lɛ Abuɔ lɛ akɛ eji hebuu hetoo ni sa. Shi kɛji akɛ baai lɛ egbɔjɔ lolo lɛ, ehe miihia ni awo tsei lɛ nu loo abu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he.

english: How does spreading dry grass around the bottom of my crops help them survive dry weather?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he fɛɛ he Te miŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like a protective blanket against the hot sun. It keeps the soil cool and stops groundwater from evaporating quickly, helping your crops stay hydrated longer.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ atade ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ shwieɔ oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa otsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why does water sit on top of my field for days after heavy rain instead of soaking down into the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu shwieɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli gbii babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Water pooling on the surface means your soil is tightly packed or heavy with clay, making it hard for water to reach plant roots. Digging the soil to loosen it and mixing in compost creates space for air and allows water to soak in properly.
ga: Nu ni buaa ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ loo eyɛ shikpɔŋ sũ ni tsii. Enɛ haa ewaa akɛ nu baashɛ tsei shishifãi ahe. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni akuɔ koni ajie lɛ ni akɛfutu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ náa gbɛ ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are there tiny white powder spots spreading across the leaves of my vegetables?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ powda bibii yɛŋ yɔɔ lɛ? egbɛ eshwa mi-vegetable lɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ

english: White powdery spots are caused by a fungal infection called powdery mildew, which develops in warm, humid weather. Removing affected leaves early and spraying with recommended remedies keeps the fungus from spreading to the rest of your farm.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Enɛ baa mli yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ, ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ. Ni ajieɔ baai ni ena hela lɛ mra Ni akɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛbaatsu nii lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli hei krokomɛi lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava leaves growing small, twisted, and yellowish green instead of large and flat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ji bibii nɛkɛ? Atsɔ mli kɛtee ŋmɔŋ-ŋmɔŋ su mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee agbo ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Twisted and pale leaves are a classic sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried from plant to plant by small insects called whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava stem varieties is the most effective way to protect your farm.
ga: Twisted and pale leaves are classic signs of cassava mosaic disease. ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ woɔ kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa ekroko nɔ lɛ. Kasava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ adumɔ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ oŋmɔ lɛ he.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they suffer from sudden heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of vital plant food. Keeping the soil moisture steady and providing essential nutrients helps the flowers stay attached and form fruits.
ga: Tomato plants will drop their flowers when they suffer from sudden heat stress. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa loo tsei niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why does the fertilizer I put on my soil sometimes just sit there instead of being taken up by my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Soil needs the right moisture and healthy texture to absorb nutrients. If the soil is too dry, too hard, or overloaded with chemicals, plants cannot soak them up, leaving nutrients wasted on top.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔtɔ ni sa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ koni enyɛ eŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ, ewa tsɔ, loo tsofai babaoo yɛ mli lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ aŋɔ amɛ. ni oshi niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii yɛ nɔ

english: Can putting too many chemicals into my soil end up damaging my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ afite kookoo tso lɛ?

english: Yes, excess chemicals that plants cannot absorb can build up in the soil, burn plant roots, and create harsh conditions that make crops weak and susceptible to rotting.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni fa fe nine ni tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ lɛ baanyɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli, ni amɛshã tsei lɛ ashishifãi, ni ekɛ shihilɛi ni esaaa aba ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi oya.

english: How can I tell if my farm land is healthy enough to feed my cocoa trees properly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua cacao tsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Healthy soil is moist, dark, and rich in organic matter. Hard or chemical-heavy soil will reject water and fertilizers, starving your cocoa trees and letting plants decay.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kpakpa mli efɔ, eyɛ ediŋŋ, ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo shikpɔŋ ni tsofai eyi mli obɔ lɛ baakpoo nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ cacao tsei lɛ ni ehaa tsei lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Pod rot is usually caused by fungal diseases that thrive in damp, dark environments and spread when leftover crop waste or unabsorbed chemicals lie rotting in the soil under the trees.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ, ni duŋ yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela baa. Ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ loo tsofai ni anyɛɛɛ aŋɔ mli lɛ kã sũ ni yɔɔ tsei ashishi lɛ mli.

english: If rotten pods lie on the ground under my trees, can they make the fresh cocoa pods up on the tree rot too?
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii ni egboi kã mitso lɛ shishi Ani ŋmeii heei ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ hu baanyɛ agbo?

english: Yes, fungi and pests live in rotting plant matter on the ground. Rain droplets bounce off the rotting ground waste and splash disease spores back up onto healthy pods on the tree.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui hiɔ tsei ni egboi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ jwɛi ni egbo lɛ nɔ ni helai ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai shwieɔ shi ekoŋŋ kɛyaa tsei ahe ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ.

english: What simple farm practices can prevent my cocoa pods from decaying before harvest?
ga: Gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo Mɛɛ ŋmɔ baanyɛ atsĩ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite dani akpa?

english: Clearing fallen rotten pods from the ground, pruning branches to let in sunlight, and maintaining proper chemical application schedules keep fungal rot away.
ga: Jiemɔ ŋmeii ni egboi ni egbee shi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei aniji koni hulu la ashɛ he. ni amɛkwɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔtoo ni sa nɔ koni ŋmeii akafite.

english: Why does sitting water or unabsorbed liquid on my farm land cause my crops to rot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni damɔ shi loo nu ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifite lɛ?

english: Trapped liquids reduce oxygen in the soil, suffocating crop roots and creating damp conditions where rot-causing fungi thrive and attack the cocoa.
ga: Nu ni amɔmɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni ekɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ aba he ni ŋmeii ni kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ daa ni amɛtutuaa kookoo lɛ.

english: How does spraying my cocoa trees actually help the pods grow stronger?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ cacao tsei ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ mli waɔ?

english: Proper spraying delivers protective fungicides and nutrients directly to the leaves and pods, preventing disease outbreaks and strengthening the outer shell of the pods.
ga: Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ ŋmeii kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ yaa baai lɛ kɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Tsiɔ helai ni baa lɛ anaa ni ehaa pod lɛ kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ mli waa

english: Why is it important to spray my cocoa trees in a specific way rather than just splashing chemicals everywhere?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afɔ cacao tsei anɔ yɛ gbɛ pɔtɛɛ ko nɔ lɛ? Yɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ he fɛɛ he lɛ najiaŋ?

english: Proper spraying techniques ensure the chemical coats the pods and trunks where diseases hide, while preventing excess chemicals from washing into the soil and causing damage.
ga: Gbɛi ni sa ni atsɔɔ nɔ ashwieɔ tsofai lɛ anɔ lɛ haa tsofai lɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe yɛ he ni hela yɔɔ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaaa tsofai ni fa fe nine lɛ akabote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni efite nii.

english: What gives cocoa pods the strength they need to mature fully without falling or rotting early?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛgbeee shi loo amɛgbooo oya?

english: Pods grow strong when the tree gets clean soil nutrients, plenty of sunlight, and regular direct spraying to shield them against fungal infections.
ga: Pods lɛ daa waa kɛji tso lɛ nine shɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse nɔ. Na hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni okɛshwie nɔ tɛ̃ɛ daa koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akamɔ bo.

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves during dry spells like the Harmattan to conserve water. Providing shade trees helps protect them from harsh sunlight and reduces water loss so they stay green longer.
ga: Cocoa tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli tamɔ Harmattan koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Shading buɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he ni ehaa nu ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi eŋɔli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Yellow maize leaves are a common sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Nitrogen is essential for building strong leaves and roots, so adding organic manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps restore healthy growth.
ga: Abɛi baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ji okadi ni afɔɔ namɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen he miihia waa kɛha baai kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots need well-drained soil to breathe. Excess standing water chokes the root system and promotes fungal growth, which rots the tubers before harvest.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ he hiaa cassava shishifãi koni amɛmu. Nu ni damɔ shi fe nine lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ daa. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ agbo dani akpa.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce small bunches when I leave many shoots growing around the main plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ miikwɛ̃ bibii bibii lɛ? Beni ashiɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ tso titri lɛ he lɛ

english: Extra shoots, known as suckers, steal water and nutrients from the main stem. Removing all but two or three healthy suckers allows the main plant to put full energy into growing larger fruit bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ, juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ, ja enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ lɛ, tso titri lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo yibii wuji.

english: Legumes like cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When left in the field, they naturally fertilize the soil for crops like maize that need lots of nitrogen.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji ashi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ Amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa ni he hiaa nitrogen babaoo lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why is it bad to grow maize on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously depletes specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases tailored to that crop to build up in the field over time.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. Ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni etsake amɛhe amɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that targets the growing center (whorl) of maize plants. Spotting them early allows you to use appropriate control methods before they destroy the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni tswaa ŋmãa tsei lɛ adalɛ hei (rings) lɛ. Amɛtaomɔ mra Enɛ baaha okɛ gbɛi ni sa ni oootsɔ nɔ okudɔ amɛ lɛ atsu nii dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Tomato plants shed flowers when temperatures get too high, when water supply is uneven, or when the soil lacks nutrients like calcium during the flowering phase.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tamɔ calcium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli.

english: Why does fertilizer give my neighbor a huge harvest but doesn't seem to work as well on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii haa mikutsoŋbii lɛ yibii babaoo shi etamɔ nɔ ni etsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Soils differ from field to field. Fertilizer only works well if it provides the specific nutrients your soil is missing and if it is applied at the right time with sufficient soil moisture.
ga: Esoro shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔ mli. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ pɛ kɛji akɛ amɛha niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ lɛ. Ni kɛji akɛ akɛwo mli yɛ be ni sa mli ni ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to produce less yield even if I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awo yibii babaoo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and absorb the fertilizer, water, and sunlight first, effectively starving your crops before they can mature fully.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛheɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la klɛŋklɛŋ. Enɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ dani amɛshɛ shweremɔ he.

english: When maize leaves turn yellow starting at the bottom leaves and moving upward, it usually means the soil is running out of nitrogen. Nitrogen is the primary nutrient crops need to stay green and grow strong, so applying manure or a nitrogen-based fertilizer will fix this.
ga: Kɛji ŋmãa baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ nitrogen fee lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaatsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil. Planting them after heavy-feeding crops like maize naturally restores soil fertility for the next season.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Nibii nɛɛ ni aduɔ yɛ kooloi aniyenii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo ekoŋŋ kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: This damage is usually caused by fall armyworms, which hide deep inside the growing center of the maize plant. You can manage them early by applying recommended insecticides or putting clean sand mixed with neem seed powder directly into the leaf center.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji fall flukes, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ dalɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ mli. Obaanyɛ otsu he nii mra. Kɛ tsofa ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni awieɔ he lɛ atsu nii loo okɛ ŋã ni he tse ni akɛ neem dumɔwu powda efutu mli lɛ afata tso lɛ teŋgbɛ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them in wet soil for too long. Planting your cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows heavy rainwater to drain away so the tubers stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu ni nɛɔ waa lɛ atsɔ mli. Koni yitso lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Young cocoa seedlings are fragile and burn easily under strong, direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa creates living umbrellas that shelter the young plants until they grow stronger.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ haa ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ tsei bibii ahe lɛ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to make food for their underground tubers. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet ground so they can catch maximum sunlight while protecting the leaves from soil-borne damp diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Staking woɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni eha amɛná hulu la babaoo yɛ be mli ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ helai ni ŋmɔtɔ jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants without forming fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii miiho kɛmiijɛ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience high heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of key nutrients in the soil. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the flowers stay on and form fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe hulutsoo ni naa wa waa he. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo niyenii mli nibii titrii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni afeɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Is it better for me to water my pepper garden in the morning or during the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi-pepper abɔɔ lɛ mli nu leebi loo shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: It is best to water early in the morning so the plants can absorb moisture before the sun gets strong. Watering in the afternoon heat wastes water through rapid evaporation and can stress hot leaves.
ga: Esa akɛ afee nu leebi maŋkpa bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani hulu lɛ mli awa tsɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ shwane latsaa mli lɛ baafite nu lɛ yɛ la ni hoɔ oya lɛ hewɔ. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ haomɔ aba baai ni mli edɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than my regular crops after clearing the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi tsei ni mikwɛɔ daa lɛ beni ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are hardy wild plants designed to sprout rapidly whenever rain hits bare soil. Planting your crops at the recommended distance helps their leaves close together quickly, blocking sunlight from reaching weed seeds in the ground.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni afee koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ baashɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ni atsɔɔ akɛ amɛdu lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe oya. Etsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ jwɛi dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Which suckers should I remove from my plantain trees to get bigger bunches?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmeii esa akɛ majie kɛjɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli koni maná ŋmeii agbo?
