english: You should keep only 2 or 3 healthy 'sword suckers' (suckers with thin, narrow leaves) per tree and cut off the rest. Having too many stems forces the parent plant to share nutrients, resulting in smaller plantain bunches.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ ‘klante tsei’ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ 2 loo 3 pɛ ato tso kome nɔ ni ofo nɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ shishifãi babaoo yɛ lɛ, enyɛɔ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ aha. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantains lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die when I cut down all the large shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tso bibioo lɛ gbo beni mifolɔ tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct sunlight because harsh sunshine burns their leaves and dries out the soil; they need shade trees like plantains or forest trees to keep them cool and retain soil moisture.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo koo mli tsei koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ajɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Cassava naturally drops leaves or turns yellow to save water when rain stops, but if you notice tiny webs on the underside, it could also be spider mites attacking the plant during dry spells.
ga: Cassava baagbee shi loo ebaatsɔ ŋmɔŋ koni ekɛbu nu he kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa. Shi kɛji ona ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ, ebaanyɛ efee ŋmeii ni tutuaa tso lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: What causes small green worms to eat the leaves in the center of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ yeɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Those are Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that attacks young maize shoots; catching them early and applying recommended organic or chemical sprays in the morning can save your crop.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni tutuaa ŋmãa bibii lɛ. Mɔ amɛ mra. Ni kɛ́ okɛ tsofai ni akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ shwie nɔ leebi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ehere oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayiwala.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over right when the fruits are getting big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛji aduawai lɛ bɔi kwɛ̃mɔ pɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and the stems are soft, so heavy fruit bunches pull the tree down; propping up the stem with strong bamboo or wooden poles prevents the heavy plant from falling in wind.
ga: Plantain shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ blɛoo Yibii akui ni tsii lɛ gbala tso lɛ kɛba shi. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei loo tso ni wa fiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ ni tsii lɛ naa koni ekagbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: If I plant maize on the same piece of land every year, why does my harvest keep getting smaller?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi Mɛni hewɔ mi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ miiba shi lɛ?

english: Maize uses up a lot of nutrients from the ground; planting legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts after maize puts nitrogen back into the soil and restores its fertility naturally.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eha adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without turning into any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the plants get irregular water, which causes stress and prevents proper pollination.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ afɔɔɔ tsei lɛ nu jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli ni ehaaa pollination ni sa aba.

english: Why do I need to guide my yam vines to climb on long sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsɔ sweet potato wain tso ko hiɛ koni makwɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines on sticks allows the leaves to get plenty of sunlight to make food, which helps build large and healthy yam tubers under the ground.
ga: Kɛ́ awó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ naa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaahoo nii. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa baa shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my vegetables with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ jwɛi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, keeps the soil cool, stops water from evaporating in the sun, and prevents weeds from growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekafee ŋmɔtɔ kɛji hulu la shɛ enɔ. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: When is the best time to apply fertilizer so that it does not wash away in the rain?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni nugbɔ akashwie nɔ?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is damp but not during heavy rainfall, and cover it slightly with soil so the nutrients stay near the roots instead of being washed away.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi jeee yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Ni okɛ sũ fioo aha nɔ koni niyenii mli hewalɛ ahi shishifãi lɛ ahe moŋ fe ni oooho.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or thrips, or by a plant virus transmitted by whiteflies that damages the new leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei amli helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ ni fiteɔ baai heei lɛ kɛbaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is the government encouraging us to replace our old cocoa trees with new seed varieties?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nɔyeli lɛ miiwo wɔ hewalɛ koni wɔkɛ dumɔwui heei awo kookoo tsei momoi lɛ anajiaŋ lɛ?

english: Old or diseased trees gradually lose their ability to produce many pods. New high-yielding hybrid varieties grow faster, resist common diseases better, and produce significantly more cocoa pods on less land.
ga: Tsei ni egbɔ loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ baafee fiofio Hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaawo ŋmeii babaoo Tsei srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ daa oya. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa kookoo ŋmeii babaoo baa yɛ he ko ni faaa.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa plants turn yellow and dry up when I plant them in full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to harsh sunlight and heat. Planting shade crops like plantains around them protects their leaves from scorching and keeps the soil cool and moist until the trees mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli tamɔ plantains yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ yibii lɛ akashã, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛyashi tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does a disease on one cocoa tree quickly spread to the healthy trees around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ hela ko ni yɔɔ kookoo tso kome nɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ anɔ lɛ? mra oya

english: Many crop diseases, such as Cocoa Swollen Shoot virus, are carried from tree to tree by tiny insects like mealybugs, meaning an infected tree acts as a source of infection for neighboring healthy trees.
ga: Tsei ahe helai babaoo, tamɔ Cocoa Swollen Shoot virus lɛ, jɛɔ tso nɔ kɛyaa tso nɔ kɛtsɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ mealybugs nɔ, ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ baanyɛ afee hela jɛɛhe kɛha tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ.

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers if the flowers are not pollinated by tiny insects, or if the tree is stressed by drought or lack of nutrients and cannot support the energy needed to grow all the pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii efɔɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. aloo kɛji akɛ hɔmɔ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ miigba tso lɛ naa ni enyɛɛɛ eye ebua hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni ekɛ ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to cut off extra branches from my cocoa tree if I want more fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo cacao tso lɛ niji krokomɛi kɛji miitao aduawai babaoo lɛ?

english: Pruning removes unnecessary branches and suckers so sunlight and air can reach the tree canopy, allowing the plant to direct its energy into producing flowers and healthy pods.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji kɛ ŋmeii ni he ehiaaa lɛ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ anyɛ ayashɛ tsei lɛ ayiteŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ fɔfɔii ni wa kɛ ŋmeii.

english: When plants are overcrowded, they compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, causing them to stretch upward for light rather than building thick stems and growing heavy fruits.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Ha amɛgbala amɛhe koni amɛmɔ kane lɛ. Mohu ɔ, e peeɔ tsohi nɛ a mi wa nɛ e woɔ yiblii nɛ mi wa.

english: High humidity and continuous rain create a wet environment where black pod fungal disease thrives and spreads quickly from pod to pod across the farm.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ haa shihilɛ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Black pod fungus hela lɛ daa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ pod mli kɛyaa pod mli yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil has lost its nutrients and needs fertilizer for my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ efo mli ni ehe miihia ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Soil missing nutrients shows through yellowed leaves, slow crop growth, small fruit sizes, and declining harvests even when rainfall is good.
ga: Niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baatsɔɔ baai lɛ ni baafee ŋmɔŋ lɛ nɔ. tso lɛ dalɛ blɛoo Yibii lɛ ji bibioo. ni nibii ni afeɔ lɛ ba shi eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ kpakpa nɛ moŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I transplant young cocoa seedlings into the farm during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mijieɔ cacao tsei bibii kɛyaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young seedlings have short root systems that cannot reach deep underground water, so dry winds and strong heat during the dry season will quickly dry out and kill them.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi kukuji ni nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ haa amɛgbiɔ oya ni egbeɔ amɛ.

english: If I switch to an improved government-recommended cocoa variety, will it need the exact same care as my traditional trees?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ mitsake kɛtee kookoo henɔi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ taakɛ nɔyeli lɛ wo ŋaa lɛ hu? Ani ebaabi ni akwɛ mi nɔ tamɔ bɔ ni akwɛ mi shishijee tso lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Improved varieties produce much higher yields, but they require proper spacing, regular weed control, and adequate soil nutrients to reach their full production potential.
ga: Henɔi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo kwraa. Shi he ni jɛkɛmɔ ni sa he miihia amɛ. Jwɛi nɔkwɛmɔ daa kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni enyɛ ewo yibii babaoo

english: Yellow leaves at the base of maize plants usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves turn deep green and store energy to produce healthy cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ni mli kwɔ ni ekɛ hewalɛ toɔ koni ekɛwo ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct, harsh sunlight and intense heat. Shade trees act like protective umbrellas, keeping the soil moist and protecting the tender cocoa leaves from burning.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo baai ni mli tse lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he.

english: Tomato plants often drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the plant hold onto its flowers so fruit can form.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ amɛkɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be mli lɛ kpe. Kɛ́ oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɔ́ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni emɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli ni ewo yibii.

english: Yam leaves need to spread out in sunlight to produce energy that feeds the growing tuber underground. Staking holds the vines up toward the light and keeps them off the damp ground where diseases spread.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato baai lɛ agbɛ ashwã hulu la mli koni ekɛ hewalɛ ni haa ŋmeii ni miida lɛ niyenii lɛ aba. Staking haa wain tso lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi kɛyaa la he ni ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ji he ni helai shwereɔ yɛ lɛ he.

english: When heavy rain leaves standing water in flat soil, the roots cannot breathe and fungi easily infect the tubers. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges lets excess water drain away to prevent rot.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu lɛ kpɛɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ tɛtrɛɛ lɛ nɔ. Shishifãi nyɛɛɛ amu ni ŋmei lɛ yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ oya. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa koni ekɛtsi fitemɔ naa.

english: Why do plantain trees fall over so easily when they carry fruit during high winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ amɛwo yibii yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa be mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots and get very heavy at the top when bearing fruit. Supporting the main stem with strong wooden props prevents the plant from snapping or uprooting in strong winds.
ga: Plantains shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛhe wa waa yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ kɛji amɛwo yibii. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni wa fĩ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ akakumɔ loo eshishijee yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Why does planting cowpeas together with my corn make the corn grow stronger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ du tsina ŋmãa lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ mli waa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans gather nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When grown alongside corn, they share this natural fertilizer through the soil, making the corn stronger without extra cost.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans buaa nitrogen naa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ adu kɛ ŋmãa lɛ Amɛbaajara adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa nɛɛ kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa ŋmãa waa ni ekɛ shika kroko fataaa he

english: Why are tiny green worms eating the deep inside leaves of my young corn stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miiye mi-bibii ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: These green worms are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that targets young corn leaves. Checking the central leaves early and applying approved pest treatments kills them before they ruin the central shoot.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii eŋɔli nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmei baai bibii lɛ anɔ. Baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Ni gbɛ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛgbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baagbe nakai baa lɛ dani baa ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ afite.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or mites that hide under the leaves and transmit plant viruses. Controlling these insects early stops the leaves from twisting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. Ekɛ ehe teeɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni egbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa tso lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Enɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ akafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and plant food in the soil. Clearing weeds early leaves all the water and nutrients in the soil solely for your crops to grow big and strong.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eshiɔ nu kɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ koni onibii lɛ adara ni amɛhe awa.

english: Why are my maize leaves curling up and turning yellow when the afternoon sun gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ shwane hulu lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up during hot afternoon sun to protect themselves from losing too much water. If they turn yellow, it means the intense heat and dry soil are preventing the plant from absorbing the nutrients it needs from the ground.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ fe nine lɛ he. Kɛji etsɔ ŋmɔŋ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ tsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my garden egg plants look wilted in the afternoon even when I water them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbo yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: In the intense hot sun, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it from the soil. This causes temporary wilting during peak heat, but the leaves usually recover in the evening as the sun cools down.
ga: Yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa amɛgboɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ. Shi bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ beni hulu lɛ mli ejɔ lɛ.

english: What causes my pepper plant flowers to drop off during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: When the sun beats down too hard and heat is extreme, pepper plants drop their flowers to save energy and stay alive instead of spending resources on growing fruits.
ga: Kɛ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi waa ni latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛhi wala mli moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ nibii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ baatsu nii kɛdu aduawai.

english: Why are the leaves on my yam vines turning brown and dry on very hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbiɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Bare, unshaded ground gets extremely hot, which bakes the root zone and burns the delicate yam vines. Using dry grass to cover the mounds (mulching) keeps the roots cool and protects the vines from burning.
ga: Hei ni bɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni hulutsoo bɛ lɛ baanyɛ afee dɔlɛ waa. Enɛ baashã shishifã lɛ he lɛ ni eshã sweet potato wain tso ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa gɔŋ lɛ nɔ (mulch) lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa wain tso lɛ shãaa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in an open field without any trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso bibioo lɛ gbo beni midu yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei kwraa bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to direct sunlight and heavy rain. Without shade trees or nurse crops like plantains to shield them from the scorching sun, their young leaves burn and the plants dry out.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he waa. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa loo tsei ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ tamɔ plantains ni baabu he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he lɛ bɛ lɛ, Amɛbaai bibii lɛ baashã ni tso lɛ baagbo.

english: Why do my cassava plants shed all their leaves when the long dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai fɛɛ fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava naturally drops its leaves during hot dry spells as a survival mechanism to conserve moisture in its stem and roots, and it will sprout fresh leaves as soon as the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli akɛ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehiɔ shi koni ekɛha ŋmɔtɔ ahi tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli. Ni baai heei baakwɛ̃ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ pɛ.

english: Does direct hot sunlight hurt my cowpea crop if there are no trees around?
ga: Ani hulu la ni mli edɔ ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaye mi-cowpea tso lɛ awui kɛji tsei bɛ he ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Cowpeas like sunshine, but extreme scorching heat without soil moisture causes them to mature too quickly and produce small, weak pods. Covering the soil with organic matter helps retain moisture under direct sun.
ga: Cowpea sumɔɔ hulu la. Shi la ni tsoɔ waa ni nu bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ daa oya tsɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: How does heavy rainfall damage my tomato plants if they are fully exposed in the open field?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baafite mi-tomato tsei lɛ eha tɛŋŋ kɛji amɛná hulu ni yeɔ emuu yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse mli?

english: Heavy rains splash soil onto tomato leaves, which spreads diseases like blight, while excessive water and sudden rain after heat cause the ripening tomato fruits to split open.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa sũ shwieɔ tomato baai anɔ. Enɛ gbɛɔ helai tamɔ late blight gbɛɔ eshwaa, yɛ be mli ni nu babaoo kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa yɛ hulutsoo be sɛɛ lɛ haa tomato yibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ tswaa.

english: Plantains have shallow roots that become loose and weak in rain-soaked soil. When heavy wind and rain hit exposed plants, the heavy fruit bunches pull the entire tree down unless supported with wooden props.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni shwieɔ shi ni egbɔjɔ yɛ shikpɔji ni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo yɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ tswa tsei lɛ Yibii akui ni tsii baagbala tso muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛba shi. ja akɛ tso ni akɛtsuɔ nii

english: Why do weeds grow so fast and choke my crops after a short rain followed by hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni efiteɔ miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ lɛ? Ani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ?

english: Weeds are native wild plants that adapt much faster to harsh sun and sudden rain than cultivated crops, allowing them to quickly suck up water and block sunshine from reaching your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni hulu la ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ nyɛɔ amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Enɛ haa amɛmɔɔ nu oya, ni etsĩɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient the plant needs to build strong green leaves. It can also happen when heavy rains wash away soil nutrients or when water stays trapped around the roots for too long.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ eŋɔli. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ loo kɛ́ nu ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: How do I know when my cassava stems are ready to be harvested under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmeii lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Most improved cassava varieties mature between 9 to 12 months after planting. You can tell they are ready when the lower leaves start to turn yellow and fall off, and the soil around the base of the main stem begins to crack as the tubers swell.
ga: Cassava henɔi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ateŋ babaoo daa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ amɛfee klalo beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni bulb lɛ mli fũuɔ lɛ.

english: Why do some of my plantain shoots grow very weak and take too long to bear fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ekomɛi bɛ hewalɛ waa ni amɛheɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Plantain shoots grow weak when too many suckers are allowed to sprout from the same mother plant, causing them to compete for sunlight and food. Cutting away extra suckers and leaving only two or three strong ones allows the plant to put its energy into growing big fruit bunches.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ ahe baajɔ kɛji akɛ aŋmɛ tsei babaoo gbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ kɛjɛ fɔlɔ tso kome mli. Enɛ haa amɛshiɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii he akaŋ. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashi ŋmeii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ yibii wuji amli.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or beans in the same field alongside my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi?

english: Legumes like cowpeas capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. When grown alongside or right after maize, they act as natural fertilizer, restoring nutrients to the soil for your maize without buying expensive chemicals.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ adu yɛ ŋmãa masɛi loo esɛɛ Amɛbaatsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa. Ye obua ni okɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha o-ŋmãa lɛ ni okɛ tsofai ni jara wa aheee.

english: What is eating small ragged holes into the leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni miiye buji bibii ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ amli ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Ragged holes in maize leaves are typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central funnel of the plant. Checking your farm early in the morning and applying neem oil extract or recommended sprays can protect your crop before severe damage occurs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ faa lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmei baa lɛ mli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli leebi ni okɛ neem fɔ ni ajieɔ yi loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ ebu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe dani efite waa.

english: Curled leaves with yellowish-green patches are signs of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies or by using infected stem cuttings. Planting disease-resistant stem varieties provided by extension services is the most effective way to prevent this.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadii. Egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔ ŋmeii bibii loo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ nɔ. Gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ enɛ naa ji tsei srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe lɛ adumɔ kɛtsɔ sɛɛkuu nitsumɔi anɔ.

english: Can I save seeds from this year's hybrid maize harvest to plant again next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ afi nɛɛ hybrid ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ ato koni madu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: It is not recommended to replant seeds saved from hybrid maize crops because second-generation hybrid seeds lose their vigor and produce much smaller yields. Buying fresh, certified seeds every season ensures your field produces full, uniform maize cobs.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa mli lɛ dumɔ ekoŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, yinɔ ni ji enyɔ ni ji hybrid dumɔwui lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo kwraa. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ ni ooohe daa be lɛ haa oŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ baaná ŋmãa ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko.

english: Why do my plantain plants fall over so easily before the fruit bunch is even mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya dani aduawai akui lɛ po daa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems and heavy stems, making them easy targets for strong seasonal winds once the fruit starts growing. Supporting the main stem with a sturdy bamboo pole tied below the bunch prevents the plant from snapping or uprooting.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni tsii. Enɛ haa efeɔ nɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni baa yɛ be mli lɛ baanyɛ atswa lɛ oya beni aduawai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei tso ni wa ni akɛfi tso lɛ shishi lɛ fi tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakumɔ loo eshishijee.

english: Cassava roots rot when the ground becomes waterlogged because roots need oxygen from the soil to stay healthy. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away from the root zone.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni jɛɔ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds from my crop farm within the first few weeks of planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni mikɛdu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During the first four to six weeks, young crops are too small to compete with aggressive weeds for water, fertilizer, and sunlight. Keeping the field clear during this early window allows your crops to grow strong roots and gain a lead over weeds.
ga: Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii ejwɛ kɛyashi enumɔ lɛ mli lɛ, tsei bibii lɛ daraaa tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni wa lɛ abɔ akaŋ kɛha nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la. Kɛ́ oha he ni oyɔɔ lɛ mli tse yɛ nɛkɛ shishijee be nɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛná shishifãi ni wa ni amɛye jwɛi lɛ anɔ.

english: What happens to my maize crop if I plant the seeds too close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni baa mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When maize is planted too close together, the plants compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition leaves you with thin, weak stalks and very small or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa onáa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ tsei bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize crop lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed to make leaves dark green and strong. Adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore the plant's health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni baaha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni mli wa Kooloo ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Maize plants curl their leaves as a defense mechanism to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun. This helps the plant trap moisture and stop water from evaporating too quickly during heat.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ akɛ hebuu gbɛ koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛmɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why does my land produce smaller maize harvests when I plant maize on the exact same plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo be mli ni miduɔ ŋmãa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Maize is a heavy feeder that quickly drains specific nutrients from the soil. Planting it repeatedly on the same plot exhausts the land, leading to weaker crops unless you rotate with nitrogen-fixing crops like cowpeas or groundnuts.
ga: Abɛi ji niyenii ni tsii ni jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya. Kɛ́ adu nii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli shii abɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ No ji ja okɛ tsei ni haa nitrogen hiɔ shi tamɔ cowpeas loo peanuts lɛ tsake.

english: Can I use the same maize I grow for food to make feed for poultry?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ni miduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ atsu nii akɛ niyenii aha mikooloi lɛ?

english: Yes, standard yellow or white maize is the main energy source used in poultry feed. It provides the essential carbohydrates birds need to grow, lay eggs, and stay healthy.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni ji yellow loo white ni afɔɔ feemɔ lɛ ji hewalɛ jɛɛhe titri ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ kooloi aniyenii mli. Carbohydrates ni he hiaa okpoi koni amɛdara, amɛwo wɔji, ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ mli.

english: Why are caterpillars eating the inner leaves of my young maize plants, and will the crop survive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ miiye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ amli baai lɛ? Ni ani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baahi shi loo amɛhiŋ shi?

english: These pests, often fall armyworms, target the soft central leaves where the plant grows. If the growth center is destroyed, the plant cannot produce food from sunlight properly, severely reducing your final harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbeeɔ parasait ŋmeii amli. Ekɛ ehiɛ fɔɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ anɔ. Kɛji akɛ akpata he ni tsei lɛ daa lɛ hiɛ lɛ, Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ afee niyenii jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛ hulu la mli. Enɛ baaha onaagbee kpamɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi kwraa.

english: How do I know when my maize crop is mature and ready to harvest from the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-ŋmãa lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Maize is fully mature when the outer leaf husks turn brown and dry, the silks become dark brown, and a small black spot forms at the base of each kernel on the cob.
ga: Abɛi eda kɛji kponɔgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbi. Siliki lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ. Ni ŋmeii bibii diji yɛ jɛmɛ. Ebaa yɛ dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko shishi yɛ ŋmei lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my harvested maize get full of tiny holes and dust after I store it for a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni sũ ni akɛto nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ?

english: Tiny insects called grain weevils burrow into dry maize to eat and lay eggs. Properly drying your maize and storing it in airtight bags or treated storage cribs prevents these pests from destroying your grain.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ seed moths lɛ shwieɔ ŋmãa ni egbi mli koni amɛye nii ni amɛwo wɔji. Kɛ́ ogbala o-corn lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛto vacuum bags loo storage hampers mli lɛ, ebaatsi nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkafite o-ŋmãa lɛ.

english: What happens to my maize crop if dry weather hits right when the plants start flowering?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-abele lɛ nɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi ba yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔi shishi lɛ?

english: Flowering is the most delicate stage of maize growth because pollen must fertilize the silks to form grains. A lack of water during this time causes incomplete fertilization, leading to cobs with missing kernels.
ga: Fɔlɔi ji be ni yɔɔ mlɛo fe fɛɛ yɛ ŋmãa dalɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, esa akɛ pollen lɛ kɛ siliki awo mli koni efee dumɔwui. Nu ni bɛ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ haa fɔmɔ nii lɛ eshɛɛɛ he. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ bɛ.

english: Why do seeds saved from last year's hybrid maize harvest produce weaker crops than new seeds bought from the store?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii ni bɛ hewalɛ fe dumɔwui heei ni ahe yɛ shwapo mli lɛ?

english: Commercial hybrid maize seeds are created by crossing specific parent plants to give maximum yield, but this special strength is lost in the second generation. Replanting saved hybrid seeds yields smaller, less uniform cobs.
ga: Afeɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni akɛfee jarayeli nibii kɛtsɔ fɔlɔi tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni akɛfoɔ mli koni ana yibiiwoo babaoo nɔ. Shi nɛkɛ srɔtofeemɔ nɛɛ baaje mli yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Hybrid dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ adumɔ baaha dumɔwui bibii ni bɛ ekomefeemɔ aba.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains or keep shade trees next to my young cocoa plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu plantains loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ mi kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that easily burn and dry out under the strong sun. Plantain trees grow very fast and provide large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, keeping the ground cool and moist for the young cocoa to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ bɔni afee ni kookoo bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Allowing too many young shoots (suckers) to grow around the base steals food and water from the main tree. Pruning them to leave only one main tree, one medium shoot, and one small shoot ensures the plant has enough energy to grow very big plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii bibii (ŋmei) babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli koni ashi tso titri kome pɛ, tso lɛ teŋgbɛ tso kome, kɛ tso bibioo kome lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ plantains wuji.

english: Why do my yam plants grow much bigger tubers when I give them tall wooden poles to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tsei lɛ shwereɔ bulbs wuji babaoo beni mikɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ ha amɛ lɛ? Ha amɛkwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi?

english: Yam plants are natural vines that need to lift their leaves high up off the ground to catch maximum sunlight. Staking allows the leaves to convert sunlight into food efficiently, which is then stored underground as large, heavy yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli wain tsei ni ehe hiaa ni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ tsakeɔ hulu la lɛ amɛfeɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ. No sɛɛ lɛ, akɛ amɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi akɛ yam ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Yellow leaves starting at the bottom of a maize plant mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed for leaf growth. Adding compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer early helps the leaves turn deep green and feed the growing cob.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa kɛha baa lɛ adalɛ Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fataa he mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ni eha niyenii aha ŋmei ni miida lɛ.

english: Why is it good practice for me to alternate planting maize with groundnuts on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji nifeemɔ kpakpa kɛha mi akɛ matsake ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the ground, while groundnuts naturally absorb nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. Rotating these crops keeps your soil healthy and fertile naturally for the next season.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ. Nibii nɛɛ ni oootsake lɛ haa oshikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: This leaf twisting and yellowing is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried and spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting certified disease-resistant cassava stems is the best way to prevent this and ensure high root yields.
ga: Yucca mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni efee ŋmɔtɔ nɛɛ baa. ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ woɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ. Cassava tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ he odaseyeli lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ he ni anáa shishifãi babaoo.

english: Why am I seeing ragged holes and yellowish powder inside the leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji ni etse kɛ powda ni tsuɔ yɛ mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central leaf funnel and eats the growing leaf tissue. Applying approved organic or chemical treatments directly into the funnel early stops them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ nu lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ baa lɛ mli fãji ni miida lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ mra. Abaatsi enaa dani ekpata ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahiɛ.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in wet, damp, and shaded conditions. Clearing undergrowth and pruning cocoa branches lets in sunlight and air to dry the farm, preventing the fungus from multiplying.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni efɔ, edɔ, kɛ shade shihilɛi amli kɛbaa. Tsɔɔmɔ tsei ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ni ofolɔ kookoo tsei lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi aba ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Koni ŋmeii akafee babaoo

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the weather gets too hot, when the soil is too dry, or if there is too much nitrogen causing leaves to grow instead of fruit. Regular watering and balanced feeding help flowers stay on and turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Aloo nitrogen babaoo yɛ ni haa baai kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ niyenii ni ja lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tomatoi.

english: Why do my groundnut plants bend down and push their flower stems into the ground after blooming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ efɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ beni ewo fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts naturally flower above ground, but the actual nuts grow underground. After the flower is pollinated, the plant grows a small peg stem that burrows down into the soil so the nut pod can safely expand under the dirt.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ŋmeii fɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ, shi anɔkwa ŋmeii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Beni afee fɔfɔi lɛ pollen sɛɛ lɛ Tso lɛ yɛ peg tso bibioo ko. Koni efo sũ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi shweshweeshwe.

english: Young cocoa trees have weak root systems and cannot handle intense heat or direct sunlight. Without shade trees or adequate water during dry spells, the sun dries out their leaves quickly, causing them to scorch and drop.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi bɛ hewalɛ, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, Hulu lɛ haa baai lɛ gĩɔ oya. Enɛ haa shãa ni egbeeɔ shi.

english: How can I tell when my oil palm fruit bunch is mature enough to harvest for making red palm oil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-oil palm yibii lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa koni maná red palm oil?

english: An oil palm bunch is ready for harvest when at least five to ten loose fruits detach naturally and fall to the ground, and the skin of the fruits changes from blackish-purple to a reddish-orange color.
ga: Mu tsei akui lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni kɛ hoo lɛ, aduawai enumɔ kɛyashi nyɔŋma ni egbɔjɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbeeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ. ni aduawai lɛ ahewolo tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ-diŋŋ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ-tsuru mli.

english: Why do some of my young oil palm trees only produce male flowers and no fruit bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tsei lɛ ekomɛi woɔ fɔfɔi hii pɛ, shi amɛwooo aduawai akui lɛ?

english: Oil palm trees often produce mostly male flowers when they are stressed by dry weather, poor soil nutrients, or when they are still too young. As the tree matures and receives sufficient water and nutrients, it will start producing female flowers that turn into fruit bunches.
ga: Mu tsei woɔ fɔfɔi hii babaoo kɛji shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ hao amɛ. Niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Aloo beni oji gbekɛ tsɔ lɛ Kɛ́ tso lɛ eda jogbaŋŋ ni enine shɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ lɛ, Ebaabɔi fɔfɔi yei ni baatsɔ aduawai akui.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting and changing color within a few days after I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ ni etsakeɔ amɛhe yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni atsa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots lack a tough protective outer skin, so once they are harvested, exposure to air causes rapid chemical changes that spoil the root within two to three days unless it is processed into food like gari or flour immediately.
ga: Cassava shishifãi bɛ kponɔgbɛ hewolo ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akpa lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ kɛ tsofa tsakemɔi baa oya. Enɛ baafite shishifãi lɛ yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ mli. ja afee lɛ niyenii tamɔ gari loo ashikishaŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Yes, intercropping maize and cassava works well because maize grows quickly and is harvested within three to four months, while cassava grows slowly early on and takes eight to twelve months to mature, so they do not compete heavily for sunlight and soil space.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya, ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli ni amɛheɔ nyɔji kpaanyɔ kɛyashi nyɔŋma kɛ enyɔ dani amɛshɛɔ shweremɔ he lɛ, No hewɔ lɛ, amɛyeee akaŋ yɛ hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ he babaoo he.

english: Yellowing lower leaves starting from the tip indicate a shortage of nitrogen in the soil. When nitrogen is low, the maize plant moves this nutrient from its older bottom leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛji nitrogen lɛ faaa lɛ Abɛi tsei lɛ jieɔ niyenii nɛɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when weather conditions are too hot or when soil moisture changes drastically. High heat damages the pollen inside the flower, preventing it from forming fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ shihilɛi lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake waa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ kpataa fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ ahiɛ. ha efee nɔ ni wooo yibii

english: What causes the leaves on my pepper plants to curl upward and look wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni ekpɔtɔ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like mites or thrips feeding on the undersides of leaves, or by viral infections passed on by those insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ mites loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ni amɛnuɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo kɛjɛ helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli

english: Why are my coconut trees dropping small green nuts before they grow to full size?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei tso lɛ miishwie ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli dani amɛdara kɛyashɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Coconut trees shed young nuts when they experience prolonged dry periods, severe nutrient deficiencies in the soil, or attacks from sap-sucking insects. The tree drops extra nuts to conserve water and energy for its own survival.
ga: Kokoo tsei jieɔ ŋmeii kɛji amɛna hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Niyenii nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ faaa kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. aloo kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ tutuaa amɛ Tsei shwieɔ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: Why are my plantain plants taking a very long time to produce bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Plantain plants require large amounts of soil moisture, organic matter, and potassium to grow strongly. In dry or nutrient-poor soil, or when crowded too closely together, their growth slows down significantly.
ga: Plantains he miihia shikpɔŋ nɔ nu babaoo, nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, kɛ potassium koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ nɔ loo kɛ́ amɛfee ekome tsɔ lɛ Dalɛ baa shi waa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep wilting and dying when exposed to full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to intense sun and high heat. They need shade from fast-growing nurse crops like plantains to protect their delicate leaves and keep the surrounding soil cool and moist.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ he waa. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni ebu amɛbaai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe ni eha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for plant growth. It can also happen when soil becomes waterlogged or when weeds are stealing food from your crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛji jwɛi ju niyenii kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when temperature drops or spikes too high, or when the plant does not get consistent water. Extreme weather causes the plant stress, making it shed flowers to preserve its own energy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi loo eshɛ ŋwɛi tsɔ. aloo be mli ni tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu nɔ daa Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛbu lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehewalɛ he.

english: Why is it important for me to cut off the extra side branches growing on my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mafolɔ niji ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-kokoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cutting unwanted shoots, or pruning, allows light and fresh air to reach the main trunk. This keeps the tree healthy, prevents fungal diseases from spreading, and helps the tree direct its strength into producing pods.
ga: Niji ni ataooo lɛ ni afoɔ loo afoɔ lɛ haa la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shɛɔ tso lɛ tso titri lɛ he. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ. Tsi fungal helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ naa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava stems too close to one another in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ aduɔ ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ko nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting cassava stems too close together causes them to fight for nutrients, water, and sunlight. Proper spacing gives roots enough room under the soil to expand into large, thick tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔmɔ ŋmeii wuji ni mli tse.

english: What makes my cocoa pods turn black and rot while they are still growing on the tree?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This blackening is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in wet, cool, and overly shady conditions. Pruning trees to let in sun and removing infected pods quickly helps stop it from spreading.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ duŋ nɛɛ baa ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ tsɔ, ni mli ejɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ofo tso lɛ he koni hulu la babaoo aba mli, ni ojie ŋmeii ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ oya lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekpa hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts fix nitrogen from the air into the soil. Planting them restores natural fertility to the land, which helps your next crop grow strong without needing as much added fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts saa nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Tsei nɛɛ adumɔ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii aba ekoŋŋ. Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ daa waa ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo awo mli.

english: Why do weeds cause my young crops to grow so slowly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔwui lɛ daraa blɛoo nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than young crops and aggressively steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients your crops need. Clearing weeds early gives your crops full access to food so they can grow rapidly.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ waa. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa onibii lɛ náa niyenii kwraa. koni amɛnyɛ amɛdara oya

english: How can I tell when my cocoa pods are ripe enough to pick?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-kookoo lɛ egbɔ bɔ ni sa ni esa akɛ ajie lɛ?

english: Cocoa pods are ready for harvest when their skin changes color completely. Green pods turn bright yellow, and reddish pods turn orange. Harvesting at this right time ensures the beans inside have fully developed.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji ŋmeii lɛ ahe su tsake kwraa. Pods eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. ni ŋmeii tsuru lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmeii ni akpaa yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ haa kɔfi ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my crops are getting damaged by too much water in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ miifite miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Excess water drowns plant roots by removing air from the soil. You will notice leaves turning yellow, roots turning dark and soft, and the whole plant wilting even though the ground around it is completely wet.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haa tsei shishifãi shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ejieɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Obaana akɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ. Shishifãi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛhe feɔ blɛoo. ni tso muu lɛ fɛɛ gĩ, eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Eyɛ mli akɛ Eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ kwraa po.

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains creates a living umbrella that keeps the young cocoa cool and moist until its roots are strong enough to handle full weather.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni haa kookoo bibii lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i kɛyashiɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsu nibii ni baa lɛ ahe nii.

english: Why are all the tiny flowers on my cocoa trees falling off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Yɛ mi koko tso lɛ nɔ koni egbee shi ni etsɔko pod?

english: Cocoa flowers drop when the tree suffers from heat stress or lack of water, or when there are not enough tiny insects in the farm to pollinate them. Maintaining shade and keeping leaf mulch on the ground helps retain the moisture trees need to hold onto flowers.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ loo nu ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni baanyɛ afee pollination lɛ. Kɛ́ afee lɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa tso lɛ koni enyɛ ehiɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi.

english: Yellow lower leaves mean the maize plant is starving for nitrogen food in the soil. When nitrogen is low, the plant takes food from its older bottom leaves and sends it up to keep the young growing top alive.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye ŋmãa tso lɛ kɛha nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ nitrogen faaa Tso lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara lɛ amli ni etsuɔ ​​kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha ŋmeii bibii ni miida lolo lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my tall rice stalks fall flat on the ground right before it is time to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ kɛlɛ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, minɔ lɛ baagbee shikpɔŋ dani kpamɔ be lɛ?

english: Rice stalks fall over—a problem called lodging—when stems become too tall and weak to support heavy grain heads. This usually happens from applying too much chemical nitrogen fertilizer or planting seeds too close together.
ga: Stalk drop - naagba ko ni ale lɛ akɛ lodging - beni tso lɛ da tsɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni enyɛŋ eye ebua dumɔwui ayitsei ni tsii lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji tsofa ni ji nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli babaoo loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain leaves standing water around the roots for too long, the roots drown from lack of oxygen, allowing rot fungi to attack them under the ground.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu lɛ shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Shishifãi lɛ baagboi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Ha ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ atutua amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why does my yam crop give me bigger tubers when I stake the vines with tall sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ haa ŋmeii wuji beni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ shwieɔ wain tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines use their leaves to turn sunlight into food for growing tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they can catch maximum sunlight instead of shading each other in a heap.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei kɛ baai ni tsakeɔ hulu la lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaaha amɛhe yɛ kui amli lɛ

english: Why does my plantain tree produce small bunches when I allow all the young shoots to grow around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ miida ni amɛmiifee ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Kɛjɛ be mli ni miha ŋmeii bibii lɛ fɛɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ Nakai plantain tso lɛ he lɛ

english: Young plantain shoots steal water, sunlight, and soil food from the main mother plant. Cutting away extra shoots and leaving only one or two allows all the food to flow directly into forming one big plantain bunch.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ sũ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli. Kpɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni oshi ŋmeii 1-2 pɛ koni niyenii lɛ fɛɛ atsɔ ekomefeemɔ mli ni etsɔ ŋmeii akuu agbo ko.

english: What causes the leaves on my pepper plants to curl up tightly and stop producing fruits?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa yibiiwoo?

english: Leaf curling is caused by tiny sucking pests like thrips or whiteflies hiding under the leaves, or by diseases spread by these insects. Inspecting leaves early and using recommended protective sprays keeps leaves open and healthy.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ mra Ni akɛ tsofa ni buɔ mɔ he ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni baa lɛ ahi shi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or beans on my farmland after harvesting my corn crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans have special roots that grab natural nitrogen food from the air and put it back into the soil. Planting them restores the soil's fertility naturally so your next crop can grow strong without relying entirely on expensive bags of fertilizer.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli nibii ni ji nitrogen mli lɛ amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei nɛɛ adumɔ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba ekoŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ adara waa ni okɛ ohe akafɔ̃ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ kotokui amli lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does my mango tree yield plenty of sweet fruit this year, but almost nothing the next year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango wo yibii ni ŋɔɔ waa afi nɛɛ shi afi ni baa lɛ ewooo kwraa lɛ?

english: Producing a heavy harvest uses up almost all the energy stores inside a fruit tree. The tree needs a year to rest and rebuild its strength before it can produce another big harvest.
ga: Nibii babaoo ni akpaa lɛ yeɔ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ato yɛ aduawai tso lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni tsei lɛ aná afi koni amɛjɔɔ amɛhe ni amɛná amɛhewalɛ ekoŋŋ dani amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii wuji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why did the seeds I planted last week fail to come out of the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni midu nyɛsɛɛ otsi lɛ ejeee kpo kɛjɛɛɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds usually fail to sprout if the ground is too dry, if they were buried too deep for the shoots to reach the surface, or if insects and heavy rains damaged them before they could grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui kwɛɛɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. Kɛji akɛ afu lɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ Aloo kɛji kooloi bibii kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fite lɛ dani enyɛ eda.

english: If some spots in my farm remain empty because seeds didn't sprout, can I put new seeds in those same holes?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ hei komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ efee efolo lolo ejaakɛ dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ hu? Ani manyɛ mikɛ dumɔwui heei awo bu kome mli?

english: Yes, you can replant empty spots, but it is best to do it within one to two weeks of the first planting so the new crops do not get shaded out by the older ones.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu yɛ he ko ni nɔ ko bɛ. Shi ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofee enɛ yɛ otsi kome loo enyɔ mli kɛjɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji koni tsei heei lɛ akafee hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei momo lɛ ahe.

english: Why do people tell me to plant soybean on the land where my maize did poorly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ko baakɛɛ mi akɛ madu soybean yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-ŋmãa lɛ wooo yibii kpakpai yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Soybean is a special crop that takes nitrogen from the air and puts it back into the ground, which naturally restores the soil's strength for future crops.
ga: Soybeans ji ŋmɔshi nibii krɛdɛɛ ko ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ. Enɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aha tsei ni baaba wɔsɛɛ lɛ.

english: Will growing the exact same crop on the same plot every year destroy my land?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni madu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ baafite mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yes, planting the same crop every season drains the exact same soil nutrients over time and allows pests and diseases specific to that crop to build up in your field.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei komekomei ni aduɔ daa be lɛ baaha niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni tamɔ nakai pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ ajɛ sũ lɛ mli yɛ be ni sa mli. Ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni kɔɔ nakai tso lɛ he pɔtɛɛ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ oŋmɔji amli.

english: How deep into the soil am I supposed to push my seeds when planting?
ga: Te esa akɛ matsi dumɔwui lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashi tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu?

english: A good rule of thumb is to plant seeds at a depth equal to two or three times their size; planting too deep prevents them from reaching sunlight, while planting too shallow leaves them to dry out or be eaten by birds.
ga: Mla kpakpa ni esa akɛ akwɛ nɔ ji ni adu dumɔwui yɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ ni ekɛ dumɔwui lɛ adalɛ toi enyɔ loo etɛ yeɔ egbɔ. Kɛ́ adu nii jogbaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaatsi hulu la ni shɛɔ tso lɛ he lɛ naa. yɛ be mli ni kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛgbi loo okpoi aye amɛ.

english: How do I know if the soil is wet enough to start planting after the first rain falls?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni obaanyɛ oje dumɔ shishi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to wait for two or three good rains that thoroughly soak the soil rather than planting after the very first light shower, so your young seeds do not dry up.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ nugbɔ kpakpa. Shii enyɔ loo shii etɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyiɔ obɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Bɔni afee ni odumɔwui bibii lɛ akagbi.

english: Why are the leaves of my young crops turning light yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your plants are hungry for nutrients like nitrogen, or that too much water is sitting around their roots and choking them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye otso lɛ kɛha niyenii tamɔ nitrogen. Aloo nu babaoo feɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni ehaa amɛtsiɔ amɛhe.

english: Why do my crop leaves roll up and look tired during the afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etamɔ nɔ ni etɔ yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rolling leaves is the plant's natural way of protecting itself to save water during extreme heat, but if they remain rolled in the cool morning, the plant urgently needs water.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe he koni ekɛbu nu he yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ. Shi kɛji akɛ eefo lolo yɛ leebi ni mli ejɔ nɔ lɛ Tsei hu he miihia nu oya.

english: What brings small worms to eat my crop leaves shortly after they sprout?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmei feɔ bibioo nɛkɛ? Ani oyeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai beni amɛje kpo lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ?

english: Moths lay tiny eggs on young leaves, which hatch into caterpillars like Fall Armyworm; checking under the leaves weekly helps you spot and control them before they destroy the field.
ga: Kplukai lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ baai bibii anɔ, ni ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworm; Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi daa otsi lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ona amɛ ni okudɔ amɛ dani amɛfite shia lɛ.

english: Is it better to buy certified seeds from an agro-dealer or use seeds saved from my previous harvest?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooohe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ? Aloo okɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ mikpamɔ ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii.

english: Certified seeds from agro-dealers give better yields because they are selected for high sprouting rates and treated against diseases, whereas saved seeds slowly lose their strength over time.
ga: Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ odaseyeli ni jɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔi adɛŋ lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai ejaakɛ ahala amɛ kɛha shweremɔ ni yaa hiɛ ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ. yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ fiofio Hewalɛ ni baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize crop turning yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baa lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is a key nutrient for plant growth. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen deep into the soil where young roots cannot reach it, so applying top-dressing fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps the leaves turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ nitrogen lɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi bibii nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it helpful for me to plant groundnuts or beans in my field after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mikpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of food out of the soil, especially nitrogen. Legumes like groundnuts and beans have special bacteria in their roots that take nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil, helping to restore soil fertility naturally for your next crop.
ga: Abele heɔ eniyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ bacteria krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ amɛshishifãi amli ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why does my paddy rice grow well in flooded water while my other crops die if water sits on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-paddy lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu afua mli lɛ? be mli ni tsei krokomɛi Mi nɔ lɛ gboɔ kɛji nu damɔ mli?

english: Rice plants have special internal air tubes in their stems and roots that allow them to transport oxygen from the leaves down to the roots under water. Most other crops drown because their roots cannot breathe in waterlogged soil.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛi krɛdɛɛi ni yɔɔ amɛmli yɛ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa lɛ jɛɔ baai lɛ amli kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ nu shishi. Nibii krokomɛi ni aduɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo shwieɔ nu mli ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu yɛ sũ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and produce broad leaves that act as temporary umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ be kukuoo mli ŋwɛi ŋta. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa cocoa gbekɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why should I cut off some of the extra shoots growing around the base of my plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ ekomɛi? Ajie mi dumɔwui lɛ ashishitoo lɛ

english: When too many shoots grow around one main plantain stem, they fight each other for water, light, and soil nutrients. Removing extra shoots leaves only the strongest stem, which will produce a much bigger bunch of plantains.
ga: Beni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso wulu kome he lɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii ni wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ eshwɛɔ. Enɛ baaha plantains ayibɔ aba babaoo.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or sudden dry spells. When the weather gets too hot or water is irregular, the plant drops its flowers to save energy and protect itself.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo hulutsoo ni baa trukaa lɛ miigba tsei lɛ anaa. Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo nu lɛ ejaaa Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe.

english: Cowpea flowers produce sweet scents and nectar that attract pests like thrips and pod borers. The insects visit the flowers to feed, which is why spraying or protecting the crop right at the flowering stage is critical to saving your pods.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ jieɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni ŋɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni gbalaa kooloi tamɔ thrips kɛ pod borers. Kplukai yasaraa fɔfɔi koni amɛyatao niyenii. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni oŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛshwieɔ shi loo obuɔ he yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ he hiaa waa koni okwɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very bushy leaves but produce very small roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ babaoo shi shishifãi bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or when cassava plants are planted too close together, the plant puts all its energy into growing big leaves above ground instead of sending food down to expand the tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo ŋmei ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeetsu niyenii kɛba shi koni ekɛwo bulb lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can spread out and catch maximum sunlight. When leaves get full sun, they make more food that gets stored underground, resulting in larger yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛha baai lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Kɛji baai lɛ ná hulu la ni fa lɛ Ebaafee niyenii babaoo ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baafee wuji.

english: Why does covering the soil around my crops with dry grass help them stay fresh during dry hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi shwie miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, acts like a shield against the sun. It keeps the soil cool and prevents moisture from evaporating quickly, allowing roots to stay wet longer.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ gãimlibii ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la he. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ, ni ehaa nu ni mli edɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves during dry spells as a natural defense to conserve water and survive. Providing shade trees and spreading dry grass or leaf mulch around the base helps keep the soil moist so the tree stays green longer.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo ha ni jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmɔshi nibii fɔ̃ɔ shishigbɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why are there small chew holes appearing in the leaves of my young maize plants overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ bibioo ko yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Eje kpo yɛ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ gbɛkɛ kome?

english: This damage is usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm, which hide inside the plant leaves during the hot day and come out to feed at night when it is cooler. Catching them early in the morning makes it easier to protect the crop stem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei ahe baai amli yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni oje kpo oyatao niyenii gbɛkɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ amɔmɔ amɛ leebi lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ abaabu tsei ahe.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with thick green leaves, but the tubers under the ground remain thin and small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛji bibii lolo.

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients like potassium, the cassava plant spends all its energy producing leaves above ground instead of expanding its root tubers below ground.
ga: Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi tamɔ potassium he lɛ, ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ shishifãi lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot or when soil moisture changes rapidly from very dry to heavily soaked. Excessive heat or water stress forces the plant to drop flowers to save energy for survival.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsakeɔ oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ waa nɔ. Haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ loo nu babaoo mli baa lɛ haa tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to get full exposure to sunlight, which fuels photosynthesis to grow large tubers below ground. Vines left trailing on the wet soil are more likely to catch diseases and get choked by weeds.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulutsoo be fɛɛ. ni ji tsofa ni akɛtsuɔ fotosintɛsis he nii koni ekɛ bulb agboi akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ wain tsei ni ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aná hela ni jwɛi shwieɔ amɛmli.

english: Why should I cut down some of the young shoots growing at the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ midumɔwui titrii lɛ ashishi lɛ ekomɛi?

english: Young plantain suckers compete directly with the parent stem for soil nutrients and water. Keeping only one or two healthy suckers ensures the main stem gets enough food to produce big, heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Dumɔwui kɛ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ to lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yibii titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo yibii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why does planting cowpea or beans in my field make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas have natural partnerships with tiny organisms in their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into plant food. When the cowpea crop finishes, that natural food stays in the soil for the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas yɛ adebɔɔ mli shihilɛ ko ni kɛ nibii bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ feɔ ekome, ni amɛgbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛfeɔ lɛ tsei aniyenii. Kɛ agbe tsina ŋmãa dumɔ naa lɛ Nakai adebɔɔ mli niyenii lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking sap from the underside of leaves and spreading plant viruses. Removing affected leaves early prevents the disease from spreading across your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ mli lɛ baa. Baai ni ena hela lɛ ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baatsi hela naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why does my lowland rice crop turn light yellow and stop growing when the mud in the field dries hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ ŋmãa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekpaa dalɛ beni muji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ egbi waa lɛ?

english: Lowland rice roots rely on saturated, wet soil to dissolve and take up soil nutrients easily. When the soil bakes dry, the roots cannot absorb water or nitrogen, causing leaves to turn yellow and growth to pause.
ga: Omɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ damɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ ni eyi obɔ lɛ nɔ koni etsɔ mlɛo ni eŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu loo nitrogen. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdalɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Why is it bad practice for me to plant pepper in the exact same spot where I harvested tomatoes last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni mifo tomato yɛ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ ji nifeemɔ gbonyo kɛha mi lɛ?

english: Peppers and tomatoes are close relatives that share the same soil diseases and insect pests. Planting them continuously in the same spot allows harmful organisms to build up in the soil and attack the new crop right away.
ga: Pepper kɛ tomato ji wekumɛi ni bɛŋkɛ kpaakpa ni kɛ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ yeɔ egbɔ. Kɛ́ aya nɔ adu nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ yɛ he kome lɛ, ehaa nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛtutuaa ŋmɔshi nibii heei amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are delicate and burn easily in direct sun. Planting shade trees like plantains or forest trees creates a cooler microclimate and preserves soil moisture while the cocoa roots establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa, ni kɛ́ hulu lɛ tso amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, amɛshãa oya. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo koo mli tsei ni aduɔ Ebaaha kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli ejɔ aba. ni ekwɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ feɔ lɛ.

english: What causes the leaves on my cocoa trees to turn yellow and fall off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves during hot, dry spells to save water. Keeping temporary shade trees and applying mulch around the base of the cocoa trees retains moisture and protects them during the dry season.
ga: Cocoa tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ ni nu egbi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Tso He Kwɛmɔ: Ha hulutsoo be kukuoo ko kɛ nɔ ko aha kookoo tso lɛ shishi koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli ni ebu he yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot right on the tree before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani akpa lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, damp conditions. Pruning excess branches and clearing weeds lets sunlight and air in, which helps prevent the fungus from thriving.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni efɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ojie jwɛi lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ akakwɛ̃.

english: Why do I need to cut mistletoe off my cocoa tree branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mifoɔ mistletoe lɛ kɛjɛɔ cacao nine lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Mistletoe is a parasitic plant that steals water and nutrients directly from the cocoa tree's branches, weakening the tree and drastically lowering the number of pods it can produce.
ga: Mistletoe ji tso ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ kookoo niji amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ, ni ehaa ŋmeii ni abaanyɛ afee lɛ baa shi waa.

english: What is Mirid or Akate damage, and how does it hurt my crop?
ga: Mɛni ji Mirid loo Akate fitemɔ ni te enaa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ hewalɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Mirids (Akate) are tiny sucking insects that bite cocoa shoots and young pods, creating black spots that destroy branches and stunt pod growth, reducing overall farm yields.
