ga: Mirids (akate) ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu. Cocoa bud kɛ young pod cutter Enɛ haa ŋmeii diji ni fiteɔ tsei niji kɛ pod lɛ adalɛ baa. Enɛ haa nibii fɛɛ ni anáa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi.

english: Why is it important for me to prune my mature cocoa trees regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-kokoo tsei ni eda lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the tree canopy so sunlight can reach lower branches. This encourages flowering, reduces humidity where diseases live, and makes harvesting much easier.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni afoɔ lɛ gbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ tsei niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ yaa hiɛ. Ha hulutsoo be lɛ aba shi yɛ hei ni helai fɔɔ baa lɛ. Ni ehaa nikpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny midges to pollinate them, and the tree will shed unpollinated flowers. Drought, extreme heat, or poor nutrition can also cause a tree to drop flowers to protect itself.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia gbɔmɔtsei bibii koni amɛná pollen, ni tsei baajie fɔfɔi ni pollen bɛ mli lɛ kpo. Hɔmɔ, latsaa ni naa wa, loo niyenii ni esaaa baanyɛ aha tsei ashwie fɔfɔi amɛshwie shi koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe.

english: Why shouldn't I chop cocoa pods off the trunk using a sharp cutlass forcefully?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsɔne ni mli wa shwieɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Hacking pods forcefully damages the flower cushions on the bark where future pods grow. Using a proper hooked pod-picker cuts cleanly without destroying future flower spots.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ, ebaafite fɔfɔi akushin ni yɔɔ tso lɛ yibii ni wɔsɛɛ ŋmeii lɛ baajɛ mli aba lɛ nɔ lɛ waa. Kɛ́ akɛ pod clipper ni sa tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha afolɔ nibii ni he tse ni efiteee wɔsɛɛ fɔfɔii ahe hei.

english: How can I tell when my cocoa pods are completely ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ eshɛ he kɛha kpamɔ?

english: Ripe pods change color clearly—green pods turn bright yellow, while red or purple pods turn orange-yellow. Harvesting at full ripeness ensures the beans have developed the sugar needed for proper fermentation.
ga: Pods ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ tsakeɔ ehiɛ su yɛ faŋŋ mli. Pods eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii tsuru loo purple lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ-ŋmei. Kɛ́ akpa amɛ beni amɛkwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ náa sugar ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛfee ŋmeii ni sa.

english: Why must I ferment my cocoa beans under plantain leaves instead of drying them immediately?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ cocoa ŋmeii lɛ woɔ plantain baai ashishi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mahã amɛgbi amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Fermentation under plantain leaves kills the bean seed to prevent germination and unlocks the rich chocolate flavor. Sun-drying beans immediately leaves them bitter, unflavored, and unmarketable.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni akɛwoɔ plantain baai lɛ ashishi lɛ gbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni egbeleɔ tsokolate ni ŋɔɔ waa lɛ naa. Beans ni hulu egbi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ebɛ ŋmɔlɔ, ni anyɛɛɛ ahɔ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Leaving land to rest, known as fallowing, gives the soil time to naturally replenish lost nutrients, rebuild organic matter, and break the life cycles of soil-borne pests and diseases that accumulate during continuous farming.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ejɔɔ ehe, ni ale lɛ akɛ defoliation lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛ niyenii ni elaaje lɛ baawo mli ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Bɔɔ nibii heei ni wala yɔɔ mli ni efiteɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni buaa amɛhe naa yɛ okwaayeli be mli lɛ ashihilɛ be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do my crops yield less when I plant maize on the exact same plot every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously consumes the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year while allowing specific pests to build up; alternating with crops like beans or peanuts restores soil fertility and keeps pests away.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni yaa nɔ amɛkwɛɔ lɛ kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii afi fɛɛ afi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi shwereɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni atsakeɔ Ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ ni ebaatsi kooloi ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ anaa.

english: Why is it beneficial to mix plant leaves and organic mulch into my soil before the planting season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ akɛ tsei ahe baai kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli baafutu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛmɔ be lɛ aba lɛ?

english: Organic matter acts like a sponge that holds water in the soil during dry spells and slowly releases essential nutrients to crop roots as it decomposes.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji, ni ehiɛɔ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ, ni ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ fiofio be mli ni efiteɔ lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize crops turn yellow and look stunted early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni etamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually signal a lack of nitrogen in the soil or poor root absorption due to waterlogged soil, meaning the crop cannot produce enough green chlorophyll to feed itself.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu ni amɛhiɛɔ mli lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei nyɛŋ afee klorofil eŋɔli ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛkwɛ amɛhe.

english: Will applying more chemical fertilizer always give me a bigger harvest?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ babaoo ni mikɛbaafata he lɛ baaha maná ŋmaa babaoo?

english: Excessive fertilizer can burn crop roots, degrade long-term soil health, and attract insect pests; crops require balanced amounts applied only at key growth stages to produce well.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛnamɔ lɛ fiteɔ be kakadaŋŋ. ni egbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ biɔ yibɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa waa lɛ pɛ koni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: Extreme weather heat, sudden dry spells, or too much nitrogen fertilizer cause stress to tomato plants, making them drop flowers to save energy rather than developing tomatoes.
ga: kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa trukaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi Aloo, nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei anɔ. Gbalamɔ tomato koni okɛ hewalɛ akafite moŋ fe ni oookwɛ tomato.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and turn yellow during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Warm, dry weather accelerates the spread of whiteflies that carry cassava mosaic virus, which causes leaves to curl, reduce food production, and slow root growth.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ haa ŋmei yɛŋ ni hiɛ ŋmei hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya. ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi Ehaa niyenii ni anáa lɛ baa shi ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ adalɛ baa shi

english: Why do my crops wither so fast when rain stops for just a week in the middle of the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ oya nɛkɛ beni nugbɔ lɛ kpaɔ otsi kome pɛ kɛyashiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛmɔ be lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Shallow root systems caused by compacted soil prevent crops from reaching groundwater deeper down, making plants dry out quickly when surface moisture vanishes.
ga: Shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ feɔ lɛ tsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛji nu ni yɔɔ amɛhiɛ lɛ je kpo pɛ.

english: Why do young cocoa trees survive better when planted alongside plantains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ plantains ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are vulnerable to harsh direct sunlight; fast-growing plantains provide living shade umbrellas that lower temperatures and conserve moisture for young cocoa seedlings.
ga: Hulu la ni naa wa lɛ nyɛɔ etswaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ oya. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ haa hulutsoo be ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi ni ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ yaa nɔ ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts together with sorghum make the sorghum grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmei duɔ lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen out of the air and deposit it into the soil, which acts as a natural fertilizer for surrounding cereal crops like sorghum.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmaa nibii ni ebɔle amɛhe tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do I see small creatures coming up to the surface of the water in my flooded field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa bɔɔ nii bibii lɛ? Ni eba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ miŋmɔ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli?

english: When fields are flooded, water forces underground and aquatic pests to swim up to the surface. They come to the surface because that is where the fresh green leaves are located, which they need to eat to survive.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔji lɛ amli eyi Nu lɛ nyɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi kɛ nu mli nibii anɔ koni amɛfo kɛya ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ. Amɛbaa ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ ejaakɛ jɛmɛ ji he ni baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ yɔɔ. ni esa akɛ amɛye koni amɛhi shi lɛ

english: Why do pests on my farm always target the greenest parts of my crop leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ tswaa mitsei lɛ baai lɛ ahe hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji fe fɛɛ lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Fresh green leaves are soft, full of water, and rich in nutrients. Pests come out of hiding specifically to eat these tender green parts because they give them the energy needed to grow and reproduce.
ga: Baai eŋɔli heei lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ. nu ni eyi mli obɔ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ jeɔ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛbaye nɛkɛ fãi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni mli tse nɛɛ. Ejaakɛ no haa wɔnáa hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛda ni amɛfɔ bii.

english: Where do the insects that damage my leaves go after they lay their eggs?
ga: Nɛgbɛ ji he ni kooloi bibii ni fiteɔ mibaai lɛ yaa beni amɛwo amɛwui lɛ sɛɛ?

english: After laying eggs in the soil or under leaves, adult insects usually come out into the open to feed on green leaves. They do this to rebuild their strength, which makes this the best time to spot and control them.
ga: Beni amɛwo amɛwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo baai lɛ ashishi sɛɛ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni eda lɛ jeɔ kpo kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛbaye baai eŋɔli. Amɛfeɔ enɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ. Enɛ haa efeɔ be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛyooɔ amɛ ni akudɔɔ amɛ.

english: Why do pests on my farm seem to come out to eat all at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni kooloi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ jeɔ kpo koni amɛbaye nii shikome lɛ?

english: Pests usually come out together when conditions like moisture and temperature are right for feeding. When fresh green leaves appear, whole groups of pests surface together to feed, making it easier for you to see them all at once.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ feɔ ekome kɛjeɔ kpo kɛ́ shihilɛi tamɔ hulutsoo kɛ latsaa sa kɛha niyenii. Beni baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni kpɛɔ lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akui muu fɛɛ buaa amɛhe naa koni amɛtao niyenii. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa bo akɛ obaana amɛ fɛɛ shikome.

english: Why am I seeing birds, frogs, and large insects gathering in my field when pests appear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa okpoi, ŋmeii, kɛ kooloi wuji ni miibua amɛhe naa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛ́ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ je kpo lɛ?

english: These animals are natural predators attracted by the pests. When plant-eating pests come out into the open to eat your crop leaves, predators follow them to feed on the pests, which naturally helps reduce pest numbers on your farm.
ga: Koolooi nɛɛ ji adebɔɔ mli kooloi ni tsɛŋemɔ helai gbalaa amɛ. Beni kooloi ni yeɔ tsei lɛ jeɔ kpo kɛyaa kpo nɔ koni amɛbaye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ. Kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ baanyiɛ amɛsɛɛ koni amɛyaye kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ayibɔ aba shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Should I spray chemicals immediately when I see pests eating my crop leaves?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai afɔse nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ mina kooloi ni yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai?

english: Not always right away. If natural predators like birds, spiders, or frogs are already eating the pests, spraying chemicals might kill those helpful predators. Allowing predators to eat the exposed pests can often control the problem naturally.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be amrɔ nɔŋŋ Kɛji adebɔɔ mli kooloi tamɔ okpoi, ŋmeii, loo ŋmeii miiye nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ momo lɛ, Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbe nakai kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ aŋmɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ gbɛ ni amɛye kooloi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye naagba lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How does water on my farm change the way pests and other animals interact?
ga: Te nu ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsakeɔ bɔ ni kooloi bibii kɛ kooloi krokomɛi yeɔ amɛhe amɛhaa lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Water brings pests up to the surface to reach your green crops. Once pests surface and expose themselves on the plants, it creates a feeding chain where bigger predator animals and birds come to hunt them.
ga: Nu kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛyashɛ onibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ ahe. Kɛji tsɛŋemɔ helai je kpo ni amɛje kpo kɛjɛ tsei amli Amɛfeɔ niyenii he gbɛjianɔtoo ko ni kooloi wuji ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ kɛ okpoi baa koni amɛbagbe amɛ.

english: What is the easiest way for me to catch pests that are destroying my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ mamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni miifite miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: The easiest time to catch pests is when they come out into the open to feed on the green leaves. Because they are focused on eating and clearly visible on top of the plants or water, you can easily pick or trap them.
ga: Be ni yɔɔ mlɛo fe fɛɛ ni abaanyɛ amɔmɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ji be mli ni amɛje kpo yɛ kpo nɔ koni amɛye baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa niyenii nɔ, ni anaa amɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ tsei loo nu nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okɛ amɛ loo omɔ amɛ oya.

english: Why is it important to control adult insects right after they lay their eggs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akudɔ kooloi bibii ni eda lɛ beni amɛwo amɛwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Adult insects come out to feed on green leaves right after laying eggs. Catching or killing the parents while they are feeding stops them from laying even more egg batches on your crops later.
ga: Kplukai ni eda lɛ jeɔ kpo koni amɛye baai eŋɔli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni amɛwo amɛwui lɛ. Fɔlɔi ni ooomɔ loo ogbe amɛ beni ohaa amɛ niyenii Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkawo ŋmeii yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii anɔ sɛɛ mli.

english: Can I safely gather edible farm insects or field crabs that come out to eat my crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ mabua ŋmɔ mli kooloi bibii ni ayeɔ loo ŋmɔ mli ŋmeii ni yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa shweshweeshwe?

english: Yes, many edible farm creatures like grasshoppers or field crabs come out to feed on green plants and can be collected for food, provided you have not sprayed toxic chemical pesticides on your farm.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔ mli bɔɔ nii ni ayeɔ tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmɔ mli ŋmeii babaoo yɛ. Amɛjeɔ kpo koni amɛbaye tsei eŋɔli ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛbua amɛnaa akɛ niyenii. Kɛji akɛ okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ gbeyei shwieee oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees suffer from extreme heat and water loss during the dry season because their roots are not deep enough yet. Planting temporary shade crops like plantain beside them provides living cover, keeping the soil moist and protecting tender leaves from burning sunlight.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni fiteɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ he amanehulu ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ bɔ ni sa. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ lateral plantains ni aduɔ Ebaaye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni obu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he

english: Why do my pepper leaves roll up into tight cups during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛfeɔ kɔɔpoi ni mli wa yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants curl their leaves during hot afternoons to reduce the leaf surface area exposed to the sun, which stops water from evaporating too quickly. However, if the leaves stay curled even in the cool morning, it is usually a sign of tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or mites underneath the leaves.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni ekɛba baa lɛ hiɛ ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ baaha nu lɛ akatsɔ oya tsɔ. Shi, kɛji akɛ baai lɛ tee nɔ amɛkpã yɛ leebi ni hulutsoo be mli lɛ, Bei pii lɛ eji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ thrips loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ yɛ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with thick green leaves, but the roots inside the ground are tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ daraaa.

english: When soil has too much nitrogen from overly rich land or wrong fertilizer, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves above the ground instead of tubers below. Cassava needs balanced soil rich in potassium to build large, heavy tuber roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii fe nine loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni ejaaa nɔ. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ baatsu nii. Shikpɔŋ ni ja ni potassium eyi mli obɔ lɛ he miihia cassava koni ekɛfee tuber shishifãi wuji ni tsii.

english: Why is it recommended that I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on the same land where I harvested my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛɔ akɛ adu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpaa ŋmeii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize feeds heavily on nitrogen in the soil and leaves the land exhausted. Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and feed it back into the soil through their roots, naturally restoring fertility for the next crop.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli ni ehaa sũ lɛ fiteɔ. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni aku sɛɛ aha adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ aba kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: What causes small holes in the central leaves of my young maize plants early in the season?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baa lɛ nɔ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli.

english: Small holes inside the funnel or center of young maize plants are caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding on tender shoots. Catching them early by inspecting the plant centers allows you to apply targeted organic or chemical treatments before they destroy the growing point.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ashishifãi loo amɛteŋgbɛ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ amɔmɔ amɛ mra lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha fall armyworm lɛ aya hiɛ. Kɛtsɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ni oookwɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo tsofai ni akɛtoɔ he gbɛjianɔ lɛ atsu nii dani amɛfite he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plant before producing any actual tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛwo tomato diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by irregular watering, sudden high temperatures, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch and avoiding heavy synthetic fertilizers helps the plant hold onto flowers until fruit forms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. hulutsoo ni yaa hiɛ trukaa loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛfataa he Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ajie ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee lɛ ni tsii lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni emɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashi yibii lɛ baawo.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava stems very close together to get more plants on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná tsei babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When cassava stems are planted too close, their roots compete fiercely underground for water and soil food, while their leaves fight for sunlight above. Giving each plant proper space ensures roots have room to expand into big tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni ebaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni jɛɔ ŋwɛi lɛ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ náa hegbɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds away from my crops even when my crops are much taller than the weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ? Shi kɛlɛ, miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ kwraa fe jwɛi lɛ.

english: Even small weeds steal nutrients and water directly from the crop's shallow roots. Weeds also harbor insect pests and crop diseases that can spread to your taller plants.
ga: Jwɛi bibii po Jwɛi hu juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi lɛ hu hiɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei ahe helai ni baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã otsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: How can I tell when my cocoa pods are ready for harvesting without damaging the tree?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ efee klalo akɛ makpa ni mifiteee tso lɛ?

english: Cocoa pods are ready when their skin color completely changes from green to bright yellow, or from dark red to orange-yellow. Harvesting green pods yields low-quality beans, while leaving pods too long causes them to rot or attract pests.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ hewolo lɛ su tsake kɛjɛ eŋɔli mli kɛtee ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse mli. aloo kɛjɛ tsuru ni mli edɔ nɔ kɛyashi ŋmɔŋ-ɔranji kwraa nɔ. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ oshi ŋmeii lɛ amli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agbo loo ebaagbala ŋmeii kɛba.

english: Why is mulching recommended over my newly made yam mounds after planting seed yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ mikɛ mulch awo mi sweet potato pile hee ni mifee lɛ nɔ beni adu sweet potato lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Covering yam mounds with dry grass or leaves keeps the soil cool and holds moisture in the soil. High soil temperatures can scorch buried yam seeds or cause them to rot before they have a chance to sprout.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ha sweet potatoes ni ato lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ashã sweet potato dumɔwui ni afu lɛ loo eha amɛgboi dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Can I plant crops on land near an illegal mining site, or will the plants die?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ hei ni ajieɔ shika tsuru yɛ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ nɔ? Aloo tso lɛ baagbo loo egboŋ?

english: Mining often leaves heavy chemicals and packed, washed-away soil that prevents crops from absorbing nutrients. Polluted or disturbed soil causes plants to turn yellow, stay stunted, or die because their roots cannot breathe or find proper food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shika tsuru tsaa nitsumɔi lɛ shĩɔ tsofai ni tsii kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni nu efo mli lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haaa tsei lɛ aná niyenii kpakpai. Shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji loo ni ehao lɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ, loo amɛgboiɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu loo amɛna niyenii ni sa.

english: Why do my crops wilt and turn yellow even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbo ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ lɛ?

english: When soil is heavily packed or damaged, rainwater cannot drain properly and stays around the roots. Overly wet roots suffocate because they need air to survive, which causes the leaves to turn yellow and wilt despite the water.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ loo efite Nugbɔ nu lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni ehiɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Shishifãi ni efɔ fe nine lɛ shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia amɛ koni amɛhi shi. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ kɛji amɛfɔ po.

english: Why does my maize stay short and pale green while my neighbor's maize grows tall and dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kooloi lɛ yɔɔ kuku ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, akutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmãa lɛ da ni etsɔ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ.

english: Maize needs a nutrient called nitrogen to grow tall and dark green. If your soil is worn out or lacks organic matter, the plants stay short and light in color, which you can fix by adding manure or compost before planting.
ga: Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃ ni efee ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ efite loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ mli lɛ Tsei lɛ ahe yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe yɛ kuku. Abaanyɛ asaa enɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli dani aduɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat stress or sudden dry soil. Keeping the soil moist with mulch and protecting young plants from excessive heat helps the flowers stay attached and turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gĩ trukaa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni abu tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Why are my pepper leaves curling up into tight cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni efee kɔɔpoi ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips sucking the juice from the under-side of the leaves. Removing affected leaves early or using mild soapy water sprays helps stop them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Ajieɔ baai ni hela lɛ emɔ lɛ mra Aloo okɛ nu ni mli ejɔ ni akɛ saamɔ eshwie nɔ lɛ atsu nii. Ebaaye ebua ni akpa amɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water accumulates in heavy soil during rainy periods. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess water to drain away, keeping the tubers safe and dry.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Ha yitso lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe ni egbi.

english: Why do my yam vines start turning yellow and dry up from the bottom moving upwards?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbi kɛjɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yam leaves turning yellow from the bottom up is often a sign of fungal infection or poor soil moisture retention. Clearing old crop leaves from around the stem and mulching the soil keeps the vines healthy longer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potato baai ni tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko eba loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni ehiii kwraa. Tso baai momoi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ Stems kɛ mulch ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni wain tso lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow back so quickly on my farm right after I clear them with a cutlass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mikɛ dade shwieɔ amɛnɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Clearing with a cutlass only cuts the weed stems above ground, leaving roots and hidden seeds intact in the soil. Covering the exposed ground with dry leaves or straw blocks sunlight and prevents new weed seeds from sprouting.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei tsu nii lɛ, jwɛi tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ pɛ shwieɔ shi. Shishifãi kɛ dumɔwui ni akɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ. Kɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi aha hei ni egbele lɛ ahe koni hulu la akashɛ nɔ ni jwɛi dumɔwui heei akakwɛ̃.

english: Why are small holes appearing all over my cabbage leaves overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ani ebaaje kpo yɛ kaabeji baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ nyɔɔŋ kome mli?

english: Holes in cabbage leaves are typically caused by caterpillars feeding in the cool evening hours. Inspecting plants in the early morning to pick them off or using neem seed extract sprays helps protect the foliage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni taoɔ niyenii yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ kaabɛji baai amli lɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ tsei lɛ amli leebi koni ojie amɛ. Aloo okɛ neem dumɔwui amli nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ atsu nii ni eye ebua ni ebu baai lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up when I remove all the shade trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ kɛ́ mijie cacao lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that easily scorch under direct sunlight. Shade trees act like protective umbrellas, keeping the air cool and moist around the young seedlings until they grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ ambrela ni buɔ mɔ he. Kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ni eeeha efee fɛ̃i ni edɔ lɛ nɔ. dumɔwui lɛ aahu kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ baadara ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo

english: Why do my harvested yams start to rot so quickly when stored in a warm place?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Yams are living tubers that continue to breathe after harvest. High temperatures and skin injuries cause them to lose water rapidly and allow fungal infections to enter and spoil the crop.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka ni yaa nɔ amɛmuɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Dɔlɛ ni mli wa kɛ hewolo nɔ pilamɔ haa nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya ni ehaa ŋmeii boteɔ mli ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my stored yams start growing green shoots even when they are not in the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ shweremɔ eyɛ mli akɛ amɛbɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Yams have a natural resting period called dormancy. Once this period ends, the tuber automatically uses its stored energy and water to sprout, preparing to grow into a new plant.
ga: Atomɔ yɛ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy. Kɛ be nɛɛ ba naagbee lɛ Bulbs lɛ kɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii amɛ diɛŋtsɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃. Koni asaa he koni eda ni etsɔ tso hee

english: Yam vines climb so their leaves can capture direct sunlight. The leaves use sunlight to manufacture food, which is sent underground to feed and expand the yam tuber.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ashɛ hulu la lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Baai kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛ feɔ niyenii. ni akɛmajeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛye niyenii ni amɛdu sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ

english: Why are the leaves on my crop turning yellow and curling up during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing and curling leaves mean the plant is under water stress or being attacked by small pests like aphids. Shedding or curling leaves helps the plant reduce water loss to stay alive.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ yɛ nu mli haomɔ shishi loo tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ aphids etutua lɛ. Baai ni gbeeɔ shi loo amɛkuɔ amɛhe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhaa nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ baa shi koni amɛhi wala mli.

english: Why do my yam tubers split open or crack while still under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ mli gbalaa loo amɛgbalaɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lolo lɛ?

english: Tubers crack when a long dry spell is followed by sudden heavy rain. The plant drinks up water too quickly, causing the inner part of the tuber to expand faster than the outer skin can stretch.
ga: Bulb lɛ tswaa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa ni nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Tsei nuɔ nu oya tsɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, yitso lɛ mligbɛ lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Yam tubers need loose, deep soil to expand downward without pushing against hard dirt. Mounds create soft soil while improving drainage so standing water doesn't drown the roots.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã kɛya shi ni amɛtsiii amɛhe kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa he. Gɔji feɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ yɛ be mli ni ehaa nu ni hoɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ bɔni afee ni nu ni ekã shi lɛ akashwie shishifãi lɛ anɔ.

english: How do I choose the best yam pieces to cut and plant for the next season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmeii ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mafolɔ ni madu kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: Select healthy, undamaged tubers from strong plants. Rubbing the cut pieces with wood ash or fungicide protects them from rotting in the damp soil before they can sprout.
ga: Halamɔ bulbs ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni efiteee kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli. Kɛ́ okɛ tso mli sũ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ shwie ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛkafite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do my yams produce much smaller tubers when I plant them in the exact same field every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii kwraa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Yams consume heavy amounts of nutrients from the soil. Planting them in the same spot continuously depletes those essential nutrients and allows yam-specific pests to build up in the ground.
ga: Atomɔ heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akwɛ amɛ yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha nakai niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni sweet potato mli tsɛŋemɔ helai pɔtɛɛ komɛi buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Can I plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same farm alongside my yams?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ ŋmeii ni ŋɔɔ?

english: Yes, planting legumes alongside yams is helpful because legumes take nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil, providing natural nutrients that feed the growing yams.
ga: Hɛɛ, sɛɛnamɔ yɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa he lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa ŋmeii ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: How do I know that my yams are fully mature and ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Yams are mature when the leaves and vines naturally turn yellow and completely dry up. This signals that the vine has stopped growing and transferred all its food into the tuber underground.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ kwraa kɛ́ baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ tsɔ adebɔɔ mli su ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi kwraa. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ wain tso lɛ ekpa dalɛ ni ekɛ eniyenii fɛɛ etee shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Yellowing leaves on maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which is a key nutrient plants need to grow green and healthy. It can also happen when heavy rains wash away nutrients or when soil stays waterlogged for too long.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná hewalɛ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ loo kɛ́ nu ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: Is it better for me to burn my land when clearing it or to cut the grass and leave it on the farm?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mashã shikpɔŋ lɛ koni mikɛjie jwɛi? Aloo ashi jwɛi ni afo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Clearing land without burning (mulching) is better for long-term farm health. Burning kills beneficial living organisms in the soil and burns away natural plant nutrients, whereas leaving cut grass to decay adds organic matter and keeps the soil moist.
ga: He ni ajieɔ lɛ ni ashãaa (mulching) lɛ hi kɛha ŋmɔ lɛ hewalɛnamɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ni eyeɔ tsei amli niyenii lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, jwɛi ni afo lɛ ni ashiɔ koni egbo lɛ haa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my bean plants have plenty of big green leaves but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pea tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: When beans grow lush leaves with few pods, it usually means the soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer. Excess nitrogen tells the plant to focus all its energy on growing leafy stems rather than producing flowers and crop pods.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ lɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsɔ. Nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛɛ tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii yɛ baai ni miida lɛ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, tso ɔ woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ fɔfɔi.

english: What is making the leaves of my pepper plants curl up and look wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni haa pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni ekpɔtɔ?

english: Wrinkled and curling pepper leaves are typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the sap from under the leaves, or by a plant virus spread by these insects. Checking under leaves early and using organic or recommended sprays helps control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai ni egbɔjɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. loo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ ashishi mra. Ni kɛ akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ baai lɛ.

english: How can I protect my young corn farm from armyworms eating the inner leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-abɛi ŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ ahe?

english: Fall armyworms hide inside the central funnel of young corn plants. You can control them by inspecting your farm early and applying recommended insecticides, or dropping clean ash or neem solution directly into the funnels when you notice small holes.
ga: Fall cutworms lɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli. Obaanyɛ okudɔ amɛ kɛtsɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni oookwɛ mra lɛ nɔ. ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu nii lɛ atsu nii Aloo okɛ sũ ni he tse loo neem solution awo funnel lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛ́ ona buji bibii.

english: Tomatoes wilting in wet soil are often infected with a soil disease like bacterial wilt or root rot. The disease blocks the water pipes inside the stem, preventing water from reaching the upper plant even if plenty of moisture is in the dirt.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli tamɔ bacteria wilt loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ yeɔ tomato ni shwieɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Hela nɛɛ tsiɔ nu paipii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ anaa. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekashɛ tso lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ kɛji ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ po.

english: When is the right time for me to plant cassava in Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ Ghana?

english: Cassava grows best when planted at the start of the main rainy season—around April to May in southern regions and May to June in the north. Planting early allows the stem cuttings to establish deep roots before dry weather comes.
ga: Cassava daa jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ adu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee mli. Aaafee April kɛyashi May yɛ anaigbɛ kpokpaa lɛ nɔ. kɛ May kɛyashi June yɛ kooyigbɛ kpokpaa lɛ nɔ. Dumɔ kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ náa shishifãi ni mli kwɔ dani hulutsoo be lɛ baa.

english: Why do cocoa flowers keep falling off my trees without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsɔɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers fall prematurely due to extreme heat stress, dry soil, or damage from tiny insects called mirids (capsids). Keeping shade trees on the farm and protecting young trees during dry spells helps flowers develop into full pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli, shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo kooloi bibii ni fiteɔ lɛ hewɔ. Ale amɛ akɛ myrids (capsids), ni amɛkwɛɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ, ni amɛbuɔ tsei bibii ahe yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ daraa kwraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do some of my yam tubers grow in strange, twisted shapes instead of long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miida ni amɛmiifee nibii ni yɔɔ srɔto, ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow twisted when they encounter hard, stony soil underground or when microscopic worms called nematodes damage the tip of the growing yam. Making tall, soft earth mounds or ridges allows yams to expand straight.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ ashishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji amɛkɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ lɛ kpe. Aloo beni ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ fiteɔ ŋmeii ni akwɛ̃ɔ lɛ ashishifãi lɛ. Gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni afee lɛ yeɔ ebuaa sweet potato lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How do I choose healthy plantain suckers to plant on my land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantain tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni mikɛdu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Choose maiden suckers with narrow, sword-like leaves and firm, clean bases (corms). Avoid suckers that show dark rot, holes, or tunnel marks inside the corm, as these are signs of plantain stem borers and root disease.
ga: Halamɔ yei tsei bibii ni yɔɔ baai bibii, tamɔ klante kɛ shishi ni he tse, ni ma shi shiŋŋ (rhizome). Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ, ni tamɔ bu lɛ ahe. aloo amɛyɛ tunnel okadii yɛ amɛyitso mli Enɛ ji akɛ, enɛɛmɛi ji plantain stem borer kɛ shishifã hela he okadii.

english: Why do I see a white powdery coating covering the leaves of my garden eggs and peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa powda yɛŋ ni miiha eggplant kɛ pepper baai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: That white powder is usually a fungal disease called powdery mildew or an infestation of tiny insects called mealybugs. It happens when plants are stressed by humid or dry weather, blocking the leaves from taking in sunlight to feed the plant.
ga: Ekolɛ powda yɛŋ lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew loo tsɛŋemɔ hela bibioo ko ni baa mɔ nɔ. Atsɛɔ no akɛ ŋmeii. Ebaa kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ loo nugbɔshiimɔ miigba tsei anaa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ naaa hulu la koni ekɛ niyenii aha tso lɛ.

english: What is that sticky white substance covering the stems of my cassava plants?
ga: Mɛni ji nɛkɛ nɔ yɛŋ ni kpɛtɛɔ he nɛɛ? No ha mi-cassava tso lɛ he?

english: That sticky white material is caused by cassava mealybugs. These small pests cluster on the stems and leaves to suck out the plant's juices, weakening the crop and leaving behind a white, waxy substance.
ga: Nibii yɛŋ ni kpɛtɛɔ he lɛ jɛɔ ŋmei mealybug lɛ mli. ŋmeii bibii Enɛɛmɛi buaa amɛhe naa yɛ tso lɛ shishi kɛ baai lɛ anɔ koni amɛnu nu kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ baa ni eshiɔ nɔ ko ni tamɔ wax yɛŋ yɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why does my harvested maize develop a white fuzzy growth when I store it in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ feɔ futafuta tamɔ mliki kɛ́ mikɛto ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: White fuzzy growth on stored maize is mold caused by moisture. If maize is not dried completely under the sun before storage, trapped dampness allows fungi to grow and spoil the grains.
ga: Fuzzy yɛŋ ni dalɛ yɔɔ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ nɔ lɛ ji ŋmãa ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛbaa. Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛtoɔ lɛ Fɛ̃i ni amɔmɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmãa lɛ akwɛ̃ ni efite dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Why are my groundnut pods soft and empty inside when I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut ŋmɔtɔi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni nɔ ko bɛ mli kɛ́ mikpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts need calcium in the soil to form hard outer shells and full seeds inside. When the soil lacks calcium, the plant forms soft or empty shells, a condition farmers call 'pops'.
ga: Calcium he miihia ŋmei yɛ sũ lɛ mli koni efee kponɔgbɛ ŋmei ni wa kɛ dumɔwui ni eyi obɔ yɛ emli. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ calcium lɛ Tso lɛ baafee ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko. This is a condition farmers call 'pop'.

english: Why does the outer layer of a cocoa pod turn into a hard shell as it grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tso lɛ kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni edaa lɛ?

english: As a cocoa pod matures, its outer wall builds up thick fibers and minerals to form a tough protective shell. This shell shields the precious beans inside from insect damage and harsh weather.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ dara kwraa lɛ, kponɔgbɛ gbogbo lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmeii kɛ shika tsuru ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ koni ekɛfee gbɛtsii nii ni mli wa. Nɛkɛ ŋmei nɛɛ buɔ kɔfi yibii ni jara wa ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa lɛ ahe.

english: Why do oil palm fruits develop such a thick, hard nut shell around the inner kernel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ oil palm aduawai lɛ yɛ ŋmei ni mli wa ni bɔleɔ emligbɛ lɛ he lɛ?

english: The hard shell around the palm kernel is nature's way of protecting the oil-rich seed inside from pests, decay, and animals until conditions are right for the seed to sprout.
ga: Kpoji ni wa ni bɔleɔ tso lɛ he lɛ ji adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ dumɔwui ni fɔ eyi mli obɔ lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe. fitemɔ kɛ kooloi srɔtoi Kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ shihilɛ ni sa mli.

english: Why does my cassava root get a hard, woody outer skin if I leave it in the soil too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ kponɔgbɛ fã ni wa ni tamɔ tso kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: As cassava grows past its main harvest time, the plant deposits tough wood fibers into its outer skin and center to protect its stored food, making the tuber hard and difficult to cook.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei eda kɛho kpamɔɔ be titri lɛ he lɛ Tsei buaa tsei ahe tsɔi ni wa anaa yɛ kponɔgbɛ kɛ teŋgbɛ koni amɛkɛbu niyenii ni ato lɛ he. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ewaa akɛ aaaho.

english: How does spreading crushed seashell powder or agricultural lime on my farm help my crops grow?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋshɔ mli ŋmeii ni atswa loo okwaayeli mli ŋmeii ni akɛshwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛshwereɔ?

english: Crushed shells and lime contain calcium carbonate, which neutralizes strong sourness (acidity) in soil. Reducing soil acidity helps crop roots absorb water and fertilizers much more efficiently.
ga: Calcium carbonate yɛ ŋmeii ni atswa kɛ lime mli. ni haa sũ ni bɛŋkɛɛɛ he lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ (acidity) Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni baa shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei shishifãi lɛ ni amɛŋɔɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my developing tomatoes get hard white or yellow patches on their skin during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni miiya hiɛ lɛ hiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni wa yɛ amɛhewolo nɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Hard white patches on tomatoes are caused by intense heat and direct sunlight, known as sunscald. The extreme sun damages the outer tissue layer of the fruit before it can ripen evenly.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli wa ni yɔɔ tomato nɔ lɛ baa. Ale lɛ hu akɛ hulutsoo. Hulu la ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ aduawai lɛ kponɔgbɛ fãi lɛ dani ekwɛ̃ɔ kwraa.

english: Why does a crusty white layer sometimes form on top of my field soil after heavy rain or watering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ ni tamɔ mliki lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-ŋmãa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo nu ni awoɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: A white crust forms when water dissolves minerals like salts and calcium deep in the soil and pulls them to the surface. As the water evaporates, it leaves behind a thin mineral layer on top.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ yɛŋ baa kɛji nu shwie nibii tamɔ ŋmei kɛ calcium ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ nɔ. ni egbalaa amɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi. Beni nu lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ Abaashi mineral layer bibioo ko yɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my maize leaves curl up into tight rolls during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmãa ni mli wa yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up like straws to reduce their surface area facing the sun. This helps the plant trap moisture inside and prevent itself from drying out when water is scarce.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ jwɛi koni ekɛba ŋwɛi ni kwɛɔ hulu la lɛ hiɛ lɛ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ emli lɛ, ni ehaaa egbi kɛ́ nu faaa.

english: Why are my pepper plants turning yellow and dropping leaves after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbaa fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plant roots need air to breathe. When excess rain leaves soil waterlogged, the roots drown and rot, preventing the plant from taking up food and causing leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Pepper tso shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ tsɔ lɛ, nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛbaagboi. Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaye nii ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Watermelons crack when they get a sudden large amount of water after a dry spell. The inside of the fruit expands faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing it to split.
ga: Watermelon lɛ tswaa kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe wo nu babaoo mli trukaa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ. Yibii lɛ amli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. kɛ mligbalamɔ baa

english: Why does my cassava produce big green leaves on top but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ hiɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi ani yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen or too much water during early growth, the cassava plant spends all its energy producing leaves instead of storing starch in the root tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo nu babaoo yɛ shishijee be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ daa lɛ. Cassava tsei kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛfeɔ baai moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ starch baato amɛshishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their blossoms without setting any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miifɔlɔ ni ewooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when temperature levels get extremely hot or water supply drops suddenly, as heat stress prevents proper pollination inside the blossom.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo nu lɛ ba shi trukaa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dɔlɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ naa.

english: Why are my sweet potato vines spreading everywhere without giving me good tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa he fɛɛ he ni ehaaa mi ŋmeii kpakpai lɛ?

english: Sweet potatoes require a brief period of mild water stress to signal the roots to store food. Continuous feeding and overwatering encourage vine leaf growth rather than tuber development.
ga: Nu fioo pɛ biɔ sweet potato yɛ be kukuoo mli. Koni ekɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ koni amɛkɛ niyenii ato. Niyenii ni akɛhaa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa fe nine lɛ haa wain tso baa lɛ daa fe bɔ ni tuber lɛ yaa hiɛ ehaa.

english: Is it bad to water my crops in the middle of a hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehiii akɛ mawo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ nu yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli?

english: Yes, watering in direct midday sun causes most water to evaporate before reaching the roots, and water droplets left on hot leaves can scorch the foliage.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kɛ́ afɔ nu yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shwane mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani eshɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ni nu ni shwieɔ baai ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha baai lɛ ashã.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and weak and fall over easily when planted close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ ni egbeeɔ shi oya kɛji akɛ adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he lɛ?

english: When crops are overcrowding each other, they compete for sunlight by stretching upwards quickly. This makes their stems thin and weak, causing wind to push them over easily.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la he akaŋ kɛtsɔ oyaiyeli ni amɛshwieɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. Ehaa tso lɛ mli tso lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tsɔɔ mli mlɛo.

english: Why do my young maize plants develop ragged holes in the leaves overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ná ŋmeii yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ nyɔɔŋ kome mli lɛ?

english: Pests like Fall Armyworm hide deep inside the center whorl of the maize plant during the hot day and come out at night to feed on the tender young leaves.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. ni amɛjeɔ kpo gbɛkɛ koni amɛye baai bibii

english: Why are my yam vines drying up and turning brown before the harvest season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ egbi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani kpamɔɔ be baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally die back when tubers reach full maturity, but early drying usually indicates root damage from heat stress, poor drainage, or underground fungal infection.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ gboi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji bulbs lɛ dara. Shi bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ egbi oya lɛ, etsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi lɛ efite kɛjɛ latsaa mli. nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ loo shikpɔŋ shishi tsɛŋemɔ hela

english: Maize leaves roll up during intense heat to protect themselves and prevent water from evaporating too quickly. It is the plant's natural defense mechanism, but if the leaves stay rolled up early in the morning, it means the soil is dangerously dry and needs water.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe ni amɛtsi nu lɛ naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ. Eji tsei adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo. Shi kɛji akɛ baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lolo leebi lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi yɛ oshara gbɛ nɔ ni nu he miihia lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves droop down in the middle of the day even when the plant looks healthy in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ leebi lɛ?

english: Cassava leaves rest or droop in the afternoon sun to expose less surface area to direct heat, saving moisture. As long as the leaves stand back up when the weather cools in the evening or early morning, your crop is behaving normally.
ga: Cassava baai lɛ jɔɔ amɛhe loo amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ shwane hulu lɛ he bɔni afee ni ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ dɔlɛ fioo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ hiɔ shi Bei abɔ ni baai lɛ teɔ shi beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ gbɛkɛ loo leebi maŋkpa lɛ, Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa nɔ tamɔ bɔ ni eji daa lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves mean the plant is lacking nitrogen. To keep growing, the crop takes nitrogen from its older bottom leaves and sends it to the top leaves, so applying nitrogen fertilizer or manure will help feed the plant.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen. koni tsei aya nɔ amɛdara Tsei lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli ni amɛkɛyaa ŋwɛi baai lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha tsei lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are the edges of my young maize leaves turning purple?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ ashishigbɛi lɛ miitsɔ purple lɛ?

english: Purple leaves on young maize are a sign that the plant cannot get enough phosphorus from the soil, often because the roots are still small or the soil is too cold. Adding phosphorus fertilizer or letting the roots expand will help the leaves turn green again.
ga: Baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ enaaa fɔsfɔs ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni haa ebaa lɛ nakai ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ darako loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ejɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ fɔsfɔs wo mli loo oha shishifãi lɛ mli alɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my young cocoa seedlings leaning and growing sideways instead of standing straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso bibioo lɛ miitsi ehe ni eekwɛ̃ yɛ afãgbɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni edamɔ shi shiŋŋ lɛ?

english: Crops naturally bend toward sunlight. If overhead shade trees are too thick on one side, the young cocoa plant will lean and stretch sideways to reach the light, so you need to trim the shade trees to balance the light.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa hulu la lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ babaoo yɛ fa kome lɛ, Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe shi ni amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa afã lɛ koni amɛmɔ la lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni ofolɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ koni la lɛ afee ekome.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with thin stems and few leaves instead of growing thick and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ miiya hiɛ waa lɛ? Eyɛ tso bibioo kɛ baai fioo. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ jwɛi ni mli edɔ?

english: When crops are planted too close together or hidden under heavy shade, they stretch upward searching for light instead of developing strong stems and roots. Spacing your plants properly lets light reach all parts of the plant.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo akɛtee yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Tsei lɛ baajie amɛhe kpo ni amɛtao la moŋ, ni amɛbaaná shishifãi kɛ shishifãi ni wa. Gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ tsei ateŋ lɛ haa la shɛɔ tso lɛ fãi fɛɛ ahe.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they feel stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or lack of nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist and providing light shade helps the plant hold onto its flowers until fruit sets.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why are my small cocoa pods turning shriveled and black before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii So mine lɛ shwieɔ ni etsɔɔ ediŋŋ dani edaa lɛ?

english: Tiny cocoa pods turn black and die due to a natural process called pod wilt when the tree has too many pods to feed, or because of fungal disease caused by excess moisture. Pruning extra branches allows sunlight and air to keep the tree healthy.
ga: cocoa pods bibii Etsɔɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ yɛ adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ pod wilting lɛ hewɔ beni tso lɛ yɛ pods babaoo tsɔ ni ekɛ niyenii haa lɛ. aloo yɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ni hulutsoo be ni fa fe nine kɛbaa lɛ hewɔ Tso lɛ ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is there a white powdery film covering the leaves of my vegetables?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sini yɛŋ ni tamɔ powda ni ha mi-vegetables baai lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: That white powder is a fungal growth called powdery mildew, which spreads when humidity is high. It blocks sunlight from reaching the leaf, so removing heavy weeds to improve air movement helps keep the leaves clean and dry.
ga: Nakai powda yɛŋ lɛ ji ŋmei ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ fa babaoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni etsĩɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ baai lɛ ahe. No hewɔ lɛ, jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ tsii koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ ahe atse ni amɛgbi.

english: Why are the stems of my yam vines turning brown and dying from the ground upward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigboi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Stems turning brown from the base usually indicates a root or soil problem, such as excessive water rotting the stem or pests attacking underneath. Ensuring good drainage on your yam mounds prevents water from collecting around the stem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni feɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ shishifã loo shikpɔŋ he naagba, tamɔ nu babaoo ni haa tso lɛ fiteɔ loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni tutuaa shishi. Nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ sweet potato gɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baatsi nu naa koni ekabua ehe naa yɛ tso lɛ shishi.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the maize plant lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient it needs to build green leaves and grow tall. Heavy rains often wash nitrogen deep into the ground where small roots cannot reach it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni afee baai eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ nitrogen lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi bibii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ. anyɛɛɛ ashɛ he

english: Why should I plant beans or cowpeas in the same farm with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas are special crops that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When grown alongside maize, they naturally enrich the soil with food that helps the maize grow better.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi amli. Kɛji akɛ adu kɛ ŋmãa lɛ Amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa niyenii ni haa ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in direct sun without any large shade trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa tso bibioo lɛ gbo beni midu lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni mibɛ tso agbo ko ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves and short roots that burn and dry out quickly under harsh sunlight. They need shade trees or plantains to shield them from high heat until their own branches canopy over.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi kukuji ni shãa ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei loo tsei bibii ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo lɛ koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa waa lɛ he, ni eha amɛniji lɛ diɛŋtsɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do many of the flowers on my cocoa trees fall off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop extra flowers when they do not get enough water, when the weather is too dry, or when tiny insects fail to pollinate them. It is the tree's natural way of saving energy for only the pods it can feed.
ga: Cacao tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi krokomɛi kɛji amɛnáaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii nyɛɛɛ afee pollination Eji tso lɛ adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ hewalɛ toɔ ŋmeii ni ebaanyɛ eye lɛ pɛ nɔ.

english: What is making small holes in my corn leaves and leaving powdery waste inside the stalk?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi lɛ amli lɛ baa? Ni ashi jwɛi yɛ tso lɛ mli?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They crawl into the central leaves of the corn plant during the day to feed on soft leaf tissue, which leaves visible ragged holes as the leaf grows out.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛkplekeɔ kɛboteɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ ahe fãji. Enɛ baaha ana buji ni elaaje lɛ beni baai lɛ daraa kɛjeɔ kpo lɛ.

english: This rot is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in wet conditions. Raindrops splash the fungus spores from dirty soil or affected pods onto healthy pods, spreading the rot quickly in cold, wet weather.
ga: Blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. ni ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ mli Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ ŋmei mli ŋmeii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji loo ŋmei ni ena hela lɛ nɔ kɛyaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmei lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ fɛ̃i kɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: How can I tell if my cassava is ready to harvest without digging up the soil?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa ni akuuu mli?

english: Cassava is typically ready when the bottom leaves dry up and fall off, and the soil right around the main stem begins to crack outward because the thick tubers underground are swelling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni amɛgbee shi. kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso titri lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa kponɔgbɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni mli tse lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce very small roots when I plant the cuttings close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ shishifãi bibii waa kɛ́ midu ŋmeii lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When cassava cuttings are planted too close, their underground roots compete fiercely for soil nutrients, space, and water. Spacing them out allows every plant enough room to form thick, heavy tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ŋwɛi, kɛ nu lɛ mli. He ni akɛtoɔ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee bulbs ni mli wa ni tsii.

english: Pepper plants curl their leaves on hot afternoons to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, which stops water from evaporating out of the plant too fast. The leaves usually unfold once temperatures cool down.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ baaha nu lɛ akajɛ tso lɛ mli oya tsɔ. Baai lɛ fɔɔ shwiemɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why does my dried maize get full of small holes and white dust after a few months in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? and white dust after being stored for a few months

english: Small insects called grain weevils lay eggs inside stored maize kernels. When the eggs hatch, the tiny grubs eat the inside of the grain, leaving empty shells and powdery dust behind.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmaa ŋmeii lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmaa ŋmeii ni ato lɛ amli. Kɛ́ wɔji lɛ fɔ lɛ, ŋmeii bibii lɛ yeɔ ŋmaa lɛ mli. Nɔ ko pɛ ni eshwɛ ji ŋshɔŋloo ko ni nɔ ko bɛ mli kɛ sũ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil or the roots are sitting in waterlogged soil, which stops the plant from absorbing nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo akɛ shishifãi lɛ eta sũ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers fall off without ever turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they are stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or when tiny pests like mirids attack the blossoms before pollination is complete.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli, loo kɛ́ kooloi bibii tamɔ fɔfɔi lɛ tutua fɔfɔi lɛ dani fɔfɔi lɛ agbe naa.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their small green fruits before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho aduawai bibii ni ji eŋɔli lɛ? Dani ebaashɛ po?

english: Pepper plants shed immature fruit when there is a sudden change in soil moisture, extremely hot weather, or when fruit flies lay eggs inside the young peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baawo yibii ni eshɛko kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake trukaa. kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa Aloo be mli ni aduawai amli ŋmeii woɔ ŋmeii bibii amli.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves drop down and look dead in the afternoon, but stand back up at night?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbo yɛ shwane mli lɛ? Shi shidaamɔ gbɛkɛ?

english: Plants wilt slightly during hot afternoons to conserve water by reducing evaporation. Once the sun sets and the air cools down, the roots catch up and restore water to the leaves.
ga: Tsei shwieɔ shi fioo yɛ shwane mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ ni amɛbaa shi lɛ nɔ. Kɛ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛkɛ nu aku sɛɛ kɛba baai lɛ amli.

english: Why do my crops struggle to grow when dirty water from nearby muddy land flows into my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ beni nu fɔŋ ni jɛɔ sũ ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ mli lɛ hoɔ kɛbaa miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Muddy water carries heavy silt and pollutants that coat plant roots and soil, blocking air and nutrients from reaching the roots, which smothers the crops.
ga: Nu ni mli ewo muji lɛ mli ŋmeii ni tsii kɛ muji ni haa tsei shishifãi kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yɔɔ mli. Etsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ baafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil stays too wet for long periods, creating a damp environment where fungal diseases thrive and destroy the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ adara ni amɛfite ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why does my land produce less maize every year when I plant it in the same place without resting the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo daa afi beni miduɔ yɛ he kome ni mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ejɔɔɔ mihe lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving the ground time to recover, causing the land to become tired and nutrient-poor.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ yaa nɔ ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛtsake ehe. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɔɔ ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up into tight cups and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ kɔɔpoi ni mli wa ni amɛkpaa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is often caused by a virus spread by tiny whiteflies, or it is the plant's natural defense mechanism to reduce water loss during hot, dry weather.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Aloo eji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe koni amɛha nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Why are holes appearing in the center of my corn stalks and leaves while they are growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-abele tsei kɛ baai lɛ ateŋ be mli ni abele ŋmeii lɛ miida lɛ?

english: Holes in the center whorl of maize are usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which crawl inside the growing tip of the plant and chew the leaves before they unfold.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni shwieɔ tsei ni miida lɛ ashishigbɛ ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ dani amɛgbeleɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ baa.

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems that can easily be damaged by microscopic soil worms (nematodes), making the roots too weak to hold up heavy fruit bunches during wind.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii bibii waa baanyɛ afite amɛ oya. (Nematodes) haa shishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛmɔmɔ aduawai ni tsii yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ be mli.

english: Why shouldn't I cut down big mahogany trees when clearing land for my food crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mifoɔ mahogany tsei wuji beni misaa shikpɔŋ kɛha niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ lɛ?

english: Deep-rooted trees like mahogany draw water and nutrients from far underground without competing with shallow-rooted food crops, while their falling leaves fertilize the topsoil and protect it from harsh heat.
ga: Tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ, tamɔ mahogany lɛ, gbalaa nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛkɛ niyenii tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ he eko lɛ yeee akaŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, baai ni egbee shi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa he.

english: Can I plant cassava and maize under fast-growing teak trees on my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ teak tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ ashishi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You can plant food crops between teak trees during their first two or three years, but as the teaks grow large, their heavy shade will stop maize and cassava from getting the sunlight they need to yield well.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu niyenii yɛ teak tsei lɛ ateŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ loo etɛ lɛ mli. Shi kɛ́ teak tso lɛ da Teak tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni tsii lɛ haaa ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa aná hulu la ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai lɛ.

english: Is it profitable to keep timber trees on the same land where I grow my seasonal crops?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ mahã tsei lɛ ahi he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni miduɔ tsei ni baa be mli lɛ?

english: Yes, combining timber trees with food crops gives you seasonal food and income in the short term, while the trees act as a long-term savings account when they mature.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni akɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ haa onáa niyenii kɛ be mli shika yɛ be kukuoo mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tso lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ shika ni akɛtoɔ be kakadaŋŋ be mli ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why do some big trees weaken the crops growing near them while other trees do not?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei wuji komɛi haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ, yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu egbɔjɔɔɔ lɛ?

english: Trees with shallow roots spread near the surface and steal fertilizer and moisture from your crops, whereas deep-rooted trees reach far down into the subsoil, leaving topsoil nutrients for your crops.
ga: Tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ Egbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ ni ejuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Yɛ be mli ni tsei ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ yaa shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ lɛ. Shi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛha onibii.

english: How do I know if a tree on my farmland has deep roots or shallow roots?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ loo amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ?

english: Trees that stay green during long droughts and have straight, tall trunks like mahogany usually have deep taproots, while trees with thick roots visible on top of the ground have shallow root systems.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni hiɔ shi eŋɔli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛlɛɔ ni ja, tamɔ mahogany lɛ, shishifãi ni mli kwɔ waa yɛ. yɛ be mli ni tsei ni shishifãi ni mli tse ni anaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ.

english: Will clearing weeds and applying fertilizer to my crops harm the large trees growing on my farm?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni mikɛbaatsu nii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye tsei ni eda ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ awui?

english: No, caring for your crops actually helps the trees grow faster and healthier because they benefit from the weed control and extra nutrients in the soil.
ga: Dabi, onibii ni okwɛɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ diɛŋtsɛ ni amɛdaraa oya ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛnáa jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ kɛ niyenii krokomɛi ni fata he ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he sɛɛ.

english: How does heavy shade from big tree leaves affect the growth of my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ hulutsoo ni jɛɔ tsei wuji ahe baai lɛ amli lɛ saa tsei lɛ adalɛ he?

english: Most food crops like maize, peppers, and cassava need direct sunlight to produce fruit, so heavy shade will cause them to grow tall, thin, and weak with very small yields.
ga: Niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo, tamɔ abele, chili, kɛ cassava, taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ dani ewo aduawai. No hewɔ lɛ, hulutsoo ni tsii baaha amɛfee kakadaŋŋ, amɛhe afee mlɛo, ni amɛhe waaa ni nɔ ko fioo pɛ amɛfeɔ.

english: What should I do if the branches of trees on my farm are blocking sunlight from my crops?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji tsei niji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miitsi hulu la ni miduɔ lɛ naa?

english: You can prune or trim the lower branches of the trees to let sunlight reach the ground while still keeping the trees alive for timber value and soil protection.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofo loo ofolɔ tso lɛ niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ koni hulu la ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni ohiɛɔ tso lɛ sɛɛnamɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hebuu mli lolo.

english: Why do extension officers on the radio advise us not to burn all the trees when clearing land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ redio nɔ nitsumɔ he nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ akashã tsei lɛ fɛɛ beni ajieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Burning destroys rich organic matter and beneficial soil organisms, whereas leaving mature trees keeps the soil cool, prevents soil erosion during heavy rains, and retains moisture during dry periods.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni jara wa kɛ sũ mli nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ. Yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i lɛ. Etsiɔ shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa. ni ekwɛ koni hulutsoo be lɛ ahi shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli

english: What happens to my soil over time if I leave leaf-dropping trees on my farmland?
ga: Mɛni baaba mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli? Ni kɛji akɛ mishi tsei ni egbee shi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli hu?

english: The leaves that fall from the trees decompose into rich natural compost, continuously feeding your topsoil and keeping it moist without needing as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tsei anɔ lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa, ni ji adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii be fɛɛ be ni okwɛ koni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuuu nii.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. They need partial shade from fast-growing plants like plantains or shade trees to retain soil moisture and protect them until their root systems grow deep enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo fã ko kɛjɛ tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Enɛ ji koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni abu he kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baatsɔ shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why should I cut off extra branches and leaves from my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji kɛ baai krokomɛi ni jɛ kookoo tso ni eda lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or overcrowded branches so air can flow through the tree and sunlight can reach the pods. This keeps the trees dry, which prevents fungal diseases like black pod disease from spreading.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni ebɔle amɛhe fe nine lɛ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ tso lɛ mli ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbi. Enɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pod hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize farm turning yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants use to build green leaves. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their deep green color and healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it good for me to plant groundnuts or beans together with maize on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmei loo ŋmei kɛfata ŋmei he yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting beans or groundnuts alongside maize helps the soil. Legumes take nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for the maize while maximizing your harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei loo ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ hu haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo. Legumes lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa ŋmãa yɛ be kome too mli. and optimize your harvest.

english: Why do extension officers advise me not to plant maize on the exact same plot every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ etsɔɔɔ akɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same plot drains the specific nutrients maize needs and allows soil pests to build up. Rotating maize with crops like cassava or cowpeas gives the soil a chance to recover.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ, abaajie niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ abele mli lɛ kɛya. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ buaa amɛhe naa Abele ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei tsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa hegbɛ ni ekɛ ehe woɔ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: What is causing tiny holes in my young corn leaves and chewing up the middle parts of the stem?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ ni mikɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ shwieɔ shi?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide in the center whorl of the corn plant. Catching them early with recommended pest treatments prevents them from destroying your harvest.
