ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmeii tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛmɔmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe ŋaa lɛ nɔ lɛ obaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when we get heavy rains for several days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Heavy rains cause waterlogging in tight or low-lying soil, choking off the oxygen that roots need to breathe. Plant cassava on raised mounds or ridges so surplus water drains away quickly.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ kɛ nu afua baa shikpɔji ni atsĩ naa loo shikpɔji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni he hiaa ni shishifãi lɛ amu lɛ faaa. Dumɔ ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ bɔni afee ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ oya.

english: Avoid planting after the very first rain, as the ground may still be too dry underneath. Wait until the soil stays consistently wet after two or three good rains so your seeds can germinate safely.
ga: Tsi ohe kɛjɛ dumɔwui ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ekolɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli egbi tsɔ lolo. Mɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi fioo komɛi asɛɛ koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow thin and weak even when I spread fertilizer on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shwie ŋmɔ lɛ mli po lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight meant for your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nutrients you apply.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ ni okɛtsuɔ nii lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the air to catch maximum sunlight. Lifting the leaves off the ground helps the plant produce more energy, resulting in bigger tuber sizes underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Kɛ́ owó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ babaoo baa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ feɔ wuji.

english: Maize takes a lot of food out of the soil. Groundnuts and cowpeas are special plants that pull nutrients from the air and put nitrogen back into the dirt, naturally repairing your farm for the next planting season.
ga: Abele heɔ eniyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛ nitrogen kuɔ sɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ saa oŋmɔ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize turning yellow while the top stays green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the maize is starving for nitrogen. When the plant doesn't get enough food from the soil, it steals nutrients from its oldest leaves to feed the young leaves growing at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. Kɛ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ejuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni etsɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ niyenii.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves and sucking out the plant's juices, or spreading a sickness that distorts leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo helai ni fiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Why are small holes appearing in the young leaves of my maize plants with small droppings left inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii jeɔ kpo yɛ ŋmãa tsei ahe baai bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ? Ani okɛ ohe ewo mli?

english: This is a sign of Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They hide inside the central funnel of the maize plant during the day, eating the leaves before they unfold.
ga: Enɛ ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ahe okadi. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli. ni oye baai lɛ dani amɛje kpo

english: Does it matter which way up I stick cassava cuttings into the soil?
ga: Ani gbɛ ni mitsɔɔ nɔ miduɔ ŋmei lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he hiaa?

english: Yes, cassava cuttings must be planted with the small bud notches pointing up toward the sky. If you plant them upside down, the stems have to bend awkwardly to grow upward, wasting energy and reducing tuber yield.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii. ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi Kɛji odu kɛtee shishi lɛ Esa akɛ tso lɛ tso lɛ abɔle ehe yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ gbeyei nɔ koni etsɔ ŋwɛi. Efiteɔ hewalɛ ni ehaa yitsoŋ shweremɔ baa shi.

english: Why do I have to make big mounds of soil to plant yams instead of planting in flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ afee shikpɔŋ agbo ko ni akɛbaadu sweet potatoes yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaadu yɛ shikpɔŋ kplanaa lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, deep, and loose soil so they can expand easily underground. Large mounds also drain away excess heavy rain so the yams don't rot.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli kwɔ, ni shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ shishi mlɛo. Gɔŋ wulu lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa fe nine lɛ hoɔ koni ŋmeii lɛ akafite.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they are stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or poor nutrients in the soil, which prevents the flower from successfully turning into fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ miigba amɛnaa. Enɛ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ aduawai yɛ omanyeyeli mli.

english: Why is it good to spread dry grass or leaves on top of the soil around my vegetable beds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi afɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-vegetables tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Spreading dry leaves or straw (mulching) shades the ground, keeping the soil moist for longer during hot days, stopping weeds from growing, and turning into natural fertilizer as it rots.
ga: Okɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi (mulch) afɔ nɔ koni eha hulutsoo aba, ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni ebafeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji egbo

english: Why do cassava tubers spoil so quickly just a few days after I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya nɛkɛ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ beni mifo amɛ lɛ?

english: Once cassava is pulled out of the ground, its roots have no natural skin barrier against air. Exposure to oxygen starts an internal chemical reaction that causes the tuber to decay rapidly within two to three days.
ga: Beni ajieɔ ŋmei kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Amɛshishifãi lɛ bɛ adebɔɔ mli hewolo nɔ ko ni tsiɔ amɛ gbɛ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Oxygen ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa tsofa ko ni yɔɔ mli lɛ jeɔ shishi ni haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ mli.

english: Can I plant beans and maize together on the same plot of land?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting beans and maize together works very well. Beans capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which helps the maize grow stronger, while the tall maize stalks give climbing beans a structure to grow on.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei kɛ ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa. Beans mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ daa waa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmãa tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ haa ŋmãa ni kwɔɔ lɛ naa gbɛjianɔtoo kɛha dalɛ.

english: How do beans help improve the soil for my other crops?
ga: Beans haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi. Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná minɔ lɛ?

english: Beans are legumes, which means they have special roots that take nitrogen from the air and convert it into natural food in the soil. This enriches the soil for nearby crops like maize and reduces the need for artificial fertilizers.
ga: Beans ji ŋmeii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛfeɔ lɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ abele, ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee lɛ he hiamɔ baa shi.

english: Should maize or beans be my main crop if I want both fast food and income?
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa afee miŋmɔshi nibii titri kɛji niyenii ni ayeɔ oya kɛ shika fɛɛ he miihia mi.

english: Maize is usually chosen as the main crop because it yields high quantities for family food and bulk sales, while beans act as a valuable secondary crop that matures quickly and restores soil fertility.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ahalaa ŋmãa akɛ ŋmãa titri ejaakɛ ewoɔ ŋmãa babaoo ni akɛhaa wekui niyenii ni ahɔ̃ɔ babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji enyɔ ni he hiaa ni daa oya ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: What should I do if the heavy rains start late in June instead of April or May?
ga: Ni kɛji nugbɔ ni naa wa je shishi yɛ June naagbee gbɛ yɛ April loo May najiaŋ hu?

english: When rains are delayed, you should switch to early-maturing seed varieties that need less time to grow. This ensures your crops mature before the dry period sets in around July or August.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛ Esa akɛ otsake kɛya dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni biɔ be fioo dani ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ akwɛ jogbaŋŋ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba yɛ July loo August he.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow when there is heavy rainfall in July?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ July mli lɛ?

english: Excessive rain leaves the soil waterlogged, which prevents plant roots from breathing and washes away nitrogen from the soil. Without nitrogen, the crop cannot make green leaves and starts turning yellow.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haaa tsei shishifãi lɛ amu ni amɛkajie nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji nitrogen bɛ lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nyɛŋ afee baai eŋɔli ni ebaaje shishi etsɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Is it good to plant maize during the minor rainy season in August?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo yɛ August mli lɛ mli?

english: Yes, but you must plant fast-maturing maize varieties because the minor rainy season is much shorter and less reliable than the main season earlier in the year.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi esa akɛ odu ŋmãa henɔi ni daa oya ejaakɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ yɛ kuku kwraa ni anyɛɛɛ akɛ he afɔ̃ nɔ fe be titri ni baa yɛ afi lɛ shishijee mli lɛ.

english: How do I calculate how many bags of fertilizer I need for my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa mi kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ he akɔntaa?

english: The number of fertilizer bags depends on your land size and crop type. Generally, one acre of maize requires about 2 to 3 bags of NPK for planting and 1 to 2 bags of Urea or SOA applied later for boosting growth.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ayibɔ damɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ dalɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ anɔ. Yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa acre 1 biɔ NPK kotokui 2 kɛyashi 3 koni ekwɛ̃ kɛ urea loo SOA kotokui 1 kɛyashi 2 sɛɛ mli koni ekwɛ̃ babaoo.

english: Why did my neighbor harvest more bags of crop than I did on the same size of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ kpaɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fe mi yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Differences in harvest size usually come down to seed quality, correct plant spacing, timely weeding, and applying the right fertilizer at the exact right crop growth stage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmaa lɛ dalɛ mli lɛ damɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe. correct plant spacing Jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ be ni sa mli kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ tso lɛ dalɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How can I safely store my harvested bags of grain so insects do not eat them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ awo kotokui amli shweshweeshwe koni kooloi akaye amɛ?

english: You must dry your grains thoroughly until they are hard and low in moisture, then store them in airtight hermetic bags (like PICS bags) or treat them with safe grain protectants in a cool, dry room.
ga: Esa akɛ ogbi oŋmaa lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi ebaawa ni ŋmɔtɔ fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛwo kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli (tamɔ PICS kotoku) loo okɛ nɔ ko ni buɔ dumɔwui ahe ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe awo tsu ko ni mli ejɔ ni mli egbi mli.

english: How do I know when my bean pods are ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-pea pods lɛ eshɛ he koni akpa?

english: Beans are ready for harvest when the leaves on the plant turn yellow and dry up, and the seed pods turn light brown and rattle when you shake them.
ga: Beans lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni tso lɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi lɛ. Ni dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ekpokpoɔ kɛ́ okpokpo amɛ.

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves of maize usually means the soil lacks nitrogen, an important food nutrient that plants need to stay green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking the juice from under the leaves, or by a plant virus spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. loo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli

english: Why are my tomato fruits rotting and turning black at the bottom before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ miifite ni etsɔ ediŋŋ yɛ shishigbɛ dani ekwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: This problem is called blossom end rot, which happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium from the soil, usually caused by irregular watering.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why do the flowers on my cocoa trees drop off without forming cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛfeee cacao ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers if there are not enough tiny pollinating insects around, or if the tree is stressed by dry weather and lacks nutrients to feed the growing pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baafɔ̃ kɛji akɛ ŋmeii bibii ni haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ faaa, loo kɛji akɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ miigba tso lɛ naa ni ebɛ niyenii ni haa ŋmeii ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn watery and soft when I harvest them during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ feɔ nu ni amɛhe yɔɔ blɛoo kɛ́ akpa amɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Excess water in the soil causes mature cassava roots to absorb too much moisture and lose their starch content, leading to rot and watery roots.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ daa, amɛheɔ nu babaoo ni amɛhaa ŋmei ni yɔɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ nu.

english: Yams need loose, deep soil to expand easily; if the soil is hard, stony, or compacted, the growing tuber struggles to push through and becomes bent.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli tse koni egbɛ eshwa mlɛo. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa, tɛi yɔɔ mli, loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, bulb ni miida lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni etsɔ mli ni ebɔle ehe.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow very bushy with lots of leaves but give me very few bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii babaoo ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi ehaa mi ŋmeii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes cowpeas to focus all their energy on growing tall stems and leafy foliage instead of making flowers and seed pods.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa cowpea kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ tsei ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni miida lɛ ahe nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee fɔfɔii kɛ dumɔwui ŋmɔji

english: Why do fall armyworms attack my young maize crop so much faster than my other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall armyworms lɛ tutuaa mi-baby corn tsei lɛ mra fe miŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Fall armyworm moths prefer laying eggs on young maize leaves because the caterpillars like to hide and feed inside the soft, central funnel of the growing stem.
ga: Autumn mli ŋmeii sumɔɔ ni amɛwo amɛwui yɛ ŋmãa baa bibii anɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛtee amɛhe ni amɛye nii yɛ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when a strong rain or wind comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ loo kɔɔyɔɔ miitswa lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots holding a very heavy stem; if soil pests damage the roots or if the soil is too waterlogged, the tree easily loses its balance.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ tsii waa. Kɛji kooloi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fite shishifãi lɛ loo kɛji nu eyi sũ lɛ mli tsɔ. Tso lɛ baafee mɔ ni ŋmɛɛɛ shi oya.

english: How do I prevent the fertilizer I put on my crops from being washed away by heavy rains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ anaa koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akaho?

english: Burrying fertilizer slightly under the soil near the root zone and applying it in small portions when the plant is actively growing prevents rain from washing it away.
ga: Fuu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi fioo yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ ni okɛwo mli bibii bibii. Kɛ́ tsei miida lɛ, etsĩɔ nugbɔ naa koni ekajie ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen. Nitrogen gives plants their green color and helps them grow big; adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help them turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Nitrogen haa tsei feɔ eŋɔli ni eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Legumes like cowpeas have special roots that grab nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When the plant leaves drop and decay, this nitrogen acts as free fertilizer for the next crop you plant.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛgbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ tsei lɛ baai lɛ gbee shi ni amɛgboi Nitrogen nɛɛ baatsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni obaadu ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When water sits in the ground for too long, it drowns the roots and causes rot, which is why planting on raised soil mounds or ridges helps water drain away.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛbaagboi. Enɛ hewɔ ni dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ lɛ haa nu hoɔ kɛyaa lɛ.

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when the weather gets extremely hot or when the soil dries out completely. Without enough water or cool air, the plant drops flowers to save its own energy.
ga: Tomato shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Kɛji nu loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ bɛ lɛ Tso lɛ hu baajie efɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi koni ekɛto lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehewalɛ he.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight. Larger shade trees act as a natural shelter to keep the cocoa cool and retain soil moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli he ko ni haa kookoo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do I need to tie my yam vines to wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ sweet potato wain tsei fĩɔ tsei ahe lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can spread out and catch direct sunlight. The more sunlight the leaves catch, the more food the plant makes to grow a large tuber under the ground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛha baai lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Babaoo ni baai lɛ shɛɔ hulu la lɛ nɔ lɛ, Babaoo ni tso lɛ feɔ niyenii lɛ, babaoo ni niyenii ni ebaanyɛ ekwɛ kɛha bulbs wuji ni baa shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Why are my plantain shoots producing smaller leaves and tiny bunches after two years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ woɔ baai bibii kɛ panicles bibii yɛ afii enyɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When too many suckers (baby plantain shoots) grow around one mother plant, they steal food and water from each other. Pruning extra suckers leaves only 2 or 3 strong stems to produce bigger bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo (ŋmeii bibii) ni miida yɛ tso kome ni ji nyɛ kome lɛ he lɛ Amɛbaaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ amɛhe. Kɛji akɛ afolɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli ekoŋŋ lɛ, ebaashi ŋmeii 2 loo 3 pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ koni ekɛfee kuu agbo.

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects sucking the sap from young leaves. Spraying with neem water or suitable insect control gets rid of the pests so healthy new leaves can sprout.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ neem nu loo tsofa ni sa ni akɛbaagbe kooloi ahe lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie kooloi lɛ koni baai heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba.

english: Why do caterpillars eat my cabbage leaves mostly during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii yeɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: In dry weather, pest insects multiply much faster because there are no heavy rains to wash them off or destroy their eggs, allowing them to eat leaves undisturbed.
ga: yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi mli lɛ, kooloi fɔji fɔɔ oya kwraa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni baafɔ ŋmeii lɛ loo efite amɛ lɛ bɛ. Enɛ haa amɛyeɔ baai lɛ ni mɔ ko gbaaa amɛnaa.

english: Why do my harvested maize grains get full of small holes and powder after a few months in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli eyi kɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni akɛto nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ

english: Weevils lay tiny eggs inside the grains while they dry. Drying your maize until it is very hard and keeping it in airtight bags starves the insects of air so they cannot eat your grain.
ga: Kpɔŋɔ lɛ woɔ wɔji bibii. yɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli beni amɛgbiɔ lɛ Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa kɛyashi ewa waa ni akɛto vacuum kotokui amli lɛ, ebaaha hɔmɔ aye kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛnyɛŋ amɛye oniyenii lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually show that the maize plant is lacking nitrogen in the soil or that heavy rains have washed nutrients away. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or manure helps the leaves turn green and photosynthesize properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ni amɛfeɔ fotosintɛsis jogbaŋŋ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the ground. Rotating with crops like groundnuts or cowpeas puts nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops curl up tightly during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe waa yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a crop's natural way of protecting itself from water loss. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to direct sun so it loses less moisture through evaporation during hot weather.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ nu ni elaajeɔ lɛ he. Kɛ́ abɔle tso lɛ baai lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baa shi. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ fioo pɛ laajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Flower drop happens when the plant experiences stress, usually from extreme heat, prolonged drought, or a lack of nutrients like calcium. Keeping the soil moist with mulch and balanced water helps flowers stay attached to form fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tsei na haomɔ. Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ calcium ni bɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ nu ni sa wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting underground before I can dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani abaanyɛ atsa amɛ lɛ?

english: Tuber rot happens when water stays trapped around the roots for too long, creating waterlogged soil where fungus spreads quickly. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away from the tubers.
ga: Tuber rot baa kɛji nu ŋmɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ baa he ni ŋmei lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya lɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ amli.

english: What is causing ragged holes in the leaves and central whorl of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ mi ŋmã tsei lɛ baai kɛ amɛteŋ ŋtayaai amli lɛ baa?

english: Ragged holes inside the central leaves are typically caused by caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm feeding on the growing shoot. Checking plants early and applying targeted controls prevents them from destroying the stalk.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni yeɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ baa. Tsei lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Ni akɛ targeted control atsu nii lɛ baatsi tso lɛ shishifã lɛ ni efiteɔ lɛ naa.

english: If I plant my seeds very close together, will I get a bigger harvest from my small land?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ. Mi nɔ loo daabi?

english: Planting too close forces crops to compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin plants and small yields. Giving crops correct spacing produces bigger, healthier plants and a higher overall harvest.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ tso lɛ atswa hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa ha lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ afee wuji. Na hewalɛ kpakpa ni ŋmaa lɛ fɛɛ fa babaoo.

english: Why do I need to place tall stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matswa shwɛmɔ wulu koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the air to catch maximum sunlight for building underground tubers. Staking also keeps leaves off the damp ground, preventing fungal rot and weed damage.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo koni amɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ kɛ jwɛi ni fiteɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why should I buy fresh certified seeds instead of saving seeds from my last harvest to plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ moŋ fe ni makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ naagbee kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu?

english: Seeds saved from previous harvests lose their vigor over time and often carry seed-borne diseases. Certified seeds are specially produced to resist diseases, grow uniformly, and deliver high yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ baafite amɛhewalɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. ni bei pii lɛ, ekɛ helai ni jɛɔ dumɔwui amli kɛbaa lɛ baa Afee dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai. Ekwɛ daa ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil or overwatering. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu babaoo yɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 to 12 months after planting. You can tell it is mature when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, and the ground around the base of the stem begins to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ edara kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni he ni ebɔle tso lɛ he lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking the sap from young leaves. Spraying the plants early with organic neem oil or soapy water helps clear these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni haa chili baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ mra Kɛ akɛ neem fɔ loo nu ni akɛ saamɔ fee lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ajie nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences stress from excessive heat, dry soil, or improper nutrients. Keeping the soil evenly moist and providing light shade during very hot days helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni fe nine, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni esaaa mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide large leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and moisture it needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: What causes my yam tubers to grow small and bent instead of long and large?
ga: Mɛni haa mi sweet potato ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ bibii ni ebɔleɔ shi moŋ fe ni eeefee kakalɛ kɛ agbo?

english: Yams grow poorly in hard or stony soil because the roots cannot expand easily. Digging deep, loose mounds or ridges gives the tubers room to expand smoothly into large, healthy shapes.
ga: Sweet potatoes kwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa loo tɛi yɔɔ nɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo. Gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni mli kwɔ ni etse ehe lɛ ni aaaku lɛ haa ŋshɔŋloo lɛ mli shwereɔ mlɛo ni etsɔɔ nɔ ko ni da ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why does the soil on my vegetable farm dry out so quickly after raining?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mi-vegetables ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ nɛ lɛ?

english: Bare soil loses moisture quickly to direct sunlight and wind. Covering the soil around your crops with dried grass or leaves (mulching) acts like a blanket to trap moisture in the ground longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ lɛ fiteɔ nu oya kɛji akɛ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tswa lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Mulching around Nibii ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ŋmɔɔ (mulching) tsuɔ nii tamɔ blanket ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Weevils thrive in moist grain. Make sure your maize is dried completely in the sun until the kernels are very hard, then store them in airtight hermetic bags to keep insects out.
ga: Beetles thrive in moist seeds. Kwɛmɔ ni o-abele lɛ agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ŋmeii lɛ amli baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛwo kotoku ko mli koni kɔɔyɔɔ akabote mli.

english: Why does my cowpea farm have plenty of big leaves but very few bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea ŋmɔ lɛ mli baa lɛ dara waa shi ŋmɔtɔi lɛ faaa kwraa lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes cowpea plants to focus all their energy on leaf growth rather than flowering. Avoid using nitrogen-heavy fertilizers on leguminous crops like cowpeas.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa cowpea tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai lɛ adalɛ he moŋ fe fɔfɔi. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ he.

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots and carry heavy bunches of fruit at the top. Supporting the main stem with sturdy bamboo or wooden poles (staking) prevents the wind from pushing the tree over.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei loo tso ni wa (staking) fi tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekatsi tso lɛ shi.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant enough space allows the roots to spread and feed properly, resulting in thick stalks and larger cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni amɛyeɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why is it important to plant plantains alongside my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu plantains yɛ mi kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that easily burn under direct hot sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide broad leaf shade and maintain soil moisture, acting as protective umbrellas while the young cocoa trees mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei bibii ni daa oya lɛ haa hulutsoo kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni amɛhaa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he yɛ be mli ni cacao tso bibioo lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant tomatoes on the exact same spot where I just harvested garden eggs or peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ tomato yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni mifolɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ abɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomatoes, garden eggs, and peppers belong to the same plant family and share the same soil diseases and pests. Planting them repeatedly in the same spot allows pests to multiply in the soil; rotating with maize or beans starves these pests.
ga: Tomato, abɔɔ mli ŋmeii, kɛ ŋmeii yɛ tsei aweku kome mli ni amɛyeɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo ni jɛɔ sũ mli kɛbaa lɛ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ shii abɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ akɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsakeɔ lɛ, hɔmɔ yeɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Yellowing starting from the tips of older leaves usually means the plant lacks nitrogen, a vital food element that gives crops their green color and growth strength. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ anaa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni haa tsei feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa kɛha dalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi aŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I avoid applying chemical fertilizer when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizers need water to dissolve properly. Applying them to dry soil creates a high concentration of salts that scorch and burn the crop roots, which can stunt or kill the plant.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ biɔ nu koni amɛtsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋmei babaoo baa. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ashã ni amɛshã. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ loo egbo.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and developing bright yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni kpɛɔ lɛ?

english: This leaf damage is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried and spread by tiny whiteflies or infected stem cuttings. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties recommended by extension officers prevents this infection.
ga: Cassava mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii loo tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ. Cassava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ he ŋaa lɛ adumɔ baaye abua ni atsĩ hela nɛɛ naa.

english: Flower drop happens when plants suffer from water stress during hot periods or when tiny insects like thrips attack the blossoms. Regular watering during dry spells and inspecting plants early for small bugs keeps the flowers attached.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ naa nu he haomɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. aloo kɛ́ kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips tutua fɔfɔi. Nu ni akɛhaa daa yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛ tsei lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Koni ana kooloi bibii ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: What is causing the center leaves of my young maize plants to look like they were shredded overnight?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni atse amɛ nyɔɔŋ kome mli?

english: This destruction is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that hides inside the central funnel of the maize plant during the daytime and eats the tender leaves at night.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbi mli, ni eyeɔ baai bibii gbɛkɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ hela nɛɛ baa.

english: How can I tell that my cassava tubers are mature enough to dig up without ruining the crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ atsa ni efiteee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Cassava is generally ready for harvest when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, usually between 9 to 12 months after planting. You can gently dig around one plant stem to inspect root size before harvesting the whole farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ dumɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ blɛoo abɔle tso kome he koni okwɛ bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ dara ha dani okpa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: How can I stop small beetles from eating holes into my harvested maize during storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi ladybugs lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ?

english: Storage beetles thrive on moist grain in open containers. Drying your maize until the grains are hard and storing them in sealed airtight (hermetic) bags suffocates pests and keeps your grain safe without heavy chemicals.
ga: Nibii ni akɛtoɔ lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ omanye yɛ dumɔwui ni mli efɔ ni yɔɔ tsɛnsii ni agbele mli lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ ogbala o-corn lɛ aahu kɛyashi ŋmeii lɛ mli wa ni okɛto kotokui ni akɛ vacuum efo mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha o-kernel lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe ni akɛ tsofai ni tsii tsuuu nii.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen. Maize needs plenty of nitrogen to stay green and healthy, so when there is not enough in the soil, the plant moves nutrients from its older bottom leaves to feed the new leaves growing at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ehiɛ hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Tsei lɛ tsiɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha baai heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ niyenii.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the heat is too intense or when the plant suffers from sudden water stress. Extreme temperatures prevent the pollen inside the flower from fertilizing properly, so the plant sheds the flower instead of making a fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu he haomɔ ba tso lɛ nɔ trukaa. Kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ tsɔ lɛ, ehaaa pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ mli lɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips, aphids, or whiteflies hiding under the leaves. When these pests suck the plant juice, they inject saliva or viruses that cause the new leaves to twist and stunt.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, aphids loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. Kɛ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ miinu tsei amli nu lɛ Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ woɔ mli koni ekɛgbala baai heei ni efite.

english: Why is my cassava producing very big leafy branches but small tubers in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ niji kɛ baai wuji waa shi ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen manure or fertilizer relative to other nutrients, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi ahe. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ baato shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cowpea plants make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and other legumes have tiny nodules on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil. When the plant harvest is done, that extra nitrogen stays in the soil to nourish the next crop you plant.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbe naa Nakai nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ niyenii.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct, hot sunlight. Plantains grow very quickly and provide broad leaves that shade the young cocoa plants, keeping them cool and moist during their first two years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ha cacao tsei lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Black cocoa pods are caused by a fungal disease called Black Pod, which thrives in cool, overly shaded, and very humid conditions. High moisture allows fungal spores to spread quickly from pod to pod.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ blackpod kɛ kookoo diji baa. ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ lɛ Shade babaoo ni mli ejɔ waa. Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo lɛ haa fungal spores lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ pod mli kɛyaa pod mli.

english: Planting the same crop in the same spot continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year, while giving crop-specific pests and diseases a permanent home to multiply.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa kooloi bibii kɛ helai ni yɔɔ tsei amli lɛ náa shia ni hiɔ shi daa ni amɛfɔɔ bii.

english: Weed seeds are extremely tough and can lie dormant in the soil for months waiting for moisture. Once the rains start, they absorb water and germinate immediately, faster than cultivated crops.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ wa waa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwɔ. yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nyɔji babaoo, ni emɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ Kɛ́ nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ lɛ Ebaaŋɔ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni ebaakwɛ̃ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why does the surface of my farm soil become hard like stone after a heavy rain drys up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli wa tamɔ tɛ beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ egbi lɛ?

english: When bare soil lacks organic matter like dried leaves or mulch, heavy raindrops break down the top soil particles. As the sun dries this muddy layer, it forms a hard crust that blocks air and roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai ni egbi loo ŋmɔshi nibii. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ gbálaa sũ mli nibii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ amli. Beni hulu lɛ gbiɔ lɛ, nɛkɛ muji nɛɛ feɔ ŋmei ni wa ni tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shishifãi lɛ anaa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are delicate and burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have broad leaves that create natural shade and retain moisture, giving the young cocoa plants the protection they need to survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo baa ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Enɛ haa cacao tsei bibii lɛ náa hebuu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my groundnuts yield better when I plant them on a farm where I previously harvested maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmeii lɛ woɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ fe be mli ni miduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mikpaa ŋmãa mra lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rotating crops breaks the cycle of pests and diseases that attack specific plants. Maize uses up certain nutrients, but groundnuts naturally put nitrogen back into the soil, benefiting from the reduced pest population left behind by the maize harvest.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ fiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa tsei komɛi lɛ. Abɛi kɛ niyenii mli nibii komɛi tsuɔ nii. Shi ŋmeii haa nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni náa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shi kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa ni akpaa lɛ mli lɛ he sɛɛ

english: Why do my maize leaves turn pale yellow after several days of heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa gbii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes essential nutrients like nitrogen deep into the ground where short roots cannot reach, and waterlogged soil stops roots from breathing properly, causing the leaves to lose their healthy green color.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen lɛ, kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi kukuji nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Ni sũ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ amu jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ ahe su ni ji eŋɔli ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with bushy green leaves, but producing tiny tubers under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ jwɛi ni baai eŋɔli yɔɔ mli, shi ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or excessive manure, the cassava plant spends all its energy developing lush leaves and stems on top instead of storing food in the roots below.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo ŋmeii babaoo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ niyenii baato shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛbaa baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nɔ.

english: What makes my pepper plants drop their flowers before turning into small peppers?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-pepper tsei lɛ miifo amɛfɔfɔi lɛ dani amɛbatsɔ pepper bibii?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience environmental stress, such as extreme heat, irregular watering, or excessive fertilizer, to conserve their energy and water.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe shihilɛ mli haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ he. loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo Koni akɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he

english: Why do armyworm caterpillars always hide deep inside the central funnels of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: The central funnel of a young maize plant provides caterpillars with a moist, sheltered environment safe from predators and direct sunlight, along with easy access to tender, growing leaves.
ga: Abɛi tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ tsu lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ naa he ko ni mli ejɔ ni amɛhe yɔɔ fɛo. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. kɛfata he lɛ, nine shɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃mɔ waaa lɛ anɔ

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl upward tightly during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi waa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato plants curl their leaves to shrink the surface area exposed to the sun, which helps prevent water from evaporating too quickly from the plant during dry, hot weather.
ga: Tomato tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛha he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ afee bibioo. Enɛ baaye abua ni nu lɛ akajɛ tso lɛ mli oya tsɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why are my oil palm trees producing far fewer fruit bunches during prolonged dry seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Oil palms need constant moisture to form female flowers, which turn into fruit bunches. When water is scarce, the tree conserves resources by producing male flowers instead or aborting young fruit bunches.
ga: Mu tsei lɛ biɔ nu ni mli edɔ be fɛɛ be koni amɛfee fɔfɔi yei, ni bafeɔ aduawai akui. Beni nu faaa Tsei lɛ buɔ nibii ahe kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi hii ni amɛfeɔ yɛ amɛ najiaŋ loo amɛfoɔ aduawai aniji bibii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers start sprouting shoots inside the barn even without soil or water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ loo nu bɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers go through a natural resting period after harvest. Once this dormancy breaks, internal signals cause the tuber to use its stored energy and water to shoot out buds, preparing to grow even without soil.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji nɛkɛ gbeekpamɔ nɛɛ fite Mligbɛ okadii haa bulb lɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni ato kɛ nu tsuɔ nii ni ekɛkwɛ̃ɔ. Saamɔ ohe koni okwɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ bɛ po.

english: Why do my cowpea crops flower faster during certain months than others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ fɔɔ mra fe ekrokomɛi yɛ nyɔji komɛi amli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are sensitive to daylight length. Shorter days signal to the plant that the rainy season is coming to an end, triggering it to stop growing leaves and start flowering quickly to produce seeds.
ga: Cowpeas nuɔ hulu la he waa. Gbii ni yɔɔ kuku lɛ ji okadi kɛha tsei akɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ miiba naagbee. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ kpaɔ baai lɛ ni ebɔi fɔfɔi feemɔ oya koni ewo dumɔwui.

english: Maize leaves curl up like tubes during hot afternoons to reduce their surface area, which helps the plant conserve water and survive extreme heat.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe tamɔ paipii yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛba ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he ni amɛnyɛɔ amɛdamɔɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa naa.

english: Why does my farmland become very hard and difficult to clear before the main rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli wa ni ewa akɛ abaajie dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ aba lɛ?

english: Soils with high clay content dry out completely during the harmattan season, packing tightly together like bricks until the first rains soften them up.
ga: Shikpɔji ni shikpɔŋ sũ babaoo yɔɔ nɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli. Akɛ amɛ ebɔ he tamɔ brikii kɛyashi klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ fee blɛoo.

english: What crop do people call 'white gold' in northern Ghana, and why is it good for me to plant?
ga: Mɛɛ tso mɛi ni yɔɔ Ghana kooyigbɛ lɛ tsɛɔ lɛ ‘shika tsuru yɛŋ’ ni mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ madu lɛ?

english: Cotton is often called 'white gold' because its white fibers sell for high prices on national markets, bringing valuable income to your household and community.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, atsɛɔ odonti akɛ ‘shika tsuru yɛŋ’ ejaakɛ ahɔ̃ɔ etsɔnei yɛŋ lɛ jara waa yɛ maŋ jarayeli hei. Enɛ kɛ shika ni jara wa baa oshia kɛ akutso lɛ mli.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the young plants fight each other for water, sunlight, and food, causing all of them to grow weak and produce small ears.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii he akaŋ, ni no haa dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛnáa toi bibii.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a water mold that spreads fast when there is heavy rain, cool air, and too much shade surrounding your cocoa trees.
ga: Nu mli tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa, kɔɔyɔŋ mli ejɔ, ni hulutsoo babaoo ebɔle kookoo tsei ahe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa.

english: Why does my soil produce a better crop after I plant groundnuts on it for one season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai beni midu ŋmeii be kome sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots, naturally feeding the soil so future crops can grow stronger.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa bɔni afee ni wɔsɛɛ tsei lɛ adara waa.

english: Why shouldn't I put dry fertilizer on my crops when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs soil moisture to dissolve into a liquid form that plant roots can drink; without water, the fertilizer stays dry and can burn the roots.
ga: Fɛ̃i he miihia shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ koni etsɔ nu ni tsei shishifãi baanyɛ anu. Kɛ́ nu bɛ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do wild weeds grow back so much faster than my planted crops right after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ yɛ nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Wild weeds are native to the area and naturally tough, allowing their seeds to sprout instantly and capture available water before cultivated seeds can catch up.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi ji jɛmɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ, ni amɛhe wa yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa amɛdumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni amɛhiɛɔ nu fɛɛ nu ni yɔɔ lɛ mli dani dumɔwui ni adu lɛ nyɛɔ amɛshɛɔ he.

english: Why are tiny white flies making the leaves of my cassava plants turn yellow and twist up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii Ani su yɛŋ lɛ haa mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ?

english: Whiteflies carry a plant sickness called cassava mosaic virus; as they drink sap from leaf to leaf, they pass the virus into healthy plants.
ga: Whitefly ji tso hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ ŋmei mosaic hela. Beni amɛnuɔ mliki lɛ kɛjɛɔ baa kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ lɛ Amɛtsɔɔ hela lɛ amɛhaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How can I tell when my cashew nuts are completely ready for me to collect?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cashews lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cashew nuts are fully ripe when the juicy cashew apple turns bright red or yellow and the whole fruit falls naturally from the tree to the ground.
ga: Cashew ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa kɛ́ aduawai lɛ batsɔ tsuru loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Ni tso lɛ yibii lɛ fɛɛ baagbee shikpɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: If I leave big trees on my farm, won't they block the sunshine that my crops need to grow?
ga: Kɛji mishi tso agbo ko yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli Ani tso lɛ baatsi hulu la ni he hiaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa?

english: While crops need light, too much harsh, direct sunlight can scorch them and bake the soil. Leaving scattered shade trees creates filtered sunlight, which protects your crops from severe heat while still giving them enough light to grow.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ la he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii moŋ Shi hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei ni eshã shikpɔŋ lɛ. Tsei ni yɔɔ shade ni egbɛ eshwã lɛ ni ashiɔ lɛ haa hulu la ni mli tse baa. Enɛ buɔ onibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, yɛ be mli ni ehaa la ni fa bɔ ni sa lolo koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do my crops dry up and wither faster when there are no big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboɔ oya be mli ni tsei ni edara bɛ he lɛ?

english: Without trees to act as natural shields, direct sunlight heats up the ground quickly and pulls water out of the soil and leaves, causing crops to suffer from severe water stress.
ga: Kɛ tsei bɛ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ko lɛ, Hulu la ni tsɔɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔɔ oya ni ejieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii naa nu he haomɔ ni naa wa waa.

english: How do I know if my crops are getting too much sun or not enough shade?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiná hulu babaoo loo amɛnáaa hulutsoo be ni fa bɔ ni sa?

english: Crops getting too much sun will show scorched, yellow, or dry brown leaves and wilt early in the afternoon. Crops with too much shade will grow very tall, thin, and weak as they stretch looking for light.
ga: Tsei ni hulu la kpɛɔ amɛ babaoo lɛ baajie baai ni eshã lɛ akpo. Yellow loo brown, egbi ni egboɔ yɛ shwane mli Tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo babaoo lɛ daraa waa, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛhe waaa beni amɛkpãa amɛhe koni amɛtao la lɛ.

english: Is it better for me to burn my land before planting, or should I clear it without burning?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ abaashã shikpɔŋ lɛ dani adu nii loo ehi akɛ abaatsumɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ashãaa?

english: Clearing without burning is usually better for long-term farming. Leaving cut weeds and leaves on the ground keeps the soil cool, holds water, and rots into natural fertilizer, whereas burning destroys organic nutrients and dries out the land.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni ashãaa lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha be kakadaŋŋ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛ́ ashi jwɛi kɛ baai ni afolɔ ashwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i, nu ahi mli, ni ebaagbo ni etsɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. yɛ be mli ni shãa fiteɔ niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli gbiɔ.

english: Why does my soil stay hard and dry compared to land that has plenty of leaf cover?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni egbi kɛ akɛto hei ni baai babaoo yɔɔ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Bare soil exposed to full sun bakes hard like a clay pot and lets water evaporate quickly. A layer of leaves or tree shade shields the earth, keeping it soft, dark, and full of moisture.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni hulu lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baawa tamɔ shikpɔŋ sũ tsɛnsi ni ebaaha nu lɛ atsɔ oya. Tso baa loo hulutsoo buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Ehaa je lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ, efeɔ duŋ, ni eyiɔ obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: My friends say burning land makes it clean, so why does my soil feel poorer after burning it for a few years?
ga: Minaanyo lɛ kɛɛ akɛ, atsumɔ he ni la shã lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ mɛni hewɔ mi shikpɔŋ lɛ nuɔ he waa yɛ afii babaoo ni eshã lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Burning gives a quick ash boost for one season, but it kills the beneficial tiny living organisms in the soil and burns away natural plant food. Over time, burnt land loses its richness and becomes hard to farm.
ga: Shãa baaha sũ lɛ aya hiɛ oya kɛyashi be kome. Shi ebaagbe bɔɔ nii bibii. ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛtsakeɔ tsei aniyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa Beni be hoɔ lɛ Shikpɔŋ ni eshã lɛ he waaa ni ewaa akɛ aaatsu nii yɛ mli.

english: Should I cut down all the wild trees on my land before I plant my crops?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ koo mli tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ dani madu nii?

english: No, it is good to leave selected healthy trees. Native trees protect the soil from strong winds, drop leaves that feed the soil, and shelter your crops during intense dry seasons.
ga: Dabi, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshi tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Tsei ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he. Baai ni egbee shi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii. ni obu onibii ahe yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa be mli.

english: Why do I see fewer weeds growing in areas where tree leaves shade the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaaa jwɛi fioo yɛ hei ni baai shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Most aggressive weeds need full, direct sunlight to germinate and grow quickly. The shade provided by tree leaves prevents weed seeds from getting the light they need, making weeding much easier for you.
ga: Jwɛi ni boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛdara oya. Shade ni baai lɛ haa lɛ tsiɔ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná la ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ feɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa bo.

english: Does strong heat from the sun destroy the food in my soil?
ga: Ani hulu ni tsoɔ lɛ miifite niyenii ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, excessive soil temperature from direct sun breaks down organic matter too fast and kills helpful soil organisms that create plant food, leaving your soil weak.
ga: Hɛɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ fe nine ni jɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ haa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ fiteɔ oya tsɔ. ni egbe nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni feɔ tsei niyenii lɛ. Ha oshikpɔŋ lɛ afee gbɔjɔmɔ

english: How can I protect my young seedlings from dying in the hot sun during their early stage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu midumɔwui lɛ ahe koni amɛkagboi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli yɛ shishijee mli?

english: Young plants are tender like human babies and need shade from taller plants, palm fronds, or shade trees to survive their first months until their roots grow deep enough to find groundwater.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ mlɛo tamɔ abifabii ni ehe hiaa ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei kakadaji, ŋmeii, loo hulutsoo tsei adɛŋ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baatsɔ shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ akpee.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is a key nutrient for growth. It can also happen when the ground gets waterlogged from heavy rain, choking the roots so they cannot absorb food from the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi obɔ kɛ nu. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the plants do not get a steady supply of water. When the crop feels stressed by heat or drought, it sheds its flowers to save energy to keep itself alive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ afɔɔɔ tsei lɛ anɔ nu daa. Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii nu he akɛ dɔlɛ loo hɔmɔ miigba amɛnaa lɛ Eshwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛto hewalɛ ni ekɛha ehe ahi wala mli lɛ he.

english: When is the right time for me to apply fertilizer to my cassava farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmɔ mli?

english: The best time to apply fertilizer is about four to eight weeks after planting, while the soil is moist from the early rains. Moist soil helps the plant roots quickly take in the nutrients before weeds steal them.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ awo mli ji aaafee otsii 4-8 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ yeɔ ebuaa tsei shishifãi ni amɛnáa niyenii mli hewalɛ oya dani jwɛi lɛ juɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and dry up on the trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in cool, wet weather. Pruning extra branches to let sunlight and air reach the trunk helps keep the pods dry and stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni edɔ waa mli. Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tso lɛ mli koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ashɛ tso lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaaa ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why should I clear weeds from my farm when they are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your young crops for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Clearing them early prevents them from starving your crops before the crop roots are strong enough to grow.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaye oŋmɔshi nii lɛ hɔmɔ dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ aná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Yams grow crooked or small when the soil is too hard or full of stones, which prevents the tuber from pushing outward. Making high, soft mounds using loose topsoil allows the yam to expand easily.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo bibioo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo tɛi eyi mli obɔ. Enɛ haaa yitso lɛ ashɛ ehe kɛya kponɔgbɛ. Gɔŋ kakadaŋŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni akɛ ŋwɛi sũ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa sweet potatoes ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa oya.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies hiding underneath the leaves and sucking the plant's juice. Using soapy water or neem oil spray helps control these pests and protects the leaf shape.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nu ni akɛ saamɔ loo neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni akudɔɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ni ebuɔ baa lɛ he.

english: Why is it harmful to burn dry leaves and grass on my land before I plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mashã baai kɛ jwɛi ni egbi yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani adu nii lɛ?

english: Burning destroys beneficial organisms in the soil and burns away natural organic matter that feeds your crops. Leaving the dead plants to rot into the soil instead creates rich natural compost and holds moisture better.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ahiɛ, ni eshãa adebɔɔ mli nibii ni haa onibii lɛ niyenii lɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ tsei ni egboi lɛ gbɛ ni amɛgboi yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa, ni ji adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa hulutsoo lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa.

english: Plantain plants have very shallow roots that stay near the surface, making them top-heavy when heavy bunches form. Supporting the stems with strong wooden props helps keep them standing straight during rainy storms.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ waa ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kɛji eje kpo yɛ kui wuji amli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni wa fiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehiɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: Why should I plant cowpea or groundnuts on the same land after harvesting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas fix natural nitrogen from the air into the dirt through their roots. Planting them after maize naturally fertilizes the soil so your next crops grow better without buying as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ tsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛhaa nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ. Abele ni aduɔ yɛ abele sɛɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohé tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli.

english: Why do my crop leaves dry up and fall off during December and the Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ December kɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During December and the Harmattan, dry winds from the desert pull moisture out of plant leaves very quickly. Crops drop leaves to save water and keep their roots alive through the dry season, but you can protect them by watering the base and covering the soil with dry leaves.
ga: Yɛ December kɛ Harmattan mli lɛ, ŋa nɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli oya. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛshishifãi lɛ ahi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli fɛɛ. Shi obaanyɛ obu tso lɛ he kɛtsɔ nu ni oooha lɛ yɛ eshishigbɛ ni okɛ baai ni egbi aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell if the first rain after the long dry season means it is truly time to plant?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ be eshɛ diɛŋtsɛ ni esa akɛ adu nii?

english: The first rain after a long dry season often only wets the surface while the deeper soil stays dry. Wait until you have two or three heavy rains that soak deep into the soil before planting, so your new seeds do not dry out and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ yaa nɔ egbiɔ. Mɛɛ ni oná nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ ni ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ dani odu. No hewɔ lɛ, odumɔwui heei lɛ egbiŋ ni amɛgboii.

english: Yellow leaves mean your maize plants are hungry and lacking nitrogen in the soil. Adding animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer gives the plants the nutrients they need to grow green and produce large ears of corn.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ ni nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi aŋmei, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛwo ŋmãa toi wuji.

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the same nutrients from the soil every year and allows soil pests to multiply. Rotating your crops gives the soil time to rest and prevents diseases from building up.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni amɛshwereɔ Nibii ni aduɔ ni tsakeɔ lɛ haa sũ lɛ naa be ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe ni ehaaa helai abua amɛhe naa.

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when the air gets too hot, when the plant lacks water, or when bees are not available to pollinate them. Keeping the soil damp and planting flowers nearby to attract bees helps flowers turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni nu bɛ tsei amli loo be mli ni ŋmeii nyɛɛɛ afee pollination Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha afee fɛ̃i kɛ fɔfɔii ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Bɔni afee ni agbala ŋmeii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔii lɛ feɔ tomatoi.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow a lot of big green leaves but very few bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ.

english: When cowpeas get too much nitrogen from soil or heavy fertilizer, they spend all their energy growing leaves instead of flowers. Avoiding extra nitrogen fertilizer encourages the plant to focus on making bean pods.
ga: Kɛji tsina ŋmei nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii mli lɛ, ŋmei kɛ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ baai ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii moŋ fe fɔfɔi lɛ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfataa he lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ baaha tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama ŋmeii afeemɔ nɔ.

english: Why do insects attack my pepper plants more during the dry season than in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii babaoo tutuaa mi-pepper tsei lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli fe nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Heat and drought weaken plants, making them easier targets for insects like whiteflies that multiply fast in warm weather. Keeping your plants watered and slightly shaded gives them the strength to resist pest attacks.
ga: Dɔlɛ kɛ hɔmɔ haa tsei gbɔjɔɔ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ nɔ ni ewaaa akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies, ni faa oya yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be mli lɛ baanyɛ atswa amɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ha otsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni oha amɛná hulutsoo fioo lɛ, ebaaha amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkɛte shi amɛwo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baatutua amɛ lɛ.

english: How does covering the soil with dry grass or leaves help my crops survive dry heat?
ga: Te baai loo jwɛi ni egboi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli egbi lɛ mli aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the ground with organic material is called mulching. The layer of dry leaves blocks direct sunlight from heating the earth, keeping the soil moist for longer so your plants do not dry out.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Baai ni egbi lɛ eko tsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa ni etsĩɔ jeŋ dɔlɛ naa. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ tsei lɛ egbiɛɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense tropical sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide living shade umbrellas that keep the young cocoa cool and moist during their first few years in the farm.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa waa lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ haa hulutsoo ni haa kookoo bibioo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo ni eyɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: Why are my harvested yam tubers rotting quickly after I store them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya beni mikɛtoɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yams rot in storage if they get bruised during harvest, exposed to direct sun, or kept in hot, unventilated rooms. Storing sound, unbruised yams in a raised, shaded, and well-ventilated barn keeps them fresh longer.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli. Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ Aloo okɛto tsu ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ mli. Akɛ sweet potatoes ni etseee lɛ toɔ ŋmɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ, ni yɔɔ hulutsoo, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli lɛ mli. Ebaaye ebua ni ehi shi ehee be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and shallow roots that burn quickly in full sunlight. They need partial shade from nurse crops like plantains to keep the air moist and soil cool while their root systems mature.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni shãa oya kɛji akɛ hulu lɛ tso waa. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo ko kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛɔ helatsɛmɛi anɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds and put sticks for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ kɛjɛ mihe lɛ? Ni okɛ niji afata he koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that need sunlight on their leaves to produce energy. Lifting the leaves off the ground with stakes prevents leaves from rotting on damp soil and allows the plant to send maximum energy down into growing huge tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa hulu la yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tso wo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛkafite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. ni ehaa tso lɛ kudɔɔ hewalɛ ni fa fe fɛɛ lɛ kɛyaa shishi kɛyaa ŋmeii wuji ni miida lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed for green growth. Heavy rains often wash this nutrient out of the soil, requiring added fertilizer or manure.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn lɛ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ Bei pii lɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata he.

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen out of the air and fix it into the ground. When planted alongside maize, groundnuts naturally feed the soil, acting like a natural fertilizer boost for the maize.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ adu kɛ ŋmãa Peanuts lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmãa.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits in waterlogged fields for too long, it smothers the roots and creates the ideal conditions for soil fungi to infect and decay the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu hi ŋmɔ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ Nu lɛ shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ ni ehaa shihilɛ ni sa baa koni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aná hela ni amɛfite ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips that suck sap from the leaves and spread plant viruses, which stunts fruit growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni shwieɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ ɔ ha nɛ yiblii ɔ kpa wami.

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when the plants get stressed by extreme heat or irregular watering, which prevents pollen from fertilizing the flower to form a tomato.
ga: Tomato baashwie efɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. Enɛ haaa pollen lɛ akawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ni etsɔ amɛ tomatoi.

english: Extra sucker shoots drain food and water away from the main plantain tree. Removing most of them leaves only the strongest shoot to concentrate energy into producing a larger bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei krokomɛi lɛ shwieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ he. Kɛ́ ajie amɛteŋ babaoo kɛjɛ mli lɛ, ebaashi ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛfee plantains babaoo.

english: Why do caterpillars hide deep inside the funnel leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai ni tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Fall Armyworm caterpillars hide in the leaf funnels of young corn to protect themselves from hot daytime sun and predators while eating the softest leaf tissue.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ teɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ amli koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni amɛyeɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do maize plants grown from my saved seed harvest produce smaller yields than new seed bought from agro-dealers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ni adu kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe dumɔwui heei ni aheɔ kɛjɛɔ okwaayeli jarayelɔi adɛŋ lɛ?

english: Hybrid maize seeds sold by dealers are specially bred for high yields in their first planting. Saving seeds from that harvest breaks down those hybrid traits, leading to weaker plants and smaller harvests.
ga: Akwɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni jarayelɔi hɔ̃ɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni ekɛ yibii babaoo aba yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔ mli. Dumɔwui ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ nakai sui ni ji hybrid lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with broad leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing essential shade and keeping the soil moist for young cocoa plants.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛha kookoo tsei bibii.

english: What is causing small green worms to chew holes in my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ shwieɔ bu yɛ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ amli?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana. They feed inside the center of young maize plants, but spraying early with recommended organic or chemical insecticides saves the yield.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana. Amɛyeɔ nii yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ. Shi atsɔɔ akɛ akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ afɔse mra. Ebaaye ebua ni nibii ni anáa lɛ aya nɔ.

english: Will planting cowpeas together with my maize help or harm my main crop?
ga: Ani tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ baaye abua loo ebaaye miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ awui?

english: Intercropping cowpeas with maize is beneficial. Cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil, which naturally fertilizes the maize while suppressing weed growth.
