ga: Sɛɛnamɔ yɛ tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he. Cowpeas mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ feɔ ŋmãa yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ be mli ni etsĩɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants before forming any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii miiho kɛmiijɛ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ dani aduawai baa lɛ?

english: Blossom drop in tomatoes usually happens because of extreme heat, erratic watering, or a lack of nutrients in the soil. Consistent watering and adequate soil nutrients help flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato ni gbeeɔ shi lɛ baa yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa hewɔ. nu ni bɛ shiŋŋ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni akɛhaa daa kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting in the ground before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when too much water gathers around them in heavy soil. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps rain water drain away from the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu babaoo bua shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Stunted crop growth, yellowish leaves on previous crops, and hard, dry soil indicate poor soil health. Adding compost, manure, or fertilizer restores the nutrients needed for healthy growth.
ga: stunted plant growth Baai ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eho lɛ anɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni egbi Etsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kpakpa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Staking raises yam leaves toward sunlight so the plant can make food to build large tubers underground, while keeping leaves off damp ground to prevent fungal diseases.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato baai lɛ kɛ hulu la lɛ akpe bɔni afee ni tso lɛ afee niyenii ni efee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ ahi he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akamɔ bo.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop during the afternoon even when the soil was moist in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: Strong midday sun causes plants to lose water faster through their leaves than roots can pull from the ground. Covering the soil around plants with dry grass (mulching) keeps the soil cooler and moist.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane teŋ lɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) shwie tso lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: How can I protect my harvested dried maize from being eaten by insects in storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-ŋmãa ni egbi ni mikpa lɛ he kɛjɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ nitoohe lɛ ahe?

english: Weevils attack grain that has residual moisture. Thoroughly sun-drying maize until it is hard and storing it in sealed, airtight bags (like PICS bags) prevents insects from surviving inside.
ga: Moth lɛ tutuaa dumɔwui ni ŋmɔtɔ ni eshwɛ yɛ mli lɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ. Gbimɔ ŋmãa lɛ kɛyashi ebaawa ni okɛwo kotoku ko ni akɛ vacuum ewo mli (tamɔ PICS kotoku) mli koni ŋmeii akahi shi yɛ mli.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies. Controlling these insects early with neem oil or targeted sprays keeps the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ kudɔmɔ mra Neem fɔ loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is a key food they need to grow strong green leaves. It can happen if the soil is poor, or if heavy rain has washed the nutrients out of the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ. Ebaanyɛ eba kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii loo kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Planting maize in the same spot repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows pests and diseases that attack maize to multiply in the ground.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi kɛ helai ni tutuaa abɛi lɛ ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When excessive rain floods the ground and water stays trapped around the roots for too long, the roots drown and rot because they cannot get oxygen.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni nu ebɔleɔ he fɛɛ he. shishifãi be kakadaŋŋ Shishifãi lɛ baafo nu mli ni amɛbaafite ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa.

english: Why is it helpful to spread dry grass on top of the soil around my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni agbɛ jwɛi ni egbi ashwã shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, sɛɛnamɔ yɛ pepper tsei ahe.

english: Spreading dry grass, known as mulching, acts like a blanket over the soil. It keeps the soil cool, stops water from drying out quickly on hot days, and prevents weeds from growing.
ga: Hay ni agbɛɔ ashwaa, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekagbi oya yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ anɔ. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: Why are small caterpillars hiding and eating inside the center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe teeɔ mi ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ?

english: These caterpillars, often called Fall Armyworms, hide inside the tender central whorl of the leaf because it provides them with soft food and protects them from heat and birds.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ, ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ amɛ Fall Armyworms lɛ, kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ amli ejaakɛ amɛhaa niyenii ni mli jɔ ni amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo kɛ okpoi ahe.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling upwards and becoming hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee shiŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is usually caused by a virus spread by tiny white insects called whiteflies, or by severe stress caused by sudden heat and lack of water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly loo kɛjɛ haomɔ ni naa wa ni hulutsoo ni baa trukaa kɛ nu ni faaa lɛ kɛbaa lɛ mli.

english: Why are my cocoa trees dropping their flowers before any cocoa pods start forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi dani kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they are stressed by hot weather, lack of water, or attacks by tiny insects like mirids. The tree sheds flowers to save its energy to survive.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji hulutsoo, nu ni bɛ, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ atatui ni shwieɔ shi lɛ hao amɛ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch as much sunlight as possible. Exposure to sunlight helps the leaves make food, which flows down to make the yam tuber underground grow big.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Hulu la ni tsoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. ni hoɔ kɛyaa shi ni ehaa shikpɔŋ shishi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daraa

english: If too many small shoots grow around the main plantain tree, they fight with the main tree for food and water. Removing extra shoots leaves only one or two strong ones, ensuring you get large plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii bibii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ he lɛ, Ekɛ tso titri lɛ baawu koni ená niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ ojie tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha niji kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni no baaha oná plantain tso agbo ko.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay green and grow, or that the field has too much water logged around the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Aloo akɛni ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu babaoo ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe hewɔ?

english: Why do my pepper plants have plenty of green leaves but no peppers growing on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ hiɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi chili ko bɛ nɔ?

english: Using too much nitrogen-rich fertilizer makes pepper plants focus all their energy on growing big green leaves instead of producing flowers and setting fruit.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa pepper tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛdaraa lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through small root bumps, acting as a natural fertilizer for future crops.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi bibii anɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up when I plant them in an open field without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to intense heat and direct sunlight; they need shade plants like plantains to act as living umbrellas and keep the soil cool during their early years.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains koni amɛtsu nii akɛ hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my crop seeds fail to sprout even after I plant them right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ po lɛ?

english: Early rains are often followed by hot dry spells that dry out the topsoil quickly, scorching tiny germinating seeds before their roots can reach deeper water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔi ni mli edɔ lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ agbi oya. shã dumɔwui bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ dani shishifãi lɛ ashɛ nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ he

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and turn yellow during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in cassava is typically caused by sap-sucking insects like whiteflies, which spread viruses that stunt the plant's growth and shrink your harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ whiteflies, ni gbɛɔ helai ni tsiɔ tsei anaa ni amɛhaa oŋmɔshi nii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when heat becomes extreme or when watering is irregular, as the plant tries to save water rather than produce fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa ba amɛnɔ loo kɛji akɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ lɛ ejaaa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tomato tsei lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu nu he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why should I cut away some of the extra small stems growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Ajieɔ mɛi krɛdɛɛi komɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ Midumɔwui titrii lɛ ahe lɛ.

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, compete directly with the mother plantain stem for soil nutrients and water, which results in smaller bunches of plantains if left unchecked.
ga: Tso lɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni fa lɛ kɛ fɔlɔ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Enɛ haa plantains lɛ feɔ bibii kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko kwɛɛɛ nɔ.

english: Lifting yam vines off the ground allows the leaves to catch maximum sunlight, which provides the energy needed to grow large tubers underground.
ga: Kɛ́ awó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ naa hulu la ni fe fɛɛ. Enɛ ji hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛkwɛ bulb agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my mature maize plants fall over flat on the ground right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei ni edara lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Maize stalks fall over when planted too close together, when roots are shallow due to hard soil, or when heavy winds and rain push down plants carrying heavy cobs.
ga: Abele tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Beni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa hewɔ lɛ Aloo be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ tsiɔ tsei ni ŋmeii ni tsii eyi mli obɔ lɛ shi.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, which is the key nutrient that keeps leaves green and healthy. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure helps the plants turn green and produce bigger ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni yeɔ ebuaa ni baa lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni ehe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni toi lɛ hu adara.

english: Why do extension officers always tell me to keep big trees on my farm when planting young cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mɛi ni kwɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛɔ mi be fɛɛ be akɛ mikɛ tsei wuji ahi ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛ́ midu kookoo bibii lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are like small babies that easily get burned and dried out by direct harsh sunlight. Shade trees protect young cocoa from scorching heat, preserve moisture in the soil, and shelter the plants from harsh Harmattan winds.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ abifabii bibii ni hulu shãa amɛ oya ni amɛgbiɔ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ buɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni obuɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ he.

english: How can I tell if my cassava is ready for harvesting without uprooting the whole stem?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni mijieee tso muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Cassava is usually mature when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil at the base of the plant begins to crack. You can gently scrape away a little topsoil near the main stem to see if the roots have expanded into thick tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ eda kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ. Obaanyɛ okɛ blɛoo ajie sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ yiteŋ lɛ fioo. Koni ana kɛji shishifãi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ kɛfeɔ yitso ni mli tse loo daabi.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the juices from the leaves and spreading viruses. Spraying neem oil solution or organic insecticidal soap helps clear these insects so new leaves can grow out flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie kooloi nɛɛ kɛjɛ ohe. Enɛ baaha baai heei lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: When too many shoots grow around one plantain stem, they all fight for the same food and water in the soil, resulting in tiny bunches. Leaving only one or two strong shoots ensures the main plant gets enough food to grow a big, heavy bunch.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ ehe Plantain kome Amɛyeɔ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli hu. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji kui bibii lɛ amligbalamɔ. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ tso agbo ni tsii.

english: What will happen to my yam crop if I do not put tall sticks for the vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi sweet potato tso lɛ nɔ kɛji mikɛ niji ni kwɔlɔ efɔɔɔ shi koni wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the air to catch sunlight, which powers the growth of the tubers underground. If vines rot or stay piled up on the hot ground, the plant cannot feed itself properly, leading to very small yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni hulu la ashɛ amɛhe. ni tsirɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ adalɛ Kɛji wain tsei lɛ egbo loo amɛbua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ amɛye amɛhe jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa anáa sweet potato ŋmeii bibii waa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant suffers from extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of balanced nutrients during flowering. Regular watering at the root level and maintaining good soil nutrients keep the flowers attached until fruit forms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni sa ni bɛ amɛmli yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔii lɛ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifã lɛ he daa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii kpakpai ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ baaha fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi kɛyashi amɛbaawo yibii.

english: Groundnuts develop their pods underground instead of in the air. After the yellow flowers are pollinated above ground, the plant grows a peg that bends downward and buries itself into the soil, where the actual groundnut pods form and ripen.
ga: Peanuts feɔ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi moŋ fe kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Beni afee fɔfɔii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ lɛ, Tso lɛ daa tamɔ ŋtayaa ni abɔle shi ni ekɛ ehe woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Biɛ ji he ni ŋmeii lɛ feɔ diɛŋtsɛ ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to weed my farm during the first month after my seeds germinate?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ mli beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young crop sprouts are weak and can easily be choked by fast-growing weeds that steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds in the first three to four weeks gives your young crop a strong advantage so it can grow taller than competing weeds.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni jwɛi ni shwereɔ oya ni juɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ amɛ oya. Kɛ́ okwɛ jwɛi lɛ anɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha onibii bibii lɛ aná sɛɛnamɔ babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eda fe jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ.

english: Why does rice grow so well in fields covered with standing water while other crops die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔji ni nu damɔ shi yɛ mli lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni tsei krokomɛi gboiɔ lɛ?

english: Rice plants have unique hollow tubes in their stems and roots that allow oxygen to travel from the leaves down to the submerged roots. Standing water also smothers land weeds and keeps the roots wet without suffocating the rice plant.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ srɔto yɛ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi amli ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ jɛɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli kɛyaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ nu shishi lɛ amli. Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni egbeɔ jwɛi ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ fũɔ ni ehaaa ŋmãa tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why are insects always attacking my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii yaa nɔ amɛtutuaa mi-kookoo tsei lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees produce sweet pods and tender young leaves that naturally attract insects like mirids (capsids). Without regular pruning and pest control, insect populations quickly multiply and damage the tree shoots and pods.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afolɔɛɛ tsei lɛ ahe daa ni akuuu amɛ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ, amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni ŋɔɔ kɛ baai bibii ni gbalaa ŋmeii tamɔ mirids (capsids) lɛ. Kplukai ayibɔ yaa hiɛ oya ni efiteɔ tsei ashishifãi kɛ tsei ashishifãi.

english: Can pests spread to my farm from a neighboring neglected farm?
ga: Ani tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛjɛ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ ni aku hiɛ ashwie nɔ lɛ amli?

english: Yes, insects and fungal spores travel easily through the air, soil, or crawling branches. If neighboring farms leave infested or overgrown trees unattended, pests will naturally migrate to clean, healthy crops nearby.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ tsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, shikpɔŋ, kɛ tsei niji ni shwereɔ lɛ amli mlɛo. Kɛji ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ shi tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ loo tsei ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko kwɛɛɛ nɔ lɛ, Tsɛi lɛ fãa kɛyaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni he tse ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli.

english: How do I know if my cocoa trees are being damaged by pests?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai efite mi-cacao tsei lɛ?

english: Pest damage usually shows up as dark or yellowing spots on leaves, stunted young shoots, small holes or scars on pods, and branches drying up as if burned by fire.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ jeɔ kpo akɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ. Akɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ egbɔjɔ. Buji bibii loo ŋmeii jeɔ kpo yɛ tsei lɛ ahe, ni tsei lɛ aniji lɛ egbi tamɔ nɔ ni ashã amɛ.

english: This is caused by a fungal infection called Black Pod disease, which thrives in overly damp, shady conditions when heavy rain splashes fungal spores from the soil onto the low-hanging pods.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela kɛ enɛ baa. Ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ fe nine kɛ hulutsoo be mli beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa ŋmeii ni jɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my young crops struggle when I clear and settle on a new piece of forest land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ waa kɛ́ mijie koo hee ko mli ni mihi shi yɛ mli lɛ?

english: Newly cleared forest soil often hides wild soil pests and fungal spores, while removing mature forest trees exposes sensitive young crops to harsh direct sunlight and heat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koo mli shikpɔŋ ni ajie lɛ ehee lɛ kɛ koo mli shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai teeɔ. Yɛ be mli ni koo mli tsei ni eda lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tsei bibii ni hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nuɔ he waa lɛ ashiɔ.

english: Cocoa trees shed their leaves to conserve water when the air is hot and the soil is dry. Providing shade trees helps lower temperatures and retain moisture around the cocoa roots.
ga: Kookoo tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛhiɛ nu mli kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi. Shade ni akɛhaa lɛ haa dɔlɛ baa shi ni ehaa fɛ̃i hiɔ kookoo shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why does allowing my cocoa trees to grow too bushy reduce my crop yields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi-cacao tsei lɛ ni mihaa amɛdaraa tsɔ lɛ haa mi-cacao tsei lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Overly bushy branches block sunlight and prevent air from circulating through the tree. This cool, humid environment creates ideal breeding grounds for pests and rot, stealing energy from pod production.
ga: Tso lɛ niji babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa ni ehaaa kɔɔyɔɔ akatsɔ tso lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni mli ejɔ nɛɛ feɔ he ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ ŋmeii fɔɔ yɛ. Kɛtsɔ hewalɛ ni ajuɔ kɛjɛɔ pods ni afeɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: What happens if I leave unharvested pods on my cocoa trees for too long?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mishi ŋmeii ni akpako yɛ cacao tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ?

english: Leaving ripe pods on the tree causes them to overripe, rot, and attract destructive pests, which then spread infections to healthy surrounding branches and future pods.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛshwere fe nine, amɛgboi ni amɛbaagbala ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ. ni no sɛɛ lɛ, ekɛ hela baa tsei niji ni ebɔle amɛhe ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛ wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmeii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does it take several years for my cocoa trees to start producing fruit compared to food crops like maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ afii babaoo dani mi-cacao tsei lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi kɛ akɛtoɔ niyenii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ he lɛ?

english: Cocoa is a perennial tree crop that must invest energy into building deep root systems and strong trunks before it has enough mature reserves to continuously support heavy fruit pods.
ga: Cocoa ji tso ko ni yeɔ afii babaoo ni biɔ ni akɛ hewalɛ awo mli koni ekɛma shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ shishifãi ni wa. Enɛ ji dani ŋmeii ni ato lɛ baadara koni amɛye amɛbua aduawai ŋmeii ni tsiimɔ yaa nɔ lɛ.

english: Why does cocoa farming require continuous pest care year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akudɔ kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii daa afi lɛ?

english: Because cocoa trees stay in the ground for decades, pests and diseases establish permanent habitats in the field, requiring ongoing seasonal monitoring and management to safeguard the tree's health.
ga: Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kookoo tsei ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii nyɔŋmai abɔ. Kplukai srɔtoi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai No hewɔ lɛ, efeɔ shihilɛhe ni hiɔ shi daa yɛ ŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ biɔ ni akwɛ tsei lɛ anɔ be fɛɛ be ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni abu tsei lɛ ahewalɛ he.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender roots and leaves that burn easily in full sunlight. Leaving shade trees or planting fast-growing plants like plantains creates a cool umbrella over the cocoa, protecting them until they are strong enough to handle sunlight.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi kɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ ni ashiɔ loo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni mli ejɔ baa kookoo lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu kookoo lɛ he kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la.

english: Maize leaves curl up to protect themselves from losing too much water in extreme heat. It is the plant's natural defense mechanism to conserve moisture until the sun goes down and temperatures drop.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe koni nu babaoo akafite yɛ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ mli. Eji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulu lɛ baa shi ni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my growing maize plants turning yellow and drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei ni miida lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the plant is starving for nitrogen, an essential soil food needed for green growth. Adding organic manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps keep the leaves green and productive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why does planting cassava stems too close together result in small, thin tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ adu ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, their roots fight each other underground for limited water and plant food. Giving each plant proper spacing allows the roots enough room to expand and produce thick, heavy cassava tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná nu kɛ tsei niyenii fioo. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko teŋ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛwo ŋmei shishifãi ni mli wa ni tsii.

english: Beans and cowpeas can take nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil through their roots. This naturally feeds the neighboring maize plants, helping them grow stronger without as much added fertilizer.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛjie kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ aye nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa waa ni ehe ehiaaa ni awo amɛ fɔ babaoo.

english: How do weeds lower my crop harvest even when my crops look taller than the weeds?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi baanyɛ aha miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa lɛ aba shi? Eyɛ mli akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛkwɔ fe jwɛi lɛ moŋ

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that secretly steal water, nutrients, and root space from your crops below the ground. Even if your crops look taller, weeds drain the energy crops need to produce big fruits or grains.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, niyenii, kɛ shishifãi ahe gbɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli yɛ teemɔŋ. Kɛji akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛkwɔ po Shi jwɛi hu jieɔ hewalɛ ni he hiaa tsei lɛ koni amɛwo yibii loo dumɔwui wuji lɛ.

english: Why should I cut off the fresh green shoots growing around the bottom stem of my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Those extra shoots, called suckers, waste valuable food and water that the tree needs to make cocoa pods. Cutting them off directs all the tree's energy toward producing healthy, large cocoa pods.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi nɛɛ akɛ ŋmeii. Enɛ baaha niyenii kɛ nu ni jara wa ni he hiaa tsei lɛ koni amɛkɛfee kookoo ŋmeii lɛ afite. Kɛ́ afolɔ lɛ, eheɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ koni ekɛfee kookoo ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when rainwater collects on my farm for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nu bua amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need oxygen in the soil to breathe and stay healthy. Standing water fills up all the air spaces in the soil, suffocating the roots and causing rot-causing fungi to attack them.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ koni amɛmu ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ hei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ tutuaa amɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and looking small and wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bibii ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves and sucking out the plant's juices, or spreading a plant virus. Checking leaf undersides early helps catch these pests before they damage the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ nu lɛ kɛ baa lɛ baa. loo egbɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwa tsei amli Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni amɔmɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce lots of blossoms, but the blossoms fall off before growing into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo shi ekɛ fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato plants shed their blossoms when they experience sudden stress, such as extreme midday heat or dry soil. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch helps the flowers stay on the plant and set fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛ kpe trukaa nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ gbi teŋ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Can I plant lettuce at any time of the year, or do I have to wait for a specific season?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu lettuce yɛ afi lɛ mli be fɛɛ be loo esa akɛ mamɛ be pɔtɛɛ ko?

english: Lettuce is a very adaptable crop that can be grown at any time in our area, right from the beginning of the year straight through to the end.
ga: Lettuce ji tso ko ni nyɛɔ etsakeɔ ehe waa ni abaanyɛ adu be fɛɛ be yɛ wɔ akutso lɛ mli. Kɛjɛ afi lɛ shishijee mli kɛyashi afi lɛ naagbee

english: Why do my cabbage plants struggle to grow well on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage tso lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cabbage is naturally a difficult crop to cultivate in our local environment, so it rarely performs well compared to other leafy greens.
ga: Cabbage ji tso ko ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli ni ewa akɛ aaakwɛ yɛ wɔ akutso lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, etsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ akɛto aduawai krokomɛi ni yɔɔ baai eŋɔli lɛ ahe.

english: If I want to farm vegetables continuously from January to December, which crop is a reliable choice?
ga: Kɛji miisumɔ ni makwɛ aduawai anɔ daa kɛjɛ January kɛyashi December. Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ji nibii ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ?

english: Lettuce is an ideal choice for year-round farming because it can be successfully grown at any month of the year.
ga: Lettuce ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha afi muu lɛ fɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ejaakɛ abaanyɛ adu yɛ omanyeyeli mli yɛ afi lɛ mli nyɔŋ fɛɛ nyɔŋ nɔ.

english: Is cabbage a good crop for a beginner farmer like me to start with?
ga: Ani cabbage ji ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpa kɛha okwaafonyo ni jeɔ shishi tamɔ mi?

english: No, cabbage is quite difficult to grow and often does not do well in our conditions, making it risky for beginners.
ga: Dabi, Cabbage ŋmɔshi nibii wa waa ni bei pii lɛ, ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ wɔshihilɛi amli. Enɛ haa efeɔ oshara kɛhaa mɛi ni jeɔ shishi lɛ.

english: Does lettuce require special seasonal timing during the year to give a good harvest?
ga: Ani be krɛdɛɛ ko he miihia lettuce yɛ afi lɛ mli koni enyɛ ekpa nii jogbaŋŋ?

english: No special seasonal timing is needed; lettuce behaves consistently and grows well no matter when you plant it during the year.
ga: Be mli ŋmɛlɛtswai krɛdɛɛi ahe ehiaaa. Lettuce feɔ enii pɛpɛɛpɛ ni edaa jogbaŋŋ ekɔɔɔ he eko be ni okɛbaadu lɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli.

english: Why is lettuce so much easier to cultivate in our region than cabbage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ lettuce dumɔ waaa yɛ wɔkpokpaa lɛ nɔ fe cabbage lɛ?

english: Lettuce thrives easily in our local conditions year-round, whereas cabbage is sensitive and hard to manage, leading to poor results.
ga: Lettuce daa oya yɛ wɔ akutsoŋ shihilɛi amli afi muu lɛ fɛɛ. Shi kɛlɛ, kaabeji lɛ waaa ni ekɛ nitsumɔ wa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yibii ni ehiii.

english: Are there common leafy vegetables that simply do not perform well in our local environment?
ga: Ani aduawai ni yɔɔ baai ni afɔɔ namɔ ni tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ wɔ akutso lɛ mli lɛ yɛ?

english: Yes, cabbage is one crop that is generally difficult to grow and usually does not do well in our local environment.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, cabbage ji tso ko ni bei pii lɛ, ewa akɛ aaakwɛ ni bei pii lɛ, ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ wɔ akutso lɛ mli.

english: Can I start a new batch of lettuce today even if we are in the middle of the year?
ga: Ŋmɛnɛ obaanyɛ oje lettuce fã hee shishi eyɛ mli akɛ eji afi teŋgbɛ moŋ.

english: Yes, you can start growing lettuce at any point in the year, as it does not rely on a strict planting calendar.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ oje lettuce shishi yɛ afi lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. Ejaakɛ ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ he afɔ̃ kalanda ni mli wa ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do many vegetable farmers in our community avoid planting cabbage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai abɔɔ mli nitsulɔi babaoo ni yɔɔ wɔ akutso lɛ mli lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ kaabii dumɔ he lɛ?

english: Farmers tend to avoid cabbage because it is hard to grow successfully and regularly fails to produce a good yield in our area.
ga: Okwaafoi sumɔɔ ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ kaabɛji he ejaakɛ edumɔ wa ni bei pii lɛ, ewooo yibii kpakpai yɛ wɔ akutso lɛ mli.

english: If I want a safe vegetable crop that won't fail because of the time of year, what should I plant?
ga: Kɛji oosumɔ ni oná aduawai ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni sɛɛ efooo lɛ, mɛni ji nɔ ni esa akɛ odu?

english: Lettuce is a safe option because it can be grown continuously from the start of the year to the end without major seasonal issues.
ga: Lettuce ji nɔ ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ejaakɛ abaanyɛ adu be fɛɛ be kɛjɛ afi lɛ shishijee kɛyashi afi lɛ naagbee ni be mli naagbai wuji ko bɛ he.

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves of maize usually means the plant lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen helps plants stay green and grow strong; when there is not enough in the soil, the plant moves what little nitrogen it has from its older lower leaves up to feed the newer top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni shishigbɛ baai lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ shikpɔŋ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni etsɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my maize stalks stay short and thin even when I give them plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nu babaoo moŋ?

english: Water alone is not enough for growth. If your soil lacks key nutrients like phosphorus, or if the soil is too hard for roots to spread out, the maize cannot feed itself properly and will stay small and weak.
ga: Nu pɛ kɛkɛ faaa kɛha dalɛ. Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii titrii tamɔ fɔsfɔs bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã lɛ, Abele lɛ nyɛŋ aye ehe niyenii jogbaŋŋ ni ebaaya nɔ ahi shi bibioo ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my vegetable plants wilt in the afternoon sun but look fresh again every morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi shwane mli shi amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa ehee daa leebi lɛ?

english: During hot afternoons, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull it from the dry ground. At night when it cools down, the roots catch up and refill the plant with water, making it stand upright by morning.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Gbi gbɛkɛ beni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baaje kpo ni amɛkɛ nu baafata tso lɛ he. Ha ema shi shiŋŋ leebi.

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling upwards during the dry heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is the tomato plant's natural shield against heat. By rolling its leaves inward, the plant reduces the leaf area exposed to the hot sun to conserve its internal moisture.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji tomato tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli dɔlɛ hebuu. Tsei haa he ni amɛbaai lɛ shɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ mli kɛyaa mli lɛ nɔ. koni hulutsoo ahi mli

english: Very hot weather can destroy the pollen inside pepper flowers, preventing fruits from forming. The plant naturally drops these useless blossoms so it does not waste valuable energy on them.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afite pollen ni yɔɔ pepper fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Ehaa aduawai lɛ efeee Tso lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔi ni he ehiaaa nɛɛ kpo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, afiteee hewalɛ ni jara wa yɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees drop their flowers without producing any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi ni ŋmɔtɔ ko bɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by drought, lack of soil food, or insect attacks. The tree sheds its flowers to save energy for its own survival until conditions improve.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hɔmɔ hao amɛ. Niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kooloi bibii ni tutuaa Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi kɛyashi shihilɛi lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do groundnut plants bend down and push their stem stems into the soil after flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsiɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ beni amɛwo fɔfɔi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts develop their fruit underground to protect them from heat and animals. Once the flower is fertilized, the plant grows a long stem called a 'peg' that pushes deep into the dirt where the nut safe matures.
ga: Peanuts woɔ yibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ kɛ kooloi ahe. Beni awo fɔfɔi lɛ mli fɔ Tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kakadaji ni atsɛɔ amɛ ‘pegs’ ni yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni ŋmeii lɛ yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ lɛ.

english: Roots need air in the soil to stay alive. When heavy rain floods the land for many days, water fills all the tiny air pockets in the soil, causing the roots to drown and decay.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he hiaa shishifãi yɛ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo lɛ Nu eyi kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ, ni no haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when the fruit bunches grow large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ dara lɛ?

english: Plantains do not have deep taproots like tall trees; their roots spread out close to the surface. When a heavy fruit bunch develops, the plant becomes top-heavy, and wet soil allows winds to easily push the roots out of the ground.
ga: Plantains bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ tamɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ. Eshishifãi lɛ gbɛ eshwa he ko ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Kɛ aduawai akuu lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baaná nɔ ni fe fɛɛ. Ni shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tswaa shishifãi lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya.

english: Why do my stored seed yams start sprouting in the barn even before the rainy season arrives?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ po baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yams have a natural internal timer. After a few months of rest post-harvest (called dormancy), the yam automatically wakes up and uses its stored food and moisture to sprout, preparing itself for the next growing season.
ga: Sweet potatoes yɛ adebɔɔ mli be he gbɛjianɔtoo. Beni amɛjɔɔ amɛhe nyɔji fioo komɛi yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ (Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ dormancy.) Sweet potatoes lɛ teɔ shi amɛ diɛŋtsɛ ni amɛkɛ niyenii ni ato kɛ nu ni mli edɔ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ̃ koni amɛkɛsaa amɛhe kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why does my plantain feel too soft and watery when I pound it into fufu nowadays?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ blɛoo ni eyɛ nu tsɔ kɛ́ atswa lɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ amrɔ nɛɛ?

english: Some newer or hybrid plantain varieties are bred for fast growth or high yield rather than high starch content, making them less sticky and harder to pound into traditional firm fufu.
ga: Afɔ tsei srɔtoi heei loo tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ ekomɛi koni amɛdara oya loo amɛwo yibii babaoo. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee nɔ ni starch babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ Enɛ haaa efee nɔ ni shwieɔ shi ni ewaa akɛ aaatswa lɛ awo kusum naa tsɔne ni mli wa, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do agriculture officers recommend these new plantain varieties instead of our old traditional suckers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi kɛ plantain henɔi heei nɛɛ baa yɛ wɔ momo lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: New improved varieties are developed to resist diseases, grow faster, and produce bigger bunches, even though their food texture might differ slightly from traditional types.
ga: Afee tsofai srɔtoi ni hi fe tsutsu lɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛte shi amɛwo hela lɛ. shwereɔ oya ni ewoɔ ŋmeii wuji Eyɛ mli akɛ niyenii lɛ mli ŋmɔlɔ baanyɛ afee srɔto fioo yɛ shishijee srɔtoi lɛ ahe moŋ.

english: Can I mix these new plantain types with cassava so my fufu turns out better?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ plantains heei nɛɛ afutu ŋmei koni miflu lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Yes, mixing softer or lower-starch plantain varieties with high-starch cassava helps give the fufu the traditional firmness and smooth texture you want.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ okɛ starch plantains ni yɔɔ blɛoo loo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ futu cassava ni yɔɔ starch babaoo lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha fluff lɛ aná kusum naa shifimɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni osumɔɔ lɛ.

english: Is it a good idea for me to plant plantains right in my backyard near the house?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ makwɛ plantains yɛ shia lɛ sɛɛ ni bɛŋkɛ mishia lɛ?

english: Yes, backyard planting works well because plantains thrive on household organic waste, greywater runoff, and shade, making them easy to care for right next to your home.
ga: Hɛɛ, amɛ ni akwɛɔ yɛ shia lɛ sɛɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ dumɔwui lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shĩa mli jwɛi ni jɛɔ bɔɔ nii amli, nu ni hoɔ, kɛ hulutsoo mli, ni no haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ abaakwɛ amɛ yɛ shia ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ mli.

english: How do I choose the best plantain suckers to plant in my backyard?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantain tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaadu yɛ mishia lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Look for healthy 'sword suckers' with narrow, spear-like leaves and strong, thick bases from healthy mother plants, as they grow faster and produce bigger fruit.
ga: Taomɔ ‘bamboo tsei’ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni baai lɛ mli tse ni tamɔ akpɔlɔ kɛ shishi ni mli wa ni mli tse ni jɛ fɔlɔ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛbaada oya ni amɛwo yibii wuji.

english: How does the way I handle my plantains after harvesting affect how long they stay fresh?
ga: Bɔ ni afeɔ plantains lɛ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ saa be ni amɛhiɔ shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ he.

english: Rough handling or bruising plantains during harvest causes them to ripen too fast and rot quickly, whereas careful cutting and keeping them in a cool shade keeps them fresh longer.
ga: dumɔwui lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ ni ehiii loo ni atswaa amɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ haa amɛshwereɔ oya tsɔ ni amɛgboiɔ oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ ofolɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛto he ko ni jɛmɛ ejɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do some of my plantain bunches ripen on the tree before I even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ miikwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani mikpa amɛ po lɛ?

english: Hot weather, lack of water, or damage from pests and diseases can stress the plantain tree, causing the fruit to ripen prematurely before it fully develops.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ, nu ni bɛ, loo kooloi bibii kɛ helai ni fiteɔ lɛ Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ aná haomɔ. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ mra dani eshɛɔ dalɛ he.

english: Why are my plantain bunches smaller today than what my farm used to produce years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ daraaa ŋmɛnɛ fe nɔ ni miŋmɔ lɛ wo afii komɛi ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Over time, soil loses essential nutrients if organic manure or fertilizer isn't added, and older roots can accumulate pests, leading to smaller yields over continuous farming.
ga: Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Sũ lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ baafite kɛji akɛ akɛ humus loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ wooo mli. Ni shishifãi ni egbɔ lɛ baanyɛ ahi tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa kɛjɛɔ okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ lɛ mli baa lɛ faaa.

english: Yellowing leaves are often a sign of nutrient deficiency in the soil or fungal diseases like Black Sigatoka, which reduce the plant's energy and shrink the fruit size.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko tamɔ sigatoka diŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ baa shi, ni ehaa aduawai lɛ feɔ bibioo.

english: How much water do plantain trees need to produce big bunches during the dry season?
ga: Nu enyiɛ he hiaa plantain koni ekɛkwɛ jwɛi agbo ko yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Plantains have shallow roots and broad leaves that lose water quickly, so they need regular watering or heavy mulching around the base to keep producing well during dry months.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni afɔse nu daa loo aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ waa. shishitoo lɛ he koni ená yibii kpakpai yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and delicate root systems that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. They need shade crops like plantain or cassava planted alongside them to protect them from heat and retain soil moisture during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiisumɔ ni adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo cassava yɛ amɛmasɛi. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he ni akɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yam is a climbing vine that needs daylight to manufacture food efficiently. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground where diseases spread and exposes more leaves to sunlight, which results in larger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ hulu la koni amɛná niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hela lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã ni ebaaha baai lɛ aná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji baa.

english: Plantain trees do not have a deep taproot; instead, they have shallow roots that spread near the top layer of soil. Digging deeper planting holes, building soil mounds around the base, and propping the stems with wooden poles helps keep them anchored during storms.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ, shi moŋ amɛyɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni aduɔ lɛ mli bu ni mli kwɔ ni afeɔ shikpɔŋ gɔŋ ni akɛbɔleɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he kɛ tsei ni akɛfiɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii. Ebaaye ebua ni ehi amɛhe yɛ ahum be mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crop turning yellow from the bottom of the plant going up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually indicate a nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Nitrogen is essential for green leafy growth, so applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or urea can help restore healthy green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he hiaa waa kɛha baa eŋɔli lɛ dalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK loo urea tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni eha baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do experienced farmers tell me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas to improve my soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ baakɛɛ mi akɛ midu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special bacteria on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. When the plants harvest and decay, they leave natural fertilizer behind for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ helai krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛhaa ehiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akpa tsei ni amɛgboi lɛ Abaashi Adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha dumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my maize leaves and sawdust-like dirt in the center of the plant?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli

english: This is typical damage caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a common pest in Ghana that feeds inside the growing tip of maize plants. Spraying recommended insecticides or applying neem extracts early in the morning or evening helps kill these pests before they destroy the crop.
ga: Enɛ ji nɔ ni Fall Armyworm caterpillar, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni yeɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ fiteɔ fe fɛɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ shwie nɔ loo okɛ neem mli nu lɛ tsu nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni egbe kooloi nɛɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids, thrips, or whiteflies that spread plant viruses. Controlling these pests early using insecticidal soaps or neem oil spray prevents the leaf twisting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ helai yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Kɛ akɛ samla ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni baai lɛ akafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off due to severe heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of specific nutrients like boron. Maintaining consistent soil moisture and using balanced fertilizer helps the flowers successfully set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa hewɔ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ boron ni bɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long, suffocating the roots during periods of heavy rain. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away and prevents tuber rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa, ni ehaa ŋmei lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Not all rice requires deep flooded fields; upland rice can grow on rain-fed dry land like maize. Standing water in lowland rice fields is mainly used to suppress weeds and regulate temperature rather than just feeding the plant.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ nu awo ŋmãa henɔi komɛi amli. Omɔ kakadaŋŋ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi, ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ nɔ tamɔ ŋmãa nɔ. Akɛ nu ni damɔ shi yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii titri kɛkwɛɔ jwɛi kɛ hulutsoo nɔ moŋ fe ni akɛhaa tsei niyenii kɛkɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is low on nitrogen, which plants need to make food and stay green. When nitrogen runs out, the plant steals it from its old lower leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni tsei he hiaa koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛkwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ Kɛ́ nitrogen lɛ ba naagbee Tso lɛ juɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi ŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ niyenii.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips sucking sap from under the leaves, or by a virus transmitted by these insects. When they feed, they damage the leaf tissue, causing it to twist and stunt the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛbaa lɛ nɔ Kɛ amɛye Ebaafite baa lɛ mli fãji. Enɛ haa etsɔɔ tso lɛ ni ehaa egbɔjɔɔ.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when temperatures get too high or when there is sudden water stress. Extreme heat dries out the flower's pollen, preventing pollination so the plant sheds the useless bloom.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ loo kɛ́ amɛna nu he haomɔ trukaa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa pollen lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Tsi pollination naa No sɛɛ lɛ tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi ni he ehiaaa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and dry up when I cut down all the big trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ beni mifolɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and burn easily under full sunlight. Shade trees act like umbrellas, shielding young cocoa from excessive sun and keeping the soil moist until the cocoa roots grow deep enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Shade tsei tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Buu kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni fe nine lɛ he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ baatsɔ shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa.

english: Planting maize continuously in the same soil drains the exact same nutrients every season and lets maize-specific pests build up in the ground. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or beans restores soil fertility.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ daa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ daa be mli, ni ehaa abɛi pɔtɛɛ ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmãa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it harmful to place fertilizer directly touching the stem of my cassava plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo ŋmei tsei lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer contains concentrated salts that attract moisture. Placing it directly against the stem draws water out of the plant tissue, burning the stem and damaging tender surface roots.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ amli ŋmei ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmei baa. Kɛ́ okɛwo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaagbala nu kɛjɛ tso lɛ fãji lɛ amli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ tso lɛ shãa ni efiteɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why are small caterpillars hiding in the center funnel of my young corn plants and eating the new leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ baai heei lɛ?

english: This is typically caused by Fall Armyworm, a pest that lays eggs on young corn. The hatched caterpillars crawl inside the growing shoot to hide from predators while eating the tender leaves from the inside out.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii bibii anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kplukai ni efɔ lɛ shwereɔ kɛboteɔ tsei ni miida lɛ amli koni amɛyatee amɛhe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start to turn soft and rot underground during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When soil stays soaked with water for too long, air cannot reach the cassava roots, causing them to suffocate. Fungi present in wet soil easily invade these weakened roots, turning them rotten.
ga: Kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ewo nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ahe. suffocate Fungi ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ abote shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ nɛɛ amli oya ni eha amɛgboi.

english: How does spreading dry grass on top of the soil help my vegetables survive during dry weather?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-aduawai lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli?

english: Dry grass acts as mulch, creating a protective layer that blocks direct sunlight from heating the soil. This stops moisture from evaporating quickly and keeps the roots cool during hot days.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ mulch. Efeɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni tsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ adɔ. Enɛ baatsi ŋmɔtɔ ni hoɔ oya lɛ naa, ni ebaaye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily after heavy rain and mild wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots near the surface rather than deep taproots. Tiny pests like root nematodes often chew these surface roots away, leaving the heavy plant without a firm grip on the wet soil.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛ nu lɛ hiɛ moŋ fe shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ root nematodes lɛ shwieɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi nɛɛ anɔ. Ehaa tsei ni tsii lɛ nyɛɛɛ akpɛtɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ he.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Keeping tall shade trees or planting plantains around them creates a protective canopy that prevents leaf scorching and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ akwɛmɔ loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Tso lɛ feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ mɔ he ni haaa baai lɛ ashã ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry spells to conserve water and protect themselves from drying out. Once the rains return, the plant will grow fresh leaves and continue developing its roots.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baaná baai heei ni ebaaya nɔ ewo shishifãi.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually show that the soil is low in nitrogen. The maize plant naturally moves the limited nitrogen it has from its older lower leaves to feed the younger top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi tsiɔ nitrogen fioo kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baa bibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Why did my maize plants wither and die after I put fertilizer right next to their stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Fertilizer placed directly against a stem draws water out of the plant's roots, burning them. Fertilizer should always be buried a short distance away from the stem in moist soil.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baajie nu kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli ni eshã amɛ. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, fumɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ.

english: Lifting yam vines on stakes allows leaves to capture maximum sunlight and keeps them off damp soil where diseases spread, which helps the plant grow larger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnáa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. ni etsĩ shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekafee ŋmɔtɔ, he ni helai gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ bulbs wuji.

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce far more flowers than they can feed. The tree drops extra flowers so it can save its energy to turn the healthiest flowers into full pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃. Tso lɛ baajie fɔfɔi krokomɛi ashwie shi koni ekɛbu hewalɛ he yɛ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ ni etsakeɔ efeɔ dumɔwui ni eyi obɔ lɛ mli.

english: This issue, called blossom-end rot, happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium or experiences irregular watering. Keeping soil moisture consistent helps roots carry calcium to the growing fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa loo ahaa amɛ nu be fɛɛ be. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛkɛ calcium baa aduawai ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up tight into little cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni efee kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Curling pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies feed on leaf sap and spread viruses. Protecting plants from these insects keeps leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ hela lɛ amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ abu tsei ahe kɛjɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni amɛbaa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why does my maize grow much better when I plant it on a plot where I previously harvested groundnuts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ midu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpaa ŋmãa tsutsu lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This leaves natural fertilizer in the soil that feeds the next maize crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ahi shikpɔŋ ni akɛbaahã ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomato leaves get dark wet spots and rot quickly during heavy rainy periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ ni amɛgboiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Continuous rain and high humidity create a wet environment where fungal diseases thrive. Spacing plants further apart allows air to flow freely and dry the leaves faster.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli ewo fɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ aya hiɛ yɛ mli lɛ baa. Gbɛ babaoo ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya.

english: The very first rain often only wets the surface while the deeper soil remains hot and dry. If a long dry spell follows that first rain, your planted seeds will germinate and quickly dry up and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ haa ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ pɛ fɔ̃ɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ kã he edɔ ni egbi. Kɛji hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ nyiɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni adu lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛgbiɔ oya ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do some maize varieties mature in three months while others take up to five months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa henɔi komɛi shwereɔ yɛ nyɔji etɛ mli lɛ? yɛ be mli ni henɔi komɛi heɔ nyɔji enumɔ.

english: Different crop varieties are bred for different growth cycles. Short-duration varieties grow quickly to survive in regions with short rainy seasons, while long-duration varieties take longer because they produce bigger yields when rains last longer.
ga: Akwɛɔ tsei srɔtoi kɛha amɛdalɛ bei srɔtoi. Henɔi ni hiɔ shi be kuku lɛ daa oya koni amɛhi shi yɛ hei ni nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo yɔɔ lɛ. Shi ŋmeii srɔtoi ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ heɔ be babaoo ejaakɛ amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Leaf rolling is the plant's natural defense against heat. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the sun, which slows down water loss and keeps the crop from drying out.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he. Tsei haa amɛhe ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe lɛ nɔ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai ni amɛfoɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ fioo, ni ehaaa ŋmɔshi nibii agbi.

english: If the rainy season starts late in my area, should I still plant my regular crop varieties?
ga: Kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi sɛɛ yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ Ani esa akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii daa?

english: A late start usually means the rainy season will be shorter overall. It is better to switch to early-maturing crop varieties so they can fully grow and yield before the rain stops completely.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishijee ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baafee kuku yɛ fɛɛ mli. Esa akɛ otsake kɛya tsei srɔtoi ni kwɛɔ mra lɛ anɔ koni amɛdara ni amɛwo amɛyibii fɛɛ dani nugbɔ lɛ akpa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without producing any tomatoes during heavy rainy periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excessive rain and high humidity prevent insects and wind from pollinating the flowers properly. Unpollinated flowers cannot turn into fruit, so the plant sheds them.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo haaa kooloi bibii kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ afee fɔfɔi lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Fɔfɔi ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli lɛ nyɛŋ afee aduawai. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: How do cowpeas manage to grow so well even when rain stops falling for weeks?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina ŋmeii akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa otsii babaoo po?

english: Cowpeas have deep root systems that reach water stored deep in the soil, and their leaves can conserve moisture, making them naturally equipped to handle dry spells during the farming season.
ga: Cowpeas yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni shɛɔ nu ni ato yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ he. Ni amɛbaai lɛ baanyɛ ahi ŋmɔtɔ mli. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ mɛi ni he esa jogbaŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛtsu hulutsoo be lɛ he nii yɛ okwaayeli be lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot when water collects on my field for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nu bua ehe naa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Crop roots need oxygen from the soil to stay alive. Standing water block air from entering the ground, effectively suffocating the roots and allowing rot-causing organisms to destroy the cassava tubers.
ga: Tse shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekabote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ agbɔjɔ jogbaŋŋ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ.

english: Can I plant maize on the exact same plot every season without changing the crop?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi ni mitsakeee miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific soil nutrients and lets pests and diseases built up in the field. Rotating with legumes like beans or groundnuts restores soil fertility for the next season.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa sũ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ hoɔ, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Legume ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni atsakeɔ lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: Why are my pepper plants turning yellow even though I see rain falling regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ minaa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ?

english: Rainfall that is too frequent can wash away essential soil nutrients below the reach of roots. Yellow leaves often mean the plant cannot access enough nitrogen from the overly soaked soil.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ shii abɔ lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ ashishi lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How does leaving dry weeds and leaves on top of my soil help my crops during warm dry spells?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi kɛ tsei ni egboi ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: Covering the soil with dry plant material acts as a protective blanket. It blocks direct sunlight from drying out the ground, keeping the soil moist and cool for your crop roots for a longer time.
ga: Akɛ tsei ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Etsiɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I plant them in the open field without any shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely delicate and cannot tolerate direct, harsh sunlight. Without shade trees or plantains to shield them, the intense sun scorches their leaves and dries them out before their root system can properly establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa kwraa, ni amɛŋmɛɛɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Kɛji tsei ni baaha hulutsoo loo dumɔwui ni baaha nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ lɛ Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaagbi amɛ dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ afee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my land produce fewer crops every year even though I clear and plant on time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii faaa daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ ajieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be naa lɛ?

english: Soil gets exhausted when you continuously grow crops on it without restoring nutrients. Every harvest removes minerals from the earth, so unless you add manure, compost, or fertilizer, or let the land rest, the soil becomes too weak to support healthy yields.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ oya nɔ okwɛ tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni okɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ eko eko eko ehãaa. Nikpamɔ fɛɛ kpamɔ be lɛ jieɔ shika tsuru kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he, loo ohaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbɔjɔ tsɔ ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai baawo.

english: Why is it bad for my soil if I burn all the clearings and grass on my farm before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji mishã shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi kɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ dani midu nii lɛ?

english: Burning destroys the organic leaf litter and beneficial insects in the topsoil that naturally feed your crops. While it clears land quickly, it leaves the soil dry, unprotected, and depleted of essential natural nutrients.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ baabii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe jwɛi kɛ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni haa adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛhaa onibii lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya moŋ Shi ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbiɔ. hebuu ko bɛ kɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni he hiaa ni laajeɔ

english: Why do the maize seeds I saved from my previous harvest produce smaller cobs than the certified seeds I buy from the store?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni mijie kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ wo ŋmãa bibii fe dumɔwui ni awo he odase ni mihe yɛ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Many improved seed varieties are bred to give their highest yield only in the first generation. When you save and replant those seeds, they lose their vigor, resulting in uneven growth and smaller cobs.
ga: Afɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi babaoo ni atsake amɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli pɛ. Kɛ́ okɛto ni odu ekoŋŋ Nakai dumɔwui lɛ ahewalɛ baaje mli. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa ni ekɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee, ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Curling and yellow leaves on cassava are typically caused by cassava mosaic disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. The disease damages the plant's ability to turn sunlight into food, causing stunted growth and poor tuber formation.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ ŋmei nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ ŋmɔŋ. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Hela nɛɛ fiteɔ nyɛmɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛtsakeɔ hulu la lɛ ewoɔ niyenii mli lɛ. Ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraaa oya, ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crowded plants compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. The maize wastes energy growing tall to out-reach its neighbors instead of developing thick stems and large cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Abele fiteɔ hewalɛ ni edaa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ koni eshɛ ekutsoŋbii lɛ ahe. Mohu ɔ, e peeɔ tsohi nɛ a mi wa kɛ tsohi nɛ a mi wa.

english: Why does planting cowpeas alongside my maize make the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ haa ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas have natural organisms in their roots that capture nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil. The neighboring maize feeds on this extra nitrogen, which acts like a free natural fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Abɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ yeɔ nitrogen ni fa fe nine nɛɛ. ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ehe lɛ

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, drain valuable water and food away from the main trunk of the cocoa tree. Removing them directs all the tree's energy into developing strong branches and healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Tso lɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ shwieɔ nu ni jara wa kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ cacao tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ mli. Amɛjiemɔ lɛ heɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ koni ekɛwo niji ni he wa kɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when they suffer from severe heat or irregular watering. Extreme heat damages the pollen inside the flower, causing the plant to drop the bloom because it cannot be fertilized.
ga: Tomatoi baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ miipiŋ amɛ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ bɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo ŋmɔshi nii lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves droop during the hot afternoon sun even when the soil is moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: In intense heat, leaves lose water through evaporation faster than roots can draw it up from the ground. Drooping is the plant's natural defense to reduce its surface area exposed to the sun until the air cools down.
ga: yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Drooping ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli hebuu nɔ koni ekɛba ehiɛ ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, which is essential for green growth. The plant starves its older bottom leaves to send the remaining nutrients to the growing top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Tsei yeɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi lɛ hɔmɔ koni amɛkɛ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ amaje ŋwɛi baai ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants produce very small cobs with missing grains when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛ dumɔwui ni elaaje kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the roots and leaves compete fiercely with each other for sunlight, soil moisture, and food, leaving no single plant with enough energy to fill out a full cob.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni feɔ ekome waa Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei komɛi bɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaawo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wither and dry up when I cut down all the large trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ mifo tsei ni eda ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn easily in full sun. Shade trees act like protective umbrellas, keeping the air cool and soil moist until the cocoa stems grow thick and strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ajɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop many of their tiny young pods before they can grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii babaoo dani edaraa lɛ?

english: This is called cherelle wilt. It happens naturally when the tree realizes it does not have enough water or nutrients to feed all the pods at once, so it sacrifices some to save the rest.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ tsɛnsi ni egbo. Ebaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa beni tso lɛ yɔseɔ akɛ ebɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha eshishifãi lɛ fɛɛ akwɛ shikome lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ ekɛ ekomɛi shaa afɔle koni ekɛbu fã ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: Extra suckers compete with the main plant for water and soil nutrients. Removing them allows the mother plant to direct all its energy into producing a bigger stem and a heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie lɛ lɛ, ehaa tso nyɛ lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ tsei wuji kɛ tsei ashishifãi ni tsii.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with leafy stems, but the tubers underground remain tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ŋmeii lɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii lolo?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen or grows in heavy shade, it puts all its energy into growing leaves and tall stems instead of storing food down in the root tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ nitrogen babaoo nɔ loo edaa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kɛ tsei kakadaji. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shishifã lɛ mli lɛ

english: Why do my yam tubers crack open underground before I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ gbá yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani mifo amɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers usually crack when a dry period is followed by sudden heavy rain. The rapid intake of water causes the inside of the tuber to expand faster than its outer skin can stretch.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, atomo tsei lɛ tswaa kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ. Nu ni anuɔ oya lɛ haa yitso mligbɛ lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni hewolo ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã.
