english: This is blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit. It often happens when soil moisture fluctuates wildly between being very dry and very wet, stopping the roots from taking up calcium smoothly.
ga: Enɛ ji blossom end rot, ni calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ kɛbaa. Bei pii lɛ, ebaa beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa teŋ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upwards into tight shapes and stopping new growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiikpa dalɛ hee lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids, thrips, or mites sucking leaf juices, or by plant viruses transmitted by these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli

english: Why does leaving dry leaves and plant stalks on top of my soil help my crops during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mishi baai kɛ tsei ahe ŋmeii ni egbi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry plant material acts like a blanket, protecting the earth from direct heat, reducing moisture loss, and keeping the soil cool for crop roots.
ga: Mulching ni akɛ tso nibii ni egbi woɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ blanket. Buu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Ha ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i kɛha tsei shishifãi

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, strong sunlight because their leaves burn easily. They need temporary shade crops like plantains or living shade trees to protect them from the harsh sun and keep the soil moist until they grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni hiɛ ka, koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he, ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi amɛbaadara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I cut off extra branches from my cocoa trees when the trees seem to be growing well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji krokomɛi kɛjɛ mi-koko tso lɛ nɔ be mli ni etamɔ nɔ ni tso lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead, weak, or crowded branches so air and sunlight can reach all parts of the plant. This prevents damp conditions that cause diseases like black pod and helps the tree focus its energy on producing heavy pods.
ga: Niji ni egboi, ni bɛ hewalɛ, loo ni egbɔjɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei lɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la anyɛ ashɛ tso lɛ hei fɛɛ. Enɛ tsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ helai tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ diji baa lɛ naa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsii ni efeɔ lɛ he nii.

english: Why are the bottom leaves on my maize plants turning yellow and dying early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi oya lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of the stalk usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the key food plants need to stay green and grow big. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer will fix this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaatsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why do my crops yield less every year if I keep planting maize on the exact same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize takes specific nutrients out of the soil every season. If you do not rotate your crop with beans, groundnuts, or cowpeas, the soil gets depleted, whereas leguminous crops help restore natural fertility to the land.
ga: Abɛi jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmeii, ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite, yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Does it matter which direction I push my cassava cuttings into the soil when planting?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esa akɛ odu ŋmei lɛ yɛ?

english: Yes, it matters very much. You must plant the cassava stem with the growth buds pointing upward toward the sky. If you plant them upside down, the shoots will struggle to grow and your root yields will be very small.
ga: Hɛɛ, ehe miihia waa. Oduɔ o-cassava tsei lɛ ni ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji odu ŋwɛigbɛ Shoots lɛ baaná naagba yɛ amɛdalɛ mli ni shishifãi ni baa lɛ baafee bibioo.

english: Why do I need to make large soil mounds or ridges to plant my yam seeds instead of planting them on flat land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafee gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ agbo ko ni mikɛdu sweet potato dumɔwui moŋ fe ni madu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow deep underground and need soft, loose soil to expand freely. High mounds or ridges give the tubers plenty of space to grow long and thick without fighting against hard, compact dirt.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ ni ehe hiaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli edɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã amɛhe. Gɔji loo ŋmeii ni kwɔlɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara ni amɛfee shwiili ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛkɛ muji ni wa ni mli edɔ lɛ akpee.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my maize leaves and small green caterpillars hiding inside the leaf funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ kɛ ŋmeii lɛ No hewɔ lɛ minɔ lɛ yɛ bu komɛi. Akɛtee baai amli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that eats the soft, growing leaves inside the central shoot of the plant. Early spraying with appropriate bio-pesticides or approved chemicals is necessary to save the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ baai bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei ashishifãi lɛ ateŋ lɛ. Tsofai ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra. Ehe miihia ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Why are the bottom ends of my green tomatoes turning dark black and rotten before they can ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishigbɛ naagbeei lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, and it happens when the tomato plant does not get a steady supply of water. Irregular watering stops the plant from absorbing calcium from the soil, causing the bottom of the fruit to spoil.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ni ebaa kɛji akɛ tomato tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu nɔ daa. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ haaa amɛná calcium ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Ehaa aduawai lɛ ashishi shwieɔ shi.

english: Why should I cover the bare ground around my pepper plants with dry grass or cocoa husks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maha he ni nɔ ko bɛ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ? Pepper tso ni jwɛi ni egbi loo kookoo ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli

english: Covering the ground, known as mulching, keeps the soil cool during dry hot days, stops water from evaporating too quickly, and blocks weeds from growing and stealing nutrients from your crops.
ga: Ale mulching hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ amli. Tsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya tsɔ. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ.

english: How do I choose the best plantain suckers to plant on my farm for a good harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantain tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ ni madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni maná ŋmaa kpakpa?

english: Look for sword suckers, which have spear-shaped leaves and a thick base. Avoid water suckers with broad leaves early on, because sword suckers grow into stronger plants that produce much larger, healthier bunches.
ga: Taomɔ klante ŋmeii, ni yɔɔ baai ni tamɔ lance kɛ shishi ni mli tse. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsei ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ ahe mra. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, klante ŋmeii lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ tsei ni he wa ni woɔ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Pale yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to make food and grow strong. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer early in the plant's life restores their green color and boosts growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni tsei he hiaa koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛdara waa Ni akɛ ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmei, loo nitrogen ŋmei fataa he yɛ tso lɛ wala shishijee mli. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha dalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Dry grass acts as mulch, which keeps the soil cool under the hot sun, traps moisture so you water less, and stops weeds from growing and stealing nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ mulch. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ woɔ mli bɔni afee ni okɛ nu akawo mli fioo ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛkaju niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: How do weeds actually harm my crops if they are just growing next to them without touching them?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui? Kɛji amɛdara yɛ amɛhe ni amɛtaaa he?

english: Weeds act like food thieves underground and above ground; their roots steal water and nutrients from the soil, while their leaves block sunlight from reaching your crop.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ amɛjuɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ fɛɛ. Amɛshishifãi lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ onibii ahe.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they get stressed by extreme heat or dry soil. Giving the plants consistent water and shade during peak heat helps them retain flowers and form fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi hao amɛ. Nu kɛ hulutsoo ni akɛhaa tsei yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛkwɛɔ fɔfɔi anɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: When too many small shoots (suckers) grow together, they fight the main plant for food and water, resulting in tiny bunches. Leaving only one or two strong suckers ensures big, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii bibii (ŋmeii) babaoo tsɔ ekomefeemɔ Ebaatswa niyenii kɛ nu ni jɛ tso titri lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmeii bibii ni jeɔ kpo. Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha plantain lɛ afee agbo ni etsii.

english: Yam leaves need to spread out in full sunlight to make energy for growing big tubers underground. Staking holds the leaves up off the ground where they get maximum light and stay free from leaf rot.
ga: Ehe miihia ni agbɛ sweet potato baai lɛ ashwã koni enine ashɛ hulu la ni fa nɔ fɛɛ nɔ nɔ koni ekɛfee hewalɛ kɛha bulbs wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ shɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ he ni amɛnáa la babaoo yɛ lɛ, ni baa lɛ fiteee.

english: Why do people say planting beans together with maize helps the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa du ŋmãa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Beans are special plants that pull nitrogen gas from the air and feed it into the soil through their roots, acting as a natural fertilizer for neighbor crops like maize.
ga: Beans ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and have wide leaves that provide living shade and moisture to protect the cocoa trees during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni buɔ kookoo tso lɛ he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground if rain falls too much right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji nugbɔ nɛ tsɔ dani akpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When rain floods the ground for long periods, the roots suffocate and harmful soil fungi quickly break them down into soft rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fiteɔ amɛ oya.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my corn leaves and caterpillars inside the central leaf funnel?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ amli kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli lɛ

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a common pest that eats young corn leaves from the inside out. Checking your farm early allows you to spray mild natural remedies or pesticides before they destroy the growing point.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmei, ni ji ŋmei ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ lɛ. Okwaafoi lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Enɛ haa okɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ shwieɔ nɔ dani amɛfiteɔ he ni ŋmɔ lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why are my young cocoa pods turning black and falling off the tree before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Young cocoa pods drop or turn black due to fungal diseases like Black Pod or natural wilting when the tree lacks water and nutrients. Removing damaged pods early keeps the disease from destroying the rest of your harvest.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ baagbee shi loo amɛbaatsɔ ediŋŋ yɛ ŋmeii ahe helai, tamɔ ŋmeii diji, loo adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai ahewɔ. Pods ni efite lɛ ni ajieɔ mra Ebaatsi hela naa koni ekafite onibii ni eshwɛ lɛ.

english: If one of my cocoa trees catches a disease, can it spread to the surrounding healthy trees?
ga: Kɛji hela mɔ kookoo tsei lɛ eko lɛ Ani ebaanyɛ egbɛ eshwa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ anɔ?

english: Yes, cocoa diseases spread easily to neighboring trees through rain splashes, insects, or dirty pruning tools. You must treat or remove infected plant parts immediately to protect the rest of your farm.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, cocoa hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ anɔ oya kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔi, kooloi bibii, loo nibii ni akɛfoɔ tsei ni he tseee lɛ anɔ. Esa akɛ otsa loo ojie tso lɛ fãi ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni obu oŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: How can I know if the spray I used for cocoa pests is actually working?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ tsofa ni akɛgbeɔ kookoo helai lɛ tsuɔ nii diɛŋtsɛ?

english: You can tell the treatment is working when new leaves grow clean without insect holes, green pods develop without dark spots, and existing damage stops spreading to nearby branches.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona akɛ tsofa lɛ miitsu nii kɛ́ baai heei lɛ ahe tse ni kooloi bibii bɛ mli. Pods green lɛ daa ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ bɛ mli. ni nibii ni efite momo lɛ kpaɔ gbɛfaŋnɔ kɛmiiya nitsumɔhe niji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to walk through and inspect my cocoa farm every week instead of waiting until harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsɔ mli ni makwɛ kookoo ŋmɔ ko mli daa otsi lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ?

english: Walking through your farm regularly helps you spot pests, diseases, and fallen pods early before they spread to whole trees. Early discovery saves you money on treatments and protects your total yield.
ga: Nyiɛmɔ ni ofeɔ daa yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua bo ni ona kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, helai kɛ ŋmeii ni egbee shi lɛ mra. dani egbɛ eshwa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ mli mra mli nibii ni ana lɛ Ehaa okɛ shika toɔ osɛɛkuu fɛɛ ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ ehebuu he.

english: What will happen to my cocoa trees if I let tall weeds grow around their bases?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji miŋmɛ gbɛ ni jwɛi kakadaji kwɛ̃ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ he?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your cocoa trees. They also act as hiding places for pests like rodents and hold excess dampness that causes fungal diseases.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha o-cacao tsei lɛ mli lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii hu akɛ shĩa kɛha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmeii ni ehiɛɔ nu ni fa fe nine ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce hundreds of small flowers, but only a few turn into real pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi bibii ohai abɔ, shi amɛteŋ fioo pɛ tsɔɔ fɔfɔi bibii diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny beneficial insects to pollinate them. The tree also naturally drops unpollinated or excess flowers so it can focus its energy on growing a manageable number of healthy, full-sized pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii biɔ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛha pollination. Tso lɛ hu woɔ fɔfɔi ni shwieee loo ni fa fe nine yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Bɔni afee ni enyɛ ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni fa babaoo ni anyɛɔ akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ ayibɔ ni anyɛɔ akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoa trees turn yellow and wilt during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves during dry periods mean the tree is losing water faster than its roots can pull from the dry ground. Providing shade trees and mulching soil with dry leaves helps trap moisture in the soil.
ga: Kɛ́ tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ nu lɛ miiho oya fe bɔ ni eshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo be ha ni akɛ baai ni egbi shwie nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why should I cut off extra branches from my cocoa trees if they look green and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji krokomɛi kɛjɛ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ kɛji akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ ni eyɛ hewalɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the canopy to let sunlight and fresh air flow around the trunk. Good airflow dries out excess dampness, which prevents mold and encourages the trunk to produce more flowers and pods.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ, egbeleɔ tso lɛ mli koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa abɔle tso lɛ he. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ mli egbiɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baa ni ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Why is it harmful to leave ripe cocoa pods hanging on the tree for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaashi kookoo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Ripe pods left on the tree attract pests, rot quickly, and cause seeds inside to germinate. Rotting pods also spread fungal diseases to young green pods nearby.
ga: Pods ni ekwɛ̃ ni ashiɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ gbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, egboɔ oya ni ehaa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ. Pods ni egboi lɛ hu gbɛɔ fungal helai eshwaa pods bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: How does protecting and feeding my cocoa trees regularly affect my harvest income over time?
ga: Te mi-cacao tsei lɛ ahe ni mibuɔ ni mihaa amɛ niyenii daa lɛ saa mi-kpamɔ shika lɛ he yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Cocoa trees respond directly to consistent care; trees kept free of disease and weeds produce larger, higher-quality pods consistently for up to thirty years, securing long-term farm income.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ tsuɔ nii tɛ̃ɛ kɛji akɛ akwɛ amɛ daa. Tsei ni helai kɛ jwɛi bɛ mli lɛ baaya nɔ awo ŋmeii wuji ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi afii nyɔŋmai etɛ. Koni ŋmɔ lɛ mli shika ni anáa lɛ ahi shi yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with wide leaves that provide vital shade and keep the soil moist during the cocoa tree's early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ cacao tso lɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava too close to my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛɔ ŋmãa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Both cassava and maize consume high amounts of nutrients and sunlight. Planting them too close together forces them to compete, resulting in smaller maize ears and thinner cassava roots.
ga: Kasava kɛ ŋmãa fɛɛ yeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ hulu la babaoo. Kɛ́ adu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha akaŋshii aba. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmãa toi lɛ feɔ bibii ni ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ hu feɔ mlɛo.

english: Why do my groundnuts make the soil better for the maize I plant next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanuts lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This leaves behind natural fertility for your next crop.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha adebɔɔ mli nibii babaoo ahi shi kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually signal a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which plants need for strong growth. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant my yams on high soil mounds instead of flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu sweet potatoes yɛ gɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Mounds loosen the soil so yam tubers can expand easily without pushing against hard dirt. Mounds also improve drainage, stopping heavy rains from pooling and rotting the tubers.
ga: Gɔŋ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo ni amɛtsiii shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ. Gɔji hu haa nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Ekpaa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ koni ekabua ŋmeii lɛ anaa ni efite.

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism plants use to shrink their surface area and save water during intense heat. If the leaves relax when temperatures cool in the evening, the plant is fine.
ga: Leaf curling ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ shi ni amɛkɛbu nu he yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ shwie shi beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ Tso lɛ hi.

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when stressed by extreme heat, dry soil, or sudden dry winds. Regular watering and partial wind protection help the flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi trukaa lɛ hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa fɔfɔi lɛ daa kɛ hebuu ko kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why is it risky to sow my seeds right after the very first light rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni adu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ fioo ko nɛ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, be lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ ji nɔ ni yɔɔ oshara.

english: The first light rain often tricks seeds into sprouting, but it is frequently followed by a dry spell. Without regular rainfall, tiny seedlings quickly dry out and die before the real rainy season settles in.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ lakaa dumɔwui lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃. Shi bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo be nyiɛɔ enɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ daa lɛ, dumɔwui bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya ni amɛgboiɔ dani nugbɔ be diɛŋtsɛ lɛ baashɛ.

english: This rot is caused by a fungal infection that thrives in wet, overly shaded conditions. Pruning overhead branches to let in sunlight and removing infected pods promptly stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni efɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ fe nine lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ afo tsei niji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ koni hulu la babaoo aba mli, ni ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: As cassava roots reach full maturity, they swell up and create visible cracks in the soil around the base of the stem. Additionally, the bottom leaves of the plant will naturally turn yellow and fall off.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eda kwraa Ebaafu ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni anaa aba shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli. Kɛfata he lɛ, tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛbaagbee shi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for leafy growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer early in the crop's life gives it the food it needs to stay green and build strong stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ wo tso lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaha ená niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ eŋɔli lɛ nɔ ni etswa shishifãi ni wa.

english: What will happen to my crops if I put the white fertilizer powder directly against the plant stem?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛ powda yɛŋ fee lɛ wo tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer directly against the stem can burn the plant's skin and damage its roots. It is best to place the fertilizer in a circle or small hole a few inches away from the stem so the roots can drink it safely without getting damaged.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ hewolo ni efite shishifãi lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he yɛ kooyigbɛ bibii loo buji amli. Inchi fioo komɛi kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi. Bɔni afee ni anu shishifãi lɛ shweshweeshwe ni nɔ ko nɔ ko akafite.

english: Why does my fertilizer turn into a wet liquid when I leave the bag open in the shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-fertilizer lɛ tsɔɔ nu ni mli ewo fɔ kɛ́ mishi kotoku lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Many chemical fertilizers, especially white nitrogen fertilizers like Urea, absorb moisture from humid air very quickly. You should always keep your fertilizer bags tightly tied until the exact moment you are ready to put it into a pail and work on your field.
ga: Tsofai srɔtoi babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii, titri lɛ, tamɔ urea, baanyɛ ajie ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ mli lɛ oya waa. Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akpɛtɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kotokui lɛ ahe jogbaŋŋ be fɛɛ be kɛyashi be mli ni obaafee klalo akɛ okɛbaawo ŋmɔshi nibii amli ni otsu nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my cassava plants dropping off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava naturally drops its lower leaves during dry periods to save water and protect itself from drying out. Once the rains return, the plant will naturally grow fresh, green leaves again.
ga: Yucca shwieɔ eshishi baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baaná baai eŋɔli ni kpɛɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Pepper plants often drop their flowers when they experience stress from high heat, heavy rainfall, or sudden dry spells. Keeping the soil evenly moist and well-drained helps the plant keep its flowers and turn them into peppers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi trukaa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do small cocoa pods on my trees turn brown and dry up before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbi dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: This is often caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly during rainy conditions. Pruning excess branches to let sunlight reach the trunk helps keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ be mli. Kɛ́ afo tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ amli koni hulu la ashɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and tall with small cobs when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ amli tsei ni amɛkwɔ ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Be ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close to each other, the crops compete for sunlight, ground moisture, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper spacing ensures every crop gets enough light and food to produce large cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la. sũ mli ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛhaa tso fɛɛ tso teŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔi wuji.

english: Why does my yam crop need a tall wooden stake to climb while it grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ko ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ beni edaa lɛ?

english: Yam is a climbing vine that needs tall stakes to lift its leaves into full sunlight. Catching sunlight allows the leaves to make energy, which feeds the plant and helps it produce large tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ ni akɛ tso kakadaŋŋ awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Hulu la ni tsoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ niyenii ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do plantains need to be planted next to young cocoa seedlings on a new farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni adu dumɔwui yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ? Kakao tsei bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ hee mli?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and produce broad leaves that shade the young cocoa plants like an umbrella during their first few years in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tamɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why does growing cowpea on my land make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpea is a legume crop that pulls natural nitrogen from the air and traps it in the soil through its roots. When the cowpea harvest is finished, that extra nitrogen stays in the ground to nourish the next crop you plant.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni jɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmli amɛjieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ agbe tsina ŋmãa lɛ naa Nakai nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ niyenii.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. They need shade trees or plantains nearby to act as living umbrellas, keeping the air cool and the soil moist while the young roots grow.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei loo tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ ni amɛha amɛfee hulutsoo koni amɛtsu nii akɛ hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ajɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni shishifãi bibii lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Yam plants need lots of sunlight on their leaves to make food for the tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground toward the sun, preventing leaf rot and helping the yam tubers grow much bigger.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Staking baaye abua ni ewó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛya hulu la lɛ mli. Ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why should I remove extra small shoots growing around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ Main plantain tso lɛ he lɛ ajie

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, steal water and plant food from the main mother tree. Leaving only one or two healthy shoots ensures the main tree gets enough energy to produce a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei loo tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ nu ni amɛduɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ mli tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo tso lɛ mli tsei babaoo ni tsii.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow instead of healthy dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is an important plant food in the soil. It can also happen when too much water stays around the roots, preventing them from taking up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-abele lɛ, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nu babaoo bua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ náa niyenii kpakpai.

english: Why does putting too much chemical fertilizer at once kill my crops instead of making them grow faster?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ babaoo shikome lɛ gbeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ moŋ fe ni eeeha amɛkwɛ̃ oya lɛ?

english: Fertilizer contains concentrated salts. Applying too much at once burns the roots and sucks water out of the plant, causing it to dry up and die instead of feeding it gently.
ga: Fertilizer lɛ yɛ ŋoo babaoo. Kɛ́ akɛtsu nii babaoo yɛ be kome mli lɛ, ebaashã shishifãi lɛ ni ebaaŋɔ nu kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli. Ha egbi ni egbo moŋ fe ni oooha lɛ niyenii blɛoo.

english: Planting the same crop every year drains the exact same nutrients from the soil over and over. It also allows specific pests and diseases that love pepper plants to build up in the ground and attack future crops.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shii abɔ. Ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai pɔtɛɛi ni tamɔ pepper tsei lɛ hu buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛtutuaa wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: The first rain is often a short rain followed by many hot, dry days. If seeds sprout during that brief rain, the hot ground dry spell afterwards will bake and kill the young tender roots before they reach deeper water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ ji nugbɔ kuku. Gbii babaoo ni mli edɔ ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ nyiɛ enɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo mli Nugbɔshiimɔ be ni mli edɔ waa yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ baashã ni egbe shishifãi bibii dani amɛyashɛ nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli.

english: Covering the soil, called mulching, acts like a blanket. It traps moisture in the ground during hot afternoons so you water less, prevents weeds from growing, and keeps the soil cool.
ga: Mulching, ni atsɛɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. koni okɛ nu akawo mli fioo Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i

english: What causes small holes in the leaves of my green corn, and why does the damage spread so fast?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa baa ni eŋɔli lɛ nɔ Ni mɛni hewɔ nɔ ni efite lɛ gbɛ eshwa oya nɛkɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They lay many eggs inside the leaf whorls, and when they hatch, hundreds of tiny caterpillars eat the leaves rapidly day and night.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛwoɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ baai lɛ amli. Ni kɛ́ amɛfɔ lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ohai abɔ yeɔ baai lɛ oya shwane kɛ gbɛkɛ.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are fully matured and ready to be dug up from the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be mli ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ edara kwraa ni esa akɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the bottom leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem starts to crack as the thick tubers expand beneath the surface.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa beni tso lɛ mli ŋmeii ni mli tse lɛ mli lɛɛɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: How do I know the best time to plant my maize to ensure a great harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa koni maná ŋmãa kpakpa?

english: Maize needs steady moisture right after planting. In Ghana, planting immediately after the first major, consistent rains of the season ensures the seeds get enough moisture to sprout and grow strong root systems.
ga: Abɛi biɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli be fɛɛ be kɛji adu lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Yɛ Ghana lɛ, aduɔ nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni nɛɔ daa lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ ana nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛgbala amɛshishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves of my young corn plants turning light yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your soil is low in nitrogen, which corn needs to grow foliage. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer early in the growing season helps restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ŋmãa he hiaa koni baai lɛ adara lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, loo nitrogen ŋmãa fata he yɛ ŋmãa be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmãa lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ ni efee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are some of my corn cobs missing seeds or not fully filled at harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ ekomɛi bɛ ŋmeii loo amɛyimɔ obɔbɔ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Incomplete cobs usually happen when corn plants suffer from water stress or high heat during the flowering stage, preventing proper pollination. Ensuring plants get enough water when the silks appear helps fill the entire cob.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni eshɛɛɛ he lɛ baa kɛji akɛ ŋmeii tsei lɛ naa nu he haomɔ loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Enɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa lɛ naa. Kɛ́ akwɛ koni tsei lɛ aná nu jogbaŋŋ beni siliki lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu awo ŋmei lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I protect my crops if people are warning that a severe dry period or famine is coming this year?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe? Kɛji mɔ ko bɔ kɔkɔ akɛ afi nɛɛ hɔmɔ loo hɔmɔ ni naa wa baaba?

english: You can protect your yield by planting drought-tolerant crop varieties, covering the soil with dry leaves or mulch to trap moisture, and growing early-maturing crops that harvest before the rains end.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu onibii ahe kɛtsɔ tsei srɔtoi ni nyɛɔ hɔmɔ naa lɛ ni ooodu lɛ nɔ. Okɛ baai ni egbi loo ŋmɔshi nibii aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛmɔ ŋmɔtɔ. ni amɛdu ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni akpaa dani nugbɔ lɛ baa naagbee.

english: Why do my crops fail in some years even when the rain seems to fall regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ehiii afii komɛi amli eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ daa moŋ?

english: Crops need water at critical growth stages, such as when they are flowering or forming fruit. Even if it rains early on, a short dry spell during flowering can prevent fruits or grains from forming properly.
ga: Nu he hiaa tsei yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa, tamɔ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi loo amɛwoɔ aduawai. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ mra moŋ Shi be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ fɔfɔii akwɛmɔ be mli lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ aduawai loo dumɔwui anaa koni amɛkafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my farmland is losing its strength and won't support good crop yields anymore?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni ebaaye ebuaaa ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai dɔŋŋ?

english: Signs of weak soil include stunted plant growth, pale leaves, and smaller harvest yields each year despite good rainfall. Rotating your crops or adding organic matter helps rebuild the soil's natural strength.
ga: Nɔ ni fata okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ lɛ ahe ji tsei ni edaaa jogbaŋŋ, baai ni tsuɔ, kɛ ŋmaa bibioo ni akpaaa daa afi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni aaatsake loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant maize on all my farm fields every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific soil nutrients and allows pests to build up in the soil. Mixing or alternating maize with legumes like cowpeas restores nutrients and protects you if one crop faces disease.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa futu mli loo okɛtsake lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba, ni ebaabu ohe kɛji hela ba ŋmãa kome nɔ.

english: How do I decide which secondary crops to grow alongside my main grain crop to support national food needs?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpɛ miyiŋ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji enyɔ ni esa akɛ madu yɛ mi ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ahe koni mikɛye mabua maŋ niyenii he hiamɔ nii?

english: Focus on stable, high-demand food crops like cassava, yam, or vegetables. Staples stored easily help secure local food supplies, while fast-growing vegetables provide income while you wait for your main grain harvest.
ga: Kɛ ojwɛŋmɔ ama niyenii ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ, ni ataoɔ waa tamɔ ŋmei, ŋmei loo aduawai anɔ. Niyenii ni akɛtoɔ mlɛo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni akɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, aduawai ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ haa anáa shika yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni akpa ŋmaa titri lɛ.

english: What causes my seeds to rot in the ground before they can sprout into healthy plants?
ga: Mɛni haa midumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ amɛfeɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ?

english: Seeds rot when planted too deep in heavy, waterlogged soil where oxygen cannot reach them. Planting seeds at the recommended depth in well-drained soil allows them to breathe and sprout safely.
ga: Dumɔwui fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli tsɔ he ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashɛ he ni atsɔɔ akɛ eshɛ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ amu ni amɛkwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my planted crop right after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ kɛji nugbɔ enɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to quickly absorb available water and soil nutrients before cultivated crops can. Clearing weeds within the first few weeks gives your crop a head start to grow taller and shade out competition.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya dani tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Kɛji ojie jwɛi lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ, oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baabɔi shweremɔ ni ebaaha akaŋshii aba shi.

english: Why should I buy certified seeds from an agro-dealer instead of just planting seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ okwaayeli mli jarayelɔ dɛŋ lɛ? Mohu ɔ, i du duwuhi nɛ a yi wami kɛ je ye nyagbe kpami ɔ mi ɔ pɛ.

english: Certified seeds are carefully bred and treated to resist local pests, germinate evenly, and give high yields, whereas saved seeds from previous harvests often lose their vigor and produce smaller harvests over time.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni atsuɔ he nii koni akafite tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. kwɛ̃ɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ kpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ fɔɔ hewalɛ ni baa shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why are the seeds I bought from the store coated in a bright pink or green powder?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ powda ni mli tse loo ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse ewo dumɔwui ni mihe yɛ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: That colored coating is a protective chemical treatment (fungicide or insecticide) that keeps soil bugs and fungi from eating or rotting the seed before it can sprout.
ga: Akɛ tsofai ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ tsuɔ penti ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ he nii. Eji tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii (ŋmei loo ŋmeii ni gbeɔ ŋmeii) ni tsiɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye loo amɛkafite dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Can I cut a large seed yam into smaller pieces before planting, or will that ruin the crop?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mafolɔ sweet potato agbo mli bibii bibii. Ani abaanyɛ afee dani adu? loo ebaafite ŋmɔshi nibii

english: Yes, you can cut clean tubers into smaller pieces (called minisetts), provided each piece has enough skin with a healthy node or 'eye' so it can sprout into a full new plant.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ ofo yitso ni he tse lɛ mli bibii bibii (ni atsɛɔ amɛ minisets), kɛji akɛ fã fɛɛ fã yɛ hewolo ni fa kɛ fãji loo ‘hiŋmɛii’ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bɔni afee ni enyɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni etsɔ tso hee.

english: Why do my crops grow tall, thin, and weak when I drop multiple seeds into a single hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ kɛlɛ, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛhe waaa beni miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together in one hole, the seedlings compete with each other for space, sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, leaving all of them malnourished and weak.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ he ko, hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ nu he akaŋshii mli, ni no haa dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ yeɔ niyenii ni esaaa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ.

english: How deep into the ground should I bury tiny seeds like pepper or tomato?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafu dumɔwui bibii tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo tomato yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Small seeds should only be covered lightly with a thin layer of fine soil—roughly twice their thickness—so the tiny sprout does not run out of energy before reaching the surface light.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni mli tseee aha dumɔwui bibii lɛ anɔ fioo. ni ji aaafee shii 2 bɔni afee ni tso bibioo lɛ hewalɛ Ekafo dani eshɛ la ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ he.

english: Seeds usually fail to sprout if the soil is too dry, if heavy rain formed a hard crust over the soil, or if underground pests like ants and cutworms destroyed the seeds before they emerged.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui kwɛɛɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni wa baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ kpata dumɔwui lɛ ahiɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Leaf curling is often the plant's natural reaction to extreme heat and lack of water to prevent moisture loss, but yellowing can also be a sign of sap-sucking insects like whiteflies or nutrient deficiencies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji bɔ ni tso lɛ feɔ enii ehaa yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni faaa lɛ mli koni ekɛtsi ŋmɔtɔ ni baa shi lɛ naa. Shi ŋmɔŋ baanyɛ afee kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo niyenii ni esaaa ni ayeɔ lɛ he okadi.

english: Why are the flowers dropping off my pepper plants without forming any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience severe stress, such as sudden hot spells, unpredictable rainfall, or a shortage of essential nutrients like phosphorus.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ ni naa wa, tamɔ ahum ni mli edɔ trukaa lɛ he. nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba loo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ

english: Why is it bad practice for me to plant maize on the exact same plot of land season after season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji nifeemɔ gbonyo akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year and allows pests and soil diseases that feed on that specific crop to build up in large numbers.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ buaa amɛhe naa babaoo.

english: How can I tell if my soil is rich enough to feed my crops without buying expensive testing tools?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi obɔ kɛ nibii ni baakwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ ni miheee kaa nibii ni jara wa?

english: Rich, healthy soil is usually dark in color, breaks apart easily in your hands, retains moisture well after rain, and contains earthworms and decayed plant leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ nii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ su ji ediŋŋ. Efoɔ yɛ nine mli oya Ehiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsei ahe baai ni fiteɔ yɛ jɛmɛ

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantains grow very quickly and produce large leaves that provide shade, acting like protective umbrellas that keep the young cocoa cool and the soil moist during hot weather.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa ni ewoɔ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni haa kookoo bibioo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hu feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil is running out of nitrogen, an essential food for plant growth. When nitrogen is low, the plant moves nutrients from older bottom leaves to feed new top leaves, causing the lower ones to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛji nitrogen faaa Tsei lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi baa heei lɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small and thin even after sitting in the ground for a whole year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe ejɔ waa yɛ be mli ni mita shikpɔŋ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need loose, soft soil to swell up properly. If the ground is packed hard or low in nutrients, the roots cannot expand, and the plant uses its energy just to stay alive rather than growing fat tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni amɛfuu jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi obɔ kɛ nibii babaoo, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa loo ewa Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã. Ni tsei kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛhi wala mli kɛkɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ fɔ.

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same plot drains the exact same nutrients from the soil continuously and gives crop-specific pests a permanent home. Rotating maize with crops like groundnuts or cowpeas restores nutrients naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, ajieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsei ahe kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ náa shia ni baahi shi daa. Abele ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei tsakeɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli niyenii mli hewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do people tell me to spread dry grass around the base of my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ mi akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ashwã he lɛ? Mi pepper tso lɛ shishitoo?

english: Spreading dry grass or leaves around plants is called mulching. It acts like a blanket over the soil, trapping water so it doesn't evaporate quickly in the sun and keeping soil cool so roots grow strong.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa Tsei ahe lɛ akɛ mulching. Efeɔ enii tamɔ kuntu ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehiɛɔ nu mli bɔni afee ni kɛ́ hulu la shɛ enɔ lɛ, ekatsɔ oya. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i koni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they feel stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients. Consistent watering and keeping the root area cool helps the plant hold onto flowers so they turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa ni ahaa shishifã lɛ he jɔɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ fɔfɔi ahe ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: How do weeds actually steal food from my crop if I put fertilizer right next to my plants?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ aju niyenii kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli? Ni kɛji akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mitsei lɛ ahe hu?

english: Weed roots spread very fast underground and drink up water and liquid fertilizer before your crop roots can reach them. Even if applied closely, nearby weeds steal those nutrients from under the soil.
ga: Jwɛi shishifãi gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛnuɔ nu kɛ nu ni ji ŋmɔshi nibii dani tsei shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe. Eyɛ mli akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ moŋ Shi jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ juɔ nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up toward the sun to make energy for growing tubers. Staking keeps leaves off the wet ground, preventing leaf diseases and helping the plant produce larger yams underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã kɛya ŋwɛi kɛya hulu lɛ he koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha bulb lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ tsei ahe helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: The first rain is often followed by a long hot dry spell before regular rains truly start. If seeds sprout during that dry gap, the young seedlings will wither and die from lack of continuous soil moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli edɔ waa nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ jeɔ shishi. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ ateŋ Tsei bibii lɛ gboɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nu ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ hewɔ.

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes the plants to grow tall, thin, and weak, producing tiny fruits or small maize cobs instead of a healthy harvest.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ daa, egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ, ni ewoɔ yibii bibii. loo ŋmãa bibii Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooona nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ

english: How can I start using my small backyard space in Ghana to grow food for my family throughout the year?
ga: Mije shishi mikɛ sɛɛgbɛ he bibioo lɛ miitsu nii. Te ooofee tɛŋŋ odu niyenii oha oweku lɛ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ yɛ Ghana?

english: Backyard farming works best when you mix quick-harvest vegetables like garden eggs, peppers, and leafy greens with longer-term crops like plantains, ensuring a steady food supply and saving money on daily market expenses.
ga: Shia sɛɛ okwaayeli tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ okɛ aduawai ni akpaa oya tamɔ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii, ŋmeii, kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai futu mli. kɛ tsei ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ tamɔ plantains koni niyenii ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛ shika ato daa gbi jarayeli he nyɔmɔwoo he.

english: How will I know the right time to start planting my crops when the rainy season begins in Ghana?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ aje tsei afeemɔ shishi beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: It is best to plant after the rains become steady—usually after two or three heavy rains that thoroughly soak the soil—rather than planting right after the first light shower, which can quickly dry up and ruin your seeds.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ sɛɛ—bei pii lɛ, yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa enyɔ loo etɛ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nuɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbi oya ni amɛfite.

english: Why shouldn't I burn all the cleared weeds and brush on my farm before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishãa jwɛi ni ajie lɛ ni mikɛ brɔshi shwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ dani miduɔ nii lɛ?

english: Burning destroys valuable natural nutrients and helpful organisms in the ground; letting cleared leaves and grass decay directly on your farm enriches the soil and keeps it moist for your crops.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni he hiaa kɛ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ oŋmɛ gbɛ ni baai kɛ jwɛi ni ajie lɛ fite yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛo ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ahi oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow while the crops are still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni tso lɛ miida lolo lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen, an essential nutrient, or that heavy rains have washed the goodness out of the topsoil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ kpakpa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers stay small and thin even though the stems and leaves look very big and healthy above ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ, shi.

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen or plants are spaced too close together, cassava puts all its energy into growing tall leafy branches instead of developing thick food storage roots below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo tsei bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Kasava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ eniji ni kɛlɛ lɛ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, a peeɔ sisi nɛ mi wa nɛ a kɛ toɔ niye ní ngɛ a sisi.

english: Why is it important to train my yam vines to climb up wooden stakes as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsɔse mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛkwɔ tsei anɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for the plant; lifting the vines off the ground on stakes allows leaves to catch maximum sun, resulting in larger yam tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni efee niyenii eha tso lɛ. Wein tsei lɛ ni awóɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni aaanyɛ. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees grow better when I plant plantain trees right next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under strong sunlight; fast-growing plantains act like living umbrellas, providing essential shade and keeping the air humid until the cocoa grows strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ha hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni oha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli afee fɛ̃i kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: How does covering the ground around my crop stems with dry leaves help them during hot, dry weather?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mitso lɛ he lɛ ni mikɛ baai ni egbi haa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry leaves, called mulching, keeps the ground cool, traps moisture in the soil so you water less often, and stops weeds from taking over your crop area.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ baai ni egbi haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i Ehiɛɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli bɔni afee ni okɛ nu akawo mli fioo. ni otsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye oŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What causes my tomato plants to suddenly dry up and die even when I water them every day?
ga: Mɛni haa mitato tsei lɛ gĩɔ trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa gbi moŋ?

english: This sudden drying is usually caused by bacterial wilt or root rot, soil diseases that block the tiny water pipes inside the stem so water cannot travel from roots to leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni baa trukaa nɛɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ nɔ hela ko ni tsiɔ nu paipii bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ anaa, ni no haa nu nyɛɛɛ ajɛ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛya baai lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upward and looking wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee tamɔ nɔ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is caused by tiny, invisible insects like aphids or mites feeding on the sap underneath the leaves, which causes the plant to distort and stunt its growth.
ga: Koolooi bibii kɛ baai lɛ akumɔ baa. ni anyɛɛɛ ana, tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ Enɛ haa tso lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaaa eda.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is missing nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green and healthy. Heavy rains can also wash this nutrient deep into the soil where young roots cannot reach it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa lɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hu baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi bibii nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains all the specific nutrients maize needs from the soil and allows maize-eating pests to build up in the ground. Rotating with crops like groundnuts or cowpeas helps refill the soil with nutrients naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa abɛi lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ baa ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the big trees away from the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mijie tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot survive harsh, direct sunlight because their tender leaves burn easily. Shade trees or fast-growing plantains act as natural umbrellas to keep the young cocoa plants cool and moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kookoo tso lɛ baai bibii lɛ shãa oya. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo koni eha cacao tsei bibii lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do I need to clear the grass and put long wooden stakes next to my yam vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi lɛ ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama sweet potato wain tso lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that need to reach high to catch full sunlight. Climbing up stakes allows their leaves to gather enough energy from the sun to grow big, heavy yam tubers under the ground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni ehe hiaa ni amɛte shi amɛwo ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Tso lɛ nɔ kwɔɔ haa ebaai lɛ buaa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa naa kɛjɛɔ hulu lɛ mli koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when heavy rain and strong winds come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots and very heavy tops full of water and fruit. Placing strong wooden Y-shaped sticks under the heavy fruit bunches helps hold the tree upright against strong winds.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni tsii waa, ni nu kɛ aduawai eyi mli obɔ. Okɛ tso ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni tamɔ Y awo aduawai ni tsii ni abua naa lɛ shishi. Ebaaye ebua ni eha tso lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he.

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long without draining away, usually during heavy rains. Planting your cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows extra water to drain so the roots can breathe.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu tsɔ amɛhe. Be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli Bei pii lɛ, yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa mli lɛ, ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu babaoo hoɔ koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ amu.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up during the hot afternoon sun even if I watered them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ amɛmli moŋ?

english: In intense heat, tomato leaves lose water into the air faster than their roots can suck it up from the dry ground. Curling their leaves is the plant's natural way of shrinking its surface to save water until the evening cool.
ga: yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli lɛ Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ ehe shwieɔ shi koni ekɛto nu he kɛyashi edɔ.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant gets too stressed from extreme heat, lack of water, or lack of pollination. When a plant feels threatened by dry soil, it drops its flowers to save energy to stay alive.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ hao tsɔ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo pollination ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ tsei nu he akɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ miiwo amɛhe gbeyei Ebaashwie fɔfɔi koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato koni amɛhi wala mli.

english: Why do green worms keep chewing big holes in my cabbage leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ yeɔ buji wuji lɛ? be fɛɛ be yɛ mi-cabbage baai lɛ anɔ

english: These worms are caterpillars that hatch from eggs laid on the leaves by visiting butterflies or moths. They eat the tender cabbage leaves rapidly so they can grow big, which weakens the plant before it forms a good head.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji ŋmeii ni jɛɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni baasara amɛ lɛ amli kɛbaa ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ baai anɔ lɛ amli. Amɛyeɔ kaabeji baai bibii oya koni amɛdara. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ dani ená bulbs kpakpai.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster than the crops I actually planted after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ diɛŋtsɛ beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that are naturally adapted to local soil and weather. They quickly steal water, sunlight, and plant food from the soil before your farm crops have a chance to settle and grow.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli. Amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni amɛduɔ oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ naa hegbɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛdaraa.

english: Yellow and curling leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nutrients like nitrogen or is being attacked by tiny sap-sucking pests like aphids. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or spraying neem leaf extract helps the plants regain their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔleɔ ehe lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli, loo kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ, tamɔ aphids lɛ etutua lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he loo okɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua otsei lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee ŋmɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do fall armyworms attack my crop, and how can I spot them early?
ga: Te fall armyworms lɛ tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mana amɛ mra?

english: Fall armyworms hide inside the center leaves of young maize plants, chewing holes and leaving small brown droppings behind. Checking the central growing tip of your maize plants every few days allows you to spot and remove them before they destroy the whole farm.
ga: Fall cutworms lɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli. Ekɛ buji shwieɔ shi ni eshiɔ ŋmeii bibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ. behind Kɛ́ okwɛ o-corn tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋwɛi ŋta ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ mli daa gbii fioo lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ onaa amɛ ni ojieɔ amɛ dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my young tomato seedlings keep dying right after sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato dumɔwui bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboiɔ beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: This usually happens because of a fungus in overly wet soil, commonly called damping-off disease. You can prevent this by raising your nursery beds, ensuring proper drainage, and avoiding overwatering young plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli ejaakɛ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Aloo nɔ ni afɔɔ lɛ tsɛmɔ akɛ Damping Off Hela. Obaanyɛ otsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ saatsoi ni yɔɔ gbekɛbii akwɛmɔhe lɛ ni ooowo nɔ lɛ nɔ. Ha nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Ni tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsei bibii ni oooha amɛ babaoo lɛ he.

english: How far apart should I space my cassava cuttings when planting them?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu lɛ, gbɛ enyiɛ esa akɛ ahi ŋmei niji lɛ ateŋ?

english: You should space cassava cuttings about one meter apart in every direction. Giving them enough space allows their roots to spread and grow large tubers without competing with neighboring plants for water and nutrients.
ga: Esa akɛ oshi gbɛ ni miihe ashɛ mita kome yɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ yɛ he fɛɛ he. Kɛ́ aha amɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ehaa amɛshishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni amɛkwɛɔ bulbs wuji ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛkɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ abɔi akaŋ kɛha nu kɛ niyenii.

english: Why do some of the maize seeds I plant fail to sprout at all?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni midu lɛ eko kwraa ekwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to sprout if they are buried too deep, damaged by insects, or planted in dry soil. Planting good quality, certified seeds about two fingers deep right after a good rain gives them the moisture they need to germinate.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ. ŋmeii efite loo adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ odaseyeli, ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni mli kwɔ aaafee inchi enyɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ ana nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do my cassava tubers stay small even when the leaves grow very big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ bibii eyɛ mli akɛ baai lɛ dara waa moŋ lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen, cassava plants spend all their energy growing tall stems and thick leaves instead of roots. Adding potassium-rich nutrients, such as wood ash, encourages the plant to direct its strength into swelling the tubers.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo yɛ shishifãi najiaŋ lɛ, ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni mli tse. Kɛ́ akɛ niyenii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ potassium, tamɔ tso mli sũ fata he lɛ, ebaawo tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛ bulbar lɛ afuu.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts naturally fix nitrogen from the air into the soil. Planting them alongside maize feeds the soil naturally, helping the maize grow stronger while suppressing weed growth.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ diɛŋtsɛ saa nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Dumɔ yɛ ŋmãa ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ masɛi Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni edara waa yɛ be mli ni etsĩɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa.

english: What causes my pepper flowers to drop off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ aduawai?

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant suffers from extreme heat, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients. Covering the soil with dried grass mulch keeps the ground moist and cool, helping the flowers stay attached and form peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ mli edɔ waa, nu bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waaa. Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: How do I know when my cocoa pods are fully ripe for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-kookoo lɛ eshɛ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha kpamɔ?

english: Cocoa pods are fully ripe when their outer skin changes color completely from green to bright yellow, or from dark red to orange. Harvesting at this point ensures the beans inside have developed full sweet pulp for high-quality fermentation.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa kɛ́ kponɔgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ tsake su kɛjɛ eŋɔli mli kɛtee ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse mli. loo kɛjɛ tsuru ni mli edɔ nɔ kɛyashi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kwraa nɔ. Nibii ni akpaa yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ haa anáa nɔmimaa akɛ kɔfi yibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ená ŋmɔtɔ ni ŋɔɔ waa kɛha ŋmɔtɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cabbage heads split open before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage yitsei lɛ mli gbalaa dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cabbage heads split when they receive a sudden heavy intake of water after a dry period, causing the inside leaves to grow faster than the outer ones. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular, light watering prevents sudden swelling and bursting.
ga: Kaabaji yitsei lɛ baatswa kɛji akɛ amɛbote nu babaoo mli trukaa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ. Ehaa mligbɛ baai lɛ daa oya fe kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ nu fioo ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛtsi trukaa kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni etse lɛ naa.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings keep dying when I clear all the big trees off my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo dumɔwui lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboiɔ lɛ? Kɛjɛ be mli ni mijie tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from harsh, direct sunlight. Leaving some large shade trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantains alongside them provides crucial shade and keeps the soil cool and moist so the seedlings can survive.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Tsei wuji ni ashiɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo loo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni yɔɔ amɛhe lɛ. Ebaaha hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni edɔ bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed for strong leaf growth. Adding compost, animal manure, or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer will help restore their green color and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa koni baai ni wa lɛ adara Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How do I know which direction to stick cassava stem cuttings into the ground when I am planting?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole he ni esa akɛ okɛ o-cassava ŋmɔtɔi lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Look closely at the tiny raised buds along the cassava stem. These buds must point upwards toward the sky so that leaves can sprout upwards easily while the roots form underneath in the soil.
ga: Kwɛmɔ fɔfɔi bibii ni teɔ shi yɛ ŋmei tso lɛ he lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Esa akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni baai lɛ akwɛ̃ mlɛo yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants without turning into any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the weather gets too hot or if the soil dries out completely. Keeping the soil consistently moist and spreading dry grass around the base helps keep the roots cool and preserves the blossoms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ jogbaŋŋ ni agbɛ jwɛi ni egbi ashwã shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunshine to make food for the tubers growing under the ground. Staking lifts the vines high up into the light and keeps the leaves off damp soil where diseases can attack them.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛyaa la lɛ mli ni ehaaa tsei ahe tsei lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ he ni helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. baanyɛ atutua

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from the leaves, or by viral diseases spread by whiteflies. Checking under the leaves early and managing pests helps keep the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni ŋmeii yɛji gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akwɛ baai lɛ ashishi mra, ni akwɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa.

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas make my farmland better for other crops later?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ aha miŋmɔ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas can take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant dies, that stored nitrogen stays in the ground as natural fertilizer for the next crop you plant.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei baanyɛ ajie nitrogen gas kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tso lɛ gbo Nakai nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ.

english: Why is it so important to remove weeds while my crops are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ yɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ darako kwraa lɛ?

english: Young crop seedlings have weak roots and cannot compete well against fast-growing weeds for water, sunlight, and soil food. Clearing weeds early gives your young crops the head start they need to grow strong.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ shishifãi bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛ jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ yeee akaŋ jogbaŋŋ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha otsei bibii lɛ afee klalo dani amɛdara ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why should I wait until the rains are steady before I put my maize seeds into the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ akpa dani madu ŋmãa dumɔwui?

english: Planting seeds in dry or barely damp soil can cause them to dry out and rot before sprouting. Waiting for regular rains ensures the soil stays wet enough for the seeds to germinate smoothly and build strong roots.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo nɔ ni mli edɔ fioo nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛgbi ni amɛgboi dani amɛkwɛ̃. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why do my harvested maize grains rot or catch mold quickly when I put them into storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya loo amɛfeɔ ŋmeii kɛ mikɛwoɔ nibii ni akɛtoɔ kotokui amli lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested grains carry hidden moisture inside them. If you bag them before drying them completely in the sun, trapped moisture creates mold and attracts insects that cause the grains to spoil.
ga: Nibii ni akpa ehee lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛtee amɛmli. Kɛji akɛ okɛwo kotoku mli dani ogbi yɛ hulu lɛ mli lɛ, Fɛ̃i ni emɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ baa ni egbalaa kooloi bibii ni haa ŋmaa lɛ fiteɔ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa seedlings need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cocoa trees too close to one another?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When trees are planted too close together, their branches block airflow and sunlight, creating a damp environment where diseases like black pod thrive. Crowded trees also compete for soil nutrients, leading to smaller harvests.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tso niji tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛ hulu la naa. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji baanyɛ aya hiɛ yɛ mli lɛ baa.
