Tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ hu kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba lɛ baafee bibioo.

english: My cocoa tree produces many small flowers, but most drop off without turning into pods. Why does this happen?
ga: Mi-cacao tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi bibii babaoo, shi amɛteŋ babaoo shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii. Mɛni he je nɛ e baa jã a?

english: It is normal for a cocoa tree to shed many flowers, but heavy shedding happens when the tree lacks water or nutrients, or when there are not enough beneficial insects like tiny midges around to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ akɛ cacao tsei baafɔ̃ babaoo. Shi tso lɛ yibii ni shwieɔ shi waa lɛ baa kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii kpakpai. aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ afee fɔfɔii amli ŋmɔtɔ lɛ bɛ.

english: Why do some cocoa trees take five years to produce pods while hybrid ones start in just two years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei komɛi heɔ afii enumɔ dani amɛwoɔ ŋmeii lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni hybrid cocoa tsei lɛ heɔ afii enyɔ pɛ?

english: Different varieties of cocoa grow at different speeds. Older traditional varieties naturally take four to five years to mature, whereas modern hybrid varieties are bred specifically to grow faster, resist diseases better, and produce pods much earlier.
ga: Kookoo henɔi srɔtoi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oyaiyeli srɔtoi amli. Kusum mli tsofai srɔtoi ni etsɛ lɛ heɔ afii ejwɛ kɛyashi enumɔ dani amɛdaraa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, atsɔse ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ tsei ni akɛ amɛhe ewo mli lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛdara oya. Helai ni hi fe fɛɛ Ni ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ kpo oya kwraa.

english: Why do I need to cut off the small side shoots growing out of my cocoa tree trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ kookoo tso lɛ mli lɛ

english: Those extra shoots, often called water sprouts or chupons, suck up water and plant food that the main tree needs. Removing them allows the tree to direct its energy into growing healthy branches and heavy cocoa pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi nɛɛ akɛ nu ŋmeii loo chupon ŋmeii. Egbalaa nu ni ekwɛ̃ɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tso titri lɛ. Tso lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ eyeɔ eniji ni wa kɛ kokoo ŋmɔji ni tsii lɛ anɔ.

english: How can I tell if my soil needs fertilizer for my cocoa trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha kookoo tsei?

english: If your cocoa leaves turn pale or yellow, grow very slowly, or produce fewer pods than usual, the soil likely lacks nutrients. Applying the right cocoa fertilizer replenishes the soil and encourages better pod production.
ga: Kɛji akɛ o-cocoa baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, amɛdaraa blɛoo waa, loo amɛwoɔ ŋmeii fioo fe bɔ ni amɛfeɔ daa lɛ. Ekolɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo mli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, wet weather. Pruning extra branches to let in sunlight and removing the black pods from the farm helps stop the disease from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ duŋ kɛ nu shihilɛ mli kɛbaa. Nibii krokomɛi ni afolɔ ashwie shi koni hulu la babaoo aba kɛ ŋmeii ni edɔ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: What causes the leaves on my young cocoa branches to dry up and look burned?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo niji bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ gĩɔ ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eshã?

english: This damage is often caused by small insects called capsids or mirids that suck the juice from leaves and young shoots. Spraying recommended treatments at the right time of year keeps these insects from destroying your trees.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Atsɛɔ amɛ capsids loo myrids ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai kɛ tsei bibii amli. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ shwie nɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akafite otsei lɛ.

english: How do I know when a cocoa pod is ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni kookoo ŋmeii lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Look at the color of the pod. Pods that start as green turn bright yellow when ripe, and pods that start as red or purple turn yellow-orange. Harvesting pods when fully ripe ensures high-quality beans inside.
ga: Kwɛmɔ bɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ ahe yɔɔ ha. Pods ni jeɔ shishi kɛ eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse beni amɛshwereɔ lɛ. Ni pods ni jeɔ shishi efeɔ tsuru loo purple lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ-ŋmei. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmeii lɛ beni amɛkwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba mli.

english: Why do I need to heap my cocoa beans under plantain leaves for a few days before drying them in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ kookoo ŋmeii toɔ plantain baai ashishi gbii fioo komɛi dani mikɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Heaping and covering the wet beans triggers fermentation, a natural chemical process that develops the chocolate flavor, changes the bean color to brown, and reduces bitter tastes before you dry them.
ga: Beans ni efɔ lɛ ni ato ni akɛha nɔ lɛ baaha amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli tsofafeemɔ gbɛjianɔtoo ko ni haa tsokolate lɛ mli ŋɔɔ lɛ. Tsakemɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe su kɛya ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni okɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ aba shi dani egbi.

english: Why do some of my crop seeds sprout and show above the soil earlier than others in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛjieɔ amɛhe kpo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya fe ekrokomɛi lɛ? Yɛ ŋmɔ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Seeds vary slightly in their vigor, depth in the soil, and access to moisture. The ones that get moisture faster will germinate and show their first shoots earlier than the rest.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ahewalɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ, kɛ bɔ ni amɛnáa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ yɛ srɔtoi fioo. Tsei ni nu yɔɔ mli oya lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛwo amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmeii lɛ oya fe ekrokomɛi lɛ.

english: Why do my crops produce lots of green leaves first before any flowers start appearing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiwo baai ŋmɔji babaoo dani fɔfɔi lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Leaves are the plant's solar panels. A crop needs to grow leaves first to gather energy from the sun so it has enough strength later to produce flowers and fruits.
ga: Baai ji tso lɛ hulutsoo tsɔnei. Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛ̃ baai klɛŋklɛŋ koni amɛbua hewalɛ naa kɛjɛ hulu lɛ mli. Koni ená hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Why does the main top shoot of my crop grow taller first before side branches start coming out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifã titri lɛ daa dani afã niji lɛ jeɔ shishi ejɛɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Crops naturally direct their initial energy upward toward the sun. Once the main stem reaches a certain height, the plant redirects energy to grow side branches.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ amɛshishijee hewalɛ lɛ yaa hulu lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Beni tso titri lɛ shɛɔ he ko lɛ. Tsei tsɔɔ hewalɛ gbɛ koni amɛkwɛ niji ni yɔɔ amɛsɛɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: What causes weeds to show up in my farm field even before my planted crops start emerging?
ga: Mɛni haa jwɛi jeɔ kpo yɛ miŋmɔji amli dani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ?

english: Weed seeds sit naturally in the soil and are adapted to sprout immediately with the first rains, often outracing cultivated crop seeds for moisture and light.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni atsake lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ hiɔ dumɔwui ni adu lɛ anɔ koni ená ŋmɔtɔ kɛ la.

english: Why do root crops like cassava show heavy leaf growth at the top before the underground tubers start swelling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shishifãi tamɔ ŋmei jieɔ baai ni mli tse kpo yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ dani ŋmei lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava uses its top leaves to manufacture food using sunlight. Once the plant has enough leaves, it sends the extra stored energy down to swell the tubers underground.
ga: Cassava kɛ eŋwɛi baai lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ niyenii kɛtsɔ hulu la nɔ. Kɛ tso lɛ yɛ baai ni fa bɔ ni sa Etsuɔ hewalɛ ni fa fe nine ni ato lɛ kɛyaa shi koni eha ŋmeii lɛ amli alɛɛ.

english: Why do male flowers often show up on crops like maize or squash before female flowers appear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ fɔfɔi hii jeɔ kpo yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa nɔ lɛ? Dani fɔfɔi yei lɛ baaje kpo?

english: Plants produce male flowers first to ensure pollen is already available in the field by the time the female flowers open, which helps guarantee successful pollination.
ga: Tsei lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi hii klɛŋklɛŋ koni amɛkwɛ akɛ pollen lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli momo beni fɔfɔi yei lɛ fɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa pollination yeɔ omanye.

english: Why do early-maturing crop varieties flower so much sooner than traditional varieties?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei srɔtoi ni shwereɔ mra lɛ fɔɔ mra kwraa fe blema tsei srɔtoi lɛ?

english: Early-maturing varieties are bred to complete their growth cycle faster so they can produce yield quickly before short rainy seasons end or dry weather sets in.
ga: Afɔɔ tsei srɔtoi ni shwereɔ mra lɛ koni amɛgbe amɛdalɛ be lɛ naa oya. Bɔni afee ni enyɛ ewo yibii oya dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba naagbee loo hulutsoo be lɛ aba.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my crops turn yellow first while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: As a plant grows, older bottom leaves get less sunlight and naturally transfer their nutrients to the younger top leaves, though it can also be an early sign of nitrogen deficiency.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ dara lɛ Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni edara lɛ naaa hulu la fioo ni amɛtsɔɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi baabii bibii lɛ anɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyɛ mli akɛ enɛ baanyɛ afee mra be mli okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa moŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their first set of flowers without setting pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ miiho eklɛŋklɛŋ fɔfɔi lɛ shi ni efeee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees often produce early flowers as a test run. If the plant is not mature enough or lacks water, it sheds those early flowers to save energy for later growth.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛwo fɔfɔi mra yɛ kaa lɛ mli. Kɛji tso lɛ edako bɔ ni sa loo nu bɛ mli lɛ Abaafolɔ klɛŋklɛŋ fɔfɔi lɛ koni akɛ hewalɛ ato kɛha sɛɛ mli dalɛ.

english: What does it mean when my crops show quick growth after the first rain but slow down soon after?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ kɛ́ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dara oya yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ shi etsɛɛɛ ni egbɔjɔ?

english: The first rain triggers seed germination, but if the moisture doesn't reach deeper soil roots, the plant slows its growth until consistent rains provide steady water.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃. Shi kɛji akɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ eyashɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ Tsei lɛ baaha amɛdalɛ aya hiɛ fioo kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ baaha nu ni yaa nɔ daa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings drying up and burning in the sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni hulu lɛ shãa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and cannot tolerate harsh direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantain or banana around them creates a canopy that protects young leaves from sun damage and keeps soil moist.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ waa ni amɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛ kpɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains loo banana ni aduɔ yɛ jɛmɛ he fɛɛ he. Efeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la he ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: What is eating small holes in my young maize leaves and leaving broad patches of damage?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? yɛ mi ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ amli ni eshiɔ fitemɔi babaoo?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide in the whorl of young maize plants. Early scouting allows you to spray targeted natural or chemical controls before the caterpillars reach the growing tip.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Early scouting Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii loo tsofai ni akɛkwɛɔ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ nɔ dani ŋmeii lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛdaraa lɛ he.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with many leaves, but producing small, skinny tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi ani eyɛ yitso bibioo ni yɔɔ mlɛo?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil causes cassava to direct its energy into growing thick upper leaves and stems instead of storing energy in underground root tubers. Avoiding high-nitrogen fertilizer encourages stronger tuber growth.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei tsuɔ hewalɛ koni ekwɛ̃ yɛ ebaai kɛ eshishifãi ni mli tse lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baato shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii amli lɛ, ŋmeii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha bulb lɛ aya hiɛ waa.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up toward direct sunlight to produce energy. Staking prevents leaf rot on damp ground and helps the plant produce large, healthy yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã ŋwɛi kɛya hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he koni amɛná hewalɛ. Staking tsiɔ baai ni fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ naa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my maize stalks turn thin and yellow when I plant four seeds in a single hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni miduɔ dumɔwui ejwɛ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Planting too many seeds together causes overcrowding, forcing plants to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each root system enough room to produce strong stalks and full cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa mɛi ayiɔ obɔ fe nine. Enɛ haa tsei wuɔ kɛha hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ eko fɛɛ eko aná he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee tso lɛ shishifã ni wa kɛ ŋmei ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do weeds slow down the growth of my pepper crops even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa mi-pepper tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ yɛ nugbɔ babaoo ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that steal fertilizers and moisture from the soil before your pepper roots can reach them, starving your crop of nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ dani pepper shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ he. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaaa niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do extension officers recommend planting groundnuts or cowpeas on the same land with maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni aduɔ ŋmei yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots, naturally fertilizing the ground for nutrient-hungry crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha tsei ni taoɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, tamɔ abele.

english: Why should I wait until two weeks after my maize sprouts before applying the first top-dress fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ otsii enyɔ beni ŋmãa lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ dani mikɛ ŋmãa klɛŋklɛŋ fã lɛ awo mli lɛ?

english: Freshly sprouted seeds rely on stored seed energy and have tiny root systems that can burn from strong fertilizer. Waiting two weeks allows roots to develop enough to absorb the nutrients safely.
ga: Dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ damɔ dumɔwui ahewalɛ ni ato lɛ nɔ, ni amɛyɛ shishifãi bibii. ni abaanyɛ atsake kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli Otsii enyɔ ni akɛbaamɛ lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ adara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Tomato flowers fall off without fruiting when plants face extreme heat stress, poor pollination, or irregular watering, which prevents flowers from developing into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ tsei lɛ kɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa kpe. pollination ni ehiii loo nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be Enɛ haaa tomato fɔfɔi lɛ afeee aduawai.

english: How do I know if the first rain of the season is enough to sow my crop seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni mikɛbaadu miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Early rains can be misleading 'false rains' followed by dry spells that kill young seedlings. Dig down into the soil to check if topsoil is wet at least finger-deep before sowing your seeds.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ baanyɛ aha ‘nugbɔ amale’ ni lakaa mɔ aba ni hulutsoo be ni gbeɔ tsei bibii lɛ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Tsɔɔmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni okwɛ akɛ kɛ hoo lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ edɔ inchi kome dani odu dumɔwui lɛ.

english: If I acquire and clear a fresh piece of virgin land, why do my crops grow so much faster in the first year than on my old farmland?
ga: Kɛji manyɛ maba ni mijie shikpɔŋ hee ko ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dara oya fe miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ momo lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Freshly cleared land contains soil that has built up natural organic matter and nutrients over many years of untouched growth. This gives your crops immediate, rich food in the first season, whereas old farmland loses nutrients over time if not replenished.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ajie lɛ ehee lɛ ji shikpɔŋ ni ebua nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ naa yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ afii babaoo ni mɔ ko mɔ ko etako he lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná niyenii babaoo amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ mli. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, okwaayeli shikpɔŋ momo lɛ baafite niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ be ni sa mli kɛji akɛ awooo mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or beans on my land make my maize grow better when I plant it in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa miŋmei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans are legumes, which means their roots work with friendly soil microbes to trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground. This leaves free natural fertilizer in the soil for your next maize crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ sũ mli nibii bibii ni yɔɔ naanyobɔɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha o-abele ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to direct, harsh sunlight and high heat. They need shade from taller trees or shade crops like plantains to keep their leaves cool and protect the soil moisture while their roots develop.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɔlɔ loo hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains amli koni amɛha baai lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛbu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ he be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why do I need to put wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb instead of letting them spread on the bare ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tso ama shi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to catch as much sunlight as possible to produce energy for growing big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the hot ground, preventing rot and fungal diseases while maximizing sun exposure.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni mli edɔ lɛ. Tsi ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ naa yɛ be mli ni onine shɛɔ hulu la babaoo nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during heavy rainstorms compared to other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli kɛ akɛto tsei krokomɛi ahe lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems that spread sideways near the soil surface rather than deep down. Because the top of the plant carries heavy bunches of fruit, strong winds and soaked soil easily top-heavy trees over unless supported with wooden props.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛyaa sɛɛgbɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ moŋ fe ni eeeya shɔŋŋ. Nɔ ni ha ebalɛ nakai ji yibii babaoo ni yɔɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ. Tsei ni tsii lɛ akumɔɔ oya. ja tsei ni akɛfiɔ sɛɛ lɛ fiɔ sɛɛ

english: Why do my cassava plants shed all their leaves during the dry season, and does it mean they are dead?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ? Ni ani no tsɔɔ akɛ egbo?

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves during dry spells as a natural survival mechanism to prevent water from evaporating through the leaves. The plant is not dead; it rests until the rains return to sprout fresh foliage.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli wala gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ nu naa koni ekatsɔ baai lɛ amli kɛho. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Ejɔɔ ehe kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ nɛ ni baai heei kwɛ̃.

english: When temperatures get too high, tomato pollen becomes sticky or sterile, preventing proper pollination. The plant recognizes that the flowers cannot produce seeds and drops them to conserve its energy.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Tomato pollen lɛ shwieɔ shi loo ebɛ fɔmɔ nii. Etsiɔ pollination ni sa naa. Tsei yɔseɔ akɛ fɔfɔi nyɛŋ awo dumɔwui ni amɛshwie dumɔwui koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my maize plants turn pale yellow and stay short when I plant the seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛhe yɔɔ kuku beni midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, their roots compete fiercely for the limited water and nitrogen in the soil. The yellow color shows that the plants are starving for nitrogen because of overcrowding.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Dumɔwui shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná nu kɛ nitrogen ni faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Yellow tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tsei kɛha nitrogen yɛ mɛi ni eyi obɔ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl upward and get hard and crinkly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually a sign that tiny insects like thrips or mites are feeding on the sap beneath the leaves, or that the plant is curling its leaves to shield itself from extreme sunlight and heat stress.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites miiye baa lɛ mli nu lɛ. Aloo etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miibɔle baai lɛ ahe koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he.

english: Why do my mango trees produce thousands of flowers, but most of them drop off before turning into mangoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tsei yɛ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ lɛ? Shi ani amɛteŋ mɛi babaoo shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ mango?

english: Mango trees produce far more flowers than they can actually feed. The tree naturally sheds excess flowers so it can focus its energy and available soil water on nurturing a smaller, healthy batch of full-sized fruits.
ga: Mango tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni ebaanyɛ ekwɛ nɔ diɛŋtsɛ. Tso lɛ baajie fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛjɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ ji koni anyɛ akɛ sũ mli hewalɛ kɛ nu ni yɔɔ lɛ atsu nii kɛkwɛ aduawai bibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni amɛyi fa babaoo lɛ anɔ.

english: Yellowing on lower leaves usually means your maize plant lacks nitrogen, an essential food for leaves. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer like urea helps the plant stay green and grow heavy ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tso lɛ mli, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa baa lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmei ni yɔɔ nitrogen tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ etoi ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my pepper plants keep dropping their flowers before any fruit can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho efɔfɔi lɛ dani ewo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience heat stress or lack enough water in the soil, which stops the flowers from pollinating and producing fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛna dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baatsi fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkawo ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: What will happen to my crops if I plant seeds very close together to save space?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni mikɛha he ko akafee nɔ ko?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak, tall stems and tiny harvests.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ Tso lɛ tso lɛ kɛlɛ ni ŋmaa lɛ hu faaa.

english: Why do I need to plant shade crops next to my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sunlight. Faster-growing plants like plantains provide broad leaf shade that keeps the soil cool and moist until the cocoa trees grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni cacao tso lɛ he feɔ fɛo.

english: Why are my tomato plants wilting in the hot afternoon even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: Midday wilting in moist soil is often caused by root rot or bacterial wilt, where microscopic organisms damage the roots and stem, preventing water from reaching the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishifãi ni fiteɔ loo helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ hulutsoo be mli ŋmɔlɔ baa. Nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ baafite shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, nu nyɛɛɛ ashɛ baai lɛ ahe.

english: What is making small holes all over the leaves of my cabbage crops?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Mi-cabbage tso lɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ?

english: Small leaf holes are typically caused by leaf-chewing pests such as caterpillars. Inspecting under the leaves early in the morning helps you spot and treat them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ baa, tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ baa bu bibii baa. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi leebi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni ona amɛ ni otsa amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: How do I tell when my yam tubers are mature and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Yams are mature when the leaves and vines above ground turn yellow and dry up naturally, showing that the plant has transferred its energy down into the root.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ shɛɔ shweremɔ he beni baai kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekɛ hewalɛ eba shi kɛtee shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my stored maize grains turn moldy and get destroyed by insects inside the sacks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni kooloi ni yɔɔ kotokui lɛ amli lɛ yeɔ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Grains spoil in storage if they are bagged before being thoroughly dried in the sun, because trapped moisture encourages mold growth and attracts grain weevils.
ga: Nibii ni akɛtoɔ lɛ baafite yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ kɛji akɛ awo kotoku mli dani agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu ni mli edɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ he hewalɛ ni egbalaa dumɔwui amli ŋmeii lɛ.

english: What makes crops high enough in quality to sell to buyers who export produce overseas?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmɔshi nibii ko yaa hiɛ bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ aha mɛi ni heɔ ni amɛkɛyaa maŋsɛɛ lɛ?

english: Export buyers look for uniform fruit size, clean surfaces without pest marks or bruises, and crops harvested at the exact right time so they do not spoil during long transport.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nibii ni akɛyaa maŋsɛɛ lɛ taoɔ aduawai lɛ adalɛ ni yaa nɔ daa. Tsumɔ he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai loo tsɛŋemɔ helai akadi. kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa yɛ be ni sa mli Bɔni afee ni ekafite yɛ gbɛfaa be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: Why do my crops seem to grow faster with natural rain than when I water them manually?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa fe kɛ́ mikɛ miniji shwie amɛnɔ nu lɛ?

english: Rainwater carries natural atmospheric nitrogen directly to roots and soaks deep into the surrounding soil, whereas hand-watering often only moistens the top surface.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ kɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ, ni eboteɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ, nine ni akɛshwieɔ nu lɛ haa ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, a key food crop needs to grow green and healthy. It can also happen when the ground stays flooded with water for too long, preventing roots from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛɛmɛi ji niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa ni ehe hiaa ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhiɛ ahi amɛhe nɔ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu

english: When soil has too much nitrogen but lacks potassium, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves and stem above ground instead of sending food down to build big root tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ shi potassium bɛ mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ ebaa kɛ eshishifãi ni edaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oootsu niyenii kɛba shi koni ekɛfee bulbs ni shishifãi wuji yɔɔ mli lɛ

english: What will happen to my crops if I plant the seeds too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni baaba midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: When crops are crowded, they compete with one another for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes them to grow tall and thin with weak stems, producing smaller yields.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ yɛ amɛteŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛshishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba lɛ baafee bibioo.

english: Why do dark spots appear on my tomato leaves and spread quickly during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ jeɔ kpo yɛ tomato baai anɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Rainwater and high humidity create the perfect moist environment for fungal diseases to multiply. The rain splashes fungal spores from the soil onto the lower leaves, causing spots that spread rapidly across the plant.
ga: Nugbɔ nu kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. Nugbɔ lɛ shwieɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ewoɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ gbɛɔ eshwaa tso lɛ nɔ oya.

english: What causes the leaves of my young maize to look chewed up with little dark drops left inside the tops?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-baby corn baai lɛ miiho ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔtɔ bibii? Ani eshwɛ yɛ ŋwɛi?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central funnel of the maize plant during the day and feeds on the soft, growing leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. ni eyeɔ baai ni miida blɛoo lɛ

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground, leading to weaker harvests over time.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni yaa nɔ amɛkwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do people advise me to cover the soil around my crops with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, keeps the soil cool under hot sun, traps groundwater so you irrigate less, blocks weeds from sprouting, and turns into manure as it rots.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ekɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu toɔ koni onyɛ okɛ nu afɔ nɔ fioo. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni ebafeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji egbo.

english: Why is it better to put fertilizer on my farm when the soil is moist instead of completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nii be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ fe ni eeegbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Plant roots can only drink fertilizer once it dissolves in water. Applying fertilizer to dry soil leaves it unusable by the plant and can even burn the roots when the sun gets hot.
ga: Tso shishifãi baanyɛ anu ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji akɛ amɛwo nu mli pɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaha tsei akatsu he nii, ni ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ kɛ́ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ enɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers when the afternoon sun becomes very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When weather temperatures get extremely high, pepper plants experience heat stress and drop their flowers to save water and energy, protecting themselves from dying even if it means losing fruit for that cycle.
ga: Kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ naa dɔlɛ mli haomɔ ni amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Buu ohe kɛjɛ gbele he kɛji akɛ no tsɔɔ akɛ obaafite yibii kɛha kpokpaa lɛ po.

english: Young cocoa trees are extremely sensitive to harsh, direct sunlight. Without shade trees to protect them, their tender leaves lose water faster than their small root systems can absorb it from the ground.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa waa he tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji tsei ni baaha hulutsoo ni amɛbu amɛhe lɛ bɛ lɛ Amɛbaai bibii lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe amɛshishifãi bibii lɛ. Abaanyɛ ajie emli nibii lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot survive direct sunlight. They need shade from taller trees like plantains or shade trees to protect their soft leaves from burning and to keep the soil moist while their roots are developing.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Koni akɛbu baai bibii ahe koni akashã amɛ. kɛ koni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ miida lɛ

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high off the ground to catch maximum sunlight. When yam leaves get plenty of sunlight, the plant produces more energy to grow large tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Kɛji sweet potato baai lɛ ná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ Tso lɛ baajie hewalɛ babaoo kpo ni ekɛ bulbs wuji akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to stay green. The plant moves nitrogen from its older leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni esa akɛ ŋmãa ahi shi eŋɔli. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi shweremɔ hee lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow very big green leaves but produce very few bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or when pests attack flower buds, cowpea plants spend all their energy growing leaves instead of flowers and pods. Insects like thrips often eat the flowers before you can see them.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo kɛji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutua fɔfɔii ashishifãi Cowpea tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ baai yɛ fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii ashishifãi najiaŋ. Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips yeɔ fɔfɔi dani obaanyɛ ona amɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when water stays on my farm for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay alive. When water sits in the field without draining away, it chokes the roots, allowing soil bacteria and fungi to attack and rot the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛji nu ŋmɛ ŋmɔ mli ni ajieee kɛjɛɛɛ mli lɛ ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ Enɛ haa helatsɛmɛi kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why should I cover the ground around my vegetable crops with dry grass during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi aha he ni mi-vegetables lɛ yɔɔ lɛ he yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, called mulching, protects the soil from hot sunlight, keeps soil water from evaporating quickly, and helps keep the roots cool.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ehaa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ oya. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, steal food and water from the main plantain tree. Removing most of them leaves only the best shoot, allowing the main tree to produce a bigger, heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: Tsoi loo tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo baaha ŋmeii ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ ahi shi. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ woɔ dumɔwui wuji ni tsii.

english: When maize plants are crowded together, they fight each other for sunlight, soil food, and water. This results in thin, weak stalks and small cobs with missing grains.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei bua amɛhe naa lɛ amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ nu, ni no haa ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmãa bibii baa. ni dumɔwui bɛ mli

english: Leaf curl in peppers is commonly caused by tiny insects like mites or aphids sucking juices from under the leaves, or by viral diseases spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off the plant before turning into green tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛmiitsɔ tomato eŋɔli lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant is stressed by very high temperatures, irregular watering, or insect attacks on the flowers, preventing fruit from setting.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa lɛ ha tsei lɛ hao. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa loo kooloi ni tutuaa fɔfɔi ni haa aduawai lɛ daaa

english: Why do my soybean plants make my farm soil richer for the next crop I plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi soybean tsei lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ afee nii babaoo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛbaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Soybeans are legumes that capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. When you harvest them, this natural fertilizer remains behind, helping future crops like maize grow bigger and stronger.
ga: Soybeans ji ŋmãa ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Beni obaakpa Adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ baakã he ahi shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmãa, ni amɛdaraa ni amɛhe wa.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a cry for help showing that the plant is hungry for nitrogen or that its roots are flooded with too much water, which prevents them from breathing and taking up food from the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji yelikɛbuamɔ he bolɔmɔ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ loo akɛ shishifãi lɛ yɛ nu babaoo tsɔ. Enɛ haaa amɛmu ni amɛye nii kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why does my cassava plant have huge, healthy leaves but small underground tubers when I harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baa agboi ni mli wa shi eyɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii kɛ́ mikpa lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen fertilizer, it puts all its energy into growing big stems and leaves above ground instead of storing nutrients in the roots to make large tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmei babaoo nɔ lɛ Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tsei agboi kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ niye níhi kɛ woɔ tso ɔ sisije ɔmɛ a mi konɛ a pee bulb nguahi.

english: Why do my crops wilt and drop their leaves during the hottest hours of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛbaa lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shwane ŋmɛlɛtswai ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: When the afternoon sun is very hot, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it up. They wilt to shrink their leaf surface area and save water so they do not dry out completely.
ga: Beni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa shwane lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Amɛhaa baai lɛ ahiɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛbuɔ nu he koni amɛkagbi kwraa.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as sudden hot spells, inconsistent watering, or when there are no bees around to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Pepper tsei jieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛmiihao, tamɔ hulutsoo trukaa. Nu ni akɛhaa yɛ be fɛɛ mli loo be mli ni ŋmeii bɛ ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmeii

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that have adapted to naturally survive harsh conditions. They absorb water, sunlight, and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated farm crops, allowing them to overpower young plants.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛhi shi yɛ adebɔɔ mli shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Amɛheɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ haa amɛyeɔ tsei bibii anɔ kunim.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops end up fighting each other for the same sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin, weak stalks and a poor harvest.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo, ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛkpaaa nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I sow my crop seeds immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ aduawai dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain of the season can be deceptive, as dry weather often returns for weeks right after. Sowing too early causes seeds to sprout and then die quickly from a lack of follow-up moisture.
ga: Nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ alaka mɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, bei pii lɛ, shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa yɛ otsii komɛi asɛɛ. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi oya yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni baa yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ hewɔ.

english: How does covering the bare soil around my crops with dry grass help them grow better?
ga: Mulching bare soil around Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ jwɛi aha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass, known as mulching, acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool, prevents water from evaporating under the sun, and blocks weeds from getting light to sprout.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Tsĩ nu naa koni ekatsɔ hulu la shishi. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ yɛ la mli

english: Why is it harmful to plant maize on the exact same plot of land every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the specific nutrients that crop loves and gives pests and diseases that attack that plant a permanent place to live and multiply in your soil.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ edaa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tso lɛ lɛ hoɔ. Ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa nakai tso lɛ feɔ shĩai ni baahi shi daa ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow well in Kumasi but struggle when I try to plant the same seeds up north in Tamale?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Kumasi shi amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ beni mibɔɔ mɔdɛŋ akɛ madu dumɔwui nɛɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ kooyigbɛ shɔŋŋ yɛ Tamale lɛ?

english: Crops react to different climate zones; Tamale has longer dry periods and hotter sunshine compared to the cooler, rainier forest zone around Kumasi, so crops need heat-tolerant varieties or more water-retention support up north.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsuɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi srɔtoi ahe nii. Tamale yɛ hulutsoo be ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ kɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa. Akɛ enɛ toɔ kooi ni mli ejɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ Kumasi he lɛ ahe, no hewɔ lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii biɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hulutsoo naa loo ni nyɛɔ amɛhiɛɔ nu babaoo yɛ kooyigbɛ lɛ.

english: Can I plant cassava in sandy soil near the coast, or will the coastal environment affect how the tubers grow?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋã shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ ŋshɔ lɛ naa lɛ nɔ? Aloo ani ŋshɔnaa shihilɛ lɛ baaná ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Cassava can grow in sandy coastal soils, but high salt in the soil or groundwater can stress the plant, causing the roots to remain smaller and woodier.
ga: Cassava baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ ŋshɔnaa shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ. Shi ŋoo ni fa babaoo yɛ sũ loo shikpɔŋ shishi nu mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei afee nɔ ni haoɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛfeɔ tsei babaoo.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes rot so fast when I transport them in sacks from my farm to a distant market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ mikɛwo kotoku mli kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee jarayeli he ko ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes continue to breathe and release natural heat and moisture after harvest; when squeezed tightly in non-ventilated sacks inside hot transport trucks, decay accelerates rapidly.
ga: Tomato yaa nɔ emuɔ ni ejieɔ dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kpo yɛ adebɔɔ naa beni akpa lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ ashɛre lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ kotoku ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli yɛ lɔle ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, fitemɔ baaba oya.

english: Why do some of my green plantains start turning yellow rapidly during long transport to other towns while others stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain eŋɔli lɛ ekomɛi bɔi ŋmɔŋ oya beni mikɛ amɛ yaa maŋ kroko nɔ yɛ gbɛ kakadaŋŋ nɔ lɛ? yɛ be mli ni kooloi srɔtoi lɛ ekomɛi yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji.

english: When a single plantain begins to ripen, it releases an invisible ripening gas that signals all surrounding plantains to ripen at once, especially under warm transport conditions.
ga: Kɛ́ plantain kome bɔi shweremɔ Ejieɔ gas ni anaaa ni akɛhooɔ nii. ni baaha okadi ko aya plantains Ripe ni ebɔle lɛ lɛ nɔ yɛ be kome mli, titri lɛ yɛ gbɛfaa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ lɛ shishi.

english: Why do my stored yams start growing green sprouts and shrinking inside my barn after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛ̃mɔ ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ yɛ mi-ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yams are living root tubers that break dormancy as temperatures shift, using up their own stored food and water reserves to push out new sprouts.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji shishifãi ni hiɛ ka ni fiteɔ ŋmiŋmi kɛji hulutsoo be tsake. Ekɛ niyenii kɛ nu ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛshwieɔ ŋmeii heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Rolling leaves is a survival mechanism where the maize plant reduces its exposed leaf surface area to stop water from evaporating into the hot air.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa wala. Abɛi tsei haa amɛbaai lɛ anɔ he ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ baa shi koni nu akatsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young seedlings bend and grow thin and crooked toward one side of the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛhe ejɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe kɛtee ŋmɔ lɛ fã kome lɛ?

english: Plants naturally lean and stretch toward light; if tall shade trees or bushes block the sun, seedlings stretch toward open sunlight, making their stems thin and weak.
ga: Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa la lɛ he. Kɛji tsei kakadaji loo tsei bibii tsi hulu la lɛ naa lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baagbala amɛhe kɛya hulu la lɛ he. Ehaa tso lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers onto the ground without forming fruits when the weather gets extremely hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ewooo yibii beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When heat stress becomes too high, pepper plants drop their blossoms to conserve energy and water rather than spending resources on developing fruit.
ga: Kɛji dɔlɛ he haomɔ fa tsɔ lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ nibii baatsu nii koni akɛfee aduawai lɛ

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my corn turning yellow in a V-shape while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing on lower leaves is a sign of nitrogen deficiency; the plant moves available nitrogen from its older bottom leaves up to nourish new growth at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha ŋwɛi dalɛ hee lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and dry up right on the branch during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Persistent rain and high air humidity create ideal conditions for the black pod fungal disease to spread across and destroy pods still attached to the tree.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baaha black pod fungus lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni efite pods ni kã tso lɛ he lolo lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when I plant them in an open field without any shade trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to strong sunlight. Without shade from larger plants like plantains or timber trees, the intense sun burns their fragile leaves and dries out their moisture faster than their small roots can drink it up.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa. Kɛji akɛ tsei wuji tamɔ plantains loo tsei ahe hulutsoo be ko bɛ lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shãa ebaa ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa nu ni mli edɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya fe shishifãi bibii lɛ. Abaanyɛ ami amɛnibii lɛ.

english: When maize plants are packed too tightly, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. The plant spends all its energy stretching upwards to reach light instead of using that energy to grow strong stems and fat corn cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛkpãa ŋwɛi koni enine ashɛ la nɔ. Mohu ɔ, moo ngɔ jamɛ a he wami ɔ kɛ wo tsohi nɛ a he wa kɛ ngmɔhi nɛ a ngɛ fɔ.

english: Why do you advise me to cut off some of the leaves and side shoots from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okɛ ŋaawoo haa akɛ mafo mi-tomato tsei lɛ ahe baai kɛ amɛsɛɛ ŋmeii lɛ ekomɛi lɛ?

english: A tomato plant uses energy from the soil to feed every leaf and branch it has. By trimming away extra foliage, you force the plant to direct its energy and water straight into growing bigger, healthier tomatoes instead of extra stems.
ga: Tomato tsei kɛ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ sũ lɛ mli baa kɛ amɛniji lɛ tsuɔ nii. Kɛtsɔ baai ni fa fe nine ni ooofo lɛ nɔ lɛ, onyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ ehewalɛ kɛ nu lɛ aya tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni miida lɛ amli moŋ fe ni ekɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi baatsu nii.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay thin and woody if I leave weeds growing around the stems during the early months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ tsei kɛji mishi jwɛi yɛ tsei lɛ ahe yɛ nyɔŋ lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Weeds steal food and water from the soil right around your cassava roots. When weeds crowd the plant, the cassava gets stressed and stops expanding its roots, resulting in poor tuber growth.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ sũ ni bɔle o-cassava shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli. Kɛ jwɛi bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ Kasava lɛ baaná haomɔ ni ebaakpa shishifãi ni kwɛ̃ɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yitso ni edaaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yam leaves need to catch as much sunlight as possible to make food for the tubers underground. When the vine climbs high on a stake, its leaves spread out toward the sun, producing more energy to build heavy yams.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii lɛ. Beni wain tsei lɛ kwɔ kɛtee akulashiŋi kakadaji lɛ anɔ lɛ Ebaai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa koni emɔ hulu la lɛ. Enɛ haa hewalɛ babaoo baa koni akɛfee ŋmeii ni tsii.

english: Why are all the blossoms falling off my pepper plants without forming any peppers during the very hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeee pepper yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat puts pepper plants under heavy stress. To protect itself from losing too much water, the plant deliberately drops its flowers to save energy and moisture until conditions cool down.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ kɛ pepper tsei lɛ woɔ haomɔ ni naa wa shishi. Koni obu ohe koni nu babaoo akafite. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ kɛ fɛ̃i ahi shi kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ lɛ, amɛjɛɔ amɛyiŋ amɛshiɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛha hewalɛ kɛ hulutsoo ahi shi.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my older maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape down the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei momo lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni V su yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves mean your maize is short on nitrogen, which is the key food plants need to stay green. The plant naturally moves available nitrogen from its old bottom leaves up to keep its newer top leaves growing.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe nɔ. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni eha ŋwɛi baai heei akwɛ̃.

english: Why does my plantain shoot take so long to produce fruit if I leave all the small suckers growing around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii lɛ? Ni kɛji akɛ mishi ŋmeii bibii ni bɔle tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ he hu?

english: All the suckers growing from one plantain stem share the same root system. Leaving too many shoots causes them to drain food away from the main plant, delaying its growth and the development of the fruit cluster.
ga: Tsofɔi fɛɛ ni jɛɔ dumɔwu kome mli lɛ yɛ shishifã kome. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo yɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha amɛjie niyenii kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Enɛ haa aduawai akui lɛ daraa blɛoo ni amɛyaa hiɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my garden egg plants roll up and droop during the afternoon sun even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulutsoo be mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ mli leebi moŋ?

english: Leaf rolling is a plant's natural shield against intense heat. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface exposed to the direct sun so it loses less moisture into the air.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Tsei haa hulu la ni shɛɔ amɛhiɛ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmɔtɔ ni baa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ fioo.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas on my farm make my maize grow better in the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua mi ŋmãa lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. When the crop is harvested, that natural fertilizer remains in the soil to feed the next crop you plant.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Beni akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Nakai adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ niyenii.

english: What are these small insects called mirids, and what do they do to my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni ji nɛkɛ kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ mirids nɛɛ ni mɛni amɛfeɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ?

english: Mirids, locally known as 'akate,' are tiny insects that suck sap from young cocoa shoots and pods. Their toxic saliva leaves dark spots and causes branches to dry up, which severely reduces your yield.
ga: Mirids, ni ale amɛ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli akɛ ‘akate’ lɛ ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ kookoo ŋmeii amli lɛ. Muji ni yɔɔ gbeyei lɛ haa tsei lɛ aniji lɛ feɔ diŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ. Enɛ baaha nibii ni afee lɛ aba shi waa.

english: Why does my cocoa crop suffer more pest attacks during the January dry season than in other months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo tutuaa mi-kokoo tsei lɛ yɛ January fɛ̃i be lɛ mli fe nyɔji krokomɛi amli lɛ?

english: During the dry season in January, cocoa trees are stressed from lack of water and produce fresh young shoots that attract hungry mirids looking for moisture and food.
ga: Yɛ hɔmɔ be mli yɛ January mli lɛ, Cacao tsei lɛ haoɔ kɛjɛɔ nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli lɛ hewɔ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii ni gbalaa ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ ni miitao nu kɛ niyenii lɛ.

english: Why do mirids stay on my farm even after I see the March rain season arrive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atatui yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ minaa akɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni baa yɛ March mli lɛ eba moŋ.

english: Mirids hide under dense shade and in canopy cracks during bad weather, so when the March rains bring new leaves and pods, the surviving insects quickly multiply again.
ga: Mirids kɛ amɛhe teeɔ hulutsoo be mli kɛ tsũi ayiteŋ ŋmeii amli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ be mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ March mli lɛ, ekɛ baai kɛ ŋmeii heei baa. Koolooi ni hiɛ ka lɛ fɔɔ ekoŋŋ oya.

english: Can my cocoa tree produce good pods again if mirids attack it early in the season?
ga: Ani mi-cacao tsei lɛ baanyɛ awo ŋmeii kpakpai ekoŋŋ? Kɛji akɛ kookoo tsei tutua mra yɛ be lɛ mli?

english: Yes, cocoa trees are naturally resilient. If you manage the pests through spraying and proper farm care, the trees will bounce back and produce healthy pods in the following crop cycles.
ga: Hɛɛ, cacao tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛshiɔ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛji akɛ okwɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi kɛ kwɛmɔ kpakpa nɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Tso lɛ baaku esɛɛ eba ni ebaawo ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli.

english: How can I tell if dark marks on my cocoa stems are from mirids or just hot weather?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ jɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ kɛkɛ?

english: Heat makes leaves wilt generally, but mirid damage leaves distinct sunken, dark brown or black scars (called blast lesions) specifically on young shoots and pod stalks.
ga: Dɔlɛ haa bei pii lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Shi nɔ ni efite fioo lɛ haa ŋmeii ni tsuɔ loo ediŋŋ baa. (ni atsɛɔ lɛ shãa), titri lɛ yɛ tsei bibii kɛ pod stems lɛ anɔ

english: What is the difference between the main cocoa season and the early year seasons in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ kookoo be titri lɛ kɛ afi lɛ shishijee be lɛ teŋ yɛ Ghana?

english: Ghana has a major crop season yielding the biggest harvest and a minor mid-crop season; early months like January and March represent transitions where trees rest, flower, or set young pods.
ga: Ghana yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ waa ni woɔ yibii fe fɛɛ, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ fioo yɛ be lɛ teŋgbɛ. Nyɔji tamɔ January kɛ March shishijee kadiɔ tsakemɔ be ni tsei lɛ wɔɔ, amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi loo amɛwoɔ ŋmeii.

english: Should I cut down my cocoa trees if pest attacks make them lose all their pods early in the year?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo tsei lɛ kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ha amɛmli ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ fite yɛ afi lɛ shishijee mli?

english: No, cutting them down is unnecessary. Pruning away damaged branches and applying recommended insecticides will help the tree grow new, productive shoots.
ga: Dabi, ehe ehiaaa ni afo mli. Kɛ́ afo tsei niji ni efite lɛ amli ni akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ awo mli taakɛ atsɔɔ lɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ tsei heei ni woɔ yibii.

english: When is the right time for me to spray my farm to stop mirids from destroying my cocoa?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa afɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ koni mirid akafite mi-kokoo lɛ?

english: You should spray your farm during peak pest months, usually starting from August through December, to reduce mirid populations before they ruin early-year crop growth.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ tsofa afɔ oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ nyɔji ni tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ August kɛyashiɔ December. Koni ajie gbɔmɛi ayibɔ ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ shi dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ yɛ afi lɛ shishijee mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa pods shrivel up and die before they are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: When mirids bite young pods, they inject fluid that kills the plant tissue around the wound, causing the young pod to starve, shrivel, and turn black.
ga: Kɛ́ mirids lɛ ŋmɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ, amɛwoɔ nu ni fiteɔ tso lɛ mli fãji ni bɔle pilamɔ lɛ he lɛ mli, ni ehaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ, amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ.

english: What basic steps should I take to keep my cocoa farm going when pest damage makes me feel hopeless?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii titrii esa akɛ mafee koni mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ aya nɔ atsu nii beni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ haa minuɔ he akɛ mibɛ hiɛnɔkamɔ ko?

english: Keep up regular weed control, reduce heavy shade, prune off dead wood, and follow a proper spraying schedule. Consistent upkeep helps trees withstand pest stress and yield well later.
ga: Kwɛmɔ jwɛi lɛ anɔ daa. Tsɔɔmɔ shade ni tsii lɛ nɔ Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei ni egboi lɛ. ni onyiɛ gbɛjianɔtoo ni sa ni akɛshwieɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ akwɛ tsei anɔ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe haomɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai yɛ sɛɛ mli yɛ amɛshihilɛ mli.

english: Why do people recommend planting fast-growing plantains alongside young tree crops like oranges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ yɛ tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo tamɔ citrus lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young tree seedlings are delicate and easily scorched by direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide temporary shade and retain soil moisture, protecting the young trees until they grow strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii waaa ni hulu la shãa amɛ oya. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Buu tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ amɛtsui shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he.

english: When is the right time to cut back plantains that are shading my main fruit trees?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ afo plantains ni haa mi aduawai tsei titrii lɛ ahe ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: You should trim or remove the plantains once your fruit trees have developed a thick stem and established their own branch canopy, usually around 3 to 4 years. At this stage, the fruit trees need direct sunlight to blossom and yield well.
ga: Esa akɛ ofolɔ loo ojie plantains lɛ beni aduawai tso lɛ yɛ shishigbɛ ni mli tse ni eyɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ eniji. Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ aaafee afii 3 kɛyashi 4. Yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, hulu la he miihia tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Will planting plantains and orange trees on the same plot cause their roots to fight for nutrients?
ga: Ani plantains kɛ citrus tsei ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ abɔi niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ?

english: If you leave sufficient space between them, they will not compete harmfuly. Plantain roots tend to stay near the soil surface, while orange tree roots grow deeper, allowing both crops to feed at different soil levels.
ga: Kɛji oshi gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ amɛteŋ Amɛjeee akaŋshii ni yɔɔ oshara. Plantain shishifãi lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛhi shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. yɛ be mli ni ŋmei tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei srɔtoi enyɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ srɔtoi anɔ.

english: How can I earn an income while waiting several years for my newly planted orange trees to produce fruit?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná shika yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ mi-orange tso hee ni midu lɛ ni ewo yibii afii babaoo lɛ?

english: You can intercrop with quick-yielding crops like plantains, cassava, or vegetables between the tree rows. These shorter-term crops produce food and cash during the early years before your main tree crops mature.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu tsei ni woɔ yibii oya tamɔ plantains, cassava loo aduawai yɛ tsei ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli nɛɛ haa niyenii kɛ shika baa yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli. Dani otsei titrii ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ

english: How long can tree crops like oranges continue to produce food on the same piece of land?
ga: Be enyiɛ tso ko tamɔ sitrus baanyɛ awo niyenii yɛ he kome?

english: With good farm management, organic fertilizer, and weed control, fruit trees like oranges can remain healthy and produce good harvests on the same land for 15 to 20 years or more.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akwɛ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, akɛ tsofai fɔji wo mli, ni akwɛ jwɛi anɔ lɛ, aduawai tsei tamɔ citrus baanyɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo yibii yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afii 15 kɛyashi 20 loo nɔ ni fe nakai.

english: How do I balance planting quick crops for fast money versus long-term tree crops for my future?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafee ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ oya koni maná shika oya kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ be kakadaŋŋ kɛha miwɔsɛɛ be lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ?

english: A practical farm plan combines both. Quick crops like plantains give you continuous food and income for daily expenses, while long-term tree crops act like a savings plan that provides steady yield for decades to secure your future.
ga: Okwaafoi agbɛjianɔtoo ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii lɛ kɛ enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ feɔ ekome. Nibii ni aduɔ oya tamɔ plantains haa onáa niyenii ni yaa nɔ kɛ shika ni okɛbaatsu daa gbi shika he nii. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsei ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ shikatoo gbɛjianɔtoo ni haa shika ni anáa daa afii nyɔŋmai abɔ koni ekɛkwɛ owɔsɛɛ be nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my fruit tree seedlings seem to grow so slowly during their first year in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso yibii lɛ dumɔwui lɛ daraa blɛoo yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi ni amɛyɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During the first year, the tree focuses most of its energy underground to build a deep, strong root system. Once those roots are well established, the visible trunk and leaf growth will speed up dramatically.
ga: Yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli lɛ, tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni ekɛma shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa. Kɛ nakai shishifãi lɛ ema shi shiŋŋ lɛ, tsei kɛ baai ni anaa lɛ adalɛ baafee oya kwraa.

english: How does shade from nurse crops help young plants survive hot dry periods?
ga: Bɔ ni shade ni jɛɔ tsei ni kwɛɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui ni amɛ hiɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ be mli, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi.

english: Shade keeps the soil cool and reduces water evaporation from the ground and leaves. This creates a moist micro-environment that keeps sensitive young seedlings from wilting during hot weather.
ga: Shade yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa shihilɛ bibioo ko ni mli edɔ ni tsiɔ dumɔwui ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ waa lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbo yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Does pruning lower branches on young fruit trees help them grow better in the long run?
ga: Ani tsei bibii ni woɔ yibii lɛ aniji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli?

english: Yes, removing weak lower branches directs the tree's energy upward to form a sturdy main trunk and healthy upper canopy, which improves air flow and makes fruit harvesting easier in the future.
ga: Hɛɛ, shishigbɛ niji ni bɛ hewalɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ yaa hiɛ koni ekɛfee tso titri ni mli wa kɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ, ni ehaa aduawai akpamɔ feɔ mlɛo wɔsɛɛ.

english: Why should I leave dead leaves and stems around the base of my plantain plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi baai kɛ tsei ni egboi yɛ mi-plantain lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ?

english: Leaving organic matter around the base acts as mulch. It suppresses weeds, retains moisture in the soil, and slowly decomposes into natural compost that feeds the plant roots.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni ashiɔ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ baatsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekpaa jwɛi Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa tsei shishifãi lɛ hewalɛ.

english: How many years can a cocoa tree keep producing pods after I plant it?
ga: Cacao tso ko baanyɛ ajie ŋmeii enyiɛ kɛji midu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Unlike quick food crops like maize that die after one harvest, cocoa is a long-term tree crop that can live and produce fruits for 30 to 40 years or more if you care for it well.
ga: Cocoa ji tso ko ni hiɔ shi daa ni ebaanyɛ ewo yibii afii 30 kɛyashi 40 loo nɔ ni fe nakai kɛji okwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ tamɔɔɔ niyenii ni ayeɔ oya tamɔ ŋmãa ni gboɔ yɛ kpamɔ kome sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How do I measure the right distance between my crops when planting if I do not have a measuring tape?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masusu gbɛ ni sa ni kã ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ lɛ he kɛ́ midu nii? Kɛji akɛ obɛ tsɔne ni akɛsusuɔ nii ahe lɛ?

english: You can use traditional physical measures like arm stretches, full strides (paces), or a measured piece of rope marked with knots to ensure your trees are evenly spaced without crowding each other.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ kusum mli gbɔmɔtsoŋ gbɛjianɔtoi tamɔ oniji ni oootsɔ mli, nyiɛmɔ ni fa (step), loo kpãa ni akɛ kpãa ebɔ he, ni asusu he lɛ atsu nii koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ otsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe ebɔ he pɛpɛɛpɛ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe.

english: How many cocoa trees am I supposed to plant on one acre of land?
ga: Cocoa tsei enyiɛ esa akɛ madu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni dalɛ ji acre kome nɔ?

english: With standard spacing of about 3 meters by 3 meters (around 10 feet apart), one acre of land usually holds around 435 cocoa trees so that each tree gets enough soil food and sunlight.
ga: Akɛni sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ ji aaafee mitai 3 x mitai 3 (aaafee ninetalɔi 10) hewɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, acre kome mli ŋtayaa tsei aaafee 435 yɔɔ, bɔni afee ni tso fɛɛ tso aná shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very tender leaves and shallow roots that burn and dry out easily under harsh sunlight; they require temporary shade trees or plantains to protect them until they grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii waa kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shãa oya ni egbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei loo tsei bibii ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo be kukuoo ko he miihia amɛ koni ebu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa.

english: What short-term crops can I plant to get quick money while waiting for my cocoa trees to grow?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni heɔ be kukuoo manyɛ makwɛ koni maná shika oya be mli ni mimɛɔ ni cacao tsei lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: You can intercrop short-term 'casual' crops like plantain, cassava, or vegetables between young cocoa trees; these give you quick food and income during the 3 to 4 years you wait for cocoa to produce.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu be kukuoo ‘casual’ tsei tamɔ plantains, cassava loo aduawai yɛ cacao tsei bibii ateŋ. Enɛɛmɛi haa onáa niyenii kɛ shika oya yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 ni omɛɛɔ ni afee kookoo lɛ mli.

english: What time of the day is best for me to transplant my nursery seedlings into the main farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbi mli be ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha mi akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ aya ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli?

english: It is best to plant early in the morning or late in the afternoon when the sun is not hot, so the young plants do not lose water quickly and suffer from transplant shock.
ga: Esa akɛ adu leebi loo shwane mli. ni ji be ni hulu lɛ edɔɔɔ No hewɔ lɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ efooo oya ni amɛnaa transplant shock.

english: Why should I cut off extra branches from my cocoa trees when they start growing tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji krokomɛi ni fata mi-cacao tso lɛ he beni ebɔi shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes unnecessary branches, allowing air and sunlight to move freely through the tree, which prevents diseases and directs the tree's energy into growing big pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la tsɔɔ tsei lɛ amli oya. Enɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ helai anaa ni ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni etsɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is lacking important soil nutrients like nitrogen, or the soil is too full of water, which chokes the plant roots and prevents them from feeding.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ sũ mli niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, loo sũ lɛ mli nu fa tsɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛhaaa niyenii.

english: This is caused by a fungal infection called Black Pod disease, which spreads quickly during heavy rains when the farm is too dark and wet without enough sunlight.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela, ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli ni ŋmɔji amli ewo duŋ tsɔ ni edɔ ni hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my soil is good enough to grow cocoa before I clear the land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ kookoo nɔ dani majie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Good cocoa soil should be deep, dark in color, crumbly to touch, and well-drained so water does not stand on it for days after heavy rain.
ga: Esa akɛ kookoo shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ afee nɔ ni mli kwɔ, ni ehiɛ edɔ, ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji mɔ ko ta he. kɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ Enɛ ji koni nu akamɔ mli gbii babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ.

english: Why does water drain away so fast from my field after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu hoɔ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Sandy soils have large spaces between particles that allow water to pass through quickly without staying near the roots. Adding organic matter like manure or compost acts like a sponge, helping the soil hold onto water longer so your crops can drink.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ yɛ gbɛjegbɛi wuji ni yɔɔ nibii bibii ni haa nu hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ mli oya ni ebɛŋkɛɛɛ shishifãi lɛ ateŋ. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ koni onibii lɛ anu.

english: Is it bad for my crops if rainwater stays trapped on top of the soil for days?
ga: Ani ebaana hewalɛ gbonyo yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo?

english: Yes, standing water drowns plant roots by blocking air from reaching them. This causes the roots to rot and leaves to turn yellow, so soil needs a balance where it holds moisture without becoming completely flooded.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nu ni damɔ shi lɛ shwieɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni etsĩɔ naa koni ekashɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ gbɛ ni baaha enyɛ ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni nu akafo mli tsɔ.

english: How can I keep moisture in the soil longer without constantly watering my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni mikɛ nu haaa mitsei lɛ be fɛɛ be?

english: Covering the soil around your crops with dry grass, leaves, or crop leaves—a practice called mulching—blocks direct sunlight. This keeps the soil cool and stops water from evaporating into the air quickly.
ga: Mulching around Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi ni egbi, baai, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ahe baai—nifeemɔ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ mulching—baaye abua ni hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ atsĩ onibii lɛ anaa. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: What causes the soil surface around my crops to get hard and crusty like concrete?
ga: Nɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle mihe lɛ feɔ nɔ Miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wa ni amɛhe ewo ŋmɔtɔ tamɔ kɔnkrit.

english: Heavy clay soils become hard and form a crust when they dry out under hot sun. Mixing compost into the topsoil breaks up the hard crust and allows both water and roots to penetrate easily.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ waɔ ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ egbi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii futu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, efiteɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ, ni ehaa nu kɛ shishifãi fɛɛ boteɔ mli mlɛo.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Rolling leaves is the plant's natural defense against heat. By curling up, the leaf reduces its exposed surface area to conserve moisture when the soil is drying out during hot hours.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ lɛ, baai lɛ baa amɛhe nɔ koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my plants turning yellow and dying off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi lɛ?

english: When a plant does not get enough water or nutrients from the soil, it sacrifices its older, lower leaves to send the remaining food and water up to the young, growing leaves at the top.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ekɛ baai bibii shaa afɔle koni ekɛ niyenii kɛ nu ni eshwɛ lɛ amaje baai bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my young seedlings wilt and fall over right after I transplant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni midu amɛ lɛ?

english: Transplanting damages tiny root hairs that take in water, causing transplant shock. Watering seedlings right after planting and shading them for a few days gives roots time to recover.
ga: Nɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fiteɔ yitsɔi bibii lɛ. ni boteɔ nu lɛ mli ni ehaa dumɔwui ni adu lɛ lɛ ahe feɔ shoo Kɛ́ afɔ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni adu amɛ gbii fioo komɛi lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ náa be ni amɛkɛbaatsa amɛhe.

english: What can I use to improve my soil if I cannot afford expensive commercial fertilizers?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mikɛfee mishikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ? Ni kɛji akɛ minyɛɛɛ mahe jarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa hu?

english: You can use decomposed animal manure, crop waste, or compost. These natural inputs feed the soil organisms, add essential nutrients, and improve how well the soil stores water.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo, ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ atsu nii. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii nɛɛ haa wala ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ hewalɛ. Kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛ bɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ afata he

english: Why do my crops stop growing big even when I give them plenty of water?
