ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nu babaoo moŋ lɛ?

english: Water alone is not enough for plant growth; crops also need food nutrients from the soil like nitrogen and phosphorus. If the soil lacks nutrients, water alone cannot make the crop yield well.
ga: Nu pɛ kɛkɛ faaa kɛha tsei adalɛ. Tsei hu taoɔ niyenii kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ Nu pɛ nyɛŋ ajie yibii kpakpai.

english: How does applying water slowly directly to the stem help crops better than splashing water all over?
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ blɛoo Te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eye ebua ŋmɔshi nibii jogbaŋŋ fe nu ni akɛshwieɔ he fɛɛ he?

english: Direct root watering places water exactly where the roots can absorb it, preventing water waste through evaporation and keeping crop leaves dry to avoid leaf fungal diseases.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa nu lɛ yaa he ko ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Etsiɔ nu ni laajeɔ lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. ni okɛ tso lɛ baai lɛ agbi koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akabote baai lɛ amli.

english: Out of ten seeds I plant in a row, why do only about five of them grow into strong crops?
ga: Kɛjɛ dumɔwui nyɔŋma ni midu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui enumɔ pɛ kwɛ̃ ni amɛbatsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa?

english: Not all seeds survive because some lack enough moisture, get eaten by soil insects, or are planted too deep. Using certified high-quality seeds and planting at the right depth ensures more of your seeds germinate and survive.
ga: Jeee dumɔwui fɛɛ hiɔ shi ejaakɛ ekomɛi bɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Kplukai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ loo aduɔ mli tsɔ Kɛ okɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ odaseyeli, ni hi jogbaŋŋ tsu nii ni okɛdu yɛ he ni sa lɛ, ebaaha odumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why should I pull out some healthy young maize seedlings if I planted them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmãa bibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When plants grow too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving all of them small and weak. Removing a few plants gives the remaining ones enough space to grow strong and yield big cobs.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ baa. Tsei komɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tsei ni eshwɛ lɛ náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees burning and turning brown in the afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have soft leaves that easily dry out under direct heat. Planting nurse crops like plantains next to them provides living shade that cools the cocoa plants until they grow strong enough to withstand full sunlight.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni kɛ́ akɛ amɛ wo la mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, amɛgbiɔ oya. Nurse tsei ni miida tamɔ plantains ni bɛŋkɛ Ehaa cacao tso lɛ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa waa bɔ ni sa ni enyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and drop off the plant before producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences heat stress, irregular watering, or pest attacks, which prevents pollination. Ensuring steady soil moisture and protecting plants from extreme heat keeps the flowers healthy so they turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli be fɛɛ be loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tsiɔ pollination naa Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa kɛ tsei ahebuu kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa bɔni afee ni amɛtsɔmɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of big leaves but very small fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei woɔ baai wuji shi amɛwoɔ yibii bibii waa lɛ?

english: When a plant puts too much energy into growing branches and leaves, it leaves little energy for the fruit. Pruning away the small extra stems allows the plant to direct its nutrients into growing bigger fruits.
ga: Kɛ tsei kɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsu nii ni amɛkɛwo tsei niji kɛ baai lɛ Tso lɛ jieɔ hewalɛ fioo pɛ kɛyaa aduawai lɛ amli. ŋmeii bibii ni afoɔ Kɛ́ ashi lɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo yibii wuji.

english: Why do some of my cassava stem cuttings fail to grow after I plant them in the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ beni midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava cuttings fail if they lose too much moisture before planting or if the soil lacks moisture. Using fresh stems, planting them at a correct angle, and planting right when the rains begin helps them take root quickly.
ga: Yucca tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ baafee nɔ ni ehiii kɛji amɛjie ŋmɔtɔ babaoo dani adu loo kɛji ŋmɔtɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ni akɛ tsei heei tsuɔ nii Dumɔ yɛ he ni sa Ni aduɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ shishifãi oya.

english: How does growing cowpeas or beans together with my maize help my crop grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Legumes like beans pull natural nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil as plant food. This enriches the soil for the maize growing beside it, helping you get a better yield without relying entirely on chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ tsei aniyenii. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo kɛhaa abele ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni onáa yibii kpakpai ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ ohe afɔ̃ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ nɔ kwraa.

english: How can using fertilizer on my farm help me make enough money to pay my children's school fees?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛaatsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni maná shika ni fa bɔ ni sa ni mikɛwo mibii lɛ askulyaa he nyɔmɔ?

english: Fertilizer gives crops essential nutrients that make them grow faster, resist diseases, and yield more harvest per acre. More harvested bags mean higher market sales, giving you extra profit for household needs and education.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ náa niyenii ni he hiaa ni haa amɛdaraa oya, amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ helai, ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo yɛ acre kome mli. Baagi ni akpaa lɛ babaoo tsɔɔ jarayeli ni yaa hiɛ. Enɛ haa onáa sɛɛnamɔi krokomɛi kɛha shia kɛ nikasemɔ he hiamɔ nii.

english: How do I know the exact time my maize is ready for harvest so it doesn't spoil in the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmãa lɛ eshɛ ni abaakpa? No hewɔ lɛ, egbooo yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Maize is ready to harvest when the leaves turn completely brown, the husks dry out, and the grains feel hard when pressed with a fingernail. Harvesting at this stage prevents mold and bird damage.
ga: Abɛi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛ́ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔtɔ kwraa, ŋmɔtɔi lɛ egbi, ni ŋmɔtɔi lɛ nuɔ he akɛ amɛhe wa kɛji akɛ akɛ nine ŋmei mii nɔ. Nikpamɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii kɛ okpoi fiteɔ nii.

english: How can I store my harvested maize safely so insects don't destroy it before I can sell it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ ato shweshweeshwe? Enɛ ji koni kooloi akafite lɛ dani abaanyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ.

english: Drying the grains completely in the sun and storing them in airtight, hermetic bags suffocates insects and blocks moisture, keeping your crop fresh so you can sell it when prices are highest.
ga: Dumɔwui ni agbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni akɛtoɔ kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe, ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni onibii lɛ feɔ ehee. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ ohɔ̃ɔ lɛ yɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ fe fɛɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it important for me to break up hard soil before planting my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo shikpɔŋ ni edɔ mli dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Just like humans need air to breathe, plant roots need air trapped in the soil to stay alive and absorb nutrients. Loosening hard soil creates spaces for air and rainwater to reach the roots easily so the crop can grow strong.
ga: Taakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he hiaa adesai koni amɛmu lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Tse shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni emɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi ni amɛhe niyenii mli hewalɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ajieɔ lɛ haa gbɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ nu koni eshɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe oya koni tsei lɛ adalɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants yellow and die when floodwater stays on my field for several days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egboɔ kɛ́ nu afua lɛ ta miŋmɔji lɛ amli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: When water sits on your land for too long, it pushes all the air out of the soil. Without air in the root zone, the roots effectively suffocate and rot, which turns the leaves yellow and kills the plant.
ga: Kɛ nu hi oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shishifã lɛ he lɛ, shishifãi lɛ baafo ni amɛbaafite jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni efite tso lɛ.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to heap soft soil into high mounds when planting yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔbua shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ naa wɔwoɔ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ amli kɛ́ wɔmiidu sweet potatoes lɛ?

english: Heaping loose soil into mounds creates plenty of tiny air pockets and makes the soil soft. This gives the yam tubers plenty of room and oxygen to swell and grow very large without fighting hard earth.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni etse ehe lɛ ni akɛaawo gɔŋ mli lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii babaoo baa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ blɛoo. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ náa he ko kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛdara waa ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛkɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa akawu.

english: Why do my crops grow poorly in soil that has been trampled flat by cattle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsinai nyɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Heavy trampling squashes the soil together, squeezing out all the natural air pockets. Without air in the soil, plant roots cannot easily spread out or drink in nutrients.
ga: tsɔne ni akɛnyiɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni tsii lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ekome ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui lɛ fɛɛ ajie. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tso shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã loo amɛnu niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: If maize plants are crowded together, they end up fighting each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and air. Giving each plant proper spacing ensures it gets enough fresh air and sunlight to produce big cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ, amɛbaatswa amɛhe adafi koni amɛná hulu la ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛaaha ŋmãa lɛ eko fɛɛ eko teŋ lɛ haa enáa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaa ŋmãa wuji.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds from my farm even when there is enough rain for all plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ bɔ ni sa kɛha tsei lɛ fɛɛ moŋ?

english: Weeds are fast growers that steal air space, light, and nutrients away from your crops. Clearing weeds ensures your main crop gets all the air, light, and soil food it needs to yield well.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni juɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ, la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why does pruning excess branches on my cocoa trees help stop pod diseases?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni tsei niji ni fa fe nine ni afolɔ yɛ kookoo tsei anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ pod hela naa lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the middle of the tree so fresh air and sunlight can flow through. Good air circulation dries off wet leaves and pods quickly, which prevents fungal rot like black pod disease from spreading.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli lɛ, egbeleɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ hulu la atsɔ mli. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ haa baai ni efɔ kɛ ŋmeii lɛ gĩɔ oya. Enɛ baaye abua ni fungal rot tamɔ black pod hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: How does leaving open pathways between crop rows protect my leaves from spoiling?
ga: Te gbɛ ni yɔɔ tsei akutsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ ni ooogbele lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni mibaai lɛ akafite lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Open pathways allow natural breeze to blow through the entire farm. This wind moves humid air away and dries rain off the crop leaves, keeping leaf-spot diseases from attacking your plants.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi ni agbele naa lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ nɛɛ tswaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli efɔ kɛyaa ni ehaa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ amli lɛ gĩɔ. Tsi leaf spot hela lɛ naa koni ekatutua otsei lɛ.

english: Besides water and manure, what other main things do my crops depend on to produce a good harvest?
ga: Kɛfata nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ Mɛɛ nibii krokomɛi ni he hiaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ damɔ nɔ koni ewo yibii kpakpai?

english: Crops need a balance of four main things to thrive: direct sunlight for energy, water for transport, air (both above ground for leaves and below ground for roots), and plant nutrients from the soil.
ga: Nibii titrii ejwɛ he miihia tsei koni amɛdara: hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha hewalɛ; Okɛ nu, kɔɔyɔɔ (ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ kɛha baai kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi fɛɛ kɛha shishifãi) ​​kɛ tsei aniyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aya.

english: How do crop roots actually take in food from the soil to grow?
ga: Te tsei shishifãi lɛ feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛheɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Crop roots use a combination of soil moisture and oxygen to absorb dissolved minerals from the earth. The air in the soil gives the roots the energy they need to pump those nutrients up into the rest of the plant.
ga: Tse shishifãi kɛ sũ mli nu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni akɛfee ekome tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛjie sũ mli nibii ni mli edɔ kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkɛ nakai niyenii lɛ aya tso lɛ fãi krokomɛi lɛ amli.

english: How do I know when my plantains are ready to harvest so they don't spoil in the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni plantain lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa ni no hewɔ lɛ egboŋ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Plantains are ready for harvest when the fruit fingers become plump and rounded, losing their sharp edges. Harvesting them while still firm and green allows them to be transported without crushing and prevents loss to pests, theft, or over-ripening.
ga: Plantains lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni aduawai lɛ aniji lɛ egbɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ laajeɔ. Nikpamɔ be mli ni eyɛ shiŋŋ lolo ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ haa anyɛɔ akɛyaa he fɛɛ he ni akumɔɔɔ ni etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii, juu, loo shweremɔ ni fe nine lɛ naa.

english: Why do my plantains ripen and rot so fast after I cut them down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ shwereɔ ni egboɔ oya beni mifo lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Once cut from the plant, plantains produce a natural gas that speeds up ripening. Exposing them to direct sunlight or hot weather makes this happen faster, so keeping harvested plantains in a cool, shaded area slows down spoilage.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afo kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, Plantains lɛ jieɔ adebɔɔ mli la ni haa tso lɛ shwereɔ oya. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ wo hulu la loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaha enɛ aba mli oya. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ ni akɛtoɔ he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ baaye abua ni amɛfitemɔ asɛɛ afo.

english: Is it better to harvest all my crops at once or harvest them bit by bit?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ makpã miŋmɔshi nii lɛ fɛɛ shikome loo makpã mli fioo fioo?

english: Harvesting gradually allows you to sell crops at peak freshness over a longer period, securing steady income and avoiding losses if buyers or transport are not available all at once.
ga: Nibii ni akpaa fiofio lɛ haa onyɛɔ ohɔ̃ɔ onibii lɛ yɛ be mli ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ be kakadaŋŋ. Kwɛmɔ shika ni onáa lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ fitemɔ he kɛji mɔ ni heɔ loo mɔ ni kɛ nibii majeɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana lɛ shikome.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant plantains alongside my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ wo mi ŋaa akɛ madu plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are fragile and burn under intense sunlight. Plantains grow very fast with broad leaves, acting as natural shade umbrellas that protect cocoa seedlings and keep the soil moist during their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya waa kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ. Amɛtsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni buɔ kookoo dumɔwui ahe ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Planting plantains about 3 meters (10 feet) apart gives each stem enough room to receive adequate sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to larger stems and bigger fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ adu plantains lɛ aaafee mitai 3 (naji 10) lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ená hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi wuji kɛ aduawai akui wuji baa.

english: Why should I wait for the rains to start before planting my suckers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ akpa dani madu tsei lɛ?

english: Young plantain suckers require continuous moisture to establish healthy new roots. Planting during the dry season without irrigation leads to the suckers drying out and dying.
ga: Plantain dumɔwui lɛ taoɔ nu ni mli edɔ daa koni amɛfee shishifãi heei ni mli wa. Kɛ́ adu yɛ fɛ̃i be mli ni nu shwieee nɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi.

english: Why does my plantain stool produce so many small shoots around the main stem, and should I remove them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain poop lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii babaoo ni ebɔle tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ he lɛ, ni ani esa akɛ majie amɛ?

english: The small shoots (suckers) compete with the mother plant for food and water. Pruning away excess suckers—leaving only one main plant, one medium sucker, and one small shoot—helps the main tree produce larger bunches.
ga: Tso bibii (tso lɛ) kɛ tso nyɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Tso lɛ mli tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ Enɛ haa tso titri kome pɛ, tso ni dalɛ ji teŋgbɛ, kɛ tso bibioo kome pɛ shwɛɔ koni eye ebua tso titri lɛ ni ekɛ tsei wuji aba.

english: What causes the leaves of my plantain trees to turn yellow and produce small bunches?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi plantain baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiifee ŋmeii bibii?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the soil lacks key nutrients like nitrogen or potassium, or that the soil is too dry. Applying organic manure or balanced fertilizer helps restore dark green leaves and increases fruit size.
ga: Bei pii lɛ baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen loo potassium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha aduawai lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my heavy plantain trees fall over before the fruit is mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui ni tsii lɛ miigbee shi dani aduawai kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: As plantain bunches grow heavy, weak root systems or strong winds can pull the plant down. Using strong wooden props to support the main stem prevents the tree from snapping or falling before full maturity.
ga: Beni plantain jwɛi lɛ da waa Shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala tso lɛ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni wa tsu nii ni akɛfi tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakumɔ loo ekagbee shi dani eshɛ shweremɔ he.

english: What can I do with surplus crops that I cannot immediately sell in the market?
ga: Mɛni mifeɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa fe nine ni minyɛɛɛ mahɔ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Crops like plantain and cassava can be processed into shelf-stable goods such as dried chips or flour, which prevents crop loss, extends storage life, and allows you to sell when market prices improve.
ga: Abaanyɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains kɛ cassava nibii ni anyɛɔ akwɛɔ nɔ tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi loo ashikishaŋ. ni tsiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ naa Ha shĩa lɛ shihilɛ aya hiɛ ni eye ebua bo ni ohɔ̃ɔ be mli ni jara lɛ hi fe tsutsu lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to intense heat and direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantain or cassava grown beside them early on to protect their leaves from burning and keep the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Amɛmiisumɔ ni adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo cassava yɛ amɛmasɛi. ekome kɛjɛ shishijee Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkashã ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning pale green or yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaahi shi ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing maize leaves are usually a sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize needs to build healthy green leaves. Adding animal manure or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps restore their dark green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baa ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ená baa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha amɛhe su ni mli kwɔ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why does my farm produce much smaller harvests if I plant maize on the exact same plot every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kwraa kɛji midu ŋmãa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Maize takes specific nutrients out of the soil every season. Planting it repeatedly in the same spot uses up those nutrients completely, causing smaller harvests unless you rotate the field with leguminous crops like beans or let the land rest.
ga: Abɛi jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Kɛ́ adu shii abɔ yɛ he kome lɛ, ekɛ nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ tsuɔ nii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ fioo. No ji ja otsake shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni okɛdu ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo oha shikpɔŋ lɛ jɔɔ ehe.

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans make my soil richer for other crops later?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo aha tsei krokomɛi yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: Cowpea and bean plants pull nitrogen from the air and store it in small bumps on their roots. When the plant roots rot after harvest, they release this natural fertilizer directly into the soil for the next crop to use.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ pea tsei lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ amli kɛ́ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ fite yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Amɛjieɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ koni ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi kɛtsu nii.

english: Cassava naturally drops its leaves during long dry spells to save water and stay alive. The roots under the soil remain healthy and will start growing fresh leaves once the rains return.
ga: Cassava baagbee shi yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ehi wala mli. Shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ mli wa lolo ni amɛbaabɔi baai heei feemɔ kɛji nugbɔ ku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ.

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that do not grow deep into the ground. When heavy rain softens the soil, the weight of the fruit bunch combined with strong winds easily pulls the roots out of the mud.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni edaaa kɛboteɔ sũ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo. Yibii akuu lɛ tsiimɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa fata he lɛ gbalaa shishifãi lɛ kɛjɛɔ muji lɛ mli oya.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the branches before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ dani ebatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather becomes extremely hot or when the plant experiences sudden dry periods without enough water. Extreme heat prevents the flowers from pollinating and setting fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na be ni nu egbi trukaa ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛkawo yibii.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves toward the sun to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground where diseases spread easily and ensures the plant gets maximum sunlight.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã hulu lɛ he koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmeii wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa hulu la babaoo

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies feeding on them. These insects suck the juices out of young leaves, causing them to twist, deform, and stunt the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai bibii amli. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ srɔtoi, amɛfiteɔ ni amɛtsiɔ tsei adalɛ naa.

english: Why do fewer weeds grow on my field when I plant groundnuts or egusi melons between my main crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi shwereɔ fioo yɛ miŋmɔji amli kɛ́ midu ŋmeii loo egusi melon yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Spreading crops like groundnuts or egusi melons grow wide leaves that carpet the ground completely. This blocks sunlight from reaching hidden weed seeds in the soil, preventing them from sprouting and competing with your crops.
ga: Tsei tamɔ ŋmei loo melon egusi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa lɛ haa baai ni mli kwɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kwraa lɛ baa. Enɛ baatsi hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ jwɛi dumɔwui ni akɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ahe. Enɛ ji koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛkɛ oŋmɔshi nibii akaye akaŋ.

english: Why do my maize plants need the silky hairs hanging out of the cob to make corn kernels?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tso lɛ yɛ yitsɔi ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni fĩɔ ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ he koni ekɛfee ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: The silk hairs catch pollen dust blown by the wind from the top flowers of the maize plant. Each silk strand is connected to a single spot on the cob, and when pollen lands on it, it fertilizes that spot so a kernel of corn can grow.
ga: Silk yitsɔi lɛ mɔ̃ɔ pollen sũ ni kɔɔyɔɔ tswaa kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ. Akɛ siliki kpãa lɛ eko fɛɛ eko tsa he kome yɛ ŋtayaa lɛ nɔ. ni kɛ́ pollen gbee nɔ lɛ Ebaafɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli bɔni afee ni ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why does my pawpaw tree produce flowers every season but never bears any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ papaya tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi daa be shi amɛwooo yibii kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Pawpaw trees can be male, female, or both. Male trees only produce pollen to fertilize other trees, so they drop their flowers and will never produce fruit themselves.
ga: Pawpaw tsei baanyɛ afee nuu, yoo, loo amɛ fɛɛ. Tsei ni ji hii lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi pɛ ni tsei krokomɛi kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli, no hewɔ lɛ amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii kɔkɔɔkɔ.

english: Tomato flowers need bees or wind to shake their pollen inside the flower so it can form fruit. If it is too hot, too dry, or there are no insects around to disturb the flower, the unfertilized flower dies and drops off.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii ahe miihia ni ŋmeii loo kɔɔyɔɔ atswa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ koni amɛwo yibii. Kɛji edɔ tsɔ, edɔ tsɔ, loo kɛji kooloi komɛi bɛ ni gbaa fɔfɔi lɛ anaa lɛ, Fɔfɔi ni afɔɔɔ amɛ fɔ lɛ baagboi ni amɛbaagbee shi.

english: How does putting fertilizer on the ground actually make my maize cobs bigger?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ daraa?

english: Fertilizer acts like food for the plant. The roots drink it up with water, and the leaves use sunlight to transform those nutrients into energy, which the plant uses to build bigger and fuller cobs.
ga: Fertilizer tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsei aniyenii. Shishifãi lɛ kɛ nu nuɔ lɛ. Ni baai lɛ kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛtsakeɔ nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ amɛfeɔ hewalɛ. ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: When a crop does not get enough food or nitrogen from the soil, it takes nutrients from its older, lower leaves to feed the young green leaves at the top, causing the old leaves to turn yellow and drop.
ga: Kɛ tsei nine shɛɛɛ niyenii loo nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Egbalaa niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ baai bibii lɛ amli ni ekɛhaa baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ. Enɛ haa baai momoi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow tall and skinny with very few fruits when I plant them under big shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ ni ewoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ beni midu lɛ yɛ tso agbo ko ni yɔɔ hulutsoo shishi lɛ?

english: Crops use direct sunlight as fuel to make their own food. In the shade, the plant stretches upward searching for light instead of using its energy to produce flowers and fruit.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ tsofa ni amɛkɛfeɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ niyenii. Yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, tsei baagbala amɛhe kɛya ŋwɛi koni amɛyatao la yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛwo fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up and look limp during the hot afternoon even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: In extreme heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it. Curled leaves are the plant's way of protecting itself to reduce water loss until the air cools down.
ga: Yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa mli lɛ Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Baai ni abɔle ehe lɛ ji gbɛ ni tso lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe he koni nu ni efiteɔ lɛ aba shi kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: How does a piece of seed yam buried underground know when to start sprouting?
ga: Te afeɔ tɛŋŋ ni sweet potato dumɔwui ni afu yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ leɔ be ni esa akɛ amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Seed yams have dormant eye buds that wake up when they feel warmth and moisture in the soil, which signals to the plant that conditions are right to send up shoots.
ga: Atomɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ hiŋmɛii ni ekpa. Eteɔ shi kɛji enu dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i he yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ leɔ akɛ shihilɛi ni sa kɛha lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Does it really matter which direction I point the buds when planting cassava stem cuttings?
ga: Ani gbɛ ni mikɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ kɛ́ midu yucca ŋmeii lɛ he miihia diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, because cassava stem buds naturally grow pointing upward toward the sun. Planting them upside down forces the new shoots to bend around to find light, wasting plant energy and delaying growth.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ daa kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛyaa hulu lɛ he. Kɛ́ adu ŋwɛi ŋwɛi lɛ, ebaaha tsei heei akumɔ shi koni amɛna la. efiteɔ tsei ahewalɛ ni ehaa amɛdalɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster than the maize seeds I carefully planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛ hiɛdɔɔ du lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to survive hard conditions, so their roots spread aggressively to steal water and food from the soil before young farm crops can reach them.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ amɛshwãa oya koni amɛju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani okwaayeli mli nibii bibii lɛ ashɛ amɛhe.

english: I want to start growing ginger on my farm, but how do I know if my land is good for it?
ga: Miisumɔ ni mabɔi ŋmei dumɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli. Shi te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi loo ehiii?

english: Ginger grows best in rich, well-drained loamy soil that is high in organic matter. It needs warm conditions and loose soil so the underground roots can expand easily without rotting.
ga: Ginger kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni sũ yɔɔ mli ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni ená kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse bɔni afee ni shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo ni amɛfiteee.

english: How can I tell when my ginger crop is fully mature and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-ginger tso lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Ginger is usually ready to harvest when the leaves start turning yellow, drying up, and falling over, which typically happens around 8 to 10 months after planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji baai lɛ bɔi ŋmɔŋ, amɛgbi, ni amɛgbee shi, ni bei pii lɛ ebaa yɛ aaafee nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 10 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ.

english: What causes ginger roots to rot in the ground before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani abaanyɛ akpa amɛ?

english: Root rot happens when the soil retains too much water and lacks proper drainage. Excess water allows fungal and bacterial diseases to infect the roots, causing them to turn soft and decay.
ga: Shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo tsɔ ni nu ni hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ bɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Nu babaoo baaha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ bacteria helai aba shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ.

english: Why are my crops giving me lower yields and smaller harvests than they used to in past years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo ni amɛkpaa nii fioo fe afii ni eho lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Yields drop over time when continuous farming depletes the natural nutrients in the soil without being replenished by compost, manure, or fertilizers, or due to hidden pest damage.
ga: Yibiiwoo baa shi yɛ be mli ni okwaayeli nifeemɔi ni yaa nɔ lɛ fiteɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he, loo yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ ahewɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow weak and thin when I plant seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with one another for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, leaving every plant undernourished and underdeveloped.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ náaa niyenii kpakpa ni amɛdaraaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does adding animal manure or compost help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛfataa he lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Manure and compost add essential nutrients back into the dirt, improve soil structure so roots can breathe, and help the ground hold moisture during dry periods.
ga: Manure kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kuɔ sɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii feɔ jogbaŋŋ koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ amu. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ

english: Weeds grow faster than most crops and aggressively steal nutrients, water, and sunlight from the soil, effectively starving your main plants.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei babaoo ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye onibii titrii lɛ.

english: Why do crop prices drop so low in the market right around the main harvest season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe jara baa shi yɛ jara nɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be titri lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During harvest season, many farmers bring large amounts of the same crop to market at the same time. This high supply gives buyers the power to pay lower prices.
ga: yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be lɛ mli Okwaafoi babaoo kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ babaoo baa jara nɔ yɛ be kome mli. Nɛkɛ nibii ni fa babaoo nɛɛ haa mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛwoɔ jara ni baa shi.

english: How can I keep my harvested ginger fresh while I search for buyers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-ginger ni mikpa lɛ ahi shi ehee yɛ be mli ni mitaoɔ mɔ ni baahe lɛ?

english: You should gently clean the soil off the ginger roots and store them in a cool, dry, well-ventilated area off the ground to prevent moisture build-up and decay.
ga: Esa akɛ otsumɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ amli blɛoo. ni akɛtoɔ he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni egbi, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Koni ŋmɔtɔ akabua ehe naa ni efite.

english: Why is it safer for my income to plant more than one type of crop on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishika ni mináa lɛ yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fe ekome ni miduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Growing multiple crops protects you financially if one crop suffers from a market price collapse, severe pest outbreak, or unfavorable weather.
ga: Nibii babaoo ni ooodu lɛ baabu ohe yɛ shika gbɛfaŋ kɛji akɛ nibii kome jara ba shi yɛ jara nɔ. Pest helai ni naa wa loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni esaaa

english: Young cocoa trees are very sensitive to direct sunlight and high heat. Leaving shade trees or planting temporary shade crops like plantains protects the young cocoa from leaf scorch and keeps the soil moist until the cocoa bushes grow big enough.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ kookoo tsei lɛ, ebaabu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ baai ni shãa amɛ lɛ ahe, ni ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during heavy rain and high winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that stay near the top soil, and heavy bunches of fruit make them top-heavy. Staking the stem with wooden props or mounding extra soil around the base helps support the plant.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yiteŋ. Ni aduawai ni eyi obɔ lɛ baaha amɛfee nɔ ni tsii. Staking kɛ tsei nibii loo muji krokomɛi ni abua naa ni ebɔle Shishitoo lɛ baaye abua ni eye ebua tso lɛ.

english: Why do my maize crops grow thin and weak when I plant many seeds together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ mli tsɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ waa beni mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo feɔ ekome yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, they fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to develop a strong stem and produce full cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná hulu la ni faaa, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo tso ni mli wa ni ekɛ ŋmei ni eyi obɔ aba.

english: Why do my yam vines produce many green leaves but very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ hiɛ baai ŋmɔji babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shishi?

english: Applying too much nitrogen fertilizer causes the yam plant to put all its energy into growing leafy stems above ground instead of sending food down to build large tubers underground.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaha sweet potato tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsu niyenii kɛya shi koni amɛma ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants produce small cobs with missing kernels even when they look green and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ miiwo ŋmeii bibii lɛ? seedless Eyɛ mli akɛ dumɔwui lɛ tamɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa moŋ, shi.

english: Maize relies on wind to carry pollen from the tassels at the top to the silks on the cobs. Dry winds or poor soil nutrients during the flowering stage prevent full pollination, resulting in missing kernels.
ga: Abɛi kɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ nɔ koni ekɛ pollen aya kɛjɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ kɛya siliki ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi loo shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ tsiɔ fɔfɔi ni baa lɛ naa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dumɔwui ni elaaje.

english: Curled, yellow cassava leaves are typically caused by sap-sucking insects like whiteflies or viral diseases like Cassava Mosaic Disease. These pests strip the plant of nutrients and stop the roots from swelling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli tamɔ cassava mosaic lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei baa ni ji ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmei baa. Nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli ni amɛtsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafuu.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in dark, overly wet, and cold shade. Pruning excess canopy branches lets air and sunlight in to keep pods dry and prevent the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. ni ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni duŋ yɔɔ Fɛ̃i kɛ fɛ̃i tsɔ lɛ, ŋmɔ ŋmei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la abote mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why does spear grass reduce my crop yields more than other weeds on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ spear jwɛi lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi fe jwɛi krokomɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Spear grass has deep, sharp underground stems that steal water and fertilizer from nearby crops. The underground roots can also puncture growing cassava tubers or yams, damaging the crop underground.
ga: Spear jwɛi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni juɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli. Shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi baanyɛ abote ŋmei loo ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ mli hu. ni kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmɔshi nibii fiteɔ

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when exposed to stress, such as dry soil, extreme heat, or sudden heavy rains. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to save energy and survive.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛ kpe nɔnyɛɛ tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt and turn yellow during heavy rains even though they have plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli kɛji nu babaoo po lɛ?

english: Too much rain water fills all the small air spaces in the soil, suffocating the roots. Waterlogged roots cannot take up nutrients and easily attract fungal diseases that make the plant wilt.
ga: Nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ yiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Shishifãi ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, ni egbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ oya.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle full sunlight because their roots and leaves are delicate. Planting shade crops like plantains nearby creates a cooler canopy that protects young cocoa from burning and keeps moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni fa babaoo ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ waaa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo ni buɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he, ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why shouldn't I let all the young shoots grow around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mihaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ fɛɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Mi dumɔwui titri lɛ shishitoo

english: When too many shoots (suckers) grow around one plantain stem, they compete for food and water in the soil, leading to small plantain bunches. Pruning them to leave only one main stem and one or two strong suckers ensures maximum fruit size.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii (ŋmeii) babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso kome he lɛ, Amɛyeɔ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji plantains kuu bibioo ko Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ yibii titri kome pɛ kɛ suckers kome loo enyɔ ni he wa lɛ, ebaaha yibii lɛ adara babaoo.

english: Yellowing starting at the tips of lower maize leaves is usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer gives the plant the food it needs to build green leaves and form large ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná baai eŋɔli kɛ toi wuji.

english: Why do my maize leaves have ragged holes with small caterpillars hiding inside the funnels?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Ani okɛ ohe ewo kone mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm pest, which burrows into the leaf funnel of maize plants. Spraying recommended treatments early in the morning or late evening when the worms emerge helps protect the growing point of the plant.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Fall Armyworm, ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ baai amli lɛ. Akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni ŋmeii yɔɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ he.

english: Why does my lowland rice field need to hold standing water during early growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ahi nu mli yɛ be mli ni edaa mra lɛ?

english: Standing water prevents weeds from taking over the field and keeps nutrients dissolved so the rice roots can easily drink them in, leading to faster tillering and stronger stalks.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ tsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekaye ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ ni shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu amɛ oya. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ shwereɔ oya ni amɛhe waa.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce huge bushy leaves but very small cassava tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai wuji shi cassava shishifãi bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen fertilizer or is planted too close together, the plant spends all its energy growing leaves instead of storing energy underground in the roots.
ga: Beni ŋmei lɛ nine shɛɔ nitrogen ŋmei babaoo nɔ loo adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ehe tsɔ. Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ baai ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Yɛ no najiaŋ lɛ, akɛ hewalɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to clear small trees and put up wooden poles for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie tsei bibii lɛ? No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ tso ko ama shi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam plants are vines that need to spread their leaves high in the air to catch maximum sunlight. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing leaf diseases and helping the plant feed its underground tuber.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni ehe hiaa ni amɛgbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã kɔɔyɔɔ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Etsiɔ tsei ahe helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛyeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii.

english: Why do my tomato leaves get dark spots and wither away during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rains cause soil containing microscopic fungi to splash onto lower leaves, triggering fungal leaf diseases. Mulching the ground around tomatoes with dry grass stops soil splash and protects the leaves.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ bibii ni ŋmeii eyi mli obɔ lɛ shwieɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. Ekɛ baa helai ni jɛɔ ŋmeii amli baa. Mulching around Tomato ni akɛ jwɛi egbi lɛ baatsi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwiemɔ naa ni ebaabu baai lɛ ahe.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience high heat stress or dry soil conditions. Giving the plants consistent water during flowering encourages the blossoms to set fruit instead of falling off.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baawo fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi shihilɛ mli lɛ he. Kɛ́ akɛ nu ha tso lɛ daa yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, ebaawo fɔfɔi lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwo yibii moŋ fe ni amɛaagbee shi.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or groundnuts on my land make the soil better for maize in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts are legumes that work with helpful soil microbes to pull nitrogen gas out of the air and store it in their roots. When the crop is harvested, that trapped nitrogen stays in the soil to nourish the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen gas kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Beni akpaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Nakai nitrogen ni aŋɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eya nɔ eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, which is a key nutrient plants need to grow and stay green. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plants recover and produce bigger cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Amɛji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara ni amɛhi shi eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná ŋmɔshi nibii ni dara.

english: Why does my cassava crop survive long dry spells while my maize crop dries up and dies without rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli yɛ be mli ni mi-ŋmã lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni egboɔ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava stores water and food in its thick underground roots and can drop its leaves to save moisture during dry weather. Maize has shallow roots and broad leaves that lose water quickly, making it much more sensitive to drought.
ga: Yucca kɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ toɔ eshishifãi ni mli tse ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli, ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ baai ashwie shi koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ. Abele yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni nu fiteɔ oya. Enɛ haa amɛnuɔ hɔmɔ he waa.

english: Why do small green cocoa pods on my trees turn black and dry up before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ ji Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, overly wet conditions. Pruning excess farm shade to let in sunlight and removing infected pods prevents the disease from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ewo duŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ fe nine lɛ. Afolɔ ŋmɔ mli hulutsoo be ni fa fe nine lɛ mli koni hulu la aba mli ni ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Enɛ baatsi hela lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa pods ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips feeding on the sap under the leaves or spreading a virus. Controlling these insects early with neem oil or approved sprays helps the plant produce normal new leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ latex loo helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Neem fɔ loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua tso lɛ ni ewo baai heei bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall wooden stakes to climb on instead of just spreading on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛkwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooogbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking raises the yam leaves high into the air so they can catch maximum sunlight. When leaves get plenty of sunlight, they produce more food for the plant, resulting in much larger tubers underground.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato baai lɛ aya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli bɔni afee ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Kɛji baai lɛ ná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa Ebaaha niyenii babaoo aha tsei lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ dara kwraa.

english: Plantains fall easily when underground pests like nematodes or weevils damage their root system, weakening their hold in the ground. Propping fruiting trees with strong wooden poles and planting clean suckers keeps them standing.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi tamɔ nematodes loo weevils fite shishifãi lɛ. ni ehaa nɔ ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ baa shi. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni woɔ yibii ni akɛ tsei ni wa wo mli lɛ wo mli, ni adu ŋmeii ni he tse lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛdamɔ shi.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds around my crops when they are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ beni amɛji bibii lɛ?

english: Weeds grow very fast and steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients away from young crops. Clearing them early ensures your crops get all the nutrients they need to grow strong root systems.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni jɛɔ tsei bibii amli lɛ. Ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha tso lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni etsɔ shishifãi ni mli wa.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the weather gets too hot or when the plants do not get a steady supply of water. Keeping the soil consistently moist and mulching around the roots helps protect the flowers so fruits can form.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ afɔɔɔ tsei lɛ anɔ nu daa. Kɛ́ okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fũu daa ni okɛ sũ wo shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my tomato fruits get a dark, flat rotten patch at the bottom before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the developing fruit, usually because the plant is not getting steady water to draw calcium from the soil. Regular, even watering prevents this problem.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ tso yibii ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni haa ebaa lɛ nakai ji akɛ, tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaajie calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: How do I know the best time to harvest my cassava so the roots don't turn woody or spoil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei? Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ akatsɔ tso loo amɛkafite?

english: Most cassava varieties are ready for harvest between 9 to 12 months after planting. Harvesting too early gives you thin roots, while leaving them in the ground past 15 months causes the tubers to become tough, woody, and lose starch.
ga: Cassava henɔi babaoo efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ akpa mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ afee mlɛo. Shi kɛ́ oshi yɛ sũ lɛ mli nyɔji 15 lɛ, ebaaha ewa. Etamɔ tso. kɛ starch ni elaaje

english: Why are my young cocoa trees turning yellow and drying up in the full sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains nearby creates a natural canopy that shields young trees from harsh heat while keeping moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Ehaa adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: How does cutting off extra branches from my crop trees help them produce more fruit?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei lɛ aniji ni fa fe nine ni mifoɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua amɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo?

english: Pruning removes dead or overcrowded branches that steal energy and water from the plant. Opening up the tree allows sunlight and air to reach the main trunk, which reduces diseases and forces the plant to focus its nutrients on growing healthy pods.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni egboi loo ni egbɔjɔ fe nine ni juɔ hewalɛ kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ. Tso lɛ ni agbeleɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ haa helai baa shi ni enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔ yɛ pod lɛ dalɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do weeds growing near my crop plants lower the amount of food I harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni miduɔ nii lɛ masɛi lɛ haa niyenii ni mikpaa lɛ baa shi?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and nutrients in the dirt. When weeds surround a crop, they steal the plant's food, causing the crop to grow weak and produce less yield.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ jwɛi bɔle nidumɔ nii ko he lɛ, amɛjuɔ tso lɛ niyenii, ni no haa nidumɔ nii lɛ waaa ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do weeds come back so quickly after I cut them down with a cutlass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa oya beni mikɛ dade shwieɔ amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Clearing weeds manually with a cutlass only trims the leaves on top, leaving the roots healthy underneath to sprout again. Covering the ground with mulch or shade blocks light from reaching the soil, stopping weed seeds from growing back quickly.
ga: Nine ni akɛfoɔ jwɛi kɛ tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ. Ha shishifãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shishi ni amɛkwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ. Okɛ jwɛi aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo okɛ ŋmɔlɔ aha nɔ koni la akashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ oya

english: Why does my farm soil feel hard and baked dry even after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nuɔ he akɛ ewa ni egbi yɛ nugbɔ enɛ po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soil without organic cover loses its ability to hold water and bakes hard in the heat. Leaving dry leaves or plant mulch on top of the soil protects it from direct sun, helping it soak up and store rainwater like a sponge.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ mli lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɔmɔ nu dɔŋŋ, ni ewaa yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛ́ ashi baai ni egbi loo ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni eŋɔɔ nugbɔ nu ni ehiɛɔ mli tamɔ sponji.

english: Why do I need to cover and ferment my cocoa beans after picking instead of drying them immediately?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni maha kookoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ ni mafee amɛ ŋmɔtɔ beni mikpa amɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha kookoo ŋmeii lɛ agbi amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ

english: Fermentation heats up the fresh beans under plantain leaves to break down bitter chemicals and unlock the rich chocolate flavor inside. Drying beans immediately without fermenting leaves them bitter, purple, and low quality.
ga: Fermentation haa ŋmeii heei ni yɔɔ plantain baai lɛ ashishi lɛ mli dɔɔ koni ekɛgbala tsofai ni mli edɔ lɛ amli ni egbele tsokolate ni mli ŋɔɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ naa. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmeii amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni akɛwooo mli lɛ, ebaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ehiii kwraa.

english: Why should I dry my harvested crops on raised wooden mats rather than on the bare ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbi mikpamɔ lɛ yɛ tsũi ni awó nɔ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Drying crops directly on the ground exposes them to damp soil, dirt, and animals, which causes mold to grow. Raised drying mats allow clean air to flow under and over the beans, drying them evenly and keeping them clean.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni agbiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ, muji, kɛ kooloi baa amɛnɔ. ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela baa Dade tsɔne ni awo nɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli tse hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ kɔfi ŋmeii lɛ amli. Gbi daa ni oha ehe atse.

english: What causes black spots to quickly spread across my cocoa pods during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii diji lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that thrives in wet, dark conditions. When rainwater stays trapped on pods due to heavy shade or weeds, fungal spores grow and spread quickly from pod to pod.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli ewo fɔ, ni mli ewo duŋ mli. Kɛji nugbɔ nu ŋmɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ yɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo jwɛi ahewɔ lɛ Fungal spores lɛ daa ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow tall with lots of leaves but produce very small roots under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eshishifãi bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil is too hard or packed down, the cassava roots cannot expand underground. The plant ends up spending all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of swelling its roots.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ lɛ, Cassava shishifãi nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi. Fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ, tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni eyɔɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeeha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Purple leaves on young maize mean the plant is struggling to absorb phosphorus from the soil, often because the dirt is too wet or cold. As the soil dries and roots grow deeper, or when phosphorus fertilizer is added, the leaves return to a healthy green.
ga: Baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miitao ejie fɔsfɔs kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni haa ebaa lɛ nakai ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ loo edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ ni shishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ lɛ, loo beni akɛ fɔsfɔs ŋmɔshi nibii fataa he lɛ Baai lɛ baaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛ su ni ji eŋɔli ni yeɔ emuu lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to keep my seeds in a nursery for several weeks before moving them to my main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ dumɔwui ato dumɔwui akwɛmɔhe lɛ otsii babaoo dani mikɛwo miŋmɔ titri lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young crop seedlings are very delicate and easily damaged by severe sun, heavy rains, or pests. A nursery gives them a protected space to grow strong root systems so they can survive when moved to the open farm.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ waaa kwraa ni hulu la ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fiteɔ amɛ oya. Nursery haa he ko ni abuɔ he kɛha shishifãi ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ. Enɛ ji koni amɛnyɛ amɛhi shi kɛ́ ajie amɛ kɛtee ŋmɔ ko ni agbele naa mli.

english: What is the best time of day for me to transplant my young seedlings into the field?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ madu dumɔwui awo ŋmɔ mli?

english: The best time to transplant is late in the afternoon or on a cool, cloudy day. Moving seedlings when the sun is not hot prevents them from drying out quickly and reduces transplant shock.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ atsake tso lɛ ji shwane loo gbi ni hulu lɛ miitso ni atatu eyi mli obɔ lɛ. Dumɔwui ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ he kroko be mli ni hulu lɛ edɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkagbi oya, ni ebaaye ebua ni eha dumɔwui ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli lɛ ahe gbeyeishemɔ aba shi.

english: What should I do if some of my young seedlings die after I move them into my field?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji tsei bibii komɛi gboi beni ajie amɛ kɛtee ŋmɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You can perform 'supplying,' which means replacing the dead seedlings with healthy ones from your nursery within the first week of transplanting so your field remains full.
ga: Obaanyɛ ‘ohe’, ni tsɔɔ akɛ okɛ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni jɛ o-nursery lɛ mli lɛ baatsake dumɔwui ni egboi lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsi ni akɛwo mli lɛ mli. koni nyɛŋmɔji lɛ ahi shi ni eyi obɔ

english: If my crop stays in the field for four months, how can I estimate how much harvest I will get?
ga: Kɛji miŋmɔshi nii lɛ hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli nyɔji ejwɛ Te mafee tɛŋŋ masusu yibiiwoo ni maná lɛ he akɔntaa?

english: Your yield depends on plant spacing, crop variety, and management. You can estimate your harvest by counting the healthy, fruit-bearing plants per row and multiplying that by the average weight expected per plant.
ga: O yibiiwoo damɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ, tsei srɔtoi, kɛ amɛkwɛmɔ nɔ. Obaanyɛ obu okpamɔ lɛ he akɔntaa kɛtsɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni woɔ yibii ni oookane yɛ sɛɛkuu fɛɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ nɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ tso fɛɛ tso lɛ mlijaa mlijaa ni akpaa gbɛ lɛ abɔ he.

english: Why is my neighbor getting a bigger harvest from their field than I am getting from mine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ naa babaoo kɛjɛɔ amɛŋmɔ mli fe bɔ ni mináa kɛjɛɔ minɔ̃ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Differences in harvest size usually come down to soil fertility, proper fertilizer timing, pest management, and consistent watering. Improving soil health and crop care will help increase your yields.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmaa lɛ dalɛ mli lɛ damɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ. Be ni sa ni esa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli Nibii ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ ahe nitsumɔ kɛ nu ni akɛhaa daa Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛnamɔ kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Will planting seeds directly in my main field give me the same yield as starting them in a nursery first?
ga: Ani dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ titri lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha yibiiwoo aba tamɔ dumɔwui ni ajeɔ shishi yɛ ŋmɔ mli klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: For many crops, nursery raising leads to higher yields because it allows you to select only the strongest seedlings for your main field, ensuring better plant survival and growth.
ga: Kɛha tsei srɔtoi babaoo lɛ Nursery okwaayeli kɛ nibii ni anáa lɛ babaoo baa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ehaa ohalaa dumɔwui ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ kɛhaa he titri ni oduɔ nii yɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei hiɔ shi ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my crops are ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eshɛ nikpamɔ?

english: Crops show clear physical signs of maturity, such as changes in color, firm fruit size, or drying of the outer leaves depending on the specific crop variety.
ga: Tso lɛ jieɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ eshɛ, tamɔ su ni etsake, aduawai lɛ adalɛ ni mli wa, loo kponɔgbɛ baai ni egbi lɛ kpo. Edamɔ tso pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ nɔ

english: Why are some of my crops taking longer than expected to mature in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi miihe be babaoo fe bɔ ni akpaa gbɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crop growth can be delayed by environmental stress such as irregular rainfall, poor soil nutrients, extreme sun, or early pest attacks that slow down plant development.
ga: Tsei adalɛ baanyɛ asɛɛ afo yɛ shihilɛ mli haomɔi tamɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii, hulu la ni fa tsɔ, loo mra be mli kooloi ni yeɔ tsei lɛ anɔ ni haa tsei lɛ daraaa oya.

english: How does proper plant spacing affect how much crop harvest I will get?
ga: Te tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa lɛ saa ŋmaa babaoo ni maná lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Giving plants the right distance apart ensures each crop gets enough sunlight, water, and soil nutrients to grow fully without competing with neighboring plants.
ga: Tsei ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ amɛhe lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ akaŋ akaŋ.

english: How can I tell if my crops in the field need extra water or fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia nu loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo?

english: Signs like yellowing leaves, slow growth, or leaf wilting during cooler parts of the day indicate that your crops need additional water or soil nutrients.
ga: Okadii tamɔ baai ni tsuɔ, amɛdaraa blɛoo loo amɛgboɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli gbɛkɛ mli Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu loo niyenii krokomɛi he miihia otso lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to protect their tender leaves from direct, intense sunlight. Without shade trees or plantain plants to shield them, the extreme heat scorches their leaves and dries out the moisture they need to grow.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ biɔ hulutsoo koni amɛbu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Kɛji tsei ni baaha hulutsoo loo dumɔwui ni baaha nɔ ko bɛ lɛ Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara lɛ agbi.

english: Why do farmers usually plant plantains on the same plot before or alongside young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi duɔ plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ dani amɛduɔ kookoo tsei bibii loo amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas. They provide essential shade and conserve soil moisture for young cocoa trees during their first few vulnerable years before the cocoa canopy can handle full sun.
ga: Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛhaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ amli dani kookoo ŋtayaa lɛ nine shɛɔ hulu la ni yeɔ emuu nɔ.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my maize when the rain schedule keeps changing?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa? Beni nugbɔshiimɔ he gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ tsakeɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ

english: Wait until the first heavy rain saturates the soil deeply, then plant within a few days while the soil is moist. Avoid planting right after a light drizzle, because if a dry spell follows, the seeds will dry up and fail to germinate.
ga: Mɛɛ kɛyashi klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa. No sɛɛ lɛ, du yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo lɛ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ dumɔ he amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ fioo lɛ. Ejaakɛ kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be ko nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baagbi ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkwɛ̃.

english: What causes small caterpillars to eat holes through the center leaves of my young corn plants overnight?
ga: Mɛni ha ŋmeii bibii ye bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ nyɔɔŋ kome?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworms, which hide inside the funnel of the plant during the day and feed on leaves at night. Catching them early and applying organic treatments like neem oil or recommended sprays helps protect the growing crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tso lɛ ŋmeii amli yɛ shwane mli, ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ gbɛkɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli tsuɔ nii tamɔ neem fɔ loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mɔ he ŋaa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii ni miida lɛ ahe.

english: Why does my cassava turn tough and bitter if I leave it in the soil for too long after it matures?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ ashi ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ lɛ, ehaa ŋmei feɔ nɔ ni wa ni ehaa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ?

english: As cassava stays in the ground past its maturity date, it continues to convert soft starches into tough plant fibers and defensive compounds. Harvesting cassava between 9 and 12 months ensures the tubers remain soft and pleasant to eat.
ga: Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmei lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be ni esa akɛ ekwɛ lɛ eho. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ feɔ tso mli tsɔi ni wa kɛ nibii ni buɔ mɔ he lolo. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmei yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmei lɛ mli ŋmei lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ blɛoo ni ŋɔɔ.

english: Do my yam vines really need tall wooden stakes to give me big tubers under the ground?
ga: Ani tso kakadaŋŋ he miihia mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ koni ekɛha eshishifãi wuji lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Yes, yam vines need stakes so their leaves can spread out toward sunlight. The extra sunlight allows the leaves to make more food, which is then sent down into the roots to grow large, heavy tubers.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso koni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã koni amɛmɔ hulu la lɛ. Hulu la ni fa babaoo lɛ haa baai lɛ woɔ niyenii babaoo. Akɛ enɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ anɔ koni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why does my land produce smaller yields each year if I keep planting maize in the exact same spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo daa afi kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously on the same soil drains specific nutrients, particularly nitrogen, without giving the land time to recover. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores natural nutrients to the soil.
ga: Abɛi ni yaa nɔ aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ. titri lɛ nitrogen ni ahaaa be ni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ekoŋŋ Abele ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni akɛtsakeɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Can I use dry poultry or cow manure instead of buying chemical fertilizers for my vegetable crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ kooloi loo tsina ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi atsu nii moŋ fe ni mahe tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛha mi aduawai lɛ?

english: Yes, well-decomposed animal manure improves soil structure, holds moisture, and supplies essential nutrients naturally. However, it releases nutrients slowly, so mixing it into the soil well before planting gives vegetables the best boost.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo, ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa haa yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi kɛlɛ, ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii fiofio. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛfutu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ dani odu lɛ, ebaaha aduawai lɛ aná hewalɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves get brown spots and dry up right after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: High humidity and wet leaves create ideal conditions for fungal diseases like blight to spread rapidly. Spacing tomato plants properly allows wind to flow through and dry the leaves faster, reducing fungal outbreaks.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ baai ni efɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ late blight ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya. Gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ tomato tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli ni egbiɔ baai lɛ oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why is it important for me to weed around my young crop plants early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Mi dumɔwui lɛ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal vital soil nutrients, water, and sunlight away from young crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food they need to build strong stems and roots.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, nu kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ tsei bibii amli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa tsei lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛma shishifãi kɛ shishifãi ni wa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize needs to stay green and grow strong. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer around the stems will help nourish the plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda jogbaŋŋ. Kooloo ŋmei ni egbo loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni eha tso lɛ niyenii.

english: Planting maize continuously on the same land drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows pests to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts puts nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Abele ni yaa nɔ aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ nɔŋŋ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake lɛ, no baaha nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start to rot in the ground before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers rot when excess water stays around their roots for too long, especially in flat, heavy clay soils during rain. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps rainwater drain away quickly.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Titri lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tsii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ, nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ oya.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep drying up when I plant them in full sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender stems and leaves that easily dry out under direct heat. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains beside them creates a cool, protective cover while the cocoa grows its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kɛ baai bibii ni kɛ́ akɛ amɛ wo la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ, amɛgbiɔ oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ Emasɛi lɛ, ebaaha he ko ni mli ejɔ aba. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, kookoo baakwɛ̃ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots that cannot easily support heavy bunches when strong winds blow. Propping up the main stem with strong bamboo poles or wooden forks gives the plant extra balance.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛŋ aye abua ŋmɔlɔ ni tsii kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei tso loo tso ni mli wa to tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do weeds harm my crops if I leave them growing in my farm?
ga: Te jwɛi baaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji miha amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for soil nutrients, sunlight, and water, which starves your main crop. Clearing weeds early in the season makes sure your crops get all the food they need to yield well.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, hulu la, kɛ nu, ni no haa hɔmɔ yeɔ oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ náa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves and catch as much sunlight as possible. Lifting the leaves off the ground allows the plant to produce enough food to grow large tubers below.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ woɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Tomato flowers often drop when temperatures get too high or when the plant experiences water stress. Giving your plants a steady supply of water directly at their base keeps the flowers healthy enough to form fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ. Nu ni oooha tso lɛ shishigbɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why should I avoid spraying chemical insecticides when my crops are blooming with flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ahe be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ewo fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Flowering crops need beneficial insects like bees to visit their blossoms so fruits can form. Spraying chemicals while flowers are open kills these helpful insects, leading to fewer fruits on your farm.
ga: Tsei ni woɔ fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ, tamɔ wuobii, koni amɛyasara amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛwo yibii. Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni fɔfɔi lɛ miikwɛ lolo lɛ baagbe nɛkɛ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ nɛɛ. Enɛ haa aduawai faaa yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites that attack young leaves. Spraying early with neem oil or a recommended insect spray helps protect the plant so leaves can grow normally.
