ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni tutuaa baa bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Akɛ neem fɔ loo kooloi amli tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ nɔ mra. Ebaabu tso lɛ he koni baai lɛ anyɛ ada bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow at the tips while the top leaves are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tso ko shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: This yellowing is usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Maize needs a lot of nitrogen to grow, and when the soil runs low, the plant pulls nutrients from its older, lower leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ su ni ji ŋmɔŋ nɛɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃. Ni kɛ́ shikpɔŋ fioo pɛ eshwɛ Tsei lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ kɛ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋmeii heei ni eda yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Planting the same crop on the same land continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving it time to recover. Rotating your crops with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts puts nitrogen back into the soil and keeps it fertile.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ nɔŋŋ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsu nii ekoŋŋ. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii atsake oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Enɛ baaha nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni eye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa nii.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning twisted and getting yellowish patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried and spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties recommended by extension officers is the best way to prevent it.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmei mosaic hela. ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ woɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ. Cassava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ he ŋaa lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ naa.

english: Why are my pepper leaves curling tightly upwards and stopping the plant from growing well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle ehe shi shiŋŋ kɛtee ŋwɛi ni etsĩɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Upward leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny pests like thrips or mites sucking the sap from young leaves. Using mild insecticidal soaps or neem oil spray can help manage these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ samla ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ blɛoo loo neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Why do my vegetable seedlings rot at the stem and fall over right after sprouting in wet weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: This is a fungal issue known as 'damping-off,' which happens when the soil is too wet and ventilation is poor. Ensuring good drainage and avoiding overcrowding of seeds helps keep the soil surface dry enough to stop the fungus.
ga: Enɛ ji nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ fungal naagba. ‘Damping’, ni baa beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ ehiii Kwɛmɔ akɛ nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ dumɔwui lɛ ni eyiɔ obɔ lɛ he tsimɔ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ agbi bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmeii lɛ akpa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when the weather becomes very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot withstand direct sunlight because their roots are shallow and leaves burn easily. Planting fast-growing nurse crops like plantains next to them provides shade and retains soil moisture during the dry season.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya. Nurse tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains ni yɔɔ Emasɛi lɛ ni akwɛɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to make energy for growing tubers underground. Stacking the vines upwards exposes more leaves to direct sunlight, which leads to bigger and healthier yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la koni amɛná hewalɛ amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ wain tso lɛ wo ŋwɛi lɛ, ebaaha hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ aba baai lɛ anɔ babaoo. Enɛ baaha sweet potato ŋmeii ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba.

english: Too many shoots (suckers) compete with the main plant for water and soil nutrients. Removing excess suckers and leaving only one or two strong ones ensures the main tree produces a larger, heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ shishifãi (shishifãi) ​​babaoo tsɔ kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo plantains ŋmeii ni dara ni tsii.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of yellow flowers, but the flowers drop off without making tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi ŋmɔŋ babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato?

english: Flower drop in tomatoes happens when temperatures are extremely high, watering is irregular, or there are not enough insects like bees around to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi yɛ tomato mli lɛ baa kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ bɛ daa loo kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii.

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer so the heavy rain does not wash it away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akashwie nɔ?

english: Fertilizer should be applied when the soil is moist but not flooded, ideally right after a light rain or just before a mild shower. Applying split doses around the plant's root zone rather than all at once prevents it from being washed away.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi nu efooo mli. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni nugbɔ enɛ fioo loo dani nugbɔ enyɔ shi fioo. Kɛ́ ojara tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli moŋ fe ni oooshwie nɔ fɛɛ nɔ shikome lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu akafɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees start rotting when I keep farming them on the exact same piece of land for many years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ be mli ni mikɛ afii babaoo edu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Growing cocoa continuously on the same land for a very long time exhausts specific soil nutrients and allows harmful fungi to build up in the ground, which eventually causes root and plant rot.
ga: Kɛ́ aya nɔ adu kokoo yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha sũ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ afite. ni oha ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ kɛ tso lɛ agbo yɛ naagbee.

english: Can my farm soil get tired or ruined if I do not give it a break from growing cocoa?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baafite loo ebaakumɔ kɛji mihaaa lɛ hejɔɔmɔ kɛjɛ kookoo dumɔ mli?

english: Yes, continuous cocoa farming without resting the soil or adding nutrients leads to land fatigue, making crops weak and vulnerable to diseases that cause overall decay.
ga: Hɛɛ, kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa nɔ ni aŋmɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hejɔɔmɔ loo akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fataaa he lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni helai ni kɛ fitemɔ fɛɛ baa lɛ baanyɛ aba amɛnɔ.

english: Is there any way to fix land that has become prone to rot after growing cocoa for decades?
ga: Ani gbɛ ko yɛ ni aaatsɔ nɔ asaa shikpɔŋ ni miifite yɛ afii nyɔŋmai abɔ ni akɛdu kookoo lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You can restore tired soil by clearing out diseased plant remains, applying organic compost or fertilizers to rebuild nutrients, and letting the land fallow or planting cover crops.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ ni etɔ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛtsɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ahe nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ ni ooojie lɛ nɔ. Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli atsu nii ni okɛsaa niyenii mli hewalɛ. ni oshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo odu ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Why are the trunks and roots of my old cocoa trees turning soft and decaying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei momo lɛ ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ efee blɛoo ni amɛmiifite lɛ?

english: Decay at the base or roots is usually caused by fungal root rot diseases that multiply over time in mature farms, especially where the soil stays wet and unmanaged.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishijee loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ shishifãi ni fiteɔ nii ni ji fungal root rot hela ni yaa hiɛ yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni eda lɛ mli lɛ baa. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri yɛ hei ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: How can I tell if the rot on my cocoa farm is coming from the soil or from the rain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shishifãi ni egbo yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ jɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nugbɔ lɛ mli?

english: Soil-based rot typically starts deep in the roots or main trunk and wilts the whole tree, while weather-related rot mainly attacks the pods during wet seasons.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ fitemɔ jeɔ shishi yɛ shishifãi loo tso lɛ shishi. ni tsei lɛ fɛɛ gbiɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kɛbaa lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ titri yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Black and rotting pods are caused by fungal spores that survive in the farm's soil and dead plant material, spreading quickly to healthy pods when humidity is high.
ga: Fungal spores ni hiɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ kɛ tsei ni egboi amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ ni fiteɔ lɛ baa. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛyaa pods ni yɔɔ hewalɛ mli kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ fa babaoo.

english: If one of my cocoa trees starts rotting, can the sickness spread to neighboring plants on my land?
ga: Kɛji kookoo tsei lɛ eko bɔi fitemɔ Ani hela lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ?

english: Yes, fungal rot can easily spread underground through touching root systems, flowing rainwater, or shared pruning tools to infect surrounding crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi oya kɛtsɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ lɛ anɔ. nugbɔ nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli Aloo okɛ nibii ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ afee ekome ni okɛ hela aba tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ anɔ.

english: What should I do with my land if my old cocoa trees have started rotting and dying off?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji akɛ kookoo tsei momoi lɛ bɔi fitemɔ ni amɛgboi?

english: You should safely remove and destroy infected trees and roots, clean the field debris, and give the soil time to recover before planting new crops.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie tsei kɛ shishifãi ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni okpãtã amɛhiɛ shweshweeshwe. Tsumɔ shia lɛ mli jwɛi lɛ. Ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛ ehe awo mli dani odu tsei heei.

english: How do I protect new cocoa seedlings from rotting if I plant them where old cocoa trees died?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kookoo dumɔwui heei lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite? Ni kɛji akɛ midu yɛ he ko ni kookoo tsei momoi gboi yɛ lɛ hu?

english: Clear out all old root systems and infected wood from the soil, treat the ground, and allow the soil to rest or rotate with non-host plants like plantains before replanting cocoa.
ga: Jiemɔ shishifãi momoi fɛɛ kɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, tsa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe loo etsake ehe kɛtsɔ tsei ni jeee gbɔi tamɔ plantains nɔ dani odu kookoo.

english: Does leaving too much shade on my farm make my cocoa plants rot faster?
ga: Ani kɛ́ ashi hulutsoo babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha kookoo tsei lɛ agbo oya?

english: Yes, excess shade traps moisture and blocks sunlight, creating a damp environment where rot-causing fungi thrive and spread rapidly across your crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, hulutsoo babaoo mɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni etsĩɔ hulu la naa. creating a humid environment Biɛ ji he ni ŋmeii ni kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ daa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ onibii fɛɛ amli.

english: Can crops in Ghana really produce harvests two times in a single year?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ baanyɛ awo yibii shii enyɔ yɛ afi kome mli diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, certain agricultural areas in southern and central Ghana experience a bimodal rainfall pattern, meaning there are two distinct rainy seasons each year. This allows farmers in those specific areas to plant and harvest crops twice annually instead of just once.
ga: Hɛɛ, okwaayeli hei komɛi ni yɔɔ Ghana kooyigbɛ kɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ gbɛi enyɔ nɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ daa afi lɛ, nugbɔnɛmɔ bei sɔrɔtoi enyɔ yɔɔ. Ehaa okwaafoi ni yɔɔ nakai hei pɔtɛɛ lɛ duɔ nibii ni amɛkpaa shii enyɔ yɛ afi mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu shikome pɛ

english: Why do my crops start getting ready for harvest between April and July?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ yɛ April kɛ July teŋ lɛ?

english: The period from April to July marks the end of the major rainy season in many parts of southern Ghana. The steady rainfall during the earlier months gives crops the water they need to grow, leading to maturity and harvest mid-year.
ga: Be ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ April kɛyashiɔ July lɛ ji be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ hei babaoo lɛ naagbee. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ nyɔŋ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛshwere. Ekɛ dalɛ ni yeɔ emuu kɛ kpamɔ baa yɛ afi lɛ teŋgbɛ.

english: Is it normal to harvest crops again in November after a mid-year harvest?
ga: Ani eji nɔ ni sa akɛ akpaa ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ yɛ November mli yɛ afi teŋ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yes, in regions with two farming seasons, the minor rainy season supports a second growth cycle. Crops planted after the mid-year break mature around late late in the year, allowing for a second harvest in November before the main dry season.
ga: Hɛɛ, yɛ kpokpai ni okwaayeli bei enyɔ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ Nugbɔshiimɔ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ fiɔ dalɛ ni ji enyɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Tsei ni adu yɛ afi teŋ hejɔɔmɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ afi lɛ naagbee gbɛ. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ akpaa kpamɔ ni ji enyɔ yɛ November mli dani hɔmɔ be titri lɛ baa.

english: Why does my harvest stretch across several months from April to July instead of happening all in one week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ tee nɔ fe nyɔji babaoo kɛjɛ April kɛyashi July yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni fɛɛ baaba yɛ otsi kome mli lɛ?

english: Crops ripen gradually depending on precise planting dates, sunlight, and how rainfall is distributed over the rainy season. This natural variation causes plants to mature in batches across a multi-month window.
ga: Tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ fiofio yɛ gbi ni adu lɛ nɔ, hulu la kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ mlijaa nɔ. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli tsakemɔ nɛɛ haa tso lɛ daa yɛ nyɔji babaoo amli.

english: Why do farmers in some regions of Ghana only get one harvest a year while others get two?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ Ghana kpokpai komɛi anɔ lɛ kpaɔ nii shikome pɛ yɛ afi mli lɛ? yɛ be mli ni mɛi krokomɛi Ani obaanyɛ okpa nii shii enyɔ?

english: Ghana has different climate zones. Northern areas generally experience one single long rainy season followed by a dry season, yielding one harvest, whereas specific southern and forest zones receive two separate rainy seasons each year.
ga: Ghana yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ hei srɔtoi. Yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ lɛ, kooyigbɛ hei lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ kome pɛ. Nɔ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ ji fɛ̃i be lɛ kɛtsɔ yibiiwoo kome pɛ ni ekɛhaa lɛ nɔ Yɛ be mli ni anaigbɛ kpokpaa lɛ kɛ kooi komɛi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɔrɔtoi enyɔ daa afi lɛ.

english: How do crops know when to start flowering and producing fruit during the two rainy periods?
ga: Te tsei feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛleɔ be ni esa akɛ amɛje fɔfɔi kɛ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ nugbɔ bei enyɔ lɛ amli?

english: Crops react naturally to changes in soil moisture and temperature. When the early rains soften the soil and supply adequate water, it triggers internal hormonal changes in plants that cause them to grow, flower, and set fruit.
ga: Tsei feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ latsaa tsake. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni ehaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Ehaa tsofai ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ tsakeɔ yɛ tsei amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei kwɛ̃ɔ, amɛfɔɔ fɔfɔi, ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: What happens to my crop yield if I miss the early planting season in the year?
ga: Mɛni baa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikpa ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ yɛ afi lɛ shishijee mli?

english: If you miss the major rainy season early in the year, you can still plant for the minor season later in the year if you live in a two-season zone, though the yield might differ depending on how heavy the second rains are.
ga: Kɛji otsi ohe kɛjɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni he hiaa lɛ he yɛ afi lɛ shishijee mli Obaanyɛ odu kɛha be ni ji enyɔ lɛ hu yɛ nakai afi lɛ naagbee gbɛ. Kɛji oyɔɔ he ko ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ bei enyɔ mli lɛ Eyɛ mli akɛ yibiiwoo baanyɛ afee srɔtoi yɛ bɔ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli wa ha lɛ naa moŋ.

english: Why do crop prices drop during certain months and go up in others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe jara baa shi yɛ nyɔji komɛi amli, ni ekrokomɛi hu yaa hiɛ lɛ?

english: When many farmers across the country harvest at the exact same time, the market gets flooded with produce, driving prices down. Harvesting during off-peak times or late in the year allows you to command higher prices because supply is lower.
ga: Beni okwaafoi babaoo ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ kpaɔ nii yɛ be kome mli lɛ Jarayelihe lɛ baayi kɛ nibii ni amɛbaakpa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ajara ni baa shi. Nibii ni akpaa yɛ be mli ni akpaa nii babaoo loo yɛ afi lɛ naagbee gbɛ lɛ haa onyɛɔ ofãa jara ni nɔ kwɔ ejaakɛ nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ faaa.

english: How can harvesting in November help me get a better price for my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmaa ni akpaa yɛ November mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni maná jara kpakpa kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Fewer regions in Ghana produce crops during the minor season late in the year. Because total national produce supply is lower in November while consumer demand remains steady or high, buyers are willing to pay more.
ga: Ghana kpokpai fioo komɛi pɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji enyɔ yɛ afi lɛ naagbee. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, maŋ lɛ mli nibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ ba shi yɛ November mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nibii ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ lɛ yaa nɔ ehiɔ shi loo eyɛ ŋwɛi. No hewɔ lɛ, mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛwo nyɔmɔ babaoo.

english: Does harvesting crops twice a year wear out my soil faster?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa shii enyɔ yɛ afi mli lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ oya?

english: Yes, growing and harvesting crops twice in twelve months draws nutrients out of the soil continuously. To maintain good harvests in both seasons, you need to replenish the soil using compost, manure, or fertilizers between planting cycles.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ ni akpaa shii enyɔ yɛ nyɔji nyɔŋma kɛ enyɔ mli lɛ baajie niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. Bɔni afee ni nibii kpakpai ahi shi yɛ bei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ mli Ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ yɛ dumɔ bei lɛ ateŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees need protection from strong sun because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the soil quickly. Planting shade crops like plantains or tree cassava nearby provides living shade that keeps the seedlings cool and moist until they mature.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa he ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Ebaaha hulutsoo ni baaha dumɔwui lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛyashi amɛbaadara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yam vines produce tubers underground by using their leaves to catch sunlight. Staking holds the leaves up towards the sun and keeps them off the wet soil, which prevents disease and helps the plant produce larger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi, ni amɛkɛ amɛbaai lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛmɔ hulu la. Staking haa baai lɛ kwɛɔ hulu lɛ hiɛ ni ehaaa sũ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni helai baa mɔ nɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ bulbs wuji.

english: Why does my plantain plant sprout so many small shoots around the stem, and should I leave them all?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ miikwɛ̃ ŋmeii bibii babaoo yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ, ni ani esa akɛ mashi amɛ fɛɛ?

english: Plantains produce side shoots called suckers to reproduce, but if you leave all of them, they steal food and water from the main plant. Cutting away most suckers and leaving only one or two strong ones ensures the main plant grows big bunches.
ga: Plantains woɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ ni atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii koni amɛfɔ. Shi kɛji oshi fɛɛ lɛ Ebaaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ babaoo ni oshi eko loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ adara ni etsɔ ŋmeii agbo.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning yellow from the middle moving outwards?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ teŋgbɛ ni amɛyaa kponɔgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is a major nutrient needed for leaf growth. Adding animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves turn dark green again and supports strong growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni baa lɛ adara lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua baa lɛ ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ ekoŋŋ ni eha amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my soil become very hard and dry shortly after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wa ni egbi kɛji nugbɔ enɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Bare soil loses water very fast when exposed to direct sun and wind. Covering the soil around your crops with dry grass, leaves, or crop residues acts like a blanket, keeping the soil cool, soft, and moist for much longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ fiteɔ nu oya kɛji akɛ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Mulching ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi, baai, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ blanket. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, efeɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow poorly when I plant maize in the exact same spot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season. Rotating maize with beans, groundnuts, or cowpeas adds nutrients back into the soil naturally and stops pests from building up.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ yaa nɔ ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii, ŋmeii, loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa niyenii kpakpai baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni etsĩ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa koni amɛkafee

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a pest that hides inside the growing center of maize leaves. Catching them early and applying safe controls like neem leaf extracts, wood ash, or recommended sprays saves the plant before the stalk is destroyed.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ ateŋ. Amɔmɔ amɛ mra ni akɛ nibii ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe tamɔ neem baa mli nu, tso sũ, loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ atsu nii. Enɛ baahere tso lɛ yiwala dani eshishifã lɛ afite.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them in low or heavy soil during heavy rains. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa shi loo shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ni naa wa be mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and aggressively drink up the water, sunlight, and soil food that your crops need. Clearing weeds early in the season makes sure all the nutrients go directly into feeding your crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛyeɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa otsei lɛ waa. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ yaa onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, dry soil, or excessive chemical fertilizer. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering and mulching helps the flowers stay on and turn into fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli babaoo lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i kɛ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why should I plant plantains in the same farm with my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings get scorched easily by the hot Ghanaian sun. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves that provide shade and keep the soil moist for the cocoa plants during their first few years.
ga: Ghana hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shãa kookoo tsei lɛ oya. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ kɛhaa kookoo tso lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small even when the plants grow very tall leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ daraaa waa lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ baai lɛ kɛlɛ waa moŋ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen fertilizer or excessive rain, the plant spends all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of storing food in the tubers below ground.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ nitrogen ŋmei babaoo loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, which is essential for green growth. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps bring back their green color and strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa eŋmɔŋ su kɛ hewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: As cocoa trees age, their natural energy drops and older branches become less efficient at producing flowers. Pruning dead wood, feeding the soil, and replacing very old trees keeps yields high.
ga: Kɛji kookoo tso lɛ da lɛ Tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ baa shi. Ni tsei niji ni egbɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛfee fɔfɔi jogbaŋŋ. Tsei niji ni egboi lɛ ni aaafolɔ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii, kɛ tsei ni egbɔ waa ni akɛtoɔ najiaŋ lɛ baaye abua ni yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why does my soil turn hard like a rock and dry out quickly in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wa tamɔ tɛsaa ni egbiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Soil hardens when it lacks organic matter like dried leaves or manure, which act like sponges to retain moisture. Covering the ground with mulch keeps the soil soft and cool.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai ni egbi loo ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ mli. ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Mulching haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni edɔɔ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too high or when plants don't get enough water. Keeping the soil consistently moist and planting shade crops helps fruits set properly.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ adumɔ yeɔ ebuaa aduawai lɛ ni amɛtswaa shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What causes my yam tubers to rot in the soil before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani kpamɔ be baashɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot when planted in heavy soils that trap water around the roots, allowing harmful fungi and pests to grow. Building high mounds helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni haa nu ŋmɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ, ni no haa ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ shwereɔ. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni afee lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my pepper plants stop bearing new fruits after only a few harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ kpaɔ aduawai heei yɛ ŋmaa fioo pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants stop flowering when soil nutrients run low or when old fruits are left on the branch too long. Regularly picking mature peppers encourages the plant to produce new blossoms.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baakpa fɔfɔii kɛji shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ faaa loo kɛji aduawai momoi lɛ ehi tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛ́ oootse ŋmeii ni eda lɛ daa lɛ, ebaawo tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwo fɔfɔi heei.

english: Why do my stored cowpea grains get tiny holes in them after a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea dumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ?

english: Insects called weevils lay eggs on the grains in the field, which hatch during storage. Sun-drying your cowpeas thoroughly and storing them in sealed, airtight containers stops the insects from destroying the crop.
ga: Kplukai ni atsɛɔ amɛ weevils lɛ fɔɔ ŋmaa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ nɔ, ni amɛfɔɔ yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha tsina ŋmeii lɛ agbi jogbaŋŋ ni okɛto tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli. Ebaaye ebua ni kooloi akafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my plantains are ready to harvest for market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-plantains lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni akɛya jara nɔ?

english: Plantains are ready to harvest when the fingers become full and rounded, losing their sharp edges, and the small dry flower ends at the tip rub off easily.
ga: Plantains lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛ́ niji lɛ eyi obɔ ni ebɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ lɛ laaje ni fɔfɔi bibii ni egbi lɛ Naa lɛ baajɛ mli oya.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and soft roots that burn easily under direct sunlight. Providing shade using plantain trees or shade nets keeps the soil moist and protects the young plants until they are mature enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui loo hulutsoo ŋshɔŋlooi tsu nii ni akɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa.

english: If too many small shoots (suckers) grow around the main plantain stem, they fight for the same soil nutrients and water. Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two strong ones, allowing the main tree to produce large, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii bibii (ŋmeii) kwɛ̃ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ main plantain trunk Amɛyeɔ akaŋ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ baashi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni no baaha tso titri lɛ afee jwɛi agbo ni tsii.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plants are hungry for nitrogen in the soil or are sitting in waterlogged ground. Applying a balanced nitrogen fertilizer like NPK or Urea helps restore their green color and healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo eta sũ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tamɔ NPK loo urea ni akɛaatsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that hides inside the central whorl of young maize leaves. Applying recommended insecticides early in the morning or late evening when the worms emerge helps control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni teɔ shi ewoɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋtayaa lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ tsu nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ beni ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: How do I know which direction to push cassava stems into the ground when planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male gbɛ ni esa akɛ matsi ŋmei tso lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ midu?

english: Cassava stem cuttings should be planted with the raised buds pointing upward toward the sky. Planting stems upside down forces shoots to grow sideways or downward, causing weak growth and very small tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ ni ŋmeii ni awó nɔ lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji akɛ tso lɛ yitso lɛ shwere kɛtee shishi lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ kɛya afã loo shishi, ni ebaaha amɛdalɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ bulbs bibii waa aba.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to produce food for the tubers underneath the ground. Staking lifts the vines off the humid damp soil, improving leaf exposure to sunlight and preventing fungal rot.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛnáa hulu la jogbaŋŋ. ni atsĩ ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ naa

english: Why is it risky to plant my seeds after just the first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a dry spell that bakes the ground. If seeds sprout and the soil dries up completely, the young roots die from heat and lack of water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Shishifãi bibii gboiɔ yɛ dɔlɛ kɛ nu ni bɛ hewɔ.

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in small nodules on their roots. When the plant roots decay after harvest, that nitrogen stays in the ground to feed the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi bibii amli beni tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ. Nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slow and remain small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo ni amɛfeɔ bibioo lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves on the farm by taking away water, fertilizer, and sunlight meant for your crops. Removing weeds early gives your crops full access to the nutrients they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ ni amɛjieɔ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa otsei lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop without fruiting due to extreme heat, irregular watering, or lack of nutrients in the soil. Consistent watering at the root level and feeding the plants proper nutrients help flowers turn into tomatoes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli daa kɛ niyenii ni sa ni akɛhaa tso lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni etsɔɔ tomato.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and drying up in the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct sunlight in their early stage. They need shade crops like plantains planted alongside them to act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and humidity needed for young roots to establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ yɛ shishijee mli. Tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Koni etsu nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa kɛha shishifãi bibii lɛ afeemɔ.

english: Why is my green maize turning pale yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the key food corn needs to grow leaves and stalks. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure restores the green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ebaa kɛ ŋmeii akwɛ̃. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them in flat, poorly drained soil. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to flow away, keeping the roots dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛhe wa

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling up and becoming small and crinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ bibii ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Tomato leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that spread a plant virus. Controlling whiteflies early using insecticidal soap or neem oil prevents the leaf curl virus from damaging the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Whitefly nɔyeli mra Kɛ akɛ samla ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem fɔ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ leaf curl hela lɛ naa.

english: Yam is a climbing vine that relies on broad sunlight exposure across its leaves to feed the tuber growing underground. Staking lifts the vines off the wet ground so they capture maximum light and avoid leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni shwieɔ shi ni kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ hulu la ni tsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli lɛ nɔ koni amɛkɛha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii. Staking woɔ wain tsei anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛmɔmɔ la ni fa fe fɛɛ ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ foliary helai ahe.

english: Why does my plantain tree fall over on its own right when the fruit bunch gets large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain tso lɛ gbeeɔ ehe nɔ kɛ́ ewo yibii wuji lɛ?

english: Plantain stems are soft and hold a lot of water, making them weak under heavy loads. Propping up the main stem with a strong Y-shaped wooden pole supports the weight of the growing bunch until harvest.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ ahe yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ nu babaoo. Ehaa ogbɔjɔɔ kɛ́ tsɔne ni tsii fiɔ osɛɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tso ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni tamɔ Y lɛ to tso lɛ shishitso wulu lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ kuu lɛ muji kɛjɛ dumɔ mli kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why are small worms eating the inside funnel of my maize plants during the night?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi ŋmã tsei lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ gbɛkɛ lɛ?

english: These worms are Fall Armyworms, which hide deep inside the central whorl of young corn during the hot day to avoid heat. Spraying targeted treatments early in the morning or late evening reaches them when they emerge to feed.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli koni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ hulutsoo be lɛ he. Targeted treatment sprays ni akɛshwieɔ shi leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ baaba beni amɛjeɔ kpo koni amɛbaye niyenii lɛ.

english: Why should I cover the bare dirt around my crops with dry grass and cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko he lɛ? Nibii ni aduɔ ni jwɛi kɛ kookoo ŋmɔji yɔɔ mli

english: Covering soil with dry plant materials (mulching) blocks heat from drying out the ground, keeps soil moisture in for roots during dry stretches, and prevents weeds from sprouting.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni egbi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (mulching) lɛ, ehaa dɔlɛ tsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ naa ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i haa shishifãi lɛ yɛ be mli ni egbiɔ lɛ. ni etsĩ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts in between my maize rows helps my soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ mi ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ teŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which takes nitrogen gas from the air and converts it into natural soil fertilizer, helping nourish neighboring crops like maize.
ga: Peanuts ji legume weku lɛ mlinyo, ni ejieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni etsakeɔ lɛ efeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ abele niyenii.

english: Why do weeds hurt my young crops much more during the first month than later on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ awui waa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ mli fe nyɔji ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Young crops have small, weak root systems and easily get starved of water and soil nutrients by fast-growing weeds. Once crops grow tall and leafy, they naturally shade out new weeds.
ga: Tso bibioo lɛ yɛ shishifãi bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ. Ni jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ bɛ nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai yɛ sũ lɛ mli oya. Kɛ tso lɛ da ni eyɛ baai Amɛbaafee jwɛi heei ahe ŋmɔlɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛsu naa.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that easily burn under full sun. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain alongside cocoa provides living shade that cools the soil and keeps moisture in the ground until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni eha hulutsoo aba, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ baadara jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of a maize plant usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient it needs to grow green leaves. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure helps restore healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa tso shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni baai eŋɔli lɛ akwɛ̃ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it good to plant groundnuts or beans together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ adu ŋmãa loo ŋmãa?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which can pull nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. Planting them alongside maize improves soil fertility naturally and helps the maize grow better without needing extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni baanyɛ agbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ abele masɛi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweremɔ yaa hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ atsu nii

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small if I plant the cuttings too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When cassava cuttings are planted too close together, their roots fight each other for water, sunlight, and nutrients in the soil. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space to absorb what it needs to produce large, healthy tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛŋɔ nɔ ni he hiaa lɛ lɛ koni ekɛfee bulbs agboi ni mli wa.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up in the air to catch maximum sunlight. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing leaf diseases and helping the plant create more energy to build large tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Etsiɔ tsei ahe helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ babaoo feɔ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my crops with dry leaves and grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko he lɛ? Nibii ni aduɔ ni baai egbi kɛ jwɛi?

english: Covering the ground with dry leaves or grass, known as mulching, keeps the soil moist by preventing water from evaporating in the heat. It also keeps the roots cool and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛtsɔ nu ni ehaaa efo yɛ latsaa be mli lɛ nɔ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ hu mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye nɔ.

english: The first rain of the season is often just a quick shower that cools the air but dries up quickly. You should wait until the soil stays moist a few inches below the surface for a few consecutive days before planting so your seeds do not dry out and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ ji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ oya kɛkɛ ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ shi egbiɔ oya. Esa akɛ omɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ 2-3 inches yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi gbii 2-3 ni nyiɛ sɛɛ dani okɛdu. Koni dumɔwui lɛ akagbi ni amɛgboi.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that suck the sap out of the leaves and spread viruses. Controlling these insects early prevents the disease from spreading to the rest of your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. No shwieɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni egbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni helai akagbɛ eshwa oŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ amli.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences extreme heat stress, lack of water, or poor pollination. Ensuring the plants have enough water during dry spells and allowing air to flow through the farm helps the flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli. Ni aaakwɛ koni tsei lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Ni aŋmɛ gbɛ ni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ aduawai.

english: Why do weeds make my crops produce a small harvest even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa midumɔ nii lɛ awo yibii babaoo yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo po lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster and stronger than most crops, taking away the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients that your crops need. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food they need to give you a heavy harvest.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei babaoo, ni amɛjieɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni he hiaa otsei lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaaha onibii lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa bo koni eha bo kpamɔ babaoo.

english: Why should I spray chemical medicine on my crops late in the evening instead of during the bright morning sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ gbɛkɛ mli moŋ fe ni mikɛbaafɔse yɛ leebi hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Spraying in the cool evening prevents the heat of the sun from evaporating the medicine too quickly. It allows the leaves to absorb the chemical properly overnight and stops the midday sun from burning leaves that have liquid sitting on them.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ, ebaatsi la ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli lɛ naa koni ekafo oya tsɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ tsofai lɛ jogbaŋŋ nyɔɔŋ kome mli, ni ehaaa hulu ni tsoɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ ashã baai ni nu lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: If I put extra fertilizer on my crops at once, will it help them grow twice as fast?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fata ŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ be kome mli Ani ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛdara oya shii enyɔ?

english: No, giving crops too much fertilizer at one time can burn their roots and kill them. Plants absorb food gradually, so it is best to apply small, measured amounts at different stages of their growth.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ha shikome lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ ni egbe amɛ. Tsei shwieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ fiofio, no hewɔ lɛ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ okɛ fioo ni asusuɔ he baatsu nii yɛ amɛdalɛ fã fɛɛ fã mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when I plant them in an open field with no big trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei ni eda bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are very sensitive to direct, intense sunlight. They need bigger trees or plantains around them to provide shade and trap moisture while their leaves and root systems are still developing.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Amɛmiitao tsei wuji loo plantains ni ebɔle amɛhe. Koni ekɛ hulutsoo aha ni emɔ ŋmɔtɔ be mli ni baai lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ miida lolo lɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop and look dead during the hot afternoon, but stand up strong again by morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ gboɔ ni etamɔ nɔ ni egbo yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Shi damɔ shi shiŋŋ ekoŋŋ leebi?

english: During the hot day, plants lose water faster than their roots can suck it up from the soil, causing them to wilt to protect themselves. At night, when it cools down, they drink up water and rest, restoring their strength by morning.
ga: Yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ Tsei fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛgbɔjɔɔ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe gbɛkɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ waa lɛ. A maa nu nyu nɛ a maa jɔɔ a he. Na ohewalɛ ekoŋŋ leebi.

english: Why do I see eaten holes in my maize leaves, but I cannot find any insects on the plants during the daytime?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ manyɛ mana bu yɛ ŋmãa baai amli shi minaaa kooloi bibii yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Many crop pests, like armyworms, hide underground or deep inside the plant stem during the hot daylight hours to protect themselves from heat and birds. They only come out to feed on your crops at night.
ga: Tsei amli tsɛŋemɔ helai srɔtoi babaoo tamɔ cutworms Hiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi loo tsei ashishifãi amli shɔŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ŋmɛlɛtswai lɛ amli. Koni obu ohe kɛjɛ latsaa kɛ okpoi ahe Amɛjeɔ kpo koni amɛbaye oŋmɔshi nibii pɛ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pumpkin plants open wide early in the morning and close tight by midday?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi pumpkin tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ fɔ̃ɔ waa leebi ni amɛŋmɛɔ amɛhe jogbaŋŋ yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Pumpkin flowers open early in the morning when bees and other insects are most active to pollinate them. Once the heat of the afternoon arrives, the flowers close to protect their pollen and save moisture.
ga: Pumpkin fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ yɛ leebi maŋkpa. Enɛ ji be mli ni ŋmeii kɛ kooloi krokomɛi Haa pollination lɛ yaa oya bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Kɛ shwane mli latsaa lɛ ba lɛ, aŋmɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni abu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Why do my tomato plants start falling over into the mud once they begin bearing fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgbeeɔ muji lɛ mli beni amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi lɛ?

english: As tomato plants develop fruits, the heavy weight overpowers their soft stems. Tying the stems gently to upright wooden sticks gives them the physical support they need to stay off the wet ground and avoid rotting.
ga: Kɛ́ tomato tsei lɛ wo yibii lɛ Etsiimɔ fa fe etso bibioo lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ tso ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ fĩ tsei lɛ ahe blɛoo lɛ, ebaaha amɛná gbɔmɔtsoŋ yelikɛbuamɔ ni he hiaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, ni amɛkafite.

english: Watering early in the morning is best because it gives the roots moisture to survive the hot sun during the day, while allowing any water splashed on the leaves to dry quickly so fungal diseases do not grow.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ ehaa shishifãi lɛ náa ŋmɔtɔ koni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha nu ni akɛshwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ agbi oya koni ŋmeii helai akakwɛ̃.

english: How can I keep growing and harvesting vegetables all year long even during the long dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ madu aduawai ni makpa afi muu lɛ fɛɛ, yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ mli po?

english: You can farm year-round by keeping soil covered with dry grass (mulching) to hold moisture, collecting groundwater, and using simple drip watering systems so plants get steady moisture even when the rains stop.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsu okwaayeli afi muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛtsɔ jwɛi (mulch) ni okɛbaawo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli lɛ nɔ. shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni akɛtoɔ Ni okɛ nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ atsu nii ni okɛha tsei lɛ aná nu be fɛɛ be beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa po lɛ.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to keep grass roots in the soil on sloping land instead of clearing everything clean?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔha jwɛi ni yɔɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋshɔ lɛ shishi lɛ mli lɛ ahi shi moŋ fe ni wɔbaajie nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni he tse lɛ?

english: Plant roots act like tiny hands holding the soil together. If you clear all roots on a slope, heavy rains will easily wash away the rich topsoil, leaving behind poor soil that cannot support crops.
ga: Tse shishifãi tsuɔ nii tamɔ niji bibii. ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ekome Kɛji ojie shishifãi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ gɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ nɔ oya. Shikpɔŋ ni ehiii ni nyɛŋ akwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ eshwɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight. Fast-growing shade plants like plantains or large forest trees act as natural umbrellas, keeping the soil cool and protecting the cocoa leaves from scorching during their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa oya, tamɔ tsei bibii loo koo mli tsei wuji tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo baai lɛ ahe koni amɛkashã yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: If too many shoots grow around the main plantain stem, they steal water and nutrients from it. Removing extra shoots leaves only one or two strong stems, which results in larger plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii wuji lɛ dara yɛ tsei babaoo ahe lɛ Ebaaju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ nakai tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, eshiɔ ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni no haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually indicate that the plant is hungry for nitrogen in the soil or that heavy rains have waterlogged the roots, preventing them from feeding properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eha shishifãi lɛ amli ewo nu. Enɛ haaa anyɛ ana niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: What causes small holes in my maize leaves and caterpillars hiding inside the center of the plant?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm pest, which lays eggs on the leaves so its caterpillars can feed on the tender growing core of the maize plant.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Fall Armyworm, ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ baai anɔ koni ŋmeii lɛ aye ŋmãa tso lɛ mli ŋmãa ni miida ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: You should plant cassava cuttings with the raised leaf nodes or 'eyes' pointing upward toward the sky so the shoots can grow straight above ground while the roots develop below.
ga: Esa akɛ odu yucca tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi ni baai lɛ ashishifãi loo ‘ashishifãi’ ni awó nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to place long wooden stakes next to my growing yam vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama emasɛi lɛ? Amɛduɔ sweet potato wain tsei

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need sunlight to create energy for tuber growth. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet ground toward the sun, preventing leaf diseases and helping roots grow larger.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa hulu la koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha bulbs lɛ adalɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni efɔ lɛ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ he. Etsiɔ baa helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by an uneven water supply or a lack of calcium in the soil while the tomato fruit is forming.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nu ni ejaaa loo calcium ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli be mli ni tomato yibii lɛ miifee lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, keeps the soil moist in hot weather, stops heavy rain from washing away soil nutrients, and reduces weed growth.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Etsiɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekajie niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. ni eha jwɛi ni yaa hiɛ lɛ aba shi

english: Why do my crop leaves wither and drop their flowers when the dry Harmattan wind starts blowing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi beni Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ jeɔ shishi etswaa lɛ?

english: The dry Harmattan air rapidly draws moisture out of plant leaves and flowers. The plant drops its blossoms to save water and protect itself from drying out completely.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ baai kɛ fɔfɔi lɛ amli oya. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi kwraa.

english: Apply fertilizer when the ground is moist but not during intense rainstorms. If applied right before heavy downpours, the water will wash the fertilizer away before roots can absorb it.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi jeee yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ akɛwo mli dani nugbɔ nɛ waa Nu baaho ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my cassava so the tubers do not spoil in the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei? Koni ŋmeii lɛ akafite yɛ sũ lɛ mli?

english: Different cassava varieties take between 9 to 12 months to reach full maturity. By tracking the exact time you planted, you can check maturity around that window; harvesting too early gives low starch yields, while waiting too long makes the roots woody and watery.
ga: Cassava henɔi srɔtoi Ebaahe nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 dani eshɛ shweremɔ he. Kɛtsɔ be pɔtɛɛ ni odu lɛ nɔ Obaanyɛ okwɛ emuuyeli ni bɔle nakai samflɛ lɛ he lɛ. Kɛ́ akpa mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha starch ni anáa lɛ aba shi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, mɛmɔ be kakadaŋŋ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ tsei kɛ nu.

english: Why is it important for me to write down the exact date I planted my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maŋma gbi pɔtɛɛ ni midu mi-ŋmã lɛ?

english: Keeping record of your planting date helps you accurately predict key growth stages like flowering and maturity based on the seed variety's natural timeline, allowing you to time fertilizer application, prepare labor, and set up storage before harvest day.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ gbi ni adu lɛ wo wolo nɔ lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ otsɔɔ bɔ ni ŋmɔ lɛ daa lɛ mli nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Edamɔ adebɔɔ mli be ni dumɔwui srɔtoi lɛ yɔɔ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa onyɛɔ otoɔ be ni okɛbaawo ŋmɔshi nibii amli, osaa ohe kɛha fɔmɔ, ni otoɔ he ni okɛtoɔ nii lɛ dani kpamɔɔ gbi lɛ baashɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize turning yellow even though we are getting enough rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Nɛgbɛ ji he ni nugbɔ miinɛ bɔ ni sa?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed to stay green and healthy. Rain provides water, but if nitrogen is depleted from the soil, the plant starves and draws nutrients from its lower leaves to feed new growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii mli hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ehiɛ hewalɛ. Nugbɔ haa nu, shi kɛji akɛ nitrogen lɛ ba shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tso lɛ hɔmɔ yeɔ lɛ ni ejieɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow huge stems and leaves but produce very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kɛ baai wuji shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen but lacks potassium, the crop puts all its growth energy into leafy green foliage above ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo shi potassium bɛ mli lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ amɛdalɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ starch toɔ tso ɔ sisi fã nɛ ngɛ sisi ɔ mi.

english: Why do my tomato blossoms drop off the plant without turning into tomatoes during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when temperatures get too high because extreme heat damages the pollen and prevents fruit formation. Providing shade or watering during cooler parts of the day helps the flowers survive and set fruit.
ga: Tomato shwieɔ fɔfɔii kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ ejaakɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa lɛ fiteɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ni ehaaa aduawai afee. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo be loo nu ha fɔfɔi lɛ yɛ gbi lɛ mli ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do some of my maize cobs have missing seeds and are not fully filled with grains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ ekomɛi efee efolo ni ŋmãa eyi mli obɔ lɛ?

english: Maize cobs fail to fill completely when pollination is interrupted by drought or heat when the silks emerge, or when plants are spaced too far apart for the wind to effectively carry pollen from the tassels to the silks.
ga: Abɛi ŋmɔji nyɛŋ ayi obɔ kwraa kɛji akɛ hɔmɔ loo dɔlɛ tsi pollination naa beni siliki baa lɛ. aloo be mli ni tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ aŋɔ pollen kɛjɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli kɛya siliki lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa plants scorch and turn brown during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain alongside young cocoa protects them from heat stress until their roots are deep enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, kɛfata kookoo bibii ahe lɛ, ebaabu tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baakɔ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and stopping the crop from growing properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids, thrips, or mites feeding on the leaf sap and transmitting viruses that distort growth and stunt the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo mites ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni amɛhaa helai ni fiteɔ tso lɛ dalɛ ni ehaa tso lɛ sɛɛ foɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. Rotating them with heavy-feeding crops like maize naturally restores soil fertility for the next planting season.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Niyenii nibii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ni akɛtsakeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo ekoŋŋ kɛha ŋmãa be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Sweet potatoes have delicate skins that easily cut during harvest, allowing soil fungi to enter. Curing them in a warm, shaded area for a few days hardens their skin and heals tiny cuts, preventing rot during storage.
ga: Sweet potatoes yɛ hewolo ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni abaanyɛ afo mli oya yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ boteɔ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ wo he ko ni hulutsoo yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli gbii fioo komɛi lɛ, ebaaha amɛhewolo lɛ mli awa ni ebaatsa pilamɔi bibii. Etsiɔ fitemɔ naa yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: What basic things can I do on my farm to make sure my cocoa trees produce a lot of pods?
ga: Mɛɛ shishijee nibii manyɛ mafee yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mana nɔmimaa akɛ cacao tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii babaoo?

english: Taking good care of your cocoa trees by clearing weeds, pruning properly, spraying against pests, and feeding them with fertilizer builds up their strength so they can produce and support a heavy harvest.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ akwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ nɔ Atsemɔ ni sa Spray ni akɛtsiɔ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ anaa Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛyeɔ niyenii lɛ baaha hewalɛ aya hiɛ bɔni afee ni cacao tsei lɛ anyɛ awo yibii babaoo ni amɛye amɛbua ŋmaa babaoo.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa tree is healthy enough to support a big harvest this season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cacao tsei lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkpa nii babaoo yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: A healthy cocoa tree displays vibrant green leaves, clean bark free from insect damage, and abundant, firm young flowers blossoming along its main trunk and branches.
ga: Cacao tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli ni kpɛɔ. Bark ni he tse ni kooloi efiteee lɛ. ni fɔfɔi bibii babaoo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ ni fɔ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi kɛ niji wuji lɛ anɔ.

english: How does putting fertilizer on my cocoa farm actually help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Fertilizer acts as direct food for the soil and tree, giving cocoa the essential nutrients it needs to grow strong stems, produce more flowers, and keep fruits healthy.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii tɛ̃ɛ kɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ tsei lɛ. Enɛ haa kookoo lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ tsei ni wa. Ha fɔfɔi babaoo ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni aduawai lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do some of my cocoa trees stay weak even when there is plenty of rain on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ekomɛi bɛ hewalɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Water alone is not enough if the soil lacks key nutrients. Trees need additional plant food through fertilizer to build up the energy required for strong growth.
ga: Nu pɛ faaa kɛji akɛ niyenii titrii bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei he miihia tsei niyenii krokomɛi kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara waa.

english: Flowers drop when the tree lacks necessary plant nutrients or gets stressed by pests; using the right fertilizer feeds the tree so flowers can successfully mature into young pods.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa loo tsɛŋemɔ helai miigba enaa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ anyɛ adara jogbaŋŋ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii.

english: What causes small green cocoa pods to fall off the tree before they mature?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ? Tso lɛ nɔ gbee shi dani eda?

english: Young pods often drop off when the tree does not have enough nutrients to feed all of them or when pests attack; giving the tree proper fertilizer and care helps it retain its fruit until harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛ fɛɛ amɛye loo kɛ́ ŋmeii tutua amɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ kɛ tso lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ eyibii lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ be mli.

english: What helps young cocoa pods grow big and full of healthy beans?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ ebuaa kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛyiɔ obɔ kɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ?

english: Young cocoa pods develop fully when the tree receives sufficient sunlight, good soil nutrients from fertilizer, and protection from pests through proper spraying.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii bibii lɛ baakwɛ̃ kɛji tso lɛ ná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa. Na niyenii kpakpai yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli. ni otsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa kɛtsɔ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it important for me to spray my cocoa trees regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsofa afɔ kookoo tsei anɔ daa lɛ?

english: Regular spraying protects your cocoa trees and developing pods from harmful insects and fungal diseases that can damage the tree and destroy your crop.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa lɛ shwieɔ kookoo tsei lɛ anɔ daa lɛ, ebuɔ kookoo tsei lɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ ŋmeii ni baanyɛ agbe tsei lɛ ni efite onibii lɛ ahe.

english: Will spraying chemicals on my cocoa trees harm the delicate flowers?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ kookoo tsei anɔ lɛ baaye fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ awui?

english: When you use approved cocoa chemicals correctly, spraying actually protects young flowers and shoots from insect attacks, helping them grow safely into pods.
ga: Kɛ okɛ kookoo tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baabu fɔfɔi bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ni baatutua amɛ lɛ ahe. Ye obua amɛ ni amɛdara shweshweeshwe ni amɛtsɔmɔ pods.

english: What can I do to stop my mature cocoa pods from rotting on the tree before harvest?
ga: Mɛni mafee koni kookoo ŋmeii ni edara lɛ akafite yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani akpa?

english: Applying protective sprays against fungal diseases and removing infected pods quickly keeps rot from spreading and saves your healthy harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ fungal disease spray wo ohe ni ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ anaa, ni ebaaye ebua ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, a vital nutrient needed for healthy leaf growth, or that heavy rains have washed nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni baa lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Tomato flowers fall off without fruiting when the weather gets too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when there are no insects around to pollinate the blooms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni yibii bɛ mli kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni kooloi ni baawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ bɛ

english: Leaf curling in peppers is typically caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips, mites, or aphids, which feed on the leaf sap and sometimes transmit plant viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, mites loo aphids, ni yeɔ baa mli nu ni bei komɛi lɛ amɛgbɛɔ tsei ahe helai amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa.

english: Why is it important to leave wide gaps between my cassava plants instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mashi gbɛ yɛ mi yucca tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ

english: Giving cassava space prevents plants from competing for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, allowing the roots under the ground enough space to grow into large, heavy tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ oha o-cassava lɛ hegbɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe wooo hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋshii mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ bulbs agboi ni tsii.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or beans alongside my maize farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer that feeds your maize while shade from their leaves keeps weeds down.
ga: Akpɔlɔi kɛ tsinabii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli. yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo ni baai lɛ haa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa jwɛi lɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: How does spreading dry grass around my vegetable plants help them during dry weather?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua mitsei lɛ ni amɛdara yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry leaves or grass traps moisture in the soil, keeps the plant roots cool from direct sunlight, and breaks down over time to enrich the soil.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ mli jɔɔ kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni amɛfiteɔ yɛ be ni sa mli koni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How can I tell if the soil is wet enough after the first rain to sow my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ koni manyɛ madu dumɔwui?

english: Dig down a few inches into the dirt and squeeze a handful of soil into a ball; if it holds its shape without crumbling or leaking dripping water, it is ready for seeds.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli inchii fioo komɛi ni okɛmimɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ eko mli ni ofee bɔɔlu. Kɛji akɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ egbɛ eshwaaa loo efoŋ lɛ, no lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaadu dumɔwui.

english: Why does planting maize on the exact same piece of land every season cause my harvest to get smaller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: What causes tiny caterpillars to chew holes deep inside the leaves of my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwieɔ bu ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ mi-abele baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, pests that hatch from eggs laid by moths inside the plant funnel and feed heavily on young, soft maize leaves.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmeii ni fɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tsei akui amli lɛ amli, ni amɛyeɔ ŋmeii bibii babaoo.

english: Why do I need to cut off extra branches from my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ niji krokomɛi kɛjɛ kookoo tso ni eda lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning extra branches lets sunlight and fresh air flow through the cocoa canopy, which dries out trapped moisture and prevents black pod disease from spreading.
ga: Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ kookoo tso lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni emɔ mli lɛ agbi. ni etsĩ black pod hela lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient in the soil. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients away or leaves the roots standing in too much water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii loo eha shishifãi lɛ damɔ nu babaoo mli.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to leave dry leaves and grass on top of my soil after clearing my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ bo akɛ oshi baai ni egboi kɛ jwɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ beni ogbe he ni oyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Leaving dry organic material on the soil acts like a blanket called mulch. It keeps the ground cool, preserves water during hot days, and slowly breaks down into natural food for your crops.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni egbi ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ. Ekɛ nu toɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli, ni ejara mli fiofio ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves wither and turn brown during the harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai lɛ egboɔ ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The dry, dusty harmattan winds suck moisture out of plant leaves much faster than roots can pull water from the dry soil. Providing shade trees helps protect cocoa plants from dry winds and harsh sunlight.
ga: Harmatta kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi ni sũ yɔɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Shade yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ hulu la ni naa wa he.

english: How deep should I dig the soil when planting cassava stems on my farm?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu ŋmei tsei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava stem cuttings need loose soil down to about 15 to 20 centimeters. Deep, soft soil allows the roots to swell easily into large, healthy tubers underground.
ga: Kasava tsei lɛ afolɔ biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni mli kwɔ aaafee sɛntimita 15 kɛyashi 20. Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei wuji ni mli wa.

english: Maize uses up a lot of nutrients from the soil. Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the ground, naturally enriching the soil for the next planting season.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why is it necessary to remove weeds from around my crops while they are still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive competitors that steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your crops. Clearing them early gives your crops the best chance to grow strong without stress.
ga: Jwɛi ji akaŋshilɔi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni amɛdara waa ni haomɔ ko bɛ he.

english: Is it better for me to water my garden vegetables in the morning or in the afternoon heat?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mibɔɔ mli aduawai lɛ anɔ nu leebi loo shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning gives plants the hydration they need to survive hot afternoon sunshine while reducing water loss from evaporation.
ga: Nu ni afɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ haa tso lɛ náa nu ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa nu ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi.

english: Flowers drop when plants experience heat stress, extended dry spells, or lack of pollination. Keeping soil moisture steady helps the plant hold onto its blossoms so they turn into fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. be kakadaŋŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli loo pollination ni bɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why should I leave space between my plantain suckers instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ yɛ plantain tsei lɛ ateŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots fight each other for water and nutrients, and their leaves block sunlight from one another, resulting in smaller bunches.
