ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. ni baai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tso bibioo ko

english: How can I tell that my yams are ready to be harvested beneath the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When the yam leaves and vines above the ground begin to turn yellow and dry up naturally, it means the plant has finished sending energy down into the tuber and the yam is ready to dig up.
ga: Beni sweet potato baai kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe hewalɛ ni ekɛbaa shi kɛyaa bulb lɛ mli lɛ naa. Ni yams lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakumɔ.

english: Why should I plant plantain trees close to my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under hot direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that provide shade and moisture to protect young cocoa until it is mature enough to survive full sun.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni buɔ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulutsoo be fɛɛ mli ŋɔɔmɔ.

english: Yellow bottom leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential plant food. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps the plant regain its healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Which direction should the buds point when I am planting cassava stem cuttings?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu ŋmei niji lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ ŋmeii lɛ atsɔɔ?

english: Cassava cuttings must be planted with the buds pointing upwards toward the sky so the shoots can grow straight out easily without wasting energy.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ ni ŋmeii lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ tɛ̃ɛ oya ni mɔdɛŋbɔɔ ko bɛ he.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by intense heat, improper watering, or a lack of insects to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. nu ni esaaa loo kooloi ni bɛ ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee pollin

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can trap as much sunlight as possible to make big yam tubers underground, while keeping the leaves off damp soil where diseases live.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ aná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛha ŋmeii wuji ahi shikpɔŋ shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni hela lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ he.

english: How does growing groundnuts or cowpeas help improve my soil for next season?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When left in the ground, they feed the soil naturally with fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Amɛbaahã shikpɔŋ lɛ aná ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling inward into tight cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle kɔɔpoi ni mli wa lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Curling leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips sucking the juice out of young leaves, or by a leaf-curl virus spread by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ leaf curl hela ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does lowland swamp rice grow better when kept in standing water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ marsh rice lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛwo nu ni mli ejɔ mli lɛ?

english: Standing water suffocates weeds that try to steal plant food from the rice, while keeping the soil loose and wet so rice roots can feed easily.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi lɛ baaha jwɛi ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛju niyenii kɛjɛ tsei lɛ amli lɛ agbɔjɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aye nii mlɛo.

english: Why must I dry my harvested maize grains until they are hard before putting them in sacks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli kɛyashi ebaawa dani mikɛwo kotokui amli lɛ?

english: Wet maize breeds dangerous mold and attracts weevils, which will rot and destroy your harvest while it is stored in sacks.
ga: Abɛi ni efɔ lɛ fɔɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni egbalaa ŋmeii. Enɛ baafite ni efite onibii lɛ beni okɛtoɔ kotokui lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why should I plant my seeds in straight, measured rows instead of scattering them across the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja, ni asusu he lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooogbɛ dumɔwui lɛ oshwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ

english: Row planting ensures every plant gets equal space, sunlight, and nutrients without crowding, while making it easy for you to clear weeds and harvest.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ haa tsei lɛ fɛɛ naa he ko, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ amɛhe ebɔko amɛhe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa bo akɛ oookpa jwɛi ni oookpa.

english: Can I plant Prekese seeds directly into my farm soil, or do I need to prepare them first?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu Prekese dumɔwui awo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ? Aloo esa akɛ masaa he dã?

english: Prekese seeds have very hard outer coats that stop water from getting inside easily. If you plant them straight into the soil, they can take months to sprout or rot; it is best to soak or gently scrape the seed coat and start them in nursery bags first.
ga: Prekese dumɔwui lɛ yɛ kponɔgbɛ fã ko ni wa waa ni haaa nu abote mli mlɛo. Kɛji odu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ Amɛbaanyɛ amɛhe nyɔji babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ loo amɛgboi. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ awo nu mli loo okɛshwie shi fioo. No sɛɛ lɛ, je shishi okɛ gbekɛbii akwɛmɔ kotokui lɛ awo mli klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Can I grow Prekese trees on the same piece of land with my food crops like maize and cassava?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu Prekese yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ niyenii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, you can plant young Prekese trees alongside crops like maize or cassava during the first few years. However, as the tree grows larger, its wide branches will shade out smaller crops, so it is best to give it enough space or plant it near farm boundaries.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu Prekese dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Shi, beni tsei lɛ daraa lɛ, Eniji ni mli kwɔlɔ lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, no hewɔ lɛ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha lɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa loo ooodu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmɔ husui lɛ.

english: Why does a Prekese tree take several years before it starts producing pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ afii babaoo dani Prekese tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Prekese is a long-term forest tree that spends its early years developing a deep root system and a sturdy trunk to support heavy branches. It naturally takes between four to seven years to mature enough to bear pods.
ga: Prekese ji koo mli tso ko ni ehiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛ eshishijee afii lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛkwɛɔ. Koni afee shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ tso ni mli wa ni baaye abua tsei niji ni tsii lɛ. Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, eheɔ aaafee afii ejwɛ kɛyashi kpawo dani edaa bɔ ni sa ni enáa ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my young Prekese tree turn yellow and drop off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi Prekese tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves during dry periods is the tree's natural way of saving water and surviving intense heat. Once the rains return, the tree will sprout fresh green leaves again.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ nu he ni ehiɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tsei lɛ baakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do flowers on my tree drop off without turning into Prekese pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii ni etsɔ hiɛ amɛba lɛ?

english: Trees drop flowers when they experience stress from prolonged heat, lack of soil nutrients, or insufficient rainfall. Without enough water and energy, the tree cannot support the flowers to form fruits.
ga: Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛbote dɔlɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛji nu kɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɛ Tsei nyɛŋ aye abua fɔfɔi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: How do I know when Prekese pods are mature and ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi Prekese pods lɛ edara kwraa ni efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ?

english: Mature Prekese pods turn from green to a shiny dark reddish-brown or purplish color and produce a strong, sweet smell. They also drop naturally from the tree when fully ripe.
ga: Prekese pods ni eda lɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa etsuru-brɔw ni mli edɔ loo purple ni kpɛɔ. ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni naa wa Amɛ hu amɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ kwraa.

english: Why are the Prekese pods on some of my trees much smaller than those on other trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Prekese pods ni yɔɔ mi tsei lɛ ekomɛi anɔ lɛ ji bibioo kwraa fe ekrokomɛi lɛ?

english: Pod size depends on soil nutrients, access to sunlight, and water availability. Trees growing in rich, moist soil with good sunlight will produce larger, plumper pods than trees in poor soil.
ga: Pod lɛ dalɛ damɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. hulu la ni anáa kɛ nu ni yɔɔ Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ, ni hulu la babaoo yɔɔ nɔ lɛ baawo ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ fe tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why are some of my green Prekese pods falling off the tree early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi Prekese pods eŋɔli lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ oya nɛkɛ?

english: Premature pod drop usually happens when insects attack the young fruits or when the tree experiences sudden dry spells. Checking the fallen green pods for small insect holes can help confirm if pests are the problem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pod ni shwieɔ shi oya lɛ baa kɛji kooloi bibii tutua aduawai bibii loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na hulutsoo be trukaa. Kwɛmɔ pods eŋɔli ni egbee shi lɛ mli kɛha kooloi bibii buji. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛye amɛbua kɛma nɔ mi kɛji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ji naagba.

english: Does a Prekese tree need continuous watering to grow well, or can it survive dry weather?
ga: Prekese tsei lɛ he miihia ni afɔ amɛ nu be fɛɛ be koni amɛshwere. Aloo ani ebaanyɛ ehi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli?

english: Young Prekese seedlings need regular watering to establish their roots. However, once the tree matures, its deep taproot reaches groundwater, allowing it to survive long dry seasons without artificial watering.
ga: Prekese dumɔwui lɛ biɔ ni afɔ amɛ nu daa koni amɛshishifãi lɛ aya hiɛ. Shi, beni tsei lɛ daraa lɛ, Babaoo ni taproot lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ shɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ he. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ ahiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli ni akɛ nu ni akɛfee lɛ tsuuu nii.

english: What kind of soil makes medicinal trees like Prekese grow best and yield good fruits?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ nɛkɛ haa tsofa tsei tamɔ Prekese lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni hi fe fɛɛ?

english: Prekese trees grow best in deep, well-drained loamy soil rich in organic matter. Soils that collect too much standing water can rot the tree's roots, while rich, well-drained soil promotes healthy fruit production.
ga: Prekese tsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu ni damɔ shi babaoo toɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei shishifãi lɛ agbo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni nɔ eyi obɔ kɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa aduawai ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa.

english: Why do some modern seed bags have numbers like 26 or 34 on them instead of traditional local names?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ dumɔwui kotokui komɛi yɛ yibɔi tamɔ 26 loo 34 yɛ maŋ lɛ mli kusum gbɛi lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Seed producers use specific code numbers to label improved or hybrid seed varieties so farmers can identify their exact characteristics, such as high yield, fast growth, or disease resistance.
ga: Mɛi ni feɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛ kood yibɔi pɔtɛɛi tsuɔ nii kɛkadiɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni atsake loo ni akɛfee ekome lɛ. Bɔni afee ni okwaafoi lɛ anyɛ atsɔɔ sui pɔtɛɛ tamɔ yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo, dalɛ oya, loo helai ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ lɛ.

english: Why do improved seed varieties yield so much more food than the local seeds I have used for years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ woɔ niyenii babaoo fe maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui ni mikɛtsuɔ nii afii babaoo lɛ?

english: Improved seeds are specially bred by plant scientists to combine the strongest traits of different plant parents, making them produce more pods, grains, or fruits than traditional seeds.
ga: Tsei ahe nilelɔi ji mɛi ni fɔɔ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ titri koni amɛkɛ sui ni mli wa fe fɛɛ ni yɔɔ tsei afɔlɔi srɔtoi lɛ amli lɛ afata he. Enɛ haa amɛwoɔ ŋmeii, dumɔwui loo aduawai babaoo fe blema dumɔwui.

english: If I plant an improved seed variety this season, can I keep some seeds from my harvest to plant next year?
ga: Kɛji midu dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ yɛ be nɛɛ mli Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui komɛi ni jɛ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu afi ni baa lɛ?

english: It is not recommended to replant harvested seeds from hybrid varieties because their offspring will lose their strong traits, resulting in uneven growth and a much lower harvest compared to buying fresh certified seeds.
ga: Akɛ ŋaawoo haaa akɛ adu dumɔwui ni akpa momo kɛjɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ ekoŋŋ. Ejaakɛ seshi lɛ baafite amɛsui ni mli wa lɛ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee kɛ ŋmaa ni akpaa lɛ baa shi kwraa kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ ahemɔ he.

english: Why do my crops grow very fast at first but fail to produce big fruits when the dry season starts early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya waa yɛ shishijee mli shi amɛwooo yibii wuji beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi mra lɛ?

english: Crops need steady water to transport nutrients into their developing fruits. When dry weather hits, the plant stops making big fruits and uses its remaining energy just to keep itself alive.
ga: Nu ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ he miihia tsei koni amɛkɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ aya aduawai ni miiya hiɛ lɛ amli. Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ tswa lɛ Tso lɛ kpaɔ yibii wuji ni ekɛ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛha ehe ahi wala mli kɛkɛ.

english: How can I safely test a new crop variety on my farm without risking my whole family's food supply?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka tsei srɔtoi heei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ makwɛ shweshweeshwe ni mikɛ miweku muu lɛ fɛɛ niyenii ni amɛnáa lɛ wooo oshara mli?

english: You can plant the new variety on a small plot next to your regular crops for one season to see how it handles your local soil and rain before committing your entire farm to it.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu tsei srɔtoi heei yɛ he bibioo ko. Yɛ onibii ni oduɔ daa lɛ masɛi kɛha be kome koni ona bɔ ni etsuɔ ​​omaŋ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ nugbɔ lɛ he nii eha dani okpɛ oyiŋ akɛ okɛ shika baawo ŋmɔ muu fɛɛ mli.

english: Why do some short-season crops mature in three months while my old seeds take four or five months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ shwereɔ yɛ nyɔji etɛ mli yɛ be mli ni midumɔwui momo lɛ he nyɔji ejwɛ loo enumɔ lɛ?

english: Short-season crop varieties are bred to complete their life cycle faster so farmers can harvest full yields even when the rainy season is short or unpredictable.
ga: Akwɛɔ tsei srɔtoi ni yeɔ be kukuoo lɛ koni amɛgbe amɛshihilɛ be lɛ naa oya. Bɔni afee ni okwaafoi lɛ anyɛ akpa amɛŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛyashɛ he ni amɛshɛɔ he fɛɛ he kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ faaa loo anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba po.

english: Why do high-yielding crop varieties seem to need more fertilizer than my local crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fe tsei ni yɔɔ mimaŋ lɛ?

english: Because high-yielding crops grow faster and produce much heavier harvests, they require more food and nutrients from the soil to support that extra growth.
ga: Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni tsii babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ niyenii kɛ niyenii babaoo he miihia amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eye ebua nakai dalɛ kroko lɛ.

english: Will planting my seeds very close together give me a bigger total harvest from my land?
ga: Ani dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ he kroko lɛ baaha maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: No, planting seeds too close together forces the crops to fight for sunlight, water, and nutrients, resulting in weak plants and very small yields.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ.

english: Why do some crop varieties stay green and healthy while insect pests attack other plants right next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛhe yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ be mli ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tutuaa tsei krokomɛi ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ?

english: Certain crop varieties are bred with natural resistance that deters pests or allows the plant to heal quickly, keeping them healthy while non-resistant plants suffer.
ga: Akwɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi koni amɛná adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ni tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa loo ehaa tso lɛ tsaa oya. Enɛ haa tsei náa hewalɛ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni nyɛɛɛ amɛshi amɛhe lɛ naa amanehulu.

english: How do I test my stored seeds to make sure they will sprout before I waste my time planting them in the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka dumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ makwɛ koni mana nɔmimaa akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ dani mafite be kɛdu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: You can place ten seeds inside a damp cloth for a few days; if eight or more sprout, your seeds are fresh and healthy enough to plant in your field.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ dumɔwui nyɔŋma awo mama ni mli efɔ mli. gbii fioo komɛi Kɛji ŋmeii kpaanyɔ loo nɔ ni fe nakai Odumɔwui lɛ baafee ehee ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni obaanyɛ odu yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need direct sunlight to make food for themselves. When you give them sticks to climb, their leaves catch more sunlight instead of lying on the ground, which results in much larger and healthier tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛfee amɛ niyenii. Beni oha nine lɛ kwɔ Amɛbaai lɛ baaná hulu la babaoo moŋ fe ni amɛaakã shikpɔŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ daraa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in a field with no tall trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei kakadaji bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under strong sunlight. Shade crops like plantains or tall trees act like giant umbrellas, protecting the young plants from heat stroke and keeping moisture in the soil until the cocoa grows strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei kakadaji tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela wuji. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ dɔlɛ he. ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean the maize plant is starving for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient that keeps leaves green. When there isn't enough nitrogen in the soil, the plant pulls it from its older bottom leaves to feed the growing top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ baai lɛ ashishi feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmei tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nitrogen ni fa Tsei lɛ gbalaa lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when heavy rain leaves standing water on my farm for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu lɛ ŋmɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy and breathe. When land stays flooded, the water pushes out all the air pockets in the soil, causing the roots to suffocate and rot.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia cassava shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛmu. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi lolo lɛ Nu lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do tiny worms hide inside the rolled-up central leaves of my young maize plants during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe teeɔ mi-babi corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai ni abɔle amɛhe lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Those are likely Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They crawl deep into the center roll of the maize plant because it stays cooler, darker, and more humid there, protecting them from hot weather, birds, and chemical sprays.
ga: Ekolɛ Fall Armyworms, amɛkpãa kɛyaa ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ ejaakɛ jɛmɛ mli ejɔ, eyɛ duŋ ni edɔ waa, ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ, okpoi kɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and drop off the plant without growing into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛfeɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too high or when the plant doesn't get enough water. If the plant feels heat stress, it sheds its flowers to save energy to keep itself alive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Kɛji tso lɛ miinu dɔlɛ he haomɔ he lɛ Eshwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛbu hewalɛ ni ekɛha ehe ahi wala mli lɛ he.

english: Why do my plantain plants easily fall over in strong winds right when the fruit bunch gets big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli beni aduawai akui lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants do not have deep taproots; their roots spread out shallowly near the surface. As the fruit bunch grows heavier, the plant becomes top-heavy, and strong winds can easily pull the shallow roots out of wet soil unless you support the stem with a bamboo fork.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Eshishifãi lɛ gbɛ eshwa fioo ni bɛŋkɛ nu lɛ hiɛ beni aduawai akutsei lɛ amli tsiimɔ yaa hiɛ lɛ. Tso lɛ baatsii waa. Ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ. Ejeɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ mlɛo Ja okɛ ŋmei fɔk tsu nii ni okɛfi tso lɛ shishi.

english: Why does my cashew tree produce hundreds of flowers but only a small number of cashew nuts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cashew tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔii ohai abɔ shi cashew ŋmeii fioo pɛ woɔ lɛ?

english: Cashew trees produce two types of flowers: male flowers that only produce pollen, and hermaphrodite flowers that can actually form nuts. Most of the flowers on the tree are male flowers, so only a small percentage of flowers are capable of turning into nuts.
ga: Cashew tsei woɔ fɔfɔi henɔi enyɔ: fɔfɔi hii ni woɔ fɔfɔi pɛ; kɛ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ hii kɛ yei ateŋ ni baanyɛ afee ŋmei su diɛŋtsɛ. Fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ tsei anɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo ji hii. No hewɔ lɛ, fɔfɔii lɛ amli oha mlijaa fioo ko pɛ baanyɛ atsɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do my maize crops grow thin and produce small cobs when I put four or five seeds in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ mli tse ni ewoɔ toi bibii lɛ? Beni akɛ dumɔwui ejwɛ loo enumɔ woɔ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When too many seeds are planted in the same spot, the plants fight each other underground for soil nutrients and water, and fight above ground for sunlight. Giving each plant its own space prevents this competition so every plant gets full nourishment.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ he kome lɛ Tsei wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. ni amɛwuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la lɛ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akaŋshii akafee nɔ ko. No hewɔ lɛ, tso fɛɛ tso baaná niyenii ni yeɔ emuu.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or groundnuts on my farmland make the soil better for the maize I plant next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that work with helpful soil microbes to pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When the crop season ends, this stored nitrogen stays in the soil as free food for the next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen gas kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto sũ lɛ mli. Kɛji dumɔ be lɛ ba naagbee Nitrogen ni ato nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are agricultural extension officers telling us not to cut down all the big trees on our cocoa farms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔkafo tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ wɔ kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Big trees act like a natural forest canopy on your farm. They create a healthy environment by providing shade and protecting soil moisture, while hosting beneficial insects that help your cocoa trees bear more fruit.
ga: Tsei ni eda lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛhaa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛtsɔ shade ni amɛhaa kɛ sũ mli ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛbuɔ he lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, jɛmɛ ji he ni kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa o-cacao tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo lɛ yɔɔ.

english: Will removing all old forest trees from my land help my cocoa trees get more sun and produce better?
ga: Ani koo mli tsei momoi fɛɛ ni ajie kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua kookoo tsei lɛ ni amɛná hulu la babaoo ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai?

english: No, clearing all shade trees actually harms your farm. Cocoa trees perform best when supported by shade trees, as complete open sun stresses the crop and removes the natural shelter needed by beneficial insects that help produce pods.
ga: Dabi, tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ fɛɛ ni oootsi lɛ yeɔ oŋmɔ lɛ awui diɛŋtsɛ. Cocoa tsei tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ fiɔ amɛsɛɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ ni ejieɔ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni he hiaa lɛ kɛha kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛmaa ŋmeii lɛ.

english: How does keeping wild shade trees on my farm actually help my cocoa crops yield more pods?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ akwɛmɔ baanyɛ aye abua mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ni amɛwo ŋmeii babaoo?

english: Wild trees turn your farm into a mini-forest shelter. They attract helpful insects that travel between flowers, ensuring more cocoa blossoms get pollinated and successfully turn into full cocoa pods.
ga: Koo Tsei lɛ tsɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli efeɔ koo mli shĩa bibioo ko. Amɛgbalaa kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni nyiɛɔ fɔfɔi ateŋ lɛ. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ ashɛɔ kookoo fɔfɔi babaoo ahe ni amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii yɛ omanyeyeli mli.

english: Why do cocoa trees need other non-cocoa shade trees growing around them to stay productive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei krokomɛi he hiaa kookoo tsei fe tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ? bɔni afee ni nibii ni anáa lɛ ahi shi

english: Cocoa originally comes from forest environments. Non-cocoa trees mimic this natural habitat, giving your farm the ecosystem it needs to sustain pollinators and keep cocoa trees healthy during hot seasons.
ga: Shishijee lɛ, kookoo jɛɔ kooi amli shihilɛi amli. Cocoa tsei kaseɔ nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli shihilɛhe nɛɛ. Ha oŋmɔ lɛ bɔɔ nii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ ni he hiaa koni ekɛkwɛ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ anɔ, ni eha cacao tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli nyɔji ni mli edɔ lɛ amli.

english: Why do many of my cocoa flowers drop off the tree without ever turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ babaoo shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee kookoo ŋmɔtɔi kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers fall off when they are not pollinated by tiny insects. If your farm lacks natural forest cover or surrounding trees, there won't be enough insects around to pollinate the flowers and form pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe wooo mli. Kɛji akɛ oŋmɔ lɛ bɛ adebɔɔ mli koo loo tsei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Kooloi bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ bɛ.

english: Why do cocoa farms situated close to natural forests usually harvest more pods than fully cleared land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ adebɔɔ mli kooi lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛkpa ŋmeii babaoo fe hei ni ajie ŋmeii lɛ kwraa lɛ?

english: Forest areas shelter high populations of pollinating insects. These insects move from forest plants onto your cocoa flowers, leading to higher fruit set and better harvests.
ga: Kooi amli hei ji hei ni ŋmeii babaoo ni shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ yɔɔ. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ fãa kɛjɛɔ koo mli tsei amli kɛyaa kookoo fɔfɔi amli. Enɛ haa aduawai babaoo baa, ni anáa kpamɔ kpakpa.

english: What natural method can I use to increase the number of cocoa pods on my trees without buying expensive inputs?
ga: Mɛɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛi manyɛ matsɔ nɔ maha kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ aya hiɛ ni miheee nibii ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ?

english: Preserving selective forest trees on your farm maintains natural insect populations. These insects pollinate your cocoa flowers naturally, directly increasing the number of pods your trees produce.
ga: Koo mli tsei ni ahala ni oookwɛ nɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni adebɔɔ mli kooloi ayibɔ yaa hiɛ. Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ feɔ kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ mli ŋmeii ayibɔ yaa hiɛ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Are all the small insects visiting my cocoa flowers harmful pests that I need to spray with chemicals?
ga: Ani kooloi bibii ni baa mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ ji kooloi ni yɔɔ oshara ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai afɔ amɛnɔ?

english: No, many tiny insects are beneficial pollinators. Spraying them kills the useful bugs that transfer pollen between cocoa flowers, which actually reduces the number of pods your trees will grow.
ga: Dabi, kooloi bibii babaoo ji ŋmeii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baagbe kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni kɛ pollen yaa kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni tso lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ ayibɔ baa shi.

english: How do wild flowers on surrounding trees help my cocoa farm produce a bigger harvest?
ga: Koo mli fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ anɔ Te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ ni ewo yibii babaoo?

english: Wild forest flowers attract tiny pollinating insects to your farm area. Once these insects arrive, they also visit your cocoa flowers, helping them set fruit and grow into harvestable cocoa pods.
ga: Koo mli fɔfɔii gbalaa kooloi bibii ni shwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Ba oŋmɔ lɛ mli Kɛ́ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ bashɛ Amɛbaasara o-cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ hu. Ye obua amɛ ni amɛwo yibii ni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔmɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni abaanyɛ akpa.

english: How do tiny forest insects know to visit cocoa flowers to help them grow into pods?
ga: Kplukai ni yɔɔ koo bibioo ko mli Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni esa akɛ oyasara kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔmɔ ŋmeii?

english: Tiny insects are naturally drawn to flower blossoms in forest environments looking for food. As they rush between nearby forest flowers and cocoa flowers, they accidentally transfer pollen, allowing the cocoa tree to bear abundant fruit.
ga: Kɛjɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, kooloi bibii sumɔɔ fɔfɔi ni fɔ̃ɔ yɛ kooi amli koni amɛtao niyenii. Beni amɛjoɔ foi yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ yɛ koo lɛ mli ni bɛŋkɛ kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ, Amɛfeɔ pollination yɛ oshara mli. Cacao tsei woɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Young cocoa plants are delicate and dry out easily under direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow quickly and have large leaves that act as natural shade umbrellas, keeping the cocoa seedlings cool and soil moist during their early growth.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa, ni kɛ́ hulu lɛ tso amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, amɛgbiɔ oya. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli shade. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hu feɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shishijee mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop lacks nitrogen, which is the key food plants need to make leaves green and grow tall. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores their green color and strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha ehiɛ afee ŋmɔŋ kɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce big leafy bushes but very small underground roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ jwɛi wuji kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi bibii waa lɛ?

english: If soil has too much foliage-building nutrients or is packed down hard, the plant spends all its energy growing leaves above ground. Loosening the soil allows the cassava to push outward and store its energy in thick roots.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ niyenii ni haa baai feɔ babaoo tsɔ loo nibii ni wa ebɔle he lɛ, Tsei kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ̃ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ toɔ eshishifãi ni mli tse lɛ amli.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts in the same field help my corn grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and release it into the earth, naturally feeding nearby crops like corn without damaging the soil.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ejieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ekɛ niyenii haa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa, ni efiteee shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why do small caterpillars eat holes in my young maize leaves mostly during the night?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu yɛ mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli babaoo gbɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Pests like the Fall Armyworm hide deep inside the center of the maize plant during the hot day to avoid the sun, then come out at night when it is cool to feed on fresh, soft leaves.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ yɛ gbii ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ amli koni hulu lɛ akashɛ amɛhe. Kɛkɛ lɛ amɛjeɔ kpo gbɛkɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ koni amɛbaye baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ.

english: Why do flowers fall off my tomato plants without turning into fruits during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rains and high humidity make flower pollen wet and sticky, preventing bees or wind from moving pollen around. Without successful pollination, the plant drops its flowers instead of developing fruit.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo haa pollen lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ekpɛtɛɔ he. Etsiɔ ŋmeii loo kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekatsi pollen kɛbɔle he. Kɛji akɛ pollination lɛ yeee omanye lɛ Tso lɛ baashwie fɔfɔi yɛ yibiiwoo najiaŋ.

english: Removing small side branches forces the plant to send its water and nutrients directly into making large, healthy tomatoes rather than wasting energy on extra leaves and thin stems.
ga: Niji bibii ni yɔɔ afã lɛ ni afoɔ Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛkɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ aba tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛwo tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ baai kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa lɛ anɔ lɛ,

english: Why do seeds saved from last year's maize harvest yield less food than the store-bought seeds I planted originally?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ ŋmãa kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ wo niyenii fioo fe dumɔwui ni mihe yɛ shwapo mli ni midu yɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Store-bought hybrid seeds are specially cross-bred for high yields, but seeds saved from their harvest lose those strong traits in the second generation, leading to smaller ears and uneven growth.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni aheɔ yɛ shwapoi amli lɛ woɔ mli krɛdɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Shi dumɔwui ni ahere amɛ kɛjɛ kpamɔ mli lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa dumɔwui bibii kɛ dalɛ ni ejaaa baa.

english: Why do my pepper plants suddenly droop and dry up even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ trukaa ni egbiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: This sudden wilting is usually caused by fungal or bacterial rot in the roots. The disease blocks the water channels inside the plant's stem, preventing water in the soil from reaching the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii ni baa trukaa nɛɛ baa. Hela nɛɛ tsiɔ nu gbɛi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ anaa. Etsiɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ naa koni ekashɛ baai lɛ ahe.

english: Weeds grow fast and steal water, sunlight, and food from the soil before your crops get a chance to use them, effectively starving your plants while they are young.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa hegbɛ ni amɛkɛtsu nii. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye otsei lɛ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient plants need to stay green and grow strong. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea helps the crop regain its green color and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛɛmɛi ji tsei ni niyenii ni he hiaa koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa lɛ yɔɔ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli, tamɔ urea tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni ehaa amɛdaraa.

english: Why are my tomato plants growing very tall with many leaves, but almost no fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomatoi lɛ miiya hiɛ waa lɛ? Baai babaoo shi aduawai ko kwraa bɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer makes tomato plants focus all their energy on growing leaves instead of fruits. Switching to fertilizers higher in phosphorus and potassium encourages the crop to produce flowers and fruit.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmɔshi nibii ni phosphorus kɛ potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua otsei lɛ ni amɛwo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai.

english: Why do my vegetable plants wilt in the afternoon heat even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: In hot weather, leaves lose water faster than roots can draw it up from the soil, causing temporary wilting. As temperatures cool down in the evening, the crop usually recovers once water uptake catches up.
ga: yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baa be kukuoo mli Kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ yɛ gbɛkɛ mli lɛ Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi kɛji nu ni shwieɔ mli lɛ tee hiɛ.

english: Why do caterpillars keep eating my maize leaves even after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii sumɔɔ ni amɛye mi-abɛi lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Rain does not wash away pests like fall armyworms because they hide deep inside the crop's leaf funnels. You need specific pest-control chemicals sprayed directly into the funnel to eliminate them.
ga: Nugbɔ lɛ shwieee kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ cutworms lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛkɛ amɛhe ewo ŋmɔshi nibii amli baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ. Esa akɛ okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ afɔ fun lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ koni ojie amɛ.

english: Leaf curling in cassava is often caused by a viral disease spread by tiny whiteflies. Controlling whiteflies with suitable crop protection chemicals early prevents the disease from spreading across your field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni haa ŋmei baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Tsofai ni sa ni buɔ tsei ahe lɛ ni oooye ŋmeii yɛji anɔ mra Ye obua ni helai akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔji lɛ amli fɛɛ.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, damp environments. Pruning cocoa trees to let in sunlight and applying protective chemical sprays keeps the pods healthy.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni nu yɔɔ. Kɛ́ afolɔ kookoo tsei lɛ amli koni hulu la babaoo aba mli, ni akɛ tsofai ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ shwieɔ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I spray pest chemicals on my crops during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Chemicals evaporate quickly in intense heat, reducing their effectiveness, and the combination of hot sun and chemical spray can burn crop leaves. Spraying early in the morning or late afternoon gives the best results.
ga: Tsofai shwieɔ oya yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa mli. kɛ nitsumɔ ni baa shi lɛ baa Ni hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ kɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei ahe baai. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ leebi loo shwane mli lɛ, ebaaha nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ aba.

english: Will spraying weedkiller on my farm damage my cassava roots growing under the soil?
ga: Ani tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baafite ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ shishifãi?

english: Non-selective weedkillers can damage plants if sprayed directly onto crop leaves or green stems, but they do not harm mature tubers underground. Always use crop-safe spray methods and avoid touching the crop leaves.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni halaaa lɛ baanyɛ afite tsei kɛji akɛ afɔse tsei lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ yɛ tsei lɛ ahe baai loo amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ anɔ. Shi eyeŋ ŋmeii ni edara kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ awui. Kɛ gbɛi ni akɛshwieɔ tsofa nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsu nii be fɛɛ be. ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ tsei ahe baai ahe ni oootaa he lɛ he

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a shortage of plant nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist and supplying balanced crop fertilizer prevents flower drop.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni jɛɔ tsei amli lɛ ni bɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ tsei ni akɛ tso ni ja baawo mli lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akagbee shi.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during small storms before the bunches are fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbee shi yɛ ahum bibioo ko mli lɛ? Dani tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ kwraa?

english: Plantain trees fall easily when microscopic pests called nematodes weaken their shallow roots under the soil. Using clean planting materials and chemical soil treatments keeps roots strong enough to hold heavy bunches.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ ha shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ gbɔjɔ. Kɛ akɛ nibii ni akɛduɔ nii ni he tse tsu nii ni akɛ tsofai tsu shikpɔŋ lɛ he nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsu ŋmeii ni tsii ahe nii.

english: Why do the leaves on my young maize plants turn yellow during the heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean the plant is drowning or hungry. Too much standing water pushes air out of the soil and washes away plant nutrients like nitrogen, which maize needs to stay green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miiho loo hɔmɔ miiye lɛ. Nu ni damɔ shi babaoo lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ejieɔ tsei amli niyenii tamɔ nitrogen, ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: If tomato plants lack water, their leaves wiltingly droop and feel dry to the touch. If they are overwatered, the lower leaves turn soft yellow, and the fruit can swell too fast and split open.
ga: Kɛji nu bɛ tomato tso lɛ he lɛ, ebaa lɛ baagbo ni ebaanu he akɛ egbi kɛji ota he. Kɛji nu babaoo yɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Ni aduawai lɛ baanyɛ afuu oya tsɔ ni etswa.

english: Can I water my vegetable crops with river water during the dry season without damaging them?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu ni jɛ faa lɛ mli lɛ awo mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli ni mifiteee amɛ?

english: Yes, using river water during dry spells keeps your vegetables growing when rainfall stops. Just make sure the water is free from mining pollution or heavy silt, which can clog soil and harm plant roots.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ okɛ faa mli nu tsu nii yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua o-vegetables lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa. Kwɛmɔ kɛkɛ akɛ muji ni jɛɔ shika tsuru loo sũ ni mli wa mli baa lɛ bɛ nu lɛ mli. Enɛ baanyɛ atsĩ shikpɔŋ lɛ naa ni eye tsei shishifãi lɛ awui.

english: How does spreading dry grass on top of the soil help my garden crops survive the heat?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni mikɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mibɔɔ mli tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Spreading dry grass, called mulching, acts like an umbrella for the soil. It blocks the blazing sun from evaporating groundwater, keeping the root area cool and moist for a longer time.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ. Etsiɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafee shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni miiho lɛ. Ha shishifã lɛ he lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Plant roots need oxygen from the air inside soil spaces to breathe. When water sits on the field for too long, it cuts off air to the roots, causing them to suffocate and rot.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia tsei shishifãi koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu hi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni kɛ ŋmɔlɔ kɛ fitemɔ baa

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when heat stress is too high or water supply is uneven. The plant discards flowers to conserve water and energy until growing conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji akɛ dɔlɛ babaoo loo nu ni bɛ shiŋŋ lɛ hao amɛ. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛyashi shihilɛi ni amɛdaraa yɛ mli lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my cassava grow slowly and stall when planted in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa blɛoo ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ adu yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need reliable moisture during their first few weeks to build strong roots. Planting during dry spells causes the plant to go into survival mode, slowing growth until rain returns.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ŋmɔtɔ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa. Dumɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ haa tso lɛ yaa wala mli. Enɛ haa edalɛ baa shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings need shade crops like plantains planted beside them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso bibioo lɛ he hiaa tso ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantain ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves are tender and easily scorch under direct sunlight. Tall, broad-leaf crops like plantains act as living umbrellas, providing cooling shade and trapping moisture around the young trees.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa amɛ oya. Tsei ni kɛlɛ tamɔ plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa hulutsoo ni mli ejɔ ni emɔɔ nu ni ebɔleɔ tsei bibii ahe lɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines wither and turn brown before I harvest the tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani akpaa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally turn brown and dry up at maturity because the plant is transferring all its remaining nutrients down into the underground tuber to make it grow large.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbi yɛ adebɔɔ naa beni amɛdaraa lɛ ejaakɛ tso lɛ miijie niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ kɛmiiya shikpɔŋ shishi koni eha eda agbo.

english: Why do weeds around my crops grow so much faster than my actual crops after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi babaoo ebɔle he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dara oya kwraa fe miŋmɔshi nibii diɛŋtsɛ ni midu yɛ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to quickly steal water and food from the soil before cultivated crops can. Clearing them early ensures your crops get all the water and nutrients they need.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya dani tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee nakai. Nibii ni ajieɔ mra lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa nu kɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ.

english: Is chicken manure better for my crops than the chemical fertilizer I buy from the store?
ga: Ani tsina ŋmɔtɔ hi fe tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni miheɔ yɛ shwapo mli lɛ?

english: Chicken manure is often better for long-term soil health because it feeds the soil with organic matter and releases nutrients slowly. Chemical fertilizers give crops a quick boost, but manure improves the soil's ability to hold water and nutrients over time, often producing healthier yields.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsina ŋmɔshi nibii hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛnamɔ be kakadaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ yeɔ nii kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ejieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ blɛoo. Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛdaraa oya. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɛɔ nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai amli yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ haa nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa.

english: Why do crops grown with chicken manure often produce better harvest than those grown with chemical fertilizers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ tsei ni akɛ tsina ŋmei duɔ lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai fe tsei ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmei mli lɛ duɔ lɛ?

english: Poultry manure contains a wide range of micronutrients and organic material that enrich the soil naturally. This creates a balanced environment for plant roots, helping crops grow stronger and produce tastier, longer-lasting harvests compared to using only fast-acting chemical inputs.
ga: Nibii bibii babaoo kɛ nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ kooloi aŋmɔji amli lɛ yɛ kooloi aŋmɔji amli. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni ja baa kɛha tsei shishifãi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa waa ni amɛwoɔ nibii ni ŋɔɔ ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ kɛ akɛto tsofai ni tsuɔ nii oya pɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ he.

english: Why does chemical fertilizer make my crops grow fast at first, but manure keeps the crop healthy longer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli lɛ haa tsei daa oya yɛ shishijee mli lɛ? Shi ani ŋmɔshi nibii haa tsei hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Chemical fertilizers contain concentrated nutrients that dissolve instantly in water, giving crops an immediate push. Manure breaks down slowly over time through soil organisms, providing a steady and continuous supply of nutrients throughout the crop's life.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yɛ niyenii ni mli wa ni shwieɔ nu mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ. ni haa ashɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ Koolooi ashishifã fiteɔ fiofio. Yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, kɛtsɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ Enɛ haa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ yaa nɔ daa ni eyaa nɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wala be fɛɛ mli.

english: What happens to my crops if I add too much manure or fertilizer to the soil?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Adding extra fertilizer or manure beyond what the soil needs creates too much salt and chemical strength in the ground. This can burn the crop's roots and leaves, stunt their growth, and damage the produce instead of making it better.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fe bɔ ni he hiaa lɛ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei kɛ tsofai babaoo aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai ashã. ni haa dalɛ kpaa ni ekɛ nɔ ni afee lɛ fiteɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know the correct amount of manure to apply so I do not spoil my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa? Bɔni afee ni mikafite miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: The correct amount depends on your crop type and soil, but you should always measure manure using standard small containers or recommended broadcast rates rather than guessing. Also, ensure manure is well-dried or composted before applying it to prevent damage.
ga: Nɔ ni sa lɛ damɔ onibii ni oduɔ lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni oyɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Shi esa akɛ okɛ tsɛnsi bibioo ko ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ asusu o-manure lɛ he. yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooosusu he Agbɛnɛ hu, kwɛmɔ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ egbi jogbaŋŋ loo afee amɛ ŋmeii dani okɛtsu nii koni akafite.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn brown or scorched after I apply fresh chicken manure?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo shãa beni mikɛ tsina ŋmɔtɔ hee etsu nii sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Fresh chicken manure is very strong and contains high amounts of nitrogen and ammonia. When applied directly without drying or composting first, it generates heat and strong chemicals that burn plant roots and leaves.
ga: Kooloo ŋmɔtɔ ni afee lɛ ehee lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ nibii babaoo, ni nitrogen kɛ ammonia babaoo yɛ mli. Kɛ akɛwo mli tɛ̃ɛ ni egbi loo ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuuu nii klɛŋklɛŋ. Enɛ haa dɔlɛ kɛ tsofai ni naa wa ni baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi kɛ baai.

english: Can I combine chicken manure and chemical fertilizer on the same crop?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ tsina ŋmei kɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmei mli lɛ afutu tso kome nɔ?

english: Yes, combining them in reduced amounts can be helpful. Chemical fertilizer gives an early push, while manure builds the soil structure. However, you must reduce the amounts of both so you do not exceed the total limit and burn your crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ akɛ amɛ fata he yɛ yibɔ ni baa shi mli lɛ, sɛɛnamɔ baanyɛ aba. Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii oya. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ maa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, shi kɛlɛ ehe miihia ni okɛ enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ aba shi koni okatsɔ husu fɛɛ ni ato lɛ nɔ ni oshã onibii lɛ.

english: Why is it often difficult for me to find chicken manure to buy in my area?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ ewaa kɛhaa mi akɛ mahe tsina ŋmɔtɔ yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Poultry manure depends on the presence of nearby chicken farms. Because not every community has large poultry operations, and because many farmers want manure at the same time, local supplies often run out quickly or are hard to transport.
ga: Kooloi ashishifã damɔ kooloi aŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, jeee akutso fɛɛ akutso yɛ kooloi akwɛmɔ nitsumɔ agbo. Ni ejaakɛ okwaafoi babaoo he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be kome mli. No hewɔ lɛ bei pii lɛ, nibii ni akɛhaa yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya loo ewa akɛ akɛbaatsu nii.

english: What can I use on my crops if chicken manure is not available in my village?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mikɛtsu nii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛji akɛ tsina ŋmei bɛ mi akrowa lɛ mli?

english: If poultry manure is unavailable, you can use manure from goats, sheep, or cattle, or make your own compost from dry plant leaves, crop scraps, and ash. Planting leguminous crops like cowpeas also adds natural fertility to the soil.
ga: Kɛji kooloi afɔfɔi bɛ Obaanyɛ okɛ tooi, tooi, loo tsinai afɔfɔi atsu nii, loo okɛ tsei ahe baai ni egbi, ŋmɔshi nibii ni etse, kɛ sũ afee bo diɛŋtsɛ o-compost. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas ni aduɔ lɛ hu haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii yaa hiɛ.

english: Why does my soil become dry and hard when I use only chemical fertilizers for many years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi ni ewa yɛ be mli ni mikɛ tsofai pɛ etsu nii afii babaoo lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizers feed the crop directly but do not feed the soil itself. Without organic material like manure or compost, the soil loses its structure, beneficial living organisms disappear, and the ground hardens, making it difficult to hold water.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ niyenii tɛ̃ɛ shi amɛhaaa sũ lɛ niyenii. Kɛji nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite egbɛjianɔtoo. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ laajeɔ. ni shikpɔŋ lɛ fee ais Ehaa ewaa akɛ aaahi nu mli

english: How do I properly clear and prepare my land before planting cocoa so the young seedlings grow well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafo he lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni masaa he jogbaŋŋ dani madu kookoo koni dumɔwui lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ?

english: Clearing land for cocoa involves removing heavy brush and weeds while leaving select tall forest trees for shade. Proper land preparation ensures soil aeration, good drainage, and easier root penetration for young seedlings.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ajieɔ kɛhaa kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ biɔ ni ajie jwɛi kɛ jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ashi tsei kakadaji ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ ekomɛi akɛ hulutsoo. Shikpɔŋ ni asaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ shishifãi ni boteɔ mli mlɛo kɛha tsei bibii

english: Is planting cocoa in straight lines better than planting them randomly across my farm?
ga: Kookoo ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ Ani ehi fe ni aaadu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ trukaa?

english: Planting in straight, measured rows makes farm management much easier, allows for proper plant spacing, and ensures each tree gets equal access to sunlight, water, and nutrients.
ga: Dumɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja, ni asusu he. Ehaa ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa. Enɛ haa gbɛ ni sa kã tsei lɛ ateŋ. ni ehaa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: How far apart should I space my cocoa trees when putting them in the ground?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashi gbɛ ko yɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ teŋ kɛ́ midu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Cocoa trees are usually spaced 3 meters by 3 meters (about 10 feet by 10 feet) apart. Proper spacing prevents trees from overcrowding each other, competing for soil nutrients, and spreading diseases easily.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, akɛ kookoo tsei lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji mitai 3 kɛ mitai 3 (aaafee ninetalɔi 10 kɛ ninetalɔi 10). He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa tsei lɛ afee ekome. Okɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ abɔ he akaŋ ni ogbɛ helai ashwã mlɛo

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn under harsh, direct sunlight. They require temporary shade crops, like plantains, to shelter them and retain soil moisture during their first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛná he ko ni amɛhi ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why is my mature cocoa tree growing lots of thick leaves and branches but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso ni eda lɛ yɛ baai kɛ niji ni mli tse babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: When a cocoa tree receives too much shade or overgrown foliage, it uses its energy for leaf growth instead of flowering. Pruning excess branches lets in sunlight, encouraging the tree to flower and set pods.
ga: Kɛ́ kookoo tso ko ná hulutsoo babaoo loo eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ, Cacao tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ baai moŋ fe fɔfɔi. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ pods.

english: How do I know if my soil is fertile enough for cocoa or if it needs fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi obɔ kɛ kookoo loo ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli?

english: Good cocoa soil is dark, loose, and rich in organic matter. If young plants grow slowly or show pale, yellowish leaves, the soil lacks key nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus, or potassium.
ga: Cocoa shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ mli edɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɛ mli. Kɛji tso bibioo lɛ daa blɛoo loo eyɛ baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, phosphorus, loo potassium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Cassava is not ideal for planting right next to young cocoa because its heavy root system aggressively competes for soil moisture and nutrients, which can stunt cocoa growth.
ga: Cassava esaaa akɛ aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ kookoo bibii. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi ni tsii lɛ baatswa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ baanyɛ atsĩ kookoo lɛ dalɛ naa.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that thrives in cold, wet, and overly shaded environments. Regular pruning and removing infected pods quickly helps stop the fungus from spreading.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ, kɛ hulutsoo fe nine. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya ni ajie amɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akpa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: When my cocoa farm produces a massive harvest all at once, how should I manage the heavy workload so the pods don't spoil?
ga: Beni mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ nibii babaoo yɛ be kome mli lɛ. Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ minitsumɔ ni tsii lɛ nɔ koni pods lɛ akafite?

english: Group labor with neighboring farmers helps speed up harvesting. Pods should be harvested as soon as they ripen and broken within 5 days to prevent the beans inside from germinating or rotting.
ga: Kuu nitsumɔ kɛ okwaafoi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni kpamɔ lɛ yaa oya. Esa akɛ akpa ŋmeii lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni amɛkumɔ yɛ gbii 5 mli koni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ akakwɛ̃ loo akafite.

english: Why do I need to heap my wet cocoa beans and cover them with plantain leaves before sun-drying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibuaa kookoo ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ anaa ni mikɛ plantain baai haa nɔ dani mikɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Covering cocoa beans with plantain leaves creates heat for fermentation, a 5-to-7-day natural process that develops the essential chocolate flavor and rich brown color required by buyers.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ plantain baai ha kookoo yibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo baa kɛha ŋmɔlɔ. Eji adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni heɔ gbii 5 kɛyashi 7 dani anyɛɔ ashɛɔ tsokolate ni he hiaa lɛ he ŋmɔlɔ kɛ su ni mli kwɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ sumɔɔ lɛ he.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas fix nitrogen from the air into the soil. This naturally enriches the soil, giving your maize extra nutrients to grow strong without relying entirely on expensive chemical fertilizers.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii saa nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa o-corn lɛ naa niyenii babaoo koni ekwɛ̃ waa ni ekɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔɔ tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does striga weed keep coming back in my cereal farm even after I weed it out by hand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Striga jwɛi lɛ yaa nɔ ekuɔ esɛɛ ebaa miŋmaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ minine shwie nɔ moŋ.

english: Striga, or witchweed, attaches directly to the roots of crops like maize and sorghum underground before you even see it above ground. Its tiny seeds can live in the soil for up to 20 years, so pulling it out late doesn't stop new seeds from growing.
ga: Striga, loo witchweed lɛ kpɛtɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa shishifãi ahe tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Dani obaana amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ po lɛ, amɛdumɔwui bibii lɛ baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashi afii 20, no hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ojie amɛ blɛoo lɛ, no haŋ dumɔwui heei akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my sorghum plants stay green during dry spells while my maize farm dries up completely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sorghum tsei lɛ feɔ eŋɔli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli yɛ be mli ni mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Sorghum has a deeper root system than maize and can go dormant when water is scarce to conserve moisture. Once the rains return, sorghum wakes up and continues growing, whereas maize requires continuous soil moisture.
ga: Sorghum yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ fe ŋmãa ni ebaanyɛ ehi shi kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi lɛ bɛ. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ, Sorghum baate shi ni eya nɔ eda. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa he miihia shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your plants are lacking nitrogen, which can happen if heavy rains wash the nutrients away or if the soil is tired. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure restores their green color and vigor.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. Enɛ baanyɛ aba mli kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fite loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛná amɛhe su kɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer stress, such as extreme heat, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to focus on growing foliage instead of fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛmiihao, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Enɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow out small and twisted instead of big and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji bibii ni egbɛ eshwa moŋ fe ni eeefee agbo ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yams become deformed and stunted when planted in hard, un-mounded soil full of stones, or when infected by microscopic soil worms called nematodes that damage the growing tip of the tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ feɔ nɔ ni ehiii ni egbɔjɔɔ kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni bɛ gɔŋ nɔ ni tɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. aloo kɛ́ sũ mli ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ emɔ lɛ. Enɛ fiteɔ ŋmei lɛ naagbee ni miida lɛ.

english: Why is it better for me to clear my land without burning the weeds and bushes first?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ majie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni mishãaa jwɛi kɛ jwɛi lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ?

english: Burning destroys valuable organic matter and kills helpful soil organisms that feed your crops. Clearing without burning allows the plant material to rot and act as natural mulch, keeping the soil cool and fertile.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni jara wa ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ni egbeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni haa onibii lɛ niyenii lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie tso lɛ mli nibii lɛ ni ashãaa lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ mli nibii lɛ afite ni etsu nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do seeds saved from my previous hybrid maize harvest produce smaller yields when I replant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ mi tsutsu ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ midu ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for high performance in their first generation. Seeds collected from that harvest lose their high-yield genetics in the second generation, resulting in uneven growth and smaller cobs.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni etsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ fɔmɔ nii ni haa yibii babaoo lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa ni ekɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee, ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why does my harvested grains get destroyed by weevils even after I dry them well in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kpata dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ ahiɛ eyɛ mli akɛ migbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Sun drying lowers water content, but invisible insect eggs may already be inside the grain from the farm. If stored in regular sacks, these eggs hatch and multiply, so sealed hermetic bags are needed to suffocate the insects.
ga: Hulu lɛ baaha nu lɛ nɔ aba shi. Shi ekolɛ kooloi bibii ni anaaa lɛ awui yɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ amli momo. Kɛ akɛto kotoku ni sa mli lɛ, nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ baafɔ ni amɛfɔ bii. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni akɛ kotoku ni atsĩ naa lɛ atsu nii koni ŋmeii akafo amɛmumɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants rot at the bottom of the fruit when I water them irregularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fiteɔ yɛ aduawai lɛ ashishi kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo amɛmli be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Irregular watering prevents the plant from continuously absorbing calcium from the soil. This deficiency causes the tissues at the bottom of the developing fruit to break down and turn dark and rotten.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be lɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekaya nɔ ekɛ calcium ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ nɛɛ haa fãji ni yɔɔ aduawai ni miida lɛ shishi lɛ fiteɔ ni efeɔ ediŋŋ ni efiteɔ.

english: Why do my mango trees take so many years before they start giving me fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mango tso lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani ebɔi yibiiwoo lɛ?

english: Mango trees planted directly from seeds spend up to 8 years building roots and trunk strength before fruiting. If you plant grafted mango seedlings instead, they will start producing sweet fruits much faster, usually within 3 to 4 years.
ga: Mango tsei ni akwɛɔ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ heɔ afii 8 dani amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ feɔ hewalɛ dani amɛwoɔ yibii. Kɛji odu mango dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ moŋ Dumɔwui lɛ baabɔi yibii ni ŋɔɔ womɔ mra kwraa, bei pii lɛ yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli.

english: If I plant a seed from a very sweet mango, will the new tree produce the exact same sweet fruits?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui kɛjɛ mango ko ni ŋɔɔ waa mli lɛ, Ani tso hee lɛ baawo yibii ni ŋɔɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ pɛpɛɛpɛ?

english: Not always. Trees grown from seeds carry mixed traits, so the fruit may turn out sour or fibrous. To guarantee you get the exact same sweet mango, you need to plant a grafted seedling made from a stem cut from that sweet tree.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be tsei ni adu kɛjɛ dumɔwui amli lɛ baaná sui ni efutu. No hewɔ lɛ, aduawai lɛ baanyɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo fiber yɔɔ mli. Enɛ ji koni akɛma nɔ mi akɛ obaaná mango ni ŋɔɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Ebaabi ni okwɛ dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli ni akɛ niji ni afo kɛjɛ tso ni ŋɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ fee lɛ.

english: What causes an old mango tree to stop producing fruits, and how can I bring it back to life?
ga: Mɛni haa mango tsei ni egbɔ lɛ kpaa yibiiwoo? Ni te abaafee tɛŋŋ aha ehi wala mli ekoŋŋ?

english: As mango trees grow old, their upper branches become thick and bushy, blocking sunlight from reaching inner branches where flowers grow. Trimming back heavy old wood allows sunlight inside, triggering the tree to sprout fresh wood that yields new fruit.
ga: Kɛ mango lɛ eda lɛ ŋwɛi niji lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔji. Tsi hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ tsei niji ni yɔɔ mligbɛ ni fɔfɔi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ ahe. Tso momo ni tsii ni afoɔ koni hulu la lɛ akpɛ yɛ mli. Kanyamɔ ​​tsei lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii heei ni woɔ yibii heei.

english: Is it safe for me to plant cassava or vegetables between my young mango trees?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu ŋmei loo aduawai yɛ mi mango tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ?

english: Yes, intercropping low crops like groundnuts or cassava between young mango trees is fine while the trees are small. Just leave a clear radius of about one meter around each mango stem so the vegetables do not steal water and plant food from the young tree.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei. Obaanyɛ ofee enɛ yɛ mango tsei bibii ateŋ be mli ni tsei lɛ darako lɛ. Shi radius ni mli tse ni miihe ashɛ mita 1 yɛ mango tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko he kɛkɛ. Enɛ ji koni aduawai lɛ akaju nu kɛ niyenii ni amɛduɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei bibii lɛ amli.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my sweet orange trees before small fruits can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ mi ŋmeii tso ni ŋɔɔ lɛ nɔ dani aduawai bibii lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Citrus trees drop their blossoms when they suffer from sudden water stress during dry spells or when sap-sucking pests attack the delicate flowers. Keeping the soil moist with mulch and checking for tiny insects helps flowers stay attached and form fruits.
ga: Citrus tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛna nu he haomɔ trukaa yɛ hɔmɔ be mli loo kɛ́ ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu lɛ tutua fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni okwɛ kɛji kooloi bibii yɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akpɛtɛ he ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my citrus trees turning yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-orange tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the tree lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, or the roots are waterlogged from poor drainage. Adding organic manure or balanced plant food around the base helps restore healthy green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo nu eyi shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo tso niyenii ni ja afata he kɛbɔle he. Tso lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my oranges taste sour even when they look big and yellow on the outside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange lɛ mli ŋɔɔ eyɛ mli akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni eda ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ kponɔgbɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: Oranges need plenty of direct sunlight and adequate time to ripen fully on the branch to develop natural sugars. Picking fruits too early or growing trees under heavy shade prevents the juice from turning sweet.
ga: Oranges he miihia hulu la babaoo tɛ̃ɛ kɛ be ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ yɛ eniji lɛ anɔ koni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli sugars aba. Kɛ́ atse aduawai mra tsɔ loo adu tsei yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa shishi lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ afee nɔ ni ŋɔɔ.

english: How do citrus trees react when there is a long dry season without rain?
ga: Te citrus tsei feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa tɛŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ mli?

english: To survive heavy dry spells, citrus trees curl their leaves inward and may drop young fruits to protect their main stem and roots. Covering the soil around the tree trunk with dry grass retains ground moisture and protects the harvest.
ga: Bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa lɛ mli lɛ, Citrus tsei lɛ baafo amɛbaai lɛ amli ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛshwie aduawai bibii koni amɛkɛbu tso lɛ shishi kɛ shishifãi titrii lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi shwie tsei akutsei ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi, ni ebuɔ ŋmaa lɛ he.

english: Can I cut heavy branches off my fruit trees for wood without killing the tree?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mafo tsei niji ni tsii. Ani abaanyɛ atsɔ mitso ni woɔ yibii lɛ afee tso ni agbeee tso lɛ?

english: Yes, carefully pruning selected branches does not kill fruit trees. In fact, cutting off dead, diseased, or overgrown wood encourages the tree to focus its energy on growing healthy new shoots and bigger fruits.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsei niji ni ahala jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni afolɔ mli lɛ egbeee tso ni woɔ yibii lɛ. Yɛ anɔkwale mli lɛ Tso ni egbo, ni hela emɔ lɛ, loo ni eda fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ woɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama ŋmeii heei kɛ aduawai wuji ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are there dark black coatings appearing on the leaves and skin of my fruit tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nɔ ko ni diŋɔ diŋŋ yɔɔ mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ ahewolo nɔ lɛ?

english: That black coating is a soot-like fungus that grows on sticky waste left behind by small insects like aphids and mealybugs. Controlling these soft insects early clears up the dark layer so leaves can capture sunlight properly.
ga: Nakai ŋmɔtɔ diŋ lɛ ji ŋmɔtɔ ko ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ jwɛi ni ŋmɔtɔ bibii tamɔ aphids kɛ mealybugs lɛ shiɔ yɛ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Ebaaha ŋwɛi ŋta ni yɔɔ duŋ lɛ mli afee faŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni baai lɛ anyɛ aná hulu la lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green leafy leaves, or it could mean the soil is too waterlogged for roots to breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli Aloo ebaanyɛ etsɔɔ akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wither and die when I clear all the big trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijieɔ cacao tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight. They need shade trees to protect their delicate leaves from sun burn and to keep the soil moist during hot periods.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo koni amɛbu amɛbaai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he, ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ.

english: Does it matter which direction I plant my cassava stem cuttings in the soil?
ga: Ani miduɔ mi yucca tsei lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he?

english: Yes, the small buds on the stem must point upwards toward the sky so that leaves and branches grow properly above ground while roots form below.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Enɛ ji koni baai kɛ tsei aniji adara jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ shishigbɛ.

english: Why do my crops yield less harvest every year even though I plant on the exact same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the specific nutrients that plant needs from the soil, leaving the land tired unless you rotate crops or add plant food.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ pɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, etɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ. Ja otsake ŋmɔshi nibii loo okɛ tsei niyenii fata he.

english: Flowers drop when the plant gets stressed, which usually happens due to extreme heat, insufficient water, or using too much fertilizer that causes rapid leaf growth instead of fruit set.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao. Bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo ni naa wa waa hewɔ ni enɛ baa lɛ. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Aloo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo atsu nii ni oha baai akwɛ̃ oya yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Extra shoots act like extra mouths to feed—they steal water and nutrients from the main stem, resulting in smaller plantain bunches if you do not remove them.
ga: Tsoi ni fa lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ daaŋ krokomɛi kɛha niyenii. Amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ haa plantains lɛ feɔ bibii kɛji ojieee amɛ.

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in little balls on their roots, which stays in the soil to feed the next crop you plant.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ bɔɔlu bibii amli yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni no hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni odu lɛ niyenii.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the sunlight to produce the energy required to grow big, heavy tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã hulutsoo be lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: What causes the leaves of my pepper plants to curl up into small cups?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ kɔɔpoi bibii?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking juices from under the leaves, or by viruses spread by sap-sucking insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ anɔ

english: How does spreading dry grass on top of the soil around my crops help them stay healthy?
ga: Akɛ jwɛi fɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ Te miŋmɔshi nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ tɛŋŋ?

english: Dry grass acts like a protective blanket over the dirt, stopping the sun from drying out the soil quickly so the plant roots stay moist for much longer.
