ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsi hulu la lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya. No hewɔ lɛ tsei shishifãi lɛ hiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Should I weed my maize farm on a fixed weekly routine or wait until the weeds reach a certain height?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli jwɛi lɛ daa otsi loo mamɛ kɛyashi jwɛi lɛ baashɛ he ko?

english: Focus on the condition of the field rather than a strict calendar count. Clearing weeds while they are still small prevents them from stealing vital soil nutrients from your young maize, saving you heavy labor later.
ga: Kɛ ojwɛŋmɔ ama ŋmɔ mli shihilɛ nɔ moŋ fe kalanda nɔ kanemɔ ni mli wa. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi lɛ be mli ni amɛji gbekɛbii lolo lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa ni jɛ o-baby corn lɛ mli lɛ. ni haa onáa nitsumɔ ni tsii sɛɛ mli.

english: How often should I prune my cocoa trees throughout the year?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ amli yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: Instead of focusing on a set number of times per month, inspect your trees regularly. Prune lightly whenever you notice overlapping branches or unwanted suckers (chupons) to allow sunlight and fresh air to reach the pods and prevent black pod disease.
ga: Mohu ɔ, mo ngɔ o juɛmi kɛ ma si abɔ nɛ o maa pee ngɛ nyɔhiɔ ɔ mi ɔ nɔ. Kwɛmɔ otsei lɛ amli daa, ŋmɔmɔ blɛoo be fɛɛ be ni obaana niji ni ebɔle amɛhe loo ŋmeii ni ataooo (chupons) koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ashɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe ni ekɛtsi black pod hela naa.

english: Is it better to water my vegetable garden every single day or just a few times a week?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oooha aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu daa gbi loo shii fioo komɛi pɛ yɛ otsi mli?

english: Soaking the soil deeply three times a week is generally better than light daily watering. Deep watering encourages roots to grow deep into the ground where moisture stays longer, making your crops stronger during dry spells.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oookɛ nu awo mli shii etɛ yɛ otsi mli lɛ hi fe nu ni oookɛwo mli fioo daa gbi. Nu ni awoɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ, he ni ehiɔ shi yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ. Ha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli

english: Why does my soil dry out so quickly even though I water my crops every morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ gbiɔ oya nɛkɛ? Ni mikɛ nu haa tsei lɛ daa leebi?

english: Direct sunlight bakes bare earth and evaporates water fast. Covering the soil around your crops with dry grass or leaves (mulching) acts as a protective blanket, keeping the ground cool and holding moisture much longer.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baajie shikpɔŋ lɛ kpo ni eha nu lɛ atsɔ la oya. Mulching around Kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi (mulching) aha oŋmɔshi nibii ahe koni etsu nii akɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be babaoo.

english: Is it better to apply fertilizer once in a large amount or split it into smaller routine applications?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo awo mli shikome loo ojara mli bibii bibii daa?

english: Splitting fertilizer into smaller, frequent doses gives crops a steady food supply as they grow. Heavy rain can easily wash away one single large application, wasting your money and leaving the crop hungry later.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii shii abɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ nitsumɔ agbo kome pɛ he. Efiteɔ shika ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ hɔmɔ sɛɛ mli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the plant is running out of nitrogen, which it needs for leaf growth. Adding a small targeted dose of top-dressing fertilizer gives the crop the energy it needs to form full, healthy cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen, ni he hiaa koni baa lɛ adara. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa fioo ko ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni etsɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Should I spray chemicals on my pepper farm every week to keep bugs away?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai afɔ mi-pepper ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ daa otsi koni mikɛbu he kɛjɛ kooloi bibii ahe?

english: Spraying on a strict weekly schedule wastes expensive chemicals and can cause pests to become resistant. Inspect your crops regularly and only spray when you actually spot harmful insects or early signs of disease.
ga: Tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ daa otsi lɛ fiteɔ tsofai ni jara wa, ni ebaanyɛ eha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akaye nɔ. Kwɛmɔ onibii amli daa ni okɛ tsofa lɛ afɔ nɔ pɛ kɛji ona kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo hela he okadii ni tsɔɔ mra.

english: Extreme heat, inconsistent watering, or sap-sucking insects can stress tomato plants, forcing them to drop flowers. Providing steady water and managing pests early helps the plant retain its blooms and set fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni akɛhaaa yɛ be fɛɛ mli Aloo, kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ baanyɛ aha tomato tsei lɛ aná haomɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji fɔfɔi lɛ ni shwieɔ shi. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ fɔfɔi amli ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Planting cassava too close forces plants to compete for sunlight and soil food. This leaves you with tall, weak stems and tiny roots, whereas giving each plant enough space yields larger, heavier tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ baaha oná tsei ni kɛlɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ shishifãi bibii, yɛ be mli ni kɛ́ oha tso fɛɛ tso he gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ mli tsei lɛ afee ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die during their first dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have shallow roots and tender leaves that easily burn under full sun. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a protective canopy that keeps them cool and humid.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai bibii ni hulu lɛ shãa oya. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ehaa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why should I plant my crops in straight rows instead of scattering the seeds everywhere?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja moŋ fe ni magbɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashwã he fɛɛ he lɛ?

english: Planting in straight rows ensures each plant gets enough space, sunlight, and soil nutrients to grow strong. It also makes weeding, applying fertilizer, and harvesting much easier for you.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekwɛ̃ waa. Ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ hu feɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa bo.

english: Why shouldn't I burn all the grass and cleared bushes on my land before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishãa mijwɛi kɛ tsei bibii lɛ fɛɛ dani miduɔ nii lɛ?

english: Burning destroys the good nutrients in the topsoil and kills useful soil organisms. Leaving cleared vegetation to decay naturally feeds the soil and keeps it moist for your crops.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ niyenii kpakpai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ, ni egbeɔ sũ mli nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ. Tsei ni ajie lɛ ni oooŋmɛ gbɛ ni amɛgboi yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a cry for help showing that your maize lacks nitrogen nutrient in the soil or that heavy rains have washed the nutrients away from the plant roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji yelikɛbuamɔ ni akɛbolɔɔ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo akɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my pepper plants keep dropping their flowers before turning into pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yaa nɔ eshwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ? Dani ebaatsɔ pepper aduawai?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they are stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or attacks by tiny insects like thrips. Keeping the soil moist helps prevent this.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be loo kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips ni tutuaa mɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Why do my yam tubers come out bent and twisted instead of long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔji lɛ ebɔle shi moŋ ni amɛfee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers bend when they hit hard ground, rocks, or compacted soil underground. Making high, soft soil mounds or ridges gives the tubers room to grow straight.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baakɔ kɛji amɛtswa shikpɔŋ ni wa, tɛi, loo shikpɔŋ shishi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ. Kɛ́ afee gɔŋ loo ŋshɔ ni nɔ kwɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ, ebaawo bulb lɛ hewalɛ ni ekwɛ̃ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes bruise and rot so quickly before I reach the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni mikpa lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egboɔ oya dani eshɛɔ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes rot quickly when they are harvested in the hot sun, thrown roughly into wooden crates, or piled too high. Gentle handling and keeping them in cool shade right after harvest keeps them fresh longer.
ga: Tomato fiteɔ oya kɛ́ akpa yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Akɛshwieɔ tso adeka mli yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ loo akɛtoɔ he ko ni nɔ kwɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ tsu nii blɛoo ni okɛto he ko ni jɛmɛ ejɔ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛhi shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad to harvest plantain bunches with a dirty or rusty cutlass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ akɛ tsɔne ni mli ewo muji loo ŋmɔtɔ baakpa plantains lɛ?

english: A dirty cutlass introduces bacteria and fungi directly into the cut stem of the plantain, which can cause diseases to spread to the rest of your plantain mat.
ga: Kakla ni mli ewo muji lɛ kɛ helatsɛmɛi kɛ ŋmeii woɔ plantain tso lɛ tso ni afo lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã plantain lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ mli.

english: How do I know if my cassava roots are fully matured and ready to harvest?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, and the soil around the base of the plant begins to crack open from the growing tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ kɛjɛɔ bulb ni miida lɛ he.

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same plot exhausts specific soil nutrients and lets maize-specific pests and diseases build up in the soil. Rotating with beans or groundnuts resets the soil quality.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ shii abɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ afite ni eha abele pɔtɛɛ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Kɛ akɛ ŋmei loo ŋmei tsakeɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under strong heat. Plantains grow fast and provide big leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving cocoa the shade and moisture it needs to survive its early stages.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Enɛ haa kookoo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eshishijee fãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize turn yellow from the tip downward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛshishigbɛ kɛmiiba shi lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for leaf growth. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer supplies this food, restoring the green color and helping the crop produce healthy ears.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha niyenii nɛɛ afee eŋɔli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa toi ni mli wa

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl into tight cups and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛfeɔ kɔɔpoi ni mli wa ni amɛkpaa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like mites or whiteflies sucking sap from young leaves. Controlling these pests protects the new leaves so the plant can grow and flower normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛŋ ni nuɔ baai bibii amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ anɔyeli yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ baai heei ahe koni tso lɛ anyɛ ada ni ewo fɔfɔi bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn soft and black?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato eŋɔli lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ediŋŋ lɛ?

english: Black spots at the bottom of tomatoes are caused by blossom-end rot, which occurs when the plant cannot get enough calcium or experiences irregular watering while the fruit is forming.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ baa ji fɔfɔi lɛ anaagbee ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa loo akɛ nu haa lɛ be fɛɛ be be mli ni aduawai lɛ miifɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all big trees from the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under harsh, direct sunlight. Taller plants like plantains or shade trees act like natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and moisture needed to survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei ni kɛlɛ tamɔ plantains loo shade tsei tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli shade. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa kookoo bibioo lɛ ni enáa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that need to lift their leaves up to catch sunlight. Staking keeps leaves off the hot ground, reduces leaf diseases, and encourages the plant to form bigger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni esa akɛ amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni hulu la ashɛ amɛnɔ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ waa yɛ lɛ, ebaaha baai ahe helai aba shi, ni ewo tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛfee bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and weak with tiny ears when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛyɛ toi bibii beni adu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room and food to grow strong and produce large ears.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni enyɛ eda ni ená toi wuji.

english: Why do my crop leaves roll or fold up on hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plants curl their leaves during extreme heat to reduce the surface area exposed to direct sun. This natural defense helps them hold onto moisture and prevent drying out until the weather cools down.
ga: Tsei baafolɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shi. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ boteɔ mli ni ehaaa egbi kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why do my crops give smaller harvests when I plant maize on the same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the ground. Rotating with legumes like beans or groundnuts helps restore the soil.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii atsakeɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baa ekoŋŋ

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting in the ground if I leave them too long past maturity?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ ni amɛdara tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots are designed to store energy, but once fully mature, remaining in wet soil exposes them to rot-causing bacteria and fungi that break down the starchy roots.
ga: Afee cassava shishifãi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ato. Shi kɛ́ amɛdara kwraa lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ ni amɛshwɛɔ lɛ haa amɛnaa helai ni fiteɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ shishifãi ni tamɔ powda lɛ.

english: How does adding dried animal manure help my crops handle dry weather better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni egbi ni akɛfataa he lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkpee shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ anaa jogbaŋŋ?

english: Animal manure improves soil structure so it acts like a sponge, holding onto soil moisture longer during dry spells while slowly releasing nutrients to feed crop roots.
ga: Koolooi ashishifã haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii feɔ fɛo. No hewɔ lɛ etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ sponji. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, fiofio lɛ Ejieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kpo akɛ niyenii kɛha tsei shishifãi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in an open field with no tall crops around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei kakadaji bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings need shade because direct sunlight scorches their soft leaves and dries up the soil before their roots can grow deep enough to find water.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi dani shishifãi lɛ aya shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛna nu.
